message.content: The building envelope refers to all components that form the exterior shell of a structure, comprising the boundary elements that separate interior space from the outside environment. Its primary function is to keep indoor spaces dry while maintaining and regulating thermal conditions, thereby enabling effective climate control through heating, cooling, and humidity management. The design of building envelopes is a specialized area within both architectural and engineering practice, drawing on diverse areas of building science and indoor climate control to optimize performance and comfort.

Continuous tracks are driven by a powered drive sprocket that engages holes or pins in the track links to propel the belt. In military vehicles, the drive sprocket is typically mounted above the ground-contact area to remain fixed relative to the hull, whereas agricultural crawlers often integrate the drive wheel as part of the bogie itself. Suspension for the sprocket is possible but mechanically more complex. At the opposite end, an idler wheel provides tension to prevent track loosening or throwing. To prevent derailment, track links frequently feature vertical guide horns that fit into grooves between the doubled road wheels and the idler or sprocket. In vehicles with a rear-mounted sprocket, the idler is placed higher than the road wheels to help the track climb over obstacles. Some track layouts employ return rollers to keep the top of the track running straight between the drive sprocket and idler. Slack track configurations allow the track to droop and ride on top of large road wheels; this arrangement was used in the Christie suspension and can lead to misidentification of other slack-track vehicles.

Continuous tracks are a common propulsion system for off-road and armored vehicles. The loss of a single track segment can render the vehicle immobile, representing a reliability concern in time-sensitive or critical operations. Tracks may disengage from guide wheels, idlers, or drive sprockets, potentially leading to a jam or detachment, a situation often described as a thrown track. When a track becomes jammed or overly tightened, repair can require breaking the track, which may necessitate the use of explosives or specialized tools to separate components. By contrast, some multi-wheeled configurations, such as eight-wheel-drive layouts, can continue to operate after the loss of one or more non-sequential wheels, depending on the wheel arrangement and how the drivetrain distributes power to the remaining wheels.

On June 15, 2011, Hewlett-Packard filed suit in the California Superior Court for Santa Clara County alleging that Oracle had breached an agreement to continue supporting the Itanium processor used in HP's high-end enterprise servers. Oracle responded by characterizing the action as an improper use of the judicial system and maintaining that any implied obligation to support Itanium would not have existed if Oracle had known that Léo Apotheker, then the chief executive of SAP, would become HP's CEO.

Oracle Corporation is a multinational technology company that develops and markets database software, cloud infrastructure, and a broad array of enterprise applications. Within the wider public-sector IT landscape, large government projects have highlighted the challenges of cost estimation and implementation risk. For example, in Oregon on April 25, 2014, the state moved to discontinue Cover Oregon and enroll residents through the federal exchange. Estimates indicated that switching to the federal portal would cost about five million dollars, whereas repairing Cover Oregon would have required roughly seventy-eight million dollars. These figures illustrate the financial pressures associated with major government IT deployments, a market segment in which Oracle provides enterprise software, cloud services, and consulting to public-sector clients.

In a 1663 account attributed to John Josselyn, Kittery is described as the most populous town in the province at a time when there were relatively few towns in the area. Josselyn notes that Kittery lay not far from Passacataway, a locality that has been identified with Portsmouth.
In 1705, during Queen Anne's War, tribes of the Wabanaki Confederacy attacked Kittery, Maine, resulting in six residents being killed and five taken captive.

Opened to the public in August 2019, the underground complex presents a retro-inspired commercial street alongside an immersive museum. Named Heping Guoju (和平菓局), it is located on the B2 basement level of the Beijing Department Store.
The Beijing Department Store (北京市百货大楼, Pinyin: Běijīng Shì Bǎihuò Dàlóu) is a major department store located on Wangfujing Street in Beijing, China.

ISO 11170:2003 prescribes a defined set of tests intended to verify the performance of filter elements. The test regimen assesses hydraulic performance, mechanical integrity, and separation efficiency. The standard is not meant to qualify a filter for a specific duty or to simulate service conditions. Instead, qualification for actual service requires a tailored test protocol that reflects operating conditions and includes the actual working fluid. The ISO 11170 procedure can be applied to a single fluid or to groups of fluids sharing similar chemistry.
The Oregonian is the city's sole daily general-interest newspaper serving Portland. It has circulation throughout the state of Oregon and is also distributed in Clark County, Washington.

Violent crime in Portland, Oregon reached a peak in 2022, when there were a record 101 homicides. The preceding year recorded 90 homicides in 2021, while earlier years showed considerably smaller figures, with 27 homicides in 2017 and 20 in 2016.

Assistive technology encompasses devices designed to enhance mobility and independence for people with physical impairments. Positioning devices enable individuals to stand and bear weight on their legs while reducing the risk of falls. Standers, a subset of these devices, are classified by the occupant’s orientation into prone and supine types. Prone standers shift body weight toward the front of the body and typically include a tray, making them suitable for users who are actively attempting to perform tasks. In contrast, supine standers distribute weight toward the back and are appropriate for individuals with limited mobility or those recovering from injury.

A screen magnifier is a software utility that integrates with a computer's graphical subsystem to provide an enlarged view of the display. By magnifying text and graphics, it improves readability and viewing comfort for users with limited vision. The tool is comparable to desktop video magnifiers and serves as an assistive technology for people with low vision. Once loaded into memory, it functions as a digital magnifier for the computer, enlarging the region around the cursor as it moves across the screen. This dynamic magnification enhances accessibility for users with a wide range of visual abilities.

Taitung City Hall serves as the headquarters of the Taitung City government, tasked with the city’s general administration and related matters. It manages education and cultural outreach, engages in negotiation, and provides emergency assistance and disaster-prevention leadership. The office handles environmental taxation and sanitation controls, as well as financial management, public property governance, treasury functions, and tax assistance. It regulates farming and fishing activities, wholesale trade, marketing, and business administration, and oversees urban planning and the operation of public facilities. In addition, it directs tourism and community development efforts, administers military service and welfare programs, and supervises the national health insurance program along with indigenous administration affairs.

Taitung City is served by Taitung Airport, through which air travelers commonly access the city. It also functions as a gateway to Green Island and Orchid Island, which are popular tourist destinations.

The Corps Francs d'Afrique, commanded by General Joseph de Goislard de Monsabert, fought in the Tunisian campaign against Rommel's Afrikakorps alongside the United States Fifth Army. They also operated with the British 139th Brigade at Kasserine Pass and Sidi Nasr. In a bayonet assault near Kef Zilia, they faced two-to-one odds against the Italian 34th Battalion of the 10th Bersaglieri, resulting in the capture of 380 prisoners and the killing of the Italian battalion commander. The unit captured the plans for Operation Ausladung and later participated in the capture of Bizerte in May 1943.

The Sudetendeutsches Freikorps was a German nationalist paramilitary organization associated with Sudeten German interests. It fought against Czechoslovakia and sought to annex the Sudetenland into Germany.

Majority bonus refers to a structural advantage conferred on certain political parties by electoral designs that are not fully proportional. In single-member district systems, particularly those using first-past-the-post rules, larger parties often secure a disproportionately larger share of seats than their vote share would justify. Mixed-member majoritarian arrangements that employ parallel voting similarly tend to produce seat allocations biased in favor of specific parties, effectively granting a bonus beyond pure proportionality. Hungary’s so-called “winner compensation” mechanism has been criticized as functioning as a de facto majority bonus presented as a compensatory feature. In mixed-member proportional systems, the presence of overhang seats can create additional, bonus-like seats for certain parties, further amplifying their representation beyond proportional expectations.

The majority bonus is an electoral mechanism intended to reinforce the winning side by awarding an additional share of seats. The approach has been adopted by several European countries, with Greece implementing it in 2004. France and Italy have also adopted the system, applying the majority bonus to regional and municipal elections.

Within DRDA, the messaging sequences, communication protocols, and structural elements used for distributed data management are defined by the Distributed Data Management Architecture. DRDA‑style distributed SQL processing is distinctive from contemporary distributed SQL databases, highlighting notable differences in architectural approach and interoperability with heterogeneous systems.

Within the SQL standard, several design decisions are explicitly left to the discretion of individual implementations. A common illustration is how to name a result column that was not named explicitly in the query, since the standard does not mandate a single naming convention for such columns. As a result, different database management systems may assign different default names to these unnamed columns, causing variability in behavior across platforms. In practice, this means that the naming of unnamed result columns is determined by the implementing system rather than by the standard itself, a factor that has implications for portability and interoperability.

John Jacob Rhodes received one of the inaugural Congressional Distinguished Service Medals from Speaker Dennis Hastert on August 14, 2003. He was among a small group of recipients to be honored with the award. In remarks to Hastert, Rhodes said that the speakership was the position he had always most desired.

John Jacob Rhodes was an American Republican politician from Arizona who, in 1950, sought the office of Arizona Attorney General with Barry Goldwater predicting defeat in a state that was then more than three-quarters Democratic. In 1952 he ran for Arizona's 1st congressional district, encompassing Phoenix and parts of Maricopa County, and defeated 11-term Democratic incumbent John Murdock by eight percentage points to join the 83rd United States Congress, becoming the first Republican ever elected to represent Arizona in the U.S. House. He remained active in the Arizona delegation to several Republican National Conventions, and Goldwater appointed him as his personal representative on the Platform Committee in 1964. Rhodes later served as chairman of the Platform Committee in 1972 and as Permanent Chairman of the Republican National Conventions in 1976 and 1980.

Peter Doig: House of Music is an exhibition at the Serpentine Gallery in London, running from 10 October 2025 to 8 February 2026, which examines the influence of music on Peter Doig's work and practice.

Peter Doig completed his studies at the Chelsea College of Arts, and soon after was awarded the Whitechapel Artist Prize, an accolade that enabled a solo exhibition at the Whitechapel Art Gallery in 1991. The show featured Swamped (1990), Iron Hill (1991), and The Architect's Home in the Ravine (1991). These works are widely regarded as among Doig's major pieces. The Architect's Home in the Ravine depicts the modernist central Toronto residence of architect Eberhard Zeidler, located in the Rosedale ravine.

Qumranet was founded in 2005. Its leadership consisted of CEO Benny Schnaider, President Rami Tamir, CTO Moshe Bar, and Chairman Giora Yaron. The company raised a total of $20 million across two financing rounds, with investors including Norwest Venture Partners, Cisco Systems, Sequoia Capital, and the founding partners.

Qumranet, Inc. was an enterprise software company that developed a desktop virtualization platform delivering hosted desktops running on server-based Kernel-based Virtual Machines (KVM). The platform integrated with the company’s SPICE protocol for remote display. The firm was the creator, maintainer, and global sponsor of the KVM open-source hypervisor, a project that originated under its auspices.

Fataluku is an Austronesian language spoken in Timor-Leste. A substantial portion of its vocabulary comprises loanwords from other Austronesian languages, reflecting long-standing regional contact. Sanskrit and Arabic loanwords have been incorporated through Malay intermediaries, illustrating historical channels of religious and commercial exchange. The language likewise bears elements borrowed from Portuguese, reflecting the colonial era and subsequent contact with Portuguese-speaking communities.

Fataluku is divided into five principal dialects: East Fataluku, South Fataluku, Central Fataluku, North Fataluku, and Northwest Fataluku. Beyond phonological variation, the precise nature and extent of differences among these dialects remain unclear and require further research. Reported dialectal distinctions encompass the phonetic realization of palatal obstruents, the presence or absence of a glottal stop as a phoneme, contrasts in voicing for stop consonants, and variations in the stress system.

Bellatrix Aerospace's Project 200 aims to develop an ultra-low Earth orbit satellite for altitudes below 200 km, with the first satellite targeted for launch in 2026. Operating in Ultra-LEO could provide higher-resolution Earth observation imagery for applications in mapping, agriculture, and climate modeling, while the reduced altitude shortens communication latency with ground stations. However, very low Earth orbit encounters significant atmospheric drag, making such orbits effectively self-cleaning as satellites re-enter after end-of-life; drag necessitates carrying considerable propellant, which adds mass and constrains operating time. Bellatrix has developed an air-intake electric propulsion system that uses atmospheric air as the propellant. The system has been demonstrated following ground testing and was showcased at the Bengaluru Space Expo 2024. The spacecraft platform measures around two meters in length and can carry a payload of 50–70 kg; it is designed to operate at roughly 180–200 km altitude with solar panels delivering more than 1 kW. The propulsion employs a hybrid approach that ionizes gas using radio waves and accelerates it with a Hall-effect thruster. The satellite’s size, geometry, and intake have been tuned to balance passive and active air compression. The propulsion system has been proven, with plans for a large-scale satellite demonstration in 2026.

Bellatrix Aerospace has developed what is described as India's first high-performance green propulsion (HPGP) system capable of replacing hydrazine-based satellite propulsion. The green monopropellant, produced by co-founder and senior scientist Saagar Malaichamy in the Mono-propellant Systems Division, was created in collaboration with Prof. Charlie Oommen of IISc's Department of Aerospace Engineering. The propulsion unit employs a 1-newton thruster designed for micro- and small satellites in the 50–1000 kilogram range and is currently undergoing ground testing. The RUDRA 0.3 HPGP achieved a successful space test on the POEM-3 mission on January 27, 2024, and an upgraded version designated RUDRA 0.3 HPGP was likewise tested in space on POEM-4 on January 2, 2025.

The Yei language, as described by Evans (2018), is spoken in the villages of Po, Torai, Bupul, Tanas, and Kwel, all situated in Elikobal District. This district lies in the eastern part of Merauke Regency, within Indonesia.

The Yei language, also known as Yey, Jei, Je, or Yei-Nan, is a Papuan language spoken in Indonesia. It is spoken along the upper reaches of the Maro River in Merauke Regency, South Papua Province. The language has two dialects, Upper Yey and Lower Yey, which are only mutually intelligible with difficulty.

Historically, power in mills and factories was transmitted through a line shaft that drove multiple machines via belts and pulleys. Electrification introduced unit drive, whereby each machine received its own electric motor. This arrangement enabled more flexible factory layouts and allowed different machines to run at different speeds as needed. In addition, unit drive supported substantially higher operating speeds, a change of particular significance for machine tools.

Mechanization denotes the use of tools and power to perform work more efficiently and encompasses the use of hand tools across various fields; in contemporary engineering and economic discourse, however, it refers to systems driven by machinery more complex than simple hand tools and excludes elementary devices such as animal-powered mills without gearing. Devices that alter speed or convert reciprocating motion into rotational motion through components such as gears, pulleys or belts, shafts, cams, and cranks are typically regarded as machines. Following electrification, mechanization came to be largely associated with motorized equipment. The concept extends into automation, describing production processes governed by closed-loop control systems that incorporate sensor feedback. In an automated machine, the coordinated operation of multiple mechanisms proceeds automatically, with minimal direct human intervention.

The longest continuous straight-line land distance entirely within the continental landmass of Asia measures 10,152 kilometers (6,308 miles). The route begins on the Indian coast near Kanyakumari and ends at the Bering Sea coast of Russia’s Chukchi Peninsula, traversing India, Nepal, China, Mongolia, and Russia.

Extremes on Earth identifies the most remote national capitals as Wellington, New Zealand, and Canberra, Australia, which are separated by about 2,326 kilometers (1,445 miles). Moreover, neither capital is closer to any other national capital than to the other, indicating that, for each city, the other serves as its nearest national capital.

Freestyle roller dancing refers to a form of movement performed on roller skates that is typically set to music. It is characterized by a lack of preplanned choreography and a strong emphasis on improvisation, resulting in performances that are highly variable from one rendition to the next. Although it can appear across a broad range of genres, including those that involve partner dancing, it is not restricted to any single style. Practitioners may perform in formal venues or in informal settings, and on some occasions a sparse, loosely structured sequence of movements is used to anchor improvisation rather than to dictate a fixed routine.

Roller skating, in the context of specialized casual footwear, has been popularized by Heelys, ordinary-looking street shoes that incorporate a single retractable wheel in the heel of each shoe. The wheel can be extended to perform skating-like maneuvers while the wearer can walk normally when the skating function is not needed, as it retracts into a recessed heel slot. The low-key, spontaneous nature of Heelys is considered appealing, particularly in many cities and suburbs where traditional skateboarding and related wheeled sports are often outlawed or restricted. In later developments, Heelys were combined with Soaps to form a single hybrid shoe.

At Lüne Abbey, women entering the convent maintained ties with their birth families, creating a dual kinship network that linked biological relatives with the sisterhood of the abbey. This pattern of contact is well documented through letters, especially those from the 15th and 16th centuries, which indicate regular and sustained communication. The presence of familial ties between the nuns and Lüneburg's patrician families points to a close integration of the convent with the city’s political life. Additionally, there is reason to believe that the convent also maintained connections with other estates controlled by a provost, beyond those directly associated with Lüne Abbey.

Lüne Abbey, a medieval convent for women, expanded in the 13th century to approximately sixty nuns, who were largely recruited from nearby noble families and the patrician circles of Lüneburg. The community’s living costs were principally covered by revenues from the local saltworks, a property the abbey held as Pfandherr (pledge lord) since 1229. In 1367, the influential and wealthy house refused a papally appointed provost, Giles of Tusculum, and elected Conrad of Soltau instead; Pope Urban V eventually sanctioned a compromise by permitting a third candidate, Johannes Weigergang, and by granting the nuns the privilege to elect their own provost. That right to freely choose a provost signified a high degree of autonomy, since premodern female convents typically depended on a male provost to represent external political and economic interests. By 1395, the Lüne provost was granted full sacramental care of the nuns, a development that effectively rendered the convent autonomous in both political and spiritual terms.

BBC Radio 4 has faced criticism from centre-right newspapers alleging a left-leaning bias across a range of issues. They have charged that interviews, particularly on the Today programme, are conducted in a deferential or sycophantic manner. These criticisms are often linked to a broader perception of malaise within the BBC's editorial culture. Journalist Mehdi Hasan has argued that the BBC is overtly socially and culturally conservative.

BBC Radio 4 broadcasts a selection of news-focused programmes, including Today, The World at One, and PM. These programmes are heralded on air by the Greenwich Time Signal pips or by the chimes of Big Ben. In addition to its news output, Radio 4 carries the Shipping Forecast, a forecast service that has a history of more than 150 years.
Geels, Michigan is located within Richfield Township, a civil township in Roscommon County, Michigan, United States. As of the 2020 census, Richfield Township had a population of 3,545.

Geels, Michigan, exhibits a relatively mature population with a median age of 49 years. The age distribution shows 19.3% of residents under 18, 4.3% aged 18–24, 21.7% aged 25–44, 28.9% aged 45–64, and 25.7% aged 65 and over. In terms of sex composition, the overall ratio stands at 100 females for every 97.3 males, indicating a slight female majority. Among those aged 18 and older, the ratio is 100 females to 93.1 males.

Early in September 2021, Idaho Governor Brad Little mobilized 150 members of the Idaho National Guard and recruited 220 additional healthcare workers in an effort to avert the first statewide activation of crisis standards of care. Despite these measures, the state ultimately activated crisis standards of care several days later, signaling a sharp escalation in hospital strain. In the same period, Hawaii was weeks away from reaching a comparable crisis point, illustrating the broader national trajectory of hospital capacity pressures during the pandemic.

Throughout 2021, hospitals across the United States faced extreme bed shortages as COVID-19 surges strained capacity, prompting interstate efforts to find available beds. In Arizona, facilities reported desperate outreach to hospitals in Wyoming, Arkansas, Texas, and California in an effort to secure space for patients. In a separate case, a Kansas hospital contacted roughly forty facilities across multiple states in search of a bed for a COVID-19 patient. Ultimately, a bed was located about 220 miles away. A physician described the moment as among the worst days in the emergency department, when clinicians were unable to provide the level of care the patient needed.
Howard D. McKibben (born April 1, 1940) serves as a senior United States district judge on the United States District Court for the District of Nevada.

Howard D. McKibben (born April 1, 1940) is an American jurist who held several public legal posts in Douglas County, Nevada. Born in Virginia, Illinois, he earned a Bachelor of Science degree from Bradley University in 1962, a Master of Public Administration from the University of Pittsburgh in 1964, and a Juris Doctor from the University of Michigan Law School in 1967. McKibben then entered private practice in Minden, Nevada, from 1967 to 1971, while serving as deputy district attorney for Douglas County from 1969 to 1971. He proceeded to serve as district attorney of Douglas County from 1971 to 1977, and subsequently as a judge of the Ninth Judicial District Court in Nevada from 1977 to 1984.

The 63rd (West Suffolk) Regiment of Foot arrived in Ireland in 1764, and in 1775 it proceeded to reinforce British forces in North America during the American War of Independence, arriving in the colonies in June 1775. It fought at the Battle of Bunker Hill, where a third assault culminated in a bayonet charge that broke American resistance. Following Bunker Hill, the regiment remained in Boston as local sentiment grew increasingly uneasy. In March 1776 it departed Boston for Halifax, Nova Scotia, with the rest of the forces. In August 1776 it took part in the Battle of Long Island, delivering a devastating blow to American forces thatWashington later reversed. In September 1777, the Grenadier and Light companies participated in the Battle of Brandywine, and in October 1777 they again fought at Germantown. That same month, the main body of the regiment engaged at Fort Clinton and Fort Montgomery. In June 1778 the regiment moved to Philadelphia and participated in the Battle of Monmouth.

The 63rd (West Suffolk) Regiment of Foot participated in the Crimean War, landing at Kalamita Bay in August 1854 as part of the 4th Division. It fought at the Battle of Inkerman in November 1854, where intense close-quarters combat occurred. During Inkerman, both colour bearers were mortally wounded: Ensign James Hulton Clutterbuck, bearer of the Queen's Colour, and Ensign Heneage Twysden, bearer of the Regimental Colour. The regiment subsequently participated in the Siege of Sevastopol and, on 8 September 1855, was part of a force assaulting a section of Sevastopol on the siege's final day, in the engagement known as the Battle of the Great Redan.

British bombing raids against German cities occurred before the Luftwaffe directed its attacks at the United Kingdom. The German air force did not commence targeting UK military and economic installations until six weeks after the campaign in France had ended, a delay that separated the end of the French campaign from the onset of Luftwaffe air operations against Britain.

Strategic bombing in World War II has been criticized for its uncertain and unpredictable effects, with some analysts arguing that it failed to produce consistently reliable military gains. The campaigns often induced sweeping changes in the societies and economies of the targeted areas, reconfiguring labor markets, demographic patterns, and urban infrastructure in ways that could undermine the intended aims. These rapid social and economic shifts could also backfire, undermining morale or reducing overall wartime efficiency. For example, bombing sometimes released non-essential workers from disrupted regions to fill shortages in war-related industries elsewhere, a consequence that could be counterproductive to the purpose of degrading industrial capacity. Consequently, the reliability and desirability of strategic bombing as a tool of war have been widely questioned in historical assessments.

Tollan is a mythical homeland of origin in several Mesoamerican traditions, including those of the Aztecs and the K'iche' Maya. In the K'iche' Popol Vuh, the first humans are gathered at Tollan, which is described as the place of seven caves. At Tollan, the earliest people are granted their languages and their gods, marking a foundational moment in the mythic history of these cultures.

Tōllān is a term historically associated with Teotihuacan, the earliest city known by that designation. After Teotihuacan's collapse, central Mexico fragmented into a mosaic of smaller polities. In the ensuing period, the Toltecs founded what is regarded as the first sizable empire in the region. The Toltec capital itself was referred to by the same name, Tollan, reflecting a deliberate reference to Teotihuacan's earlier prominence.

Canadian punk rock emerged in the late 1970s, drawing on the energy of international acts such as the Ramones, the New York Dolls, Blondie, and the Sex Pistols. Early influential groups included The Vile Tones, The Diodes, and The Demics, while Vancouver’s Skulls featured members who would later shape other scenes—Joey, who founded DOA, and Brian Roy (Wimpy), who would go on to lead the Subhumans. In Hamilton, Teenage Head earned a nickname linked to the Ramones because of their brisk recordings and high-octane live performances. Across the country, a vibrant network of local scenes developed in Toronto, Vancouver, and other Canadian cities, helping to establish punk rock as a formative and enduring movement within Canada.

Canadian hardcore punk emerged in the early 1980s. D.O.A. is regarded as the first Canadian hardcore band. Their 1981 album Hardcore '81 helped establish the standards for the genre. The album's title is often cited as the origin of the term hardcore punk.

Amid the aftermath of the Revolutions of 1848, Franz Joseph I, newly enthroned as Emperor of Austria, asserted renewed Habsburg authority by promulgating the March Constitution in 1849. The measure centralized power in Vienna and dismantled the Hungarian constitutional framework established by the 1848 April Laws, with the stated aim of abolishing the Hungarian Diet and the historic constitution of Hungary, thereby curbing Hungary's constitutional autonomy within the empire. The revocation of the April Laws and the reduction of Hungary’s traditional status and territorial arrangements provoked a renewed Hungarian uprising. Its legality was debated, with some arguing that it was unconstitutional because the laws had been signed by Ferdinand and thus could not be reversed by a later monarch, while supporters contended that Franz Joseph, who had not sworn oaths to Hungary as his predecessor had, was not bound by the same limitations. Nevertheless, the Imperial Diet of Austria accepted the March Constitution, marking a restoration of centralized Habsburg authority after the concessions of the 1848 revolutions.

On 7 March 1849, an imperial proclamation issued in the name of Emperor Francis Joseph announced the establishment of a united constitution for the Austrian Empire. The measure created a single constitutional framework for the empire as a whole. It provided that Hungary’s traditional territory would be partitioned into five distinct military districts, each administered separately. The proclamation also reestablished the Principality of Transylvania.

Mano Negra briefly dissolved after its initial recordings, during which Manu Chao pursued work with Les Casse Pieds and Antoine collaborated with The Kingsnakes and Los Carayos (with Santi). The following year the group reassembled to record its first LP, Patchanka. The album assembles songs written by Manu Chao and features Dirty District along with musicians from Les Casse Pieds, Hot Pants, and Los Carayos, reflecting the era's DIY ethos by being produced on a modest budget and through imaginative means. Chao permitted several tracks to be captured as unedited renditions, including Mala Vida, Indios de Barcelona and Ronde de Nuit, among others.

Mano Negra is regarded as a cult band, with its frontman Manu Chao later pursuing a successful solo career and performing several of the group's Casa Babylon tracks with his group Radio Bemba Sound System. The band's enduring spirit and approach have continued to influence a diverse array of acts around the world.

Crude (2009) concludes with the suggestion that the lawsuit is unlikely to be resolved for around a decade, signaling a lengthy horizon for the dispute within the film’s narrative. The roughly ten-year estimate conveys the anticipated pace of litigation depicted in the ending, while the film also notes that an out-of-court settlement could expedite resolution, offering the possibility of concluding the dispute sooner if such a settlement are reached.

Crude is a 2009 documentary directed by Joe Berlinger that investigates the environmental litigation between Ecuadorian communities and Chevron over oil contamination in the Amazon and the broader dynamics of corporate accountability. Berlinger reportedly spent approximately $1.3 million in legal fees related to the case depicted in the film. He later expressed concerns about whether such subject matter would allow him to continue making documentary films about legal proceedings in the future.

In May 2021, Berg announced his resignation from the Alternative for Germany (AfD) party and its ID faction. He criticized the party conference resolutions issued in April 2021, which included a proposal for Germany to withdraw from the European Union. Following his departure, he served as an unaffiliated member. On 23 June 2021, he joined the European Conservatives and Reformists Group.

Lars Patrick Berg has advocated closer EU engagement with Morocco, supporting Morocco as a partner within the European Union's Euro-Mediterranean Partnership and European Neighbourhood Policy, and endorsing the EU–Morocco Association Agreement. He has criticized Turkey's military actions against the Kurdish population in Syria. In a debate in the European Parliament, he argued that the Kurds were betrayed after they had fought ISIS on behalf of the international coalition.

Iceland's music scene features a flourishing extreme metal milieu that has gained international recognition. Within Icelandic black metal, Svartidauði is widely regarded as a central figure in the movement's development. A substantial portion of the genre's output has been produced at Studio Emissary, a studio founded by Irish musician Stephen Lockhart. The cassette label Vánagandr has also played a significant role in promoting and distributing Icelandic black metal. Oration MMXVI, Iceland's first black metal festival, debuted in 2016 and concluded with editions in 2017 and 2018. In 2016, Misþyrming was selected as an artist in residence at Roadburn Festival, signaling international recognition for the Icelandic scene.

In Iceland, music labels differ in their scope, with some focusing on a single genre and others promoting a wider variety of styles. Notable examples include 12 Tónar, which operates a record store in Reykjavík, and Smekkleysa, which likewise maintains a record store in the same city.

The Tso Kar lake basin currently lacks formal protective status. Plans have been advanced to designate the area within a national park. The proposed park would be located in the highlands of south-eastern Ladakh. However, its establishment remains uncertain, with final designation still to be determined.

Tso Kar is accessible from the village of Miru (also spelled Meroo) along the Leh–Manali Highway. Visitors can reach the lake’s western and southern shores by taking the Meroo-Giu-Chutak Road, while the northern and eastern shores are accessed via the Meroo-Pongunagu-Thukje-Mahe-Nyoma route.

ISO 9564 is an international standard that addresses the security of personal identification numbers used in electronic card payments. It specifies that when the PIN entry device and the card reader are not part of a single integrated secure module, the PIN must be encrypted during its transmission from the entry device to the reader to protect against interception or tampering.

ISO 9564 sets out the secure handling of PINs in card-based payment systems. It requires that the PIN be encrypted during transmission from the PIN entry device to the verifier, and it mandates encoding the PIN into a PIN block using one of several formats defined by the standard. The resulting PIN block is then encrypted with an approved cryptographic algorithm as described in Part 2 of ISO 9564.

The chief security officer (CSO) is a senior executive responsible for establishing and maintaining relationships with senior law enforcement officials and international counterparts, and for engaging with domestic and international security agencies. The role encompasses involvement with intelligence activities and other related governmental functions, facilitating information sharing and coordinated response across jurisdictions. It also entails collaboration with private-sector counterparts worldwide to align security practices, risk management, and incident response. Throughout these duties, the CSO maintains a global, cross-sector focus to address evolving threats and safeguard organizational assets across industries and regions.

The Chief Security Officer directs personnel in recognizing, designing, implementing, and maintaining security processes, practices, and policies across the organization, overseeing a comprehensive security program. Its primary objective is to reduce organizational risk, coordinate incident response, and limit exposure and liability. The scope of the role encompasses information, financial, physical, personal, and reputational risks, reflecting an integrated approach to protecting assets and stakeholders.

Rot-Weiß Erfurt, a German football club based in Erfurt, experienced a surge of prominence following German reunification and the merger of East and West German leagues in the early 1990s. A third-place finish in the 1990–91 NOFV-Oberliga earned them promotion to the 2. Bundesliga and qualification for the UEFA Cup. In Europe, the club defeated Groningen in the first round but were eliminated by Ajax in the second round, with Ajax ultimately crowned champions. That tie marked the last time an East German club appeared in European competition.

In 1965, East German football underwent a reorganization that replaced broad general sports clubs with dedicated football clubs. The following year, the top sides of SC Turbine Erfurt and BSG Optima Erfurt merged to form FC Rot-Weiß Erfurt, while the junior squads remained with their original clubs. The club’s name, Rot-Weiß (red and white), was notable for its departure from the period’s typical socialist symbolism. In 1980, Rot-Weiß Erfurt advanced to the East German Cup final, where they were defeated 3–1 by Carl Zeiss Jena.

A 2020 genomic study found a close relationship between Himalayan wolves and wolves of the Tibetan plateau. The findings indicate admixed ancestry that includes contributions from gray wolves, domestic dogs, and a ghost population of an unknown wolf-like canid. This ghost lineage is deeply divergent from modern Holarctic wolves and dogs. It contributed approximately 39% of the Himalayan wolf’s nuclear genome. The same ghost population also supplied the EPAS1 allele found in Himalayan wolves and dogs, a variant associated with adaptation to high-altitude environments.
Lupus tschiliensis, described by Matschie in 1907, is based on the skull of a wolf specimen. The individual skull originated from a wolf shot in the coastal region of Zhili Province, China.

Henry Murray was an American psychologist whose work has been the subject of controversy; some sources claim that Murray's experiments were part of or funded by the U.S. government's mind-control research, with the program identified as MKUltra.

In 1943, Henry Murray contributed to the Analysis of the Personality of Adolf Hitler, a study commissioned by OSS head General William "Wild Bill" Donovan. The project was conducted with collaborators Walter C. Langer, Ernst Kris, and Bertram D. Lewin, and was associated with the New School for Social Research and the New York Psychoanalytic Institute. Informants included Ernst Hanfstaengl, Hermann Rauschning, Princess Stephanie von Hohenlohe, Gregor Strasser, Friedelind Wagner, and Kurt Lüdecke. The endeavor has been described as groundbreaking, helping to inaugurate both offender profiling and political psychology. The report forecast that Hitler would likely opt for suicide if Germany faced imminent defeat. It also asserted that Hitler was impotent in heterosexual relations and possibly involved in a homosexual relationship. The homosexual interpretation was linked to identified feminine traits and to the notable presence of homosexuals within the Nazi Party; the document notes that Hitler reportedly called Albert Forster "Bubi," a name associated with homosexual circles.

John Fitzgerald Kennedy (May 29, 1917 – November 22, 1963) was an American politician who served as the 35th president of the United States from 1961 until his assassination in 1963. A member of the Democratic Party, he previously represented Massachusetts in both chambers of Congress, serving in the House of Representatives from 1947 to 1953 and in the Senate from 1953 to 1960. At 43, he became the youngest person elected to the presidency. His tenure occurred during the height of the Cold War, with foreign policy principally focused on the Soviet Union and Cuba. Kennedy’s term ended with his death in office in 1963.

John F. Kennedy inherited an economy that had experienced two recessions in three years and was in recession at the outset of his presidency. He pursued expansionary measures, loosening monetary policy to keep interest rates low and stimulate growth, while moving away from previously tight fiscal policies. The Kennedy era saw an acceleration of economic expansion, with fiscal policy shifting as evidenced by the 1961 budget, which produced the first deficit not tied to war or recession, followed by a 1962 budget that exceeded $100 billion in outlays. In historical context, the economy under Dwight D. Eisenhower had grown at about 2.2 percent per year, barely outpacing population growth, and contracted by about 1 percent in his final year.

Conservation management of protected areas presents a range of challenges for effective stewardship. These difficulties stem from interactions with local populations, the particularities of each ecosystem, and the design and management of the reserves themselves. Because ecological dynamics are inherently unpredictable, the complexity of conservation planning is heightened. Accordingly, each protected area calls for a unique, context-specific set of guidelines rather than a universal approach.

On 21 May 2019, The Moscow Times published a piece citing a World Wildlife Fund (WWF) report that Russia ranked first worldwide in protected natural areas, outlining a total of 63.3 million hectares designated as specially protected natural areas. The article did not provide a hyperlink to the WWF report, and there is uncertainty that the figures may be based on previously gathered data rather than current measurements.

Omar Al Soma broke into his club's first team at the age of 17 during the 2008–09 season, scoring 12 league goals to finish as the club's top scorer, though the team was relegated to the Syrian First Division after that campaign. In the following season, he played a pivotal role as the side secured immediate promotion back to the top division. He added five goals in the 2010–11 season, which was suspended in March 2011 due to the Syrian revolution.

Omar Al-Somah is a professional footballer who typically operates as a center-forward. He is recognized for his finishing ability and proficiency with free kicks. His height, strength, jumping ability, and heading technique give him an advantage in aerial duels. He is two-footed, capable of scoring with either foot. He has been nicknamed "the Syrian Ibrahimović" for his playing style.

The Diocese of Vila Real (Latin: Dioecesis Villaregalensis) is a Latin Church diocese of the Catholic Church in Portugal. It was established in 1922, formed from portions of the Diocese of Bragança-Miranda, the Archdiocese of Braga, and the Diocese of Lamego. It is a suffragan of the Archdiocese of Braga, within the Norte region. The diocesan see is at the Cathedral of Vila Real.

JRiver Media Center automatically saves a newly created library view as a saved view within the library, ensuring its availability for future use. This saved view can be opened from multiple user interfaces supported by the software, providing consistent access across different workflows. It includes a real-time search box that allows instant filtering, and the search functionality is customizable to target any field or tag found in the library.

JRiver Media Center provides broad compatibility across audio, video, photos, and documents. The complete list of supported formats is documented on the JRiver Media Center wiki, organized into sections for supported audio formats, supported video formats, and supported image formats. The software also supports DirectShow, enabling playback of any video or audio format for which a DirectShow filter is installed on the host system.

Romani language shows regional variation in phonological prosody. In conservative Romani dialects, word stress is typically placed on the final syllable. Nevertheless, certain affixes remain unstressed despite the overall final-stress pattern, such as the vocative suffix, the case endings that mark the accusative noun, and a remoteness tense marker. By contrast, Romani dialects spoken in Central and Western Europe tend to assign stress earlier within the word, producing a different stress profile.

The classification of the Romani language within the Indo-Aryan family has not been fixed and has varied across scholarly treatments. Some classifications place Romani within the Central Zone of Indo-Aryan languages, while others align it with the Northwestern Zone. In other schemes, Romani is considered to constitute its own distinct group or branch, reflecting ongoing debate about its precise historical and genetic position within Indo-Aryan.

Eric Melvin married Australian-born artist Sarah Melvin in 2016. The couple have identical twin daughters, Ivy Laine Melvin and Phaedra Rose Melvin, who were born 21 minutes apart, and he also has two sons, Eli Melvin and Caspian Melvin. He resides with his wife and four children in the Encinitas area of Southern California. In 2017, Melvin sold his home in San Francisco; observers remarked that the residence was unexpectedly tasteful for a punk rock musician.

Eric Melvin is a founding member of Punk Rock Karaoke, a project he co-founded with Greg Hetson and Steve Soto. Although he helped establish the group, Melvin rarely performs with Punk Rock Karaoke. He is also an irregular touring member of Me First and the Gimme Gimmes.

Child Helpline International's work is based on the principles of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC). The UNCRC foregrounds the right to privacy for children and underscores the obligation to protect them from harm, principles that guide CHI's approach to offering confidential support and safeguarding children's well-being.

Child Helpline International is a global network in which member helplines learn from one another through structured peer exchanges. Knowledge transfer occurs during visits, allowing participants to share effective solutions, compare areas of expertise, and discuss experiences, thereby strengthening collective practice and responses to children’s needs.

The Kindly Ones, issued in 1962, is a novel by Anthony Powell and the sixth installment in his twelve-volume cycle A Dance to the Music of Time. The title alludes to the placatory name given to the Furies in Greek mythology. The work principally charts the period surrounding Britain's entry into World War II, tracing social and personal developments of the time. It is dedicated "For R.W.K.C." to the biographer and historian R. W. Ketton-Cremer.

The Kindly Ones is structured into four episodes, with the opening segment set at Stonehurst during Nick Jenkins's boyhood on the eve of World War I. It introduces figures from earlier installments of the sequence, including the retired General Conyers. In a scene at Stonehurst, General Conyers tactfully handles the nude appearance of a parlour maid who is jealous after learning that the family servant Albert will marry. After lunch at Stonehurst, the General then has a chance encounter on the road with the eccentric cultist Dr. Trelawney and Nick's Uncle Giles.

Central German refers to a group of central German dialects spoken across several of Germany’s most populous and influential urban centers. Among the cities where Central German varieties are used are Berlin, Bonn (the former West German capital), Cologne, Düsseldorf, Frankfurt (Germany’s main financial center), Leipzig, and Dresden, highlighting the prominence of these urban areas in the linguistic landscape.

The Central German region is a geological region in Germany characterized by the hilly Central Uplands. It stretches from the North German Plain in the north to the South German Scarplands in the south, and covers the states of Saarland, Rhineland-Palatinate, Hesse, Thuringia, and Saxony.

On 21 July 1950, a BOAC Canadair C-4 Argonaut carrying seven crew members and twelve passengers was flying from Dakar to Natal when engine problems necessitated an emergency diversion. Initial technical issues included both starboard-wing engines shutting down, leaving only two functioning engines on the port wing, a drag problem caused by an inboard propeller that could not be feathered, and a persistent fire affecting the same engine. With the aircraft cruising at about 20,000 ft and losing altitude at roughly 400 ft per minute, an SOS was issued and the crew faced the prospect of ditching in the South Atlantic. The decision was made to divert to Fernando de Noronha, roughly 480 miles southwest of the route, where, on the way, the outboard engine was restarted and altitude was maintained near 9,000 ft. Additional difficulties included coolant temperature problems on the port-wing engines and difficulties locating the archipelago. The aircraft achieved a safe landing at Fernando de Noronha, about four hours after the onset of the ordeal.

One theory among the explanations for Fernando de Noronha's discovery holds that the island was already encountered in 1500, not long after Brazil's own discovery by the Second India Armada led by Pedro Álvares Cabral. Cabral's voyage included a brief landfall at Porto Seguro to report the discovery, after which a supply ship was dispatched back to Lisbon to convey the news. The captain of that returning vessel is named in different sources as either Gaspar de Lemos or André Gonçalves, with the historical record showing conflicting attributions. If that returning ship sailed north along the Brazilian coast and reached Lisbon with the report by July 1500, Noronha could have been reported at that time. This scenario, however, clashes with the Quaresma naming, since the return would have occurred after Lent, thereby challenging the rationale for the island's name.

NatureServe conservation status denotes a framework of ranks that evaluate the relative imperilment of species and natural ecological communities. The system is applied at global, national, and subnational levels and covers plants, animals, other organisms, and natural ecological communities. It originated in the United States during the 1980s, developed by The Nature Conservancy, and the ranks are now maintained and presented by NatureServe in cooperation with the Natural Heritage Network. In common usage the scheme is referred to as NatureServe ranks or Natural Heritage ranks, with occasional reference to TNC ranks reflecting the historical involvement of The Nature Conservancy.

NatureServe conservation status includes consideration of regionally native species or other taxa that have recently established in a given area through natural dispersal—such as windborne spread, flood-mediated movement, or migratory birds—without any direct or indirect human intervention. In these cases, the taxa are evaluated using the same ranking framework and notation that are applied to other native taxa, ensuring consistency in regional conservation assessments.

AfE-Turm was a high-rise building on Goethe University’s Bockenheim campus. Completed in 1972, it housed offices and seminar rooms for the university’s Social Sciences and Education faculties until 2013. The initials AfE denote the Abteilung für Erziehungswissenschaft (Department of Pedagogy); however, the Department of Pedagogy never relocated there, as it had been closed prior to the tower’s completion. The structure was subsequently demolished on 2 February 2014.

AfE-Turm’s planning and construction began in the early 1960s, prompted by the 1961 incorporation of the College of Pedagogy into the university which generated a need for dedicated facilities. Before the tower was available, the Bettinaschule building in the Westend served as a provisional arrangement, but this solution proved inadequate and the structure itself lacked the functionality required by the university’s expanding needs.

Kerch's economy rests on several key sectors, with construction materials, food processing, and light industries making significant contributions. The city also serves as a base for a fishing fleet, reflecting its maritime orientation. Furthermore, Kerch operates as an important processing centre for a broad range of fish products, linking primary fishing activities with downstream processing and distribution.
The Kerch city municipality spans a substantial area and includes multiple neighborhoods, notably Eltigen (Heroyevskoe), Kamysh-Burun (Arshyntsevo), Port Krym, Adzhimushkai, and Tuzla Island.

Socialism has been an influential current in Australia’s labor movement, notably shaping the Builders Labourers Federation (BLF) and its green bans of the 1970s. In the Victorian branch, leadership came largely from Maoist members of the Communist Party of Australia (Marxist-Leninist), including Norm Gallagher, while the New South Wales branch was led by Communist Party of Australia members such as Jack Mundey. In 1974, Gallagher and allied Maoists occupied the NSW branch office and expelled CPA-aligned unionists. By 1983, union officials, including CPA members, agreed to the Prices and Incomes Accord, trading reduced industrial action for parliamentary reforms. The Accord signaled the end of the BLF’s guerrilla-style actions and radical protest, and the federation was de-registered shortly thereafter under the Hawke Labor government. Following deregistration, members were blacklisted from working on construction sites.

Within the Australian Labor Party, some dissident figures pursued a more interventionist, democratic-socialist direction. A notable advocate was Peter Baldwin, a minister in the Keating government, who campaigned on a Bennite platform that sought to revive the party’s long-standing commitment to socializing the means of production, a principle many had treated as largely neglected. The programme called for the nationalization of key industries as part of the policy agenda for a future Labor government. Baldwin argued that industrial democracy, involving workers in management and decision-making, would be essential to achieving these aims.

From the postwar period through 1971, the San Francisco Chronicle underwent notable changes under editor Scott Newhall, who introduced a bold and provocative approach to news presentation. The paper's investigative reporting was highlighted by Pierre Salinger, who would later hold a prominent national political role, and Paul Avery, who actively pursued the Zodiac Killer trail. In the late 1960s, the Zodiac Killer sent a cryptogram divided into three sections in letters to the Chronicle and two other newspapers, underscoring the paper's role in covering the notorious case. The Chronicle also featured a distinguished lineup of columnists, including Pauline Phillips (Dear Abby), Count Marco (Marc Spinelli), Stanton Delaplane, Terence O'Flaherty, Lucius Beebe, Art Hoppe, Charles McCabe, and Herb Caen, whose writings helped shape its editorial and cultural voice. Together, these elements contributed to the Chronicle's reputation for vigorous reporting and distinctive opinion journalism during that era.

Under the joint ownership arrangement, the San Francisco Chronicle and the San Francisco Examiner were officially owned by the San Francisco Newspaper Agency, which oversaw sales and distribution for both papers and was charged with preventing any one title’s circulation from expanding at the expense of the other. Revenues from the two papers were divided equally, a policy widely perceived as advantageous to the Examiner. Nevertheless, the Chronicle’s circulation was about four times larger than that of the Examiner, effectively subsidizing the afternoon paper within the overall revenue model.

Yahoo China, within the broader media landscape of the region, drew notable attention in December 2015 when Alibaba Group agreed to acquire the South China Morning Post and related media assets for a reported $266 million. The company pledged to maintain editorial independence for the acquired outlets, and Alibaba vice-chairman Joseph Tsai emphasized the importance of offering a plurality of views in coverage of China, citing the country’s rising influence and its relevance to world stability. The deal nevertheless sparked discussions about potential implications for the newspaper’s reporting and editorial direction.

Beginning in 2005, Yahoo! invested in Alibaba Group through a variable-interest entity, acquiring a 40 percent stake for around $1 billion. The investment produced substantial returns when Alibaba's initial public offering occurred, with Yahoo! realizing approximately $10 billion from the IPO. In 2012, the China Investment Corporation, together with Chinese investors, led the purchase of Yahoo!'s 40 percent stake and of Alibaba shares trading on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange.

Static random-access memory (SRAM) is a form of random-access memory that stores each bit with a bistable latching circuit, typically implemented as flip-flops. As a volatile memory technology, SRAM requires continuous power to preserve its data, and the stored information is lost when power is removed.

Zero Bus Turnaround (ZBT) is a designation applied to certain static random-access memories to indicate a design that eliminates the waiting time typically required when the memory switches access direction. Turnaround is defined as the number of clock cycles needed to switch SRAM access from write to read or from read to write. In ZBT SRAMs, the read/write turnaround latency is zero, allowing immediate switching between reading and writing without any additional clock-cycle penalty.

The 979 ISBN prefix includes a registration group 0 reserved for compatibility with International Standard Music Numbers (ISMNs); however, ISMNs are not assigned ISBNs. Under the 979 prefix, the assigned registration groups are 8 for the United States, 10 for France, 11 for the Republic of Korea, and 12 for Italy.

The original Standard Book Number (SBN) was a nine-digit identifier that did not include a registration group identifier. By prefixing a leading zero to this nine-digit SBN, a valid ten-digit ISBN could be formed. Consequently, ISBN-10 is derived from the nine-digit SBN by adding a leading zero.

Jan Baptist Brueghel, born in Antwerp, was a Flemish painter who traveled to Rome, where he joined the Bentvueghels, an association of predominantly Dutch and Flemish artists. Members of the group adopted informal nicknames, known as bent names, and Brueghel was assigned the sobriquet Meleager. The artist is referenced by Arnold Houbraken, who in his Biographical Dictionary includes a poem about the Bentvueghels at the end of his second volume on artists and also notes Brueghel among those who signed Abraham Genoels’ bentbrief in the third volume.
Jan Baptist Brueghel, the younger brother of Abraham Brueghel, accompanied his sibling to Naples. He returned to Rome after Abraham’s death. Like his brother, he is known for his fruit still lifes.

Greed, attributed to Thomas Aquinas, is described in his moral theology as a sin against God and is regarded as akin to the other mortal sins. It arises when a person values temporal possessions or earthly gains more highly than eternal goods, thereby condemning the eternal for the sake of the temporal. This emphasis highlights a misprioritization of eternal over temporal goods, reflecting Aquinas’s broader argument that the proper ordering of loves and ends is essential to virtuous living.

Thomas Aquinas articulated a hylomorphic anthropology whereby a human being is a composite of body and soul. The rational soul is the configured subsistent form that orders matter into a living, bodily human, thereby defining what it is to be human. Because the soul is spiritual, it does not depend on matter and may exist independently of the body, allowing for the continued existence of the person after death. Accordingly, the human being is a soul-matter composite, with the body contributing to human nature while the soul provides the intelligible principle that animates it. For Aquinas, perfected human nature consists in the dual unity of embodied existence and intellectual activity.

Design for testing is an approach in electronics that evaluates a device under test by comparing its responses to a predetermined set of test vectors with the corresponding responses from a known-good reference circuit, using identical input patterns for both. When the DUT’s output matches the reference, the circuit is considered to conform to its intended design; conversely, any discrepancy between the responses suggests that the circuit may be defective or outside its specified parameters, indicating potential manufacturing or design issues.

Design for testing is an engineering approach that integrates testing considerations into a device’s design to enable efficient diagnosis of circuit problems that may occur in the future. The practice entails incorporating features or provisions—such as accessible test points, built-in self-test modules, or diagnostic interfaces—so that hardware can be tested and faults identified while the system is operating. By facilitating ongoing verification and fault isolation during normal use, design for testing supports quicker maintenance, reduces downtime, and improves overall reliability.

Willem Usselincx authored the treatise Naerder Bedenckingen, Over de zee-vaerdt, Coophandel ende Neeringhe, als mede de versekeringhe vanden Staet, which was first printed in 1608. In this work he presents his arguments for the establishment of a West India trading company, outlining the case for organized overseas commerce and commercial enterprise in the Atlantic region. The treatise frequently references Spanish power and identifies potential sources of wealth in the West Indies, thereby situating his proposals within the broader context of European competition over the Americas.

Willem Usselincx, a Flemish merchant from Antwerp, operated during a period when the city’s surrender terms allowed Protestant citizens four years to settle before departing. The ensuing exodus reduced Antwerp’s population from about 100,000 to 40,000, with the majority of settlers migrating to the Republic of the Seven United Netherlands—the northern, unoccupied portion of the Union of Utrecht—and thereby helping establish the commercial foundations of the Dutch Golden Age. Antwerp’s banking came under Genoese control for a generation, while Amsterdam emerged as the new regional trading center, its population increasing from roughly 30,000 in 1570 to about 60,000 by 1600. The Amsterdam Canal District was built to accommodate traders and Antwerp bankers, signaling a broader shift in the Low Countries, which the Southern Netherlands came to be known as the Spanish Netherlands.

Autumn Cox, portrayed by Shirley Rumierk, is a fictional passenger aboard Flight 828 in the television series Manifest. She has outstanding arrest warrants stemming from being a victim of identity theft, and Laurence's superiors exploit her to glean what Ben knows about the Singularity project. In season four, Cox joins Angelina's cult along with other Flight 828 passengers. In the series finale, she is among the eleven passengers who burn to ash on the Death Date for their alleged evil deeds.

Sarah Fitz, portrayed by Lauren Norvelle, is a fictional character in Manifest who is the Major’s daughter. Throughout the series she enters into a relationship with Jared, and following her mother’s disappearance she seeks help from the New York Police Department to investigate the case.

The Casagrandes Movie follows Shara and Ronnie Anne as they secretly enter a museum, where Ronnie Anne encounters a gateway to a realm that contains the mask. Shara steals the mask and is revealed to be Punguari, leaving Ronnie Anne trapped in the other realm. Ronnie Anne’s grandfather, Hector, locates her with the aid of a magical mirror, and she recounts her predicament to the family, who then infiltrate the museum at night to rescue her. In the course of these events, Ronnie Anne discovers that the conventional tale of Punguari is flawed: Punguari wields the mask, and cracks in the ground allow Ucumu, the god of the underworld, to rise.

In The Casagrandes Movie, Maria, aided by the Chancla Warriors, lifts a colossal chancla long enough for Frida to fling a paper cutout of Arturo, encircled by sacred flame, into the chancla. The weapon strikes Ucumu, reducing him to a skeletal form. Ronnie Anne then fires at Ucumu, destroying him and petrifying all of his minions. Punguari uses the temple she constructed to seal the cracks, preventing Ucumu’s return. She is also reunited with her parents, who had been turned into gemstones. Meanwhile, Sisiki and Maria repair their relationships with their daughters, putting aside their differences.

Emperor Decius did not intend to assert the superiority of the Roman pantheon over other deities; rather, the edict is regarded as an effort to bolster his authority amid anxieties about the notion of a Roman millennium. The measure sought to reaffirm Pax Romana and reassure the Roman population that the empire remained secure, but it generated a crisis of authority among Christian bishops and their communities. Under the terms of the edict, bishops and other church officials were required to perform a sacrifice on behalf of the emperor, a sacrifice pro imperatore rather than directed to the emperor, since a living ruler was not deemed divine. Fortyeight certificates were issued to those who complied with the edict; forty-six certificates have been published, all dated to the year 250, with four arising from Oxyrhynchus. Refusal to perform the sacrifice by the deadline carried the threat of torture and execution, affecting Christians and others alike. Several prominent Christians complied and were killed, including Pope Fabian in 250; anti-Christian sentiment also sparked killings at Carthage and Alexandria. By the end of Decius’s second year, the ferocity of the persecution abated and a climate of greater tolerance began to reemerge. Contemporary Christians remembered Decius as a harsh tyrant. In June 251 Decius and his co-emperor Herennius Etruscus died at the Battle of Abrittus against the Goths, and their successors Trebonianus Gallus and Hostilian repealed the edict, bringing the persecution to an end after roughly eighteen months.

Under Emperor Philip the Arab, Decius was entrusted with a significant command on the Danube around 245. By late 248 or 249, he was dispatched to suppress Pacatian’s revolt in Moesia and Pannonia; some modern historians view the uprising as indicative of emerging Balkan separatism. After Pacatian’s rebellion was crushed, Decius was proclaimed emperor by his troops. Philip advanced against him and was killed at Verona in September 249. The Senate recognized Decius as emperor and accorded him the epithet Traianus in reference to Trajan. Zosimus notes that Decius was clothed in the imperial purple and compelled to undertake the burdens of government, despite his initial reluctance.

In practice, the PhD is sometimes a prerequisite for certain non-academic research roles, including positions within major international agencies, and it may be expected for some executive-director tracks at specific foundations. In various employment contexts, particularly within foreign policy think tanks, the degree is regarded as a qualifying credential for advanced research or policy analysis. A 2013 article from U.S. News & World Report noted that while a master’s degree is often the standard in Washington’s foreign policy arena, the PhD can function as a costly signal to potential employers, signaling deeper specialization or commitment but possibly imposing higher opportunity costs. In the Australian public service, credentialism has led to PhDs and master’s degrees becoming common base entry-level qualifications for many graduate positions.

Although the English-language degree commonly known as the Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) denotes the same doctoral level, in many regions the credential is simply titled Doctor (Doktor) rather than "Doctor of Philosophy." The field of study is indicated by a Latin suffix attached to the title, creating distinct designations such as Dr. med. (Doctor medicinae) for medicine; Dr. rer. nat. (Doctor rerum naturalium) for the natural sciences; Dr. phil. (Doctor philosophiae) for philosophy; and Dr. iur. (Doctor iuris) for law.

Shell keeps are a form of fortification in which a stone curtain encircles the upper perimeter of a motte, with lean-to buildings along the outer wall and a small courtyard at the centre. Some castles, such as Farnham and Berkeley, possess stone-enclosed mottes that have been identified as variants of shell keeps. At other sites—including Durham, Warkworth, Clifford's Tower in York, and Sandal in Wakefield—the shell-keep form appears to have evolved into a freestanding tower rather than remaining a complete enclosure. Clifford's Tower is frequently interpreted today as a shell keep by visitors, a view conditioned by the 1684 explosion that removed the roof and the central supporting masonry. Authentic shell keeps are defined by a continuous stone wall along the motte's upper edge, with lean-to structures attached to this outer barrier and a central courtyard enclosed within. Restormel's plan is cited as illustrating this arrangement.

A gazetteer of shell keeps was compiled by archaeologist Robert Higham, cataloging twenty-one examples across England and Wales. Among these, the Round Tower at Windsor Castle is cited as a representative instance of a shell keep. The majority of such fortifications were constructed during the eleventh and twelfth centuries.

During 2017, Microsoft announced that Windows development would transition to Git, the open-source distributed version control system created by Linus Torvalds. In May 2017, the company stated that the migration to a new Git repository had been completed, marking a shift in the project's source-control workflow and aligning Windows development with contemporary version-control practices.

Windows 11 was announced on June 24, 2021, during a livestream as the successor to Windows 10, with the design emphasized as more user-friendly and understandable to facilitate everyday use. The operating system was released on October 5, 2021. By May 2022, Windows 11 was available as a free upgrade for Windows 10 users who meet the system requirements, reflecting Microsoft's approach to offering a transition path for eligible devices.

Mudanjiang has a monsoon-influenced humid continental climate (Köppen Dwa), characterized by hot, humid summers and very cold, dry winters, with spring and autumn being relatively brief. The basin-oriented location helps shield the city from biting winds, and winter temperatures are warmer than in much of the province. The 24-hour average temperature ranges from −16.7 °C in January to 22.3 °C in July, producing an annual mean of about 4.78 °C. Precipitation is heavily seasonal, with approximately 60% of the annual rainfall occurring from June to August. Sunshine is seasonally variable, with around 46% daily sunshine in July and about 62% in February–March, yielding an annual total of roughly 2,368 bright sunshine hours. Extreme temperatures recorded range from −38.3 °C on January 3, 1963 to 38.4 °C on July 24, 1998.

Mudanjiang University, established in 1983, was among the first cohort of 100 local universities founded in China. The institution comprises three components: the main campus in Mudanjiang, the Hailin campus, and an industrial park training base. It covers an area of 500,000 square meters with a building area of 186,000 square meters, and its fixed assets total 450 million yuan alongside 90 million yuan of teaching equipment. The library holds approximately 644,800 books. The university has a student body of over 10,000 and administers 10 secondary schools and 43 majors, including two central-government-supported construction majors and six provincially financed construction majors. Its facilities include 104 on-campus laboratories or training bases and 125 off-campus training bases. Nationally designated backbone bases for teacher training have been identified in mechatronics, animation design and production, and computer information security and data storage.

Tianhe Coach Terminal station serves as an interchange on the Guangzhou Metro for Lines 3 and 6, and functions as the northern terminus of the Line 3 branch. The station opened on 30 December 2006 and is located beneath the junction of Tianyuan Road and the Guangzhou North Ring Expressway in the Tianhe District. It is situated at the East Square of the Tianhe Coach Terminal, which offers long-distance coach services to Guangdong and other provinces. Line 6 began operations at the station on 28 December 2013, expanding its role as a regional transit hub.

The article concerns Tianhe Coach Terminal station. In Chinese, the facility is named 天河客运站; because the term 客运站 already contains the character 站, the name does not end with a separate instance of 站. The character 站 is pronounced zaam or jaahm in Cantonese readings. The Cantonese transliteration of 客运站 is Haak wan zaam or Haak'wahnjaahm, and the term translates as "passenger moving station."

Wolmirsleben is a municipality in the Salzlandkreis district of Saxony-Anhalt, Germany. It lies roughly 25 kilometres southwest of Magdeburg. As of 2016, the population was 1,417. The settlement is first mentioned in 937 under the name Wilmersleve, with later spellings including Wilmarslope in 1144 and Wolmersleve in 1214. The town's coat of arms depicts a tower, which corresponds to the water tower that remains in use as the community's functional facility.

Cyber-nationalism refers to nationalist movements and activities conducted in cyberspace that are triggered by perceived threats or harms to a nation’s interests, often arising when China’s national interests are damaged by external actions and events. These movements are typically reactive and event-driven, and they tend to respond to actions by other states, with anti-American cyber-nationalism increasing when the United States raises its threat level against China. A common feature of such movements is the frequent use of cyber attacks as a primary tactic. An illustrative case is the China Eagle Club, a hacker collective that carried out the Taiwan Blitz to oppose Chen Shui-bian’s ascent to power.

The Martin RB-57D Canberra was a high-altitude reconnaissance aircraft delivered to the Strategic Air Command (SAC). First deliveries occurred in April 1956 to the 4025th Strategic Reconnaissance Squadron, which was part of the 4080th Strategic Reconnaissance Wing within SAC. The RB-57D remained in service for about five years before being retired. Initially based at Lockbourne AFB, Ohio, the aircraft were later relocated to Turner AFB, Georgia.

Martin RB-57D Canberra was a high-altitude strategic reconnaissance aircraft developed from the Martin B-57 Canberra, the United States‑built license-produced version of the English Electric Canberra. Engineered for extended endurance at extreme altitudes, the RB-57D served with the United States Air Force in the 1950s as part of its early long-range reconnaissance capability. The B-57 Canberra lineage derives from the British design, with the American variant produced under license, and the RB-57D’s development and deployment occurred prior to the operational deployment of the Lockheed U-2.

Benton County, Missouri has been reliably Republican in presidential elections. Donald Trump carried the county in both 2016 and 2020. The last Democratic presidential candidate to win Benton County was Bill Clinton in 1996, though he did so by a plurality rather than a majority. Since Franklin D. Roosevelt's victory in 1932, no Democrat has achieved a majority of Benton County votes in a presidential election.

On March 10, 2020, Missouri held its presidential primaries for both the Democratic and Republican parties. In the Democratic contest, Joe Biden won the statewide vote, and he secured Benton County by a substantial margin. In the general election, Biden defeated Donald Trump.

MathWorld is an online reference resource for mathematics. It was created and largely authored by Eric W. Weisstein. The project is sponsored by and licensed to Wolfram Research, Inc. It also receives partial funding from the National Science Foundation's National Science Digital Library program, awarded to the University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign.

MathWorld drew extensive headlines in online publishing circles after a notable case brought it to prominence. In the wake of MathWorld’s unavailability, the PlanetMath project emerged as an alternative resource.

The Haw Wars were a series of armed confrontations that stretched from 1865 to 1890, fought against Chinese quasi-military refugee bands that invaded parts of Tonkin and Laos. The invading groups were irregular and poorly disciplined, and they raided communities while demolishing Buddhist temples.
