Although the combatants were later identified as remnants of secret societies, they were commonly misnamed Haw, a label arising from incomplete understanding of their origins. The designation Haw appears across Lao, Thai, and Chinese contexts (Lao: ຫໍ້; Thai: ฮ่อ; Chinese: Hao). Efforts to suppress the bands were undertaken by forces dispatched by King Rama V, but these campaigns failed to quell the incursions. The last of the groups disbanded in 1890, bringing the Haw Wars to a close.

McCarthy was ordered to return to Laos at the end of the rainy season and departed Bangkok in November 1884. He traveled via Uttaradit and Nan before arriving at Luang Prabang on 14 January 1885. There he witnessed the outbreak of hostilities, which endured for three months and ultimately ended in failure.

Angkor experienced a Hindu restoration beginning circa 1243 CE, following the death of Indravarman II, who was the successor of Jayavarman VII. Jayavarman VIII, a Shaivite iconoclast, ordered the destruction of Buddhist imagery and reestablished Hindu shrines that had been converted from Buddhism by his predecessor. In the course of this renovation, the Bayon temple was rededicated as a shrine to Shiva, and its central Buddha statue, approximately 3.6 metres in height, was cast into a nearby well. Across the site, Buddhist cult statues were replaced by lingams.

Within the Angkor era, inscriptions dated to 881 CE attribute to king Indravarman I the erection of a lingam named Indresvara, and a separate inscription notes that eight lingams were installed in his courts, each named after one of the eight aspects associated with Shiva. Rajendravarman began his reign in 944 CE and subsequently oversaw the construction of the temple Pre Rup, whose central tower housed the royal lingam known as Rajendrabhadresvara.

In 1815, Winfield Scott was admitted as an honorary member of the Pennsylvania Society of the Cincinnati in recognition of his service during the War of 1812. The society’s insignia prepared for Scott was crafted by Philadelphia silversmiths Thomas Fletcher and Sidney Gardiner, and it takes the form of a solitary solid gold eagle standing about three inches tall. The piece is regarded as one of the most distinctive insignias ever produced for military societies. There are no known portraits or photographs showing Scott wearing the insignia. The artifact is presently housed in the collection of the United States Military Academy Museum.

A statue honoring Winfield Scott stands at Scott Circle in Washington, D.C., and his likeness has appeared on a United States postage stamp. A paddle steamer named Winfield Scott was launched in 1850, and a U.S. Army tugboat bearing the same name remained in service into the 21st century. The name has been borne by several notable figures, including Union General Winfield Scott Hancock, Confederate General Winfield Scott Featherston, and Admiral Winfield Scott Schley. The U.S. Army Civil Affairs Association has referred to him as the "Father of Civil Affairs," and regimental award medallions also bear his name.

Floyd Shaman was an American sculptor trained as a stone carver who achieved his most significant impact in wood through laminated construction. He is profiled in Arthur Williams's textbook The Sculpture Reference, which includes detailed photographs of his techniques and tools, illustrating his method of laminated wood sculpture. Shaman refined lamination by inventing a hollow-core approach that produced pieces that were stronger yet lighter. A recurring, playful motif in his work involved filling empty cavities with small objects known only to the artist, a device that amused yet perplexed patrons. His life-size figures tend to depict everyday encounters with wry humor, irony, and sober reflection, and his work is frequently described as whimsical. He also produced pieces for puppeteer Peter Zapletal, a collaboration that further highlights the whimsical aspect of his oeuvre. While his life-size figures often honored working-class individuals he admired, his subjects extended to historical figures, animals, and literary or film characters, including an altarpiece of The Last Supper at Good Shepherd Lutheran Church in Cleveland, Mississippi. In addition to wood, Shaman worked in stone, bronze, ceramics, and painting.

Floyd Shaman was born in Wheatland, Wyoming, and spent his early years in the state with a brief sojourn in Seattle when his parents worked in the aircraft industry during World War II. After graduating from University Prep High School in Laramie, he excelled in basketball and earned a three-sport scholarship to North Dakota State Normal and Industrial School in Ellendale. Shaman enlisted in the U.S. Navy as a dental technician, a vocation that foreshadowed his later artistic career. In 1960 he returned to Wyoming to study sculpture as an undergraduate at the University of Wyoming under Robert Russin, earning a Bachelor’s degree in art and, in 1969, a Master’s degree with a thesis on the chemical patination of bronze. In 1970 he moved to Cleveland, Mississippi to teach art at Delta State University, where he established the sculpture division and instituted a bronze casting foundry. Facing difficulty obtaining stone in Mississippi, he began working in wood. A 1976 residency at Yaddo led to the major piece Janus Road Show, depicting three jazz musicians glimpsed in New Orleans. He left academia after ten years at Delta State to pursue full-time work as a sculptor. As an independent artist, Shaman achieved national visibility, regularly exhibiting across the country, and developed a notable gallery relationship with the Elaine Benson Gallery in Bridgehampton, New York, which hosted a charity invitational for a local animal rescue group. His home and studio attracted local attention, and from the mid-1990s his wife Molly operated a bed-and-breakfast incorporating his work. He is regarded as one of the South’s most important figurative artists of the late twentieth century, with works held in major collections across the United States and internationally.

On many large pleasure craft, beginning in the 1980s a flying bridge is located toward the stern to serve as an outdoor seating area and to provide space for storing a tender. Among the smallest surface vessels, such as sport fishing boats, the flying bridge may incorporate helm controls that allow piloting from that elevated position, though it typically does not include the full range of pilot-house controls found on the main bridge. In somewhat larger small vessels, the flying bridge can be enclosed, in which case it is more properly referred to as an upper pilot house or upper bridge.

Modern remote-control technology enables the bridge to assume direct control of the ship’s operations, with the helm and propulsion levers operable from the bridge and linked to machinery spaces that may run unmanned. In contemporary warships, navigational command originates from the bridge, which serves as the central node for steering, speed management, and navigation decisions. Electronically directed weapon systems are typically controlled from an interior compartment rather than the bridge, reflecting a separation between navigation and fire-control functionality. Together, these arrangements underscore the bridge’s role as the primary command center while relying on automation and remote controls for other ship systems.

DisplayPort connectors are common in premium products such as high-end displays, desktop computers, and graphics cards, with the majority of DisplayPort-enabled devices produced by companies in the computer hardware sector. According to the DisplayPort website, the interface is intended to complement HDMI rather than replace it. In 2016, HDMI connectivity was present on all HD and Ultra HD televisions. DisplayPort has supported advanced capabilities, including 5K resolution and Adaptive-Sync, which have been valuable for multimedia content creators and gamers and have been a major reason for GPUs to include DisplayPort support. These features were added to HDMI a few years later, and the HDMI 2.1 standard has since narrowed the gap by incorporating, among other features, variable refresh rate technology.

HDCP-stripping devices are hardware tools that remove High-bandwidth Digital Content Protection information from a video signal, enabling playback on displays and receivers that do not support HDCP. This allows protected content to be viewed on non-compliant equipment, though the use of such devices is typically subject to regulatory controls. In many cases, individuals must sign a fair-use and non-disclosure agreement with a designated registering agency prior to operation.

UPS Airlines operates an all-jet fleet and does not own turboprop or short-haul aircraft. As of November 2025, the airline maintains an active fleet of 291 aircraft, complemented by 210 leased or chartered aircraft to augment its operations.

Located at Miami International Airport in Miami-Dade County, Florida, the UPS Airlines facility there acts as the Latin America/Caribbean Hub. It serves primarily Central and South America, while also handling domestic packages for the southern United States. The facility spans 36,000 square feet and processes approximately 6,500 packages per hour, underpinning the company’s regional and cross-border logistics operations.

In the aerospace sector, functional safety is treated as a component of the overall safety of a system or piece of equipment. It implies that the system or equipment can be operated in a proper manner and that its operation does not introduce any danger, risk, damage, or injury.

The United Kingdom historically maintained a substantial in-country aerospace industry, producing civilian airliners and military aircraft. In recent decades, the sector has increasingly shifted toward cooperative arrangements with continental European companies, integrating into broader European supply chains. As a result, the UK has become a major importer of aerospace products, sourcing equipment from the United States among others. Despite these shifts, the country continues to sustain a highly active aerospace sector. A central player in the industry is BAE Systems, which supplies fully assembled aircraft as well as components, sub-assemblies, and sub-systems to other manufacturers. Its customers span European producers and clients worldwide.

South Korea and Iran share a long-standing football rivalry dating to official matches beginning in 1958. As of March 2022, the teams had played 33 matches, including 11 World Cup qualifying encounters. Both nations were among Asia's strongest sides during the 1960s and 1970s. They met only once in the Asian Cup final, in 1972, and subsequently confronted each other in five consecutive Asian Cup quarter-finals from 1996 to 2011, with each side recording two wins, two losses, and one draw in those five fixtures. Iran leads the all-time head-to-head, with 13 victories, 10 draws, and 10 defeats against South Korea.

In 1985, South Korea secured qualification for the FIFA World Cup by winning the East Asian tournament, defeating Japan twice in the final round and earning a return to the World Cup stage for the first time since 1954. The year also marked the arrival of Cha Bum-kun to the national team, a development that contributed to the 1986 squad being regarded as a golden generation. At the 1986 World Cup, Korea were defeated by Argentina, the eventual champions, 3-1. In the group phase, Park Chang-sun scored Korea’s first-ever World Cup goal; the team opened with a 1-1 draw against Bulgaria and then suffered a 3-2 defeat to Italy in the final group match, a game that saw Altobelli strike twice, an own goal by Cho Kwang-rae, and a late Korea goal by Huh Jung-moo. Contemporary media criticized referee David Socha for contentious officiating, including a penalty award to Italy. The season closed on a high note for the national program, as Korea captured the gold medal at the 1986 Asian Games.

Internet media types, also known as MIME types, consist of a primary type and a subtype, often accompanied by optional parameters. The identifiers for the type, the subtype, and the parameter names are treated as case-insensitive, allowing equivalence across differing capitalizations. In contrast, the values assigned to parameters are typically case-sensitive, preserving distinct meanings when capitalization differs. However, depending on the intended use and the particular application, parameter values may be interpreted in a case-insensitive fashion, reflecting practical variations in how these values are processed.

Defined in January 2001 under RFC 3023, the +xml suffix forms part of the Internet media type taxonomy. In January 2013, it was included in the initial contents of the Structured Syntax Suffix Registry (RFC 6839), together with other suffixes such as +json, +ber, +der, +fastinfoset, +wbxml, and +zip. Since then, the registry has been expanded to include additional suffixes, including +gzip, +cbor, +json-seq, and +cbor-seq.

East Turkestan is a label whose meaning and appropriateness are contested. In the People's Republic of China, terms such as East Turkestan, Uyghurstan, and Turkestan are linked to Western imperialist histories, former East Turkestan republics, and militant groups including the East Turkestan Islamic Movement (ETIM). Chinese authorities categorize the violence attributed to various separatist factions, including ETIM and the East Turkestan Liberation Organization, under the collective designation of "East Turkestan forces." Chinese diplomatic missions oppose foreigners’ use of the term, arguing that it is political rather than geographical or historical, and that it challenges China’s sovereignty. Historians and observers note that definitions of East Turkestan have varied and remained ambiguous; outside China, Xinjiang has not consistently been regarded as a single geographic or demographic entity.

Following the events of 1867, when the territories west of the Pamirs were consolidated into the Turkestan Governorate, often identified as Russian Turkestan, Western scholarship increasingly treated Turkestan as comprising a Russian-controlled portion and a Chinese portion. While foreign observers generally recognized Xinjiang as a Chinese polity, some preferred appellations that emphasized Turkic, Islamic, or Central Asian characteristics. In British and other English-language sources, there was no prevailing terminological consensus for Xinjiang, with designations such as Chinese Turkestan, East Turkestan, Chinese Central Asia, Serindia, and Sinkiang appearing in different texts. Before the twentieth century, locals tended to employ toponyms based on cities or oases, and these names could widen or narrow in scope; for example, Kashgaria derived from Kashgar referred to the southwestern part of Xinjiang. Another common label, Altishahr, meaning “six cities,” referred collectively to six largely undefined southern settlements south of the Tian Shan.

Tondero is a regional creole music tradition of northern Peru, closely tied to chinganas, traditional creole music bars where performances are held. In some chinganas, white flags are displayed as invitations for newcomers or solitary bohemian northern farmers, known as Piajenos. The invitation offers a chance to escape the northern heat and to drink Chicha de Jora, while also presenting an opportunity to hear an elderly Piajeno farmer sing and accompany himself on tondero rhythms. These rhythms are most typical of the northern Lambayeque region and the southern Piura region.

Tondero is a Peruvian musical and dance form characterized by a principal vocalist supported by a small chorus and two Criollo-style guitarists, with one guitarist providing the distinctive tundete or tondero bass line. The ensemble may incorporate the Peruvian cajon, a percussion instrument now widely used in Latin American commercial rhythms, and it has absorbed influences from modern flamenco, evolving jazz, and Peruvian spoon percussion. Performances may be accompanied by palm clapping. An Afro-Peruvian variant uses the checo, an instrument made from dried and flattened pumpkins.

Nanjing Olympic Suning Tower, known in Chinese as 南京奥体CBD苏宁广场, is a skyscraper project in Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, China. The development, situated near the Nanjing Olympic Sports Centre, was originally expected to be completed in 2017 but was subsequently put on hold. Construction resumed in 2020, with the latest plans aiming for a completion in 2025.

Two of the three submarines planned for the Romanian Navy were laid down at the Galați shipyard in 1938, launched in May 1941, and commissioned in May 1943. Marsuinul was a 620-ton attack submarine equipped with a 105 mm deck gun, a 37 mm anti-aircraft gun, and six 533 mm torpedo tubes (four in the bow and two in the stern). Rechinul was a 585-ton minelaying submarine carrying a 20 mm anti-aircraft gun, four 533 mm torpedo tubes, and a payload of forty mines. The third planned submarine was replaced by five Italian CB-type midget submarines, which were commissioned in late 1943. In addition, the two minelaying vessels were acquired in 1941.

During the interwar period, the Romanian Navy concentrated on building and maintaining a Black Sea fleet. In 1920, Italy delivered two Aquila-class destroyer-designated ships, which Romania renamed Mărășești and Mărăști. Four gunboats were purchased from the French Navy—Stihi, Dumitrescu, Lepri, and Sublocotenent Ghiculescu—with a further gunboat of the same class acquired for spare parts. Seven torpedo boats were obtained as war reparations from Austria-Hungary. The torpedo boat Fulgerul capsized and sank in the Bosphorus in 1922 while on passage to Romania. Three of the older torpedo boats, Năluca, Sborul and Smeul, would later see service in World War II. In 1926, two additional destroyers, Regele Ferdinand and Regina Maria of the Regele Ferdinand class, were ordered from Italy; these accompanied the navy's first submarine, Delfinul, and the submarine tender Constanța. All of these ships were commissioned between 1930 and 1936.

Discovery Life is a Polish television channel owned by TVN, a division of Warner Bros. Discovery. The channel's programming encompasses documentary, feature, and entertainment productions. It launched on 1 February 2015, replacing the standard-definition feed of Animal Planet in Poland. At its introduction, Discovery Life was available to approximately 55.5 percent of Polish households. The station began broadcasting in high definition on 16 January 2017, superseding the SD version.

Barbie: Mermaid Power depicts an underwater kingdom called Pacifica, where eight mer-people are designated as guardians by a beam of light emanating from a giant golden pearl. When Isla returns, she discovers only six guardians are present, with the two missing guardians identified as Malibu Barbie and Brooklyn Barbie. Isla then employs a pearl necklace she had given during Barbie: Dolphin Magic to transform the Barbie-girls and Malibu Barbie’s sisters into mermaids, resulting in Skipper, Stacie, and Chelsea gaining mermaid identities. For Skipper and Stacie, this marks their first experience of mermaid life, while Chelsea already possessed mermaid experience from Barbie: Dreamtopia. Subsequently, Brooklyn Barbie begins to learn that the mermaid myth is real.

Barbie: Mermaid Power is the eponymous soundtrack album released on 15 August 2022 across global online music streaming services. The collection comprises five original songs, with songwriting credits awarded to Matthew Tishler and Andrew Underberg, and two additional tracks written by Matias Mora. The project was produced by The Math Club. Principal singers include Jordyn Kane performing as Barbie "Malibu" Roberts and Lydia Li portraying Barbie "Brooklyn" Roberts.

Within the ISO 5775 designation, the second numeral denotes the nominal rim diameter, which corresponds to the bead diameter of the tire when mounted on the rim. This dimension is also known as the bead seat diameter (BSD). The circumference associated with this diameter can be determined by using a suitably narrow measuring tape to measure around the interior of the rim.

ISO 5775 is an international standard that governs the relationship between tire sizes and rim widths. For each tire size, the standard designates a rim design width, a measurement derived from the tire’s nominal section width, which provides the designed rim dimension associated with that tire. It also defines the range of rim widths that are considered acceptable for service with a given tire section width, thereby ensuring compatibility and safe operation across rims within that range.

Graduate assistants are a type of support position within higher education institutions. The role is typically held by individuals who are enrolled in graduate or postgraduate programs. They perform instructional duties as teaching assistants, helping professors deliver course content and support student learning, and they contribute to research as research assistants, assisting with projects, data collection, and analysis. In some cases, graduate assistants may also support athletic programs by aiding coaches with team operations and practices. Beyond academic units, they may be employed by other university departments, including housing services and academic advising, performing a range of tasks to assist operations.

Graduate assistantships are typically remunerated with stipends rather than hourly wages, distinguishing them from ordinary student employment. They provide practical experience and professional development for graduate students, complementing their academic work. By offering hands-on duties and opportunities to network, assistantships can broaden future employment prospects in the job market. In U.S. college sports, the graduate assistant position is frequently seen as an initial rung on the coaching career ladder, serving as a stepping stone to higher coaching roles.

Judicial discretion refers to the authority of judges to decide cases within the framework of applicable law. It is bounded by statutory provisions, binding precedent, and constitutional constraints, ensuring that discretionary choices remain within the scope permitted by the legal system. When a decision exceeds these limits, it may amount to a misuse of discretion and undermine the rule of law. In such instances, the ruling may be described as ultra vires, or outside the court’s powers. These decisions may be described as judicial activism.

Judicial discretion refers to the authority granted to judges to make certain legal determinations based on their own judgment and interpretation of the facts and applicable law. Within the framework of the separation of powers, it represents an aspect of judicial independence, enabling courts to exercise autonomous decision-making. When circumstances warrant, this discretion allows a judge to resolve a case within a spectrum of legally permissible outcomes, rather than being confined to a single prescribed result.

In California, and particularly in the Los Angeles area, the term liquor store is used more broadly than its literal meaning. In this regional usage, the label may apply to establishments that primarily function as convenience stores, corner shops, minimarts, or other small, local neighborhood groceries that sell alcoholic beverages in addition to a range of everyday items. This broad usage reflects local retail practices and diverges from a narrow definition that designates only dedicated alcohol retailers; the exact scope can vary by city or neighborhood.

Licensed retailers of alcoholic beverages are commonly referred to as liquor shops or wine shops. In practice, wine shops may devote most of their inventory to beer and spirits rather than wine. Consequently, some wine shops may not carry wine at all despite the name.

Reg Revans was born in Portsmouth, where his father worked as a marine surveyor. As a boy, Revans observed his father receiving a visit from seamen's representatives in the wake of the sinking of the RMS Titanic. He later recalled attending Florence Nightingale's memorial service with his mother in 1910.

In the 1990s, Reg Revans became associated with the City of London, where he met Raymond Mahoney and Alan Wenham-Prosser. The two colleagues applied his action-learning techniques to address workload-management problems within the City and to help manage long-standing personal difficulties in handling challenging professional situations. For these efforts, Revans was made a Freeman of the City of London.

The Czech Republic women's national football team announced a roster call-up ahead of the 2025 UEFA Women's Nations League play-off ties against Austria, with the fixtures scheduled for 24 and 28 October 2025.

The 2003 Internationaux de Strasbourg was the seventeenth edition of the women's tennis tournament played on outdoor clay courts at the Centre Sportif de Hautepierre in Strasbourg, France, from 19 to 24 May 2003. Classified as a WTA Tour Tier III event, the competition crowned Silvia Farina Elia, the seventh seed, as the singles champion. Her victory marked her third consecutive singles title at the tournament, and the winner's prize money amounted to $27,000.

ISO 3166-3 is the component of the ISO 3166 standard that covers codes for former countries and territories. When an entity is removed from ISO 3166-1, its corresponding alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes are placed on reserve. This reservation is maintained for a transition period of at least fifty years. After the transition ends, the codes may be reassigned to other entities.

ISO 3166-3 provides a set of codes for former country names by aligning them with the current ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 designation of the corresponding state. When a nation's name change also changes its alpha-2 code, the new two-letter code is used in the ISO 3166-3 entry. If the name change does not alter the alpha-2 code, a special code AA is employed. For example, Burma's change to Myanmar is reflected by the new alpha-2 code MM in ISO 3166-3, whereas the Byelorussian SSR's transition to Belarus retained the same alpha-2 code, leading to the use of AA.

Joachim Frank was a Harkness postdoctoral fellow who spent two years conducting research in the United States. During this period he studied with Robert Nathan at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory of the California Institute of Technology, with Robert M. Glaeser at the Donner Laboratory of the University of California, Berkeley, and with Benjamin M. Siegel at Cornell University in Ithaca, New York. In the fall of 1972 he briefly returned to the Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry in Martinsried as a research assistant, where he worked on the theory of partial coherence in electron microscopy. In 1973 he joined the Cavendish Laboratory at the University of Cambridge as a Senior Research Assistant under Vernon Ellis Cosslett.

Joachim Frank was born in Siegen, in the borough of Weidenau. He earned a Bachelor of Science in physics (Vordiplom) from the University of Freiburg in 1963, followed by a Diplom from Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich under Walter Rollwagen; his Diplom thesis investigated the secondary electron emission of gold at its melting point in 1967. He then obtained his Ph.D. from the Technical University of Munich, conducting research in Walter Hoppe's laboratory at the Max Planck Institute for Eiweiss- und Lederforschung, now the Max Planck Institute of Biochemistry. His doctoral dissertation, completed in 1970, examined high-resolution electron micrographs using image-difference and reconstruction methods, and it addressed digital image processing and optical diffraction in the analysis of electron micrographs, including image alignment via cross-correlation.

The Timeline of information theory provides a chronological overview of notable developments in information theory and its allied disciplines. It surveys topics across classical information theory, quantum information theory, and statistical physics, and documents advances in data compression and the design of error-correcting codes. The timeline also encompasses related subjects that intersect with information-theoretic ideas, illustrating how theoretical concepts have informed practical methods and cross-disciplinary research. By presenting these milestones in sequence, the article traces the historical progression of ideas, techniques, and applications that have shaped the field and its connections to broader areas of science.

London dispersion forces are the weakest type of intermolecular interaction and form part of van der Waals forces. They arise from temporary fluctuations in electron density that generate instantaneous dipoles in atoms or molecules, which then induce corresponding dipoles in neighboring species to produce a short-range attraction. These forces can give rise to van der Waals complexes. They drive the condensation of nonpolar substances from gas to liquid under suitable conditions and, when temperatures are sufficiently low, can contribute to solidification.

Within chemistry, a molecule is an electrically neutral assembly of two or more atoms held together by chemical bonds. Molecules can be classified by their elemental composition: homonuclear molecules consist of atoms from a single element, as exemplified by O2, while heteronuclear molecules are formed from different elements, such as water (H2O). Moreover, a molecule represents the smallest unit of a substance that retains its characteristic physical and chemical properties.

Performativity, in the context of Bourdieu's work, is linked to the concept of habitus, which he formulated in the 1970s as a disciplined improvisation that shapes and conditions social practices. Developed partly in reaction to the structuralist view of culture as a fixed system of rules, particularly in his 1972 Outline of a Theory of Practice, habitus mediates the transition from productive to reproductive social orders, where everyday practices and embodied dispositions generate and reproduce social structures. In this view, simulations and models become constitutive of social reality, gradually erasing a clear distinction between what is real and what merely appears to be so. Although the term "performance" is not central to Bourdieu's vocabulary, his emphasis on the bodily habitus as a formative site has nonetheless inspired later performance theory and debates about how embodied actions contribute to the production of meaning.

Within debates on gender theory, Butler’s account has been criticized for reconfiguring ethnomethodological and symbolic interactionist analyses into a framework of performativity. Scholar A. I. Green contends that the work of Kessler and McKenna (1978) and West and Zimmerman (1987) builds on the foundations laid by Garfinkel (1967) and Goffman (1959). These approaches deconstruct gender into moments of attribution and repetition that arise within an ongoing social process of enacting masculinity and femininity, a dynamic described as occurring in the performative interval. The works share the view that gender does not precede practice but instead emerges from practice, being instantiated through micro-level interactions.

North District (Chinese: 北區; pinyin: Běi Qū) is an urban district of Taichung, Taiwan. It was part of Taichung prior to the 2010 amalgamation of Taichung City and Taichung County. The district is one of Taichung's major hubs for shopping, education, and culture.

North District was a district of Taichung Provincial City prior to Taiwan’s 2010 municipal reorganization. Taichung Provincial City merged with Taichung County to form the Taichung Special Municipality on 25 December 2010, after which North District became part of the expanded municipal administration.

In 1997, the company shortened its name from Pacific Mutual Life Insurance Company to Pacific Life Insurance Company, reflecting a transition from mutual ownership to a mutual holding company framework. In the same year, Pacific Life adopted the humpback whale as its corporate emblem, citing the whale’s persistence, performance, and strength as guiding qualities.

During the Great Depression, Pacific Life faced significant financial difficulties. In 1936, Insurance Commissioner Samuel L. Carpenter advocated mutualization as a measure to protect both policyholders and the company. Through mutualization, policyholders were made part-owners of the firm, effectively converting ownership to those with policies and aligning their interests with the insurer’s financial stability. The aim of this restructuring was to preserve solvency and secure policyholder commitments amid economic distress.

Mohammed bin Ibrahim bin Jubair (1929–2002) was a Saudi judge and government minister who served as the chairman of Saudi Arabia's Majlis ash-Shura, the Consultative Assembly. He held the leadership post from 1992 to 2002, guiding the body in its advisory functions to the government and overseeing its deliberative processes during that period.

Mohammed bin Jubair was appointed as the chair of the Majlis ash-Shura following its reconstitution in 1992, a position he held for nearly a decade until his death in early 2002. He passed away on 24 January 2002 in Riyadh.

The RB12 helped Red Bull Racing establish themselves as the leading challenger to Mercedes after the Austrian Grand Prix, frequently contesting for race victories. The team achieved podium finishes at every race except the Italian Grand Prix and the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. Max Verstappen's arrival at the team for the Spanish Grand Prix intensified internal competition, with Daniel Ricciardo facing stiffer pressure from Verstappen than he had from Daniil Kvyat. Ricciardo later indicated that he learned from Verstappen's driving techniques and incorporated those insights to enhance his own performance.

During the season, Daniil Kvyat was demoted to Scuderia Toro Rosso for the remainder of the year, with Max Verstappen promoted to Red Bull Racing to take his place. In the race, Verstappen qualified fourth while Daniel Ricciardo qualified third, with Ricciardo’s lap approximately half a second faster. On lap one, a collision between Lewis Hamilton and Nico Rosberg exiting Turn 3 led to retirement for both and a safety-car period. During the safety-car phase, Ricciardo led the field with Verstappen just behind him. The teams pursued different strategies, as Ricciardo adopted a safer three-stop plan and Verstappen a riskier two-stop approach. Ultimately Verstappen won the race, finishing ahead of the two Ferrari drivers, and became the youngest-ever Formula One race winner as well as the first Dutch driver to win a Formula One race.

Submarine canyons exhibit several forms of slope failure, including mass wasting, slumping, and submarine landslides. Mass wasting is the slower, smaller downhill movement of material under gravity. Slumping refers to the rotational movement of masses on a hillside. Landslides (slides) involve the detachment and displacement of sediment masses.

Submarine canyons are steep-sided valleys carved into the seabed of the continental slope, and they may extend onto the shelf; their walls are nearly vertical, with heights reaching as much as five kilometers from the canyon floor to the rim, a characteristic exemplified by the Great Bahama Canyon. These structures act as channels for turbidity currents, which are dense, sediment-laden flows that move downslope across the seafloor. Such currents are fed by riverine sediment supply or generated locally on the seabed by processes such as storms, submarine landslides, earthquakes, and other disturbances that disturb sediments. Turbidity currents can advance downslope at speeds of up to roughly 70 kilometers per hour. In their passage, they erode the continental slope and transport sediment to the abyssal plain, where particles eventually settle out, contributing to deep-sea sedimentation.

Longboarding has diversified, expanding its repertoire of styles and techniques. It has come full circle by embracing street-oriented tricks alongside ramp-based crossover events, integrating urban and park elements. At the same time, it retains its original emphasis on slalom, ditch skating, and cornering. Across these developments, longboarding continues to push toward greater speeds.

Salima Pasha was an Iraqi Jewish singer who gained recognition when Umm Kulthum described her as the most famous woman singer since the early 1930s. She was married to Nazem Al-Ghazali, a successful Iraqi singer and actor. She remained in Iraq after most Iraqi Jews left the country, living there until her death in 1974.

Salima Pasha, also known as Salima Mourad or Salima Murad (Arabic: سليمة مراد; February 2, 1900 – January 28, 1974), was an Iraqi Jewish singer who achieved wide recognition and was highly respected throughout the Arab world. She was nicknamed "Pasha" by Iraqi Prime Minister Nuri al-Said.

Huacheng Dadao station (花城大道站), formerly Shuangta station (双塔站, Twin Towers station), is an underground Guangzhou Metro station on the APM line. It is located in Zhujiang New Town, Tianhe District, at the intersection of Huacheng Avenue with East Zhujiang Road and West Zhujiang Road. The station opened on 8 November 2010.

Mike Levin addressed Middle East policy in 2024 by advocating a temporary cease-fire to permit humanitarian aid into Gaza while also urging the continuation of military assistance to Israel. He supported a cessation of fighting conditioned on the release of Israeli hostages. In April 2024, Levin stated that new leadership was needed in Israel and criticized Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for not steering toward a more peaceful outcome.

The race for the district's congressional seat, in which Mike Levin was a candidate, was marked by intense competition due to the lack of an incumbent. The primary ballot featured sixteen candidates, and the election used a nonpartisan blanket format (top-two), under which the two top finishers advance to the general election regardless of party. The sizable field prompted concerns that the Democratic Party could be excluded from the general election.

Martin Dugas is a Canadian former professional soccer player who spent his career across North American outdoor leagues and indoor competitions, beginning with the St. Catharines Wolves from 1987 to 1993 before moving to the Dutch club SC Cambuur. He subsequently had brief periods with FC St. Pauli in Germany and Watford in England, though he did not make a league appearance for Watford. In fall 1996, he returned to Canada to sign with the Edmonton Drillers of the National Professional Soccer League, and throughout his career he divided his time between outdoor summer play and indoor winter seasons. Dugas remained with the Edmonton Drillers until the start of the 2000–01 NPSL season, after which he was traded to the Detroit Rockers following nine games and finished the season there. From 2001 to 2003 he played for the Milwaukee Wave. In 2003 Monterrey Fury selected Dugas in the NPSL Expansion Draft and then traded him to the Dallas Sidekicks for the 2003–04 indoor season. He also appeared for the Toronto Lynx through the 1998 USISL season. In May 1999 he signed with the Staten Island Vipers of the USL A-League, a club that folded at the end of the season. Dugas played for the Montreal Impact in the 2001 USL A-League and for the Calgary Storm in 2002. In 2007 he moved to the Edmonton Drillers and took on the role of player-coach.

Martin Dugas (born 15 October 1972) is a Canadian former professional soccer player whose twelve-year career at the professional level was followed by a transition into coaching, most recently as coach of the Edmonton Drillers.

Anthony Powell was born in Westminster, the son of Lt-Col Philip Lionel William Powell of the Welch Regiment (1882–1959) and Maud Mary (d. 1954), daughter of Edmund Lionel Wells-Dymoke of The Grange, East Molesey, Surrey. The Wells-Dymoke line traces to a Lincolnshire landowning family that provided hereditary Champions to monarchs since the time of Richard II and through marriage linked to the Barons Marmion, the first holders of the office. The Powell family itself is said to descend from ancient Welsh kings and chieftains. Powell developed a strong interest in genealogy and undertook extensive research into the Powell lineage, establishing paternal descent from Gwriad ap Elidyr, a figure identified as a descendant of Coel Hen in genealogical materials such as Jesus College MS 20 and other sources. This lineage was validated to the satisfaction of the heralds at the College of Arms, and in 1964 he was granted permission to bear the ancient Powell arms. The pedigree was also documented in Burke's Landed Gentry.

Anthony Powell was a British literary critic and writer who balanced a career in reviewing with pursuits in creative writing. He served as the Times Literary Supplement’s principal reviewer of fiction, providing extensive coverage of novelists for the publication, and he held the post of literary editor at Punch from 1953 to 1959. From 1958 to 1990 he wrote regularly for The Daily Telegraph, resigning after a vitriolic personal attack on him by Auberon Waugh appeared in the newspaper. He also contributed occasional reviews to The Spectator. A substantial portion of his criticism was later collected and republished in two volumes of critical essays: Miscellaneous Verdicts (1990) and Under Review (1992).

Cambiamo!, an Italian political party, by the end of 2020 advocated a more moderate conservatism than Forza Italia. It supported forming a national unity government to replace Giuseppe Conte's centre-left administration. In February 2021, during the process surrounding Mario Draghi's national unity government—which was also supported by the League, Forza Italia, and other major centre-left parties—Cambiamo! began attracting centrists from Forza Italia. Consequently, it formed a larger sub-group within the Chamber of Deputies' Mixed Group, comprising ten deputies, eight of whom were full party members.

Cambiamo! (CI) faced an internal crisis within a short period after its formation due to limited broad voter support. In response, Toti advocated forming an alliance with Matteo Renzi’s Italia Viva and launched a new party named Italy in the Centre (IaC). By contrast, Brugnaro preferred remaining within the centre-right coalition and rejected politics associated with the establishment. In February 2022, CI’s sub-group in the Mixed Group, formerly known as IDeA–Cambiamo!–Europeanists, was renamed Italy in the Centre. In March 2022, a federation between Coraggio Italia and Italy in the Centre was announced, involving separate organisations and parliamentary groupings. In May 2022, the national leadership approved a provisional statute for Italy in the Centre, and regional coordinators and a secretariat were appointed, effectively supplanting Cambiamo!.

The IS version of ISO/IEC 15504 comprises six parts. Part 7 has advanced to a Final Draft Standard form, signaling that it is nearing completion. Work has begun on Part 8, indicating ongoing development of subsequent components in the series.

ISO/IEC 15504 describes a process assessment framework in which data are collected through interviews with process performers, examination of relevant documents and quality records, and the gathering of statistical process data. The assessor validates the collected information to ensure its accuracy and that the assessment scope is fully covered. The data are then evaluated during the process rating step against the process's base practices and the generic practices of the relevant capability dimension, employing expert judgment. The rating relies on the evaluator’s qualifications and competency requirements. A preliminary process rating is presented to the sponsor, and ideally to the individuals or teams assessed, to confirm its accuracy. Depending on the feedback received, further assessment may be required before a final process rating is issued.

Media reports following his death described unsettled and unpredictable behavior in the final weeks of his life. In John Swenson's 1982 biography, he is portrayed as making a sequence of odd, largely one-sided late-night telephone conversations with friends and relatives, with his coherence waning toward the end. His former wife recalled that he would call and ramble, often dwelling on past events. The biography also notes that he painted the windows of his house black. Apart from these accounts, information about his final days remains scarce.
In March 2007, the Original Comets established the Bill Haley Museum in Munich, Germany. On October 27, 2007, former Comets guitarist Bill Turner opened the museum to the public.

In Khmer temple architecture, the central sanctuary (prasat) functions as the dwelling place of the temple’s principal deity rather than a public space for worship, and it is typically only a few metres across. The deity reflected in the temple's tradition may be a Hindu form such as Shiva or Vishnu, or a Buddhist figure such as the Buddha or a bodhisattva; the divine presence is represented either by a statue or, in the case of Shiva, a linga. The sanctuary’s importance is demonstrated by the height of the surrounding tower, its central location within the complex, and its comparatively richer wall decoration. Symbolically, the sanctuary is interpreted as Mount Meru, the legendary abode of the Hindu gods.

Khmer architecture encompasses both religious monuments and secular dwellings; the latter were constructed from perishable materials, notably timber, and have largely not survived. By contrast, Angkor’s religious architecture is distinguished by a characteristic repertoire of structural forms, architectural elements, and decorative motifs. These features are catalogued in a glossary cited in the text, providing a standardized guide to their identification. Across the Angkorean period, a succession of architectural styles emerged, causing the presence and prominence of particular features to vary over time. Consequently, scholars frequently rely on the distribution of these features to date remains and to understand the stylistic evolution of Angkorian architecture.

The terminus of a glacier reflects the influence of a range of factors, including its thermal structure, stress regime, and external conditions. When a glacier is retreating, the front typically adopts a gently inclined profile resulting from ongoing melt at the terminus. However, variations in thermal fields and diverse internal and external stresses can modify this conventional geometry, promoting fracturing and enhancing melting in a feedback that affects the terminus. This cracking–melting feedback can drive calving and produce a variety of terminus forms, from smooth, swept fronts to highly fragmented margins, depending on local conditions.

The glacier terminus can be monitored over time to assess glacier movement. Measurements are taken relative to a fixed reference point on adjacent bedrock, ensuring consistency across observation epochs. Variations in terminus position between successive time intervals yield a record of glacier change, including advances or retreats. In addition, researchers may compare photographs of the glacier captured at different times to evaluate terminus fluctuations.

During the 1984–1985 miners' strike, the British anarchist movement experienced a revival that attracted a large influx of new participants and contributed to the emergence of new anarchist organizations in the wake of Class War. In 1984, former members of the Libertarian Communist Group formed the Libertarian Communist Discussion Group, drawing inspiration from Makhno's Platform and Fontenis's Manifesto of Libertarian Communism. The LCDG began collaborating with the editor of Virus magazine and started publishing anarcho-communist texts, subsequently adopting the name Anarchist Communist Discussion Group. Following the 1986 split of Syndicalist Fight from the Direct Action Movement, the Anarchist Communist Discussion Group merged with Syndicalist Fight to establish the Anarchist Communist Federation.

During the late 1980s, the Anarchist Communist Federation (ACF) drew a large influx of newcomers to anarchism, effectively becoming a largely reconstituted organization detached from its historical roots. In the early 1990s, it participated in the poll tax protests and argued for the abolition of all hierarchical structures in favor of a worldwide classless society. A 1991 Economic League report described the ACF as highly militant, ranking it only behind Class War in terms of militancy and willingness to resort to violence. Despite its small size, the group exerted influence through cordial ties with other libertarian socialist currents, notably collaborating with Subversion, an autonomous Marxist tendency. In 1999 the ACF renamed itself the Anarchist Federation (AF) to shorten the name and to emphasize that it was not an alliance of anarchists with other forms of communists.

Tailings in the aluminium industry refer to the residual materials produced from processing bauxite ore to manufacture aluminium. About 70 million tonnes of tailings are generated each year, roughly 150 billion pounds. The management and disposal of these tailings presents one of the principal environmental and engineering challenges faced by aluminium manufacturers.

Tailings are the solid wastes left after ore processing; in the phosphate fertilizer industry, a major by-product is phosphogypsum, generated during the conversion of phosphate rock into fertilizer. The estimated annual production of phosphogypsum waste ranges from 100 to 280 million tons. Although phosphogypsum is abundant, it is generally regarded as a low-value by-product and is largely disposed of as waste. The material is radioactive due to naturally occurring radionuclides, including uranium and thorium and their daughter isotopes. Depending on prevailing uranium market prices, the uranium content in phosphogypsum can be economically recoverable, making extraction potentially attractive even in the absence of other incentives such as environmental harm reduction.

Tipping Point Australia generally achieves the highest ratings in its time slot, outperforming its main competitors, including The Chase Australia, a game show broadcast by the Seven Network, and Network 10's 10 News.

Tipping Point Australia is an Australian television game show broadcast on the Nine Network. It premiered on 29 January 2024 and is hosted by Todd Woodbridge. In the program, three contestants answer general-knowledge questions to accumulate counters that advance on a large coin-pusher arcade machine, with the outcome determining cash and prize winnings. The show replaced Nine's Millionaire Hot Seat, which had aired on the network from 2009 to 2023.

Numismatics, the scholarly study of currency, coinage, and related objects, covers a broad range of approaches to monetary history and material culture. In this field, investigations into Chinese numismatics have been influenced by both Western reinterpretations and inland scholarly work. Helen Wang's A Short History of Chinese Numismatics in European Languages (2012–2013) analyzes how Chinese coinage has been understood within Western contexts, tracing the reception and translation of Chinese numismatic topics across European languages. Conversely, Lyce Jankowski's Les amis des monnaies offers an in-depth examination of Chinese numismatics as practiced within China during the nineteenth century, focusing on domestic practices, networks, and knowledge production surrounding coin study. Together, these works reflect the discipline’s range, highlighting cross-cultural reception as well as internal 19th‑century Chinese scholarship.

Numismatics, the scholarly study of coins and monetary history, has a long tradition of producing comprehensive publication series that document coin collections. In 1931 the British Academy established the Sylloge Nummorum Graecorum to publish collections of ancient Greek coinage, providing standardized references for researchers. Several decades later, the field gained another influential project with the Sylloge of Coins of the British Isles, whose first volume appeared in 1958, initiating a major program of cataloguing British coinage. Together, these initiatives illustrate the discipline's emphasis on systematic documentation and the dissemination of numismatic data to scholars worldwide.

Nguyễn Khoa Nam (23 September 1927 – 30 April 1975) was a Vietnamese military officer who served in the Army of the Republic of Vietnam (ARVN), attaining the rank of major general. A native of Đà Nẵng, he received his primary education at the École des Garçons in his hometown, completing his studies in 1939. He joined the French-sponsored Vietnam National Army (VNA) in the colonial era and subsequently attended the Thủ Đức Military Academy, from which he graduated in 1953. Nam went on to continue his service within the ARVN until his death in 1975.

Nguyễn Khoa Nam is a Vietnamese military officer who attained the rank of Major General. He conducted operations across the Mekong Delta with the aim of preventing the Viet Cong from taking over regional districts. He was awarded the National Order of Vietnam, Fourth Class and Third Class medals in recognition of his service.

The alveolo-palatal ejective affricate is an affricate consonant produced by first completely stopping the airstream and then releasing it through a narrow constriction at the alveolo-palatal place of articulation, with the constricted flow generating turbulence.

The alveolo-palatal ejective affricate is a consonantal sound characterized as an ejective affricate produced at the alveolo-palatal region. It has been attested in the Ubykh language. In the International Phonetic Alphabet, this sound is transcribed as tɕʼ.

Since the onset of market-oriented reforms, China has experienced a pronounced rise in income inequality. The Gini coefficient, a standard measure of inequality, climbed from 0.30 in 1986 to 0.42 in 2011. Researchers focusing on poverty have suggested that a Gini index above 0.40 can be potentially destabilizing, a threshold that the 2011 figure surpasses. This increase in inequality has been a notable social issue associated with the reform era, influencing discussions on distributional outcomes and policy responses.

Following constitutional commitments to gender equality across political, economic, cultural, and social domains, China has enacted laws and programs aimed at prohibiting sex-selective abortion, safeguarding maternal rights, improving girls’ livelihoods, and criminalizing discriminatory hiring. Nevertheless, practical progress has been limited, and discrimination persists across multiple sectors. In the employment sphere, the gender wage gap remains and may be widening, with women often steered toward lower‑paid roles; stereotypes constrain job opportunities, and motherhood can carry penalties. These gaps are linked to restricted access to lower‑level administrative and sales positions and to educational differences, with employers reportedly hiring men for experience while favoring younger, appearance-conscious women, thereby reinforcing traditional career paths. Illegal but widespread practices include avoiding female recruitment to sidestep costs associated with childbearing and terminating pregnant workers as “inefficient.” In the family domain, sex‑selective abortions and higher female child mortality have intersected with the one‑child policy, cultivating a son preference that is culturally and economically advantageous for lineage, elder care, and family influence. Even when daughters are born, they frequently face gender inequalities, and some evidence suggests males receive greater shares of household resources. Taken together, female discrimination remains a significant social issue in China, shaped by enduring cultural norms as well as political and economic structures.

Carrie Nation, a temperance campaigner, helped fund a portion of her hatchet-based protests—often described as "hatchetations"—through the sale of hatchet-shaped stick pins. The souvenirs were supplied by a pharmacist in Topeka, Kansas, and the handle of each pin carried the inscription "Death to Rum." The label "hatchetations" is used in reference to her campaign actions.

Tie pins, particularly those resembling gold- or silver-toned safety pins, began to be used as tie and collar pins in the early twentieth century. They were employed to fasten the tie to the shirt, becoming a conventional element of men’s dress and, in some contexts, school uniforms. The devices proved especially useful on formal occasions or in windy weather, when a properly secured tie helped maintain a neat appearance. Although various alternative methods for securing ties exist, an ordinary safety pin inserted from behind the shirt can secure the tie discreetly, without marring the fabric’s surface.

Joseph Hooton Taylor Jr. earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in physics from Haverford College in 1963 and a Doctor of Philosophy in astronomy from Harvard University in 1968. After completing his Ph.D., he held a brief research position at Harvard before joining the University of Massachusetts Amherst, where he rose to the rank of Professor of Astronomy. During his time at UMass Amherst, he also served as Associate Director of the Five College Radio Astronomy Observatory.

Joseph Hooton Taylor Jr. is an American physicist whose work with colleagues led to the discovery and ongoing study of a binary pulsar system whose orbit gradually shrinks as energy is carried away by gravitational radiation. This decay shortens the orbital period, in precise agreement with predictions derived from Albert Einstein's General Theory of Relativity. Across roughly three decades of pulsar timing, Taylor and his team measured the orbital changes and found concordance with the GR prediction to better than one percent. The achievement marked the first indirect confirmation of gravitational radiation. Since then, scores of binary pulsars have been discovered, and independent measurements have borne out Taylor's results.

Juan de Betanzos, a sixteenth‑century Spanish chronicler, produced the Relacion de las cosas del Peru, a work largely based on information gathered from Indigenous informants, including the wife of Atahualpa, making it one of the rare sources that preserves an Indigenous perspective on the Inca. In the absence of native written records, the account offers a unique illumination of Inca civilization before the conquest. It traces the early expansion and the development of the kingdom of Cuzco under Yupanqui, and it describes Huayna Capac’s imperial policies. The narrative further provides insight into the civil war between Huáscar and Atahualpa that unfolded prior to Pizarro’s arrival. Because part of the testimony comes from Atahualpa’s wife, the portrayal is influenced by her viewpoint, yielding a perspective that can be biased against Huáscar.

Juan Diez de Betanzos (born 1510 in Betanzos, Spain; died March 1, 1576 in Cusco, Peru) was a Spanish chronicler best known for his Narrative of the Incas, a key source on the Spanish conquest of the Inca civilization. The narrative incorporates testimony from his wife, Cuxirimay Ocllo (also known as Doña Angelina), who had previously been married to the Inca king Atahualpa. Betanzos conducted interviews with Inca individuals who participated in the Battle of Cajamarca or who were present in Atahualpa's camp, using these firsthand accounts to inform his chronicle.

In formal methods, a formal specification is developed to model the aspects of a system under study with mathematical precision. This specification can be used to prove properties about the specification itself, enabling rigorous verification of its internal consistency and correctness. Inferences drawn from these proofs can then establish properties of the system implementation, linking specification-level reasoning to the behavior of the actual system.

Formal methods denote a collection of mathematically based techniques for specifying, developing, and verifying systems. Among these techniques, model checking serves as a method for confirming whether a system satisfies a given specification or property. The approach relies on exhaustively traversing the system's state space, examining every possible state and transition that could occur during execution to detect violations or establish correctness. While highly effective for certain classes of verification tasks, model checking often requires abstraction or symbolic representations to manage large or infinite state spaces.

MY is the abbreviation for model year and is frequently placed before the year in automotive industry technical documentation and regulatory contexts (for example, MY2019 or MY93). Regulatory agencies that reference this convention include the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA), the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Transport Canada, and Environment Canada. In North America, the model year is typically used as the reference point rather than the vehicle’s production calendar year, even when the MY designation is not explicitly included.

The model year, often abbreviated as MY, denotes a version of a product that is produced across several consecutive years. This designation is used to identify a specific iteration of a product, rather than tying it strictly to a single calendar year. In some cases, the model year does not correspond to the calendar year in which the product was manufactured, meaning the year used for branding or identification may differ from the actual production year.

El Paso, Texas, occupies a notable place in the early history of the Rio Grande region as a corridor of exploration and governance in northern New Spain. The Chamuscado and Rodríguez Expedition of 1581–1582 passed through the area that is now El Paso, crossed the Rio Grande, and reached lands later associated with New Mexico; led by Francisco Sánchez “El Chamuscado” and Fray Agustín Rodríguez, the party was among the first to trek the Rio Grande and to acquaint themselves with Pueblo groups since Coronado’s expedition about four decades earlier. Don Juan de Oñate, born in 1550 in Zacatecas, became the earliest-known New Spain explorer to lodge near the Rio Grande at El Paso for about ten days in 1598 and to celebrate a Thanksgiving Mass there on April 30, 1598. Earlier still, four survivors of the Narváez expedition—Álvar Núñez Cabeza de Vaca, Alonso del Castillo Maldonado, Andrés Dorantes de Carranza, and Estevanico, an enslaved Moroccan—are thought to have crossed the Rio Grande into territories that would become present-day Mexico roughly 75 miles south of the El Paso region in 1535. El Paso del Norte, today Ciudad Juárez, was founded on the south bank of the Rio Grande in 1659 by Fray Garcia de San Francisco. In the wake of the Pueblo Revolt of 1680, El Paso served as the temporary base for Spanish governance of New Mexico until 1692, when Santa Fe was reconquered and restored as the capital.

El Paso, Texas, contains a sizable military presence centered on Fort Bliss, the William Beaumont Army Medical Center, and Biggs Army Airfield, together forming a major component of the city's defense infrastructure. The defense industry in the city employs more than 41,000 people and generates an estimated $6 billion in annual economic activity. In 2013, Fort Bliss was selected as the U.S. Air Force Security Forces Regional Training Center, a designation that is expected to bring roughly 8,000–10,000 Air Force personnel to the area each year.

In August 1944, partisan activity intensified in the rear of the Gothic Line. On 17 August, German troops at Bardine, situated about two kilometres from San Terenzo Monti, traveled by trucks and confiscated livestock. The inhabitants of Bardine urged the partisans to strike the returning convoy. In the ensuing clash, sixteen German soldiers were killed.

The San Terenzo Monti massacre, also known as the Bardine massacre or Bardine San Terenzo massacre, was a wartime atrocity that occurred near Fivizzano in Tuscany, Italy, from 17 to 19 August 1944. It was perpetrated by the German 16th SS Panzergrenadier Division, and 159 Italian civilians were killed.
The 1997 Italian Indoor concluded with Albano earning his first title of the year and the fifth of his career, while Nyborg achieved his sole title of the year, the third of his career.

The 1997 Italian Indoor was a men's tennis tournament contested on indoor carpet courts at Palatrussardi in Milan, Italy. It was part of the Championship Series of the 1997 ATP Tour. This edition marked the 20th occurrence of the event and ran from 24 February to 2 March 1997. The singles title was captured by the top seed, Goran Ivanišević.

During the early phase of microcomputing, BASIC interpreters spread to smaller machines and minicomputers, making interactive programming widely accessible. A number of vendors adopted a variant closely mirroring the Hewlett-Packard dialect, with Data General's Nova line cited as a prominent early success in the 1970s. Meanwhile, Wang Laboratories found commercial traction with purpose-built BASIC systems, most notably the Wang 2200 series. Because there was no universal standard, multiple dialects and variants of BASIC circulated across different platforms. DEC initially did not embrace BASIC, instead engaging with the JOSS project at SRI and developing its own language, FOCAL, inspired by that system. Nevertheless, the rising popularity of BASIC during the early 1970s compelled DEC to release their own version of BASIC, augmented with modifications.

Minimal BASIC is a compact variant of the BASIC programming language designed for devices with limited memory, offering a pared-down set of statements that cover data handling, program structure, and user interaction. Core elements include a comment directive, an array dimension command, and facilities for configuring extensions as well as for defining user-defined functions. It provides assignment and output facilities, along with a means for capturing user input. For data-driven programs, it supports embedded data declarations, data retrieval, and restoring the data pointer. Logical control is achieved through a conditional construct, and loops are implemented with a counter-based construct that advances in defined steps. Program flow is governed by direct jumps, while subroutines are supported through a call-and-return mechanism, and a form of computed jumping enables branching to different targets at runtime. A command to seed the random-number generator is available, and execution is terminated with explicit stop or end directives. Together, these components form a minimal yet functional core intended for simple programming tasks on early hardware.

High-definition television demands substantial data rates; uncompressed HD video requires bandwidth exceeding one gigabit per second for studio-quality output. Digital HDTV became feasible through discrete cosine transform–based compression, a lossy image compression technique introduced by Nasir Ahmed in 1972. This DCT was later incorporated into motion-compensated DCT algorithms that underpin key video coding standards, including the H.26x lineage beginning in 1988 and the MPEG family introduced around 1993. The use of motion-compensated DCT compression markedly reduces the bandwidth required for digital television signals. By 1991, DCT-based compression delivered data rates of about 70–140 Mbit/s with compression ratios in the range of 8:1 to 14:1 for near-studio-quality HDTV. Between 1988 and 1991, DCT video compression was widely adopted as the prevailing video coding standard for HDTV, enabling practical digital HDTV. Additionally, DRAM began to be used as framebuffer memory, and advancements in manufacturing scale coupled with falling DRAM prices contributed to the commercialization of HDTV.

High-definition television uses both 50 Hz and 60 Hz families of standards, with 50 Hz systems supporting 50i as well as progressive 25p and 50p, while 60 Hz systems accommodate a wider range including 59.94i, 60i, 23.976p, 24p, 29.97p, 30p, 59.94p, and 60p. In standard-definition contexts, fractional rates were often rounded to whole numbers, for example 23.976p being labeled as 24p and 59.94i as 60i. HDTV operating at 60 Hz therefore employs both fractional and near-integer rates, making precise notation important to avoid ambiguity. In practice, the combination 29.97p/59.94i is almost universally referred to as 60i, while 23.976p is commonly called 24p.

TFramedTransport is a transport class in Apache Thrift that transmits data in discrete frames. It is required when using a non-blocking server, as the framing scheme enables proper message delineation in asynchronous I/O. Each frame is prefixed with its length, allowing the recipient to determine where a frame ends and the next begins.

Apache Thrift is a software framework that generates source code from a descriptive interface definition language (IDL). The compiler converts the IDL specifications into language-specific bindings, enabling cross-language communication based on defined data types and services. In the Java implementation, the generated code may place an enumeration such as PhoneType inside the containing Phone class, treating it as a nested enum.

Personification is a widespread motif in classical literature, visual art, and drama, where abstract ideas and social concepts are depicted as minor deities or daemons. In classical Athens, each geographical division used for local governance was associated with a personified deity that received cultic attention. Among the best-attested examples are demos, the male personification representing the body of free citizens who compose the governing assembly, and boule, the female personification representing the ruling council. These personifications appear in artistic works, though they are often difficult to identify unless they are explicitly labeled.

By the late 16th century, writers such as Karel van Mander began to treat personification as a topic within the visual arts, a development evident in the Schilder-boeck (1604). Emblem books describing and illustrating emblematic images, largely composed of personifications, gained popularity among intellectuals, artists, and craftsmen seeking motifs. The most famous emblematic handbook is Cesare Ripa's Iconologia, whose first edition appeared unillustrated in 1593. From 1603 onward, Iconologia appeared in numerous illustrated editions by different artists. These editions established the defining attributes of many personifications, traits that persisted in artistic iconography into the nineteenth century.

The First Philippine Commission sought to establish civil government in the Philippines, proposing that this be implemented through a provincial organization act. The initiative was undertaken on February 6, following the Philippine-Spanish conflict and the subsequent Filipino-American conflicts. This move formed part of the broader transition toward formal provincial administration in the archipelago, a process that underpins the later development of provincial governance in areas that would eventually become Rizal province.

In 1853, the Distrito Politico-Militar de los Montes de San Mateo (Political-Military District of the San Mateo Mountains) was established, comprising Antipolo, Bosoboso, Cainta, and Taytay from the Province of Tondo, and Morong, Baras, Tanay, Pililla, Angono, Binangonan, and Jala-jala from the Province of La Laguna, with Morong serving as its capital. Four years later, the district was renamed Distrito Politico-Militar de Morong.

The surviving copy of the original German version is incomplete, lacking several scenes. A 106-minute reconstruction, prepared from the available sources, was released on DVD by Kino International and includes English intertitles. The disc offers an optional commentary track as an added feature. In the course of restoration, the original intertitles have been recovered.

In 2022, guitarist Steve Gunn performed his own original soundtrack for the 1926 silent film Faust. The screening was presented as part of the City Dudes blindfolded film program and took place in New York City.

Facing financial pressures in 1987, the Craven Herald & Pioneer was sold to Westminster Press, the publisher of the Bradford Telegraph and Argus. Seven years later, Westminster Press was acquired by Newsquest, bringing the Craven Herald & Pioneer under the ownership of the latter publisher.

Craven Herald & Pioneer, in 2001, broke with its longstanding practice by suspending front-page advertisements for a single edition. That issue instead featured a photograph to report the arrival of foot-and-mouth disease in Craven.

The City of Film is an international designation within the Network that recognizes film as one of its seven creative fields. The Network’s remaining six fields are Crafts and Folk Art, Design, Gastronomy, Literature, Media Arts, and Music.

Bradford was designated the first City of Film in 2009, with Sydney joining the initiative in 2010, establishing the two cities as early members of the program. Sydney hosts Fox Studios Australia, a major production facility associated with high-profile projects such as The Matrix trilogy, The Great Gatsby, and The Wolverine. In addition to its studio infrastructure, the city offers diverse landscapes, including unspoiled beaches and verdant mountains, which provide versatile settings for on-location filming.

Aotea is described in Māori tradition as a double-hulled canoe built by Toto from one half of a great tree from Hawaiki, with the remaining half used to fashion the Matahourua. Toto gave Aotea to his daughter Rongorongo, who was married to Turi. In a dispute with the chief Uenuku, Turi killed the chief's son and fled for New Zealand with 33 passengers. During the voyage they paused at Rangitahua; some identify Rangitahua as Raoul Island in the Kermadec Islands, but Tregear contends that the island cannot now be identified. At Rangitahua they encountered some of the crew from the Kurahaupō canoe.

The Aotea canoe is said to have made landfall on the west coast of the North Island, north of Kāwhia. Its people then trekked overland to the Taranaki region, where they established settlements. The canoe was left behind and gave its name to Aotea Harbour.

Betacam, launched on August 7, 1982, is an inexpensive cassette-based analog component video format designed for professional use. The format records the luminance signal on one track and stores the chrominance signal on a separate track, with chrominance represented as alternating segments of R-Y and B-Y. It utilizes a Compressed Time Division Multiplex (CTDM) scheme to multiplex the signals, and channel splitting enables higher quality recording. The system provides approximately 300 lines of horizontal luminance resolution and about 120 lines of chrominance resolution, and its image quality marked a substantial improvement over domestic Betamax and professional U-Matic.

Betacam was introduced by Sony as a professional camera family alongside a corresponding video cassette recorder/player. The initial cameras included the BVP-3, which used three Saticon tubes; the BVP-30, with three Plumbicon tubes; and the BVP-1, a single tri-stripe SMF Trinicon tube. These cameras could operate independently or be docked with the BVV-1 docking deck (later BVV-1A) to form an integrated camcorder in the BVW-1 (BVW-1A) system. Docking decks were record-only, offering transport controls limited to eject and rewind, while the docked camera’s VTR button controlled starting and pausing the tape recorder. Betacam SP docking decks later gained full transport functionality except for a record button, and tapes could not be played back except through the camera’s monochrome viewfinder. For color playback, Sony provided the VA-500 playback adapter, a separate portable unit connected by a multi-pin cable with a composite video output. Early color playback required a studio source deck, the BVW-10, which could only play back and served as a feeder deck for A/B roll edit systems, enabling edits to 1-inch Type C or 3/4" U-matic masters. A field playback option was the BVW-20, a portable, DC-powered deck with a handle used to verify color playback on location, though it did not include an internal time base corrector.

During 2012, Shutl reportedly offered Jamaican sprinter Usain Bolt a 1% stake in exchange for his endorsement. The same year, the company was honored with the DHL Online Fulfillment Initiative of the Year award, and Startups.co.uk ranked it first in its Top 100 Startups list for the year. In November 2012, Shutl also won the National Business Awards' Start-up Business of the Year award, highlighting its early impact within the industry.

Shutl received trademark protection from the United States Patent and Trademark Office in August 2011. By Christmas 2011, the service network had reached about half of online shoppers in the United Kingdom. By mid-2012, Shutl operated in more than 50 cities and towns across the United Kingdom, serving roughly 70 percent of UK shoppers.

Sign in with Apple has been positioned as an alternative to social login options offered by platforms such as Facebook. Social login features can, however, allow third-party services to access personal information associated with a user’s account.

Sign in with Apple is a privacy-conscious authentication feature that allows users to log in to apps and websites using their Apple ID. Users may opt to share the email address associated with their Apple account, or choose the "Hide My Email" option to generate a disposable relay address for the service. The disposable addresses produced by this feature end in the privaterelay.appleid.com domain.

The European Federation of Journalists (EFJ) is a pan-European federation that represents journalists through a network of national unions and associations. It advocates for the social and professional rights of journalists by mobilising its member organisations. It also promotes and defends freedom of expression and of information as guaranteed by Article 10 of the European Convention on Human Rights. In addition, the EFJ supports the development of trade unions and strives to cultivate media environments that sustain high-quality reporting, pluralism, and journalistic independence.

The European Federation of Journalists is the European regional organisation of the International Federation of Journalists (IFJ). It identifies itself as the continent's largest association of journalists and represents roughly 320,000 journalists. The federation comprises 74 member organisations across 46 countries and is headquartered in Brussels.

Ubuntu Kylin differentiates between its pro and enhanced editions and the vanilla image published on the main Ubuntu server. WPS Office, a closed-source office suite, is the default office application in the pro and enhanced editions. In contrast, the official vanilla Ubuntu Kylin image released via the Ubuntu server repository uses LibreOffice as its default office suite and does not include WPS Office by default.

In the 14.10 release of Ubuntu Kylin, two new components were introduced: the Ubuntu Kylin Software Center (UKSC) and Youker Assistant.
