The UKSC functions as a centralized software management hub for Ubuntu Kylin, providing a streamlined interface for discovering, installing, and updating applications. Youker Assistant is a utility designed to assist users with everyday computing tasks, aiming to improve usability for the operating system.

James Watt integrated theoretical science with practical application, bridging conceptual understanding and engineering practice. Humphry Davy described him as not merely a practical mechanic but also a natural philosopher and chemist. Watt’s inventions illustrate a deep command of natural philosophy and chemistry and their practical deployment. The hallmark of his genius lies in the fusion of scientific knowledge with its practical use.

In 1794, James Watt was commissioned by Thomas Beddoes to manufacture equipment for producing, purifying, and storing gases used at the Pneumatic Institution in Hotwells, Bristol. He continued to experiment with a variety of gases, exploring their potential medical applications. By 1797, however, the medical uses for these artificial gases—historically referred to as "factitious airs"—had effectively run their course, marking the end of that line of inquiry.

Nine California counties are named for saints, a total that ties with Louisiana for the most in the United States. Santa Cruz County is not included in this count, since its name translates to Holy Cross rather than a saint’s name. Merced County derives its name from Saint Mary, Our Lady of Mercy, while Los Angeles County is named for Saint Mary, Our Lady Queen of the Angels. Ventura County’s name is a shortened form of Saint Bonaventure, the namesake of the mission.

The state of California is subdivided into 58 counties. At the time of statehood, 27 counties were formed on February 18, 1850. By 1860, a further 16 counties were created through subdivision of existing ones, and between 1861 and 1893, 14 additional counties were established. Imperial County, created in 1907, is the most recently formed county. In terms of geography and population, San Bernardino County is the largest county by land area in the contiguous United States, while Los Angeles County is the most populous county in the United States.

Carlos P. Romulo became a professor of English at the University of the Philippines in 1923, while simultaneously serving as secretary to Manuel Quezon, who was then the president of the Senate of the Philippines.

Carlos Peña Romulo Sr. (January 14, 1899 – December 15, 1985) was a Filipino diplomat, statesman, soldier, journalist, and author who played a prominent role in both national and international affairs. He was among the founders of the Boy Scouts of the Philippines and achieved the rank of general in both the United States Army and the Philippine Army. Romulo also served as president of a university and held the notable position of President of the United Nations General Assembly.

During the 2024–25 UEFA Europa League qualifying rounds, the standard match day is Thursday, reflecting the competition’s typical Thursday scheduling. However, a subset of fixtures may be played on Tuesdays or Wednesdays to accommodate scheduling conflicts, ensuring the qualifying program fits within the broader calendar.

The 2024–25 UEFA Europa League qualifying phase features a list of participating clubs, each shown with its 2024 UEFA club coefficient. While these coefficients are provided for reference, they were not used to seed the Champions Path. Clubs are arranged according to the starting rounds at which they enter the qualifying competition, reflecting the different entry points of the participating teams.

Self-aligning torque is the rotational moment that tends to realign a tire with the actual direction of travel, and it can persist even when both slip angle and camber are zero on a flat surface. This torque arises from inherent asymmetries in tire construction and from the uneven shape and pressure distribution within the contact patch, which together produce a lateral restoring moment independent of slip angle. In typical production tires, the self-aligning torque reaches a maximum at approximately 2 to 4 degrees of slip angle, with the exact value influenced by a range of variables including tire design, loading, inflation, and operating conditions. As the tire approaches its peak lateral grip, the self-aligning torque diminishes and eventually falls to zero at the limit of lateral force capability.

Self-aligning torque (SAT) is the turning moment generated by a rolling tire, also referred to as aligning torque or aligning moment (Mz, the moment about the vertical axis). It acts to rotate the tire about the vehicle’s vertical axis, thereby producing a steering effect. When the tire exhibits a nonzero slip angle, SAT tends to rotate the wheel toward the direction of travel, contributing to the steering response of the tire.

During November 2020, Min Aung Hlaing publicly questioned the legitimacy of the forthcoming general elections, a stance that raised concerns about potential breaches of the Civil Services Personnel Law. On 5 November 2020, the Tatmadaw announced that his rank would be treated as equivalent to Vice President of Myanmar. After voting in the election, he pledged to accept the results. The 2020 ballot produced a larger landslide for the National League for Democracy than in 2015, constraining his political ambitions. In response, the military intensified its accusations of electoral fraud and irregularities, submitting formal complaints to the Union Election Commission.

On 27 March 2025, during the 80th anniversary of Myanmar Armed Forces Day, spokesperson Min Aung Hlaing announced that a general election would be held by the end of the year and that the military would transfer power to the winning party in a structured and lawful manner.

In New South Wales, a court may grant an apprehended violence order (AVO) to protect a person who fears violence, harassment, abuse, or stalking. The order prohibits the respondent from assaulting, harassing, threatening, stalking, or intimidating the applicant and may include additional conditions, such as prohibiting contact or attempts to locate the applicant online. A court may issue an AVO if it finds that the applicant has reasonable grounds for their fears, or in some circumstances if the applicant has no reasonable grounds for fear. Non-compliance with an AVO may attract penalties ranging from fines to imprisonment, and, for non-citizens, may also result in deportation.

An injunction is an equitable remedy that takes the form of a formal court order, capable of compelling a party to perform a specified act or to desist from particular conduct. Developed by the English courts of equity, injunctive relief serves to prevent harm or injustice in situations where monetary damages would be insufficient. Its origins trace back to Roman law, where the equitable remedy of the interdict provided a predecessor for modern injunctions and influenced the evolution of this essential tool in common law.

In January 1942, Erich Hoepner sought permission from Hans Kluge, commander of Army Group Centre, to withdraw his overstretched forces. Kluge indicated that he would discuss the matter with Adolf Hitler and ordered Hoepner to prepare for withdrawal. Believing permission would be granted, Hoepner ordered the withdrawal to begin on 8 January 1942. Kluge, fearing Hitler's reaction, immediately reported Hoepner, which provoked Hitler’s fury. Hoepner was dismissed from the Wehrmacht on the same day. Hitler then decreed that Hoepner be deprived of his pension and barred from wearing his uniform and medals, a move that contravened the law and Wehrmacht regulations. Hoepner filed a lawsuit against the Reich to reclaim his pension. Judges at the time could not be dismissed, even by Hitler, and Hoepner ultimately won the pension suit.

Erich Hoepner, a senior German commander, ordered an investigation into the Le Paradis massacre in which the SS Division Totenkopf killed nearly 100 British prisoners, and he demanded Theodor Eicke’s dismissal if evidence showed prisoner mistreatment or killing by SS forces. Eicke subsequently told Himmler that the British had used dum-dum bullets against his troops. No disciplinary action was taken against Eicke or the Totenkopf, and the affair was effectively forgotten in official circles. Hoepner maintained a personal and professional dislike of Eicke, repeatedly referring to him as a butcher, and he held a generally low opinion of the Waffen-SS.

During the 2023–24 Welsh Cup, the second round featured thirty-six victors from the first round, alongside sixteen Tier 2 clubs that had been granted byes to this stage, and twelve clubs from the Cymru Premier entering at the same round. The draw for the second round was conducted on 20 September 2023.

Connah's Quay Nomads won the 2023–24 Welsh Cup, defeating The New Saints 2–1 in the final on 28 April 2024 to claim the club's second Welsh Cup title. Because the Nomads had already qualified for European competition through their league position, the cup winner's berth in the UEFA Conference League was reallocated, with the spot awarded to the third-placed team in the 2023–24 Cymru Premier.

A sefer Torah, or Torah scroll, is a hand-copied copy of the formal Hebrew biblical text written on parchment, traditionally called gevil or klaf, with a quill dipped in ink. Entirely in Hebrew, it contains 304,805 letters. Each letter must be reproduced exactly as in the standard text by a trained scribe, or sofer, and the work can take roughly eighteen months to complete. In most modern Sifrei Torah, the text is arranged in 42 lines per column, though Yemenite Jewish communities commonly use 50 lines per column. There are strict rules governing the position and appearance of the letters, with authoritative guidance often cited from halakhic works such as the Mishnah Berurah. A variety of Hebrew scripts may be employed, most of which are ornate and exacting in character.

The Torah serves as the central religious text of Judaism, outlining core commandments including those governing Shabbat. Shabbat violations have historically been associated with severe penalties, including capital punishment in certain legal contexts, underscoring the seriousness attached to the day. Given the gravity of Shabbat observance, one would expect explicit and unambiguous guidance on how to uphold the day. In practice, much of the practical information about Shabbat rules, prohibitions, and traditions does not originate directly in the Written Torah but is developed in the Talmud and other works that derive from Jewish oral law.

Cusco is the seventh-most populous city in Peru, with a 2017 population of 428,450, and it stands as the largest city in the Peruvian Andes. The city sits at an elevation of approximately 3,400 meters (11,200 feet) above sea level. It lies within the Cusco Region, which contains a metropolitan area that ranks as the seventh-most populous in Peru. The largest district within the city is Cusco District, which recorded a 2017 population of 114,630, roughly one-quarter of Cusco’s total population.

In Inca tradition, the Sapa Inca Pachacuti is credited with rebuilding Cusco and transforming the Kingdom of Cusco into the expansive empire known as Tawantinsuyu. However, archaeological evidence indicates that the city’s development prior to Pachacuti proceeded more slowly and organically. The urban design reflects a deliberate plan in which two rivers were channeled around the city’s core, a feature that underscores the built environment’s formal organization. Archaeologists have also suggested that this city plan was replicated at other sites, pointing to a broader pattern of regional planning and administrative strategy.

Lakatoi, also known as Lagatoi, are multi-hulled sailing vessels originating from Papua New Guinea. The name Lakatoi (Lagatoi) derives from the Motu language. Historically, these vessels were employed in the Hiri trade cycle.

The Lakatoi is a traditional Melanesian sailing vessel whose name literally means "three dugouts." It is constructed by fastening two or more dugout logs together to provide stability and increase cargo capacity. The individual dugouts are linked by booms, forming a framework that supports a platform on top. The sails are of the crab-claw type, a distinctive rig associated with these vessels. In his 2008 study, Horridge analyzes the rigging and explains how the craft is maneuvered.

Top 40 is a radio format that played a key role in the spread of rock and roll, with Storz credited by some sources as having helped popularize the genre. By the mid-1950s, his station and other Top 40 outlets were playing records by Elvis Presley, Jerry Lee Lewis, Bill Haley, Chuck Berry, and Fats Domino.

Todd Storz, a radio executive associated with KOWH in Omaha, Nebraska, has been described by producer Richard Fatherley as the inventor of the Top 40 radio format. He devised the concept in the early 1950s by analyzing how often songs were played on jukeboxes and translating that ordering into a weekly on-air chart. The Top 40 format proved commercially successful, and together with his father, Robert Storz, he expanded its reach by acquiring additional stations through the Storz Broadcasting Company to adopt the format. In recognition of his influence on broadcasting, Todd Storz was inducted into the Nebraska Broadcasters Association Hall of Fame in 1989.

Oakridge, a district of Vancouver, was among the last parts of the city to retain its natural state, with much of its landscape remaining undeveloped until the interwar period. In 1926, a golf course was established near West 49th Avenue and Cambie Street, marking an early addition of recreational facilities to the area. In the years leading up to World War II, the neighborhood also saw institutional construction, including the erection of hospitals and boarding schools, reflecting a shift toward a more built environment prior to the war.

Oakridge is a rectangular district of Vancouver bounded to the west by Granville Street and to the east by Main Street. Its northern boundary runs along West 41st Avenue, while West 57th Avenue marks the southern edge. Oak Street and Cambie Street run north–south through the area. These streets are among Vancouver’s busiest arteries, contributing to substantial traffic during both morning and evening rush hours. The district covers 401 hectares (approximately 4.01 square kilometers).

In 2006, Malaysia Airlines relocated its corporate headquarters from a Kuala Lumpur building to the Subang site that had formerly housed the airline's headquarters, thereby making Subang the location of its new head office. The Subang building, situated in Subang, subsequently served as the airline's primary office. Channel News Asia reported that the airline had been compelled to sell the Subang headquarters.

On Malaysia Airlines' Airbus A380s, infants are not allowed in First Class due to the absence of baby bassinets in the cabin. The policy was explained by then-chief executive Tengku Azmil Zahruddin, who cited feedback from First Class passengers that they pay for the premium cabin and are unable to sleep because of crying infants.

Apple’s early product aesthetics featured bright, translucent finishes, beginning with the iMac’s initial hue Bondi Blue—a vivid candy-tone named after the water at Bondi Beach in Sydney. In January 1999, Bondi Blue was replaced by a five-color set inspired by fruit: Blueberry, Grape, Tangerine, Lime, and Strawberry. Tangerine and Blueberry were adopted as the initial colors for the iBook line. Blueberry was also applied to the Blue and White Power Mac G3 and its displays. The use of these playful, see-through colors is credited with helping spur a broader trend toward brightly colored translucent enclosures in consumer electronics and other products, including clock radios and hamburger grillers.

Apple Inc.'s design motif, first introduced in 1997 with the eMate and carried into 1998 on the Power Macintosh G3 All-In-One and the original iMac, marked a shift toward translucent casings and soft, bulbous forms. The approach was subsequently applied to the first iBook models in 1999 and to the blue-and-white Power Mac G3 and Studio Displays. Key features include translucent surfaces rendered in candy-like or milky-white hues and gently bulging contours, with subdued vertical pinstripes visible through the translucent panels. A lenticular plaque on the back panel displays ports and regulatory marks and features a distinctive wavy three-dimensional pattern. The aesthetic is further expressed by translucent power cords whose twisted conductors can be seen inside.

During the Texan rebellion, the Alamo briefly functioned as a fortress for Texian forces in December 1836 and again in January 1839. The Mexican army later regained control in March 1841 and September 1842 amid its occupation of San Antonio de Bexar. According to historians Roberts and Olson, both sides carved their names into the walls, excavated musket rounds from the interior storage holds, and damaged stone decorations. Debris from the Alamo was sold to tourists; in 1840 the San Antonio town council allowed residents to haul stone from the site for five dollars per wagonload. By the late 1840s the four statues on the front wall of the chapel had been removed.

In 1883 the Catholic Church sold the chapel to the State of Texas for $20,000. The state hired Tom Rife to manage the building, and he offered tours but did not pursue restoration, a policy that drew criticism from preservation-minded observers. For decades, soldiers and members of the local Masonic lodge used the building for meetings, and graffiti was inscribed on walls and statues. In May 1887, a devout Catholic angered by Masonic emblems on a Saint Teresa statue was arrested after breaking in and smashing the statues with a sledgehammer.

Standards New Zealand is an ISO member organization that develops New Zealand standards (NZS) aligned with international norms. It participates in standards-related activities designed to yield benefits for the country. In partnership with Standards Australia, it co-produces joint standards designated AS/NZS, and the majority of New Zealand standards are developed through this collaboration.

Standards New Zealand is the national standards body of New Zealand, and it is known in Māori as Te Mana Tautikanga o Aotearoa. It operates as a business unit within the Ministry of Business, Innovation and Employment (MBIE) and is supervised by the New Zealand Standards Executive, an independent statutory office held by a ministry employee under the Standards and Accreditation Act 2015. Previously, Standards New Zealand operated as a Crown entity and served as the operating arm of the Standards Council of New Zealand. Following the enactment of the 2015 act, the council’s responsibilities were assumed by the New Zealand Standards Approval Board. Standards New Zealand moved to MBIE on 1 March 2016.

Manuel I Komnenos succeeded John II in 1143 and sought to restore imperial power across the eastern empire, though his aims were tempered by inherited political arrangements and his own ambitions. He prioritized campaigns in Italy, Egypt, and the Balkans while not neglecting Anatolia, maintaining fortified frontiers and conducting only limited raids into the Sultanate of Rum. By 1162, a truce with Kilij Arslan II allowed Manuel to redirect his attention elsewhere, but the agreement aided Arslan in consolidating power and eradicating rivals, after which he grew more belligerent and less willing to honor it. When Manuel moved to seize Iconium, his expedition suffered from poor scouting and predictable routes, culminating in the ambush and rout at Myriokephalon, a defeat reminiscent of Manzikert. Manuel subsequently rallied his forces and Arslan sought peace in the aftermath. In the end, the Byzantine gains in Anatolia were maintained, though no additional territory was acquired.

Following the First Crusade, the Byzantine Empire recovered the westernmost portions of Anatolia, while the central plateau remained under the sovereignty of the Sultanate of Rum. The emergence of Crusader States introduced a new threat to Byzantine power in the region. In 1108, Emperor Alexios I defeated Bohemond, who returned to Italy; Antioch, however, remained outside Byzantine hands. Nevertheless, Byzantium gained a foothold in western Anatolia, allowing renewed efforts to reassert control over the rest of the peninsula.

Gross income, a tax term, denotes total income before deductions. In some cases, a portion of Social Security benefits is exempt from taxation, and the amount that can be excluded has varied from year to year. The exemption is gradually reduced as gross income exceeds certain thresholds, such that higher-income individuals may have a larger share of their benefits subject to tax. This phased-out approach reflects an effort to adjust the tax treatment of Social Security benefits according to overall income levels.

Under the Internal Revenue Code, gross income is defined as all income from any source whatsoever and is not restricted to cash amounts unless the law provides an exception. Federal tax regulations interpret this general principle and guide its application. The amount recognized as income is typically the fair market value of what is received or the value to which the taxpayer has a right to receive. Additionally, certain categories of income are expressly excluded from gross income for tax purposes.

The City Nature Challenge (CNC) originated in 2016 through the collaboration of Lila Higgins and Alison Young. In its first edition, participants across the Los Angeles area and the San Francisco Bay Area documented more than 20,000 observations using the iNaturalist platform. In 2017 the event expanded to 16 U.S. cities, with over 125,000 observations collected within five days. The following year marked a global expansion, reaching 68 cities in 19 countries, and although some cities used platforms other than iNaturalist, the four-day event gathered more than 440,000 observations from over 17,000 participants. The 2019 edition saw approximately 35,000 participants in 159 cities, contributing 964,000 observations of over 31,000 species. The 2020 CNC coincided with the COVID-19 pandemic, which reduced overall observation counts; the challenge shifted from a competitive to a more collaborative framework, while still attracting more cities and participants and resulting in the documentation of more species than in previous years.

iNaturalist is a mobile application that enables users to create nature observations and contribute them to an online dataset. The app also allows users to explore observations nearby and around the world, and to learn about different species.

Magic Radio is a UK-based digital radio service owned and operated by Bauer Media Audio UK. It broadcasts on 105.4 FM in London and on 106.5 FM in Bristol, and is available nationwide on DAB digital radio, via Bauer's Rayo platform, and on compatible smart speakers. The station's format is adult contemporary, with a playlist that includes artists such as Elton John, Madonna, Ed Sheeran, Whitney Houston, UB40, and Simply Red.

On 8 May 2025, the Magic Soul brand announced a branding update for Magic (UK radio station), retiring its existing strapline and introducing a new one. The former tagline claimed to deliver the best of soul and Motown, while the updated strapline emphasizes a wider variety of soul and Motown music.

Aleksei Brusilov, a prominent Russian military figure, noted that some of his former soldiers later served in the Red Army. He argued that radical reform was necessary in the face of the era's upheavals, and he saw cooperation with the Soviet state as a means to preserve the territorial integrity of the former Russian Empire in service of the Russian nation. Privately, he believed the communist system would be transient and ultimately be replaced by a Russian nation-state. He also criticized exiled White émigrés and the White movement for prioritizing class interests over those of the Russian nation. These positions reflect a pragmatic, nationalist stance during the transition from empire to post-revolutionary state.

Aleksei Brusilov began his military education at the Cavalry Officer School in Saint Petersburg in 1881, and two years later was appointed riding instructor at the same institution. Over a thirteen-year period he served in a variety of roles within the school, including Adjutant, Senior Teacher of Riding and Breaking Horses, Section Commander, Troop Commander, Squadron Commander, and Assistant Chief of the School. In 1900 he was promoted to Major General and transferred to the Household Troops, a unit whose officers were retained for the tsar’s official duties. He married in 1884, and their son was born in 1887.

At the 2008 Australian Open, part of the tournament’s wheelchair tennis events, Esther Vergeer defeated fellow Dutch player Korie Homan in the final of the women’s wheelchair singles, winning in straight sets, 6–3, 6–3. Vergeer, the two-time defending champion, secured her third consecutive Australian Open singles title, underscoring her prolonged dominance in women’s wheelchair tennis.

Dance in Zimbabwe represents a spectrum of traditional practices that continually adapt to changing times, with ongoing innovation arising largely from within the Zimbabwean community rather than from external cultural pressures. Although the aims of dances may shift over time, their core meanings and significance are regarded as enduring. Traditionally, dances are performed for important individuals or events—such as the arrivals of government officials at airports—and they are not typically choreographed for the concert stage. Some rituals, including those involving spirit possession, can extend for many hours or even days, and the precise timing of entering and re-entering the spirit world is considered essential, making such performances difficult to reproduce in formal settings. Consequently, these dances are preferably carried out in natural surroundings. Neo-traditional dances have emerged, altering contexts and being described as traditional-like but not wholly traditional; they can employ the same movements and hold comparable importance while reflecting changed social circumstances. These forms preserve historical memory and chronicle time-based changes in the culture, with shifts in dance reflecting politics, weather, urbanization, and outside influences, and through these evolutions, dances forge a strong emotional connection to contemporary life and everyday struggles.

Dance in Zimbabwe is historically centered on three principal instruments: the drums, known as ngomas, the mbira, and the marimba. The acoustic character of drums depends on factors such as size, shape, membrane tension, and materials, producing variation in tone and pitch, in a manner comparable to how the dimensions of marimba wood strips shape its tonal output. The mbira occupies a central place in the musical repertoire and is plucked with the fingers to produce melodic lines. In many religious ceremonies, spirit mediums use the mbira as a conduit to communicate with ancestral spirits, underscoring its ceremonial significance. The mbira, along with the mbira dance, has deep historical roots, and archaeological evidence indicates mbira-like instruments dating to the twelfth century.

Astrochemistry is an interdisciplinary field that arises from the intersection of astronomy and chemistry, with its development rooted in the shared history of those disciplines. Advances in observational and experimental spectroscopy have enabled the detection of an expanding repertoire of molecules in the solar system and in the interstellar medium. The ongoing discovery of new chemical species through spectroscopy and related technologies broadens the chemical space available for astrochemical inquiry.

Astrochemistry employs infrared astronomy to infer the chemical and mineralogical composition of solid materials within the interstellar medium. Observations focus on constituents such as silicate minerals, carbon-rich solids resembling kerogen, and icy mantles associated with grains. Infrared radiation can traverse the microscopic dust particles that populate interstellar space, yet distinctive absorptions appear at specific wavelengths that reflect the grain composition and provide diagnostic signatures. Nevertheless, there are limitations analogous to those in radio astronomy; for example, nitrogen gas (N2) is challenging to detect using either infrared or radio techniques.

The golden ratio has been studied only intermittently for roughly a thousand years. During the medieval period, Abu Kamil (c. 850–930) employed the ratio in geometric calculations for constructions involving pentagons and decagons. His writings influenced later European scholars, notably Leonardo of Pisa, known as Fibonacci (c. 1170–1250). Fibonacci applied the ratio to related geometry problems, yet he did not recognize the later-established link between the golden ratio and the Fibonacci numbers.

The golden ratio, noted for its simple proportional relationship and distinctive mathematical properties, has long captivated mathematicians. Throughout history, it has been associated with a number of prominent figures, including Pythagoras, Euclid, Fibonacci (Leonardo of Pisa), Kepler, and Roger Penrose. Its influence extends beyond mathematics, shaping thought across biology, art, music, history, architecture, psychology, and mysticism. Due to its ubiquity and enduring appeal, the golden ratio is often regarded as one of the most influential numbers in the history of mathematics.

Following the death of Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, in April 2021, political parties temporarily halted campaigning for the local and devolved elections held that year. The pause covered both local government contests and elections to devolved legislatures, and the mourning period endured for several days, during which political campaigning and related activities were suspended.

During the 2021 United Kingdom local elections, all four police and crime commissioner positions in Wales were contested, corresponding to the four police force areas of Dyfed-Powys, Gwent, North Wales, and South Wales.

Real estate development in China began to take shape in the late 1970s, with several early milestones. In October 1979, Guangzhou approved the first commercial housing project, the Donghu New Village, for construction. In January 1980, the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone signed the country’s first cooperative housing construction contract, signaling a new model for housing development. In the same month, the Shenzhen Special Economic Zone Real Estate Company was established as the first real estate enterprise on the mainland, marking the formal emergence of a dedicated real estate industry. Collectively, these events signaled the initial steps toward a modern housing market and the growth of real estate enterprises in China.

Following a period of rapid growth in housing demand, the Chinese real estate market experienced a price bubble, whose expansion ended in late 2011 as property prices fell. In response to complaints that affordability for the middle class in large cities had deteriorated, policymakers implemented measures to stabilize the market and address housing costs. The deflation of the property bubble has been identified as one of the primary causes of slower economic growth in 2012.

Glacial landforms arise from both the ice itself and the features sculpted in the surrounding terrain. Glaciers stand out as dramatic elements of the landscape, and they are especially prominent in Earth’s polar regions. Beyond the ice bodies, the landscape bears a range of landforms created by glaciation, reflecting the processes of erosion, transport, and deposition driven by ancient and current glacial activity.

Glacial landforms traditionally associated with ice erosion include roches moutonnées, yet some interpretations argue that these features may not be exclusively glacial in origin, with much of their form potentially established before glaciation. In this view, the jointing and fracturing of bedrock that contribute to their characteristic shape typically predate glacial activity, reducing the necessity of ice sculpting as the sole formative process. Roche moutonnée–like forms are also observed in tropical regions, including East Africa and Australia, indicating that similar landforms can arise under nonpolar conditions. A published example from Ivö Lake in Sweden shows how kaolin mining exposed rocks that weathered to resemble roche moutonnée, illustrating how weathering of preexisting relief can mimic glacially sculpted forms.

LCCN, an identifier used in library catalogs, has been in use since 1898. The acronym originally stood for Library of Congress Card Number, and over time it has been referred to as the Library of Congress Catalog Card Number among other names. The Library of Congress prepared bibliographic cards for its catalog and sold duplicate sets to other libraries, a practice described as centralized cataloging. Each of these card sets was assigned a unique serial number to identify it.

Although bibliographic information is largely created, stored, and exchanged electronically among libraries, there remains a need to identify each individual bibliographic record. The Library of Congress Control Number (LCCN) continues to serve as the distinctive identifier for unique bibliographic records, maintaining a stable reference across cataloging and library systems.

During March 1943, Kampfgeschwader 100 relocated to Salon in southern France, where it was re-equipped with the Lotfernrohr 7D bombsight on 2 April. The I./KG 100 based itself at Stalino from 24 April. On 13 May the unit resumed mining and anti-shipping operations over the lower Volga. On 1 June 1943 it was moved to Seshchinskaya to begin bombing the Molotov tank factory in the Gorki region, and from 1 to 7 June operations continued, with a raid on 7 June targeting oil refineries and ball bearing factories in Saratov, after which the group returned to Stalino for long-range bombing over the Caspian Sea from 7 to 20 June. In a large coordinated attack on 4–5 June, 128 He 111s and Ju 88s from III./KG 1, KG 3, II./KG 4, III./KG 4, KG 27, I./KG 100, II./KG 55 and III./KG 55 dropped 179 tons on the No. 1 Molotov plant; wooden workshops burned, the water supply was severed, blacksmiths, chassis, the main conveyor and spring workshops were destroyed, and living compounds and a nursery were hit, causing a disastrous impact on Soviet capabilities. German losses in the raid were five bombers shot down. On 8 June, Soviet 1st, 2nd, and 15th Air Armies attacked German airfields; JG 51 intercepted and claimed 40 Soviet aircraft destroyed for one loss.

III. Gruppe of Kampfgeschwader 100 was formed on 20 September 1942 from Aufklärungsgruppe (See) 126. Commanded by Hans Schulz, the unit was based at Athens-Kalamaki and later Athens-Eleusis, and it was subordinated to Fliegerkorps X. It operated the He 111, Arado Ar 96, and BV 138, and initially undertook convoy escort duties in the Aegean Sea. From late November 1942 to February 1943, it conducted operations from Catania, Sicily, attacking ports along the Tunisian and Algerian coastlines. A small detachment was dispatched to Yugoslavia to participate in Case White. On 10 February 1943 it received orders to revert to its original identity, an instruction that was carried out ten days later.

In April 2012, Integrated Device Technology announced its plan to acquire PLX Technology. The proposed transaction was terminated in December 2012 after the Federal Trade Commission challenged the merger.

In January 2009, PLX Technology completed the acquisition of Oxford Semiconductor. The transaction was structured with consideration comprising 5.6 million shares of PLX common stock, together with an additional promissory note valued at $14.2 million.
British V-class submarines were built by Vickers at Barrow during World War I, developed in response to the S class built by Scotts at Greenock and the W class produced by Armstrong Whitworth.

KPop Demon Hunters is a production in which casting for voice actors and singing voices occurred in separate phases, with the singers being selected earlier than the actors. Ejae joined the project as a songwriter and later provided Rumi’s singing voice, a credit tied to the directors’ familiarity with her vocal demos. Arden Cho, the voice of Rumi, initially auditioned for the character Celine and switched to Rumi after encouragement from co-director Maggie Kang. Park Jin-young was originally considered for Gwi-Ma, a role conceived as flamboyant and comedic, but as the concept evolved into a more menacing antagonist, Lee Byung-hun was cast in the part. Ji-young Yoo was revealed in April 2025 as the performer for Zoey, with the remainder of the cast announced later in the same month.

KPop Demon Hunters is a documentary that analyzes the growth of K-pop fandom and its cultural implications. BBC News reported that the film’s release coincided with the emergence of K-pop–themed dance classes in Belfast, and noted that its success has heightened the visibility of K-pop more broadly. The New York Times’ Alex Vadukul described a fervent fan culture forming around the groups Huntrix and the Saja Boys, and May Hong remarked on the experience of being the recipient of such devoted attention as overwhelming. In The Atlantic, Yvonne Kim argues that the film reframes fandom from a pastime into a creative practice, while also examining the parasitic dynamic between artist and listener and the dominant influence exercised by performers; the piece portrays the film’s fans as ordinary, everyday people who dedicate themselves to K-pop.

Drury Inlet is a coastal inlet in the Queen Charlotte Strait region of the Central Coast of British Columbia, Canada. It extends westward from Wells Passage and lies to the northwest of North Broughton Island. The inlet is also positioned northwest of the town of Port Hardy. Actaeon Sound branches off to the northeast from the northern side of the head of Drury Inlet.

Within the Drury Inlet region, Sutherland Bay lies at the head of the inlet, to the west of the Actress Passage, at 50°55′30″N, 127°10′59″W. The Muirhead Islands lie east of Sutherland Bay and south of Dove Island and the Actress Passage, occupying the western reaches of Drury Inlet, at 50°55′16″N, 127°08′14″W.
In January 2008, Engine Yard secured a $3.5 million investment from Benchmark Capital. Some industry commentators interpreted the funding as supporting the Ruby on Rails framework.

Engine Yard is a privately held platform-as-a-service (PaaS) company headquartered in San Francisco, California. The firm focuses on deployment and ongoing management for applications built with Ruby on Rails, PHP, and Node.js.

MPEG Multichannel, also known as MPEG-2 Backwards Compatible (MPEG-2 BC), is an extension to MPEG-1 Layer II audio compression defined within the MPEG-2 Audio standard (ISO/IEC 13818-3). It enables surround configurations of up to 5.1 channels. To preserve compatibility with existing two-channel stereo systems, it employs a channel-matrixing technique that blends the additional channels into the two primary channels. The bitstream includes extra information that is ignored by older hardware, providing the signals needed to derive the additional channels from the matrix in compliant decoders.

MPEG Multichannel provides for a conformity marking system in which devices that meet the standard bear a logo indicating compatibility. The marks associated with this system include the MPEG Multichannel logo and the MPEG Empowered logo. These indicators may appear on product packaging and in accompanying documentation to inform users of compliance with the standard.

In 2019, Skype introduced a background blur feature for video chats, developed entirely in software using artificial intelligence algorithms and without the need for depth-sensing hardware. The technology enables blurred backgrounds even when using standard webcams that lack depth-sensing capabilities.

Skype maintained compatibility with Sony’s handheld consoles, with functionality depending on the model. The PSP Slim and Lite required a specially designed microphone peripheral to access Skype, whereas the PSP-3000 includes a built-in microphone, enabling Skype communication without any external accessory. The PSP Go additionally supports Skype via Bluetooth alongside its built-in microphone. On the PlayStation Vita, Skype could be downloaded from the PlayStation Network in the United States, and the app could receive incoming calls while running in the background. Support for Skype on the PSP and PlayStation Vita was discontinued on June 22, 2016.

Meghan Trainor rose to prominence in 2014, with Rolling Stone naming her one of the year's most unlikely pop stars. After the release of All About That Bass, Billboard's Andrew Hampp described her as a model of self-acceptance for children worldwide. The Guardian described her as a leading example of body positivity and a prominent symbol of self-acceptance within pop music. She was subsequently included in Billboard's feature on musicians delivering body-positive messages, and MTV Australia noted that she has consistently stood by her beliefs and championed body positivity for women at large. In March 2015 she collaborated with FullBeauty Brands as a consultant to develop clothing lines for women across a range of body types. Billboard's Jada Yuan characterized her public image as defined by her curves, while acknowledging she does not fit the extremes of either exceedingly curvy celebrities or ultra-thin models. Her approach to social media has been described as upbeat and playful, with little emphasis on personal revelations or moralizing.

In 2013, Meghan Trainor traveled to Nashville, New York City, and Los Angeles to write and help produce country and pop songs, while also contributing lead and background vocals on demos for other artists, with some of her vocal takes ultimately appearing on final recordings. She co-wrote the song "In the Sun," which Danish artist Aya Katrine released as a single in May 2013. In June of that year, she met producer Kevin Kadish in Nashville through Wallace and a mutual friend, and the pair discovered a shared interest in retro-style music, beginning a productive collaborative relationship. Frustrated by the lengthy commutes from Nantucket to Los Angeles for songwriting and facing parental concerns about the cost of relocation, Trainor moved to Nashville in November 2013. While based there, she wrote songs for artists including Hunter Hayes, Rascal Flatts, R5, and Sabrina Carpenter, laying groundwork for her subsequent breakthrough in the music industry.

Garth Jennings directed the coming-of-age drama Son of Rambow, which follows two schoolboys as they make an amateur film inspired by First Blood. Set during a summer at the dawn of Thatcher's Britain, the film premiered on 22 January 2007 at the Sundance Film Festival and subsequently screened at festivals in Newport Beach, Seattle, Toronto, and Glasgow, as well as at the 51st BFI London Film Festival. It was released in the United Kingdom on 4 April 2008, with a limited release in the United States on 2 May 2008.

Garth Jennings directed the 2005 science fiction comedy film The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, an adaptation of the Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy franchise created by Douglas Adams. The film's principal cast comprises Martin Freeman, Sam Rockwell, Mos Def, and Zooey Deschanel, while voice performances are provided by Stephen Fry, Helen Mirren, and Alan Rickman.

Rhythm refers to the organization of musical time in which unaccented beats are grouped in relation to a primary accented beat. A rhythmic group is perceived when its individual elements can be distinguished from one another, enabling the listener to recognize the pattern. In its simplest form, rhythm expresses the relationship between a single strong beat and one or two weaker, unaccented beats that follow, though more complex patterns may involve additional subdivisions.

Rhythm refers to a pattern defined by a median duration of several seconds or more, a timescale that enables the establishment of a discrete rhythmic unit. It arises from the arrangement of accented, unaccented, and silent pulses within the cells of a measure. From this organization, the briefest intelligible and self-contained musical idea may emerge: a motif or figure. Through processes of repetition and variation, the motif can be developed into a definite phrase. A phrase may characterize an entire genre of music, dance, or poetry and is often regarded as the fundamental formal unit of music.

In 2023, Balbir Singh, a graduate of Langara College, faced deportation. He was among roughly 150 students affected by the case. The deportation was tied to an entry into Canada that began with a fraudulent college acceptance letter.

Langara College is a public degree-granting college located in Vancouver, British Columbia, Canada. The institution traces its origins to 1965 when it operated as part of Vancouver City College, and it opened its West 49th Avenue campus in 1970. It subsequently gained status as an independent public college under the Provincial College and Institute Act on April 1, 1994. The college is also known by the Musqueam First Nation name snəw̓eyəɬ leləm̓, which means house of teachings.

Atlahua refers to a figure depicted in the Florentine Codex, Fray Bernardino de Sahagún’s General History of the Things of New Spain. The original image illustrating Atlahua appears in Book II, The Ceremonies, of this codex.

Atlahua is a water deity in Aztec mythology, regarded as the blue aspect of Tlaloc, the southern manifestation of the rain god, and is also described as a fisherman and an archer. There were at least four ancient Aztec temples dedicated to Atlahua, the tallest of which is said to have risen over 200 feet (61 meters) in height. The Aztecs prayed to Atlahua in cases of deaths that occurred in water, and the deity is associated with events surrounding the Spanish conquest of Tenochtitlan by Hernán Cortés, during which the lake around the city was described as being filled with heads and corpses.

In 607, Emperor Yang of Sui visited Ashina Rangan, where a Goguryeo envoy representing King Yeong-yang was introduced to him. He instructed Yeong-yang to come to the imperial presence, promising a reward for compliance and punishment for nonattendance; Yeong-yang offered no reply. By 611, angered by this silence, the emperor prepared a campaign against Goguryeo. The Sui state appeared strong, and officials and much of the populace supported an expedition to subjugate Goguryeo. In the spring of 611, Yang traveled to Zhuo Commandery to announce the Goguryeo campaign. Several hundred men were conscripted, but disease and fatigue inflicted substantial losses before the force could reach Zhuo Commandery. Consequently, some conscripts deserted and joined agrarian rebels.

Following the death of Ashina Rangan, his son Shibi Khan Ashina Duojishi succeeded him as ruler of the Tujue. In accordance with Tujue custom, Ashina Duojishi sought permission from Emperor Yang of Sui to marry Ashina Rangan's widow, Princess Yicheng, who was the daughter of a clansman of Emperor Yang. Emperor Yang granted the marriage request. In 609, however, Emperor Yang, envious of Xue Daoheng's literary talent, falsely accused him of defaming the emperor and had him strangled.

The Football Association of Serbia, known in Serbian as Фудбалски савез Србије (ФСС) and in Latin script as Fudbalski savez Srbije (FSS), is the governing body of football in Serbia. Based in Belgrade, it administers the national football leagues, including the Serbian Superliga, oversees the Serbia national football team, and governs the country's second-tier leagues.

The Football Association of Serbia (FSS) traces its roots to the Football Association of Yugoslavia, which was founded in Zagreb on 13 April 1919, and operated as part of that body. In 2003, it was incorporated into the Football Association of Serbia and Montenegro as the political state union persisted. Following Montenegro and Serbia’s dissolution into separate states, the Football Association of Serbia was established in 2006 as the national governing body for football. Javier Clemente was appointed as the first coach of the Serbia national football team, and the current head coach is Dragan Stojković.

Although voters often understand how plurality voting operates, this familiarity does not necessarily translate into awareness of its consequences for electoral outcomes. Many citizens may be unaware of the issues and implications inherent in the system, including how it can influence strategic considerations and systemic incentives. As a result, some voters cast ballots sincerely even when voting theory suggests they should vote tactically to maximize their preferred result. Theoretical analyses of plurality voting sometimes prescribe tactical voting as a means to improve outcomes under certain conditions. Consequently, voters may end up voting contrary to their own rational interests.

Plurality ballots are commonly divided into two main forms: blank ballots and structured ballots. On a blank ballot, voters write the names of candidates by hand. In contrast, a structured ballot lists all candidates and requires marking the name of a single candidate, although in some cases more than one choice may be selected. Some structured ballots also provide space for write-in candidates.

At CERN, the Antiproton Decelerator (AD) slows antiprotons to roughly 0.1 times the speed of light, a velocity suitable for antimatter research. The decelerated antiprotons are employed in experiments that study the properties of antimatter. The AD was reconfigured from the earlier Antiproton Collector (AC) machine, transforming its design to provide lower-energy antiprotons for research purposes.

The European Southern Observatory (ESO) has adopted a governance and organizational structure influenced by CERN's model. In addition, CERN and ESO maintain a joint pension fund that covers staff from both institutions.

Naukowa i Akademicka Sieć Komputerowa (NASK) operates the computer emergency response team CERT Polska, which has been active since 1996. CERT Polska handles security incidents and undertakes research and development related to Internet security. The team has been a member of the International Forum of Incident Response and Security Teams (FIRST) since 1998 and of the European TF-CSIRT working group under TERENA since 2000.

Zespół Dyżurnet.pl, będący częścią NASK (Naukowa i Akademicka Sieć Komputerowa), działa od 2005 roku jako punkt kontaktowy dla użytkowników sieci. Jego zadaniem jest przyjmowanie anonimowych zgłoszeń dotyczących treści mogących naruszać prawo, w tym materiałów odnoszących się do przestępstw przeciwko dzieciom w sferze seksualnej. Ponadto prowadzi działania mające na celu podnoszenie świadomości oraz edukację w zakresie bezpiecznego korzystania z Internetu wśród dzieci i młodzieży. W zakres realizowanych inicjatyw wchodzą kampanie informacyjne, organizacja konferencji, szkolenia dla profesjonalistów i ekspertów oraz warsztaty dla młodych internautów.

Matsya Purana, a Vaishnavite text within the Puranic tradition, articulates a comprehensive system of temple design and iconography, advocating square-grid layouts in which large temples are planned on a 64-square mandala (yantra) and smaller shrines on a 16-square grid. It assigns an east-facing orientation to the temple entrance and sanctum to align with the sunrise. Conceptually, the temple is described as a bodily template, with the Atman and the Brahman (Purusha) resident in the heart, and the work supplies detailed spatial rules for successive levels, internal spaces, entrance heights, lengths, and sculptural work, with full specification given in chapters 253–269 and 58–65. The stambha, or temple pillar, is divided into nine parts—including Padma, Kumbha, and Antara—with prescribed widths, ratios, and correspondingly arranged carvings across these sections. Although the text bears the name of Vishnu’s Matsya avatar, it also contains substantial material on the installation of Shiva Linga and mentions Vishnu murti, goddesses, and other deities.

Matsya Purana is one of the eighteen major Puranas (Mahapurana) in Hindu literature. It is among the oldest surviving and best-preserved works within the Puranic corpus written in Sanskrit. The text is a Vaishnava work named after Vishnu’s Matsya, the fish-incarnation, reflecting devotion to Vishnu within the broader Hindu devotional tradition. Some scholars, including Horace Hayman Wilson, have described it as Shaivism-related but not exclusively so, noting that it also exalts a wide range of Hindu gods and goddesses.

In 2004, Peter Morville of Google designed the User Experience Honeycomb, a framework created to guide the design of user interfaces. The model offered a structured approach to evaluating and improving user experiences, and for about a decade it served as a widely used reference for many students studying web development.

User interfaces are designed using a range of methods that prioritize usability and adaptability. Central to contemporary practice is user-centered design, which emphasizes understanding users’ needs, tasks, and contexts to guide development decisions. Designers may also use personas—fictional representations of typical users—to anchor understanding and communicate requirements. Activity-oriented design focuses on the tasks and workflows users perform, organizing the interface around practical activities rather than isolated features. Scenario-based design employs narrative scenarios to examine how users interact with the interface in realistic contexts, informing design choices and evaluation criteria. Finally, resiliency design aims to create interfaces that remain usable under varying conditions, withstand disturbances, and recover gracefully from errors or disruptions.
In April 2001, upon joining Yahoo, Terry Semel was granted stock options with an SEC fair value of more than $110 million as a signing bonus. In June 2006, his annual base salary was reduced to $1.

Terry Semel joined Yahoo as its chief executive officer, and during his early discussions with Yahoo’s founders, Jerry Yang and David Filo, they suggested he consider acquiring Google. The founders of Google, Larry Page and Sergey Brin, who reportedly admired Yahoo’s leadership, met Semel and dined with him; at the time Yahoo was Google’s largest licensor of search technology, paying roughly $7 million annually. Semel then proposed buying Google, but Page and Brin countered with a demand of about $1 billion and indicated they did not wish to sell. Semel indicated he would think about the price.

Legion of Boom was met with a mixed critical reception upon its release. On Metacritic it received a score of 58 out of 100, reflecting mixed or average reviews. Billboard’s assessment was likewise ambivalent, noting that the tracks often adhere to a straightforward progressive trance framework, though some material was highlighted as strong. Mojo awarded the album 3 out of 5, characterizing it as more akin to a horror movie soundtrack than traditional DJ breaks or dance-floor energy. Playlouder gave it 2 out of 5, comparing the project to the notion of dance music imagined by a US major-label executive. URB also rated it 2 out of 5, suggesting the band had become utterly irrelevant. Blender offered 1.5 out of 5, criticizing the work for its lumbering mid-tempo rhythms, weak lyricism, and overfamiliar synthesized textures.

Legion of Boom is the third studio album by the American electronic music duo the Crystal Method, released on January 13, 2004, by V2 Records. The record features contributions from Milla Jovovich and Kyuss frontman John Garcia, and includes guitar riffs by Wes Borland of Limp Bizkit, who also co-produced three tracks. Vocals on the album are provided by beatboxer Rahzel. The title is widely interpreted as a reference to the Legion of Doom, a fictional supervillain team.

Astron (spacecraft) carried a payload that included an ultraviolet telescope with an 80-centimeter aperture. The ultraviolet instrument was designed through a collaborative effort between the Soviet Union and France. The payload also housed an X-ray spectroscope for complementary high-energy observations. The ultraviolet telescope was capable of obtaining spectra in the 150 to 350 nanometer range.

Astron was a Soviet spacecraft project directed by Alexandr Boyarchuk. The spacecraft was designed and built by the Crimean Astrophysical Observatory in collaboration with NPO Lavochkin. A group of scientists from these institutions was awarded the USSR State Prize in recognition of their work on the project.

The Serpentine Galleries are two contemporary art galleries located in Kensington Gardens, City of Westminster, Greater London. Following a branding update, the organization now operates under the single name Serpentine. It is structured around two venues, Serpentine South and Serpentine North. Serpentine South was previously known as the Serpentine Gallery, while Serpentine North was formerly the Sackler Gallery.

In 2013, Serpentine North opened to the public as the Serpentine Sackler Gallery, and the name was changed to Serpentine North in 2021, a shift that revitalized The Magazine, a Grade II* listed former gunpowder store built in 1805. An extension to The Magazine was designed by Zaha Hadid Architects, and The Magazine lies about a five-minute walk from Serpentine South across the Serpentine Bridge. The complex comprises 900 square metres (9,700 sq ft) of gallery space, together with a restaurant, shop, and social space, while The Magazine Restaurant adjoins the gallery space.

In its initial 1925 planning, U.S. Route 10 was proposed to connect Detroit with Chicago, with the corridor continuing northwest into Wisconsin along the roadway that would later be designated as U.S. Route 12.

U.S. Route 10 enters Wisconsin at Prescott and travels southeast, passing through Durand, Neillsville, Marshfield, Stevens Point, and Appleton, with its eastern terminus at Manitowoc near Lake Michigan. The seasonal SS Badger ferry provides a link between the route’s western and eastern portions from May to October. A four-lane divided highway extends from Wisconsin Highway 80 (south of Marshfield) to Interstate 39, enabling a bypass around Hewitt, Auburndale, Blenker, Milladore, Junction City, and downtown Stevens Point. This upgrade completes the plan to convert US 10 into a freeway/expressway corridor from Marshfield to Menasha. The segment between Stevens Point and Waupaca is an expressway, and portions in the Waupaca area as well as the stretch between Fremont and Appleton have been upgraded to freeway standards.

Proven oil reserves denote the volumes of crude oil that are recoverable under current economic conditions. They may increase when known deposits become economically viable to develop. In Canada, proven reserves rose in 2003 as Alberta's oil sands became economically viable. In Venezuela, reserves expanded in the late 2000s when the Orinoco Belt heavy oil became economically viable to exploit.

Proven oil reserve figures in lists ranking countries by reserves vary considerably across sources, reflecting differences in methodological choices and data sources. Variations arise from what oil categories are included, with some tallies counting shale oil and other unconventional sources while others exclude them, and from differing definitions of what qualifies as "proven" reserves. As a result, estimates can diverge markedly depending on whether unconventional resources are incorporated. North America is often highlighted for its unconventional wealth, with estimates indicating more than three trillion barrels of shale oil reserves. In the United States, shale resources contribute a substantial portion of oil production, and a majority of U.S. oil output has come from shale plays. Some compilations also present a paradoxical projection suggesting the United States could exhaust its oil reserves within about ten years at 2024 production levels, though such claims hinge on specific assumptions about reserves, future production, and discovery rates and are subject to considerable debate.

The Sihl is a river in Zürich on which the SZU railway line runs in a tunnel along and beneath it near the city centre. Access to Selnau station is via an artificial island in the river. Downstream, the Schanzengraben moat flows into the Sihl just before the river passes under Zürich Hauptbahnhof; the moat is fed from Lake Zürich and historically protected the western Altstadt. Zürich Hauptbahnhof contains two levels of platforms; the river tunnels beneath the upper platforms and then runs above the lower platforms through five culverts, each 190 metres long with a clear opening of 12 by 3 metres. After passing under the station, the Sihl joins the Limmat at the apex of Platzspitz park.

The Sihl river rises on the northeastern slopes of the Druesberg mountain in Unteriberg, in the canton of Schwyz, and flows northward toward the village of Studen. About two kilometres downstream of Studen, it enters the artificial Sihlsee reservoir at the lake’s southern end. The Minster also drains into the Sihlsee and, prior to the construction of the reservoir, flowed directly into the Sihl. Additionally, the Eubach, Rickentalbach, and Grossbach reach the Sihl via the Sihlsee.

Vishnu’s Dashavatara, the ten-avatar framework, is marked by a notable disagreement over whether Buddha or Balarama should be counted among the ten incarnations. This divergence originates from the Dashavatara enumeration given in the Shiva Purana, which has fueled ongoing scholarly debate about the canonical list. The Garuda Purana presents an alternate ten-avatar scheme that includes Balarama; in that tradition, the Vamana avatar occupies the position associated with Buddha, effectively omitting Buddha from the list. Both versions of the Dashavatara have scriptural grounding in authentic Vedic literature, and they are not derived from the Garuda Purana Saroddhara.

Vishnu is a deity in the Rigveda, though not among its most prominent figures, with Indra, Agni, and others being cited more frequently. Only five of the Rigveda’s 1028 hymns are devoted to Vishnu, though he is also mentioned in other hymns beyond those dedicated pieces. In addition to the hymns, Vishnu is referenced in the Brahmana layer of the Vedas, reflecting his presence in the ritual- and prose-oriented portions of the scripture. Across the history of Indian literature, scholars such as Jan Gonda describe Vishnu as rising to a divinity of the highest rank, ultimately equated with the Supreme Being.

Lake Kuş, also known as Kuş Gölü ("Bird Lake") and Lake Manyas (Manyas Gölü) in western Turkey, lies in the Bandırma region. It is a shallow, nutrient-rich freshwater body with an average depth of about three metres. The lake receives water from groundwater and four streams, and small deltas form where these streams enter the lake. The deltas feature extensive marshes and tree-lined riverbanks. Narrow belts of reed (Phragmites) fringe much of the lake. Water is abstracted for factory use and irrigation. Cattle and sheep grazing are common along the lake's shores.

Lake Kuş, also known as Lake Manyas, is a lake in northwestern Turkey that serves as an important site for breeding and wintering waterbirds. The Kuş Cenneti nature reserve, established in 1938, encompasses 64 hectares in a largely pristine lakeside area near Sığırcık, at the northeastern edge of the lake. The reserve's name, Kuş Cenneti, translates to the Bird Paradise in Turkish. It was founded by Curt Kosswig, a German zoologist and hydrologist who worked in Turkey from 1937 to 1955. The area includes a small ornithological museum housing mounted birds, though the exhibits are in poor condition, as well as remote-controlled viewing cameras. An observation tower, erected in 1952 by the Hydrology Department of Istanbul University, is another notable feature of the reserve.

Part of the 2011 United Kingdom census, Scotland's component included 13 household questions and up to 35 questions for each individual respondent. Preparations for the census plans were rehearsed in west Edinburgh and in Lewis and Harris.

Prior to the 2011 census, a rehearsal was conducted in England and Wales, piloting the questionnaire in about 135,000 households located in Lancaster, the London Borough of Newham, and Anglesey on 11 October 2009, with a concurrent test carried out in Birmingham. The questions to be used in the 2011 census were the same as those trialled during the 2009 Census Rehearsal. The legislative framework for the census was established when the 2011 Census Order, detailing proposed topics, the census date, and who should complete the questionnaire, was laid before Parliament in October 2009, approved by Parliament, and became law in December 2009.

Maxwell Anderson began his career in journalism, working for The New York Globe and later The New York World. In 1921 he founded The Measure: A Journal of Poetry, a magazine devoted to verse. His first play, White Desert, appeared in 1923, running twelve performances and receiving favorable notices from Laurence Stallings of the New York World. Stallings subsequently collaborated with Anderson on his next play, What Price Glory?, which was successfully produced in New York City in 1924. Following this production, Anderson resigned from The New York World to pursue a career as a dramatist.

Maxwell Anderson wrote Saturday's Children, a 1927 comedy-drama about married life. Humphrey Bogart made an early appearance in the stage production. The work was filmed three times: in 1929 as a part-talkie; in 1935 as the B-film Maybe It's Love, in which the original material is almost unrecognizable; and again in 1940 under its original title. The 1940 film featured John Garfield, in one of his few romantic-comedy performances. The play was adapted for television in three condensed versions in 1950, 1952, and 1962.

Phnom Thnout-Phnom Pok Wildlife Sanctuary, spanning 42,097 hectares in Siem Reap Province in northern Cambodia, was designated as a wildlife sanctuary in August 2017. The sanctuary receives support from Our Future Organization, and its conservation program traces its origins to the BeTreed ecotourism social enterprise, which was established in 2013. In Khmer, the area is known as ដែនជម្រកសត្វព្រៃភ្នំត្នោត-ភ្នាពក.

Phnom Thnout-Phnom Pok Wildlife Sanctuary is a protected area that has more than 70 species recorded within its boundaries. It serves as an important refuge for several endangered species, including the banteng, green peafowl, and pileated gibbon. The sanctuary, however, is threatened by hunting, particularly snaring, as well as illegal logging and land clearance linked to agricultural expansion and land speculation.

Broadside weight is defined as the total mass of projectiles that a ship can deliver to one side in a single broadside, calculated by multiplying the weight of an individual shell by the number of gun barrels that can bear on that side. If some turrets cannot be oriented to fire to that side, only the barrels that can actually bear on that side are counted. For example, Iowa-class battleships have nine 16-inch guns that can be trained to a single broadside; each 16-inch shell weighs 2,700 pounds (1,200 kg), so the calculation yields 2,700 × 9 = 24,300 pounds (11,022 kg), which is approximately 12 short tons (11.0 metric tonnes) of ordnance that could land on a target in one firing.

Broadside (naval) concerns the development and use of gunports and gunfire from the side of ships. Gunports cut into the hull appear around 1501, possibly by the Breton shipwright Descharges, though they may reflect a gradual adaptation of stern-loading ports from centuries of merchant vessel practice. Initially these openings were used to mount heavy stern chasers pointing aft. Over time, the gun ports migrated to the sides of ships, enabling the theoretical possibility of firing coordinated volleys from all guns on a single side. In practice, however, the 16th century saw guns fixed in place and fired independently rather than in concerted volleys. The word broadside entered English in the 1590s to refer to gunfire from the side of a ship, rather than to describe the ship’s own side.

On 13 June 2019, the United Nations and the World Economic Forum signed a Strategic Partnership Framework with the aim of jointly accelerating the implementation of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.

The United Nations allocates a substantial portion of its expenditures to its core mandate of maintaining international peace and security, with the budget for peacekeeping operations managed separately from the organization’s regular budget. For 2021–2022, the peacekeeping budget totaled $6.38 billion and supported 66,839 personnel deployed across 12 missions worldwide. Peacekeeping financing is drawn from assessments that derive from the regular funding scale, augmented by a weighted surcharge applied to the five permanent members of the Security Council (the P5), which retain veto power over peacekeeping actions. The surcharge serves to offset discounted rates applied to less developed member states. In the 2023–2024 period, the largest contributions to the UN’s peacekeeping budget came from the United States with 26.94%, followed by China at 18.68%, Japan at 8.03%, Germany at 6.11%, the United Kingdom at 5.35%, France at 5.28%, Italy at 3.18%, Canada at 2.62%, South Korea at 2.57%, and Russia at 2.28%.

West Germany, under Chancellor Willy Brandt, pursued Ostpolitik with the aim of achieving mutual recognition between East and West and broader normalization of interstate relations. The 1970 Treaties with the Soviet Union and with Poland helped to normalise ties by affirming the postwar borders and renouncing force, thereby creating a framework for closer engagement. Building on these steps, the Four Power Agreement on Berlin (1971), the Transit Agreement (1972), and the Basic Treaty (1972) further reduced tensions and established formal mechanisms for interaction between the two German states. As a consequence of these measures, both German states moved toward international recognition, culminating in their admission to the United Nations. The policy also marked the abandonment of the Hallstein Doctrine, with West Germany relinquishing its claim to exclusive representation of the German nation.

Konrad Adenauer became Chancellor of West Germany in 1949 at the age of 73. While initially regarded as a caretaker due to his advanced years, he nevertheless led the government for fourteen years (1949–1963), shaping the early trajectory of the Federal Republic and earning a reputation as a leading statesman in postwar German politics. His departure in 1963 occurred under sustained political pressure, with accounts describing the exit as nearly forced by his opponents.

Throughout its history, the Eastern Orthodox Church has relied on councils to articulate and refine its faith and practice. Several synods convened in Constantinople across the centuries—namely in 1484, 1583, 1755, 1819, and 1872—to address doctrinal and disciplinary matters. Additional regional developments include the Synod of Iași in 1642 and the Pan-Orthodox Synod of Jerusalem in 1672. In recent times, a pan-Orthodox Holy and Great Council was convened in June 2016 to consider contemporary developments, relations with other Christian denominations and world religions, and questions pertaining to fasting practices within Orthodoxy.

The Order of Saint Benedict is an Eastern Orthodox monastic affiliation that follows the Rule of Saint Benedict. The Catholic Church's equivalent monastic order bears the same designation, known as the Order of Saint Benedict (OSB).

Pragyan employs a rocker-bogie type suspension to stabilize the rover as it traverses irregular lunar terrain. The vehicle is built with six wheels, with each wheel independently powered by its own brushless direct-current motor. Steering is accomplished through skid steering, achieved by varying the speeds of wheels on opposite sides.

Pragyan, the rover of ISRO's Chandrayaan-2 mission, employs a pair of 1-megapixel monochrome navigation cameras mounted in front of the rover to provide stereoscopic 3D vision. This dual NAVCAM setup gives ground control a three-dimensional view of the surrounding terrain and assists path planning by generating a digital elevation model of the terrain ahead. IIT Kanpur contributed to the project by developing subsystems for light-based map generation and for rover motion planning, integrating these components into Pragyan's navigation and control framework.

Sunrise Tower is part of a larger development in Zurich. The first construction phase involved the demolition of four older buildings on the site before construction began. The four office buildings are grouped around Quadroplatz Square, and the arrangement is intended to create one of the most heavily trafficked areas in the Leutschenbach River area. Sunrise Tower forms a component of the development, while MainTower, a sixteen-story building, is also planned to be included and would be slightly shorter in height than Sunrise Tower.

Sunrise Tower in Zurich, Switzerland, is a high-rise completed in 2005, with construction beginning in 2000. The design was selected through an architectural competition and executed by the Wäschle Wüst consortium in collaboration with Max Dudler's studio. The building is also known as the diAx Tower, a name promoted by its principal tenant, diAx. After Tele Danmark merged Sunrise Communications with diAx to form TDC Switzerland (Sunrise Communications Group AG), the project was taken over and the structure was renamed Sunrise Tower to align with the corporate identity. The development and ownership are held by the Civil Servants' Insurance Fund of the Canton of Zurich (BVK). The general contractor was Zschokke, and construction costs were around 200 million Swiss francs (approximately €212 million).

In January 2008, Mokulele Airlines reached an agreement with Aloha Airlines to provide cargo service to Molokai, Lanai, and Kapalua, with the operation to run under the Aloha Cargo Express banner beginning in April and employing a Cessna 208 Cargomaster. Following Aloha’s bankruptcy filing in March 2008, Mokulele’s leadership indicated that there was an agreement with Aloha CEO David Banmiller to work with the buyer of Aloha’s cargo operations to continue the Mokulele–Aloha contract. Under this arrangement, Mokulele would proceed with cargo operations under its own name, Mokulele Air Cargo.

Mokulele Airlines is a Hawaii-based regional carrier that has historically been voted by local news media as Hawaii’s leading island-hopper and commuter airline. It has also received awards recognizing its air-tour offerings, including the Best Air Tour award.
In the United Kingdom, the 2:1 undergraduate degree classification is sometimes referred to in rhyming slang, with examples including “Attila,” named after Attila the Hun, and “Trevor Nunn.”

Ortaköy Mosque, located in Istanbul, was designed by the Balyan family, a prominent group of architects in the Ottoman era. Its architectural language blends European Revivalist influences, most notably Neoclassical, with the earlier Ottoman Baroque tradition. The structure is distinguished by its exceptionally ornate stone-carved decoration, more elaborate than the attire of mosques produced during its period.

Ortaköy Mosque, located in the Ortaköy district of Istanbul, is commonly regarded as a symbol of the area. The structure is a frequent subject of photography, reflecting its prominence in visual representation. From its vicinity, visitors enjoy a distinctive view of the Bosphorus Strait, with sightlines that also encompass the Bosphorus Bridge, underscoring the site's status as a notable scenic landmark in Istanbul.

Georgia experiences winter temperatures around 10°C, and the cold conditions complicate reliance on hydropower. Therefore, natural gas serves as the primary winter power source. Hydropower and natural gas maintain a complementary relationship that helps optimize the country’s overall energy potential. In 2019, Georgia consumed 84,756 million cubic feet of natural gas, much of which was imported from Armenia, Azerbaijan, Russia, and Turkey.

In 2016, Georgia's total primary energy supply (TPES) amounted to 4.793 Mtoe. That year, electricity consumption stood at 11.5 TWh and electricity production totaled 11.6 TWh. The electricity mix was dominated by hydropower, which contributed about 81% of generation, with natural gas making up roughly 19%.

Bounce is an album by Bon Jovi that debuted at number two on the Billboard 200, the highest debut the band had achieved at that time. It was the first Bon Jovi album in the United States not to reach Platinum certification.

Following the completion of the Crush world tour in July 2001 with two sold-out Giants Stadium performances, Bon Jovi took a three-week break after which Jon Bon Jovi and Richie Sambora began writing new material, initially in Los Angeles and later in New Jersey. Some tracks were demoed in New Jersey in November 2001. While Jon fulfilled an acting commitment on Ally McBeal and stayed at Sambora's home in Los Angeles, writing and demoing continued at Luke Ebbin's house. The songwriting and demoing process persisted through March 2002, and the album Bounce was recorded between March and June 2002. By early July 2002, all of the album's songs had been mixed, and by late July 2002 the album had been mastered. Over the course of less than a year the band wrote about 40 songs, of which 12 were selected for the album, with several additional demo versions appearing as B-sides on singles. Some cathartic songs were written in the wake of the September 11 attacks, featuring somber lyrics influenced by the tragedy; Jon Bon Jovi stated that these songs were written but would not be recorded.

The Yahk River is a Montana watercourse that is augmented early on by the South Fork Yaak River, entering from just downstream of the confluence with the West Fork Yaak River. After this junction, the river broadens its course, bending first toward the west and then turning to the south. Its tributary system includes Spread Creek, Hellroaring Creek, and Burnt Creek, the latter also known as Burnt Grizzly Bear Creek. The river ultimately flows into the Kootenai River at a point near Yaak Mountain and the town of Troy, Montana.

Yahk is a Kootenai word that can be interpreted as meaning either “arrow” or “bow.” The name may refer to either the Yaak River or the Kootenai River. The Kootenai River’s southward curve, spanning from Canada into the United States and back into Canada, has been described as bow-shaped. If the name derives from the Kootenai word a’k, which means arrow, the Yaak River would be the source of the “arrow” reading.

Epiphrase is a rhetorical device that can function within argumentation by having voices other than the author articulate the point of view.
