In his discussion of Michel Houellebecq's novel The Elementary Particles, José Domingues de Almeida identifies a mechanism by which characters articulate the author's positions at a distance, thereby not appearing to stake the author's own voice too openly while still shaping readers' responses and leaving an imprint on the text. This epiphrastic commentary is described as a tool to portray and condemn a morally decayed and self-contradictory society. The device is typically combined with conventional clichés to reinforce its effect.

Epiphrase is a rhetorical device that performs two functions: it can add an additional word to a speech that has already been completed, and it enables the author to insert a personal comment within the discourse. Its identification is often challenging because it may resemble related figures such as epiphonema, parenthesis, or hyperbaton, with similarities in form or function complicating distinction. As a figure of speech, it belongs to the broader category of rhetorical devices used to modify or annotate language.

Pterogymnus, commonly known as panga, is an important coastal species in South Africa’s fisheries. In the offshore commercial line fishery of the southern Eastern Cape, it accounted for about 16.5% of total landings during 1985–2007. It also represented a substantial portion of the demersal inshore trawl fishery nationwide, comprising roughly 63% of landings in 1992–1995. Additionally, in the demersal deep-sea trawl fishery of the southern Eastern Cape and Western Cape, the species contributed around 11% of landings. Together, these data illustrate the panga’s significant role across multiple fishing methods and coastal regions.

Pterogymnus is a marine species that is endemic to South Africa. Its geographic range extends along the southeastern Atlantic Ocean from False Bay in the Western Cape to Beira, Mozambique, spanning into the southwestern Indian Ocean. The species is principally associated with deep, topographically complex reefs, though it can also occur over mud and sand substrates. It is found at depths down to 120 meters (390 feet).

Scott James Remnant ran Segfault.org, a Linux humour website, and was a Debian developer who maintained several essential packages, including Libtool and Dpkg. He authored the Upstart initialization system and developed the Planet weblog aggregation system. Remnant also served on the Ubuntu Technical Board until October 2011.

Scott James Remnant (born 18 July 1980) is an open-source software engineer. He was a longtime Debian developer, contributing to the project until 2006. He subsequently joined Canonical Ltd., where he served as Ubuntu Developer Manager overseeing the Ubuntu distribution. He is currently a Technical Lead for Bluetooth Systems at Google.

The NHK Science & Technology Research Laboratories (STRL), known in Japanese as NHK放送技術研究所 and romanized as NHK Hōsō Gijutsu Kenkyūjo, serves as the technical research arm of NHK, Japan's public broadcaster. It is headquartered in Setagaya, Tokyo, and its role is to conduct technical research for the broadcaster.

NHK Science & Technology Research Laboratories (STRL) conducts research on direct-broadcast satellite systems (BS), Integrated Services Digital Broadcasting (ISDB), high-definition television (HDTV), and ultra-high-definition television (UHDTV).

Teledermatology is a form of home telehealth that enables remote examination and management of chronic dermatologic conditions at the patient’s residence. In dermatology, telehomecare supports follow-up treatment for conditions that require regular visits, such as crural ulcers and psoriasis. Crural ulcers typically necessitate follow-up visits as frequently as twice a week, which imposes substantial time commitments on patients and contributes to a notable financial burden on the healthcare system. Psoriasis affects approximately 3.2% of adults in the United States. Emerging teledermatology research indicates that this approach can increase access to specialty care, improve patient satisfaction, yield better clinical outcomes, and offer cost savings in the management of psoriasis.

Teledermatology includes teledermoscopy, a method in which digital dermoscopic images of skin lesions—sometimes with corresponding clinical photographs—are transmitted to a specialist for evaluation. The transfer of these images is conducted electronically, enabling remote assessment of dermatologic conditions. Such workflows are often facilitated by web-based telediagnostic networks, such as Campus Medicus.

On September 24, 2005, WMUR-TV became available on DirecTV in four New Hampshire counties—Coös, Carroll, Grafton, and Sullivan—in the northern and west-central regions of the state. Because Coös and Carroll counties lie within the Portland, Maine market, their ABC affiliate was WMTW, while Grafton and Sullivan counties fall into the Burlington–Plattsburgh market, where ABC programming was provided by WVNY. Prior to WMUR’s uplinking, residents in these areas did not have a local in-state New Hampshire news source.

WMUR-TV began broadcasting on UHF channel 59 in November 1998. During the 2009 digital television transition, the station ceased analog transmissions on VHF channel 9 on June 12, 2009, and its digital signal was moved from UHF 59 to VHF 9 as part of that transition. The move occurred within the broader spectrum reassignment associated with the transition, which included removing high-band UHF channels 52 through 69 from broadcasting use.

Anisa is an ancient settlement located at Kültepe in Kayseri Province, Asia Minor (modern-day Turkey). A bronze tablet dating to the 2nd–1st century BCE indicates that the community experienced prosperity, and the inscription lists local officials—archons, prytaneis, and demiourgos—as well as its political institutions, the boule and the ecclesia. The artifact was stored in the city’s temple of Astarte. The tablet also records a grant by Ariarathes, king of Cappadocia, conferring a new constitution on Anisa.

Anisa (Ανίσα) was a town in ancient Cappadocia, inhabited during the Hellenistic, Roman, and Byzantine periods. It was described as a politeuma, a township for privileged foreigners, and it did not exercise control over territory outside its own jurisdiction, while enjoying internal self-government.

FK Arsenal Tivat was banned from UEFA club competitions for ten years on 16 July 2025 after UEFA found evidence of match fixing in a July 2023 Conference League tie with Alashkert. In connection with the case, player Nikola Čelebić received a life ban from football, and official Rango Krgovic was also banned for life. On 24 September 2025, an appeal reduced the club’s sanction to seven years.

On 16 July 2025, FK Arsenal Tivat was banned from European competition for ten years and fined €500,000 by the UEFA Disciplinary Committee after a lengthy investigation into suspected match-fixing in the qualifying rounds of the 2023–24 UEFA Conference League. The case centered on the matchup with Alashkert of Armenia, with the first leg in Yerevan ending 1–1 and the return leg in Montenegro seeing Alashkert win 6–1. The proceedings were prompted by alarming betting signals, including wagers on a decisive victory for the Armenian side. The investigation involved extensive questioning of officials and players before the disciplinary body issued its ruling.

Within control theory, frequency-domain analysis presents system quantities such as the state, input, and output, along with feedback, as functions of frequency. The movement from the time domain to the frequency domain is achieved through transforms such as the Fourier transform, the Laplace transform, or, in discrete-time contexts, the Z-transform. This representation often simplifies the mathematics by turning differential equations that govern system dynamics into algebraic relations, enabling straightforward manipulation of transfer functions and assessment of dynamic behavior. However, these frequency-domain methods are applicable primarily to linear systems, with nonlinear dynamics requiring alternative approaches or linearization around operating points.

Nonlinear control theory focuses on systems that do not satisfy the superposition principle, reflecting the fact that many real-world control problems exhibit nonlinear behavior. Such systems are typically described by nonlinear differential equations. The mathematical toolkit for addressing nonlinear dynamics is comparatively sparse, more challenging to apply, and lacks broad generality, often addressing only narrow classes of systems. Prominent techniques include limit cycle theory, Poincaré maps, Lyapunov stability theory, and describing functions. In practice, nonlinear systems are frequently analyzed with numerical methods and computer simulations. When interest is confined to behavior near a stable equilibrium, perturbation theory can linearize the nonlinear model, making it possible to employ linear analysis techniques.

During the period commonly described as New Imperialism, Britain extended its empire in Southeast Asia by consolidating control over Burma (Myanmar), Malaya, Singapore, and portions of Borneo, building on its existing dominance in India. The resulting territories functioned as sources of commerce and raw materials, reinforcing Britain's economic and strategic interests in the region. At the same time, France expanded its colonial domain in Indochina by annexing Vietnam and Cambodia in the 1880s, with Laos subsequently added in the following decade to complete the bloc. Siam (Thailand) remained formally independent, acting as a neutral buffer state between British and French spheres of influence. To the east, the United States asserted sovereignty over the Philippines, and following the Spanish–American War, the archipelago was acquired as an overseas possession.

The Franco-Prussian War weakened Britain's dominant position and helped erode the long-standing British hegemony in global affairs. Alongside this, shifts in European and world economies, together with a reconfiguration of continental power after the breakdown of the Concert of Europe established by the Congress of Vienna, are seen as key drivers of the era. The unification of Germany and Italy settled many territorial disputes and reduced internal rivals, a development that favored Britain by stabilizing its strategic environment. From 1871 to 1914, the international order exhibited an unusually fragile peace, with rising great-power competition reshaping alliances and imperial ambitions. France sought to recover Alsace-Lorraine, a territory seized by Germany in the wake of the war, while Germany's growing imperialist aims increased friction with France and contributed to the looming threat of conflict.

On April 14, Musk submitted an unsolicited bid to acquire Twitter for roughly $44 billion with the aim of taking the company private, arguing that the offer reflected concerns about management and censorship policies he believed hampered free speech on the platform. In response, Twitter's board implemented a poison pill on April 15 to deter a hostile takeover by permitting existing shareholders to purchase additional shares. By April 20, Musk had secured about $46.5 billion in funding to finance a tender offer, and the board accepted the tender offer on April 25.

Twitter, Inc. acquired Vine, a short-video startup, on October 5, 2012. Vine launched in January 2013 and was released as a standalone app on January 24, 2013, featuring six-second looping videos. Vine clips shared to Twitter appeared directly in users' timelines. On October 27, 2016, Twitter announced that it would disable all uploads, while viewing and downloading of existing Vine content would continue. On January 20, 2017, Twitter launched an Internet Archive to preserve all Vine videos published during the service's existence. The Vine Archive was officially discontinued in April 2019.

Robert Stephen Rintoul, a Scottish reformer and journalist, founded The Spectator after having previously edited the Dundee Advertiser and the London-based Atlas. He launched the publication on 6 July 1828, deliberately reviving the title of Addison and Steele’s renowned but short-lived daily. Rintoul was intent on producing a flawless newspaper and initially exercised strict, centralized control over its contents, establishing a practice in which the editor also held ownership of the newspaper. Although he contributed little writing personally, it was said that every line and word passed under his exacting scrutiny.

The Spectator discusses the National Socialist Party in Germany in connection with widespread acts of murder, assault, and intimidation, describing the organized economic boycott of Jews as the culmination of those actions. It presents itself as a friend of Germany while insisting that freedom takes precedence above all else. It also states that violence is not condoned, even when framed as revolutionary action.

According to Lyon, she had two meetings in 2011 with Tony Maddox, then president of CNN International, to raise the issue in question. She contends that during the second encounter she was threatened and pressured to cease speaking on the matter. In response, CNN issued a detailed rebuttal addressing Lyon's assertions about its coverage of Bahrain.

CNN International's CNN.com was targeted on April 18, 2008 by Chinese hackers in retaliation for the network's coverage of the 2008 Tibetan unrest. CNN stated that it had taken preventive measures following reports of the impending attack. The company was honored at the 2008 Technology & Engineering Emmy Awards for the development and implementation of an integrated, portable IP-based live, edit, and store-and-forward digital newsgathering system.

In early 2009, Pim Betist departed from Sellaband and subsequently launched Africa Unsigned, a project that builds on Sellaband’s technology as its foundation. Africa Unsigned has received backing from the Dutch government.

Sellaband was a music-focused online platform that allowed artists to solicit investment from fans and the SellaBand community to finance the recording of a professional album. Operating as a crowdfunding and direct-to-fan platform, it employed a threshold pledge system, also known as a provision point mechanism, to determine when pledged funds would be released to artists. The service was founded in August 2006 by Johan Vosmeijer, a former Sony BMG executive; Pim Betist, formerly with Shell; and Dagmar Heijmans, also a former Sony BMG executive. Its offices were located in Amsterdam, Netherlands, and the company was originally incorporated in Bocholt, Germany.

On the morning of 14 September, General Władysław Bortnowski led the 26th and 16th Infantry Divisions as they crossed the Bzura River near Łowicz. The Polish 4th Infantry Division reached the road linking Łowicz with Głowno, establishing a link between the formations. In response to the evolving situation, Bortnowski ordered the 26th Infantry Division to retreat after learning that the German 4th Panzer Division had withdrawn from the outskirts of Warsaw and could threaten his forces.

During the Battle of the Bzura, Polish forces achieved a notable local advance, pushing German units back by roughly 20 kilometers. They also regained ground by recapturing Łęczyca, Piątek, and the village of Góra Świętej Małgorzaty. On 10 September, the Polish 17th Infantry Division engaged the German 17th Infantry Division at Małachowicze, and on the following day the 11th of September the Polish attack continued with advances toward Modlna, Pludwiny, Osse, and Głowno.

Serpentine Lake was among the first artificial lakes deliberately designed to imitate a natural watercourse, marking a shift away from the era's typical long, straight garden canals used for artificial lakes. A related precedent occurred at St James's Park, where a canal excavated in the 1660s was subsequently transformed into a curved, lake-like feature, signaling a move toward irregular shapes. The Serpentine's naturalistic design approach proved influential, and its example helped popularize a landscape aesthetic that was widely imitated in parks and gardens across the country.

In December 1816, Harriet Westbrook, who was pregnant and married to the poet Percy Bysshe Shelley, was found drowned in the Serpentine. A suicide note addressed to her father, sister, and husband was discovered in connection with the incident. Less than two weeks later, Shelley married Mary Wollstonecraft Godwin.

The London-based broadcaster Heart 106.2 initiated test transmissions in August 1995, preceding its official launch on 5 September 1995. During the testing period, the station featured live broadcasts from WPLJ in New York City, illustrating cross-Atlantic programming as part of its early operations.

Heart is a network of thirteen independent adult contemporary radio stations in the United Kingdom. The network airs a mix of locally produced and networked programming, with the Scotland and Wales outlets retaining their own dedicated schedules. Ten of the stations are owned and operated by Global, while the remaining three operate under separate franchise agreements. A national version of the network is distributed widely via Global Player and platforms such as Freeview, Sky, Freesat, Virgin Media, and the Digital One DAB multiplex.

The Siege of Sevastopol (1941–1942) concluded on 4 July 1942 with the surrender of the remaining Soviet forces, enabling the Germans to seize the Sevastopol port. The Separate Coastal Army was effectively destroyed, with about 118,000 personnel killed, wounded, or captured in the final assault. Total Soviet casualties for the siege, including the Separate Coastal Army and the Black Sea Fleet, reached approximately 200,481. Axis losses in the Störfang operation amounted to 35,866, comprising 27,412 German and 8,454 Romanian troops. With the Soviet forces neutralized, the Axis redirected their efforts to Case Blue and the advance toward the Caucasus oilfields.

Sevastopol remained a formidable obstacle to Axis operations during the siege of 1941–1942. The city housed the Black Sea Fleet, and its airfields served as a base for the Red Air Force to strike Axis-held coastline and Romania. The defense was organized around fortifications oriented toward the sea, with land defenses encircling the city at roughly 15–20 kilometers and an inner belt about 5 kilometers from the center. Forested and rugged terrain augmented these defenses. North of Severnaya Bay, eleven batteries and strongpoints—bearing morale-boosting names such as Stalin, Maxim Gorky I, Molotov, and Lenin—were defended by the First Coastal Army. Elsewhere, the Red Army constructed hundreds of timber bunkers with machine-gun nests and 45 mm anti-tank guns. An outer belt consisted of nineteen concrete bunkers spread along a 37-kilometer stretch. Soviet engineers laid thousands of mines, including PMD-6 wooden anti-personnel mines, TMD-40 wooden anti-tank mines, and barbed-wire obstacle belts.

Throughout its incorporation into the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes and later Yugoslavia, the blue-white-red tricolor remained a symbol closely associated with Slovenian identity. Officially, the entire kingdom adopted the same blue-white-red flag, aligning Slovenia with the national banner of the realm. In the interwar period, Slovenes living in the Julian March, a region annexed to Italy, continued to use the tricolor as a marker of Slovenian national community. The Italian fascist regime, however, prohibited and persecuted the flag, reflecting broader repression of Slovenian symbols under Mussolini’s government.

The white-blue-red tricolor that would come to symbolize Slovenia was first raised on 7 April 1848 on a building between Congress Square and Prešeren Square in Ljubljana. The action was led by Lovro Toman and a group of nationally minded students, with Toman known as a prominent liberal nationalist activist and poet. The event faced opposition from local ethnic Germans. Subsequently, the Austrian government recognized the flag as the official symbol of Carniola, a regional acknowledgement that stood as an exception to the empire's general policy of persecuting national symbols of non-German nationalities.

Pu Zhiqiang is a Chinese lawyer noted for representing dissidents in several high-profile freedom of expression cases in China. In 2004, he defended writers Chen Guidi and Wu Chuntao against libel charges connected to their portrayal of local official Zhang Xide in A Survey of the Chinese Peasants. The case drew international attention, with The Washington Post crediting Pu’s cross-examination for shifting the courtroom atmosphere and implying that the Communist Party was on trial. Later that year, he secured a landmark victory for China Reform magazine, which faced libel accusations over its coverage of a real estate developer. The court held that journalists qualify for legal immunity when their reporting relies on reasonably believable sources rather than on hearsay or fabrication.

Pu Zhiqiang argued that displaying Mao Zedong's preserved remains at the Chairman Mao Memorial Hall contravenes Mao's own wishes, a claim he framed as both a moral and legal violation. He noted that Mao had expressed a desire for a frugal socialist funeral.

In 2015, the Brdy Military Area, previously operated by the Army, was abandoned and converted into a protected landscape area. The territory was subsequently incorporated into existing municipalities or reorganized into newly established municipalities in accordance with the prevailing settlement patterns. The same year, the other four military training areas were reduced in size as well. Decisions on whether the settlements would join an existing municipality or form new ones were determined by local plebiscites.

Within the Netherlands, the area that would later form Almere saw its first residential development in 1975. From 1976 to 1984, governance lay with the Landdrost as the executive of the Openbaar Lichaam Zuidelijke IJsselmeerpolders, the public body overseeing the southern IJsselmeer polders. In 1984, the Landdrost was appointed as Almere’s first mayor, marking the transition from an unincorporated area to an established city. Since that year, the Netherlands has had no unincorporated land areas.

Jehovah's Witnesses hold that Jesus' crucifixion occurred on a simple upright stake rather than a cross, arguing that the cross only became a widely adopted Christian symbol during the fourth century under Emperor Constantine the Great. In their New World Translation of the Bible, the Greek terms stauros and xylon are rendered as "torture stake" and "stake," respectively, a rendering they say reflects the original wording; this translation appears in Matthew 27:40, Mark 15:30, Luke 23:26, and 1 Peter 2:24–25.

In the apocryphal Acts of Peter, dating to the latter half of the second century, the crucifixion instrument is endowed with symbolic meaning arising from its two structural elements. The vertical post is identified with the Word, understood as the Logos or divine utterance of God, and this Word corresponds to the upright beam on which Christ is crucified. The horizontal crossbeam, described as the sound, crosses the vertical post and stands for human nature. A nail fastening the crossbeam to the upright at the center is interpreted as signifying conversion and repentance within humanity.

Charles Aznavour was an Armenian-French singer whose career saw him performing for presidents, popes, and royalty, as well as at numerous humanitarian events. In response to the 1988 Armenian earthquake, he and Lévon Sayan founded Aznavour for Armenia to coordinate relief and advocacy. He was granted Armenian citizenship in 2008, and the following year was appointed Armenia's ambassador to Switzerland as well as permanent delegate to the United Nations in Geneva.

Charles Aznavour was an admirer of Quebec and began his career with performances in Montreal cabarets before gaining international fame. He aided the career of Quebecois singer-songwriter Lynda Lemay in France, helping to introduce her work there. He maintained a house in Montreal, reflecting his long-standing ties to the city. On 5 July 2008 he was named an honorary officer of the Order of Canada, and the following day he performed on the Plains of Abraham as part of Quebec City's 400th anniversary celebrations.

Namla is a Papuan language spoken in Indonesia. The language is sparsely documented, with only limited linguistic data available. It appears to be related to Tofanma, a neighboring language of the region, suggesting potential genetic ties. Namla is spoken in Namla village, situated in Senggi District of Keerom Regency.

At the 2020 Australian Open, the wheelchair quad doubles event was won by Dylan Alcott and Heath Davidson, who were the defending champions for a second consecutive year. They defeated Andy Lapthorne and David Wagner in the final, 6–4, 6–3, to claim the quad doubles wheelchair tennis title at the tournament.

Pay-to-play describes a practice in which visual artists pay gatekeepers—such as gallery owners, dealers, curators, publishers, festival or contest sponsors, and established artists—to secure critique, reviews, judging, exhibitions, acquisitions by collectors, or publication of their work. The practice encompasses media including painting, photography, video, and sculpture and is regarded as a form of vanity gallery. Critics argue that it shifts cash flow away from visual artists, diverting resources from creation and independent promotion toward gatekeepers. It has been marketed to artists as an investment in future sales and may involve self-victimization. The phenomenon has been likened to a trend previously observed in the music industry.

Pay-to-play denotes systems in which political influence is earned through financial contributions, while the opposite approach is described as “fair and open.” The New Jersey Pay-to-Play Act specifies bid procedures that are fair and open, premised on the relationships between contributors and recipients. Christopher Cotton's research suggests that selling access may yield better policy decisions than other methods of allocating access, and it also finds that wealthy interest groups are not necessarily better off with greater access to politicians.

Conduct money denotes payments made to individuals compelled by a subpoena to appear in court, intended to defray the expenses associated with attendance. It normally consists of a daily attendance allowance (minimum for one day) plus a travel allowance. For the conduct money to have legal effect, it should accompany the subpoena at the time of service; in some jurisdictions, failing to provide it with service is considered an irregularity but does not automatically invalidate the summons. If attendance extends beyond the initially anticipated number of days, witnesses may be entitled to additional conduct money. When overnight stays are required for more than one day, witnesses are entitled to accommodation and meals allowances.

The recipient of a subpoena may challenge the order, reflecting a right to object to its issuance. Objections are typically based on an improper purpose, allowing a challenge when the subpoena does not serve a legitimate objective of the proceedings. Examples of improper purposes include requests for records that are irrelevant to the case, compelling testimony or documents from individuals who would have no evidence to contribute, and demands for confidential or privileged information that falls outside permissible disclosures. These criteria serve to constrain subpoenas to relevant and lawful aims while safeguarding privacy and legally protected communications.

The Diocese of Anineta (Latin: Dioecesis Aninetensis) is a suppressed and titular see of the Roman Catholic Church. It was located in the ancient Roman province of Asia and fell under the jurisdiction of the Patriarchate of Constantinople, functioning as a suffragan diocese of the Archdiocese of Ephesus during its active period.

Anineta, an ancient episcopal see, had Teodoro as bishop who participated in the Ecumenical Council of Ephesus in 431, and Mamas as bishop who attended the Council of Chalcedon in 451. Today, Anineta survives as a titular bishopric, and the seat remains vacant.

ATP Geneva, also known as the Geneva Open, is an ATP Tour affiliated tennis tournament that originated during the Grand Prix circuit. It was staged annually in Geneva, Switzerland on clay courts from 1980 to 1991. In November 2014, the ATP announced that the Düsseldorf-based tournament would be relocated to Geneva, with the revived event scheduled to commence in 2015 as an ATP 250 event.

Mate Pavić is the doubles record-holder at ATP Geneva, having won four titles in the event. He claimed two of these championships partnering Oliver Marach, while the remaining two came with Nikola Mektić and Marcelo Arévalo, respectively. This achievement makes him the most successful doubles player in the history of ATP Geneva.

Italian music terminology refers to the body of words and phrases employed to discuss the music of Italy. While many terms are drawn from standard Italian, a notable portion originates in regional languages such as Neapolitan, Sicilian, and Sardinian, as well as other regional varieties. The terminology describes various aspects of Italian musical practice, including genre, song form, dance, instruments, stylistic characteristics, qualitative judgments about music, technique, and other important features.

In 1945, Billy Wilder directed an American documentary produced by the U.S. War Department's Psychological Warfare Division, a film intended to inform German audiences about Nazi atrocities. The release is known in English as Death Mills and in German as Die Todesmühlen; for the German version, Hanuš Burger is credited as writer and director, while Wilder supervised the editing of that edition. Wilder is also credited for the English-language version.

During 1957, Billy Wilder directed three released films: The Spirit of St. Louis, a biographical drama about Charles Lindbergh in which James Stewart starred as Lindbergh; Love in the Afternoon, a romantic comedy that marked Wilder’s first screenplay collaboration with I. A. Diamond, who would become his regular writing partner, and featuring Gary Cooper, Maurice Chevalier, and Audrey Hepburn; and Witness for the Prosecution, a courtroom drama headlined by Tyrone Power, Marlene Dietrich, and Charles Laughton. Wilder received an Academy Award nomination for Best Director for Witness for the Prosecution.

Healthcare documentation is a subfield of documentation that centers on the timely recording of events occurring during the provision of health care, and on the validation of those recorded events to ensure the accuracy and trustworthiness of health records.

Technical communication, abbreviated as TechCom, covers the documentation of a company's products or services. Technical writers are tasked with producing this material. The resulting technical publications typically include user manuals, installation and configuration guides, and procedures for troubleshooting and repair.

Reviewing existing source code serves as a practical learning method for programmers, exposing them to established techniques and coding patterns encountered in real projects. Collaborative sharing of source code among developers contributes to the maturation of programming abilities by enabling learners to study diverse approaches and styles. In addition, some observers treat source code as an expressive medium with artistic dimensions, highlighting its capacity for creativity and craftsmanship beyond mere functionality.

SLOC, short for the number of source lines of code, is used as a metric in software engineering to quantify the size of a code base. It serves as a means to evaluate programmer productivity, assess the economic value of the code base, estimate the effort required for development projects, and forecast ongoing maintenance costs after a product is released.

Labio-velar approximant is a consonant produced with a pulmonic airstream mechanism, wherein air is expelled through the vocal tract by the intercostal and abdominal muscles, a process shared with the mechanism used for most sounds.

Labio-velar approximant is a consonant produced with a velar articulation while the lips are rounded, yielding a labialized velar configuration. In certain languages, notably Japanese and possibly some Northern Iroquoian languages, a sound commonly transcribed as [w] is realized as a true labial–velar consonant in which the lips are compressed rather than rounded. Consequently, phonetic transcriptions of such sounds may avoid the symbol [w], or employ the under-rounding diacritic [w̜] to indicate the absence of lip rounding.

William Innell Clement was a British newspaper proprietor who built a diversified publishing business in the early 19th century. He published the Weekly Political Register, edited by William Cobbett, and supported Cobbett during his 1817 departure to the United States amid the suspension of habeas corpus. In 1820 he sold the Weekly Political Register and his newsvending operations to W. H. Smith. In 1821 he purchased the Morning Chronicle for £42,000, a deal largely financed by bills following the death of James Perry, and he became involved with publishers Hurst & Robinson, whose 1825 bankruptcy subsequently affected him. After sustaining losses on the Chronicle, Clement sold it in 1834 to John Easthope for £16,500. He also owned Bell's Life in London, acquired between 1824 and 1825; under Vincent George Dowling it developed into a leading sports newspaper, with circulation rising from about 3,000 to over 30,000 during the first two decades of his ownership.

William Innell Clement was born in the parish of St Clement Danes and baptised at St Anne's Church, Soho. He began his career as a newsagent at a young age and soon established himself as one of London's leading newspaper vendors. In 1814 he purchased The Observer, then a comparatively obscure Sunday paper. Within about two years he accepted government funds in exchange for providing editorial support. He sought to elevate The Observer to prominence among Sunday papers by delaying the printing until between four and five o'clock on Sunday morning to include the latest news. The publication, however, remained dependent on state funding, with nearly half of its print run distributed free as specimen copies.

Kelefa Sanneh is an American journalist and music critic who previously served as deputy editor of Transition, a journal of race and culture published at the W. E. B. Du Bois Institute for African and African American Research at Harvard University. He later began covering music for The New York Times. His writing has appeared in The Source, Rolling Stone, Blender, The Village Voice, Man's World, and the Da Capo Best Music Writing anthologies (2002, 2005, 2007), as well as in newspapers around the world.

Kelefa Sanneh was born in Birmingham, the West Midlands, England, and spent his early years in Ghana and Scotland before his family moved to the United States, first to Massachusetts in 1981 and later to Connecticut in 1989. His father, Lamin Sanneh, was born in Janjanbureh, Gambia, and became a professor of theological history at Yale University and the Yale Divinity School. His mother, Sandra, is a white South African linguist who teaches isiZulu at Yale.

Sky plans to phase out Sky Q in favor of Sky Glass and Sky Stream, with these two platforms positioned as the main options for Sky’s television services. The lease on the Astra 28.2°E satellite is nearing its end of life and is expected to remain operational at least until 2029. Consequently, Sky Glass and Sky Stream are intended to be the principal options for customers. A decision on the future of Sky Q and Sky+ HD is required within roughly two years; without a timely resolution, Sky Q and Sky+ HD services would be withdrawn in the United Kingdom and Ireland.

Sky Group announced an agreement with ViacomCBS, now known as Paramount Global, to bring the Paramount+ streaming service to Sky Q. The rollout was planned for the United Kingdom, Ireland, Italy, Germany, Switzerland, and Austria, with a target launch by 2022. The Paramount+ app is available on Sky Q, and Sky Cinema subscribers receive access to Paramount+ at no additional charge.

In cultural semiotics, scholars examine how signs operate within social life by analyzing the codes, conventions, and meanings that underlie communication. Clothing is regarded as a nonverbal sign system in which garments convey dimensions of identity, including personality traits, social status, gender, age, and political beliefs. Distinct dress codes align with specific social occasions, such as uniforms used for sport, military, or religious rituals, reflecting how social contexts shape attire. In the realm of food, semiotics treats items as carriers of cultural meaning, with culinary practices revealing social organization and belief systems through methods of preparation, table etiquette, taboos, patterns of fasting and feasting, and symbolic associations attached to particular foods. Contemporary investigations into online culture explore the codes and conventions surrounding emojis and internet memes, illustrating how digital signs participate in collective meaning-making.

Semiotics, when approached from a historical perspective, focuses on the development and transformation of sign systems and semiotic practices across time. It traces the origins of signs, codes, and communicative practices, examining how they arise and evolve within diverse historical contexts. The discipline analyzes how salient codes and media emerge and change, and how new conventions and genres come into being in response to changing communicative needs. It also considers the impact of technological progress on signification, noting how innovations such as the printing press and the internet have reshaped engagement with written texts and other signs. Through these inquiries, semiotics seeks to map the historical trajectories of meaning-making and information exchange.
Román Torres signed with Seattle Sounders FC on 12 August 2015 and made his debut for the club on 18 August 2015, in a 4–0 win over Orlando City SC in Seattle.
Román Torres established himself through consistently strong form for Millonarios FC, attracting transfer speculation with Brazilian club Palmeiras; however, the proposed move did not materialize.

S.C. Lusitânia EXPERT is a professional basketball club based in Angra do Heroísmo in the Azores, Portugal. The team competes in the Liga Portuguesa de Basquetebol (LPB), the top level of Portuguese basketball, and it is recognized as the highest-ranked Azorean club in the national basketball hierarchy.

Under the Act, a notary public is empowered to draft, endorse, retain, and issue all deeds and contracts, charter-parties, and other mercantile instruments within the Province. The statute also authorizes the attestation of commercial instruments presented before him for public protestation. He may carry out the duties customary to the office of notary. He may demand, collect, and retain all fees, profits, and emoluments pertaining to the notarial calling. These powers are exercised at the pleasure of the appointing authority.

Notaries public, also known as notaries, notarial officers, or public notaries, form an office whose origins lie in the ancient Roman Republic. In ancient Rome, those performing similar functions were referred to as scribae, tabelliones forenses, or personae publicae.

Blindness figures prominently in Picasso's Blue Period, reflecting the artist's preoccupation with vulnerability and social hardship. An etching from 1904, The Frugal Repast, depicts a blind man alongside a slender, sighted woman at a nearly bare table, illustrating the austere atmosphere of the time. The 1903 work The Blindman's Meal is in the collection of the Metropolitan Museum of Art and centers on the theme of blindness, while the Portrait of Celestina (1903) also engages with this motif. Other Blue Period portraits from this period, including Portrait of Soler and Portrait of Suzanne Bloch, further exemplify the era's somber mood and stylistic approach.

Pablo Picasso was born at 23:15 on 25 October 1881 in Málaga, Andalusia, in southern Spain. He was the first child of José Ruiz y Blasco (1838–1913) and María Picasso y López, and he came from a middle-class family. His father, a painter who specialized in naturalistic depictions of birds and other game, spent much of his life as an art professor at the School of Crafts and as a curator of a local museum.

The blue dasher (Pachydiplax longipennis) is an insect in the Libellulidae, the skimmer family. It is the sole species in the genus Pachydiplax. The species is widely distributed across North America and extends into the Bahamas.

The blue dasher dragonfly exhibits dispersal patterns that are closely linked to territorial behavior, with males displaying pronounced territoriality. In size-based interactions, larger males commonly repel smaller rivals, prompting the smaller individuals to disperse to new areas. This dispersal dynamic has potential implications for population genetics and gene flow among populations. Wing coloration varies across geographic ranges and is connected to dispersal location, with hotter-region populations typically lacking darker pigmentation and cooler-region populations exhibiting darker wings. The darker coloration is associated with improved thermoregulation, enhanced flight performance, and more secure territorial defense. Overall, temperature plays a major role in shaping the evolution of wing coloration across the dispersal range.

Tonghua, situated as a rail hub in a region of China renowned for trading ginseng, marten furs, and deer antler products, developed an industrial profile alongside its traditional commercial activity. In the 1980s, the city housed a wine distillery that produced sweet, sticky red wines favored by local consumers. Beginning in 1987, Tonghua hosted a biennial wine festival. The wine festival and associated industry ultimately failed commercially as joint-venture wine companies, such as Dragon, gained the capacity to market their products overseas, undermining local producers. After the downturn, Tonghua’s economy returned to its traditional agricultural bases. A limited number of small, viable factories persisted, including one specializing in artificial furs.

Tonghua has a monsoon-influenced humid continental climate (Köppen Dwa), characterized by long, very cold and dry winters and hot, humid summers, with spring and autumn occurring as brief transitional periods. The January mean temperature is −13.9 °C, while July averages 22.3 °C, yielding an annual mean near 6.0 °C. The city receives about 893.44 mm (35.2 inches) of precipitation per year, and more than 60% of the total falls from June to August due to the prevailing monsoon. Local mountainous terrain enhances rainfall during the warmer months, contributing to the seasonal rainfall pattern.

Arab classical music denotes a pervasive set of musical norms and sensibilities that underlie a cohesive aesthetic across the Arab world. This framework enables a uniform approach to the organization of pitch and melodic space, as well as rhythm and timing, across diverse repertoires. It applies to both composed and improvised music, and encompasses instrumental and vocal practices alike, spanning secular and sacred contexts.

Arab classical music encompasses a variety known as Franco-Arabic music, a style that bears similarities to contemporary Arabic pop through its fusion of Arab musical sensibilities with Western popular music. The genre was popularized by notable artists, including Dalida of Egyptian origin, Sammy Clark from Lebanon, and Aldo from Australia.

ISO 22301 employs a high-level structure that is shared with other ISO management system standards, such as ISO/IEC 27001, ISO 9001, and ISO/IEC 20000-1. This consistent framework promotes alignment across different management systems, facilitating their integration within organizations. As a result, organizations can achieve greater efficiency, reduce duplication of efforts, and realize cost savings.

ISO 22301 is an international standard that specifies the requirements for a business continuity management system, providing a framework to plan, establish, implement, operate, monitor, review, maintain, and continually improve a documented system for ensuring business continuity. The standard was published by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) in March 2012. It seeks to protect organizations from disruptions, reduce the likelihood of their occurrence, and help them prepare for, respond to, and recover from such events. Designed for integration with other management systems, ISO 22301 is applicable to any organization or part thereof, regardless of type, size, or the nature of its activities.

Constitutionalism addresses the question of government legitimacy, considering both descriptive analyses of constitutional arrangements and prescriptive standards for how power ought to be exercised. Within the American tradition, constitutionalism identifies the sources and parameters that authorize and constrain governmental authority. Scholar Gordon S. Wood traces a lineage of advanced constitutional thought to the idea that a constitution functions as a core set of rules by which even the state’s supreme power is to be governed, a notion associated with Demophilis and possibly George Bryan. Ultimately, American constitutionalism rests on the collective sovereignty of the people as the source of government legitimacy.

Following the deposition of the democratically elected Dominican president Juan Bosch, the Constitutionalist movement emerged in opposition to the new regime, alongside an anti-constitutionalist faction. Bosch subsequently went into exile in Puerto Rico. The movement’s initial leader was Colonel Rafael Tomás Fernández Domínguez, who advocated Bosch’s return to power; Fernández Domínguez himself was later exiled to Puerto Rico, where Bosch resided. Eventually, the Constitutionalists elected a new leader, Colonel Francisco Alberto Caamaño Deñó.

Hayden released his second album, The Closer I Get, in 1998, which was produced by Steve Fisk, John Hanlon, and Scott Litt. To promote the record, he undertook a North American tour with a full band, including Josh Malinsky, Mitch Roth (of Poledo), and Damon Richardson (of Change of Heart). Subsequently, Outpost Records dissolved amid the late-1990s decline in the commercial viability of alternative rock, leaving Hayden without an international label.

In 2001, Hayden issued an initial limited run of Skyscraper National Park consisting of 100 handwritten, individually numbered copies that were distributed to friends and independent record shops in Toronto. This was followed by a larger edition of 1,500 hand-numbered copies featuring professionally printed liner notes, predominantly sold at live performances. The favorable critical reception of these limited editions contributed to a full commercial release of the album later in 2001.
In the 1997 Sybase Open doubles competition, the defending champions, Trevor Kronemann and David Macpherson, were eliminated in the semifinals, losing to Mark Knowles and Daniel Nestor.

Book censorship in educational settings involves balancing access to information with concerns about appropriateness for minors. The American Library Association emphasizes that the school library is a core element of learning and is most effective when guided by a qualified librarian who prepares students for college, careers, and life. Despite this, libraries may face challenges from third parties who seek to remove or restrict titles they deem unsuitable for students. A key moment in the legal landscape occurred in 1982 with Island Trees Union Free School District No. 26 v. Pico, where students and their parents challenged the school board’s removal of several books from the district’s library. The contested works were described by critics as anti-American, anti-Christian, anti-Semitic, and "just plain filthy." The Supreme Court held that the removal of books from school libraries is permissible only when the material is deemed educationally unsuitable, highlighting the ongoing tensions between censorship concerns and the obligation to provide broad access to information in schools.

Book censorship is often shaped by political influence, occurring when a censor regards a work as politically motivated or acts with political motives for suppressing it. A notable example from Ireland in 1958 involved the banning of Borstal Boy by the Irish Censorship of Publications Board, which cited its critiques of Irish republicanism, social attitudes, and the Catholic Church. In England, Areopagitica by John Milton was banned for its philosophical defense of the right to freedom of speech and expression. These cases illustrate how censorship decisions can be driven by political considerations and concerns about ideology and liberty.

Bleomycin is associated with several adverse effects, the most common of which are flu-like symptoms—including fever, rash, dermatographism, hyperpigmentation, alopecia, and chills—as well as Raynaud's phenomenon, which can manifest as discoloration of the fingers or toes. The most serious complication is pulmonary toxicity with fibrosis and impaired lung function, a risk that rises with higher cumulative doses. The drug may induce sensitivity to oxygen toxicity, and proinflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-18 and interleukin-1β have been implicated in bleomycin-related lung injury. Clinically, prior bleomycin exposure should be disclosed to an anaesthetist before procedures requiring general anesthesia. In addition, owing to oxygen sensitivity and the potential for greater risk with supplemental oxygen, scuba diving after bleomycin treatment has been questioned. Bleomycin can also disrupt the sense of taste.

Bleomycin is a therapeutic agent first identified in 1962. It is included on the World Health Organization’s List of Essential Medicines, reflecting its significance in essential healthcare. The drug is available in generic form and is produced by the bacterium Streptomyces verticillus.

BBC Brit's programming is distributed exclusively through BBC Player Malaysia, the Malaysian edition of BBC iPlayer, and access is restricted to subscribers of unifi TV. In October 2021, BBC Brit content was expanded to subscription video on demand via Astro, a subscription television provider.

BBC Brit is a subscription-based entertainment television channel, offering programming that blends factual content with entertainment-oriented formats, and is wholly owned and operated by BBC Studios. The service was initially slated for an international rollout in 2014, but later announcements indicated a launch in 2015, beginning with Poland.

Alpha Sigma Phi is a collegiate fraternity consisting of 181 chapters and more than 8,000 undergraduate active members. It also counts over 72,000 living members among its alumni. The organization is a member of the North American Interfraternity Conference.

Alpha Sigma Phi has been recognized by the North American Interfraternity Conference with two Laurel Wreath Awards. In 2006, the fraternity received the Laurel Wreath Award for its Ralph F. Burns Leadership Institute for new members. A decade later, in 2016, it earned the award again for its educational initiative, Toastmasters' Lite, which provides undergraduate brothers the opportunity to learn and practice public speaking skills.

On 20 May 2017, The Telegraph reported that the BBC Store would be closing. A subsequent BBC announcement on 25 May 2017 confirmed that the service would shut down on 1 November 2017. It was stated that all customers would receive a full refund of money paid for programmes, while existing purchases would remain viewable until the closing date of 1 November 2017.

BBC Store was launched as the BBC's digital storefront for on-demand content, while the BBC Shop for the UK’s physical and online retail operations closed on 29 March 2016. The online shop serving customers in the United States and Canada continues to operate. In November 2017, BBC Director-General Tony Hall stated that the download-to-own model had been an experimental venture and had been phased out promptly. Since then, the BBC has pursued a video-on-demand subscription service model modeled on Netflix, rather than a buy-to-own framework.

The Taiwan Entry Permit (入臺證) is an official entry permit issued by Taiwan’s National Immigration Agency. Formally named the Exit & Entry Permit Taiwan Republic of China, it is designated for Chinese citizens from mainland China, as well as those from Hong Kong and Macau, and it authorizes both entry into and exit from the Taiwan Area.

Under Taiwan's tourism entry policy, individuals born in Hong Kong or Macau are exempt from the requirement to obtain a Taiwan Entry Permit for tourism purposes. Those born in Hong Kong or Macau are automatically eligible for either the no-fee entry permit or the permit-on-arrival service, with eligibility based on birthplace rather than nationality.

Sankei Shimbun is a daily national newspaper published in Japan by Sankei Shimbun Co., Ltd. Its full Japanese name is Sangyō Keizai Shinbun (産業経済新聞), meaning "Industrial and Economic News." The publication ranks among the five most widely circulated newspapers in the country. In addition to its Japanese edition, the English-language newspaper Japan Forward serves as its sister publication; together, the two outlets have been described by some observers as conservative, nationalist, and ranging from right-wing to far-right. The Sankei Shimbun has also published materials that downplayed or denied Japanese war crimes, a stance that has attracted controversy.

Sankei Shimbun is a Japanese national daily newspaper that supports cultural activities, including the Sankei International Calligraphic Art Exhibition (Sankei Kokusai Sho-Ten; 産経国際書展). Founded in 1984, the exhibition is recognized as a major award in the field of kanji calligraphy, highlighting notable achievements in Japanese brush script.

In 1935 the Los Angeles Times relocated its headquarters to a newly built Art Deco structure known as the Los Angeles Times Building. Over the following years the facility expanded with additional amenities until it entirely occupied the city block bounded by Spring, Broadway, First, and Second streets. The block came to be known as Times Mirror Square and served as the newspaper's home until 2018. Harry Chandler, then president and general manager of Times-Mirror Co., described the building as a monument to the progress of the city and Southern California.

Bettina Boxall and Julie Cart of the Los Angeles Times received the 2009 Pulitzer Prize for Explanatory Reporting in recognition of their in‑depth analysis of the costs and effectiveness of wildfire suppression efforts in the western United States. Their reporting explored the escalating threat posed by wildfires across the region, evaluating how suppression strategies performed in practice and considering the broader implications for public policy and fire management.

Jean Baudrillard was born on 27 July 1929 in Reims, in northeastern France. His grandparents were farm workers and his father served as a gendarme. While in a Reims lycée for his high school education, he was introduced to pataphysics by philosophy professor Emmanuel Peillet (1914–1973), an exposure that is regarded as influential for his later thought. He became the first in his family to attend university, moving to Paris to study at the Sorbonne where he pursued German language and literature. From 1960 to 1966 he taught German at several lycées in Paris and in the provinces.

Jean Baudrillard has been the subject of sustained critical analysis, including work by Douglas Kellner, a Frankfurt School–critical theorist who authored Jean Baudrillard: From Marxism to Postmodernism and Beyond. Kellner investigates Baudrillard's relationship to postmodernism as an ongoing, uneasy, and rarely explicit engagement, while also seeking to advance a Marxist counter to Baudrillard's ideas. In the broader debate on Baudrillard's connection to postmodernism, William Merrin published more than one denunciation of Norris's position on this topic, reflecting persistent scholarly contention about the interpretation of Baudrillard's stance within postmodern discourse. Baudrillard himself described the Marxist counterargument as reductive, a critique that remains central to discussions of his thought and its political implications.

Tomasz Urbanowicz's glassworks have been featured in three publications, reflecting recognition within the field of contemporary glass and architecture. These include Colours of Architecture by Andrew Moor (London, 2006), Contemporary Kiln-formed Glass by Keith Cummings (London/Philadelphia, 2009), and Szkło we Współczesnej Architekturze by Ewa Wala.

Tomasz Urbanowicz is a glass artist noted for creating large-scale architectural glass installations, often working in collaboration with his son, architect Konrad Urbanowicz. One of his notable works, The Spirit of Health, is installed at the Integrative Medical Center Clinic in Żerniki Wrocławskie. Another project, EGG, is a glass installation designed for the concierge desk within the baroque interior of the historic Main Building of the University of Wrocław.

Numismatic Guaranty Company (NGC) is an international third-party coin grading and certification service headquartered in Sarasota, Florida. It has certified more than 60 million coins, with its services encompassing authentication, grading, attribution, and encapsulation in clear plastic holders. NGC operates as a subsidiary of the Certified Collectibles Group (CCG), which owns six collectible certification services. The Certified Collectibles Group is owned by Blackstone, a multibillion-dollar hedge fund based in New York City.

Numismatic Guaranty Company (NGC) began operating in 2002 at its Sarasota, Florida location. In 2005, world-class grader Ron Drzewucki joined as a Finalizer, later becoming a shareholder, and remained involved with the firm through 2012. In 2006, NGC relocated to a 60,000-square-foot secure facility that houses sister companies owned by CCG, including NCS, PMG, CGC, CSG, and CCS. The company expanded its services in 2008 by introducing ancient coin certification under the NGC Ancients program.
SpaceX CRS-19 (SpX-19) was a Commercial Resupply Service mission to the International Space Station conducted under a contract with NASA and flown by SpaceX on a Falcon 9 rocket.

SpaceX CRS-19, a mission conducted as part of SpaceX's Commercial Resupply Service program, was successfully launched on 5 December 2019. The first stage subsequently achieved a successful landing on the drone ship Of Course I Still Love You (OCISLY).

Paperity is an open-access aggregator of scholarly articles that, as of December 2020, comprises about 7.2 million articles drawn from roughly 15,300 journals. The collection spans multiple disciplines, including the mathematical sciences, life sciences, medicine, social sciences, and humanities. The platform offers full-text search functionality and RSS feeds, and it also provides a mobile application for convenient access. All items indexed by Paperity are available in full text at no cost, reflecting its open-access model.
Paperity is a multidisciplinary aggregator of open access journals and papers. The platform launched in October 2014, coming online with an initial collection totaling around 160,000 articles.

An editorial by Alice Marble published in American Lawn Tennis Magazine on July 1, 1950, endorsed Althea Gibson and urged the sport to confront racial barriers with integrity, calling tennis to embody sportsmanship and to meet Gibson's challenge on the courts rather than succumb to hypocrisy. Marble contended that denying Gibson the opportunity would leave an indelible stain on tennis and would be shameful for the game. Shortly thereafter, Gibson, then 23 years old, was granted entry to the 1950 U.S. Championships, making her the first African-American player, man or woman, to compete in a Grand Slam event.

Alice Marble was an American tennis player who achieved the world No. 1 ranking in 1939. Based on the world rankings published by A. Wallis Myers and John Olliff in The Daily Telegraph and The Daily Mail, Marble remained in the world’s top ten from 1936 to 1939, with no rankings issued between 1940 and 1945. At the national level, she appeared in the USLTA year-end top ten in 1932–33 and 1936–40, and she was the top-ranked U.S. player from 1936 to 1940.

Cloud Infrastructure Management Interface (CIMI) is an initiative designed to enable straightforward management of cloud infrastructure. By standardizing interactions across diverse cloud environments, CIMI promotes interoperable cloud infrastructure management. This standardization facilitates consistent management across providers and platforms. Stakeholders include service providers, their consumers, and developers, who rely on a common interface for managing cloud resources.

Cloud Infrastructure Management Interface uses a dedicated Use Cases whitepaper to catalog use cases that illustrate the challenges anticipated by infrastructure-as-a-service providers. These use cases typify next-generation issues faced by IaaS providers and are being considered for inclusion in the next version of the CIMI specification. Illustrative examples include Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery, Service Level Objective Management, Log and Metadata Management, and Multicloud Management.

At Lady Molly's is the fourth volume of Anthony Powell's A Dance to the Music of Time. The novel won the James Tait Black Memorial Prize in 1957. Set in mid-1930s England, it functions primarily as a comedy of manners, tracing the social rituals of Nick Jenkins's circle of bohemian and landed-class acquaintances. The work places its narrative amid the period's broader political tensions, including the emergence of Adolf Hitler and the worldwide ascent of fascist movements. A central concern is married life and the institution of marriage within this social milieu, as Powell maps how relationships are formed, sustained, or dissolved. The plot follows the career trajectories of a variety of characters, who advance, are checked, or are put on hold, providing a portrait of social mobility and timing within the ensemble.

Two Tolland sisters, Susan and Isobel, arrive as the meal concludes. Nick meets Lady Molly's husband, Ted Jeavons, in a Soho pub. The party then proceeds to Umfraville's nightclub, where they encounter Widmerpool, who is suffering another bout of jaundice, along with Mrs Haycock and Templer.

In traditional biographies, Aśvaghoṣa is linked to a northern Indian episode in which an elder bhikṣu named Pārśva seeks to propagate the Dharma by converting an ascetic. Pārśva travels from northern India and signals his arrival with the sounding of a wood-block. The ascetic questions the purpose of the sound, underestimating the elder’s debating ability but agreeing to a contest. After seven days, a public debate is held before the king, his ministers, and a large assembly of ascetics and brahmans, with the stipulation that the loser would become the disciple of the winner.

In Aśvaghoṣa's account, Pārśva opens by expressing a longing for a peaceful world under a long‑reigning king, with abundant harvests and communal joy, free from calamities. An ascetic becomes Pārśva's disciple and receives full ordination as a bhikṣu. Initially he remains skeptical of Pārśva's virtues until the teacher demonstrates mastery of the bases of spiritual power, the r̥ddhipādāḥ, after which he places faith in him. Thereafter Pārśva instructs him in the five faculties, the five powers, the seven factors of enlightenment, and the eightfold path. Ultimately the disciple attains mastery of the teaching.

C++ is designed to operate within a multi-language software landscape, enabling collaboration with other programming languages and avoiding the creation of a standalone, incompatible environment. The central aim is interoperability rather than isolation, supporting interlanguage communication and integration through standardized interfaces and compatible tooling.

Published in 1985, the first edition of The C++ Programming Language served as the principal reference for C++ at a time when there was no official standard. In the same year, October saw the release of the language’s first commercial implementation, marking the practical emergence of C++ alongside its widely used reference text.

In geology, a joint is a fracture in rock along which there has been little to no movement of the walls parallel to the fracture surface, with the distinction from faults depending on what is visible or measurable and the scale of observation. Faults show visible or measurable lateral slip between opposite surfaces of the fracture, a form of displacement that aligns with fracture modes II and III (shear) behavior. Joints can form by strict movement perpendicular to the fracture plane, i.e., opening normal to the fracture, and they can also develop through varying degrees of lateral displacement parallel to the fracture surface, which may be invisible at the current observation scale.

Nonsystematic joints in geology are fractures characterized by irregular geometry, spacing, and orientation, lacking the uniformity often seen in more orderly joint patterns. Because their shapes and alignments do not follow a consistent regional or local trend, these joints cannot readily be grouped into distinctive, through-going joint sets that extend across substantial distances.

William Boyd Carpenter (26 March 1841 – 26 October 1918) was an English cleric in the Church of England who held high ecclesiastical office as the Bishop of Ripon and served as a chaplain to Queen Victoria.

William Boyd Carpenter was the second son of Henry Carpenter, the perpetual curate of St Michael's Church, Aigburth, Liverpool. Henry Carpenter married Hester Boyd, whose marriage licence was issued in 1837 in Derry; Hester Boyd hailed from Derry and was the sister of Archibald Boyd, who served as the Dean of Exeter.

Wuhan University maintains a notable historical connection to China–Japan relations through a series of cherry tree gifts. In 1972, as Sino-Japanese relations were normalized, a batch of cherry trees was presented to Premier Zhou Enlai. Zhou Enlai subsequently donated twenty of these trees to Wuhan University. The university’s website records further donations: in 1983, biology professor Wang Mingquan, who had studied in Kyoto, contributed additional trees, and in 1992 a Japanese delegation donated more trees to the university. Collectively, these gifts reflect a ceremonial exchange that links the university to broader diplomatic ties between the two countries.

In 1926, a number of institutions based in Wuchang were amalgamated, including National Wuchang University; National Wuchang University of Commerce; Hubei Provincial Medical University; Hubei Provincial University of Legislation; Hubei Provincial University of Liberal Arts; and the private Wuchang Zhonghua University. The consolidation gave rise to the National Wuchang Sun Yat-sen University, a entity also known as the National Second Sun Yat-sen University.

Newspapers.com is a platform operated by Ancestry.com LLC, an American genealogy company based in Lehi, Utah. As the largest for-profit genealogy organization worldwide, Ancestry maintains a network of genealogical and historical-records sites, including offerings related to genetic genealogy. The company is owned by Blackstone Inc., which acquired Ancestry.com on December 4, 2020 in a deal valued at approximately $4.7 billion.

Newspapers.com is a digital archive service offering access to historical newspapers and related materials. It has been used by individuals researching family history, including a case in which a woman utilized vintage photographs found on the site to document eight generations of her family dating back to 1805, featuring an interracial pairing. The corporate parent, Ancestry.com, faced public controversy when it aired a Utah television advertisement depicting a slavery-era interracial couple. The spot drew criticism from media figures, including WBUR-FM/MSNBC news correspondent and law professor Melissa Murray, who contended that it romanticized slavery in the antebellum South. In response to the backlash, Ancestry withdrew the advertisement in April 2019 and issued an apology.

Within corporate governance, secondary stakeholders are typically external to the organization and do not participate in direct economic transactions with the firm. Despite their lack of direct market dealings, they are affected by the corporation's actions or can themselves influence those actions. Examples of such stakeholders include the general public, local communities, activist groups, business support organizations, and the media.

Stakeholder (corporate) governance examines how firms are steered to reflect the interests of various groups beyond shareholders. The framework posits that if shareholders held absolute control, normative considerations of stakeholder interests would carry little practical weight. In practice, power is frequently believed to reside with top managers, particularly chief executive officers, due to the structures and functioning of boards of directors. As a result, this arrangement is commonly interpreted as a transfer of control from shareholders to senior management, shaping the governance dynamics and the emphasis placed on stakeholder considerations in corporate decision-making.

Ressentiment is analyzed by scholars such as Mulhall, Ansell-Pearson, and Hughes as arising in situations where the formerly subordinate group defeats the dominant one. The concept encompasses disappointment that the tangible or symbolic rewards of victory fall far short of what the enslaved expected. The long-standing grievance rooted in enslavement can be intensified when the outcome is perceived as inadequate, thereby amplifying ressentiment and potentially giving rise to further manifestations of the sentiment.

Ressentiment is thought to arise in ages characterized by self-scrutiny and a lack of emotional dynamism. In such periods the society curtails creative energy and genuine zeal in those who display passionate temperaments. Individuals who do not conform to prevailing norms are subjected to scapegoating and ridicule by the majority. This process helps maintain the existing social order, resisting challenges to it. Consequently, it also reinforces the majority’s sense of superiority.

"I'm Not Alone" is a composition released in 2010. In that year, a songwriter identified as Harris received a writing credit on Chris Brown's single "Yeah 3x" after it was perceived that the two songs bore similarities. The credit arises from the belief that elements of "I'm Not Alone" were resonant with the track, leading to Harris being recognized as a writer on "Yeah 3x."

The music video for "I'm Not Alone" was filmed in Oslo, Norway, on 6 February 2009, under the direction of Christian Holm-Glad. The opening sequence features a young boy—potentially a young Harris—in heavy snow within a forest setting, pushing a sled that bears a toy bear. He establishes a camp, lights a fire, and cuddles the toy bear, which is later seen on the sled again before being dropped. The scene then shifts to a dungeon-like environment where Harris is depicted as a Frankensteinian figure, performing experiments on several female captives whose essences are combined in an effort to reanimate his lost teddy bear.

Dickenson Road Studios functioned as a broadcasting venue in Manchester, hosting a program that featured a number of prominent acts during the 1960s. The Kinks made their Top of the Pops debut at the studio on 19 August 1964 with You Really Got Me, and the Who followed on 11 March 1965 with I Can't Explain. Early performers included the Merseybeats, Gerry and the Pacemakers, Peter and Gordon, the Fourmost, the Small Faces, Ken Dodd, Val Doonican, Them, Cliff Richard, and the Animals. The Beatles did not appear in person because of building limitations; their performances were pre-recorded at Riverside Studios in London. There are no surviving archive recordings of the initial Dickenson Road broadcasts, and it remains unknown whether the earliest episodes were recorded. Photographer Harry Goodwin, born in Fallowfield, Manchester, captured images of stars at Dickenson Road in the 1960s, including James Brown and Stevie Wonder. Goodwin’s £30 weekly fee was regarded as a very low rate, with Mick Jagger advising him to seek higher pay, though Johnnie Stewart secured a compromise by granting him a weekly closing-credit mention.

Dickenson Road Studios, located in Manchester, served as the base for John E. Blakeley's expansion of Blakeley's Productions Ltd during the 1930s. Working from rented, unsatisfactory spaces, the productions suffered from limited production values due to the makeshift facilities. Despite these constraints, the studio's releases helped launch the career of George Formby, a prominent figure in British variety entertainment. In response to ongoing commercial pressures, Blakeley's films were relaunched under the Mancunian Films banner, marking a rebranding of the company.

The Thavung language, also known as Aheu, is spoken by the Phon Sung people in Laos and Thailand. In Laos, an estimated 1,770 speakers are reported, with the majority of Thavung speakers concentrated in Khamkeut District. In Thailand, about 750 speakers are documented, residing in Sakon Nakhon Province's Song Dao District, with villages including Ban Nong Waeng in Pathum Wapi Subdistrict, Ban Nong Charoen, and Ban Nong Muang. Overall, the language has roughly 2,520 speakers.

Thavung exhibits a four-way phonation system that pairs clear and breathy voice with glottalization of final consonants, producing distinct phonemic contrasts shaped by both laryngeal quality and coda articulation. In Pearic languages, a comparable pattern is observed, though glottalization affects the vowel nucleus rather than the final consonants.

Srah Srang, also known as the royal bathing pool or pool of ablutions, lies to the east of Banteay Kdei and was excavated to roughly 700 by 300 meters during Rajendravarman’s 10th-century reign. The site was later embellished by Jayavarman VII with a succession of laterite steps and a sandstone margin along the shoreline facing the sun. Surrounded by large trees, the pool maintains turquoise waters throughout the year, and the approach to the water’s edge is marked by steps flanked by two stone lion statues with ornamented Nāga balustrades. Historically, the pond served as a reserve for the king and his wives, and its central island bears a stone base that once supported a wooden temple used for the king’s meditation. Sunset reflections on the lily-filled surface have been described as a memorable experience, while today the water is used by local farmers for rice cultivation.

Banteay Kdei displays features associated with Bayon-style architecture. In the third enclosure, the eastern and western pavilions have roofs carried by freestanding pillars arranged in a cross-shaped layout, with an inner row of pillars supporting the roof. The pillars are linked to the walls by tie beams employing a mortise-and-tenon joinery pattern modeled on wooden construction. In the western pavilion, four central pillars were reinforced with temporary supports formed by laterite stone blocks. Buddha imagery decorates these pillars, though most have been defaced. The use of a temporary roof-support system on freestanding pillars indicates structural design problems encountered in temples built during this period.

Apple discontinued the 12-inch MacBook line on July 9, 2019. In the following years, software updates dropped support for its individual models: macOS Monterey, announced June 7, 2021, removed support for the early 2015 MacBook, which was subsequently added to the vintage products list on June 30, 2021, limiting service. macOS Ventura, announced June 6, 2022, dropped support for the early 2016 MacBook, and macOS Sonoma, announced June 5, 2023, ended support for the 2017 MacBook, effectively ending macOS updates for the line. On June 30, 2023, the early 2015 MacBook was moved to the obsolete products list, ending all hardware service.

With the 12-inch MacBook, Apple employs the San Francisco typeface for the lettering on the keyboard, replacing the VAG Rounded font that had been used on previous Apple notebooks. This change marks a typography shift within Apple’s notebook lineage, moving from VAG Rounded to San Francisco across its portable computers.

Lapeer, Michigan, has a name whose origin remains a matter of historical interpretation. It is believed that the first settlers from New York State introduced the name after transferring it from a similarly named settlement in New York, thereby carrying a toponym across state lines. An alternative account suggests that French missionaries named the community Le Pere, meaning "The Father," a designation that may have informed the town's early nomenclature. Together, these explanations illustrate the mix of migratory and religious influences that shaped the area’s early naming.
On August 15, 2012, a Powerball ticket purchased at a Sunoco gas station in Lapeer, Michigan, won what was then the fourth-largest Powerball jackpot, with an annuity value of $337 million.

The 1997 Romanian Open was an ATP Tour men's tennis tournament played on outdoor clay courts in Bucharest, Romania. It formed part of the World Series of the 1997 ATP Tour and marked the event's fifth edition. The tournament was held from 22 September through 29 September 1993. Unseeded Richard Fromberg won the singles title.

Dharmarajika Stupa exemplifies an Indian-influenced approach to early stupa construction, featuring a semi-hemispherical mound set almost directly at ground level. The monument is generally dated to the 3rd century BCE, placing it among the earlier forms of the structure in the region. It shares morphological traits with other ancient stupas such as Butkara Stupa, Manikyala Stupa, and Chakpat Stupa, which together reflect a broader tradition of stupa development in the area.

In addition to monumental examples, stupas occur in a wide range of smaller sizes. These diminutive stupas typically feature drums that are comparatively tall relative to the height of the dome. Votive stupas funded or erected by pilgrims can be less than a metre in height. Such small monuments are frequently arranged in long rows, sometimes numbering in the hundreds. An example location is Ratnagiri in Odisha, India.
Jenny Lake derives its name from a Shoshone woman named Jenny, who married the Englishman Richard Leigh, known by the nickname “Beaver Dick.” The couple’s six children died of smallpox in 1876.

Jenny Lake serves as a popular starting point for many day hikes and overnight trips. The Jenny Lake Trail circles the lake over a distance of 7.1 miles (11.4 km).
