The route is considered relatively easy, featuring a modest elevation gain of about 700 feet (210 m). However, the grade increases sharply once Cascade Canyon is entered, with elevation rising rapidly.

Jānis Rudzutaks was recalled to Moscow in April 1923 to serve as one of the Central Committee’s three secretaries, working alongside Stalin, who at the time held the post of General Secretary. In early 1924, Lenin’s Testament called for Stalin to be removed from that position. There were persistent rumors that Lenin intended to appoint Rudzutaks as the new General Secretary.

Jānis Rudzutaks, a Soviet political figure, was expelled from both the Politburo and the Central Committee on 24 May 1937 and arrested the following day, 25 May 1937. His detention occurred soon after the arrest of Red Army Marshal Mikhail Tukhachevsky. There are two differing accounts of the circumstances surrounding his arrest: a 1963 Soviet press report says he was seized during a lively conversation at his dacha, in the company of the painter Aleksandr Gerasimov and two other artists, while an alternative narrative claims the arrest took place while he was hosting a supper party after a theater visit, with the NKVD arresting all individuals present.

Historically, the designation "president" served as the ceremonial head of the constituent colleges within the University of Wales. In Cardiff University, Neil Kinnock held that office from 1998 to 2009, after which Sir Martin Evans, a Nobel Prize laureate, succeeded him in 2009. The practice is not exclusive to Wales, as several member institutions of the University of London, including Birkbeck, University of London, also appoint a president as their ceremonial head.

Within public higher education, the chief ceremonial officer is typically titled the chancellor. The International Islamic University of Malaysia (IIUM), however, uses the designation Constitutional Head in place of the traditional chancellor. This Constitutional Head is described as possessing the same degree and status as a chancellor, ensuring parity in authority and ceremonial functions within the university’s governance framework.

The Bakerloo line historically operated two northern branches, the current Queens Park branch and the Stanmore branch, the latter being incorporated into the Jubilee line. On the Stanmore route, Neasden depot served as the line's principal maintenance and storage facility. In 1979, the Jubilee line absorbed the Stanmore branch, and the change prompted the construction of a new Stonebridge Park depot to support the expanded operations.

The Bakerloo line is served by three depots: Stonebridge Park, London Road, and Queens Park. Stonebridge Park operates as the line’s principal maintenance facility and opened on 9 April 1979 on the site of a former British Rail power station. The London Road depot lies between Elephant and Castle and Lambeth North, and is connected to the line on the stretch between Lambeth North and Waterloo. The Queens Park depot is a small facility located at Queens Park station.

The 8th Congress of the Kim Il Sung Socialist Youth League took place in February 1993, representing a twelve-year gap since the 7th Congress held in 1981. The league’s most recent conference was held on 12 July 2012, ten years after the previous meeting conducted on 21–22 March 2002. The 9th Congress was convened for January 2016, twenty-three years after the 8th Congress in 1993.

Kim Il Sung Socialist Youth League was founded on 17 January 1946 as the Democratic Youth League of North Korea and functioned as the youth wing of the Workers' Party of North Korea. In June 1946 it joined the World Federation of Democratic Youth, establishing international ties with Marxist-Leninist and anti-imperialist youth movements. The organization was renamed the Democratic Youth League of Korea in 1949, and later rebranded as the League of Socialist Working Youth of Korea in May 1964. On its 50th anniversary in 1996, it adopted the name Kim Il Sung Socialist Youth League.

The Quebec City–Windsor Corridor represents Via Rail's central service region, extending from Quebec City to Windsor and constituting the busiest portion of the company's network. Via Rail provides intercity passenger service across the corridor, operating largely on tracks that are CN freight lines. In Via Rail's timetables, the corridor is identified as the principal corridor and stands as the most active part of the system. The corridor carries the majority of Canada's intercity passenger trains and accounts for the bulk of ridership. About 67 percent of Via Rail's total revenue is earned within the corridor. Prior to the formation of Via Rail in 1978, corridor services were operated by Canadian National and Canadian Pacific.

The Quebec City–Windsor Corridor formed a central focus of the North American theatre of the Seven Years' War, with settlements along its length playing a pivotal role in the conflict between Great Britain and France. These communities functioned as important strategic hubs throughout the hostilities, influencing military operations and administrative control in the contested region. At the conclusion of the war, the territories of New France, including the Corridor, were transferred to British sovereignty, marking a major shift in colonial boundaries. This cession was formalized by the Treaty of Paris, which resolved the war in North America and established the new imperial arrangement.

Turner demonstrated prodigious talent from an early age, with his abilities quickly recognized by peers and patrons. As his finances became secure, he enjoyed the freedom to pursue experimental approaches and to develop his distinctive vision. In his mature work, he employed a bold chromatic palette and broad atmospheric washes that gave his paintings an immediacy and luminosity. Art historian David Piper described his later pictures in The Illustrated History of Art as enigmatic, puzzle-like compositions that invite close examination. He was widely regarded as an artistic genius throughout his career. John Ruskin praised him as the artist best able to vividly and honestly capture the changing moods of the natural world.

J. M. W. Turner was an intensely private, eccentric, and controversial figure during his career. Although he never married, he fathered two daughters, Evelina (1801–1874) and Georgiana (1811–1843), with the widow Sarah Danby. After his father's death in 1829, Turner grew more pessimistic and morose; his outlook darkened, his studio and gallery fell into disrepair, and his art took on greater intensity. In 1841 he rowed a boat along the Thames to avoid census enumeration at any fixed address. From 1845 he lived in poverty and with poor health, dying in London in 1851 at the age of 76. He is buried in St Paul’s Cathedral, London.

Chinese varieties are classified within the Sino-Tibetan language family, a broader group that also encompasses Burmese, Tibetan, and other languages spoken across the Himalayan and Southeast Asian massifs. The idea of Sino-Tibetan as a genetic unit dates to the early nineteenth century and is broadly accepted by linguists. Nonetheless, the reconstruction of Sino-Tibetan remains underdeveloped compared with other large families such as Indo-European or Austroasiatic. Difficulties arise from extensive linguistic diversity, a general lack of inflection in many languages, and the effects of prolonged language contact, which complicate historical inferences. Moreover, a substantial number of Sino-Tibetan languages are spoken in rugged mountainous areas that are hard to access and often lie in border regions that are politically sensitive. In the absence of a secure Proto-Sino-Tibetan reconstruction, the higher-level structure of the family is not yet well established. As a result, although a top-level split into Chinese and Tibeto-Burman is frequently assumed, this dichotomy has not been convincingly demonstrated.

In Chinese, compounding often leads to a two-syllable lexical item, as the disambiguating syllable is generally dropped in pronunciation; for instance, the morpheme 石 participates in compounds such as 石膏 (shígāo), 石灰 (shíhuī), 石窟 (shíkū), 石英 (shíyīng), and 石油 (shíyóu). Many monosyllabic morphemes can stand alone as words but are more commonly combined into multi-syllabic formations known as cí, a practice that aligns with the Western concept of a word. A Chinese cí may consist of more than one character or morpheme, typically two, though it is possible for words to be formed from three or more elements.

Hengshui contains a Buddhist temple situated on the outskirts of the city, reflecting the religious heritage of the area. In the historic core, a bridge remains as one of the few surviving elements of the old town, serving as a tangible link to the city's past. Taken together, these sites help illustrate Hengshui's architectural and cultural heritage.

Hengshui is home to the Harrison International Peace Hospital, a comprehensive teaching and research medical facility located in the city. The hospital bears the name of Dr. Tillson Harrison, a Canadian physician who is regarded by the Chinese Communist Party as a martyr of the Chinese Communist Revolution. Harrison died in 1947 during an effort to transport medical equipment and supplies, and some of that equipment is kept on display in an exhibition room within the hospital.

Chris Young released the lead single "I'm Comin' Over" on May 12, 2015 from his fifth studio album of the same name, which was issued on November 13, 2015. The track reached No. 1 on the country charts in May 2015, giving Young his sixth chart-topping country single and his first since February 2012's "You." A second single, "Think of You" (a duet with Cassadee Pope), was issued January 4, 2016 and subsequently topped the country chart in May 2016. The third single, "Sober Saturday Night" (a duet with Vince Gill), was released June 6, 2016 and later topped the Country Airplay chart in March 2017. In October 2016, Young released the country Christmas album It Must Be Christmas. In late 2016, a fourteen-show I'm Comin' Over Tour was mounted to promote the album.

In 2013, American country music artist Chris Young acted as an ambassador for the CMA Songwriter's Series, undertaking engagements in Belfast, Dublin, London, and Paris with the aim of promoting country music to audiences overseas.

In EVE Online, players may begin by selecting an existing character on their account or by creating a new one. An account is limited to a maximum of three characters. New characters start by selecting a race from Amarr, Gallente, Minmatar, or Caldari. Each race offers three bloodlines, which define different preset appearances. Within these choices, players can further refine the character's visual traits to tailor their look.

David Braben, one of the original Elite developers, regards Eve Online as a reimagining of the 1980s classic rather than a direct successor to that game. In contrast, several of Eve Online’s developers, including John Cameron, James Cassidy, and Joe Chaney, maintain that the game constructs a world in which players can inhabit identities that would be impossible to realize in real life, offering personas that exist only in the imagination.

In November 2023, amid widespread layoffs at G/O Media, the Gizmodo sub-blog’s final remaining staff member, Angely Mercado, was laid off. Thereafter, no personnel were listed as employed on the sub-blog.

Following Gizmodo's return of the iPhone to Apple, California's Rapid Enforcement Allied Computer Team (REACT) executed a search warrant at editor Jason Chen's residence on April 26. The authorities seized computers, hard drives, servers, cameras, notes, and a file containing business cards. The warrant was issued under the direction of San Mateo County Chief Deputy District Attorney Stephen Wagstaffe. Gizmodo and the prosecution agreed that a special master would review the seized materials to determine whether they contained information relevant to the case. As a consequence, Gizmodo was barred from Apple-hosted events and product launches through August 2014, after which the publication was invited again to Apple's September 2014 event, titled "Wish we could say more."

An unofficial designation attached to the president’s spouse is used, with the titles First Lady of Tanzania or, when the spouse is a man, First Gentleman of Tanzania; these are not formal government offices. Until 19 March 2021, the role was held by women and referred to as the First Lady. The current First Gentleman is Hafidh Ameir.

In Tanzania, both current and former first ladies are commonly addressed with the honorific "Mama." Public discussion has intensified regarding the growing prominence of the roles of the first ladies and gentlemen of Tanzania. There have also been calls for Parliament to formalize the office of the first lady and first gentleman of Tanzania.

VESA Digital Flat Panel (DFP) is a VESA interface standard for flat-panel displays that defines a dedicated video connector and the use of digital TMDS signaling. It employs a 20-pin interface and the PanelLink data protocol for transmission. The standard traces its roots to the earlier VESA Plug and Display (P&D) specification, which was ratified in 1997. Although a later standard, DVI, introduced in 1999 and designed to be electrically compatible with DFP, attracted far greater adoption, DFP itself never achieved widespread use.

The VESA Digital Flat Panel connector was employed across several display models and graphics solutions. Notably, Compaq Presario flat-panel displays such as the FP400, FP500, FP700, FP720, 5204, and 5280 used the connector. In the graphics card segment, ATI Technologies offered the interface on the Xpert LCD and Rage LT Pro models. Additionally, the Oxygen GVX1 from 3Dlabs supported the connector.

Roger Federer entered the 2019 Australian Open as the two-time defending champion in the men's singles. He was defeated in the fourth round by Stefanos Tsitsipas, who went on to become the first Greek player to reach a Grand Slam singles semifinal.

The 2019 Australian Open marked the first time since 1982 that the tournament employed a final-set tiebreak in the men's singles. Under the new rule, the fifth set is decided by a 10-point tiebreak once the score reaches 6–6, with the winner determined by a two-point margin. The first main-draw men's singles match to utilize the ten-point tiebreak was the first-round encounter between Jérémy Chardy and Ugo Humbert.

The GNU General Public License version 2 has undergone judicial review in both Germany and the United States. In a 2004 German ruling involving netfilter/iptables, the court did not challenge the GPL’s validity but held that compliance with the license is required, noting that a defendant who did not accept the GPL would lack rights to copy, distribute, or publicly make the software available. Non-compliance in that case led the defendant to discontinue use of the software. In the United States, the MySQL v. Progress Software Corp. matter was settled prior to a verdict, and at an initial U.S. hearing Judge Saris indicated there was no reason to doubt the GPL’s enforceability.

SLUC is a software license published in Spain in December 2006 that permits all uses except military applications. Its authors describe the license as free software, but the Free Software Foundation contests this designation, arguing that the license does not meet the criteria for freedom. The FSF contends that SLUC infringes the GPL’s principle of freedom to use the software for any purpose.

Font sizes are measured in points on an international basis. The two principal point systems are the Didot point, used in continental Europe and about 0.376 millimeters per point, and the American point, about 0.352 millimeters per point. China employs the American point system. In China, a parallel numbering system for Chinese characters, known as zihao (字号), is also used. Zihao was introduced by an American for Chinese printing in 1859. The zihao values are listed in a table accompanying this article.

Following 1949, mainland Chinese type designers sought to reduce Japanese stylistic influence by developing typefaces that resembled handwritten Chinese characters. In the 1960s, the state-owned Shanghai Printing Technology and Research Institute (SPTRI) produced simplified-character typefaces organized into four principal families: Fangsong (an imitation of Song style), Gothic (a sans-serif), Ming, and Kaiti. The PRC government favored Gothic designs for their plain, unadorned appearance, which was taken to symbolize a deliberate break with traditional typographic conventions. SPTRI was privatized in the 1990s.

Within the United Kingdom, Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs (HMRC) employs customs officers who possess law enforcement powers in addition to standard regulatory duties. These officers undertake both uniformed enforcement, such as tackling the misuse of red diesel, and investigative work conducted by the Criminal Investigation Branch. Their authority is derived from the Customs Management Acts and the Police and Criminal Evidence Act 1984 (PACE), enabling them to arrest, search, and detain persons and goods as appropriate under those statutes.

Beyond the police forces, there are non-police organisations operating within the United Kingdom, the Crown Dependencies, and British Overseas Territories that have been granted specific enforcement powers. These authorities, while not traditional police bodies, are empowered to enforce a range of rules, regulations, and laws within their designated remit, enabling them to undertake compliance activities and, where authorised, impose penalties or undertake other enforcement actions.

Within the entry on The Garth Brooks Stadium Tour, the March 26, 2022 performance in Orlando, Florida, is noted as a representative instance of the tour. The accompanying set list reflects the songs performed at that specific show and does not purport to characterize the program for other dates on the Stadium Tour.

The Garth Brooks Stadium Tour was a concert tour by American country music singer Garth Brooks. It began on October 20, 2018, with a performance at Notre Dame Stadium in Notre Dame, Indiana, and concluded on September 17, 2022, after five sold-out shows at Croke Park in Dublin, Ireland.

Stiff voice denotes a phonation in which consonants or vowels are produced with a narrower glottal opening and firmer vocal folds than those of modal voice. There is no dedicated International Phonetic Association diacritic for stiff voice; instead, the voicing diacritic (subscript wedge) may be used with a symbol for a voiced consonant to indicate this phonation. In the Bru language, stiff-voiced vowels show tenseness in the glottis and pharynx without becoming creaky voice. Conversely, slack-voiced vowels in Bru are lax in the glottis and do not develop breathy voice.

In Mpi, a Loloish language, vowels contrast in phonation between modal realizations and stiff-voiced realizations. Across the language’s six lexical tones, a given word may be realized with either a modal vowel or a stiff-voiced vowel, indicating that the contrast operates at the level of phonation rather than as a tonal register system. For example, within the low tone, /sì/ denotes “blood” with a modal vowel, while /sì̬/ denotes “seven” with a stiff-voiced vowel.

Cloud database technologies rely on cloud computing infrastructure to host the data store and much of the database management system on remote servers. In such deployments, the majority of the DBMS operates off-site in the cloud rather than on local hardware. Applications that interact with the database are created by developers and are subsequently maintained to ensure ongoing functionality and compatibility. End users access these applications through a web browser and via open application programming interfaces, which enable integration with other software systems.

Michael Stonebraker built on the lessons from INGRES to develop Postgres, the project that evolved into PostgreSQL. PostgreSQL has grown into a widely used open-source relational database management system that supports mission-critical applications on a global scale. It serves as the primary data store for the .org and .info domain registries, illustrating its capacity to handle large, high-demand workloads. In addition, a substantial number of large corporations and financial institutions rely on PostgreSQL as their main data repository, reflecting its reliability and scalability.

On 28 February 1996, Abkhazia's Parliament adopted a referendum law that established the framework for plebiscites. The statute permits referendums to be initiated by the Parliament, by the President, or by a citizens’ movement that has gathered at least 10,000 signatures. In 1999, Abkhazia held two referendums: one to approve its constitution and another to declare independence. A 2016 referendum on holding early presidential elections was declared invalid due to low voter turnout.

In early March, approximately 150 candidates contested the 35 seats in the Parliament of Abkhazia. The election was monitored by non-governmental organizations from CIS member states, and by an observer delegation from Tuvalu.

In 1929, the Union of Romanian Jews held a congress that brought together representatives from across Romanian Jewry. At this gathering, the organization adopted a new statute. The charter outlined the Union’s objective as defending both the individual and collective rights of Romanian Jews, deriving these protections from the Constitution, national laws, and international treaties. The Union maintained a pragmatic political stance and refused to collaborate with groups aiming to establish a national Jewish party. Intensified internal political tensions during this period contributed to the formation of the Jewish Party (PER) in 1931.

Initially named the Union of Native Jews (Uniunea Evreilor Pământeni, UEP), the organization was founded in Bucharest on November 27, 1909. It conducted advocacy on behalf of Romanian Jews, dispatching memoranda to Romanian authorities and seeking international support, notably from France and Great Britain. The group also urged Jewish citizens to fulfill their duties toward the Romanian state, noting that citizenship had begun to be granted to Jews on an individual basis starting in 1879.

Military Occupational Specialties (MOS) in the United States Marine Corps are organized by a four-digit code. The first two digits identify an Occupational Field (OccFld), a broad grouping that collects related MOSs under a single category. The last two digits designate a specific job code within that field, pinpointing a particular duty or specialty. This two-tier numeric structure facilitates systematic classification of Marine Corps occupations by linking related roles through the common field while distinguishing individual positions by their unique two-digit code.

Within the United States Marine Corps, the inclusion of a Military Occupational Specialty (MOS) in the official list is contingent on its justification as a Billet MOS (BMOS) within the Total Force Structure Manpower System (TFSMS). This requires that the MOS is needed in sufficient numerical strength to warrant its status as a billet in the force structure. In contrast, MOSs that have no Table of Organization (T/O) requirement or that lack an inventory are subject to deletion or disapproval, reflecting the Corps' emphasis on standardized manpower planning and verifiable needs.

In 2018, DMAX, in collaboration with Eurosport, secured the broadcasting rights to the Winter Olympic Games for Spain. The same arrangement was renewed for the 2022 Winter Olympics, ensuring continued coverage by DMAX and Eurosport. This represented a shift from Televisión Española (TVE), which had historically served as Spain's broadcaster of the Winter Olympics, as DMAX replaced TVE in carrying the Games.

On September 12, 2016, the channel formerly known as Discovery MAX was rebranded as DMAX and expanded its slate with additional series and films. As part of the transformation, Discovery, Inc. acquired ownership rights to the channel. Concurrent with the rebrand, DMAX shifted its target toward a male audience, a move linked to the launch of DKISS, a sister channel owned by Grupo Radio Blanca that is aimed at women and is supplied with Discovery programming.

UKTV announced in October 2008 that its documentary service UKTV Documentary and the channel UKTV People would be rebranded in early 2009, as part of a broader brand realignment that had already seen the company’s entertainment channels renamed Watch, Gold, and Alibi two days earlier. The new name, Eden, was applied to the former UKTV Documentary and the rebrand took effect on 26 January 2009. Following the relaunch, Eden prioritized natural environment programming, with remaining documentary output redistributed to UKTV History or UKTV People according to their subject matter.

U&Eden expanded its programming slate in January 2024, incorporating reality series, game shows, drama, and history programming into its lineup. The newly added content is sourced from the entities U&W, U&Drama, U&Dave, and U&Yesterday. By early 2025, nature programming had been removed from the channel's schedule, with such content no longer broadcast.

Martin D. Hamilton was elected to the San Diego Board of Trustees on April 18, 1887, and was installed as president at the board’s first meeting. At that time the presiding officer was informally called the mayor of San Diego as a courtesy, although no official mayoralty existed. The office of mayor was reinstated in 1888, and Hamilton continued to serve as president of the board following the restoration. After Mayor William Jefferson Hunsaker resigned on November 13, 1888, Hamilton was elevated to acting Mayor of San Diego until the next election.
Martin Davis Hamilton (1855–1922) was an American Republican politician from San Diego, California, who served as acting mayor of San Diego after the resignation of William Jefferson Hunsaker.

Young's lattice is a combinatorial description of the irreducible representations of the symmetric groups S_n for all n in characteristic zero and their branching behavior. The irreducible representations are labeled by partitions, equivalently by Young diagrams. The restriction from S_{n+1} to S_n is multiplicity-free, and an S_n representation corresponding to a partition p of n appears inside the S_{n+1} representation labeled by q of n+1 if and only if q covers p in Young's lattice. By iterating these branching steps along a chain of inclusions, one obtains the Young's semicanonical basis within the irreducible representation of S_n with shape p, with basis elements indexed by standard Young tableaux of shape p.

Young's lattice is the partially ordered set consisting of all integer partitions, organized by inclusion of their Young diagrams (Ferrers diagrams). Named after Alfred Young, who advanced the representation theory of the symmetric group in his influential work On Quantitative Substitutional Analysis, the lattice reflects the combinatorial structure underlying that theory. Central to its study are the Young diagrams and the containment relation among them, which provide the fundamental framework for the theory. In algebraic combinatorics it is recognized as the simplest example of a differential poset, a notion introduced by Stanley in 1988. Moreover, it exhibits close connections with crystal bases for affine Lie algebras in the context of representation theory.

Johnny Kelly formed the metal group Patriarchs in Black in late 2021 in collaboration with guitarist Dan Lorenzo (Hades/Non-Fiction). Since its inception, the band has released three full-length albums, each built around a rotating lineup that includes various guest vocalists and bassists. A fourth studio album is scheduled for release on August 15, 2025, with Metalville Records handling the release.

Johnny Kelly has served as the drummer for Danzig, Glenn Danzig's self-titled solo project, since 2002, with a hiatus from 2003 to 2005. He recorded the drums for Deth Red Sabaoth (2010), the group's ninth studio album. He contributed to Skeletons (2015), a covers album. He played on two tracks on Black Laden Crown (2017).

ISO 21001, the Educational Organization Management Systems standard, is an international standard published by the International Organization for Standardization. It was released on May 1, 2018. The standard provides a universal management framework for organizations that deliver educational products and services, with the aim of satisfying the needs and expectations of learners and other beneficiaries. It concentrates on the interactions among the educational organization, the learner, and other relevant interested parties, guiding organizations in structuring and refining their processes to support educational outcomes.

ISO 21001 provides a framework for the management systems of educational organizations and for the bodies that audit and certify those systems. Since its publication, numerous educational institutions have adopted the standard and pursued third-party certification from conformity assessment bodies. ISO/TS 21030:2023, titled Educational organizations — Requirements for bodies providing audit and certification of educational organizations management systems, was developed to harmonize accredited certification approaches globally. The technical specification was produced by ISO CASCO/TC 232 Joint Working Group 58, a collaboration between CASCO (ISO conformity assessment) and TC 232 (education and learning). The initial draft of ISO/TS 21030 drew on the proprietary VET21001 Protocol, which is publicly available.

Santa Monica Boulevard is a major east–west thoroughfare in Los Angeles County, California. It extends from Ocean Avenue in Santa Monica, near the Pacific Ocean, to Sunset Boulevard at Sunset Junction in Los Angeles. The route passes through Beverly Hills and West Hollywood. A portion of the boulevard is designated as State Route 2 (SR 2), while the full length of the avenue was Historic Route 66.

Santa Monica Boulevard begins at Ocean Avenue near the Pacific Ocean, where its western terminus lies, and extends eastward to Interstate 405 as a densely developed commercial artery in the western Los Angeles region. Beyond Centinela Avenue, the boulevard proceeds northeast through West Los Angeles, Westwood, Century City, Beverly Hills, and into West Hollywood. It is a major thoroughfare with at least four lanes for most of its length, reflecting its significance in local traffic and commerce. A substantial portion of Westside car dealerships is located along Santa Monica Boulevard, underscoring its role as a key commercial corridor.

The directive aims to prevent and reduce adverse environmental impacts arising from landfilling waste across the full lifecycle of landfill operations, addressing contamination and other effects throughout its lifecycle. It targets pollution of surface water, groundwater, soil, and air, as well as broader impacts on the global environment, including contributions to the greenhouse effect. It likewise seeks to prevent or minimize risks to human health associated with landfilling. Consequently, the directive has significant implications for how waste is handled and disposed of, guiding waste management practices and policy in relation to landfill activities.

Under the Landfill Directive, EU Member States are required to report to the European Commission at three-year intervals on their implementation of the directive. The instrument also imposes binding reduction targets for biodegradable municipal waste (BMW), specifying a reduction to 50% of 1995 levels by 2009 and a further reduction to 35% of 1995 levels by 2016.

The President of France serves as the head of state and, in that capacity, is responsible for ensuring that the Constitution is observed. Through arbitration, the president secures the regular functioning of public authorities and the continuity of the State. The office is conceived as the guarantor of national independence, of the country’s territorial integrity, and of the observance of treaties.

The President of the French Republic, as head of state, exercises the diplomatic prerogative of accrediting French ambassadors and extraordinary envoys to foreign states, thereby establishing and maintaining formal relations with other countries. Conversely, diplomats from other states who are named as ambassadors or extraordinary envoys to France present their letters of credence to the President, who receives them on behalf of the republic and grants them access to the French diplomatic apparatus.

Elmer Snowden was the founding leader of the Washingtonians. He moved the group from Washington, D.C., to New York City in 1923 in search of engagements; however, the band struggled to secure bookings. Snowden then brought Duke Ellington into the ensemble, who joined the group. The pair recorded three test sides for Victor Records, none of which were issued. Ellington eventually assumed leadership of the band, whose personnel formed the nucleus of what would become Ellington's orchestra in later years.

Elmer Chester Snowden (October 9, 1900 – May 14, 1973) was an American banjoist active during the Jazz Age. In addition to the banjo, he played guitar and, in the early stages of his career, all reed instruments. Snowden made significant contributions to jazz in its formative years as both a performer and a bandleader, influencing the development of the genre. He also helped launch the careers of many leading musicians, fostering the emergence of a new generation of jazz talent.

Diacritics play a central role in Welsh orthography, where four marks—circumflex, diaeresis, acute, and grave—are applied to the seven vowels a, e, i, o, u, w, and y. The circumflex, the most common diacritic, denotes a long vowel and is frequently used to distinguish it from a related short vowel or semivowel; in Welsh tradition it is known as to bach ("little roof"), acen grom ("crooked accent"), or hirnod ("long sign"). By contrast, the grave accent is rarer and serves to shorten vowels that would otherwise be long. The acute accent and the diaeresis are used only intermittently, the former to indicate stress and the latter to separate adjacent vowels. The w-circumflex ŵ and the y-circumflex ŷ are among the most commonly accented characters in Welsh, though such forms are unusual in many other languages. These characters were until recently difficult to render in word-processing and HTML documents.

Non-Faroese accented letters are not added to the Faroese alphabet, with the standard orthography not incorporating such characters. Examples include é, ö, ü, and å. More recently, other diacritic letters such as š, ł, and ć have likewise not been incorporated into the Faroese system.

Sintra National Palace includes two remarkable kitchens, notable for their large scale. Each kitchen contains a continuous wall lined with ovens and cooking stoves, underscoring the functional role of these spaces within the palace. Rather than a conventional ceiling, an enormous pair of conical chimneys rises above the rooms, tapering as they ascend toward the sky and forming a distinctive architectural feature of the complex.

Sintra National Palace stands to the south of the Castelo dos Mouros and historically served as the residence of the Moorish Taifa rulers of Lisbon. The earliest reference to the settlement appears in the accounts of the Arab geographer Al-Bakri. In the 12th century, the area was conquered by King Afonso Henriques, who integrated the Sintra fortress into the royal domain and used it as a royal seat. The present palace results from building campaigns in the 15th and early 16th centuries, producing an architectural synthesis that combines Gothic and Manueline features with Moorish and Mudéjar influences.

MeatEater is an American non-fiction outdoors hunting television series available on Netflix, hosted by Steven Rinella. The program debuted on January 1, 2012, and is produced by Zero Point Zero Production. Its twelfth season premiered on October 12, 2023, with release through the MeatEater website and the show's YouTube channel.

Carl Zuckmayer pursued higher education at the University of Frankfurt after the war, initially studying humanities before switching to biology and botany. In 1920 he married his childhood friend Annemarie Ganz, but the marriage ended in divorce about a year later after Zuckmayer had an affair with actress Annemarie Seidel.
Carl Zuckmayer married Austrian actress Alice Herdan in 1925. The couple bought a house in Henndorf, near Salzburg, Austria. His subsequent play Der Schinderhannes achieved renewed success.

TechTarget, Inc. is a technology media company established in 1999. It is headquartered in Newton, Massachusetts, and operates additional offices in London, Munich, Paris, San Francisco, Singapore, and Sydney.

TechTarget was established in 1999 by Greg Strakosch and Don Hawk as a spin-off from United Communications Group (UCG), the owner of the Oil Price Information Service. In 2001, B2B magazine recognized the company by including it in its Media Power 50 list, highlighting its influence in the business-media landscape. Four years later, AdAge named CEO Greg Strakosch a Top 25 Newsmaker, reflecting his prominence in the industry.

Guanqiao station is an upcoming elevated station on Line 4 of the Guangzhou Metro. It is located in Guanqiao Village, Shilou Town, Panyu District, Guangzhou. Construction of the station commenced in December 2023, and the project is slated for completion by the end of 2026.

Guanqiao station is a planned component of the Guangzhou–Huizhou intercity railway, designed to funnel passengers onto the intercity line and with planning activities centered around 2020. In February 2021, the preliminary design estimate for the station received approval, and the project was originally scheduled to begin construction in the latter half of 2021 with an anticipated opening in 2024. A supervision tender was issued in October 2021 but was suspended in March 2022, after which bidding for supervision resumed in May 2022. By September 2022, officials indicated that the project’s bidding had been completed and that preliminary works—including land acquisition, planning, and construction approvals—were underway.

Sex therapy is practiced by certified sex therapists who do not engage in sexual activity with clients. The field is distinct from sex surrogacy, in which sexual surrogates participate in the exercises with clients to help practice and develop skills. In typical practice, sex therapists discuss and guide clients through sex-related exercises to be performed at home between sessions, while sexual surrogates may take part in the exercises with clients to facilitate learning. In some instances, therapists and surrogates collaborate on cases to address the needs of clients.

Modern sex therapy combines psychotherapeutic methods with medical management to address sexual dysfunction. Pharmacotherapy may include erectile-dysfunction medications such as sildenafil (Viagra) and tadalafil (Cialis) to enhance erections, and selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors like paroxetine (Paxil) to treat premature ejaculation. Sex therapists assist individuals and couples in overcoming sexual problems and restoring a fulfilling, active sex life. The contemporary, holistic approach seeks to understand a range of contributing factors—psychological, biological, pharmacological, relational, and contextual—for a comprehensive assessment and personalized treatment plan.

During early excavations at Hisarlik, Troy II was initially interpreted as the Homeric Troy. This misclassification arose from the site's monumental architecture, the presence of substantial treasure hoards, and evidence of extensive destruction. Schliemann maintained that Troy II’s western gate bore a resemblance to the Scaean Gate described in Homer. Later excavations established that the settlement dates roughly a millennium before the Mycenaean Greeks, indicating that the two cultures did not coexist.

The city of Troy is dated to have been destroyed around 1180 BCE, a period broadly associated with the Late Bronze Age collapse. This destruction followed the earlier dismantling of the Mycenaean palatial centers in the region. Archaeological examination of the destruction layer reveals signs consistent with an assault by an external force, including scorch marks evident on burned deposits. These findings contribute to the interpretation that Troy's final destruction was the result of a violent episode near the close of the Bronze Age.

Signum manus denotes a historical practice of royal monograms placed on the obverse of coinage, beginning in the 5th century with obverse monograms used in Byzantine and Roman contexts. The practice persisted in the 6th century among Germanic rulers, including the Merovingians. Early designs tended to be enclosed or box-like monograms. The first cruciform monogram is attributed to Justinian I in the 560s. Later, Tiberius III adopted a cruciform arrangement that combined the letters R and M to represent Rome, and T and B to signify the emperor's own name. Pope Gregory III is recorded as using the letters G, R, E, O.

Signum manus refers to a chrismon, or sign/monogram, used in this context. In the Merovingian period the sign was abbreviated as I. C. N. for in Christi nomine, while in the Carolingian era the abbreviation shortened to I. C., representing in Christo. By the High Middle Ages the form had further contracted to C., denoting Christus. Across these periods the symbol’s form diminished in extent even as its explicit meaning evolved from the phrase in Christi nomine to in Christo, and finally to Christus.

Systems management comprises functions to monitor and optimize performance, which can be divided into end-to-end performance measurement and measurement of individual infrastructure components. A growing sector within this field is operational intelligence (OI), which concentrates on real-time monitoring of events in business processes to support operational insight and decision making. OI is closely related to business activity monitoring (BAM), sharing many objectives in providing timely visibility into ongoing business operations.

Systems management often implements a licensed-user cap, establishing a maximum number of concurrent users permitted by the license. When this cap is reached, access for additional users can be blocked to enforce the limit. Some configurations, however, permit overflow beyond the licensed boundary. In cases where overflow is allowed, the system typically triggers a notification to the accounting department indicating that additional licenses should be procured.

Epanadiplosis, commonly described as narrative epanadiplosis, is a narrative device employed across diverse literary genres. It involves repeating the initial scene or motif, the incipit, at the end of the plot, known as the clausule. This deliberate restatement fosters the impression that the narrative is self-contained and circles back to its origin.

Epanadiplosis is a rhetorical device in which a word or idea recurs at the end of one clause and at the beginning of the next. The concept is illustrated in the film P.R.O.F.S., where a student asks for its definition and, in a concluding moment, Laurent Gamelon states the term, a scene in which he is shown standing beside a horse. Patrick Schulmann's films have been described as forming an epanadiplosis, highlighting a cinematic deployment of the device across his work.

Almeta Crawford High School, a proposed addition within the Fort Bend Independent School District, was conceived to relieve overcrowding at Ridge Point High School, which opened in 2010. Since mid-2020, Hightower High School has been enrolling students who would previously have been zoned to Ridge Point in order to address the enrollment pressure. Crawford High School is intended to divert students away from Ridge Point to help mitigate the overflow. The opening was planned for the 2022–2023 school year but was delayed to the 2023–2024 school year due to COVID-related construction delays.

Seven days after the high school's opening, on August 16, a student was arrested after a firearm was found in the student's backpack. The incident prompted increased calls for a greater police presence within FBISD.

Natural resources are components and phenomena drawn from the natural environment that are used with minimal modification. They possess a range of valued characteristics, including potential for commercial and industrial use, aesthetic appeal, scientific interest, and cultural significance. On Earth, natural resources encompass sources such as sunlight, the atmosphere, water, land, minerals, vegetation, and wildlife.

The 1982 UN World Charter for Nature argued for the protection of nature from depletion caused by human activity and called for protective measures at every level of society, from international governance to individual conduct, while endorsing the sustainable use of natural resources and urging that safeguarding resources be integrated into national and international law. Building on this foundation, the 1990 World Ethic of Sustainability, produced by IUCN, WWF, and UNEP, set out eight core sustainability values, including the protection of natural resources from depletion. Since these documents were issued, policy and practice have evolved to encompass the establishment of conservation biology as a scientific discipline and the adoption of habitat conservation as a practical approach to preservation.

Huangge station is an elevated station on Guangzhou Metro Line 4. It began service on 30 December 2006. The station is located at the intersection of Huangge Avenue and Shinan Road in Huangge Town, Nansha District, Guangzhou. The name is written in Simplified Chinese as 黄阁站 and in Traditional Chinese as 黃閣站, with the Cantonese Yale pronunciation Wòhnggok Jaahm.

Broadcatching refers to a method that operates independently of any specific technology or implementation, focusing on a flexible, platform-agnostic approach. In contemporary practice, it is widely applied to Internet television and Internet radio, enabling the collection and distribution of online media through various networks. Internet radio, in particular, is also described as podcasting or IPradio, terms that reflect its place within the broader digital media distribution landscape.

As of 2010, there had been no legal action taken against individuals who share TV episodes, a pattern that contrasts with the strong enforcement posture taken against the distribution of copyrighted movies and music by industry groups such as the MPAA and RIAA. This contrast suggests a disparity in how TV episode sharing is policed compared with the distribution of films and recorded music.

The US Holocaust Memorial Museum oversees a two-volume scholarly project that covers the Nazi camp system and its broader history. Volume I surveys early camps established by the SA and SS in the regime’s first year, as well as camps later administered by the SS Economic Administration Main Office and its sub-camps; it comprises about 1,100 entries written by around 150 contributors. The bulk of Volume I is devoted to cataloguing the camps, detailing locations, durations of operation, purposes, perpetrators, and victims. Volume II, published in 2012, is dedicated to ghettos in German-occupied Eastern Europe. Archival material housed at the Center has enabled post-mortem reconstructions of achievements, such as the work of Lodz ghetto artist Melania Fogelbaum and others, which would have been lost otherwise to Nazi extermination and total-war terror.

Researchers at the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum have documented approximately 42,500 ghettos and concentration camps established by the Nazi regime across territories controlled by Germany in Europe, spanning the period from 1933 to 1945.

Hoka, a footwear brand, sponsors a diverse roster of professional runners, initially focusing on trail and ultra-distance athletes before expanding to track and field, triathlon, and road running. The company maintains long-term sponsorship arrangements with training groups, including Northern Arizona Elite (HOKA NAZ Elite) based in Flagstaff, Arizona, and the HOKA Aggies Running Club in California. It was previously a sponsor of the New Jersey New York Track Club. In 2023, Hoka partnered with Runna, a running-coach app, and in 2024 formed a collaboration with The Mesa Marathon to support its annual marathon event.

Hoka (brand) was founded in 2009 by Nicolas Mermoud and Jean-Luc Diard, both former employees of Salomon, with the aim of designing a shoe optimized for faster downhill running. The company developed a model featuring an oversized outsole and enhanced cushioning to achieve greater performance on descents. The brand name derives from a Māori expression meaning "to fly."

The Italian hip hop scene emerged in the early 1990s, headed by the Milan-based group Articolo 31, whose sound was predominantly shaped by East Coast rap. Other early acts tended to pursue politically oriented themes, with 99 Posse cited as a notable example. Over time, 99 Posse incorporated influences from British trip hop, reflecting shifting sonic horizons within the genre. In later years, the movement produced a new wave of artists, including Fabri Fibra and Club Dogo, who contributed to its evolving presence in Italy's popular music landscape.

Within the landscape of Italian popular music, the jazz scene is anchored by two major centers, Rome and Milan, which host the most influential local activities. A considerable number of Italian jazz musicians have established residence in Paris, contributing to the international exchange of the genre. Among the instrumentalists, saxophonists Stefano di Battista and Francesco Cafiso stand out, as do pianists Danilo Rea and Stefano Bollani, while trumpet players Paolo Fresu and Enrico Rava are noted figures. Palermo maintains a lively jazz community, and Enzo Rao, a Palermo-born musician, has fused native Sicilian influences with American jazz forms.

Ecological psychology posits that perception is grounded in information present in the environment rather than in sensory stimulation alone. It emphasizes understanding what is perceived—affordances—through information itself, prior to considerations of underlying mechanism or the material implementation. Dynamical systems theory and complexity theory are regarded as essential methodological tools for examining the structure of ecological information. The Gibsonian approach remains relevant and applicable to cognitive science.

Ecological psychology is a framework that treats perception as the direct uptake of ambient, ecologically available information from the environment rather than internal sensations. Drawing on Gibson's perspective, it emphasizes understanding perception by considering what the head is within, rather than what resides inside the mind. The theory is information-based rather than sensation-based, focusing on analyzing environmental structure through affordances—opportunities for action that the environment offers. Organisms are described as detecting information that specifies those affordances, allowing direct perception of real, perceivable chances to act within a setting. From the 1970s through his death in 1979, Gibson highlighted the primacy of the environment and developed the affordance concept as central to ecological perception.

The Strategic Arms Limitation Talks were bilateral negotiations between the United States and the Soviet Union that culminated in the Strategic Arms Reduction Treaties, a series of agreements known as START I, START II, and New START. START I, completed in 1991, established ceilings on the number of strategic launchers and warheads and imposed additional restrictions on each side’s nuclear arsenal. START II, concluded in 1993 between the United States and Russia, sought further reductions on multiple-warhead systems and overall weapon counts but never came into effect. New START, the successor to START I, was proposed and ratified in February 2011, representing the latest framework for limiting strategic nuclear forces.

The Strategic Arms Limitation Talks II agreement, concluded in Vienna in 1979, did not receive ratification from the United States Senate, which cited the 1980 Soviet invasion of Afghanistan as a reason for its opposition; the Soviet Supreme Soviet likewise did not ratify the treaty. The agreement expired on December 31, 1985 and was not renewed. Nevertheless, both sides continued to observe its provisions in practice after expiration.

Verdigris River originates near Madison, Kansas, at the confluence of its two short headwater streams, the North Fork and the South Fork. It generally flows southward along its course. South of Coffeyville, Kansas, the river crosses into Oklahoma and continues to join the Arkansas River near Muskogee, Oklahoma, roughly one mile upstream of the Neosho River’s mouth. The convergence of the Arkansas, Verdigris, and Neosho rivers occurs at a locality known as Three Forks.

The Verdigris River forms part of the McClellan-Kerr Navigation System, which enables barge traffic from just north of Catoosa, Oklahoma to the Verdigris’ confluence with the Arkansas River. The system consists of a series of locks and dams implanted along both the Arkansas and Verdigris rivers, creating a navigable waterway for commercial use. This network links the Tulsa metropolitan area with the Mississippi River, and from there to the Gulf of Mexico.

Hans-Ulrich Obrist has been affiliated with the Serpentine Galleries and, since 2018, has served as the international programs advisor to Moscow's Garage Museum of Contemporary Art as well as the artistic adviser to The Shed in New York.

Hans-Ulrich Obrist curated the Swiss Pavilion for the 14th International Architecture Biennale in Venice in 2014. The presentation featured the concept by Lucius Burckhardt and Cedric Price, A stroll through a fun palace. The pavilion building was designed by Herzog & de Meuron, while the accompanying program was developed in collaboration with artists Liam Gillick, Philippe Parreno, Tino Sehgal, and Dominique Gonzalez-Foerster.

The Municipal Borough of Surbiton expanded through a series of administrative changes in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. In 1895, the parishes of Hook and Tolworth were incorporated into Surbiton from the short-lived Kingston Rural District. Later, in 1933, the suburban area of Chessington was added to Surbiton, having been transferred from the Epsom Rural District. A few years afterward, in 1936, Surbiton was granted a charter of incorporation, formalizing its status as a municipal borough.

The Municipal Borough of Surbiton retains the former Town Hall on Ewell Road, which remains standing. The building's façade incorporates the winged lion featured on the borough's crest. Following the formation of the Royal Borough of Kingston upon Thames, the Town Hall was repurposed for use as a Sessions House (courthouse). It is designated as a Grade II listed building.

In heraldry, cross quadrate refers to the practice of rendering certain ordinaries with squared ends. Generally, only a subset of ordinaries is shown in this quadrate form; the ones most commonly treated in this way are the cross, the pale, and the fess. Other ordinaries, however, are not typically displayed quadrate, with bordure and chevron among those that usually retain their standard, non-quadrate shapes.

Service of process laws regulate how service is effected, the licensing or authorization of process servers, the forms to be used, and the deadlines that apply, with substantial variation across states and jurisdictions. For example, New York may require licensing of process servers, while Pennsylvania generally requires service by the sheriff or a sheriff’s deputy, with Philadelphia permitting service by any competent adult. New Jersey, by contrast, requires service by mail after an affidavit of diligent efforts, accompanied by two copies of the pleading (one via regular mail and one via certified mail), subject to conditions related to the certified mail receipt or unclaimed mail. In practice, most courts at both local and federal levels maintain specific rules, forms, guidelines, and procedures that must be followed to effect valid service, and noncompliance can render service improper. Consequently, the defense of “I was not served” is a common affirmative defense, often successful where service procedures were not properly followed. Federal courts follow the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, which underpin and influence many state service-of-process laws.

Service of process in certain jurisdictions imposes day-specific restrictions, particularly on Sundays. In Florida and Tennessee, Sunday service is generally prohibited unless a court order permits it. Other states that restrict Sunday service include Maine, Massachusetts, New York, Rhode Island, South Dakota, Texas, Virginia, and West Virginia. Michigan prohibits service on Sundays on election days or at places of religious worship on Sunday. Minnesota prohibits service on holidays. In New York, service to a person who observes Saturday as holy time is not allowed on Saturdays.

Digital watches incorporate push-buttons that allow users to modify settings and modes. The arrangement of these controls is typically designed so that their operability is equally convenient when the watch is worn on either the left or right wrist.

Digital watches and other contemporary timepieces commonly present calendar information including day, date, month, and year. Mechanical watches may include complications such as moon-phase indicators and the tourbillon. Quartz watches frequently offer functions like timers, chronographs, and alarm features. Smartwatches and other advanced electronic watches extend capability with calculators, GPS, and Bluetooth connectivity. They may also provide heart-rate monitoring. A number of models rely on radio-controlled timekeeping to synchronize with standard time signals and maintain accurate time.

City in Fear is a crime thriller set in Los Angeles during a wave of murders of young women. The narrative centers on Vince Perrino, a frustrated, cynical, alcoholic, chain-smoking newspaper columnist, and Harrison Crawford III, a wealthy publisher who has purchased a small Los Angeles newspaper agency. The killings serve as a catalyst for Crawford to enlist Perrino in producing sensational, front-page reporting designed to boost readership. The investigation follows LAPD detectives John Armstrong and Raymond Zavala, with Tony Pate, a dangerously unsettled grocery-store employee, identified as one of several suspects and shown to be the killer to viewers. Loosely inspired by the Son of Sam murders, the work explores themes of media sensationalism and the ways in which newspapers and television news can exploit a local crisis to drive sales.

City in Fear originated from a discussion between screenwriter William Goldman and producer Pete Masterson, sparked by Goldman’s realization that his 12-year-old daughter had attempted to dye her hair in response to Son of Sam killings blamed on dark-haired women. He was disturbed that sensational press coverage could intrude into the home and terrify his child, interpreting a dynamic between the killer and the media as a compelling subject for television. Director Jud Taylor noted that the premise illustrated how deeply women’s fear had permeated society. Goldman proposed the idea as a strong television movie to Masterson. Albert Rubin was hired to write the screenplay, and Linda Stewart developed a novel based on the concept. Delacorte published the novel under the title Panic on Page One, which drew positive reviews from the New York Times on October 28, 1979 and the Los Angeles Times on September 16, 1979. For the ABC television movie adaptation, Mickey Rourke was cast as the killer, one of his early major roles, regarded as capable of delivering a casual menace, exemplified by a bag boy in a Los Angeles supermarket.

Bobby Durham was an American jazz drummer best known for his work in organ trios with Charles Earland and Shirley Scott. Throughout his career, he led his own ensembles and contributed as a sideman on numerous projects, with many opportunities arising from his long association with producer Norman Granz, who featured him in performances with Ella Fitzgerald, Count Basie, Harry Edison, Tommy Flanagan, and Joe Pass. Durham also built a reputation for his dynamic scat singing integrated with his drum solos. In the 1990s, his work benefited from a renewed interest in acid jazz, which helped renew attention to his contributions. He frequently collaborated with pop and soul artists such as Frank Sinatra, James Brown, Ray Charles, and Marvin Gaye.

Bobby Durham, born in Philadelphia, learned to play the drums in his youth and at sixteen performed with The Orioles. He served in a military band from 1956 to 1959, and after his discharge he played with King James and Stan Hunter. In 1960 he relocated to New York City, where he performed with a range of notable artists, including Lloyd Price, Wild Bill Davis, Lionel Hampton, Count Basie, Slide Hampton, Grant Green, Sweets Edison, Tommy Flanagan, Jimmy Rowles, and the Duke Ellington Orchestra for about five months. While with Basie he met Al Grey and subsequently joined Grey's small ensembles. Durham later accompanied Ella Fitzgerald for more than a decade and also worked with Oscar Peterson in a trio setting.

Aswan is characterized by predominantly clear and sunny skies throughout the year, with little seasonal variation in sunshine. The city records approximately 4,000 hours of sunshine annually, a level that is very close to the theoretical maximum for sunshine duration. Consequently, Aswan is among the sunniest places on Earth.

Aswan is traditionally linked with the southern origins of the Nile’s waters, which in ancient conception connected the beginnings of Egypt to Swenett, the southernmost town identified as the starting point of the country. The town sits on a peninsula on the eastern bank of the Nile and lies immediately north of the Nile’s first cataract, a feature that stretches from Philae to Aswan. From this location, navigation toward the delta can proceed without encountering further barriers.

Direct-acting antiviral agents (DAAs) have been available since 2014 and are generally well tolerated with high cure rates. In the majority of patients, DAA-based regimens can achieve sustained virologic response within eight to twelve weeks. These therapies have markedly transformed the hepatitis C treatment landscape by offering shorter, more tolerable courses with high efficacy. Despite these advances, a preventive vaccine remains necessary to avert initial infection and limit transmission. Achieving complete eradication of hepatitis C is unlikely to be accomplished by DAAs alone, underscoring the ongoing need for a vaccine to prevent infection in the first place.

Hepatitis C vaccines seek to elicit an antibody response against the virus’s surface components. The hepatitis C virus is highly variable across strains, and it mutates rapidly, resulting in substantial genetic diversity and swift evolutionary changes. This combination of variability and rapid mutation presents a major obstacle to developing a broadly effective vaccine for hepatitis C.

Yangmei railway station is a station on the West Coast line of the Taiwan Railways Administration. It is located in Yangmei District, Taoyuan City, Taiwan. The Chinese name for the station is 楊梅車站, and its pinyin transcription is Yángméi Chēzhàn.

Yangmei railway station comprises two island platforms. A second entrance is under construction, and an overpass connecting the two entrances is also under construction, with both projects aimed at improving pedestrian access and flow.

Passive rewilding describes ecological change that arises when human management of land declines, allowing natural processes to restore habitats and wildlife without targeted intervention. In Peneda Geres National Park in Portugal, a historic stronghold for wild boar, centuries of agriculture and settlement reduced boar numbers, and by the 20th century both wild boars and ibexes had returned after previous regional extinctions. The district's winter villages around Castro Laboreiro have largely been abandoned, enabling forests to move back onto former pastures and clearings. Vilarinho da Furna, another Portuguese site, sits submerged under a dam and only reappears in drought conditions, illustrating how changing water regimes interact with landscape recovery. In Vatheia, Greece, the settlement is largely depopulated, with vegetation growing inside some towers and the church, a sign of ecological succession in a landscape freed from intensive human use.

Passive rewilding is illustrated by several Spanish sites where natural processes have gradually reclaimed former human settlements. Aldea da Barca, in the Ourense province of Galicia, was abandoned in the 1980s and has since become overgrown, with vegetation obscuring roads and building facades. In Turruncún, a village in La Rioja, abandonment has allowed nature to advance, slowly reclaiming the site. Belchite, in the province of Zaragoza, Aragon, preserves an abandoned old town where weeds have penetrated the cracks and crevices of remaining structures. Taken together, these examples demonstrate how passive rewilding operates, with ecosystems gradually reasserting themselves on landscapes once shaped by people.

During the 1990s, a wave of clubs dedicated to garage music opened across the United Kingdom, fostering the emergence of prominent scenes in Birmingham, Manchester, Bristol, and other university towns. By 1996, the UK garage movement extended beyond the mainland club circuit to popular holiday destinations, with scenes established in Ayia Napa, Ibiza, and Faliraki, reflecting its broadened appeal among international partygoers.

In 2022, Harris County jails experienced assault rates that were higher than those observed in other large Texas jail systems, and the rate of prisoner deaths increased over the year. According to Lucio Vasquez of Houston Public Media, Texas Senate Bill 6, which curtailed many cashless bail options, may have contributed to overcrowding and the resulting fatalities. By October 2022, the jail complex housed more than 10,000 inmates, and by November 2022, 24 inmates had died in custody in that year within the same complex.

Harris County, Texas jails refer to the county's detention facilities and have been described publicly as among the most violent and deadly in the United States. The system has a long history of guards assaulting prisoners to death and failures to protect inmates from violence. Solitary confinement has been used as a punitive measure, and the facilities have faced criticism for allowing suicide attempts by vulnerable detainees. Reports have also highlighted medical neglect of pregnant inmates, contributing to widespread concerns about the treatment of those in custody within the Harris County jail system.

The Soviet Union national football team advanced from the group stage by finishing atop their group after scoring nine goals, demonstrating a potent attacking display. In the knockout rounds, they were eliminated in the Round of 16 by Belgium in a 3–4 defeat after extra time. Despite an overall underwhelming showing in the tournament, the team remains the most prolific World Cup side produced by the Soviet Union, having netted 12 goals in World Cup play.

The Soviet Union national football team achieved its best European result by finishing as runners-up at Euro 1972; however, the remainder of the 1970s was characterized by a decline in form. The side was disqualified from the 1974 World Cup after refusing to play Chile in the aftermath of the 1973 Chilean coup d'état. Thereafter, it failed to qualify for the 1976 European Championship, the 1978 World Cup, and the 1980 European Championship, reflecting a prolonged period of missed opportunities for the national team during that era.

AOL Active Virus Shield was released to the public as a free antivirus solution by AOL. The product integrates features that are also found in Kaspersky Anti-Virus, with its primary capability centered on malware scanning that utilizes Kaspersky's underlying engine. It is capable of detecting a range of malicious software, including viruses, spyware, and prank programs. In addition, it provides real-time protection through ongoing scanning of files and e-mail, helping to block threats as they arise.

AOL Active Virus Shield (AVS) was a no-cost antivirus utility distributed by AOL for personal computers. Its underlying scan engine was derived from the core technology used in Kaspersky Anti-Virus, adapted for AOL's product. The program has since been discontinued and is no longer available to users.
Alexandre Alexandrovich Mnouchkine (Russian: Алекса́ндр Алекса́ндрович Мну́шкин; 10 February 1908 – 3 April 1993) was a Russian-born French film producer.

Alexandre Mnouchkine moved to Paris in 1925 and entered the cinema in 1932, later founding Ariane Films in 1945. He was married twice, with his second wife being the comedian Simone Renant, and he is the father of Ariane Mnouchkine. He also served on the jury of the 15th Moscow International Film Festival in 1987.

During the era of large-scale sailing ships, vessels commonly spent time at an anchorage, waiting at anchor for favorable wind conditions to emerge. The interval served to enable the voyage to proceed once wind patterns shifted in a beneficial direction, allowing the next leg of the journey to commence. Thus, anchorage functioned as a practical interim station in long-distance sailings, aligning travel plans with prevailing winds to ensure onward movement.

An anchorage, in maritime usage, refers to a designated location where ships can drop anchor and secure themselves to the seabed to remain stationary. Moorings, by contrast, involve tying a vessel to buoys or other fixed structures rather than using an anchor. The suitability of an anchorage is determined by conditions that promote safe anchoring, including protection from weather and other hazards.

The Himalayas arose from the collision between the Indian tectonic plate and the Eurasian plate. Uplift occurred as the uppermost Indian crust folded in nappe-like fashion, while the deeper Indian crust continued to push northward into Tibet, thickening the plateau; concurrently, the lower crust and the underlying mantle were subducted beneath Eurasia. The range extends roughly 2,400 km in a west-northwest to east-southeast arc. Its western end is anchored by Nanga Parbat, located just south of the Indus river’s northern bend, while its eastern end reaches Namcha Barwa, just west of the major bend of the Yarlung Tsangpo. The Indus–Yarlung suture zone forms the boundary between the Himalayas and the Tibetan plateau and lies adjacent to the Karakoram, Hindu Kush, and Transhimalaya regions, with the headwaters of the Indus and Yarlung rivers coursing along it. The width of the range varies from about 350 kilometers in the west to about 151 kilometers in the east.

Western rivers coalesce to form the Indus Basin, and the Indus River itself delineates the northern and western boundaries of the Himalayas. The river originates in Tibet at the confluence of the Sengge and Gar rivers, then generally flows northwest through India into Pakistan before turning southwest toward the Arabian Sea. Along its course it is nourished by major tributaries draining the southern slopes of the Himalayas—Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Sutlej—collectively known as the five rivers of the Punjab.

As evening fell, the combatants withdrew in relatively orderly fashion, and French artillery and other matériel passed into the hands of the Prussian and Anglo-allied armies. The retreating Guards were enveloped by thousands of fleeing French troops, while Coalition cavalry harried the fugitives for several hours, continuing until about 23:00, with General Gneisenau pressing on as far as Genappe before ordering a halt. At Genappe, Napoleon's abandoned carriage was captured, its contents including an annotated copy of Machiavelli's The Prince and a cache of diamonds, which subsequently became part of King Friedrich Wilhelm of Prussia's crown jewels. Major Keller of the F/15th earned the Pour le Mérite with oak leaves for the feat. By that time, the Allies had also taken 78 guns and about 2,000 prisoners, among them additional generals.

On the night of 15 June, Wellington remained uncertain whether the Charleroi attack constituted the main French thrust. In the early hours of 16 June, at the Duchess of Richmond's ball, he learned from the Prince of Orange of Napoleon's rapid advance toward the allied position, and accordingly ordered the army to concentrate at Quatre-Bras. There, the Dutch-Belgian forces under the Prince of Orange, reinforced by the brigade of Prince Bernhard of Saxe-Weimar, occupied a precarious stance against Ney's left wing. The actions of Prince Bernhard and General Perponcher, who were better informed about the French movement, proved pivotal in maintaining the crossroads. General Constant de Rebeque defied Wellington's orders to concentrate near Nivelles and instead chose to hold the crossroads, sending urgent messages to the prince and Perponcher. This episode illustrates Wellington's disbelief in a rapid French move toward Brussels and his mistrust of certain intelligence, including reports from General Dörnberg about French outposts south of Charleroi and from the Prussian First Corps. Had the two generals complied with his instructions, Quatre-Bras might have fallen to the French, potentially enabling them to support Napoleon's attack on the Prussians at Sombreffe via the swift cobbled road and possibly altering the campaign's outcome.

Hex maps employ a tiling of regular hexagons in which the centers of all immediately neighboring cells are at an equal distance from the central cell. This uniform adjacency distance stands in contrast to square grids, where diagonal neighbors are farther away than edge-adjacent ones by a factor of sqrt(2). The equal-distance property is advantageous for movement measurement in games, since each step to a neighboring cell corresponds to the same distance. In such maps, neighboring cells share a common edge rather than meeting only at a corner, ensuring there is no corner-only contact among adjacent hexes.

Hex maps have figured prominently in the history of strategy gaming, with early examples including Nobunaga's Ambition (1983), Military Madness (1989) which is the first in the Nectaris series, and Master of Monsters (1991). A hex-based variant of Civilization was considered during development but ultimately abandoned, as developers argued the concept was not yet ready for players and perceived as too unconventional; the series' initial four main installments used square grids, while later entries shifted to hex tiles starting with Civilization V and continuing through Civilization VI and Civilization VII. Beyond the Civilization line, several other titles employ hex maps, such as The Battle for Wesnoth, Dragon Age Journeys, Heroes of Might and Magic III, Forge of Empires, and UniWar.

String Lake, located in Grand Teton National Park, was part of a 2005 assessment of the park’s lake water quality. The study found that the lakes examined, including String Lake, remained pristine and had not been affected by air or water pollution.

Timberline Lake lies at the head of Stewart’s Draw, within the cirque formed by Buck Mountain and Static Peak. A trail that is not maintained connects the Death Canyon trailhead area to the lake, reflecting limited infrastructure in the surrounding terrain. The site is principally frequented by climbers attempting Buck Mountain through its East Ridge or East Face, underscoring its role as a staging point for ascents.

MobaHO!, the satellite's former owner, entered bankruptcy, after which the spacecraft was sold in 2013 to Asia Broadcasting Satellite (ABS) of China. It was relocated to the 75° East orbital position and redesignated ABS 2i, and it was later renamed ABS 4 (Mobisat).

MobaHo! operated music channels that were largely produced in-house. The service specialized in popular genres presented in Japanese and Korean to serve their respective regional markets. It also aggregated programming from several commercial and non-commercial FM stations on the U.S. West Coast that broadcast English-language music, including American pop, hip-hop, jazz, and various forms of both old and contemporary rock. In its later phase, MobaHo! carried WQXR, New York City's classical music station, which at that time was America's highest-rated classical station and was owned by the New York Times.

The Mangyan languages comprise a set of mutually unintelligible but related tongues spoken by the Mangyan peoples of Mindoro, with some shared vocabulary and the languages written in the Hanunó’o script. Among them, Tawbuid and Buhid are particularly closely related. A distinctive feature within this group is the presence of an /f/ phoneme, a rarity among Philippine languages. Tawbuid is divided into eastern and western dialects, the latter of which is described as lacking glottal phonemes, having neither /h/ nor /ʔ/. The term damuong is used by the Mangyan to refer to lowlanders who reside in the surrounding suburbs and plains.

Among the Mangyan peoples, traditional religious beliefs are predominantly animistic. Approximately ten percent have embraced Christianity, including Catholic and Evangelical Protestant communities. Translations of the New Testament have been published in six Mangyan languages.

Historically, the Federal Communications Commission required television operators to hold a First Class License. Presently, there is no FCC restriction that mandates such a license for employment in broadcasting. The Television Operator Certification examination assesses the knowledge appropriate for entry-level, non-technical master control operators. Consequently, a growing number of television stations require this certification as a condition of employment.

The Certified Television Operator (CTO) is a professional designation conferred on individuals who meet the certification examination requirements in the United States. The credential is administered and regulated by the Society of Broadcast Engineers (SBE). The CTO designation is protected by copyright law, and unauthorized use of the title without consent from the SBE may result in legal action.

Ɩ, the Latin capital letter Iota, has been adopted as a distinct letter in the orthographies of several African languages, including Gurunɛ, Kabiyé, and Mossi. Its uppercase form is designed with a hook to distinguish it from the standard capital I, reflecting its status as a separate character in those writing systems. An accented italic variant, ɩ, exists as well, though in serif fonts this form is frequently indistinguishable from the italic lowercase i, which can complicate typographic differentiation.
