Latin iota was historically used in the International Phonetic Alphabet to denote the vowel [ɪ], the sound found in the word "bit." In 1989 the IPA adopted a small capital I, ɪ, as the standard symbol for that vowel, and the Latin iota subsequently fell from regular use, though it persists in some later publications. Additional glyphs have been employed for phonetic transcription, including the symbols ᵼ and ᶥ.

Art film is a form often linked to stylistic experimentation and thematic depth, and Terrence Malick's The Thin Red Line is frequently cited as an example within the war film tradition. In 1997, Malick returned from a twenty-year hiatus to release the movie, a war drama notable for its integration of poetic language and natural imagery that sets it apart from conventional battlefield cinema. The film earned seven Academy Award nominations, including Best Picture and Best Director.

Art film, a term used for cinema pursuing artistic aims and formal experimentation, reached its peak influence in the 1950s and 1960s, a period Roger Corman has described as art film’s greatest influence; after that period its impact waned. Hollywood subsequently absorbed lessons from European cinema and integrated them into its own productions, and by the 1970s Hollywood films carried a residual imprint of European art cinema. Over time art film evolved from European cinema into a broader world cinema, though it has often struggled to attain broad recognition. At the same time, Hollywood widened its aesthetic scope to address the conditions of image-making, film production, and the experience of modernity mediated by media. A new audience emerged through video stores, where viewers first encountered many art films. Some observers see potential for a rebirth of American art film.

Viewed in political terms, the Nixon shock proved politically successful, with public perception turning to view the government’s actions as shielding citizens from price gouging and from an exchange-rate crisis blamed on foreign powers. The stock market responded positively, as the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose by 33 points on August 16, the largest one-day gain recorded to that date. In its coverage, The New York Times editorial praised the President’s boldness, signaling broad media approval of the administration’s measures.

The Nixon shock refers to a series of policy actions and accompanying market movements in the early 1970s that collectively redefined the international monetary system. The Smithsonian Agreement, described by President Nixon as a major reordering of international monetary markets, sought to realign exchange rates even as the dollar’s value in the gold market continued to pressure its official rate. On February 14, 1973, the United States announced a further 10 percent devaluation of the dollar. In the wake of these developments, Japan and the Organisation for European Economic Co-operation shifted to floating exchange rates, a transition that was subsequently followed by most industrialized nations over the next decade. Under a regime of floating rates, the U.S. dollar declined by about one-third during the 1970s and was subjected to substantial speculation against foreign currencies.

Grange Corners is located in the northern portion of Ganges Township, Michigan, at the junction of 66th Street and 122nd Avenue. It lies at coordinates 42°34′39″N, 86°11′26″W, and sits at an elevation of 682 feet (208 meters) above sea level.

Ganges lies in the northwest part of Ganges Township, at the intersection of 122nd Avenue and Blue Star Highway. It is situated at coordinates 42°34′37″N 86°12′37″W. Interstate 196, which carries US Route 31, runs less than a quarter mile to the west, and the nearest access to the interstate is from M-89 about a mile to the north.

Some observers, including Crovitz, have argued that Craigslist's lawsuits were designed to suppress competition. On July 11, 2012, Craigslist filed a trademark lawsuit against Jameslist.com, a Swedish luxury marketplace. The action compelled Jameslist.com to rename itself JamesEdition. Jameslist.com is described as a Swedish luxury marketplace website.

Craigslist, an online classifieds platform, saw rapid growth in 2009, with more than two million new job listings added each month, positioning it as one of the world’s leading job boards. By October 2011, the homepage listings for the 23 largest U.S. cities collectively surpassed 300,000 postings per day in the for sale and housing sections. The site’s classified advertisements cover a broad spectrum, ranging from traditional buy/sell notices and community announcements to personal ads.

During the Middle Ages, persistent rumors suggested that Livy’s History had survived by being hidden in a monastic library in northern Europe, with possible locations in Denmark or Germany. A witness testified under oath in the papal court of Martin V that he had seen the entire work, described as being written in Lombardic script, in a Danish monastery. These reports were later found to be unsubstantiated.

Among the Periochae, some passages are known only through quotations preserved by later ancient authors. The most famous example concerns the death of Cicero, a passage whose transmission rests on a quotation found in the works of Seneca the Elder.

Confidencen, also known as Ulriksdal Palace Theatre (Ulriksdals slottsteater), is a historic theatre situated in the park of Ulriksdal Palace in Solna, Stockholm County, Sweden. The venue dates from the 1750s, and a restoration project began in the late twentieth century to preserve its legacy. It is recognised as the oldest Rococo theatre in Sweden.

The new theatre was completed in 1753, and in the same year a French theatre troupe visited the venue, reflecting early cross-cultural artistic exchanges. The establishment derives its name from a distinctive piece of furniture, the table à confidence, which inspired its moniker. Originally, the theatre could accommodate about 200 spectators.

General Dynamics sold its Canadair subsidiary back to the Canadian government in 1976 for $38 million. By 1984 the company operated four divisions: Convair (San Diego), General Dynamics-Fort Worth, General Dynamics-Pomona, and General Dynamics-Electronics. A 1985 reorganization created the Space Systems Division from the Convair Space division, and in the same year General Dynamics acquired Cessna. In 1986 the Pomona division was split to form the Valley Systems Division; Pomona produced the Standard Missile and Phalanx CIWS, while Valley Systems produced the Stinger SAM and RAM, and the two divisions were recombined into a single entity in 1992. Also in 1986 the Quincy Shipbuilding Division was closed.

General Dynamics Corporation is an American industrial and technology company headquartered in Reston, Virginia. It develops and manufactures advanced military equipment, including nuclear submarines, main battle tanks, and armored fighting vehicles, and it also produces Gulfstream business jets for civil aviation while providing information technology services. As a major defense contractor, General Dynamics ranks as the third-largest contractor among the top 100 U.S. federal government contractors and accounts for more than three percent of total federal government contractor spending.

Line length refers to the number of characters per line in a column of text. In CSS, a width set to 66ch fixes the measure at approximately sixty-six characters per line, because the ch unit corresponds to the width of the glyph for the digit zero (U+0030) in the element’s font. If the ch unit is not supported, a common fallback is 33em, given that, on average, a single character occupies about 0.5em. These conventions help maintain readable line lengths across different fonts and display contexts.

Line length influences reading performance. Longer lines support quick scanning, whereas shorter lines enhance reading accuracy. The optimal length depends on the reading task: longer lines are advantageous for information likely to be skimmed, while shorter lines aid thorough reading and detail retention. For on-screen text, researchers commonly propose a compromise of about 55 characters per line (roughly 55 cpl) to balance speed and comprehension. Some empirical studies have found that lines near 100 characters can be read more quickly than lines around 25 characters, without a loss of comprehension.

Thomas Cowling's 1933 paper, titled "The Magnetic Field of Sunspots," engaged with Joseph Larmor's hypothesis that sunspots are sustained by a dynamo process. In his analysis, Cowling demonstrated that Larmor's dynamo explanation could not account for the observed magnetic characteristics of sunspots, thereby challenging the proposed regeneration mechanism. The publication contributed to Cowling's strong reputation within the field of astrophysics.

During the 1930s, Thomas Cowling contributed to the theory of stellar structure by incorporating the roles of radiation and convection, independently of Ludwig Biermann. He developed a stellar model featuring a convective core enclosed by a radiative envelope, a configuration that later became known as the Cowling model through the work of Chandrasekhar. Beyond structural theory, Cowling investigated magnetic fields within stars, and he also classified the non-radial oscillation modes of stars, a framework that formed the basis of helioseismology.

Sports Illustrated covered the event and featured Leon Spinks on its cover in recognition of his historic upset over Muhammad Ali. Spinks was stripped of the WBC heavyweight title on March 18, 1978, for refusing to fight the organization’s No. 1 contender, Ken Norton. He subsequently signed for a rematch with Ali at the Louisiana Superdome in New Orleans, which took place on September 15, 1978, contested for the WBA and Lineal heavyweight championship titles. Ali emerged victorious by unanimous decision, regaining the heavyweight crown.

Following a unanimous decision victory over Earnie Shavers, Muhammad Ali agreed to face Leon Spinks, the 1976 Olympic gold medalist. The bout was pursued in part to prevent a fourth matchup with Ken Norton and to safeguard his WBC heavyweight title. At the time, Norton was ranked No. 1 and had defeated No. 2 Jimmy Young in a title eliminator in November 1977.

Alan Jackson recorded a cover of My Own Kind of Hat for his 1999 album Under the Influence. The track was not released as a single, yet it nevertheless charted, reaching number 71 due to unsolicited airplay.

Alojzy Jarguz (19 March 1934 – 22 April 2019) was a Polish native of Rogoźno. Known by the nickname Alek, he played volleyball during his youth. Jarguz served in the Polish military and attained the rank of corporal. He was married and had two children, and he died in Poland on 22 April 2019.

Alojzy Jarguz was a Polish football referee who officiated at the 1978 FIFA World Cup, becoming the first Polish official to referee at a FIFA World Cup. He was described by many experts, journalists, and fans as one of the premier referees in the history of Polish football. Throughout his career he refereed in Poland's top flight as well as in European competitions, including the UEFA Cup Winners' Cup, the UEFA Cup, the European Cup, and the FIFA U-20 World Cup, and he later worked as a referee in the Emirati football league. Jarguz retired from professional refereeing in 1984 and subsequently worked for the Polish Football Association.

Bank of America began an organic expansion in 2015 by establishing branches in markets where it had previously lacked a retail presence. The expansion that year targeted Denver, the Minneapolis–Saint Paul metropolitan area (the Twin Cities), and Indianapolis. In these markets, existing competition from other large banks included Chase Bank in Denver and Indianapolis, and Wells Fargo in Denver and the Twin Cities. The Twin Cities market is also the home base of U.S. Bancorp, the largest non‑Big Four rival to Bank of America.

The TC Energy Center, an office tower located in downtown Houston, Texas, was completed in 1983 and designed by architect Philip Johnson in the postmodern architectural style. It was formerly known as the Bank of America Center, with Bank of America ending its tenancy in June 2019. The structure remains a recognizable landmark of the downtown Houston skyline.

General George Joulwan comes from a distinguished military family and is of Lebanese Maronite heritage. He had a twin brother, James Joseph Joulwan, who died in 2013. He is married and has eight grandchildren. His family history includes a father who served in the United States Navy during World War I, and a cousin who fought with the U.S. Army in World War II and was captured twice.

George Joulwan served as a special assistant to General Alexander Haig during Haig’s tenure as White House Chief of Staff, with Joulwan holding the rank of major in the United States Army at that time. His assignment extended from May 4, 1973, to September 21, 1974.

Musepack provides the capability for sample-accurate editing, and the distribution package includes a utility named mpccut. This application enables lossless cutting of stream segments, with the cut points defined by the user’s selected start and end samples.

Musepack is an audio encoding format optimized for achieving transparent quality at approximately 175–185 kbps when using the standard preset. In the lower-bitrate range around 128 kbps, comparatively few optimizations have been implemented. Independent listening tests have found that Musepack delivers strong performance across both low and high bitrate settings, indicating its versatility for different encoding requirements.

In late December 2004, the United Nations General Assembly designated 2005–2014 as an international decade for the world's indigenous peoples. The primary objective was to strengthen international cooperation in addressing the challenges faced by indigenous populations. The initiative focused on safeguarding culture, advancing education and health, promoting human rights, protecting the environment, and fostering social and economic development.

Aboriginal rights in Canada arise from the long-standing occupancy and use of the land by Indigenous peoples, including traditional practices such as hunting and fishing within a defined territory. These rights are distinct from treaty rights, which are rights set out in specific negotiated agreements between Indigenous groups and the state. Treaty rights are enumerated in those instruments, whereas Aboriginal rights derive from Indigenous peoples' historical relationship to the land. Both treaty rights and Aboriginal rights are protected under Section 35 of the Constitution Act, 1982.

Pedestrian circumnavigation denotes completing a journey around the globe and returning to the origin entirely under one’s own power, typically by walking or running. The concept is defined by two prominent sets of criteria. Guinness World Records requires a minimum distance of 18,000 miles (approximately 29,000 kilometers) and the crossing of four continents. The World Runners Association, a small, specialized group within the ultrarunning community, requires traversing four continents in an ocean-to-ocean fashion and totaling at least 26,232 kilometers (16,300 miles), along with additional requirements, with no time limit.

The article concerns the list of pedestrians circumnavigators, detailing individuals who have completed or claimed to have completed a walk around the world. Attempts to circumnavigate the globe on foot date back to 1786, and from 1875 a significant number of circumnavigation attempts by ultrawalkers emerged. Many of these early figures were later regarded as frauds who exploited wagers and lectured about fictitious journeys. In later years, only a small number achieved legitimate circumnavigations. The first recognized legitimate ultrarunner to complete a circumnavigation was Konstantin Rengarten, and the most recent to succeed is Marie Leautey. The list includes those who have completed or claimed to have completed a circumnavigation on foot, and is organized chronologically by date of departure.

The Indian Express was founded in 1932 in Chennai by Ayurvedic physician P. Varadarajulu Naidu and published by Tamil Nadu Press. Facing financial difficulties, Naidu sold the newspaper to Swaminathan Sadanand, the founder of The Free Press Journal. In 1933, a second office was opened in Madurai and the Tamil edition Dinamani was launched. Sadanand introduced innovations and reduced the newspaper’s price, but continued financial pressures led him to sell part of his stake to Goenka in the form of convertible debentures. After The Free Press Journal collapsed in 1935, a protracted court battle with Goenka resulted in Sadanand losing ownership of Indian Express. In 1939, Goenka purchased Andhra Prabha, a prominent Telugu daily. The three dailies—Indian Express, Dinamani, and Andhra Prabha—were nicknamed the "Three Musketeers."
According to the Indian Readership Survey (IRS) 2017, The Indian Express ranked sixth among English-language newspapers in India, with a readership of roughly 1.6 million readers.

Julkinen osakeyhtiö is the Finnish term for a publicly traded stock corporation, abbreviated Oyj and pronounced [ˈoːˌyːˌjiː]. Such an entity may be listed on the Helsinki Stock Exchange, and its Swedish equivalent is Abp (publikt aktiebolag). In English usage, these companies are generally described as public limited companies or public companies, and the name may include the abbreviation PLC or the term Corporation. Notable examples include Finnair Plc, Remedy Entertainment Plc, Kone Corporation, and Nokia Corporation.

Osakeyhtiö is the Finnish designation for a stock company, equivalent to a Finnish limited liability company. In Finnish usage the standard abbreviation is Oy, pronounced [ˈoːˌyː]. The Swedish-language counterpart is aktiebolag, abbreviated Ab, which is sometimes used in Finland as Ab or included in names alongside Oy. Corporate names may combine the two forms, yielding examples such as Ab Company Oy, Oy Company Ab, or Company Oy Ab. Abbreviations for the designation appear in a variety of styles, including Oy, OY, O.Y., and O/Y. In English-language contexts the analogous term is Ltd.

Historiography of early Islam examines how the origins of Islam are reconstructed from a variety of sources, including a substantial number of references in contemporary non-Islamic writings. These early non-Islamic references have been collected and organized in Robert G. Hoyland's compilation Seeing Islam as Others Saw It. Among the initial attempts to analyze these sources was Hagarism, authored by Michael Cook and Patricia Crone, which was one of the first studies to examine external materials for insight into early Islamic history. Hagarism contends that these non-Islamic accounts portray a markedly different picture of early Islam than that presented by later Islamic historiography. The dating of several of these early non-Islamic sources remains controversial among scholars. Since its publication, Hagarism has been widely dismissed by academics as overly conjectural in its hypotheses and biased in its use of sources.

Within the historiography of early Islam, Crone defends the use of non-Muslim sources, arguing that although these works are hostile to the conquering Muslims, they can still provide valuable evidence when interpreted carefully. She notes that, from a classical Islamic perspective, these sources have often been dismissed as entirely unreliable, yet Crone contends that they have simply got many points wrong rather than being universally false. She also rejects the notion of an all-pervading literary conspiracy among non-Muslim Middle Eastern peoples to manipulate the historical record. A central point of her argument is that these sources misstate a number of the same issues, suggesting a shared bias rather than a single, coordinated effort to distort events.

Phocaea was renowned for its extensive maritime activity, and its southern trade is thought to have involved contacts with Naucratis in Egypt as well as the Milesian colonial network. To the north, its expansion likely included the establishment of settlements such as Amisos (Samsun) on the Black Sea and Lampsacus at the northern entrance to the Hellespont. Its western colonial program was particularly significant, giving rise to Alalia in Corsica, Emporiae and Rhoda on the Iberian Peninsula, and Massalia (Marseille) in Gaul (France).

According to Herodotus, the Phocaeans were among the first Greeks to undertake long-distance sea voyages, and their explorations extended to the coasts of the Adriatic, the Tyrrhenian region, and parts of Spain. The voyage impressing Arganthonios, king of Tartessus in Spain, led him to invite them to settle there; the Phocaeans declined the invitation. In response, the Tartessian ruler provided a substantial sum of money to aid in fortifying Tartessus by building a wall around the city.

An electron is held near a nucleus by the attractive Coulomb force between the negatively charged electron and the positively charged nucleus. A system consisting of one or more electrons bound to a nucleus is called an atom, and when the electron count does not equal the nucleus’s charge, the entity is a charged species known as an ion. The wave-like nature of a bound electron is described by atomic orbitals, which define the spatial distribution of the electron’s probability density. Each orbital is characterized by quantum numbers that specify its energy, orbital angular momentum, and the projection of that angular momentum along a chosen axis. Only a discrete set of orbitals exists around the nucleus, reflecting the quantized nature of these states. According to the Pauli exclusion principle, an orbital can hold up to two electrons with opposite spins, ensuring distinct quantum states for each occupied electron.

Experiments examining electron–electron scattering have yielded results in precise agreement with Coulomb's inverse-square law, indicating that the electron behaves as a structureless, point-like particle. In addition, Penning-trap studies of a solitary electron have set an upper bound on the electron’s radius of approximately 10^-22 meters, underscoring that any finite size remains undetectable with current techniques.

The article seeks to provide a complete inventory of National Register of Historic Places listings in Frio County, Texas. Frio County contains exactly one property listed on the National Register. That listing is additionally designated as both a State Antiquities Landmark and a Recorded Texas Historic Landmark.

Peregrine is a Turkish program designed to integrate the Bozdoğan and Gökdoğan missiles into the PO-III configuration of F-16 aircraft. Preparations for mass production began in 2022, and a first prototype contract for supply to the Turkish Air Force was signed in 2023. The project envisions arming F-16s with 25 Bozdoğan missiles, 25 Gökdoğan missiles, and 14 launchers, with first deliveries planned for 2025. The initial prototypes were delivered on July 28, 2024. In a February 2025 test, the Gökdoğan successfully hit a target aircraft.

Peregrine is a missile developed under a 2013 contract to advance its development, with its first successful flight test recorded in 2018. The system features a solid-state active RF smart seeker with fire-and-forget capability, and includes electronic counter-countermeasures, enabling all-aspect engagement and home-on-jam operations. It employs an update-capable tactical data link that allows lock-on after launch, and is powered by a high-thrust, reduced-smoke solid propellant with a fully electronic safe-and-arming firing system. The design emphasizes maximizing the probability of kill and incorporates a reliable fuze. The weapon is compatible with MIL-STD-1553 and MIL-STD-1760 interfaces and is designed for use with the LAU-129 guided missile launcher. The first variant lists an official range of over 65 kilometers, and the system is described as Gökdoğan-compatible with the referenced standards.

NuGet is a package manager that enables packaging, distribution, and consumption of libraries and tools built for the .NET platform and the .NET Framework. It is pronounced "New Get." The project was created by the Outercurve Foundation, which originally named it NuPack, and it was introduced in 2010. Since then, NuGet has evolved into a broader ecosystem that includes a free, open-source client application, hosted package servers, and a suite of software deployment tools.

NuGet is a package management system for the .NET platform that originated as a Visual Studio extension. From Visual Studio 2012 onwards, NuGet packages can be used natively within Visual Studio and Visual Studio for Mac. The NuGet client, nuget.exe, is a free, open-source command-line tool capable of both creating and consuming packages. When present, NuGet can be utilized by MSBuild and by the .NET Core SDK (dotnet.exe). The tool is also integrated with JetBrains Rider.

In classical electrostatics, the electric potential is a scalar field, commonly denoted V or φ, that assigns to each point the potential energy per unit charge at that location. The electric field, avector field, relates to the potential through E = -∇V, meaning the field is the negative gradient of the potential. The potential at a point can be defined as the potential energy U of a test charge q divided by the charge itself, so V = U/q and hence U = qV; because this quotient depends only on the configuration of the electric field and not on the particular test charge, the potential is a property that characterizes the field rather than the particle. Therefore, electric potential is understood as the potential energy per unit charge, acting as the scalar quantity whose spatial variation yields the electric field.

In the presence of time-varying electromagnetic fields, the electric field cannot be described by the scalar potential alone; the magnetic vector potential must also be included to fully characterize the field. Collectively, the scalar potential and the magnetic vector potential form a four-vector in spacetime. Under Lorentz transformations, the components of this four-vector mix, so the scalar potential and the spatial components of the vector potential transform into each other as parts of a single relativistic object.

Louis Roederer owns 240 hectares of vineyards distributed across the Montagne de Reims, the Vallée de la Marne, and the Côte des Blancs. These vineyards account for two-thirds of the house's grape requirements, a proportion relatively uncommon among Champagne houses and providing greater control over production. Of these holdings, 75 hectares are cultivated biodynamically, making it the largest biodynamic estate in Champagne.

Louis Roederer's Rosé Vintage is produced by the saignée method following a brief period of cold maceration, a process that concentrates color and structure through skin contact. The blend consists of about 70% Pinot Noir and 30% Chardonnay. Roughly one-fifth of the wine is aged in oak barrels and undergoes no malolactic fermentation. The Rosé Vintage cuvée then spends four years aging in Roederer’s cellars before a further six months of rest after disgorgement to reach full maturity. The Chardonnay component is predominantly sourced from Cumières, a locality situated on the banks of the River Marne.

Approximation is used when the exact form or exact value is unknown or difficult to obtain, and the available representation may approximate the real quantity with only a small deviation. A known form may reflect the true value with negligible difference. Scientific notation communicates precision through significant figures, which set the corresponding rounding interval. For example, 1.5 × 10^6 implies the true value lies between 1,450,000 and 1,550,000, corresponding to rounding to the nearest hundred thousand. In contrast, 1.500 × 10^6 indicates a higher degree of precision, with the true value between 1,499,500 and 1,500,500, effectively rounding to the nearest thousand. Increasing the number of digits in the mantissa yields greater precision and a smaller rounding interval.

Approximation is inherent in scientific practice, as theories provide simplified representations of complex phenomena. Predictions derived from a model can diverge from measured values because real situations involve factors not included in the theoretical framework. For example, many straightforward calculations neglect air resistance, which can cause deviations between anticipated and observed outcomes. Consequently, a theory is best viewed as an approximation to reality rather than a complete description. Additional discrepancies may also stem from limitations of measurement techniques, since observed quantities are themselves estimates of the true underlying values.

Service operations management highlights the dependence on supply chains to provide the inputs that enable service delivery. Hospitals serve as a typical illustration, sourcing a broad array of goods from external vendors to construct and furnish their facilities. In routine operations, inventories of consumables and equipment are maintained across departments, including operating rooms and other areas of the building. The pharmacy manages medications, while the kitchen procures food and related supplies. Taken together, the hospital’s overall supply chain for such enabling goods is extensive, encompassing procurement, inventory management, and distribution to support ongoing clinical and support activities.

Within services operations management, the service blueprint is a visualization instrument that maps the full customer journey through a service operation, detailing both front-stage interactions with customers and back-stage activities performed by staff. It records the sequence of actions by customers and service providers across visible touchpoints and the underlying processes that support them. For example, in a suit purchase at a retail store, the blueprint would trace the process from store entry and initial greeting through needs identification, searching for suitable suits, selecting and trying on, alterations carried out behind the scenes, payment, and final pickup. A blueprint flowchart provides a step-by-step depiction of the entire service process. The approach is used to illustrate how the service operates and to identify opportunities for process improvement and service delivery redesign.

Multilateralism embeds a target state within a coalition, reducing the overall cost for a dominant actor seeking influence or control. It provides binding commitments that constrain behavior in ways akin to coordinated, multi-state pressure, offering a mechanism to project power without bearing all risks unilaterally. In cases involving control over a smaller power, coalitions may be the only feasible option because of the limited resources of minor powers. The system accommodates power disparities by relying on the greater predictability of stronger states and on collective-action mechanisms to achieve influence. Powerful states participate in such arrangements by shaping the rules and securing privileges such as veto rights and special status within the multilateral framework.

Multilateralism is a mode of international cooperation in which multiple states work together, in contrast to bilateralism, which involves coordination between two countries. It seeks to establish common ground by anchoring shared norms of conduct while negotiating the specific provisions of an agreement. Political scientist Victor Cha contends that power asymmetries influence which structural form offers greater control: multilateral approaches tend to be more effective when smaller powers attempt to constrain a larger power, whereas bilateral alliances are usually more effective when great powers seek to direct the actions of weaker states.

In the mid-1990s, thin clients were primarily diskless corporate intranet workstations, whereas WebTV targeted consumers as an affordable alternative to a personal computer for Internet access. WebTV and later MSN TV connected a television to the Internet to enable basic web browsing and electronic mail, presenting a curated, walled-garden experience that included newsgroups, weather and news updates, a Favorites bookmark system, and IRC (with MSN Chat available briefly), along with a Page Builder to host and share user webpages, background music while browsing, and topic-focused content sections such as entertainment, romance, and stocks. Following Microsoft's acquisition, the service was integrated with MSN Messenger and Hotmail. The hardware consisted of a thin-client set-top box operated with a remote control and using dial-up connectivity, with broadband access arriving later via Rogers Interactive TV and the MSN TV 2 platform. An optional wireless keyboard was marketed during the 2000s.

By October 1995, Artemis had about 30 employees, consisting mainly of engineers with a small number of business development staff. Among its early hires were two former Apple employees, Andy Rubin and Joe Britt. Rubin would later become the creator of the Android mobile operating system. Subsequently, Rubin and Britt co-founded Danger, Inc., a company that originally operated under the name Danger Research.

A tropical island resort is an island or archipelago whose economy predominantly relies on tourism as its main revenue source. Such destinations typically provide beachfront accommodations, recreational amenities, and cultural experiences aimed at attracting visitors, thereby supporting local employment and economic activity. Widely recognized examples of island resorts include The Bahamas in the Caribbean, Bali in Indonesia, Phuket in Thailand, Hawaii in the United States, Fiji in the Pacific, and the Mediterranean destinations Santorini and Ibiza.

In 2017, France, the United States, and Spain were the three leading international destinations by international arrivals, collectively attracting approximately 234 million visitors to the three countries. Tourism contributed 8.9 percent of GDP in France, 7.7 percent in the United States, and 14.9 percent in Spain.

Deusdedit of Canterbury, who died circa 664, was a medieval Archbishop of Canterbury and the first archbishop born in England, an Anglo-Saxon by birth. He was enthroned in 655 and presided for a little over nine years until his death. It is probable that he died from plague. His successor was one of his priests at Canterbury. The exact date of his death is contested due to discrepancies among early and later records. Little is known about his episcopate. He was regarded as a saint after death, and a hagiography detailing his life was composed after his relics were translated from their original burial place in 1091.

At the Synod of Whitby, convened in 664, church authorities debated whether the Northumbrian church should observe Easter according to the Roman calculation or the Celtic tradition. Deusdedit of Canterbury is not recorded as having attended the synod. The absence may have been due to a plague outbreak that was prevalent across England at that time.

DHL has served as the principal sponsor for Penske Racing's Porsche RS Spyder LMPs competing in the IMSA American Le Mans Series for several seasons. The company began backing Andretti Autosport's #28 IndyCar entry driven by Ryan Hunter-Reay in 2011, a sponsorship later transferred to Romain Grosjean in 2022 and then to Álex Palou with Chip Ganassi Racing in 2024. With DHL in place, Hunter-Reay captured the 2012 IndyCar Series championship and won the 2014 Indianapolis 500. In Formula One, DHL was the main title sponsor of the Jordan team in 2002 and has since maintained a regular trackside presence at various Formula One races while also serving as the Official Logistics Partner of Formula One. Additionally, since 2007 DHL has sponsored the DHL Fastest Lap Award for the driver with the season’s fastest laps.

In 2014, DHL partnered with IMG Fashion to establish DHL Exported, a program aimed at helping designers who have achieved local success gain international momentum. The initiative sponsors one designer for two consecutive seasons at a major fashion week in New York, London, Milan, or Tokyo. Applications are accepted from February 17 to April 2 via dhlexported.com.

Pyoljji-1-2 is a North Korean air defense system that was first shown publicly on 3 May 2012 to Supreme Leader Kim Jong Un during his visit to the Korean People’s Army Air and Anti-Air Force Command Headquarters, where it was presented under the designation Pongae-6. The system’s existence and designation were subsequently clarified by its display at the Workers’ Party of Korea’s 75th anniversary parade in 2020, which solidified its identification as Pyoljji-1-2.

Pyoljji-1-2 is a radar configuration that was observed during a test firing on 30 September 2021. In the background of the footage, a radar unit resembling the Pongae-5 radar was visible. The installation featured a large radar module mounted behind the truck cabin, with a smaller radar unit mounted atop the cabin. It is not known whether the smaller radar unit is capable of rotation.

Tell the Vision achieved a multi-territory chart presence, with the main version debuting on the Billboard Global 200 at number 33 and peaking in the United Kingdom at number 55 on the UK Singles Chart. In Australia, the song peaked at number 47 on the ARIA Singles Chart. In Greece, it entered the International Digital Singles Chart at number 25 in the 28th week of 2021 and rose to number 21 the following week. In Switzerland, it appeared at number 50 on the Swiss Hitparade Singles Top 75. A separate alternate version also charted, opening at number 90 on the Billboard Hot 100, entering the Canadian Hot 100 at number 71, and reaching number 69 on the ARIA Singles Chart.

Tell the Vision entered the US Billboard Hot 100 at number 49 following the release of Faith, and remained on the chart for one week. It also debuted on the US Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart at number 16 concurrently with its Hot 100 entry. In Canada, the track reached a peak of number 19 on the Canadian Hot 100 and spent four weeks on that chart.

The Province of Maryland arose from George Calvert, 1st Lord Baltimore, seeking a royal charter from King Charles I in 1629 to establish a colony to the south of the Virginia settlements. Calvert was driven by a perceived religious obligation to provide a refuge for his Catholic brethren and to create a place where English Catholics could practice their faith with greater freedom. He also anticipated economic advantages from tobacco cultivation and trade associated with the Virginia region. Additionally, the enterprise was envisioned as a means to recover financial losses incurred from his earlier Newfoundland colonization venture.

Following Maryland's Protestant Revolution, a Catholic member of the Darnall family was compelled to maintain a clandestine home chapel for the celebration of Mass. In 1704, the colonial assembly passed legislation aimed at curbing the growth of Catholic influence in the province. The act barred Catholics from holding political office.

Richard H. Brown is an American business executive who has held multiple high-profile leadership and board positions. He served as chief executive officer of Cable & Wireless plc from 1996 to 1998, and subsequently led Electronic Data Systems Corporation as chairman and chief executive officer from 1999 to 2003. In addition to his executive roles, Brown was a director of DuPont from 2001 to 2015, and he also served on the board of Home Depot, though the specific years of service are not specified.

Richard H. Brown is the President and chief executive officer of H&R Block, Inc. He also serves as vice chairman of Ameritech Corporation and participates in The Business Council. Brown has previously been a member of the U.S.–Japan Business Council and is a member of the French-American Business Council. In addition, he serves on the President's National Security Telecommunications Advisory Committee.

Investigations concerning the 173rd Airborne Brigade Combat Team during the Vietnam War documented a pattern of abusive interrogation practices by some personnel, corroborated by reports from Lt. Col. Anthony Herbert. The inquiries found episodes of beatings, torture with electrical impulses, and forced water administration designed to induce a drowning-like sensation, following Herbert’s allegations of war crimes. A U.S. Army assessment characterized these actions as cruelty and maltreatment, spanning from March 1968 to October 1969. One specific technique cited was the water rag, in which water was poured onto a cloth covering a detainee’s nose and mouth to create the risk of asphyxiation. Herbert was relieved of his command shortly after he reported these incidents. Additionally, a former counterintelligence officer testified under oath about further abuses, including punches and kicks, beatings with sticks, electrified shocks, and urination on prisoners.

On 23 April 2014, four airborne infantry companies from the 173rd Airborne Brigade Combat Team were deployed to Poland, Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania to reassure NATO allies threatened by Russian military maneuvers along the borders of eastern Ukraine, in the context of the 2014–15 Russian military intervention in Ukraine.

Hans Detlef Sierck, born on 26 April 1897 in Hamburg, came from a family of Danish descent; his father worked as a newspaper reporter. He spent several years in Denmark during childhood before his parents returned to Germany and obtained citizenship. Sierck discovered theatre in his mid-teens, with an interest in Shakespeare’s history plays, and began frequenting cinemas, later describing his exposure to melodramatic works marked by heightened emotional intensity. His early screen favorite was the Danish-born actress Asta Nielsen. In 1919 he enrolled at the University of Munich to study law, but left the city after the violent collapse of the Bavarian Soviet Republic. Between university stints, he wrote for his father's newspaper; his father later became a school principal.

Douglas Sirk initially rejected an offer from Dr. Paul Eger that would have given him a raise and the opportunity to stage modern Expressionist works, choosing instead to pursue directing classic drama. He then became the first director of a new playhouse in Chemnitz, Saxony, where the season opened with classical plays by Molière, Büchner, and Strindberg. However, the financier vanished overnight, forcing the cast and crew to organize themselves as a collective in order to keep the theatre operating. As a result, the repertoire shifted toward comedies and melodramas that were more financially viable. Sirk later described that period as a terrible time, yet he regarded it as formative, learning his craft and how to manage actors under extreme pressure. The turbulent period coincided with runaway German inflation; after distributing money to the company, they had to rush to the bank before noon to cash takings at the new rate, or risk losing a large portion of their earnings.

Motocross encompasses off-road motorcycle racing, with supercross representing a prominent variant that employs specialized high-performance motorcycles. Races are conducted on purpose-built dirt tracks featuring steep jumps and various obstacles, and these courses are designed to have shorter straight sections and tighter turns than traditional motocross layouts. In the United States, professional supercross events form the AMA Supercross Championship, and virtually all races are staged in stadiums built for baseball and football rather than in conventional outdoor venues.

Regulations of the era favored four-stroke motorcycles produced by smaller European manufacturers, a trend that saw Husqvarna, Husaberg, and KTM achieve world championships on four-stroke machinery. In 1997 Yamaha introduced the YZM 400, a prototype 400cc four-stroke developed for the FIM Motocross World Championship, which also marked its United States debut that year; Doug Henry subsequently won the 1997 AMA Supercross Finale on a four-stroke, the first such victory in the series. The release of Yamaha’s production YZ400F in 1998 helped Henry secure the 250cc AMA Motocross Championship, representing the first major AMA Motocross title won on a four-stroke. Yamaha’s success more broadly motivated Honda, Kawasaki, and Suzuki to develop their own four-stroke race bikes, and by 2006 all manufacturers were contesting the AMA 125 (FIM MX2) and 250 (MX1) classes with four-stroke machines.

Nicktoons (European TV channel) expanded its regional availability across Europe, beginning with a launch in Russia on 12 December 2018. The service then entered Hungary and Romania on 1 April 2019, followed by Bulgaria on 5 June 2019. The Czech Republic joined on 30 October 2019, with Ukraine added on 22 January 2020. Subsequently, on 14 July 2020, the channel broadened further to Serbia, Croatia, Slovenia and Albania.

Nicktoons (European TV channel) is a European international children's television network operated by Paramount Networks EMEAA. It is sometimes referred to as Nicktoons Global. The service launched on March 1, 2012, and functions as the international version of the American Nicktoons channel. It serves numerous countries across the European Union and operates multiple feeds differentiated by time zones, with local languages provided as the primary audio track. Other languages are available through second audio program options, and some networks may display subtitles in the domestically used language as open-access content.

Adversarial systems vary in how they treat a defendant’s silence; in some jurisdictions, courts may permit an inference to be drawn from an accused’s silence or from failure to face cross-examination or answer questions, which can undermine the defensive value of remaining silent. In the United States, the Fifth Amendment protects against such inferences by prohibiting juries from drawing a negative inference from a defendant’s right not to testify, and if the defendant requests, juries must be instructed that no adverse inference may be drawn.

An adversarial system is a legal framework used in common-law countries in which two advocates represent the positions of their respective parties before a neutral decision-maker, typically a judge or jury. The decision-maker endeavors to determine the truth and to render a judgment based on the evidence and arguments presented. This approach contrasts with the inquisitorial system found in some civil-law jurisdictions, where the judge takes an active role in investigating the case, a structure that derives from Roman law and the Napoleonic Code.

Live at Shepherds Bush Empire (Björk video) is the official Björk VHS release, titled Live at Shepherds Bush Empire, released on 16 November 1998. It was recorded on 27 February 1997 toward the end of the Post tour, at a free, fan-club-only concert held at the Shepherd's Bush Empire in London, England. The performance's setlist is dominated by material from the album Post, with several tracks originating from Debut. The track I Go Humble later appeared as a B-side on the Isobel single.

Live at Shepherds Bush Empire (Björk video) is a video recording of Björk's performance at the Shepherds Bush Empire. Several performances from the concert were later released on the Post Live album, which forms part of the Live Box set issued in 2003 and subsequently made available separately. The end credits feature "Glóra," a flute‑based instrumental recorded during Björk's time with The Elgar Sisters. Two songs performed at the show were omitted from the release—"It's Oh So Quiet" and "Sweet Intuition," which opened the set. The release was later issued on DVD, with a re‑release dated 19 November 2001.

In 2003, The Rayware Group acquired the Ravenhead brand, and the Kilner jar line, which operated as a Ravenhead subsidiary, was included in the purchase. Since then, Rayware has continued producing Kilner jars, with manufacturing taking place in China.

The Kilner Jar originated with John Kilner (1792–1857) and his associates. It was manufactured by the Kilner Glass Bottlemakers Company, a Yorkshire‑based firm established by Kilner himself. The Kilner bottlemakers operated from 1842, the year of its founding, until 1937, when the company went into liquidation.

Tai Nuea is a tonal language characterized by a restricted syllable inventory and the absence of consonant clusters. Its syllable structure comprises 16 initial consonants that can be combined with 84 possible syllable endings, yielding a limited range of syllables. The language also features six distinct tones.

Tai Nuea is traditionally written in the Tai Le script, a writing system that belongs to the Mon-Burmese family of scripts. The Tai Le script is closely related to the Ahom script, reflecting a shared historical lineage within the region’s writing traditions. Scholarly assessment generally places the origin of this script in the 14th century, indicating its development several centuries ago.

September of My Years is a 1965 studio album by Frank Sinatra, released on Reprise Records. The LP appeared in August 1965, with a compact disc release following in October 1986. It stands as the fifth album Sinatra recorded with arranger Gordon Jenkins. Issued shortly before Sinatra’s fiftieth birthday in December 1965, the work revisits the ballad-oriented concept albums associated with his 1950s Capitol era, and centers on themes of aging, self-reflection, and nostalgia, delivered through subdued arrangements and a restrained vocal delivery.

September of My Years was released on compact disc on October 10, 1986. It was subsequently issued in a remastered form on May 26, 1998 as part of the Entertainer of the Century series from Reprise and Capitol Records, a version that is now out of print. Concord Records issued another remastered CD edition on August 31, 2010. The 2010 Concord release includes two bonus tracks: a live performance of "This Is All I Ask" recorded at Carnegie Hall in June 1984, and the single mix of "How Old Am I?" from 1968.

In 1966, the New York Stock Exchange introduced a composite index comprising all listed common stocks. It was initially referred to as the common stock index. The index is disseminated daily, with a base value of 50 established at its inception, and it was later renamed the NYSE Composite Index.

On select occasions, the New York Stock Exchange has invited fictional figures to ring the opening bell, often serving as mascots for companies listed on the exchange or as characters drawn from films, television, or toy lines produced by those firms. These appearances have included such recognizable figures as Mickey Mouse, the Pink Panther, Mr. Potato Head, the Aflac Duck, and characters Gene and Jailbreak from The Emoji Movie, as well as Darth Vader.

Olivia Dean began writing songs at the age of sixteen and taught herself to play guitar and piano. She performed at her graduation concert, an appearance that attracted the attention of music manager Emily Braham. Braham then arranged an audition with Rudimental, who hired her as a backing vocalist; Dean later said she did not thrive in that role, frequently singing the lead melody rather than providing harmony. Her first live performance came at Sziget Festival in Hungary in 2017, before a crowd of 16,000.
Olivia Dean is a supporter of West Ham United F.C. During her childhood, she frequently attended games at Upton Park with her father, who held a season ticket for the club.

Philip S. Gutierrez is a former American judge who served on the Los Angeles County Superior Court from 1997 to 2007 before his appointment to the United States District Court for the Central District of California. He was nominated by President George W. Bush on January 9, 2007, to fill the seat vacated by Judge Terry J. Hatter Jr., and was confirmed by the Senate on January 30, 2007, receiving his commission on February 16, 2007. Gutierrez later became the chief judge of the Central District of California on June 26, 2020, following a brief tenure by Cormac J. Carney, and his term as chief judge ended on March 30, 2024. He retired from active service on October 22, 2024.

Philip S. Gutierrez was born in Los Angeles, California. He earned a Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of Notre Dame in 1981 and subsequently obtained a Juris Doctor from UCLA School of Law in 1984. He practiced privately as a lawyer in California from 1986 to 1997. Gutierrez is of Mexican American descent.

Chronic stress is understood within a framework in which stress responses, especially the fight-or-flight mechanism, are fundamental to adaptive behavior. As the environment continually changes, a system is required to respond to perceived threats, and the stress response is inherently adaptive, aiming to restore homeostasis by making physiological adjustments. The endocrine component of this response involves the release of corticosteroids. The concept of allostasis, defined as achieving stability through change, was proposed by Sterling and Eyer in 1988 to describe how such adaptive adjustments operate. Evidence supports the view that the stress response functions primarily as a short-term adaptive system, with the immediate effects of stress hormones being beneficial in the short term and acting as a protective defense against threats, typically not posing health risks.

In the field of chronic stress research, progress depends on the development of more accurate and reliable measures of the stress process. The inherent complexity of stress presents substantial challenges to establishing measurement tools that are both consistent and comprehensive across different populations and timeframes.

During 2017, Apple announced plans to invest approximately $1 billion in its original programming for Apple TV over the coming year. Later in the same year, a report projected that Apple would spend about $4.2 billion on original programming by 2022. By August 2019, industry sources indicated that Apple had already spent more than $6 billion on original programming.

In June 2017, Apple appointed Jamie Erlicht and Zack Van Amburg to head its newly established worldwide video unit. By November 2017, the company announced an expansion into original scripted programming. It subsequently ordered straight-to-series commitments for two projects: a reboot of the anthology series Amazing Stories produced by Steven Spielberg, and The Morning Show, a drama featuring Jennifer Aniston and Reese Witherspoon.

American English comprises a range of regional varieties, with the New York City and Southern accents among the most widely recognized in the United States, though they are also among the most stigmatized and socially disfavored. Southern speech is most prominent in southern Appalachia and parts of Texas, where it is frequently identified by Americans as a “country” accent. A defining characteristic of the Southern variety is the treatment of the /aɪ/ vowel, which often loses its glide and surfaces as a lengthened [aː], a shift associated with a broader Southern vowel movement and a drawl that makes short front vowels sound distinctly gliding. Fronting of vowels in GOOSE, GOAT, MOUTH, and STRUT also helps characterize Southern speech, as well as the accents spoken in the Midland, a broad region that lies between the traditional North and South. The Midland itself is an expansive dialect belt considered intermediate between northern and southern varieties. By contrast, Western United States accents predominantly fall within the General American spectrum.

American English reflects a complex history of contact, innovation, and social change that shaped its lexicon. Following the War of 1812, interactions with Mexican Spanish influenced western expansion and helped popularize the term ranch as a descriptor of a house style on the frontier. Mexican culinary vocabulary—cilantro, queso, tacos, quesadillas, enchiladas, tostadas, fajitas, burritos, and guacamole—entered everyday usage with few direct English equivalents and remains common in mainstream dining. Over centuries, dwelling terminology evolved from 18th‑century log cabins and adobe houses to 19th‑century apartments and shanties, and into the 20th century with references to housing projects, condominiums, townhouses, and mobile homes, along with everyday parts terms such as driveway, breezeway, and backyard. The rise of industry, railroads, and transportation from the 19th century onward produced new words and idioms, including descriptors for road types (dirt roads, freeways) and infrastructure (parking lot, overpass, rest area), while automotive terminology spread internationally. Some existing English words shifted in meaning; others remained in American use even as meanings shifted in Britain. Advances in science, urbanization, and democracy helped drive changes in both written and spoken American English. In business and finance, terms such as merger, downsize, and bottom line entered common parlance, and sports and gambling jargon contributed widely used idioms, including several baseball-related expressions. Finally, some American inventions and terms stayed largely North American—for example elevator and gasoline—while elevator usage in general discourse is often associated with the North American context, and words like truck and trunk remained typical of everyday American speech.

Sky Sci-Fi lists the ten most watched programmes on the British channel Syfy (formerly Sci-Fi). The rankings are based on live-plus-seven viewing data supplied by BARB and cover the period up to 10 September 2017. The figures exclude Irish viewers, repeats, and airings on the Syfy +1 timeshift channel.

Sky filed a trademark application for the name Sky Sci-Fi on May 4, 2022. In a subsequent announcement dated June 14, 2022, Sky stated that the channel would rebrand to Sky Sci-Fi at 11:00 a.m. on July 26, with the relaunch accompanied by a revised programming lineup that would incorporate both new premieres and existing content.

According to the 2010 census, Ellendale, North Dakota, had a population of 1,394 residents, comprising 562 households and 313 families. The population density was 917.1 people per square mile (354.1/km2), and there were 698 housing units at an average density of 459.2 per square mile (177.3/km2). The racial composition was 94.5% White, 1.2% African American, 1.7% Native American, 0.2% Asian, 0.1% Pacific Islander, 0.4% from other races, and 1.9% from two or more races, with Hispanic or Latino of any race making up 1.2% of the population.

Ellendale, North Dakota exhibits an aging demographic pattern, with a median age of 38 years and a notable share of residents aged 65 and over (24.1%). The age composition comprises 18.7% under 18, 20.1% from 18 to 24, 18.6% from 25 to 44, 18.5% from 45 to 64, and 24.1% who are 65 or older. The community also shows a lower number of men relative to women, recording an overall sex ratio of 85.2 males for every 100 females, while among adults aged 18 and over the ratio stands at 76.0 males per 100 females.

Montenegro's women’s national handball team competed at the 2016 Summer Olympics in Rio de Janeiro, marking its second appearance at the Olympic Games. The squad endured five defeats in the group stage and finished near the bottom of the final standings.

In November 2017, the Handball Federation of Montenegro announced the appointment of Per Johansson as the head coach of the women's national team, succeeding Dragan Adžić, who had guided the side for seven years. During Adžić's tenure, Montenegro participated in nine major international competitions, including a European Championship title in 2012 and a silver medal at the 2012 Summer Olympics under his leadership.
The CMA Awards are presented annually by the Country Music Association to honor achievements in country music. Willie Nelson has won 11 CMA Awards and has 48 CMA Award nominations.

The Academy of Country Music Awards, presented annually by the Academy of Country Music, recognize achievements in country music over the course of the year. Willie Nelson has secured twelve ACM Awards from forty-three nominations.

The Gupta Empire’s homeland is theorized by some scholars to lie in the Bengal region of the Ganges basin, a view drawn from the travel account of the Chinese monk Yijing. In Yijing’s records, the Gupta king Che-li-ki-to is identified with the ruler Shri Gupta, who is said to have erected a temple for Chinese pilgrims near a site he transcribed as Mi-li-kia-si-kia-po-no (Mriga-shikha-vana). The temple is described as lying more than forty yojanas east of Nalanda, a detail that has been interpreted as evidence for a Bengal location of the early Gupta state. An alternative proposal suggests a broader early Gupta realm extending from Prayaga in the west to northern Bengal in the east.

The Gupta Empire is commonly regarded as the apex of Sanskrit literature, a period during which a flourishing of poetic and scholarly activity produced several prominent authors. Harisena, an early kavya poet, composed a number of works including Apabhramsa Dharmapariksa, Karpuraprakara (also known as Suktavall), Jagatsundari-Yogamaladhikara, Yasodharacanta, Astahnikakatha, and Brhatkathakosa. In the realm of Sanskrit grammar, Amarasimha contributed influential treatises that enriched linguistic scholarship. The era also witnessed Kalidasa, a celebrated dramatist, whose works include Abhijnanashakuntalam and Shakuntala. Additionally, Bhartṛhari produced major linguistic and literary works, notably the Trikāṇḍī and Śatakatraya. Together, these writers underscore the Gupta period’s central role in advancing Sanskrit literature and grammatical study.

Established in 2008, the UK Statistics Authority has undertaken reviews addressing technical matters. A 2015 review focused on economic statistics and was led by Professor Sir Charles Bean, while a 2016 review concentrated on methodology and was led by Dr Andrew Garrett.

The UK Statistics Authority (UKSA) was established on 1 April 2008 under the Statistics and Registration Service Act 2007. It is directly accountable to the Parliament of the United Kingdom and reports to Parliament through the Minister for the Cabinet Office.
The 1989–90 Welsh Cup was won by Hereford United. The final was held at the National Stadium in Cardiff, and was attended by 4,182 spectators.

In the 1970 US Open men's doubles tournament, eighth-seeded Pierre Barthès and Nikola Pilić captured the title, defeating the sixth-seeded duo Roy Emerson and Rod Laver in the final by a score of 6–3, 7–6, 4–6, 7–6.
The 1970 US Open – Men's doubles tournament featured the defending champions, Ken Rosewall and Fred Stolle, who were eliminated in the semifinals and therefore did not retain the title.

Super Expander 64 exhibits a quirk in its editing feature that hinges on a particular control sequence combined with a quotation mark. The procedure requires typing a control sequence (Ctrl+F) together with a double quotation mark, and then deleting the quotation mark. As a result, the machine would replay the keystrokes entered during the editing process. Additionally, pressing the G key would trigger a musical cue described as a “Pling!” at the pitch of a G note.

Super Expander 64 is a cartridge-based extension for the Commodore 64’s built-in BASIC interpreter, released by Commodore Business Machines in 1983. The Commodore BASIC implementation that shipped with the C64 was derived from the PET and VIC-20 line and did not provide native support for the machine’s sound and graphics hardware. Consequently, accessing those capabilities typically required manipulating memory-mapped registers through explicit PEEK and POKE commands. The Super Expander 64 expands BASIC by adding a set of new functions for graphics drawing, sprite handling, joystick input, audio playback, and other features, thereby simplifying hardware access and broadening the programming possibilities on the platform.

Bunhill Fields traces its origin to 1498, when a portion of the open countryside was set aside to form a sizable field. The space was designated for martial training, including archers and other troops. It came to be known as the Artillery Ground. The field formed part of the manor and was used for sport and occasional military activities.

Bunhill Fields is a historic burial ground in London that preserves several early monuments. The earliest recorded monumental inscription there notes Grace, the daughter of T. Cloudesly from Leeds, dated February 1666. The earliest surviving monument is believed to be the headstone of Theophilus Gale, with the inscription indicating his Master of Arts qualification and giving his birth year as 1628 and his death year as 1678.

The 1968 Scotland storm originated from a cold front near Bermuda on 13 January 1968 and intensified into a shallow low-pressure system as it moved north of the Azores the following day. It explosively deepened, with its central pressure dropping by about 50 millibars to 956 mb (28.2 inHg) within 24 hours, and subsequently passed over Central Scotland. The system continued across Northern Europe before dissipating on 18 January 1968.

During the 1968 Scotland storm, winds were measured at hurricane-force intensities, though the term “hurricane” is a misnomer since hurricanes are tropical cyclones originating in the North Atlantic or North Pacific.

Knowledge workers are professionals who perform activities that involve capturing, organizing, and providing access to knowledge, enabling organizations to harness information for decision making, innovation, and learning. These functions are typically carried out by technical staff who support knowledge-management efforts within projects. The idea of knowledge work has ancient antecedents, with early examples dating to around 450 BCE in the Library of Alexandria. In its modern form, the concept is linked to the emergence of information management in the 1970s, when systematic practices for handling knowledge began to take shape within organizations.

Toffler (1990) observed that knowledge workers operating in the knowledge economy require a personal system for generating, processing, and enhancing their own knowledge. This requirement is especially pronounced for scientists and engineers engaged in research and development, whose work depends on continual creation and refinement of knowledge. Additionally, such professionals may be charged with organizing and coordinating the knowledge of their coworkers, facilitating accessible information and collaborative work across teams.

Agriculturalism rejected the division of labour, a stance that contrasted with Confucian doctrine. Proponents argued for policies grounded in egalitarian self-sufficiency and social parity, advocating price fixing that set identical prices for similar goods regardless of quality or demand. They also proposed paying the same amount for the same services, urging uniform remuneration across comparable labor. Confucian critics maintained that such measures would encourage the production of lower-quality goods and undermine standards of craftsmanship.

Agriculturalism, an ancient Chinese school of thought that emphasized the primacy of agricultural life and rural virtue, was suppressed during the Qin dynasty. As a result, most of its original writings have not survived. Despite this loss, the ideas associated with Agriculturalism influenced Confucianism, Legalism, and Chinese philosophy more broadly. At various points in history, Agriculturalism has been regarded by some as a defining expression of Chinese identity.

In Louisiana, since 1792 the term Creole has been used to designate individuals of African or mixed heritage, as well as those of French and Spanish descent whose lineages had not intermarried with other racial groups. In linguistics, the word first appears as an adjective describing languages around 1748, and it was later adopted in 1879 as the name for a family of languages. This reflects the term’s dual trajectory across population labels and linguistic classifications over time.

In the islands, Spanish Americans included a substantial number of individuals of pure Spanish descent. A notable portion of Mestizos and Castizos from Spanish America also lived in the East Indies. Collectively, these groups were classified as "Americanos."

On 20 January 1699, Louis XIV issued the first statutes for the institution, which would be known as the Royal Academy of Sciences (Académie Royale des Sciences), and it was installed in the Louvre in Paris. The academy began publishing an annual volume featuring members’ scholarly work and obituaries, and a reform codified the method for awarding pensions to academy members for their contributions.

During the eighteenth century, the Académie Royale des Sciences came to exercise influence over French patent laws. It served as an interface between artisans' knowledge and the public domain, effectively translating craft know-how into publicly accessible scientific and policy discourse. As a result, its academicians occupied a leading role in France's technological development.

Atlanta serves as a major hub for higher education in the United States, hosting more than 15 colleges and universities. The city includes three law schools and two medical schools, reflecting its broad mix of professional programs. Consequently, Atlanta ranks among the nation's largest centers for higher education. Three of its universities hold the top classification, designated as R1 for Doctoral Universities with very high research activity.

Desegregation in Atlanta proceeded through a series of phased changes in the public sphere. By 1959, public transportation had eliminated racial segregation in service and facilities. In 1961, the restaurant at Rich’s department store ended its policy of separate facilities. Movie theaters followed suit in 1963, integrating seating and admission practices. Public schools were not desegregated until 1973, nearly two decades after the Supreme Court ruling in Brown v. Board of Education that state-sponsored segregation in public schools was unconstitutional.

Uppsala Central Station serves three principal directions for its rail services. Southbound connections run to Arlanda, Stockholm, and Linköping, while northwestbound trains head toward Dalarna and Sala. Northbound services link to Gävle, Sundsvall, Östersund, and other parts of northern Sweden. Additionally, sleeper trains operate to Narvik in Norway.

Uppsala Castle was built under the direction of King Gustav Vasa and has historically served as one of the royal residences of the Swedish monarchs. Over the centuries it underwent several enlargements, and these expansions contributed to Uppsala's status as a de facto secondary capital during the period of its greatest extent. In contemporary times, the castle functions as the residence of the Governor of Uppsala County.

In March 2022, the United States Department of Agriculture announced a grant of 250 million dollars intended to promote domestic nitrogen fertilizer production. The program, administered under the Commodity Credit Corporation, seeks to bolster fertilizer output that is independent of dominant international suppliers, emphasize products manufactured in the United States, and encourage the use of innovative production techniques to stimulate future competition.

Nitrogen fertilizers are essential for modern cultivation in agriculture and horticulture. Nevertheless, soil acidification constitutes a significant concern in these sectors, defined as the progressive shift toward higher soil acidity over time.

Adam Brand released his sixth studio album What a Life in July 2006, which peaked at number 28 on the ARIA Albums Chart and was certified gold; in the same year he received a nomination for Best Country Album at the ARIA Music Awards. In January 2007 Brand won the inaugural Country Music Channel Oz Artist of the Year Award, and in January 2008 he, along with Lee Kernaghan and Steve Forde, won three CMA Awards for the song Spirit of the Bush. That month also saw the release of his seventh studio album Blame It on Eve, his first to reach the ARIA top ten, followed by the September 2008 release of Greatest Hits 1998–2008. In January 2009 Brand secured his third consecutive CMC Oz Artist of the Year Award and was named Male Artist of the Year at the CMA Awards, his twelfth CMA Award overall; his eighth studio album Hell of a Ride appeared in March 2009 and peaked at number 19 on the ARIA Albums Chart. In March 2009 he also served as the lead act at the Victorian Bushfire Appeal concert in Traralgon.

Adam Brand is a musician whose career is anchored in the Queensland music scene. The Queensland Music Awards, initially established as the Q Song Awards, are held annually to honor Queensland's most promising newcomers as well as veteran performers, with the ceremony first taking place in 2006.

Apache Helix is a notable open-source framework for cluster management that coordinates resources and lifecycle management across distributed systems. It was originally developed by LinkedIn, and its development occurred alongside other LinkedIn initiatives such as Apache Samza, Apache Kafka, and Voldemort. The origins of Helix can be traced to Espresso, LinkedIn’s distributed NoSQL database, with Helix designed to provide scalable, automated resource allocation and stateful partition management for such platforms.

Apache Helix is an open-source project developed by LinkedIn. It serves as a stable cluster management framework, delivering automated management of partitioned, replicated, and distributed resources hosted on a cluster of systems.
Oligodon cyclurus, commonly known as Cantor's kukri snake, is a snake species native to Asia. It was described by Theodore Cantor in 1839.

Latin has functioned as an official or widely employed language within several European states across different periods. In the Kingdom of Hungary, it remained an official language from the eleventh century until the mid‑nineteenth century, after which Hungarian became the sole official language in 1844. The most renowned Latin‑language poet to emerge from Hungary is Janus Pannonius. In the Kingdom of Poland and the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, Latin was officially recognised and broadly used from the tenth through the eighteenth centuries, serving in foreign affairs and as a second language for some members of the nobility. The Croatian Parliament designated Latin as an official language from the thirteenth to the nineteenth century, with 1847 often cited as a significant marker in this continuity. The oldest preserved records of the Croatian assembly date to 1273, known as Congregatio Regni totius Sclavonie generalis, and kept in Zagreb, reflecting the long Latin‑language tradition in Croatian governance. Croatian Latin literature is extensive, and Latin continued to appear on Croatian coinage in even years until Croatia joined the euro on 1 January 2023.

Latin formed a central element of education in the colonial and early United States. Many founders received a classical education through grammar schools or from private tutors, which emphasized Latin and related classical studies. At Harvard College during the colonial period, admissions explicitly required applicants to demonstrate the ability to readily compose and discuss Latin prose, to read and translate Latin, and to show skill in composing Latin verse. Across American secondary schools and colleges, Latin study and the wider classical curriculum remained a prominent feature well into the Antebellum era.

On 10 March 1793, the National Convention established the Revolutionary Tribunal to try those considered enemies of the republic. In its early phase, about half of the individuals arrested were acquitted. After the Law of 22 Prairial on 10 June 1794, the rate of acquittals declined to roughly a quarter, signaling a harsher judicial regime during the Terror. In March 1793, the Vendée uprising broke out in response to mass conscription, developing into a civil war within the nation. Discontent in the Vendée persisted, according to some accounts, until after the Terror.

During the Reign of Terror, the revolutionary government extended its emergency powers and pursued a campaign of political suppression across the republic. On 10 October the Convention declared that the provisional government would remain in a state of revolution until peace was achieved, reinforcing its extraordinary authority. The same period saw the execution of Marie Antoinette on 16 October, a symbolic blow against the monarchy, and the initiation of the trial of the Girondins, who were subsequently executed on 31 October by Charles-Henri Sanson after a rapid proceedings. In the provinces, leaders moved to quell dissent and enforce the central line: Joseph Fouché and Collot d’Herbois suppressed the Lyon revolt against the National Convention, Jean-Baptiste Carrier ordered drownings at Nantes, and Jean-Lambert Tallien oversaw the operation of the guillotine in Bordeaux. Elsewhere, Barras and Fréron addressed upheavals in Marseille and Toulon, while Joseph Le Bon was dispatched to the Somme and Pas-de-Calais regions to impose security measures.

In mathematics, several named measures are employed across distinct theories of measure, each tailored to capture particular notions of size, volume, or distribution in specific contexts. Notable examples include the Borel measure, Jordan measure, ergodic measure, Gaussian measure, Baire measure, Radon measure, Young measure, and Loeb measure.

Measure theory can be developed with values in Banach spaces, yielding vector-valued measures, and a projection-valued measure is a map that takes values among the self-adjoint projections on a Hilbert space. Such projection-valued measures are fundamental in the spectral theorem of functional analysis, where they provide the spectral resolution of operators. The terminology of positive measures distinguishes measures that take nonnegative values from more general constructions; positive measures are closed under conical (nonnegative linear) combinations but not under arbitrary linear combinations, while signed measures arise as the linear closure of positive measures. In addition, measure theory can be generalized to topological vector spaces, broadening the scope of the theory and its applications.

During the 1960s, Uruguay saw the emergence of the Tupamaros, an armed Marxist-Leninist urban guerrilla movement. They carried out bank robberies, kidnappings, and assassinations as part of their campaign and sought to depose the government.

Uruguay is a South American country that, in 2024, was classified as a full democracy by The Economist's Democracy Index, ranking fifteenth globally and first in Latin America. Latinobarómetro surveys have consistently shown Uruguay among the highest in public support for democracy and in satisfaction with its functioning. The 2023 V-Dem Democracy Indices rank Uruguay 31st in the world for electoral democracy, while the same indices place the country second worldwide for citizen-initiated direct democracy, behind Switzerland.
