Opercular powder, derived from the calcareous lids (opercula) of a variety of gastropod mollusks, has a role in traditional Chinese and Japanese incense making as a fragrance fixative. In Chinese usage, the material is known as bèi xiāng (貝香), literally "sea shell fragrance," while in Japanese practice it is referred to as kai kō (甲香), meaning "shell" or "armor fragrance." The opercula employed originate from numerous conches and other marine snail species, with sources spanning Southeast Asia, South America, and East Africa. Before processing, the raw opercula are treated with vinegar, alcohol, and water to remove any fishy odor. Once dried and ground into a powder, it is used to fix scent in incense, performing a function analogous to resin-based plant perfumes.

The operculum in gastropods is a structure attached to the upper surface of the foot and functions as a trapdoor that closes the shell aperture when the animal withdraws into its shell. Its shape varies considerably across gastropod families, though it is commonly circular or oval. When the operculum fits snugly, its outline matches the shell aperture and it effectively seals the entrance.

Leon Mestel (born 5 August 1927 in Melbourne, Australia) is the son of Solomon Mestel, a rabbi, and Rachel (née Brodetsky), a schoolteacher who was the sister of Selig Brodetsky. The family moved to England when he was three years old, settling in Forest Gate in east London. He attended West Ham Secondary School in London and later studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, where he earned a BA in 1948 and a PhD in 1952.

Mestel was a lecturer in mathematics at the University of Cambridge for eleven years, serving from 1955 to 1966. He began as an assistant lecturer from 1955 to 1958 and was promoted to full lecturer from 1958 to 1966. He was also a fellow of St John's College, Cambridge, holding that position from 1957 to 1966. During the 1961–1962 academic year, he was a visiting member of the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton.

Seymour A. Papert, a pioneer in educational technology, developed the Logo programming language at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology by applying Piagetian ideas. Logo was designed to enhance children's thinking and problem-solving abilities, and it was accompanied by a small mobile robot known as the Logo Turtle, created to help children tackle simple problems in a playful environment. The Logo Foundation research group seeks to strengthen learners' ability to acquire knowledge. Papert also contended that a simple language such as Logo can possess advanced functionality for expert users.

Seymour A. Papert helped revolutionize three interrelated fields: how children understand the world, the development of artificial intelligence, and the intersection of technology and learning. His influence left a lasting imprint at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, where President L. Rafael Reif described him as possessing an exceptionally broad range of interests and a high degree of creativity. Reif credits Papert with a visionary approach that redirected MIT’s emphasis toward digital learning, a trajectory the institution aims to expand by extending its digital-learning work and deepening its efforts in that area. The broader objective is to open doors to learners of all ages around the world.

Rice Hotel in Houston is notable for its association with John F. Kennedy, who visited the property on several occasions. On September 12, 1960, he delivered the religion-in-politics address to the Greater Houston Ministerial Conference held at the Rice. Following his Moon speech at Rice University on September 12, 1962, he visited the Rice Hotel again, and he returned there once more on November 21, 1963, before proceeding to Fort Worth and then Dallas, where he was assassinated. During his Houston visits, Kennedy used a suite at the Rice for meetings that was stocked with caviar, champagne, and his favorite beer; after a brief League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC) event and a speech at the Albert Thomas Convention Center, he went back to the suite to change clothes and spent less than six hours in the city before flying to Fort Worth. In addition to these visits, the Rice has hosted other notable speakers, including Texas Governor William P. Hobby and Captain James A. Baker of Baker and Botts.

Abraham Groesbeck razed the original structure and, in 1881, erected a five-story Victorian hotel named the Capitol Hotel. The building was designed by architect George E. Dickey, and the project represented Dickey’s first major commission since relocating to Houston in 1878.

Apple SIM is a digital SIM technology introduced by Apple that enables wireless service across several carriers without the need to insert a traditional physical SIM. The selection of a carrier is performed through a built-in user interface in iOS and iPadOS, allowing users to switch between networks as needed. Because the SIM is managed within the operating system, there is no requirement to install a carrier-provided SIM card. Apple did not publicly acknowledge the feature in presentations of iPad models that shipped with Apple SIM. Promotional materials characterize the technology as well suited for short-term mobile Internet arrangements across multiple carriers.

Apple SIM is a removable SIM that supports remote provisioning and can be configured with multiple operator profiles. By contrast, an embedded SIM (eSIM) is built into the device and cannot be removed, although it can also be provisioned remotely. In newer devices, Apple has begun including both the removable Apple SIM and an embedded SIM, offering flexible options for provisioning cellular service.

Specials (Unicode block) comprises code points reserved for non-typographic placeholders and similar control functions, including U+FFFD, the Unicode replacement character used to indicate undecodable input. A practical illustration involves the Latin-1 encoding of the word “für,” which yields the bytes 66 FC 72; here 0x66 corresponds to the ASCII letter f and 0x72 to r, while 0xFC represents ü. When such a byte sequence is interpreted as UTF-8, the ASCII bytes 0x66 and 0x72 are valid, but 0xFC does not constitute a valid UTF-8 sequence. In many text-processing tools, the invalid byte may be replaced with the replacement character from the Specials block, resulting in a display of the sequence f followed by the replacement symbol and then r. This scenario illustrates the role of the replacement character in Unicode text handling.

In Unicode, the replacement character, displayed as �, occupies code point U+FFFD and is located in the Specials block. It is commonly rendered as a black diamond-shaped glyph containing a white question mark. The character serves as an indicator of problems when a system cannot render a stream of data into the intended symbols, such as in cases of unknown, unrepresentable, or corrupted input data or decoding failures.

In 2010, U&W introduced idents that incorporated a full tagline within the sequence. The tagline follows a format of successive phrases built around the idea of doing things together, and it ends with a final directive to watch together. Examples, described without direct quotation, include lines encouraging singing in unison, playing as a group, and getting one’s act together, before concluding with an instruction to view the content collectively. This approach emphasizes multiple interconnected “together” expressions that culminate in a communal viewing call.

In May 2010, UKTV announced plans to overhaul the brand identity of its channel Watch after around eighteen months on air. A branding agency pitch was conducted, leading to an appointment within a month, with the review overseen by Creativebrief. The planned changes encompassed a redesigned logo, a new strapline, and a revised tone of voice for Watch. A UKTV spokesperson denied any intention to rename the channel, stating that the overhaul was a branding refinement designed to align Watch with UKTV’s broader strategy.

An early women's magazine directed at wives and mothers appeared in 1852. In the 1920s, German periodicals began to target young women with a sensuous visual style and advertisements for clothing and accessories. Publications such as Die Dame and Das Blatt der Hausfrau highlighted the Neue Frauen (the New Woman), embodied by the American flapper. The archetype of the ideal young woman was stylish, financially independent, and an avid consumer of the latest fashions. Through these magazines, readers were kept informed about developments in fashion, the arts, sports, and modern technologies such as automobiles and telephones.

Magazines that feature coverage of celebrities, including stories and photographic content, have long been popular in the United States. In 2019, People Magazine ranked second in total reach among such publications, behind ESPN Magazine. That year, People Magazine achieved a total reach of 98.51 million.

Adaptive Multi-Rate Wideband (AMR-WB) is a speech coding standard designed for wideband audio in mobile networks. Nokia developed the VMR-WB format for CDMA2000 networks as a variant aligned with AMR-WB. The VMR-WB format is fully interoperable with the 3GPP AMR-WB specification, enabling seamless cross-compatibility between CDMA2000 and 3GPP-based deployments. AMR-WB has achieved broad adoption in mobile handsets, including use for ringtones.

Adaptive Multi-Rate Wideband (AMR-WB) deployments have been adopted by mobile operators on 3G+ networks. Orange UK disclosed in late 2009 that it planned to deploy AMR-WB during 2010. In France, Orange S.A. and SFR have employed AMR-WB on their 3G+ networks since the end of summer 2010.

The United States federal government comprises three coequal branches: the legislative, the executive, and the judicial. Their powers are defined and vested by the Constitution, which has been in effect since March 4, 1789. The powers and duties of these branches are further defined by Acts of Congress, which include provisions for the creation of executive departments and the establishment of courts subordinate to the Supreme Court.

The concept and institutions of the United States federal government took shape in the late eighteenth century, beginning with the formation of the Continental Army and the appointment of George Washington as its commander. The army engaged British forces during the American Revolutionary War, which commenced in 1775. In July 1776, the Second Continental Congress convened at the site now known as Independence Hall in Philadelphia and, with the assent of 56 delegates, unanimously adopted the Declaration of Independence. By September 1783, the Thirteen Colonies had achieved independence, establishing the United States as a new nation. The Constitution, drafted in Philadelphia, was ratified and went into effect on March 4, 1789, laying down the federal rule of law and forming a system grounded in federalism, republicanism, and democracy.

The South American gray fox occupies a broad range of habitats, reflecting its ecological adaptability. Among these environments are the warm, dry scrublands of the Argentine uplands, which provide open terrain and sparse vegetation for hunting and cover. The species also occurs in the cold, arid Patagonian steppe, a landscape characterized by low productivity and extreme conditions. In addition, it is found within the forests of southern Chile, where dense woodlands offer different shelter and resources. Together, these habitats illustrate the fox's ability to exploit diverse ecosystems across its geographic range.

The South American gray fox occurs in Argentina and Chile within the Southern Cone of South America. Its distribution spans both sides of the Andes Mountains, indicating occupancy on the eastern and western slopes. The species’ latitudinal range extends from approximately 17°S in northern Chile to 54°S in Tierra del Fuego.

Master of Physics (MPhys) programs are typically organized around a core set of modules shared by all tracks, supplemented by modules specific to each specialization. In the first year, students generally undertake the same core subjects across tracks, establishing a common foundation in physics. In the second year, learners begin to specialise within their chosen track, selecting options aligned with their interests and future aims. Depending on the institution, students may also enroll in optional modules drawn from other tracks or schemes, allowing wider or interdisciplinary study.

The Master of Physics (MPhys) is an integrated undergraduate master's degree that is typically completed over four years in the United Kingdom and certain other systems. Its structure mirrors that of a bachelor’s program, featuring annual cycles of lectures, laboratory work, coursework, and assessments. The fourth year usually centers on one or more substantial projects, frequently incorporating a research element. Progress to the final year generally requires meeting an academic performance threshold based on examinations taken in the earlier years. Final results are commonly awarded according to the British undergraduate degree classification scale, though some universities employ a scheme such as Distinction, Merit, Pass, or Fail, paralleling classifications used for taught postgraduate master’s degrees.

Established in 1941, the General Counsel of the Navy serves as the Department of the Navy’s principal legal adviser, with the first holder of the post appointed that year. Prior to its creation, the legal advisory function from 1862 to 1941 was performed by the Solicitor General of the Navy. Both offices performed essentially the same duties, providing legal counsel on matters pertaining to the Navy and its operations within the broader defense framework.

The General Counsel of the Navy maintains a close working relationship with the Judge Advocate General. The Judge Advocate General is the senior uniformed lawyer in the Department of the Navy and performs statutory duties under the Uniform Code of Military Justice.

The 1910 United States census marked the first use of metropolitan districts, administrative units created to delineate the urban influence surrounding large cities. These districts served as an early precursor to the modern metropolitan statistical areas (MSAs), providing a framework for aggregating surrounding urbanized populations beyond municipal boundaries. The districts were defined specifically for all cities with populations of 200,000 or more, establishing a standardized basis for analyzing major urban centers in the census.

Comprehensive documentation of the 1910 United States census is available, detailing the instruments used to collect data and the enumerator instructions that guided the enumeration process. The collection includes the actual census forms as well as the guidelines provided to census takers. Access to these materials is provided through the Integrated Public Use Microdata Series (IPUMS).

During 2016, the Niger Delta experienced renewed and intensified attacks on oil infrastructure carried out by several militant groups, including the Movement for the Emancipation of the Niger Delta (MEND), the Niger Delta People's Volunteer Force (NDPVF), the Ijaw National Congress (INC), and the Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF). In response, the Buhari administration pursued a dual strategy that combined coercive security measures with negotiations, aiming to address the militancy through both repression and dialogue.

In central Nigeria, clashes between Muslim Hausa-Fulani herders and indigenous Christian farmers have flared anew, with renewed intensity observed in Kaduna, Plateau, Taraba, and Benue states. These conflicts have claimed hundreds of lives in individual incidents. The disputes are primarily a contest over land and resources, while contributing factors include ongoing desertification in northern Nigeria, rapid population growth, and a fragile economic situation.

Signedness describes how integers encode magnitude and sign. Signed integers are capable of representing negative values, whereas unsigned integers use the same bit width but allocate all representable patterns to non-negative numbers. As a result, with a fixed number of bits, the signed form loses portion of the positive range because a portion of the patterns encode zero or negative values, so roughly half of the possible values are non-positive in signed representations. Consequently, unsigned types offer a larger positive range by using every representable value for non-negative numbers.

Signedness is a property of numeric data types in computing that determines whether values carry a sign. A signed numeric type permits representation of both positive and negative values, often with a separate sign indicator. By contrast, an unsigned numeric type is capable of representing only non-negative numbers, including zero and positive values.

Nigerian reggae emerged in the 1980s with political underpinnings comparable to those of other influential Nigerian artists such as Fela Kuti. Prominent within the scene was Majek Fashek, whose music was notably political. The reggae tradition in Nigeria drew on spiritual elements as well as aims of social, economic, and political empowerment, while also reflecting Afrocentric thought and anti-colonial critique. Musicians like Victor Essiet and The Mandators foregrounded political topics in tracks including Inflation, Dem Belly Full (But We Hungry), Things Fall Apart, and Politicians I and II. The Mandators further cemented the genre’s political orientation with the 1994 album Power of the People: Nigerian Reggae, which consists entirely of songs with political underpinnings.

After Jah Stix disbanded in 1987, Nigerian reggae musician Raji Canal reemerged under the moniker Majek Fashek. He signed with Tabansi Records and launched a solo career with the debut album Prisoner of Conscience. The track Send Down the Rain became the year's most popular single, elevating Fashek to the forefront of Nigeria’s reggae scene. In 1989 he won six PMAN awards, including Song of the Year, Album of the Year, and Reggae Artist of the Year, among others.

Movement in music refers to a self-contained section of a larger composition or formal structure. Movements, or selections from a work, are sometimes performed independently as standalone pieces. For a complete performance of the work, all movements are typically played in a prescribed order, one after another. A movement is regarded as a major structural unit, perceived as the product of the convergence of a variety of structural phenomena that give the section its distinctive character within the overall composition.

A movement is a discrete unit of a larger musical work that may stand by itself as a complete composition. Movements are usually self-contained, providing internal coherence while functioning as separate sections within the whole. The common sequence is fast-slow-fast, though other orders may be employed to provide contrast within the work.

Where the state does not exercise exclusive control over the use of force, non-state actors may step in to meet the demand for protection and coercive enforcement. The Sicilian Mafia in southern Italy has been cited as a prominent example of this phenomenon, operating not only as a criminal organization but also as a provider of private protection services. By creating and supplying security arrangements, these groups establish a market for private protection and enforcement, effectively substituting or supplementing the state's security role in affected locales and influencing local governance and rule-of-law outcomes.

In Wiseman's discussion in the Encyclopedia of Violence, Peace, & Conflict, the state's monopoly on violence is presented as a prerogative that rests on a legitimacy conferred by the people. The condition of this grant is a social compact wherein individuals consent to cede certain powers in exchange for the protection of their persons and property. Consequently, the state acquires the capacity to coerce behavior and, in some theoretical accounts, to exploit those it governs. Taxation is often cited as an exemplar of coercion and exploitation made possible by the monopoly on violence.

In March 2020, Adrian Bye, described as a tech startup leader rather than a physician, advised cryptocurrency investors Gregory Rigano and James Todaro that chloroquine would prevent most people from needing hospital care. He later acknowledged that his assertion rested on philosophical considerations rather than medical research. Within two days, Rigano and Todaro promoted chloroquine in a self-published article that claimed affiliations with the Stanford University School of Medicine, the National Academy of Sciences, and the Birmingham School of Medicine, affiliations the respective institutions later stated they had no links to. Google subsequently removed the article for violating its terms of service.

COVID-19 misinformation is an article authored by Drs. Robert R. Brown and Beverly Rubik that addresses claims surrounding the pandemic and the 5G network. The work states that there is no causal connection between the virus responsible for COVID-19 and 5G technology. It also highlights how the conclusion was misread in social media, being interpreted as evidence of a relationship between COVID-19 and 5G, thereby illustrating the tendency for scientific statements to be misinterpreted in online discourse.

Across countries, national laws establish age-based thresholds that govern children's rights to contact social services, be heard in judicial or administrative proceedings, participate as litigants or parties, appeal decisions, and seek redress. These age limits vary considerably between jurisdictions and among different laws that apply to distinct groups of children and contexts. The entitlement of younger children to have a voice is often distinguished from the rights afforded to adolescents, reflecting different perceptions of capacity and appropriate forms of participation. To prevent the exclusion of younger children from participation, some states implement special measures designed to ensure their right to be heard is respected in practice.

In procedures related to children’s participation in legal processes, testimony from child victims or witnesses is frequently collected through video-recorded interviews or analogous methods. This practice is designed to spare the child from testifying in open court and to prevent direct visual contact between the victims or witnesses and the defendants during proceedings.

Hekhalot literature refers to a body of Jewish writings produced in the post-rabbinic era and is not considered the literature of the rabbis themselves. Rather than constituting rabbinic scholarship, it aims to stand in continuity with Rabbinic literature, presenting itself as an extension of that tradition. The corpus is frequently pseudepigraphical, with many works attributed to earlier authorities or legendary figures rather than to contemporary authors.

Hekhalot literature derives from a Hebrew term meaning "palaces" and comprises texts that describe visions of ascending to heavenly realms while still alive. The tradition overlaps with Merkabah mysticism, a strand sometimes called Chariot literature that centers on Ezekiel’s throne‑chariot vision. It is occasionally identified as the Books of the Palaces and the Chariot (ספרות ההיכלות והמרכבה) and forms a distinct genre within Jewish esoteric and revelatory writing. Scholarly work places its composition from late antiquity into the Early Middle Ages, though some scholars argue that certain elements may date to Talmudic times or earlier, indicating a long and complex development.

OpenBitTorrent’s website experienced a renewed shutdown in July 2017, continuing a period of disrupted availability. It briefly returned to operation in late 2018, but by late 2019 the site had become unresponsive again.

OpenBitTorrent underwent a temporary shutdown from 16 July to 2 August 2012 as a protest against the slow adoption of a proposed protocol improvement. The proposal, advanced by Fredrik Neij, co-founder of The Pirate Bay, was directed at the developers of uTorrent. The interruption led to widespread difficulties for users attempting to download content through BitTorrent.

A British Airways flight departing from Aldergrove Airport near Antrim Town in County Antrim, Northern Ireland, bound for London Heathrow, was subjected to a ransom-like threat after a telephone call to The Irish News stated that a bomb was on board and would detonate over the Irish Sea. In response to the alert, the crew diverted and carried out an emergency landing at Manchester Airport, where all 85 passengers and crew were evacuated. Police subsequently discovered the device in a plastic bag beneath a seat on the aircraft; the bomb contained about 2 kilograms (4.4 pounds) of explosives and was removed for a controlled explosion.

Following the 1974 bombing attempt against a British Airways flight, the British Airline Pilots' Association urged enhanced security measures at Aldergrove Airport in County Antrim. The recommendations included a ban on carry-on luggage, excluding cleaning staff from boarding during aircraft turnaround, and a halt to loading catering supplies at Aldergrove.

Around 2008, about a year after the initial developments, GPLv3 was added to the set of recommended licenses. It was strongly encouraged to be used in tandem with the Apache License, a permissive option, while the AGPLv3 was excluded from these recommendations. The overarching goal of this effort was to reduce license proliferation by consolidating preferred licensing options.

In 2010, Google revised its licensing policy for projects, removing previously imposed restrictions on permissible licenses. The company stated that projects could be released under any license approved by the Open Source Initiative, thereby expanding the range of acceptable licensing options. Public-domain projects, however, were allowed only on a case-by-case basis, requiring a single decision for each proposal.

Lincoln County is a county in the U.S. state of Montana. It covers a total area of 3,675 square miles (9,520 km2), of which 3,615 square miles (9,360 km2) is land and 62 square miles (160 km2) is water, making up about 1.7 percent of the total area. The county borders the Canadian province of British Columbia to the north. Montana’s lowest point lies on the Kootenai River within Lincoln County, at the point where the river exits the state into Idaho. Upstream, Libby Dam creates Lake Koocanusa, a reservoir that extends into British Columbia; the name Koocanusa is a fusion of Kootenai, Canada, and the United States.

As of the 2010 census, Lincoln County, Montana, had a population of 19,687 people, comprising 8,843 households and 5,608 families. The population density stood at 5.4 persons per square mile (2.1/km2). There were 11,413 housing units at an average density of 3.2 per square mile (1.2/km2). The racial composition was 95.9% White, 0.9% American Indian, 0.3% Asian, 0.1% Black or African American, 0.4% from other races, and 2.3% from two or more races, while those identifying as Hispanic or Latino origin made up 2.3% of the population. In terms of ancestry, residents reported 31.5% German, 15.7% Irish, 15.3% English, 10.2% Norwegian, and 3.3% American.

GitHub began as a flat organization with no middle managers, relying on self-management as its guiding principle. Under this approach, employees were able to choose projects that matched their interests through an open allocation system. Remuneration, meanwhile, was set by the chief executive.

GitHub Actions, introduced at GitHub Universe in October 2018 to automate software workflows, reached general availability on November 13, 2019. It provides integrated CI/CD capabilities that allow testing, building, releasing, and deploying software without reliance on external platforms. The service features a marketplace that enables users to share and reuse prebuilt actions for tasks such as testing, linting, and deployment. A primary objective is to reduce dependence on third‑party services and keep developers within the GitHub ecosystem. Additionally, GitHub Actions offers hosted runners for Linux, Windows, and macOS with dynamic scaling, removing the need for self-managed build servers.

Traditional news media, including television news and newspapers, have downsized both the number and the size of their news bureaus over the past several decades. This consolidation has been driven by declining profitability, a trend linked to rising competition from Internet-based news sources. As a result, media organizations have less financial capacity to invest in field reporting and other news-gathering activities, reducing the reach and depth of their coverage.

The Montenegrin Cup (women) is the national knockout cup competition for women's football in Montenegro. In Montenegrin, the tournament is known as Kup Crne Gore za žene. The competition was established in 2015, seven years after the Montenegrin Women's League had been formed.

Montenegrin Cup (women) is the national knockout football cup competition for women's football in Montenegro. The Montenegrin Women's League was established in 2008, providing the domestic framework for the sport. The Football Association of Montenegro organized the first Montenegrin Women's Cup in the 2015–16 season, marking the competition's inaugural edition. The inaugural tournament featured seven participating teams, and the first round was played as the quarterfinals.

Biathle is a sub-discipline of modern pentathlon that comprises running and freestyle swimming. Races feature seamless transitions between the segments, in a format reminiscent of triathlon competition. It is a sport in its own right, with its own competitive structure and events. The discipline shares notable similarities with aquathlon, another multisport discipline that also combines swimming and running but originates from triathlon. Typical Biathle events involve a 200-meter swim followed by a 3-kilometer run, a distance that is shorter than the standard aquathlon distances.

Biathle is an internationally recognized sport with world-class status. It is not part of the Olympic program. Competitions are conducted under the rules of the Union Internationale de Pentathlon Moderne (UIPM).

Within the period of the Republic of China, the Kuomintang pursued comprehensive reforms of land tenure and use as a central element of its policy program. On 8 January 1933, Chiang Kai-shek established the Chinese Institute of Land Economics to coordinate these aims, operating under the 1932 Ten Principles for promoting Party Land Policy. The initiative sought to regulate ownership rights, secure equal land rights, improve land use, and create land governance bodies to facilitate redistribution. Contemporary observers, including U.S. Ambassador Patrick Hurley, characterized the ideological gap between the Nationalists and the Communists as not greater than that between the Republican and Democratic parties in the United States, reflecting a comparatively narrow difference in policy orientation.
Việt Nam Quốc Dân Đảng, also known as the Vietnamese Kuomintang, was organized along lines inspired by the Kuomintang. Within its ideological spectrum, socialism constituted a notable component.

Apache TinkerPop is a framework for graph computing that encompasses Gremlin, the traversal language and its underlying execution environment. Gremlin operates as a virtual machine composed of a defined instruction set and an execution engine that processes traversals. In its architectural discussions, Gremlin has been compared to Java, with commentators drawing parallels between Gremlin’s instruction-based execution model and Java’s approach to running bytecode.

Apache TinkerPop provides a framework for graph computing in which the Gremlin traversal machine is capable of running on a single machine or across a distributed compute cluster, allowing scalable execution from local environments to large-scale deployments. Its execution-agnostic design enables Gremlin traversals to operate on both graph databases (OLTP) and graph processors (OLAP), thereby supporting a unified approach to graph data processing across different backends.

Cosmological horizon refers to two distinct causal boundaries in the universe: the particle horizon and the event horizon. The particle horizon defines the limit beyond which light has not had time to reach an observer since the beginning of cosmic history, effectively dividing space into regions from which light has already arrived and regions that remain unobservable due to insufficient light travel time, thereby marking the boundary of the observable universe. The event horizon, by contrast, delineates the set of points from which light signals can ever reach the observer in the future; regions lying beyond it cannot be observed at any time. In this way, the event horizon bounds all possible future observations. These boundaries arise from the framework of general relativity within an expanding universe as described by Big Bang cosmology.

In cosmology, the particle horizon denotes the boundary at a specified moment that separates events that have already been observed from those that remain unobservable at that time. It corresponds to the greatest distance from which causal signals could have reached an observer since the origin of the universe. Consequently, it defines the observable universe by delimiting the region within which information from the past can be retrieved at that epoch.
In 2015, the University of Leeds was ranked as the tenth most targeted British university by graduate employers, indicating a decline of two places from its eighth-position in 2014.

The University of Leeds is a founding member of major research and university networks, including the Russell Group of leading UK universities, the N8 Group for research collaboration, the Worldwide Universities Network, the Association of Commonwealth Universities, the European University Association, the White Rose University Consortium, the Santander Network, and the CDIO Initiative. It is affiliated with Universities UK. Leeds University Business School has earned the Triple Crown of international accreditation from AACSB, AMBA, and EQUIS.

Kluwer Academic Publishers, through its association with Springer, reflects Springer’s involvement in open-access publishing, as Springer is a member of the Open Access Scholarly Publishers Association (OASPA). In certain Springer journals, authors retain copyright and may choose between open-access licenses or traditional restricted licenses. Open-access publishing often requires an author payment to retain copyright, though such charges can be funded by a third party. For example, a national institution in Poland enables its authors to publish in open-access journals without personal costs, with funding supplied by public funds.

Kluwer Academic Publishers, a major commercial publisher of scientific and scholarly literature, has been cited in analyses of the incentives shaping for-profit publishing. Proponents citing Goodhart's law and signatories of the Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA) contend that commercial publishers stand to benefit from calibrating bibliometric and scientometric indicators to maximize perceived value. Central to this critique is the journal impact factor, which is frequently used as a proxy for prestige and can influence where authors submit work, as well as library subscription decisions and funding allocations. The resulting emphasis on metrics can affect publisher revenues, including subsidies linked to access through subscriptions financed by public or institutional funds. At the same time, academics contribute a substantial amount of unpaid labor—through peer review, editorial tasks, and other services—that underpins the revenue-generation model of such publishers. Critics argue that these dynamics encourage metric-driven practices and raise concerns about transparency and the distribution of costs and benefits within the scholarly communication system.

Within the ISO 639-3 standard, 520 codes in the range qaa–qtz are designated for local use. These locally assigned identifiers are intended to cover languages or language constructs not included in the main code set, and new local-use assignments are issued upon request. An illustrative example is Rebecca Bettencourt's application of a local-use code to certain constructed languages.

ISO 639-3 is part of Wikimedia’s language-tagging framework, under which the Wikimedia Foundation requires that every new language-based project be assigned an ISO 639 code. Acceptable codes come from any of the ISO 639-1, ISO 639-2, or ISO 639-3 standards, ensuring consistency across projects. This requirement applies to the creation of new language Wikipedias and similar ventures within the Wikimedia ecosystem.

Project 621, the initial concept for an amphibious assault submarine, was never built. Subsequent designs were larger and more ambitious in scope, but the addition of capabilities such as at-sea replenishment for other submarines and submarine rescue operations introduced delays. Although the concepts were considered feasible in principle, the extra requirements hindered progress. In 1964, Project 664 initiated construction at Severodvinsk, yet the integration of replenishment, transport, and mine-laying duties generated significant technical and logistical complications, even in the presence of proposals for nuclear propulsion.

During the history of amphibious assault submarines, the United States Navy explored a number of preliminary designs for submarine transports, though these efforts remained comparatively limited in scope relative to the more extensive submarine transport design initiatives undertaken by the Soviet Union.

Karachi features six uninterrupted corridors designed as urban expressways to allow traffic to traverse substantial distances without stopping at intersections or traffic signals. These corridors comprise Karsaz Road (16 km), which connects the PAF Museum in central Karachi with the SITE Industrial Area; Rashid Minhas Road (20 km), linking Surjani Town with Shah Faisal Town; University Road (19 km), extending from the urban core of the city to the Gulistan-e-Johar suburb; Shahrah-e-Faisal (18 km), running from the Sadar area to Jinnah International Airport; Shahrah-e-Pakistan (18 km), connecting the city centre to Federal B. Area; and Sher Shah Suri Road (18 km), linking the city centre to Nazimabad.

Karachi faces challenges in urban planning and the delivery of municipal services that have not kept pace with the city’s rapid population growth, a gap that contributes to relatively low livability rankings. The city lacks a cohesive transportation policy and its transport system is regarded as inadequate. As many as 1,000 new vehicles are added to already congested streets on a daily basis. In addition, the road network shows widespread deterioration, with many roads and streets in disrepair and repairs often not carried out in a timely manner.

Lewis-acid–catalyzed carbonyl additions are a staple strategy for forging carbon–carbon bonds in natural product synthesis. Among representative examples, the initial two transformations come from the routes to the natural products (+)-lycoflexine and zaragozic acid C, illustrating direct applications of the Sakurai and Mukaiyama reactions. A third example, encountered on the route to (+)-fawcettimine, involves a Lewis-acid–catalyzed opening of a cyclopropane that proceeds in a manner analogous to a Mukaiyama–Michael-type process.

Under Lewis acid catalysis, the Mukaiyama aldol reaction and the Sakurai reaction enable the addition of silyl enol ethers and allylsilanes to carbonyl substrates, respectively, and both are productive chiefly under such catalysis. These transformations proceed through acyclic transition states corresponding to 1,2- or 1,4-addition, with steric factors predominantly governing the stereochemical outcome, in contrast to the rigid Zimmerman–Traxler cyclic transition state invoked for aldol reactions that employ lithium, boron, or titanium enolates. Consequently, the double bond geometry of the participating silane does not reliably dictate the product stereochemistry. In the Sakurai 1,2-addition, Kumada’s model predicts the syn diastereomer to predominate for the (E) silane and to be only slightly favored for the (Z) silane. By comparison, Heathcock’s analysis shows that, for simple substrates, there is essentially no diastereoselectivity in intermolecular Mukaiyama aldol reactions.

Skins, stylized SKINS, is an Australian manufacturer of compression garments for athletes and sports enthusiasts. Founded in 1996, the company designs and produces performance apparel intended to enhance athletic activity and recovery. In 2019, Skins filed for bankruptcy, after which its assets were acquired by Symphony Holdings, a Hong Kong–based holding company, which holds the rights to use the SKINS brand.

Skins, a sportswear brand, and its associated intellectual property filed for bankruptcy with a Swiss court in January 2019. The brand was subsequently acquired by Symphony Holdings, a publicly traded company based in Hong Kong. Following the acquisition, the brand was placed under new management.

Space Station Freedom was NASA's planned space station program during the 1980s and early 1990s. The agency initially underestimated the program’s costs, while the United States Congress was reluctant to provide the necessary funding, leading to persistent funding shortfalls that delayed both design and construction. In response to budget constraints, the program was repeatedly redesigned and re-scoped, and between 1984 and 1993 it underwent seven major redesigns, each one reducing the station’s planned size, capacity, and capabilities. As a result, it failed to meet the timeline associated with the project and did not come to fruition within the decade that the administration had projected; Freedom was never built. Additionally, no Space Shuttle launches were conducted as part of the Freedom program.

Following a presidential announcement, NASA initiated studies to determine potential uses of Space Station Freedom for scientific research and industrial applications. The contemplated uses encompassed activities conducted domestically in the United States as well as overseas. To support planning, NASA compiled a database cataloging thousands of prospective missions and payloads. The studies also assessed how the station might support future planetary exploration missions in addition to activities conducted in low Earth orbit.

Access to the UEFI shell is not uniform and depends on the firmware implementation, varying by manufacturer and motherboard model. In some firmware environments, there is a direct option to launch the shell, and for 64-bit systems the shell executable is typically stored on the EFI System Partition at the path /SHELLX64.EFI. Other platforms provide an embedded UEFI shell that can be invoked through specific key combinations during startup. On systems without an integrated launcher, users can create a USB flash drive containing the shell or configure a manual boot entry using the UEFI boot manager command (bcfg) that points to the shell file.

The EDK2 Application Development Kit (EADK) is a development toolkit that enables the use of standard C library functions within UEFI applications, supporting the creation of secure boot components and other UEFI software. It is freely available for download from Intel's TianoCore UDK/EDK2 project on SourceForge, which hosts the codebase and build tools for UEFI development. Demonstrating its capabilities, a port of a Python interpreter has been released as a UEFI application built with EADK. Since 2015, development of the UDK/EDK2 project has shifted to GitHub, reflecting ongoing maintenance and community-driven evolution.

During the spring of 617, Dou Jiande proclaimed himself the Prince of Changle. He also replaced the era name used by his followers, substituting Daye with Dingchou, a move that signified an official break from the Sui dynasty.

Dou Jiande was placed in command of the base’s garrison, while Gao dissented and took the field against Yang. Gao initially achieved victories over Yang, but his successes bred arrogance on the battlefield, prompting Dou to warn that the Duke of Donghai’s hubris would invite disaster and that, if Sui forces prevailed, their stronghold would be attacked with little mercy. Yang then defeated Gao in battle and killed him. He subsequently turned on Dou; Dou’s army collapsed, he fled, and Yang withdrew, doubting Dou’s potential. Dou soon returned, rallied the remnants of Gao’s forces, observed a mourning period for Gao, and thereafter assumed the title of general, beginning to seize nearby territory. While the rebels despised Sui officials and slaughtered them, Dou did not, treating Sui officials and scholars with clemency, which led some to surrender cities to him. Before long Dou commanded more than 100,000 soldiers.

Makuva displays substantial influence from neighboring East Timorese Papuan languages, a contact pattern that has led some observers to categorize it as Papuan. The ethnic population associated with the language numbered about 50 individuals in 1981. Among younger speakers, Fataluku is increasingly used as a first or second language, indicating an ongoing language shift away from Makuva.
Makuva, also known as Maku’a or Lóvaia, is an Austronesian language that appears to be extinct. It was spoken at the northeast tip of East Timor, near the town of Tutuala.

Kaliningrad Oblast, a Russian federal subject on the Baltic coast, traces its historical ties to Königsberg, the former Prussian capital central to the Napoleonic-era events that followed Prussia's defeats at Jena–Auerstedt in 1806 and the French occupation of Berlin. In response to these developments, the Prussian court sought aid from Russia after taking refuge in Königsberg. Russia intervened in the conflict, a shift that culminated in the battles of Eylau and Friedland in 1807. After the French victory at Friedland, the Treaties of Tilsit were signed, reconfiguring the European power balance. Today, Königsberg is known as Kaliningrad and serves as the administrative center of Kaliningrad Oblast.

Kaliningrad Oblast encompasses Kaliningrad, the sole Russian port on the Baltic Sea that remains ice-free throughout the year, a condition that enables and sustains the maintenance of Russia's Baltic Fleet.

John Bernhard Leiberg (1853–1913) was a Swedish-American botanical explorer, forester, and bryologist who, as a self-taught naturalist, conducted extensive field work in the northwestern United States. His investigations broadened knowledge of regional flora and forest resources, and he is remembered for contributing to bryology and the understanding of plant distribution in that part of the country.

John Bernhard Leiberg contributed plant specimens to the New York Botanical Garden and spent the winter of 1892 in Hamilton, Montana. He served as a field botanist for Frederick Vernon Coville, the curator of the United States National Herbarium. In 1897 he was transferred to the United States Geological Survey, where he was assigned to examine the 6,480 square mile Bitterroot Forest Reserve, a region that would later be incorporated into the National Forests in Montana and Idaho. The reserves had been expanded by a February 22, 1897 proclamation issued by President Grover Cleveland. Leiberg conducted surveys of the Bitterroot reserve in 1897 and 1898 and authored the 19th and 20th USGS annual reports, describing the topography, tree cover, and mapping locations in a previously undocumented area. From 1900 to 1904 he published descriptions of several additional western forest reserves.

In 1994, Sandia National Laboratories demonstrated muzzle velocities exceeding 9,000 m/s for a 1-gram (approximately 15-grain) projectile using a two-stage gun design. In the first stage, burning gunpowder drives a piston that pressurizes hydrogen to about 10,000 atmospheres (1.0 gigapascal). In the second stage, the pressurized hydrogen releases to propel a secondary piston that travels into a cushioned energy-absorbing layer, with the energy transferred from the piston to the projectile situated on the opposite side of the cushion, producing the extreme muzzle speed. This experiment highlighted the capacity of staged light-gas systems to attain hypervelocity for small projectiles.

In conventional firearms and artillery, muzzle velocity is determined by a combination of propellant charge, the burn rate and expansion characteristics of the propellant, the mass of the projectile, and the length of the barrel. Propellants that burn more slowly require longer barrels to complete the combustion process before the projectile exits, whereas faster-burning formulations can push lighter projectiles to higher speeds with the same charge. There is a tradeoff in propellant and projectile selection: slower-burning formulations are often paired with heavier projectiles, while higher burn rates can produce greater velocities for lighter projectiles. Ultimately, the maximum achievable velocity is constrained by the internal pressure generated during combustion, which acts as a limiting factor for safety and design. Therefore, attaining a desired muzzle velocity involves balancing propellant quantity and burn characteristics, projectile mass, and barrel length to optimize performance within safety margins.

Within Nissan's early history, a sequence of mergers among Osaka-based automobile manufacturers occurred in the 1920s. In 1926, DAT Motors merged with Jitsuyo Jidosha Co., Ltd (also known as Jitsuyo Jidosha Seizo) to form DAT Jidosha Seizo Co., Ltd., an Osaka-based automobile producer that continued in operation until 1932. Jitsuyo Jidosha Seizo itself had been established in 1919 as a Kubota subsidiary, and from 1923 to 1925 it produced light cars and trucks under the Lila name. In 1929, DAT Automobile Manufacturing Inc. merged with a separated part of Ishikawajima-Harima Heavy Industries’ manufacturing business to form Automobile Industries Co., Ltd.

In March 2025, Nissan announced that Ivan Espinosa, then Chief Planning Officer, would become chief executive officer, with the transition scheduled for 1 April 2025 and incumbent CEO Uchida stepping down. The move was attributed to mounting concerns over declining earnings and the collapse of merger discussions with Honda, which had influenced the company's strategic direction.

Black Hat Briefings, commonly known as Black Hat, is a series of information security conferences that, given their high-profile nature, has experienced several security-related incidents involving attendees, staff, and venues. In 2008, three individuals were expelled after engaging in packet sniffing within the press room LAN. The following year, websites belonging to security researchers and groups were compromised, with attackers exposing passwords, private emails, instant messages, and sensitive documents from a vandalized page associated with Dan Kaminsky in the days leading up to the conference. During Black Hat USA 2009, a USB flash drive circulated among participants carrying the Conficker computer worm. Earlier, attendees had targeted hotel infrastructure, with efforts to hijack wireless networks and compromise hotel television billing systems; a replica that appeared to be an automated teller machine was also placed in a hotel lobby. These incidents illustrate the security challenges surrounding large, technically oriented events and their ecosystems.

Black Hat Briefings are organized into tracks, with topics spanning areas such as reverse engineering, identity and privacy, and hacking. The event also features keynote addresses from prominent figures in the information security field, including Robert Lentz, the Chief Security Officer of the United States Department of Defense; Michael Lynn; Amit Yoran, the former director of the National Cyber Security Division of the Department of Homeland Security; and General Keith B. Alexander, the former director of the National Security Agency and former commander of U.S. Cyber Command.

History's high-definition service launched across Europe in October 2007, with its Nordic region debut on 13 December 2007, and the HD schedule operated independently of the standard-definition channel. History Channel HD subsequently launched in the Netherlands in January 2008.

History is carried on major German cable platforms, including Kabel Deutschland, Kabel BW, Unitymedia, Primacom and KabelKiosk, and is also available on cable networks in Austria and Switzerland, ensuring coverage across all German states. The channel previously aired on satellite via Arena, but was not carried by Premiere until the latter was renamed Sky on 4 July 2009. History HD was launched in July 2009, aligning with the Sky rebranding. In addition, History organizes the annual History Award, an event established in 2005.

Shelton interprets “Like a Rolling Stone” as beginning by praising a dropout lifestyle accessible to those who can endure it, before turning to express compassion for individuals who have disengaged from bourgeois society. The track is regarded as addressing the loss of innocence and the harshness of experience. As the narrative unfolds, myths, props, and long-held beliefs are stripped away, exposing a demanding and uncompromising reality.

Like a Rolling Stone faced initial resistance from Columbia Records in 1965, when Shaun Considine, the release coordinator, deemed the six-minute track and its raunchy rock sound unsuitable for radio and assigned it to the label's file of canceled releases. Considine then retrieved a discarded acetate and carried it to Arthur, a New York club and disco popular with celebrities and the media, where he persuaded a DJ to spin the demo. The crowd demanded repeated plays until the recording wore out. The next morning, a disc jockey and a programming director from New York City's top‑40 stations rang Columbia to request copies. Consequently, on July 20, 1965, the single was issued with "Gates of Eden" as its B-side.

Frank Wheeler Mondell, born in St. Louis, Missouri and educated in public schools, engaged in farming, stock-raising, and railroad construction for many years before settling in the Wyoming Territory in 1887. He served as mayor of Newcastle, Wyoming, from 1888 to 1895, and subsequently represented Wyoming in the United States House of Representatives from 1895 to 1897 and again from 1899 to 1923. During the 66th and 67th Congresses he was the majority leader on the House floor, and he took a prominent part in shaping the legislation enacted by Congress. Mondell remained active in Republican politics, participating in conventions from 1902 to 1924 and chairing the 1924 Republican National Convention. He died in 1939 in Washington, D.C.

7 is a U2 EP that gathers material connected to the band’s Pop era and subsequent live performances. The drum track on Walk On is the same as the one used on Summer Rain, while Always appears here as an early version of Beautiful Day. Big Girls Are Best is a leftover from the Pop sessions. The Influx mix of Elevation was employed to open shows on the Elevation Tour. The blue-cover single version of Walk On was featured in concert performances, and a live rendition of Walk On was released on America: A Tribute to Heroes. Additionally, in 2002 a Hallelujah mix of Walk On, with a hallelujahs coda, was issued on a promotional CD.

Shiv Dayal Singh is a poet whose poems appear in the collection Sar Vachan Chhand Band. His work is distinguished by a pronounced emotional appeal, and it blends popular idiomatic expressions drawn from north Indian languages, including Khari Boli, Awadhi, Brij Bhasha, and Rajasthani, with elements drawn from the Gurmukhi linguistic tradition.

Sar Vachan Vartik, a work associated with Shiv Dayal Singh, comprises two parts. The first part contains an introduction written by Salig Ram, while the second part consists of notes drawn from the discourses delivered by Shiv Dayal Singh in satsang up to 1878. These discourses articulate the essential teachings of the faith.

The article concerns a five-year campaign in the Nahua town of Tepoztlán, near Mexico City, opposing the construction of a golf course. During the movement, younger participants played distinct yet complementary roles: children assisted with the preparation of meals and refreshments, while adolescents recruited peers and helped broaden political engagement, with both groups actively taking part in marches and demonstrations. Authorities’ repressive actions were not interpreted as negative by the participants; rather, such measures appeared to spur additional political activity among the youth. Participation facilitated greater integration into the local political process, expanding children’s and adolescents’ understanding and enabling them to contribute new perspectives and potential solutions. The process was voluntary: adults encouraged interest but left the decision to the individual child, accommodating the pace of involvement and ensuring that participation proceeded at a comfortable tempo for each participant.

In Tepoztlán, residents actively encourage children's participation in community activities, reflecting a belief that every member can contribute to communal endeavors. Mothers commonly bring young children to meetings and activities to foster early involvement, and as they mature, children increasingly express a desire to join groups on their own initiative.

Slobodan Živojinović represented SFR Yugoslavia in international tennis competition. At the 1988 Summer Olympics in Seoul, he was the 15th seed in the men's singles event and was defeated in the second round by France's Guy Forget.

On 23 November 2000, Stefan Živojinović, eight-year-old son of Slobodan Živojinović and Lepa Brena, was abducted by the Zemun Clan in front of the couple's home in Belgrade. He was released five days later, and the family reportedly paid a ransom that exceeded two million Deutsche Marks.

Number 6 fuel oil is a highly viscous residual fuel oil produced as the residue remaining after the lighter, more valuable cuts of crude oil have boiled off during distillation. Its high viscosity necessitates preheating to about 104–127 °C (219–261 °F) before use. The designation “residual” refers to the portion left after the lighter fractions have been removed, and the residue may contain impurities such as roughly 2 percent water and 0.5 percent mineral oil. Also known as residual fuel oil (RFO), it is specified in naval contexts under the Bunker C designation and in Pacific specifications as PS-400.

Fuel oil, especially substandard bunker fuels used in maritime shipping, emits pollutants when burned that are linked to adverse health effects, including serious illnesses and fatalities. Before the International Maritime Organization implemented its 2020 sulfur cap, shipping-related air pollution was estimated to cause about 400,000 premature deaths annually, largely from lung cancer and cardiovascular disease. In the same period prior to 2020, maritime pollution was also associated with approximately 14 million cases of childhood asthma each year.

Dascylium, also rendered Daskylion, was a town of ancient Bithynia. It was known in Greek as Δασκύλιον and Δασκυλεῖον (the latter corresponding to Daskyleion). The town was mentioned by Stephanus of Byzantium.

Area codes 418 and 581 serve eastern Quebec, with 418 representing the last of the region’s original four area codes to be split around the turn of the millennium. By 2006, 418 was nearing exhaustion under Canada’s number allocation system, which assigns blocks of 10,000 numbers to competitive local exchange carriers for each rate centre, tied to a single three-digit prefix. Once a number is allocated to a carrier and rate centre, it cannot be moved to a different rate centre, a constraint that contributed to significant waste of numbering resources as demand expanded. The rigid framework was further amplified by the proliferation of cellphones and pagers, particularly in larger cities, leading to inefficiencies in utilization. In 2002, several megacities were created that were then divided among multiple rate centres and have not been amalgamated, a fragmentation that persisted over time. Saguenay, for example, is split across four rate centres. To address these capacity and allocation issues, an overlay code, 581, was introduced to provide additional numbering capacity within the same geographic region.

Area codes 418 and 581 are part of the North American Numbering Plan and illustrate the early practice of assigning more than one area code to a single province. Historical records indicate that Ontario and Quebec were the only Canadian provinces to receive multiple area code designations, with the allocations made by the American Telephone and Telegraph Company (AT&T) at the inception of the original North American area codes in 1947.

There is a general consensus among commentators that The Onion's satirical portrayal contributed to shaping Joe Biden's public image during his political career. In 2014, Jonathan Bernstein of Bloomberg Opinion attributed Biden's public persona to a blend of The Onion's satirical depiction and Biden's own actions and temperament. Bernstein suggested that any vice president is prone to being perceived as ridiculous, with the central question being how that perception emerges. He also argued that once The Onion devised the corresponding image, it seemed to align closely with Biden's public persona.

The Onion’s early coverage of Joe Biden presented him as a conventional vice president within its satirical framework. The publication also ran a spoof centered on the National Thanksgiving Turkey Presentation, featuring a headline that lampooned the ceremony by depicting Biden pardoning a single yam during the vice-presidential Thanksgiving ritual. By 2010, editors had gravitated toward a portrayal by Nackers that was widely described as nearly unrecognizable compared with Biden’s public image. The character’s popularity, however, contributed to a backlog of rejected pitches as editors faced a high volume of joke submissions about Biden, many of which were ultimately dismissed.

In 1860, Adolf Bastian argued for a shared mental core across humanity, contending that a rigorous cross-cultural comparison would reveal that worldviews are built from the same fundamental elements. He maintained that all societies harbor universal ideas, while observed differences stem from locally rooted variations in beliefs. This approach helped lay the groundwork for the modern understanding of culture. Franz Boas was educated within this intellectual tradition and later carried these ideas to the United States.

Culture is a central concept in anthropology, referring to the learned and shared ways of life that people inherit and transmit across generations through social learning within their communities. While diverse in form, all human societies exhibit cultural universals—patterns and capacities that recur across cultures, though expressed in context-specific ways. Expressive domains include art, music, dance, ritual, and religious practice, which convey meaning and identity. Technological practices encompass tool use, cooking methods, shelter construction, and clothing. The material dimension of culture comprises tangible expressions such as technology, architecture, and artistic objects. By contrast, immaterial aspects cover the principles governing social organization and political life, along with mythologies, philosophy, literature (both oral and written), and scientific thought; together these constitute the intangible cultural heritage of a society.

Changdeokgung sustained a major fire on November 10, 1917, around 5 p.m., which began in Daejojeon, the former emperor’s bedchambers, and soon spread to the naejŏn area of the complex. The flames were extinguished by about 8 p.m. that same day, but the blaze caused the loss of numerous valuables and historic relics. Reconstruction began soon afterward and continued for years, its progress slowed by the 1919 March First Movement protests. During this period, the colonial government ordered the demolition and recycling of many Gyeongbokgung buildings to facilitate Changdeokgung’s reconstruction. By 1920, Daejojeon had been rebuilt, and the former royal family resumed living there.

Within Changdeokgung, Sujeongjeon (originally Sujeongdang) was renamed Sujeongjeon in 1794. Repairs were completed on the 8th day of the 12th month that year, and the crown prince began residing there in 1796, followed by occupancy by Queen Jeongsun and Queen Hyoui. A fire broke out on the 13th day of the 12th month in 1813, with the main building sustaining little damage. Queen Hyoui died there in the third month of 1821. In the third month of 1881 the hall was repaired and renamed Hamnyeongjeon, a designation distinct from Deoksugung’s Hamnyeongjeon, but it was subsequently destroyed by fire on the 7th day of the 11th month of 1881, soon after the renaming. The rebuilding was interrupted by Empress Myeongseong’s assassination in 1895, and Hamnyeongjeon was relocated to Gyeongbokgung, where it became the building Jibokjae.

Oracle provides the Java platform for use with the Java programming language. The Android Software Development Kit serves as an alternative software platform, and it is primarily employed for the development of Android applications, featuring its own graphical user interface system.

Java is a high-level, object-oriented programming language designed to promote portability and simplicity. It does not support operator overloading and does not permit multiple inheritance of classes. Instead, a Java class can implement multiple interfaces, enabling a form of multiple inheritance for types while avoiding the complexities that arise from inheriting behavior from multiple classes. By contrast, C++ supports operator overloading and allows multiple inheritance for classes.

Phosphate compounds are medicinal salts of phosphorus used in a range of clinical applications. Some phosphate preparations are employed in the treatment of urinary tract infections, while others are used to acidify urine, and certain phosphates are utilized to reduce the risk of calcium stone formation in the urinary tract by altering urinary chemistry. They are also prescribed as dietary supplements for patients who cannot obtain sufficient phosphorus due to particular disorders or diseases. Injectable phosphate formulations, however, require administration and handling by qualified health care professionals.

Salts derived from mono-phosphate and di-phosphate ions can be selectively crystallised from aqueous solutions. This selective crystallisation is achieved by adjusting the solution’s pH to about 4.7 or 9.8, which governs the relative solubilities and allows formation of the desired phosphate species.

Victor L. Berger has witnessed multiple splits within his party, reflecting the recurring factionalism that has characterized its history. Historically, the party confronted utopianism and fanaticism rather than anarchism, maintaining a pragmatic socialist program rather than endorsing anarchist tendencies. In the contemporary period, anarchist currents are again perceived as a threat, described as eroding the party’s core vitality. This trajectory indicates a shift in internal pressures over time, moving from battles with utopianism and zealotry to concerns about anarchist influence.

Victor L. Berger was a founding member of the Social Democracy of America in 1897. He led the split of the faction committed to political action to form the Social Democratic Party of America in 1898. He then served on the SDP's National Executive Committee, the party's governing body, for the entire duration of the party's existence.

Within Latin grammar, the noun phrase res militaris serves as the base element in the nominative singular, rendered as res militaris. The genitive singular form is rei militaris, and the ablative singular form is re militari. Accordingly, rei militaris and re militari are the genitive and ablative forms of res militaris, respectively.

De re militari, attributed to Vegetius, frames its account of the Roman army on descriptions drawn from the middle to the later Republic. G. R. Watson notes that it is the sole surviving ancient manual of Roman military institutions in a complete form. He also questions its value, arguing that Vegetius was neither a professional historian nor a soldier and that the work is a loosely assembled compilation drawn from material across different ages, resulting in a mixture of inconsistencies. In the text, Vegetius lists his antiquarian authorities as Cato the Elder, Cornelius Celsus, Frontinus, Paternus, and the imperial constitutions of Augustus, Trajan, and Hadrian (1.8).

CASPAR is an Integrated Project within the European Union’s research framework, designed to boost European competitiveness in both fundamental and applied science. Its activities are guided by the Priority Themes of the Framework Programme, focusing on addressing major societal needs identified within that structure. A key characteristic of IPs, including CASPAR, is the strong involvement of small and medium-sized enterprises to ensure that research outcomes can be translated into commercially viable products or services. The requirement for SME participation in IPs is comparable to that governing STRePs, reflecting a shared emphasis on industry engagement across EU research instruments.

The CASPAR digital preservation project operates within the Horizon 2020 framework, which implements the European environmental research and innovation policy. This policy sets out a transformative agenda aimed at greening both the economy and society as a whole, with the overarching objective of achieving sustainable development.

The British Columbia Social Credit Party maintained a comparatively modest political operation that nonetheless secured two additional terms in the 1979 and 1983 provincial elections, despite controversy surrounding Bennett's Restraint program. The operation, nicknamed the Baby Blue Machine, was largely composed of political advisers imported from Ontario's Progressive Conservative Party. It never evolved into a major political apparatus comparable to Ontario's Big Blue Machine. Bennett retired from politics in 1986.

Under the Bennett government, the British Columbia Social Credit Party pursued a blend of free-market rhetoric with strategic state involvement in key sectors. In 1961 it nationalized the province's largest private hydroelectric company to create BC Hydro, a measure intended to underpin the government's extensive dam-building program. Earlier, in 1958, it established BC Ferries to provide coastal transport links. It also created the Bank of British Columbia, with the provincial government owning a 25 percent stake.

A Beautiful Time received positive reception from music critics. Metacritic, which normalizes reviews from mainstream critics onto a 100-point scale, assigned the album a score of 84 out of 100 based on four reviews, a rating that Metacritic regards as universal acclaim.
A Beautiful Time is a 2022 release by Nelson. On February 10, 2022, Nelson released the single "I'll Love You Till the Day I Die," a song written by Chris Stapleton and Rodney Crowell.

In Apache Pinot, queries are received by broker nodes, which act as the entry point for client requests. The brokers then verify the request and determine its path by consulting the segment-to-server routing table, a guidance map that shows which servers hold the relevant segments. Using this routing information, the brokers distribute the query across the appropriate real-time and offline servers, enabling parallel processing and subsequent aggregation of results for delivery to the client.

Apache Pinot uses Apache Helix for cluster management, with Helix embedded as an agent within Pinot components to enable centralized control. Helix relies on Apache ZooKeeper to coordinate operations and maintain the overall cluster state and health. Through Helix, all Pinot servers and brokers are managed. Helix itself is a generic cluster-management framework designed for managing partitions and replicas in distributed systems.

Nasdaq-100, launched by the Nasdaq Stock Market on January 31, 1985, was created alongside the Nasdaq Financial-100 as two separate indices. The Nasdaq-100 encompasses a broad array of sectors, including industrials, technology, retail, telecommunications, biotechnology, healthcare, transportation, media, and services, while the Nasdaq Financial-100 concentrates on financial-sector firms such as banks, insurers, brokerages, and mortgage lenders.

Nasdaq-100 is the only one of the three Nasdaq indices that undergoes a regularly scheduled annual re-ranking. The re-ranking occurs in December each year, and it serves to ensure that the largest non-financial companies listed on Nasdaq are accurately included in the index.

Germanicopolis, an ancient town in the region of Bithynia, is attested by the Greek name Γερμανικόπολις and is also identified with Caesarea in Bythinia. It should not be confused with Caesarea Germanica, a different locality, which is a former bishopric and presently exists as a Latin Catholic titular see.

Germanicopolis in Bithynia was brought under Ottoman control in 1326 as the empire expanded into northwestern Anatolia. The Ottomans subsequently established Bursa, situated nearby, as the capital; Bursa corresponds to the ancient city of Prusa. This relocation marked an important administrative development for the early Ottoman state, which used Bursa as its capital for several decades before later changes.

In the northwestern part of Ward County, archaeological investigations have revealed evidence of prehistoric human activity, including occupation debris as well as petroglyphs and pictographs. These findings reflect long-standing human use of the landscape and provide insight into the region’s ancient inhabitants. The area is noted to have been occupied by a sequence of Indigenous groups, among them the Suma-Jumano, Apache, and Comanche peoples. Additionally, the county’s sand hills contain native artifacts, underscoring the enduring presence of people in this landscape.

Ward County is a county located in the U.S. state of Texas. Its population was 11,644 at the 2020 census. The county seat is Monahans. The county was created in 1887 and organized in 1892, and it is named for Thomas W. Ward, a soldier in the Texas Revolution.

The Hexagonal and Grid Mapping System was reviewed by Lewis Pulsipher in The Space Gamer, issue No. 50. In the review, Pulsipher described the system as an impressive product and highlighted its usefulness as a key tool for hex-mapping large regions of a role-playing world, stating that he could not imagine a better aid.

The Hexagonal and Grid Mapping System is a package containing fifty one-sided sheets printed on letter-sized paper, featuring hexagonal grids designed for game mapping, and stored in a wrap-around folder.

Pakistan is a sovereign nation located in South Asia. It has a coastline measuring 1,046 kilometres (650 miles) along the Arabian Sea and the Gulf of Oman to its southern edge. The country shares land borders with Afghanistan to the west, Iran to the southwest, India to the east, and China to the far northeast.

The Toronto Purchase refers to an 1787 agreement concluded on September 23 at the Carrying-Place of the Bay of Quinte between the British Crown and the Mississaugas of New Credit for the transfer of lands along Lake Ontario. In the Toronto region, approximately 250,808 acres were exchanged for goods, and the tract later became York County, encompassing much of present-day Toronto and the Regional Municipality of York. The land was bounded to the south by Lake Ontario; the western limit ran near Etobicoke Creek and along what is now Highways 427 and 50, formerly designated as the Indian Line, which served as the purchase boundary; the eastern boundary stretched roughly from Ashbridge's Bay through Woodbine Avenue to Highway 404; and the northern boundary extended south of Sideroad 15–Bloomington Road. The consideration consisted of cash and an assortment of goods: 2,000 gun flints, 24 brass kettles, 120 mirrors, 24 laced hats, a bale of flowered flannel, and 96 gallons of rum. The Mississaugas understood the agreement as a perpetual rental for British use rather than a complete extinguishment of their rights, with gifts and presents exchanged as part of the transaction.

Following the Treaty of Paris, which fixed the boundary of British North America roughly through the middle of the Great Lakes, lands north of that line were regarded as strategically vital and desirable for Loyalist settlement after the war. In 1781 the Mississaugas surrendered a strip of land along the Niagara River, and in 1783 land on the Bay of Quinte was ceded for Mohawks loyal to the British, today represented by the Tyendinaga Mohawk Territory. Between 1783 and 1785, about 10,000 Loyalists arrived and established settlements on land the Crown recognized as Indian land. In 1784 the Mississaugas surrendered additional territory in the Niagara peninsula, including land on the Grand River intended for the Iroquois. Taken together, these transfers and settlements provided the Indigenous land base and demographic context that underpinned the Toronto Purchase.

Critical reception of Thriller was decisively positive. J. D. Considine praised its victorious sound, noting that Jackson and producer Jones preserved the lean grooves and polished arrangements that defined Off the Wall. John Rockwell of The New York Times described the album as a standout pop work and a significant statement by a gifted singer, pointing to its string of hit songs. Rockwell also argued that Thriller helped bridge divides between white and black popular music, suggesting that some white publications and radio outlets that had historically shunned black artists were more willing to overlook Jackson’s race. Christopher Connelly of Rolling Stone characterized Thriller as a brisk, lively record with darker, more urgent themes, linking its songs to challenges Jackson had faced since Off the Wall and noting a shift from a youthful falsetto to a fuller, more mature voice and determined resolve. Connelly further asserted that Jackson’s renewed attitude lent the album deeper emotional urgency and marked a turning point in his creative development. Robert Christgau of The Village Voice labeled it a hits-driven project with some filler, yet regarded the work overall as nearly classic at a high level.

At a time when MTV and cable television held a smaller share of the United States market compared with broadcast networks, CBS/Epic Records aimed to promote Thriller to a national broadcast television audience by coordinating with ABC, NBC, CBS affiliates and major independents. The national broadcast premiere of the album’s first video, Billie Jean, occurred during the Halloween week in October 1984.
