The premiere concept originated with Video Concert Hall executive producers Charles Henderson and Jerry Crowe, whose network—recognized as the first nationwide music-video television service—produced a one-hour special filmed in Hollywood and Atlanta. The Thriller television special was hosted by Vincent Price and distributed by Henderson-Crowe Syndications, Inc., and it reached the top twenty television markets as well as a broad national audience, airing on approximately 150 stations including WNEW in New York, WFLD in Chicago, KTTV in Los Angeles, WPLG in Miami, WQTV in Boston, and WXIA in Atlanta.

The TUMO Center for Creative Technologies is under construction in Bilbao, with a planned opening in 2026, and will be the first TUMO Center in Spain. It is located within Azkuna Zentroa – Alhóndiga Bilbao, a building that was originally constructed in 1909 as a wine warehouse and has since become a cultural hub of the city, redesigned by Philippe Starck. The center is planned to have a weekly capacity of 1,500 students and will focus on education in technology and design.

TUMO Labs acts as the educational arm of the EU TUMO Convergence Center, guiding its strategic direction in education and innovation. It functions as a tuition-free hub for applied science and engineering, offering access to practical learning without fees. By linking higher education institutions with industry partners, it fosters collaboration and real-world relevance. Participation is open to individuals aged 18 and older. The curriculum is tailored to the goals of TUMO Labs, reflecting its focus on bridging academic study with industry-oriented, hands-on technology education.

Crime in New York (state) shows a downward trend across the early to late 2010s, as reflected by reported figures for specific years. In 2012, 451,142 crimes were reported, including 686 murders. By 2014, total crimes declined to 409,386 with 616 murders, and in 2019 the figure further dropped to 335,736 crimes and 558 murders. Over the period from 2010 to 2019, violent crime decreased by 8.0 percent, while property crime fell by 29.0 percent.

In New York City, homicide counts have risen since 2017, diverging from broader crime trends. The year 2020 saw a sharp jump in murders, increasing by 47 percent to 468, up from 319 in 2019. This surge ranks among the most substantial year-to-year increases in the city’s history. However, the 2020 total of 468 was still lower than the numbers recorded in any year from 1960 through 2011. In 2021, the city recorded 488 murders, the highest annual total since 2011.

The East Bay Phase 2 Project involves the construction of a water treatment plant in Barangay Kabulusan, Pakil, Laguna, with construction starting in 2023. The facility is designed to have a capacity of 200 million liters per day and is intended to serve the Metro Manila East Zone. Water will be delivered through a submarine pipeline laid beneath Laguna de Bay.

Laguna de Bay faces significant pollution from municipal waste generated by Metro Manila residents. About one-tenth of the total 4,100 metric tons of waste produced by these residents is dumped into the bay, amounting to roughly 410 metric tons, or about 4,000 long tons (approximately 4,500 short tons). This dumping contributes to the lake’s siltation by increasing sediment deposition. Data from the Metropolitan Manila Waterworks and Sewerage System indicate that only around 15 percent of residents in the area have an effective waste disposal system. Additionally, roughly 85 percent of shoreline households do not have toilets or septic tanks, highlighting substantial sanitation deficiencies. The Metropolitan Manila Waterworks and Sewerage System has since become defunct.

Bethlehem Church in Copenhagen is one of the churches financed and erected by the Copenhagen Church Trust, an organization founded in 1890 to raise funds for constructing new churches in the city. The design of Bethlehem Church was entrusted to architect Peder Vilhelm Jensen-Klint, who had previously designed notable Copenhagen churches such as Anna Church and Grundtvig's Church, as well as Gedser Church on Falster and St. Hans Tveje Church in Odense. In addition to the church itself, Jensen-Klint also designed a nearby congregation house, which was completed in 1931.

Bethlehem Church in Copenhagen was the first church in Denmark to replace traditional benches with individual chairs, a seating solution that was specially designed for the church. The design soon gained substantial popularity and was adopted by other churches, and it was later made commercially available for private homes.

Religion in Palau is characterized by a predominantly Christian population, with smaller minority faiths and non-religious affiliations. The 2015 census recorded an adult population (age 18 and over) of 13,300. Among these adults, Roman Catholics comprised 45.3%, Evangelicals 26.4%, Seventh-day Adventists 6.9%, and Latter-day Saints 1.5%. Protestant denominations such as the Assemblies of God and Baptists accounted for 0.9% and 0.7%, respectively, while the syncretic Modekngei faith—an animist Christian tradition unique to Palau—made up 5.7%. Muslims represented 3.0%, and another 11.2% were categorized as other, not listed, or non-religious.

Religion in Palau, according to the 2020 census, is predominantly Christian, with Roman Catholicism accounting for 46.9% of the population. Protestant denominations, largely Evangelical, comprise 25.9%, while Seventh-day Adventists represent 5.0%. The traditional Palauan belief system Modekngei accounts for 5.1%, and Muslim adherents make up 4.9%. The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints constitutes 0.9%, and all other religions together total 11.4%.

Choson Yesul is a monthly publication established in 1956. It serves as the official organ of the Central Committee of the Korean Federation of Literature and Arts, and its headquarters are in Pyongyang.

Choson Yesul is a monthly cultural and arts magazine published in Pyongyang, North Korea, since 1956. It functions as the official media outlet of the Korean Federation of Literature and Arts, a state-owned federation that coordinates the country’s literary and artistic unions. The Korean title, 조선예술, translates to "Korean art."

Ipubi's economy centers on industry and agribusiness, reflecting a blend of manufacturing activity and agricultural enterprise. The area supports a broad livestock sector, including cattle, sheep, pigs, goats, horses, and chickens. Manioc plantations constitute a major agricultural activity, with production exceeding 35,000 tons.

Ipubi is a city and municipality located in the state of Pernambuco, Brazil. According to the 2020 census by the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE), its population was 31,187 inhabitants. The municipality covers an area of 693.91 square kilometers.

Panemotichus was an early Christian episcopal see originally situated in Isauria, with its territory later reassigned to Pamphylia Secunda. The episcopal record is sparse, but Faustus is documented as having attended the First Council of Nicaea in 325 while the see was in Isauria; Cratinus is believed to have attended the Council of Chalcedon in 451; Hierius is known for signing the provincial letter to Byzantine Emperor Leo VI the Wise; and Helladius is recorded as having participated in a minor Council of Constantinople in 536. According to Le Quien's Oriens Christianus (I, 1031), no additional bishops are known and the see is not mentioned in the Notitiae Episcopatuum.

Panemotichus, also known as Panemoteichos, was an inland town in the late Roman province of Pamphylia Secunda. It functioned as a bishopric and served as a suffragan diocese to Perge, the metropolitan see overseeing the province's church hierarchy. The site was inhabited from the Roman era through the Byzantine period.

The Hungry Years is a collection of archival recordings by American country musician Willie Nelson. It was released in November 1991, concurrently with the IRS-mandated direct-sales release of Who'll Buy My Memories. The material comprises recordings captured in Bogalusa, Louisiana, in 1976.

Joshua Sinclair left acting in the 1980s to pursue a career in medicine. He earned an MD with a specialization in tropical medicine from the University of Virginia and Johns Hopkins University. He became a member of Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders). He worked at Grant Medical College in India, where he collaborated with Mother Teresa. He also worked at Chris Hani Baragwanath Hospital in South Africa.
Joshua Sinclair, born John Louis Loffredo in New York City, initially planned to become a missionary and began writing screenplays at age fourteen.

Karl Brunner, an SS general, was detained after World War II at the Island Farm Prisoner of War Camp. Subsequently, he entered service in the Bavarian government. He died in 1980, and he did not face prosecution for wartime criminal conduct.

Karl Brunner, a Waffen-SS general, has been blamed for some of the final atrocities committed by German forces in Italy after the surrender. In the immediate aftermath, celebrations by the Italian-speaking population were followed by civilian killings, with 11 people killed in Merano on 30 April 1945. A further massacre occurred in Bolzano on 3 May 1945, when Wehrmacht and SS units fired on civilians, resulting in 41 deaths. Together with ongoing clashes between German troops and Italian partisans, these incidents are referred to as the Battle of Bolzano (Battaglia di Bolzano).

Pope Nicholas V (Latin: Nicolaus V; Italian: Niccolò V) was born Tommaso Parentucelli on 15 November 1397 and died on 24 March 1455. He headed the Catholic Church and governed the Papal States from 6 March 1447 until his death. He was created a cardinal by Pope Eugene IV in 1446 after successful journeys to Italy and Germany, and was elected pope the following year after Eugene IV's death. Upon his accession, he adopted the name Nicholas in memory of his obligations to Niccolò Albergati. He remains the most recent pope to take the pontifical name Nicholas.

Pope Nicholas V sought to reinforce the faith of the Roman populace through public displays of grandeur and visible splendor intended to inspire devotion. However, the Roman people did not regard his motives or their results with approval, and discontent persisted. In 1452 a conspiracy led by Stefano Porcari to overthrow the papal government was uncovered and suppressed, underscoring lingering dissatisfaction within the city. The revelation of disaffection, together with the fall of Constantinople in 1453, darkened the final years of his pontificate. According to Thomas of Sarzana, there is a report that Nicholas V lamented that he had more happiness in a day than in an entire year.

The official title assigned to the presiding officers of justice courts is "justice," a designation that mirrors the terminology used for the New York Supreme Court, though in everyday usage these officials are typically referred to as judges. Qualifications vary by jurisdiction: village-jurisdiction courts require their justices to be lawyers, while, in general, the majority of justices need not be trained as lawyers. This pattern reflects the broader reality that many justice courts operate in small towns and villages that lack resident attorneys, whereas in larger towns the position is almost always held by individuals who are lawyers.

In New South Wales, a justice of the peace (JP) is appointed by the Governor for five-year terms. JPs are volunteers drawn from all walks of life and all sections of the community. They are trusted to perform their functions with honesty, care, and impartiality. They must not charge a fee for JP services, nor accept a gift in relation to their JP duties. They must not tell people what to write in a statutory declaration or affidavit, must not write such declarations or affidavits for anyone, and must not provide legal advice.

VP9 has been evaluated in a benchmark conducted by the same developer, comparing the ffvp9 decoder with ffh264. The assessment indicates that ffvp9 decodes video roughly 10% faster than ffh264 when the content is of equivalent quality. When the bitrate is held constant, the decoded quality between ffvp9 and ffh264 is reported as identical. The study notes that performance can be affected by implementation differences in the software. Based on these findings, ffvp9 is concluded to outperform libvpx consistently by about 25–50% across tested scenarios.

VP9 provides support for multiple color spaces to accommodate a range of video content and display standards. These include Rec. 601, Rec. 709, Rec. 2020, SMPTE-170, SMPTE-240, and the sRGB color spaces. For each supported color space, VP9 defines a corresponding YCbCr-to-RGB transformation matrix to perform the color conversions during decoding, enabling accurate color reproduction across different devices and formats.

Siston's council comprises voluntary, unpaid members who serve four-year terms. It holds monthly meetings on the third Thursday of each month at the Warmley Community Centre. The council's remit includes managing Siston affairs, such as bus shelters, local planning, and the upkeep of rural footpaths.

Siston Common, also known as the Commons, extends across the full width of the parish and contains a network of bridleways and footpaths. Historically, it served as grazing land for local farmers, supporting livestock such as cattle, goats, horses, ducks, and chickens. The western edge of the common is defined by the Avon Ring Road, which was built along that boundary.

In food microbiology, microorganisms display a range of adaptations to osmotic stress and to oxygen availability. Osmophilic bacteria can tolerate relatively high osmotic environments, though they are less osmophilic than yeasts and molds. Regarding respiration, aerobes require the presence of oxygen for growth, while anaerobes are inhibited by oxygen. Some organisms are facultative anaerobes, capable of growing in either the presence or absence of oxygen, which allows them to persist across fluctuating environmental conditions encountered in food processing, storage, and fermentation.

Food microbiology employs coliform bacteria as indicators of sanitation and hygienic quality. Fecal coliforms are a subset of the broader coliform group, with Escherichia coli frequently cited as an example of a fecal coliform. Enteric pathogens have the potential to cause gastrointestinal infections, and some of these pathogens can be encompassed within the coliform group as part of this indicator system.

Central China Normal University traces its historical origins to Zhongyuan University, which was co-founded by Chen Yi. Chen Yi later held major national and municipal offices, serving as the mayor of Shanghai from 1949 to 1958 and then as the foreign minister of China from 1958 to 1972. This sequence—first the mayoralty, then the foreign ministry—reflects the transition in 1958 from regional administration to international diplomacy.

Central China Normal University, historically connected to the Hubei Teachers Training College and to the Hubei Correspondence School, which was incorporated in 1972, was at one time part of the South China Institute for Nationalities.

The Central Cadres Training School of the Workers' Party of Korea recruits its lecturers from the managerial staff of the Central Committee, as well as from the Academy of Sciences and Kim Il Sung University.

The Central Cadres Training School of the Workers' Party of Korea is a principal educational institution of the ruling party in North Korea. It was founded on June 1, 1946 as the Central Party School of the Communist Party of North Korea, based in Pyongyang, and was established on the site of the Kim Il Sung High School, which had operated since November 1945 to train political and educational officers as well as Russian-language translators. In April 1972, commemorating Kim Il Sung's sixtieth birthday, the school was renamed the Kim Il Sung Higher Party School. A year later, in 1973, it merged with the Marxist–Leninist School. Since 1978 it has functioned as the central educational institution of the party.

Björk Guðmundsdóttir, an Icelandic singer-songwriter, producer and actress from Reykjavík, first achieved international recognition as the lead singer of The Sugarcubes and later rose to prominence with her debut solo album Debut (1993). During the Debut period she received notable awards, including the Brit Award for International Breakthrough Act and the NME Award for Best Solo Artist. At the 1994 MTV Video Music Awards, the video for her first single “Human Behaviour” garnered six nominations. Her sophomore album Post (1995) earned five Icelandic Music Awards and the MTV Europe Music Award for Best Female, and she became the first artist to receive ASCAP’s Vanguard Award. The video for “It’s Oh So Quiet” went on to win the MTV VMAs for Best Choreography in a Video. Homogenic (1997) was accompanied by highly regarded videos, with Michel Gondry’s “Bachelorette” and Chris Cunningham’s “All Is Full of Love” receiving multiple accolades, including three MTV VMAs in the categories of Best Art Direction, Breakthrough Video, and Best Visual Effects.

Among Björk's recognitions, the video for "Wanderlust"—the fourth single from Volta (2007)—was one of the earliest music videos produced in stereoscopic 3D and earned three UK Music Video Awards. In 2010 she received the Polar Music Prize from the Royal Swedish Academy of Music, an honor frequently described as the Nobel Prize of Music. For Biophilia (2011), she was named Artist of the Year at the Webby Awards and received the Music Producers Guild Innovation Award. Biophilia and its accompanying app were later included in the Museum of Modern Art's permanent collection. In 2015 MoMA staged a retrospective titled Björk, a self-titled artist retrospective curated by Klaus Biesenbach. Following the exhibition, she conceived Björk Digital, an immersive virtual reality installation presenting videos from Vulnicura (2015). The video for "Notget" won the Grand Prix in the Digital Craft category at the 2017 Cannes Lions festival.

Mathematical notation makes use of symbols drawn from multiple alphabets, notably the Greek alphabet in addition to the familiar Arabic numerals and Latin letters. Greek letters are widely used to denote a diverse array of mathematical objects and variables, serving as constants, indices, parameters, or special functions depending on the field. Hebrew letters appear less frequently but are employed in specific areas, particularly for infinite cardinal numbers in set theory and related disciplines. The choice of symbol is influenced by historical conventions and aims to provide clarity, with researchers often standardizing meanings to prevent ambiguity across subfields.

Zero and its notation occupy an essential place in the history of mathematical notation. The use of zero as a mere placeholder predates its recognition as a number by centuries, with Babylonian sources employing a symbol to denote the absence of a value in a positional system and Greco-Egyptian mathematical practice using a similar device. Subsequently, zero emerged as a distinct integer within the numeral traditions of the Maya, Indian, and Arab scholars, who incorporated it into a functional decimal framework. For a more comprehensive treatment, see the history of zero.

Odd Arne Westad is a prominent historian focusing on international history and contemporary international affairs. He has published fifteen books in these fields, including a revised edition of the Penguin History of the World issued in 2013. In 2010 he co-edited, with Melvyn Leffler, the three-volume Cambridge History of the Cold War. His 2012 work Restless Empire: China and the World since 1750 surveys the last two and a half centuries of China’s relations with the wider world. Westad also authored The Cold War: A World History in 2017, which offers an overview of the conflict and its enduring significance. The Times Literary Supplement named The Cold War: A World History a book of the year, praising it as a work of considerable importance for understanding both historical developments and their implications for the future.

Odd Arne Westad is a scholar of global and international history who, in 2014, became the first holder of Harvard University's S.T. Lee Chair of US-Asia Relations. During his Harvard tenure, he lectured on international affairs and global history at the Harvard Kennedy School and held the position of Senior Scholar at the Harvard Academy of International and Area Studies. In 2019 he transitioned to Yale University, where he teaches courses on global and international history and is based in both the Yale History Department and the Jackson School of Global Affairs.

In 1598 the governance of the Spanish Netherlands was transferred to Isabella Clara Eugenia and Archduke Albert VII of Austria. Their rule coincided with a period of peace and economic stability, and it helped foster a distinct southern Netherlandish identity while reinforcing the Habsburg dynasty and moderating anti-Spanish sentiments. In the early 17th century Brussels became the seat of a thriving court under the Archdukes, with notable artists such as Peter Paul Rubens contributing to its cultural prominence. Although the arrangement provided formal independence from the Spanish crown, the territory remained unofficially within the Spanish sphere of influence. Albert died in 1621, after which the region returned to formal Spanish control, while Isabella continued as governor until her death in 1633.

Under the Habsburgs, the title Duke of Burgundy remained linked to the family’s Burgundian inheritance and was associated with the rulers who governed the Low Countries, including Charles V and his successor Philip II, even though the actual Duchy of Burgundy had been ceded to France in 1477. The Free County of Burgundy, today known as Franche-Comté, remained under Habsburg rule from 1493 onward. In imperial practice, the term Burgundy came to denote the Habsburg hereditary lands across both the historic Burgundian territories and the Low Countries, a usage formalized by the creation of the Imperial Burgundian Circle in 1512 and lasting until 1795. The Austrian Netherlands, or the Low Countries under Habsburg administration, were governed by a Governor-General of the Netherlands. Notably, Charles V was born and raised in the Low Countries and frequently resided at the Palace of Coudenberg in Brussels.

In gastropods, the tropical abalone Haliotis asinina has shown expression of the conserved Pax-258 gene in its statocysts, which serve as gravity- and balance-sensing organs. Pax-258 is a conserved gene across metazoans and is implicated in the development of balance-related structures in eumetazoans. The localization of Pax-258 in the statocysts of a molluscan species points to a conserved role for Pax-258 in sensory balance organs across eumetazoans, underscoring shared molecular mechanisms underlying balance perception among diverse animal lineages.

Bathynerita naticoidea is a deepwater gastropod snail. Research indicates that it can detect mussel beds hosting Bathymodiolus childressi and is drawn to water containing chemical cues associated with Bathymodiolus childressi. These findings illustrate that this species relies on chemosensory detection to locate mussel beds, highlighting the role of chemical cues in the sensory ecology and habitat localization of gastropods.

Latin American Canadians constitute a diverse and predominantly recent immigrant community in Canada, with the bulk of arrivals occurring in the late twentieth century. The community's origins span many countries, led by Mexico, Colombia, El Salvador, Puerto Rico, and Peru, with sizable but smaller groups from Chile, Venezuela, Brazil, Cuba, Guatemala, and other nations, such that almost every Latin American country is represented among newcomers. Migration has been driven chiefly by the prospect of improved economic opportunities in Canada, although some migrants have left because of political instability, civil conflict, or repression at home. Illustrative examples include Chileans who departed after Pinochet's dictatorship, Salvadorans fleeing the civil war, Peruvians escaping internal conflict, Dominicans opposed to the Trujillo and Balaguer regimes, Mexicans affected by the drug war, and Colombians fleeing violence.

As of the 2021 Canadian Census, Latin American Canadians form sizable communities within several Census Metropolitan Areas, with the Toronto CMA accounting for 396,459 people (3.5%), Montreal CMA 287,856 (3.2%), Vancouver CMA 151,500 (2.0%), Calgary CMA 134,395 (2.3%), Edmonton CMA 121,960 (1.6%), Ottawa CMA 90,620 (1.4%), and Hamilton CMA 30,605 (1.9%). The fastest-growing Latin American communities are reported in the provinces of Alberta, Manitoba, and Nova Scotia.

After 1931, a number of artists still adhered to De Stijl principles, though not all continued in the same direction. Gerrit Rietveld persisted in designing furniture in line with the De Stijl idiom, sustaining the movement’s emphasis on geometric form and functional design. Piet Mondrian continued to work within the De Stijl style that he had begun around 1917, applying its formal vocabulary to his ongoing practice. Bart van der Leck left the group and returned to figurative compositions, signaling a shift away from De Stijl’s abstract program.

De Stijl, a Dutch art movement, emerged in 1917 as the result of collaboration among artists and architects. It was centered in several towns, notably Leiden (Theo van Doesburg and J.J.P. Oud), Voorburg (Vilmos Huszár and Jan Wils), and Laren (Piet Mondrian and Bart van der Leck). The Dutch name translates to The Style and is pronounced [də ˈstɛil].

Within conversation analysis, researchers have identified a core idea in which speakers adjust their language to fit the audience's likely interpretive resources. Harvey Sacks introduced recipient design, arguing that speakers tailor their utterances toward referents that participants are likely to recognize to ensure successful comprehension. Herbert H. Clark described the equivalent notion as audience design, stressing the speaker’s consideration of the listener’s interpretive commitments. Howard Giles characterized the process as accommodation, highlighting adjustments in speech style to suit the conversational partner. Collectively, these labels refer to the same overarching principle: the deliberate adaptation of communication to the audience to facilitate understanding in interaction.

Conversation analysis is a methodical approach to examining the organization and structure of spoken interaction, and it is applied across a wide range of contexts with benefits for multiple disciplines. Its investigations have encompassed doctor–patient interactions, media interviews, second-language acquisition, and various institutional settings, among others. Among notable work, Tanya Stivers explored the social pressures that lead physicians to prescribe antibiotics, demonstrating how interactional dynamics shape professional decisions. The field gained renewed emphasis with the 1992 publication Talk at Work by Paul Drew and John Heritage, which shifted attention toward interaction within professional contexts and broadened the scope beyond narrowly defined institutional settings. In recent years, conversation analysis has also been used to inform the development of conversational user interfaces and chatbots, linking empirical analyses of talk with advances in emerging technologies.

Hoorae Media entered into a partnership with Velvet Hammer Media in 2024 to produce a slate of television series. The slate is led by executive producers Jennifer O’Connell and Rebecca Quinn. O’Connell and Quinn had previously co-produced Sweet Life: Los Angeles and Project Greenlight: A New Generation, evidencing their experience in developing and overseeing television projects.

Hoorae Media, pronounced hooray and also known simply as Hoorae, is an American independent media production company founded in September 2020 by Issa Rae, who previously operated under the name Issa Rae Productions. The company serves as an umbrella brand to organize Rae’s activities across film, television, and digital ventures. It has produced the television series Insecure, A Black Lady Sketch Show, and Rap Sh!t in collaboration with HBO. Looking ahead, Hoorae is developing a television adaptation of Brit Bennett's The Vanishing Half and the feature film Sinkhole, the latter of which is being co-produced with Monkeypaw Productions and Universal Pictures.

The plan for a map of the Russian Empire originated under Peter the Great and was realized roughly two decades later during the reign of Empress Anna. Ivan Kirilov invited Joseph Nicolas Delisle to Russia to collaborate on the enterprise, but the partnership was marked by methodological friction: Delisle advocated a network of points determined astronomically, while Kirilov favored surveying based on geographical features with later adjustment to astronomical controls. Kirilov, consulting Delisle, published in 1734 a general map along with the first fourteen regional maps of an intended total of 120; the 1734 edition, however, was abandoned after Kirilov’s death in 1737. The Atlas Rossicus, produced by the Saint Petersburg Academy in 1745–1746 in Latin and Cyrillic, consisted of a general map and 29 regional maps. Delisle’s rigorous scientific approach during the 1730s slowed the atlas’s progress, and in 1740, while on an expedition to Siberia, he was removed from the supervisory board overseeing the atlas. Schumacher, the Academy secretary, accused him of sending secret documents to France. Delisle sought permission to leave Russia in 1743, which was granted four years later, in 1747; in the interim the Atlas Rossicus had been published under his name. Historiography remains contested: Leo Bagrow argues that the atlas should not bear his name, whereas Marie-Anne Chabin contends that Delisle should be regarded as its principal architect.

Joseph Nicolas Delisle was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society in 1725 and later became a foreign member of the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in 1749. In 1760 he proposed coordinating observations of the 1761 Transit of Venus to determine the Earth–Sun distance, and he developed a map showing where the transit would be visible and where observing stations should be located. The execution of this plan was hindered by the Seven Years' War. He retired to the Abbey of St Genevieve in 1763 and died in Paris in 1768.

Alain de Benoist, a French political writer associated with the early Nouvelle Droite, traveled to South Africa in the mid-1960s at the invitation of the National Party government led by Hendrik Verwoerd. He co-authored Vérité pour l'Afrique du Sud (1965) with Gilles Fournier, a work that endorsed apartheid. In 1966 he published Rhodesia, pays des lions fidèles with D'Orcival, defending Rhodesia's white-minority rule; the book was prefaced by Ian Smith. After returning from a 1965 trip to the United States, de Benoist deplored what he perceived as the suppression of racial segregation there and predicted that the segregated system would persist outside the law, in a more violent form.

Alain de Benoist (born December 11, 1943) is a French political philosopher and journalist. He has published under several pen names, including Fabrice Laroche, Robert de Herte, and David Barney, among others. A founding member of the Nouvelle Droite, France's New Right, he also led the ethno-nationalist think tank GRECE.

Great Petition (sculpture) references the Monster Petition, the mass drive for women's suffrage in Victoria, Australia, created in 1891. It was signed by about 30,000 Victorian women over six weeks and consisted of sheets of paper glued onto calico fabric, forming a continuous roll roughly 260 metres in length. The original petition is held by the state's Public Record Office and was tabled in Parliament in September 1891. The Women's Franchise Bill supported by the petition was rejected by the Upper House. Nineteen years later, the Victorian government passed the Adult Suffrage Bill. The petition is regarded as an important milestone in Victoria's suffrage campaign.

Great Petition is a sculpture situated in Burston Reserve, near Melbourne’s Victorian State Parliament Building in Australia. It was commissioned by the State Government of Victoria and the City of Melbourne. The work was designed by artists Susan Hewitt and Penelope Lee and constructed by Brecknock Consulting.

Monkey Day is associated with artist Eric Millikin, who has undertaken a series of projects tied to the event. In 2012 he produced The 12 Stars of Monkey Day, a collection of paintings published by USA Weekend that drew inspiration from pioneering space monkeys. The following year he expanded the observance with a Monkey Day mail art series that circulated greetings to strangers, including Koko the sign-language gorilla and former U.S. president Barack Obama. In 2014 he further explored the theme with a three-dimensional Monkey Day experience. Beginning in 2016, Millikin has also produced the Danger Beast project, a series of street art portraits of endangered animals crafted from endangered plant materials, including a Harambe portrait assembled from Venus flytraps.

Monkey Day is an informal observance dedicated to celebrating films and music that feature monkeys and other nonhuman primates. The date has become associated with Peter Jackson’s 2005 release of King Kong, which coincided with the holiday’s fifth anniversary. For Monkey Day 2014, the creators of Night at the Museum: Secret of the Tomb released a short feature starring Crystal the Monkey. The festivities frequently center on mainstream American monkey-themed cinema, with King Kong and the Planet of the Apes film series often highlighted at parties and gatherings. Monkey Day also embraces monkey-focused kung fu cinema, including titles such as Lady Iron Monkey. In addition, songs about primates, such as Major Lance’s “The Monkey Time” and The Rolling Stones’ “Monkey Man,” are incorporated into the holiday’s celebrations.

The G56 Hangzhou–Ruili Expressway, commonly known as the Hangrui Expressway or Hangzhou–Ruili Expressway, is an east–west expressway in China designed to connect Hangzhou in Zhejiang Province with Ruili in Yunnan Province near the border with Myanmar. When completed, the route is planned to span approximately 2,935 kilometres (1,824 miles). The corridor traverses predominantly mountainous terrain, necessitating a large number of tunnels and bridges to maintain continuous travel. Among its notable engineering features are the Duge Bridge, the Puli Bridge, and the Dimuhe River Bridge.

The G56 Hangzhou–Ruili Expressway, a major cross‑province route in China, shows varied progress across its length: Zhejiang, Anhui, and Jiangxi have fully completed their respective sections, while the segment through Hubei remains entirely under construction. In Hunan, development continues overall, with the Changde–Jishou stretch already finished. Guizhou also has the expressway under construction along its entire course, and in Yunnan construction persists for most of the corridor, though the portion from the Guizhou border to Baoshan has been completed.

The Europe Declaration was signed by leading European statesmen including Konrad Adenauer of West Germany, Joseph Bech of Luxembourg, Robert Schuman of France, Count Carlo Sforza of Italy, Dirk Stikker and Jan van den Brink of the Netherlands, and Paul van Zeeland and Joseph Meurice of Belgium. It stated that the aim was to remind future generations of the enduring obligation to bring Europe together on the basis of freedom, democratic governance, and the rule of law. The signatories viewed the declaration as a significant early step in the process of creating an integrated Europe.

The Europe Declaration, also known as the Charter of the Community, was a joint statement issued on 18 April 1951 by the foreign ministers of Belgium, France, Italy, Luxembourg, the Netherlands, and West Germany. Issued in conjunction with the signing of the Treaty of Paris, which created the European Coal and Steel Community (ECSC) and was based on the Schuman Plan, the declaration articulated the rationale and aims of the newly proposed community.

A sort, also called a type block, is a block that bears a single typographic character. When arranged with other sorts, it enables the printing of text. In movable-type printing, a sort is cast from a matrix mold. Sorts are manually assembled with other characters to form lines of type, which collectively create the page form. The page form is then used to print the page.

During traditional hot metal typesetting, matrices were used to cast individual characters as needed during the composition process. The Linotype system introduced line casting, producing entire lines of type in a single operation rather than individual sorts. In contrast, the Monotype system cast each sort separately, one at a time. With the rise of phototypesetting, the use of sorts largely disappeared from mainstream printing.

Gerstle Cove State Marine Reserve is part of California's central coast network of marine protected areas that are subject to monitoring under the Marine Life Protection Act. The act mandates ongoing scientific observation of selected MPAs to evaluate their effectiveness and to enhance understanding of ocean health in the region. In related efforts, monitoring of MPAs off the Santa Barbara Channel Islands has documented gradual improvements in the size and abundance of fish, illustrating potential ecological benefits that central coast reserves like Gerstle Cove aim to document through continued study.

Gerstle Cove State Marine Reserve is a California state marine protected area designated to conserve marine life by prohibiting the take of all living resources. In keeping with the broader purpose of California’s MPAs, it encourages recreational and educational uses of the ocean. Accordingly, activities such as kayaking, diving, snorkeling, and swimming are permitted, unless restricted by particular regulations or exceptions.

In the United States, the market infrastructure for securities settlement is supported by three central securities depositories and four clearing organizations that handle settlement for large volumes of trades. Market data consolidators supply real-time bid and ask prices for each security to investors and regulators. Real-time data is distributed through one of two securities information processing systems. Transactions are governed by self-regulatory organizations in conjunction with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC).

In the United States, securities traded on stock exchanges include equity securities of listed companies, unit investment trusts, derivatives, pooled investment products, and bonds. Stock exchanges commonly function as continuous auction markets, where orders are matched on an ongoing basis during trading sessions. Transactions are consummated by paired buyers and sellers at a central location, traditionally the exchange floor.

The term pandemic derives from the Greek elements pan- meaning “all” and demos meaning “people,” combining to express the idea of something that is common to or affecting all members of a population. The etymology is sometimes discussed with Aphrodite Pandemos as a cf. in origin. In Modern Greek, the word survives with senses such as “all-people’s” or “concerning all the people.” An illustrative use in the i.e. sense is the phrase “a pandemic assembly.”

European contact introduced smallpox to Native American populations, making it the deadliest disease in the Americas in terms of both illness and fatalities. The first well-documented smallpox outbreak in the hemisphere began on Hispaniola in late 1518 and spread to Mexico. In central Mexico, mortality is estimated at roughly 25 to 50 percent of the population. Over roughly a century after 1492, indigenous populations declined from about 60 million to around 6 million. The majority of deaths are attributed to introduced diseases such as smallpox, measles, and typhoid fever, together with war and famine.

During the 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War, the Pakistani military and the Razakar paramilitary force carried out a systematic campaign of genocidal rape in East Pakistan. An estimated 200,000 to 400,000 Bengali women and girls were subjected to sexual violence as part of the conflict. Many victims died in captivity or took their own lives, while others fled across the border to India seeking refuge.

During the Bangladesh Liberation War of 1971, Bengali Muslim and Bengali Hindu women were subjected to systematic rape by West Pakistani men connected to the Pakistani military and Razakar militias. The acts were driven by an ideology of cleansing the nation of Hindu influence, with Hindu women often framed as Hindu or Hindu-like. The consequences included thousands of pregnancies and births to war-related offspring, abortions, infanticide, suicides, and social ostracism of the victims. These acts are widely regarded as among the most severe instances of wartime sexual violence. The abuses ceased with the surrender of the Pakistani military and Razakar militias in December 1971.

TestFlight originated as a platform for beta testing both Android and iOS applications. In March 2014, Apple discontinued Android support, leaving the service focused on iOS development. By 2015, distribution through TestFlight required developers to publish apps using Xcode. Invitations for testers were managed through iTunes Connect.

On 17 December 2023, a cache on the Wayback Machine containing terabytes of pre-release iOS apps came to light. The material originated from 2012–2015, dating to a period when TestFlight’s servers were publicly accessible by mistake, effectively exposing unreleased software to the public. The incident was nicknamed “Teraleak” or “Terascrape,” and commentators drew comparisons to Nintendo’s Gigaleak from roughly three years earlier.

A regression-based decomposition of the SORCE/TIM measurements was used to separate the influences of sunspots and faculae on total solar irradiance (TSI). The approach accounts for about 92 percent of the observed variance in the TSI data, indicating a strong explanatory power for solar variability. Its trends align with the observed TIM records within the instrument’s stability band, suggesting that the reconstructed changes reflect real solar behavior rather than instrumental noise. Collectively, the level of agreement supports the view that TSI variations are primarily driven by magnetic activity on the solar surface.

Insolation refers to the solar radiation received by Earth and plays a central role in determining the planet's energy balance. However, instrument inaccuracies yield substantial uncertainties in estimating this balance. Observations of the energy imbalance during the deep solar minimum of 2005–2010 yielded values around +0.58±0.15 W/m², +0.60±0.17 W/m², and +0.85 W/m², illustrating the spread among different measurement methods. In contrast, space-based measurements have suggested a markedly larger imbalance, in the range of +3–7 W/m². The lower total solar irradiance value reported by SORCE/TIM reduces this discrepancy by roughly 1 W/m². The gap between TIM’s revised low value and earlier TSI measurements implies a climate forcing of about −0.8 W/m², a magnitude comparable to the energy imbalance.

Culling is the selection or segregation of individuals from a group according to chosen traits, with the aim of shifting the population's genetic composition to favor certain characteristics while reducing others. In animal breeding, it entails removing individuals from breeding stock based on a specific trait. The practice seeks to amplify desirable traits and lessen undesirable ones by altering the population's genetics. In livestock and wildlife contexts, culling often involves the killing of those removed based on characteristics such as sex or species, and may be employed as a measure to prevent the spread of infectious diseases.

Economy and Society is abstracted and indexed in the Social Sciences Citation Index and Scopus, ensuring its visibility in major scholarly databases. According to Journal Citation Reports, the journal recorded a 2021 impact factor of 4.182.

Economy and Society is a quarterly peer-reviewed academic journal devoted to theory and politics. Established in 1971, it is published by Routledge. As of 2022, the managing editor is Paul Langley of Durham University.

The Tonlé Sap Basin in Cambodia features a landscape where roughly 55 percent of the area is forest and 45 percent is agricultural land. Surrounding the lake are freshwater mangroves, referred to as flood forests, which cover about 3 percent of the basin. The floodplain is bordered by low hills and supports evergreen or deciduous seasonal tropical vegetation. The forest is dominated by Dipterocarpaceae, Leguminosae, Lacelandaceae, with in some areas the presence of Pinaceae, Rohan pineaceae, or bamboo. Farther from the lake, the forest gives way to thicket and ultimately meadow. Areas with higher quality soils or greater elevation host deciduous mixed forests and semi-evergreen forests. The diversity of vegetation underpins broader biodiversity, with interlocking forests, grasslands, and swamps providing refuge for wildlife.

Tonlé Sap functions as a hydrological part of the Mekong system, receiving water from three main sources: about a third from rivers feeding the lake, roughly 53.5 percent from the Mekong River itself, and around 12.5 percent from local precipitation. The region exhibits a pronounced seasonal cycle, with a rainy season spanning May to October in the lower Mekong plain and a dry season from November to March, accompanied by annual rainfall of 1,000 to 4,000 millimeters concentrated in the wet months. During the end of the dry season the lake typically sits at a depth of about one metre, but with the onset of the monsoon the Mekong’s water level rises and its flow reverses into the lake, causing the Tonlé Sap water level to swell by approximately 10 metres. As the rainy season wanes and Mekong discharge diminishes, the lake reverses again to help replenish the Mekong’s flow.

Following the 1967 Arab–Israeli War, an oil embargo imposed by Arab states exerted pressure on Israel through diplomatic, economic, and military channels. In the aftermath, numerous African and Asian countries severed diplomatic ties with Israel. The Soviet Union shifted its support to the Arab side, and most Eastern Bloc states cut relations in 1967, including the USSR as well as Poland, Czechoslovakia, Hungary, and Bulgaria. During this period, China and Mongolia did not establish diplomatic relations with Israel. After the collapse of the Eastern Bloc in 1989, diplomatic ties with many of these states were restored or established, with the Soviet Union reestablishing relations in October 1991, and the newly independent states that emerged from its dissolution also recognizing Israel. China then established formal relations with Israel in January 1992.

By the late 1960s, Israel had established diplomatic relations with nearly all countries across Western Europe, North America, South America, and Sub-Saharan Africa, indicating broad international recognition in those regions.

The BAFTA Award for Outstanding British Film is an annual accolade presented by the British Academy of Film and Television Arts (BAFTA) during the British Academy Film Awards. The prize was first awarded at the inaugural British Academy Film Awards, in recognition of films released in 1947, and continued through the 1968 ceremony. After more than two decades without a dedicated British cinema category, it was revived at the 46th British Academy Film Awards to honor films released in 1992. It was originally known as the Alexander Korda Award for Best British Film, and is now titled Outstanding British Film, intended to honor outstanding and original British filmmaking that demonstrates exceptional creativity and innovation.

The BAFTA Award for Outstanding British Film recognizes productions that involve substantial creative input from British individuals, including those who have lived in the United Kingdom for at least a decade. Nomination candidates are limited to the film’s director(s), writer(s), and up to three producers. If none of these principal contributors are British, the film is eligible only in exceptional circumstances.

ISO/IEC 8859-5 is part of the ISO/IEC 8859 family of eight-bit single-byte encodings designed for Cyrillic scripts. The ISO-IR-201 registration corresponds to a Volgaic Cyrillic supplement created to support the Chuvash, Komi, Mari, and Udmurt languages, which are spoken in the corresponding republics of Russia. The specification was introduced by Everson Gunn Teoranta. In FreeDOS the encoding is designated as code page 58259.

ISO/IEC 8859-5:1999 belongs to the ISO/IEC 8859 family, a collection of eight-bit, single-byte, ASCII-based graphic character sets. Designated as Part 5, the specification covers a Latin/Cyrillic alphabet. In informal usage, it is commonly referred to as Latin/Cyrillic. The initial edition of this part was published in 1988.

Pyrrhonism presents five tropes that structure its skeptical program. The first and third tropes provide a concise restatement of the earlier Ten Modes of Aenesidemus, while the remaining three tropes exhibit the evolution of the Pyrrhonist system. These later tropes rest on objections drawn from the fallibility of sense perception and of opinion, and they progressively shift the ground of argument toward more abstract and metaphysical considerations. Scholar Victor Brochard described the five tropes as the most radical and most precise formulation of skepticism ever offered, and he argued that, in a sense, they remain irresistible even in contemporary thought.

Pyrrhonism is a skeptical philosophical stance in which adherents challenge dogmatists’ claims to have secured truth about matters that are not evident, arguing that such issues cannot be known with certainty. They regard these non-evident topics as dogma, asserting that accepting them hinders the attainment of eudaimonia. To illustrate the unresolved nature of each purported dogma, Pyrrhonists present both supporting and opposing arguments, aiming to show that the conclusion is not attainable. Central to their method is the practice of epoché, or suspension of judgment, which is said to produce ataraxia, a tranquil state of mind.

The All of Mexico Movement encompassed United States military operations across Mexican territory, where forces faced persistent guerrilla warfare in Tamaulipas and along the corridor from Veracruz to Mexico City, hindering efforts to establish stable control. The campaign incurred losses of personnel, supplies, and military equipment. In Tamaulipas, American troops tried to subjugate local populations through violence and terror, while in Mexico City and Veracruz they pursued a policy of restraint, seeking not to interfere with locals. Both approaches proved unsuccessful. The escalating violence and insurrection led Mexican leaders to recognize the need for peace with the United States. From the American perspective, there was an urgent aim to end the conflict promptly while maximizing territorial gains and minimizing losses.

The All of Mexico Movement was a political initiative that ended with the Mexican Cession, which transferred Alta California and Nuevo México to the United States. The newly incorporated territories were less densely populated than the remainder of Mexico, a factor that influenced the practical viability of pursuing further expansion. After the cession, the movement rapidly diminished in prominence, a trajectory similar to that of the All of Oregon movement.

The ATP Singapore Open was a professional men's tennis tournament that formed part of the Grand Prix circuit and later the ATP Tour. It was held in two separate periods, from 1989 to 1992 and from 1996 to 1999. The event carried the title Epson Singapore Super Tennis until 1992 and was renamed the Heineken Open for the 1996–1999 editions. The competition originally took place on outdoor hard courts at the Kallang Tennis Centre, while the final four editions (1996–1999) were held indoors at the Singapore Indoor Stadium.

Vespertine is Björk's album that emphasizes analog sonic traces—loops, static, and white noise—forming a predominantly electronic soundscape. Acoustic elements appear only as intermittent interjections, rather than as central pillars, marking a shift from the approaches of Debut and Post. The work draws on the New Ancient Strings aesthetic, notably the kora duets by Toumani Diabaté and Ballaké Sissoko, which inform its textural and melodic sensibilities. Björk deliberately reworked the timbres of traditionally angelic instruments such as the harp and glockenspiel to diminish their pristine tone. Vocals serve to augment the intricate electronic fabric, recorded close to the microphone with minimal processing and frequently delivered in an unstable whisper, a technique that fosters a sense of immediacy and intimacy.

According to a 2015 interview with The Pitchfork Review, Björk stated that Vespertine's work had not been fully acknowledged by the press. She claimed that Matmos contributed percussion in the final two weeks, layering additional elements onto the songs rather than providing the primary parts. She asserted that Matmos did not contribute the core components of the album. Nonetheless, Matmos are widely credited in liner notes and other credits as having produced the entire album.

Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area (SMMNRA) is a national recreation area that encompasses numerous individual parks and open-space preserves. It is located primarily in the Santa Monica Mountains of Southern California and lies within the greater Los Angeles region. Roughly two-thirds of its parklands are situated in northwestern Los Angeles County, while the remaining one-third, including an extension into the Simi Hills, resides in southeastern Ventura County. The area is administered by the National Park Service in coordination with state, county, municipal, and university agencies.

The Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area (SMMNRA) encompasses 153,075 acres (61,947 hectares) within the Santa Monica Mountains of the Transverse Ranges. Its southeastern slopes contribute to the headwaters of the Los Angeles River. Land ownership is distributed among public and private entities: the California State Park system and other public agencies hold 49,756 acres (20,136 hectares); the National Park Service owns 25,117 acres (10,164 hectares); the remainder consists of land owned by local agencies, university reserves, and private property conservation easements.

Fathometer refers to a depth-measuring instrument that uses echo sounding to estimate the depth of a body of water by timing the return of an emitted sound pulse. The broader term sounding encompasses all forms of depth measurement, including methods that do not rely on acoustic signals, and its etymology is not connected to the notion of audible noise or tones. Historically, depth was determined by lowering a weighted line until it touched the seabed, a technique known as using a sounding or lead line. Echo sounding offers a faster alternative to this older approach, allowing rapid depth determinations without the need to physically reach the bottom.

A fathometer is an instrument that measures ocean depth by emitting an acoustic pulse and recording the travel time of the returning echo. Charted depths are generally based on a standard speed of sound in seawater. For greater accuracy, regional averages and seasonal sound-speed standards may be applied to specific ocean regions. For highest precision, a probe can be lowered to measure local temperature, pressure, and salinity, which then allow an estimate of the actual sound speed in the local water column. This technique is used by the U.S. Office of Coast Survey in navigational surveys of United States coastal waters.

Interquartile range (IQR) is a measure of dispersion that captures the spread of the central portion of a data set. It is defined as the difference between the third and first quartiles, equivalently the range of the middle 50% of observations, which corresponds to trimming 25% from each tail. By excluding the lower-contribution and outlying values, the IQR increases robustness and provides a more reliable scale estimate in the presence of outliers. The IQR is commonly visualized as the height of the box in a box plot, with the box spanning from the first to the third quartile.

Interquartile range (IQR) is defined as the difference between the third quartile (Q3) and the first quartile (Q1). Q3 denotes the upper quartile, while Q1 denotes the lower quartile. Each quartile is defined as a median obtained through the customary calculation used to partition a data set into four equal parts.

The 1997 Estoril Open was a men's tennis tournament contested on outdoor clay courts. It was the eighth edition of the event and served as part of the 1997 ATP Tour World Series. The competition was staged at Estoril Court Central in Oeiras, Portugal, and ran from April 7 to April 14, 1997.

Gymnocranius euanus is a fish species native to the Western Pacific Ocean, with a distribution spanning from the eastern Gulf of Thailand to New Caledonia and Tonga, and extending north to southern Japan and south to the coast of Australia. In Australian waters, its range runs from NW Kalbarri in Western Australia along the northern coastline to the Solitary Islands in New South Wales, and it includes the Coral Sea reef systems as well as Lord Howe Island and Norfolk Island. The species is typically found at depths of 15 to 50 meters (49 to 164 feet) and occupies sandy and rubble substrates adjacent to rock and coral reefs, including lagoons and outer-slope habitats.

Gymnocranius euanus is a fish species whose distribution includes certain regions where it is subject to commercial fishing. In these areas, it is actively targeted by fisheries and is typically captured using longlines and handlines.

In 2011, WWWN in Chicago and WEMP in New York moved from an alternative rock format to an all-news lineup branded as FM News following their acquisition by Merlin Media. As a transitional stunt, the stations aired a format identified as FM New, which blended adult contemporary music with regular news, traffic, and weather updates. These updates were presented by on-air personalities who would later become part of the staff for the FM News formats.

Stunting, in broadcasting, refers to promotional broadcasts or programming arrangements used by networks in the run-up to official launches in order to generate attention. For instance, G4 staged a week-long Pong programming event as a pre-launch stunt ahead of its April 24, 2002 debut. The Pong stunt was later acknowledged in the network’s December 31, 2014 sign-off and again in a 2021 return video. Similarly, MLB Network conducted a soft launch by repeatedly airing baseball highlights and promos in the weeks preceding its formal debut on January 1, 2009. In Canada, Sun News Network employed an on-screen countdown clock during the hours immediately before its launch on April 18, 2011.
Henri Sautot was born in Bourbonne-les-Bains. He received his schooling in Nancy and studied at Nancy-Université, after which he completed his national service.

Henri Sautot was appointed Governor of Ubangi-Shari in 1942 by Charles de Gaulle and served in that capacity until his retirement in 1946. After leaving office, he returned to New Caledonia with his New Caledonian wife and entered local political life there, ultimately serving as the mayor of Nouméa from 1947 to 1953.

On 4 August 1996, a Thailand-localized feed of Channel [V] was launched for Thai audiences, distributed via local cable and satellite providers. It appears to have supplanted Channel [V] International within Thailand, while the pan-Asian Channel [V] service remained accessible in the country through AsiaSat and Palapa satellites.

Channel V is a 24-hour music television channel that began broadcasting on 15 September 1991. It originated as MTV Asia (音樂台) before adopting its current branding. The service offers round-the-clock music programming and transmits in English, Hindi, and Chinese, with an emphasis on pop music.

Jordal Amfi, an indoor ice hockey rink in Oslo, Norway, was the first venue to bear the Jordal Amfi name. Opened in 1951 to serve as a venue for the 1952 Winter Olympics, the arena later hosted the IIHF World Championship in 1958 and again in 1999. In the ensuing decades it also hosted boxing matches and concerts, reflecting its role as a multi-purpose facility beyond ice hockey.

Jordal Amfi, opened in 1951, functioned as a versatile indoor venue in Oslo. In 1955, the famous figure skater Sonja Henie staged a major skating production there, and she returned for occasional performances in later years. In summer, the venue hosted a variety of events, including concerts and public meetings. Between 1958 and 1979, Jordal Amfi regularly hosted international professional boxing bouts, underscoring its role as a multipurpose facility for sport and public events.

Shacklewell is a hamlet in the Parish of Hackney. It is one of four small settlements within the parish, alongside Dalston, Newington, and Kingsland. The four settlements were grouped together for assessment purposes, and collectively they contained as many houses as the village of Hackney. Shacklewell originated on Shacklewell Green, situated along Shacklewell Lane.

Shacklewell began as a small hamlet situated along Shacklewell Lane, and historically formed part of the Ancient Parish of Hackney before later becoming part of the Metropolitan Borough of Hackney. In the modern era it lies within the London Borough of Hackney, though the designation Shacklewell is no longer widely used to refer to the area. In contemporary usage, the locality is generally viewed as part of Dalston, a settlement situated about 500 yards to the south that originally stood as a separate hamlet; Dalston itself was within the Parish and Borough of Hackney.

During the 1976 Zagreb mid-air collision, accounts from the scene described casualties on the ground. A police officer arriving at the site stated that a baby lying near the British aircraft still showed faint signs of life, but the arrival of ambulances would have been too late to save the infant. In a separate account, local residents discovered a boy on a road near a field who remained alive for up to fifteen minutes after the collision, but he ultimately died.

British Airways Flight 476 (BA476) departed London Heathrow for Istanbul Atatürk Airport at 08:32 UTC. The aircraft involved was a Hawker Siddeley Trident. The flight carried 54 passengers and 9 crew members. The crew consisted of Captain Dennis Tann, aged 44, First Officer Brian Helm, and Flight Engineer Martin Flint. By the time of the accident, Captain Tann had accumulated 10,781 flying hours.

The Tamang community uses a script called Tamyig for writing the Tamang language. Literary activity in Tamang includes the publication of several books. In 2001, the Information and Public Relations department of the Government of Sikkim initiated a Tamang edition of the Sikkim Herald as an official news bulletin.

Tamyig script closely resembles the standard Tibetan script in form, yet its use is largely confined to religious and scriptural texts. It is not generally taught in formal schooling, with only rare local exceptions such as Konjyosom Rural Municipality where instruction may occur. As a result, a substantial portion of Tamang speakers writes and publishes in the Devanagari script, which is more widely adopted for everyday use.

The American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), pronounced ASH-ray, is an American professional association dedicated to advancing the design and construction of heating, ventilation, air conditioning, and refrigeration (HVAC&R) systems. The HVAC&R designation stands for heating, ventilating, air conditioning and refrigeration, reflecting the focus of the organization. ASHRAE has more than 50,000 members in over 130 countries worldwide.

ASHRAE, founded in 1894 at a meeting of engineers in New York City, is a professional society whose former headquarters were located at 345 East 47th Street in the United Engineering Center. The organization has held an annual meeting every year since 1895. It was originally established as the American Society of Heating and Ventilating Engineers (ASHVE) and retained that name until 1954, when it was renamed the American Society of Heating and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHAE). In 1959, ASHAE merged with the American Society of Refrigerating Engineers (ASRE) to form the current American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers, known as ASHRAE.

Pingxiang County is a county in southern Hebei province, China, administered by the prefecture-level city of Xingtai. It is situated about 45 kilometers from the urban core of Xingtai and covers an area of roughly 406 square kilometers, with an estimated population of around 280,000. In the Han dynasty, the area was known as Julu County (钜鹿县) and was the site of the Battle of Julu in 207 BCE. The region is also notable as the birthplace of Zhang Jue and his brothers Zhang Bao and Zhang Liang, who organized the Yellow Turban Rebellion in the late 2nd century CE.

Mozart's Piano Sonata No. 13, its second movement Andante cantabile, is composed in sonata form but is set in the subdominant key of E-flat major. The opening presents a right-hand figure of thirds that leads into a lyrical theme supported by flowing broken triads in the left hand. A minuet-like section in B-flat major provides contrast, after which the music returns to E-flat major for a repeat of the exposition. Following the first reprise, the development begins in F minor, even as the music gives the impression of settling in E-flat major, and it travels through a sequence of keys—F minor, C minor, A-flat major, back to F minor, D-flat minor, and A-flat minor—before reasserting E-flat major for the recapitulation. The movement is notable for its striking dissonances, particularly at the outset of the development.

Recent musicological research has invalidated the previously assumed date for Mozart's Piano Sonata No. 13. Wolfgang Plath dates the work to roughly 1783–84, probably shortly before its first printing. By contrast, Alan Tyson, analyzing the manuscript's paper, proposes a dating toward the end of 1783, most likely November. That proposed late-1783 date coincides with Mozart's Linz period and with the Linz Symphony, K. 425, when he and his wife paused in Linz on their return from Salzburg to Vienna. The revised dating is also consistent with the work's stylistic features.
WildFly is software that is freely available and open source, released under the GNU Lesser General Public License, version 2.1.

WildFly is a Java-based application server that forms the continuation of the JBoss AS/JBoss lineage. It was originally written by JBoss and is now developed by Red Hat. The project is implemented in Java and adheres to the Java Platform, Enterprise Edition (Java EE) specification. WildFly runs on multiple platforms, enabling deployment of Java EE applications across diverse environments.

The Muda language is spoken by more than two thousand people, according to Xu (1991). It is spoken in Nanlianshan Village Community (南联山村委会), Jinghong City, Yunnan Province, China. Administratively, the area was formerly Nanlianshan District/Township (南联山乡) and is now part of Gasa Township (嘎洒镇).

Hsiu (2018) classifies Muda as an Akha language. The language possesses a Bisoid substratum, with the substrate representing an early split from Bisoid and indicating substantial historical layering in its development. Phonologically, Muda features consonant clusters of the type Cl-, a trait that aligns it with Bisoid languages as well as Siloid languages and Jinuo. Lexical evidence of Bisoid influence includes words for leg, house, and smoke in Muda.

KLSR-TV began as the low-power station K25AS, launching on June 12, 1987 with a music-video format. It initially lacked cable carriage, a situation that persisted until 1989, and within months of its debut it affiliated with Fox in response to strong local viewership. Despite its low-power status, the station produced its own prime-time newscast for several years. When full-power KEVU commenced operations on channel 34 in 1991, KLSR remained Eugene’s Fox affiliate. California Oregon Broadcasting, Inc. acquired KLSR in 1993 and KEVU in 1994, and the company planned to relocate Fox programming to the full-power channel 34 facility, a move completed on April 1, 1997. Cox Media Group acquired KLSR in 2022. Weeknight 7 p.m. and 10 p.m. newscasts for KLSR are produced by Eugene’s CBS affiliate KVAL-TV.

On June 12, 1987, a low-power television station began broadcasting in Eugene under the call sign K25AS, known on-air as KLSR, and owned by Metrocom of Oregon. During weekdays the station primarily aired music videos, with on-air shifts staffed by three Eugene radio personalities and the general manager. Weekends featured on-the-hour newscasts alongside traditional syndicated programming. A midday live bingo program offered prizes. The morning show was hosted by Christopher Judge, a former University of Oregon football player, after he won a hosting contest. By the latter part of 1987, the station held roughly a 1 percent audience share, which helped secure an affiliation with the Fox network. Notwithstanding the Fox affiliation, KLSR struggled to obtain carriage on Eugene's Tele-Communications Inc. (TCI) cable system, finally gaining a slot in 1989. In 1989, the station added a translator to extend service to the Corvallis area.

On December 31, 2017, Delfin Midstream LLC, an LNG exporter, acquired approximately 71 percent of TheGlobe.com's outstanding shares, a move intended to position TheGlobe.com as a potential vehicle for going public through a reverse merger. In November 2022, TheGlobe.com stated that it expected to operate as a public company for the next twelve months with funding provided by Delfin. Since 2018, Frederick Jones, a founder of Glencore, has served as TheGlobe.com's chief executive officer and chief financial officer.

TheGlobe.com experienced a leadership change in 2000 when founders Paternot and Krizelman were ousted from the company, after which the firm came under the control of a former vice president of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants (AICPA). Throughout its history the company had not achieved profitability, and mounting losses necessitated severe reductions in operations. In August 2001, TheGlobe.com closed its flagship site and laid off half its workforce. Despite these cutbacks, the company continued to host a limited number of partner sites and published Computer Games. The domain www.theglobe.com displayed only an informational message regarding the site's termination until 2003.

The article examines a title that advocates disregarding formal guidelines, treating it as a provocative statement rather than a prescriptive policy. It notes that the surrounding discussion often links feelings of anxiety and depressive mood to the existence and enforcement of rules that can deter participation in collaborative projects such as the wiki. Within this framing, the work presents a controversial recommendation associated with the phrase: to overlook these constraints and proceed with personal activities instead. The discussion situates this stance within broader debates about community norms, user autonomy, and the tension between moderation and open collaboration.

Ignore all rules (IAR) is the acronym referenced in connection with the project described by the article’s title. At its inception, IAR functioned in part as an acknowledgment by early contributors that certain situations defied sensible interpretation under any existing rule. As the project evolved, the relevance of that limitation diminished, with expanding guidance and established norms making most scenarios resolvable within the prevailing framework. By 2015, it had become markedly difficult to identify a circumstance in which no applicable rule existed.

The Tapanuli orangutan (Pongo tapanuliensis) is distinguished from Pongo abelii by several craniofacial characteristics, including a deeper suborbital fossa, a triangular pyriform (pear-shaped) aperture, and a more angled facial profile.

The Tapanuli orangutan (Pongo tapanuliensis) is a critically endangered primate confined to the South Tapanuli region of Sumatra, Indonesia. It is one of the three extant orangutan species, alongside the Sumatran orangutan (Pongo abelii) and the Bornean orangutan (Pongo pygmaeus). The species was formally recognized as distinct in 2017. By 2018, estimates placed its population at about 800 individuals, highlighting its status as one of the most endangered great apes.

Prior to the introduction of the 7-inch single, the standard format for popular music was the 78 rpm shellac records, typically 10 inches in diameter and offering around three minutes of music per side. The 7-inch single emerged after this era, providing a more compact release. In later years, 10-inch vinyl singles were commonly issued as limited edition collector's items, and these releases sometimes featured rare tracks or distinctive artwork.

RCA introduced boxed seven-inch 45 rpm singles to compete with Columbia, designing them to play in sequence with the company's record changer system for uninterrupted playback. In addition to standard black pressings, RCA issued a number of singles in different colors to designate genres and assist customers in locating music. By 1952, the novelty of multicolored singles had diminished, and RCA returned to pressing all 45s in black vinyl. The lowest catalog numbers observed for RCA 45s, noted by color, include 47-0146 (yellow), 47-2715 (black), 48-0001 (green), 49-0100 (deep red), 50-0000 (cerise), 51-0000 (light blue), and 52-0000 (deep blue). The fate of catalog number 48-0000 remains unknown, with speculation that copyright or other legal issues may have contributed to its disappearance.

Douglas Crockford described JSON as a strict subset of JavaScript and of the ECMAScript specification; however, in practice JSON and JavaScript are not perfectly interchangeable, since a value that is valid JSON may not constitute valid JavaScript code. A notable point of divergence concerns certain Unicode characters: JSON permits unescaped U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR and U+2029 PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR within string literals, whereas ECMAScript up to and including the 2018 edition prohibits these characters in strings unless they are escaped. This inconsistency stems from JSON’s rule that strings may not contain only the control characters (U+0000 through U+001F). To maximize portability across environments, many implementations backslash-escape these two code points as \u2028 and \u2029 within JSON strings.

According to the JSON specification, the order of properties within an object is not significant and should not be relied upon to convey meaning. The standard advises developers to avoid attaching semantic importance to member order in order to promote interoperability. Consequently, even if a parser or software reveals a particular sequence, that sequence should not be treated as meaningful for interpretation or processing.

During the 2015 Christmas season in Wadena, Minnesota, the city faced a threatened lawsuit from the Freedom From Religion Foundation over a city-owned nativity display in a municipal park. To avoid litigation, the city sold the nativity to a private buyer and relocated the display to a more prominent private site. In the aftermath, more than 1,000 nativity scenes appeared around the city, while the former park site was leased on a day-to-day basis to individuals legally entitled to display nativity scenes. The incident drew national media attention.

Following the tornado, secondary education in Wadena was temporarily conducted across three sites: the Wadena campus of Minnesota State Community and Technical College, a Deer Creek facility that had been closed, and Wadena Elementary School. In 1991, Deer Creek consolidated with Wadena. To accommodate high school students, some early childhood classes at Wadena Elementary were relocated to Saint Ann's Catholic School. Outdoor athletic programs were largely unaffected, with home volleyball and basketball games staged in the Elementary School gymnasium. A purpose-built Middle-High School opened in fall 2012.

From March 2019, BBC Three programming was carried on BBC One, with broadcasts scheduled from Monday to Wednesday and airing after the BBC News at Ten. The arrangement was accompanied by a joint branding that linked BBC Three with BBC One, presenting the two channels as a single outlet for the content.

BBC Three's programming encompasses comedy, drama, spin-off series, and repeats of programs from BBC One and BBC Two. It also features other programmes aimed at informing audiences about specific actions by presenting a series that challenges common beliefs.

Void-ppc was an unofficial fork of Void Linux created for PowerPC and Power ISA architectures. The project supported both 32-bit and 64-bit devices and operated across both big-endian and little-endian environments, offering builds with either musl or glibc as the C library. It maintained its own build infrastructure and separate package repositories, with the goal of compiling all of Void Linux’s packages for its targeted platforms. The fork largely arose from technical issues with Void Linux’s build system and infrastructure, and the project ended in early 2023.

Void Linux is a general-purpose Linux distribution that distinguishes itself by employing runit for system initialization rather than the more widely adopted systemd. The project also offers distinct software repositories and installation media that can be built with either the GNU C Library (glibc) or musl, allowing users to choose between these C library implementations.

Let X be a compact separable space. The space of finite signed Baire measures on X is isometrically isomorphic to the dual of C(X), the real Banach space of all continuous real-valued functions on X. Concretely, every bounded linear functional on C(X) arises uniquely from integration against a finite signed Baire measure on X, and conversely such a measure defines a bounded linear functional by pairing with continuous functions. This fundamental duality is given by the Riesz–Markov–Kakutani representation theorem.

In measure theory, a signed measure μ on a measurable space (X, F) admits a Jordan decomposition into two non-negative measures μ+ and μ−, with μ+ finite. The signed measure is recovered as the difference μ = μ+ − μ−, reflecting its positive and negative components.
