Together, these references illustrate the lack of uniform agreement among early Christian writers regarding which deuterocanonical books belonged to the canon versus ecclesiastical use.

Deuterocanonical books are a collection of writings regarded as canonical by some Christian traditions but not universally accepted in all denominations. In churches subscribing to sola scriptura, the status of these texts is contested: most Protestant groups do not include them in the canon, while Catholic and Orthodox traditions affirm them as part of Scripture. The debate revolves around historical provenance, authority, and doctrinal usefulness, contributing to divergent canons across different churches. Given these differences, commentators emphasize that having a precise and comprehensive list of the canonical books is necessary and critical for doctrinal clarity, liturgical coherence, and consistent interpretation of Scripture.

In the United Kingdom, admission to research degrees is typically contingent on a strong undergraduate qualification, including the Scottish M.A., with the latter acceptable at a minimum of lower second-class honours and, in many cases, a preference for upper second- or first-class honours. Some institutions admit doctoral candidates initially to an MPhil or MRes, with a transfer to PhD or DPhil considered only if progress is satisfactory within eight to twelve months. Ed.D candidates generally must hold a good bachelor's degree together with an appropriate master's degree before admission.

Before 2004, the French equivalent of a postgraduate degree was known as the maîtrise. The Bologna Process, established in 2004, introduced a European framework based on the Licence–Master–Doctorat (LMD) structure to harmonize higher education across participating countries. Thus, Maîtrise served as the French equivalent of a postgraduate qualification prior to the adoption of the LMD system.

During the 2014 Swiss referendums, voters were presented with two notable proposals. One sought to end the flat-tax system, proposing that residents and non-working foreign nationals would be taxed solely on their income and wealth. The other, known as the Ecopop initiative, aimed to restrict immigration to Switzerland to 0.2 percent of the population per year in order to safeguard natural resources.

The 2014 Swiss referendums included a proposal that would obligate the Swiss National Bank to maintain gold reserves totaling at least 20 percent of its asset value and to repatriate all Swiss gold held abroad, including assets stored at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. Initiated by SVP member of parliament Luzi Stamm and two other MPs, the campaign reached the requisite 100,000 signatures for a nationwide vote by early 2013. The initiative was opposed by the SNB and the Swiss government, which argued that implementing such a measure would limit the central bank’s monetary policy flexibility by constraining its ability to print money and manage the money supply.

Critical reception to Bombshell (2019) was mixed, with Moira Macdonald of The Seattle Times awarding two out of four stars and arguing that the film veers off course due to a light, almost playful screenplay and a pace that feels cartoonish, more appropriate to a dark comedy. Simran Hans of The Observer gave two out of five stars and faulted the work for sanitizing the protagonists' politics to solicit sympathy, noting the smoothing of Kelly’s racism and the erasure of Carlson’s homophobia; she contends the film should confront their dual roles as conservatives and as targets of a sexist organization, warning that portraying them as merely sympathetic weakens its critique of right-wing ideology. Linda Holmes of NPR described only a few strong moments, largely due to Robbie, and found the film overall underwhelming, overworked, and inelegantly structured, missing something fundamental at its core. Joe Morgenstern of The Wall Street Journal characterized it as a compelling story that devolves into a blunt-force polemic, persistently hammering its message home.

Providence served as the capital of the Colony of Providence from 1636 to 1663. With the creation of the Colony of Rhode Island and Providence Plantations in 1663, it remained the capital from 1663 to 1686 and again from 1689 to 1776. Following the formation of the State of Rhode Island and Providence Plantations in 1776, Providence acted as a co-capital through 1900. Since 1900, Providence has been the sole capital of Rhode Island.

By 1684, Yingge was inhabited by Hakka migrants who cultivated tea. The area's ceramics history began roughly two centuries ago when Wu An (吳鞍) arrived from Guangzhou and became its first potter. Subsequently, brick maker Chen Kun (陳昆) relocated to Yingge. The collaboration between Wu An and Chen Kun helped establish Yingge as a center of Taiwan's ceramics industry.

Yingge District is commonly accessed by taking a train from Taipei to Yingge, a journey of about 30 minutes with trains departing roughly every hour. From Yingge Station, Ceramic Street is within easy walking distance. The street is noted for its small-town charm and its local snacks. Shops typically open at 9:00 am, and visitors are advised to arrive around 10:00 am to make the most of their visit.

Tri-state buffers provide a high-impedance output that enables several devices to be connected to a common data bus without electrical contention. While this arrangement supports multi-device communication on a bus, tri-state logic is generally discouraged for on-chip interconnections due to potential timing, loading, and routing complexities; it is more appropriate for inter-chip connections where drivers are physically separated. In practice, tri-state buffers allow devices to take turns driving the bus by placing non-selected outputs in the high-impedance state. An alternative approach to bus sharing is the use of multiplexers, which can employ a selection mechanism to choose the output from among several devices and present a single, consolidated signal onto the bus. Consequently, multiplexers can replace tri-state buffers for bus arbitration on-chip while still accommodating multiple sources to a single bus line.

Tri-state buffers can place their outputs in a high-impedance state, during which they exert no influence on the surrounding circuitry. Consequently, if no other device asserts a drive on the shared node, the line becomes floating and may assume an indeterminate voltage. To prevent such ambiguity, designers commonly apply pull-up or pull-down resistors to bias the line when the outputs are tri-stated. These biasing resistors are typically sized in the range of 1 to 100 kilohms.

The Treaty of Accession 2003 was the accord that expanded the European Union by ten member states. Signed in Athens, Greece, on 16 April 2003, it entered into force on 1 May 2004 as part of the Union's enlargement. The ten new members were Cyprus, the Czech Republic, Estonia, Hungary, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Poland, Slovakia, and Slovenia.

The Treaty of Accession 2003 was an international agreement between the European Union’s then-member states and ten candidate states, outlining the terms under which these countries would join the Union as part of the 2004 enlargement. The ten nations named in the accord—Czech Republic, Estonia, Cyprus, Latvia, Lithuania, Hungary, Malta, Poland, Slovakia, and Slovenia—were to become EU members, and the treaty adjusted several provisions of the Treaty of Nice to accommodate their accession. Signed in 2003, it entered into force on 1 May 2004.

Variations among English dialects influence the spelling and naming of SI units, their prefixes, and certain non-SI units. In American English, the prefix for ten is rendered as deka-, and the basic units appear as meter and liter, whereas International English uses deca-, metre, and litre. The symbol t denotes the metric ton, which in US English is called the metric ton and in International English is called the tonne, with a defined value of 1000 kilograms.

While the International System of Units (SI) is the preferred framework for measurement, non-SI units continue to appear in scientific, technical, and commercial literature. Some units are historically and culturally entrenched and have not been fully replaced by SI. To accommodate practical usage, the CIPM has prepared a list of non-SI units that are accepted for use with SI, allowing their coexistence with SI units under specified guidelines. Illustrative examples include the hour and the minute for time, the degree of angle for angular measurement, the litre for volume, and the decibel for sound level.

Rotten Tomatoes features a user-based metric called the Popcornmeter, which functions as the site’s user average for an individual film. This metric is defined as the percentage of registered users who rated the movie positively on a five-star scale, effectively indicating the share of favorable votes among the user base. The calculation parallels the method used for the site’s recognized critics’ reviews, and the underlying data are drawn from registered users.

A September 2023 article in Vulture criticized Rotten Tomatoes' review rating system, arguing that it can be susceptible to manipulation by large companies seeking to influence public perception. The piece contends that such firms can boost a film’s apparent consensus by recruiting obscure, often self-published reviewers, citing the publicity company Bunker 15 as an illustrative example. It describes this practice as a method of elevating scores to sway discourse around releases. The article uses the 2018 film Ophelia as the specific example referenced to illustrate the alleged manipulation.

Campylobacteriosis refers to infection with Campylobacter species, most often Campylobacter jejuni. Some strains of C. jejuni produce an enterotoxin with cholera‑like activity, which contributes to the watery diarrhea commonly observed in affected individuals. The infection can cause enteritis that is diffuse and inflammatory, frequently accompanied by blood, edema, and exudation. In a small number of cases, Campylobacter infection has been associated with hemolytic uremic syndrome and thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura, though the mechanism behind these associations remains poorly understood.

Campylobacteriosis is an infection that is typically self-limiting. In the majority of human cases, management consists of supportive, symptom-directed care, with rehydration and electrolyte restoration as the central approach.

Windows Workflow Foundation supports both a visual designer approach and a code-centric model for building workflows. In the designer mode, users drag activities from the toolbox onto the workflow design surface and can create and configure workflow arguments and variables directly within the interface. In the code-based assembly approach, activities are instantiated as CLR objects and arranged into a composite collection under a single root activity, typically a Sequence or a Flowchart. The framework’s execution model runs the root activity by invoking it through either a WorkflowApplication or a WorkflowInvoker, thereby executing the workflow. The term workflow refers to this root activity as executed by the host. Activities may be either built-in (out-of-the-box) or custom; examples of built-in activities include DoWhile for iteration, FlowDecision within a Flowchart for branching, Send for WCF messaging, and primitive actions such as Assign and WriteLine. Custom activities are user-created CLR objects that derive from System.Activities.Activity and implement their behavior in code. Designer support can extend to custom activities by providing a dedicated activity designer, improving visual authoring within the Visual Studio Integrated Development Environment.

Windows Workflow Foundation is a framework for modeling and executing business processes, particularly those whose underlying logic may require periodic updates. In commerce-related scenarios, rules such as tax calculations and shipping calculations can affect the final purchase price, and these rules can be incorporated into the workflow. Conceptually, a workflow represents the sequence of steps required to complete tasks such as approving a purchase, hiring, or processing a transaction, coordinating activities and decisions throughout the operation.

Overflows in oceanography are driven by the density differences between water masses. These density contrasts stem from variations in temperature and salinity, which together determine seawater density. A widely cited instance is the Denmark Strait overflow, in which cold, dense water from the Nordic Seas flows into the North Atlantic Ocean.

Overflow in oceanography describes the downward movement of denser seawater from one basin into an adjacent basin beneath a lighter overlying layer, forming a deep-water undercurrent. It is a central mechanism of thermohaline circulation and underpins the global formation of deep-water masses. By transporting heat and salt between basins, overflows influence regional and global climate patterns. They also affect sea level through shifts in mass distribution and density structure, while the associated changes in temperature and salinity can impact marine ecosystems by altering nutrient transport, habitat conditions, and overall ecological dynamics.

Stile rappresentativo, Italian for “representational style,” denotes a term used in opera to describe a manner of vocal declamation that arose in late-16th-century Italian opera. It is more expressive than ordinary speech yet less melodic than conventional song, functioning as a form of dramatic recitative associated with the early Baroque era. In performance, melodic lines unfold with considerable freedom over a simple, chordal accompaniment, providing a flexible framework for narrative delivery without ornate musical elaboration. The style thus served to emphasize verbal immediacy and dramatic expression within early operatic drama, bridging spoken declamation and lyrical Song.

Subcutaneous administration refers to delivering a substance into the tissue beneath the skin, a route that allows relatively gradual absorption. Insulin is commonly delivered by subcutaneous injection. The slang term “skin popping” denotes subcutaneous injections and is often associated with recreational drug use. In clinical practice, fluids can be slowly infused subcutaneously through a method known as hypodermoclysis.

Within neural tissue engineering, the route of administration encompasses more than simply applying growth factors to nerve guidance conduits. Modern drug delivery systems enable regulation of the release kinetics of growth factors, allowing their concentrations to be maintained or adjusted over defined time intervals. This temporal control is crucial for establishing an extracellular milieu that more closely imitates developmental conditions observed in vivo, thereby supporting more effective neuronal regeneration.

Subtropical climates are defined by hot summers and mild winters with infrequent frost, and they are typically classified into two main forms: humid subtropical climates (Köppen classifications Cfa and Cwa) and dry-summer or Mediterranean climates (Csa and Csb). In humid subtropical regions, precipitation is concentrated in the warmest months, as seen in areas such as Southeast China and the Southeastern United States. By contrast, the Mediterranean or dry-summer subtype receives most of its rainfall during the cooler months, with examples including the Mediterranean Basin and Southern California.

Subtropical climates comprise the humid subtype, typically situated on the western fringe of the subtropical high-pressure zone. Summers are hot and humid, with unstable tropical air masses driving convective overturning and frequent heavy downpours, producing the season’s maximum rainfall. Winters bring a pronounced dry spell as the monsoon retreats and the trade winds weaken, delivering cooler, drier air and clearer skies. This climate is found in regions such as Australia, the Indo-Gangetic Plain in South Asia, and parts of South America. In the warm-ocean–bounded subtropics—for instance the southeastern United States and much of East Asia— tropical cyclones contribute substantially to rainfall totals. In Japan, typhoons account for more than half of annual precipitation.

On December 6, 2011, at 6:00 a.m., WXKT ended the former Wild Thing branding, and Tim Bryant announced a new format for the station at 103.7 FM. The revised schedule featured North Georgia's Morning News in the mornings, hosted by Tim Bryant and Martha Zoller; at noon, Jim Rome's sports radio program was aired; from 3:00 to 6:00 p.m., America's Radio News supplied the afternoon lineup; and overnights were programmed with Yahoo! Sports Radio.

WXKT is the current callsign assigned to the 103.7 FM station after Cox Radio acquired the outlet in August 2008. In the same reshape, WPUP was moved to 100.1 FM, and the two frequencies briefly simulcast the Bulldog format for a little over a year. WPUP remains on 100.1 FM, licensed to Watkinsville, Georgia, operating as the top-40 station Power 100.1.

In February 2016, McGraw-Hill Financial announced that it would rename itself S&P Global Inc., with the change to take effect by the end of April 2016. The name change became official on April 27, 2016, following a shareholder vote. In April 2016, McGraw-Hill disclosed the sale of J.D. Power and Associates to XIO Group for $1.1 billion. On August 3, 2020, S&P Global Platts Analytics launched its fundamental oil information on the redesigned S&P Global Platts Developer Platform, which provides rapid access to product price databases, business statistics, and market insights. In November 2020, S&P Global announced an agreement to acquire IHS Markit in a transaction valued at $44 billion. In 2023, S&P Global sold the former IHS engineering operations to KKR & Co, which subsequently rebranded IHS as Accuris.

S&P Global Energy, formerly Platts, is a division of S&P Global that delivers information services and benchmark price assessments across a range of markets, including commodities, energy, petrochemicals, metals, and agriculture. Headquartered in London, the unit operates from more than 15 offices worldwide, with major hubs in London, Tokyo, Dubai, Singapore, and Houston, and international centers in São Paulo, Shanghai, and New York City.

Eleven individuals have been designated as National Heroes of Barbados to date. The original group of ten was nominated by Prime Minister Owen Arthur and formally appointed by the Governor-General in 1998 under the relevant act. Of these ten, only Sir Garfield Sobers remains alive. Sarah Ann Gill was the only woman among the initial ten National Heroes until 2021. In November 2021, Rihanna, a singer and businesswoman, was honoured as a National Hero, bringing the total to eleven.

In 2020, the West Wing of Parliament, which houses the National Heroes Gallery, was closed due to environmental concerns. The closure drew criticism of the government for leaving the facility abandoned and vulnerable to robberies, highlighting concerns about the preservation and security of Barbados's National Heroes collection.

The hyporheic zone encompasses the subsurface region where streamwater exchanges with groundwater, and these interactions influence the volume of water carried downstream. In gaining reaches, groundwater discharges into the stream as it flows downstream, adding to the main-channel water and increasing the downstream surface-water volume. By contrast, losing reaches occur when surface water infiltrates into the subsurface, producing a net loss of surface water as the stream progresses. These exchange processes are described as portions of the stream where water is gained from or lost to the groundwater, reflecting the dynamic connectivity between surface and subsurface waters within and around the stream channel.

The hyporheic zone is a region of sediment and porous space located beneath and alongside a stream bed, where shallow groundwater mixes with surface water. The flow through this subsurface area, known as hyporheic flow or underflow, underpins interactions between surface water and groundwater. It plays a key role in mediating surface water–groundwater exchange and associated ecological processes, including influences on fish spawning. In urban water management, the hyporheic zone can be deliberately designed and actively managed to improve water quality and enhance riparian habitat.

World Heritage inscriptions have been the subject of critique directed at UNESCO, with accusations of geographic bias, racism, and colorism in the inscription process. Critics contend that a substantial portion of sites designated or inscribed come from regions whose populations are typically lighter-skinned, with Europe, East Asia, and North America frequently cited as representative examples of this pattern.

Sites may be added to the List of World Heritage in Danger when conditions threaten the characteristics for which they were inscribed on the World Heritage List. The causes of danger include armed conflict and war, natural disasters, pollution, poaching, and uncontrolled urbanisation or human development. The danger list is intended to raise international awareness of these threats and to encourage counteractive measures. Threats may be proven imminent dangers or potential hazards that could have adverse effects on a site.

China is the second-largest country in the world by land area, behind Russia. By total area, its global ranking is typically considered to be third or fourth, reflecting differences in measurement and the treatment of inland waters. The total area is generally cited as about 9,600,000 square kilometers (approximately 3,700,000 square miles). Britannica records an area of 9,572,900 km2 (3,696,100 sq mi), while the UN Demographic Yearbook and The World Factbook list 9,596,961 km2 (3,705,407 sq mi).

Chinese architecture demonstrates a broad spectrum of building traditions that align with social status and affiliations, ranging from imperial projects and religious structures to ordinary domestic forms. In addition to these formal types, vernacular styles develop regionally, influenced by geography and the cultural heritage of different ethnic groups. Illustrative examples include the stilt houses of the south, adapted to wet lowland environments; the yaodong cave dwellings of the northwest that are carved into the Loess plateau; the yurts used by nomadic communities; and the siheyuan, the northern courtyard houses that organize living spaces around an enclosed central court.

White nationalism in the United States has a historical through-line with the Ku Klux Klan, which originated in the wake of the Civil War to preserve the Southern racial order during Reconstruction. The first Klan aimed to maintain the antebellum social order, while a revived movement founded in Atlanta in 1915 promoted white nationalism and American nativism, and developed a modern, businesslike recruiting system beginning in 1921. The second Klan expanded rapidly across the nation during times of economic prosperity, with growth tied to urban industrialization and increased immigration; membership expanded most in cities and spread from the South to the Midwest and West. Its platform called for strict moral codes and tougher enforcement of Prohibition, accompanied by rhetoric that attacked Catholicism and promoted nativism. Although some local factions engaged in violence, including attacks on private houses, the majority of violent episodes occurred in the Southern United States.

White nationalism in Finland has been linked to discussions and actions within the Finns Party and its affiliates. An Iltalehti survey found that around one-third of Finns Party voters believed that the European racial stock should not mix with darker races to prevent the extinction of the native European population. Additionally, Mari Rantanen, who served as interior minister, argued that a naive approach to immigration would cause Finns to lose their blue-eyed characteristics and she circulated writings describing refugees as parasites. Moreover, Toni Jalonen, then deputy chair of Finns Party Youth, posted an image depicting a Black family with a caption implying a negative vision for Finland’s future. Collectively, these episodes illustrate how white nationalist ideas have appeared in connection with the party and its youth wing, highlighting ongoing debates over immigration and national identity in Finland.

Launeddas are a traditional Sardinian wind instrument played with circular breathing to sustain a continuous, intricate style of music. The instrument has attracted international attention. Notable players include Efisio Melis, Antonio Lara, Dionigi Burranca, and Luigi Lai. Melis and Lara were the leading figures of the 1930s golden age of launeddas, and both passed on their approaches to apprentices, including Aureliu Porcu, Lara's apprentice.

Scholars trace the launeddas’ lineage to a broader tradition of reed-pipe instruments that spread across North Africa and the Middle East. In ancient Egypt, reed pipes dating to around 2700 BCE were known as memet. During the Old Kingdom (2778–2723 BCE), memets are depicted on reliefs in seven tombs at Saqqara, and likewise in six tombs at Giza as well as on the pyramids of Queen Khentkaus.

An exhibition dedicated to Ernst Ludwig Kirchner was presented at the Singer Laren museum in the Netherlands under the title Kirchner: Paradise in the Mountains. Running from 9 December 2015 to 10 April 2016, the show examined Kirchner's time in a sanatorium in Davos.

Ernst Ludwig Kirchner faced significant health problems during 1936–37, and physicians prescribed Ovaltine and the opioid Eukodal as part of his treatment. In 1937, amid the Nazi regime’s campaign against “degenerate art,” 639 of his works were removed from German public museums, while 25 pieces were placed in the Degenerate Art Exhibition. He was subsequently expelled from the Academy of Arts in Berlin. Despite these setbacks, Kirchner continued to create and organized a major retrospective in Basel, which elicited mixed critical responses.

Tom Hayes, a former trader, faced a Libor-related trial, during which it was disclosed that he had been diagnosed with a mild form of Asperger syndrome prior to the proceedings. He was accompanied by a court-appointed aide throughout the trial. Prosecutors used his interviews with the Serious Fraud Office to portray him as greedy and corrupt. In contrast, the defense argued that Libor manipulation was widespread and an expected aspect of Hayes's role, noting that senior management were aware of the manipulation tactic.

Tom Hayes, a former trader, was implicated in the manipulation of Libor rates. He was arrested by British authorities on 11 December 2012 and was subsequently charged by United States authorities on 19 December 2012. Hayes initially cooperated with the United Kingdom’s Serious Fraud Office, providing around eighty hours of interviews in an effort to avoid extradition to the United States. Following the filing of charges by the SFO, he withdrew his cooperation and signaled an intention to contest the SFO charges. The SFO later narrowed the scope of the charges to reduce overlap with the U.S. case, a move that created the possibility of a second trial in the United States.

In the mid-1980s, a concept emerged for an advanced variant of the A-6 Intruder, designated as the A-6F Intruder II. The proposal called for replacing the Pratt & Whitney J52 turbojets with non-afterburning General Electric F404 turbofan engines, the powerplants used on the F/A-18, to provide improved power output and better fuel efficiency. It also envisioned modern avionics, including the Norden-designed AN/APQ-173 synthetic aperture radar, paired with a suite of multifunction cockpit displays to enhance situational awareness. The APQ-173 radar was intended to deliver air-to-air capability and to accommodate a potential AIM-120 AMRAAM. Additionally, the design would extend wing-pylon capacity by two stations, increasing the total to seven hardpoints for external stores.

During the Vietnam War, 84 A-6 Intruders were lost, with losses by cause totaling ten to surface-to-air missiles, two to MiGs, sixteen due to operational causes, and fifty-six to conventional ground fire and anti-aircraft artillery. The last Intruder loss occurred on 24 January 1973 when a VA-35 aircraft from USS America was shot down during close air support; the aircrew, LT C. M. Graf and LT S. H. Hatfield, ejected and were rescued by a Navy helicopter. The carrier air war saw about twenty U.S. Navy aircraft carriers rotate through Southeast Asian waters to provide air strikes from the early 1960s to the early 1970s. A-6 losses were borne by several carriers, including Constellation (11), Ranger (8), Coral Sea (6), Midway (2), Independence (4), Kitty Hawk (14), Saratoga (3), Enterprise (8), and America (2). United States Marine Corps A-6s were predominantly shore-based in South Vietnam at Chu Lai and Da Nang, and at Nam Phong in Thailand; they retained carrier-embarkation capability but were not typically deployed as carrier-based aircraft.

Giacomo Matteotti has left a lasting imprint on popular culture, with references across awards, cinema, music, sport, stamps, television, and theatre. In 2005, the Italian government established the Giacomo Matteotti Prize under the Presidency of the Council of Ministers, awarding recognition to works that illustrate the ideals of brotherhood between peoples, freedom, and social justice that guided Matteotti’s life. The prize comprises three categories: essays, literary and theatrical works, and graduate theses. In the realm of sport, the Matteotti Trophy was created in 1945 alongside a men’s road cycling race, which as of 2025 had reached its 77th edition. Philatelic commemorations include a 1955 Italian stamp issued to mark the 70th anniversary of Matteotti’s birth, in a red design with a value of 25 lire, and a 2012 commemorative stamp issued by San Marino with a face value of €2.64.

Following the fall of fascism and the establishment of the Italian Republic, Matteotti's memory has been commemorated with a wide array of monuments and tributes, including busts, gardens, gravestones, murals, plaques, squares, and streets; among them is the Monument to Giacomo Matteotti on Lungotevere Arnaldo da Brescia in Rome, situated at the site of his kidnapping and murder. In July 2025 that monument was vandalised, prompting condemnation across the political spectrum. Matteotti's murder has inspired several films and television productions; most notably, the 1973 film The Assassination of Matteotti, directed by Florestano Vancini, features Matteotti portrayed by Franco Nero. The 2024–2025 television miniseries Mussolini: Son of the Century, directed by Joe Wright and based on Antonio Scurati's 2018 novel M. Son of the Century (the 2019 Strega Prize winner), depicts Matteotti as played by Gaetano Bruno. In May 2024, on the centenary of Matteotti's death, Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni described him as a free man killed by fascist squads for his ideas, without naming Mussolini. In the early 21st century, Matteotti's murder has been likened to the deaths of Jamal Khashoggi and Alexei Navalny.

According to the historian Cai, both sides in the Qinghai–Tibet War were implicated in war crimes. Tibetan forces are reported to have looted monasteries and destroyed villages in Yushu, after which they raped nuns and local Qinghai Tibetan women. Ma Biao’s troops were accused of summarily executing Tibetan soldiers who had surrendered or were fleeing. In addition, Ma Biao’s army is said to have appropriated supplies from local nomadic civilians, reflecting a broader pattern of resource exploitation during the conflict.

In 1931, Ma Biao became the leader of the Yushu Defense Brigade as its second brigade commander, with Ma Xun commanding the first brigade. During the war against Tibet, Wang Jiamei served as Ma Biao's secretary. Ma Biao directed the defense of Lesser Surmang against a Tibetan assault from March 24 to 26, 1932. The Tibetan invaders significantly outnumbered Ma Biao's Qinghai forces. Cai Zuozhen, the Buqing tribal chief, fought on the Qinghai side against the Tibetans.

Backplane, in the context of bus expansion, denotes a configuration in which expansion cables link a computer’s internal bus to an external backplane, typically housed in an enclosure. This arrangement broadens the system’s expansion capabilities by providing additional or different slots beyond those offered by the host machine. A typical cable set comprises three components: a transmitter board installed in the host computer, an expansion board located on the remote backplane, and the cable that interconnects the two boards to carry data and control signals.

A backplane is a common orthogonal midplane that interconnects a set of vertical telephone line cards mounted on one side of a chassis. Each vertical line card is connected to copper telephone wires, and the backplane provides a connection to a horizontal communications card on the opposite side, thereby linking the line cards to the broader system.

Venus is a Belgian band. The group’s debut full-length album, Welcome To The Modern Dance Hall, was released in November 1999, ahead of 2000, and its European distribution helped broaden the band's audience by highlighting its organic instrumental approach. The record yielded singles such as Pop Song and a vinyl EP titled She’s So Disco, which enjoyed substantial radio play at the time. Belgium-based EP releases drew from the album’s material while adding new songs and were issued later under the 62 TV label. Before Western European touring began in 2000, the band underwent a lineup change when double bassist Walter Jenssens left and was replaced by Pierre Jacqmin, who is listed as a current member.

Venus, a Belgian band, issued its first release on the BGM/RCA label with the Royal Sucker EP. In March 1999 the group ended its relationship with BGM/RCA and signed with the Italian label Sonica. In April 1999 they won the Best Rock Act at the French festival Le Printemps de Bourges. The band then aimed to record and release a full-length album within 1999.

Kempinski The Boulevard Dubai, formerly Address Boulevard, is a 73-storey hotel located in Downtown Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Standing at about 370 metres (1,214 feet) in height, the building ranks among the tallest in Dubai and the world. The property contains 198 five-star rooms and suites. It features a restaurant and three swimming pools, and its location offers views of the Burj Khalifa.
Address Boulevard is a development by Emaar Properties, launched in 2012. Its serviced residences sold out on the launch day in September 2012.

Joiks, the most spiritually rooted form in Sámi music, occupy a central place in Sámi musical culture; in Northern Sami they are called luohti and in Southern Sami vuolle. The term joik is occasionally used to refer to lavlu or vuelie, though this is technically inaccurate. Joiks typically feature little or no text, do not rhyme, and have no fixed structural form. They may depict any subject important to the singer and show considerable variation in content. In northern regions, individuals often possess their own joik, sometimes bestowed at birth, which is regarded as personal to and representative of the bearer, akin to a name. Purely folk joiks diminished in popularity during the 20th century due to pop radio and religious fundamentalism, notably Laestadianism. Joiking gained wider visibility in Sweden and Scandinavia with the 1959 release of Sven-Gösta Jonsson's "I'm a Lapp," which presented joiking directed at heathen stones set to a skiffle-like beat. The first commercial recordings of joiking were made by Nils-Aslak Valkeapää in 1968, in Finland, and his recordings incorporated instrumentation and ambient sounds (such as barking dogs and wind), representing a departure from traditional joiking forms.

Sámi music encompasses the traditional and contemporary practices of the Sámi people of the Arctic regions. Among its most internationally recognized figures is Mari Boine, a Norwegian Sámi singer whose work is noted for a spare, folk-rock-inflected sound that draws on joik, the indigenous vocal tradition. In addition, non-Sámi musicians have incorporated joik and other Sámi stylistic elements into their music, broadening the reach of Sámi-inspired sound, with examples including RinneRadio, Xymox, and Jan Garbarek.

Valves are devices that regulate the flow of liquids or gases by controlling the opening within a valve body. The motion that actuates the closure can be transmitted through the stem as linear displacement, rotation, or a combination of both; an example is an angle-type valve that employs a torque reactor pin and hub assembly to convert movement. In many designs, the valve stem and body are threaded so that the stem screws into or out of the body to position the closure disc within the flow path. A packing seal located between the stem and bonnet prevents leakage along the stem. Some valves operate without any external control and therefore do not require a stem, as in the majority of check valves.

In many contexts, the term valve denotes poppet valves, a class of devices widely used in contemporary internal combustion engines within fossil-fuel powered vehicles. These components regulate the intake of the fuel–air mixture and facilitate the venting of exhaust gases as part of the engine's exhaust cycle.

The diagonal Δ: M → M × M, defined by Δ(x) = (x, x), is typically studied through perturbations within its equivalence class rather than by forcing direct self-intersections, enabling a stable interpretation of how the diagonal may intersect itself. This approach links to global topological invariants such as the Euler characteristic and the behavior of zeros of vector fields. For instance, on the circle S^1 the Betti numbers satisfy b0 = 1 and b1 = 1 with higher groups vanishing, which yields Euler characteristic χ(S^1) = 0 and reflects constraints on perturbative self-intersections. On the torus T^2 = S^1 × S^1, the diagonal can be displaced off itself by a small shift in one factor, exemplified by the map (θ, φ) ↦ (θ, φ + ε), illustrating how perturbations can remove self-intersections. More generally, the intersection number between the graph of a map f: M → M and the diagonal can be computed using homology, with the Lefschetz fixed-point theorem providing a unifying framework that ties such intersections to the fixed points of the induced map on homology. In this light, the self-intersection of the diagonal is a particular case of the identity map, since the diagonal corresponds to the graph of the identity on M.

Diagonals are line segments that connect two vertices of a polygon or polyhedron that are not joined by an edge, i.e., non-adjacent vertices. In everyday usage, the term can also refer to any sloping line. The word derives from the Greek diagonios, literally meaning "from corner to corner," formed from dia- "through/across" plus gonia "corner," with a cognate root gony relating to "knee." Historically, Strabo and Euclid used the term to denote a line joining two vertices of a rhombus or cuboid. In Latin, the concept was rendered as diagonus, meaning "slanting line."

In Windows networking, a domain refers to a logical collection of computers whose central directory is maintained by domain controllers. A domain controller is a server running Windows or Samba that performs authentication and policy enforcement for users and machines, consolidating security management and administrative control across the domain. Domains are typically deployed in networks with more than about ten computers, where centralized administration offers clear benefits. Computers that are members of a domain may be on the same local area network or spread across distant locations; geographical placement does not affect domain membership so long as network connectivity to the domain controllers is available.

Computers can connect to a domain via local area networks, wide area networks, or virtual private networks. Domain membership enables enhanced security for VPN connections, a benefit that arises from the domain’s support for a Certification Authority when it is integrated into a network. With CA support, smart cards and digital certificates can be used to authenticate identities. Digital certificates help protect stored information.

Laissez-faire capitalism is an economic doctrine that argues for minimal government intervention in economic activity. Some of its earliest formulations are attributed to P. S. de Boisguilbert, who reportedly stated that nature should be allowed to take its course. This early formulation predates later advocates such as d'Argenson and Gournay. By contrast, d'Argenson is more commonly associated with a maxim promoting limited governance rather than total nonintervention, summarized as governing not too much. Together these statements illustrate the spectrum of early thought that contributed to the development of laissez-faire ideas.

Within the framework of laissez-faire capitalism, the Manchester Liberal tradition, led by Richard Cobden and John Bright, championed free trade as a central policy. After Cobden’s death, the Cobden Club was established in 1866 to continue their free-trade advocacy. As the British Empire evolved, the breakdown of laissez-faire was partly driven by British companies seeking government backing abroad, with British oil firms playing a particularly influential role in pressing for such state support.

The State Council (국무회의) serves as the principal executive body and the national cabinet of South Korea. It examines and determines major policy matters within the scope of the executive power as defined by the Constitution. The ministries form the most influential component of the executive branch, playing a central role in policy formulation and implementation.

As of August 2020, the executive branch operates 23 ministries, 18 administrative authorities, two boards, four offices, and seven committees. The State Council comprises the president, the prime minister, and eighteen ministers, for a total of twenty members. Ministers must be appointed into the State Council before they are confirmed by the National Assembly. The president serves as the chairperson of the State Council, and the prime minister serves as its vice-chair.

Latin literature underwent a final flowering from the late third century into the fifth century, a period when pagan writers sustained vitality within the fading classical tradition. In historical writing, Ammianus Marcellinus contributed a major prose history; in oratory, Quintus Aurelius Symmachus produced notable rhetorical works; and in poetry, Ausonius and Rutilius Claudius Namatianus expanded the poetic repertoire. Ausonius’s Mosella is frequently cited as illustrating a more modern sensibility, a development that is often seen as signaling the end of classical literary forms as such.

Cicero is traditionally regarded as the leading figure of Latin prose. From roughly 80 BCE until his death in 43 BCE, his writings surpass those of any other surviving Latin author in volume, range of genres, and stylistic refinement. His oeuvre is commonly divided into four parts: letters, rhetorical treatises, philosophical works, and orations. The letters yield detailed portraits of a crucial period in Roman history and provide vivid depictions of public and private life among the Roman governing class. The rhetorical treatises constitute the principal Latin sources for ancient theories of education and eloquence. The philosophical writings laid the foundations of medieval moral philosophy. Through his orations, Cicero influenced many European political leaders and the framers of the United States.

In November 2000, the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission approved ATN's proposal to launch a television channel to be known as Urdu Channel. The commission described the service as a national ethnic Category 2 specialty television service, aimed at serving the Urdu-speaking community. The channel was targeted specifically at Urdu-speaking viewers within the national audience.

On August 30, 2013, the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission approved the Asian Television Network's application for its ATN Urdu service, reclassifying it from a licensed Category B specialty service to an exempted Category B third-language service.

In the 2009–10 season the competition was rebranded as the UEFA Europa League to raise its profile, accompanied by an expansion of the group stage that added eight more qualifiers. The group stage comprised 12 groups of four teams each in a double round-robin format, with the top two sides in each group advancing to the knockout rounds. The knockout phase consisted of four rounds of two-legged ties, culminating in a one-off final hosted at a neutral venue that met UEFA’s Category Four stadium criteria. Generally, matches were played on Thursdays, while the final in 2010 took place on a Wednesday in May, ten days before the Champions League final.

Under UEFA competition regulations, clubs may display jersey advertising even where a sponsor conflicts with the competition’s official Europa League sponsors. A maximum of two sponsorship logos may appear on a jersey in addition to the manufacturer's logo, with placements limited to one on the chest and one on the left sleeve. Non-profit organisations have exemptions allowing their logos to appear on the front of the shirt, integrated with the main sponsor, or on the back in one of two positions: beneath the squad number or between the player's name and the collar.

3D scanning encompasses techniques for capturing the shape of physical objects, with laser scanning serving as a method to sample surfaces by projecting and detecting laser light. The range of applications depends on the laser power and the nature of the resulting data, and lower power is often employed when it is important not to influence the surface being scanned, such as during digitisation. Confocal methods and other three-dimensional laser scanning approaches are used to derive quantitative information about surface geometry. In low‑power contexts, structured light projection systems are applied for solar cell flatness measurements, enabling rapid assessment and, consequently, stress calculations for large production runs, with more than 2,000 wafers processed per hour.

Silhouette-based 3D scanning relies on outlines extracted from a sequence of photographs taken around an object against a high-contrast background. The resulting silhouettes are extruded into volumetric prisms along the corresponding viewing directions, and the intersections of these volumes yield the visual hull, an approximate representation of the object's outer shape. A notable limitation of this approach is its inability to capture certain concavities, such as the interior of a bowl, because hidden geometry cannot be recovered from silhouette information alone.

La Resistencia Dios, Patria y Familia is a Peruvian political organization associated with anti-communist activism. Its opposition to leftist movements intensified during Pedro Castillo's 2021 presidency, when it organized and coordinated protests aimed at his removal, alleging fraud in the June 2021 elections and branding his administration as a usurper and terrorist regime. Sociologist Carmen Rosa Balbi contends that the group's interpretation of Castillo's victory frames it as a resurgence of Marxism-Leninism and Mariateguismo in Peru. In contrast, Tirso Molinari argues that the organization does not articulate a coherent ideological program beyond a McCarthyist posture.

La Resistencia Dios, Patria y Familia, a Peruvian movement, was involved in widespread protests against President Dina Boluarte. Its members gathered outside the headquarters of IDL-Reporteros and near the homes of Gustavo Gorriti, the chief journalist of IDL-Reporteros, and Rosa María Palacios, a journalist for La República. The nearby Peruvian National Police observed the demonstrations. La Resistencia subsequently attacked the IDL-Reporteros headquarters, throwing objects and explosives at the building. The group also issued antisemitic statements and directed death threats at Gorriti. The Committee to Protect Journalists condemned these actions as intimidation of journalists.

CBS News Radio is one of two national news services carried by Skyview Networks. Skyview Networks also distributes a broad range of programming, including national news, talk, music, and special event content, as well as local news, weather, video news, and other information to radio and television stations, and it provides traffic reporting services.

In March 2021, CBS News Radio hired John Batchelor to host a nightly newsmagazine titled Eye on the World. Batchelor had previously hosted a program under the same title, Eye on the World. The show's prior syndication had been carried initially by ABC Radio Networks and subsequently by Westwood One.

The Oskar Reinhart Collection was formed by Oskar Reinhart and is exhibited at two sites in Winterthur: Am Römerholz, Reinhart’s former residence in Winterthur in the canton of Zurich, Switzerland, and the Museum Oskar Reinhart in central Winterthur. The collection is owned by the Swiss Confederation and administered on its behalf by the Federal Office of Culture (Bundesamt für Kultur) in Bern.

The Oskar Reinhart Collection owns paintings by Matthias Grünewald, Lukas Cranach, Vincent van Gogh (two Hospital in Arles paintings, Ward and Garden), Pieter Bruegel the Elder (Adoration of the Magi in the Snow), Pierre-Auguste Renoir, Édouard Manet, Paul Cézanne, Eugène Delacroix, Théodore Géricault, Camille Corot, Honoré Daumier, Jean-François Millet, Gustave Courbet, Edgar Degas, Camille Pissarro, and Alfred Sisley.

Lambeth North tube station was designed by architect Leslie Green and opened on 10 March 1906 by the Baker Street & Waterloo Railway. It was originally named Kennington Road and served as the line’s temporary southern terminus until 5 August 1906, when Elephant & Castle station opened. In July 1906 it was renamed Westminster Bridge Road, and later, in April 1917, it became Lambeth (North). The name was simplified to Lambeth North in 1928.

Lambeth North is a London Underground station in the Lambeth district, located at the junction of Westminster Bridge Road and Baylis Road. It is the penultimate stop on the Bakerloo line, lying on the segment between Waterloo and Elephant & Castle. The station sits in Zone 1 and is the nearest Underground access to the Imperial War Museum’s exit. In 2017, it was ranked as the least-used Underground station in Zone 1.

Dirty Jobs used Faith No More's We Care A Lot as its opening theme, featuring a line implying that a dirty job must be performed by someone. Each episode begins with a Dirty Jobs logo screen before a commercial break, followed by a segment of Matt Koskenmaki's Get On Out In Here. In the first half of 2007, licensing issues led to the replacement of the original theme with Koskenmaki's Pop Rock Theme, and several episodes from that period were subsequently reedited. Mike Rowe explained that rights to We Care A Lot were not renewed in time or were not properly secured. The network did not issue an official statement clarifying the situation. The original theme returned starting with the June 26, 2007 episode and has since been used in later DVD releases of earlier episodes.

Discovery, Inc. announced on November 15, 2021 that Dirty Jobs would be revived, with Mike Rowe returning as host. The inaugural episode of the revived series aired on January 2, 2022, and was available on both Discovery and Discovery+.

Democrazia è Libertà – La Margherita (DL), commonly known as The Daisy (La Margherita), was a centrist political party in Italy that emerged from the merger of three centre-left groups—the Italian People's Party, The Democrats, and Italian Renewal—within the broader centre-left coalition. It was led by Francesco Rutelli, a former mayor of Rome, who served as party president and stood as its prime ministerial candidate in the 2001 general election as part of the Olive Tree coalition. In that election, The Daisy's list secured about 14.5 percent of the national vote.

Democracy is Freedom – The Daisy was a centrist political formation in Italy that aimed to unite the centrist components of The Olive Tree, which had been divided among numerous parties since 1996. In the 1996 general election, two centrist lists operated within the Italian centre-left: Populars for Prodi, grouping the PPI, UD, PRI and SVP, and Italian Renewal (RI), which later merged into the SDI in 1998. In 1998, splinters from the centre-right formed the Democratic Union for the Republic (UDR), a faction that later became the Union of Democrats for Europe (UDEUR) to support the D'Alema I Cabinet. The following year saw further realignment with splinters from the PPI, UD and others forming The Democrats (Dem). Also in 1999, Union for the Republic (UpR), a breakaway from UDR, SDI and PRI, joined forces in The Clover, a short-lived alliance.

On the Native American (U.S. Census) context, the Hispanic origin question uses the same set of checkboxes as the 2010 census, including Mexican, Mexican American or Chicano; Puerto Rican; Cuban; and an option for Yes, another Hispanic, Latino, or Spanish origin. Two changes were introduced under this item: first, the wording was shortened from "Print origin, for example" to "Print, for example," removing the word origin to reduce confusion and to reflect respondents with diverse backgrounds; second, the write-in instructions for the Some Other Race category were revised from "Print race" to "Print race or origin" to align with the instruction to mark one or more boxes and print origins.

The treatment of Native American identities in the U.S. Census has shifted markedly from the late 18th century to the present, reflecting broader changes in the government’s approach to race and ethnicity. From 1790 through 1960, census takers determined an individual's race, with racial categories evolving across successive decennial censuses. Beginning with the 1970 census, individuals began to self-identify their race, a change driven by reforms associated with the Civil Rights Act of 1964 and the Voting Rights Act of 1965 aimed at producing more accurate population data. Since the 1980 census, the survey has separately classified respondents by both race and ethnicity, explicitly distinguishing Hispanic or Latino from Not Hispanic or Latino. This methodological separation has attracted criticism from bodies such as the American Anthropological Association and the U.S. Commission on Civil Rights, which have questioned the validity and utility of bifurcating race and ethnicity in census data.

MØ, a Danish singer and songwriter, expanded her international profile in 2019 through a combination of television appearances, collaborations, festival performances, and new releases. She performed the single "Blur" on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon in 2019. She co-wrote and provided vocals for the theme song of Moominvalley. She also served as a supporting act on Panic! at the Disco's UK tour. Her festival appearances that year included Glastonbury Festival and Roskilde Festival. In October 2019 she released her debut mixtape, MMMMØ – The Mix, and issued the single "On & On" on 31 October 2019.

During 2014, MØ participated in several high-profile collaborations that broadened her international profile. She contributed to Iggy Azalea's track Beg for It, the lead single from Azalea's reissued album Reclassified, and the two artists performed the song on Saturday Night Live on October 25, 2014. Earlier that year, MØ was featured on Elliphant's single One More, released on September 22, 2014 with the official video released the following day. In addition, she co-wrote Major Lazer's song All My Love, a track that features Ariana Grande.

Nuri al-Said led Arab troops who secured Damascus for Faisal in 1918 after the retreat of Ottoman forces. When Faisal was deposed by the French in 1920, he accompanied him to Iraq. In 1922 he became the first director-general of the Iraqi police, and in that post he tended to fill the force with his loyalists, a strategy he repeated in subsequent positions. This approach underpinned the basis of his considerable political clout in later years.

Nuri al-Said, a trusted ally of Faisal, played a pivotal role in shaping the early Iraqi state. In 1924, Faisal appointed him deputy commander in chief of the army to secure the regime’s troop loyalty, a post he leveraged to forge a personal power base within the military establishment. Throughout the 1920s, he supported the monarch’s policy to expand the nascent armed forces, which drew their cohesion from Sharifian officers—former Ottoman soldiers who formed the backbone of the regime.

Developed by Fritz and Heinz London in 1935, the London equations are a set of constitutive relations that relate the superconducting current to the electromagnetic fields inside and around a superconductor. They provide the most straightforward description of superconducting phenomena, in contrast to Ohm's law for ordinary conductors. The framework formed the genesis of virtually all modern introductory treatments of superconductivity. In particular, the equations account for the Meissner effect, describing the exponential expulsion of magnetic fields from the interior of a material as it transitions into the superconducting state.

Wang BASIC provides refined control over output through its PRINT statement, which accepts both comma and semicolon as parameter separators: the comma advances the cursor to the next 16-character-wide column, while the semicolon leaves the cursor at the end of the printed value. TAB() is supported as a formatting function, whereas SPC() is not implemented. In addition, the language offers formatted output via a dedicated PRINTUSING facility paired with a separate image that defines the formatting rules. An image is defined on a line that begins with a percent sign, such as a line like 180 % ##,###.##, and it can be invoked with 190 PRINTUSING 180, N to render the value N in that specified format. Characters that are not part of the image’s formatting codes are echoed during printing, enabling fully customized output that can include fixed text around the numeric value, for example text like ANGLE= and RADIANS surrounding the formatted number.

Wang BASIC, a dialect of the BASIC programming language used on Wang systems, received notable enhancements with the 2200B revision, including the addition of the ON...GOTO and ON...GOSUB multi-branching constructs that had been absent previously. The KEYIN command enables reading a single character from the keyboard without requiring a pause, and is comparable to MS BASIC's INKEY$ routine. The VAL function is designed to search a string and extract the numeric value embedded within it. The NUM function, while akin to LEN in purpose, returns the length of the numeric substring from the start of a string up to the first non-numeric character, with spaces considered valid within numbers; for example NUM("1234.5") = 6 and NUM("1234.5    ") = 10.

Sentai Filmworks is an entity that is unrelated to the Super Sentai media franchise. It has no role in the international distribution of Super Sentai content. The name is often regarded as misleading, as it does not reflect any affiliation with Super Sentai.

Sentai Filmworks licenses properties outside the United States by sublicensing to regional distributors. In 2011, MVM Entertainment secured the license for Mahoromatic: Something More Beautiful following Sentai’s re-release of the series. The same arrangement occurred with Broken Blade, which was licensed by MVM Entertainment after Sentai’s re-release.

From late 1970 through 1985, Billboard published two Bubbling Under charts: Bubbling Under the Top LPs and Bubbling Under the Hot 100. These lists tracked records that had not yet appeared on the main albums chart, the Top LPs & Tape. At the time, the Top LPs & Tape served as the primary albums chart and functioned as the predecessor to the Billboard 200.

One Direction became the first group to debut at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with its first three studio albums. This milestone was reached when Midnight Memories entered the chart at the top for the issue dated December 14, 2013. The group later extended the record by becoming the first act to debut at No. 1 with its first four albums, when Four likewise debuted atop the Billboard 200 on the chart dated November 26, 2014.

Semai is an Austroasiatic language of western Malaysia. It is spoken by approximately 60,438 individuals belonging to the Semai. It is one of the few Aslian languages that are not endangered, with around 2,000 monolingual speakers. The language is currently spoken by three principal groups: Northern Semai, Central Semai, and Southern Semai.

Asli (2017), directed by David Liew, is a film that follows a bi-racial girl as she discovers her cultural heritage. The work is notable within Semai-language cinema for being the first film to allocate approximately half of its dialogue to Semai, marking a milestone in the use and visibility of the language in narrative film.

Within British Columbia, the designation of town constitutes a particular class of municipalities. A community may pursue incorporation as a town by means of letters patent, a process that requires the endorsement of the provincial Minister of Communities, Sport and Cultural Development. The incorporation pathway is limited to communities whose population falls between 2,501 and 5,000 residents. In addition, the proposal must be approved by those affected through a referendum, with more than half of the voters casting a yes vote for incorporation to be realized.

Mountain resort municipalities are governed by an elected mayor and council, operating on a four-year electoral cycle. Elections take place on the third Saturday in October. The most recent municipal election occurred on October 15, 2022, with the subsequent election set for October 17, 2026. Each municipality participates in a regional district, with the council electing representatives to the district's governing board. This board of directors serves as a forum where regional issues pertinent to the municipalities are discussed and addressed.

The Mamberamo River in New Guinea is formed where the Tariku, which runs from west to east, joins the Taritatu, coming from the east; the river then threads swampy terrain with substantial internal descents before its confluence, and it reaches the ocean after breaking through the Coastal Mountains, remaining navigable up to Marine Falls. The Sepik River is the island’s more important watercourse, gathering waters from a broad pool and extending roughly 1,100 kilometers from the Victor Emanuel Range to its estuary, making it the longest river in New Guinea; its course is winding, its waters muddy and sluggish, and navigation is feasible for about 500 kilometers. The Ramu River runs roughly 650 kilometers, with the lower section suitable for navigation while the upper reaches exhibit a high-gradient, fast-flowing regime, and its energy is utilized by a hydroelectric plant near Kainantu.

New Guinea covers approximately 786,000 square kilometers of tropical terrain, a land area that accounts for less than 0.5 percent of Earth's surface. The region supports a remarkable share of global biodiversity, with estimates placing roughly five to ten percent of all living species on the planet within its borders, a proportion comparable to that found in the United States or Australia. A large portion of its flora and fauna are endemic, and thousands of species remain unknown to science. Current estimates identify more than 200,000 insect species, between 11,000 and 20,000 plant species, and over 650 resident bird species. Most of its taxa trace their origins to lineages shared with Australia, reflecting their common paleogeographic history, as Australia and New Guinea were part of the same landmass until relatively recent geological times. Given its vast size and distinctive ecological assemblages, the island is often regarded as nearly a continent in terms of biological distinctiveness.

During his tenure, the Baron of Paraná sought to broaden conservative support by inviting liberal figures to join the governing ranks and appointing some to ministerial posts. Although the cabinet achieved notable success, it encountered persistent opposition from ultraconservative factions within the Conservative Party, who charged that the administration had become a political machine of converted liberals pursuing office rather than upholding the party’s ideals. Paraná demonstrated resilience by weathering threats and overcoming obstacles to governance. He died unexpectedly in September 1856, at the height of his career, and the cabinet remained in power until May 1857.

Politicians who rose to power in the 1830s faced the practical difficulties of governing and by 1840 had grown skeptical of ruling the country alone. They therefore acknowledged Pedro II as an indispensable authority whose presence was considered essential to Brazil's survival. A faction among them formed the Conservative Party in the 1840s, arguing that a neutral figure above factional disputes was necessary to address growing discontent and moderate conflicts. They envisioned an emperor who would be more dependent on the legislature than the constitutional monarch under Pedro I, yet endowed with greater powers than those sought at the start of the Regency by their rivals, who would become the Liberal Party. In response, the Liberals pressed to lower Pedro II's age of majority from 18 to 14. The Emperor was declared fit to rule in July 1840.

The BET Her Award is an accolade presented by BET recognizing motivational and empowering songs that center on women. It was first awarded in 2006 as the BET J Cool Like That Award to honor outstanding neo-soul and traditional R&B artists. The award’s name changed when BET J was rebranded as Centric in 2009, and it changed again in 2018 when Centric was rebranded as BET Her. Regarding nominations, until 2012, artists themselves were nominated; starting in 2013, BET began nominating artists with a respective song. Beyoncé is the most awarded artist in this category with three wins.

Scholars have debated the most effective means to counter insurgencies, with some arguing that political strategies can outperform direct military action. Francis Fukuyama contends that addressing underlying political grievances, strengthening legitimate governance, and improving institutions are often more successful in defeating insurgencies than military measures alone. In a related vein, David Kilcullen emphasizes the need to distinguish between Al Qaeda and broader militant movements that employ terrorism from the tactic of terrorism itself, arguing that understanding this distinction is essential for developing appropriate counterinsurgency responses.

Legitimacy in governance is not secured by rhetoric about democracy or electoral processes alone; it depends on the perception that political authority rests on the consent of the governed. This requires tangible institutional performance, including relatively low levels of corruption and a functioning law enforcement and judiciary. In addition, these institutions must actively enforce human rights and ensure due process. When these conditions are met, public confidence in the state is strengthened, whereas deficits in these areas can undermine legitimacy and contribute to support for insurgent alternatives.
Yellowstone National Park was established on March 1, 1872, within the boundaries of the Montana Territory. In 1978, the park’s Montana portion was divided between Park County and Gallatin County.

Montana contains two consolidated city–counties, Anaconda-Deer Lodge County and Butte-Silver Bow County. The portion of Yellowstone National Park that lies within the state was not part of any county until 1978, when a segment of Yellowstone within Montana was assigned to Gallatin County in name, and the remaining portion was assigned to Park County.

Post-nominal letters are characters appended to a person’s name to indicate that the individual holds a particular position or office, or has been honoured. In formal writing, these suffixes convey the bearer’s credentials or distinctions beyond the name itself, signaling recognitions or appointments associated with the person.
Certain obsolete orders are not included in the list; however, an order is listed if there are living recipients who still use the associated post-nominal letters after the order has become obsolete.

Teleophthalmology employs telecommunications technologies to enable remote assessment and management of eye health. Central to its practice is fundus photography, in which retinal images are captured with a fundus camera. A fundus camera is a specialized, low-magnification microscope that integrates an attached camera, purpose-built to obtain detailed views of the retina for evaluation by clinicians who may be distant from the patient.

Teleophthalmology encompasses the use of mobile applications and digital imaging technologies to conduct eye tests and support education in ophthalmology and optometry. Mobile apps facilitate basic assessments such as visual acuity tests and color vision assessments, as well as viewing and sharing retinal or ocular images, while also serving educational purposes. Advances in digital ocular imaging devices are central to teleophthalmology, enabling higher quality data and remote analysis. New retinal imaging modalities, notably optical coherence tomography, yield micrometer-resolution digital images of the retina that can be transmitted for research or diagnostic use. In parallel with professional, clinician-oriented systems, patient-centered platforms such as Eye-File designed for general public use are emerging, with examples archived on the Wayback Machine.

Esquire described Sinatra's performance as clearly executed, hard-edged, precise, and utterly in command. He was awarded the Grammy Legend Award in 1994. At that year's Grammys, Bono introduced him, praising his unmistakable attitude and calling him a definitive boss figure in show business.

In 1954, Frank Sinatra co-starred with Doris Day in the musical film Young at Heart. In the same year, he earned critical praise for his portrayal of a psychopathic killer who impersonates an FBI agent in the film noir Suddenly, opposite Sterling Hayden.

In 1813, the Cortes of New Spain issued a decree prescribing at least partial secularization of the missions. The measure was framed as applying to all missions across the American territories and to outposts that had been in operation for a decade or longer. However, the decree was never enforced in California.

During the late 18th century, the growing Spanish settler population in Alta California intensified disputes over mission boundaries and access to natural resources. Conflicts emerged between the Crown and the Catholic Church over land tenure, accompanied by debates among state and ecclesiastical officials about the scope of mission authority. In 1782, Franciscan priests from Mission Santa Clara de Asís submitted a petition to the governor arguing that Indigenous people affiliated with the mission owned land and cattle and represented the Ohlone in conflicts with nearby Spanish settlers in San José. The petition described damage to Indigenous crops caused by pueblo settlers’ livestock and noted that the intermingling of cattle from the two groups led to losses. The priests contended that Indigenous communities should be permitted to own property and to defend it.

In the late 19th and early 20th centuries, researchers pursued primate studies to illuminate human evolution, while wary of being perceived as peddling Garner-style primate folklore. By the early 1900s, observational investigations conducted in Western science were often regarded as unprofessional and inadequately controlled, prompting many to favor laboratory experiments as the ideal method. Yet the development of suitable primate housing and the maintenance of controlled conditions proved to be difficult, limiting progress on experimental approaches. Furthermore, primates are not native to Europe or North America, and the cost of importing them added a substantial financial barrier to extensive primate research.

Richard Garner was among the earliest researchers to devote himself to primate field studies. He advanced the practice by erecting a cage within an African forest to observe gorillas in their natural habitat. He documented primate vocalizations and conducted playback experiments to assess how they responded to auditory stimuli. In his writings, he offered anthropomorphic, speech-like portrayals of monkeys and apes, a stance that attracted sensational newspaper coverage and accompanying illustrations.

Bronisław Huberman was married to the German actress Elza Galafrés, who is also described as a singer and ballerina. The couple had a son named Johannes, but the marriage did not endure. Elza later became involved with Hungarian composer and pianist Ernő Dohnányi, and neither Huberman nor Dohnányi's wife consented to a divorce. Elza and Dohnányi had a child out of wedlock in 1917. In 1919, after Huberman granted her a divorce, Elza married Dohnányi. Dohnányi subsequently adopted Johannes.

Bronisław Huberman left Vienna in 1937 and sought refuge in Switzerland, arriving a year before the Anschluss. In 1938, a plane accident in Sumatra nearly ended his career, injuring his left wrist and two fingers. After extensive retraining, he resumed performing. At the outset of World War II, he was touring South Africa and could not return to Switzerland until after the war. Shortly thereafter, he fell ill from exhaustion and never regained his strength. He died in Corsier-sur-Vevey, Switzerland, on 16 June 1947, at the age of 64.

El (Cyrillic) refers to the Cyrillic letter Л, used across several Slavic languages. In most Slavic languages employing the Cyrillic script, a distinct orthographic convention exists to indicate whether the lateral /l/ is hard or soft. Consequently, the letter Л can represent either a hard [l] or a softened [l], with the actual pronunciation determined by the following letter in the spelling. This particular distinction is not applied in the same way in Serbian and Macedonian.

The Cyrillic letter el typically denotes the alveolar lateral approximant /l/. In Slavic languages, the articulation of this sound can be either palatalized or slightly velarized, reflecting language-specific phonetic variation.

Smooth jazz developed as a recognizable radio format and attained popularity in the 1980s and 1990s. Its appeal waned gradually during the early 2000s, and by 2009 a substantial number of stations had moved away from the format, including outlets in the major markets of New York City, Washington, D.C., and Boston.

Within the history of smooth jazz, a notable backlash developed as critics raised concerns about the direction of the genre, with Kenny G attracting especially pointed scrutiny. Critics characterized his sound as bland, a description that echoed broader debates about the artistic merits of the style. Despite these criticisms, Kenny G established himself as one of the top-selling saxophonists, and his popularity reached its zenith with the 1992 album Breathless, which remains his best-known and commercially successful release.

Although the euro is the official currency of the eurozone, its use extends beyond the European Union through unilateral adoption and foreign-trade practices. Montenegro and Kosovo have adopted the euro unilaterally as their sole legal tender. In addition, the euro is utilized as a foreign-trading currency in several countries, notably Cuba (since 1998), Syria (since 2006), and Venezuela (since 2018). In Zimbabwe, the abandonment of the local currency in 2009 led to the practical adoption of major global convertible currencies, including the euro and the United States dollar. Overall, direct usage of the euro outside the official EU framework affects roughly three million people.

Outside the euro area, several currencies maintain exchange-rate arrangements anchored to the euro. The Bosnia and Herzegovina convertible mark is kept at a fixed level through a currency-board system. The Central African CFA franc, West African CFA franc, CFP franc, Cape Verdean escudo, Comorian franc, and São Tomé and Príncipe dobra all operate under conventional fixed exchange-rate regimes linked to the euro. The Macedonian denar is governed by a stabilized arrangement. The Moroccan dirham is pegged to the euro via a basket of currencies. As of December 2023, additional countries with exchange-rate regimes linked to the euro include Romania, Serbia, Singapore, Botswana, Tunisia, Samoa, Fiji, Libya, Kuwait, Syria, China, and Vanuatu.

In Crimes of the Heart, the lives of the three sisters Meg, Babe, and Lenny are tested by the gravely ill Old Grandaddy, around whom the action centers as news of his likely death unfolds. Chick inquiries about his condition, and Lenny confirms that death appears probable; after Chick departs to place calls, Lenny confesses that she had wished for the elder’s passing and urges the family to reduce their fighting. Meg returns home in a buoyant mood, claiming she feels empathy for others, and the sisters respond with a shared, almost gallows-humor reaction to the prospect of their grandfather’s death. Lenny articulates a fear of being left alone, and Meg suggests she consider contacting an old lover. Lenny goes upstairs while Babe shows Meg photographs; Barnette arrives to collect them and outlines a plan related to Babe’s case. Meg leaves with Barnette to purchase a birthday cake for Lenny, and Lenny returns as Chick arrives, criticizing Meg for how she treats their sister, prompting Lenny to drive Chick away. Lenny then phones her former lover to arrange a date. She goes outside to find Meg, during which Babe makes a suicide attempt. Meg returns to find Babe, who reveals she understands why their mother killed the family cat at the time of her own suicide. Lenny comes back, and the sisters sing Happy Birthday to her, expressing a wish for happiness; after the cake is cut, they laugh and, for the moment, seem finally happy.

A 1986 film adaptation of Crimes of the Heart, directed by Bruce Beresford, features Sissy Spacek as Babe, Jessica Lange as Meg, Diane Keaton as Lenny, Tess Harper as Chick, Sam Shepard as Doc, and Hurd Hatfield as Old Granddaddy. The production earned three Academy Award nominations: Beth Henley for Best Adapted Screenplay, Spacek for Best Actress, and Harper for Best Supporting Actress.

Maximum density refers to the phenomenon by which a substance attains its greatest density under conditions of very low temperature and, in some cases, high pressure.
