In general, most materials expand when heated, leading to a increase in volume with rising temperature; conversely, at sufficiently low temperatures a given mass occupies a smaller volume, resulting in a higher density. Moreover, many substances—especially weakly interacting fluids—are compressible and shrink in volume when pressure is applied. Taken together, these tendencies imply that nearly all substances exhibit a density maximum at extreme low temperatures and elevated pressures. This density maximum is regarded as a characteristic property of the solid state of matter.

Water exhibits an anomalous density behavior in which its density increases as temperature falls until it reaches a maximum at about 4 °C (39 °F); below this temperature, further cooling causes density to decrease as water nears the freezing point. This unusual density peak has important ramifications for Earth's ecosystems, influencing the vertical structure and mixing of aquatic systems, shaping the distribution of nutrients and dissolved oxygen, and thereby affecting habitat conditions for aquatic organisms, particularly in temperate regions where seasonal stratification and turnover are tied to this property.

NCBI Bookshelf is a digital repository of biomedical books and documents maintained by the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI), which is part of the National Library of Medicine (NLM). The NLM itself is a branch of the National Institutes of Health (NIH), within the United States government, and the NCBI is funded and approved by the federal government. The organization is based in Bethesda, Maryland, and was founded in 1988 under legislation sponsored by U.S. Congressman Claude Pepper.

NCBI Bookshelf hosts information about the Conserved Domain Database (CDD) for proteins, a resource that uses a set of sequence profiles to characterize highly conserved protein domains. The CDD provides curated profiles that facilitate the identification and analysis of domain architectures, enabling functional inference across diverse protein families. In addition to its own records, the database incorporates entries from external resources such as SMART and Pfam, thereby offering an integrated collection of protein-domain annotations within the broader platform.

GNU Multiple Precision Arithmetic Library (GMP) provides facilities for integer arithmetic with arbitrary precision and is widely used in computational mathematics. It is employed by many computer algebra systems, including Mathematica and Maple, to perform large-integer computations. Additionally, GMP serves as a component of the Computational Geometry Algorithms Library (CGAL), where exact arithmetic is essential for robust geometric algorithms.

The GNU Multiple Precision Arithmetic Library (GMP) is primarily intended for cryptography applications and research, and it is also widely used in Internet security contexts as well as in computer algebra systems.

Backplanes are circuit boards that provide the connectors and power distribution required to attach hard drives within a system. They commonly feature multiple slots, each capable of housing a hard drive, allowing several drives to be connected via a single backplane. To indicate the status of each slot, backplanes are typically equipped with LEDs; the color or blinking pattern of a given LED reflects the slot's current state.

SGPIO was developed to drive LEDs on backplanes using low-cost CPLDs or microcontrollers. However, timing variations and differing interpretations of the bit-stream across vendors introduce compatibility challenges. A simple CPLD implementation typically applies to only a single tested vendor’s product. Although microcontrollers are more suitable, the 4-bit SGPIO bus is not implemented on them. Reading the 4-bit lines via general-purpose I/O pins at roughly 100 kHz proves too slow for many affordable microcontrollers to manage alongside LED control and other tasks. The length of the bit stream varies among host bus adapters and storage controllers. Some vendors terminate the bit-stream once the desired drive is reached, while others clock it through to the end. In SAS environments, expanders can have bit streams as long as 108 bits (36 × 3).

In 1958, United Press merged with the International News Service to form United Press International (UPI), and British United Press was renamed United Press International of Canada (UPI Canada). In 1979, eighty percent of UPI Canada was sold to the Toronto Sun newspaper chain, and the agency was renamed United Press Canada. In 1985, United Press Canada was sold to Canadian Press, which absorbed it.

United Press International (UPI) emerged from the merger of United Press and the International News Service, undertaken by Scripps and Hearst to create a stronger competitor to the Associated Press and a more robust economic entity than UP or INS. The resulting agency had about 950 client newspapers. Antitrust concerns were anticipated from the Eisenhower Administration's Justice Department, prompting Scripps and Hearst to push the merger through with unusual speed and secrecy to avoid regulatory scrutiny.

Francis Irénée du Pont (December 3, 1873 – March 16, 1942) was an American chemist and executive at E.I. du Pont de Nemours Company. He was the great-grandson of Éleuthère Irénée du Pont, the founder of the firm, situating him within the family lineage that shaped the company’s early leadership.

In 1913, Francis Irénée du Pont published a taxation treatise issued by Saylor Show Print in Wilmington, Delaware, entitled Taxation: A Treatise written by F. I. DuPont. The work develops the ideas of Henry George, the author of Progress and Poverty, which is described as the best-selling book ever on political economy. It analyzes several potential tax bases and argues that taxation of privilege, via land value taxation, represents the most desirable basis. The treatise condemns land speculation as a gross misuse of the power of government and contends that taxing such activity would foster prosperity. Du Pont later campaigned for Mayor of Wilmington on that platform, running on the Progressive ticket, but was unsuccessful.

The refectory is situated on the south side of the cloister, with the kitchen at its western end reached through an anteroom and a long passage. Nearby lie the bake house, brew house, and the servants’ sleeping-rooms. The upper story of the refectory is known as the vestiarium, a chamber designated for storing the monks’ ordinary clothes.

An abbey is a self-sufficient religious community that typically sustains itself through agricultural production and crafts, using its surplus to care for the poor and needy. Historically, abbeys have also served as refuges for those facing persecution and as centers of education for the young. In addition, several abbeys offer lodging for individuals seeking a period of spiritual retreat. Across the Mediterranean Basin and Europe, numerous abbeys are renowned for their religious, cultural, and architectural significance.

At the 1999 Australian Open men's singles event, Yevgeny Kafelnikov captured the title by defeating Thomas Enqvist in the final, in a four-set match that ended 4–6, 6–0, 6–3, 7–6(7–1). The victory marked Kafelnikov's second Grand Slam singles title and would be his last at majors, the first having come at the 1996 French Open. It also established him as the first Russian player, male or female, to win an Australian Open singles championship, a milestone in the tournament's history.

PlayStation 5 features a cooling system centered on a 120 mm (4.7 in) diameter, 45 mm (1.8 in) thick fan configured to intake air from both sides. The system employs a large heatsink with a heat pipe design intended to approximate vapor chamber performance due to its geometry and airflow. A liquid metal interface layer between the processor die and the heatsink enhances heat transfer. An internal power supply rated at 350 watts accompanies the unit. The design is also aimed at reducing power consumption in rest mode relative to the PlayStation 4.

PlayStation 5 employs a custom AMD-based system-on-a-chip developed in collaboration with Sony that integrates the console’s central processing unit and graphics processing unit. The eight-core processor is based on AMD’s Zen 2 architecture, fabricated on a 7-nanometer process and capable of a variable clock rate up to 3.5 GHz. The GPU adheres to AMD’s RDNA 2 design, comprising 36 compute units, operating up to 2.23 GHz and delivering up to 10.28 teraflops of performance. The hardware supports real-time, hardware-accelerated ray tracing, and the GPU is programmed through Sony’s graphics API, AGC. A bespoke boost system, leveraging AMD SmartShift, dynamically adjusts CPU and GPU frequencies to balance peak performance with power consumption.

The Senate of the Republic serves as the upper chamber of Italy's Parliament. It comprises 200 members, of whom 196 are elected from Italian constituencies and four are elected by Italian citizens living abroad. In addition, there is a category of life senators—six at present—appointed by the President of the Republic or as former presidents. Members are styled as Senator or, formally, The Honourable Senator (Onorevole Senatore). The Senate meets at Palazzo Madama in Rome.

Historically, Italy maintained a uniform voting age of 18 for all elections, while Senate elections imposed a higher threshold of 25 years. In 2021, Constitutional Law No. 1/2021 redefined the franchise for the Senate, reducing its voting age to 18 and harmonizing it with the Chamber of Deputies. Consequently, the 2022 general election marked the first occasion on which both chambers were elected by the same electorate, giving them identical electoral bodies.

The 2024 Icelandic Cup was won by Knattspyrnufélag Akureyrar (KA) following a 2–0 victory over Víkingur Reykjavík in the final on 21 September 2024, securing KA's first Icelandic Cup title. The final was a rematch of the previous season's championship decider, featuring the same two clubs.

The 2024 Icelandic Cup was the 65th edition of Iceland's national football cup. For sponsorship reasons, it carried the name Mjólkurbikarinn ("The Milk Cup"). The winners earned qualification for the first qualifying round of the 2025–26 UEFA Conference League.

Historically, orthopaedics originated with an emphasis on correcting deformities in children and gradually broadened to address deformities in adults. The management of traumatic injuries grew into a central aspect of the specialty, with substantial advances occurring during World War I, continuing through the interwar years, and accelerating during World War II. After the war, orthopaedics established itself as the dominant discipline for fracture treatment on a global scale.

Nicolas Andry coined the term orthopaedics in his 1741 treatise Orthopédie, which addressed the correction of childhood deformities and laid the foundation for the discipline. The book’s frontispiece depicts a young sapling restrained by a supporting stake to illustrate how early, guiding intervention can promote proper growth. This image, known as the Tree of Andry, has endured as a symbolic emblem for the field, being adopted by numerous international orthopaedic associations as a representative mark.

My Savior is a gospel covers album by American singer Carrie Underwood, released after her first Christmas collection, My Gift, arrived in September 2020 amid the COVID-19 pandemic. Underwood described the project as part of her enduring artistic vision and framed it as legacy material she had long wanted to make, noting that both My Gift and the gospel covers had been planned well before the events of the past year and had been on her musical bucket list since the start of her career. In a January 2021 interview with People, she expressed a desire to stay positive and hoped the songs would bring joy to listeners during difficult times. The album is portrayed as inspirational and deeply personal, with Underwood calling the undertaking a blessing to create.

My Savior is an album that features gospel standards and hymns with subtle inflections of country and pop. The production is sparse and acoustic, designed to highlight Underwood's voice and to evoke a church-service atmosphere rather than a grand, stadium-scale sound. Critical reception was broadly positive, with Entertainment Weekly’s Hilary Hughes awarding it an A and praising the restrained production and intimate, worshipful mood; Riff Magazine emphasizing the album’s fidelity to gospel standards and Underwood’s graceful, soothing vocal delivery while noting modest country and pop influences; Worship Leader commending the balance of a traditional hymns feel with a contemporary touch; Country Universe giving four out of five stars for conveying faith and musicality without compromising sincerity; and Spectrum Culture offering a more mixed view at 68 percent, suggesting the project targets a specific audience though it features a remarkable vocal performance.

Notable individuals from the Kapampangan community include Jomar Sadie, a native of Angeles City who serves as a Philippine diplomat assigned to Iraq, is a member of Mensa International, and is active in anti-trafficking advocacy.

Francisco Alonso Liongson was an outstanding Philippine playwright who wrote in Spanish, and he played a pivotal role in Kapampangan cultural life as the founding president of Círculo Escenico, Pampanga’s Spanish-language theater troupe. Under his leadership, Círculo Escenico gained national renown, helping to elevate regional Spanish theater and contributing to the broader Filipino cultural scene.

Diocaesarea, also spelled Diocaesareia or Diokaisareia (Greek Διοκαισάρεια), was a Graeco-Roman town in ancient Cappadocia situated near Nazianzus. The settlement was described by Gregory of Nazianzus as a small locality. In antiquity it is also recorded by Ptolemy and by Pliny the Elder, indicating its inclusion in classical geographical sources.

Representatives from Ankara argued that improving the conditions of minorities in Turkey depended principally on excluding foreign intervention, and they added that preventing external provocation was also essential. They contended that external influence was the primary factor shaping minority welfare, rather than internal reforms alone.

The population exchanges between Greece and Turkey, formalized in the 1923 Lausanne Convention, followed the Greco-Turkish War and aimed to create ethnically homogeneous nation-states by relocating Orthodox Christians from Turkey to Greece and Muslims from Greece to Turkey. Some historians describe Turkish policy during this period as an effort to erase the Greek element deemed hostile to the state, drawing parallels with earlier actions against Armenians. The operation involved compulsory relocation inland and away from regions of origin, with insufficient provisions for the newcomers' welfare, exposing many to risks of death, hunger, and disease. In numerous areas, abandoned properties were left behind and subsequently looted or burned, reflecting the disruption and material loss accompanying the demographic shift.

The W.W. Kimball House is a historic residence in Arlington, Massachusetts. This 2.5-story wood-frame building was constructed sometime between 1847 and 1865 and is one of two houses built by John Squire, the other being the House at 5-7 Winter Street. Squire is believed to have never inhabited the property, which he sold in 1865 to William and Nancy Kimball, who apparently rented the house out. The structure preserves Greek Revival detailing, including a columned porch that extends along two sides of the facade. A period carriage house remains on the property.

VoiceOver originated on Apple Macintosh computers running OS X and was subsequently added to the iPod Shuffle following its success on that device. On the iPod Shuffle, VoiceOver reads aloud the titles of tracks to assist users in navigating and controlling playback. A 2010 revision of the Shuffle expanded VoiceOver to include spoken playlist information. Unlike the OS X version, which is marketed as an accessibility feature for those with disabilities, the iPod Shuffle implementation is designed for universal use, irrespective of disability status.

VoiceOver, Apple’s screen-reading technology, received a significant update with the release of Mac OS X 10.5 when Apple introduced the Alex voice. Alex provides higher-quality, more human-sounding speech compared with earlier voices, which were built on Apple’s Speech Manager technology that originated in the early 1990s. A notable characteristic of Alex is its natural breathing, a feature that sets it apart from other Apple voices.

The Government of Malta forms the executive arm of the Republic of Malta and consists of the Cabinet and the Parliamentary Secretaries. The Prime Minister is appointed by the President of Malta in accordance with the prevailing parliamentary situation. Upon appointment, the Prime Minister designates the allocation of government departments to Permanent Secretaries. The President then appoints the remaining members of the cabinet with the Prime Minister's assent. In Maltese, the government is known as Gvern ta' Malta.

Null set is a subset of a measure space that has measure zero. It embodies the idea of null invariance under translations: if a set A has measure zero, then every translate A + x likewise has measure zero, illustrating the stability of zero-measure sets under the action of the ambient group. This notion is closely connected to the complete invariance demonstrated by Haar measure on locally compact groups, which is inherently translation-invariant and complete, ensuring that all subsets of null sets are measurable and themselves have measure zero.

In measure theory, a measure is deemed complete if every subset of a set of measure zero is measurable. For measures that are not complete, completion can be achieved by declaring all subsets of null sets to have measure zero, thereby producing a complete measure. The Lebesgue measure exemplifies a complete measure. In certain constructions, however, Lebesgue measure is defined as the completion of a non-complete Borel measure.

The Italian campaign of World War II unfolded after the Allied invasion of Sicily in July 1943, a turning point that precipitated the collapse of the Fascist regime and the deposition and arrest of Benito Mussolini by order of King Victor Emmanuel III on 25 July 1943. A new Italian government then signed an armistice with the Allies on 8 September 1943, but German forces soon occupied northern and central Italy, committing atrocities against civilians and anti-German units while the Italian resistance movement began to organize. Mussolini was later rescued by German paratroopers and established the Italian Social Republic, a German puppet state in the occupied territories. The Allies recognized Italy as a co-belligerent in the war against Germany on 13 October 1943. The Italian Co-Belligerent Army and Italian partisans fought alongside Allied forces against German troops and the RSI, effectively marking a civil conflict within Italy. In 1944, central Italy, including Rome, was liberated after Axis defeats at Cassino and Anzio, and northern Italy followed with the final spring offensive and a sweeping partisan uprising on 25 April 1945. Mussolini was captured by the resistance and executed by firing squad, and the campaign concluded with Army Group C’s unconditional surrender to the Allies on 2 May 1945, a week before Germany’s overall surrender. Both sides committed war crimes, and San Marino and Vatican City—though surrounded by Italian territory—suffered damage during the fighting.

During World War II, Britain, under Winston Churchill, advocated a maritime, peripheral approach characterized by blockade, coalition warfare, and a succession of limited operations designed to wear down the Axis powers gradually. In contrast, the United States pressed for a direct assault on the main German field army in northwestern Europe, a plan that depended on the successful maintenance of supply lines and thus on achieving victory in the Battle of the Atlantic. The Italian campaign arose within this strategic debate as a Mediterranean venue intended to tie down German forces and divert resources, while aligning with American aims for a Western Front once Allied sea power had been firmly established.

A stumping is a dismissal attributed to the wicket-keeper. It occurs when the ball has passed the stumps into the keeper’s hands and the batsman is out of his crease; the keeper completes the dismissal by removing the bail(s) from the stumps. The batsman is declared out if he remains outside the crease when the bails are dislodged.

Until 2017, substitutes were not permitted to act as the wicket-keeper. The 2017 edition of the Laws of Cricket abolished this restriction, enabling a substitute fielder to stand as wicket-keeper when required.

The United States has been the most active external participant in upgrading Azerbaijan’s Air Force airfields. Under the Azerbaijan-NATO Individual Partnership Action Plan, Gala airfield and Nasosnaya Air Base near the Haji Zeynalabidin settlement were modernised with American assistance, including the installation of specialized equipment to enhance flight security and the provision of new facilities for launch command points, engineering control systems, and engineering air force service operations. Negotiations are under way to modernise Kurdamir airfield. In addition, Dollyar Air Base has received an advanced Flight Control System installed with U.S. support.

In 2023, Azerbaijan signed a contract to upgrade the Su-25 fleet operated by its air force. The program aims to integrate Turkish-guided munitions and weapon systems into the Su-25 aircraft, and to incorporate Turkish avionics into the aircraft’s systems, enhancing interoperability and overall capability.

In the study of Hindu units of time, verse 1.71 has been interpreted in different ways by traditional commentators and modern scholars. Bühler’s translation, which is also endorsed by Jones, renders 1.71 as twelve thousand years within a four-aged period, a reading grounded in Kulluka Bhatta’s commentary. By contrast, Medhatithi interprets the verse as twelve thousand four-aged periods within an age of the gods. This interpretation is rejected by Kulluka Bhatta and by Olivelle, who argue that 1.79 mentions twelve thousand without a qualifier such as etat (this), thereby indicating that the measurement should be read as years rather than as four-aged periods.

Hindu cosmology presents time as a catur-yuga, or mahā-yuga, a fourfold cycle comprising Krita (Satya) yuga, Treta yuga, Dvāpara-yuga, and Kali yuga. Across a catur-yuga, the dharmic practices and the lengths of the successive yugas diminish by a quarter, producing a 4:3:2:1 ratio with Satya yuga being the most virtuous and Kali yuga the least; in moral terms, Satya begins at full strength and Kali ends at zero. After Kali yuga, the cycle recommences with Satya yuga in the next iteration, making a complete catur-yuga the mahā-yuga. Each yuga is divided into a main period and two yuga-sandhis (dawn and dusk), with each sandhi lasting 10% of the main period. The durations are measured in divine years, where one divine year equals 360 solar years; consequently a catur-yuga totals 12,000 divine years, or about 4.32 million solar years, with Krita-yuga lasting 1,728,000 solar years, Treta-yuga 1,296,000, Dvāpara-yuga 864,000, and Kali-yuga 432,000.

In 2015, the State Council promoted the Internet Plus initiative as a five-year program aimed at integrating traditional manufacturing and service sectors with digital technologies such as big data, cloud computing, and the Internet of Things, as part of advancing electronic commerce. The initiative receives policy support from the government to facilitate this digital transformation, with particular emphasis on expanding cross-border e-commerce and rural e-commerce to broaden online trade and bolster the digital economy.

Security is a major concern for electronic commerce worldwide, affecting markets in both advanced and developing economies. E-commerce security refers to the protection of online platforms and their users from unauthorized access, use, modification, or destruction of information and services. A range of threats challenge these systems, including malicious software, adware and spyware, phishing schemes, hacking incidents, and acts of cyber vandalism. To mitigate these risks, organizations employ a variety of defensive tools such as firewalls, cryptographic encryption, digital certificates, and strong password protocols.

Dichong station (低涌站; Cantonese Yale: Dāichūng Jaahm) is an elevated station on Guangzhou Metro Line 4. The station opened to the public on 30 December 2006. It is situated at the intersection of Nande Road and Qianqing Road in Shiqi Town, Panyu District.

Great Books are integrated into university curricula as part of efforts to engage students with canonical literary and philosophical works. Notable implementations include The Reading List at St. John's College, Rutgers University, and Dharma Realm Buddhist University. Studying these classic texts acquaints students with some of the most revered authors and intellectual traditions throughout history. The aim of such programs is to furnish students and emerging scholars with abundant resources for scholarly inquiry and lifelong study.

Great Books programs are curricular offerings that foreground canonical Western texts as central to undergraduate study. In the United States, several renowned core curricula emphasize these works, including Columbia University's Core Curriculum, the University of Chicago's Common Core, and Boston College's Core Curriculum, which are regarded as leading Classics programs with broad participation from students. Other institutions incorporate the Great Books approach in specific honors or first-year sequences, such as Fordham University's Honors Program at Rose Hill, where the Great Books curriculum is integrated into the first four semesters. Loyola University Chicago's Honors Program similarly blends a Great Books sequence with elective offerings on topics outside traditional Western thought, pursued over a four-year span. Across the United States, Canada, and Europe, more than 100 institutions maintain some version of a Great Books program as an option for students.

St. Mary's Cathedral, Yangon stands within a broader tradition of Catholic ecclesiastical architecture shaped by European training and transnational collaboration. Notably, Father Janzen studied at the École Polytechnique under the Dutch architect Pierre Cuypers, a designer of numerous Catholic churches in the Netherlands who also conceived the Rijksmuseum in Amsterdam. Cuypers' architectural lineage continued through his son, Joseph Cuypers, who was likewise an architect, and who collaborated with Janzen on the Rijksmuseum project, illustrating the cross-border networks that influenced major religious and cultural monuments of the era.

A land parcel of more than fifteen acres located to the east of St. Paul’s High School was identified as a suitable site for the cathedral project. The Bishop then filed an application with the Government of Burma seeking permission to sell the existing cathedral site as a freehold. It was planned that the proceeds from the sale would be used exclusively to finance the construction of the new cathedral.

At that stage of the Battle of Uman, the situation had become critical as the encirclement of the 6th and 12th Armies was completed. This development posed a direct threat to the integrity of their joint combat order, risking the disintegration of the combined formations. The forces had no reserves, and supplies were severely strained, with ammunition exhausted and fuel running out.

On 2 August, the German 1st Mountain Division advanced to the Sinyuha River and linked up with the 9th Panzer Division of the XIV Motorized Corps, thereby strengthening the encirclement against Soviet forces. Elements from the XXXXVIII and XIV Corps repelled the Ponedelin Group’s attempts to break out toward the east and northeast, preventing a successful collapse of the ring. The encirclement perimeter was completed, though it remained comparatively tenuous at that stage. The encirclement received a further reinforcement the following day when the German 16th Panzer Division met the Hungarian Mobile Corps at Pervomaysk, augmenting the encirclement’s manning and coordination.

Snow Mountain Wilderness is a federally designated wilderness area covering 60,076 acres (243.12 km2). It is located about 65 miles (105 km) north of Santa Rosa, California, and lies within the Mendocino National Forest. The designation was created by the California Wilderness Act of 1984, which established 23 new wilderness areas, including Snow Mountain. The wilderness sits within the North Coast Range of mountains.

On October 17, 2006, the Northern California Coastal Wild Heritage Wilderness Act was signed into law (Public Law No. 109-362), adding 23,706 acres (95.93 square kilometers) to the Snow Mountain Wilderness. In July 2015, that area became part of the Berryessa Snow Mountain National Monument.

The 2025 Adelaide International is a professional tennis tournament that is part of both the 2025 ATP Tour and the 2025 WTA Tour, offering an ATP Tour 250 event alongside a WTA Tour 500 event. The competition is staged on outdoor hard courts at the Memorial Drive Tennis Centre in Adelaide, Australia. It is scheduled to be held from 6 to 11 January 2025.

In the climactic confrontation, Finch unexpectedly confronts V and a scuffle follows, during which Finch shoots V while V wounds Finch with a knife. V then asserts that an idea cannot be destroyed, implying that he is bulletproof, and is mortally wounded as he retreats to the Shadow Gallery, where he dies in Evey's arms. After these events, Evey weighs unmasking V but ultimately recognizes him as a symbol rather than an individual and decides not to reveal his identity; she subsequently adopts V's persona by donning one of his spare costumes and masks. Finch, observing a blood trail, concludes that V has been fatally wounded. In a parallel development, Creedy pressures Susan to appear in public; during a parade, Susan stops to shake hands with Rose and then shoots Creedy in the head. With Rose under detention, Creedy seizes emergency leadership, and Finch emerges from the subway to announce V's death.

In the narrative, Evey Hammond is confronted by an interrogator who offers her a choice between collaboration or death, and she rejects the offer. Although she anticipates execution, she is informed that she is to be released rather than killed. It later emerges that her imprisonment was an elaborate ruse devised by V to subject her to an ordeal resembling his own at Larkhill. The Valerie letter is shown to be authentic: Valerie, a detainee at Larkhill, died in the adjacent cell, a fact that underscores the regime’s brutality. Amid these revelations, Evey forgives V for the events she endured. V then reveals that he infiltrated the government's Fate computer and used it to manipulate Adam Susan through psychological mind games. This manipulation drives Susan into increasing madness, culminating in a fixation on the Fate computer itself.

Following the Vue Mai incident, debate in the United States over Hmong repatriation to the Lao People's Democratic Republic intensified, drawing opposition from conservative groups and some human rights advocates. Although officials denied plans for forcible returns, thousands of Hmong chose not to return to Laos. In 1996, as Thai refugee camps approached closure, the United States agreed to resettle Hmong refugees who had passed screening. Approximately 5,000 unregistered Hmong sought asylum at Wat Tham Krabok in central Thailand, where more than 10,000 Hmong refugees had already been living. Thai authorities sought their repatriation, while Lao authorities refused to accept them, accusing them of involvement in drug trafficking and questioning their Lao origin. Following threats of forcible removal by Thailand, the United States agreed in 2003 to accept about 15,000 of the refugees. Meanwhile, several thousand Hmong, fearing forced repatriation, fled the camp to reside elsewhere in Thailand; a substantial Hmong population had lived in Thailand since the 19th century.

Within the Lao People's Democratic Republic, the population is organized by elevation into three broad zones—lowlands, midlands, and upper highlands—each associated with distinct ethnic groupings. The majority, accounting for more than half the population, are ethnic Lao, who form the principal inhabitants of the lowland areas. The Lao belong to the Tai linguistic family and are believed to have migrated southward from the region of present-day southern China during the first millennium CE. Around ten percent belong to other lowland communities; together with the Lao, these groups constitute the Lao Loum, or lowland people.

The Staircase (French miniseries) received generally positive reviews from critics and went on to win two major awards in 2005: the Peabody Award for excellence and an IDA Award in the Limited Series category.

During April 2012, Jean-Xavier de Lestrade announced a two-hour follow-up feature for Canal+ to accompany The Staircase, focusing on Michael Peterson's release from custody pending a retrial. The film, titled Last Chance, premiered at the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam in November 2012. It subsequently aired on Canal+ on January 30, 2013, and on BBC Four's Storyville on February 4, 2013. A shorter alternative cut was later presented by the Sundance Channel, which framed Last Chance as two new episodes of the original miniseries; these airings occurred on March 4 and March 11, 2013.

At the 1927 conference, call sign prefixes were allocated predominantly to European colonial powers rather than to Oceanian states. Among the Oceanic entities referenced, the sole modern polity mentioned was the Anglo-French condominium of the New Hebrides, which existed from 1906 until it gained independence as Vanuatu in 1980. For that territory, the designated call sign range was YHA to YHZ.

Amateur radio prefixes are organized by the International Telecommunication Union into three regions. Oceania's countries and territories are located in ITU Region 3. The region also encompasses CQ zones 27, 28, 31, 32, and 12, which designate the geographic areas used for station location, contesting, and QSL routing.

Review aggregators exert an influence on the economic dynamics surrounding products that are subject to evaluation, affecting incentives for creators and manufacturers. The effect is particularly noticeable in high-cost sectors, including electronic games. Some companies adjust royalty payment structures and employee incentive schemes in response to aggregated review scores. Financial markets have observed that stock prices can align with review ratings, reflecting expectations of sales performance. Across academic and industry literature, there is a widely acknowledged link between aggregated scores and sales, indicating a strong correlation between the two.

Review aggregators are tools used by manufacturers to gauge the reception of their own products, reflecting the influence that reviews can exert on consumer perception and market performance. To support corporate assessment, business-facing product review aggregators collate and analyze feedback from multiple sources. Reuters notes that in the film industry, major studios monitor aggregators, but they do not always view them as highly influential in decision making. An example of a historical service in this area is Movie Review Intelligence, a platform that collected and analyzed movie reviews to provide aggregated insights.

Odense Municipality is centered on the city of Odense, which serves as the municipality's main town and seat of the municipal council. The administration employs around 17,000 people, including those in the social sector. The municipal budget amounted to 6,881 million Danish kroner in 2006. The municipality operates 37 schools, while the city of Odense contains 13 private schools.

Odense Municipality maintains extensive road links to every part of the island of Funen. The E20 motorway runs across Funen and passes through Odense, connecting the island to Zealand in the east via the Great Belt Bridge and to the Danish mainland (Jutland) in the west via the Little Belt Bridge. A motorway built between 2006 and 2009 links Odense with Svendborg, the island’s second-largest city. Svendborg is served by the Svendborgbanen railway line, and Odense stands as a major stop on Denmark’s national railway network.

Reed Business Information, through a corporate subsidiary, was involved in the mercury contamination of the Wabigoon River in Ontario, Canada, from 1962 to 1970. The incident has been described as one of the worst cases of environmental poisoning in Canadian history. In 1980, Reed sold the Dryden Mill to Great Lakes Forest Products. As of 2017, Grassy Narrows First Nation Chief Simon Fobister stated that the river remained highly contaminated.

In July 2009, Reed Elsevier announced plans to divest most of its North American trade publications, with Publishers Weekly, Broadcasting & Cable, and Multichannel News identified for sale, while stating that Variety would be retained. Video Business, a sister publication to Variety, was subsequently closed in January 2010.

Predation on American eels is not extensively documented in the published literature. Early life stages such as elvers and small yellow eels are preyed upon by largemouth bass and striped bass, though these predators do not rely on them as major dietary components. It is likely that leptocephali, glass eels, elvers, and small yellow eels are consumed by a variety of predatory fishes. Cannibalism occurs among eels, with larger individuals preying on incoming glass eels. Eels also fall prey to other eels as well as to avian and other fish-eating birds such as bald eagles and gulls. In addition, adult rainbow snakes feed exclusively on American eels, a specialization that has given the snakes the common name eel moccasin.

The American eel (Anguilla rostrata) was first described in 1817 by Lesueur. The genus name Anguilla is Latin for eel, while the specific epithet rostrata derives from Latin rostratus, meaning beaked or curved, or long-nosed. In French, the species is known as Anguille d'Amérique, and in Spanish as Anguila americana.

The Serpentine Galleries comprise two contemporary art venues, the Serpentine Gallery and the Serpentine Sackler Gallery, located in London's Hyde Park within Kensington Gardens. The two sites are a short five-minute walk apart and are linked by a pedestrian bridge that spans the Serpentine Lake, from which the institutions take their name. Their exhibitions, architecture, education initiatives, and public programmes attract roughly 1.2 million visitors annually, and admission to both galleries is free. The organization is led by Chief Executive Officer Bettina Korek and Artistic Director Hans Ulrich Obrist.

Serpentine Gallery, located in Kensington Gardens in London, comprises two linked sites within the Serpentine complex. In 2013 the northern component opened to the public as the Serpentine Sackler Gallery, later renamed Serpentine North in 2021. The Magazine, a Grade II* listed former gunpowder store dating from 1805, was given a new extension designed by Zaha Hadid Architects, creating about 900 square metres (9,700 square feet) of gallery space alongside a restaurant, shop and social space. The Magazine is situated a five-minute walk from Serpentine South across the Serpentine Bridge, and its facilities include The Magazine Restaurant, which adjoins the gallery space.

During the era of Socialist Yugoslavia, its national youth sides achieved notable success on the international stage. The under-20 team qualified for two FIFA World Youth Championships, including triumph at the 1987 tournament in Chile. The under-21 team qualified for four UEFA European Under-21 Championships, capturing the inaugural edition in 1978 and finishing as runners-up in 1990.

During the final years of socialist Yugoslavia, Red Star Belgrade achieved the nation’s most prestigious club-level European success by defeating Olympique de Marseille in the 1990–91 European Cup final on 29 May 1991. Later that year, the club further distinguished itself by capturing the Intercontinental Cup with a 3–0 victory over Colo-Colo, thereby being recognized as world club champions.

Within the music video for Money in the Bank, the second portion shifts to a segment presenting the song Top Down, which appears on Swizz Beatz's album One Man Band Man. The accompanying video for Top Down features cameo appearances by Busta Rhymes and Eve.

Miss Universe Australia 2018 was the fourteenth edition of the national pageant. The competition took place on 28 June 2018 at the Sofitel Melbourne on Collins in Melbourne, Victoria. Francesca Hung, representing New South Wales, was crowned Miss Universe Australia 2018 by Olivia Rogers of South Australia.

Barbie Riding Club reached the number-one position in PC Data's US computer game sales rankings during its opening week, and it debuted at number two on PC Data's US monthly charts for November 1998, a position it maintained into December 1998. According to PC Data, the title was the United States' 15th-best-selling computer game of 1998. Additionally, it was named a finalist for "PC Children's Entertainment Title of the Year" at the 2nd Annual Interactive Achievement Awards, presented by the Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences.

Barbie Riding Club is an equestrian fantasy video game that centers on the bond between a girl and her horse, with a core objective of locating a mysterious horse. The gameplay combines light adventurous elements, puzzle solving, and timed races, presented from a first-person perspective in which the screen subtly bobs to simulate riding. The player can dismount to explore short stretches on foot, while progression unfolds along predetermined trails that include occasional obstacle jumps such as fallen logs. Movement of the horse is largely automated, though the game offers a variety of activities and settings to maintain engagement. Navigation is designed to be intuitive, supported by on-screen menu icons and verbal prompts to assist players. Ambient audio, including birdsong and hoofbeats, enhances the overall atmosphere of the experience.

As of 2019, downloading on SSRN typically requires user registration and/or solving a ReCAPTCHA, a barrier that has led some observers to view the site as not a fully open access repository. This stance contrasts with open archives such as most institutional repositories, which generally provide unrestricted access to materials. The platform allows publishers and academic institutions to upload papers, and these entities may impose fees for readers to download the documents.

In May 2016, Elsevier completed the purchase of the Social Science Research Network (SSRN) from Social Science Electronic Publishing Inc. On 17 May 2016, SSRN’s founder and chairman, Michael C. Jensen, addressed the SSRN community in a letter that referenced a post by SSRN’s chief executive officer, Gregg Gordon, on Elsevier Connect. The letter described anticipated benefits as a result of the acquisition, including a broader global network and enhanced capabilities for uploading and downloading papers, along with increased data, more resources, and new management tools. Jensen also acknowledged potential conflicts over the alignment of interests between former competitors, but he regarded these challenges as surmountable.

Scientific realism is a view in the philosophy of science that seeks to explain the notable success of scientific theories by maintaining that they track not only observable phenomena but also unobservable aspects of the world. The central issue concerns the ontological status of entities that are not directly accessible to sense perception but are posited by scientific theories. Realists argue that statements about such unobservables can be true or approximately true and that these unobservables hold a status similar to that of observable entities. This position contrasts with instrumentalism, which treats theories as merely predictive tools for observable outcomes without committing to the real existence of unobserved entities.

Scientific realism is typically presented as consisting of three core commitments. The first two commitments together imply that an idealized theory makes definite claims about entities that exist independently of our theories or observations. The third commitment provides justification for believing that a substantial subset of those claims is true. Taken together, these commitments articulate a view in which science aims to describe a mind-independent reality and where the success of science warrants belief in a significant portion of its ontological claims.

ISO 31-3 was a standard in the ISO 31 family that defined the names and symbols for quantities and units used in mechanics. It was published on 27 August 1992 and withdrawn on 17 March 2006, and it was superseded by ISO 80000-4.

La Aventura de Scooby-Doo is a theme park attraction at Six Flags St. Louis. Unlike other installations, this version employs a water ride system rather than a conventional track-based ride. The experience centers on a voyage through a swamp environment, designed to evoke marshland exploration. Throughout the route, a range of Scooby-Doo monsters appear, while the Mystery Inc. gang emerges from trees and shrubs as part of the scenes, adding interactive elements to the narrative.

During the 2014 season at Six Flags St. Louis, Scooby-Doo Ghostblasters: The Mystery of the Scary Swamp was closed permanently on September 14, 2014 to accommodate future improvements, with the St. Louis installation slated to be replaced by Justice League: Battle for Metropolis. In late 2017, Six Flags Fiesta Texas announced that its Scooby-Doo Ghostblasters installation would close permanently on January 7, 2018, and Pirates of the Deep Sea opened as Fiesta Texas’ replacement on January 12, 2019.

ISO 12006-3:2007, officially titled Building construction - Organization of information about construction works - Part 3: Framework for object-oriented information, constitutes the third installment in the ISO 12006 series. The standard provides a framework for organizing object-oriented information within building construction projects. It is commonly known as the BuildingSMART Data Dictionary (BSDD) and is also referred to as the International Framework for Dictionaries (IFD) Library.

Thulium is utilized in solid-state laser systems, notably in configurations that combine holmium, chromium, and thulium doping within a yttrium aluminum garnet host. The Ho:Cr:Tm:YAG arrangement, a triple-doped crystal, serves as a highly efficient active laser medium and emits light at approximately 2080 nanometers in the infrared. By contrast, lasers based on a single-element Tm:YAG medium produce radiation near 2010 nanometers. The thulium-based emission wavelengths are especially well suited to superficial tissue ablation with shallow coagulation depths, both in air and in water, which makes these lasers attractive for laser-assisted surgery. In addition to medical applications, thulium lasers find use in meteorology for atmospheric sensing and in military contexts. Together, these attributes underlie the appeal of thulium-based laser systems for precise, minimally invasive procedures and reliable infrared laser sources.

Thulium, a rare earth element, is principally recovered from monazite-bearing sands and, more recently, from ion-adsorption clays in southern China. Historically, thulium occurs at about 0.007 percent in monazite ores mined from river sands and is separated through ion-exchange processes. Recent advances in ion-exchange and solvent-extraction techniques have facilitated easier separation of the rare earths and substantially lowered production costs for thulium. Today, the dominant sources are the ion-adsorption clays of southern China, where yttrium accounts for roughly two-thirds of the rare-earth content while thulium comprises about 0.5 percent, a level roughly tied with lutetium in rarity.

In January 1927, Tetsurō Watsuji decided to undertake a three-year study trip to Germany to examine the history of moral thought. He departed on 17 February 1927 and arrived in Berlin in early April of that year. During the early summer of 1927 he read Martin Heidegger’s Being and Time, which had just been published, before proceeding to Paris, though the exact date of that move is not recorded. In early December 1927 he left Paris and arrived in Genoa on 12 December.
Tetsurō Watsuji's study, Studies on the History of Japanese Art—Kabuki and Jōruri (日本芸術史研究——歌舞伎と操り浄瑠璃), was issued by Iwanami Shoten in 1955 and later reprinted in CW16:1-716.

The World Alliance of International Financial Centers was established to strengthen collaboration among financial centers and to facilitate dialogue with public authorities on financial technologies and sustainable development. Arnaud de Bresson, the Executive Director of Paris Europlace, was elected as the Alliance’s first president, with Jochen Biedermann serving as managing director and Frederic de Laminne as treasurer. In January 2021, Jennifer Reynolds, president and chief executive of Toronto Finance International, was elected the first chairwoman of the Alliance. The body began with eleven member centers and has since expanded to twenty, adding centers from Japan, Hong Kong, Mauritius, Qatar, and the United Kingdom.

In 2016, representatives from Paris, Frankfurt and Moscow proposed establishing a non-profit association to facilitate cooperation among major financial centers and to promote best practices and dialogue with international public authorities. The World Alliance of International Financial Centers was subsequently founded in 2018, with its inception in Paris, and was officially registered on 1 October 2018 in Brussels. At its launch, eleven financial centers from Germany, France, Belgium, Russia, Canada and the United Arab Emirates joined the association as members.

Hanking Center is a skyscraper located in Shenzhen, Guangdong, China. The building rises to a height of 358.9 metres (1,177.5 feet). Construction began in 2013 and was completed in 2018, adding a prominent feature to the city's skyline.

Sci Fi (Balkans TV channel) is a regional science fiction broadcaster whose programming schedule mirrors the Polish version of Syfy. The channel provides Serbian-language subtitles for its broadcasts. The feed is hubbed from Warsaw, and it retains the former Sci-Fi branding rather than adopting the contemporary Syfy mark. The branding choice has been attributed to phonetic similarities between the name Syfy and the Polish plural form of syphilis, a consideration that influenced branding decisions in the region.

Sci Fi (Balkans TV channel) was launched on October 1, 2009, in Serbia, Slovenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia and Montenegro. The network focused on science fiction, fantasy, and horror programming, including both television series and films, and was distributed via cable networks throughout the region. On October 14, 2010, the channel adopted the Sci Fi Universal branding, changing from Sci Fi Channel to Sci Fi Universal.

Within the Paraguayan Air Arm, each corps operates its own weapons school under the direction of its commanding authority, ensuring corps-specific training and doctrine. A dedicated logistical command oversees materiel management, mobilization readiness, health care, and related support functions essential to sustaining operations. In the area of education and professional development, the Army Institute of Education administers three schools for commissioned and noncommissioned officers, a military academy, and CIMEFOR, a center for pre-military studies that trains reserve officers.

The Paraguayan Air Arm is the air force component of Paraguay's armed forces and is the most recently established and smallest service, with approximately 1,100 personnel as of 2012. It is organized as an Air Brigade comprising seven air groups and a battalion-sized brigade of paratroopers. Nearly all of its operating units are based at or near Silvio Pettirossi International Airport (SGAS) in Asunción.

David da Silva joined Persebaya Surabaya in 2018 ahead of the Indonesia President's Cup and Liga 1 campaigns. He made his preseason debut for the club on 28 January 2018 in a match against Madura United. He subsequently featured in Liga 1 for the first time on 30 March 2018 as a substitute against Persela Lamongan, scoring his first Persebaya goal in the 70th minute at Surajaya Stadium. On 13 April 2018 he registered his first hat-trick for Persebaya in a 4–1 victory over TIRA-Persikabo at Sultan Agung Stadium. He added a brace on 5 August 2018 in a 3–1 win over Persela Lamongan. On 22 September 2018 he completed a second hat-trick in a 4–1 win away to Mitra Kukar, and later, on 18 November 2018, he produced a third hat-trick of the season in a 5–2 away victory over Bali United.

David da Silva signed a one-year contract with Pohang Steelers of the K League 1 on 9 January 2019. He made his league debut for the club on 3 March 2019, being included in the starting lineup against FC Seoul at the Seoul World Cup Stadium. A week later, on 10 March 2019, he scored his first league goal for Pohang in a 1–2 defeat to Gimcheon Sangmu at the Pohang Steel Yard.

In the 1970s, the Kuomintang, led by Premier Chiang Ching-kuo, conducted public diplomacy in the United States to mobilize political opinion against the People’s Republic of China. The effort relied on grassroots initiatives, including mass demonstrations and petition campaigns designed to influence American policymakers. It worked in collaboration with the John Birch Society to expand its reach within conservative circles. A prominent petition-writing drive encouraged Americans to contact their local officials and urge the severing of formal ties with Communist China, reflecting the campaign’s aim to shape U.S.–China policy in favor of the KMT’s position.

Public diplomacy encompasses government-sponsored efforts aimed at communicating with foreign publics to inform and influence their views in order to secure backing for the state's strategic objectives. Although it may involve propagandistic elements, the field has evolved alongside changes in the international order over the course of the twentieth century. Practitioners deploy a diverse set of instruments and methods, ranging from direct personal engagement and media interviews to online outreach and educational or cultural exchanges.

The Iditarod Trail Sled Dog Race requires teams to observe three mandatory rest periods during the event: one continuous 24-hour rest and two eight-hour rests, scheduled at designated checkpoints along the course. At each checkpoint, mushers typically provide nourishment for their dogs, with feeding often limited to a modest snack. The physiological demands on the canine athletes are substantial, with energy expenditure averaging about 10,000 kilocalories per day for the dogs during the race.

Iditarod: Toughest Race on Earth is a 2008 American reality television miniseries that aired on the Discovery Channel. The program chronicles the 2008 Iditarod Trail Sled Dog Race and follows competitors along the course from Anchorage to Nome, Alaska.

Sixtus V, who led the papacy from 1585 to 1590, in 1586 sought to align Rome's secular legal code with religious doctrine by incorporating the Old Testament sanction of capital punishment for adultery; however, the measure failed to pass and was not enacted into law.

Pope Sixtus V broadened the reach of excommunication, extending the penalty to offenses related to contraception and abortion within Catholic teaching. The Catholic Church holds that both abortion and contraception are gravely sinful, reflecting its normative moral doctrine on these issues. At the same time, excommunication is not imposed for every mortal sin, as the discipline distinguishes which offenses carry the penalty.

The 1988 Nabisco Grand Prix was the primary men’s professional tennis circuit for that year, functioning as the sole circuit of its type in 1988. The tour encompassed the four Grand Slam championships, three events conducted under the World Championship Tennis (WCT) banner, and a series of Grand Prix tournaments that together constituted the season’s competitive schedule.

Maximilian von Weichs served as commander of Army Group B from August 1942, during the Case Blue offensive in southern Russia. In 1944 he commanded Army Group F in the Balkans, directing the German withdrawal from Greece and most of Yugoslavia. At the Nuremberg Trials he was implicated in war crimes committed in the Balkans and was slated to participate in the United States Army's Hostages Trial; however, he was removed from the proceedings on medical grounds, and never stood trial or received a judgment.

During Case Blue in 1942, General Maximilian von Weichs commanded the newly formed Army Group B. The German component consisted of the 2nd Army under Salmuth, the 4th Panzer Army under Hoth, and the 6th Army under Paulus. The army group also included non-German forces—the 2nd Hungarian Army, the 8th Italian Army, and the Third and Fourth Romanian Armies. The primary objective assigned to the 6th Army was to seize Stalingrad while maintaining roughly 800 kilometers of front.

In the United Kingdom, a substantive title refers to a title of nobility that is held in its own right by the individual who bears it. It is not shared among cadets, and it is not borne as a courtesy title by a peer's relatives; nor is it acquired through marriage.

Substantive titles refer to dynastic designations used by former royal houses whose monarchies have been abolished, a practice catalogued by the Almanach de Gotha. The head of the house typically bears a traditional dynastic title, which functions as a defining element of the family’s name. This dynastic designation may be used in place of the given name or appended after it, thereby signaling the individual’s place within the former royal lineage.

FC Alay is a professional football club from Kyrgyzstan, based in the city of Osh. The team competes in the Kyrgyz Premier League, the top division of the Kyrgyz football league system. In Kyrgyz, the club is known as Алай футбол клубу.

Data lakes are often built on cloud storage platforms such as Google Cloud Storage and Amazon S3 or on distributed file systems like the Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS). The concept has attracted increasing scholarly attention in recent years. An illustrative example is Cardiff University’s Personal DataLake, which aims to manage individuals’ large datasets by providing a single point to collect, organize, and share personal data.

In the early phase of data lake development, implementations such as Hadoop 1.0 offered limited capabilities, primarily enabling batch-oriented data processing through the MapReduce framework. Access and interaction with these systems typically required specialized expertise in Java, MapReduce, and higher-level tools built on top of the platform, including Apache Pig, Apache Spark, and Apache Hive. Additionally, these higher-level interfaces themselves were originally designed for batch processing, limiting the scope of immediate, interactive analytics in early data-lake deployments.

Beach House is an American duo widely associated with dream pop, though the band resists rigid labeling or categorization. Their breakthrough in the late 2000s helped solidify the subgenre’s popularity among millennial listeners, while critics have also described them as indie rock and shoegaze. Vocalist Victoria Legrand’s singing on the group’s self-titled output has drawn comparisons to Nico and Hope Sandoval in timbre and mood. The self-titled Beach House (2006), Devotion (2008), and Teen Dream (2010) are frequently described as indie pop and lo-fi, with Teen Dream notable for its use of live drums. On Bloom (2012) the band adopts more live percussion and a darker sonority than Teen Dream, moving away from lo-fi toward a more polished pop aesthetic. The group has stated an ambition to realize a vision akin to landmark albums such as Pet Sounds, Disintegration, and Violator, signaling an intent to fuse lush texture and mood with refined melodic craft.

During 2009, Beach House recorded a cover of Queen's "Play the Game" for the iTunes edition of Dark Was the Night, and the duo began composing their third studio album. Victoria Legrand contributed backing vocals to Grizzly Bear's "Two Weeks" and later lent vocals to Grizzly Bear's "Slow Life" for the Twilight: New Moon soundtrack. In September 2009, the band signed with Sub Pop, leaving Carpark, and announced plans to record their third studio album. In October they revealed the album title Teen Dream. The Sub Pop deal enabled a DVD edition of the album and the hiring of producer Chris Coady. Teen Dream was recorded at Dreamland Studios in Hurley, New York. On November 17, 2009, the lead single "Norway" was released as a free download on Beach House's website; the track had originally been written on a train in Norway in 2008.

Within the common-practice period, a musical phrase typically spans four measures and concludes with a cadence that can be either relatively weak or comparatively strong. The strength of the cadence is linked to the phrase’s function as antecedent or consequent, with the antecedent often producing a softer pause and the consequent delivering a firmer resolution. A period, in turn, comprises two phrases: the first functions as the antecedent and the second as the consequent, together forming a complete musical idea with a conclusive cadence.

In music theory, a phrase-group refers to a sequence of three or more phrases that are linked together but do not form the two-part cadence typically associated with a musical period. Alternatively, a phrase-group may consist of two adjacent phrases in which the first repeats the second or where an antecedent–consequent relationship is not established.

In 1995 Fred Rouhling proposed Akira as the world's first 9b (5.15b) route, asserting that it surpassed the then-top grade of 9a (5.14d) held by Action Directe. The claim provoked significant controversy and criticism within parts of the climbing community, as no other climber had managed to repeat the route. In 2020 Sébastien Bouin completed the first repeat of Akira and assigned it a 9a (5.14d) grade. Bouin's grade aligned with Rouhling's broader body of work, contributing to the acceptance of Rouhling's claim of the First Free Ascent (FFA) of Akira.

The history of first ascents in mountaineering follows a progression from the Golden Age of alpinism, during which many of the principal Alpine peaks were climbed for the first time, frequently employing aid climbing techniques. In the 1930s, attention moved toward the conquest of the Alps’ most formidable north faces, with the Eiger standing out as a symbol of this shift. The 1950s saw the first ascents of most of the fourteen eight-thousanders, with Everest noted as a particularly significant achievement within the period. By the 1980s, the focus broadened further to include prominent rock spires beyond the Alps, such as the Trango Towers in the Karakoram and the Torres del Paine in Patagonia.

The Color Book refers to a class of published collections of national WWI diplomatic documents, with the British Blue Book representing the second such compilation to appear. It emerged mere days after the German White Book and comprises 159 items. The collection was submitted to Parliament before 6 August 1914, following Britain’s declaration of war on Germany. A later, expanded edition exists under the title Great Britain and the European Crisis, which preserves the original introductions and adds reports from early August parliamentary sessions. The expanded version retains the same 159 items and includes two additional documents from British embassies in Vienna and Berlin, added after the outbreak of war. The compilation is incomplete in places, notably omitting files on English promises of aid to France and on German concessions or proposals. It is regarded as the richest of the color books; Max Beer described it as a true treasure trove of historical insights into the great crisis, despite its gaps.

The Color Book is a postwar parliamentary report by German jurist Hermann Kantorowicz that examined the causes of World War I. It concluded that Germany bore a large share of responsibility for triggering the conflict. To support this conclusion, the White Book was cited as an illustration, with the claim that roughly 75 percent of its documents were falsified.

Apt-build is designed to facilitate software installation on APT-based systems by allowing users to specify one or more package names to be installed. The input should consist of the package names themselves, not the corresponding file names or archives (for example, libc6 rather than libc6_1.9.6-2.deb). When a package name is provided, the package manager (APT) automatically retrieves and installs the dependencies required by that package. This automatic dependency resolution has been a hallmark of APT-based distributions, reducing the risk of dependency hell and installation failures caused by missing components.

During its development, the Deity project aimed to replace the dselect user interface, but the goal ultimately did not succeed. Consequently, UI development was abandoned and the UI directories were removed from CVS after apt-get's first public release. APT's strong positive reception as both a replacement for dselect and as a capable command-line tool redirected development toward maintaining and improving the package-management system itself. Much later, independent developers built user interfaces on top of libapt-pkg.

Off-Broadway productions frequently transfer to Broadway, with notable examples including Hair, Godspell, Little Shop of Horrors, Sunday in the Park with George, Rent, Grey Gardens, Urinetown, Avenue Q, The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee, Rock of Ages, In the Heights, Spring Awakening, Next to Normal, Hedwig and the Angry Inch, Fun Home, Hamilton, Dear Evan Hansen, Hadestown, and Kimberly Akimbo. Grease and A Chorus Line, two Broadway hits that originated off-Broadway, helped spur a trend toward premiering shows off-Broadway. Plays that moved from off-Broadway to Broadway include Doubt, I Am My Own Wife, Bridge & Tunnel, The Normal Heart, Oh, Mary!, and Coastal Disturbances. Productions with long off-Broadway runs but never moved to Broadway include Stomp, Blue Man Group, Altar Boyz, Perfect Crime, Forbidden Broadway, Nunsense, Naked Boys Singing, Bat Boy: The Musical, and I Love You, You're Perfect, Now Change. The Fantasticks is the longest-running musical in theatre history, with an off-Broadway run from 1960 to 2002 (42 years) and a subsequent off-Broadway revival from 2006 to 2017.

Off-Broadway emerged in the 1950s as a response to Broadway's commercialism, offering cheaper venues and serving as a fertile training ground for many artists who would later work on Broadway. An early milestone occurred when the Circle in the Square Theatre presented Tennessee Williams's Summer and Smoke in 1952. Historians Ken Bloom and Frank Vlastnik describe Off-Broadway as a new outlet for poets, playwrights, actors, songwriters, and designers. The 1954 revival of The Threepenny Opera is often cited as the first major Off-Broadway musical, illustrating that such productions could achieve financial success. Critics such as John Gassner contended that Broadway is just as eclectic—and as unconstrained—as Off-Broadway. Theatre Row, located on West 42nd Street between Ninth and Tenth Avenues, concentrates off-Broadway and off-off-Broadway theatres, a district that was developed in the mid-1970s and modernized in 2002.

The modern swarmandal resembles the European psaltery in form. In present-day India, autoharps are employed as an equivalent instrument, with the chord-button mechanism removed. Modern swarmandals are trapezoidal, approximately 51 cm (20 in) long and 28 cm (11 in) wide. They may carry up to forty strings, whereas nineteenth-century examples typically had about twenty-one. The strings are anchored on a nail at the right edge and, on the left, are wound around tuning pegs tightened with a special key. In the medieval period, tuning pegs were made of wood rather than metal. A sharp ridge, measuring 1/2 inch (13 mm), runs along both sides and serves as a bridge near the nails. The swarmandal bears similarities to autoharp or zither in several respects.

The swarmandal may be the same instrument as the 13th-century mattakokilā, a name associated with the nickname “the intoxicated cuckoo.” In Mughal-era sources, the Ā'īn-i-akbarī equates the swarmandal with the qanun. By the 19th century, a writer remarked that few notable performances on the instrument existed, attributing this to its difficulty to play and the high cost of purchase.

In March 2012, Google consolidated its various privacy policies into a single, unified policy. The working group comprising all European Union data protection authorities concluded that the merged policy did not comply with the EU legal framework. In response, several countries opened investigations to determine whether the policy breached their respective privacy rules.

Scroogle processed roughly 350,000 search queries daily prior to its shutdown, and it ranked among the top 4,000 websites globally. At the national level, it held a position within the top 2,500 sites in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia, and various other countries.

HMS Ormonde was a 24-class sloop of the Royal Navy built by the Blyth Shipbuilding and Dry Dock Company. She was launched on 8 June 1918 and was converted into a survey vessel in March 1924. After more than a decade of service, she was sold on 6 August 1937 for breaking up.

The 24-class sloop was constructed by Barclay Curle and launched on 11 May 1918. In September 1923 it was transferred to the Royal Naval Volunteer Reserve and renamed Irwell, and it was later renamed Eaglet in 1926.

Cenovus Energy Inc. is a Canadian integrated oil and natural gas company headquartered in Calgary, Alberta. Its corporate offices are located at Brookfield Place, following a 2019 relocation of operations from The Bow. The name is pronounced "se-nō-vus."

Cenovus Energy operates four oil sands producing projects in Alberta—Foster Creek, Christina Lake, Sunrise (jointly owned with BP Canada and operated by Cenovus), and Tucker—each employing steam-assisted gravity drainage (SAGD). In May 2017, Cenovus completed the consolidation of Foster Creek and Christina Lake as wholly owned and operated assets. The Tucker project was sold to Strathcona Resources in December 2021. In June 2022, Cenovus announced it would acquire the remaining 50 percent interest in Sunrise to achieve full ownership, with Sunrise having previously been a joint venture with BP Canada and operated by Cenovus.

Originally conducted on an invitation-only basis, the Scottish Chess Championship restricted its title to players who were eligible to represent Scotland in international competition. On occasions, the organizers extended invitations to titled players from other nationalities to participate. The invitation policy was implemented with the aim of increasing the likelihood that participants would achieve the norms required for official chess titles.

The Scottish Chess Championship is the national chess championship of Scotland, organized by Chess Scotland, the body formerly known as the Scottish Chess Association. The event has been contested since 1884. The main competition is a nine‑round tournament conducted over two weekends with an intervening week, while the first seven days host auxiliary tournaments, including grading‑limited sections and a senior championship. A Weekend Congress is then held on the second weekend as part of the championship programme.

An apostolic prefect ranks below a vicar apostolic in the hierarchy of the Catholic Church's missionary jurisdictions. His authority is more limited and he does not ordinarily possess the episcopal character, unlike a vicar apostolic who normally bears it. The prefect's duties are centered on directing the work of the mission entrusted to his charge, with powers limited to the ordinary administration of the office. Examples of his functions include the assignment of missionaries and the formulation of regulations for the sound management of the mission's affairs.

During the later centuries of the second millennium, the Holy See governed certain territories not by dioceses but through apostolic prefectures or apostolic vicariates. These arrangements were employed in regions lacking a diocesan structure with resident bishops, where local realities—such as the culture and temperament of the people or resistance from civil authorities—made a stable episcopal see doubtful. The establishment of an apostolic prefecture thus signified that the Church's institutional development in those areas remained limited. As conditions improved and after further growth, an apostolic vicariate often succeeded the prefecture as an intermediate stage before the eventual establishment of a diocese.

Field Marshal Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher was rewarded by King Frederick William III of Prussia for his victories in 1814 by being elevated to the princely title Fürst of Wahlstatt in Silesia, an honor tied to the Katzbach battlefield. He was also granted estates near Krieblowitz (now Krobielowice, Poland) in Lower Silesia and a grand mansion at 2, Pariser Platz in Berlin, a residence that would later become the United States Embassy in 1930. Following these honors, Blücher visited England, where he was received with royal honours and greeted with public enthusiasm throughout the country.

Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher, a Prussian field marshal, was made an honorary citizen of Berlin, Hamburg, and Rostock. Renowned for a fiery temperament, his soldiers dubbed him Marschall Vorwärts ("Marshal Forward") in recognition of his aggressive approach to warfare. Together with Paul von Hindenburg, he is counted among the most highly decorated Prussian-German soldiers in history, and Blücher and Hindenburg are the sole Prussian-German officers awarded the Star of the Grand Cross of the Iron Cross. A statue once stood in Blücherplatz square in Breslau, present-day Wrocław.

In late 2010, Tony Sly planned to record a forthcoming No Use for a Name studio album for a spring 2011 release, which would have marked the band's first new material since 2008's The Feel Good Record of the Year. However, the plans were delayed after Sly decided to pursue a second solo album, thereby postponing the No Use for a Name project.

Anthony James Sly (November 4, 1970 – July 31, 2012), commonly known as Tony Sly, was an American singer, songwriter, and guitarist. He was best known as the lead vocalist and guitarist for the punk rock band No Use for a Name. In his later years, Sly drew attention for his acoustic solo work, releasing two acoustic split albums with Joey Cape, the frontman of Lagwagon, as well as two solo albums.

Timbre arises from the spectral content of a sound, with the primary pitch often anchored at 440 Hz and accompanied by its harmonic series at integer multiples such as 880 Hz, 1320 Hz, and 1760 Hz, among higher overtones. Each instrument generates a distinctive blend of these frequencies, including additional harmonics that contribute to its unique sonic signature. The various frequency components propagate as sound waves that overlap and sum through the air, a phenomenon described by the principle of superposition. The relative amplitudes, or balance, of these constituent frequencies largely determine the instrument's characteristic timbre.

Timbre, often described as the tone color of a sound, is the perceptual quality that allows listeners to differentiate between voices or instruments even when the same pitch is produced. For example, when a guitar and a piano play the identical note at the same loudness, the two sounds remain distinct due to their timbres. This uniqueness persists even if the instruments are tuned to the same frequency and produce the same amplitude, because each source has a distinctive spectral content and temporal evolution that shape its overall tone color. Musicians rely on timbre to identify instruments and to convey expressive nuance, including passages where pitch and volume are identical.

Grammatical mood denotes a category of the verb that expresses the speaker’s attitude toward the action or state described, and it is distinct from grammatical tense, which situates the event in time, as well as from grammatical aspect, which concerns the temporal structure or progression of the event. In many languages, including English and most modern Indo-European languages, a single verb form can carry multiple grammatical meanings at once, reflecting overlap among mood, tense, and aspect in actual usage. For a discussion of how these categories interact, see tense–aspect–mood.

Presumptive mood is a grammatical category that marks presupposition or hypothesis about an event irrespective of the verb’s stated truth value. It also conveys speaker attitudes such as doubt, curiosity, concern, condition, indifference, and perceived inevitability. The mood is found in several languages, including Romanian, Hindi, Gujarati, and Punjabi, where it appears through dedicated verb forms or particles and interacts with surrounding mood and aspect systems to hedge assertions or signal a speculative stance.

According to Borgman, VIAF, ISNI, and ORCID are considered a set of loosely coordinated initiatives aimed at standardizing personal-name forms. All three seek to address author name disambiguation, a challenge that intensifies as bibliographic data grows. In terms of governance, VIAF is led primarily by libraries, whereas ISNI and ORCID are driven by individual authors and creators.

The Virtual International Authority File (VIAF) is an international authority file that brings together authority records through a collaborative effort of several national libraries, and it is operated by the Online Computer Library Center (OCLC).

Nick Fatool was a jazz musician active on the Dixieland revival circuit in the 1950s and 1960s. He played with Pete Fountain from 1962 to 1965 and also performed with the Dukes of Dixieland. His only session as a bandleader occurred in 1987, when he led a septet whose members included Eddie Miller, Johnny Mince, Ernie Carson, among others.

Fatool was born in Millbury, Massachusetts, United States, and began his professional career in Providence, Rhode Island. He joined Joe Haymes's band in 1937 and soon after performed with Don Beston in Dallas. In 1939 he briefly played with Bobby Hackett before joining the Benny Goodman Orchestra that year.
