He rose as a prominent drummer during the 1940s, performing with Artie Shaw (1940–41), Alvino Rey (1942–43), as well as Claude Thornhill, Les Brown, and Jan Savitt. In 1943 he relocated to Los Angeles to pursue session work, subsequently recording extensively. His credits include collaborations with Harry James, Erroll Garner (1946), Louis Armstrong (1949, 1951), Jess Stacy, Tommy Dorsey, Matty Matlock, John Scott Trotter, and Glen Gray. Fatool also began a long association with Bob Crosby, playing regularly from 1949 to 1951 and with Crosby's Bobcats into the 1970s.

Renault's entry into Formula One began in 1977 when the team planned a debut at the French Grand Prix, the ninth round of the season, but the car was not ready and the debut was postponed to the British Grand Prix. In their first qualifying session, driver Jean-Pierre Jabouille lined up 21st on a grid of 30 entrants (26 starters), 1.62 seconds behind pole position held by James Hunt of McLaren. In the British Grand Prix itself, Jabouille rose as high as 16th before a turbocharger failure ended his race on lap 17. Following the British setback, Renault skipped the German and Austrian Grands Prix to focus on improvements to the car. The team returned at the Dutch Grand Prix, where Jabouille qualified tenth; although he endured a poor start, he ran as high as sixth during the race before a suspension failure stopped proceedings on lap 40.

Prior to the 2011 season, media speculation linked Kimi Räikkönen, the 2007 World Champion, with a possible move to Renault to replace Vitaly Petrov. Räikkönen publicly rejected the claims, criticizing Renault for using his name for promotional purposes and indicating that the alleged approach would prevent him from lining up for the team.

James Hird’s farewell phase consisted of two high-profile games, with his final in Victoria played at the Melbourne Cricket Ground against Richmond and his ultimate appearance occurring at Subiaco Oval against West Coast. The occasions were notable in part because they doubled as the last matches coached by Kevin Sheedy, who had a 27-year tenure as a coach. In his final game, Hird recorded 34 disposals, one fewer than his career high. As they left the field for the last time, the crowd rose for both Hird and Sheedy in a standing ovation.

James Hird was appointed head coach of the Essendon Football Club in September 2010. In August 2013, he was suspended from coaching for twelve months after being charged by the Australian Football League with conduct prejudicial to the game in relation to the Essendon supplements controversy. He returned to the club after the 2014 season. Hird resigned from Essendon in August 2015.

Netball is a limited-contact team sport played by two teams of seven players, who aim to score by delivering the ball through a raised hoop. The ANZ Championship, the Australia–New Zealand Championship, has been regarded as the premier netball league and enjoys particular fame in Australia and New Zealand. Historically, netball was played exclusively by women, but contemporary competitions include mixed-gender formats.

In basketball, a block occurs when a defender touches the ball in flight after a shooter releases a shot and alters its trajectory. Goaltending refers to contacting the ball during its downward arc toward the rim, which is illegal. Under NBA and men's NCAA rules, it is prohibited to block a shot once the ball has touched the backboard or while any part of the ball is directly above the rim. By contrast, international rules forbid blocking the ball in the downward arc or after it has touched the backboard until the ball hits the rim. Once the ball makes contact with the rim, touching it becomes legal again, though such contact is no longer considered a block.

Tradition refers to a system of beliefs, practices, and social behaviors transmitted within a group or society that carries symbolic meaning or significance and typically traces back to the past. As a fundamental component of cultural expression and folklore, traditions encompass holidays and attire that, while socially meaningful, may be impractical, such as lawyers' wigs or military officers' spurs. The concept also extends to customary social norms and greetings. Traditions can endure for millennia, persisting and evolving in response to changing circumstances. The term derives from the Latin tradere, meaning to transmit, hand over, or entrust for safekeeping. In addition, many traditions have been deliberately created within short timeframes for political or cultural reasons, and the word is employed in a variety of ways across different academic disciplines.

Tradition denotes information transmitted through oral cultural practices rather than independent documentary evidence, and as such may lack solid verification or be susceptible to challenge. The phrase according to tradition or by tradition signals that the claim derives from customary retellings rather than established records, thereby indicating its traditional source rather than being corroborated. An illustrative case is the attribution of Homer’s birthplace to Chios by tradition, a claim that many places contest and which may never be definitively proven or disproven. Similarly, statements such as “King Arthur, according to history, a true British king,” have nonetheless spurred extensive storytelling. Regardless of their evidentiary status, traditional claims retain value as components of cultural history and literature, offering insight into collective memory and the ways communities imagine their past.

The Malaysia Songs chart is a weekly ranking of the top songs in Malaysia. It tracks a Friday-to-Thursday reporting period and is updated on Tuesday mornings in Eastern Time. The chart comprises 25 entries, with rankings determined by a blended consumption metric that combines streaming activity and sales within Malaysia during the tracking period. Data for the chart are supplied by Luminate Data, the data provider formerly known as MRC Data.

Malaysia Songs is a national music chart that ranks the most popular songs within Malaysia. The chart's inaugural number-one track was "Angel Baby" by Troye Sivan, appearing in the issue dated February 19, 2022. As of the most recent update, the current top song is "Golden," credited to Huntrix and featuring Ejae, Audrey Nuna, and Rei Ami.

The narrative surrounding the so-called conspiracy of fools is described as extending beyond Andrew Fastow to encompass a broader set of participants. Investigations and accounts have implicated Enron’s auditors, Arthur Andersen, as well as both internal and external counsel retained by the company. Senior executives Kenneth Lay and Jeffrey Skilling have been identified as implicated, and Michael Kopper—Fastow’s longtime partner in numerous deals—has also figured in the inquiries. In addition, Enron’s board of directors is implicated, suggesting that governance structures played a role alongside executive actions in the alleged misconduct.

Conspiracy of Fools documents Enron’s collapse by pointing to an unrestrained corporate culture that routinely sidelined basic business principles. A small circle of insiders manipulated the system for personal gain, focusing on the appearance of profitability rather than the generation of real earnings. Losses were concealed through accounting tricks, allowing the firm to present a healthier financial position than its underlying economics warranted. Consequently, those insiders extracted substantial profits and bonuses for themselves, while the broader organization bore the consequences of the deception.

Vishaan Chakrabarti was appointed dean of the University of California, Berkeley's College of Environmental Design (CED) in 2020. In September 2021, he announced his resignation from the deanship after approximately one year, citing health issues within his family. He is an alumnus of CED's graduate architecture program, reflecting his formal training at the school. Previously, he had served on the College's Dean's Advisory Council.

Vishaan Chakrabarti began his career at Skidmore, Owings & Merrill LP in New York, where he served as associate partner and director of urban design. In 2003, he was named director of the Manhattan Office of the New York Department of City Planning under Mayor Michael Bloomberg. In 2005, he served as president of Moynihan Station Venture at The Related Companies. In 2009, he was named Marc Holliday Professor and Director of the MS in Real Estate Development program at Columbia's GSAPP. In 2011, he became the founding director of the Center for Urban Real Estate (CURE).

Ellingtonia, Vol. Two continues the practice of replacing ensemble-specific group names with the name of Duke Ellington. Previously credited outfits included the Kentucky Club Orchestra, the Washingtonians, the Cotton Club Orchestra, and the Jungle Band, but those attributions were superseded by the designation Duke Ellington and His Orchestra.

Following Decca Records' acquisition of Brunswick and Vocalion's metal master records, Ellingtonia, Vol. 1 was released as the premiere entry in the series. The debut volume was well received by Billboard magazine. Ellingtonia, Vol. Two emphasizes Ellington's longer-length pieces.

The flag of Kyrgyzstan consists of a plain red field charged at the center with a golden sun bearing forty rays. The forty rays symbolize the forty tribes historically comprising Kyrgyz culture prior to Russian expansion during the rise of the Soviet era. Within the sun, a set of lines forms a stylized crown, or tündük, of a yurt—a motif that recurs in Kyrgyz architectural design. The red field represents peace and openness in Kyrgyzstan.

On 3 February 2009, Kyrgyz President Kurmanbek Bakiyev announced plans to close Manas Air Base, then the sole United States military facility in Central Asia. The Kyrgyz Parliament endorsed the closure on 19 February 2009 with a 78–1 vote in favor of the government-backed bill. After intensive negotiations among Kyrgyz, Russian, and American representatives, the closure decision was reversed in June 2009, allowing the United States to remain under a new contract. The revised arrangement significantly increased annual rent from $17.4 million to $60 million. The U.S. military ultimately completed its withdrawal from Manas Air Base in 2014.
Igor Ustinov, a French sculptor, designed the statuette awarded for the Prix Benois de la Danse in 1992. He is the son of the actor Peter Ustinov and is a great-nephew of Alexandre Benois.

The Prix Benois de la Danse is an annual ballet competition held in Moscow. It was established in 1991 by the International Dance Association. The event is held on or around April 29 each year. A jury, whose membership changes annually, evaluates the performances, with the panel comprising leading figures in ballet.

Within the Byzantine Rite, the divine liturgy is ordinarily celebrated on most days, though certain days are designated as aliturgical and do not include liturgical celebration, a pattern that is especially evident around Great Lent. Daily liturgy occurs only in cathedrals and larger monasteries, whereas elsewhere liturgy is celebrated on Sundays, on major feast days, and on a selection of additional days, with particular emphasis during Great Lent.

In the Byzantine Rite, baptism is understood as a transformative sacrament in which the believer’s former life and sins are forgiven, leaving a clean slate as the person is regarded as a new creation in Christ. Through the rite, the initiate is incorporated into the Body of Christ and admitted as a full member of the Orthodox Church. A distinctive feature of the service is the blessing of the water, which is employed in the baptismal act. The catechumen is fully immersed in the water three times, each immersion performed in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. This immersion signifies the death of the old self with Christ’s crucifixion and burial, followed by rebirth through his resurrection. In many cases, a new name is conferred at baptism, and this name becomes the individual’s baptismal name.

ISO 3166-2:SS comprises the subdivision codes for South Sudan, with the subdivision names presented in accordance with the ISO 3166-2 standard as published by the ISO 3166 Maintenance Agency (ISO 3166/MA). Some administrative areas, namely Pibor and Ruweng, do not have ISO 3166-2 codes and are therefore not listed. In addition, the currently disputed region of Abyei likewise lacks a corresponding code and is not included in the listing.

Changes to the ISO 3166-2:SS entry have historically been announced through newsletters published by the ISO 3166 Maintenance Agency (ISO 3166/MA). This notification mechanism dates back to the initial publication of ISO 3166-2 in 1998 and continued until the agency ceased issuing newsletters in 2013.

Following the arrival of the railway, Aberystwyth experienced a Victorian tourist boom, becoming a major holiday destination for working- and middle-class families from South Wales in particular. The town was marketed as the “Biarritz of Wales,” prompting the construction of hotels and fine townhouses, including the Queens Hotel. The Queens Hotel was renamed Swyddfa'r Sir (County Office) when used as offices by the town council, and has also served as external scene locations for the police station in the television series Hinterland. One of the era's largest hotels, the Castle Hotel, was never completed as a hotel; after bankruptcy it was sold cheaply to the Welsh National University Committee, which sought to establish a Welsh University. The University College of Wales, later Aberystwyth University, was founded in 1872 within the Castle Hotel building.

In 1896, the Aberystwyth Improvement Company established Constitution Hill Ltd to develop the project on Constitution Hill. The endeavor was directed by chief engineer George Croydon Marks. It led to the construction of the United Kingdom's second-longest funicular railway, the Aberystwyth Cliff Railway, which climbs a gradient of 50 percent.

Governorates constitute the second-level administrative divisions of Saudi Arabia, falling under the kingdom’s thirteen primary provinces that form the top-tier territorial units. They operate as local governance entities and are led by governors who are appointed to oversee affairs within the governorate. As of 2012, there were 136 governorates in the kingdom.

Within the Saudi administrative framework, each governorate is led by a governor (muḥāfiẓ) appointed by royal decree. The governor is assisted by a deputy governor, forming the governorate’s executive leadership. Governorates are subdivided into centers (مراكز), also known as sub-governorates, which are charged with delivering local services. These centers coordinate with provincial authorities to ensure alignment with regional governance and policy implementation.

Frederick Augustus I of Saxony was the second, and eldest surviving, son of Frederick Christian, Elector of Saxony, and Maria Antonia Walpurgis, Princess of Bavaria. He was underage when his father died of smallpox in 1763, and his mother governed as Regent until 1768, with his uncle, Prince Francis Xavier, acting as his representative during the regency. He is descended from two kings of Poland on his father's side, while on his mother's side he traces lineage to Siemowit, the earliest clearly attested Duke of Poland.

Frederick Augustus I of Saxony organized a pivotal meeting at Pillnitz Castle in August 1791 with Holy Roman Emperor Leopold II and King Frederick William II of Prussia to demonstrate support for the French Bourbon monarchy amid revolutionary agitation in France. The aims of the gathering culminated in the Pillnitz Declaration, issued by Leopold II and William II, which warned that external military action might be taken against the French revolutionary government to restore the monarchy. The declaration is widely regarded as a provocative move that provided France with grounds to declare war on Austria in April 1792. Frederick Augustus himself did not sign the declaration.

Before European contact, First Nations peoples practiced a variety of religious traditions, largely animistic in character. In 1607, official support for Port Royal was conditioned on efforts to convert local First Nations to Christianity. Catholicism predominated among French settlers along the Saint Lawrence River, and Jesuit missionaries were among those devoted to converting Indigenous peoples. Over time, these missionary efforts yielded converts among Indigenous communities.

Saint Pierre and Miquelon is a French overseas collectivity, officially the Collectivité territoriale de Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon. The territory comprises a small group of islands located about 25 km (16 miles; 13 nautical miles) off the coast of Newfoundland in the western Atlantic. It was ceded to France by Britain in 1763 to secure and support French fishing rights in the surrounding waters. The islands are not remnants of the historical colony of New France.

Following the First Opium War, the Qing government was compelled by the resulting settlements to permit the presence and activity of foreign missionaries in China. The unequal treaties that accompanied the peace accord granted Western powers jurisdiction over missionary affairs, effectively placing the governance of these activities under foreign legal authority. In addition, these agreements conferred Western states with a degree of oversight over Chinese Christians, enabling external influence over religious life and the conduct of Christian communities. Together, these provisions illustrate how postwar arrangements extended European control over religious structures and adherents within China.

During the First Opium War, British naval forces pressed their advance toward Shanghai in mid-June 1842. On June 14, the British fleet seized the mouth of the Huangpu River, establishing control near the city. Two days later, at the Battle of Woosung, Chinese forces were defeated and the British subsequently captured Wusong and Baoshan. By June 19, the undefended outskirts of Shanghai had fallen to the British advancing from the river approaches. The occupation was followed by looting in Shanghai carried out by retreating Qing bannermen, British soldiers, and local civilians. In the fighting around Woosong, Qing Admiral Chen Huacheng was killed defending a fort.

Advertising is the practice of delivering targeted communications to current and prospective customers to convey information about products or services and influence perceptions. It informs consumers about offerings, persuades them of the superiority of a company’s offerings, and helps foster a favorable corporate image. By identifying and generating demand, it points out needs and demonstrates new uses for established items, while also announcing launches of new products and programs. In addition, advertising reinforces the messages conveyed by sales personnel, attracts customers to the business, and aids in retaining existing customers, thereby supporting both immediate sales and long-term customer relationships.

In 1836, the French newspaper La Presse is credited with introducing paid advertising, a development that lowered the paper’s price, broadened its readership, and increased profitability, a method quickly imitated by others. By 1840, Volney B. Palmer in Philadelphia had laid the foundations of the modern advertising agency. In 1842, Palmer began purchasing large blocks of newspaper space at discounted rates and reselling them at a profit, acting as a space broker while the actual advertisement copy and artwork were provided by the advertiser. The first full‑service agency, N. W. Ayer & Son, was established in Philadelphia in 1869, offering planning, creation, and execution of campaigns. By 1900, advertising agencies had become the central locus of creative planning, and the profession of advertising had established itself as a distinct field.

Camutanga's economy comprises several principal activities, with the food and beverage industry forming a core component alongside commerce. Agriculture and related activities are also prominent, particularly the cultivation of sugarcane and bananas. In addition, livestock farming plays a notable role, with cattle accounting for a major portion of the local animal husbandry.

Camutanga is a city and municipality in the state of Pernambuco, Brazil. It lies approximately 120 kilometers from Recife, the state capital. As of 2020, the estimated population was 8,572 according to the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE). The municipality is notable for having one of the highest GDP per capita levels in the Zona da Mata Pernambucana region.

During the 2008 NCAA Division II football season, the California University of Pennsylvania Vulcans defeated Seton Hill 48–7. The Vulcans were led by quarterback Kevin McCabe, who threw three touchdown passes and completed 19 of 24 attempts for 253 yards. Terrence Johnson added a special-teams highlight with an 82-yard kickoff return for a touchdown. Seton Hill's lone score came on a 30-yard fumble return for a touchdown.

In the 2008 NCAA Division II football season, Grand Valley State, the top seed in Super Region 3, defeated Ashland University 40–7. The Lakers struck on their first two possessions and led 24–0 at halftime. Ashland’s only score came on the first play of the fourth quarter, when Billy Cundiff found Christian Livingston for an 8-yard touchdown pass, but Grand Valley State responded with a 62-yard touchdown run on the next offensive play. The GVSU defense finished with eight sacks and nine tackles for lost yardage.

Minetta Lane Theatre hosted a brief transfer of Balm in Gilead in 1984. The theatre's inaugural production followed in 1985 with 3 Guys Naked from the Waist Down. It subsequently staged a number of notable productions, including Marvin's Room (1992), Jeffrey (1994), The Last Five Years (2002), and Adding Machine (2008).

Minetta Lane Theatre has functioned as Audible's principal site for its creative work, hosting both full productions and staged readings since 2018. Among the Audible productions staged at the venue are Harry Clarke and Girls & Boys, both presented in 2018. As part of Audible's residency program at Minetta Lane, The Half-Life of Marie Curie was presented in 2019, with Dead Outlaw appearing in 2024 and Mexodus in 2025.

Jai Hind was a Gujarati-language daily newspaper published from Rajkot, with a circulation extending to major centers in Gujarat, including Ahmedabad, Jamnagar, Junagadh, Porbandar, Bhavnagar, Amreli, Surendranagar, and the Kutch region. It was founded by N. L. Shah, who was also known as Babubhai or Babulal. The publication is recognized as the first daily Gujarati newspaper produced in Rajkot.

Jai Hind, a Gujarati daily newspaper, was founded in 1948 in Rajkot. The publication later expanded with an Ahmedabad edition in 1962. It is noted for being the first Gujarati newspaper to adopt modern printing technology and for implementing an efficient, rapid distribution system. Additionally, Jai Hind became the first daily in Gujarat to publish concurrent editions from two publication centers.

Uruguay's current departmental boundaries were established through a sequence of creations and detachments from preexisting jurisdictions between 1837 and 1885. On 17 June 1837, Salto and Tacuarembó were created as separate departments, and Minas was formed from portions of Cerro Largo and Maldonado, a designation later renamed Lavalleja. In 1856, the Florida department was established. On 7 July 1880, Río Negro was split from Paysandú and Rocha from Maldonado. In 1884, Treinta y Tres was formed from parts of Cerro Largo and Minas, Artigas was detached from Salto, and Rivera was detached from Tacuarembó. Finally, in 1885, Flores was separated from San José.

Within Uruguay’s system of territorial administration, the General Assembly has the authority to create new departments and to establish their boundaries, but both actions require a two-thirds supermajority in each chamber (the Senate and the Chamber of Deputies). This power and its procedural thresholds are anchored in the constitution, specifically Article 85. Consequently, any proposal to alter the departmental landscape or to redefine borders must attain broad cross-chamber support, reflecting the high level of consensus deemed necessary for changes to the country’s subnational divisions.

Joy is associated with improvements in health and well-being and can trigger psychological changes that raise mood. Individuals differ in their natural propensity to experience joy, with some people more predisposed to feeling joyous than others. Although some sources describe joy as hereditary, the evidence for a genetic basis of happiness remains inconclusive. Nevertheless, the experience of joy can be enhanced through healthy habits such as sharing meals with others, engaging in physical activity, expressive writing, and practices that foster self-connection.

In the view of philosopher Michela Summa, joy is distinguished from happiness by its intimate association with the ongoing process rather than with a completed achievement. Joy is experienced throughout the activity and remains tightly bound to the present moment, functioning as a direct emotional response to events embedded in concerns about life. By contrast, happiness presupposes an evaluative stance toward a span of life or one’s life as a whole, signifying a judgment about overall well-being rather than an immediate affect tied to the ongoing pursuit.

The Zuellig Building is an office skyscraper located in the Makati Central Business District of Metro Manila, Philippines. Rising to 160 meters (520 feet), it stands among the district's tallest structures. The building is owned by the Zuellig Group and was developed by Bridgebury Realty Corp., the group's real estate arm. Completed in 2013, it earned Platinum-level LEED Core and Shell certification, the first such designation awarded in the Philippines.

The Zuellig Building was designed by Skidmore, Owings and Merrill (SOM) in collaboration with the local architectural firm W.V. Coscolluela & Associates. The façade design was carried out by Meinhardt Hong Kong Pte. Ltd., while Meinhardt Philippines provided the structural, mechanical and electrical engineering as well as fire protection design for the project.

The hydronym Kelvin is generally regarded as of Brittonic origin, though its precise etymology remains a matter of scholarly debate. One line of analysis connects the name to the Brittonic element celeμïn, whose Welsh cognate celefyn is interpreted as meaning “stem” or “stalk.” An alternative proposal posits that the river name derives from the zero-grade form of the Proto-Indo-European root *kl̥h1-, which carries the sense of “rise up.”

Several crossings span the River Kelvin in Glasgow. The most notable is the Great Western Bridge on Great Western Road in the West End, beneath which the Kelvinbridge underground station is located, a linkage that anchors the surrounding area to the Kelvinbridge name. Another crossing lies near Balmuildy, close to the Antonine Wall. The Ha'penny Footbridge is situated within the Glasgow Botanic Gardens. Additional minor road bridges are found at Queen Margaret Drive, Belmont Street, and Eldon Street. The river also crosses through the grounds of Kelvingrove Park, which contains multiple bridges. Partick Bridge traverses Dumbarton Road. Near Yorkhill, where the Kelvin flows into the Clyde, there are prominent railway and road viaducts.

The 2021 census showed that ethnic Poles accounted for 98.84% of Poland’s population. Among those identifying as ethnic Poles, 96.28% reported Polish heritage alone, while 2.56% indicated both Polish and another ethnicity (respondents could select up to two ethnicities). Those declaring only non-Polish ethnicities made up 1.13%, and 0.03% did not report an ethnicity. At the voivodeship level, Holy Cross Voivodeship recorded the highest share of ethnic Poles at 99.70%, while Silesian Voivodeship recorded the lowest at 95.49%.

Poland's Constitution stands as the supreme law of the land, with the judiciary rooted in civil rights and operating under the civil code. The current democratic constitution, adopted by the National Assembly of Poland on 2 April 1997, establishes a multi-party system and enshrines fundamental freedoms, including the rights to religious liberty, freedom of expression, and peaceful assembly. It also bars forced medical experimentation, torture, and corporal punishment, and recognises the inviolability of the home. Additionally, the Constitution protects workers’ rights to form trade unions and to strike.

Richer Sounds began trading in 1978, founded by Richer, who was nineteen years old at the time. The first shop was opened near London Bridge with the assistance of Vic Odden, a photography retailer. In 1994, a Richer Sounds shop set a world-record for the highest sales per square metre of any retail outlet, recording £195,426 per m² (approximately $27,830 per ft²). Guinness World Records indicated that the record remained current as of 2023.

In November 2013, Julian Richer announced that, upon his death, 100% of Richer Sounds would be bequeathed to an employee-owned trust co-owned by the staff. In May 2019, at the age of 60, he disclosed that 60% of his shares would be transferred into a trust, effectively transferring ownership to the employees. Separately, he introduced a bonus scheme under which each non-director employee—numbering over 500—receives £1,000 for each year of service; the total of these bonuses was about £4 million, calculated using an average length of service of roughly eight years.

During the 2023–24 Gibraltar Football League season, players’ national team eligibility is indicated by flags corresponding to FIFA-defined nationalities, ensuring consistent representation across official materials. Some players also hold multiple nationalities that are not recognized by FIFA, reflecting the presence of non-FIFA nationalities among competitors.

In November 2023, Lynx announced plans to report the Gibraltar Football Association (GFA) to UEFA and FIFA after allegations that Lincoln Red Imps fielded an ineligible player—believed to be Ibrahim Ayew—in their opening league match, a 3–2 Lincoln win. The GFA subsequently ruled that although the player was suspended, Lincoln would not be punished for the error. By contrast, Mons Calpe had been sanctioned for a similar infraction in the previous season. These developments fueled accusations of bias and corruption within the GFA, which formed the basis of Lynx’s formal complaint.

Born March 25, 1852, in Kinsman, Ohio, the physician was the son of Dudley Allen and the grandson of Peter Allen, both of whom were doctors. He earned an AB from Oberlin College in 1875 and received his MD from Harvard Medical School in 1879. After settling in Cleveland, Ohio, in 1883, he became one of the city's early physicians to specialize in surgery. He taught surgery at Western Reserve Medical College from 1884 to 1890, and in 1893 he was named Professor of Principles & Practice of Surgery. He was designated Professor Emeritus of Surgery in 1910 and later Senior Professor of Surgery in 1911, reflecting his enduring role in surgical education and practice in Cleveland.

The Dittrick Museum of Medical History began as a collection focused on doctors and the medical profession, and it was transformed by artifacts donated by its curator and founder to document the history of medicine in relation to instruments and technology. Since its foundation, the museum has become more analytical of past medical technology and seeks to study doctor–patient relationships across time. A central figure in its development was Dudley Peter Allen, a prominent late‑nineteenth‑century surgeon. In 1894 a museum committee was formed, and Allen contributed steadily until his death in 1906; thereafter his wife Elizabeth Severance Allen continued donations to support the construction of the Allen Memorial Medical Library alongside the museum. The institution opened to the public in 1960 and has maintained public accessibility since. By 2017 it served as a study center for Case Western Reserve University’s College of Arts and Sciences in addition to functioning as a museum.

Piece of My Heart is a song performed by Erma Franklin, released in 1967. It reached number 10 on the US Billboard Hot Rhythm & Blues Singles chart in December of that year and attained a peak position of number 62 on the US Billboard Pop Singles chart. In Canada, the track climbed to number 3 on the CKFH Soul Survey. Contemporary trade publications offered favorable notices: Cash Box remarked that the record begins more quietly than expected, a feature that underlines the subsequent rise in intensity, while Record World praised the gospel-tinged vocal delivery and stated that Erma Franklin really delivers.

“Piece of My Heart” is a song originally recorded by Janis Joplin with Big Brother and the Holding Company, which became a hit in 1968. Faith Hill’s interpretation of the track presents a markedly different vocal approach, delivering a bright, buoyant performance that contrasts with Joplin’s raw, commanding delivery. Critics weighed in on the reinterpretation: Billboard’s Larry Flick suggested that enduring songs can accommodate diverse interpretations and that Hill’s lighter, more effervescent rendition can succeed if performed convincingly. The Gavin Report’s Cyndi Hoelzle and Lisa Smith observed that Hill’s version redefines the piece, making it readily identifiable as her own while recasting Joplin’s classic into a brisk, country-tinged lament. Taken together, these assessments place Hill’s rendition within the lineage of the original, a 1968 hit for Joplin and her band, while highlighting its distinct tonal recalibration.

Dua Lipa first performed Levitating on The Graham Norton Show on 20 November 2020, and she delivered a subsequent rendition two days later at the American Music Awards 2020. Although the AMAs ceremony was staged at the Microsoft Theater in Los Angeles, the performance was filmed at London's Royal Albert Hall on a custom-built set. In the closing moments, Lipa appeared to levitate upward, supported by a wire system operated through pulleys. The sequence drew praise from critics, with Olivia Horn of The New York Times highlighting the levitation while also noting Lipa’s dancing, and Justin Curto of Vulture calling it one of the ceremony’s standout moments. Marty Rosenbaum of Radio.com ranked the moment eighth among the night's highlights, lauding the levitation segment.

Levitating (song)'s music video was filmed primarily in London over four days in June 2020, with Elliott recording her portions in Atlanta alongside Dua Lipa's UK team. It stood as one of the early large-scale productions to shoot under APA guidelines following lockdown restrictions. Due to social distancing, real couples were cast for the project, with Hadid ultimately being selected. News of the filming, noting the song was not yet publicly identified at the time, was reported on 18 June 2020 alongside Hadid's casting. The video premiered on 14 August 2020 at 05:00 PT (12:00 UTC). In reception, Billboard described the remix video as vibrant and dreamlike, while Consequence of Sound highlighted candy-colored, Miami-glaze lenses and mythic, celestial imagery, calling it snazzy and reminiscent of a four-minute Ring Pop. Radio.com compared the visuals to Sailor Moon, Euphoria, and Twilight, and Vogue praised the trippy visuals, bright hues, and wardrobe that aligned with Future Nostalgia’s retro rave concept.

Prior to the 1906 legalization of land ownership, a substantial number of Japanese settlers sought farmland in Korea, a push supported by the administration of Governor-General Terauchi Masatake who promoted settlement through land reform. The Korean land system at the time featured absentee landlords, partially owner-tenants, and cultivators who retained traditional verbal rights but lacked formal written proof of ownership. By 1920, Koreans held formal ownership to the vast majority of the land, but Terauchi’s Land Survey Bureau carried out cadastral surveys that defined ownership based on written documentation such as deeds, titles, and other records. Those lacking such written proof were denied ownership, a situation that often affected individuals who previously possessed only verbal cultivator-rights and included members of the higher social strata with independent holdings. Japanese landlords included both private individuals and corporate entities, among them the Oriental Development Company, and as a consequence, Japanese landownership and land held by private Japanese companies expanded.

Under Japanese rule, governing policies sought to suppress Korean linguistic traditions and promote assimilation, markedly restricting opportunities for Korean language study. By 1943, Korean-language instruction had been completely terminated, and both the teaching and everyday use of Korean were prohibited. A government report urged further radical reforms, but the proposed decade-long reform plan was never fully realized, leaving its implementation incomplete.

The Siege of Port Royal in 1710 was the third British expedition during Queen Anne's War aimed at capturing the Acadian capital. The operation produced far-reaching consequences that continued to influence regional developments over the next half-century. It helped shape the North American dimensions of the 1711–1713 French–British negotiations and contributed to the establishment of the British colony of Nova Scotia to administer Acadia. Moreover, the events raised enduring questions about the future of the Acadian and Mi’kmaq populations in Acadia. Seen in historical perspective as a foundational moment in the history of the Canadian state, the siege also served as a precursor to the British conquest of New France in the mid-century.

The Siege of Port Royal (5–13 October 1710), also known as the Conquest of Acadia, was a British operation in which forces commanded by Francis Nicholson besieged Port Royal, the capital of Acadia, defended by a French Acadian garrison and its Wabanaki Confederacy allies led by Daniel d'Auger de Subercase. The surrender produced a British victory and marked the start of enduring British sovereignty over the peninsular region of Acadia, which the British referred to as Nova Scotia since 1621. The event is notable as the first instance in which the British permanently captured and held a French colonial possession. After capitulation, the fort was renamed Annapolis Royal and occupied with formal ceremony.

On November 30, 1991, American Top 40 began deriving its chart from the Top 40 Radio Monitor after a 21-year period using the Billboard Hot 100, with the chart being identified as the Top 40 Radio Monitor during that interval. This arrangement persisted until January 1993, when AT40 resumed using the Billboard Mainstream Top 40 chart. The shift occurred amid broader changes in the early 1990s, when Top 40 radio experienced fragmentation as stations adopted more narrowly defined formats. Consequently, many outlets limited their playlists to genres aligned with those formats, reducing the breadth of styles that had previously characterized the Hot 100.

Radio Songs (chart) is a Wikipedia article that documents a chart ranking songs by their peak radio airplay. The list records, for each track, the highest level of airplay impressions it has achieved. To maintain a non-redundant record, a song is included only once on the chart, even if it appears across multiple weeks with sufficient impressions.

Vancity withdrew its cards from the market in 2021. The Canada Post / Zenwallet prepaid Visa returned to the market in October 2022, with Peoples Trust serving as the issuing institution for the returned card.

Vancity participates as a member of Central 1 Credit Union and holds registration with the Credit Union Deposit Insurance Corporation of British Columbia. In December 2010, the credit union joined the Global Alliance for Banking on Values (GABV).

In May 2014, the United States reported its first laboratory-confirmed MERS-CoV infection, identified in a healthcare worker in Indiana who had recently returned from Saudi Arabia and was initially described as in good condition. A second confirmed case followed in a Florida resident from the Orlando area. A third case, identified in Illinois, involved an asymptomatic individual who had tested positive for a past infection linked to the Indiana healthcare worker, and was at the time described as the first instance of possible human-to-human transmission within the United States. However, on May 28, 2014, the CDC announced that the Illinois individual's positive result did not indicate an active infection, and subsequent laboratory analysis indicated that the person had never been infected with MERS-CoV.

On 31 October 2013, the World Health Organization announced three deaths attributed to Middle East respiratory syndrome (MERS) in Saudi Arabia, comprising one woman and two men. All three individuals had underlying medical conditions, and each reported no contact with animals prior to falling ill.

In 1859, James Croll took a position as a janitor at the museum of the Andersonian University in Glasgow. He used the university library to access books, and he taught himself physics and astronomy in order to develop his ideas.

James Croll, FRS, was a Scottish scientist who, in the 19th century, developed an astronomical theory of climate variability. He argued that long-term fluctuations in Earth's climate were driven by changes in the planet's orbit, integrating astronomical factors into explanations of climatic change. Born on 2 January 1821 and dying on 15 December 1890, Croll's work helped establish an early link between celestial mechanics and terrestrial climate.

LZX is a compression algorithm employed in a range of archival formats, notably within Amiga LZX archives and in some Microsoft Cabinet (.cab) files that use the LZX method. Tools exist to unpack these formats: unlzx and XAD can decompress Amiga LZX archives, while cabextract is able to extract Cabinet files that utilize LZX compression. The broader ecosystem of related formats is reflected by CHM-related tooling, with the CHM article noting a wide selection of cross-platform utilities for decompiling or viewing CHM files. Additionally, LIT e-book files can be unpacked using ConvertLIT software.

LZX is a data compression method used within the Cabinet archive format, which saw notable development after Forbes joined Microsoft in 1996 to oversee enhancements to the cabinet archiver that integrated the LZX technique. The update introduced a variable sliding window size, in contrast to the Amiga implementation that fixed the window at 64 KB. Microsoft’s LZX, by comparison, supports window sizes that are powers of two ranging from 32 KB up to 2048 KB (32,768 to 2,097,152 bytes). Additionally, a preprocessing stage was added to identify Intel 80x86 CALL instructions and convert operands from relative to absolute addressing, enabling repeated code strings to be matched and thereby improving compression for 80x86 binary code. This approach was later generalized and formalized as Branch-Call-Jump (BCJ) filtering.

Christianity in Canada encompasses a range of churches and denominations. The largest Christian bodies—primarily the Roman Catholic Church, United Church, and Anglican Church—together account for more than half of Canadians as nominal adherents. The country also hosts numerous smaller Christian communities, including Orthodox congregations. The Orthodox presence includes a growing Coptic Orthodox population in Ontario and Quebec, with a notable concentration in the Greater Toronto Area. A sizeable Ukrainian community in Manitoba and Saskatchewan sustains Ukrainian Catholic and Ukrainian Orthodox institutions. Southern Manitoba is largely settled by Mennonites. The distribution of smaller Christian groups varies across the country. Baptists are notably numerous in the Maritimes, while Lutherans are substantial in the Maritimes, the prairie provinces, and southwestern Ontario. Southwest Ontario hosts a significant German and Russian immigrant milieu, including Mennonites, Hutterites, and Dutch Reformed. Alberta is characterized by a notable Mormon minority resulting from immigration from the American plains. The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints reported a global membership of 178,102, with 74,377 in Alberta as of the end of 2007, and Jehovah’s Witnesses have reported 111,963 active members in Canada.

Within the broader context of Christianity in Canada, the Old Order Amish community numbered about 5,375 people as of 2018. The Amish maintain settlements in four provinces—Ontario, Prince Edward Island, Manitoba, and New Brunswick—with Ontario hosting the largest share. In Ontario, the majority of Old Order settlements are concentrated in Oxford County, including the Norwich Township area, and in Norfolk County. A smaller community is also established in Bruce County, in Huron-Kinloss Township near Lucknow.

OCR-A’s development includes notable work by Matthew Skala, who in 2006 used the mftrace utility to convert the font’s Metafont definitions into TrueType format. In 2011 he released a revised version that rewrote the Metafont sources to be compatible with METATYPE1, allowing outlines to be generated directly without an intermediate tracing step. On September 27, 2012, he updated the implementation to version 0.2.

OCR-A is a typeface that exists in both free and commercially distributed implementations. In 1995, Tobias Frere-Jones produced Estupido-Espezial as a satirical redesign of OCR-A, which features decorative swashes and a long s. The redesign was used in a technology-themed section of Rolling Stone magazine.

Doubly fed electric machines constitute an alternative to the conventional DC-fed field and armature arrangement used in many generators. The design employs two distinct three-phase windings in place of a single field and armature, enabling a two-winding configuration. In operation, one winding is stationary while the other rotates, typically corresponding to a stationary stator winding and a rotating rotor winding. Each winding is independently connected to external electrical equipment outside the machine. The term “doubly fed” reflects the external connections of the two windings, indicating that both windings are fed from outside the generator.

Doubly fed electric machines in wind energy applications enable the turbine to operate over a range of rotor speeds by accepting the generator’s variable frequency, rectifying it to direct current, and then inverting it to the desired alternating current frequency. This arrangement allows flexible power generation as wind speeds change. The approach is commonly used in small-scale installations for houses and farms, where modest power outputs and simpler electrical integration suit the design. In megawatt-scale wind turbines, however, the required inverters are large and expensive, which raises overall cost and complexity for these larger systems.

Martyrdom of the Ten Thousand is a work by Albrecht Dürer that is repeatedly referenced in the correspondence between Dürer and Jakob Heller of Frankfurt. The letters show that Dürer received 280 florins as payment for the work.

Martyrdom of the Ten Thousand was commissioned by Frederick III, Elector of Saxony, for All Saints' Church in Wittenberg. Frederick, who had been a patron of Albrecht Dürer since 1496, personally selected the subject of the work. The choice reflected the elector's interest in relics, his collection including items associated with the Ten Thousand martyrs.

ICL systems were used to process the 1971 Indonesian Population Census. In the United Kingdom, the Filan software was employed during the 1970s by the Office of Population Censuses and Surveys to process data from the General Household Survey. Due to a small user community, ICL elected not to port the software to its 2900-series computers in the 1980s.

International Computers Limited's mid-1980s line featured licensed Rair designs built around the 8085 processor with CP/M and MP/M, introduced in 1983. The subsequent models 15, 25, 26 and 35 superseded earlier designs, employing a faster 8085A and offering an upgrade path to the 8088. Memory was expanded to 512 KB, and the serial interface count increased to four, with some configurations capable of eight ports. Storage options for floppy and hard drives were enhanced, and features such as disk caching and RAM disk functionality were added. In 1984, the Model 36 topped the range with a standard 8088 and support for Concurrent CP/M. The following year, ICL released the Quattro, a multi-user system derived from Rair that used a single 8086 CPU with an 8087 FPU, running Concurrent CP/M and supporting multiple serial terminals.

Arizona does not observe Daylight Saving Time, remaining on standard time year-round, unlike most states in the United States; Hawaii is the other state that does not observe Daylight Saving Time. Within Arizona, the Navajo Nation, located in the northeastern portion of the state, does observe Daylight Saving Time, creating a time-keeping distinction between Navajo Nation territories and surrounding areas.

In March 2000, Arizona hosted what was described as the first legally binding election conducted over the internet to nominate a candidate for public office. In the 2000 Arizona Democratic Primary, Al Gore defeated Bill Bradley. Voter turnout in the Arizona primary surged by more than 500 percent compared with the 1996 primary, a dramatic increase that drew worldwide attention to the state’s electoral experiment.

ISO 1000 is an ISO standard that addresses the International System of Units (SI). Published in 1992 by the International Organization for Standardization, it covers the SI units and provides guidance on the use of their multiples as well as certain related units. The standard also offers a description of the International System of Units.

Olivia Newton-John attended primary school with Daryl Braithwaite, who also pursued a career in singing. When she was fourteen, she formed an all-female group with three classmates, which was named Sol Four. The group lasted only a short time, and they frequently performed at a coffee shop owned by her brother-in-law.

On 2 November 2019, Julien’s Auctions conducted a sale of hundreds of Olivia Newton-John memorabilia, generating about $2.4 million in total proceeds. The event included the Grease outfit, which sold for $405,700, while Newton-John’s Grease pants and leather jacket were acquired separately by two different billionaire buyers. Sara Blakely, founder of Spanx, purchased the black skintight Grease pants for $162,000, and an anonymous bidder paid $243,200 (£185,000) for the leather jacket, which was later returned to Newton-John. The return accompanied a statement indicating that the garment should not reside in a billionaire’s closet and referencing the potential of new therapies to improve cancer outcomes. All proceeds from the auction were donated to Newton-John’s Cancer Wellness and Research Centre in Australia.
In the 2016 Wimbledon Championships men's doubles, the defending champions, Jean-Julien Rojer and Horia Tecău, were defeated in the opening round by Jonathan Marray and Adil Shamasdin.

At the 2016 Wimbledon Championships, Pierre-Hugues Herbert and Nicolas Mahut claimed the men's doubles title by defeating Julien Benneteau and Édouard Roger-Vasselin in straight sets, 6–4, 7–6(7–1), 6–3. The outcome also marked the first occasion that two French teams contested the Wimbledon men’s doubles final, underscoring a notable national milestone in the tournament’s doubles history.

Vitale's random Brunn–Minkowski inequality is a theorem in mathematics introduced by Richard Vitale. It generalizes the classical Brunn–Minkowski inequality by extending its applicability from fixed compact subsets of R^n to random compact sets in n-dimensional Euclidean space.

Vitale's random Brunn–Minkowski inequality concerns a random set X that can take two deterministic, non-empty compact sets K and L as its outcomes, with P(X = K) = 1 − λ and P(X = L) = λ for some λ in [0, 1]. In this two-point scenario, the randomized inequality specializes to the classical Brunn–Minkowski inequality for compact sets, thereby recovering the standard relation governing the n-dimensional volume of the Minkowski sum of K and L.

Shield bidding is a form of bid manipulation in online auctions in which an auxiliary account, referred to as the shield, places bids to deter competition by creating an impression of higher bidding activity. The shield bid is typically retracted at the last moment, enabling the intended buyer to win the item at a lower final price than the inflated bid would have indicated. Since many online auction platforms prohibit bid withdrawals except under specified circumstances, shield bidding is feasible only on sites that do not enforce strict withdrawal rules.

Online auctions are bidding processes conducted via the internet, and they provide advantages that are not found in traditional auction formats. A key benefit is the use of automated bidding, where bids are submitted automatically on behalf of participants according to predefined limits. Moreover, online auctions have greatly expanded the variety of goods and services that can be bought and sold through auction mechanisms.

In October 2012, the World Wide Web Consortium brought together a coalition of major web players and publishers to launch a collaborative, MediaWiki-based wiki. The platform, named WebPlatform and WebPlatform Docs, was established with the aim of documenting open web standards.

On 1 January 2023, the World Wide Web Consortium reorganized as a public-interest 501(c)(3) non-profit organization. In October 2023, Seth Dobbs was appointed as the organization's chief executive officer.

Mustafa II's stratagem failed; disaffected troops bound to a Georgian campaign mutinied in the capital, an episode historians designate as the Edirne event. This uprising contributed to his deposition on 22 August 1703.

Şehzade Mehmed, an Ottoman prince and the favorite son of Sultan Mustafa II, was born on 27 November 1698 and died on 3 June 1703. He died at Edirne Palace in Edirne and was buried in Turhan Sultan's türbe at the New Mosque. His mother was Afife Kadın. The death of Şehzade Mehmed is said to have left Mustafa II deeply distressed.

On September 25, 1939, the Luftwaffe conducted a bombing raid on Warsaw with the aim of breaking Polish morale and forcing surrender. Under the 1939 laws of war, Warsaw was a defended military target, reflecting its role in Poland's defense. Therefore, the Luftwaffe raid could be construed as a legitimate military operation under the contemporary legal framework.

During World War II, the Luftwaffe carried out numerous air strikes against Warsaw, targeting both Polish resistance and civilian targets. The bombing damaged the city’s infrastructure extensively and left the urban fabric profoundly scarred. In the ensuing ruins, desperate street-to-street combat occurred as fighters clashed amid the destruction. After about 63 days of intense urban warfare, Luftwaffe attacks combined with artillery bombardment and systematic devastation had destroyed roughly 85 to 90 percent of Warsaw’s buildings by January 1945.

WQQW (Illinois) had its license revoked by the Federal Communications Commission on March 20, 2020, after the commission determined that the principal ownership entity, Entertainment Media Trust, operated as a shell for a convicted felon. The action also led to the cancellation of the licenses of three additional Greater St. Louis AM stations owned by the same group: KFTK (1490 AM), KQQZ, and KZQZ.

Mark Kern's 2012 challenge to the renewals of WQQW and its sister stations alleged that Robert Romanik, a convicted felon often referred to as the Grim Reaper of Radio, controlled the outlets in violation of FCC rules prohibiting felons from owning broadcast stations. He further contended that Romanik had arranged a local marketing agreement for one of the stations. On June 5, 2019, the Federal Communications Commission designated the licenses of all four EMT stations for hearing. The FCC concluded that Romanik had formed EMT and provided the full funding to acquire its stations, even though he was not a party to any FCC applications.

Buddies is a 10-inch split album by British folk-punk artist Frank Turner and American alternative-country musician Jon Snodgrass. The project was written in a four-hour session, with recording taking place the following day in early August 2010. The 10-inch vinyl was released in the United Kingdom in September 2010, and a digital download release on iTunes followed on 28 January 2011 in response to popular demand.

In 1754, at the Albany Congress, Benjamin Franklin, a Pennsylvania colonist, proposed the Albany Plan, a framework intended to establish a unified government for the Thirteen Colonies to oversee defense and other common concerns. The plan was rejected by the leaders of most colonies.

In 1629 a wave of Puritan settlers established the Massachusetts Bay Colony, numbering roughly 400 inhabitants, with the aim of reforming the Church of England by creating a theologically distinct church in the New World. By 1640 the Puritan migration had grown to about 20,000, though many died soon after arrival; those who survived encountered a climate favorable for settlement and ample food. The Plymouth and Massachusetts Bay colonies helped catalyze the formation of additional Puritan communities in New England, including New Haven, Saybrook, and Connecticut. In the course of the 17th century, New Haven and Saybrook were absorbed by the Connecticut Colony, consolidating these Puritan settlements under a single colonial administration.

In the wake of cross-border attacks in Sabah, UPKO stated that it would present proposed solutions once it has access to the full Royal Commission Inquiry report; among the suggested measures is the recall and re-issuance of all Sabah identification cards. Additionally, a number of former politicians have urged the federal government to investigate individuals who claim royal blood of the Sulu Sultanate, alleging that these individuals have continued to confer Datukship titles on local Sabahans as well as on people from Peninsular Malaysia up to the present.

Cross-border attacks in Sabah refer to a pattern of terrorist incursions conducted by Moro pirates from Mindanao, Philippines, with origins dating to before the British colonial era. These acts have caused civilian deaths and hardship, contributing to rising anti-Filipino sentiment among Sabah's indigenous communities. The most notable attacks occurred in 1985, 2000, and 2013. The level of violence during certain periods was higher under the administrations of Diosdado Macapagal and Ferdinand Marcos, who supported irredentist claims to eastern Sabah. In more recent times, renewed infiltrations and militant assaults, together with unregulated migration from Mindanao into Sabah, have heightened local unease. Approximately 78 percent of Sabah's prison population is jailed for offenses and lawlessness largely originating from the southern Philippines.

Westphalia is a region roughly bounded by the Rhine to the west and the Weser to the east, with its territory extending on both sides of the Ruhr River. In addition to these principal waterways, the Ems and Lippe are among the other important rivers in the area.

Charlemagne spent considerable time in Paderborn and the surrounding region, and the Saxon Wars extended into areas that are today part of Westphalia. In popular legend, Widukind, Charlemagne's adversary, is connected to places around Detmold, Bielefeld, Lemgo, Osnabrück, and other Westphalian localities. A legend holds that Widukind was buried in Enger.

Human-centered computing is an interdisciplinary field that integrates computer science with disciplines such as human factors, sociology, psychology, cognitive science, anthropology, communication studies, graphic design, and industrial design. It covers research into how individuals and social groups adopt, adapt to, and organize their lives around computational technologies, as well as efforts to design and develop new computational artifacts that support human activities. By combining studies of use with the creation of technological tools, the field seeks to understand the social and cognitive dimensions of computing and to produce systems and interfaces that align with human needs and practices.

Human-centered computing is grounded in designing and evaluating technology around human needs and capabilities. The Center for Cognitive Ubiquitous Computing (CUbiC) at Arizona State University embodies these principles by developing tools and applications for assistive, rehabilitative, and healthcare settings. Founded in 2001 by Sethuraman Panchanathan, CUbiC's research spans three core areas: sensing and processing, recognition and learning, and interaction and delivery. The work emphasizes transdisciplinary collaboration and foregrounds individuals in the process of technology design and deployment. Notable projects include Note-Taker, which assists students with low vision to follow instruction and take notes, and the VibroGlove, a haptic device that conveys facial expressions to visually impaired users.

Irving Saul Shapiro (July 15, 1916 – September 13, 2001) was an American lawyer and businessman. He became the first attorney to ascend to the chief executive position at DuPont, and he served as DuPont’s chairman from December 1973 to 1981. In 1987, Shapiro assumed leadership of the Howard Hughes Medical Institute.

Irving S. Shapiro was an American businessman and lawyer who served as chairman and chief executive officer of DuPont from 1973 to 1981. Born in Minneapolis, Minnesota, he was the son of Lithuanian Jewish immigrants, with his father working as a dry cleaner and tailor. He earned his law degree from the University of Minnesota Law School and began his career as a government lawyer before joining DuPont in 1951 to work in the legal department. Over the years he advanced within the company and ultimately led its operations during the 1970s. He was a member of the American Academy of Arts and Sciences and the American Philosophical Society.

Endianness denotes the arrangement of bytes within a word, and it has implications for both data transmission over communication channels and the addressing of bytes in computer memory. It determines the significance order of the bytes, indicating which byte carries the most significant value. In common usage, endianness is described using two principal schemes: big-endian, where the most significant byte is placed or transmitted first, and little-endian, where the least significant byte is placed or transmitted first.

Endianness denotes the byte order used to represent multi-byte data. In digital electronics, both big-endian and little-endian conventions are widely employed. The initial choice of endianness for a new design is often arbitrary, but once established, it is typically preserved in subsequent updates to maintain backward compatibility. In networking, big-endian is the standard convention, referred to as network order, with the most significant byte transmitted first. By contrast, little-endian predominates in processor architectures and memory layouts, as illustrated by x86, the majority of ARM implementations, and the base RISC-V design. File formats, meanwhile, may adopt either ordering; some formats combine both and others explicitly indicate the ordering in use.

Ultraviolet-C (UV-C) light is employed to irradiate the airstream within air conditioning systems, inactivating harmful microorganisms before the air is recirculated back into indoor environments. The effectiveness of this approach depends on several factors, including the UV-C light intensity, the duration of exposure for the microorganisms, the speed of the airflow, and the cleanliness of the system components.

Ultraviolet radiation is used to authenticate collectibles and works of art, providing a non-invasive means of verifying authenticity. It is also employed in the detection of counterfeit currency. Materials that are not marked with UV-sensitive dyes can still exhibit fluorescence when exposed to ultraviolet light, and the fluorescence can vary depending on whether short-wave or long-wave UV radiation is used.

Amid the early phase of the French Revolution, a vigorous British political debate arose over the legitimacy of popular sovereignty and reform. Central to this discourse were two influential pamphlets that articulated support for Richard Price and the notion that the French people possessed the right to overhaul their state. Mary Wollstonecraft's A Vindication of the Rights of Men is among the earliest of these pamphlets, arguing for political reform and the universality of rights. A few months later, Thomas Paine's Rights of Man expanded on the same line of thought, challenging hereditary privilege and defending the revolution's principles. In 1792, Christopher Wyvill published Defence of Dr. Price and the Reformers of England, advocating gradual, moderate reform within constitutional bounds. Collectively, these works are described as a defining strand of British political debate during the era and are regarded as one of the great exchanges in British political history.

In the late August elections for the National Convention, the franchise was sharply narrowed to about 3.3 million voters, down from roughly 4 million in 1791, with intimidation widespread. The Brissotin faction divided into two principal camps—the moderate Girondins, led by Brissot, and the radical Montagnards, headed by Robespierre, Danton, and Marat. Loyalty among deputies shifted, with approximately 160 of the 749 deputies affiliating with the Girondists and about 200 with the Montagnards, while the remainder belonged to the centrist La Plaine faction, led by Barère, Cambon, and Carnot.

In 2011, the company adopted the name GreenButton and joined the Microsoft Partner Network. In the same year, GreenButton was named Microsoft's Windows Azure ISV Partner of the Year. In May 2011, it formed a strategic alliance with Microsoft, a partnership that included an investment exceeding US$1 million and the addition of Mark Canepa to its board of directors.
In December 2011, GreenButton opened two offices in the United States. The U.S. headquarters is located in Palo Alto, California, while a sales office is situated in Seattle.

Mudstone is a fine-grained sedimentary rock whose definition can be applied in two ways: it may describe carbonate rocks such as limestone or dolomite in which the mud-sized carbonate component is the dominant phase; more often, the term refers to siliciclastic mudstone, a rock formed primarily from silicate minerals.

Mudstone, a fine-grained sedimentary rock, has its mineral composition characterized through a combination of analytical methods, including scanning electron microscopy, electron probe microanalysis, and X-ray diffraction. The bulk mineralogy is dominated by clay minerals, quartz, and feldspars, while a variety of accessory minerals occur in smaller amounts.

1080i is a high-definition video format used in HDTV and related display technologies. It offers 1080 lines of vertical resolution and employs interlaced scanning. Once a standard within HDTV, it was widely used for broadcast television owing to its ability to deliver high-resolution imagery with relatively modest bandwidth requirements. In professional video interfaces, 1080i is defined by the SMPTE 292M standard.

1080i is an HD interlaced video format that uses two fields per frame to produce the full picture, with the field rate depending on the broadcasting region: 50 Hz in PAL/SECAM areas and 60 Hz in NTSC areas, corresponding to 50 fields per second or 59.94 fields per second, respectively. When the two fields are paired, 50 Hz yields 25 full frames per second, while 59.94 Hz yields 29.97 full frames per second. Interlacing alternates between fields captured at slightly different moments in time, which can smooth motion compared with progressive scanning at similar effective frame rates, but it may also generate motion artifacts in fast-moving scenes if the field alignment is imperfect. The EBU notation prefers the resolution and frame rate to be presented in a slash-separated format, with examples such as 1080i/29.97 and 1080i/25 (paralleling 480i/29.97 and 576i/25). In EBU terms, 1080i59.94 is understood as 1080i/29.97, and 1080i50 corresponds to 1080i/25.

On 20 January 2015, ASELSAN of Turkey and Eurojet Turbo GmbH signed a memorandum of understanding to explore collaboration on the EJ200 military turbofan engine program. The proposed collaboration aimed to develop a derivative of the EJ200 with thrust-vectoring capabilities for Turkey's TFX fifth-generation air-superiority fighter program. The EJ200 was not ultimately selected for the TFX program. In the interim, the TFX is to be powered by the General Electric F110 engine until domestic production by TEI and TRMOTOR is established.

Plans for an enhanced variant of the EJ200 propulsion system aim to raise overall thrust by approximately 30 percent above the baseline EJ200. The dry (non-afterburning) thrust is projected to be around 78 kN (approximately 17,500 lbf), while the afterburning (reheated) thrust is expected to be about 120 kN (roughly 27,000 lbf).

The 1995–96 UEFA Cup was the 25th edition of UEFA's competition viewed as the third-tier in the European club football hierarchy at the time. Bayern Munich defeated Bordeaux of France on aggregate to claim the title. Bordeaux reached the final through its involvement in the 1995 UEFA Intertoto Cup in its inaugural year, and they were the only Intertoto entrant to advance to this stage of the UEFA Cup. With the victory, Bayern Munich became the third club to complete the set of major European trophies by having won the European Cup/Champions League, the UEFA Cup/Europa League, and the Cup Winners' Cup. The final was also notable for being the only UEFA Cup final of the 1990s without an Italian side.

Based on the 1994 UEFA ranking, the distribution of spots for the 1995–96 UEFA Cup was adjusted accordingly. As a result, both the Netherlands and Hungary each lost a slot, while Israel gained an additional slot. Additionally, owing to a UEFA special decision, the Czech Republic and Slovakia were still regarded as a single country for the purposes of the competition’s qualification and slot allocation during that season.

The 1964 Brownlow Medal was the thirty-seventh presentation of the award, which recognizes the fairest and best player in the Victorian Football League's home-and-away season. Carlton Football Club's Gordon Collis won the medal, polling 27 votes during the 1964 VFL season.

Blue became the color most commonly associated with the Democratic Party in the United States around the 2000 presidential election, a development attributed to the color schemes used by major television networks that consistently assigned blue to Democrats and red to Republicans. This arrangement makes the United States an outlier relative to the general pattern in many countries, where blue is typically linked with conservative parties; in the United States, the major conservative party, the Republican Party, is associated with red. In 2010, the Democratic Party formally adopted an official blue logo to reinforce this association.

In discussions of political color symbolism, the United Nations flag features a light blue hue. This shade was chosen to symbolize peace and hope, reflecting the organization's stated aims and aspirations. The color has also given rise to the term bluewashing, a label used to critique image-enhancing branding practices that rely on the blue color to convey virtue or credibility, potentially masking controversial actions.

The work, titled Resilience (sculpture), is an abstract sculpture whose composition incorporates text arranged at an oblique angle and features angled glass screens. Its overall silhouette resembles a cross, a form deliberately chosen to evoke the X mark voters place on ballots, thereby linking the piece to themes of participation and democratic choice.

Resilience is a sculpture located in Brisbane, Queensland, Australia. The work commemorates the efforts of Queensland's men and women who campaigned for women's suffrage in the state, recognizing their role in securing voting rights for women.
Brackenridge is a borough located in Allegheny County, Pennsylvania, United States. The community lies along the Allegheny River and is part of the Greater Pittsburgh metropolitan area.

Brackenridge, Pennsylvania is located at 40°36′30″N 79°44′32″W and has an average elevation of 827 feet (252 meters) above sea level. According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the total area covers 0.6 square miles (1.6 square kilometers), of which 0.5 square miles (1.3 square kilometers) is land and 0.04 square miles (0.10 square kilometers) is water, making up 7.27 percent of the total area.

During a meeting held in Nyon, Switzerland, the UEFA Executive Committee decided on the venue for the 2005 UEFA Cup Final, selecting Estádio José Alvalade as the host stadium and announcing the decision on 5 February 2004.

The 2004–05 UEFA Cup final, the 34th edition of UEFA's second-tier club competition, was played on 18 May 2005 between Sporting CP of Portugal and CSKA Moscow of Russia. CSKA Moscow won the match 3–1 to claim the trophy. The scoring sequence saw Rogério open the scoring for Sporting in the first half; Aleksei Berezutskiy equalised for CSKA after the interval; Yuri Zhirkov put the Russian side ahead, and Vágner Love added a third on a counterattack. Vágner Love also became the youngest scorer in a UEFA Cup final at 20 years and 341 days. The triumph marked CSKA Moscow's first UEFA Cup title and the first European trophy won by a Russian club. It was the first European final involving a club from the former Soviet Union since Dynamo Moscow's defeat in the 1972 Cup Winners' Cup final, and the first European title for a former Soviet Union side since Dynamo Kyiv's Cup Winners' Cup victory in 1986.

The quaestura exercitus was a late Roman military-administrative arrangement in which Moesia Inferior and Scythia Minor on the lower Danube, together with Cyprus, Caria, and the Aegean Islands, were gathered under a single command. These provinces were detached from the praetorian prefecture of the East and placed under the authority of a new army official known as the quaestor exercitus. The office possessed powers comparable to those of a magister militum, granting its holder substantial military and administrative authority over the detached territories.

The Danubian provinces tied to the quaestura exercitus did not endure the Avar invasions of the 6th–7th centuries. Isolated fortresses on the Danube Delta and along the Black Sea coast were maintained through provisioning supplied by sea routes. Charles Diehl contended that the Karabisianoi, a naval corps that emerges in the 680s, were formed from remnants of the quaestura exercitus. This hypothesis has been accepted by some scholars but challenged by others, notably Helene Ahrweiler in her study of the Byzantine navy. The question is connected to a broader debate over whether these formations were military-naval in nature or civil-administrative in character.

Kirti Nagar is connected to the Delhi Metro via the Kirti Nagar station, which is notable for being among the few stations that offer a feeder bus service to enhance local connectivity. The areas of Mansarovar Garden and Kirti Nagar lie adjacent to Ring Road on one side and to Patel Road on the other, positioning them along two major urban corridors. Ring Road provides a link to Dhaula Kuan, while Patel Road connects to Connaught Place, the Central Business District.

Kirti Nagar’s commercial landscape features two principal markets, the Main Market and the Nehru Market, and forms a dense cluster of Western-style indoor shopping complexes, including TDI Mall, Moments Mall, TDI Paragon Mall, Shoppers Stop, City Square, West Gate Mall, and Paradise Mall. The adjacent Rajouri Garden neighborhood is a well-known market area that helps shape the broader retail milieu surrounding Kirti Nagar. Collectively, this area represents the largest single locality shopping concentration in Delhi, surpassing the retail footprint of South Delhi.

"Another Day in Paradise" is a composition by Phil Collins, initially developed under the working title Homeless. The lyrics were influenced by Collins's encounter with a homeless person with two children asking for financial help, as well as his observation of people sleeping on an outdoor grill after one of his concerts. He described the contrast of homelessness near Capitol Hill as an extraordinary contradiction, and these experiences guided the lyrical direction of the song.

Another Day in Paradise, a song by Phil Collins, is presented through a third-person narrative that centers on a man who passes by a homeless woman, highlighting social neglect of homelessness. The lyrics urge listeners to resist turning a blind eye to the issue and to acknowledge a moral obligation to those in need. Religious imagery permeates the piece, most notably through a refrain that frames life as a form of paradise for some while foregrounding the hardship of the homeless woman. In addition, the narrator directly addresses God, posing questions about whether more can be done and whether there is anything meaningful that could be said, thereby intensifying the ethical appeal for compassion and action.

Gyirong Port, located at the China–Nepal frontier, embarked on development in the early 1990s to promote cross-border trade between China and Nepal. When the 2015 Nepal earthquake severely damaged the neighboring Zhangmu Port, Chinese authorities reoriented priorities to regard Gyirong as an alternative trade corridor. This repositioning was followed by significant investments aimed at expanding Gyirong into a modern logistics hub capable of handling increased regional commerce and improving connectivity.

Gyirong Port has evolved from a modest border crossing into a modern commercial hub, reflecting a deliberate upgrade of cross-border infrastructure. The transformation highlights China’s commitment to bolstering regional connectivity and integration across the area. The port’s development is intended to foster mutual prosperity through expanded transport networks and related facilities, including streamlined processes and logistics capacity. Policy measures accompany the infrastructural program, supplying the regulatory framework and strategic support necessary to sustain progress.

Under Augustus, in 27 BCE, the Roman province of Aquitania was enlarged northward to the Loire River. The expansion brought together the traditional Gaulish tribes with the older Aquitani who lived south of the Garonne, forming a broader provincial domain. This expanded region is associated with Novempopulania and Gascony, which lie within the same southwestern Gaul area.
