Charlemagne, in 781, proclaimed his son Louis as king of Aquitaine within the Carolingian Empire, a realm that encompassed the Duchy of Aquitaine and the Duchy of Vasconia. He suppressed a series of uprisings by Basque groups, associated with Gascony, and subsequently advanced beyond the Pyrenees into Pamplona’s territories after ravaging Gascony in order to impose authority over Vasconia south of the range. According to his biography, he achieved all of his objectives. After an overnight stay in Pamplona, his army was attacked at Roncevaux on the return in 812, narrowly escaping an engagement at the Pyrenean passes.

Valais features a metre-gauge railway axis that links the canton with central and eastern Switzerland and is operated by the Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn. The route runs from Zermatt through Visp and Brig to Disentis and Chur, forming a corridor that connects alpine communities with the wider Swiss rail network. The principal alignment passes through the Furka Base Tunnel in the canton’s eastern reaches, while the historic Furka Summit Tunnel remains popular for its panoramic scenery. The Glacier Express—a renowned long-distance service—connects Zermatt and St. Moritz by traversing sections of both the Matterhorn Gotthard Bahn and the Rhaetian Railway networks.

Valais is a canton in southwestern Switzerland whose territory is embraced by some of the highest Alpine peaks. Its geography is defined by these surrounding mountains, and the region maintains several major mountain passes that connect it with the rest of Europe. The principal road routes include the Grimsel Pass toward Bern and the Swiss Plateau, the Furka Pass toward Uri, the Nufenen Pass toward Ticino, and the Simplon and Great St Bernard Passes toward Italy, as well as the Forclaz and Morgins passes toward France. In addition, a set of notable historical or pedestrian routes links Valais to the Swiss Plateau via the Bernese Oberland, among them the Sanetsch, Rawil, Gemmi, and Lötschberg passes. These corridors have historically served as important transit routes across the Alpine barrier.

Between 2021 and 2023, Yandex developed and deployed an automated voice-over translation system for YouTube videos, delivering synthesized narration in English, Chinese, French, Spanish, and German. The feature aimed to broaden accessibility of online video content for multilingual audiences and to demonstrate Yandex's capabilities in cross-language translation technology.

In October 2023, Yandex introduced Yandex SpeechKit, a technology that combines speech recognition and synthesis capabilities. The platform provides a public API for performing speech recognition, enabling developers to integrate voice processing into their applications. It is available to Android and iOS developers, facilitating cross-platform use.

John Horne Blackmore was a Canadian politician who drew criticism for his stance toward Jewish people. The Encyclopaedia Judaica described him as repeatedly lending support to anti-Semitic sentiment. In 1953, reports claimed that he circulated the infamous Protocols of the Elders of Zion from his parliamentary office. Earlier, in a January 31, 1944, speech in the House of Commons, he advocated establishing a national homeland for the Jews in Palestine.

John Horne Blackmore published Money the Master Key in 1939, a volume derived from his speeches. The book presents an analysis of Money Power and argues for the existence of a deliberate unseen will that steers events from behind the scenes.

The Armenian Chess Championship is a national chess competition in Armenia, and the article provides a complete list of its winners. The inaugural event was held in 1934, at a time when Armenia was part of the Transcaucasian SFSR, and during the Armenian SSR era the championship occurred only sporadically until 1945. From 1945 onward, the championship has been contested annually, a pattern that has continued into independent Armenia. Typically, the tournament is conducted in a round-robin format featuring the country’s top players.

Mindspark Interactive Network originated as iWon.com, Inc., which on October 1, 2000 launched its sales force and established offices in New York, Los Angeles, San Francisco, and Chicago. On November 18, 2001, the company acquired the assets of Excite from bankruptcy, marking a significant shift in its corporate structure. Subsequently, the enterprise adopted the name The Excite Network, reflecting its expanded scope and rebranding.

Mindspark Interactive Network is a software distribution platform associated with a family of browser add-ons that have been described as intrusive and difficult to remove. In its older iterations, the network’s products displayed pop-up advertisements and hijacked the user’s browser, altering settings such as the default homepage and search provider without the user’s consent. The installation often occurred without permission, leaving users unaware of the changes to their browser. The MyWay toolbar and its successor myWebSearch have been classified by security researchers as spyware or adware due to their behavior and persistence. Widely regarded as a browser hijacker, Mindspark’s software is notorious for its tenacity in removal, yet reports persist that it continues to seize control of the browser and its search functionality.

Speed flying is a sport that emphasizes rapid forward flight, with typical speeds ranging from about 30 to 153 kilometers per hour (20–95 mph). It requires operating in very close proximity to the slope and surrounding obstacles, a condition that heightens the potential for hazardous incidents. The activity carries substantial risks of injury and death. As of March 2024, 93 pilots worldwide had died from injuries associated with speed flying since 2006.

Speed flying is a high-risk activity that, over the period from 1994 to 2019, was associated with 91 BASE jumping fatalities, of which 51 occurred in the Lauterbrunnen valley. In 2017, the estimated worldwide population of BASE jumpers stood at approximately 2,800, indicating a relatively small but globally distributed community of participants.

Among the Celts, the dominant weapon was a long, single-edged or双-edged sword optimized for edge cutting rather than stabbing, as described by Polybius (2.33). Classical authors such as Polybius and Plutarch also claim that Celtic warriors frequently had to pause in battle to straighten bent blades, a point that has been questioned by some archaeologists. Noric steel, produced in the Norican region, gained renown within the Roman Empire and was widely employed to arm Roman troops. In The Celtic Sword (1993), Radomir Pleiner argues that metallographic evidence partially supports Polybius’s claim, estimating that roughly one third of surviving swords may have exhibited behavior requiring blade realignment. Beyond the long slashing swords, Celts also utilized spears and specialized javelins as components of their broader weaponry.

Scholars have limited reliable sources on how Celts conceived gender roles. Archaeological evidence suggests that Celtic social norms may have differed from those of the Greco‑Roman world, which tended to be less egalitarian. In northeastern Gaul, certain Iron Age burials appear to indicate that women could participate in warfare during the early La Tène period, though the interpretation remains tentative. Some interments feature individuals accompanied by both female‑type jewelry and arms, with the Vix Grave in northeastern Gaul cited as a notable example. Debates persist about the gender designation of some weapon-buried individuals. Some researchers argue that the presence of weaponry signals high social status rather than a straightforward masculine identity. Overall, while archaeological finds point to varied gender conventions and possible warrior roles, firm conclusions about Celtic gender roles remain elusive.

Suffs, a musical, was initially titled Suffragist during its development. It was planned to premiere at the Public Theater in fall 2020, with a cast that would have included Stephanie Hsu and Kate Wetherhead. The premiere was delayed due to the COVID-19 pandemic. A later plan slated the production to open at the Delacorte Theater as part of the Public Theater’s Shakespeare in the Park return the following summer. Ultimately, the decision was made to push the production to 2022.

Suffs presents the internal tensions of the suffrage movement by following Ida and Mary Church Terrell (along with Phyllis) as they contend with divergent tactics—Ida endorsing direct action and Mary advocating dignified agitation—creating a rift even as they both work to elevate Black voices, a dynamic highlighted as Terrell's Theme. The film also chronicles the Woman Suffrage Procession, which faces violent counterprotests yet persists to complete the march, underscoring a persistent demand for equality. Doris experiences distress after being derided as a “bitch” by counterprotestors, and is urged by Alice, Ruza, Inez, and Lucy to embrace the slur as a sign of strength against sexist men, an arc labeled the Great American Bitch. Carrie extends backing from NAWSA to the newly formed Congressional Union for Woman Suffrage, which comprises the march organizers, though she and Alice continue to disagree on strategic approaches. The CU travels to the White House for a meeting with President Wilson, whose response offers only lip service and condescension, with his public stance shifting only later, as depicted in the Ladies segment. In response, Alice proposes NAWSA withdraw its support, but Carrie resists antagonizing Wilson on the grounds that he has pledged to keep the United States out of the European war, shaping ongoing strategic calculations within the movement.

Fought during the 1812 campaign of the Napoleonic Wars near the village of Borodino, the Battle of Borodino remains a pivotal episode in the conflict between Napoleon's Grande Armée and Russian forces. The Bagration flèches on the Borodino battlefield are preserved as enduring physical remnants of the engagement. In addition, a modest memorial has been erected to commemorate the French soldiers who fell in the Battle of Borodino.

Documentation surrounding pivotal battles of the early nineteenth century is frequently incomplete and contested, with the Battle of Waterloo often cited as illustrating these difficulties in reconstructing events. Likewise, numerous campaigns of the War of 1812 in North America face similar challenges to accuracy and interpretation. The Battle of Borodino itself presents its own particular problems of reliability, complicating efforts to establish a definitive narrative. In addition, Borodino has been repeatedly employed to advance overt political purposes, a factor that has further shaped its historiography.

The United States Coast Guard Academy organizes its cadet corps to ensure leadership duties are distributed among all students and to replicate the command structure found on Coast Guard cutters. In this framework, division officers and department heads are staffed by junior officers, providing mentorship and oversight at multiple levels. Within the corps, third-class cadets mentor fourth-class cadets within their divisions, paralleling the relationship between junior petty officers and the most junior enlisted personnel. Second-class cadets function as non-commissioned officers, enforcing regulations and maintaining accountability across cadet units. First-year cadets, known as firsties, hold supervisory responsibilities and oversee mission execution as well as the welfare of those under their command. Exchange cadets from other federal service academies join the corps and participate in activities alongside USCGA cadets, fostering inter-service collaboration.

The United States Coast Guard Academy began with a very small student body, averaging roughly five to ten cadets per incoming class. In 1900 it relocated to Curtis Bay, Baltimore, prompted by changes to its training vessels. A decade later it moved again to Fort Trumbull in New London, Connecticut, an Army installation dating from the Revolutionary War era. In 1914 the institution was renamed the Revenue Cutter Academy. Following the 1915 merger that joined the Revenue Cutter Service with the United States Life-Saving Service to form the U.S. Coast Guard, the academy adopted its current name.

Black Pearls is a studio album by American jazz musician John Coltrane. The album was released in 1964 on Prestige Records, and its contents were recorded in a single session on May 23, 1958 at Rudy Van Gelder's studio in Hackensack, New Jersey.

Don Nelson of DownBeat reviews Black Pearls by noting Coltrane’s commanding technical facility on the saxophone, while also suggesting that he is not yet fully in command of the performance. The critic further emphasizes Coltrane’s total immersion in his music and instrument, highlighting a profound, all-encompassing commitment to his craft.

Gardiol Occitan is the language variety associated with Guardia Piemontese in Calabria, Italy. It is regarded as an outlying dialect within the Occitan family, belonging to the Alpine Provençal branch. According to Glottolog, it is treated as a separate language rather than merely a dialect of Occitan.

Algherese Catalan is a linguistic variety linked to Alghero, a town in northwestern Sardinia. It is a peripheral dialect of the Catalan language, forming a regional variant at the edge of Catalan-speaking areas. It is not listed separately by SIL International.

Landing Zones 1 and 2 are situated at Launch Complex 13, which has been demolished and replaced by two circular landing pads. Each pad has a diameter of 282 feet (86 meters) and features a stylized X derived from the SpaceX logo. Four additional pads, measuring 150 feet (46 meters) across, were planned to enable simultaneous recovery of Falcon Heavy boosters, but only one of these auxiliary pads has been built. The planned infrastructure includes enhanced roadways to facilitate crane movement, a rocket pedestal area, remotely controlled fire suppression systems for landing failures, and a substantial concrete foundation located away from the envisioned trio of future landing pads to attach the booster stage during the transition from vertical to horizontal orientation.

In January 2016, Elon Musk articulated SpaceX’s expectations for Landing Zones 1 and 2, estimating a roughly 70 percent probability that all attempted landings during 2016 would be successful. He anticipated the success rate rising to about 90 percent in 2017, while also cautioning that the company expected a few additional failures as the system was further developed. These statements reflected an optimistic trajectory for the early reusable-launch program and acknowledged the challenges inherent in refining booster recovery operations at the landing sites.

ISO 4 governs the abbreviation of scientific journal titles by using the List of Title Word Abbreviations (LTWA) as the basis for standardized shortened forms. For instance, Journal of Biological Chemistry is rendered as J. Biol. Chem., and Journal of Polymer Science Part A as J. Polym. Sci. A. The standard does not specify a particular approach to capitalization, leaving it unspecified. Although abbreviations are typically indicated with periods, the final punctuation may be omitted in contexts with limited punctuation, in line with the guidance in Section 4.6.

ISO 4 is an international standard whose full designation is Information and documentation — Rules for the abbreviation of title words and titles of publications. It defines a uniform system for abbreviating the titles of serial publications, which are works issued in regular installments, such as scientific journals.

Point Cabrillo Light is a historic lighthouse complex situated roughly 1.5 miles (2.4 km) north of Mendocino, California. The site comprises the lighthouse and several outbuildings, with most of the original structures remaining intact. The barn, however, is no longer present, having been destroyed in 1986 during a fire department training exercise. The surviving components of the lighthouse station are regarded as among the best-preserved light stations in the United States, reflecting a high degree of historical integrity.

Point Cabrillo Light is a lighthouse located in northern California, United States. It sits on the coast between Point Arena and Cape Mendocino, just south of the community of Caspar. The structure has served as a federal aid to navigation since 1909. It is part of the California state park system as Point Cabrillo Light Station State Historic Park.

Cross-contamination refers to the unintended introduction or transfer of contaminants within a system, process, or result, and its meaning in scientific contexts is notably nuanced. The interpretation can depend on whether the contaminant is a solid or a liquid, since the physical state influences how it interacts with materials and processes. Furthermore, the environmental context—such as the surrounding medium, equipment, and workflow—shapes how contamination is defined and assessed. Contaminants may be tangible substances like chemicals, biological agents, or particulates, or they may be more abstract factors, including unwanted energy sources, radiation, or electromagnetic interference that disrupt a process. The following content presents examples of different contamination types based on these variances and other related considerations.

Cross-contamination involving radioactive materials is complicated by terminology that can carry unintended implications; the expression “radioactive contamination” signals only the presence of radioactivity without indicating its magnitude or level of hazard. As a result, the term does not communicate how dangerous the radioactivity is. In practice, radioactivity can be quantified in several ways, including a measured quantity at a specific location, on a surface, or as an areal density per unit area of a surface, with areal measurements commonly expressed per square meter or per square centimeter.
MIPJunior is a spin-off from the MIPCOM trade event. It is staged in the period leading up to MIPCOM and is devoted exclusively to the children's television industry.

MIPCOM is an international marketplace and trade event dedicated to television content, drawing representatives from television studios and broadcasting networks. The gathering functions as a venue for the purchase and sale of new programmes and formats intended for international distribution. In addition, celebrities attend to promote programming, contributing to the event's promotional and networking activities.

In 2022, the International Organization for Migration's involvement in housing refugees in Indonesia drew criticism from the Refugee Council of Australia, which described the role as a "humanitarian veneer" masking rights-violating activities. The assertion was advanced by researchers Asher Hirsch and Cameron Doig and reported by The Globe and Mail, which stated that the alleged rights-violating activities were carried out on behalf of Western nations.

Established in 1951 to address post-World War II displacement in Europe, including internally displaced persons and war refugees, the organization began as a logistics agency tasked with coordinating the transport of nearly one million migrants during the 1950s. Its name has changed several times: PICMME in 1951, ICEM in 1952, ICM in 1980, and finally IOM in 1989. Over time its mandate broadened from logistical operations to a wider remit encompassing migration management, protection, and assistance, reflecting evolving international priorities. As a result, it grew to become the leading intergovernmental organization in the field of migration.

Gere publicly called for a boycott of the 2008 Beijing Olympic Games in September 2007 as a means of pressuring China to pursue Tibetan independence. He later appeared in a Free Tibet-themed Lancia commercial featuring the Lancia Delta. On June 27, 2011, Gere meditated at Borobudur Temple in Indonesia. He is an active supporter of Survival International, an organization dedicated to safeguarding the rights and lands of tribal peoples worldwide.

Richard Gere's interest in Buddhism began in his twenties. He studied Zen Buddhism under Kyozan Joshu Sasaki, and after roughly five to six years of practice, in 1978 he traveled to Nepal with Sylvia Martins. While in Nepal, he encountered numerous Tibetan monks and lamas, enriching his exposure to Tibetan Buddhist traditions. Gere later met the 14th Dalai Lama in India and consequently became a practicing Tibetan Buddhist in the Gelugpa tradition, remaining an active supporter of the Dalai Lama.

HDMI is a digital interface for audio and video that has evolved to increase overall bandwidth by both raising the bitrate of individual data channels and increasing the number of channels. Early HDMI revisions relied on three TMDS data channels, delivering up to 6.0 Gbit/s per channel in HDMI 2.0 or up to 3.4 Gbit/s per channel in HDMI 1.4, complemented by a TMDS clock channel that carried signaling at a fraction of the data rate (about one-tenth up to 340 MHz for 3.4 Gbit/s, or about one-fortieth up to 150 MHz for 3.4–6.0 Gbit/s). In HDMI 2.1, the data-channel signaling rate was raised to 12 Gbit/s. A packet-based data format with an embedded clock allows the TMDS clock channel to be repurposed as a fourth data channel at 12 Gbit/s, producing an aggregate bandwidth growth from 18.0 Gbit/s (three channels × 6.0) to 48.0 Gbit/s (four channels × 12.0), a 2.66× improvement. The introduction of 16b/18b encoding increases data efficiency to 88.8% (versus 80% for TMDS), boosting usable throughput. Consequently, the maximum data rate reaches 42.6 Gbit/s, with an effective usable rate after forward error correction overhead of about 42.0 Gbit/s, roughly 2.92× HDMI 2.0.

HDMI 1.3, released on June 22, 2006, expanded the HDMI specification by increasing the maximum TMDS clock to 340 MHz, yielding a total data rate of 10.2 Gbit/s and a maximum video bandwidth of 8.16 Gbit/s, which enabled high-refresh-rate and higher-resolution displays such as 1920 × 1080 at 144 Hz or 2560 × 1440 at 75 Hz. The update introduced deep color support with 10-, 12-, and 16-bit per color channels (30/36/48 bits per pixel) and added the xvYCC wide color space alongside BT.601 and BT.709. It also permitted the transmission of metadata that defines color gamut boundaries, and offered optional output of Dolby TrueHD and DTS-HD Master Audio for external decoding by AV receivers. In addition, HDMI 1.3 included automatic audio-video synchronization and defined cable categories: Category 1 up to 74.25 MHz and Category 2 up to 340 MHz. The specification also introduced the HDMI Type C (Mini) connector for portable devices.

New York Botanical Garden traces its early roots to 1889, when members of the Torrey Botanical Society proposed locating the planned institution within Bronx Park, in the center of the Bronx in New York City. At that time, the bulk of the land in the area was owned by the Lorillard family. The 1884 New Parks Act authorized the city to acquire land for preservation as areas that would become part of New York City's park system. Accordingly, about 640 acres surrounding the Lorillard estate were acquired by the City of New York as part of Bronx Park in 1888–1889, providing the landscape that would ultimately host the garden.

In 1932, Thomas H. Everett expanded an existing training program at the New York Botanical Garden into a two-year, full-time curriculum designed to train professional horticulturists. The program was patterned after diploma schemes at the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, and the Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. Historically known as the School for Gardeners, it combined formal academic study with practical, hands-on experience. The school experienced a hiatus during World War II and for a time afterward, but otherwise has educated students continuously. Today it is known as the School of Professional Horticulture and isFully accredited. It prepares horticulturists for roles in both public and private gardens, and upon completion graduates receive the New York Botanical Garden Diploma in Horticulture.

Compressed data structures are representations whose size reflects the information content of the data rather than a fixed encoding length. Within this field, succinct data structures constitute a class that, in the worst case, achieves space that is asymptotically close to the information-theoretic lower bound. In general, the storage requirements of compressed structures depend on the particular data being represented. When the data are highly compressible, such as natural language text, these structures can approach the theoretical minimum. Consequently, compressed representations can use substantially less space than many conventional compression schemes for the same data.

Compressed data structures constitute a family of data structures studied in algorithms, data structures, and theoretical computer science. They aim to realize storage that is substantially smaller than conventional representations while preserving operation times that are nearly the same as those of traditional structures for the underlying problem. The space savings are typically closely linked to the information entropy of the data being represented, so that the storage size can approach the information-theoretic lower bound in favorable instances.

Eupleres is a genus that includes two species of mongoose-like euplerid mammals native to Madagascar, where they are commonly referred to as falanoucs. They are predominantly terrestrial and feed chiefly on invertebrates.

Present value of revenues auction (PVRA), also known as the least present value of revenues auction, is a proposed procurement mechanism for privately financed highway projects. In PVRA, bids are made for the total present value of the cash flows generated by the project. The contract is awarded to the bidder with the lowest bid. The winner then collects user fees until the present value of those fees equals the bid amount. The PVRA concept has been proposed specifically for private highway construction.

In August 2007, the V2 Music Group was sold to Universal Music Group for £7 million. Later that year, in October, UMG established a partnership between Fontana Distribution’s U.S. operations (Fontana International) and the London-based Cooperative Music, which encompassed V2 Music. The collaboration aimed to broaden international reach by granting Cooperative Music’s European independent labels access to the American independent market through Fontana International’s marketing, promotion, and distribution networks. Cooperative Music has achieved notable success with acts such as Fleet Foxes, Phoenix, and The Black Keys.

V2 Records Benelux was established in 1997 as the regional arm of the V2 International group founded by Richard Branson, with affiliated operations spanning the United States, the United Kingdom, the Scandinavian countries, Germany, France, Italy, and the Benelux region. In February 2007, managing directors Chris Boog and Tom Willinck completed a management-led buyout in collaboration with Bertus Distribution, a distributor that is part of the Artone Group. The Artone Group comprises V2 Records Benelux, Bertus Distribution, Townsend Music, and Record Industry. V2 Records Benelux maintains offices in the Netherlands, France, Germany, and Belgium.

Maria Ressa's arrest drew widespread criticism from the international community, with many observers viewing the move as politically motivated. As an outspoken critic of President Rodrigo Duterte, Ressa's supporters argued that the case was aimed at silencing her work, while a Malacañang Palace spokesperson denied any government involvement. The lawsuit against Ressa was reportedly filed by private individual Wilfredo Keng.

Maria Ressa joined the Real Facebook Oversight Board on September 25, 2020. The board, an independent watchdog body of 25 members, provides public commentary on Facebook's content moderation policies and examines their influence on civic life.

Missin' Mississippi is a song by Charley Pride that embodies his transition from traditional country toward a country-pop sound that persisted into the early 1980s. The composition was written by Byron Gallimore, Blake Mevis, and Ben Shore and is classified within the country pop genre. It was recorded in April 1984 at Music City Hall, a studio located in Nashville, Tennessee. The track was produced by Norro Wilson, who collaborated with Pride during his final years with RCA Records.

Confederate military leadership drew from a substantial pool of veterans who had previously held commissions in the United States Army or Navy and resigned those federal posts to assume senior positions in the Confederate armed forces. A significant portion of these officers had gained combat and organizational experience during the Mexican–American War, informing Confederate military planning in its early years. Among the most prominent figures were Robert E. Lee, who directed field operations, and Jefferson Davis, who served as the Confederacy's president and overall commander of military affairs. By contrast, some leaders possessed relatively little prewar experience; for example Leonidas Polk, a West Point graduate who had not served in the U.S. Army prior to the conflict.

During the Civil War, Southern churches faced a shortage of ordained Army chaplains within the Confederate Army and responded by sending missionaries to accompany the troops. This expansion of spiritual leadership by denominations helped sustain religious life in the field and contributed to a pattern of recurring revival meetings among Confederate soldiers, reinforcing morale and devotion amid the conflict.

The Pacific Science Association (PSA) comprises national, individual, and NGO/corporate membership categories. National members are typically the adhering organizations represented by each country’s National Academy of Sciences, though some universities within countries that themselves hold national-member status may also be designated as national members; for example, the University of the Ryukyus in Okinawa, Japan is a national member despite Japan’s own national-member status. In addition to national bodies, individual and NGO/corporate memberships constitute an important portion of PSA’s constituency.

The Pacific Science Association (PSA) is a regional, non-governmental scholarly organization dedicated to advancing science and technology to support sustainable development across the Pacific Rim. Established in 1920, the association pursues collaborative scientific activities and capacity-building within the region. Its secretariat is based at the Bishop Museum in Honolulu, Hawaii, United States.

An embolism in liturgical practice refers to a brief concluding prayer appended to certain rites, in which the petitioner requests deliverance from all evils, seeks peace in their days, asks for mercy to be continually free from sin, seeks protection from all disturbances, and expresses the blessed hope in the coming of Jesus Christ, the Savior.

Within the Roman Rite, the embolism is a brief post-consecration prayer that includes a petition for peace in which the Mother of God and the apostles Saint Peter and Saint Paul, along with Saint Andrew, are invoked. The presence of Saint Andrew's name in the Gelasian Sacramentary indicates that Andrew's inclusion in the embolism predates the reforms associated with Pope Gregory I. In the medieval period, the practice expanded as provincial churches and religious orders allowed the celebrant to insert additional saints' names—often founders or patrons—at his discretion, broadening the commemorative scope of the embolism.

During the spring clay season, Sousa advanced to the second round at the Monte-Carlo Masters before losing to Milos Raonic, and he subsequently exited in the early rounds at both the Barcelona Open and the Estoril Open. In Madrid he was eliminated in the second round by Stan Wawrinka, and at Rome he suffered a first‑round defeat to John Isner. At the Geneva Open, he defeated João Souza in the first round in a match noted for the umpire’s nationality-based calls, before reaching his first final of the season where he was defeated by Thomaz Bellucci. In Paris, Sousa overcame Vasek Pospisil in straight sets in the first round of the French Open singles, but was ousted in the second round by Andy Murray, the third seed; in doubles he teamed with Bellucci to lose in the first round to Jamie Murray and John Peers, the 11th seeds. The grass-court season in June brought early exits at the Rosmalen Grass Court Championships, the Queen’s Club Championships, and the Nottingham Open. At Wimbledon, Sousa was eliminated in the first round of the singles competition by Stan Wawrinka in straight sets, while the doubles pairing with Santiago Giraldo also exited in the opening round.

During March, Sousa participated in the season’s first two Masters 1000 events. At the BNP Paribas Open, he was eliminated in the second round by Mischa Zverev. In the Miami Open, where he was the 30th seed and received a bye in the first round, Sousa exited in the second round after a defeat to Fabio Fognini.

Code-excited linear prediction is a speech coding method developed in the 1980s. The original implementation, simulated in 1983 by Schroeder and Atal, required about 150 seconds to encode one second of speech on a Cray-1 supercomputer. Since then, improvements in codebook design and advances in computing power have reduced the computational burden and enhanced performance. These developments have made it feasible to run the algorithm on embedded devices, including mobile phones, broadening its practical applications.

Code-excited linear prediction (CELP) denotes a family of linear predictive speech coding algorithms. It was proposed in 1985 by Manfred R. Schroeder and Bishnu S. Atal. Compared with prior low-bit-rate approaches such as RELP and LPC-based vocoders like FS-1015, CELP offered markedly higher perceptual quality at equivalent bitrates. Over the years, multiple variants have been developed, including algebraic CELP, relaxed CELP, low-delay CELP, and vector sum excited linear prediction (VSELP). Today, CELP and its variants are among the most widely used speech coding methods, and CELP-based techniques are employed in MPEG-4 Audio speech coding. It is important to note that CELP is a generic term for a class of algorithms rather than a single codec.

Recapitulation is a section of a movement written in sonata form, occurring after the development. In this portion, the principal themes first presented in the exposition are restated, typically in the movement’s tonic key, a practice that serves to reaffirm the home key and restore tonal stability.

Recapitulation in music, particularly within sonata form, typically presents a restatement of the exposition’s themes in the home key. In some movements, this recapitulation provides a straightforward echo of the exposition, but many works depart from this simple procedure, a practice evident even among early examples. Departures are achieved through a variety of devices, including the addition of a secondary development section within the recapitulation, alterations in the character or treatment of the original material, changes in the ordering of thematic material, the introduction of new material, the omission of certain ideas, and the overlaying of material that had been kept separate in the exposition. These approaches illustrate the flexibility with which composers treated recapitulations and reflect a broader range of formal experimentation within the sonata form.

The Dallas Sidekicks (1984–2004) refers to the original Dallas indoor soccer club that competed from 1984 to 2004. An expansion franchise bearing the same name commenced play in the Professional Arena Soccer League on November 3, 2012, preserving the legacy of the original team. The expansion club hosts its home games at the Allen Event Center in Allen, Texas.

The Dallas Sidekicks were a professional indoor soccer club based in Dallas, Texas, that operated from 1984 until suspending operations following the 2003–04 season. Founded as a member of the original Major Indoor Soccer League, the team also competed in the CISL, WISL, PSA, and the second MISL over the course of its history. The Sidekicks are best known for featuring the celebrated forward Tatu, whose goal celebrations—most notably tossing his shirt into the stands—became a defining trait of the franchise. They hosted the 1989 MISL All-Star Game and established a reputation as one of indoor soccer’s most successful franchises, making the playoffs in 16 of their 19 seasons and reaching the championship series on eight occasions, where they captured four titles.

Peter Wittgenstein was a Russian general who commanded the right wing of the Russian Army during the War of 1812. He fought in the First and Second Battles of Polotsk, as well as at Chashniki and Smolany. The engagements around Polotsk near Klyastitsy were pivotal in the defense of Saint Petersburg, earning him the sobriquet “Saviour of Saint Petersburg.” For his services, he was awarded the Order of St. George by Emperor Alexander I. During the Berezina campaign in November 1812, Wittgenstein attempted to coordinate with Pavel Chichagov. Subsequently, he aligned with the Prussian army corps under Ludwig Yorck von Wartenburg.

Peter Wittgenstein assumed command of the Russian army during the 1813 campaign after Kutuzov’s death in April, and he led Russian forces at Möckern, where he also directed the Prussian troops. He fought at Lützen and Bautzen in the spring of 1813, and after the defeats of the spring campaign he relinquished overall command of the Russian army. He subsequently commanded an army corps at the Battle of Dresden in August 1813 and at Leipzig in October 1813.

Proponents of Taiwan independence contend that retrocession is invalid because there is no recognized international-law precedent for transferring sovereignty through an instrument of surrender. They cite a declassified CIA report from March 1949 indicating that Taiwan was not part of the Republic of China. They also reference President Truman's June 27, 1950 statement describing Taiwan as having an undetermined status, interpreting this as evidence of Allied views at the time. In 1972 Ng Chiau-tong of World United Formosans for Independence published a legal essay analyzing British Parliamentary records and other documents, concluding that Taiwan's political status remained undetermined.

The article "Retrocession of Taiwan," published in July 2000 in the American Journal of International Law and authored by Jonathan I. Charney and J. R. V. Prescott, presents the view that the Chinese Nationalists, or the Republic of China, began a military occupation of Taiwan in 1945 as a consequence of Japan's surrender. It further maintains that none of the postwar peace treaties explicitly transferred sovereignty over Formosa and the Pescadores to any particular state or government, thereby challenging traditional interpretations of the island's status in the immediate postwar period.

Vierde Klasse (English: Fourth Class) constitutes the ninth tier of football in the Netherlands and the seventh tier within Dutch amateur football. It is the lowest league in the South I region, and the competition is organized into 55 divisions, with 29 scheduled on Saturdays and 26 on Sundays.

Vierde Klasse is a Dutch amateur football division at the lower end of the football league system. Each division typically comprises 12 to 14 teams. The champions are promoted to the Derde Klasse, while the bottom two teams are relegated to the Vijfde Klasse in districts where that division exists. The season is divided into several periods (periodes). The winners of these periods qualify for promotion playoffs, provided they finish in the top nine overall in the season standings. Teams finishing third from bottom at the end of the season take part in relegation playoffs.

i24NEWS, an Israeli news channel, signed an agreement to broadcast in Germany on Kabel Deutschland. It initially reached the United States market through the Jewish Life Television network. After Cablevision was acquired by Altice USA, the Drahi-owned company formerly associated with the Optimum brand, i24NEWS broadened its U.S. distribution across a range of cable and television operators, including Optimum channel 14, Verizon Fios 610, DirecTV 343, U-verse 223, Suddenlink 49, Mediacom 228, Xfinity 1118, and providers such as Spectrum, as well as FuboTV. In addition, i24NEWS is available on multiple streaming platforms, including Amazon Fire TV, Apple TV, Roku, Android TV, and Samsung Smart TV, and its apps are available on both the Android and iOS App Stores.

i24NEWS, the Israeli television channel, unveiled a refreshed English-language programming schedule in November 2025. The lineup includes The Rundown, which airs on a daily basis, Middle East Now focusing on regional developments, and Global Eye covering international affairs. Additional offerings comprise Jewish World Weekly, Innov'Nation, and On The Record, collectively completing the network's updated schedule.

The 1894 Swiss referendums encompassed three separate questions: the right to work, tariffs as a popular initiative, and trade as a mandatory referendum. The first two were launched as popular initiatives, while the third was a mandatory referendum. All three measures required a double majority to be approved, meaning they needed not only a majority of the national popular vote but also a majority of the cantons. Each canton’s vote determined its contribution, with full cantons counted as one vote and half cantons counted as half.

Three referendums were held in Switzerland in 1894. On 4 March, a federal resolution to amend the constitution relating to trade and commerce was rejected by a double majority, failing to secure a majority of both voters and cantons. On 3 June, a popular initiative proposing a right to work was defeated in the nationwide vote as well as by all cantons. On 4 November, a popular initiative calling for a partial cantonal contribution to tariffs was likewise rejected by majorities of both voters and cantons.

One Maritime Plaza is a high-rise office building in San Francisco's Financial District, located near the Embarcadero Center towers at the intersection of Clay and Front Streets. Completed in 1967, the structure was built for the Alcoa Corporation and originally known as the Alcoa Building. It rises to 121 meters (398 feet) with 25 floors of office space, and the surrounding plaza was finished in the same year. The building is notable for being among the earliest to employ seismic bracing through external trusses and X-bracing, reflecting a pioneering approach to earthquake-resistant design in high-rise construction.

Modal voice is the vocal register in which the vocal folds' length, tension, and mass vary in a coordinated way to shape the vibration frequency and, consequently, the perceived pitch. With higher pitches, the folds lengthen, their tension increases, and their edges become thinner, all contributing to a higher rate of vibration. If any one of these three factors remains fixed or if the normal progression among them is disrupted, the laryngeal function can become static, resulting in breaks and noticeable alterations in vocal quality.

Modal voice is the typical phonation register used in everyday speech, produced by coordinated laryngeal muscle activity that sustains a stable glottal configuration during vocal fold vibration. At the lowest pitches, the thyroarytenoid muscles are primarily active, establishing the necessary stiffness and mass for low-frequency vibration. As pitch increases, the cricothyroid muscles engage, lengthening and tensening the vocal folds to raise frequency. The rise in longitudinal tension tends to create a central gap within the glottis. In response, the lateral cricoarytenoid muscles activate to counter this gap by pulling the arytenoid cartilages forward via their muscular processes, a mechanism commonly described as medial compression.

An alternator is a device that converts mechanical energy into electrical energy. It operates by generating a rotating magnetic field that induces an alternating voltage in the stator windings. The electrical current in these windings varies in step with the rotor's position, reflecting the synchronous operation of the machine. Therefore, an alternator is classified as a synchronous generator.

An alternator is a type of electrical generator that produces alternating current, and it can be classified by the number of output voltage phases it provides. This yields either single-phase or polyphase outputs, with polyphase designs used for higher power and more stable operation. Among polyphase configurations, three-phase units are by far the most common in modern power systems due to their favorable performance characteristics, including smoother voltage delivery and improved efficiency of transmission and distribution. Other polyphase arrangements exist as well, such as two-phase and six-phase configurations, as well as higher-phase designs in specialized applications.
Monalysa Alcântara was born in Teresina, Piauí. She began modeling at the age of fourteen. She is a university student studying business administration and fashion.

Monalysa Maria Alcântara Nascimento (born 24 January 1999) is a Brazilian model and beauty pageant titleholder. She was crowned Miss Brasil 2017, becoming the first representative from Piauí and the third Afro-Brazilian descent winner of the national title. Alcântara represented Brazil at Miss Universe 2017, where she finished in the Top 10. Since 2023, she has served as the State Director for the Miss Piauí pageant, guiding the state's participation in the national competition.

Addis Ababa, the capital of Ethiopia, has seen notable urban development in recent years, including the completion of the Abrehot Library in 2022. The library sits on land that was formerly parkland and is located opposite the Parliament Building, placing it within the city’s central governmental and cultural precinct. Upon its opening, it became the largest library in Ethiopia, marking a major expansion of the country’s library infrastructure.

Addis Ababa has historically been connected to Djibouti City by a railway, notable for a French-inspired station. The original line was subsequently abandoned, and in September 2016 a new Addis Ababa–Djibouti Railway began operations, with the modern route running parallel to the former alignment.

ATN Times Now is a Canadian Category B English-language specialty channel owned by Asian Television Network (ATN). The channel broadcasts programming from Times Now alongside Canadian-produced content. It offers live news coverage with a focus on international affairs and breaking news.

In the RFC editing program at USC/ISI, Sandy Ginoza joined in 1999 to focus on RFC editing, followed by Alice Hagens joining in 2005. Bob Braden subsequently assumed the position of RFC project lead, while Joyce K. Reynolds remained a member of the team until October 13, 2006.

Within the RFC framework, Internet Standards are assigned fixed STD numbers, and these identifiers do not change when a standard is updated or replaced; instead, the STD can be associated with different RFC documents over time as revisions occur. A given STD n may be linked to more than one RFC simultaneously and, later, to a different RFC as updates take effect. A concrete illustration involves STD 1: in 2007, RFC 3700 was an Internet Standard designated as STD 1. In May 2008, RFC 3700 was superseded by RFC 5000, RFC 3700 was marked Historic, RFC 5000 attained Internet Standard status, and STD 1 began pointing to RFC 5000. In December 2013, RFC 5000 was superseded by RFC 7100, and RFC 2026 was updated to discontinue the use of STD 1.

Operation Tiger Hound was a United States air campaign conducted during the Vietnam War, with its geographic scope drawn from Laos territory that had already been bombed under Operation Steel Tiger. The decision to establish the operation came at the request of General William C. Westmoreland, the commander in South Vietnam, who regarded the Laotian area adjacent to the five northernmost South Vietnamese provinces as an extension of his operational zone. The proposal received approval from the U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff. Bombing in the newly defined area would be carried out by Republic of Vietnam Air Force aircraft in coordination with United States Air Force units based in South Vietnam, contrasting with Barrel Roll and Steel Tiger, where aircraft were generally based in Thailand.

By late 1968, Tiger Hound operations were incorporated into Operation Commando Hunt, marking the consolidation of aerial operations in Laos. During the period, a total of 103,148 tactical air sorties were flown over Laos, complemented by 1,718 B-52 Stratofortress sorties conducted under Operation Arc Light. In the same timeframe, 132 U.S. aircraft or helicopters were shot down over Laos.

Battery towers are typically circular in plan and capable of housing a substantial number of cannons. The guns could be arranged on several levels and directed in multiple directions, enabling coverage across a wide field of fire. This layered configuration provided a firepower advantage over attackers, who, at best, could bring their own artillery to bear only on the principal line of assault.

A battery tower is a defensive artillery structure characterized by several interconnected levels linked by ramps, allowing cannons to be positioned in a variety of configurations across different elevations. The ramps provide access and flexibility for arranging artillery, while a large number of embrasures furnish firing openings for the cannons.

Paraguayans have long been defined by extensive miscegenation dating to the Spanish colonial era, a pattern that has contributed to one of the most homogeneous populations in South America. The population is currently estimated to be about 75% mestizo, reflecting mixed Spanish and Guaraní descent, around 20% White, with the remaining portion consisting of Indigenous peoples and Afro-Paraguayan communities.

According to a 2020 Instituto Cervantes report titled El Español: Una lengua viva, a substantial portion of Paraguayans demonstrate a solid command of Spanish, comprising 68.2 percent of the population or about 4,946,322 individuals. In contrast, 31.8 percent are categorized as belonging to the Group of Limited Competence with minimal Spanish mastery, totaling 2,306,350 people. Within this Limited Competence group, most are Guaraní speakers who use Spanish as a second language, while 7.93 percent are monolingual in Guaraní.

Following the establishment of the Italian Republic in 1946, Giacinto Carini remained in service with the Marina Militare. In 1953 she was reclassified as a minesweeper. On 31 December 1958 she was struck from the naval list and redesignated as a pontoon under the designation GM 517. As GM 517 she served as a training hulk for the Corpo degli Equipaggi Militari Marittimi (CEMM) at La Maddalena, Sardinia, for several years. Scrapping began in May 1963 after the vessel had been sold.

The Italian destroyer Giacinto Carini remained under repair for the remainder of World War I. By late October 1918, Austria-Hungary had effectively ceased to exist as a functioning state, with its empire rapidly disintegrating. The Armistice of Villa Giusti was signed on 3 November 1918 and took effect on 4 November 1918, bringing hostilities between Austria-Hungary and the Allies to an end. About a week later, the war concluded with the Armistice of 11 November 1918 between the Allies and the German Empire.

In the context of regular polygons, the monogon—defined as a figure with a single side—is regarded as degenerate in ordinary Euclidean space. As a result, many authorities do not classify the monogon as a true polygon. The objections rest on its degenerate nature, the inapplicability of standard polygonal formulas such as perimeter and area, and the fact that its geometry does not align with the formal, abstract definitions of polygons used in geometric theory.

Let a regular n-gon be inscribed in a circle of radius R, with side length s, and denote by Mi the midpoint of the i-th side (i = 1,...,n). For any point P on the circumcircle, the sum of the squared distances from P to the n midpoints satisfies sum_{i=1}^n |P Mi|^2 = 2nR^2 − (n s^2)/4. Moreover, this total is independent of the particular position of P on the circumcircle, remaining constant as P moves around the circle.

Constructed in 1937 as the West Point Bullion Depository, the facility opened in 1938 to store silver bullion. In 1988, it was renamed the West Point Mint and designated as a branch of the United States Mint, with March 31, 1988 marking its official status as a Mint branch. The repository houses extensive deep storage, containing 54,067,331.379 fine troy ounces of gold, and occupies a four-acre (1.6-hectare) parcel of land at West Point, New York.

During the mid-20th century, the New York Central Railroad operated a number of daily passenger trains on the West Shore Railroad that served West Point through its Gothic-style academy station. These services comprised a limited-stop run to Albany as well as local trains to Newburgh and Kingston, with all trains stopping at the West Point station. The passenger service was discontinued in 1958.

Libertarians for Life is a political advocacy organization that promotes a pro‑life interpretation of libertarian principles. The group contends that a fetus has the right to remain in the mother's body, treating that right as a fundamental liberty of the unborn child. It argues that parents do not have the authority to eject a fetus from the womb or to abandon an infant in a crib, thereby risking death. The organization also maintains that both parents owe their child financial support and protection from harm. Through these positions, Libertarians for Life seeks to align libertarian commitments to individual rights with protections for the unborn.

Libertarians for Life is a libertarian advocacy organization that presents its positions as independent of religious dogma, seeking to engage both atheists and theists. It emphasizes science and reason as the foundation of its arguments and frames its positions as grounded in empirical inquiry rather than faith. The group also characterizes its opponents as relying on non-scientific or unreasoned arguments, using this critique to distinguish its approach within libertarian discourse.

In 1980, a strike halted publication of Melody Maker (and NME) for a period, after which Williams left the magazine. Coleman promoted Michael Oldfield, previously on the design staff, to the role of day-to-day editor. For a time, Melody Maker briefly regained its former position, with a cover focused on Jethro Tull’s lineup news rather than features on Andy Warhol, Gang of Four, or Factory Records. During this period, several journalists, including Chris Bohn and Vivien Goldman, departed for NME, and Jon Savage joined The Face. Coleman left Melody Maker in 1981, the same year that the paper’s design was updated. In the early 1980s, Melody Maker experienced low sales and diminished prestige as NME maintained dominance.

In early 1997, Allan Jones left Melody Maker to assume the editorship of Uncut, and was succeeded by Mark Sutherland, formerly of NME and Smash Hits, who edited the magazine for three years. The leadership change coincided with a wave of departures among long-standing writers, many of whom migrated to Uncut. Simon Price departed allegedly in protest against an edict mandating positive coverage of Oasis. The magazine's sales, already substantially lower than NME's, entered a serious decline.

Alpha Motherfuckers is an album released in multiple editions, reflecting regional variations in its track listings. The German limited first pressing includes a bonus disc comprising cover songs that were not part of the standard edition. The United States release adds a single bonus track drawn from the contents of the German limited bonus disc. The Australian edition reproduces the tracklist of the later German editions, sharing an identical sequence of tracks.

Alpha Motherfuckers is a compilation album that gathers contributions from artists affiliated with prominent bands, including Queens of the Stone Age, HIM, Satyricon, and Therapy? It also features performers from punk and hardcore scenes such as The Real McKenzies, The Dwarves, and The Supersuckers. In addition, the release includes several lesser-known Scandinavian artists. The covers were recorded between mid-2000 and May 2001.

Pharisees, first attested in the four Gospels and the Acts, were a Jewish movement within Second Temple Judaism renowned for their careful interpretation of the Torah and their eschatological outlook. The 1st-century historian Josephus lists four principal Jewish sects—Pharisees, Essenes, Sadducees, and Zealots—highlighting the diversity of religious currents at the time. The Essenes are described as generally apolitical and possibly dissident priests opposing certain high-priestly factions. By contrast, the Sadducees are often portrayed as the principal opponents of the Pharisaic movement, while the Zealots represent another distinct faction. In addition to these groups, early Christian communities in Jerusalem and the Therapeutae in Egypt are contemporary currents, though the precise status of these groups within Judaism remains a matter of scholarly debate.

The Pharisees maintained that the Torah expresses a vision in which all Israelites may serve in a priestly capacity, effectively transferring priestly functions from the hereditary priesthood to lay Jews. This interpretation asserts that the Torah provides avenues for every Jew to lead a priestly life, rather than restricting such a life to Temple priests alone. Accordingly, many laws originally directed at the priesthood were generalized to the entire community, including the kosher animal regulations, which were extended to all people, and the prohibition against cutting the flesh in mourning, likewise broadened to encompass all Jews. For the Pharisees, ordinary Jewish life should be permeated by rules and rituals concerning purification, not solely by Temple-centered practice.

The SMILES notation is described extensively in the SMILES Theory Manual, a reference work published by Daylight Chemical Information Systems. The manual includes a range of illustrative SMILES examples to demonstrate encoding techniques. Daylight's Depict utility offers users a means to verify their own SMILES strings, functioning as an educational and validation aid. The depict tool is regarded as a valuable resource for teaching and learning SMILES concepts.

In the Simplified molecular-input line-entry system, the slashes ( / and \ ) indicate the orientation of single bonds adjacent to a carbon–carbon double bond, allowing stereochemical information to be encoded in SMILES-like strings. For example, the difluoroethene isomer can be represented as F/C=C/F to denote the trans form, with fluorines on opposite sides of the double bond, and as F/C=C\F to denote the cis form, with fluorines on the same side.

Harlingerland Frisian was an extinct dialect of East Frisian once spoken in the Harlingerland region. It contributed several linguistic features that originally appeared in Old Frisian, reflecting its transitional role within the Frisian language landscape. The evidence for Harlingerland Frisian is limited to a single 1691 source, Memoriale linguae Frisicae, authored by Johann Cadovius-Müller. Over time the dialect faded away as it was displaced by the Harlings dialect of Low German. In classification, Harlingerland Frisian belonged to the Weser group of East Frisian dialects, alongside the Wursten and Wangerooge Frisian varieties.

Telipok is a town located roughly 15 kilometres north of Kota Kinabalu, the capital of Sabah, Malaysia. It is administered by Kota Kinabalu City Hall and constitutes a sub-district within the city. As part of the urban expanse and metropolitan area of Kota Kinabalu, Telipok forms part of the city's broader urban region. The town is located near the Kota Kinabalu Industrial Park, reflecting its proximity to industrial activity. It lies within 5 kilometres of the towns of Manggatal, Sepanggar, and Tuaran, indicating close geographic relationships with these neighbouring communities.
During World War II, Telipok functioned as a military base from which the Kinabalu Guerrillas operated, under the leadership of Albert Kwok, with the aim of actively opposing Japanese forces.

Testament of Orpheus (Le testament d'Orphée) is a 1960 film directed by and starring Jean Cocteau, in which he portrays a version of himself as an eighteenth-century poet. The production is principally black-and-white, with a brief sequence of color spliced into the imagery. Notable cameos include Pablo Picasso, Jean Marais, Charles Aznavour, Jean-Pierre Léaud, and Yul Brynner. It serves as the final installment of Cocteau's Orphic Trilogy, following The Blood of a Poet (1930) and Orphée (1950).

Testament of Orpheus is a film by Jean Cocteau in which critics describe it as a wry, self-conscious re-examination of a lifetime's obsessions. The work places Cocteau at the center of the mythological and fictional world he had developed across his books, films, plays, and paintings. The film is notable for its frequent double takes, a stylistic feature that reinforces its self-reflective character. In a particular sequence, Cocteau walks past his own image and looks back, a moment described by a scholar as a retrospective on Cocteau's body of work.

Pancho & Lefty is described as a collaboration between two legendary figures in country music. AllMusic reviewer Martin Monkman argues that the album lives up to expectations and, at times, exceeds them, while also feeling like a genuine collaboration in every sense. Robert Christgau notes that Haggard has not sung with so much care in years, attributing this development to Nelson's influence.

Pancho & Lefty is a collaborative studio album by Willie Nelson and Merle Haggard, anchored by the title track written by Townes Van Zandt and recorded late in the sessions. The song tells the story of Pancho, a Mexican outlaw, and his associate Lefty; Pancho is killed after being betrayed by Lefty, who is paid off by Mexican federales. In the Be Here to Love Me documentary, Nelson recalls that the project needed a commercially strong single, a notion reinforced by Lana Nelson, Nelson’s daughter, who proposed performing Pancho and Lefty. She brought a copy of the tune, and Nelson recorded it quickly with his band at night, waking a sleeping Haggard to add his vocal. Townes Van Zandt also appears in the accompanying video, portraying a Mexican federale, an appearance he described in 1994 as a pleasant inclusion. The track rose to the top of the Billboard country singles chart, and a second single, Reasons to Quit, also reached the Top 10.

Qingshui railway station is a railway facility in Taiwan, situated in Qingshui District, Taichung. It is situated on the Taiwan Railways Administration’s West Coast line, also known as the Coastal line. The station is written as 清水車站 in Chinese, with transliterations including Hanyu Pinyin Qīngshuǐ chēzhàn, Tongyong Pinyin Cingshuěi Chejhàn, and Pe̍h-ōe-jī Chheng-chúi Chhia-chām.

Gu Mei was a renowned Chinese courtesan who became the concubine of Gong Dingzi after he paid 1,000 ounces of silver for her services. In 1643 she relinquished her former profession and moved to the capital to join Gong's household. Gong Dingzi's public expressions of affection for her drew considerable attention and were regarded as flouting Confucian norms. Her influence over Gong Dingzi became legendary, according to contemporary accounts. She is credited with saving the poet Yan Ermei from execution and acted as a patron to the artist Zhu Yizun.

Gu Mei, also known as Gu Hengbo, was a Kunqu performer noted for specializing in male sheng roles. She portrayed Zhou Yu (周羽) in the play Disciplining the Son (教子). According to the writer Yu Huai (余懷), after he aided her when she faced legal trouble, she offered to perform a stage drama for him on his birthday.

Pay television services are commonly offered on an à la carte basis, allowing viewers to subscribe to individual premium networks, such as HBO, without subscribing to others like Showtime. Subscribing to a specific service typically grants access to the network’s full lineup of channels and often includes its on-demand catalog, and may also provide access to a companion on-demand streaming service. Most providers also market bundles that group several premium networks (for example, HBO, Showtime, and Starz) at a discounted price to promote subscriber retention or to attract new customers. Trial periods for general-interest or movie-focused premium channels are frequently available, typically lasting one to three months, with rare cases of free trials extending up to a year for newer subscribers.

Pay television is a distribution model in which revenue is generated predominantly through monthly subscription fees paid by individual customers. By contrast, most other multichannel broadcasters rely on advertising revenue and carriage fees from distributors. The subscription-based structure leads pay TV to emphasize programming that justifies the service’s cost, prioritizing content perceived as delivering value for subscribers. This approach aims both to attract new customers and to retain existing subscribers, shaping a strategy focused on subscriber growth and loyalty.

The article provides a compilation of military legions arranged chronologically where feasible. In contemporary practice, legion units commonly recruit individuals who share a defined ethnic, national, religious, or ideological background, a trait often reflected in the legion’s name. Since the Napoleonic era, the term legionnaire has come to denote a recruit who is not a citizen or imperial subject of the government whose armed forces he joins. While governments frequently organize foreign recruits into units bearing the designation “legion,” this practice is not universal.

The Flemish Legion (Dutch: Vlaams Legioen) was a unit listed among the military legions, recruited from Dutch-speaking volunteers in German-occupied Belgium, with recruitment notably concentrated in the Flemish region of Flanders.

Naamyam is a traditional Cantonese vocal form whose repertoire was largely performed in venues linked to sex work, with themes centered on male–female love. A distinct subset, known as Lou Geoi Naamyam, was sung by prostitutes in brothels and opium dens. The term Pipa Zai (琵琶仔) designates girls who primarily played music without providing sexual services. Beginning in the 1930s, Hong Kong banned prostitution and closed brothels and opium dens, leading to the disappearance of Lou Geoi Naamyam.

Dei Seoi Naamyam constitutes a distinctive Cantonese regional form of narrative song performance that rose to prominence in the 20th century amid the flourishing teahouse culture of Canton, Hong Kong, and Macao. Its presentations were commonly held in teahouses as well as on streets and in brothels, and the tradition was traditionally performed by blind singers known as the blind master (瞽師). Notable pieces in the repertoire include the piece commonly rendered as Hegemon-King Bids His Lady Farewell (霸王别姬) along with Nan Siu Yi (男燒衣) and Nui Siu Yi (女燒衣). The art form entered a decline in the late 1920s as Cantonese opera gained popularity, and it was subsequently adapted into Cantonese Opera, where it became known as Hei Kuk Naamyam.

In 2014, the United States Navy announced plans to install a railgun onto a ship by 2016. The weapon was projected to reach ranges exceeding 160 kilometers (approximately 100 miles). Its form factor would resemble a conventional naval gun and would reuse components largely in common with those developed and demonstrated at Dahlgren. The hyper-velocity rounds would weigh about 10 kilograms (23 pounds) and measure 18 inches (460 millimeters) in length, and would be fired at speeds of Mach 7.

In 1999, ARL and IAT collaborated to develop a radiometric technique capable of measuring the temperature distribution of a railgun armature during pulsed discharges without perturbing the magnetic field. In 2001, ARL achieved the first accurate data on electromagnetic gun‑launched projectiles through jump tests. By 2004, ARL researchers published papers addressing the interaction of high-temperature plasmas with the goal of developing efficient railgun igniters. Early ARL publications described the plasma-propellant interaction group and their efforts to distinguish chemical, thermal, and radiative effects of plasmas on conventional solid propellants. Utilizing scanning electron microscopy and other diagnostic methods, they evaluated the influence of plasmas on specific propellant materials.

In the 2010 United States House elections in West Virginia, Republican incumbent David McKinley benefited from a strong Republican mood within the state. He framed the contest as a rebuke of the national Democratic leadership, arguing that the policies of President Obama and Speaker Pelosi did not reflect West Virginia priorities. The campaign tapped into an outsider sentiment that McKinley sought to channel, and it featured frequent attacks on the established Washington political class. In a debate, McKinley charged Oliverio with backing the Pelosi-Obama agenda, while Oliverio responded that he would work with national leaders whose policies aligned with the interests of West Virginians, rather than with Washington leadership.

During the 2010 United States House of Representatives elections in West Virginia, the Democratic challenger Oliverio faced significant intra-party headwinds. His decision not to publicly endorse Nancy Pelosi for Speaker became a sticking point with Democratic leaders, and he only moderated that rhetoric toward the end of the campaign. Oliverio also struggled to secure backing from traditional Democratic labor allies, notably the United Mine Workers of America and the AFL-CIO, which had backed Mollohan and endorsed every other West Virginia Democrat running for Congress except Oliverio. In addition, former West Virginia Secretary of State Ken Hechler launched a political action committee aimed at Oliverio, an effort Hechler had previously pursued in a 2004 bid to primary him.

Gyala Peri, with an elevation of 7,294 metres, is a notable peak associated with the Namcha Barwa Himal range. It is positioned at 29°48′51″N, 94°58′06″E, approximately 22 kilometres north-northwest of Namche Barwa, and lies across the Yarlung Tsangpo River from it. Although it forms part of the Nyenchen Tanglha Shan range, its proximity to Namcha Barwa commonly leads to its inclusion in the Namcha Barwa Himal.

Namcha Barwa Himal, also referred to as the Namjagbarwa syntaxis or the Namjagbarwa Group Complex, constitutes the easternmost segment of the Himalaya in southeastern Tibet and northeastern India. It spans roughly 180 kilometers in length. The region extends from the headwaters of the Siyom River on the international boundary northeastward into Tibet, terminating at the canyon of the Yarlung Tsangpo, which becomes the Brahmaputra in India. While the Himalaya are said to end at the Yarlung Tsangpo canyon, the Hengduan Mountains along the China–Myanmar border continue about 300 kilometers further east.

Buffalo, Missouri features two sizable municipal parks and an extensive network of trails and sidewalks. The trail system connects Buffalo Prairie Middle School to the south with the new city park situated to the north, spanning across town.

Buffalo, Missouri, was platted in 1841 and derives its name from a Buffalo Skull marker erected at the intersection of present-day highways 65 and 32, which marked the native homeland of one of the area's earliest settlers. A post office has operated in Buffalo since 1846.

Per capita is a statistical term that denotes a value on a per-person basis, typically obtained by dividing a total amount by the size of the population. Its Latin origin is per caput, which translates to "per head" and reflects the concept of distributing an aggregate measure among individuals. As a common convention, per capita figures are used to facilitate comparative analysis of quantities such as income, expenditure, or output across different groups or regions by standardizing totals to an average per person.

Per capita is a method of estate distribution in which each named beneficiary receives an equal portion of the devise or bequest. In contrast, per stirpes allocates the estate by the branches of the family, with each branch receiving an equal share (the Latin term stirpes is used to denote this approach). The two methods differ in how shares are allocated among individuals and branches, with per capita focusing on individual beneficiaries and per stirpes on lineage-based divisions. The 2-0 rule is a statistical principle applied in per capita calculations to determine which group has the larger per-person allocation; under this rule, the largest per-capita group is identified as the one that combines the greatest overall size with the largest count of objects, producing a 2-0 result.

Civil War Roundtables (CWRTs) are local groups dedicated to the study and discussion of the Civil War, with no single national body coordinating or publicizing all CWRT activity. The Civil War Roundtable Congress has played a supportive role for many chapters and maintains information for interested participants at www.cwrtcongress.org. Most CWRTs meet on a regular basis, often with on-site or nearby dining options, and these gatherings typically announce local Civil War history-related events while featuring a guest speaker who may be a scholar, professor, author, artist, park ranger, preservationist, reenactor, or other expert. In addition to presentations, meetings frequently include raffles, book signings, door prizes, auctions, fundraisers, and similar activities. Some CWRTs also sponsor battlefield preservation efforts, battlefield walks, excursions, tours, and other sanctioned events.

Civil War Round Tables (CWRTs) are independent organizations dedicated to promoting interest in the study of Civil War history, including its military, political, and sociological dimensions. The Civil War Round Table of Chicago, established in 1941 and based in Chicago, Illinois, is recognized as the oldest CWRT in the United States. Following closely are the Milwaukee CWRT (founded in 1947) and the Atlanta CWRT (founded in 1949), both among the earliest chapters. The DC CWRT, founded in 1951 by Bruce Catton and others, likewise contributed to the early growth of the movement. Today, there are hundreds of CWRTs across the United States, with additional groups operating in other countries.

Animals exhibit an extraordinary range of body sizes. The blue whale (Balaenoptera musculus) is the largest animal ever documented, reaching up to about 190 tonnes in mass and 33.6 metres in length. Among today’s terrestrial mammals, the African bush elephant (Loxodonta africana) is the largest, with individuals weighing as much as around 12.25 tonnes and measuring roughly 10.67 metres long. In the fossil record, the largest terrestrial vertebrates were titanosaurs, such as Argentinosaurus, estimated at about 73 tonnes, while Supersaurus may have approached 39 metres in length. On the opposite end of the spectrum, some organisms are microscopic; for example, Myxozoa are obligate parasites within cnidarians and never exceed about 20 micrometres in size. Among the smallest described species is Myxobolus shekel, which reaches a full grown size of roughly 8.5 micrometres.

Extremely small placozoans lack a fixed digestive cavity, exhibit no symmetry, and present a morphology that superficially resembles amoebae. The phylogenetic placement of placozoans remains ill defined and is the subject of ongoing research.

ISO 3166-2:DE is the designation used to define the codes for Germany’s 16 federal states (Länder). The standard employs the German terms Land for the singular and Länder for the plural. Each code is composed of two parts separated by a hyphen, with the first part being DE, the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code for Germany, and the second part consisting of two letters derived from the name of the respective Land.

ISO 3166-2:DE serves as Germany’s entry in the ISO 3166-2 standard. ISO 3166-2 constitutes a component of the broader ISO 3166 framework, published by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). The standard provides codes for the names of the principal subnational divisions of every country that carries an ISO 3166-1 code, such as states or provinces.

The Grumman E-2 Hawkeye has served in carrier-based airborne early warning and command-and-control roles. In August 1981, an E-2 Hawkeye from VAW-124 "Bear Aces" directed two F-14s from VF-41 "Black Aces" in an intercept mission over the Gulf of Sidra, resulting in the downing of two Libyan Su-22 aircraft. Six years later, Hawkeyes from VAW-123 aboard the USS America directed a group of F-14s on combat air patrol during Operation El Dorado Canyon, the joint strike by two carrier battle groups in the Mediterranean against Libyan targets.

During the mid-1980s a number of Grumman E-2C Hawkeye aircraft were assigned to the United States Coast Guard and to the Customs Service for counter-narcotics and maritime interdiction missions. The Coast Guard subsequently built a small naval flight officer (NFO) cadre by absorbing Navy NFOs with E-2 flight experience and by training Coast Guard officers to serve as NFOs. Following a fatal mishap involving an E-2C on August 24, 1990, at Naval Station Roosevelt Roads in Puerto Rico, the Coast Guard halted E-2C operations and returned the aircraft to the Navy. The Customs Service similarly withdrew its E-2Cs from service and redirected its counter-narcotics efforts toward former Navy P-3 Orion aircraft.

Isabelle Huppert's early screen career included a series of notable performances in 1975 and 1976. In 1975 she appeared in Yves Boisset's drama The Common Man, which was awarded the Silver Bear Grand Jury Prize at the Berlin International Film Festival. That year she also starred in the American action thriller Rosebud, directed by Otto Preminger, opposite Peter O'Toole and Richard Attenborough, and played the title role in Aloïse, a drama that premiered at the Cannes Film Festival. In 1976 she appeared in Bertrand Tavernier's The Judge and the Assassin, and in Christine Lipinska's I Am Pierre Riviere.

Isabelle Huppert's work in the early 2010s included a prominent presence at the 2012 Cannes Film Festival as one of two Palme d'Or contenders—Michael Haneke's Amour and Hong Sang-soo's In Another Country—with Amour ultimately securing the prize. In 2013 she expanded her stage work with a co-starring role in Sydney Theatre Company's The Maids, a Genet drama featuring Cate Blanchett and Elizabeth Debicki, directed by Benedict Andrews in a new English translation prepared by Andrews and Andrew Upton.
