The production continued to tour in 2014, reaching New York as part of the Lincoln Center Festival. Critical reception highlighted the performances of Blanchett and Huppert, with Marilyn Stasio of Variety describing Huppert's Solange as the sharper, more nuanced, and more bitterly ironic observer compared with Blanchett's Claire. In film, Huppert remained active, appearing in works such as The Disappearance of Eleanor Rigby (2013), Macadam Stories (2015), and Louder Than Bombs (2015).

The Sovereign Wealth Fund Institute (SWFI) provides access to its research and data through a subscription model. Its client base comprises asset managers, banks, researchers and universities, governments, institutional investors, asset owners, corporations, law firms, and other entities. The SWFI Subscription product is available at www.swfi.com.

The Sovereign Wealth Fund Institute (SWFI) is an American research and data organization that analyzes public asset owners, including sovereign wealth funds and other long-term governmental investors. In its early years, the institute concentrated on sovereign wealth funds alone, but it subsequently broadened its scope to encompass a wider range of public institutional investors. It operates as a financial data vendor, offering subscription services and API/data-feed products, and it also provides information to the media.

Highest median voting rules encompass Bucklin's rule and its reversal, often called Anti-Bucklin. Bucklin's method ranks candidates according to the inverse of their number of opponents, so that a candidate facing fewer rivals is given higher priority. By contrast, the Anti-Bucklin variant selects the candidate with the largest share of supporters, effectively reversing Bucklin's criterion. Consequently, Bucklin tends to favor candidates with less opposition, whereas Anti-Bucklin emphasizes candidates who enjoy broader backing.

Highest median voting rules are electoral procedures in which voters provide evaluative scores for candidates rather than producing a full rank-order. The winner is the candidate whose median evaluation, calculated across all ballots, is the highest. Because these rules rely on cardinal judgments and use the median as the summary statistic, they circumvent Arrow's impossibility theorem, which applies to certain ordinal aggregation schemes. They satisfy the unanimity criterion and the independence of irrelevant alternatives, ensuring that unanimous support for a candidate yields that candidate's victory and that the outcome depends only on the evaluations of the candidates under consideration. However, they fail to satisfy the near-unanimity criterion, meaning that a scenario with broad but not universal agreement may not guarantee the chosen candidate aligns with that near-consensus.

OmniROM is an open-source operating system for smartphones and tablets built on the Android platform. The project brings together a number of prominent developers, many of whom have previously contributed to other projects.

In 2013, Russell Holly of Geek.com described OmniROM as a premier Android tweaking ROM. A later review characterized OmniROM as a community-focused Android build designed to support as many devices as possible while frequently adding new features.

Afro-Brazilians faced a system of slavery in Brazil that only ended when enslaved people fled en masse and organized resistance against their masters and the legal framework supporting bondage. A striking example of collective action occurred when more than 20,000 enslaved individuals joined the quilombo at Jabaquara near Santos, turning it into a focal point of abolitionist agitation. On May 13, 1888, the Lei Áurea formally recognized abolition by law, effectively legitimating an outcome already achieved through mass revolt and thereby preserving public authority.

Afro-Brazilians are Brazilians whose ancestry is entirely or predominantly Sub-Saharan African, and they are commonly referred to as Black Brazilians. While most multiracial Brazilians carry some African ancestry, perceptions of Black identity in Brazil often correlate with the visibility of African features, with those exhibiting more pronounced African traits typically being perceived or self-identifying as Black, whereas individuals with less noticeable African features may not be categorized as Black. The term Afro-Brazilian is infrequently used by Brazilians as an explicit ethnic label, and it does not figure prominently in informal discourse.

Big Machine Label Group, which originated as Big Machine Records, played a key role in Taylor Swift’s early career by releasing her first recording, the single “Tim McGraw,” and her debut album Taylor Swift. In 2006, an affiliate named Keith ended his association with the label. In November 2014, reports identified Keith as an equity stakeholder in the company alongside the Swift family and Scott Borchetta. That same year Borchetta was described as owning a 60 percent stake in the company. Earlier, in October 2012, Borchetta stated that Taylor Swift’s father, Scott Swift, owned a 3 percent share of Big Machine.

On January 12, 2015, Zac Brown Band announced a four-way strategic partnership for its fourth studio album, involving Southern Ground Artists, Big Machine Label Group, Republic Records, and John Varvatos Records. Under the arrangement, marketing and distribution duties were assigned to Big Machine Label Group, radio promotion to Southern Ground Artists, non-country radio formats and international promotion to Republic Records, and branding and styling to John Varvatos Records.

The King's Guard is a ceremonial unit based in London whose guard-change ceremony takes place in the forecourt of Buckingham Palace at 11:00 am. In the early summer months, the change occurs daily, whereas outside that period it takes place four times per week.

Until 2001, sentries were stationed permanently on the Esplanade at the castle entrance to guard the Honours of Scotland, with changes in shifts occurring hourly. The permanent castle guard was abolished as part of army cutbacks. The 2003 defence review reorganised the infantry so that the 1st and 2nd Battalions of the Royal Regiment of Scotland—the Royal Scots Borderers and the Royal Highland Fusiliers—were permanently based in Edinburgh and rotated between 19 Light Brigade and 52 Infantry Brigade, with the battalion assigned to 52 Brigade taking responsibility for Edinburgh’s public duties. In the 2010 defence review, the 5th Battalion, Royal Regiment of Scotland was reduced to an incremental company, establishing a public duties unit permanently based in Scotland, analogous to the Foot Guards in London.

Multiple integrals generalize the notion of integration to functions of several variables. For a positive function of a single variable, the definite integral corresponds to the area between the graph of the function and the x-axis. If the function depends on two variables and is positive, the double integral computes the volume beneath the surface z = f(x, y) over its domain in the xy-plane, bounded above by the surface and below by the plane z = 0. When additional variables are involved, the corresponding higher-dimensional integral yields the hypervolume of the associated multidimensional region.

The original two-variable function is f(x, y) = (x − 1)^2 + √y. A change of variables is performed by defining u = x − 1 and v = y, with the inverse relations x = u + 1 and y = v. In these new coordinates, the integrand is rewritten as f2(u, v) = u^2 + √v.

Bake-out is a post-construction procedure that uses elevated temperatures to drive volatile organic compounds from building components such as paints and carpets. VOCs are solvents left behind in materials after installation. The technique aims to reduce odors and improve indoor air quality by removing these compounds. The process involves raising the interior temperature significantly above normal levels for an extended period, which causes the VOCs to volatilize and enter the indoor air. The resulting vapors are then vented to the exterior atmosphere to remove them from the interior environment.

Bake-out is a manufacturing process used in physics and vacuum engineering. It is employed in fields such as particle accelerators, semiconductor fabrication, and vacuum tubes. The procedure involves placing a component inside a vacuum chamber, or in its operating vacuum, and heating it with built-in heaters. The applied heat drives off adsorbed gases and contaminants, which are continuously removed by the vacuum pumps operating during the process. In some cases, a low-hydrogen anneal, commonly referred to as hydrogen baking, is used to reduce or remove hydrogen from bulk stainless steel components.

CNET en Español was launched by CBS Interactive on September 19, 2013 as a Spanish-language sister site to CNET, intended to reach Spanish-speaking technology enthusiasts with a fresh perspective on technology. The publication was headed by managing editor Gabriel Sama, and featured a strong reviews section led by Juan Garzon, alongside news coverage and tutorials. Following Red Ventures' acquisition of CNET, the Spanish-language edition was closed, with the closure announced on November 11, 2020. The shutdown removed what had been the largest Spanish-language technology site in the United States from the market.

CNET began publishing AI-generated articles in November 2022 with human editors overseeing the content. The practice drew criticism for not disclosing AI authorship and for continuing to use human bylines on AI-generated material until independent investigators uncovered the approach. In January 2023, CNET reviewed those AI-produced articles after many were found to contain serious errors and instances of plagiarism. Reporters said that Red Ventures pressed staff to deliver more favorable coverage of advertisers and to develop sponsored content. Subsequently, about 10% of the workforce was laid off, leading to unionization among employees who argued that AI-generated content posed a danger to their professional reputations. A former staff member even demanded her byline be removed to protect her reputation if AI revised her articles.

Apple's A10 Fusion employs a big.LITTLE architecture in which only one class of cores is active at any given time—either the high-performance cores or the high-efficiency cores—rather than both simultaneously. As a result, software and benchmarks typically report a dual-core appearance. The high-performance cores deliver about 40 percent greater speed than those in the A9. The two high-efficiency cores consume roughly 20 percent of the power of the high-performance Hurricane cores and are used for light tasks such as checking email. A real-time performance controller dynamically assigns tasks to the appropriate pair of cores to optimize either peak performance or battery life. The processor includes 64 kilobytes of L1 data cache and 64 kilobytes of L1 instruction cache, a 3 megabytes L2 cache shared by both core types, and a 4 megabytes L3 cache serving the entire system-on-chip.

The Apple A10 integrates a six-core graphics processing unit clocked at 900 MHz, forming the GPU component of the SoC. It delivers roughly 50 percent higher performance than the A9 GPU while consuming about two-thirds as much power. The design retains the GT7600 GPU core from the A9, but replaces portions of the PowerVR-based architecture with Apple’s own proprietary designs. Additionally, it utilizes half-precision floating-point numbers to boost throughput and reduce energy consumption.

Pisco is a distilled spirit whose origins are contested between Chile and Peru, with both nations claiming it as a national drink. The dispute centers on cultural and historical factors rather than agriculture alone, as each country seeks to demonstrate its national spirit and the long-standing tradition associated with the beverage. A precise geographical designation for branding is unlikely to emerge, and branding labels that explicitly reference a country—such as "Peruvian pisco" or "Chilean pisco"—are also unlikely due to a protective agreement that forbids branding that suggests national origin.

Most production uses a boutique-type distillate, reflecting a focus on select, high-quality outputs. Some varieties, however, are produced via double distillation, carried out in copper or in other materials.

Fe del Mundo was born on November 27, 1911, at 120 Cabildo Street in Intramuros, Manila. She was one of eight children of Bernardo del Mundo, a prominent lawyer from Marinduque who served one term in the Philippine Assembly representing Tayabas, and Paz (née Villanueva; d. 1925). The family home stood opposite the Manila Cathedral. Of the eight siblings, three died in infancy, and an older sister died of appendicitis at age 11. The death of her younger sister Elisa, who had expressed a desire to become a doctor for the poor, inspired Fe del Mundo to pursue a career in medicine.

Fe del Mundo began her higher education at the University of the Philippines Manila in 1926 at the age of fifteen. She earned an Associate of Arts degree in 1928, two years after her enrollment, and then continued at the UP College of Medicine on the same campus. In 1933 she completed her medical degree as the valedictorian of her class, and in the same year she passed the medical licensure examination, ranking third among the examinees. Her observations of pediatric health conditions in rural areas, especially in Marinduque, led her to specialize in pediatrics.

On July 19, 2000, CNET Networks announced its acquisition of ZDNet, bringing GameSpot and the formerly separate Gamecenter under a single corporate umbrella. By December 2000, The New York Times described GameSpot and Gamecenter as leading gaming sites, likening their prominence to that of Time and Newsweek. In February 2001, as part of a broader efficiency drive to reduce redundancies, GameSpot was retained while Gamecenter was shuttered, resulting in a consolidation of the group’s gaming coverage on GameSpot.

GameSpot UK, the British edition of the GameSpot website, was launched in October 1997 and operated as a distinct counterpart to the U.S. site until mid-2002, delivering content tailored to the British market. It earned the 1999 PPAi award for best website and was shortlisted in 2001. PC Gaming World was considered a sister print magazine, with some material appearing on both outlets. Following ZDNet’s acquisition by CNET, GameSpot UK merged with the main U.S. site, and the UK edition was relaunched on April 24, 2006.

Sue Downey is an American beauty pageant titleholder who won the Miss Ohio USA title and subsequently the Miss USA crown in 1965. She then represented the United States at Miss Universe 1965, where she finished as the second runner-up and was awarded the Best National Costume prize.

Sue Ann Downey (born May 8, 1945) is an American former model and beauty pageant titleholder who was crowned Miss USA in 1965. She subsequently competed in Miss Universe 1965, where she finished as the second runner-up.

The earliest amniotes appeared during the Pennsylvanian subperiod of the Carboniferous, evolving from earlier reptiliomorph amphibious tetrapods. They occupied terrestrial habitats alongside insects, invertebrates, ferns, mosses, and other plants, forming ecosystems suitable for land-dwelling life. From these early amniotes two major lineages diverged: the synapsids and the sauropsids. The synapsids would later give rise to the mammalian lineage, whereas the sauropsids came to include turtles, lizards, snakes, crocodilians, and dinosaurs (including birds). A distinguishing feature of synapsids is a single temporal fenestra on each side of the skull, positioned low behind the eye socket. Primitive synapsids included large early Permian predators such as Dimetrodon, illustrating their early ecological roles. Nonmammalian synapsids were historically described as mammal-like reptiles, or pelycosaurs, but they were neither true reptiles nor part of the reptile lineage.

Mammals beyond the monotremes are characterized by two core reproductive adaptations — live birth and lactation — which imply a group-wide variation in parental investment. These adaptations foster differing degrees of care across species, with some lineages building nests or digging burrows and others provisioning and guarding their young for extended periods. Many mammals are considered K-selected, allocating substantial time and resources to fewer offspring relative to r-selected species. In mating, both sexes have a stake in offspring success, though the magnitude of their investment often differs. Female mammals commonly exhibit maternal aggression, a behavioral form of parental care that can target rival females or threats to their young. Alloparental care, where individuals other than the parents help raise offspring, also occurs in several mammal groups. Male participation in child-rearing does occur, though it varies by species; tenrecs show notable paternal involvement, whereas other taxa display limited or no male care. Within primates, patterns of male caregiving vary, as southern pig-tailed macaques typically do not participate in infant care while Japanese macaques may have males that engage in caring for offspring.

Ngātokimatawhaorua, also known as Matawhaorua, is one of the major ocean-going voyaging canoes in Māori tradition. It was employed in the migrations that settled New Zealand, and it remains a component of Māori cultural heritage.

Ngātokimatawhaorua is the name given to Matawhaorua, Kupe’s canoe, who is traditionally regarded as the Polynesian discoverer of New Zealand. On Kupe’s return voyage to Hawaiki, the waka was re-adzed by Kupe and Nukutawhiti, after which it was renamed Ngātokimatawhaorua. The Māori name is understood to mean “the adzes” (ngā toki).

In Nepalese historical scholarship, the Licchavi dynasty’s period is regarded as a golden age in the country’s history. In addition, researchers have published an online table that tracks the evolution of certain Gupta-script characters found in Licchavi inscriptions. This table was prepared by Gautamavajra Vajrācārya.

The list of Licchavi rulers presented in this article has been adapted from The Licchavi Kings by Tamot and Alsop, and the dates assigned to the reigns are approximate, with substantial uncertainty regarding the precise years.

Scholars have challenged the concept of familialism as historically and sociologically inadequate to describe the complexity of actual family relations. In modern American society, the male head of the household can no longer be guaranteed a wage sufficient to support a family. Consequently, the traditional framing of familial responsibility fails to reflect current economic and social realities. Furthermore, 1950s-style familialism is criticized as counterproductive to family formation and fertility.

Familialism in Singapore denotes the pronounced emphasis on family values within political and social life, particularly as promoted by the ruling People’s Action Party. The party, along with its leaders, has maintained that the family constitutes the basic building block of society, a point articulated by prime minister Lee Hsien Loong. Within official discourse, the notion of family is defined as a heterosexual marriage between a man and a woman, with children raised within a stable family unit, a definition that underpins policy design and public messaging aimed at reinforcing traditional family structures.
Hussein Jwayed (Arabic: حُسَيْن جَوِّيْد; born 1 January 1993 in Aleppo, Syria) is a Syrian professional footballer who plays as a right-back for Hutteen.

Tom Wolfe has been widely recognized by peers and critics for his distinctive blend of journalism and fiction, as well as for his incisive social critique. Kurt Vonnegut described Wolfe as one of the most thrilling and provocative journalists of his era, and as a genius willing to push boundaries to attract attention. Paul Fussell praised Wolfe as a superb writer and noted that reading him is exhilarating because it conveys the enthusiasm with which Wolfe perceives reality. Dwight Garner highlighted Wolfe as a brilliantly gifted social observer and satirist, emphasizing his penchant for close and often sharp detail and his willingness to challenge the pretensions of the literary establishment. Harold Bloom referred to Wolfe as a vigorous storyteller and a capable social satirist, while Louis Auchincloss lauded The Bonfire of the Vanities as a marvelous book.

Tom Wolfe adopted wearing a white suit as a trademark in 1962. He purchased his first white suit with the plan to wear it in the summer in the style associated with Southern gentlemen; however, the garment proved too heavy for warm weather, so he wore it in winter, where it drew considerable attention. At that time, white suits were traditionally reserved for summer wear. Wolfe maintained the white suit as a defining element of his public image, occasionally pairing it with a white tie, a white homburg hat, and two-tone spectator shoes. He described the effect as disarming, saying the outfit presented him to others as "a man from Mars, the man who didn't know anything and was eager to know."

The Times Telegram was formed on August 3, 2015, through the merger of The Telegram, which served the Herkimer area, and The Times, which served Little Falls. It is owned by USA Today Co., the company that had owned both predecessor newspapers prior to their consolidation. The Telegram had previously been purchased by Thomson Newspapers in 1965.

The Times Telegram is a historic newspaper whose title has appeared in several forms. The Telegram has also been published under the name The Evening Telegram. Similarly, the publication known as The Times has been issued under alternate titles, including The Evening Times and the Little Falls Evening Times.

Societal views on patents, particularly in the pharmaceutical sector, include ethical objections to patent protection for medicines and the high prices these rights can enable. Such pricing can limit access to essential drugs for poorer individuals in both affluent and less wealthy nations. Critics also challenge the assertion that exclusive patent rights are indispensable for recouping substantial investments in research and development. Additionally, empirical work has shown that marketing expenditures for new drugs often exceed the funds spent on development, with some studies indicating marketing outlays double those devoted to research and development.
In July 2008, Sir John Sulston, a Nobel Prize–winning scientist, called for the creation of an international biomedical treaty intended to address and clarify patent-related issues.

Anthony Joseph Battaglia (born April 10, 1949) is a senior United States district judge of the United States District Court for the Southern District of California. He previously served as a United States magistrate judge for the same court.
Anthony J. Battaglia was chosen in 1993 to serve as a United States magistrate judge for the United States District Court for the Southern District of California.

Joma is a Spanish footwear and sportswear company founded in 1965 by Fructuoso López to manufacture general-purpose shoes. The brand name derives from López's eldest son, José Manuel. In 1968, the firm redirected its focus toward the design, production, and distribution of athletic footwear. It achieved notable success and expanded into the football market, attaining both domestic and international recognition. Joma Sport subsequently opened offices in the United States, Europe, and Asia, extending its global footprint. Today, the company operates in more than 70 countries worldwide.

Qadsia Sporting Club, commonly known as Qadsia SC, recorded a series of mid-table finishes in the early 1980s. In the 1980–81 season, the side placed third in the league and advanced to the Prince Cup quarter-finals, where they were eliminated by Kuwait Club. The 1982–83 campaign saw them finish sixth in the league and take third in the Prince Cup. For the 1983–84 season, Milan Milanić was appointed as coach; the team ended the season fifth in the league and reached the quarter-finals of the Prince Cup. In 1984–85, Muayad Al-Haddad joined from Kheitan Club, and the club again finished fifth in the league, with a fourth-place finish in the Prince Cup.

From 1970–71 through 1978–79, Qadsia SC experienced a period of notable domestic activity and success, with the club securing the Kuwaiti league title for a second time in 1970–71 under Ron Lewin, whose side also exited the cup in the quarter-finals to Al-Arabi on penalties. In 1971–72 the team reached the league playoffs semi-finals and won the Prince Cup for the first time in club history. The 1972–73 season saw a fourth-place finish in Group A with six points and elimination from the league, followed by a Cup quarter-final defeat to Al Arabi. In 1973–74 the club finished third in the league and claimed the Prince Cup by defeating Kuwait SC. The 1974–75 campaign coincided with the Federation Cup's introduction, and Qadsia finished third overall, captured a fifth league title, and won the Prince Cup 2–0 against Kuwait Club, with Faisal Al-Dakhil scoring. The 1975–76 season saw the league title won undefeated, while the Prince Cup final ended in a defeat to Kuwait SC. In 1976–77 the team finished as league runners-up behind Kuwait SC, losing the final 5–3, and in 1977–78 Lewin returned as coach as the club again finished third in the league. The final year, 1978–79, culminated in Prince Cup glory with a victory over Kazma.
The Assistant Secretary of the Treasury for Financial Stability is the head of the Office of Financial Stability, an organizational unit within the United States Department of the Treasury.

The Assistant Secretary of the Treasury for Financial Stability is a position within the United States Department of the Treasury that is filled by presidential appointment with the advice and consent of the Senate. If the office is vacant, the Secretary of the Treasury may appoint an acting Assistant Secretary for Financial Stability to carry out the duties of the office.

Apache Shale was a web application framework maintained by the Apache Software Foundation. It was based on JavaServer Faces, leveraging its component-based model for building user interfaces. In May 2009, the project was retired and placed in the Apache Attic.

The Peace of Acilisene, dated circa 387 (between 384 and 390), was a treaty between the Eastern Roman Empire and the Sasanian Persian Empire that partitioned the former Kingdom of Armenia and established a defined frontier. The boundary stretched from just east of the city of Karin, which would later be renamed Theodosiopolis, to the southwest of Nisibis in Mesopotamia. As a consequence of the accord, East Roman influence along the border increased, while approximately four-fifths of the old Armenian kingdom remained under Persian rule.

Following Rome’s eastern consolidation, the Senate minted coins bearing a Latin inscription signaling that Armenia and Mesopotamia had been brought under Roman authority, thereby establishing Armenia as the empire’s newest province. This administrative move occurred alongside the quelling of a rebellion led by the Parthian claimant Sanatruces, though pockets of resistance persisted in the frontier regions after the suppression. In the wider regional struggle, Vologases III of Parthia secured a southeastern portion of Armenia just before Emperor Trajan’s death in August 117, underscoring the continuing contest for influence in the area.

Leamington, Ontario, is home to a large marina that serves as a central hub for sailing and a variety of water-based activities. A promenade along the marina extends from the harbor facilities to the Historical Leamington Dock, which functions as a port for ferry services to Pelee Island. These ferries operate on vessels including the Jiiman and the Pelee Islander II.

According to a 2006 survey, Leamington had 7,485 immigrants or migrants and 19,365 native-born residents. The migrant population predominantly originated from Mexico and Jamaica, with many workers employed as seasonal farm laborers under Canada's Temporary Foreign Worker Program. A separate 2006 census found that Leamington had the highest share of Latin Americans in Canada, accounting for 4.9% of the population.

Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń took on its modern form during the 19th century. At the time of the partitions of Poland, the Prussian government envisaged establishing a University of Theology in Toruń, which would have encompassed faculties of law and economics; however, the proposal did not materialize.

During the interwar years, local authorities in Toruń pursued the creation of a university as a means to expand higher education in the region. With the annexation of Pomerania to the reconstituted Polish state in 1920, these efforts were intensified. Even before 1920, the Supreme People’s Council considered establishing higher education institutions in Polish territories annexed by Prussia, including both Gdańsk and Toruń. However, amid unfolding political developments and uncertainties regarding Pomerania’s future, the council accepted the December 1918 Sejm resolution to overlook Toruń as a location for a new university. The Sejm resolution redirected efforts toward developing a university in Poznań.

Pseudocode is a method of representing the steps of an algorithm through a hybrid notation that blends elements of programming syntax with informal, self-explanatory descriptions. It is designed for human readers rather than for execution by computers. Because it omits details required for actual implementation in a specific programming language, verification of correctness is typically performed manually. The notation often augments formal constructs with natural-language clarifications or concise mathematical expressions. Its primary aims are to convey the algorithm’s logic more clearly than conventional source code and to provide an environment-independent description of the algorithm’s core principles. Consequently, pseudocode is widely employed in textbooks, in scientific publications, and during the planning stages of software development and other computational procedures.

Pseudocode is a high-level, human-readable description of an algorithm that conveys its logic without committing to a particular programming language. In the broader context of mathematical notation, non-ASCII typesetting is normally employed to render equations, with widely used systems including TeX, MathML, and various proprietary formula editors.

Double Live is the first live album by American country music singer Garth Brooks. Released on November 17, 1998, the record comprises a two-disc compilation of live performances. The recordings were captured during Brooks's world tour, which spanned from 1996 to 1998.

Double Live, a live album by Garth Brooks, has been issued in several variations since its original release, featuring different packaging and occasionally revised track lists to reflect particular performances or tours. Notable variants include an initial edition with unique artwork, Reunion Arena ’91, Texas Stadium ’93, World Tour I and II, Central Park ’97, Dublin ’98, USS Enterprise ’01, The Last Show, and Off-Stage. In 2014, a 25th Anniversary Edition was released, presenting a new cover, additional bonus tracks, and a DVD. This edition was issued to promote the digital remaster and Brooks' digital music distribution via GhostTunes.

Within Mahayana Buddhism, Bodhisattvayāna denotes the path often described as the Great Vehicle. It is also referred to as the Great (Causal) Vehicle and as the Vehicle of Enlightened Beings. The aim of this path is to attain full enlightenment for the sake of liberating all sentient beings from Saṃsāra, the cycle of birth and death.

Internal administration within the Nyingma tradition would revolve around the heads of its six principal monasteries—Kathok, Dzogchen, Shechen, Mindrolling, Dorje Drak, and Palyul. The decision was unanimous. Representatives are appointed for three-year terms at the annual Nyingma Monlam.

In numerous nineteenth-century editions of Mozart's Piano Sonata No. 17, a violin accompaniment is printed alongside the piano, though the source of this line remains unclear. The piano part itself is identical to the solo version, implying that the violin line may have been introduced later rather than by Mozart. The Neue Mozart-Ausgabe (NMA) attributes the violin accompaniment to an addition by either Johann Anton André or Johann Mederitsch, rather than to Mozart himself.

Piano Sonata No. 17 (Mozart) was commissioned by the court of Frederick William II of Prussia for Princess Frederica and is part of a set of six relatively accessible piano sonatas. The commission was placed in May 1789, and the work was produced during Mozart's Berlin journey.

Alfred Music's Ensemble Development for Concert Band is a program consisting of exercises designed to help students develop musical concepts and to establish the foundational qualities required for proficient performance in a concert band setting.

Alfred Music is an American music publishing company that was established in New York in 1922. It is headquartered in Van Nuys, California, and maintains additional offices in Miami and New York, along with international branches in Germany, Singapore, and the United Kingdom.

Global LGBTQIA+ Employee & Allies at Microsoft (GLEAM) took on a more formal organizational structure in 1993, establishing a defined presence within the company’s diversity initiatives. The group was organized under Microsoft’s Diversity Advisory Council, integrating its activities with the broader framework of corporate diversity governance. This development occurred alongside other employee resource groups, such as Blacks at Microsoft (BAM) and the women’s group Hoppers, along with additional affinity networks pursuing similar aims.

GLEAM (Global LGBTQIA+ Employee & Allies at Microsoft) lobbied Microsoft to extend health insurance and other benefits to the same-sex domestic partners of its employees. The advocacy intensified after Lotus Software began offering these benefits to its workers. In 1993, Microsoft added same-sex domestic partner benefits.

After 1860, the expansion of the railway network reshaped the Russian Empire's economy, culture, and daily life by tying distant regions into a broader national system. While central authorities and the imperial elite retained most of the decision-making power, local elites pressed for additional rail linkages. Local nobles, merchants, and entrepreneurs viewed railways as a means to advance regional interests and to anchor their locality within the empire. They frequently competed with neighboring cities to secure rail connections. By imagining their place within a national rail network, local actors came to see themselves as integral to the empire's economic framework.

Alexander I's accession in 1801 was widely interpreted as an opening to liberal Enlightenment ideas, with promises of reforms that, in practice, were limited before 1820. After 1820 attention drifted toward foreign policy and personal religious matters, and reform efforts waned. The empire sustained a comparatively small bureaucracy of roughly 17,000 officials, concentrated primarily in Moscow and Saint Petersburg. Modernizing the state required a larger administrative apparatus and an educational system to train officials; however, Russia lacked such a framework, with university education often taking place abroad in Western Europe. The army and the church maintained their own, narrowly focused training programs. Within this context, the most significant successful reform of Alexander I's tenure was the creation of a national system of education.

Nanping features a rugged terrain with prominent, soaring peaks and extensive low mountain ranges. Interspersed among these are river valleys and small basins, contributing to a varied relief. The landscape embodies a southern Chinese geomorphic pattern commonly described as many mountains surrounding a single river and a single plain, underscoring the predominance of hills and mountains in the area.

Nanping is served by a network of sixteen high-speed railway stations, including Wuyishan North Station, Yanping Station, Nanping City Station, Jianou West Station, Yanping West Station, Wuyishan Station, Jianyang Station, Jianou Station, Yanping East Station, Songxi Bus Station, Zhenghe Station, Jianou East Bus Station, Shaowu Station, Guangze Railway Station, Laizhou Station, and Shunchang Station.

Sub-band coding is an audio compression technique that starts with a digital filter bank that splits the input signal's spectrum into several subbands, typically around 32. A psychoacoustic model assesses the energy in each subband and in the original signal in order to establish masking thresholds for perceptual encoding. Each subband is then quantized and encoded so that the introduced quantization noise remains below its masking threshold. The quantized subband samples are subsequently organized into frames to enable smooth playback by a decoder.

Sub-band coding is a signal processing approach in which the decoding stage is typically easier than encoding. The decoding process does not involve a psychoacoustic model. During decoding, frames are unpacked and the subband samples are decoded, after which a frequency–time mapping reconstructs the output audio signal.

Darts regulations were introduced to harmonize discrepancies in throwing distances observed between the United Kingdom and the rest of the world. To reconcile these differences, authorities established a standard playing length of 2.37 metres (7 feet 9 inches) from the throwing line to the dartboard, serving as a compromise intended to unify competitive play.

Dart points are the tips of darts and are typically produced in two common lengths, 32 mm and 41 mm (about 1.3 and 1.6 inches). To improve grip and control, many points feature knurled surfaces or protective coatings. Some designs, moreover, are built to retract slightly upon impact, a feature intended to reduce the likelihood of bounce-outs by ensuring firmer engagement with the board.

John Hyungseung Chun (born 1970) is an American lawyer and jurist from Washington state who serves as a United States district judge for the Western District of Washington. He previously served as a judge on the Washington State Court of Appeals, Division One, from 2018 to 2022.

John H. Chun was appointed in 2018 by Governor Inslee to serve on the Washington State Court of Appeals, Division One. He ran unopposed to retain his seat in the November 2019 retention election. His tenure on the state judiciary ended when he was commissioned as a federal judge.

Bithynia, in the Hellenistic period, was an autonomous kingdom established in the 3rd century BCE. Its capital, Nicomedia, was rebuilt in 264 BCE on the site of the ancient Astacus by Nicomedes I. In 74 BCE, the kingdom was bequeathed to the Roman Republic, and it later united with the neighbouring region of Pontus to form the Roman provincial entity of Bithynia and Pontus.

Bithynia is a historic region in the northwestern part of Asia Minor, corresponding to portions of present-day Turkey. It lies beside the Sea of Marmara, the Bosporus strait, and the Black Sea, giving it notable maritime adjacency. Its boundaries extend to Mysia to the southwest, to Paphlagonia along the Black Sea coast to the northeast, and to Phrygia to the southeast as one moves toward the interior of Asia Minor. In Koine Greek, the region was known as Βιθυνία, and it is romanized as Bithynía.

In the Sasanian Empire, Syriac developed into a prominent language of administration and intellectual life, competing with Greek in significance. Centers of higher learning arose in several cities, notably Mosul, al-Hira, and Harran. Harran is particularly associated with the Pythagorean School of the Sabians. The Grand School in Ctesiphon, the imperial capital, served as the principal center of learning for the era, though detailed records about its operations are scarce. The Academy of Gundishapur stands out as perhaps the most famous Persian scholarly institution, offering instruction in medicine, mathematics, astronomy, and logic. Gundishapur’s academy subsequently influenced the emergence of Baghdad as a major learning center and provided a model that underpinned the first Muslim hospital (bimaristan) established in Damascus.

During the late 18th century, the Austrian composer Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart organized a series of publicly subscribed concerts in Vienna that were designated as academies. The designation helped establish the term as a label for organized musical performances, a usage that persists in modern musical practice. Today, academy-named ensembles and venues remain common, with examples such as the Academy of St Martin in the Fields, a well-known concert orchestra, and Brixton Academy, a major concert hall in Brixton, South London.

Within the history of Islam in Hong Kong, the Happy Valley Muslim Cemetery, located in Happy Valley, stands as a historic burial ground for the Muslim community. The first recorded burial at the site dates to 1828, as documented by the Food and Environmental Hygiene Department. On 15 July 1870, the British Hong Kong government issued a deed of appropriation for the lands surrounding the current cemetery to be used specifically for Muslim burials, formalizing its function as a dedicated cemetery for the community.

Islam in Hong Kong reflects a diverse community shaped by historical migration and intermarriage. An estimated 12,000 Muslim families in the city are described as "local boy" families, descended from early Muslim South Asian immigrants who intermarried with local Chinese communities, including the Tanka, and raised their children within the Muslim faith. Hui Muslims from mainland China have also contributed to the development of Islam in Hong Kong. Kasim Tuet of Guangzhou is recognized as a pioneer in Muslim education in the city, and the Islamic Kasim Tuet Memorial College is named in his honor, representing his influence on religious schooling in Hong Kong.

On March 31, 2022, Akeel Morris re-signed with the Long Island Ducks. He pitched in 24 starts for the Ducks, posting a 6–10 record and a 5.65 ERA. He struck out 96 batters across 122 2/3 innings pitched. Following the season, Morris became a free agent.

On November 6, 2019, Morris was selected by the Long Island Ducks in the New Britain Bees dispersal draft. The 2020 season saw him unable to participate due to the Atlantic League season's cancellation amid the COVID-19 pandemic, and he subsequently became a free agent after the year. He re-signed with the Ducks on May 17, 2021. In three starts for Long Island, he delivered 14 scoreless innings and registered 17 strikeouts.

The James Madison Program in American Ideals and Institutions is an academic initiative directed by Robert P. George. It has been described as not conservative, and it adopts an approach aimed at reconciling competing points of view by bringing them into productive dialogue. The program's stated goal is to raise the level of intellectual debate on campus.

The James Madison Program in American Ideals and Institutions states that it welcomes a broad spectrum of ideological perspectives; however, it is widely regarded as a conservative institute and is described as existing to advance conservative viewpoints on campus. Commentators have pointed to a donor and fellows base that is predominantly conservative. The program has also been associated with platforming figures identified as far-right or extremist.

ISO 1413, published by the International Organization for Standardization as Horology—Shock-resistant watches, specifies the minimum requirements and the testing method for a watch's shock resistance. It is intended for homologation or type-approval testing rather than testing every unit in a production batch. The test replicates a shock caused by a fall of one meter onto a horizontal hardwood surface. The standard has been adopted by numerous countries.

Shock resistance testing for the watch comprises two initial impacts, one at the nine o'clock side and another on the crystal with a vector perpendicular to the face. The shock is delivered by a pendulum-mounted hammer of hard plastic weighing 3 kg, traveling at 4.43 m/s, delivering about 3.7 joules to the watch. The resulting peak acceleration reaches approximately 3100 g (±15%), in a predominantly sinusoidal pulse that lasts around 350 microseconds. Following the first shock, the hour hand displacement must remain under five minutes. After the second shock, the watch must retain timekeeping accuracy within ±60 seconds per day relative to pre-test values. A third shock is then applied on the crown side. The protocol requires that no bending or breaking of components occur as a result of the shocks. A separate free-fall test is conducted on the complete watch in two orientations: crown up with the clasp open, and case back down. For deployant clasps, the clasps are opened but remain under the watch. A trap door releases the watch onto a surface calibrated to reproduce the same shock profile as the impact tests. Throughout the free-fall portion, no components should be broken or lost.

Books in the United States have been shaped by milestones in publishing and retail, including the New York Times Best Seller list, first published in 1931, which has long served as a widely cited measure of popular titles. In the realm of book retail, Amazon.com began operations in July 1995 and is headquartered in Washington state, marking a major development in online bookselling in the United States.

Books in the United States traces its development from the colonial era, when Stephen Daye printed the Bay Psalm Book in Cambridge, Massachusetts in 1640, the first book produced in British North America and a marker of New England’s early role in American publishing. In Philadelphia, William Bradford established the first paper mill and Benjamin Franklin launched his own printing operation, signaling the growth of a regional publishing infrastructure. By the mid-19th century, New York City emerged as the industry’s center, with major houses such as Harper, Wiley, Putnam, and Scribner rising to prominence, aided by copyright protections and expanding distribution networks, although the trade initially relied on pirated British works until international copyright laws were established in 1891. The era also saw the proliferation of dime novels, or affordable paperback fiction, which broadened public access to literature. Professional associations formed to support the field, notably the American Library Association in 1876 and the Bibliographical Society of America in 1904. After World War I a publishing boom followed, bringing new writers and firms to prominence, including Simon & Schuster and Random House, though the Great Depression imposed a downturn that the industry did not fully recover from until after World War II. From the 1960s onward, mergers and consolidation accelerated, a trend aided by online retailers and ebooks; New York City remained a leading global center, housing the major trade publishers—the so‑called Big Five: HarperCollins, Penguin Random House, and Simon & Schuster—alongside large educational publishers such as Macmillan Learning, McGraw-Hill, Scholastic, and Wiley, as well as a diverse array of independent houses. The university-press model took hold earlier with Cornell University Press (1869) and Johns Hopkins University Press (1878), a pattern that encouraged many universities to publish scholarly works by faculty and graduate students. In the 21st century, financial pressures have reduced the output of many university presses, shaping a landscape that remains influential but economically constrained.

Within libertarianism in the United States, the distinction between left and right is often treated as imprecise, with left-libertarianism and right-libertarianism reflecting different and sometimes mutually exclusive orientations. Some libertarians reject affiliation with either of the traditional political wings. The movement has produced notable writings on this question, such as Leonard Read’s essay arguing that libertarians are not bound to left or right categories and should transcend authoritarian degeneration. Prominent thinkers like Harry Browne have contended that libertarian positions should not be defined by liberal or conservative labels, maintaining that libertarianism centers on individual liberty and personal responsibility on all issues at all times, not merely on fiscal conservatism or social liberalism.

Liberty International, originally named the International Society for Individual Liberty, adopted its current title in 1989 after merging with Libertarian International. The merger was coordinated by Vince Miller, who subsequently became president of the merged organization.

FC Ingolstadt 04 established a blind football department in 2022. The department has competed in the Blind Football Bundesliga since 2023, making the club the first Bavarian team to participate in the league.

FC Ingolstadt 04 was formed in 2004 through the merger of MTV Ingolstadt and ESV Ingolstadt. The club’s supporters comprised the fan bases of both predecessor clubs, which had previously been rivals in local football. Following the merger, those former rivals developed a cordial relationship and supported the new club as allies, marking a shift from rivalry to unity within the fan community.

The war guilt question concerns the attribution of responsibility for the outbreak of the First World War. Proponents of this view contend that all of Europe’s major powers felt external pressures to act and believed that their opponents were driving events toward war. In this frame, each state adopted decisions—ranging from mobilization and alliance commitments to various policy measures—that contributed to the escalation of the crisis. Consequently, responsibility for the war is attributed to all of the major powers, rather than to Germany alone.

During World War I, the German war plan known as the Schlieffen Plan anticipated a decisive victory within six weeks. After briefly leaving retirement, General Paul von Hindenburg and General Erich Ludendorff rose to extraordinary prestige, and in 1916 Hindenburg was appointed Chief of the General Staff, signaling the consolidation of their leadership over the German war effort. In 1917 a monumental statue was erected in Berlin in honor of Hindenburg, reflecting his elevated status. As Kaiser Wilhelm II gradually lost power, the two generals effectively assumed control of the state, directing military and political policy for much of the war. These developments fed into the broader debates surrounding the war guilt question by illustrating the concentration of authority in the hands of a small leadership circle.

Benét Laboratories, part of the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities Development Command Armaments Center, serves as the Army's principal design, development, engineering, production, and field-support facility for large-caliber armament systems. Its remit covers cannons, mortars, and recoilless rifles, and it also undertakes work on tank gun mounts, turret components, and munition handling systems.

In 2016, the U.S. Army awarded a contract to KeyLogic Systems to furnish technical support services at the Benét Laboratories facility located at Watervliet Arsenal. The five-year agreement was valued at $9.5 million.

WebMD is an American provider of online health information services, best known for its public Internet site that offers health information and healthcare resources. The site features a symptom checker, drug and pharmacy information, physician blogs on various topics, and a feature that enables users to store their personal medical information. In the first quarter of 2007, it reported more than 17.1 million average monthly unique visitors and was described as the leading health portal in the United States. Content is contributed by qualified professionals and is reviewed by a medical review board of four physicians to help ensure accuracy.

A.D.A.M., which stands for Animated Dissection of Anatomy for Medicine, is a biomedical reference that provides articles on diseases, diagnostic tests, symptoms, injuries, and surgical procedures. The content is reviewed by physicians to ensure that it presents evidence-based health information, and it includes a library of medical photographs and illustrations. MedlinePlus is a free online resource offering consumer-oriented health information for patients, families, and health care providers. It aggregates information from the U.S. National Library of Medicine, the National Institutes of Health, other U.S. government agencies, and health-related organizations, and it is produced and maintained by the U.S. National Library of Medicine.

According to the Mishnah, a progression of religious obligations is tied to specific ages—five, ten, and thirteen. At age five, individuals are to study the Scriptures; by age ten, the focus shifts to learning the Mishnah; and at age thirteen, one attains the obligation to observe the commandments of the Torah.

Bar and bat mitzvah are Jewish coming‑of‑age ceremonies that signify the transition to adult religious responsibilities. In Orthodox communities, bar mitzvah occurs for boys at age 13 while bat mitzvah for girls takes place at age 12; by contrast, Reform, Reconstructionist, and Conservative communities observe the milestone at age 13 for both genders. Upon reaching the milestone, individuals are expected to acquire knowledge of Jewish ritual law, tradition, and ethics, and they may participate in all areas of Jewish community life to the same extent as adults. Nonetheless, certain communities continue to maintain gender-differentiated roles in some respects. For example, in Orthodox practice, a boy who turns 13 may be counted for a minyan and may lead prayers and other services within the family and wider community.

Handysize vessels constitute a class of relatively small bulk carriers designed to access smaller ports for loading and unloading cargoes. They are typically geared, meaning they are fitted with cranes, which allows operations at ports lacking dedicated cranes or cargo handling systems. When compared with larger bulk carriers, handysize ships accommodate a broader range of cargo types, including steel products, grain, metal ores, phosphate, cement, logs, woodchips, and other break-bulk commodities. They are the most common size segment of the bulk-carrier fleet, with about 2,000 vessels in service, and collectively offer a capacity of around 43 million tonnes.

Handysize bulk carriers are built predominantly in Japan, South Korea, China, Vietnam, the Philippines, and India, with additional capacity in a few other countries. They typically displace about 32,000 deadweight tonnes and operate on a summer draft of around 10 metres (roughly 33 feet). The standard layout includes five cargo holds with hydraulically operated hatch covers and four cranes rated at 30 tonnes each. Some vessels are equipped with stanchions to load logs stacked on deck, a configuration commonly referred to as handy loggers. Despite a recent uptick in orders, handysize ships retain the highest average age among major bulk-carrier sectors.

In the East Texas Oil Field, water influx originates from deeper portions of the Woodbine formation, which serves as the source of the intruding water. This influx drives oil through the reservoir toward existing producing wells, functioning as a natural water-drive mechanism that influences reservoir pressure and production dynamics. A 1932 study concluded that oil production would cease if the water pressure dropped below approximately 800 psi, underscoring the critical role of adequate water-pressure support in sustaining flow.

The East Texas Oil Field surged as independent producers, including H. L. Hunt, who had previously found success in the 1920s in Arkansas’s El Dorado and Smackover fields. In November 1930, after meeting Dad Joiner at the Baker Hotel in Dallas, Hunt purchased the Daisy Bradford No. 3 discovery well along with 5,580 acres for $1.34 million. On December 20, 1930, Hunt’s Panola Pipeline Company began moving crude to a Missouri Pacific Railroad branch line for shipment to Sinclair Oil’s Houston refinery. By the summer of 1931, roughly 1,200 wells in Rusk County were producing about 900,000 barrels of oil per day, reflecting the field’s rapid development. The financial gains from the Daisy Bradford acquisition provided the foundation for Hunt to establish the Hunt Oil Company in 1934.

Among Romani communities in Ireland, linguistic research on the Romani language indicates its origins lie in the Indian subcontinent. The language retains grammatical features that are characteristic of Indian languages and a substantial portion of its basic vocabulary is cognate with Indian languages. In particular, shared terms cover body parts and everyday activities, underscoring the long-standing linguistic connections between Romani speech and Indian linguistic traditions.

Romani people in Ireland are part of a broader European presence and are discussed within transnational conversations about Romani identity and diaspora. In February 2016, the International Roma Conference addressed issues facing Romani communities worldwide. During the proceedings, the Indian Minister of External Affairs described the Romani as descendants of India. The conference also proposed that the Government of India formally recognize Romani communities in thirty countries as members of the Indian diaspora, a recommendation that highlights ongoing debates over origin and diaspora affiliation that extend to Romani populations in Ireland.

During the Tang dynasty, fǔ (府, "prefectures") was established as an administrative category for major urban centers, including the capital, functioning as a distinct prefectural-level jurisdiction. By the Ming and Qing dynasties, fǔ had become the predominant provincial-level division within Chinese provinces. In those periods, the term fǔ was typically appended to the name of each prefecture's capital city on maps and geographic works, producing designations such as Hangzhou-fu, Wenzhou-fu, and Wuchang-fu.

Under the Sui and Tang dynasties, the zhou were consolidated with the subordinate commanderies (jùn), eliminating their distinct tier in the administrative hierarchy. The Tang also introduced a higher level, the circuit (dào), which established a three-layer structure and positioned zhou at the second level. Accordingly, the term zhou is typically rendered in English as “prefecture.” The institution of the zhou persisted for centuries, existing as either second- or third-level divisions through to the Qing dynasty.

In the philosophy of education, scholars have long debated methodological directions, commonly described as a paradigm wars between quantitative and qualitative research. Proponents of the quantitative approach favor large-scale experimental designs and statistical analyses aimed at identifying general causal factors underlying educational phenomena. Critics argue that methods rooted in the natural sciences may be ill-suited for capturing the complex cultural, motivational, and social dimensions that characterize educational contexts. By contrast, qualitative researchers emphasize in-depth examination of particular cases to illuminate processes and meanings within specific settings, though such approaches are sometimes criticized for lacking rigorous methodological warrant or generalizability. Mixed-method research has emerged as a contemporary approach that integrates quantitative and qualitative strategies to harness the strengths of both. The relevance of this debate extends beyond theory, shaping funding priorities and, consequently, influencing policymaking decisions in education.

Within the philosophy of education, teachers may incorporate contemplative practices into their preparation and professional work. The Waldorf education movement is widely regarded as an early pioneer of this contemplative approach to teaching. The source of inspiration for content, formats, and instructional methods can be drawn from practices such as reviewing the previous day’s activities, consciously acknowledging students’ presence, and contemplating influential pedagogical texts. Zigler argued that teachers’ own spiritual development is necessary in order to positively influence the spiritual development of their students.
In Valletta, the church-affiliated school St. Albert the Great is led by headmaster Mario Mallia, who is a politician affiliated with Alternattiva Demokratika.

Valletta Local Council was established under Malta's Local Councils Act of 1993, alongside the other local councils created at that time. Its first elections were held on 20 November 1993, with subsequent elections taking place in 1996, 1999, 2002, 2005, 2008, 2013, and 2017. The current council was elected in 2019. The council's offices are located in a building on South Street.

Line 7 of the Guangzhou Metro is a rapid transit line in Guangzhou, China. The line's initial phase began operations on 28 December 2016, with a route extending from Guangzhou South Railway Station to the Higher Education Mega Center South. It provides interchanges with Line 2 at Guangzhou South Railway Station and Shibi, with Line 3 at Hanxi Changlong, with Line 18 at Nancun Wanbo, and with Line 4 at the Higher Education Mega Center South, enabling transfers to multiple corridors. The line covers a total length of 18.6 kilometers (11.56 miles) and comprises ten stations.

Line 7 of the Guangzhou Metro was initially planned to operate with 4-car L-type light metro trains. Following the openings of Line 3, which uses 3-car Type B trains, and Line 6, which employs 4-car L-shaped trains, congestion concerns prompted a reassessment of ridership projections. As a result, planners upgraded the line to 6-car Type B trains to better handle anticipated passenger volumes. To accommodate the longer rolling stock, station structures at Guangzhou South Railway Station and the Higher Education Mega Center South were expanded during construction.

Coastal geography examines how sea level changes in response to climate, noting that cooling tends to store water as ice and thus lowers sea level, while warming releases water and raises it. Today’s sea level is comparatively high, in contrast to the late Pleistocene when, about 18,000 years ago, it was substantially lower. Projections indicate that ongoing global warming could drive further rises in sea level in the future. Even modest increases could threaten many coastal cities through increased flooding and inundation of low-lying zones. Additionally, rising seas influence coastal landforms, drowning and reshaping glacially carved valleys, which contributes to the formation or enlargement of features such as fjords and rias.

Waves entrain sediment and push it slightly down the shoreline, producing a persistent alongshore movement of material. This alongshore transport helps explain why long stretches of coast remain sediment-covered, not only near river mouths. Longshore drift (LSD) relies on a steady supply of sediment from rivers. If the sediment supply ceases or sediment is removed to submarine canals at any point, downstream beaches can become bare.

Håkan Georg Ericson (born 29 May 1960) is a Swedish football manager and former player who has held the position of head coach for the Faroe Islands national team. In his playing career, he appeared for clubs such as Åby IF, FK Kick, and IK Sleipner. He is the son of Georg Ericson, who previously led the Sweden national team as head coach.

Alazán-Apache Courts is a public housing development in San Antonio, Texas, established during the federal drive to alleviate urban housing shortages. In 1930, San Antonio housed the largest Mexican population in Texas, a community largely employed in unskilled, low-wage occupations, and poverty contributed to a low standard of living for people of Mexican descent. Homeownership rates that year were about 30 percent for Mexican Americans, 40 percent for Black residents, and 50 percent for White residents, illustrating the racial disparities in property ownership that shaped housing policy in the city. Against this backdrop, Alazán-Apache Courts represented an effort to provide affordable housing within a segregated urban environment.

During the 1990s, Alazán-Apache Courts was the largest housing project in San Antonio, reflecting the scale of urban development in the city at the time. The complex faced serious overcrowding, which led to renovations of several buildings within the decade. In addition, new structures were constructed, with the architectural design drawing on the style of the nearby Guadalupe Homes.

Owen Davis began his higher education at the University of Tennessee, where he studied from 1888 to 1889 before transferring to Harvard University in 1890. He completed his degree at Harvard in three years. While at Harvard, he was active in the Society of Arts, the university's drama organization. In addition to his academic pursuits, Davis spent a period coaching the football team of a New York preparatory school.

Owen Davis served as a screenwriter on the staff of Paramount Pictures from 1927 to 1930. During this period he contributed to several productions, including They Had to See Paris (1929) and So This Is London (1930), both of which featured the humorist Will Rogers in starring roles.

From 1715 to 1742, both battalions of the Royal Scots were stationed in Ireland; after 1742, the two battalions generally operated separately. The 1st battalion served in Flanders during the War of the Austrian Succession, taking part in the Battle of Fontenoy in 1745, while the 2nd battalion had returned from Puerto Bello in 1743. The latter also aided in suppressing the Jacobite rising of 1745. Following these events, the 2nd battalion was posted back to Ireland.

Two battalions of the Royal Scots were sent abroad in the early 19th century, the 1st Battalion serving from 1801 to 1812 and the 2nd Battalion from 1803 to 1806, after which the latter moved to India where it remained until 1826. In February 1812 the regiment was retitled the 1st Regiment of Foot (Royal Scots), marking the first official appearance of the popular name. The 1st Battalion occupied Saint Thomas in 1801, participated in the Saint Lucia operations, and captured Demerara and Essequibo in 1803, followed by the seizure of Guadeloupe in 1810. With the outbreak of the War of 1812, it was deployed to Quebec, where it fought at Sackett’s Harbor and at Buffalo and Black Rock, captured Fort Niagara in 1813, and then took part in engagements at Longwoods, Chippawa, and Lundy’s Lane, as well as the Siege of Fort Erie and the Battle of Cook’s Mills in 1814. Meanwhile, the 2nd Battalion remained in India throughout the period until 1826.

Philander C. Knox’s 1916 election to Pennsylvania’s U.S. Senate seat led to the commencement of his term in 1917, but he died in October 1921 during his first Senate term. In response, William E. Crow was appointed to fill the vacancy created by Knox’s death; however, Crow died in August 1922, before the term expired.
The 1916 United States Senate election in Pennsylvania was held on November 7, 1916. The incumbent Republican senator, George T. Oliver, did not run for re-election.

In architectural terms, an arch is built from wedge-shaped blocks whose half-spans are referred to as arcs, with each side forming part of the curved outline. The aggregate contour of the arch is called the arcature, a label also used for an arcade consisting of successive arches. The archivolt constitutes the exposed, front-facing surface of the arch and is frequently ornamented, though it can occasionally denote the intrados. When the sides of the voussoirs are not straight but are angled or curved to interlock, the arch is described as joggled.

In Maya architecture, corbelled arches were employed to span openings, a method that differs from the true arch. By contrast, many other Mesoamerican cultures favored flat-roofed structures without arches. Scholarly debate surrounds the extent to which Maya and Aztec builders understood the principle of the true arch; while some researchers have suggested such knowledge, evidence for widespread use of genuine arches remains inconclusive.

Subsidiary communications authority refers to the set of subcarrier services embedded within FM broadcasts, carried as low‑amplitude channels alongside the main program. Historically, a number of firms—Norver, ComPol, Mani National Corporation, McMartin, and Dayton Industrial—designed and manufactured radio receivers and adapters that could access SCA and SCMO channels, with the field currently represented by Metrosonix. These devices enable reception of secondary audio channels that ride on the FM carrier as subcarriers separate from the main audio signal. A central technical challenge in SCA reception is preventing interference from the primary FM stereo difference subcarrier into the SCA decoding circuits, since the main stereo component is substantially stronger than the SCA content and can overwhelm or distort the subcarrier signal. In addition, multipath distortions—reflections and varying propagation paths—can worsen reception quality for SCA decoders, complicating reliable extraction of the subsidiary audio.

The Subsidiary Communications Authority (SCA) is the Federal Communications Commission’s official designation for this class of subcarrier services carried alongside standard broadcast signals. In 1983, the regulatory regime was deregulated, allowing AM and FM stations to use subcarriers without obtaining a separate authorization, with licensing still required only for uses that remain regulated, such as common carrier or Land Mobile Radio Service. FM SCA channels exhibit limited fidelity and bandwidth, producing audio quality that is comparable to AM broadcasting. By contrast, the narrower bandwidth of AM makes multiplexing secondary audio impractical, so SCA on the AM band would be effectively limited to text-only transmissions.

NK Bravo is a professional football club that operates within the framework of FIFA eligibility rules for national teams. In official listings, the flag displayed alongside a player’s name denotes the national team for which the player is eligible under these rules, though there are limited exceptions to this convention. Additionally, players may hold more than one non-FIFA nationality, reflecting the presence of multiple citizenships beyond FIFA’s standard criteria.

NK Bravo, officially Nogometni klub Bravo, is a Slovenian professional football club based in Ljubljana. Commonly referred to simply as Bravo, the club competes in the Slovenian PrvaLiga, the highest tier of Slovenian football. It was founded in 2006.

State religion arrangements occur when subnational administrations sponsor and fund religious denominations. A prominent example is the Alsace-Moselle region of France, where local authorities manage funding and oversight for designated religious communities under regional law rather than under France’s national secular policy. This system preserves the pre-1905 concordat framework rather than the modern separation of church and state, and its characteristics mirror patterns observed in Germany.

State religions are formal endorsements of religious institutions by governments, a phenomenon that has appeared across nearly all cultures, including those of the Ancient Near East and prehistoric societies. The relationship between religious cult and political authority was articulated by Varro under the label theologia civilis, or civic theology. The Armenian Apostolic Church is often cited as the earliest Christian denomination to receive state backing, having been established in 301 CE. In Christianity, a state church refers to a church that is officially sanctioned by the state; historically, this described the imperial church in late antiquity, and in modern usage it may denote a national or traditional church. Ecclesiae are closely related to state churches but typically carry a more limited connotation.

On-demand ride-sharing services, notably Uber and Lyft, have shaped travel technology by improving mobility and simplifying the logistics of getting around. Their availability reduces the need for advance arrangements when traveling to and from airports or other locations, offering flexible, on-demand transportation options. Moreover, they can function as substitutes for rental cars, providing a mobile alternative that can influence travelers’ decisions about vehicle ownership and trip planning.

Travel technology, also referred to as tourism technology and hospitality automation, is the use of information technology and information and communications technology within the travel, tourism, and hospitality sectors. It encompasses deploying IT/ICT to support services and experiences related to travel, shaping both operations and consumer-facing solutions. Examples include flight-tracking systems, pre-travel planning enabled by online travel agencies, and platforms that enable travelers to review or share their experiences.

In Mudéjar contexts, Muslims living under Christian rule faced various restrictions but retained certain rights defined by surrender treaties—whether written, oral, or customary in origin. These agreements established a parallel Islamic society with its own religious, legal, administrative, and fiscal autonomy and institutions, while remaining under the overarching authority of the crown and local lords. Muslim administrators governed the community and taxes were collected by Muslim tax collectors. A central entitlement was permission to be governed by Islamic law and to practice Islam. Mozarabic Christians were occasionally employed in Mudéjar governance because of their familiarity with local language and customs. At times, Muslim elites fled the territories because Islamic law prohibited submission to the authority of infidels.

In the territories of Aragon and Catalonia, Mudéjar communities spoke Romance languages akin to those used by their Christian neighbors. Unlike Castile, the Aragonese and Catalan Mudéjars encompassed Muslim villages that predated the Christian reconquests, signaling a continuity of Muslim cultivation and settlement. Large Muslim populations were concentrated in Granada and Valencia, while Aragonese Muslims formed the most established community within their lands; in Catalonia, autochthonous Muslim presence remained limited to the Low Ebro and Low Segre regions. Under the Crown of Aragon, Aragonese and Catalan Muslims enjoyed a special status that shaped Mudéjar cultivators, known as exarici, who remained subordinate to Christian superiors and were obliged to work on royal estate lands; this status also allowed land to be transmitted within Muslim families across generations. After the Morisco expulsions, architectural remnants in Aragon bear witness to Mudéjar influence, whereas in Catalonia remnants survive mainly in Gothic churches and cathedrals in Lleida’s counties. From the mid-fourteenth century onward, several Mudéjar served as diplomats for the Aragonese crown.

In the 2008 general election, Democratic Left participated within the Left–The Rainbow alliance, which also included the Communist Refoundation Party, the Party of Italian Communists, and the Federation of the Greens. The alliance received 3.1 percent of the national vote but did not secure any seats in the Italian Parliament.

Democratic Left, known in Italian as Sinistra Democratica (SD), was a democratic-socialist political party in Italy. Its official English full name was Democratic Left, and the party carried the subtitle For European Socialism (Italian: Sinistra Democratica. Per il Socialismo Europeo) to signify its European-oriented program.

Meaningful youth participation entails recognizing and fostering the strengths, interests, and abilities of young people. It is achieved when youths are provided with substantive opportunities to engage in decision-making processes that affect their lives, ensuring their involvement goes beyond tokenism. Participation thus takes place at both the individual level, promoting personal empowerment, and the systemic level, influencing structures, policies, and practices that shape youth experiences.

In 2006, the Commonwealth Youth Programme and UNICEF highlighted participation as a complex concept, noting that it cannot be understood as a single phenomenon due to the diversity of developmental processes, cultural contexts, and individual differences. Consequently, there are multiple definitions of participation across different frameworks. At its core, participation involves the freedom of people to engage in social and developmental processes, with genuine self-involvement characterized by activity, voluntariness, and being informed.

In February 1944, planners weighed accelerating Operation Granite by bypassing Truk and directing attention to Palau or the Marianas after securing the Marshall Islands. On March 7, Admiral Nimitz and Rear Admiral Forrest P. Sherman met with the Joint Chiefs of Staff in Washington, where they were questioned by General George C. Marshall and Admiral William D. Leahy. Sherman argued that neutralizing Truk would require occupying the Mariana Islands in order to cut the air route from Japan to Truk. A few days later, on March 12, the Joint Chiefs directed Nimitz to neutralize Truk and to occupy the Mariana Islands, a directive that helped shape the subsequent Mariana campaign and the operations leading to the Battle of Tinian.

During the Battle of Tinian, elements of the 25th Marines captured Mount Lasso without opposition as Japanese forces withdrew during the night. The advance outpaced the range of Saipan’s artillery, prompting the 105 mm howitzer battalions of the 10th and 14th Marines to relocate to Tinian on July 26–27 and rejoin their divisions to provide artillery support. Subsequently, the Marines pressed forward on July 27–28 against sporadic Japanese resistance.

In September 2010, Sean Kovacs announced on Twitter that Apple had renewed approval for GV Mobile+. The app subsequently became available as a paid download in the Apple App Store. It marked the second Google Voice client offered in Apple's App Store, a position it held for roughly eighteen months. Its release followed that of GV Connect by one day.

On June 22, 2010, Google Voice ended its invitation-based access, making the service available to all U.S. users who possessed a Google account. This change represented a major shift in Google's approach to communications. The expansion opened several features to the general public, including voicemail transcription at no charge, call forwarding, personalized greetings, and a single telephone number that could reach multiple devices. The move was aimed at increasing user adoption and positioning Google Voice as a rival to traditional telephone services and other VoIP platforms.
