The list of Channel 4 television programmes is a Wikipedia list article that collects Channel 4 programmes that have their own articles on Wikipedia. It notes that Channel 4 is one of the five major terrestrial television channels in the United Kingdom.

The magnetic scalar potential ψ produced by a finite source outside the region can be represented by a multipole expansion, where each term carries a characteristic magnetic moment and contributes a potential that falls off with distance r. In this expansion, the leading term scales as 1/r (monopole), followed by the dipole term that scales as 1/r^2, then the quadrupole term at 1/r^3, and so on, with higher-order contributions diminishing more rapidly than lower-order ones. The dipole term is the lowest-order nonzero contribution for magnetic sources and thus dominates the far field at large distances. Accordingly, at sufficiently large separations any magnetic source manifests as a dipole with a magnetic moment.

The magnetic dipole is the magnetic counterpart of the electric dipole. Nevertheless, the analogy between magnetic and electric dipoles is not exact. A true magnetic monopole—the magnetic analogue of an electric charge—has never been observed in nature.

Theodore Sturgeon, a science fiction writer who also played guitar and wrote music, occasionally performing at science fiction conventions, lived for several years in Springfield, Oregon. He died on May 8, 1985, from lung fibrosis at Sacred Heart General Hospital in Eugene, Oregon. A lifelong pipe smoker, his death from lung fibrosis may have been linked to asbestos exposure during his Merchant Marine years.

Theodore Sturgeon was a member of the all-male literary banqueting club the Trap Door Spiders, a group that later provided the basis for Isaac Asimov's fictional mystery-solving collective, the Black Widowers. In 1959, he relocated to Truro, Massachusetts, where he befriended Kurt Vonnegut, Jr., who at that time was still relatively unknown. Sturgeon was the inspiration for Kilgore Trout, a recurring character who appears in Vonnegut's novels.

Audio Lossless Coding encompasses a reference implementation of the MPEG-4 ALS encoder and decoder, distributed under the name mp4als (for example, mp4alsRM23). This implementation is available from the MPEG-4 ALS homepage. The standard was published as ISO/IEC 14496-5:2001/Amd 10:2007/Cor 3:2009.

MPEG-4 ALS employs a hybrid predictive framework that combines short-term and long-term modeling to achieve lossless audio compression. The short-term path resembles the approach used in FLAC, using a quantized linear predictive coding predictor and losslessly coded residuals, with the residuals encoded by Golomb-Rice coding or Block Gilbert Moore Coding (BGMC). Complementing this, the long-term predictor handles longer-range periodic structure by using five long-term weighted residues, each associated with its own lag, which can span hundreds of samples. This long-term component enhances compression efficiency for sounds with rich harmonic content—multiples of a single fundamental frequency that are phase-locked—a feature commonly found in many musical instruments and the human voice.

Cretopolis (Kretopolis) was an ancient town whose precise regional assignment is disputed, with various classical authors locating it in different regions of southwestern Asia Minor. Diodorus Siculus, the historian of the Wars of the Diadochi, places Cretopolis in Pisidia; Ptolemy situates it in Cabalia, a district attached to Pamphylia; and Polybius places it in Milyas, Lycia. The Battle of Cretopolis was fought nearby in 319 BC.

Al Mamzar is a locality in Dubai. The north-eastern portion of the locality is predominantly residential. Notable landmarks within Al Mamzar include Al Ittihad School, the Dubai Cultural and Scientific Association, Al Gaz Mosque, the Dubai Police Headquarters, and Al Mamzar Park, reflecting a mix of educational, cultural, religious, administrative, and recreational functions in the area.

Al Mamzar,Arabic الممزر, is a locality of Dubai in the United Arab Emirates. It is situated in Deira, the northeastern part of the emirate, and is bounded to the north by the Persian Gulf, to the west by Al Waheda, to the south by Hor Al Anz, and to the east by the emirate of Sharjah.

The Barcode of Life Data System (BOLD) represents a data release that originated from the BARCODE 500K project conducted by the International Barcode of Life (iBOL) Consortium from 2010 to 2015. The project aimed to assemble DNA barcode records for five million specimens representing about five hundred thousand species. Specimen collection, sequence assignment, and information curation were contributed by scientists, collaborators, and facilities worldwide. As the dataset grew, its accumulation enhanced the accuracy of DNA barcode identifications and supported the broader objective of the barcoding of life.

Barcode of Life Data System (BOLD) is an openly accessible platform for researchers engaged in DNA barcoding. It provides dedicated services to facilitate the publication of records that conform to the BARCODE standard for entry into international nucleotide sequence databases. Its web-based interface and flexible data-security framework position it to support projects that involve broad research collaborations.

Zagreb Indoors resumed play in 2006 after a nine-year hiatus. During its run from 2006 to 2008, it was classified as an ATP International Series tournament. Earlier in its history, the event competed as an ATP World Series tournament in 1996 and 1997.

The Zagreb Indoors was an ATP Tour tennis tournament staged in Zagreb, Croatia; in 1998 the event was held in Split, and from 1996 through 1998 the tournament was known as the Croatian Indoors. The competition was sponsored by Privredna banka Zagreb (PBZ). From 2009 to 2015 it operated as part of the ATP World Tour 250 series, awarding 250 ranking points to the singles champion. Played on a fast indoor hard court surface referred to as RuKort, the event featured both men’s singles and doubles draws.

Giambattista Vico’s central argument, known as the medius terminus, is that the proper understanding of the order of things unfolds from how they appear in experience, rather than from abstract precepts. He also maintains that probability and circumstance bear proportionate weight, and that discovery proceeds through loci and particular experiences rather than through universal axioms detached from life. In his reading of Roman rhetoric, the orator is educated as the transmitter of the oratio, with ratio, or reason, placed at the center of discourse. The essential craft consists in an orderly linkage between common sense and an end appropriate to oratory, with that end drawn from common sense rather than imposed from above, opposing modern pretensions and dogmatic Christianity. Following Socrates and Cicero, the true orator is conceived as a midwife who brings forth the true from the certain, addressing the student’s ignorance.

Giambattista Vico was born in Naples, Italy, to a bookseller. He attended several schools in his youth, but ill health and dissatisfaction with Jesuit scholasticism led him to pursue home instruction. He is thought to have been largely autodidactic, receiving education from his father during a three-year withdrawal from formal schooling after an accidental fall at the age of seven. He later pursued formal studies at the University of Naples, where he earned the degree of Doctor of Civil and Canon Law in 1694.

Approximately 17 percent of the Norwegian mainland is protected. Of these protected areas, about 8.3 percent are national parks, around 1.3 percent are nature reserves, and roughly 4.7 percent are protected under other designations.

Skywave propagation is commonly degraded during periods of enhanced geomagnetic activity, with impairments that can be severe. On the sunlit side of the Earth, skywave propagation may be wholly disrupted during abrupt disturbances of the ionosphere.

Skywave propagation denotes the conveyance of radio signals beyond the line of sight through reflection off the ionosphere, allowing reception of distant AM broadcasts, international shortwave services, and, at times, far-off VHF FM and television transmissions with clarity comparable to locally received signals. Sporadic E propagation, most prevalent in summer across both hemispheres, can enable reception of distant VHF FM and TV stations via skywave. The majority of long-distance shortwave communication, in the band roughly 3 to 30 MHz, depends on skywave effects. Since the early 1920s, amateur radio operators, commonly called hams, have exploited skywave with relatively low transmitter power to achieve long-distance DX communication.

Within the music of Kiribati, composers are often commissioned to craft songs based on a story presented by an individual. The composer then performs the song and trains the rurubene in its rendition, making any necessary modifications. In addition to these on-demand works, composers also occasionally produce songs of their own accord.

In 1963, Gerd Koch recorded traditional dances and songs on Tabiteuea as part of the ruoia series. The Tabiteuea segment documented kawawa, an introductory song and dance, and featured the kamei with a dance leader, along with performances by wan tarawa and kabuakaka. The footage also includes a bino song and dance performed with accompanying arm movements. Koch later broadened his recordings to include traditional songs and dances on the atolls of Onotoa and Nonouti.

Grade III historic buildings are a designated subset within Hong Kong's historic buildings list. The designation is conferred by the Antiquities and Monuments Office (AMO) and refers to structures that hold value but do not yet meet the criteria for designation as possible monuments. These buildings are documented and retained as a reservoir for future consideration for monument status. The Chinese designation for this category is 香港三級歷史建築列表.

The article on the List of Grade III historic buildings in Hong Kong provides information about structures designated as Grade III within the city’s historic preservation framework. The list is considered accurate as of 6 November 2009. Since that date, a territory-wide reassessment of historic-building grades has been conducted to update classifications across the region. A link to the latest grading update is included for readers seeking the most current status.

ISO 3166-2:GT is Guatemala’s entry in the ISO 3166-2 standard. ISO 3166-2 forms part of the broader ISO 3166 framework, which is published by the International Organization for Standardization. The overarching ISO 3166 standard provides codes for the names of the primary subnational divisions—such as provinces or states—for every country that has an ISO 3166-1 code.
ISO 3166-2:GT codes are composed of two elements separated by a hyphen. The first element is GT, the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code representing Guatemala, while the second element consists of two digits.

The Sugarhill Gang was reformed in 1994 by Joey Robinson, the son of Sylvia Robinson. In 1999 they recorded Jump On It!, a hip hop children's album. O'Brien did not rejoin the group, and Robinson began performing under O'Brien's former stage name, Master Gee. Wright, Robinson's bandmate, had urged him not to adopt the alias. Robinson subsequently trademarked the stage names Master Gee and Wonder Mike. In response, O'Brien and Wright filed a court action seeking to reclaim rights to their names.

In 2005, Wright left Sugar Hill Records, together with producer Henry "Hen Dogg" Williams. He later rejoined with O'Brien and began performing under the billing "Rapper's Delight Featuring Wonder Mike and Master Gee." This development occurred as Joey Robinson performed with Jackson under the Sugarhill Gang name, at the same time Sugar Hill Records asserted rights to the Sugarhill Gang name.

Cockos is a software development firm that has employed a small group of programmers, including Justin Frankel, the founder who is best known for creating Winamp, and John Schwartz, who joined in 2008 and has contributed to numerous audio plug-ins as well as creating Olga, a virtual analogue synthesizer. From 2005 to 2014, Christophe Thibault, a French programmer, was also employed by the company and is known for founding the Kaillera and K-Meleon projects. In April 2014, Thibault left Cockos to join Blizzard Entertainment.

Cockos concentrates primarily on music software, while also developing a range of smaller tools frequently released under open source licenses. Jesusonic, a programmable effects processing software, was the company’s first music software product and released on December 21, 2004. In 2005 Cockos released NINJAM, an online music jam software, under the GNU General Public License. Later in 2005, REAPER, the company’s flagship product, was released.

In the European Union, there are estimated to be over 2.5 million potentially contaminated sites, with about 342,000 identified as contaminated. Municipal and industrial wastes constitute the largest share of soil contamination, comprising roughly 38%, followed by the industrial and commercial sector at about 34%. Mineral oils and heavy metals are the dominant contaminants, together accounting for around 60% of contamination. The management and remediation of these sites costs approximately €6 billion annually.

In agriculture, insecticides are deployed to protect crops from pests that damage both standing crops and those stored for later use. In tropical regions, approximately one-third of total production is lost during storage, illustrating the substantial impact of post-harvest pests on food yields. The earliest insecticides, introduced in the nineteenth century, were inorganic chemicals, including Paris Green and other arsenic-based compounds. In addition, nicotine has been used as an insecticide dating back to 1690.

Chad Smith, the drummer for the Red Hot Chili Peppers, blends rock with funk and incorporates metal and jazz influences into his drumming, drawing on the styles of Buddy Rich and John Bonham. This approach helped yield a tighter, faster feel on Mother's Milk, while his performance on Blood Sugar Sex Magik exhibits greater power and intensity. Smith is widely recognized for his ghost notes, his rhythmic drive, and a notably rapid right foot. MusicRadar ranked him sixth on its list of the 50 Greatest Drummers Of All Time. In the band's early years, they developed a provocative stage persona, performing nude with socks over their genitals, a stunt that contributed to their early notoriety.

After guitarist Arik Marshall was dismissed from the lineup following John Frusciante's departure, the Red Hot Chili Peppers conducted auditions for a replacement, considering several candidates including Buckethead; Flea later stated that Buckethead did not fit with the band. Jesse Tobias of Mother Tongue was briefly hired but dismissed due to poor chemistry. Dave Navarro signaled his readiness to join the group, and in August 1993 the band released the non‑album single Soul to Squeeze, which appeared on the Coneheads soundtrack and topped the Billboard US Modern Rock chart.

During the winter of 1916–1917 on the Western Front, Germany refined its aerial warfare by opening a fighter training school at Valenciennes and introducing aircraft equipped with twin guns, signaling a shift toward more capable air power. This change contributed to higher Allied losses, especially among British, Portuguese, Belgian, and Australian air crews who faced outmoded Allied aircraft, uneven training, and weak tactics. The Allied air successes achieved over the Somme earlier in the year were not repeated during the Arras operations, where losses were heavy: 316 British air crews, 114 Canadian air crews, and 44 German air crews were recorded. The Royal Flying Corps subsequently labeled this period Bloody April, reflecting the severe casualties and intense aerial combat that characterized the phase.

The Western Front was a principal theater of World War I. In August 1914, Germany opened the front by invading Luxembourg and Belgium, gaining access to important industrial regions in France. The German advance was halted at the Battle of the Marne, and after the Race to the Sea both sides dug in along a meandering line of fortified trenches. The trench system stretched from the North Sea to the Swiss frontier with France, and the front’s position changed little for most of the conflict, with notable shifts occurring only in early 1917 and again in 1918.

On 10 August 1792, ministers serving under the National Convention were appointed following the suspension of King Louis XVI by the French Legislative Assembly; the Assembly also revoked the ministers named by Louis XVI, thereby reconstituting the executive leadership in the wake of the king's removal.

On 12 Germinal Year II (1 April 1794), Lazare Carnot proposed sweeping away the existing executive council and the six ministers, and replacing them with twelve standing committees that would be accountable to the Committee of Public Safety. The National Convention adopted the proposal unanimously, establishing a committee-based framework to oversee executive governance during the period.

In contemporary Orthodox Judaism, the status of the Zohar and Isaac Luria’s Kabbalistic teachings remains a topic of ongoing debate. Certain Modern Orthodox groups centered on Dor De’ah and a large share of Rambam study circles reject the Arizal’s Kabbalah and deny the Zohar’s authority or its attribution to Shimon bar Yochai, although they may accept, in principle, elements of mystical tradition such as Ma’aseh Bereshit and Ma’aseh Merkavah. The central dispute concerns whether present-day Kabbalistic teachings faithfully reflect the esoteric contents referenced in Talmudic literature. By contrast, mainstream Haredi and Religious Zionist currents generally revere Luria and the Kabbalah, yet rabbinic opinions vary widely, with some leaders sympathetic, others critical, and some orthodox voices deeming such reverence inappropriate or even heretical. Among Haredi authorities, figures like Eliyahu Dessler and Gedaliah Nadel maintained that it is permissible to doubt Shimon bar Yochai’s authorship of the Zohar and to regard its composition as late. Additionally, Yechiel Yaakov Weinberg has suggested possible Christian influence on Kabbalah, pointing to a messianic vision of universal redemption as a Jewish parallel to Christian conceptions of Christ.

Scholarly engagement with Kabbalah has increasingly drawn on nonlinear concepts from dialectical, psychoanalytic, and deconstructive thought. These approaches provide tools for interpreting kabbalistic symbols in a contemporary frame, allowing interpretations that align with modern philosophical concerns. Consequently, those equipped with these concepts are likely to be better positioned to understand the philosophical dimensions of Kabbalah than the kabbalists themselves.

Traian Băsescu is a Romanian politician who has been associated with controversial remarks about Romani people, a small and economically disadvantaged community in Romania. In a 2010 television interview, he claimed that Roma avoid work and live by theft, a statement that led to a sanction from Romania’s national anti-discrimination authority. He has also advocated using the exonym “gypsie,” a term that most Roma consider a racial slur. Earlier, in 2007, he directed an insult at a journalist who was filming him, employing language that referenced Roma-related slurs.

Traian Băsescu, who served as Romania’s president from 2004 to 2014, saw the Romanian Constitutional Court rule 6–3 that the referendum against him was invalid, thereby reinstating him as president. In June 2015, the Romanian Attorney General opened investigations into alleged irregularities involving some members of the Constitutional Court, actions described as aimed at preserving the president’s position. During this period, the United States envoy Philip Gordon visited Romania, publicly backing Băsescu and accusing the opposition of widespread fraud, a stance that provoked anger among approximately 8.4 million voters, according to Romania TV. Despite extensive probes into election fraud, only one conviction emerged, which some outlets described as a "saving face" verdict for the envoy’s claims. Băsescu urged moving beyond past conflicts to address Romania’s problems and restore a functioning democracy and credibility. Crin Antonescu, who served as acting president during the proceedings, maintained that Băsescu was illegitimate because he had been suspended by Parliament and rejected by the electorate.

Research into Moken children's underwater vision has led scientists to rule out several alternative explanations for their performance, and they concluded that the Moken did not evolve enhanced underwater sight through a trade-off that would transfer focusing power from the cornea to the lens; moreover, the Moken’s eyes are not nearsighted, and their ability to adjust lens power is not superior to that of other groups. In parallel work, Gislén and colleagues trained European children to see better underwater by crossing their eyes, a practice that increases lens power and reduces pupil diameter. After the training, the European children were able to see underwater as well as the Moken children, suggesting that comparable underwater acuity can be achieved through specific ocular adjustments rather than population-specific adaptations.

The Moken are an Austronesian ethnic group, also known as Mawken or Morgan. In Burmese, they are referred to as ဆလုံ လူမျိုး, and in Thai they are known as ชาวเล (chao le), a term meaning "sea people." They are associated with the Mergui Archipelago, a collection of roughly 800 islands claimed by Myanmar and Thailand, as well as with the Surin Islands. Most Moken lead a semi-nomadic hunter-gatherer lifestyle that is heavily oriented toward the sea. This traditional seaborne way of life is increasingly under threat.

In the 2023 season’s promotion play-offs for the League of Ireland Premier Division, First Division clubs contested the quarter- and semi-finals, with the quarter-finals staged over two legs. The ties featured Waterford, finishing second, against Athlone Town, who ended in fifth place, and Cobh Ramblers, in third, facing Wexford, who were fourth. Winners from these fixtures advanced to the semi-finals, where they would meet the ninth-placed Premier Division club for a final chance to secure a place in the 2024 Premier Division.

The 2023 season of the League of Ireland Premier Division, commercially known as the SSE Airtricity League Premier Division, marked the competition’s 39th season. Functioning as the highest level of competition for men’s association football clubs in Ireland, the Premier Division traces its origins to its establishment in 1985.
The enterprise that would be known as Cobalt Networks was established in 1996 by Vivek Mehra under the name Cobalt Microserver, and in June 1998 the firm adopted the designation Cobalt Networks, Inc.

In September 2000, Sun Microsystems announced its plan to acquire Cobalt Networks in a deal valued at approximately $2 billion, with payment to be made in Sun Microsystems stock. The transaction was completed on December 7, 2000.

Poultry diseases are illnesses that affect domesticated birds kept for meat, eggs, or feathers. The term refers to birds reared for agricultural purposes, and the principal species involved include chickens, turkeys, ducks, geese, and ostriches.

Darkcore is a subgenre of jungle and drum and bass that emerged in the early 1990s, distinguished by its dark atmospheres, heavy basslines, and a generally harsher, more ominous mood. Notable early releases include Rufige Cru's "Terminator" and Doc Scott's "Here Comes the Drumz," both issued by Reinforced Records in 1992, with Reinforced also releasing 4hero's "Journey from the Light" in 1993. The style further gained traction in 1993 through a series of tracks across various labels, such as Top Buzz's "Living in the Darkness" (Basement), DJ Hype's "Shot in the Dark" (Suburban Base), Origin Unknown's "Valley of the Shadows" (RAM Records), Ed Rush's "Bloodclot Artattack" (No U Turn), and Omni Trio's "Feel Good" (Moving Shadow). These releases collectively illustrate the cross-label development of darkcore within the early British drum and bass scene.
Darkcore, also referred to as darkside hardcore, is a subgenre of breakbeat hardcore that emerged in the UK rave scene in late 1992. It is regarded as one of the direct precursors of drum and bass.

Ria Cheyne contends that representations of disability are widely regarded as inherently regressive. These depictions tend to reduce individuals to their impairment rather than recognizing their full humanity and social identities. The so-called supercrip trope has drawn sustained critique for implying that disability should be associated with extraordinary talent, genius, or insight. Such framing engenders unrealistic expectations about what people with disabilities should be capable of, and underscores the need for more nuanced, person-centered portrayals that reflect everyday experiences and capabilities.

Within disability studies, the political/relational model offers an alternative to both the social and medical frameworks by foregrounding how political structures, institutions, and interpersonal relationships shape disability. Alison Kafer argues that the central problem lies in inaccessible environments, discriminatory attitudes, and ideologies that normalize some minds and bodies while stigmatizing others. She also contends that impairments of mind or body can continue to produce disabling experiences through barriers and exclusion, even when the individual is not medicated by a medical account. In this view, the medicalization of disability is a political question that warrants critical examination and challenge, rather than a straightforward explanation of disability.

Mary, mother of Jesus, is venerated in varying ways across Christian traditions. In certain Lutheran churches, such as the Anglo-Lutheran Catholic Church, Mary and the saints are honored in a manner comparable to Roman Catholic practice, and these communities affirm Marian dogmas as part of their faith.

According to apocryphal sources such as the Gospel of James, Mary is described as the daughter of Joachim and Anne, with Anne previously barren before Mary’s birth. The narratives place Mary’s early life in the Temple in Jerusalem, where, at the age of three, she is dedicated to service as a consecrated virgin. The accounts also note the apparent impossibility of keeping a girl within the Temple precincts in the company of companions. These traditions are not part of the canonical New Testament, which does not name Mary's parents or recount her childhood, instead presenting her role in the infancy narratives and her later betrothal to Joseph.

Convenienze illustrates a broader pattern in Western music in which a significant share of terminology originates from Italian. This reflects the central role played by Italian composers in shaping European musical life from the Renaissance through the Baroque era. In that period, a substantial number of performance directions and expressive indications were introduced and adopted extensively for the first time, establishing a standardized vocabulary that guided interpretation and execution across continental musical practice.

45 or 46 Songs That Weren't Good Enough To Go On Our Other Records is a NOFX compilation album. The second CD collects two EPs, Fuck the Kids and Surfer, each containing roughly 13 very short tracks that had previously appeared only on 7-inch vinyl. In assembling the CD, Fat Mike omitted one track from each EP, a decision explained as an attempt to provoke a small degree of annoyance among fans.

45 or 46 Songs That Weren't Good Enough To Go On Our Other Records is a compilation that collects tracks not featured on the band's studio albums. A number of these songs had previously appeared on compilation albums, vinyl singles, or as B-sides. The exclusion of these tracks from earlier releases was attributed to Fat Mike's preference for releases that did not run excessively long.

During the Maariv service, the Shema is surrounded by four blessings: two introductory blessings, HaMaariv Aravim and Ahavat Olam, precede the Shema, while two concluding blessings, Emet V'Emunah and Hashkiveinu, follow it. In some communities, on weekdays an additional blessing named Baruch Hashem L'Olam is included.

In the film The Shoes of the Fisherman, a fictional pope named Kiril, portrayed by Anthony Quinn, secretly traverses Rome’s back streets disguised as a simple priest, and in a notable scene he recites the Shema Yisrael at the bedside of a dying Roman Jew.

Onze-Lieve-Vrouwekerk, also known as Sint Niklaas, is a church located in Sint-Niklaas, Belgium. It was built in the 19th century and is notable for its Byzantine revival interior. Atop the structure rises a six-meter-tall statue of Our Lady, gilded in gold.

Sint-Niklaas lies along the Ghent–Antwerp axis, benefiting from strong rail and road connectivity. The E17 highway passes through the city, and the N16 dual carriageway provides direct access toward Mechelen and Brussels, making the municipality a well-connected node in the regional transport network.

A spectrogram is a graphical representation that shows how a signal's frequency content changes over time. It is laid out with time on one axis and frequency on the other, while the magnitude of each frequency component at a given moment is conveyed as a third dimension, typically through variations in brightness or color. This encoding allows observers to assess the evolution of spectral components and their relative intensities across the duration of the signal.

Spectrograms are visual representations that show how the frequency content of a signal evolves over time. They can be derived from a time-domain signal by two principal methods. The first treats the signal as passing through a bank of band-pass filters, effectively an approximate filterbank arising from early approaches in digital signal processing. The second method computes the frequency content by applying the Fourier transform to the time-domain signal, typically in a windowed or short-time form. These two techniques produce distinct time–frequency representations in general, reflecting their different constructions, but they can be equivalent under certain conditions, such as when the analysis design aligns the filterbank with the corresponding Fourier basis.

Tufnell Park's landholding history includes the sparse remnants of the freehold, which passed to Henry Archibald Tufnell (d. 1898), who died without children. After his death, the freehold passed to Lieutenant Colonel Edward Tufnell (d. 1909). Edward Tufnell subsequently held several notable public posts, including HM Inspector of Schools, Factory Commissioner, and Director of Greenwich Hospital.

In the 20th century, the A1 was rerouted via Edgware, where the M1 also runs, bypassing its former path through High Barnet. The new alignment then joined the more direct A41 from Marylebone. As a result, the eastern section of the A1 through Tufnell Park diminished in arterial importance. This shift contributed to the fading of the historic designation “the Great North Road,” long associated with a coaching route. Today, the A1 mainly serves traffic traveling between the A1/M1 corridor and the City of London.

Australia is characterized by high levels of competitiveness and economic freedom, underpinned by strong indicators of development and a conducive business environment. In 2022, it ranked tenth on the Human Development Index and twelfth on the Index of Economic Freedom, reflecting solid achievements in human development and regulatory performance. In the realm of tourism, the country attracted 9.5 million international visitors in 2019 and was the 13th-busiest inbound market in the Asia-Pacific region that year. The 2021 Travel and Tourism Competitiveness Report placed Australia seventh globally among 117 economies for travel and tourism competitiveness. International tourism receipts in 2019 amounted to $45.7 billion.

Australia has participated in every Summer Olympic Games of the modern era and has hosted the event on two occasions, with Melbourne welcoming competition in 1956 and Sydney in 2000. The nation is slated to host the 2032 Summer Olympics in Brisbane. In the Commonwealth Games, Australia has competed at every edition and has served as host on five occasions: 1938, 1962, 1982, 2006, and 2018.

William Painter, an English author, is recorded as having married Dorothy Bonham around 1565. The marriage produced at least five children, consisting of one son and four daughters, and by 1587 their son Anthony had joined his father in his government work, demonstrating the family's involvement in public service across generations.

William Painter, an English author and translator active in the late 16th and early 17th centuries, is best known for The Palace of Pleasure, a prose collection of tales drawn from continental sources. From this work, the narratives of Appius and Virginia and Tancred and Gismund were taken, and Painter’s translations and those of his contemporaries became a major wellspring for later dramatists. Shakespeare’s Romeo and Juliet, Timon of Athens, Edward III, and All’s Well That Ends Well are commonly traced to Painter’s material, with All’s Well specifically derived from his translation of Giletta of Narbonne. Beyond Shakespeare, Painter’s influence extended to other playwrights who relied on his and similar translators’ work, including Beaumont and Fletcher’s Triumph of Death; John Webster’s The Duchess of Malfi, drawn from Belleforest; and James Shirley’s Love’s Cruelty, all believed to be based on Painter’s or related translations.

Greenfield Community College is situated in Greenfield, Massachusetts, and serves residents of the northern Pioneer Valley. The college offers a range of courses for Greenfield High School students who are seeking advanced learning opportunities, reflecting its role in supporting local secondary education pathways.

Wilson's Department Store, established in 1882 in Greenfield, Massachusetts, was among the few remaining large, independent, family-owned department stores in the United States. It remained in operation for 138 years before closing in 2020.

During the Pets.com wind-down, Wainwright and nine other executives remained with the firm and organized a meeting of its shareholders on January 16, 2001 to finalize the liquidation. Wainwright received a severance package of $235,000 in addition to a $225,000 retention payment while overseeing the closure. On January 16, 2001, the company changed its name to IPET Holdings, Inc. The liquidation was completed on January 18, 2001.

Pets.com partnered with Best Friends Animal Sanctuary to establish the charitable initiative Pets.commitment, which funded and supported a range of efforts including animal shelters, animal therapy programs, service-dog initiatives, and organizations focused on pet care and wellness. The charity's guiding motto reflected a reciprocal relationship between people and animals, underscoring mutual assistance. Following the website's closure in November 2000, Pets.com donated more than 21 tons of dog food in December 2000 to assist mushers operating in Alaska's Interior.
Grossmünster, a church in Zürich, Switzerland, houses a Reformation museum in its cloister. An annex to the cloister accommodates the University of Zurich's theological school.

Grossmünster in Zurich is regarded as the origin of the Swiss-German Reformation in 1520, when Huldrych Zwingli began reforming the church in his role as a pastor there. A sequence of debates overseen by the city magistrates in 1523 led to civil authorities sanctioning the severance of the church from papal authority. Reforms initiated by Zwingli and continued by Heinrich Bullinger produced a simple, unadorned interior. In 1524, iconoclastic reformers removed the organ and religious statues. The reforms extended across liturgy and practice, including dropping Lent, replacing the Mass, repudiating clerical celibacy, permitting meat on fast days, replacing the lectionary with a seven-year cycle of New Testament readings, and banning church music, among other significant changes. Together these developments cement Grossmünster's status as a major site in Reformation history and the birthplace of the Swiss-German Reformation.

Flight tracking software, used by commercial operators to monitor aircraft, provides real-time oversight of flights to ensure adherence to the planned path. It continuously checks for deviations from the agreed route and generates a warning alarm when a deviation is detected, signaling a potential issue requiring attention. The system also imports and reviews global weather information and NOTAM data, integrating these inputs to enhance situational awareness. By monitoring meteorological conditions and NOTAMs, operators can identify emerging issues that could affect a flight’s safety, efficiency, or timetable.

Flight tracking systems commonly rely on automatic dependent surveillance–broadcast (ADS-B) transponders aboard aircraft, which periodically transmit a unique aircraft identifier together with GPS-derived position data and altitude as radio signals. Civilian ground-based or portable ADS-B receivers situated near the flight capture these transmissions. Because reception depends on distance and terrain, receivers can only collect data for flights that fall within their radio range. The data collected by numerous receivers is subsequently transmitted to centralized servers that aggregate feeds from many contributors around the world, enabling real-time or near-real-time tracking across broad coverage areas.

Software package management systems distribute software as binary packages that contain precompiled executables. These packages are prepared to be installed and used directly, enabling users to deploy applications without performing local compilation or assembly. By providing ready-to-run software in a standardized format, such systems streamline installation, management, and maintenance of applications on a given operating environment.

Uplay is a cross‑platform digital distribution, licensing, and social gaming service operated by Ubisoft. It provides a storefront through which users can browse, purchase, download, install, and update Ubisoft's video games. The platform is supported across a broad range of devices and operating systems, including Windows NT, Windows Phone, PlayStation 3 and PlayStation 4, Xbox 360 and Xbox One, Wii U, iOS, and Android.

The Forward class comprised two Royal Navy scout cruisers, Foresight and Forward. Throughout much of their early service they were kept in reserve. With the outbreak of the First World War in August 1914, the pair were assigned to coastal defence duties, Foresight operating in the English Channel and Forward covering the Yorkshire coast. Forward was present at Hartlepool during the December 1914 German bombardment yet did not open fire. The ships were later transferred to the Mediterranean in 1915, and by mid-1916 moved to the Aegean, where they remained until 1918. Both vessels survived the war but were scrapped shortly thereafter.

The Forward-class cruisers consisted of two sisters, Foresight and Forward, which were in reserve for most of their first decade. In August 1914, Foresight was assigned to the Dover Patrol and then to a destroyer flotilla patrolling the English Channel, while Forward was allocated to coastal defence duties on the East Coast of England. Forward was present during the German bombardment of Hartlepool in mid-December 1914 but played no significant role. The sisters were sent to the Mediterranean in 1915, and in 1916 they were reassigned to the Aegean Sea, where they remained for the remainder of the war. They returned home in 1919 and were paid off and broken up in 1920–1921.

Jean Debry, who was wearing an arm sling, returned to the Council of Five Hundred on 20 May 1799, where he was warmly acclaimed by his colleagues. On the same day, he was elected to another term as president of the Council of Five Hundred.

Jean Debry was appointed administrator of the Aisne department in June 1790 and was elected in September 1791 as a deputy for Aisne to the Legislative Assembly. He was known as an ardent revolutionary, aligning with the radical currents of the period. In January 1792, he proposed and secured passage of a decree that altered the royal line of succession, rendering Louis Stanislas ineligible to the throne on account of his emigration. Louis Stanislas would later reign as Louis XVIII during the Restoration.

Bert Joris (born 18 January 1957 in Antwerp) is a Belgian jazz trumpeter, composer, and arranger who has gained international renown for his work. His career as a performer, composer, and arranger has earned him recognition beyond his native Belgium. In 1996, Joris was awarded the Golden Django.

Elisabeth Schumacher, together with her husband Kurt Schumacher, formed an organization dedicated to opposing the Nazi regime. Kurt, a sculptor and committed anti-Nazi activist, and Elisabeth expanded their involvement as World War II intensified, with Elisabeth taking on a more prominent role in their activities. The Schumachers spent considerable effort helping those affected by Nazi Germany. They were arrested in September 1942, and in December of that year the Nazi regime sentenced both to death.

Elisabeth Hohenemser, who later became Elisabeth Schumacher, was born in Darmstadt into a well-off family. Her father, Fritz Hohenemser, was Jewish; he was an engineer who served as a soldier in World War I and came from a family of bankers in the Frankfurt area. Her mother was Christian and originated from Meiningen. In 1914, the family moved from Strasbourg (then part of Germany) to Frankfurt am Main. That same year, Fritz Hohenemser died in action in World War I. Following his death, Elisabeth moved to Meiningen with her mother and siblings.

A chemically amplified photoresist was developed at IBM around 1980 by Hiroshi Ito, C. Grant Willson, and J. M. J. Fréchet. The new resist demonstrated substantially greater sensitivity to ultraviolet light, being about five to ten times more responsive than earlier resists. IBM later introduced chemically amplified photoresist for the production of DRAM devices in the mid-1980s.

In 2012, researchers at MIT's Microsystems Technology Laboratories demonstrated an InGaAs-based transistor with a nominal 22-nanometer feature size, reportedly the smallest non-silicon transistor built to that date. The team adapted fabrication techniques developed for silicon devices to realize the III–V transistor, with the aim of achieving superior electrical performance relative to silicon-only counterparts. The work was framed as part of broader efforts to extend Moore's law beyond silicon, and researchers outlined ambitions to scale devices further toward the 10-nanometer regime.
Olympique Lillois were crowned champions of the 1932–33 Division 1 season, the first professional edition of the French top flight, after defeating AS Cannes in the final.

During the Second World War, the Combined Allied Intelligence Corps, operating from Malta, began recruiting in 1940 after Italy joined the war on Germany's side. In the Mediterranean, its duties included the debriefing and interrogation of high-ranking prisoners of war in East Africa following Mussolini's invasion of Abyssinia, with Eldoret P.O.W. Camp No. 365 cited as an illustrative example. The corps also conducted counter-intelligence operations in the aftermath of Operation Husky, the Allied invasion of Sicily in August 1943. It implemented the Allied Screening Commission, established by Field-Marshal Sir Harold Alexander a few days after the fall of Rome in June 1944 to identify and reimburse Italian civilians who had aided Allied escapees.

During the early 20th century, the field of military intelligence in the United Kingdom began to mature as understanding of its methods improved. The Directorate of Military Intelligence established a domestic counter-intelligence service, MI5, under Captain Vernon Kell, who would later rise to the rank of major-general. At the same time, overseas intelligence gathering took shape with the creation of MI6 in 1912, led by Commander Mansfield Smith-Cumming, who subsequently attained the rank of captain. These early developments reflect the expansion and formalization of military intelligence functions in the period that preceded the later establishment of the Intelligence Corps.
ISO 3166-2:NI codes are composed of two parts separated by a hyphen; the first part, NI, corresponds to Nicaragua’s ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, and the second part consists of two letters.

ISO 3166-2:NI denotes Nicaragua’s set of subdivision codes within the ISO 3166-2 standard. ISO 3166-2 forms a component of the broader ISO 3166 framework, which is published by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). The standard provides codes for the names of the principal administrative subdivisions—such as provinces or states—of every country that has an ISO 3166-1 code, and consequently these subdivision codes are only defined for nations assigned an ISO 3166-1 designation.

From 1958 to 1960, Les Leston campaigned a Riley 1.5, achieving notable success by winning the British Saloon Car Championship in Class B. He also entered the Riley 1.5 in the Monte Carlo Rally, illustrating his involvement across both circuit racing and rallying. Off the track, the Riley 1.5 served as his daily transport for business and leisure purposes.

Les Leston was a British racing driver who began competing in a Jaguar SS100 before acquiring a 500cc Cooper and constructing his own Leston Special. He achieved a notable victory at the 1952 Luxembourg Grand Prix, a race that attracted prominent entrants including Stirling Moss and Peter Collins. In 1954 he joined Cooper as a works driver, and that year also won the British Formula Three Championship. Leston later participated in three World Championship Formula One Grands Prix, making his debut on 2 September 1956 and failing to score any championship points. He was selected to contest the 1962 Le Mans with Lotus, partnered with Tony Shelly in a Lotus 23 under Colin Chapman’s arrangement, but the entry was denied by the ACO amid the Lotus Le Mans affair. His best Le Mans result came in 1957 when he drove for Aston Martin as a works driver alongside Roy Salvadori, finishing sixth overall.

During the siege, Dundas, the senior Army officer in the Mediterranean, assumed command of the land forces. He and Hood harbored mutual hostility, an animosity intensified by the chaotic scenes surrounding the evacuation of Toulon. Dundas was cautious and dour, and he grew to resent Hood's command, particularly Hood's apparent lack of understanding of the logistics of land warfare. Hood responded by writing letters to London that criticized Dundas and undermined his authority. On 7 February, troops disembarked from transports and landed unopposed along the coast to the west of the Torra di Mortella.

Following the 1789 French Revolution, Pasquale Paoli returned to Corsica to widespread popular acclaim after having fled the island in 1768 during France's invasion and annexation, an exile supported by Great Britain. He promptly routed his political opponents and reestablished himself as the de facto ruler of Corsica, while resisting repeated efforts by the National Convention to impose central authority over the island. The confrontation between Paoli’s Corsican leadership and Parisian control intensified, and in 1793, amidst the Reign of Terror, orders were issued for his arrest, situating the episode within the broader conflict that culminated in the siege of Saint-Florent.

IS-IS is an interior gateway protocol that operates independently of IP and provides built-in hostname resolution. Within its link-state protocol data units, a type-length-value field designated as TLV 137 may be present, carrying a hostname that is associated with a Network Entity Title (NET).

IS-IS uses PDU type 17 for point-to-point links, and on these connections adjacencies are established without separate Hello exchanges for each IS-IS level, unlike on broadcast networks where per-level Hello traffic is typical. In addition, the protocol does not require neighboring routers to have matching Hello interval timers, a contrast to OSPF where such synchronization is necessary for neighbor formation.

Chișinău was struck by a devastating earthquake on 4 March 1977, which caused fatalities and widespread panic. The following year, 1978, saw the completion of the Intourist Hotel, the flagship property of the Soviet state-owned travel monopoly Intourist.

Chișinău sits on the Bâc River, a tributary of the Dniester, and is located at coordinates 47°0′N 28°55′E. The city proper covers 120 square kilometers (46 square miles), while the larger municipality spans 635 square kilometers (245 square miles).

Bobby Darin's health was a persistent concern throughout his life. He was frail as an infant, and from around eight years old he endured recurrent bouts of rheumatic fever that left his heart seriously weakened. Aware that his life might be shorter than that of others, he conducted his career and personal affairs with that awareness in mind. In the final years, he frequently required oxygen during and after performances on stage and on screen, reflecting the extent of his cardiovascular limitations.

In 1963, Bobby Darin utilized his New York Brill Building office to recruit songwriters Roger McGuinn (then known as Jim McGuinn) and Frank Gari. McGuinn was instructed to listen to radio broadcasts and imitate the melodies he heard. The pair, along with Gari, presented the composition “Beach Ball” to Darin, and the trio recorded it at the Brill Building demo studio with Darin on drums, Gari on piano, McGuinn on guitar, and all three providing vocals. The recording was later recorded by Australian presenter Jimmy Hannan with backing by the Bee Gees. Capitol Records released the Darin–McGuinn–Gari version in 1963 under the name The City Surfers. Later that year, a second City Surfers single appeared, with songs credited to Frank Gari, Artie Resnick, and Kenny Young, writers employed by Darin. Both singles were produced by T. M. Music/T. M. Productions, Darin’s production company. Details of the second City Surfers session are not documented, but Darin appears to be the lead vocalist on the second release.

Racing slicks are a type of dry-weather tyres introduced by Firestone at the 1971 Spanish Grand Prix. They carried compulsory circumferential grooves designed to lower overall grip and slow cornering speeds. They were commonly called slicks, as the grooves did not function to disperse water and their wet-weather performance remained limited. The tyres were banned for the 1998–2008 seasons and were reintroduced in the 2009 season.

Racing slicks describe a class of tires engineered to deliver maximum traction in dry conditions. Their inexpensive slick technology originated in drag racing and later influenced tire development across other competitive series. In classes requiring DOT‑approved street tyres, manufacturers marketed tyres that resembled high‑performance street tyres but featured minimal tread and an extremely soft, adhesive compound optimized for competition, known as R‑compound tyres. R‑compound tyres evolved independently and now bear little relation to the original street tyres of the same brand. As racing disciplines updated their rules, new classes have mandated DOT approval along with a minimum treadwear rating, effectively excluding R‑compound tyres and requiring the use of genuine street tyres.

Cumaru is a municipality in the state of Pernambuco, Brazil. It lies approximately 132 kilometers from Recife, the state capital. According to the Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics (IBGE), the estimated population in 2020 was 10,192 inhabitants.

Cumaru's local economy is driven by agribusiness, with beans and corn forming the principal crops. The area also sustains livestock farming, including cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, and poultry, which together support the agricultural sector and overall economic activity.

Within New Jersey, several broadcast outlets have aligned with national networks. WMGM has become an affiliate of the True Crime Network. WJLP, licensed to Middletown, is an affiliate of MeTV. Telemundo operates affiliates in Fort Lee, Linden, and Mount Laurel, while Univision operates affiliates in Paterson and Vineland.

In 2020, a voter-approved measure amended New Jersey's constitution to legalize the possession and sale of marijuana and to authorize expungement of prior possession convictions, receiving about two-thirds of the vote in favor. At that time, roughly a dozen other states had legalized marijuana for sale and possession. By 2024, local governments and municipalities retained authority to regulate marijuana-related businesses within their jurisdictions, resulting in a patchwork regulatory landscape across the state.

Heilig Hüsli is a small chapel located close to the site of the former medieval wooden bridge that connected Rapperswil and Hurden over the Obersee. It is first documented in 1485, described at the time as a wooden prayer house or pilgrim's chapel serving travelers on the regional pilgrimage routes. The area lies on the Way of St. James, which in this region comprises two principal branches: Route A runs from Wattwil via the Ricken Pass to Schmerikon and Lachen, then continues to Buechberg and along the left bank of the upper lake to the St. Meinrad Pass; Route B proceeds from Schmerikon through the Obersee to Bollingen, Wurmsbach, Jona-Busskirch and Rapperswil, before crossing the bridge to Hurden. A further alternative route traverses the Hörnli mountain through the Töss Valley, passes the former Rüti Abbey by Kempraten and Rapperswil, and then crosses the wooden bridge to reach the St. Meinrad Pass in the direction of Einsiedeln Abbey. Through these connections the chapel is tied to medieval pilgrimage networks in the region and marks a waypoint for travelers heading toward Einsiedeln and other pilgrimage sites.

Heilig Hüsli is a small bridge chapel that sits on a base about four metres high. The structure measures roughly two metres by three metres, with eaves at approximately 3.5 metres. It features a west-facing apse that formerly housed a miraculous fresco. Inside, the outlines of the altarpiece remain visible, and a representation of the Virgin Mary with the body of Christ is preserved in the Stadtmuseum Rapperswil-Jona. The fresco was replaced by a replica crafted by Swiss artist Marlies Pekarek, which was inaugurated and blessed on 7 April 2011 to restore the bridge chapel to its original function. Access to the interior is possible only through the latticed east side. In keeping with an old custom, pilgrims throw coins into the interior.

Cobham plc, a British technology and defense company, developed the Siva+ back-mounted, self-mixing rebreather, which is also known as the Canadian Underwater Mine-countermeasure Apparatus (CUMA). The device autonomously blends oxygen with a diluent in a ratio that varies with ambient pressure, enabling operation at depths of up to 90 metres. It supports diluent options including air, trimix, or heliox, providing versatility for diverse underwater missions.

Cobham plc pursued a series of strategic transactions between 2013 and 2014. In May 2013 it acquired Axell Wireless, a provider of antenna systems. In July 2013 it bought out the joint venture partner Bristow Helicopters in the FB Heliservices venture, thereby gaining full ownership of the aviation services entity. In April 2014 Cobham sold Chelton Flight Systems and S-TEC Corporation to Genesys Aerosystems. In May 2014 Cobham completed the acquisition of Aeroflex Holding Corporation, a wireless communications company, for $1.46 billion.

Manel De Aguas, a Catalan photographer, is associated with cyborg art through the development of sensory fins that grant him the ability to perceive atmospheric pressure, humidity, and temperature. This augmented perception is achieved by implants positioned on either side of his head, forming a direct interface between environmental data and his sensory system.

Cyborg art, also called cyborgism, is an art movement that emerged in Britain in the mid-2000s. It centers on developing and integrating new sensory modalities into the human body through cybernetic implants, with the aim of expanding perceptual capabilities. Artworks within cyborg art are produced by cyborg artists—creators whose senses have been voluntarily augmented by implanted technologies.

Migration to North America began with North German Mennonites in 1683, followed by a larger influx of Swiss and South German Mennonites in 1707. The Amish emerged as an early split from the Swiss/South German Mennonites in 1693, a division that would shape subsequent Mennonite–Amish relations. Over time, many Amish individuals and even entire congregations left the Amish and rejoined the Mennonite community, reflecting shifting identities within the broader Mennonite family.

The Mennonites are a family of Anabaptist communities that function as a loose federation rather than a single church body, consisting of autonomous conferences and fellowships. Conservative Mennonites uphold modest, traditional dress and exercise caution in embracing technologies beyond basic utilities. They are not united under one organization; instead they are rooted in independent conferences and fellowships, such as the Eastern Pennsylvania Mennonite Church Conference. The late nineteenth century brought significant social change that produced Old Order splits, yet the majority of Mennonites in the United States and Canada preserved core traditional beliefs. Central among these beliefs is a literal reading of the New Testament, complemented for much of their history by external plain practices aimed at maintaining separation from mainstream society through the early twentieth century. Disputes between conservative and progressive leadership in North America emerged in the first half of the century and continue to influence Mennonite life today, with progressives typically adopting a less literal approach to scriptural interpretation.
Gigaom secured $2.5 million in financing in October 2010. In May 2011, it completed a $6 million funding round that valued the company at $40 million, with RELX leading the investment.

Gigaom was acquired by Knowingly Corp. in June 2015, and the publication subsequently relaunched in August of that year. In addition, the technology conferences associated with Gigaom were relaunched under a new company.

The history of the term probability traces to medieval learned Latin probabilis, from which not only English words such as probable and probability but cognates in other languages are ultimately derived. In Cicero’s usage, probabilis described opinions that were plausible or generally approved, signaling an early semantic link to credibility. The form probability entered through Old French probabilite in the fourteenth century, borrowed directly from the Latin probabilitatem, itself derived from probabilitas and carrying the sense of credibility or likelihood. Thus probabilitas sits at the root of the lineage, stemming from probabilis. The modern, mathematical sense of probability as a quantitative measure of chance emerged later, with the term taking on its formal meaning in 1718.

The history of probability traces its origins to Huygens, who, drawing on the ideas of Pascal and Fermat, published De ratiociniis in aleae ludo in 1657, the first book devoted entirely to probability. In this work he offered systematic solutions to gambling problems and introduced formulas for calculating probabilities, thereby promoting probability as a formal mathematical discipline. Pascal's results concerning the arithmetic triangle were published posthumously in 1665, highlighting the triangle's role in combinatorics; in Traité du triangle arithmétique he described the figure as the arithmetic triangle, reflecting its central place in early combinatorial mathematics.

Géza, Grand Prince of the Hungarians, pursued expansion against Bavaria, seizing Melk fortress in 983 amid wider instability in the Holy Roman Empire following Otto II's death. In 991, Bavarian forces launched a counter-offensive, forcing Géza to withdraw his troops from lands east of the Vienna Woods. By 996, he agreed to a peace settlement with Henry IV of Bavaria, renouncing territories east of the Leitha River. In the framework of dynastic diplomacy, Géza arranged for his son Stephen to marry Henry IV's sister Giselle. Before finalizing the marriage alliance, he convoked the Hungarian leaders and compelled them to swear an oath recognizing his son's right to succeed him.

Géza, Grand Prince of the Hungarians, succeeded his father circa 972 and immediately pursued a centralizing policy intended to concentrate royal authority. He earned a reputation as a harsh ruler; the Life of his son describes him as having hands stained with blood, reflecting perceptions of severity in his governance. Some scholars, notably Pál Engel, contend that Géza conducted a large-scale purge of relatives, which would account for the paucity of references to other members of the Árpád dynasty after 972, with Koppány remaining the main regional exception in southern Transdanubia. The same period saw a marriage alliance between the German and Byzantine dynasties, which fostered rapprochement with neighboring powers and prompted Géza to seek peaceful relations with the Holy Roman Empire. A monk named Bruno, dispatched by Otto I, arrived in Hungary around 972, and Hungarian legates later attended a conference convened by the emperor at Quedlinburg in 973, marking increased diplomatic engagement with the empire.

Data structures are the concrete means by which data is stored and organized in computer memory. They provide the foundation on which abstract data types (ADTs) are built, since ADTs encapsulate the intended operations and logical behavior of a data type. Conversely, ADTs specify the conceptual form of a data type, while data structures realize that form by supplying a concrete physical representation and layout that enables the practical implementation of the associated operations.

Data structures are fundamental constructs that enable the efficient management of large volumes of data, supporting systems such as large databases and internet indexing services. The effectiveness of algorithms often depends on the underlying data structures, as their organization can significantly influence performance and scalability. In some formal design methodologies and programming languages, data structures are treated as the primary organizing principle of software design, at times taking precedence over algorithmic considerations. Data structures govern how data is stored and retrieved across both main memory and secondary storage, shaping access patterns and efficiency in practice.

On 1 April 1937, Burma was separated from British India and became a distinct British colony with its own administration. Ba Maw became the first Prime Minister and Premier of Burma, and he advocated Burmese self-rule while opposing Burma's participation in World War II in cooperation with Britain. His stance led to his resignation from the Legislative Assembly and his arrest on charges of sedition. In 1940, prior to Japan's formal entry into the war, Aung San formed the Burma Independence Army in Japan.

On 1 February 2021, the Tatmadaw detained Aung San Suu Kyi and other members of the National League for Democracy as Parliament was due to convene, after which the military transferred authority to commander-in-chief Min Aung Hlaing and declared a one-year state of emergency. Borders were closed and travel as well as electronic communications were restricted nationwide. The military announced it would replace the existing election commission with a new body. A military-controlled media outlet indicated that new elections would be held within about a year, though no formal commitment was issued. NLD Members of Parliament were expelled from Naypyidaw. By 15 March 2021, martial law had been extended to additional areas of Yangon. Security forces killed 38 people in a single day of violence.

Robert Venables became engaged in 1649 to Elizabeth Lee, a widowed mother of seven children born in 1614 and who died in 1689, and the couple proceeded to wed in 1654 after Venables returned from Ireland. Elizabeth Lee's family ties extended through marriage as her eldest son, Thomas Lee, married Frances Venables, while Venables's own son, Thomas Venables, married Elizabeth Lee, the daughter of the elder Elizabeth Lee, thereby linking two generations of the family. This union also disrupted the prior betrothal of Elizabeth Lee's daughter to another girl. The marriage between Robert Venables and Elizabeth Lee was not successful, with Elizabeth Lee reportedly disliking his political views, disdaining his religion, and disapproving of his manners.

Robert Venables was a Parliamentarian commander during the early stage of the First English Civil War. Brereton established his headquarters at Nantwich, a move that allowed Venables to secure superiority over Royalist commander Arthur Capell across Shropshire, Cheshire, and North Wales. From August to September 1643, Venables based his operations at Cholmondeley, using it as a staging point to strike at nearby Royalist garrisons. These garrisons contributed to the blockade of Chester, a strategic measure designed to funnel troops and supplies from Royalist areas in Ireland and North Wales. The successes of Venables and his forces helped bring about Capell's replacement by Lord Byron in October 1643.

The Movie Channel traditionally scheduled lengthy promotional breaks between feature presentations, often extending 20 to 25 minutes depending on the airtime of the upcoming film. A minute-based countdown ticker indicating the start time of the next film appeared during these intermissions from May 1988 through August 1997. Showtime adopted a comparable countdown graphic for its next scheduled program beginning in January 1990, which remained in use until its August 1997 rebrand. In February–March 1993, The Movie Channel ran trials to shorten breaks to five minutes or less and eliminated fixed top- or bottom-of-hour start times, instead employing a pattern of top-of-hour, bottom-of-hour, and random five-minute intervals. Following findings that showed higher audience retention, The Movie Channel established the five-minute break as standard practice in August 1993, and the rigid break limits were abandoned in 1997. The tightening of break lengths reduced the number of internally produced interstitials; over the subsequent four years interstitial content largely comprised trailers and shorter behind-the-scenes segments for upcoming or current films produced by their originating studios.

The Movie Channel presents reruns of theatrical films drawn from a broad roster of major studios and their subsidiaries. Its sub-run slate incorporates titles from Sony Pictures, including Columbia Pictures, TriStar Pictures, Screen Gems, Revolution Studios, and Morgan Creek Productions, as well as Warner Bros. Pictures (with New Line Cinema), Universal Pictures (including Focus Features), and additional participants such as Open Road Films, Screen Media, and Oscilloscope. The channel also airs sub-runs from Summit Entertainment for films released prior to 2013 and from Paramount Pictures for titles released before 2017. Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer, including United Artists and Orion Pictures, distributes films in these sub-runs, while Lionsgate holds sub-run rights with United Artists and Orion for titles released before 2009. In addition, Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures, along with its divisions Pixar, Walt Disney Animation Studios, Walt Disney Pictures, 20th Century Studios, Touchstone Pictures, Hollywood Pictures, and Marvel Studios, contributes titles to the channel’s sub-run lineup.

Sweden's climate is comparatively mild and relatively dry for its latitude, and even somewhat farther south than might be expected, a pattern attributed to the warming influence of the Gulf Stream and the prevailing westerlies generated by Earth's rotation. The country’s high latitudinal position leads to substantial seasonal variation in day length, with regions north of the Arctic Circle experiencing extended daylight in summer and continuous darkness for portions of winter. In Stockholm, daylight exceeds 18 hours in late June and falls to about six hours in late December. Annually, Sweden receives roughly 1,100 to 1,900 hours of sunshine.

During the 1960s and 1970s, Sweden emerged as a leading international advocate of the sexual revolution and actively pursued policies to promote gender equality. The country has long been noted for liberal attitudes toward homosexuality, with broad social acceptance illustrated in popular culture, such as the film Show Me Love. On 1 May 2009, Sweden repealed its registered-partnership laws and introduced a gender-neutral marriage regime, replacing the prior framework; previously, domestic partnerships were available for both same-sex and opposite-sex couples. Cohabitation, known locally as sammanboende, remains widespread across all age groups, from youths to older adults.

E. H. Crump, a notable figure in Memphis politics, is referenced in popular culture by the Old Crow Medicine Show in the song Motel in Memphis, which mentions "Mr. Crump." The lyrics connect this figure to a political machine, portraying it as an influential force that shaped the city of Memphis.

E. H. Crump leveraged his ascending business career to establish lasting political connections. He served as a delegate to the Tennessee Democratic State Convention in 1902 and again in 1904, signaling his growing influence within the party. In 1905 he was named to the municipal Board of Public Works, and two years later he was elected Commissioner of Fire and Police, one of the three commissioners who governed the city.

In 1985, a scholar noted that waterfalls had been a neglected aspect of river studies. The study of waterfalls then expanded substantially in the latter half of the 20th century. A large number of guidebooks focusing on waterfalls have been published. Online resources have also developed, including the World Waterfall Database, a website that catalogs thousands of waterfalls globally.

Waterfalls are geomorphological features that commonly form when a river flows over resistant bedrock that overlies softer rock; the softer material erodes more quickly, causing the water to plunge over the edge. As the erosion of the softer rock continues, the waterfall tends to become higher. They have been studied for their impact on the species living in and around them, including effects on habitat structure and the distribution of aquatic and terrestrial organisms.

During the siege of Port Royal in 1707, August 31 saw Wainwright carry out a second landing at a different point, while Subercase discharged 120 French soldiers from the fort to engage. Approximately 70 French fought the New Englanders in close-quarters combat, employing axes and musket butts. Saint-Castin and about 20 of his men were wounded, with five killed in the engagement. On September 1, the British reembarked on their ships and sailed back to Boston. Accounts differ on losses: French reports claimed as many as 200 French were killed, whereas British sources put fatalities at about 16 killed and 16 wounded.

By August 21, the British fleet arrived near Port-Royal, and on the following day Wainwright landed troops about two miles south of the fort before moving to a position roughly one mile to the north. The area to the fort’s north had previously been used by March and contained additional earthworks constructed by Subercase. On August 23, Wainwright dispatched a detachment of about three hundred men to clear a route for heavy cannon; Subercase’s forces repulsed the effort and harassed the detachment. The fort’s defenders employed guerrilla tactics and cannon fire, driving the New Englanders back to their camp.

Amahai is a nearly extinct Austronesian language spoken in the Moluccas (Maluku) region of eastern Indonesia, where some analyses indicate that the language may actually comprise two distinct languages.

Phyllodactylidae is a family of geckos within Gekkota, comprising 163 species across 10 genera with a distribution spanning the New World, North Africa, Europe, and the Middle East. The group was established as a distinct lineage in 2008 following a molecular phylogenetic analysis, reflecting relationships revealed by genetic data. A distinctive feature shared by all members is a single codon deletion in the phosducin (PDC) gene. Taxonomic revisions have placed Bogertia as a synonym of Phyllopezus. The name derives from the leaf-like shape of the digits.

Joe Bishop-Henchman is a Libertarian Party official who, in the lead-up to the vote, was associated with a set of statements concerning the party’s ticket: Jo Jorgensen was identified as the presidential nominee, she said she would vote for John Monds as her vice presidential running mate, and she declined to endorse any candidate beyond that commitment, with the remarks made prior to the voting.

Joe Bishop-Henchman, a Libertarian Party official, played a leading role in party operations during early 2019, including the organization of a national contest to choose the 2020 Libertarian National Convention theme that required five dollars per vote. The winning theme, TANSTAAFL—There Ain't No Such Thing As a Free Lunch—was announced on April 11. The phrase embodies a libertarian economic idea that gained prominence through the work of Robert A. Heinlein and Milton Friedman. Moreover, the concept already featured in the Libertarian Party’s early branding, appearing in the party’s first logo adopted in 1972, commonly called the Libersign.

A subscription pricing model enables the cost of expensive goods or services to be spread over time, potentially making them appear more affordable to consumers. Some offerings, such as newspaper or magazine subscriptions, require upfront payment, which may deter certain customers. Fixed pricing benefits frequent users by providing predictable costs, yet it can disadvantage those who plan to use the service only for a limited period. The ongoing commitment inherent in subscriptions can, for some buyers, prove more expensive than a one-time purchase. Additionally, subscriptions tend to increase vendor lock-in, which can have critical implications for businesses that depend on particular software. Licensing checks conducted over the internet may cause software to stop working or revert to a freemium model if verification fails. If a vendor ceases to support a version or goes out of business, customers may lose access to data or designs stored in the software. In some industries, maintaining access to old files for many years is vital, highlighting potential long-term risks of subscription arrangements. Finally, repeated payments can be onerous for consumers.

Subscription-based business models frequently collect or rely on large volumes of customer information as part of their operating and service-delivery processes. Magazine mailing lists illustrate how personal contact details and preferences are gathered to tailor distribution and communications. The practice of data collection in this context can raise privacy concerns, prompting attention to data protection, user consent, and related privacy obligations.

The National Democratic Front (Philippines) advocates for the rights to self-determination and democracy for the Moro people, the Cordillera peoples, and other national minorities or indigenous peoples.

During the 1980s, certain factions within the Communist Party of the Philippines sought to dissolve the National Democratic Front of the Philippines and establish a new federation known as Bagong Katipunan. They envisioned Bagong Katipunan as an equal partner to other revolutionary mass organizations, with the aim of superseding the NDFP's organizational framework. The proposal was ultimately defeated as part of the Second Great Rectification Movement.

One Frankfurt is a mixed-use high-rise in which the lower fourteen floors are occupied by a hotel and conference facilities. Floors 15 and 16 are allocated to coworking spaces, while the upper levels accommodate around 42,000 square meters of office space.

One Frankfurt is a high-rise complex in Frankfurt that integrates a four-star hotel, a conference center, office spaces, and a sky bar named NFT. The hotel offers 375 rentable rooms and is operated by the NH Hotel Group. The conference center covers about 1,000 square meters of space. The NFT sky bar occupies the 47th floor at a height of 185 meters and features a wraparound rooftop terrace. It is the tallest bar located in a skyscraper in Germany.

In 1935, Eric Trist returned to the United Kingdom with his first wife, Virginia Traylor, who was born on 11 September 1909, having married him in Manhattan on 6 July 1935. Virginia was a granddaughter of John Henry Traylor, and the couple were accompanied by her mother and sister. During this period Trist met Oscar Adolph Oeser, then head of the psychology department at the University of St Andrews in Scotland. He subsequently carried out a study of unemployment in Dundee.

In 1949, Eric Trist, together with Ken Bamforth, conducted organizational research on the work crews at the Elsecar Collieries. The study culminated in the article "Some Social and Psychological Consequences of the Longwall Method of Coal Getting," which examined how miners were organized and how the longwall method shaped social relations and workflow. The analysis identified organizational features that would today be described as lean or agile in nature.

Television in the United States encompasses the production, distribution, and international reach of programming created by American networks, which are among the largest and most widely distributed in the world. Content made for U.S. networks is among the most extensively syndicated outside the United States. The 2000s and 2010s saw a marked rise in both the number and critical reception of American television series, a trend that critics have described as a modern golden age of television. In the early 2020s, debate continued over whether this era had ended or was still unfolding, with analysts differing on the trajectory and ongoing influence of American television.

In the United States, television production companies may either commission teleplays intended for pilot episodes or acquire speculative scripts, with some of these works advancing to become pilots for proposed series. Producers then market commercially viable scripts to networks or to distributors for initial distribution, including first-run syndication.
