An illustrative example is CBS Media Ventures, which distributes Dr. Phil in first-run syndication, a program that is syndicated rather than carried by a particular network. When networks decide whether to order a show, they assess factors such as alignment with the network’s target audience, anticipated production costs, support from network executives, and often the results of test audiences.

Jedek is a language spoken by around 280 people living in Sungai Rual along the Rual River, located just south of Jeli town in Jeli District, Kelantan, in northern Peninsular Malaysia. During the 1970s, the Malaysian government resettled several Semang foragers, including speakers of Jahai and Jedek, from the middle reaches of the Pergau River to Sungai Rual. The Sungai Rual area presently comprises three hamlets. The community is organized into seven bands, four of which are predominantly Jedek-speaking and three predominantly Jahai-speaking.

Jedek displays a distinctive phonological pattern in which word-final nasals are realized as prestopped when they follow an oral vowel, differentiating final nasals by articulatory shape. In addition, nasal consonants induce progressive nasalization of vowels, with nasality spreading through the vowels as a result of the nasal consonants' influence.

The Kurma Purana is attested in multiple recensions, with textual traditions varying between versions. Each version is organized into two sections: Purva-vibhaga, the older portion, and Upari-vibhaga, the upper portion. Across different manuscripts, the total number of chapters is not uniform, reflecting variant codices. In the critical edition, the Purva-vibhaga comprises 51 chapters and the Upari-vibhaga contains 44 chapters.

Within the Kurma Purana, a philosophically oriented section mirrors the Bhagavad Gita tradition found in other Puranas. This portion is titled Ishvaragita. Ishvaragita comprises eleven chapters, which present the Bhagavad Gita’s teachings within a framework in which Shiva acts as the speaker. The eleven chapters are situated in the Uttaravibhāga, the later portion of the Kurma Purana.

Multibranding is a branding strategy in which a single company markets multiple distinct brands within the same product category. This approach tends to raise promotion and advertising costs because each brand must be developed and promoted independently, without the benefit of established consumer impressions. The main advantage is that each brand can be tailored to a specific market segment, so a failure or poor performance of one brand does not automatically jeopardize the others. Conversely, the additional cost and complexity of managing several brands can outweigh potential benefits for some organizations. A well-cited example is Unilever, which reduced its brand count from more than 400 to around 14 with sales exceeding €1 billion, accomplished through the elimination of underperforming brands and the disposal of brand assets. In addition, some firms create new product brands as a defensive response to competitive pressure, a practice known as fighting brands or fighter brands.

A challenger brand operates in an industry in which it is neither the market leader nor a niche brand. It is defined by a mindset of ambitions that extend beyond conventional resources, reflecting a willingness to pursue transformative objectives. Its purpose is to bring about change in the industry by challenging established players and reshaping the competitive landscape.

During the 16th century, the Italian theorist Gioseffo Zarlino argued for the primacy of the triad as a foundational element in Western music, reflecting an early emphasis on triadic harmony. More than a century later, Johannes Lippius introduced the term harmonic triad in his 1612 work Synopsis musicae novae, marking a formal naming of triadic harmony within musical theory.

During the late Renaissance and into the Baroque period (roughly 1600–1750), Western music shifted away from strictly horizontal, polyphonic writing—where independent melodic lines predominated—toward a primarily vertical conception of harmony built from triads. Central to this transformation were progressions, sequences of triads that defined functional relationships among tones. This emphasis on harmonic succession supported Baroque basso continuo practice, in which bass lines were sustained while chords implied above provided the harmonic framework. The shift demanded a more vertical approach to composition and elevated the triad to the fundamental building block of functional harmony.

Within the Indian linguistic landscape, Standard Hindi (Shuddh) and Standard Urdu (Saaf or Khaalis) are regarded as the formal "H" varieties. The H varieties are written in their respective scripts—Hindi uses Devanagari, while Urdu is written in Nastaʿlīq. Hindustani, by contrast, is the "L" variety commonly used by the general population. It may be written in either Devanagari or Nastaʿlīq, and when written, Hindustani is typically identified as Hindi in Devanagari orthography and Urdu in Nastaʿlīq orthography.

Introduced in 1947, the BGN/PCGN transliteration system is a standardized romanization scheme developed by the United States Board on Geographic Names (BGN) in collaboration with the Permanent Committee on Geographical Names (PCGN). It provides agreed methods for rendering names written in non-Latin scripts into Latin letters and has been employed for British official use.

In a review of Raydiation, AllMusic editor Andy Kellman judged the album to be as derivative as Ray J's previous efforts, including Everything You Want and This Ain't a Game. He observed that Ray J imitates the stylistic influences of R. Kelly and Usher and maintains a performative persona without meaningful deviation or growth. Kellman also noted that there are no standout tracks or notable positives to single out. He further suggested that if Ray J intends to continue with a four-year release cycle, he should devote less time absorbing external influences and more time developing an independent artistic voice.

Raydiation is the third studio album by American singer Ray J. It was released in the United States on September 20, 2005, by Sanctuary Records in collaboration with Knockout Entertainment, marking his first release in four years. The project was primarily produced by Detail, with additional contributions from Rodney "Darkchild" Jerkins, R. Kelly, Ric Rude, and Timbaland. The album features guest vocal appearances by Fat Joe, Mýa, and Brandy, Ray J's sister.

Amelia Vega advanced into the performing arts by recording her first demonstration at age 15 and pursuing roles in her hometown’s musical productions. Her debut single, “Pasa Un Segundito,” was issued on 26 April 2010 via iTunes and swiftly climbed to a top position on Latin music charts within two days. A few months later she released an environmental track titled “Smog.” Vega announced on Twitter that her full-length album Agua Dulce would be released on 30 August 2011, with an initial release on iTunes. In the following period she broadened her promotional activities to markets in Puerto Rico, Ecuador, Panama, and the Dominican Republic, including an opening performance for Marc Anthony and Chayanne before audiences of about fifty thousand people.

Amelia Vega won the Miss Dominican Republic title and subsequently represented the Dominican Republic at Miss Universe 2003 in Panama City on June 3, 2003. She became the first contestant from the Dominican Republic to win the Miss Universe crown, and at the time she was the youngest winner since 1994. As of 2024, Vega is the tallest Miss Universe winner, measuring 6 feet 2 inches.

XBLite is a software project that includes a compiler and a dedicated code editor. The compiler is currently released as version 2.4.0, while the XSEd code editor has reached version 1.30. Among its recent developments, the project has produced viXen, a visual GUI designer.

XBLite’s development includes the viXen project, an open-source software package originally created by John “prujohn” Evans. Version 0.50a was released on July 22, 2006. ViXen serves as a WYSIWYG screen designer and a generator for XBLite code. It enables users to prototype a Windows GUI application before implementing the actual functionalities in XBLite within the generated skeleton. At present, Guy Lonné develops and maintains the viXen project on SourceForge.

FinanceKit is an application programming interface (API) that enables third-party iOS and iPadOS applications to display data from Apple Card, Apple Cash, Savings, and Orders stored in Apple Wallet. The information is retrieved from Apple Wallet and presented within these apps. Access to FinanceKit is restricted to applications listed in the United States or United Kingdom App Store.

To add Japanese IDs to Wallet, provisioning requires the Mynaportal app. WatchOS integration is not supported currently. Availability is limited to iPhone XR, XS, SE (2nd generation) or newer devices running iOS 18.5 or later.

Sensible heat and latent heat are not themselves separate forms of energy; rather, they denote heat transfer, and the description of these processes is defined by the effect they produce on a material or thermodynamic system.

Sensible heat flux in meteorology describes the conductive transfer of heat from the Earth's surface into the atmosphere, constituting a key element of the Earth's surface energy budget. This flux is routinely quantified using the eddy covariance method.

Construction of Naval Base Banika Island commenced in February 1943 by United States Navy Seabees Construction Battalions, including the 33rd and 35th, who built the base complex and most of the airfields. On June 25, 1943, enemy aircraft attacked the site, bombed tank farms, destroying one 1,000-barrel tank and damaging three others, while pipelines to the port and airfields were damaged; repairs took five days, and the airfields remained operational, with four Seabees killed. A pontoon bridge connected Banika Island at Renard Sound to Pavuvu Island, where a barge landing dock and a small rest and relaxation facility were established. The complete base was completed by November 1943. In Fall 1943, the port’s operation was turned over to the 6th Seabee Battalion and the 9th Special Battalion; in February 1944, operations were reassigned to the 11th Battalion and the 12th Special Battalion. The 93rd Battalion constructed Naval Mobile Hospital MOB 10, a facility with about 1,300 beds. A pontoon assembly depot (PAD 2) was built and run by the 20th Battalion, storing pontoons in flat sections to reduce transport space. Two airfields, Banika Field and Renard Field, were developed for use by the U.S. Navy, U.S. Army Air Forces, and U.S. Marine Corps. By February 1945 Banika Island was no longer front-line; portions of the base were packed and moved to forward bases, with MOB 10 among the first units shipped out, and much of the base subsequently removed over a four-month span. The base was closed and abandoned after World War II.

Naval Base Banika Island was a United States Navy installation established during World War II on Mbanika Island in the Russell Islands, part of the Solomon Islands. The base supported the Pacific War by housing a substantial supply depot to sustain fighting ships and by providing a repair facility for landing craft, PT boats, and other small vessels. Its location offered a favorable fleet anchorage, aiding American operations in the area, and the island was captured during the Solomon Islands campaign. In addition, the Renard Sound Seaplane Base was constructed at the site to bolster aerial reconnaissance and patrol capabilities.

The Woolrich Electrical Generator, built in 1844, is regarded as the earliest electrical generator to be employed in an industrial process. Today it is housed in Thinktank, the Birmingham Science Museum. The device was utilized by the firm of Elkingtons for commercial electroplating.

Induction AC motors can function as generators, converting mechanical energy into electrical energy when the rotor speed exceeds the synchronous speed, a condition known as negative slip. A conventional AC asynchronous motor can generally be used as a generator without modification to its components. Induction generators are particularly useful in mini-hydro power schemes, wind turbines, and in recovering energy from high-pressure gas streams, owing to their simple control requirements. They do not require a separate starting circuit because the rotating magnetic field is produced by the driven source. Likewise, they do not require speed governor equipment, since their operation is inherently synchronized to the connected grid frequency.

Ethnoexodus denotes a strategy of ethnic self-identification used to evade discriminatory sociocultural marginalization faced by Maya communities. Ethnic self-identification as Maya is variable and situational, shifting across different contexts and moments. Consequently, the emphasis rests on escaping marginalization rather than constructing a fixed, cohesive Maya identity. The concept is attributed to Juan Castillo Cocom.

Since 2003, Maya language instruction and Maya cooking classes organized by Maya communities from Yucatán living in the United States have operated in California and other states. Yucatec Maya clubs are registered in Dallas and Irving, Texas; Salt Lake City, Utah; Las Vegas, Nevada; and numerous California cities, including San Francisco, San Rafael, Chino, Pasadena, Santa Ana, Garden Grove, Inglewood, Los Angeles, Thousand Oaks, Oxnard, the San Fernando Valley, and Whittier. Maya language study is offered at college and graduate levels, with Indiana University offering beginning, intermediate, and advanced courses since 2010. In addition, the Open School of Ethnography and Anthropology provides six-week immersion Maya courses as part of its summer program.

Anak ng Kumander, which translates to "Child of the Commander," is a 2008 Filipino action film directed by Jose "Kaka" Balagtas and written by Rod Santiago, starring Manny Pacquiao and Ara Mina. It was released on January 1, 2008 and formed part of the 33rd Metro Manila Film Festival. The production is notable for featuring Palito in his final on-screen appearance during his lifetime.

Within Piatnitzkysauridae, Condorraptor and Piatnitzkysaurus are grouped together in a clade that excludes Marshosaurus. This arrangement is supported by shared locality and temporal range, as well as common morphological features such as flat anterior faces of the presacral vertebrae and a pronounced ventral keel on the anterior dorsal vertebrae. Some scholars have proposed that Condorraptor may represent individual variation within Piatnitzkysaurus rather than a separate species. Distinguishing differences between the two include a less developed enemial crest in Condorraptor and a shallower fossa in the first sacral vertebra when compared to Piatnitzkysaurus.

Xuanhanosaurus is regarded as a problematic tetanuran with an uncertain phylogenetic position. In analyses published around 2010, it was recovered as the sister taxon to the three genera then assigned to Piatnitzkysauridae, a finding that suggested a close relationship to the family. However, the reliability of this affiliation is compromised by the incomplete fossil material of Xuanhanosaurus, and later studies have cast doubt on the proposed relationship. Some researchers have recovered Xuanhanosaurus as a basal tetanuran outside Piatnitzkysauridae, while others continue to treat it as a piatnitzkysaurid in certain classifications.

The Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC) was established in October 1999 by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. It unified seven preexisting laboratories into a single organization. The consolidation brought together four laboratories at the ERDC site in Vicksburg, Mississippi—the Coastal and Hydraulics Laboratory, Environmental Laboratory, Geotechnical and Structures Laboratory, and Information Technology Laboratory—along with the Construction Engineering Research Laboratory in Champaign, Illinois; the Cold Regions Research and Engineering Laboratory in Hanover, New Hampshire; and the Topographic Engineering Center in Fort Belvoir, Virginia. Through this reorganization, ERDC integrated expertise across coastal hydraulics and environmental science, geotechnical and structural engineering, information technology, construction engineering, cold-region research, and topographic engineering.
The Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC) is a research and laboratory organization within the United States Army Corps of Engineers (USACE).

Łódź has emerged as a hub for foreign investment, with many international companies establishing offices in the city in recent years. Infosys, the Indian information technology company, operates a development center in Łódź. In January 2009 Dell announced the relocation of production from Limerick, Ireland to its Łódź plant, highlighting the city’s growing manufacturing appeal. Investor-friendly policies helped attract a large influx of foreign investors, totaling 980 by January 2009. The resulting capital inflow contributed to a reduction in unemployment, which fell to 6.5% in December 2008 from 20% four years earlier.

During the interwar period, Łódź displayed a pronounced left-wing orientation and served as a notable hub for socialist, communist, and Bundist activity within Polish politics. This confluence of leftist currents underscored the city’s significance in shaping Polish political life between World War I and World War II.

Vibin Mohanan is an Indian professional footballer who plays as a midfielder for Kerala Blasters FC in the Indian Super League. He recorded his first senior assist on 18 August 2023 in a 2–2 Durand Cup group-stage draw against Bengaluru FC reserves, and three days later added two assists in a 5–0 victory over Indian Air Force. He made his ISL debut for the 2023–24 season as a substitute against Bengaluru FC on 9 September 2023. Following Jeakson Singh’s shoulder injury in October 2023, Mohanan cemented his place in the Blasters’ midfield and emerged as a key contributor during Adrian Luna’s early-season absence. In November 2023 he was named Emerging Player of the Month in the ISL, with standout statistics that included 112 successful passes at 84.9% accuracy, 18 long passes (the second highest among outfield players), 25 possessions won (the most), and 13 duels won. On 24 December 2023 he sustained an injury in the home win against Mumbai City FC. He returned to action on 24 February 2024 in the 4–0 victory over FC Goa, and on 13 March 2024 he scored his first goal for the Blasters in a 3–4 home defeat to Mohun Bagan SG.

Vibin Mohanan is a footballer who operates predominantly as a dynamic central midfielder, recognized for his ability to impact play across the field. His versatility allows him to contribute in multiple roles, including serving in a deeper, defensive midfield position when required. He is capable of adapting to different midfield architectures, functioning effectively in both single-pivot and double-pivot setups.

CubeSmart is an American real estate investment trust that specializes in owning and operating self-storage facilities across the United States. As of December 31, 2024, the company owned 631 self-storage properties located in 25 states and the District of Columbia, totaling approximately 45.8 million rentable square feet. It ranks as the third-largest self-storage company in the United States.

Within Hindu literature, the Sadhyas are described as a gaṇa, or class, of deities mentioned in the Puranas. They constitute one of the nine gaṇas of divine beings, a group that also includes the adityas, rudras, vasus, visvedevas, tushitas, abhasvaras, anilas, and maharajikas. In some traditions, the Sadhyas are regarded as a subdivision within the gaṇadevas, a class of devas.

The sadhyas are a class of minor deities in Hinduism. In Puranic literature they are described as the offspring of Dharma and Sadhya, who is depicted as a daughter of Daksha. The number of sadhyas varies between texts, with lists that count twelve or seventeen members. They are associated with the ritual and liturgical elements of the Vedas, embodying the rites and hymns that underlie Vedic practice. Traditionally, they are said to reside among the devas or to dwell in the region between heaven and earth.

ISO/IEC 38500 traces its origins to Australia’s AS 8015, introduced in 2005 as the first standard addressing IT governance without focusing on management systems and processes. The 12-page document drew substantial international attention, which led ISO/IEC JTC 1 to invite Standards Australia to participate in the international adaptation of AS 8015. On February 1, 2007, ISO/IEC published the first Draft International Standard of the revised AS 8015 as ISO/IEC DIS 29382. In July 2007, the DIS gained fast-track status, allowing its submission for ISO approval, and revisions to the DIS were undertaken in September 2007. By January 2008, the final disposition of comments was completed, after which the standard was sent to the ISO/IEC Information Technology Task Force for consideration in the international standards process.

Development proceedings indicate that final approval occurred in spring 2008, with sources differing on whether this took place in April or May. The document was renamed to ISO/IEC 38500 shortly before the final approval. The completed standard was published on 1 June 2008 as ISO/IEC 38500:2008.

North Asia had an estimated population of about eight million in 1875. From 1801 to 1914, roughly seven million settlers relocated from European Russia to Siberia, reflecting a substantial demographic shift within the region. Of these migrations, about 85 percent occurred in the twenty-five years preceding World War I, roughly 1890 to 1914.

During the Pleistocene, glaciation influenced northern Asia, though its geological impact was comparatively smaller than that of similar processes in North America and Europe. The Scandinavian ice sheet extended east of the Urals, advancing across the northern two-thirds of the Ob Basin and reaching the Angara Shield between the Yenisei and Lena rivers. A lasting legacy of mountain glaciation is evident in the eastern Siberian ranges, the Kamchatka Peninsula, the Altai, and the Tian Shan, with contemporary ice caps persisting on Severnaya Zemlya and Novaya Zemlya and glaciers remaining on several Central Asian peaks. Permafrost is extensive across the region, with depths ranging from about 30 to 600 metres and covering roughly 9.6 million square kilometres.

Deep technical diving often relies on the use of more than one breathing gas during a single dive. The bottom gas is formulated to minimize both inert gas narcosis and oxygen toxicity in the deep portion of the ascent, while in open-circuit configurations it usually represents the largest portion of gas carried due to higher consumption at depth. For dives extending beyond approximately 65 metres (213 feet), the bottom gas’s oxygen fraction would not reliably sustain consciousness if breathed at surface pressures, which prompts the use of a travel gas carried from the surface to begin the dive and reach the intended depth. There remains a substantial overlap in the depths at which either gas can be employed, depending on the planned profile. The decision as to where to switch from one gas to the other is made by considering cumulative toxicity, narcosis risk, and the practicalities of gas budgeting for the overall dive plan.

Decompression practice encompasses methods used to manage ascent in order to minimize decompression stress. A delayed stop occurs when the ascent rate is slower than the table’s nominal rate, causing the planned decompression stops to be encountered later than expected. Computers used for decompression modeling account for the theoretical ingassing of slow tissues and the reduced outgassing of fast tissues, thereby refining the schedule. When using a table, the ascent schedule should be adjusted to compensate for these delays, including adding a delay to the bottom time before reaching the first decompression stop to reflect assumed ingassing. Delays between scheduled stops are generally ignored, under the assumption that no further ingassing has occurred during those intervals. In this sense, decompression practice can be regarded as a specific instance of a multi-level dive framework.

Bill Haley's Chicks is the eighth studio album by Bill Haley & His Comets for Decca Records (Decca 8821), released in January 1959 and produced by Milt Gabler. It constitutes the third entry in Decca's themed album series, following Rockin' the Oldies and Rockin' Around the World, and its repertoire centers on women's names, with each track portraying a different girl. The record includes Skinny Minnie, a major hit of 1958, which peaked at number 22 on Billboard and number 25 on Cashbox, and presents a blend of original compositions and cover versions of standards and jazz tunes. Lean Jean also charted in 1958 (Cashbox No. 52) and is musically and thematically reminiscent of Skinny Minnie. Additionally, B.B. Betty was co-written by Haley, issued as a Decca 45 single, and features Billy Williamson on a steel-guitar solo vocal.

Music therapy is a collaborative, person-centered practice conducted by a qualified therapist. It uses musical experiences and the varied dimensions of music—physical, emotional, cognitive, social, aesthetic, and spiritual—to enhance health or maintain well-being. Some needs are addressed directly through musical engagement, while others are met by fostering a therapeutic relationship. The approach is applied across the lifespan and across a wide range of conditions, including psychiatric disorders, medical illnesses, physical disabilities, sensory impairments, developmental and aging-related challenges, substance use issues, communication and interpersonal problems, and other health-related concerns. Goals typically encompass improved learning or cognitive functioning, increased self-esteem, reduced stress, support for physical activity, and related health-promoting outcomes. Methods include singing, instrument playing, composing or arranging songs, and other structured musical activities, all tailored to the individual’s objectives.

Contemporary music psychology seeks to explain and understand how people engage with and experience music. The discipline is predominantly empirical, progressing through the interpretation of data obtained from systematic observation and studies involving human participants. It concentrates on core perceptual and cognitive processes that underlie musical experience, listening, performance, and creativity. The findings hold practical relevance for diverse activities such as performance practice, composition, music education, criticism, and therapeutic contexts. Additionally, research within the field examines human aptitudes, skills, intelligence, creativity, and social behavior as they relate to musical phenomena.

Glenn Sutton left Columbia Records in 1976 and subsequently continued to produce records independently. He did not pursue a solo career as a singer, but he released two singles that charted on the Billboard country charts. One of these releases was the novelty song "The Football Card," which also gained crossover attention by approaching the Top 40 of the Billboard Hot 100 in 1979.

Glenn Sutton was an American songwriter and record producer renowned for his close personal and professional partnership with country singer Lynn Anderson, to whom he was married from 1968 to 1977. As producer for Anderson's Columbia Records years (1970–1976), Sutton oversaw the sessions that yielded the global hit "(I Never Promised You a Rose Garden)," written by Joe South. The accompanying album Rose Garden, which shared its title with the single, achieved broad international success, charting in 16 countries and becoming the best-selling album by a female country artist from 1970 to 1997. Sutton received an RIAA platinum award in recognition of his work on Rose Garden. In addition to his production work, he wrote three of Anderson's Billboard number-one country records—"You're My Man," "Keep Me in Mind," and "What a Man My Man Is"—as well as several of her top-ten and top-20 hits, contributing significantly to Anderson's commercial apex in the 1970s.

Following the Luxembourg Crisis, the 1867 Treaty of London mandated the dismantling of the fortifications surrounding Luxembourg City. The project lasted sixteen years and cost about 1.5 million gold francs. It involved the destruction of more than 24 kilometres (15 miles) of underground defences and roughly 4 hectares (about 9.9 acres) of casemates, batteries, barracks and related works. The agreement also provided for the withdrawal of the Prussian garrison stationed at the fortress.

Luxembourg City's fortifications include a network of casemates whose earliest galleries date to the 17th century. Beginning in 1644, the Spanish constructed roughly 23 kilometers (14 miles) of tunnels to bolster the defenses. Under French rule, Marshal Vauban expanded the tunnel complex, increasing its extent and capacity. The system was subsequently augmented again under Austrian rule in the 1730s and 1740s, reflecting successive rounds of enhancement that shaped the city’s underground military works.

The Economist Intelligence Corporate Network is a members-only service of The Economist Group that delivers global and regional business intelligence briefings, presentations, and advisory services to its subscribers. The network draws on the information, insights, and interactions supplied by regional experts within its parent organization to inform its offerings. Around 81% of its clientele are business executives at the director level or in senior management positions. The Economist Group runs the network from offices located in Dubai, Johannesburg, Beijing, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Singapore, and Tokyo.
Canback & Company, a strategy consulting firm with operations in more than 70 countries, was acquired in July 2015. Since the acquisition, it has been renamed EIU Canback.

In the Central African Republic, camera-trap records documented mongooses during 2011 and 2012. The individuals were tentatively identified as Pousargues's mongoose (Dologale dybowskii), though the designation remains preliminary and has not been definitively confirmed.

Dologale, known as Pousargues's mongoose, is a small species of mongoose distinguished by brown fur with a grey belly and a grey face. It features a bushy tail and front feet equipped with strong claws. The body measures approximately 25 to 33 cm in length, with a tail length ranging from 16 to 23 cm (about 6.5 to 9 inches).

Seborrheic-like psoriasis is a dermatological condition in which psoriatic lesions occur in conjunction with seborrheic dermatitis, resulting in an overlap of features from both disorders. It is also known by the alternative terms sebopsoriasis and seborrhiasis. The condition is characterized by the coexistence of psoriasis with seborrheic-type inflammatory changes, reflecting the simultaneous presence of two distinct inflammatory processes rather than a single, unified disease.

Sebaceous adenitis is an autoimmune disorder that targets the sebaceous glands, leading to hair loss in affected animals. It is primarily described in dogs, with certain breeds such as poodles and Akitas showing increased susceptibility. In canine populations, the condition is thought to follow an autosomal recessive inheritance pattern. Cases have also been documented in cats, with a single report in a rabbit. The disease manifests with alopecia, and the characteristic pattern and distribution of hair loss vary among species.

The Persian Gulf includes Iranian island groups that serve as important nesting grounds for seabirds. A 2009 survey of ten Iranian islands in the gulf documented more than 100,000 breeding pairs across 11 waterbird species, highlighting the ecological significance of these habitats. Notable species cited in the study included the bridled tern (Sterna anaethetus), the lesser crested tern (Thalasseus bengalensis), and the crab plover (Dromas ardeola). The islands provide critical nesting habitat for seabirds, and variations in seabird populations have been proposed as indicators of the broader regional ecological health.

The Gulf has carried several names in antiquity. The Assyrians called it the Bitter Sea. Following the expansion of the Achaemenid Empire into Persis (Pars, in what is now Fars Province on the southwestern Iranian plateau) around 550 BCE, Greek writers began to apply a Persian designation to the neighboring waters. By the time of Nearchus's Indikê (circa 300 BCE), the expression Persikon kolpos—literally "Persian gulf"—appears repeatedly, reinforcing the same geographic referent. These early usages reflect the longstanding association of the region with Persian power and underscore the antiquity of the gulf's nomenclature in classical literature.
Bill.com completed its initial public offering on the New York Stock Exchange in December 2019. In early 2020, the company relocated its headquarters from Palo Alto to San Jose, California.

Bill.com experienced significant governance activity in 2025 as major investors increased their holdings in BILL Holdings. Hedge fund Elliott Management owned roughly 5% of BILL Holdings' stock during 2025, while activist investor Starboard Value held about 8.5% and signaled an intention to pursue governance changes. In early 2025, Starboard Value, alongside Autodesk, reached a settlement to add two independent directors to BILL Holdings' board. In March 2025, Kenvue agreed to nominate three directors to the board. In September 2025, Starboard nominated four directors for election to the board, with four of BILL Holdings' 12 directors standing for election at the upcoming annual meeting. By September 2025, BILL Holdings had a market value of around $5 billion.

The article presents notable petroleum companies involved in exploration and production (E&P). The entries are organized alphabetically by continent, and within each continent, by country. Firms whose activities are limited to refining or marketing are excluded from the list.

In phonology, tautosyllabic phonemes are those that occupy the same syllable, while phonemes that do not share a syllable are described as heterosyllabic. An example illustrating this distinction can be found in the word mustard, where the phonemes /m/ and /t/ are heterosyllabic, since they belong to different syllables within the word.

Tautosyllabic is a term used in phonology to describe segments that lie within the same syllable. Specifically, two or more segments are tautosyllabic with each other when they occur in the same syllable, meaning they share a syllabic environment without an intervening boundary. In a monosyllabic word, all phonemes are mutually tautosyllabic since there is only one syllable. An illustrative example is the English word "cat," where the phonemes /k/, /æ/, and /t/ are all contained in a single syllable and are therefore tautosyllabic with one another. The concept may also be described as indicating a shared tautosyllabic distribution across the word's phonological structure.

Xian H-6, a Chinese jet-powered bomber adapted from the Soviet Tu-16, participated in flight tests at the Lop Nur site, where nine nuclear devices were released from the aircraft. With advancing ballistic missile technology, the aircraft's utility as a nuclear delivery platform declined, its role shifting toward other forms of strike capability. In 1976, the Central Intelligence Agency assessed that the H-6 had transitioned to a dual-capability mission, able to carry and deliver both nuclear and conventional ordnance.

One H-6 bomber, serial number 086, was converted into an engine testbed to test and evaluate propulsion engines. The modified airframe remained in service for twenty years before its role was superseded by a converted Ilyushin Il-76.

Something's Coming: The BBC Recordings 1969–1970 is a two-disc compilation of BBC performances from 1969 and 1970. The release includes liner notes written by Peter Banks, the original guitarist who was dismissed from the band shortly after the sessions. It appeared in 1997 with Banks providing supervision and accompanying notes. In the United States, the edition was licensed to Purple Pyramid, Cleopatra Records, and issued under the title Beyond and Before: The BBC Recordings 1969–1970. A European release issued by Double Classics carried the title Something's Coming.

Something's Coming: The BBC Recordings 1969–1970 is a compilation of live BBC Radio performances by the English progressive rock group Yes, recorded during 1969 and 1970. It features the only Yes performances to date that showcase the band's original lineup, and its material is drawn from early BBC broadcasts. The tracks are largely drawn from Yes's first two albums, providing a snapshot of the group's formative period in that era. The release also includes two rarities: a live version of "Something's Coming" from West Side Story, which had previously appeared as the B-side to "Sweetness," and "For Everyone," a piece not issued in any other version.

In May 2020, Bechevinka, a former naval base, was selected as the site for a new LNG transshipment hub to be developed by Novatek. The facility is intended to function as a liquefied natural gas transshipment hub, with a projected annual throughput of 20 million long tons. The project is largely oriented toward supplying Asian export markets, with an estimated cost of about $1.5 billion.

Bechevinka was a naval base used by the Soviet and Russian Navies, located in a remote portion of Russia’s Kamchatka Peninsula. Established in the 1960s to support submarines of the Soviet Pacific Fleet, the facility was abandoned in 1996 and has since become a ghost town that attracts tourists. In May 2020, the energy company Novatek proposed developing the site into a transshipment hub for liquefied natural gas.

Independent Press Standards Organisation (IPSO) is the self-regulatory body that handles complaints about the UK press. The National Union of Journalists has argued that journalists have little protection from editors who press for sensational, commercially driven stories at the expense of ethical considerations. In 2016, the NUJ endorsed IMPRESS as the regulator with the best prospect of delivering genuinely independent press regulation. The union framed IMPRESS as an alternative to the major national newspaper publishers, which it believed did not consistently uphold their professional responsibilities.

IPSO, the Independent Press Standards Organisation, functions as the regulator for the press, overseeing adherence to the Editors' Code of Practice. The code governs matters such as accuracy, privacy protections, intrusion into grief or shock, and harassment. The organization considers concerns about editorial content and the conduct of journalists across newspapers and magazines, and it conducts investigations into alleged breaches of editorial standards and compliance. It undertakes monitoring activities, including requiring publications to submit annual compliance reports. When necessary, IPSO can require the publication of prominent corrections and may issue adjudications critiquing coverage. In cases of particularly serious and systemic failings, it retains the authority to sanction publications, including imposing fines.

Keelung's early history includes the Spanish establishment of Fort San Salvador in 1626 at the site of what is now Keelung. The area was inhabited by indigenous peoples of Taiwan. Sovereignty over the settlement eventually passed to the Qing dynasty. In the 19th century, fighting around Keelung occurred during both the First Opium War and the Sino-French War. In 1895, following the First Sino-Japanese War, Taiwan was ceded to the Empire of Japan, and the city was known as Kirun under Japanese rule. After 1945, Keelung became part of Taiwan Province under the Republic of China. In 2018, the city was elevated to a first-level subdivision after the abolition of the provincial government.

Following World War II, Taiwan's economy shifted from import substitution to an export-oriented growth model, a transition that coincided with Keelung's emergence as a major foreign-trade hub and a key international shipping node in northern Taiwan. In the 1970s, rising trade activity led to expanded port logistics services, including transportation, warehousing, and customs brokerage, while the city also experienced growth in shipbuilding and ship maintenance industries. By 1984, the Port of Keelung ranked as the seventh-largest container port in the world.

The Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals (GHS) delegates the task of establishing and validating toxicity testing requirements for substances and mixtures to regulatory authorities such as the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency and the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development. Hazard criteria within the GHS are designed to be test-method neutral, allowing a range of scientifically valid and validated approaches that are aligned with internationally recognized procedures referenced by existing classification frameworks. In addition, the framework emphasizes that data already generated for classification under established systems should be accepted within the GHS, thereby avoiding duplicate testing and reducing the use of animals in safety evaluations.

Under the Globally Harmonized System of Classification and Labelling of Chemicals (GHS), the aspiration hazard denotes the potential for a liquid or solid to reach the trachea and lower respiratory tract, leading to severe acute outcomes such as chemical pneumonia, pulmonary injury, or fatality after aspiration. Aspiration itself is defined as the entry of a liquid or solid into the trachea and lower respiratory system, whether entering directly through the oral or nasal cavity or indirectly as a result of vomiting. Within this hazard class, substances and mixtures are categorized into two hazard categories, assigned according to their viscosity.

An open vowel is part of the broader category of low vowels, defined as vowels produced with a greater degree of articulatory openness than mid vowels. This group includes open-mid vowels, near-open vowels, and open vowels themselves, all classified as low due to their increased openness relative to mid vowels. The determination that a vowel is low is inherently relative to the mid-vowel reference point, and the exact height can vary across languages and phonological analyses.

An exceptionally uncommon phonetic distinction among open unrounded vowels at the front, center, and back has been documented for the Hamont-Achel variety of Limburgish. The dialect exhibits long realizations of these open vowels, while short forms are attested for the open-front and open-back vowels. The open-central vowel, however, lacks a short counterpart and occurs only in a long realization. Consequently, the short open-front and short open-back vowels do not form a direct phonemic contrast with the open-central vowel.

Ayeshteni (Arabic: عيشتني) is the fourth album by Belgian singer Natacha Atlas. Released by Mantra Records on May 8, 2001, the release received extensive airplay on college radio and sold approximately 15,000 copies in its first two years of release.
The 2016 campaign prioritized obtaining federal funding for the Salton Sea Red Hill Bay restoration project, and Ruiz's platform also highlighted his advocacy for veterans.
Raul Ruiz was reelected, defeating Republican challenger Erin Cruz, an author who had been a candidate for the United States Senate in 2018. Ruiz won with 60.3% of the vote.

Antoine Augustin Cournot was a French mathematician whose work significantly influenced economics despite his primary focus on mathematics. In his 1838 treatise, Researches on Mathematical Principles of the Theory of Wealth, he applied mathematical methods to economic analysis, though the work faced criticism and was not highly successful during his lifetime, leading him to revise it twice. Today the book is regarded as a foundational text for modern economic analysis. Cournot also introduced functions and probabilistic reasoning into economic thought and derived what is now seen as the first formal expression of the law of supply and demand as a function of price. He was the first to graphically depict supply and demand curves, a move that anticipated Alfred Marshall’s graphical treatment by roughly thirty years. Moreover, the Cournot duopoly model contributed to the development of game-theoretic concepts, introducing the idea of a pure-strategy Nash equilibrium, together with the reaction function and best-response dynamics.

Antoine Augustin Cournot was born on 28 August 1801 in Gray, in the Haute-Saône department of France. He began his education at the preparatory school of the Collège de Gray in 1809 and remained there until he was about fifteen years old. He then continued his studies at the Collège Royal de Besançon.

Chick sexing is the practice of determining the sex of chicks, historically conducted using instrument-based methods. Instrument or machine-based sexing has largely disappeared due to the unavailability of instruments and spare parts. When employed, the approach used a Keeler Optical device in English-speaking contexts or the Chicktester in Japan. These machines feature a blunt-ended telescopic tube that contains a light; the sexer inserts the tube into the evacuated cloaca, and the illumination helps determine whether the chick possesses testes or ovaries.

Chick sexing refers to the classification of poultry chicks by sex to route them into appropriate production pathways. In egg-production operations, male chicks are typically undesirable, since they do not contribute to egg production and are not efficient for meat. In meat-production systems, breeders maintain distinct male and female lines to produce hybrids that are raised for consumption. Chicks of the opposite sex to a given line are regarded as surplus. To limit costs, unwanted-sex chicks are culled soon after hatching.

Richard Olney was an American attorney and local politician who was elected as a selectman in West Roxbury, Massachusetts. He served a single term in the Massachusetts House of Representatives in 1874, during which he was a member of the Committee on the Judiciary. After choosing not to seek reelection, Olney returned to his law practice.

Richard Olney was an American statesman who served as United States Secretary of State under President Grover Cleveland in the 1890s. He played a central role in the Venezuelan crisis of 1895, articulating a robust interpretation of the Monroe Doctrine that asserted U.S. authority to resolve hemispheric disputes. In domestic and foreign policy, he helped manage Cleveland's anti-expansionist stance in response to the overthrow of the Hawaiian Kingdom and the Cuban War of Independence. While Hawaii would later be annexed under President William McKinley, Cuba's status remained unresolved after its struggle for independence. Olney also contributed to elevating the status of American diplomacy by upgrading many diplomatic legations to full embassies, thereby strengthening the formal standing of the United States on the world stage.

On June 18, 1977, the inaugural St Magnus Festival of the Arts opened in Orkney, marking its establishment by Sir Peter Maxwell Davies, a local resident and renowned composer. The event's opening performance featured Davies's opera The Martyrdom of St Magnus.

On August 20, 1977, NASA launched the uncrewed probe Voyager 2, which carried the Golden Record—a phonographic archive intended to convey Earth's life and culture to potential extraterrestrial listeners. The record featured a range of sounds and images, including the first movements of Bach's Brandenburg Concerto and Beethoven's Fifth Symphony, Guan Pinghu's Liu Shui performed on the guqin, and Chuck Berry's Johnny B. Goode.

Slot-die coating, developed in the 1950s, is a scalable method for depositing thin, uniform films with relatively low operating costs. It minimizes material waste and supports rapid production, making it suitable for large-area applications. The technique is used to apply a variety of liquid chemistries onto substrates such as glass, metal, and polymers. Precise metering of the process fluid is achieved, with material dispensed at a controlled rate as the coating die moves relative to the substrate, ensuring consistent film thickness. The inner geometry of conventional slot dies is complex and typically requires machining, though fabrication can be accomplished with three-dimensional printing.

A coating is a layer applied to a substrate, encompassing paints and lacquers, whose primary aims are to protect the underlying material and to provide decoration. Although some artists’ paints are used solely for ornamental purposes, industrial coatings applied to pipelines serve both corrosion prevention and identification through color coding—for example blue denotes process water lines and red indicates fire‑fighting control systems. Functional coatings are designed to modify surface properties such as adhesion, wettability, or wear resistance, while certain formulations introduce entirely new capabilities, including magnetic responsiveness or electrical conductivity. In semiconductor device fabrication, coating steps on wafers form an essential component of the completed product.

Cristina Fernández de Kirchner, along with Florencio Randazzo, sought the Senate seat for Buenos Aires Province in the 2017 midterm elections. Fernández de Kirchner refused to participate in primaries and conditioned her candidacy on a shared ticket, a demand Randazzo did not accept. In the general election, the Frente para la Victoria (FPV) split, with the Justicialist Party of Buenos Aires Province backing Randazzo while other FPV parties supported Fernández de Kirchner. The remaining FPV factions formed the Unidad Ciudadana (Citizen's Unity) coalition. Esteban Bullrich was the candidate of Cambiemos.

Cristina Fernández de Kirchner began her political career in Santa Cruz, and in 1989 was elected as a deputy to the Santa Cruz provincial legislature. In the same year, the Justicialist Party, led by Carlos Menem, returned to the presidency after the general elections. She briefly served as interim governor of Santa Cruz in 1990 for a few days following the impeachment of Ricardo del Val. She later organized Néstor Kirchner's gubernatorial campaign when he was elected governor of Santa Cruz in 1991. In 1994 she was elected to the constituent assembly that amended the Constitution of Argentina.

"America" is widely regarded as a significant step in Simon & Garfunkel's artistic development. In a 1972 review, Stephen Holden described the piece as a compact narrative of about three and a half minutes, distinguished by precise detail and sweeping observation, conveying a restless sense of America and a drama of shared loneliness during a bus trip with implications that reach toward the cosmic. Record World observed that the Greatest Hits single version adopts a more commercial stance with a more elaborate production than the Bookends version. Thom Jurek of AllMusic argues that the song centers on a fundamental, unanswerable question—an ellipsis or cipher—while the sophisticated harmonic invention of the music is ultimately undercut by the message. David Nichols, in 1001 Albums You Must Hear Before You Die, calls it a splendid vignette of a road trip by young lovers, intimate in scope yet epic in scale, tracing an inner journey from naive optimism to mature understanding. American Songwriter describes it as essentially a road-trip song that reveals as much about the travelers as about the lands they traverse.

Yes guitarist Steve Howe has described the band's cover of Simon & Garfunkel's "America" as a somewhat overlooked entry within their discography. The recording has seldom been featured on Yes compilations, and when it does appear, it is typically presented in a shortened form. Howe's interaction with Paul Simon occurred at a disaster-relief benefit concert in 1992, where Howe asked whether Simon appreciated Yes's version; Simon stated that he did indeed like the rendition.

Maren Morris became the first active country artist to reach the No. 1 position on the Dance/Mix Show Airplay chart, achieving this distinction as a featured artist on the collaboration between Zedd and Grey for the track "The Middle." The song reached the top of the chart in the March 3, 2018 issue.

Kelly Osbourne's song "One Word" made history by becoming the first track to ascend to the top position on all three Billboard dance charts—Dance/Mix Show Airplay, Hot Dance Club Play, and Hot Dance Single Sales—in the same charting week, achieving this on June 18, 2005.
Dabanas is the site of the ruins of a fortress located near the village of Döğer, in the Dicle district of Diyarbakır Province, in present-day Turkey.

Dabanas is a fortress located in the historical region of Osroene. It was known in antiquity by the Greek designation Δαβανάς. The site remained inhabited during the Roman and subsequent Byzantine eras, and it is mentioned by the chronicler Procopius. The fortress was utilized during the reign of Emperor Justinian I.

Lizzy Caplan began her acting career in 1999, making her screen debut as Sara in Freaks and Geeks, a role that places her as the romantic partner of Jason Segel’s character. She went on to make guest appearances on a variety of television series and appeared in Jason Mraz’s music video for “You and I Both.” In 2000 she appeared in her first film, the direct-to-television release From Where I Sit. In 2001 she portrayed Tina Greer on Smallville, a role she reprised in 2003. She also appeared in two episodes of ABC’s Once and Again. In 2003 Caplan starred as Faith Pitt in The Pitts. Her profile rose with the role of Janis Ian in Mean Girls (2004). She later played Avery Bishop in the second season of Tru Calling.

Lizzy Caplan (born June 30, 1982) is an American actress known for her work in film and television. Born in Los Angeles, she was raised in the Miracle Mile neighborhood and comes from a Reform Jewish family of Ashkenazi descent, having celebrated a Bat Mitzvah and attended Jewish summer camps. Her father, Richard Caplan, is a lawyer, and her mother, Barbara (née Bragman), worked as a political aide. She is the youngest of three siblings, with a brother named Benjamin and a sister named Julie. Her mother died of cancer when Caplan was thirteen. Her uncle, Howard Bragman, is a publicist. Caplan attended Alexander Hamilton High School in the Castle Heights area, where she joined the Academy of Music; she initially pursued piano before turning to drama, and she also played on the school's soccer team. She graduated in 2000 and chose not to attend college in order to focus on acting.

Pods and Gods is a 7-inch EP by the punk rock band NOFX, released a month before their album Pump Up the Valuum. The title track was originally planned for inclusion on Pump Up the Valuum, while the EP’s B-side was also slated for the album; however, the group ultimately decided to feature the song "My Vagina" on the album instead. That track later appeared on the compilation 45 or 46 Songs That Weren't Good Enough to Go on Our Other Records. The EP was issued in a limited run of 12,000 copies on orange vinyl.

The AP Stylebook recommends using Latino for persons of Spanish-speaking ancestry and for people from or whose ancestors are from Latin America, including Brazilians. Historically, Latinos has also been used to refer to people from the Caribbean region. However, that Caribbean usage does not extend to individuals from former French, Dutch, and British colonial territories in the Caribbean.

In 1997, the U.S. government officially adopted the ethnonym Hispanic or Latino, adding Latino as a parallel term and thereby replacing the previously used single term Hispanic. The shift reflected regional differences in usage: Hispanic tends to be more common in the eastern United States, while Latino is more common in the western United States.

Re Smith & Fawcett Ltd [1942] Ch 304 is a leading UK company law case that examined the interpretation of the phrase “the interests of the company” within directors’ duties. The court held that the expression refers to the interests of the company as a whole rather than the private interests of individual shareholders, thereby reinforcing the notion that directors owe duties to the company entity itself. The decision has proven influential in the development of modern corporate governance doctrine and is frequently cited in discussions of directors’ duties under statute, particularly in relation to the Companies Act 2006, section 172, which requires directors to promote the company’s success while having regard to factors such as stakeholder interests and long-term outcomes.

Re Smith & Fawcett Ltd concerned the directors’ discretionary power under Article 10 of the company’s constitution to refuse to register share transfers. After the death of Mr. Fawcett, who was both a director and a shareholder, Mr. Smith co-opted another director. The directors then declined to register a transfer of shares to Fawcett’s executors. In the arrangement at issue, half of the shares had already been bought, while the remaining half were offered to the executors.

IEC 60870 denotes a family of companion standards that extend the broader IEC 60870 framework to support telecontrol and related data communications in automation networks. The standards IEC 60870-5-101, -5-102, -5-103, and -5-104 specify distinct functions: Part 101 defines the basic telecontrol tasks and the general characteristics of telecontrol equipment and systems; Part 102 governs the transmission of integrated totals; Part 103 covers data exchange from protection equipment; and Part 104 provides network access for the IEC 101 protocol, along with the associated transmission mechanisms. Collectively these parts enable remote operation, measurement, protection-data exchange, and networked access within utility automation and supervisory control and data acquisition contexts.

IEC 60870 refers to a family of standards that define telecontrol and supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) applications in electrical engineering and power-system automation. They are used to oversee electric power transmission networks and widely distributed control installations. The protocols established by IEC 60870 enable interoperable operation among equipment from different vendors. The collection comprises six parts, addressing general information, operating conditions, electrical interfaces, performance requirements, and data transmission protocols. The standards were developed by IEC Technical Committee 57, Working Group 03.

On January 20, 2025, Le Monde announced its withdrawal from X (formerly Twitter). The decision was attributed to an escalation of Elon Musk’s activism on the platform and the increasing toxicity of discussions taking place there. The editors stated that stepping back aligns with the paper’s commitment to editorial independence and to avoiding participation in an online environment deemed harmful to public debate. The editorial team acknowledged that the choice was difficult, but insisted it was necessary.

Le Monde came under the control of a trio—Matthieu Pigasse, Pierre Bergé, and Xavier Niel—when they secured a controlling stake in June 2010. In October 2018, Pigasse sold 49% of his stake to Czech entrepreneur Daniel Křetínský. The Independency Group, a minority shareholder dedicated to safeguarding the newspaper’s editorial independence, said it had not been informed of the 2018 sale. It requested that Pigasse and Křetínský sign an approval agreement granting the group the right to approve or reject any future controlling shareholder. As of September 2019, the approval agreement had not been signed.
The Battle of Hoople's Creek, sometimes referred to as Hoople Creek, was a skirmish that took place on November 10, 1813, and it served as a precursor to the Battle of Crysler's Farm.

During the Battle of Hoople's Creek, the Stormont and Glengarry Militias clashed with the 1st U.S. Rifles along Hoople's Creek in Stormont County. The engagement slowed the American advance toward Cornwall, a delay that allowed the evacuation of important military supplies from the town. The postponement also gave General Morrison time to consolidate his forces around Crysler's Farm in preparation for the forthcoming decisive battle.

Secondary literature concerning deconstruction is markedly heterogeneous, spanning a wide range of approaches, aims, and degrees of technical detail. Critics argue that problems arise when scholars rooted primarily in literary criticism and with only limited philosophy training attempt concise introductions to the topic, sometimes producing oversimplified or skewed accounts. These secondary works are frequently criticized for diverging from Derrida's original texts and for not accurately reflecting the nuances of his positions. Invoked as representative examples in such critiques are titles like Deconstruction for Beginners and Deconstructions: A User's Guide.

Deconstruction, as developed by Jacques Derrida, seeks to resist being absorbed into Hegel’s dialectical scheme. In Hegel's framework, opposing concepts are seen as culminating in a synthesis that purportedly resolves their tension. Derrida contends that such oppositions cannot be genuinely dissolved into a synthesis that eliminates the original contradiction, and thus aims to distinguish deconstruction from the Hegelian method. Accordingly, Derrida treats these pairs as inherently unstable, with meaning and significance dependent on what lies beyond any given opposition. The approach and its critiques shaped the intellectual life of late 20th-century French thought, influencing discussions among figures such as Kojève and Hyppolite, and intersecting with Marxist dialectics and Sartre’s existentialism, among others.

Mallory Franklin is an athlete who has competed at the ICF Canoe Slalom World Championships, where she has earned a total of sixteen medals. Her gold medals total seven, achieved across several events: the C1 individual title in 2017 and 2023; the C1 team titles in 2017, 2018, and 2023; and the K1 team titles in 2019 and 2021. She has five silver medals, four of which come from the C1 individual event (2013, 2014, 2018, 2021) and one from the K1 event (2018). Her four bronze medals include a C1 individual bronze in 2022, a C1 team bronze in 2022, and K1 team bronzes in 2018 and 2023.

Mallory Franklin has achieved considerable success in European competition, winning 21 medals at the European Championships, consisting of seven golds, eight silvers, and six bronzes. At the 2023 European Games held in Kraków, she earned a silver and a bronze medal.

Vanessa Maria van Arendonk (born 22 November 1980 in Curaçao) is a Curaçaoan model and beauty pageant titleholder. She won Miss Curaçao in 2003 and represented Curaçao at Miss Universe 2003, the international pageant held in Panama. Earlier in her career she captured the titles Miss International Curaçao (2001) and Miss Curaçao Universe (2003), making her the first Miss Curaçao to hold two major island titles.

The Topeka Capital-Journal is a newspaper that was formed through a history of name changes and mergers in Topeka, Kansas. Among the mergers contributing to its creation was the union of The Topeka Daily Capital and The Topeka State Journal.

From 1976 to 1982, Argentina operated a naval facility, Corbeta Uruguay, on Thule Island in the South Sandwich Islands. The Royal Navy ordered its closure in 1982. Argentina’s claim to South Georgia was among the factors that contributed to the 1982 Falklands War, during which Argentine forces briefly occupied South Georgia. Argentina continues to assert sovereignty over South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands as part of its Tierra del Fuego, Antártida e Islas del Atlántico Sur Province.

Fisheries management and environmental protection within the territory of South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands are the responsibility of its Government, the Government of South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands (GSGSSI). To fulfill these duties, GSGSSI contracts Workboat Services Limited (WBS), a Falkland Islands–based company, to operate the vessel MV Pharos SG. The MV Pharos SG operates within the South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands Maritime Zone, supporting the government's activities in the region. The current contract for the operation of MV Pharos SG runs through 2028.

In the early Renaissance, composers increasingly treated the interval of a third and its inversion, the sixth, as a foundation for harmony, marking a shift from medieval practice in which thirds and sixths were regarded as dissonant and consonance was defined primarily by perfect intervals such as the octave, unison, fourth, and fifth. The 14th century saw polyphony become more intricate, with voices—whether sung or played on instruments—developing greater independence. At the beginning of the 15th century, musical texture began to simplify and favor smoother melodic lines. This smoothing was made possible by a substantially expanded vocal range, which reduced the need for voice crossing and allowed clearer, more continuous melodic contours across parts.

Within Renaissance music, Musica reservata denotes a distinct style or performance practice applied to a cappella vocal music. Emerging in the latter half of the 16th century, it developed chiefly in Italy and southern Germany. The approach is associated with a refined manner, a sense of exclusivity, and a pronounced, emotionally charged rendering of the sung text.

Men in Vogue was a British non-pornographic men's magazine that ceased publication in 1970. Its demise, alongside the failure of other British titles such as Town (which had previously been About Town and before that Man About Town) and Esquire in the 1950s, is cited as part of a broader decline of non-pornographic men’s magazines in the United Kingdom. Explanations for the downturn point to the smaller size of the UK market compared with the United States and to advertising competition from commercial television and the rising prominence of colour newspaper supplements. The launch of the first UK colour supplement in The Sunday Times in February 1962 proved highly successful, drawing approximately 250,000 new readers, and as a result, many of the large Sunday newspapers soon adopted similar colour features, altering the advertising and editorial landscape for men's magazines.

Men in Vogue is a Vogue feature that examines whether the Englishman represents the best-dressed man in the world. The piece gathers profiles of a cohort of prominent individuals, including James Astor, Cecil Beaton, Brinsley Black, Gay Kindersley, Nigel Lawson, Jocelyn Stevens (editor-in-chief of Queen), Sir Fitzroy Maclean, Christopher Gibbs, Lord Gormanston, and Julian Ormsby-Gore.

Indian football has a long history, with organized competitions dating back to the eighteenth century. The National Football League (NFL) was established in 1996, with its inaugural season in 1996–97, and its champions were regarded as the national champions of Indian football. Following the 2006–07 season, the NFL was rebranded as the I-League, and its champions continued to be treated as national champions until 2017. In 2017, the Indian Super League (ISL) emerged as the country’s joint premier top-tier competition. By 2022, the ISL had become the sole top-tier league in India. Up to the 2021–22 season, ISL playoff winners were considered the champions; beginning with the 2022–23 season, the designation is awarded to the team that finishes atop the league table.

Within India's top-tier football history, twelve clubs have won the championships awarded under the National Football League (NFL) and the I-League and their various titles, while six clubs have claimed ISL honours since it was elevated to joint top-division status. JCT FC became the first club to secure a national championship with the 1996–97 NFL title. Mohun Bagan is the most successful club, having won seven championships across the NFL (three titles), the I-League (two titles), and the ISL (two titles).

Newcastle, Wyoming comprises 1,253 households, of which 30.4% have children under 18. Married couples living together account for 54.0% of all households, while households headed by a woman with no husband present make up 10.1%. Nonfamily households constitute 32.6% of the total, and individuals living alone represent 28.4% of all households, including 13.0% of residents living alone who are 65 years of age or older. The average household size is 2.35, and the average family size is 2.88.

Historically, U.S. Route 85 extended southward from Newcastle along the eastern side of the adjacent railroad corridor. The highway crossed the railroad on a five-span steel girder bridge constructed in 1929, utilizing wide-flange girders. In 1963, the segment from Newcastle to just south of the crossing was realigned to the west, effectively bypassing the bridge itself.

Qinhuangdao, whose name translates to “Qin Emperor Island,” derives from a legend that the Jieshishan Scenic Area in Changli County was the site of a ritual performed by the First Emperor of Qin during his eastward survey in 210 BCE. The so‑called island in the city’s name refers to the Nanshan area within the Port of Qinhuangdao, located at the southern edge of Haigang District. Historically, Nanshan was a small offshore island until the late Qing dynasty, when it was connected to the mainland by the dumping of dredged silt after the Guangxu Emperor approved port construction in the late 19th century.

Qinhuangdao has attracted a wide range of suppliers, both Chinese and foreign, to support the city’s port development and related infrastructure projects. China Ocean Shipping (Group) Co (COSCO), the largest shipping company in China, has signaled approximately US$49 billion in port-related spending over the coming five years. The anticipated investment is intended to address bottlenecks created by China's unprecedented economic growth.

Robert A. Molloy began his legal career as a law clerk to Judge Raymond L. Finch of the District Court of the Virgin Islands, and subsequently served as the Assistant Attorney General of Labor for the Virgin Islands Office of Collective Bargaining.

Robert A. Molloy completed a Bachelor of Science degree at Hampton University, earned a Juris Doctor from American University’s Washington College of Law, and obtained a Master of Business Administration from American University’s Kogod School of Business.

Seaworthiness denotes the suitability of a vessel to operate safely within its operating environment. The operating environment comprises the conditions under which the ship is operating and is described by factors such as the sea state, the wind speed, and the geographic region of operation. These elements may occur alone or in combination, and their interplay determines whether the vessel is considered seaworthy for a given voyage.

In seakeeping, human factors frequently determine overall seaworthiness, particularly on small vessels where crews may be limited in resources. The most consequential elements are the crew's experience and their proficiency in handling extreme or unexpected conditions. Related considerations include mitigating seasickness, ensuring adequate sleep, maintaining sufficient food and hydration, and preventing injuries throughout the duration of an extreme event. Together, these factors interact with vessel design and equipment to influence safety, performance, and the ability to respond effectively to adverse weather or offshore conditions.

Canada's Walk of Fame recognizes successful Canadians, with the honor signified by a row of stars embedded in the sidewalks. The stars are positioned on designated blocks of the sidewalk along King Street and Simcoe Street in Toronto, creating a public route that commemorates national achievement.

Toronto experiences precipitation that is relatively evenly distributed throughout the year, with the summer months being the wettest, largely due to thunderstorms. The city averages 822.7 mm (32.4 inches) of precipitation annually, while average snowfall per year is about 121.5 cm (48 inches). Sunshine is relatively abundant, totaling around 2,066 hours per year, which corresponds to roughly 45 percent of daylight. Seasonal sunshine varies from about 28 percent in December to around 60 percent in July.

Pope Stephen VII (Latin: Stephanus VII) held the office of bishop of Rome and the nominal rulers of the Papal States from February 929 until his death on 15 March 931. He was presented as pope by Marozia, a notorious Roman noblewoman who exerted substantial influence over papal politics at the time. His pontificate occurred during the Saeculum obscurum, a period characterized by strong secular influence over the papacy.

Very little is known about Pope Stephen VII's pontificate, which lasted for about two years. During his tenure, he confirmed the privileges of several religious houses in France and Italy. As a reward for helping free Stephen from the oppression of Hugh of Arles, he granted Cante di Gabrielli the position of papal governor of Gubbio and control over several key fortresses. He was noted for severity in punishing clergy who strayed morally. A hostile Greek source from the 12th century claims he was the first pope to be clean-shaven while pope.

The X-24A featured a short, bulbous teardrop-shaped fuselage and a three-fin tail arrangement, consisting of a central vertical fin with outward-canted fins on the left and right. Its first unpowered glide flight occurred on April 17, 1969, piloted by Major Jerauld R. Gentry, and the first powered flight followed on March 19, 1970 with the same pilot. The aircraft was drop-launched from a modified B-52 at approximately 45,000 feet (13.7 km). After release, it typically glided downward, though it could also use its rocket engine to ascend to a higher altitude before resuming a glide. During testing, the X-24A flew 28 flights, reaching speeds up to 1,036 mph (1,667 km/h) and altitudes as high as 71,400 feet (21.8 km).

Martin Marietta's X-24A participated in a flight program that, like the HL-10, demonstrated that a Space Shuttle could land unpowered. The aircraft completed 28 flights in this program. It reached a maximum speed of 1,036 mph (1,667 km/h; Mach 1.6) and a maximum altitude of 71,400 ft (21.8 km). Its propulsion came from an XLR-11 rocket engine with vacuum thrust up to 8,480 lbf (37.7 kN).

Neurofunk is a dark subgenre of drum and bass that emerged in London, England, during the late 1990s, specifically between 1997 and 1998. It developed as a progression of the techstep strand of the genre and is informally referred to as "neuro" by practitioners and fans.

Neurofunk developed by juxtaposing darker, heavier, and harder funk with influences from techno, house, and jazz. Its distinguishing features include consecutive stabs over the bassline and razor-sharp backbeats, while traditional melodies are scarce or nonexistent. The style places a hyper focus on sub sound design, with producers employing modulated, distorted, and filtered synthesizers to craft its distinctive textures. Audio material is frequently captured from samplers such as the Akai S1000 and the Emu E6400, which serve as primary sources for the genre’s aggressive timbres.

Ralph Norman, a member of the United States House of Representatives, violated House rules in 2021 by not wearing a face mask in the House Chamber and was fined $500 under those rules. He, along with two other Republican lawmakers, filed suit against Speaker Nancy Pelosi over the incident. On August 5, 2021, Norman tested positive for COVID-19 and said that he was fully vaccinated and had only mild symptoms.
According to FiveThirtyEight's analysis, Ralph Norman voted in alignment with President Joe Biden's stated position on 2% of votes during the 117th Congress.

The Paris Economy Pact was an agreement among the Allied Powers aimed at isolating the Central Powers—the German Empire, the Austro-Hungarian Empire, the Ottoman Empire, and the Kingdom of Bulgaria—by restricting trade relations in the postwar period. To enforce this strategy, the Allies envisaged sanctions on trade after the war to prevent economic rehabilitation of these states. A permanent international committee, the Comité permanent international d'action économique, based in Paris, was established to monitor adherence to and implementation of the pact.

The Paris Economy Pact was an international economic agreement concluded at the Paris Economic Conference, held in Paris on 14 June 1916, during the height of World War I. The conference brought together representatives of the Allied Powers, including the United Kingdom, France, Italy, Japan, and Russia, who participated in negotiations that produced the accord.

Lexico is an online dictionary service that was launched in June 2019 when free English and Spanish dictionaries moved to Lexico.com through a collaboration between Oxford University Press and Dictionary.com, with content authored exclusively by OUP staff. The migration ended the US English dictionary on Oxford Living Dictionaries, leaving only words not present in the UK dictionary accessible on that platform, and the US English dictionary was restored in full on Lexico by early 2020. The name Lexico also forms part of the former corporate designation of Dictionary.com, Lexico Publishing Group, LLC.

Lexico was a dictionary website offering English and Spanish dictionaries compiled by Oxford University Press (OUP). Although the content originated with OUP, the site was operated by Dictionary.com, a platform that hosts dictionaries from a range of publishers, including Random House. On 26 August 2022, Lexico was closed and its pages redirected to Dictionary.com.

Romance of the Three Kingdoms, a classic work of Chinese literature, is noted for its intricate narrative technique, as Yao Yao’s example from Chapter 79 (Mao edition) demonstrates the weaving of two plot strands within a single chapter and the blending of poetry with prose. Chapter 79 itself contains two interrelated episodes: Liu Bei’s attempt to punish two generals who refused to aid Guan Yu, a move that contributes to Guan Yu’s death, including the execution of one of the generals who is his adopted son. In the following sections, Chapters 82–84 recount Liu Bei’s consolidation of his forces to oppose Sun Quan at the Battle of Yiling, where he suffers a total defeat, marking a major reversal in the broader conflict among the Three Kingdoms.

Romance of the Three Kingdoms is a historical novel that draws on multiple sources, most prominently Chen Shou's Records of the Three Kingdoms from the third century. The Records trace events from the Yellow Turban Rebellion of 184 through the unification of Jin in 280. The work also incorporates elements from Tang dynasty poetry and Yuan dynasty operas, reflecting a broad literary lineage.
