The author infuses the narrative with personal interpretations of virtue and legitimacy, shaping its perspectives on leadership and authority. By blending historical knowledge with storytelling, the novel creates a rich tapestry of personalities and a nuanced portrayal of its historical world.

At the conclusion of her Miss USA reign in 1979, Judi Andersen crowned Mary Therese Friel as Miss USA 1979. She subsequently pursued acting, appearing on television programs such as Fantasy Island, Magnum, P.I., and Jake and the Fatman. Andersen later served as a judge at Miss USA 1980. After her entertainment pursuits, she returned to Hawaii and owned and operated a chiropractic clinic.

Judi Andersen Harrison (born Judi Andersen, October 11, 1958) is an American actress, model, and beauty pageant titleholder who was crowned Miss USA in 1978. Born in Honolulu, Hawaii, she attended Punahou School before moving to Millbrook, New York to study fashion design at Bennett College.

In 1982, Fred Rosen was appointed chief executive and relocated Ticketmaster’s headquarters to Los Angeles to align with the live entertainment industry, a move that facilitated contracts with major venues such as the Los Angeles Forum. Under Rosen, the company intensified its investments and led the transition to computerized ticketing, modernizing its sales processes. By 1985, Ticketmaster had extended its operations beyond the United States into Canada and Europe, signaling substantial international growth. During this period the firm also diversified into publishing and established a travel agency, expanding its business portfolio. In 1991, Ticketmaster acquired rival Ticketron, consolidating its position as the leading company in the market.

Hackers leaked customer information and event barcodes, with the leaked data covering more than 70,000 Ticketmaster events, including performances from Taylor Swift's Eras Tour and hundreds of other events.

The 1962 Roman Missal refers to the earlier edition of the Roman Rite used prior to the reforms of the Second Vatican Council. Priests may hold faculties to celebrate Mass according to this Missal. Nevertheless, a clergyman is not permitted to celebrate a 1962 Missal Mass and a post-Vatican II Mass on the same day.

Within the 1962 Roman Missal, the ancient discipline governing the reception of the Eucharist is presented as remaining in effect, rooted in the Didache’s guidance. Admission to Holy Communion is conditioned on three prerequisites: baptism, correct faith, and a life in accordance with Christ's commandments. These criteria were already described in the early second century by Saint Justin Martyr, who in his First Apology portrays the Eucharist as intended for those who accept the teachings, have been washed for the remission of sins and rebirth, and live according to Christ's injunctions. In this way, the Missal reflects a continuity of early patristic testimony within its liturgical practice.

In 1044, Emperor Renzong of the Song dynasty commissioned a new compilation of Tang history, driven by concerns that the earlier Old Book of Tang was insufficiently organized and unclear. The undertaking required seventeen years to complete and was finished in 1060.

The New Book of Tang illustrates a broader pattern in Chinese imperial historiography in which successive dynasties justify their rule by compiling histories of their immediate predecessor. In the period of the Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms, the Later Jin had already produced a formal history of the Tang dynasty, which is known as the Old Book of Tang. The existence of this prior work provides the historical backdrop for the New Book of Tang, a subsequent effort to recount the Tang era within the same dynastic historiographical tradition.

The Tibetan red deer is native to northern Bhutan and southern Tibet. Additional records have been reported from the Chumbi Valley near Sikkim and from Lake Manasarovar. The species was long regarded as extinct until a rediscovery in 1988, with confirmed populations in Bhutan and southeastern Tibet. The historical range is thought to have extended across numerous smaller valleys of the Brahmaputra River system north of the Himalaya, aligned with the Yarlung Tsangpo River in Tibet.

Washington Irving’s early output included Letters of Jonathan Oldstyle, Gent. (1802) and the short-lived periodical Salmagundi (1807–1808). He completed A History of New York in 1809, a project undertaken after the death of his seventeen-year-old fiancée, Matilda Hoffman. The work represented Irving’s first major book and presented a satire of local history and contemporary politics. In a notable bid to promote it, Irving staged a hoax involving missing-person notices about Diedrich Knickerbocker, a fictional Dutch historian said to be missing from his New York City hotel. As guerrilla marketing, a notice from the hotel proprietor warned that if Knickerbocker did not return to pay his bill, a manuscript he had left behind would be published.

A History of New York, published on December 6, 1809 by Washington Irving under the Knickerbocker pseudonym, quickly achieved both critical and popular success. The work’s framing tale about Knickerbocker and his manuscript drew broad readership, to the extent that New York City officials offered a reward for the missing historian. Irving later noted that the publication resonated with the public and elevated him to celebrity, a notable development for an American author at the time. The name Diedrich Knickerbocker subsequently became a byword for Manhattan residents, and the nickname was later adopted by the New York Knickerbockers basketball team.

The 2000 United States census counted the resident population of the United States, including those living in the 50 states and the District of Columbia, as well as residents of Puerto Rico, whose figures were collected by the Census Bureau. Puerto Rico recorded a population of 3,808,610, representing an increase of 8.1 percent from ten years earlier.

The 2000 United States census did not include questions on sexual orientation, leaving formal data on heterosexual and homosexual populations unavailable. However, two questions about the sex of household members and their relationship enabled the counting of same-sex partnerships, with census responses that used labels such as “husband/wife” or “unmarried partner” to tally same-sex couples. The Census Bureau reported more than 658,000 eligible households headed by same-sex couples, comprising 336,001 same-sex male couples and 329,522 same-sex female couples. While non-census surveys suggest that only about a quarter of gay men and 40 percent of lesbians were in shared-household partnerships at any given time, researchers have also noted that for every counted same-sex couple there could be three to six additional homosexual individuals who were un-partnered and not counted as gay. Extrapolation from available data yields a rough upper bound of as many as 4.3 million homosexual adults living in the United States in 2000. The exact number cannot be known because bisexual and transgender populations were not counted and there were no questions addressing these groups, and consequently the total of additional same-sex and heterosexual households remains unavailable. The absence of precise counts complicates policymaking on hate crimes and social services for gay families with children and reduces precision in fertility projections.

Xiled to Infinity and One presents tracks that are credited to Wade Black and Jack Frost as the primary writers. The Burning is a collaboration between Frost and Jon Oliva, while See You in Hell was written by Nick Bowcott and Steve Grimmett.

In 1989, the first Internet service providers were established in Australia and the United States to offer the public direct access to the Internet on a subscription basis. The World, based in Brookline, Massachusetts, became the United States’ first commercial ISP, with its inaugural customer served in November 1989. These early ISPs typically delivered connections via dial-up over the public switched telephone network, providing the last-mile link between households or businesses and the wider Internet. The relatively low barriers to entry for dial-up services encouraged the emergence of numerous providers, contributing to a rapid expansion of consumer Internet access in the nascent commercial era.

ISPs are organizations that provide direct Internet access to end users, including businesses and households. They rely on a variety of technologies to connect subscribers to their networks, reflecting the range of available infrastructures. These techniques encompass traditional dial-up connections using computer modems paired with acoustic couplers over telephone lines, as well as access delivered via cable television networks (CATV). In addition, wireless methods such as Wi‑Fi and optical fiber systems are used to supply connectivity, enabling different speeds and service models.

Jyutping originated as a phonetic transcription system designed to indicate Cantonese pronunciation. It has been adopted to render Cantonese in an alphabetic script, thereby treating the language as an alphabetic written form rather than solely a tool for pronunciation guidance. This shift elevates Jyutping from an auxiliary aid to a fully fledged written language.

The Jyutping input method enables the entry of Chinese characters through the Jyutping romanization. Users input the Jyutping corresponding to the desired character, with tone marks either included or omitted depending on the system. The method then presents a list of characters that share that pronunciation, allowing the user to select the appropriate character.

The Working Environment (Air Pollution, Noise and Vibration) Convention, 1977 concerns the conditions of the workplace as they relate to environmental factors, specifically atmospheric pollution, noise, and vibration. A decision was made to adopt certain proposals connected to improving the working environment under this convention. The instrument's scope encompasses issues of air pollution, noise exposure, and vibration within occupational settings.

Algerian Jewish Sign Language (AJSL), also known as Ghardaïa Sign Language, is a moribund village sign language that originated in Ghardaïa, Algeria. It is now used in Israel and possibly also in France.

Algerian Jewish Sign Language (AJSL) refers to the sign language historically used by Algerian Jewish communities, particularly those from Ghardaïa. Between 1943 and 1962, the Ghardaïa Jewish community emigrated to France and Israel. In the diaspora, deaf Algerian Jews tended to marry deaf Israelis from diverse backgrounds, and Israeli Sign Language (ISL) became their principal language of communication. As a result, AJSL has declined in intergenerational transmission and is now used primarily by older generations, with younger members typically utilizing ISL or other dominant sign varieties.

The Solar and Heliospheric Observatory (SOHO) carries the LASCO coronagraph, which suppresses the Sun's bright glare to reveal surrounding comets. Roughly half of all known comets have been detected by SOHO. Over about fifteen years, more than 70 individuals from 18 countries contributed to these discoveries, often by examining publicly accessible SOHO/LASCO imagery posted online. By April 2014, SOHO had identified over 2,700 comets, equating to an average discovery rate of roughly one new comet every 2.59 days.

Following the anomaly, the Recovery Team gradually supplied limited electrical power to the spacecraft to enable basic operations. Engineers subsequently determined that SOHO was in an unusual orientation relative to its intended solar configuration. On 12 August 1998, thermal control heaters initiated the thawing of the frozen hydrazine fuel tank. The thawing then extended to the associated pipes and thrusters, and by 16 September 1998 the spacecraft had been reoriented to face the Sun. After roughly a week devoted to restoring the spacecraft bus and performing an orbital correction maneuver, the bus returned to normal mode on 25 September 1998 at 19:52 UTC. Instrument recovery followed, beginning on 5 October 1998 with the SUMER instrument and concluding on 24 October 1998 with CELIAS.

Glomeromycota is a fungal division known for forming arbuscular mycorrhizal associations with plants. Phylogenetic analyses have shown that several species that bear glomoid spores are not part of the core Glomeromycota but belong to deeply divergent lineages, now placed in the orders Paraglomerales and Archaeosporales. This reclassification also encompasses the Geosiphonaceae family, which presently includes a single fungus, Geosiphon pyriformis. Geosiphon pyriformis engages in endosymbiosis with the cyanobacterium Nostoc punctiforme and, in addition to its symbiotic lifestyle, produces spores that are typical of Archaeosporales, aligning its spore morphology with that order.

Glomeromycota comprises obligate biotrophic fungi that form arbuscular mycorrhizae with plants, and their biochemical and genetic characterization was long impeded by their dependence on host tissues, which prevented routine laboratory culturing. Over time, root culture techniques allowed these organisms to be grown and studied more effectively. More recently, a culture-independent approach that sequences a single nucleus derived from fungal spores has been developed to circumvent the culturing barrier. In the early genetic work on mycorrhizal members of this group, the first gene to be sequenced was the small-subunit ribosomal RNA (SSU rRNA), a highly conserved marker that remains widely used in phylogenetic analyses of fungi. For this study, SSU rRNA was isolated from spores representing each taxonomic group before amplification by PCR.

In 1913, the Black Country experienced a major strike within its steel tube industry, as workers demanded a minimum weekly wage of 23 shillings for unskilled labor and parity with Birmingham. The action began on 9 May at the Old Patent Tube Works in Wednesbury, operated by John Russell & Co. Ltd., and rapidly drew in as many as around 40,000 workers across the region within weeks. Prominent supporters and organizers included Tom Mann, associated with syndicalist ideas, and Jack Beard and Julia Varley of the Workers' Union. The dispute confronted the Midlands Employers' Federation, an organization founded by Dudley Docker, highlighting industrial opposition to the movement. Nationally, the stoppage carried significance by threatening the Armaments Programme and the procurement of naval equipment and other industrial supplies during the Anglo-German naval arms race. The strike persisted for about two months, from 9 May to 11 July, and was resolved through arbitration by Board of Trade officials led by Sir George Askwith, 1st Baron Askwith, on 11 July. Its settlement contributed to the growth of organized labor in the Black Country, an area that had previously eschewed trade unionism.

The Express and Star is one of the two daily newspapers serving the Black Country region. Published from a Wolverhampton headquarters, it issues eleven local editions and maintains five district offices. The Dudley edition features content that differs markedly from the Wolverhampton and Stafford editions. It is the best-selling regional newspaper in the United Kingdom. Historically associated with the Black Country, the paper has extended its distribution to Birmingham city centre.

Function points are a size metric for software that aims to be independent of the implementation language. Despite this aim, lines-of-code (LOC) metrics are influenced by the level of the programming language, with lower-level languages typically requiring more source lines to achieve the same functionality as higher-level languages. This introduces a bias when comparing software size or development effort across languages using LOC. To address such biases, researchers have sought corrective methods, and C. Jones proposed a method to adjust for this language-level bias in LOC-based measurements.

Function points are a software size estimation method that measures the functionality delivered to an end user rather than the amount of code produced. In early project phases, LOC metrics prove ineffective because forecasting the eventual volume of delivered code is difficult, making function points a practical alternative that can be derived directly from requirements. Consequently, function points provide a useful estimation proxy for assessing project size, effort, and cost before detailed design or coding begins.

Daguannanlu Station (Chinese: 大观南路站, Pinyin: Dàguānnánlù zhàn) is a Guangzhou Metro station on Line 21. The station opened on 20 December 2019, coinciding with the launch of the western section of Line 21.

Daguannanlu station was initially planned in 2003 under the name Grand World Scenic Park Station (世界大观站), a designation intended to reflect its proximity to the nearby Grand World Scenic Park. The park closed in 2009, and regulatory restrictions that prohibit naming a station after a commercial entity led to a change in the proposed designation. Consequently, the station was renamed to reflect the adjacent thoroughfare, Daguannan Road.

With the advent of powerful personal computers, researchers have been able to pursue more extensive exploration of Post's inversion formula. The primary focus of current work involves developing approximations and conducting asymptotic analyses of the inverse Laplace transform that underpins the method. In parallel, derivatives required by the formulation are evaluated through the Grunwald–Letnikov differintegral, applying a fractional-calculus framework to enable numerical implementation and facilitate comparative assessments of the technique.

Post's inversion formula is a result in the theory of Laplace transforms named after Emil Post. Although the formula presents with an apparently simple structure, it is generally considered impractical for routine computations. Despite this limitation, it has been used to evaluate inverse Laplace transforms in certain contexts, contributing to the historical and theoretical understanding of inversion procedures within the Laplace transform framework.

Mersey Beat began life as a regional bi-weekly publication issued on 13 July 1961. By 1963 it had started assembling a Top 20 chart from around ten stores, evolving into a national newspaper. The charts and the newspaper then adopted a weekly schedule on 24 April 1964. In September 1964, Brian Epstein invested in the venture, enabling expansion of the chart and its sampling, with the first Top 100 published on 3 December 1964. On 6 March 1965 the title was rebranded as Music Echo & Mersey Beat, and later that year it became Music Echo. The chart ceased publication on 16 April 1966, and the following week it was incorporated into Disc, becoming Disc and Music Echo.

Wonderful Radio London, popularly known as Big L, was a pirate radio station that operated from the MV Galaxy off the coast of Essex. It was established and financially supported by American Don Pierson and played a pivotal role in introducing contemporary hit radio, a format widely used in the United States, to the United Kingdom. The station's weekly chart, the Fab 40, was broadcast every Sunday and was derived entirely from airplay. Big L ceased transmissions on 14 August 1967 following the enactment of the Marine Broadcasting Offences Act 1967. In the years that followed, rival chart compilations that challenged the official UK Singles Chart began to incorporate airplay data, reflecting the influence of pirate radio on chart practices.

The Südkreis-Liga represented a historical regional football competition in the Südkreis, a region regarded as one of the strongest in the sport during its era. During that period, clubs from the Südkreis frequently secured the majority of Southern German championships, underscoring the region’s dominance at the regional level. Moreover, teams from the Südkreis achieved notable success on the national stage, reflecting the high performance and competitive caliber of the region’s football.

The Südkreis-Liga's second season was contested by nine clubs, with Karlsruher FV emerging as champions of both the Southern German championship and the German national title in that year. In the 1909–10 season the league expanded to ten clubs, and Karlsruher FV again won the league title and the Southern German championship. In the national title round, Karlsruher FV were defeated in the semi-finals by VfB Leipzig.

Đặng Văn Quang served as commander of the 21st Division from 1 June 1964 until 20 January 1965. On 20 January 1965 he was promoted to the rank of Lieutenant General, a promotion that entailed the addition of two further stars to his insignia.

Lieutenant General Đặng Văn Quang (21 June 1929 – 15 July 2011), popularly known as Fat Quang, was an officer in the Army of the Republic of Vietnam (ARVN). He held a senior military position within the ARVN and later served as a special adviser to South Vietnam's President Nguyễn Văn Thiệu.

Garth Brooks is an American country singer-songwriter whose touring career began with his first concert series in 1991. He expanded his stagecraft by introducing high-energy performances and pyrotechnics, forging a hard rock–country crossover that broadened his appeal. From those early itineraries, his touring life has evolved into a current worldwide, record-breaking circuit. Brooks has appeared in a range of settings, including global tours, residencies, and benefit concerts, reflecting versatility in the venues and formats that have characterized his live performances.

Data as a service (DaaS) provides controlled access to data through dedicated data services, which improves data quality by enabling centralized governance and validation. The architecture establishes a single point of update via these services, streamlining change management and ensuring consistency across systems. Once the data services have been thoroughly tested, subsequent deployments require only regression testing if the services remain unchanged, as preserved interfaces and behavior reduce the need for extensive revalidation.

Data as a service (DaaS) is a data provisioning model in which data is delivered over a network, with cloud-based delivery being common. In this arrangement, organizations can acquire, monetize, or exchange digital data as a DaaS offering, enabling on-demand access to data assets through a managed service platform.

Lady Cynthia Mosley was a British political figure who joined the Labour Party in 1924 and was elected as the Labour Member of Parliament for Stoke-on-Trent in the 1929 general election. She subsequently aligned with Oswald Mosley by joining his New Party, and she was defeated when contesting Stoke in the 1931 election. Mosley died in London in 1933 at the age of 34, after undergoing an operation for peritonitis that followed an episode of acute appendicitis.

According to The Liberal Westminster Gazette, Oswald Mosley was described as one of the most polished literary speakers in the House of Commons. His speeches were characterized by graceful epigrams that delivered pointed criticisms of the government and the Conservatives. For many listeners, engaging with his oratory amounted to an education in the English language and in a repartee that was at once delicate and incisive. He was portrayed as possessing human sympathies, courage, and intellect.

Taxonomic revisions by the Angiosperm Phylogeny Group have substantially narrowed Verbenaceae, with a large number of its genera transferred to Lamiaceae, while Avicennia, previously placed in Verbenaceae, has been reassigned to Acanthaceae. Consequently, the name Verbenaceae pro parte can be interpreted as a synonym of Acanthaceae for the transferred portion and as a synonym of Lamiaceae for the portion retained within Verbenaceae. The use of the term pro parte is rare in taxonomy and is generally reserved for cases that divide a taxon in which the type genus lies in one part while other material lies in another.

Within taxonomy, the status of a synonym can be indicated by specific symbols in scholarly listings. In paleontological literature, Rudolf Richter proposed a formal system to illustrate these conventions. Under this notation, a 'v' placed before the year signals that the authors have inspected the original material, while a preceding dot denotes that the authors assume responsibility for the act of synonymizing the taxa.

British Vogue has recorded two notable milestones in its cover history: in June 2020, actress Judi Dench, then 85 years old, became the oldest person to appear on the magazine’s cover; and in 2022, Timothée Chalamet became the first solo male to headline a print cover in Vogue's history.

During the First World War, Condé Nast faced significant logistical obstacles, including restrictions on overseas shipments and shortages of American paper, which prevented the American edition of Vogue from being distributed in Britain. To ensure that British readers continued to receive Vogue content, a local British edition was launched to provide coverage across the British Isles.

Proton Drive is a cloud storage service that exited its beta phase, with the public web application becoming available on September 22, 2022. The service expanded to mobile platforms later that year, releasing iOS and Android clients on December 7, 2022.
Proton Drive entered a beta phase for paid subscribers on November 16, 2020, and was later opened to non-paying users in June 2021.

Jeirani, meaning gazelle, is a Georgian dance that narrates a hunt. The piece integrates movements derived from classical ballet within a Georgian choreographic framework and features a hunting scene as a central element. It was choreographed by Nino Ramishvili for the Georgian National Ballet.

Kintouri is a traditional Georgian dance that depicts the city life of old Tbilisi. The piece derives its name from the Kintos, small-time merchants who operated in the city. Dressed in black outfits with baggy trousers, Kintos carried their merchandise on their heads as they traversed the streets. When a customer selected goods, a kinto would remove a silk shawl from his silver belt to wrap fruits and vegetables in order to weigh them for sale. The Kintos were reputed for their cunning, swiftness, and informal demeanor, and the dance embodies these characteristics. Overall, the performance is characterized by a light, buoyant mood.

On graphs that display both positive and negative values, the four Cartesian quadrants are commonly identified with Roman numerals I through IV to prevent confusion with the Arabic numerals used to represent the data. Quadrant I corresponds to positive values on both axes (x > 0, y > 0), Quadrant II contains points with negative x and positive y (x < 0, y > 0), Quadrant III comprises negative values on both axes (x < 0, y < 0), and Quadrant IV encompasses positive x with negative y (x > 0, y < 0). This labeling convention provides a clear, language-neutral method for distinguishing the quadrants from the numerical data.

The ancient Romans employed a duodecimal system for fractions rather than the decimal basis later common in arithmetic, with the factorization 12 = 2^2 × 3 contributing to easier representation of certain fractions such as one-third and one-quarter compared with base-10. Surviving Roman monetary artifacts show fractions beyond one-half primarily as duodecimal subdivisions of the unit, and those below one-half were indicated by a system of dots: each uncia, or twelfth, was marked by a dot, yielding representations from one twelfth up to five twelfths. Six twelfths, equivalent to a half, were denoted by the symbol S standing for semis, while additional dots appended to S signified seven through eleven twelfths. This dot-tally convention paralleled the use of marks added to V to signify whole numbers from six to nine, although the exact arrangement of the dots varied and was not always linear. In some instances, five dots arranged in a quincunx pattern appear on the same coins as a visual cue connected to the Roman fractional system. The Latin terms sextans and quadrans also influenced the English vocabulary, giving rise to the words sextant and quadrant.

The Santa Clara River watershed is bounded on the west by the Ventura River–Matilija Creek watershed and on the northwest by the Santa Ynez River watershed. To the north, it adjoins the interior drainage basin of Tulare Lake in the Central Valley, while the Mojave River lies to the east and the Los Angeles River to the south. It ranks as the second largest river in Southern California, with the Santa Ana River being the larger.

The Santa Clara River in California was the focus of planning and environmental-review controversy surrounding the proposed Newhall Ranch development, which faced legal actions and concerns from Ventura County officials and residents over downstream impacts and other ecological effects. Proponents and opponents alike invoked the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) in challenges that argued the project could be redesigned to better protect essential habitat. In 2014, the California 2nd District Court of Appeal ruled that the environmental impact report adequately analyzed effects on endangered fauna and flora as well as Native American cultural artifacts, overturning a Los Angeles County Superior Court decision. The appellate decision also upheld the finding that storm-drain runoff from 2,587 acres into the Santa Clara River would not harm juvenile steelhead trout downstream in Ventura County. The California Supreme Court agreed to review a petition concerning whether the appellate ruling could extend to other protected species such as the California Condor, and directed lower courts to discard the EIRs for two phases of construction; after May 2016 changes were implemented to address concerns, the California Department of Fish and Wildlife certified the EIR in 2017. In July 2017, the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors certified a revised environmental analysis and re-approved land-use permits for Mission Village and Landmark Village, marking a continuation of the project’s regulatory trajectory along the river.
Reproductive toxicants are substances that cause adverse effects on sexual function and on fertility, with these effects potentially affecting either the parent or the offspring.

Skin toxicity is categorized by the dermal outcomes it produces, with distinct criteria for corrosion and irritation. Skin corrosion criteria require that the damage penetrates from the epidermis into the dermis within four hours of exposure and remains irreversible, not resolving within fourteen days. Skin irritation, which is considered less severe than corrosion, is defined by one or more of the following: damage appearing within seventy-two hours after application; damage that lasts for three consecutive days within a fourteen‑day observation period; or inflammation persisting for fourteen days in two test subjects. Mild skin irritation denotes even less severe effects, described as minor damage occurring within seventy-two hours of exposure or lasting for three consecutive days after exposure.

John T. Koch is a scholar whose central hypothesis has generated considerable controversy within the discipline. He co-edited three volumes that constitute part of the Celtic from the West series, edited by Koch in collaboration with Barry Cunliffe. The volumes were published between 2012 and 2016 as part of this series.

John T. Koch is a scholar who served as a co-editor of The Inscriptions of Early Medieval Brittany (Les inscriptions de la Bretagne du Haut Moyen Âge), a work published in 2000 by the University of Aberystwyth.
Engadget launched its inaugural mobile application for Apple's iPhone and iPod Touch on December 30, 2009. The app was subsequently relaunched in 2017, and it has since been discontinued.

Engadget was founded by Peter Rojas, who had previously served as an editor at Gizmodo and helped establish that publication. It became the leading blog within Weblogs, Inc., a network that contained more than 75 weblogs. Among the network's well-known titles were Autoblog and Joystiq, with Hackaday having been included previously. In 2005, Weblogs, Inc. was acquired by AOL.

During the Japanese occupation of Korea, the Samcheok Development Company was established in April 1936 alongside the Samcheok Railway Company, with infrastructure projects aimed at channeling Korean resources to Japan. The Samcheok Railway was built to transport coal, and Mukho Port was developed to ship resources from the railway to Japan. Development in Samcheok focused on anthracite coal fields and chemical industries that used local mineral resources, including Samcheok coal, as inputs, along with related enterprises along the railway line. The Samcheok coal was valued for improving Japan’s coal trade balance and for meeting domestic demand, while reducing reliance on coal from Manchuria, China, and former French territories, and supplying raw materials for industries in Japan and Korea. The majority of the coal moved to Japanese cities such as Osaka, Nagoya, and Niigata, with some shipments directed to northern Korea. All of these ventures were established with Japanese colonial capital.

During the occupation, Korea's public education system was implemented with Korean educators delivering the curriculum. The system represented a hybrid approach that fused efforts to assimilate Korea into the Japanese Empire with elements of Korean cultural education. It placed particular emphasis on the history of the Japanese Empire and sought to cultivate reverence for the Imperial House of Japan, including instruction in the Imperial Rescript on Education.

Air-displacement pipettes are widely used in biology and biochemistry to measure extremely small volumes of liquids. Calibrated measuring cups and spoons are suitable for cooking and daily life but do not provide the precision required in laboratory settings. In scientific work, volumes are measured with instruments such as graduated cylinders, pipettes, and volumetric flasks. Among the largest calibrated containers are petroleum storage tanks, some with capacities reaching about 1,000,000 barrels, equivalent to roughly 160 million liters. Even at such large scales, accurate volume determination depends on knowing the substance's density and its temperature, since these properties affect volume measurements.

During the Middle Ages there was a proliferation of volume measures, including sester, amber, coomb, and seam. English rulers moved toward standardization, culminating in Henry III’s 1258 Assize of Bread and Ale, which regularized practices and established a defined set of volume units alongside weight and length. The statute introduced terms such as peny, ounce, pound, gallon, and bushel, linking volume measurement with other standard measures. In 1618, the London Pharmacopoeia designated the Roman gallon, or congius, as the primary volume unit for medicines and supplied a conversion table to apothecaries’ weight units. From this period onward, volume measurements became more precise, with remaining uncertainty narrowed to roughly 1–5 milliliters (about 0.03–0.2 US fluid ounces or 0.04–0.2 imperial fluid ounces).

In the UEFA Euro 2020 semi-final at Wembley Stadium, England faced Denmark, with the Danish side taking the lead in the 30th minute when Mikkel Damsgaard struck from a free-kick; the effort was saved by Jordan Pickford but nevertheless crossed the line, giving Denmark the advantage. England drew level less than ten minutes later through an own goal credited to Simon Kjær. There were no further goals in regulation time, and in extra time England were awarded a penalty for a foul on Sterling; Harry Kane converted from the rebound after Kasper Schmeichel saved his initial attempt, his fourth goal of the tournament, shifting the score to 2–1. England subsequently defended the lead through the remainder of additional time to advance to the final. Shortly after the match, congratulatory messages were issued by Queen Elizabeth II, UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson, and FA president Prince William (Duke of Cambridge) wishing England luck in the final.

Following the UEFA Euro 2020 Final, the Football Association announced on 12 July 2021 that it would conduct a full review into how ticketless fans breached security and gained access to the stadium. Four days later, two men were arrested on suspicion of theft of items that aided ticketless supporters in storming the venue. In August 2021, Baroness Casey was appointed to oversee an independent review of the incident. The report, published in December 2021, concluded that there was a collective failure in the preparation for the match and identified seventeen mass-entry breaches at the stadium.

Brooks & Dunn recorded a cover of Husbands and Wives for their 1998 album If You See Her, with Ronnie Dunn on lead vocals. The track was released as the album’s third single and topped the country singles chart in December 1998. It also marked the duo’s first appearance on the Billboard Hot 100 Top 40, peaking at number 36.

Roger Miller recorded Husbands and Wives in 1966 for the album Words and Music, with the track issued as the album’s lead single. The song became a crossover hit, reaching the Top Five on both the country and the Adult Contemporary charts, and it also ascended into the Top 40 of the Billboard Hot 100. The single’s B-side, I’ve Been a Long Time Leavin' (But I’ll Be a Long Time Gone), peaked at number 13 on the country chart.

In March 2004, Space Delta 6 underwent a change in designation, resulting in its reformation as the 50th Network Operations Group. The unit subsequently assumed control of the 21st, 22nd, and 23rd Space Operations Squadrons, with the objective of centralizing command and control of the Air Force Satellite Control Network (AFSCN).

An expanded space communications mission at Schriever Air Force Base led to the activation of the unit then designated the 50th Communications Group, marking its place within Space Delta 6’s lineage. In 2002, the 50th Communications Group was inactivated and its components reassigned to the 50th Maintenance Group. However, the inactivation and transfer were reversed less than a year later.

Psychoneuroimmunology has become increasingly focused on the connections between social and relational stressors and immune system functioning. Notable examples studied include marital discord, loneliness, and the demands of caregiving for a family member with a chronic illness. Such interpersonal stressors are linked to dysregulation of immune function, illustrating how emotional and social factors can influence physiological health.

Psychoneuroimmunology examines the bidirectional interactions among the nervous, endocrine, and immune systems in health and disease. In many disease states, chronic activation of the stress axis leads to sustained release of glucocorticoids and catecholamines, which can interfere with brain neurotransmitter signaling—particularly serotonin, norepinephrine, and dopamine—contributing to neurohormonal dysregulation. Norepinephrine is released from sympathetic nerve terminals upon stimulation, and immune cells express adrenoreceptors that can respond to locally released norepinephrine or to circulating catecholamines such as epinephrine. Activation of these receptors influences lymphocyte trafficking, circulation, and proliferative capacity, thereby shaping immune cell distribution and activity. In turn, adrenergic signaling modulates cytokine production and the functional status of diverse lymphoid populations, reflecting a tightly integrated neuroimmune communication network.

Türkiye Basketbol Ligi (TBL) is the second-tier of Turkish men's professional basketball. In the 2023–24 season, eighteen clubs participate, and the regular season adopts a double round-robin format in which each team faces every other club twice. The team finishing first earns promotion to the Turkish Basketball Super League for the following season, while the clubs finishing from second through ninth place advance to the playoffs, with the playoff champion also securing promotion. The bottom two teams are relegated to the Turkish Basketball Second League, the third tier of Turkish basketball.

The Turkish Basketball First League (TBL) is the second-highest level of professional club basketball in Turkey. In Turkish, the competition is named Türkiye Basketbol Ligi, and it is abbreviated as TBL. It was previously referred to as the Turkish Basketball Second League (TB2L).

Ogham, an Early Medieval alphabet, was used to write the early Irish language. In traditional inscriptions it is dated to the 4th through the 6th centuries CE, with later use for Old Irish (scholastic ogham) extending from the 6th to the 9th centuries. Approximately 400 orthodox inscriptions survive on stone monuments across Ireland and western Britain. The majority of these inscriptions come from Munster in southern Ireland, particularly the counties of Cork and Kerry, which together contain about 60 percent of all Irish ogham stones. The largest concentration outside Ireland is found in Pembrokeshire, Wales. Ogham is also known as ogam and ogom.

Ogham is an early medieval alphabet used to write early Irish, with the earliest inscriptions generally dated to around the 4th century AD. Some scholars, including James Carney, have argued for an origin earlier than that, in the 1st century BC. The classical ogham stone inscriptions flourished in the 5th–6th centuries around the Irish Sea, yet phonological evidence indicates that the alphabet predates the 5th century, containing letters for archaic phonemes that were no longer spoken by that time and are not attested in inscriptions. This combination of data suggests an extended period of ogham writing on perishable materials such as wood before the preserved monumental inscriptions were produced. Among the archaic letters and their proposed values are úath, equated with H; straif, associated with Z in the manuscript tradition (likely F from the southwest); and gétal, linked with NG in the manuscript tradition (etymologically probably GW).

Buses reflect the quality of the local road network; in less developed countries, rugged, high-floor bus designs mounted on truck chassis are common to withstand harsh operating conditions. Population density significantly influences bus design, with configurations tailored to the level of urban concentration. Dense urbanisation, as seen in Japan and other parts of East Asia, drives the use of high-capacity, long, multi-axle buses, often in double-decker form. In South America and China, large-scale deployment of articulated buses supports bus rapid transit schemes and high-capacity services.

Buses are employed for a variety of transportation tasks, including scheduled public bus services, scheduled coach services, school transport, private hire or charter arrangements, and tourism. In addition to their typical roles, promotional buses may be used to support political campaigns. Many buses are privately operated, serving a wide range of purposes beyond standard passenger service, such as functioning as tour vehicles for rock and pop bands.

Byrhthelm was a medieval English churchman who, after the death of Archbishop Oda, was nominated in 959 by King Eadwig to succeed him as archbishop. This followed an earlier nomination of Ælfsige of Winchester, who died of cold in the Alps while en route to Rome for the pallium. When Edgar ascended the throne in October 959, he overturned Byrhthelm’s nomination, stating that Byrhthelm could not govern the Diocese of Wells properly, and he instead appointed Dunstan. Byrhthelm returned to Wells and served there as bishop until his death on 15 May 973.

Byrhthelm (died 973) was a medieval English churchman who served as the Bishop of Wells and, briefly, as Archbishop of Canterbury. A monk from Glastonbury Abbey, he became Bishop of Wells in 956 and, in 959, was translated to Canterbury. Later that same year he was translated back to Wells, continuing his episcopal service there until his death in 973.

Super Video CD (SVCD) emerged as a unified standard after the Chinese Ministry of Information and the Video CD Consortium agreed to consolidate competing formats by incorporating HQ-VCD features into a single SVCD specification. The SVCD specification was completed in July 1998. Prior to this, CVD had already been adopted by major manufacturers and had around 600,000 players installed. In order to preserve compatibility across the differing ecosystems, the government imposed a compromise between SVCD and CVD to ensure interoperability.

Super Video CD specifies a maximum combined bitrate of 2.7 megabits per second for the audio and video streams carried on the disc. This limit was selected to ensure compatibility with slower and less expensive 2×-speed CD drives, thereby promoting broader accessibility and adoption of the format.

Kos is the main town and port on the island of Kos. The island’s principal villages include Kardamena, Kefalos, Tingaki, Antimachia, Mastihari, Marmari, and Pyli. In addition, smaller settlements on the island comprise Zia, Zipari, Platani, Lagoudi, and Asfendiou.

Over the past decade, Kos has experienced a shift toward luxury accommodation, with increases in four- and five-star hotels while one- and two-star establishments declined. Between 2014 and 2023, the five-star segment nearly doubled in number, rising by 95.83%, and its total beds expanded by 103.32%. Four-star properties also grew, increasing by 34.15% in the count of hotels and by 8.5% in total beds over the same period.

The 2000 Missouri gubernatorial election was held on November 7, 2000. With incumbent Mel Carnahan unable to seek another term due to term limits, the race featured Democrat Bob Holden, a former state treasurer, challenging Republican Jim Talent, a U.S. Representative, along with several minor candidates. Holden won the contest by a narrow margin, narrowly defeating Talent and other contenders to become governor. Earlier that year Carnahan had died in a plane crash on October 16, 2000, near the end of his term, and Lieutenant Governor Roger B. Wilson had succeeded him as governor.

The 2000 Missouri gubernatorial election was a tightly contested race in which Democrat Bob Holden narrowly defeated Republican Jim Talent, making it one of the closest gubernatorial contests in Missouri history with a margin of less than one percent. Holden carried the state's urban strongholds of St. Louis and Kansas City, while Talent won most rural areas; Holden's weaker performance in the St. Louis suburbs was outweighed by his urban support. Because the margin was under 1 percent but not below 0.5 percent, Talent technically could have pursued a recount at his own expense, though such action would have been unlikely to alter the result, and he ultimately did not request one. Talent trailed by 21,445 votes and conceded defeat in the late evening of November 14. The outcome did not align with the concurrent presidential result, as George W. Bush won the presidency while Holden secured the governorship. In a later development, Talent would win the 2002 Missouri Senate special election, defeating Mel Carnahan’s widow Jean Carnahan to begin the remainder of Mel Carnahan’s unexpired term.

Lower Klamath National Wildlife Refuge is a United States National Wildlife Refuge located on the California–Oregon border. It is operated by the United States Fish and Wildlife Service. On October 16, 1965, it was designated a National Historic Landmark.

Lower Klamath National Wildlife Refuge supports a diverse avifauna, including prominent raptors such as the bald eagle, golden eagle, and peregrine falcon; a wide range of waterfowl, such as the American white pelican, snow geese, Ross's geese, greater white-fronted geese, Canada geese, northern pintails, mallards, gadwalls, and canvasbacks; and additional species like the white-faced ibis, western grebe, eared grebe, black tern, and tricolored blackbird.

Life Technologies Corporation, a biotechnology company formed in November 2008 through a US$6.7 billion merger of Invitrogen Corporation and Applied Biosystems Inc., brought together two leading life sciences businesses. In its early integration phase, the combined entity reported joint annual sales of approximately $3.5 billion and employed around 9,500 people. The company also maintained a substantial intellectual property portfolio, owning more than 3,600 licenses and patents.

Life Technologies Corporation originated in 2008 and operated as an independent multinational company headquartered in Carlsbad, California. It maintained its standalone status from 2008 until 2014, when it was acquired by Thermo Fisher Scientific, subsequently becoming part of the Thermo Fisher corporate group.

Rachel Agatha Keen (born 24 October 1997), known professionally as Raye and pronounced /reɪ/ (RAY), is a British singer-songwriter and record producer. She rose to prominence after signing with Polydor Records and releasing a series of dance-oriented singles and EPs. Her departure from Polydor subsequently attracted media attention, with allegations that the label refused to release her planned debut album.

Raye is an English singer and songwriter who emerged in the late 2010s through a combination of high-profile collaborations, live performances, and solo releases. In February 2017 she performed at XOYO in London to favorable notices, with The Line of Best Fit describing her as a rising pop force worth watching. That year she contributed to Charli XCX’s After the Afterparty project and appeared on the VIP remix featuring Rita Ora and Stefflon Don, and she also starred in Stormzy’s Big For Your Boots music video. Additionally, she was featured on Charli XCX’s Number 1 Angel track Dreamer and released the singles The Line and Decline, the latter featuring Mr Eazi. In June 2017 she performed at the Summertime Ball in London. The following year, 2018, saw the premiere of her third EP Side Tape, preceded by the single Cigarette, a collaboration with Mabel and Stefflon Don. Beyond her own releases, she has writing credits on songs by Little Mix and John Legend. Later in 2018 she issued a standalone single dedicated to her friends and supported Rita Ora and Halsey on their tours. By the end of 2018, Raye embarked on her first headlining tour.

The 2026 South Carolina gubernatorial election is scheduled for November 3, 2026, to determine the state's next chief executive. The current governor, Henry McMaster, is ineligible to seek another full term due to term-limit rules governing consecutive terms. McMaster took office on January 24, 2017, after Nikki Haley resigned to become the United States ambassador to the United Nations under the Trump administration, and he subsequently won full terms in 2018 and 2022.

In Egyptian iconography, the flail, a symbol of royal authority, would come to be closely associated with the heqa-scepter, forming the crook-and-flail emblem of kingship. In early royal representations, the ruler is shown bearing only the flail, without the accompanying crook. This progression is corroborated by material evidence such as a late pre-dynastic knife handle now in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, which depicts the king with solely the flail. Likewise, the Narmer Macehead presents the monarch with the flail as a central insignium of sovereignty.

Pharaoh is a title associated with the ancient Egyptian monarchs, first adopted in the Eighteenth Dynasty of the New Kingdom and subsequently retroactively applied to earlier rulers. Historically, the term referred more to the ruler’s administrative role than to the office itself. The earliest firmly attested contemporaneous use of the title for a king appears in a letter directed to Akhenaten (circa 1353–1336 BCE), though some inscriptions may preserve an earlier reference to Thutmose III (circa 1479–1425 BCE). Although the designation emerged during the Eighteenth Dynasty, scholars typically extend its application to rulers from the First Dynasty (approximately 3150 BCE) through to Egypt’s annexation by the Roman Republic in 30 BCE.

The symphonic Club Future Nostalgia remix of "Boys Will Be Boys" by Zach Witness blends club and Baltimore club influences with a Rio Carnival-inspired atmosphere. It rests on a Latin-inflected groove framed by frantic drums, whistles, horns, and cowbells, and features a distorted, chanted chorus. The original remix version did not include verses; on the album’s DJ Mix edition, Blessed Madonna contributed new verses to the vocal arrangement. A Lyn Collins sample from "Think (About It)" (1972) appears as a break in the DJ Mix edition. Rupert Christie is credited as a lead producer alongside Koz for the remix, and the track was mastered by Matt Colton at Metropolis Studios in London.

Boys Will Be Boys is a track by English singer Dua Lipa that presents its messages through direct, economical lyrics organized in rhyming couplets. The song foregrounds feminist and empowerment themes, lamenting how girls are forced to grow up faster than boys while celebrating the strength of women. It denounces gender inequality and sexist double standards, and it argues that the harms of patriarchy affect individuals and society alike. The lyrics address manifestations of male violence, misogyny, sexual harassment, and toxic masculinity, and it critiques persistent gender stereotypes and the tendency of men to avoid accountability. It also highlights male privilege and the unequal expectations placed on girls versus boys. Additionally, the song notes how women often brush off sexist remarks, underscoring the broader social dynamics the track seeks to challenge.

The lesser goldfinch exhibits sexually dimorphic coloration, with males displaying bright yellow underparts and conspicuous white patches on the tail and at the bases of the primary flight feathers. The dorsal plumage ranges from a dark back to a greenish tinge on the upper head and ear-coverts, with the back, crown, and ear regions showing relatively independent variation in darkness. The ear region is not typically darker than the rest of the head. There are two color morphs: a dark form known as psaltria (black-backed goldfinch) and a lighter form known as hesperophilus (green-backed goldfinch). Across the species’ range, psaltria is more widespread, while hesperophilus is most common in the far western United States and northwestern Mexico.

The lesser goldfinch is characterized by females and immatures having grayish olive-green upperparts and yellowish underparts, with immatures often exhibiting a buffier tone. Its wings show a narrow white wing stripe, and some forms display additional white markings. The tail contains little or no white. Among the genus, it is distinguished by its small size, the absence of white or yellow on the upperparts, and a dark gray bill. In plumage, it can be mistaken for a New World warbler if the typical finch bill is not clearly observed.

Billboard Radio China Top 10 Chart, also known as the Top 10 Hero Chart, was a music chart that tracked the airplay of Mandarin and Cantonese songs. The rankings were determined by a synthesis of mainstream radio airplay across Chinese-speaking regions and digital engagement, including online streaming and sales. The chart drew on data from major Chinese-language platforms, notably Taiwan's KKBox, mainland China's Kugou and QQ Music, Weibo's Asia New Songs Chart, and YinYueTai's V Chart.

On October 3, 2016, Billboard Radio China rebranded its weekly Top 10 Mandarin singles chart and Top 10 Cantonese singles chart into a single program known as the Top 10 Hero chart. The Top 10 Hero is delivered as a series of short video episodes. Each installment features a special guest who participates in the presentation.

Within the Duke University area, the 36th parallel north passes through the campus at several points. The Campus Drive, which links Duke's campuses, crosses the 36th parallel on multiple occasions. Duke Gardens maintains a group known as the 36th Parallel Club, and the gardens lie just north of the 36th parallel.

Historically, the boundary separating the Kansas and Nebraska territories was drawn along the 40th parallel north, as established by the Kansas–Nebraska Act of 1854. This line later continued to serve as the boundary between the contemporary states of Kansas and Nebraska, preserving the division between the two states into the present day.

Winter recreation in the Laramie region is supported by volunteers and federal management. Volunteers from the Medicine Bow Nordic Association, working with the U.S. Forest Service, maintain cross-country skiing trails in a portion of the Laramie Range about 10 miles east of Laramie (roughly 16 km). To the west, cross-country routes in the Snowy Range traverse the national forest west of Centennial. Additional trails on gentler terrain lie roughly 32 miles (51 km) southwest of Laramie near Woods Landing. The forested areas include extensive snowmobile networks, and many forest areas are open to snowshoe travel.

According to the 2000 census, the city of Laramie, Wyoming, had a population of 27,204, living in 11,336 households and comprising 5,611 families. The population density was 2,442.5 inhabitants per square mile (942.9/km2), and there were 11,994 housing units at a density of 1,076.9 per square mile (415.7/km2). The racial makeup was predominantly White at 90.81%, with African American 1.24%, Native American 0.89%, Asian 1.92%, Pacific Islander 0.06%, other races 2.89%, and those identifying with two or more races at 2.19%; Hispanic or Latino residents of any race accounted for 7.94% of the population.

Lensman is a tabletop game designed by Philip N. Pritchard. It debuted in 1969, with a second edition released later that year by Spartan International. A third edition followed in 2010, issued under the title Phil Pritchard's Lensman.

Lensman (game) was the first commercially available science fiction wargame, marking a milestone in the development of tabletop gaming within the genre. It is regarded as an important influence on subsequent science fiction wargames, shaping later titles through its design approaches and thematic emphasis.

Elfdalian, also known as the Älvdalen speech, is typically considered a Sveamål dialect within the North Germanic language group, and today it has an official orthography in use. Although it has traditionally been regarded as a Swedish dialect, it is not mutually intelligible with Swedish, a factor that has led many linguists to treat Elfdalian as a separate language. Some criteria place Elfdalian closer to West Scandinavian varieties, reflecting features that diverge from standard Swedish. Consequently, by the standard of mutual intelligibility, Elfdalian is commonly classified as a distinct language rather than merely a regional Swedish dialect.

Within the North Germanic language group, English loanwords have become increasingly influential. A 2005 survey found that English loanwords among speakers of Scandinavian languages had doubled over the previous thirty years. At that time, English-derived vocabulary was estimated to constitute about 1.2 percent of the lexicon. Icelandic has incorporated fewer English terms than the other North Germanic languages. Nevertheless, Iceland is the North Germanic country that uses English most, even though its rate of English lexical borrowing remains lower than that of the other languages in the group.

Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete began publication in 1932. The first issue, Knotentheorie by Kurt Reidemeister, was published as Band 1 (Volume 1) of the series, a designation echoed by an English note that also refers to it as volume 1. The series shows evidence of dual numbering in its volume sequence, indicating a double numeration within its publication scheme.

Ergebnisse der Mathematik und ihrer Grenzgebiete is a series of scholarly monographs in mathematics and related areas, published by Springer Science+Business Media. The title translates to "Results in mathematics and related areas." Most volumes are in German or English, with a number issued in French and Italian. Over its publication history, the series has appeared in several sequential runs, including the original series, the Neue Folge, and the 3. Folge.

The Castaic Lake State Recreation Area centers on Castaic Lake, a reservoir that marks the terminus of the West Branch of the California Aqueduct. It holds roughly 320,000 acre-feet of water and has a surface elevation near 1,500 feet above sea level. Part of the inflow originates from the 154-square-mile Castaic Creek watershed upstream of the dam. The lake is bisected by the Elderberry Forebay Dam, which creates the adjacent Elderberry Forebay. Aqueduct water reaching the lake is conveyed from Pyramid Lake through the Angeles Tunnel. The water drives the Castaic Power Plant, a pumped-storage hydroelectric facility at the northern end of the forebay, with most of the water’s energy used to power the turbines rather than to pump water back uphill.

Castaic Lake, known to the Chumash people as Kaštiq, is a reservoir formed by the construction of Castaic Dam on Castaic Creek. It is located in the Sierra Pelona Mountains in northwestern Los Angeles County, California, near the town of Castaic.

Bifora, in architectural usage, experienced renewed popularity in the nineteenth century as part of a broader revival of historic forms. This resurgence occurred within the framework of eclecticism and a broader rediscovery of earlier architectural styles. During this period, biforas became associated with the Gothic Revival and the Romanesque Revival movements, reflecting the era’s fascination with medieval design influences.

The bifora, a two-arched window opening divided by a central mullion, appears in Byzantine architecture with notable exemplars such as the Basilica of Sant'Apollinare Nuovo in Ravenna. It subsequently became a common ornamental motif in the Romanesque and Gothic periods, frequently employed for windows and for embellishing belfries. The Renaissance period also saw widespread use of the motif. In Baroque and Neoclassical architecture, its application declined, with many examples replaced by elements such as the three-light Venetian window. The bifora's influence extended to Moorish architecture in Spain, where it was adopted under the name ajimez, derived from the Arabic ash-shammīs.

Oman’s mid-20th century politics featured a contest between the ruling sultan Said bin Taimur and the Imamate, as the sultan sought to seize the Imamate after the death of Imam Alkhalili to capitalize on the instability anticipated during the Imamate elections. The British government, viewing a sultanate-led takeover as a possible route to access interior oil reserves, provided aid in 1946 in the form of arms, ammunition, auxiliary supplies, and officers to prepare the sultan to move against the interior. In May 1954, Imam Alkhalili died and Ghalib Alhinai was elected Imam, a development that coincided with increasing strain between Said bin Taimur and the new Imam over oil concessions, thereby underscoring the political and economic dimensions of Oman’s internal conflict.

Oman maintains a sizeable land force, with the Royal Army of Oman numbering about 25,000 active personnel in 2006, alongside a small contingent of Royal Household troops. Although the country allocates relatively substantial funds to defense, modernization has progressed slowly and the tank arm remains limited. The armoured fleet comprises six M60A1s, seventy-three M60A3s, thirty-eight Challenger 2 main battle tanks, and thirty-seven aging Scorpion light tanks.

The spice module serves as the reference implementation for the server component of the SPICE protocol. It is distributed as a dynamic library that can be linked into any application to expose a SPICE server. By 2013, QEMU used the module to provide a SPICE interface for virtual machines. The SPICE codebase is licensed under the GNU Lesser General Public License version 2 or later.

SPICE, the Simple Protocol for Independent Computing Environments, defines client connections that are composed of multiple data channels. Each channel operates over its own transport endpoint, selecting either a TCP socket or a UNIX domain socket. Data channels can be configured to carry data in unencrypted form or under Transport Layer Security, enabling administrators to adjust the balance between security and performance on a per-channel basis. When TLS is enabled, the entirety of the channel’s traffic is protected by strong encryption.

Broadcasting House in Cardiff, formerly the hub of BBC Wales, underwent a major relocation after the BBC announced in 2015 that Central Square would serve as its new headquarters. The transition began in 2019 with the gradual withdrawal of operations from the Llandaff studios, and on 25 September 2020 Wales Today completed the final move to Central Square. Later that same month, BBC Wales formally closed Broadcasting House, thereby finalising the move to the Central Square site.

Broadcasting House, Cardiff, is a broadcasting facility designed by Welsh architect Dale Owen (1924–1997). Construction work began in 1963, and the BBC moved its production and technical facilities there in 1966, establishing the building as the principal base for BBC Cymru Wales. It was officially inaugurated on St David's Day, 1 March 1967, by Princess Margaret.

Algebraic number theory is a branch of mathematics that studies the algebraic aspects of numbers and their generalizations, and it engages with a broad range of other mathematical fields. It employs techniques from homological algebra to develop and apply cohomological methods in number-theoretic problems. Additionally, it relies on ideas from algebraic geometry through the function field–number field analogy, which compares the arithmetic of number fields with the geometry of function fields of varieties. In this broader picture, arithmetic geometry concerns higher-dimensional schemes over the integers, offering a geometric lens for arithmetic phenomena. Among its applications is the investigation of arithmetic hyperbolic 3-manifolds.

Algebraic number theory studies the properties of algebraic numbers and their arithmetic, and its development was profoundly shaped by David Hilbert, who formulated a series of conjectures on class field theory. His ideas left a lasting impact on the subject and are commemorated in constructs such as the Hilbert class field and the Hilbert symbol of local class field theory. Building on Teiji Takagi’s foundational contributions, most of Hilbert’s conjectures were proved by about 1930, marking a decisive period in the maturation of the theory.

All the Queen's Men is a television series loosely adapted from Christian Keye's 2015 urban novel Ladies Night, reworking its characters and plot for television. The series centers on Marilyn "Madam" DeVille and her criminal enterprises, whereas the novel focuses on Amp Anthony and his crimes and romantic entanglements. In the adaptation, the book’s Mary Fox is renamed Marilyn DeVille, and she remains the owner of Club Eden. The show interlaces Amp Anthony with Madam by portraying him as her estranged nephew, creating familial ties that influence the narrative. A character analogous to DJ Dime is reimagined as Allison, who befriends Amp and enters a romantic relationship with him. The premise also emphasizes the lives of the exotic dancers at Club Eden, with Madam at the center as a figure who functions both as antagonist and as a salvific force within the series.

All the Queen's Men is an American television series set in Atlanta, centering on Marilyn "Madam" DeVille, portrayed by Eva Marcille. She is depicted as a formidable businesswoman who commands the male-oriented exotic nightclub industry and is supported by a trusted cadre of employees committed to the success of her empire. The series follows her efforts to expand her Queendom, with the accumulation of money and power bringing increasingly complex challenges and complications.

Dos de Mayo Uprising was a largely civilian insurrection in Madrid on 2–3 May 1808 against the occupation by French troops, with limited participation from junior officers. The rebellion was violently suppressed by French imperial forces, resulting in hundreds of public executions. The uprising galvanized broader Spanish resistance to the French occupation and is regarded as the opening phase of the Peninsular War, ultimately contributing to the breakdown of the Franco-Spanish alliance within the Napoleonic Wars.

Villa de Madrid was a screw-driven frigate of the Spanish Navy that remained in service from 1863 to 1884. The ship’s name, which literally translates to "City of Madrid," was chosen to honor the significant role played by the people of Madrid in the Dos de Mayo Uprising.

The Spain national American football team represents Spain in European competition and has appeared in the EFAF European Championship on four occasions. The squad currently competes in Group C, the third division of the continental championship. In the qualifying series for the 2018 edition staged in Germany, Spain was eliminated after a 28–20 defeat by Israel in the opening round, a game that also marked the team's first-ever international match.

Single Album received mixed-to-positive critical reception. Kerrang! reviewer David McLaughlin awarded four out of five stars and suggested that for listeners who have already formed an opinion about NOFX, the album is unlikely to change that stance, though it is seen as a significant work for the band’s troubled frontman. Wall of Sound critic Carys Hurcom gave it eight out of ten, noting that listeners who do not engage with NOFX beyond the late 1990s may be disappointed; the review highlights the album’s musical variety, adding that some fans may need time to adjust while others welcome the range on display.

Three music videos were released in conjunction with Single Album, each presenting a distinct concept. The video for “I Love You More Than I Hate Me” is set at a house party where four band members die by suicide in various ways, yet are ignored by the revelers as The Bombpops substitute for NOFX to perform the song. The “Doors and Fours” clip compiles archival footage from the early 1980s Los Angeles hardcore scene, the environment from which NOFX originally emerged. The “Linewleum” video offers a sardonic reinterpretation of “Linoleum” from Punk in Drublic, featuring Avenged Sevenfold performing the track alongside footage of numerous local bands covering “Linoleum.” A subsequent, separate video for “Linewleum” soon followed, consisting entirely of additional footage of more bands performing covers of the song.

CIND-FM is an FM radio station based in Toronto, Ontario, Canada. It broadcasts on 88.1 MHz and uses the branding Indie88. The station features an adult album alternative format. A soft launch occurred on July 31, 2013, ahead of its official launch on September 3, 2013.

CIND-FM operated a 24-hour online music stream from the date its license was issued until its formal launch. On July 25, 2013, the station announced that its official launch would take place on July 31 at noon. The online stream was subsequently replaced by the FM signal as test broadcasts began on 88.1 FM. As a promotional stunt, the station aired a looping segment of Rick Astley's “Never Gonna Give You Up” in reference to Rickrolling.

Billboard Global 200 operates on a Friday–Thursday tracking week and is compiled by MRC Data/Nielsen Music through the Music Connect analytics platform, a recently launched system for measuring and analyzing music data. The chart is published on Billboard.com every Tuesday.

BTS became the first act to reach the summit on Billboard's Global 200, the Global 200 Excl. US, and the Hot 100 concurrently, and they remain the only act to accomplish this across five songs. Ariana Grande subsequently became the first female artist to lead all three charts, while Justin Bieber, Daniel Caesar, and Giveon are the first male soloists to top all three. Sam Smith is the first non-binary artist to achieve top status on all three charts.

West Virginia participated in the 1868–69 United States House of Representatives elections, with contests scheduled on various dates ranging from June 1, 1868, to August 2, 1869, reflecting the fact that each state arranged its own election timing for the House and that these elections could occur before or after the first session of the 41st Congress, which convened on March 4, 1869. The elections occurred alongside the 1868 presidential contest, in which Ulysses S. Grant secured the presidency. Nationwide, all 243 House seats were contested across 37 states, and as part of the postwar realignment, all former Confederate states were represented in Congress for the first time since secession.

West Virginia’s 1868 United States House of Representatives elections were held to fill seats for the remainder of the 40th Congress and to initiate service in the 41st Congress. The two elections produced identical vote totals, and the United States House of Representatives accepted both results. The newly elected members were seated in 1870, completing the transition between the two Congresses.

Historians and contemporaries doubted the accuracy of early U.S. census counts, with prominent figures such as George Washington and Thomas Jefferson contending that the official tallies undercounted the population. They attributed potential undercount to multiple factors, including a reluctance among some individuals to participate, inadequate transportation networks and poor road infrastructure that complicated outreach to remote or dispersed communities, and the widely dispersed settlement pattern of the era. In addition, the limited capabilities of contemporary technology constrained the precision of enumeration, further challenging the reliability of census estimates.

During a period of reform in the U.S. Census, racial classifications were reorganized to replace the term mulatto and to introduce explicit guidelines for reporting individuals of mixed heritage. A one-drop rule was applied, whereby a person with white and black ancestry was recorded as Negro regardless of the relative proportion of white or black ancestry. For those with mixed black and American Indian lineage, the designation was Negro unless the individual was predominantly American Indian and widely accepted as such within their community. Similarly, individuals with white and American Indian ancestry were classified as American Indian unless Indigenous heritage was minor and they were accepted as white in their community. In cases where a person possessed white ancestry together with any other racial background, the census would assign the race corresponding to that non-white lineage. Additionally, individuals with minority interracial ancestry were recorded as the race of their father.

On March 27, 1997, Hearst Broadcasting announced a merger with Argyle Television Holdings II valued at $525 million. The agreement was completed in August 1997, resulting in the creation of Hearst-Argyle Television, which later underwent a branding change to Hearst Television in 2009.

Debi Chirichella was appointed president of Hearst Magazines in 2020, taking the helm of the magazine division within Hearst Communications. David Carey previously led Hearst Magazines as group head, and since 2019 he has served as senior vice president of public affairs and communications for Hearst, a corporate role overseeing external communications and public affairs.

Orta Osmanlı Türkçesi (Middle Ottoman Turkish; اورتا عثمانلي توركچه‌سي), also known as Klasik Osmanlıca (Classical Ottoman Turkish), denotes the form of Ottoman Turkish used in poetry and administration. This classical register prevailed from the sixteenth century until the Tanzimat reforms, serving as the language for literary production and bureaucratic discourse during that period.

In Ottoman Turkish, a final consonant may undergo softening when it is followed by a vowel sound, a process that occurs specifically if the next segment begins with a vowel; conversely, no softening takes place when the following sound is non-vowel. This rule applies across writing systems, appearing in both the traditional Ottoman orthography and the modern Latin-based orthography.

Sigma receptors are a family of protein receptors that bind a range of ligands, including 4-PPBP, SA-4503 (cutamesine), ditolylguanidine, dimethyltryptamine, and siramesine. They are divided into two principal subtypes, sigma-1 (σ1) and sigma-2 (σ2), distinguished by pharmacology yet not sharing a common evolutionary origin, which underpins their classification as sigma receptors. An early hypothesis proposed a third subtype, sometimes labeled sigma-3 on the basis of PAT ligands; however, subsequent evidence identified this entity as the histamine H1 receptor, and the designation sigma-3 is not part of current receptor nomenclature.

The concept of a sigma-3 receptor emerged in the early 1990s from studies using phenylaminotetralin (PAT) ligands and assays that linked PAT binding with stimulation of tyrosine hydroxylase and increased dopamine synthesis in the rodent brain. However, subsequent pharmacological and radioligand-binding investigations demonstrated that these so-called sigma-3 sites actually correspond to histamine H1 receptors rather than representing a distinct sigma receptor subtype. In contemporary classifications, only the sigma-1 and sigma-2 receptor subtypes are recognized.
Anci District is subdivided into eight towns: Laofa (落垡镇), Matou (码头镇), Geyucheng (葛渔城镇), Donggugang (东沽港镇), Diaohetou (调河头镇), Beishijiawu (北史家务镇), Yangshuiwu (杨税务镇), and Qiuzhuang (仇庄镇).

Anci District features the folk dance known as Geyucheng Zhonggehui (葛渔城重阁会). It is performed by a two-layer cast, with the lower tier composed of strong men who excel in dancing, while the upper tier consists of children, who perform the role of the “female horn.”

Tianpingjia station was first identified in the 1997 Guangzhou City Urban Expressway Traffic Network Planning Study (Final Report) as part of the alignment envisioned for the future Line 7. In the 2003 planning revision, the line initially designated as Line 7 was renamed Line 6, with Tianpingjia station retained at a location near where the current station would ultimately be situated. Construction on the station formally commenced in 2009.

Tianpingjia Station (天平架站; Pinyin: Tiānpíngjià Zhàn; Jyutping: tin1ping4gaa3 zaam6) is a Guangzhou Metro station on Line 6. It is located underground in the Tianhe District of Guangzhou, China, and began operations on 28 December 2013.

Jerry Voorhis was a United States politician who, during his career, advocated a range of controversial policy positions. He supported the internment of Japanese-Americans, proposing voluntary evacuations and a system in which officials would administer property to prevent forced sales at bargain prices. He called for more efficient taxation of higher incomes and wartime profits, and he proposed planning measures to address postwar unemployment as well as the nutritional needs of the American population.
