He also opposed the domination of big business in the war economy. Nevertheless, Congress largely ignored his pleas.

Jerry Voorhis had a writing career spanning about fifty years, during which he authored several books. Following his defeat by Nixon, he retired from politics. He then spent almost twenty years as an executive within the cooperative movement. Voorhis died in a California retirement home in 1984 at the age of 83.

Queen Charlotte Strait derives its name from a designation made by James Strange on August 5, 1786 during a fur-trading expedition that used two vessels, the Captain Cook under Captain Henry Lawrie and the Experiment under Captain John Guise. While surveying Goletas Channel on a boat excursion, Strange observed an opening ahead and named it Queen Charlotte Sound in honor of Queen Charlotte, consort of King George III. The water body initially labeled Queen Charlotte Sound is today known as Queen Charlotte Strait.

Queen Charlotte Strait is defined by a boundary established by BC Geographical Names, running from Cape Sutil at the north end of Vancouver Island to Cape Caution on the mainland. The southern end is described as comprising several narrow channels located to the north and east of Malcolm Island.

Bayer 04 Leverkusen established a reputation as a persistent near-miss in German football, finishing as runners-up four times between 1997 and 2002. The club came close to the Bundesliga title in both 2000 and 2002; in 2000 they only needed a draw with SpVgg Unterhaching to clinch the championship, but a decisive 2–0 defeat—assisted by an own goal from Michael Ballack—allowed Bayern Munich to claim the title with a 3–1 victory over Werder Bremen. In 2002, Leverkusen led the table by five points but deteriorated in the final fixtures as Borussia Dortmund won three consecutive matches to overtake them. That season earned the label “Treble Horror” in reference to losses in the DFB-Pokal final to Schalke 04 (4–2) and the Champions League final to Real Madrid (2–1). English-language media sometimes dubbed the team “Neverkusen” due to the series of near-misses. Leverkusen also became the first club to reach a Champions League final without ever winning a national championship. Additionally, five Bayer Leverkusen players were part of the Germany squad that finished as runners-up at the 2002 World Cup.

Bayer 04 Leverkusen announced on 26 May 2025 that Erik ten Hag would take over from Alonso as head coach, with the appointment to begin on 1 July 2025. Ten Hag, a former manager of Manchester United and Ajax, was brought in to lead the club ahead of the next season. On 1 September 2025 he was sacked after only two league matches. On 8 September 2025 Kasper Hjulmand was named as Ten Hag's replacement.

RPM magazine, a Canadian music publication, initially printed airplay rankings derived from major-market Top 40 stations rather than a national chart. A formal national RPM chart was introduced in the 22 June 1964 issue, establishing a single national standard for tracking a single’s popularity. The first national number-one single on RPM’s chart was Chapel of Love by the Dixie Cups. Before RPM’s national chart, the CHUM Chart from Toronto’s CHUM radio station was widely regarded as the de facto national chart for Canada. The last single to reach number one on RPM’s chart was Madonna’s Music.

The modern Juno Awards originated from RPM magazine's annual survey, a voting tradition established by the publication. Since its founding, RPM has conducted yearly surveys, inviting readers to submit ballots by mail to cast their votes. The ballots encompassed a range of categories recognizing both individuals and companies within the music industry.

The Oaxaca Valley was part of the Aztec tribute system, with Tenochtitlan as the capital, before Spanish settlement established towns to exploit the valley’s land and mineral resources. By 1521, Christian influence began to take root in the region, and the first recorded baptism occurred that year when the ruler of Teozapotlan was baptized as Don Juan Cortes. In 1557, Philip II of Spain issued an order allowing nobles who had converted to Christianity to retain their traditional rights. Spanish authorities continued missionary efforts throughout the eighteenth century, aiming to save the souls of their subjects.

Oaxaca encompasses a broad spectrum of wildlife across its terrestrial and marine environments. Its fauna includes diverse birds, small to medium mammals, deer, wildcats, reptiles, and amphibians, while the adjacent coastal waters host fish, shellfish, dolphins, and migratory whales. The state's reptile fauna is particularly rich, with 245 of Mexico's 808 registered species, making Oaxaca a center of reptile diversity that includes turtles, lizards, snakes, and crocodiles. It also records the highest amphibian diversity in the country, with 133 species, about one-third of all Mexican frogs and salamanders. The region supports 120 freshwater fish species and around 190 mammal species, as well as about 738 bird species, roughly 70 percent of Mexico's total avifauna. Insects of economic importance include grasshoppers, larvae, and cochineal, and among the notable large insects are the giant stick insect Bacteria horni, which can reach lengths of up to 22 cm. On the marine side, commercially important species include shrimp, tuna, bonito, huachinango, and mojara. Sea turtles were historically exploited for meat and eggs but were protected by federal action in the 1990s; the Oaxaca coast remains a critical breeding area for the endangered leatherback sea turtle (Dermochelys coriacea), with nesting sites and numbers declining despite conservation efforts dating back to the 1970s.

On May 6, 2011, Jumping the Broom was released by Our Stories Films in association with TriStar Pictures. The release drew mixed critical responses but achieved a notably strong opening weekend at the box office. Los Angeles Times critic Kevin Thomas offered a favorable assessment, describing the film as a lively comedy anchored by a talented ensemble cast. The movie was later released on home media, with DVD and Blu-ray editions arriving on August 9, 2011.

Our Stories Films is an American film studio established on July 13, 2006, by Robert L. Johnson. The company aims to produce comedic, family-oriented feature films intended for African American and urban audiences. It originated as a partnership between RLJ Companies and The Weinstein Company. The organization is based in Los Angeles, with offices in New York City. On August 31, 2006, Tracey Edmonds was appointed president and chief operating officer, making her the first African American to head a film studio.

During the 1970 Big Sur Folk Festival at the Monterey County Fairgrounds, the Beach Boys performed as part of the event's lineup. The appearance is seen as pivotal in broadening their image from a pop-oriented act to a bona fide rock and roll group and in reinforcing their reputation as a strong live act. Manager Jack Riley asserted that the Big Sur engagement led to an invitation to perform at Carnegie Hall in the near future. A recording of "Wouldn't It Be Nice" from the performance was included on the Live at Big Sur Folk Festival release, issued as both a single and an album.

During the Big Sur Folk Festival, Carlen invited notable figures from the folk scene to participate, including Malvina Reynolds, Mark Spoelstra, Roger Abraham, Janet Smith (a local artist), and the duo Richard and Mimi Fariña. Carlen also performed at the festival. He described the event as a festival for performers, conceived to provide artists with peace and solitude together after a lengthy summer on the festival circuit.

Within the history of logic, a consequence is defined as a hypothetical conditional proposition of the form “if … then.” A classic illustration is the conditional relation in which an action by a person is linked to the assertion of God’s existence. In his Summa Logicae, Book III, William of Ockham develops a comprehensive account of consequences. Ockham distinguishes between material consequences, corresponding to what is now called material implication, and formal consequences, corresponding to modern deductive (logical) implication. Similar accounts of consequence are found in the works of Jean Buridan and Albert of Saxony.

Supposition theory is a branch of historical logic that analyzes how predicates and terms extend over a domain of individuals. It examines questions such as in the proposition “every man is an animal” whether the term “man” supposes only present individuals or also those of the past and future, highlighting how reference and predication operate across time. The approach also raises the issue of whether a term can supposit for a non-existing or nonexistent individual, challenging straightforward notions of reference. In medieval scholarship, many thinkers regard this line of inquiry as a precursor to modern first-order logic, anticipating key concerns about quantification and interpretation. Within its broader framework, supposition, together with copulatio (the sign‑capacity of adjectival terms), ampliatio (the widening of the referential domain), and distributio (distribution of terms), is regarded as a major achievement of Western medieval logic, influencing subsequent developments in semantic theory and logical analysis.

Sky Show was an Italian television channel that principally aired comedy programming, including Shake It (a program produced by the channel) and Scherzi a parte, which originated on Happy Channel; the lineup also featured sitcoms and a range of international programs. The channel's slogan was "Si fa per ridere" (It makes for a laugh). It closed on 21 April 2009, following the relaunch of Sky Vivo as Sky Uno. On 1 August 2015, Sky Show was replaced by MTV.it, a relaunched version of MTV Italy.

The Eastern Time Zone is the most populous time zone in Canada, paralleling its status in the United States. In Canada, daylight saving time is observed by most regions in alignment with the United States, resulting in synchronized clock changes across the border. Nevertheless, there are notable exceptions to this alignment, including Saskatchewan, Yukon, and several localized areas that follow different practices. Southampton Island in Nunavut uses Eastern Standard Time year-round, remaining on standard time throughout the year.

Florida is predominantly located in the Eastern Time Zone, with the majority of the state observing Eastern Time. The western half of the Florida Panhandle does not observe Eastern Time, effectively placing it in the Central Time Zone, whereas the eastern half of the Panhandle adheres to Eastern Time. The Big Bend region, situated east of the Apalachicola River, also follows Eastern Time. In addition, portions of Gulf County south of the Intracoastal Waterway observe Eastern Time.

Kidandali is a Ugandan music genre that has been the subject of sustained discussion within the country’s contemporary music scene. In the years after the turn of the century, prominent figures such as Mesach Semakula, Geoffrey Lutaaya, Ronald Mayinja, and Haruna Mubiru helped shape its development, building on the legacy of the Afrigo Band. The Eagles Production label continued to cultivate talent, featuring female artists Cathy Kusasira, Irene Namatovu, and Stecia Mayanja. Around 2007, David Lutalo’s hit Kapapala broadened the genre’s reach by opening opportunities to solo artists beyond Eagles Production. Simultaneously, advances in digital audio production and workstation-based workflows diminished the reliance on traditional band configurations. Central to contemporary production were studios Kann, Dream Studios, Mozart, and Paddyman, which facilitated a growing roster of practitioners. As a result, many independent solo artists began to practice Kidandali, and figures such as Dr Tee, Martin Angume, and Chameleone achieved significant success within the genre. Today the genre is described as being at a peak of evolution, with newer artists like Papa Cidy and Chris Evans further strengthening its dominance in Ugandan music.

Kidandali is a Ugandan musical style that draws directly from Kadongo Kamu and Soukous (Lingala), and indirectly from the Dem Bow riddim through the early Ragga influence that shaped Ugandan pop. The Kadongo Kamu aspect furnishes a driving bass guitar that anchors the rhythm and tempo, along with parallel playing patterns, a vocal delivery reminiscent of Kadongo Kamu, and themes rooted in storytelling and admonition. Lingala’s imprint appears in lead and electric guitars played in Lingala-like textures, and in the use of trumpets deployed in a similar fashion. Taken together, these diverse influences combine to produce a notably organic form of Ugandan popular music.

Romani dance encompasses a range of styles shaped by communities across Europe, with the most prominent traditions rooted in the Balkans where Roma communities have long resided. The historic Sulukule district in Istanbul is renowned for its Romani dance and performance practices. In Western Europe, flamenco stands out as a prominent Romani-influenced dance, tracing its origins to Andalusia in southern Spain. In Wales, the Romani community is noted for a distinctive style of dance, particularly its version of clog dancing that has become characteristic of their practice.

Romani havasi is a variant of the traditional havasi and is widely performed as a Turkish folk dance in East Thrace. The form reflects the region’s cultural blend by incorporating the principal foundations and elements of Byzantine music into its melodic and rhythmic expression.

On 1 April 2016, Pop migrated to a nationwide Freeview multiplex, delivering coverage to more than 90% of the country. The capacity vacated on the local multiplex by Pop was subsequently allocated to carry the Kix channel from 7 April 2016. To facilitate this change while preserving a local service, Pop +1 was moved to logical channel number 128, freeing LCN 127 for Kix, and Pop continued broadcasting locally to Manchester until its eventual withdrawal from Freeview.

Sony Pictures Television announced on 13 April 2017 that it would launch an Italian version of Pop. The Italian Pop began broadcasting on 4 May 2017, taking the place of Neko TV in the wake of Sony's acquisition of the Television Broadcasting System. The move marked Sony's first free-to-air offering in Italy. The Italian incarnation was designed to deliver programming in line with Pop's UK counterpart, offering a similar slate of shows and formats.

In October 2023, OpenAI integrated its image-generation model DALL-E 3 into ChatGPT Plus and ChatGPT Enterprise, enabling the chat platform to generate visual content by crafting prompts for DALL-E. The process relies on ChatGPT to draft these prompts, with prompt creation guided by ongoing conversations with users that help refine preferences and specify requirements during the dialogue.

In April 2023, Brian Hood, the mayor of Hepburn Shire Council in Australia, announced plans to pursue defamation action against OpenAI's ChatGPT after the model asserted that Hood had been jailed for bribery during his tenure at a subsidiary of Australia’s national bank. In reality, Hood was a whistleblower and faced no criminal charges. Hood's legal team subsequently issued a concerns notice to OpenAI, representing the initial formal step in pursuing the defamation case.

During the 1588 campaign, the Spanish Armada included eight Bazán/Barros galleons, two Alonso-built galeoncetes, and four large Neapolitan galleasses from Naples. The Bazán/Barros vessels and the Alonso galleoncetes proved seaworthy and returned to Spain after the defeat, while the four Neapolitan galleasses proved ill-suited to Atlantic weather. Each Neapolitan galleass carried about 50 guns, some 300 soldiers or sailors, and roughly 300 rowers. They were frontline fighting ships, but their design proved too fragile and they were overcrewed. In the Channel actions, they operated as a small squad in calmer conditions to rescue stragglers or to cut off stray English vessels. Their commander was wrecked after the Battle of Gravelines, and only two of the four Neapolitan galleasses reached Spain safely.

By the 1580s, Atlantic galleasses were falling out of favor as naval design shifted toward ships that relied exclusively on sails, since galleasses—combining oars with sails—were powerful and adaptable but comparatively complex and costly to operate. In 1580, Álvaro de Bazán the Younger and Cristóbal de Barros agreed on a new galleon design that would come to predominate in the Spanish navy. A notable early embodiment of this evolution was the construction in Lisbon in 1584 of two galizabras by Alonso de Bazán, the Julia and the Augusta, each roughly two hundred tons in size. However, the rowers proved inadequate for vessels of that scale, and both ships were subsequently rebuilt as galeoncetes.

InterNorth acquired HNG, after which the two entities were operated under the combined designation HNG/InterNorth. This blended name was in use for about nine months, and in April 1986 the organization was renamed Enron Corp.

InterNorth's most valuable asset was Northern Natural Gas, which for a period was the largest natural gas distributor in North America. After Enron's bankruptcy, Northern Natural Gas briefly became part of Dynegy Corp. Dynegy's chairman, Daniel Dienstbier, had previously served as president of Northern before Ken Lay gained control of InterNorth. Dynegy subsequently sold Northern to Warren Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway, which moved Northern Natural Gas operations back to Omaha.

Chelsea Market is a multi-use complex located in the Chelsea neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City. It comprises a food hall, retail space, office facilities, and a television production facility, and it occupies an entire city block. The complex is connected by a bridge spanning 10th Avenue to the adjacent 85 Tenth Avenue building. The High Line runs along the complex’s 10th Avenue side, situating Chelsea Market near the elevated park.

Chelsea Market houses Morimoto, a restaurant at the complex owned by Iron Chef Masaharu Morimoto. The dining space was designed by Japanese architect Tadao Ando and opened in January 2006. It operated on the 10th Avenue side for 15 years, until 2020. The Food Network formerly filmed Iron Chef America and Emeril Live within the Chelsea Market complex.

The dagger, or obelus, is one of the earliest editorial signs used in ancient textual criticism to indicate words or passages in Homeric manuscripts that were considered questionable or corrupt. It originated with Zenodotus, a Homeric scholar, who devised the obelus as part of a broader system of textual-marking symbols. The framework was refined by Aristophanes of Byzantium, who introduced the asterisk and employed a symbol resembling a top (⊤) to signify the obelus, among other marks. Aristophanes’ student Aristarchus expanded the repertoire of these marginal signs, and the collection of symbols associated with him came to be known as the Aristarchian symbols.

Within the practice of textual criticism, the dagger (mark) forms part of a set of editorial signs used to annotate the text, with the asterisk, or asteriscus, signifying corrective additions. By contrast, the obelus signals corrective deletions of invalid reconstructions and is also employed when words are reconstructed to support an argument, implying that such non-attested terms may not have existed. Some scholars have placed the obelus alongside other critical symbols in the vicinity of a metobelos, which serves as an end marker for the annotated passage. The metobelos itself can be depicted in several ways—two vertically arranged dots, a gamma-like symbol, a mallet-like symbol, or a diagonal slash, with or without one or two dots—and it marks the termination of the marked passage.

The Gulf South Conference, originally known as the Mid-South Athletic Conference or Mid-South Conference, was formed by six universities in the summer of 1970. Founding members included Delta State, Florence State (now North Alabama), Jacksonville State, Livingston (now West Alabama), Tennessee–Martin, and Troy State (now Troy). Due to scheduling difficulties for the 1970–71 academic year, the conference operated exclusively as a football league that season, and Jacksonville State secured the football championship.

Jim McCullough, a former commissioner of the Gulf South Conference, relocated the conference office to Birmingham in 1979 upon taking the post. In May 2014, the Gulf South Conference appointed its seventh commissioner, Matt Wilson, who succeeded Nate Salant, who retired after a 22-year tenure.

Computer scientists typically receive formal training through degrees in computer science, with the majority holding PhDs, master's degrees, or bachelor's degrees in the field. Some practitioners hold degrees in related disciplines, such as Information and Computer Science (CIS). Others come from closely related areas, including mathematics or physics.

Computer science is concerned with developing and validating models, often mathematical in nature, that describe the behavior and properties of computational systems. These models cover a range of elements, including processors, software, human–computer interactions, and computer-to-computer communication, providing a framework for analyzing and predicting system performance. The overarching aim is to identify designs and methods that yield practical benefits, such as faster execution, smaller size, reduced cost, or greater precision.

Yangon University has long been a center of student political engagement in Burma, and it played a pivotal role in the nationwide protests of 1988 against General Ne Win's socialist government. Beginning with demonstrations in March 1988 that met with a harsh government crackdown, students persisted in their opposition. The momentum culminated on 8 August 1988, when protests spread across the country and included large contingents of Yangon University students; the events became known as the 8888 uprising, drawing hundreds of thousands into the streets in opposition to military rule. The movement was crushed when the army, led by General Saw Maung, seized power and established the State Law and Order Restoration Council (SLORC, also na wa ta). Estimates place the death toll at more than 300 students, and many more were imprisoned in the ensuing months and years. These events are remembered as the 8888 uprising, a defining moment in Burma's modern history.

Yangon University is a historic institution of higher education in Yangon, Myanmar, with a long-standing tradition of contributing to science and the region’s intellectual life. Within the broader Southeast Asian scientific landscape, Benjamin Peary Pal is cited as a notable figure, having served as the first Director of the Indian Council of Agricultural Research and being regarded as one of the foremost scientists in wheat genetics and breeding.

Lymphoid leukosis is a cancerous disease of chickens caused by a viral infection. It may form tumors in the bursa of Fabricius and can metastasize to other tissues within the bird. In affected birds, the abdomen may become enlarged and swollen.

Lymphoid leukosis is a disease of chickens marked by notable enlargement of the abdomen and the bursa of Fabricius, accompanied by weight loss, weakness and emaciation, and depression. The condition predominantly affects birds in the age range of about five to eight months. As it progresses, a green diarrhea may develop in the terminal stage of the illness.

Asian Hispanic and Latino Americans are Americans who carry both Asian and Latin American ancestry, forming a cross‑heritage subgroup within the broader Asian American and Latino American populations. They are also known as Asian Hispanics or Asian Latinos. The category includes individuals born in Latin America who have Spanish or Portuguese as their native language and later immigrated to the United States. It also encompasses Hispanic and Latino Americans who identify as Asian Americans or are officially classified as such by U.S. government agencies, including the Census Bureau and the Office of Management and Budget.

According to the 2000 Census, 119,829 Hispanic and Latino Americans identified as Asian race alone. By 2006, estimates from the American Community Survey placed the figure at 154,694, while the Census Bureau's official Population Estimates counted 277,704. The 2010 Census recorded 598,146 Asian Hispanic and Latino Americans, including individuals of multiracial origin.

On November 2, Johnson signed the Fish Protein Concentrate Act into law in the Ballroom of the Anchorage Westward Hotel. He stated that the act would enable translating laboratory research into the commercial-scale production of a wholesome, nutritious protein concentrate.

On January 13, Lyndon B. Johnson held his fifty-third news conference in the Fish Room during the afternoon, addressing a range of topics including the District of Columbia, Vietnam, the Department of Housing and Urban Development, the role of women in military service, and the continuation of American peace efforts.

Lahti railway station serves as a terminus for two Helsinki commuter rail lines, designated Z (to Helsinki) and G (to Riihimäki), and is also the terminus of an unnamed line to Kouvola, which at certain points merges with the Z line. On weekdays, two Kouvola–Helsinki trains pass through Lahti in the early morning, and a late-night Helsinki–Kouvola service operates via Lahti. On weekends, the Kouvola–Helsinki service via Lahti runs around midday. A subset of Lahti–Kouvola services extend to Kotka, and some trains either originate from Kotka or continue toward Kotka.

Lahti railway station, situated on the Helsinki–Saint Petersburg line, emerged in the context of a government-driven effort to begin construction of the route in the following year after the Finnish Diet approved the Senate’s proposal in 1867. The ambitious timetable sought to mitigate the economic consequences of the famine that afflicted 1866–1868, and the project drew a large workforce from across Finland, with some laborers choosing to settle in Lahti. The labor force faced poverty and malnutrition and was struck by a typhoid outbreak, and in 1868 about 1,010 people died in Hollola parish (then about seven thousand residents) with roughly six hundred additional deaths among workers from other areas. The scale of the fatalities overwhelmed the parish cemetery, prompting the creation of a dedicated burial ground for the builders in Järvenpää, which also housed a temporary hospital.

Thermal comfort research recognizes several modeling approaches, among which the Predicted Mean Vote (PMV) is one of the best-known models. PMV was developed from heat-balance principles and validated through controlled climate chamber experiments conducted under steady-state conditions. By contrast, adaptive models arise from hundreds of field studies and emphasize that occupants interact with their surroundings, adjusting both the environment and personal conditions. Occupants influence their thermal environment via clothing choices, operable windows, fans, personal heaters, and sun shades. The PMV framework is typically applied to air-conditioned buildings, whereas adaptive models are considered applicable only in buildings without mechanical conditioning. There is no consensus on which approach should be used for spaces that are only partially conditioned, either spatially or temporally, reflecting ongoing debate about suitable modeling under mixed conditions.

Thermal comfort encompasses the state in which an individual feels thermally neutral, with metabolic heat being dissipated sufficiently to preserve thermal equilibrium with the surrounding environment. Thermal neutrality is determined by several principal heat-transfer factors, including metabolic rate, the insulation of clothing, air temperature, mean radiant temperature of surrounding surfaces, air velocity, and relative humidity. In addition to these physical determinants, both psychological and physiological parameters influence the attainment and perception of thermal neutrality. The neutral temperature is the environmental temperature at which thermal neutrality is achieved, and it varies across individuals according to activity level, clothing, and humidity. Humans exhibit high sensitivity to small differences in ambient temperature; for instance, at a fixed air temperature of 24 °C, a difference as small as about 0.38 °C can be perceived between two rooms.

Studio A, a multi-purpose production studio in BBC South, encompasses 1,929.6 square feet (179.27 square metres). It is primarily used for South Today and is designed to accommodate an audience. The facility also features a separate, dedicated scene-dock to support production workflows.
In June 2020, a small BBC studio located at Gunwharf Quays in Portsmouth was closed, as part of a wider programme of cost reductions across BBC English Regions.

In On Liberty, John Stuart Mill argues that suppressing the opinion of a lone dissenter is unjust even when all but one share the prevailing view, asserting that the majority has no right to silence minority voices. He contends that if the dissenting individual possessed power, they would not be justified in silencing the majority, and the same standard applies to both sides. The argument thus functions as a defense of freedom of opinion and speech, opposing the suppression of dissent and underscoring the value of open discussion in the pursuit of truth.

Mill contends that government-run education would threaten the diversity of opinion by mandating a curriculum developed by a narrow group, thereby curtailing dissenting viewpoints. A less pernicious model, he argues, is one in which the state provides schooling that competes with privately run institutions, preserving pluralism rather than monopoly. He further maintains that governments ought to require and fund private education rather than control the content of schooling itself. Education, in his view, should be compulsory and enforceable by minor fines, accompanied by annual standardized testing that focuses on broadly agreed, uncontroversial facts. A crucial aim is to foster a diverse curriculum that exposes students to opposing perspectives, exemplified by thinkers such as Kant and Locke. Additionally, Mill suggests that states may legitimately regulate marriage, permitting prohibition unless couples can demonstrate the means to support a family through education and other basic necessities.

Chinese classifier systems are analyzed as comprising mass-classifiers and count-classifiers, with mass-classifiers appearing universally because many mass nouns resist straightforward division into discrete units; for example, while three splotches of mud is natural, three muds is ungrammatical, illustrating how mass nouns commonly require a suitable classifier to indicate quantity. Count-classifiers, by contrast, are not mandatory and are largely absent in most languages. They occur with relatively low frequency in everyday speech, and speakers frequently avoid selecting a specific classifier by using bare nouns or the general classifier gè. Some linguists and typologists, such as Joseph Greenberg, have argued that many specific count-classifiers are semantically redundant. Nevertheless, count-classifiers can be employed for stylistic effect or to clarify or constrain intended meaning when a noun is vague or ambiguous. An illustrative case is the noun kè, meaning “class,” which can denote courses offered in a semester or class periods in a day; disambiguation is frequently achieved through the classifier used, with mén indicating courses and jié indicating periods.

In traditional accounts, each classifier is viewed as encoding a category defined by a finite set of criteria. For instance, the classifier tiáo (条) is associated with objects that are elongated, slender, and one-dimensional, and nouns that bear this classifier are interpreted as conforming to all such criteria. Proponents of count-classifier theory contend that classifiers organize nouns into semantic classes according to characteristic properties, including shape, size, consistency, animacy, and function. The shape category covers forms that are elongated, flat, or round; the size category distinguishes between large and small items; the consistency category concerns softness or hardness; the animacy category separates humans, animals, and inanimate objects; and the function category groups items by typical use, such as tools, vehicles, or machines.

The precise location of Aztlán is difficult to determine with confidence. The ambiguity largely stems from conflicting accounts and narratives about the place, which produce a range of competing theories and retellings regarding its geographic setting.

Aztlán is a toponym whose precise meaning remains uncertain. Some interpretations, notably in the Crónica Mexicáyotl, render the name as a “place of herons” or “place of egrets.” Nevertheless, this reading is not straightforwardly compatible with Nahuatl morphology, since the translation for “place of egrets” would ordinarily yield Aztatlan rather than Aztlán. Additional suggested derivations include readings such as “place of whiteness” and “at the place near tools.” Across these proposals, the common āz- element is highlighted and linked to related Nahuatl terms, for instance teponāztli, the word for drum, which is connected to tepontli, meaning log.

Ari Hoenig has collaborated with bassist Johannes Weidenmueller on Intro to Polyrhythms Vol 1 and Metric Modulations, Expanding and Contracting Time within Form Vol 2 (Mel Bay, 2009, 2012). In 2011, Alfred Publishing released Systems Book 1, Drumming Technique and Melodic Jazz Independence, and the DVD Melodic Drumming. A Rhythm Training video issued in 2014 addresses time and rhythmic vocabulary. In 2017, Hoenig issued Mastering Odd Times and Drums: Jazz Coordination.

Ari Hoenig is a member of the faculty at both New York University and The New School in New York. In addition to his university teaching duties, he is recognized as an educator and has taught students across a range of educational contexts. He also conducts clinics and delivers lectures at music schools and universities around the world.

RANS Cilegon F.C. was founded in 2012 and was initially named Cilegon United. In its early years, the club achieved back-to-back league successes, securing the Second Division title followed by the First Division title within a two-year span. These victories stand as the most significant achievements in the club’s history.

RANS Nusantara, later known as RANS Cilegon F.C., competed in Liga 1 in their inaugural season, finishing 18th and bottom of the standings. Relegation was not enforced that season due to the Kanjuruhan Stadium disaster, which led to the suspension of relegation. In the 2023–24 Liga 1 campaign, the club began strongly and remained among the top four by mid-season. However, they ended the campaign 16th and were relegated to Liga 2, ending a two-year tenure in the top division.

MTV aired a documentary charting Sum 41's trip to the Democratic Republic of the Congo, with the program examining the conflict affecting the country. During the visit, the band was caught in an attack outside their hotel and was subsequently flown out of the country.

In October 2008, MTV launched MTV Music, later renamed MTV Hive, as a response to the Internet becoming the principal platform for viewing music videos. The service offered a large library of videos drawn from MTV's and VH1's catalogs, featuring thousands of titles. The collection dated back to 1981, encompassing some of the earliest videos in the archives.

Ontario's agricultural profile, according to the 2001 census, shows cattle farming, the production of small grains, and dairy farming as prevalent types of farming. The province's fruit and wine sectors are concentrated in the Niagara Peninsula, Prince Edward County, and along the northern shore of Lake Erie, with tobacco farming also present in that region. Market vegetables are grown in the Holland Marsh near Newmarket. The Windsor area is notably fertile, contributing to Ontario's agricultural capacity.

Ontario lies at the heart of Canada's inland water transportation system, with the Saint Lawrence Seaway crossing much of its southern region and connecting the Great Lakes–St. Lawrence system to the Atlantic Ocean. The Seaway serves as the province's main conduit for waterborne freight, particularly for iron ore and grain. Historically, the Great Lakes–St. Lawrence route was a major corridor for passenger travel, aided in the early 20th century by Canada Steamship Lines, though passenger volumes fell sharply during the 1930s. By 2022, cruise activity exists along portions of the system, yet cargo traffic remains dominant, with fewer than 20 percent of movements being non-cargo or passenger vessels. Ontario's three largest ports are the Port of Hamilton, the Port of Thunder Bay, and the Port of Nanticoke, while the province's sole saltwater port is Moosonee on James Bay.

Tractor trucks, also known as tractor units, are heavy-duty vehicles whose primary function is to provide the motive power for towing a separated trailer or semitrailer. They are described by a wide range of names, including truck unit, lorry unit, power unit, prime mover, semi-tractor, semi-truck, semi-lorry, big rig, and rig, among others. The largest examples approach locomotive scale and share a similar size and design philosophy. Commercial and military usage generally divides tractor units into two main categories: rear-wheel-drive semi-tractors designed for heavy- to medium-duty hauling of semi-trailers, and extremely heavy-duty, off-road-capable variants (often in 6×6 configurations) used in specialized roles, including ballast tractors for moving exceptionally heavy loads.

Tractor trucks are equipped with a range of multi-axle configurations to balance steering, traction, and load distribution. Vehicles with three or more axles may feature more than one steering axle, and in some cases the steering axles can also be driven to provide additional propulsion. In 6×2 layouts, the non-powered rear axle can be raised when lightly loaded or operated without a trailer, reducing tire wear, toll charges, and enhancing traction on the driven axle. The 6×6 arrangement comprises three axles with all of them capable of being driven. The 8×6 configuration presents four axles in which either the rear three are driven with the front undriven, or the front and the two rear-most axles are powered, using a liftable center axle to distribute the load when needed. An 8×8 setup has four driven axles. The 10×8 format consists of five axles, with the rear four typically driven and the front axle used for steering. In the 10×10 variant, five axles are all driven, with the front two commonly serving as steerable axles. Overall, axle configurations are typically determined by axle load legislation and maximum gross vehicle weight ratings (BDM).

The close front rounded vowel is characterized by a compressed degree of lip rounding, wherein the margins of the lips are held tense and drawn together. Consequently, the inner surfaces of the lips are not exposed, reflecting a compact, closed lip configuration during articulation.

The close front rounded vowel system in Greek is seen in both short /y/ and long /yː/ in pre-Modern Greek. In the Attic and Ionic varieties of Ancient Greek, the sounds /y/ and /yː/ arose through fronting of an originally back high vowel /u/ and its long counterpart /uː/ during the 6th–7th centuries BCE. Shortly afterward, the diphthong /yi/ (when not followed by another vowel) underwent monophthongization and merged with the long /yː/. In Koine Greek, the diphthong /oi/ shifted toward [yː], probably passing through intermediate stages such as [øi] and [øː]. Vowel shortening in Koine then caused the long /yː/ to merge with the short /y/. Subsequently, /y/ unrounded to [i], producing the modern Greek realization of the sound.

Within the United States, the ATSC A/53 specification defines the use of MPEG-2 video encoded in the Main Profile at High Level (MP@HL). The system sets a maximum bit rate of 19.39 Mbit/s for broadcast television and up to 38.8 Mbit/s for cable television. The video streams utilize 4:2:0 chroma subsampling, and the standard requires that colorimetry information be included as mandatory metadata.

MPEG-2 is a widely adopted video compression standard that underpinned earlier digital broadcasting, DVD, and many streaming applications. In the broader context of television transmission standards, ATSC A/72 stands as the most recent update to the ATSC suite governing digital television. This revision allows the use of the H.264/AVC video coding format and supports 1080p60 signals, underscoring the industry's shift toward more efficient codecs and higher-resolution delivery alongside MPEG-2–based systems.

Peter Paul Rubens underwent a period of service as a page to Marguerite de Ligne-Arenberg, the widow of Count Philippe de Lalaing, a position associated with a family whose father-in-law had served as governor general of the Spanish Netherlands, and she is believed to have resided in Oudenaarde. In his youth he copied a range of prints, including woodblock works after Hans Holbein the Younger and Tobias Stimmer, as well as Marcantonio Raimondi’s engravings after Raphael. Pursuing a career in art, he began an apprenticeship in 1592 with the landscape painter Tobias Verhaecht. Verhaecht was married to Suzanna van Mockenborch, who was a granddaughter of Rubens's stepfather Jan de Landmetere and a cousin of Rubens's mother, thereby linking the families. This familial connection potentially explains Rubens's decision to study under Verhaecht as his first master.

Within the chapel, a marble altar portico framed by two columns houses Rubens's altarpiece of the Virgin and Child with Saints. The work is understood to express Counter-Reformation tenets through its depiction of the Virgin surrounded by saints. An upper niche in the retable features a marble statue of the Virgin as Mater Dolorosa, the heart pierced by a sword, a sculpture likely executed by Lucas Faydherbe, Rubens's pupil. The chapel also serves as a family memorial, containing the remains of Rubens's second wife, Helena Fourment, and two of her children (one of whom was fathered by Rubens). Over the centuries, roughly eighty of Rubens's descendants have been interred in the chapel as well.

The single "Miranda," released in November 2021, was subsequently explained by Turner as drawing on his personal family history. The track tells the story of Turner's father, who transitioned and is living as a transgender woman named Miranda. Its lyrics portray Turner's previously fraught relationship with Miranda and chart their reconciliation following the transition. In a Guardian interview, Turner indicated that Miranda is a kind person, contrasting that with his father’s earlier demeanor.
FTHC, short for Frank Turner Hardcore, is the ninth studio album by English singer-songwriter Frank Turner, released on 11 February 2022.

Within ISO 2033, the JIS C 6527 font renders both the slash and the backslash with a doubled appearance. The character names used are Solidus and Reverse Solidus, aligning with the Unicode designations for the ASCII slash and backslash. The Unicode OCR block adds an additional code point, OCR Double Backslash (⑊), though there is no corresponding OCR code point for a double forward slash in that block. A double slash variant exists in a different context at U+2AFD, named DOUBLE SOLIDUS OPERATOR.

ISO 2033:1983 specifies character sets intended for use in optical character recognition (OCR) and magnetic ink character recognition (MICR) systems. A closely related Japanese standard, JIS X 9010:1984 (initially published as JIS C 6229-1984), shares a close relationship with ISO 2033.

Sixty-four clubs competed in the first round of the 2004–05 Danish Cup, with forty-eight teams drawn from the Denmark Series and its lower divisions and sixteen teams advancing from the 2003–04 Danish 2nd Division.

In the third round of the 2004–05 Danish Cup, the field comprised the 20 winners from the second round and was augmented by eight entrants from higher divisions: six clubs from the 2003–04 Danish 1st Division (finishing 3rd through 8th) and two clubs from the 2003–04 Danish Superliga (finishing 11th and 12th).

Uneapa exhibits a phonotactic system in which syllables may take one of four shapes: a sole vowel (V), a consonant plus a vowel (CV), a syllable consisting of two vowels (VV), or a consonant followed by two vowels (CVV). In terms of prosody, stress reliably falls on the penultimate syllable of a word. Additionally, vowels at the end of clitics may be optionally omitted; for instance, balitaza 'is not' can surface as baltaza.

Uneapa is a language that is also known by an exonym Bali, a designation used by foreigners. The name Bali is derived from the local term bali, which means “to be not.” This exonym is not etymologically related to the Indonesian island Bali. The Indonesian island Bali is home to a distantly related language called Balinese.

An integral lighthouse is a type of lighthouse in which the beacon’s tower and the keeper’s dwelling are housed within a single, unified building. This integrated arrangement contrasts with lighthouses in which the light tower stands apart from living quarters or other facilities. The term is generally not applied to caisson- or screw-pile-based lighthouses, which are typically not described by this designation.

The central part of the Maksimir district is predominantly residential, with a notable exception being the extensive campus of the University Hospital Centre Zagreb that forms a major institutional complex in the area.

Maksimir is a district of Zagreb, and its eastern portion encompasses Maksimir Park, one of the city’s largest green spaces. The park houses Zagreb Zoo, which is the second-largest zoological garden in Croatia. In addition, Maksimir Park contains five lakes that are collectively known as the Maksimir lakes.

In the 2020 Davis Cup World Group I, twenty-four national teams participated. The ties were conducted on a home-and-away basis, and seedings were determined according to the nations’ rankings as of 9 March.

The 2020 Davis Cup World Group I, despite its label, was staged in 2021 with ties held on 5–6 March and 17–19 September. The eight highest-ranked winners from the World Group I ties earned automatic advancement to the 2022 Davis Cup qualifying round. The four lowest-ranked winners then contested an additional knockout in November 2021, with the two victors securing berths in the 2022 qualifying round while the two losers moved to the 2022 World Group I play-offs. Meanwhile, the nations that lost in the World Group I ties were set to compete in the 2022 Davis Cup World Group I play-offs.

Starz TV is a British free-to-air television channel that has appeared on the Freesat platform in multiple periods. It was launched on 15 April 2014, replacing the music channel BuzMuzik, which had ceased broadcasting twelve days earlier. On 31 July 2018, Starz TV was removed from Freesat, along with Chart Show TV, Scuzz and Tiny Pop +1. The channel subsequently returned to Freesat on 21 October 2019, occupying the slot previously held by The Vault.

Starz TV is a television channel whose history around 2012 includes significant ownership changes. Mushroom TV went into liquidation on 22 June 2012, and an Ofcom television broadcast licensing update published in May 2012 records that Starz TV had been sold to Cloud Television One Limited, indicating a transfer of ownership during that period.

Long Endurance Multi-Intelligence Vehicle is a military platform designed to provide persistent communications relay capabilities, ensuring that personnel operating in mountainous terrain remain connected even without line-of-sight. It conducts semi-permanent overwatch of convoys, major road corridors, and other critical infrastructure, functioning as an escort and surveillance asset over extended deployments. The system also monitors urban areas of interest to inform operational planning and security measures. A stated emphasis of the platform is to address border chokepoints, with the aim of enhancing control and reducing vulnerabilities at strategic borders. By enabling the U.S. Department of Defense to deploy the most advanced payloads available in the near term as they become accessible, the vehicle supports the rapid integration of new capabilities as they mature.

As of January 2020, Hybrid Air Vehicles planned to manufacture a batch of certified production-standard Airlander 10 hybrid airships. Compared with the original prototype, the production version was expected to feature reduced aerodynamic drag, upgraded landing gear, and a larger payload cabin. The company estimated the Airlander 10’s CO2 footprint per passenger at around 9 grams per kilometer, or roughly 4.5 kilograms per passenger for typical journeys, in contrast to about 53 kilograms per passenger on a jet aircraft.

FanDuel Sports Network South traces its origins to Fox Sports South, which in October 2008 was divided into three localized feeds—Fox Sports Carolinas, Fox Sports Tennessee, and Fox Sports South—to provide more targeted regional coverage. Fox treated these feeds as separate networks, each maintaining its own sub-site within the Fox Sports Local website. On March 31, 2021, the three channels were consolidated under the Bally Sports South brand, adopting a common non-gametime schedule. Nevertheless, the three feeds persist as distinct channels within the Bally Sports South framework.

FanDuel Sports Network South is distributed on local cable systems throughout Alabama, Georgia, Kentucky, Mississippi, North Carolina, South Carolina, and Tennessee, and is available nationwide via DirecTV satellite service.

The episode concentrates on a single murder investigation, in which the body of a woman is discovered in a suitcase that has been burned in the Hampshire countryside. The early stage of the inquiry is hampered by ambiguities in forensic and DNA evidence. A number plate leads investigators to Ziaul Haque, who is employed at the same hotel as a Polish woman reported missing. Haque is questioned, and CCTV footage captures him moving a suitcase to his room and later pulling it back down. He is charged with murder, and subsequently dies by suicide in his cell.

The Force is a television documentary conceived by The Family, with no formal season and the concept expanding into a broader series examining social institutions. The planned programmes address the family, the police, the benefits system, and the NHS, and were due to air from last autumn through the end of the year. The Hospital episode portrays NHS workers' feelings about their jobs and how they carry out their duties. The Force is presented in a similar manner, with participants speaking directly to camera in a natural, on-camera style rather than adopting a procedural tone.

List of countries and dependencies by population is a compilation that ranks populations for sovereign states, inhabited dependent territories, and certain constituent countries of sovereign states. The selection of entries primarily follows the ISO 3166-1 standard, though the list also includes a few entities with limited recognition that are not part of ISO 3166-1. For example, the United Kingdom is treated as a single entity, whereas the constituent countries that form the Kingdom of the Netherlands appear as separate entries. Each entry notes its share of the world population, calculated with reference to the United Nations' estimate of global population, which was 8.232 billion in 2025.

Where up-to-date national population data are unavailable, the list relies on United Nations 2024 estimates or projections for those countries and dependencies. These figures are produced by the United Nations Population Division, a subdivision of the United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA).

Naval vessels, particularly large platforms such as aircraft carriers and amphibious assault ships, commonly host onboard medical facilities. These facilities account for only a limited portion of the ship’s overall capability. They are primarily intended to care for the ship’s crew and embarked amphibious forces, and may be used for humanitarian relief missions on occasion. A warship equipped with hospital facilities does not receive the protected status accorded to genuine hospital ships under international law.

Hospital ships derived from the Izumo-class helicopter destroyer are outfitted with a medical complex that includes two operating rooms, two beds in intensive care units, and 35 general hospital beds. In addition, there is one battle dressing station and several medical-imaging facilities, including X-ray, to support onboard diagnostic and treatment capabilities.

Breaking the fourth wall is a narrative device in which characters acknowledge the audience, thereby interrupting the fictional world. Oliver Hardy frequently engaged in such moments with Stan Laurel, directing his gaze toward the camera to elicit sympathy from viewers. Groucho Marx likewise addressed the audience directly in the Marx Brothers films Animal Crackers (1930) and Horse Feathers (1932); in Horse Feathers he even tells viewers to head to the lobby during Chico Marx's piano interlude. Later, comedy productions by Mel Brooks, Monty Python, and Zucker, Abrahams and Zucker made frequent use of this technique, with The A.V. Club noting that the fourth wall is so fragile and so often breached that it can seem almost non-existent.

Fourth-wall breaking is a narrative device in which characters address the audience or acknowledge the fictional nature of the work. In American television, the practice has been used to varying degrees. Saved by the Bell frequently employs it, beginning with Zack Morris directly addressing viewers in the opening sequence and featuring additional interruptions throughout many episodes. Other series that incorporate the device to shape narrative setup or to offer self-referential commentary include The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air, Clarissa Explains It All, and Malcolm in the Middle. Shameless employs a more explicit variant, with a principal character breaking the fourth wall at the start of each episode to critique and threaten the audience, emphasizing morally questionable plots and characters and with the aim of dissuading naive viewers while potentially increasing the show's popularity.

In Kazakhstan, the development of specific mechanisms for solid waste management has introduced a targeted set of regulatory, financial, and organizational tools aimed at improving the collection, treatment, and disposal of municipal and industrial waste. This advancement has also created additional investment opportunities for investors, expanding private sector involvement and financing prospects in the waste-management sector.

A new waste management facility is planned for Karaganda, Kazakhstan, as part of efforts to improve regional waste processing capacity. The Taza Dala company has been established to oversee the project. The construction sites and the defined project polygon have been selected, delineating the geographical scope of development. Negotiations are ongoing with several banking institutions to participate in financing the project.

Potassium iodide is a chemical compound that functions as both a medication and a dietary supplement. In medical use, it treats hyperthyroidism, and it also plays a role in radiation emergencies by protecting the thyroid gland when certain radiopharmaceuticals are used. In addition, it is employed to treat skin infections such as sporotrichosis and phycomycosis. As a supplement, it helps individuals with low dietary iodine intake. It is administered orally.

Potassium iodide is used as a nutritional supplement in both animal feeds and the human diet. In human nutrition, it is the most common additive employed to iodize table salt in order to prevent iodine deficiency in populations with limited seafood consumption. However, iodide incorporated into salt is prone to oxidation when exposed to excess air, resulting in a gradual loss of iodine content. Over time and with continued exposure to oxygen and carbon dioxide, alkali metal iodides can oxidize to metal carbonate and elemental iodine, the latter of which tends to volatilize. To counteract this loss, some salts are iodized with potassium iodate (KIO3), which is less susceptible to oxidation. Additionally, stabilizers such as dextrose or sodium thiosulfate are often added to iodized table salt to stabilize potassium iodide and reduce the loss of iodine.

Serverless computing describes a cloud execution model in which applications rely on managed services, blurring the line between infrastructure management and the execution of business logic. Applications are typically distributed across multiple services rather than confined to a single deployment unit. This distributed nature elevates the importance of integration testing to maximize test effectiveness across service boundaries. Within a bounded context, orchestration coordinates internal workflows, while between bounded contexts, choreography governs interactions to aid debugging and implementation. The approach supports scalable resource usage and reduces operational overhead, though it can complicate observability and tracing across multiple services.

Serverless computing, which offers on-demand execution without requiring users to manage servers, presents a mixed outlook for high-performance computing (HPC) workloads. A primary limitation arises from provider-imposed caps on memory, CPU, and maximum runtime, which can hinder long-running or resource-intensive HPC tasks. For workloads with sustained or predictable resource usage, bulk-provisioned servers or clusters can often be more cost-effective than pay-per-use serverless execution due to greater efficiency and predictable performance. Nevertheless, advances in cloud technologies have progressively expanded the range of HPC tasks that can be supported by serverless approaches, particularly those that are highly parallelizable or event-driven, where elasticity and scalable provisioning can be advantageous. The overall suitability of serverless for HPC continues to evolve as cloud platforms improve resource controls, performance, and orchestration capabilities.

Architectural acoustics is the scientific and engineering discipline devoted to creating favorable sound conditions inside enclosed spaces. In the field of audio engineering, this involves tasks such as ensuring clear speech intelligibility in large venues like stadiums and enhancing the quality of music in theatres. The design of an environment’s acoustic properties is typically carried out by acoustic consultants who specialize in shaping how sound behaves within these spaces.

Audio engineering has been advanced in part through organizations such as Women's Audio Mission (WAM), founded in 2003 to address the underrepresentation of women in professional audio. Since its inception, WAM has trained more than 6,000 women and girls in the recording arts and operates the only professional recording studio built and run by women. The organization has been involved in a range of notable projects, including collaborations with the Kronos Quartet, a Grammy Award–winning ensemble, and with Angelique Kidjo, a 2014 Grammy winner; it has also engaged with author Salman Rushdie. WAM contributed to the Academy Award–nominated soundtrack for the documentary Dirty Wars, and its projects have featured artists such as Van-Ahn Vo, whose work was recognized by NPR as among the Top 50 Albums of 2013, as well as the St. Lawrence Quartet, Grammy-nominated, and world music performers Tanya Tagaq and Wu Man.

Dubuque, Iowa is a regional tourist destination notable for its distinctive architecture, casinos, and riverside location. The city is home to five institutions of higher education. Historically, Dubuque served as a center of manufacturing, and the contemporary economy includes health care, publishing, and financial services sectors.

Dubuque, Iowa, ranked among the 100 largest urban areas in the United States between 1860 and 1880, illustrating its prominence in the mid-19th century. In the broader Iowa Territory, organized religious life took shape with Methodists building Iowa's first church in 1833, a milestone that underscored early community development in the region that would foster Dubuque's later growth.

Kathleen Hogan worked for Oracle Corporation following her time at university, first as a software developer and subsequently as a software development manager, with her tenure at the company lasting until 1992.

Kathleen Hogan is a corporate executive who has held several senior leadership roles at Microsoft. She began her career at McKinsey & Company, where Microsoft was among her clients, and joined Microsoft in 2003 after being recruited by Kevin Johnson. In 2005 she was promoted to Corporate Vice President of Customer Service and Support. In 2009, she advanced to Corporate Vice President of Microsoft Worldwide Services, a division that encompasses customer service, enterprise support, and consulting, overseeing more than 20,000 employees. That same year she was recognized by Profiles in Diversity Journal as part of its Women Worth Watching list.

According to a 2009 report by The Washington Post, the North Korean government was implicated in a global insurance fraud scheme. The state-owned Korea National Insurance Corp (KNIC) pursued reinsurance contracts with international reinsurers and subsequently filed fraudulent claims under those agreements. The contracts were governed by North Korean law, which hampered efforts to pursue legal redress, and reports also described instances of document forgery associated with the scheme.

Room 39, also referred to as Office No. 39, is described by North Korean defector Kim Kwang-jin as a central party department established in 1972 by Kim Jong Il. According to Kwang-jin, the designation arose from the arbitrary office number where the unit began its operations. In its early configuration, Office No. 39 operated under the Finance and Accounting Department of the Central Committee of the Workers' Party of Korea.

Enacted in 1850, the Oregon Donation Land Claim Act allowed white settlers in the Oregon Territory—comprising present-day Washington, Oregon, Idaho, and portions of Wyoming—to claim land, with individuals eligible for 320 acres and married couples for 640 acres. Claims remained valid from 1850 until the act was repealed in 1855, and land could be purchased for $1.25 per acre prior to repeal. Following the creation of the Oregon Territory in 1848, the United States government pursued what was described at the time as the most generous land distribution bill in the nation’s history. The Homestead Act of 1862 continued this approach by broadening land settlement opportunities on a national scale.

Implemented in 1862, the act established acreage limits that were, at the time, regarded as reasonable within the framework of federal settlement policy. Some scholars argue that many prospective settlers did not fully understand the demanding physical conditions of the plains. Over a span of several generations, a single family could accumulate a sizable landholding through continued occupancy and improvement.

Between 1876 and 1877, Edvard Grieg prepared a two-piano arrangement of Mozart's Piano Sonata No. 16. In this version, additional accompaniment was added on the second piano while the first piano retains Mozart's original material. Grieg described the aim as imparting a tonal quality to several of Mozart's sonatas that would appeal to contemporary listeners.

Piano Sonata No. 16 in C major, K. 545, is a piano sonata by Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart. In his thematic catalogue, Mozart describes the work as suitable for beginners. It is commonly known by the nicknames Sonata facile and Sonata semplice.

At the 1981 Wimbledon Championships, Chris Evert Lloyd defeated Hana Mandlíková in the final, 6–2, 6–2, to claim the ladies' singles title. It was Evert's third Wimbledon singles title and her twelfth major singles title overall, surpassing Margaret Court's Open Era record for the most major singles titles. Notably, Evert did not lose a set throughout the tournament.

At the 1981 Wimbledon Championships – Women's singles, Hana Mandlíková was seeded second despite her world ranking being fifth, a elevation attributed to her French Open title as the most recent Grand Slam winner before Wimbledon. The All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club retains the authority to determine seedings independently of the rankings. The Women's Tennis Association filed a petition with the club, objecting to the seeding arrangement.

By 1991 the Communist Party of the Philippines recognized the need for a broad rectification movement to address past errors and realign its political line. In 1992 it held a plenum to discuss two documents: Stand for Socialism Against Modern Revisionism and Reaffirm Our Basic Principles and Rectify Errors. The documents repudiated a range of strategic and tactical mistakes from the preceding decade and reaffirmed adherence to the protracted people’s war as the central path. The reaffirmation triggered an internal split within the CPP, reducing overall strength while streamlining the organization by limiting regional committees’ autonomy and ensuring tighter ideological coherence. Those who rejected the reaffirmation, known as rejectionists, departed from the movement, though the opposition was not entirely cohesive.

On August 25, 2023, a fire occurred at Marathon Petroleum's Garyville refinery located in Garyville, Louisiana, beginning at approximately 8:04 a.m. local time. As a precaution against deteriorating air quality, nearby residents and several local schools were evacuated. Reports described the response to the incident as not immediate.
Marathon Petroleum completed a $3.9 billion expansion of its Garyville, Louisiana, refinery in 2009, significantly enlarging its capacity by 180,000 barrels per day.

Gina G, a British singer, was involved in a 1998 lawsuit alongside songwriter Simon Tauber against FX Music and its owner Steve Rodway, seeking £136,000 plus additional claims. In February 1999, the High Court voided her recording contract after determining that she had received less than £30,000 in royalties from the song. A ten-year legal battle with her former manager continued in the courts, preventing her from issuing another album during that period.

By 2000, Gina G had worked with the Swedish production team Lagoona, recording several songs with them. The recordings included a reworked version of her debut hit “Ooh Aah... Just a Little Bit” and a cover of Nancy Sinatra’s “These Boots Are Made for Walkin’.”

UBM plc, rooted in United News & Media, pursued a merger with Carlton Communications in 1999 that ultimately collapsed because Meridian would have to be sold as a condition of the deal. As a result, UNM's television assets were sold to Granada. Regulatory constraints prevented the group from maintaining control of a large audience share, leading to the sale of HTV's broadcasting arm to Carlton. The HTV sale was linked to Central Independent Television acquiring a 20% stake in Meridian.

United News and Media (UNM) reached an agreement to acquire Scottish Television's remaining 20 percent stake in HTV. On 28 June 1997, UNM completed the takeover, obtaining full ownership of HTV. The transaction was valued at £370 million.

By the close of the nineteenth century, the British Museum's collections had outgrown the capacity of its building. In 1895, the trustees purchased 69 surrounding houses with the aim of demolishing them and redeveloping the site. The expansion plan envisaged surrounding the museum on the western, northern, and eastern fronts. The initial phase of the project involved adding a northern wing, with construction commencing in 1906.

The Montagu House acquisition enabled the first exhibition galleries and a scholars' reading room, which opened on 15 January 1759. The core of the initial collection consisted chiefly of a library on the ground floor and a substantial wing housing natural history specimens on the first floor. In the years after its foundation, the museum received notable gifts, including the Thomason Collection of Civil War Tracts and David Garrick's library of about 1,000 printed plays. In 1763, guided by Peter Collinson and William Watson, Daniel Solander reorganized the natural history collection according to the Linnaean system, transforming the institution into a public centre of learning for European natural historians. In 1772 the museum acquired its first major antiquities, Sir William Hamilton's collection of Greek vases, for £8,410, a purchase that shifted emphasis away from natural history, books, and manuscripts toward antiquities. In 1823, George IV donated the King's Library assembled by George III, and Parliament granted the right to a copy of every book published in the country, thus ensuring ongoing expansion of the library.

A hole punch, also known as a hole puncher or paper puncher, is an office tool designed to punch holes in sheets of paper. By creating holes, it facilitates filing the sheets in a binder or folder, yielding a collection commonly referred to as loose-leaf paper. The designation can also extend to equivalent tools employed on other materials, including leather, cloth, plastic, or metal sheets.

The ring-binder system was originally patented in the 1970s under the name Multo. In Dutch usage, Multomap is commonly used to refer to this binding system, regardless of brand, with the term itself derived from Multo and signifying a binder. The same term is occasionally extended to denote any ring binder in general. Multomap is included in the official Dutch spelling list, reflecting its established status in the language, and the Van Dale Dutch–English dictionary renders the term as "ring binder."

EE Times is a trade publication serving the electronics industry, offered at no cost to qualified design engineers, managers, and corporate leadership. The publication maintains an online presence and publishes news, columns, and feature articles on topics including semiconductor manufacturing, communications, electronic design automation, electronics engineering, technology, and related products. In November 2012, UBM Electronics announced that the December 2012 issue would be the last printed edition; from 2013 onward, EE Times has appeared online only. A European print edition began in 2018, indicating regional expansion of its print format.

On June 3, 2016, UBM announced the sale of EE Times and its electronics media portfolio, including EDN, Embedded.com, TechOnline, and Datasheets.com. The buyer was AspenCore Media, a company owned by Arrow Electronics. The sale was valued at US$23.5 million, and the acquisition was completed on August 1, 2016.

In Cyprus, halloumi, also known as hellim, was familiar to the Lusignan rulers. Some writers contend that halloumi originated in Cyprus during the Byzantine period, while the name itself is thought to be of Arabic origin. There is no surviving documentary evidence linking the cheese to Cyprus before 1554; in that year Florio Bustron described a Cypriot sheep‑milk cheese called calumi. Halloumi is commonly served sliced, grilled, fried, or sometimes fresh, and it is typically presented as an appetiser or as part of a meze dish.

Cyprus is a developed representative democracy with an advanced high-income economy and a very high level of human development. Its Mediterranean climate and cultural heritage, reflecting Greek and Turkish elements, make it a major tourist destination. The country is a member of the Commonwealth of Nations. It was a founding member of the Non-Aligned Movement and remained so until it joined the European Union in 2004. Cyprus joined the eurozone in 2008. It has long maintained good relations with NATO and in 2024 announced its intention to officially join the alliance.

The Swiss Inventory of Cultural Property of National and Regional Significance is maintained by the Federal Office of Civil Protection. In 2009, the register of A-class objects was made available online, with access provided in both geographic information system (GIS) format and PDF documents. The online data were current as of 1 April 2010. A printed catalogue, publication number 408.980, was issued in 2010.

The Swiss Inventory of Cultural Property of National and Regional Significance is Switzerland’s official register of culturally important properties. To reflect the country’s multilingual heritage, the inventory is presented with titles in German, French, and Italian. It was established under Article 5 of the Second Protocol to the Hague Convention for the Protection of Cultural Property in the Event of Armed Conflict, which provides for national inventories of cultural property.

The 2023 Armenian Supercup marked the 25th edition of Armenia's annual football super cup. It pitted Urartu, the previous season's champions of both the Armenian Premier League and the Armenian Cup, against Shirak, the Armenian Cup runners-up from the prior season. The contest concluded with a 0–0 draw, and Shirak triumphed 6–5 in the ensuing penalty shootout.

Gunnar Heckscher was a prominent Swedish diplomat who served as Sweden's ambassador to New Delhi from 1965 to 1970 and to Tokyo from 1970 to 1975. He was a delegate to the United Nations in 1975. In addition to his diplomatic postings, Heckscher held positions in international and regional bodies, including vice-chair of the International Political Science Association and membership in the Consultative Assembly of the Council of Europe, where he chaired its Economic Committee. His career also involved participation in government committees on psychological defense, public administration, and constitutional reform.

Gunnar Heckscher (born 8 July 1909 in Danderyd, Sweden) was the son of Professor Eli Heckscher and Ebba Westberg and a Swedish political scientist and academic. He earned a Bachelor of Arts degree from Uppsala University in 1927, followed by a licentiate in 1932 and a PhD in 1934. He was appointed a docent in political science at Uppsala University in 1933, and he lectured there from 1933 to 1941. He then taught political science at Stockholm University College from 1941 to 1948.

Molkwerum is a historic settlement in the Netherlands that is first documented in 1398 under the name Molkenhuzen. The etymology of its name remains uncertain. Geographically, it lies north of the former Zuiderzee and south of the former Staverse Meer, the latter having been reclaimed as a polder in the seventeenth century. Historically, the community was populated by seafaring traders who operated routes to the Baltic Sea. In addition, Molkwerum maintained its own office in Amsterdam.

Molkwerum is a village in the Netherlands that had a population of 301 in 1840. In 1885 a railway station shared with Koudum, on the Koudum–Molkwerum line, began operation. The harbour was filled in during the 1960s and the adjacent sluice was demolished. In 2000 the village opened an Elvis Presley museum, which houses authentic clothing of Elvis and an autographed guitar. Administratively, Molkwerum belonged to Hemelumer Oldeferd municipality prior to 1984 and later became part of Nijefurd municipality, remaining so until 2011.

The U.S. Food and Drug Administration advises that bug zappers should not be installed above areas where food is prepared. To prevent insects from escaping, the devices are designed to retain captured insects within the unit. Accordingly, manufacturers have developed scatter-proof containment designs intended to minimize dispersion of insects and debris around the appliance.

Outdoor bug zappers have limited efficacy against biting insects, such as female mosquitoes, while they disproportionately attract and kill harmless or beneficial species. A University of Delaware study evaluated six devices over 15 summer nights, recording a total of 13,789 insects killed, of which only 31 were biting insects.

Set is an abstract data type in computer science that stores unique values and has no inherent order. It represents a computer implementation of the mathematical concept of a finite set. The typical operation is membership testing, i.e., determining whether a given value is contained in the set rather than retrieving a specific element.

In Java, the Set interface represents a collection of unique elements. HashSet provides an implementation of Set that organizes its elements with a hash table, delivering efficient basic operations on average. Java also defines a sub-interface called SortedSet for sets that maintain a defined ordering. As an implementation of SortedSet, TreeSet uses a binary search tree to keep elements in sorted sequence.

Nonverbal learning disorder (NVLD) presents notable challenges during adolescence, a period when rising demands for abstract reasoning, time management, organization, and social interaction strain affected students. Individuals with NVLD often attend to isolated details rather than synthesizing them into a coherent whole, which can hinder their abilities to summarize material and to integrate ideas across different domains. They may struggle to transfer knowledge to new situations, infer information that is not explicitly stated, and anticipate potential outcomes. Organizational difficulties further impede the logical arrangement of information, contributing to broader academic and social difficulties.

Nonverbal learning difficulties (NVLD) have been identified as a subject of inquiry since the early days of child neurology, reflecting a longstanding interest in how nonverbal skills relate to cognitive function. Current discourse centers on whether the prevailing conceptions of nonverbal learning disorder constitute a valid diagnostic category, and questions persist about the extent to which these conceptions accurately delineate a distinct, clinically recognizable syndrome.

Smoke on This... is the first solo studio album by American musician Rex Brown, released on July 28, 2017, through Entertainment One. The release marks Brown's inaugural foray into lead vocals and guitar, supplementing his long-standing role as a bassist.

Chamdo is organized into eleven county-level divisions, consisting of one district, Karuo District, which serves as the principal district, and ten counties: Jonda, Gonjo, Riwoche, Dengqen, Zhag'yab, Baxoi, Zognang, Maarkam, Lhorong, and Banbar.

Chamdo, officially known as Qamdo (Tibetan: ཆབ་མདོ; Wylie: chab mdo; ZYPY: qamdo), is a prefecture-level city in the eastern part of the Tibet Autonomous Region of China. In Chinese, the city is referred to as Changdu (昌都; pinyin: Changdu). Its administrative seat lies in the town of Chengguan within Karuo District. Chamdo ranks as the third-largest city in the Tibet Autonomous Region, following Lhasa and Shigatse.
