The men's doubles competition at the 1984 Australian Open was held from 26 November to 9 December 1984 at Kooyong Stadium in Melbourne, Australia, played on outdoor grass courts. Mark Edmondson and Sherwood Stewart won the title, defeating Joakim Nyström and Mats Wilander in the final.

José Ortega y Gasset was a Spanish philosopher whose influence was considerable within intellectual circles. This prominence stemmed largely from a broad sympathy for his philosophical writings, which resonated beyond narrow academic confines. His works are notable for their accessibility, presenting complex ideas without requiring readers to be well-versed in technical philosophy, thereby inviting a wider audience to engage with broader questions of culture and society.

José Ortega y Gasset was a Spanish philosopher and essayist whose work integrated social criticism with a distinctive ontology. He remained open to certain strains of socialism, including non-Marxist forms, while maintaining a critical stance toward capitalism, particularly its laissez-faire variant. He praised Pablo Iglesias Posse in reverent terms for his ethical commitment. His thought was influenced by German social democrats Paul Natorp and Hermann Cohen, and he developed a communitarian ontology that emphasized the social character of human life. In his economic critique, he argued that nineteenth-century capitalism degraded moral sensibilities and diminished the ethical consciousness of individuals.

In 2020, NBN expanded into digital programming by launching Amplified, a music show that highlighted local and up-and-coming musicians. The program was hosted by Matt Field and aired at 8 p.m. on Thursdays on NBN's Facebook page, with episodes subsequently rebroadcast on 9Go! on Saturday afternoons. The series lasted one season.

On 1 March 1985, Jim Sullivan began his tenure as NBN's news director, a role that has led him to become Australia's longest-serving holder of that position. NBN's coverage of the 1989 Newcastle earthquake was broadcast to a global audience, and NBN reporters were interviewed by international news services.
Palewyami, also referred to as Altinin and Poso Creek Yokuts, was a major dialect of the Yokuts language in California, though some researchers regard it as a distinct but closely related language.

Killing horizon is a geometric construct that features in the study of cosmic censorship hypotheses in general relativity. These hypotheses advance the idea that singularities—points where physical quantities become infinite—are always concealed within black holes and thus cannot be observed from the rest of the Universe. As such, the concept of a Killing horizon provides a framework for understanding the boundaries that separate accessible regions of spacetime from those containing hidden singularities.

The term Killing horizon originates from the Killing vector field, a central notion in differential geometry. Within a spacetime, a Killing vector field is defined as a vector field that preserves the metric, i.e., leaves the spacetime geometry unchanged under its flow.

In the 1930s, at the Accademia di Brera, an opposition group emerged to challenge the Novecento Italiano movement. It was led by Aldo Carpi, the director, and brought together Brera students such as Afro, Aldo Badoli, Aldo Bergolli, Renato Birolli, Bruno Cassinari, Cherchi, Alfredo Chighine, Grosso, Renato Guttuso, Dino Lanaro, Giuseppe Migneco, Mantica, Ennio Morlotti, Aligi Sassu, Ernesto Treccani, Italo Valenti, and Emilio Vedova; later members included Giuseppe Ajmone and Ibrahim Kodra, while Trento Longaretti participated but did not join the core discussions because he had returned home after classes. The movement adopted the name Corrente and established a magazine of the same title. In a 1939 editorial, Corrente denounced fascism, rejected the Novecento Italiano, and criticized Futurism, signaling a clear stance within the artistic and political debates of the era.

Novecento Italiano, an Italian art movement named to evoke the 1900s and to recall Italy’s Quattrocento and Cinquecento as a sign of renewed tradition, rejected European avant-garde art and aimed to revive large-format history painting in a classical idiom. It did not follow a single, rigid programme and included artists of diverse styles and temperaments, such as Carlo Carrà and Marino Marini. The movement's objective was to promote a renewed yet traditional Italian art. Sironi contended that the most significant painters emerged in the late nineteenth century, and that the Novecento artists should draw inspiration from the world around them rather than imitate a world conceived by God.

The News of the World Darts Championship emerged as a leading tournament during the first wave of televised darts, with coverage expanding in the 1970s and continuing into the early to mid-1980s. By 1989, the surge in televised darts had collapsed, and most darts competitions disappeared from broadcast schedules, leaving only the World Championship as the enduring televised event.

The News of the World Darts Championship originated before World War II, but no national champion was declared for the event prior to the conflict. After the war, the competition was revived as a national championship in 1947–48. For decades it was regarded as the sport’s premier event, often described as the championship that every darts player aspires to win, a status that persisted until its decline in the 1990s. Because it drew international participants and counted winners from several countries, the tournament is sometimes regarded as the first world darts championship.

Rich Kids on LSD is a punk rock project featuring guitarist Chris Rest, who has also performed as a session musician for other prominent acts. Rest played guitar on the Mad Caddies' 2001 album Rock the Plank and contributed guitar to The Real McKenzies' 2008 release Off the Leash. In addition to these collaborations, he has been a member of Lagwagon since 1997, having stepped in to replace Ken Stringfellow. He later joined No Use for a Name in 2009, filling the vacancy left by Dave Nassie, and remained with the band until their final show in the wake of Tony Sly's death in 2012.

Rich Kids on LSD, a punk rock group, has been cited by contemporary musicians for the notable skill of its members. In a TimesTalks discussion on musicianship in punk rock, Billie Joe Armstrong of Green Day highlighted Rich Kids on LSD drummer Bomer Manzullo as an example of high-caliber punk talent, describing him as an exceptionally skilled and intense drummer. Further praise came from Erik Sandin of NOFX in a Communities Digital News interview, where he lauded Manzullo as extraordinarily talented and notably powerful behind the drums.

As of 1912 Salisbury Cathedral possessed at least eight external consecration crosses, three on the north wall, three on the east wall, and two embossed on the south wall; the sacristy on the south side and the statuary along the west frontage are thought to have concealed the remaining four crosses, while the extant marks were carved into the stone buttresses. Interior painted crosses corresponded to the positions of the exterior ones, including one that commemorates the dedication of the Trinity Chapel on 30 September 1225. Beyond Salisbury, the ruined Elgin Cathedral and the Church of the Holy Rude in Stirling also have crosses. St Mary’s Church at Ottery St Mary preserves several well‑maintained crosses, and Sacred Heart Church at Bushey, consecrated in 1977 by Cardinal Hume, contains twelve commemorative crosses donated by the local social club. The Church of St Peter and St Paul at Ampton includes a painted cross, while St Mary’s Church, Shipton Solars, contains medieval red‑lead‑painted crosses in the chancel and nave. Interior crosses are visible at All Saints Church, Kenton; St Mary, Thornham Parva; and St Peter, Great Livermere, and St Peter’s Church at Creeting St Peter features exterior crosses; there is also a single consecration cross in the nave of Dunfermline Abbey.

Consecration crosses are physical markers placed on the walls of a church during its consecration, serving as an enduring sign that the building has been set apart for sacred purposes. The mark indicates that the structure is permanently bound to holy use and may not be transferred to secular or profane uses. This understanding is grounded in the writings of Saint Thomas Aquinas, specifically Summa Theologiae II-II, q. 34, a. 3, where he treats the permanence of consecration for church buildings. The cross functions as the visible manifestation of the consecration, embodying its permanent, non-transferable character.

Voiceovers are a common element in advertising, providing narration and character voices for commercials and promotional content. Historically, men have performed a substantial majority of voiceovers, with estimates indicating up to 94% of such work being undertaken by male performers. In recent years, the share of female voice actors has risen, reflecting a gradual shift in the industry. Female voiceovers are predominantly used in advertisements for food products, household goods, and feminine-care items.

The advertising profession has seen continued diversification of agency models. Large multinational clients are increasingly perceived as less dependent on traditional large global agencies, instead engaging a broader mix of partners and specialized capabilities. This shift has coincided with the growth of non-traditional agencies across global markets, with notable examples including TAXI in Canada and SMART in Australia. Industry observers have described these developments as a revolutionary shift in the advertising industry.

Red Bull Road Rage does not employ a universally recognised points system, with each race run as a stand-alone event. Accordingly, the overall ranking for the series is based on a full season of race results rather than per-event scoring. The season's results identify the riders who finished as the number-one world-ranked Red Bull Road Rage athletes.

Red Bull Road Rage's 2009 season finale marked the event's return to racing in Switzerland. Held on 28 October 2009, the race route started at Rengg and descended into the Entlebuch region, covering a 2.1-kilometer course with an overall elevation loss of 210 meters. The descent featured an average gradient of 10 percent, with the steepest sections reaching up to 16 percent.

Bacillati and Pseudomonadati diverged around three billion years ago, indicating that prokaryotes had already colonized terrestrial environments by that time. Collectively, these two lineages form a large clade that comprises about 97 percent of prokaryotes and roughly 99 percent of all described bacterial species known by 2009. This lineage is classified within the taxon Selabacteria, a designation that alludes to their phototrophic abilities and derives from the Greek selas, meaning light. In contrast, the bacterial phyla outside Selabacteria remain a matter of debate, with ongoing discussion about their composition. In particular, the status of Fusobacteria within or outside this outer group remains unresolved, leaving their classification unsettled.

Bacillati is the name assigned to a proposed prokaryotic kingdom following the 2022 introduction of updated rules governing kingdom-level taxa. In 2024, the same two authors, Battistuzzi and Hedges, proposed new names for such higher taxa and argued that the taxonomically preferable solution for bacterial kingdoms is to recognize the subdivision indicated by their study, with further refinements. Consequently, the new and only valid designation for this kingdom is Bacillati.

Administratively, the Faroe Islands are divided into six sýslur: Norðoyar, Eysturoy, Streymoy, Vágar, Sandoy, and Suðuroy. A sýsla denotes a district; in contemporary administration it is primarily a police district, but the term continues to be widely understood as a geographical region. In earlier periods, each sýsla possessed its own assembly, the várting, or spring ting.

In the aftermath of the 2022 Faroese general election, a three-party governing coalition was formed, bringing together the Social Democratic Party, Republic, and Progress. The coalition governs under the leadership of Prime Minister Aksel V. Johannesen.

Walker Arboretum, situated on the hillside above Rodman Hall with the Twelve Mile Creek running below, forms a notable botanical site in St. Catharines. The estate's original owner was Thomas Rodman Merritt, the son of William Hamilton Merritt. In the late 19th century, Merritt enlisted English landscape designer Samuel Richardson to curate and shape the grounds. The arboretum comprises an extensive, rambling garden that houses a collection of rare conifers thriving in an exceptional local micro-climate. Among its notable specimens is one of Canada's largest Chinese Empress trees.

Following the 1970 reorganization that created the Regional Municipality of Niagara, portions of Louth Township lying east of Fifteen Mile Creek were annexed by the City of St. Catharines, including the eastern parts of the Hamlet of Rockway and the Hamlet of Power Glen. The remaining sections of Grantham Township in the northeast, including Port Weller, were also transferred to the city. With the Louth lands incorporated, the city’s western periphery began to take shape, spurring development along Martindale Road in 1983 and Vansickle Road in 1987 as these districts neared completion. A late-1990s effort to extend expansion further west was halted by Ontario Greenbelt legislation.

During the sequence, Holt takes Callie and Owens’ gun to the nearby hot springs for a bath. A rider approaches the outpost, raising suspicion of escaped convicts in the area. Owens advances while Todd hides in the stable tack room with his rifle. The rider flashes a Huntsville deputy sheriff badge and claims to be hunting escaped convicts. Owens signals Todd that the danger is not immediate. The visitor is revealed as Rafe Zimmerman, who had escaped Huntsville the day before his scheduled hanging for murder. Zimmerman then signals three other convicts to ride into town. The other convicts are Tevis, a hardcore outlaw; Yancy, a simpleton; and Gratz, an obedient follower; they had been with Zimmerman during the breakout.

Rawhide (1951 film) follows Tom Owens, the son of J. C. Owens of the Overland Mail Company, who is portrayed as clean-cut and sophisticated. His father intends for him to learn the business from the ground up and sends him west to the remote relay station Rawhide Pass to gain practical experience. There, he is mentored by stationmaster Sam Todd, a longtime associate who has known J. C. Owens for more than four decades. Tom eagerly anticipates his return to civilization within a week.

The crab-eating mongoose is characterized by white specks on the crown, a white chin, and a gray throat. Its iris is yellow, and the ears are small and rounded. The species possesses webbing between the digits. Its head-to-body length ranges from 47.7 to 55.8 cm (18.8 to 22.0 in), with a tail measuring 28 to 34 cm (11 to 13 in). The body mass falls between 1.1 and 2.5 kg (2.4 to 5.5 lb).

Crab-eating mongooses are typically active during the morning and evening hours, displaying crepuscular activity. They occur in small groups, often consisting of up to four individuals. They are believed to be proficient swimmers. Their hunting is concentrated along the banks of streams and in close proximity to water.

The Apostolic Canons, also known as the Ecclesiastical Canons of the Same Holy Apostles, comprise a collection of early church decrees. In the Eastern Church they are traditionally counted at eighty-five, while the Western Church records fifty. These canons address the governance and discipline of the early Christian community, outlining rules for ecclesiastical conduct and administration. They are transmitted together with the Apostolic Constitutions, a larger composite work, and the Apostolic Constitutions themselves are included in the Ante-Nicene Fathers collection.

Canon law refers to the internal ecclesiastical legal system that governs the Catholic Church (including both Latin and Eastern Catholic rites), the Eastern Orthodox and Oriental Orthodox churches, and the national churches within the Anglican Communion. The manner in which church law is legislated, interpreted, and adjudicated varies markedly among these four ecclesial bodies. Across these traditions, a canon originally denoted a rule promulgated by a church council, and such canons formed the foundational framework from which canon law developed.

The University of Malta engages in collaborations with other institutions and has established formal links with the Chamber of Commerce, Enterprise and Industry, and the Employment and Training Corporation. Through these partnerships, the university seeks to explore and advance connections among higher education, the industrial sector, business communities, and public authorities, with the aim of promoting joint initiatives, research collaboration, and workforce development.
According to post-nominal conventions, the University of Malta is abbreviated as Melit, a shortened form of Melita, which is the Latinised rendering of the Greek Μελίτη.

As of 2011, Trinidad and Tobago’s mass media and communications infrastructure relies on five submarine cable systems that serve the country: AMERICAS-II, the Eastern Caribbean Fibre System (ECFS), the Global Caribbean Network (GCN), the Suriname-Guyana Submarine Cable System (SG-SCS), and the Trinidad-Curaçao link. These networks provide international connectivity to the United States, portions of the Caribbean region, and parts of South America, supporting cross-border telecommunications and media transmission essential to the sector.

Mass media in Trinidad and Tobago operate within a constitutional framework that protects freedom of expression and press freedom. The constitution and associated laws prohibit arbitrary interference with privacy, family life, homes, or correspondence. In practice, the government generally respects freedom of speech and the press, a climate reinforced by the presence of an independent press, an effective judiciary, and a functioning democratic system that together sustain media freedom. Legislation also bars acts that insult or offend individuals on grounds of race, ethnicity, or religion and prohibits the incitement of racial or religious hatred. Privacy protections are likewise enforced in practice, with authorities typically respecting these prohibitions on interference with private life.

Seven Network's principal programming is delivered by fibre from HSV Melbourne to its sister stations and regional affiliates, while ATN Sydney provides national news and current affairs programming. Receiving stations and affiliates insert their own localized news bulletins and advertising, ensuring regional variation. The network's broadcast footprint covers both metropolitan and regional areas across Queensland, New South Wales, Victoria, and Western Australia. Owned-and-operated stations include ATN Sydney, HSV Melbourne, BTQ Brisbane, SAS Adelaide, and TVW Perth, with regional O&Os comprising NEN (Northern New South Wales and the Gold Coast), CBN (Southern New South Wales and the Australian Capital Territory), AMV (regional Victoria), PTV (Mildura), STQ (regional Queensland), Seven Regional WA, TNT (Tasmania), GTS/BKN (Spencer Gulf and Broken Hill), TND (Darwin), and QQQ (remote central and eastern Australia).

During the 2008 Summer Olympics in Beijing, the Seven Network held exclusive rights in Australia across free-to-air, pay television, online, and mobile platforms. The live telecast of the XXIX Olympiad was presented as a joint effort by Seven and SBS Television. Seven produced coverage of the opening and closing ceremonies and the primary competitive events such as swimming, athletics, rowing, cycling, and gymnastics, while SBS complemented this schedule with coverage emphasizing long-form events, including soccer, road cycling, volleyball, and table tennis.

Delivery Multimedia Integration Framework (DMIF) is an extension of the MPEG-2 DSM-CC standard (ISO/IEC 13818-6:1998) that seeks to unify interactive, broadcast, and conversational multimedia within a single specification for use on set‑top boxes, desktops, and mobile devices. The DSM-CC work continued under the MPEG-4 umbrella as the DSM-CC Multimedia Integration Framework (DMIF), defined in ISO/IEC 14496-6. DSM-CC stands for Digital Storage Media – Command and Control. DMIF has also been the designation of a working group within the Moving Picture Experts Group (MPEG). In 1997, the acronym DSM-CC was replaced by Delivery, resulting in the Delivery Multimedia Integration Framework.

Delivery Multimedia Integration Framework (DMIF) is a component of the MPEG-4 standard that provides a consistent interface between applications and the underlying transport, enabling MPEG-4 developers to abstract away transport-specific concerns. Defined in MPEG-4 Part 6 (ISO/IEC 14496-6) in 1999, DMIF specifies two interfaces, the DMIF/Application Interface (DAI) and the DMIF-Network Interface (DNI). Through appropriate DMIF instantiation, a single application can operate over different transport layers, offering flexibility and interoperability across diverse networks and media environments.

No. 321 Squadron RAF participated in relief operations after Japan's surrender, undertaking relief flights and aid drops to thousands of internees held in prisoner-of-war camps in Java and Sumatra. In October 1945 the unit relocated to a new air base near Batavia to continue postwar duties in the region. On 8 December 1945 control was transferred to the Netherlands’ Marineluchtvaartdienst (MLD), with the squadron continuing under the designation No. 321 Squadron MLD. Subsequently, alongside No. 320 Squadron, it conducted maritime patrol missions from Valkenburg for several decades. The squadron was disbanded in January 2005 as part of budget reductions.

No. 321 Squadron RAF was re-formed at RAF Trincomallee in Ceylon on 15 August 1942 and operated Consolidated Catalina flying boats, the crews being drawn from personnel of the Malayan Labour Detachment who had escaped to Ceylon. The squadron’s headquarters were at RAF China Bay, with detachments established at Mombasa, the Cocos Islands, Socotra, Masirah, Ceylon, Durban, Port Elizabeth, Aden, and Cape Town. In July 1945 it was supplemented by Consolidated Liberator aircraft. Subsequently, the air echelon moved to Cocos Island in preparation for Operation Zipper, the proposed invasion of Malaya.

Ann Aiken is an American jurist who serves as a senior United States district judge for the District of Oregon. She was nominated by President Bill Clinton to fill the seat vacated by Judge James A. Redden, with an initial nomination in November 1995 and a renewed nomination on January 7, 1997. Aiken was confirmed by the U.S. Senate on January 28, 1998 and received her commission on February 4, 1998. She became the district’s chief judge on February 1, 2009, the first woman to hold that position there, and served in that role until January 31, 2016. She assumed senior status on December 29, 2023.

Ann Louise Aiken (born December 29, 1951) is an American attorney and jurist from Oregon. A native Oregonian, she has served as a state court judge in the Oregon circuit courts and has worked in private legal practice. She serves as a senior United States district judge for the District of Oregon, and she was chief judge of the district from February 1, 2009 to January 31, 2016.

Univision changed the station's call letters to KUVS and relocated its operations from Modesto to Sacramento, establishing a new facility in a former bank building across from Arden Fair Mall to house the Sacramento operation. The local news lineup was expanded by adding an 11 p.m. newscast to the existing 6 p.m. broadcast, broadening Sacramento coverage. This move marked the first instance of a network-owned and operated television station operating in Sacramento. Following the relocation, only the sales and news staff remained based in Modesto.

Chester Smith sold KCSO to Univision in 1997, but retained the KCSO call sign, after which the outlet was renamed KUVS-TV. Subsequently, the bulk of its operations were shifted from Modesto to the Sacramento area. Today, the station provides locally produced Spanish-language newscasts for the market and also creates a weekly public affairs program that is broadcast on other Univision stations throughout California.

Mikhail Glinka's body of work, together with the outputs of composers and other creatives he inspired, helped establish a distinctly Russian artistic style. This distinctive style has since secured a prominent place in world culture, underscoring its sustained international influence.

Mikhail Glinka's orchestral works have enjoyed substantial popularity in concert programming and recordings outside Russia. Among his widely recognized operatic overtures, the overture to Ruslan is noted for its energetic character. His major orchestral work includes the symphonic poem Kamarinskaya (1848), based on Russian folk songs. He also wrote two Spanish-inspired pieces, A Night in Madrid (1848, 1851) and Jota Aragonesa (1845). In addition to these works, Glinka composed numerous art songs and piano pieces and produced a number of chamber works.

During the early phase in the Indian subcontinent, Buddhist art was largely aniconic, avoiding direct representations of the Buddha; by the 1st century CE this practice gave way to an iconic phase in which the Buddha was depicted directly. As Buddhism spread to new regions, its artistic production diversified and adapted to local traditions. The northern transmission progressed through Central Asia into Eastern Asia, shaping Buddhist art to the north, while a southern trajectory carried influence eastward to Southeast Asia. In India, Buddhist art flourished and also influenced contemporary Hindu artistic production. By the 10th century, Buddhism had largely declined in the region as Hinduism and Islam expanded, contributing to its near disappearance there.

Musical chanting constitutes an integral aspect of Buddhist cultural practice. In many traditions, chants are performed in Tibetan or Sanskrit, reflecting the linguistic heritage of the liturgy. These vocalizations are often intricate, comprising recitations of sacred scriptures or serving as celebrations during various festivals. Yang chanting is performed without metrical timing and is accompanied by resonant drums and low, sustained syllables, producing a continuous sonic texture that accompanies ritual activities.

PAL (Phase Alternating Line) is an analog television color-encoding system that uses a phase-alternating chrominance method to mitigate color phase errors across a frame. By contrast, the SECAM system transmits only one of the U and V chroma components on each TV line and recovers the other via a delay line, a method that does not rely on quadrature amplitude modulation. SECAM achieves added robustness through frequency modulation of the chrominance subcarrier rather than QAM, a difference that sets it apart from PAL’s approach. The sequential U/V transmission concept that underpins SECAM was later reused in Europe’s final generation of analog video standards, collectively known as the MAC standards.

PAL denotes a family of analog color-encoding standards used in various regions. Tapes recorded from PAL-N or from PAL-B/G, D/K, H, or I broadcasts contain a downconverted color subcarrier that is identical across these variants, making recordings from these systems indistinguishable when transferred to tape. A PAL-recorded tape made in Europe will run in color on any PAL-N VCR and PAL-N television set in Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay. Likewise, recordings made in Argentina, Paraguay, or Uruguay from a PAL-N broadcast can be viewed in color on European PAL hardware as well as on devices in Australia and New Zealand. These tapes also play back successfully in Russia and other SECAM countries, since the USSR mandated PAL compatibility in 1985. Such cross-compatibility is regarded as highly convenient for video collectors.
Guy Parmelin married Caroline Merotto in 1995. Merotto is the daughter of Aldo Merotto, an engineer of Italian origin. Caroline's mother is Maria, née Moosrainer. The couple have no children.

Guy Bernard Parmelin (born 9 November 1959) is a Swiss Federal Councillor and a member of the Swiss People's Party (SVP/UDC). Since entering the Federal Council in 2016, he led the Department of Defence, Civil Protection and Sport from 2016 to 2018 and has headed the Department of Economic Affairs, Education and Research since 2019. Parmelin served as President of the Swiss Confederation in 2021, and has held the office of Vice President in 2020 and again from 2025 onward.

In the episode The Ties That Bind, Elena frees herself, knocks Jamie down, and assists Stefan in removing the wooden pieces embedded in his chest. She also reveals to Stefan that she kissed Damon. Abby takes Bonnie to the Hybrid, while Bonnie remains reluctant to disclose the coffins’ locations; Abby persuades her to reveal them in order to save her life. Abby then writes a message for Bonnie instructing her to warn their friends about the threat. She further states that she will help Bonnie only if Bonnie can restore Abby’s magic, noting that Bonnie is the only one capable of doing so.

Several studies have compared the number of publications indexed by different academic research databases to gauge relative coverage. In a 2024 study conducted at the University of Jordan, researchers compared their university’s publications across several databases. The results showed a systematic decline in coverage from Scopus to Web of Science to The Lens, with Scopus providing the highest coverage and The Lens the lowest.

Scopus is a bibliographic database owned by Elsevier, a major international publisher of scientific journals. In 2009, an independent Scopus Content Selection and Advisory Board (CSAB) was established to oversee the journal selection process. The CSAB is charged with preventing conflicts of interest in Scopus’s journal selection and maintaining an open and transparent policy for content coverage that applies irrespective of publisher. The board comprises scientists and subject librarians. Despite these safeguards, criticisms regarding potential conflicts of interest have persisted in assessments of Scopus’s coverage decisions.

ISO 19114, titled Geographic information — Quality evaluation procedures, is an international standard developed by the International Organization for Standardization. It provides a procedural framework for assessing the quality of digital geographic datasets, and it aligns with the data quality principles defined in ISO 19113. The standard also delineates three conformance classes: quality evaluation, evaluation of data quality, and reporting of quality information, which together define the scope and responsibilities for quality assessment within geographic information systems.

Manchester, Iowa's county courthouse, completed in 1894, was erected at a cost of $38,000. Its clock tower was funded through contributions from 700 county residents. The building was designed by architect C. E. Bell in the Romanesque Revival style and constructed of red pressed brick. The main block measures 76 by 100 feet, and the tower with its spire rises to 135 feet (41 meters). The walls are 18 inches thick (45.7 centimeters). Inside, the first floor features decorative metal ceilings and intricate woodwork that remain original to the building. In 1981, it was listed on the National Register of Historic Places as part of the County Courthouses in Iowa Thematic Resource.

In Manchester, Iowa, the age distribution is distributed with 26.2% of residents under 18, 7.6% aged 18 to 24, 26.6% between 25 and 44, 19.6% from 45 to 64, and 20.0% 65 years and older, resulting in a median age of 38 years. The overall sex ratio stands at 87.5 males for every 100 females, while among the population aged 18 and older the ratio is 82.4 males per 100 females.

During the 1996–97 Scottish Premier Division, Hibernian secured a 1–0 victory in the first leg at Easter Road and followed with a 4–2 win in the return at Broadwood Stadium, yielding a 5–2 aggregate margin and enabling Hibernian to retain their Premier Division status for another season.

The 1996–97 Scottish Premier Division season began on 10 August and concluded on 10 May. The campaign opened with Gary McSwegan of Dundee United scoring the first goal in a 1–1 home draw with Motherwell. The season ended with Tommy Johnson of Celtic netting the final goal in a late 3–0 home victory over Dundee United.

By June 1979, the Sandinista National Liberation Front (FSLN) had established control over virtually the entire country, with Managua remaining the principal exception. On 17 July 1979, Anastasio Somoza Debayle resigned from the presidency, and two days later FSLN forces entered Managua. Somoza Debayle fled to Miami, effectively ceding state power to the revolutionary movement. The Nationalist Liberal Party was practically rendered defunct, and numerous government functionaries along with pro-Somoza business figures went into exile. The Catholic Church and the professional sectors generally welcomed the new political arrangement.

During the Nicaraguan Revolution, the roles of international actors in assessing alleged antisemitism within the Sandinista movement were contested. The United Nations, the Organization of American States, and Pax Christi disputed Heritage Foundation's accusations, arguing that the seizure of property belonging to Nicaraguan Jews stemmed from ties to the Somoza regime rather than from Jewish identity, and they pointed to Sandinista officials of Jewish descent as part of the movement’s diverse background. By contrast, the Anti-Defamation League supported the charges of Sandinista antisemitism and worked with Nicaraguan Jewish exiles to reclaim a synagogue that had been firebombed by Sandinista militants in 1978 and subsequently expropriated in 1979.

Local elections are held at regular intervals across all municipalities in Germany to elect the mayor and the members of the municipal council. The elections for the municipal council are known in German as Kommunalwahlen. The timing of these elections varies by state: Bremen conducts elections every four years, Bavaria every six years, and the remaining states generally hold them on a five-year cycle.

Municipalities (Gemeinden) represent the lowest tier of official territorial division in Germany. Depending on their status and the state (Land) in which they are situated, a Gemeinde can occupy the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, or 5th administrative level. The city-states of Berlin, Bremen, and Hamburg function as second-level divisions due to their status as states in their own right. In states that maintain intermediate Regierungsbezirke, namely Baden-Württemberg, Bavaria, Hesse, and North Rhine-Westphalia, a Gemeinde resides one level below the corresponding Regierungsbezirk. A Gemeinde is at one level higher when it is not part of a Gemeindeverband (municipal association).

Within the Eastern United States, the East South Central subregion tends to be more politically and culturally conservative than the neighboring South Atlantic region. From 2012 through 2023, Mississippi, Alabama, Kentucky, and Tennessee have been described as hosting among the most conservative state governments in the country. The region is characterized by the predominance of Conservative Evangelical Protestantism, which shapes its religious and social life. Consequently, East South Central constitutes a core area of the Bible Belt.

Geographically, the Eastern United States encompasses a large portion of the country, with the Southeastern United States forming a major subregion. Its core extends north to Maryland and West Virginia, where the northern boundary follows the Ohio River and the Mason–Dixon line. From there, the region stretches westward to include areas as far as Arkansas and Louisiana.

The downtown redevelopment initiative in Guelph culminated in the Baker District project, finalized in 2018 after discussions dating back to 2007. The plan seeks to transform the Baker Street parking lot and the properties fronting the northern end of Wyndham Street into a mixed-use, higher-density urban district that combines residential and commercial development. The project is estimated to cost between 315 million and 369 million Canadian dollars and was envisioned to include a new library, along with commercial, institutional, and office space, plus an underground parking facility. The private partner selected is Ottawa-based Windmill Development Group, with discussions also taking place regarding potential partnerships with Conestoga College and the YMCA. Construction was not anticipated to commence before 2023, and up to 7.5 million was planned to be spent prior to 2023 to acquire the remaining land.

Guelph's municipal government opted against acquiring further land in late 2018 due to economic considerations. The following year the province announced the sale of the remaining 362 acres of Ontario government land. These developments reflect a period of adjustment in land-use planning and municipal growth strategy for the city as government-held parcels were released from public ownership.

Since 1954, the UCLA Band has included a version of "I'm Looking Over a Four Leaf Clover" in its repertoire. The chorus from this arrangement is used as the second part of Rover, the Bruins' victory song. Similar lyrics have been employed in two other songs.

In 1948, Salt Lake City-based disc jockey Al “Jazzbo” Collins popularized Art Mooney's rendition of I'm Looking Over a Four Leaf Clover by repeatedly playing the track on air for an extended period. Sources disagree on the duration, with some citing about three and a half hours and others reporting as long as twenty-four hours; a particular detail notes that the record continued to play for 120 minutes. The stunt elicited listener feedback, with some callers praising Collins for selecting something different, a compliment that was nonetheless taken as an insult toward him.

There are no surviving texts in Aquitanian. Knowledge of the language derives from onomastic data, including about two hundred personal names and around sixty deity names. These names are preserved indirectly in Latin inscriptions from the Roman imperial period, principally dating to the first through the third centuries AD, with some possibly dating to the fourth or fifth centuries. The Gascon language is believed to retain an Aquitanian substrate, with several lexical items showing affinities to Basque.

The Aquitanian language refers to the tongue once spoken by the ancient Aquitani, a people who inhabited a region bounded by the Pyrenees, the Garonne River, and the Atlantic coastline during the Roman period. What survives for Aquitanian is primarily epigraphic evidence, with inscriptions discovered not only in the core area but also south of the Pyrenees, in present-day Navarre and Castile.

ISO 11992 uses a protocol architecture that is broadly comparable to SAE J1939, but it differs in several key aspects. The principal distinctions concern the timing scheme, the bus voltage levels employed for signaling, and the formatting of the 29-bit message identifier that accompanies each transmission. These differences reflect the specific design choices of ISO 11992 relative to J1939 and influence how messages are timed, encoded, and addressed on the network.

ISO 11992 is an international standard governing the interchange of digital information over electrical connections in road vehicles, specifically addressing communication between towing and towed units. It relies on a CAN-based vehicle bus framework to define the data exchange used in tractor–trailer configurations. Developed by the International Organization for Standardization, the standard enables a tractor to communicate with one or more trailers, facilitating coordinated control and monitoring across the towing system.

Neuromuscular fatigue can constrain extremely powerful contractions in untrained individuals. In novices, the nerve’s ability to sustain high-frequency signaling serves as the primary limiter of force production, and after extended maximum contractions the discharge frequency declines, causing the generated force to diminish. There is typically no pain; the muscle may become unresponsive, gradually ceasing to move and often appearing to lengthen. When muscles and tendons do not experience sufficient stress, little or no delayed onset muscle soreness may occur. Strength training aims to enhance the nerve’s capacity to sustain high-frequency signals, enabling greater maximal force. Neural adaptations can yield several weeks of rapid strength gains, which plateau once neural drive approaches its maximum. Beyond this neural limit, further strength increases arise from myofibrillar or sarcoplasmic hypertrophy, with metabolic fatigue becoming the limiting factor.

Perceived weakness is described as non-neuromuscular in origin. It occurs when more effort than normal is required to exert a given amount of force, even though the actual muscle strength remains normal. To illustrate the concept, an example is provided, showing that an individual can feel or appear weaker despite preserved muscular capability.

Jonas Sibley was born in Sutton in the Province of Massachusetts Bay, where he completed his preparatory studies. He married Lydia Rice, a native of Sutton. Sibley held several local offices, including selectman, town moderator, and town treasurer. At the state level, he served as a member of the Massachusetts House of Representatives and the Massachusetts State Senate, and he was a delegate to the Massachusetts Constitutional Convention of 1820–1821.

Jonas Sibley was elected to the United States House of Representatives as an Adams-Clay Republican, serving in the Eighteenth Congress from March 4, 1823, to March 3, 1825. He was unsuccessful in his bid for reelection. After his congressional service, he took up farming. He died in Sutton on February 5, 1834, and was interred in Center Cemetery.

The article on MHealth surveys the use of mobile technologies in health care and public health, highlighting how this field has emerged alongside rapid advances in digital tools. It notes that mobile technologies have recently and swiftly become prevalent in low- and middle-income countries, reshaping the delivery and access to health services. In mHealth, the reference is usually to mobile phone technology as the principal platform for applications and solutions. The discussion also addresses the introduction of other technologies into these nations to support health care, illustrating an expanding ecosystem of digital tools aimed at improving health outcomes and health system performance.

MHealthHUB was launched as a virtual forum designed to bring together technologists, researchers, and clinicians to connect, learn, share, and pursue innovation in mHealth tools with the aim of transforming healthcare. The initiative seeks to create an innovation ecosystem that supports collaborative team science, which is viewed as essential to advances in both mHealth and data science innovations. It has been described as a collaboratory—a shared gathering place for the mHealth research community—where participants can convene to exchange ideas, foster interdisciplinary collaboration, and accelerate progress.

In 1987, astronomer R. Brent Tully, affiliated with the University of Hawaii's Institute of Astronomy, identified the Pisces–Cetus Supercluster Complex as a major large-scale structure of galaxies. The complex is described as extending roughly one billion light-years in length and about 150 million light-years across. Tully contended that the Local Supercluster is embedded within this extensive complex.

In cosmology, a cosmic event horizon defines a radius around Earth that changes as the universe evolves. At present, the distance to this horizon is roughly 16 billion light-years. Consequently, any event occurring within about that distance could, in principle, emit a signal that will eventually reach Earth, whereas signals from sources lying beyond this boundary would never be observable on Earth. Because the horizon distance is time-dependent, it reflects the ongoing expansion and dynamic history of the cosmos rather than remaining fixed.

In 1966, Igor Stravinsky praised Charles Ives for having explored a wide range of modern techniques well before most composers. He credited Ives with experiments in polytonality, atonality, tone clusters, and perspectivistic effects, as well as with incorporating chance operations, statistical approaches to composition, and permutation. Stravinsky also noted ideas such as add-a-part procedures, the use of practical jokes in music, and improvisatory practices as part of Ives’s innovative toolkit. He argued that Ives had pursued these innovations roughly fifty years earlier, portraying him as quietly ahead of his time and effectively consuming the contemporary musical landscape before the rest of the field.

While at Yale University, Charles Ives was a prominent figure on campus, belonging to HeBoule, Delta Kappa Epsilon (Phi chapter), and Wolf's Head Society, and serving as chairman of the Ivy Committee. He also played on Yale's varsity American football team, and coach Michael C. Murphy later remarked that Ives spent so much time with music that he might have achieved championship potential in sprinting had he devoted himself to athletics. The influence of collegiate life and sports on his work is evident in pieces such as Calcium Light Night and Yale-Princeton Football Game, which reflect the integration of his experiences with composition. Ives wrote Symphony No. 1 as his senior thesis under the supervision of Horatio Parker. He continued to work as a church organist until May 1902.

Paul John Kvale died on June 14, 1960, in Minneapolis, Minnesota. He was buried in the Protestant Cemetery in Swift County, Minnesota. The name is pronounced “qually,” rhyming with “golly,” as stated to The Literary Digest.

Paul John Kvale was born in Orfordville, Wisconsin, the son of Ole J. Kvale. He attended the Orfordville school and pursued higher education at the University of Illinois. In 1917, he moved with his parents to Benson, Minnesota, and that year graduated from Luther College in Decorah, Iowa. Kvale served in the United States Army during World War I as a sergeant in the machine gun corps, with his service lasting from September 7, 1917, to August 4, 1919.

Tecsun Co., Ltd. is a Chinese radio manufacturer founded in 1994 and headquartered in Dongguan, Guangdong. In Chinese, the company is known as 德生, with Jyutping dak1 saang1 and pinyin Déshēng. The firm designs and manufactures a broad range of radios, from simple handheld AM/FM receivers to digital models that support shortwave, longwave, airband, and single-sideband (SSB) operation. A portion of its products is rebranded and sold by Etón Corporation.

Some observers have drawn a parallel between the 1992 United States presidential election and the 1945 United Kingdom general election, invoking Winston Churchill as an illustrative figure. The comparison frames Churchill as a wartime leader who was highly regarded for national security yet not deemed effective in peacetime governance, and it is used to suggest a similar dynamic for President George H. W. Bush. The analogy also recalls that Churchill was voted out of office after the conclusion of hostilities, implying a comparable outcome in a postwar political environment.

Bill Clinton secured the Democratic nomination in the spring of 1992. In early polls following the nomination, Ross Perot led, with George H. W. Bush in second and Clinton third, and initial two-way trial heats in early 1992 showed Bush ahead of Clinton. The economic downturn and declining approval ratings for Bush helped mobilize Democrats to rally behind Clinton. On July 9, 1992, Clinton announced Al Gore as his running mate. Perot withdrew from the race before Clinton's acceptance speech, contending that staying in could allow the House to determine the outcome. Clinton's acceptance speech on July 16, 1992 outlined a commitment to a new social compact and to bridging the economic divide. The Clinton campaign subsequently enjoyed the largest convention bounce in history, lifting support from about 25 percent to roughly 55 percent, while Bush stood around 31 percent.

The first XF-104 (Lockheed 083-1001, serial 53-7786) was secretly ferried to Edwards Air Force Base during the night of 24–25 February. Lockheed test pilot Tony LeVier was designated to carry out the initial test program. On 28 February 1954, the aircraft executed a planned five‑foot hop during a high‑speed taxi run. The first official flight occurred on 4 March 1954; during that flight, the landing gear failed to retract, and LeVier landed after a low‑speed flight of roughly 20 minutes. Investigations identified low hydraulic system pressure as the underlying cause of the gear issue. Adverse weather kept the XF‑104 on the ground until 26 March 1954, when subsequent flights demonstrated that the landing gear retraction function operated normally.

Development of Lockheed's XF-104 Starfighter proceeded rapidly in the early 1950s. A wooden mock-up had been completed and was ready for inspection at the end of April, and work began on two prototype airframes in late May. With the J79 engine not yet ready, the prototypes were designed to accept the Wright J65 turbojet, a licensed version of the Armstrong Siddeley Sapphire. The first XF-104 prototype, serial 53-7786 and designated Buzz FG-786, began assembly at Lockheed's Burbank plant in the summer of 1953. The aircraft was powered by a Buick-built Wright J65-B-3 turbojet without afterburner. By early 1954 the first example was completed and made its first flight in March. The interval from contract award to first flight was about one year, unusually fast for the era, while construction of the second prototype (serial 53-7787) proceeded at a slower pace.

Robert Charbel Farah Maksoud (born 20 January 1987) is a Colombian former professional tennis player who specialized in doubles, attaining the world No. 1 ranking in that discipline. In singles, he achieved a career-high ATP ranking of No. 163 in June 2011.

Robert Farah attended the University of Southern California from 2006 to 2010, where he helped USC secure two NCAA Division I team championships as a Trojan. In his senior year, 2010, he finished as the top-ranked NCAA Division I singles player in the United States and was also No. 2 in NCAA Division I doubles. He captured the 2008 NCAA Men's Doubles Championship alongside Kaes Van't Hof. During his time at USC, he occasionally partnered in doubles with Steve Johnson, who would later become a prominent ATP Tour professional.

The Nationalist Party (Iceland) was a small nationalist political organization in Iceland whose membership never exceeded about 450 individuals. The group began to decline following arrests of several of its members, and its marching squads were last observed in 1938. In 1939 it issued Aims of the Party of Nationalists as its final major publication; thereafter only sporadic issues of the periodical Island appeared. During the winter of 1939–40 the party organized a Reykjavík debating club, though it had little impact, and thereafter the organization largely met in local cells. After the 1940 invasion of Iceland, the group was largely suppressed by the occupying Allied forces. The party was formally disbanded in 1944 as the defeat of Germany drew near.
The Party of Nationalists (Icelandic: Flokkur Þjóðernissinna) was a minor political party in Iceland that promoted a limited form of fascism and existed in the period before and during World War II.

In the 2022–23 Indian Super League season, the playoff field consisted of six clubs, an expansion from four in the previous edition. The top two teams earned direct progression to the semifinals, while the clubs finishing third through sixth contested single-leg knockout matches to determine the remaining two semifinalists. The quarterfinal pairings were 3rd against 6th and 4th against 5th, with the higher-ranked teams hosting the ties. The winners of the quarterfinals then joined the top two in the semifinals to contest the final four.

During the 2022–23 Indian Super League season, Mumbai City FC emerged as champions and earned their second League Winners' Shield for finishing atop the regular-season table. Mohun Bagan SG captured their inaugural ISL Cup title, defeating Bengaluru FC in the final.

Within the Japanese administrative framework, districts persist as subdivisions of prefectures, and following mergers or reconfigurations of provinces, certain districts may be shared by more than one prefecture. A notable example is Adachi District of the historic Musashi Province, which today is divided between Adachi Ward in Tokyo and Kita-Adachi District in Saitama Prefecture. Many former provincial districts have been dissolved as their chief towns were absorbed into larger cities or towns. For details on the mergers and abolition of districts, see the individual prefecture pages.

Historically, the names used for Japan’s provinces designated distinct subregions within what are now contemporary prefectures, while also signaling the cultural and geographical characteristics unique to each area. In many instances, these toponyms are combined with directional elements to denote a broader regional sense, such as the designation Hoku-Setsu (北摂), which refers to the northern part of the former Settsu region. Through these naming conventions, provincial identities encapsulated local traditions, landscapes, and spatial relations, linking historical divisions to the modern understanding of regional geography.

The Triple Crown of Surfing was founded by Fred Hemmings, the 1968 World Champion, and Randy Rarick. Rarick served as the producer of the Triple Crown events. In 1998, Vans assumed ownership of the series.

The Triple Crown of Surfing comprises three major events—Haleiwa, Sunset Beach, and Pipeline—held on Oahu's North Shore, forming the final trio of premier competitions in the professional surfing season. The Pipeline Masters traditionally served as the concluding event of the World Surf League Championship Tour through 2019. In December 2020, the Pipeline Masters was redefined as the opening event of the newly instituted 2020–21 wraparound season.

Fiberglass production began with A-glass (alkali-lime or soda-lime glass), which was crushed and remelted as cullet to form the first fiberglass glass. In contrast, pure silica fused quartz fiber requires extremely high working temperatures, prompting the use of fluxing agents to lower the melting point and reduce processing temperatures. The most widely used fiber today is E-glass, an alkali-free formulation developed for continuous filament production; it now dominates global fiberglass manufacture and is the largest consumer of boron minerals, but it is susceptible to chloride ion attack and is poorly suited for marine environments. S-glass, designated for high tensile strength, plays a key role in building and aircraft composites, and in Europe this material is referred to as R-glass (R for reinforcement). C-glass is distinguished by chemical resistance, while T-glass, the North American variant of C-glass, serves as a thermal insulator; together they are common in insulation-grade blown fiberglass.

In the evaluation of glass fiber strength, measurements are typically taken on virgin, pristine fibers immediately after manufacture. The freshest and thinnest fibers often show the greatest strength, with the reduced diameter associated with higher ductility. Surface scratches erode tenacity, underscoring the importance of handling and surface integrity. Glass fibers possess an amorphous internal structure, which yields isotropic mechanical properties that are effectively uniform along the fiber's length and across its cross-section. Environmental humidity also exerts a notable influence on tensile strength, as moisture adsorption can propagate microscopic cracks and aggravate surface defects, thereby lowering tenacity.

Freshwater systems such as lakes, reservoirs, and floodplains store sizable stocks of organic carbon and sediments. In the water column, these systems are typically net heterotrophic, meaning respiration surpasses primary production and driving a net release of CO2 to the atmosphere; this flux is roughly one-tenth the magnitude of that observed in river networks. The sediments of these environments are often anoxic, supporting substantial methane production.

The carbon cycle describes the exchanges of carbon among different reservoirs, driven by chemical, physical, geological, and biological processes. Among these reservoirs, the ocean contains the largest active pool of carbon near the Earth's surface, making it a central component in short-term carbon exchange and climate dynamics.

Poolbeg peninsula in Dublin hosts several landmarks, including the Great South Wall, Poolbeg Lighthouse, and Irishtown Nature Park. It also comprises the southern portion of Dublin Port and contains an energy-from-waste facility. The peninsula is the site of a power station that formerly served as Dublin’s main electricity-generating plant, notable for its two tall chimneys, which stand among the city’s tallest structures.

Poolbeg derives its name from Poole Begge, a term that originally described a tidal pool in Dublin Harbour encircled by sandbars. In 1767, Poolbeg Lighthouse was erected on this tidal pool, marking the location as a coastal beacon. The lighthouse was subsequently connected to the mainland by the Great South Wall, which was completed in 1795.

During the late Ottoman period, life expectancy stood at about 49 years, a figure that contrasts with Serbia’s life expectancy in the early 19th century, which was in the mid-20s. Epidemic diseases and famines caused substantial disruption and marked demographic shifts across the empire. In 1785, plague in Egypt is estimated to have killed roughly one-sixth of the population. Epidemics in Aleppo contributed to a population decline of about 20 percent during the 18th century. Egypt experienced six famines between 1687 and 1731, and the last famine to affect Anatolia occurred roughly four decades after 1731, around 1771. The plague epidemic that struck the Ottoman realm from 1812 to 1819 left at least 300,000 people dead.

The Ottoman legal system fused Sharia, the religious law, with a secular dynastic code known as kanun, allowing religious and civil-law traditions to operate in parallel rather than in strict opposition. Sharia governed many subjects alongside the imperial kanun, and both frameworks coexisted within a broader apparatus of local jurisprudence and legal administration that sought to balance centralized authority with local governance. Central power revolved around the management of land rights, a focus that enabled autonomous millets to address the needs of their communities within imperial policy. The jurisdictional structure was designed to accommodate a culturally and religiously diverse population, and adjudication was organized along three parallel tracks: Muslim courts; non-Muslim communal courts overseen by appointed leaders from Jewish and Christian communities; and a distinct court of trade. Across these layers, the system was regulated by an administrative kanun that drew upon Turkic Yassa and Töre from pre-Islamic times, providing a unifying legal framework for the empire.

In the context of the digital encoding of APL symbols, later IBM terminals introduced an alternative keyboard arrangement, with the IBM 3270 display stations being especially notable for this development. This rearranged layout formed the basis for some contemporary APL keyboard configurations that are in use today.

Code page 909 is an alternative encoding for the APL character set, offering a different mapping from code page 907. It omits the underlined APL characters that are present in 907, resulting in a distinct repertoire. In the 0xB0–0xDF range, the assignment of APL symbols differs from 907, producing a separate coding scheme for those characters. Additionally, code page 909 replaces some of the C0 replacement graphics inherited from code page 437 with alternative encodings for certain APL symbols.

Scholars, notably Christophe Jaffrelot, identify stigmatisation and emulation as central themes in RSS ideology, a pairing that is observed alongside currents within the Arya Samaj and the Hindu Mahasabha. Within this framework, Muslims, Christians, and the British are depicted as foreign elements inserted into the Hindu nation, whose presence is said to exploit internal Hindu disunity and a perceived lack of valor to subdue Hindus. The proposed response is to imitate the characteristics attributed to these perceived threats—such as a disciplined, quasi-military organization, strengthened unity, and a robust nationalist spirit. This emulation is combined with selective borrowing from Hindu past traditions, yielding a synthesis that is presented as uniquely Indian and Hindu.

Critics have described the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh as promoting an assimilationist form of Hindu nationalist ideology in Hindustan, wherein non-Hindu residents are urged to adopt Hindu culture and languages, to learn, respect, and revere the Hindu religion, and to entertain only ideas that glorify Hindu race and culture. They argue that such expectations would effectively render adherents no longer foreigners if followed; alternatively, those who remain unassimilated would be perceived as subordinate to the Hindu nation, renouncing claims, privileges, and even citizenship rights.

On 13 September 2012, the World Meteorological Organization announced that the World Archive of Weather and Climate Extremes, maintained by the WMO Commission on Climatology, had determined the 56.7 °C reading from Death Valley to be invalid. Despite this determination, the world record for the hottest temperature is 56.7 °C (134.1 °F), a measurement recorded on 10 July 1913 at Greenland Ranch, Death Valley, California, United States.

The weather station at Al 'Aziziyah was originally located in the town of ʽAziziya. In 1919 it was moved to a hilltop fort, where it was installed on a black tarmac surface. The dark pavement absorbed more solar radiation, warming the surrounding air and producing spuriously high temperature readings. As a result, measurements from 1919 to 1928 were exceptionally hot, a pattern now attributed to the heat-absorbing surface rather than genuine regional climate conditions.

The defending champions in the doubles at the 2005 BNP Paribas Masters were Jonas Björkman and Todd Woodbridge, but they did not participate together that year. Björkman formed a new pairing with Max Mirnyi, yet they were eliminated in the first round. Todd Woodbridge, meanwhile, had retired from professional tennis earlier in the year, preventing any attempt to defend the title.

Within the study of Scottish Gaelic phonology and orthography, the absence of preaspiration coincides with the full voicing of unaspirated stops. Area 6 dialects largely retain the Middle Irish stops, a pattern also observed in Manx and in Irish.

Scottish Gaelic displays dialectal variation in its diphthong inventory, with the total number of diphthongs generally reported as nine or ten. The set most often cited by researchers comprises the following phonemes: /ei, ɤi, ai, ui, iə, uə, ɛu, ɔu, au, ia.

Backward compatibility in video gaming refers to the ability of a newer console to run games from earlier generations, a capacity often compared to emulation in effect. It is typically achieved through a combination of dedicated hardware and built-in software within the platform that enables the legacy titles to run on contemporary hardware with minimal or no modification. A prominent example is the PlayStation 2, which popularized the concept by allowing PlayStation-era discs to be used in the new system to play their games. The Nintendo Wii offered a parallel approach by supporting GameCube software directly, enabling players to access a broad portion of the GameCube library on the Wii hardware.

By 2021 there was no universally accepted industry definition of the term "video game," a point raised in the context of Epic Games v. Apple concerning games offered on Apple's iOS App Store. The case cited Fortnite Creative and Roblox as examples of expansive metaverses composed of interactive experiences, which raised questions about whether such experiences should be treated as "games" for App Store fees. Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers acknowledged the absence of a standard industry definition in this area. A key criterion articulated in the ruling was that video games involve some interactivity or engagement between the player and the medium. In addition, video games are generally graphically rendered or animated, unlike passive media such as film, music, or television. The judge also observed that what counts as a video game appears to be highly eclectic and diverse.

Jump On It! received mixed critical reception, with AllMusic awarding the release three out of five stars and critic Keith Farley highlighting its fun, educational qualities for children while suggesting that its comparatively simple rhymes may deter hip-hop fans. In a separate review, BET Weekend gave it three and a half out of five stars, noting that the album has the potential to teach young listeners.

Jump On It!, released in 1999, is a studio album by The Sugarhill Gang that marks a venture into children's music and is recognized as the first hip hop album created specifically for a young audience by rap artists. It stands as the sole Sugarhill Gang record produced after the group’s reunion in the 1990s, bringing together original members Big Bank Hank, Master Gee, and Wonder Mike. The project was developed under the guidance of Rhino Records executive Richard Foos and was conceived as part of a broader multimedia plan designed to pair the album with a line of children’s clothing, educational videos, and television programming. Promotion featured a jump rope contest for children conducted in collaboration with the Boys & Girls Clubs of America, which received a portion of the album’s sales proceeds.

Low Prussian was a regional dialect of East Prussia that suffered a rapid decline after World War II when almost all its speakers were evacuated or expelled from the region. The dispersal of expellees across Western Germany contributed to the dialect’s erosion as intergenerational transmission ceased and the language gradually became moribund. Some speakers who had not been displaced subsequently joined later repatriation movements, relocating from Poland to Western Germany in the 1970s and 1980s and from Russia in the 1990s as Spätaussiedler, further complicating efforts to maintain the variety. In the present day, the language is nearly extinct, with use confined mainly to within-family contexts and expellee gatherings, often spoken in nostalgic registers. In Poland, postwar repression further reduced active use among the small number of non-displaced speakers. Across both Poland and Germany, High Prussian varieties were not transmitted to the next generation, leaving only a handful of elderly speakers. Since 1991 the German minority in Poland has been officially recognized and predominantly uses Standard German.

Low Prussian is a dialect of Low German. It features a small set of distinctive lexical items, including doa, which corresponds to dor meaning there; joa, which corresponds to jo meaning yes; goah, which corresponds to goh meaning go; and noa, which corresponds to nober meaning neighbor. These words employ the digraph 'oa' rather than the usual single-letter spellings 'o' or 'a' found in related varieties.

Westwood/VA Hospital station is a planned stop on the D Line Extension, located in Section 3 and currently under construction. Construction contracts were awarded in 2019. The station is slated to open in fall 2027, in conjunction with the Westwood/UCLA station. In the Sepulveda Transit Corridor study, one of the five corridor alternatives proposes connecting to the D Line at this location.

Westwood/VA Hospital station is an underground rail facility currently under construction on the D Line of the Los Angeles Metro Rail system. It is situated beneath the ground between Bonsall Avenue and the I-405 freeway, just south of Wilshire Boulevard. The primary entrance lies south of Wilshire Boulevard near Bonsall Avenue and provides access to the West Los Angeles VA Medical Center, while a secondary entrance is located to the north of Wilshire Boulevard. Upon completion, the station will directly serve the West Los Angeles VA Medical Center.

Transport in Laos maintains an ocean-going merchant marine that, as of 2004, consisted of a single cargo ship with a gross tonnage of 2,370 GT. By 2023, the Lao merchant marine had not expanded and continued to comprise only one vessel.

Transport in Laos is dominated by river routes, with the Mekong and the Nam Ou serving as the primary natural waterways capable of accommodating large-draft vessels. Seasonal hydrological changes significantly affect navigation, as low-water conditions from December through May reduce the draft that may be used on many routes. By contrast, residents of lowland villages along smaller rivers have traditionally relied on pirogues for fishing, local trade, and short-distance river travel.

Lustschloss, the German designation for a "pleasure palace" (French: maison de plaisance), refers to a country house or palace built for the private enjoyment of its owner. Such estates are typically inhabited only seasonally, serving as retreats from court ceremonies and state duties. In France, the Château de Madrid in the Bois de Boulogne is cited as an early example. Louis XIV maintained a pattern of annual travel from Versailles to the Marly estate, while he increasingly favored the Grand Trianon, with a Petit Trianon added in the following century.

Lustschloss and Jagdschloss are often used interchangeably to describe non-formal residences associated with rulers, rather than formal state palaces. The term Jagdschloss, in particular, denotes a hunting retreat that was typically used to accommodate a sovereign and his hunting party during excursions.

During the 2012 cycle, Anderson won a plurality of delegates in the Peace and Freedom Party's non-binding preference primary, but he did not secure enough votes to place his Justice Party on the ballot. He also failed to win seats on the PFP's Central Committee and withdrew from the race one week before the convention. Subsequently, the Peace and Freedom Party endorsed Roseanne Barr, the PSL's preferred candidate.

The Peace and Freedom Party (PFP) initiated a petition campaign in the aftermath of the Century City anti-Vietnam War march on June 23, 1967. Its founders criticized the Democratic Party for its approach to the Vietnam War and contended that Democrats failed to provide adequate support for the civil rights movement.

The Federal Reserve System, the central banking system of the United States, operates within the framework of fractional-reserve banking, whereby banks are required to hold only a fraction of their deposit liabilities as reserves, comprising currency in circulation and deposits at other institutions. Banks typically deploy most of the funds deposited by customers into loans and other investments, retaining reserves to satisfy potential withdrawal demands. Bank runs occur when a large number of depositors withdraw their funds, threatening a bank’s operations and contributing to broader social and economic instability. The Federal Reserve was established to prevent or minimize such runs and to function as a lender of last resort during periods of financial stress. Some economists, following Milton Friedman, contend that during the 1929 bank panics the Fed failed to lend to smaller banks, a decision they argue helped precipitate the severity of the Great Depression.

During the American Revolutionary War, the initial attempt at a national currency involved the issuance of paper notes by the Continental Congress and the states, known as Continentals, which were backed solely by anticipated future tax revenues and used to finance the war effort. However, overissuance coupled with British counterfeiting led to rapid depreciation of the Continentals, undermining confidence in the currency. This problematic experience influenced early constitutional thinking, as the draft of the U.S. Constitution on August 16, 1787 removed the power to issue Bills of Credit and barred states from issuing such notes; further provisions added on August 28 restricted states to gold or silver coin as legal tender. Taken together, these episodes underscored the challenges of decentralized monetary issuance and helped shape the later move toward a centralized monetary authority, a development that would culminate in the federal framework that includes the Federal Reserve.

According to Arnold of Lübeck's Chronica Slavorum, in 1172, during Henry the Lion's pilgrimage to Jerusalem, the meeting near Tarsus saw Kilij Arslan II greet the German duke with an embrace and a kiss, claiming that they were blood relatives. He further articulated a genealogical narrative tracing his own line to a German noblewoman who married a Russian king, with their granddaughter arriving in Kilij Arslan's land, thereby making him a descendant of that union. The episode is often noted as illustrating a purported cross-cultural noble kinship spanning the German, Russian, and Turkish realms.

In 1173 Kilij Arslan II formed an alliance with Nur ad-Din against Mosul and maintained a peace with the Byzantine Empire, a treaty that endured until 1175. He refused to surrender to Manuel I Komnenos the lands won from the Danishmends, even as both powers prepared for renewed hostilities. Although he sought to negotiate, Manuel invaded the sultanate in 1176 with the aim of capturing Iconium. Kilij Arslan then defeated Emperor Manuel I Komnenos's forces at the Battle of Myriokephalon, forcing the emperor to accept a fragile peace.

Sulfur oxides, collectively denoted as SOx, are chemical compounds that consist of sulfur bonded to oxygen. The most common members of this group are sulfur dioxide (SO2) and sulfur trioxide (SO3). These oxides form naturally through volcanic activity, contributing to their presence in the atmosphere even without human activity. Human activities, notably the combustion of fossil fuels and certain industrial processes, also release sulfur oxides into the atmosphere.

Organizational architecture involves delineating the appropriate boundaries between a system and its subsystems, a central task in determining how elements interact. When goals are precisely defined and distinct, boundary setting becomes more straightforward and easier to manage. Several factors influence where these boundaries are drawn, including the impact of the surrounding environment, the availability of people and machines, scheduling requirements for both design and ongoing operation, the cost differences among alternative configurations, and the biases or perspectives held by designers. Considering these factors collectively helps guide decisions about the proper demarcation between the system and its subsystems.

Organizational architecture refers to the arrangement of structural elements by which an organization organizes and coordinates its activities. The fundamental options for how work is strategically grouped each confer their own set of benefits and drawbacks, making trade-offs context-dependent. Relying on broad, generic advantages and disadvantages is not enough to identify the most effective form of grouping, since suitability varies with circumstances. Therefore, assessment of organizational structure should be conducted in the context of a defined business strategy, taking into account the organization's goals, market conditions, and resource capabilities to determine the architecture best aligned with strategic aims.

Within Estonia's protected areas, a limited management zone denotes a portion of land or water designated for use under regulated conditions. Economic activities may be carried out in this zone, provided that they adhere to the restrictions laid out in the Act.

Protected areas in Estonia are designated as nature conservation areas, a category of protected site established to safeguard the country’s natural environments and biodiversity. These areas are prescribed for the preservation and protection of ecosystems, the restoration of degraded habitats, the advancement of scientific research, and the introduction and reestablishment of natural environments and species where appropriate.

Blogging refers to the practice of creating and sharing content on the internet, typically involving longer posts published on a regular basis and distributed through social media channels. It can occur directly on social platforms such as Facebook or Instagram, where users publish material for their audiences. By 2022, the number of publicly accessible blogs was estimated at over 600 million, a figure situated within a broader landscape that includes more than 1.9 billion websites.

Blogs cover a wide range of topics, with many focusing on specific subjects such as politics, journalism, health, and travel (travelogs); other popular niches include gardening, home life, Book Blogs, fashion, beauty, lifestyle, parties, weddings, photography, projects, psychology, sociology, education, niche subjects, classical music, quizzing, legal matters (blawgs), and dreamlogs. How-to or tutorial blogs have become increasingly popular as a format that provides actionable guidance. Two commonly encountered genre blogs are art blogs and music blogs. A home-and-family discussions blog is often described as a mom blog. Blogs created solely for spamming are known as splogs and are not considered legitimate.
Paul Signac died in Paris on 15 August 1935 from sepsis, aged 71. His body was cremated, and three days later, on 18 August 1935, his remains were interred at Père Lachaise Cemetery.

Paul Signac served as president of the Société des Artistes Indépendants from 1908 until his death, guiding the organization through a period of intense artistic experimentation in early 20th-century Paris. In this role, he actively championed younger artists by organizing exhibitions that showcased the controversial works of the Fauves and the Cubists, thereby extending the reach of avant-garde movements. He was also notable for his early support of Henri Matisse, being the first patron to purchase a painting by the artist.

Chalk (military) refers to a convoy organization technique in which a larger convoy is temporarily divided into smaller groups when formal convoy clearance cannot be obtained. Each subgroup, typically comprising four or fewer trucks, is designated with a sequential chalk label—chalk one, chalk two, chalk three, and so on—to indicate its position within the overall movement.
