The practice is intended to circumvent the need for official convoy clearance while preserving the perceived advantages of traveling as a larger, coordinated unit.

Chalk (military) refers to a marking practice in which chalk was used to designate units or aircraft during operations. The method originated in World War II, most notably during Operation Overlord, the Allied invasion of Europe, where chalk marks were applied to airborne troops to indicate the associated flight numbers. The practice persisted into the Vietnam War era, with chalk numerals appearing on the sides of helicopters involved in operations to identify participating aircraft or unit components. Overall, these markings served primarily to identify units and aircraft taking part in a given operation, aiding coordination and command in high-tempo environments.

Zuoying–Jiucheng railway station, located in Kaohsiung, Taiwan, is a station on the Taiwan Railways Administration (TRA) network. Its Chinese name is 左營·舊城, romanized as Zuǒyíng–Jìuchéng. The station is served by TRA and accommodates local trains.

Zuoying–Jiucheng railway station began operations on 29 November 1900. The station underwent its most recent reconstruction in 2018, a renovation that replaced the temporary facilities that had been opened in 2013.

The Faroese chain dance is a traditional group dance from the Faroe Islands performed in conjunction with folk ballads. Dancers form two parallel rows with a spacing of about two to four feet between them, placing men on one side and women on the other, with a ribbon held between each couple. During the stanzas, participants remain still and stamp the floor in rhythm; when the refrain begins, they raise their ribbons. At the end of the row, dancers bend forward in pairs and pass beneath the raised ribbons, forming a tunnel. They then exit the tunnel, turn around, and lift their ribbons over the following couples. When the refrain ends, they lower their ribbons and continue this sequence until the ballad concludes. The dance is lively and energetic, though physically tiring.

The Faroese chain dance begins after the midnight singing on 29 July. People also gather in Sjónleikarhúsið in Tórshavn during the evenings around Ólavsøka to dance together. The dance has no instrumental accompaniment; the melody is provided entirely by Kvæði, traditional folk songs. Kvæði are sung texts of varying length, performed in either Faroese or Danish.
On August 17, 2017, Paramount Players acquired its first project, a film adaptation of the book Vacation Guide to the Solar System, authored by Jonathan Goldstein and John Francis Daley.

Paramount Players, a division within Paramount Pictures, experienced a series of leadership changes within the studio’s Motion Picture Group during 2020. Emma Watts succeeded Wyck Godfrey as president on June 30, 2020, and she formally began the role on July 20, 2020, after which Godfrey returned to producing. In October 2020, Watts appointed Jeremy Kramer to serve as president of the group. These leadership reshuffles reflected the studio’s ongoing reorganization of its development and production leadership during that period.

Roosevelt Independent School District covers the unincorporated communities of Acuff and Roosevelt, and extends into the northern portions of the incorporated municipalities of Buffalo Springs and Ransom Canyon. A small portion of Lubbock also lies within the district's boundaries.

Roosevelt Independent School District is a public school district located about 8.5 miles east of Lubbock, Texas, in the United States. It is described as small and is noted for its innovative approaches to education.

OpenAlex is an open bibliographic knowledge base. As of March 2024, it contained metadata for about 209 million works, including journal articles and books, along with metadata for roughly 13 million authors whose identities are not uniquely disambiguated, metadata for around 124,000 sites hosting works (such as journals and online repositories), and metadata for about 109,000 institutions. In addition, approximately 65,000 Wikidata concepts were linked to OpenAlex works through an automated multi-tag hierarchical classifier. In March 2024, OpenAlex announced a $7.5 million grant from Arcadia aimed at establishing it as a genuine open alternative to commercial solutions.

In 2024, France's Ministry of Research and Higher Education pledged to provide financial support for the OpenAlex project, signaling government backing for the initiative. The ministry regards OpenAlex as a crucial component of open science infrastructure, underscoring its importance to the nation's research ecosystem.

IEC 61851 is an international standard that governs the conductive charging of electric vehicles. As of 2017, some portions of the standard were still under development. It forms part of the IEC’s suite of standards pertaining to electric road vehicles and electric industrial trucks. The standard is developed and overseen by IEC Technical Committee 69 (TC69).

An August 2024 interview on the UPWAWR Podcast with Julie Weir, the former founder of Visible Noise, discussed the impact of Ian Watkins’s crimes on Lostprophets and the subsequent end of her record label. In the same discussion, she highlighted No Devotion’s 2015 Kerrang! Award for their debut album, describing the accolade as evidence that the public still valued the remaining band members as songwriters and musicians. Weir characterized the award as restoring what had been taken from them, calling it one of the most meaningful validations the music industry could provide.

The Kerrang! Awards are a British rock music awards ceremony with a varied broadcast history. The first ceremony to be televised occurred in 2001 on Channel 5 in the United Kingdom, while Channel 4 aired late-night recordings through 2004. The 2007 edition was carried on Hits, a channel that has since ceased operations, and the 2008 ceremony was shown on 4Music, which is owned by Channel 4. In its early years, MTV UK and MTV Europe featured footage of winners collecting their awards and conducting interviews. Since 2001, Kerrang! TV has served as the ceremony’s televised home. The 2018 ceremony did not air on traditional television. More recently, the event has been streamed live on YouTube, with highlights subsequently uploaded to Kerrang’s channel.

Chinatown, Sydney features bilingual signage for streets, lanes, and roads that present their names in both English and Chinese. The naming convention reflects different Chinese pronunciation traditions, with some street names rendered according to Cantonese pronunciation, such as Hay Street (禧街; Cantonese: Hēi Gāai, Mandarin: Xǐ Jiē), while others are based on Mandarin pronunciation, such as Liverpool Street (利物浦街; Mandarin: Lìwùpǔ Jiē, Cantonese: Léihmáhtpóu Gāai).

Chinatown, Sydney, is an urban district located in the southern portion of the city's central business district in New South Wales, Australia. It is represented in Chinese as 悉尼唐人街, with the Cantonese Yale reading Sīknèih Tòhngyàhn'gāai and the Mandarin pinyin Xīní Tángrénjiē. The district comprises the majority of the Haymarket suburb and lies between Central Station and Darling Harbour, within the City of Sydney local government area. It is the largest Chinatown in Australia.

Jo Durie is a British former professional tennis player who captured junior national titles on grass, hard court, and indoor surfaces in 1976 before turning professional the following year. Her Wimbledon debut occurred in 1977, where she faced Virginia Wade, who would later win the tournament. In 1980 she endured a major back injury that sidelined her for eight months, but she returned to competition in 1981. That year she advanced to the fourth round at both the Wimbledon Championships and the US Open and achieved her career-high singles ranking of No. 31.

Jo Durie is a British former professional tennis player who formed a doubles partnership with Jeremy Bates. The duo captured the Wimbledon mixed doubles title in 1987, becoming the first British doubles team to win that event in 51 years. They later won the Australian Open mixed doubles title in 1991, the first British doubles team to claim the Australian Open mixed doubles crown. As of 2013, both achievements remained British records in the discipline. Durie and Bates also reached three additional Wimbledon mixed doubles quarterfinals (1986, 1990, 1993) and advanced to the Australian Open mixed doubles quarterfinals in 1992 while defending their Melbourne title.

Grumman initiated a postwar study to identify prospective production types, resulting in the G-65 Tadpole designed by Hank Kurt’s team. The aircraft was a two- to three-seat shoulder-wing cantilever monoplane equipped with retractable tricycle gear. Its powerplant was a 125 hp Continental C125 mounted atop the rear fuselage and driving a pusher propeller. The Tadpole made its maiden flight on 7 December 1944. After World War II, manufacture was not pursued due to an overly optimistic outlook for private aviation, the availability of inexpensive military surplus aircraft, and the firm’s assessment that it could not compete in the amphibious aircraft sector. Although not fielded by Grumman, the concept was later developed by designer David Thurston into amphibious designs such as the Colonial Skimmer and Lake Buccaneer.

The Grumman G-65 Tadpole was an American prototype light amphibious aircraft designed and built by Grumman. Only a single example was constructed, and the type did not enter production. The concept was subsequently developed into a family of amphibious aircraft by designer David Thurston.

Kenneth S. Wherry was the third of five children born in Liberty, Nebraska, to David Emery Wherry and Jessie (née Comstock) Wherry. He received his early education in the public schools of Pawnee City and subsequently graduated from the University of Nebraska in 1914, where he was a member of the Beta Theta Pi fraternity. Wherry then studied business administration at Harvard Business School from 1915 to 1916. During World War I, he served in the U.S. Navy Flying Corps from 1917 to 1918.

Kenneth S. Wherry asserted that Adolf Hitler had provided Joseph Stalin with a list of secretly homosexual government officials who could be blackmailed into becoming Soviet spies. In the spring of 1950, he joined Senator Lister Hill in a congressional inquiry into homosexuality in government, focusing on the State Department. Wherry linked this issue to concerns about communist influence, arguing that the Communist movement would exploit such individuals as part of a fifth column in the United States.

Myrna Hansen negotiated a seven-year contract with Universal in August 1954, receiving an initial salary of $200 per week with the prospect of increases to as much as $900 per week. Because she was a minor at the time, she was required to purchase a weekly $25 U.S. savings bond.

Myrna Hansen's screen career included a sequence of notable 1950s roles. Following contract negotiations, she filmed The Purple Mask (1955), in which she portrayed Constance de Voulois, one of three female spies in a narrative set in France in the period after the French Revolution. In Cult of the Cobra (1955), she was cast as the fiancée of Jack Kelly's character. She later appeared as a showgirl in Party Girl (1958), a film featuring Robert Taylor and Cyd Charisse. Her final film appearances were in Goodbye Charlie (1964) and Black Caesar (1973).

Skydance Bridge is located in downtown Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, with its site selected under the Core to Shore initiative, which aims to connect the city's core to the Oklahoma River shoreline. In the surrounding area, an urban park was in early planning as part of the MAPS 3 project. The bridge itself links the park’s upper and lower portions, providing a direct connection between the park’s contrasting levels.

In June 2019, city officials approved a repair project for the Skydance Bridge, budgeting $840,000 for the work. The initiative sought to replace the aging wooden deck with a composite fiberglass deck. Construction was conducted from summer 2019 through summer 2020.

South Carolina experiences an average of about fifty thunderstorm days per year, reflecting the state's propensity for convective weather. This level is lower than that of some states farther south. The state is somewhat less vulnerable to tornadoes than Gulf Coast states, although it has nonetheless been struck by several notable tornado events. On average, South Carolina records around fourteen tornadoes annually. Hail is a common feature associated with many of the state’s thunderstorms, resulting from a temperature contrast between warm surface conditions and colder air aloft that supports hail formation.

South Carolina contains a number of prominent reservoirs, most of which are artificial lakes created by damming rivers. Together they span more than 683 square miles (1,770 square kilometers). All of the state’s major lakes are man-made, reflecting an extensive program of water resource management. The lakes are listed by size, typically with the largest by surface area presented first.

Greenwood Publishing Group, Inc. (GPG) was an educational and academic publisher serving audiences from middle school through university level. It operated as part of ABC-Clio. Beginning in 2021, ABC-Clio and its imprints, including Greenwood Publishing Group, became imprints of Bloomsbury Publishing, a British company. The Greenwood name was no longer used for new titles starting in 2023.

Greenwood Publishing Group (GPG) became part of Harcourt Education following Reed Elsevier’s acquisition of Harcourt. On July 12, 2001, Reed Elsevier completed the purchase of Harcourt, after which Harcourt became a wholly owned subsidiary of the company. As a result, Greenwood Publishing Group was integrated into Harcourt Education, the education-focused division within Harcourt under the Reed Elsevier umbrella.

Mysida, commonly referred to as mysids, constitute an order of small crustaceans with a global distribution in both shallow and deep marine waters. They occupy a range of habitats, being benthic or pelagic, and are also present in certain freshwater and brackish ecosystems where they contribute to local food webs. A substantial number of benthic species undertake daily vertical migrations, rising into upper layers of the water column. Mysids function as filter feeders and omnivores, feeding on algae, detritus, and zooplankton. Some species are cultured in laboratory settings for experimental work and serve as a nutritional resource for other cultured marine organisms. Because of their high sensitivity to water pollution, mysids are widely used as bioindicators to monitor aquatic environmental quality.

Mysid crustaceans are readily cultured on a large scale due to their broad adaptability and tolerance of a wide range of conditions, which supports efficient mass production. Although they exhibit relatively low fecundity, their short reproductive cycle enables rapid population growth. They can be raised in static or flow-through culture systems, with flow-through setups allowing higher stocking densities. In flow-through arrangements, juveniles are continuously separated from the adult brood stock to reduce mortality from cannibalism. The most common live feed is Artemia (brine shrimp) nauplii incubated for about 24 hours, with occasional enrichment using highly unsaturated fatty acids to enhance nutritional value.
The 1871 Minnesota gubernatorial election was held on November 7, 1871 to elect the state's governor. The results saw the incumbent, Horace Austin, reelected to a second term in office.

Bodie, California, developed as a thriving center for gold mining. Its urban amenities included a Wells Fargo Bank, four volunteer fire companies, a brass band, railroad access, a miners' and mechanics' union, several daily newspapers, and a jail. At its height, roughly 65 saloons lined Main Street, which extended for about a mile. The town also gained a reputation for violence, with murders, shootouts, barroom brawls, and stagecoach holdups occurring with regularity.

In 1876 the Standard Company identified a lucrative vein of gold-bearing ore, transforming Bodie from a modest mining camp into a bustling Wild West boomtown. Rich discoveries in the nearby Bodie Mine in 1878 attracted a larger influx of prospectors and settlers. By 1879 the town's population was estimated at roughly 7,000 to 10,000, with about 2,000 buildings clustered across the settlement. A popular legend maintained that Bodie was California’s second or third largest city in 1880, yet census records for that year do not support the assertion. From 1860 to 1941, Bodie’s mines produced gold and silver valued at approximately US$34 million in 1986 dollars (about US$85 million in 2021 dollars).

Solar time is characterized by a seasonal variation in the length of the solar day, which can differ from the mean solar day by as much as about 16 minutes. This variation arises from two primary factors: the eccentricity of Earth's orbit and the tilt of its axis relative to the orbital plane. The orbital eccentricity causes Earth to move faster near perihelion and slower near aphelion, altering the Sun’s apparent pace along the ecliptic. Additionally, the Sun follows an annual path that is inclined to the Earth’s equator, so the Sun’s daily motion projected onto the equator changes with its declination; the projection is smaller around the equinoxes and larger around the solstices. When the Sun is farthest from the equator, a given along-ecliptic shift translates into a larger equatorial shift, thereby shortening the observed solar day. Consequently, the apparent solar days are shorter in March and September than in June or December.

Solar time is a time scale based on the Sun’s apparent motion across the sky and therefore differs from standard clock time; the discrepancy between the two is described by the equation of time. The length of the apparent solar day relative to 24 hours changes over the year: in September it runs shorter than the mean solar day, while in December it is longer, with differences ranging from about 21 seconds behind to about 29 seconds ahead of 24 hours. This variation stems from two principal geometric factors: the eccentricity of Earth’s orbit and the obliquity of the ecliptic. The non-circular orbit causes the Earth–Sun distance to fluctuate, which affects the Sun’s apparent speed along its path. At the same time, the tilt of Earth’s axis relative to its orbital plane modifies the Sun’s diurnal path, contributing to changes in the length of solar days throughout the year.

Mule (coin) is named after the animal mule, the hybrid offspring of a horse and a donkey. In zoological terms, a mule results from crossing two distinct species, the horse and the donkey. The coin is designed with two sides intended for different coins, a feature that mirrors the mule’s dual parentage by reflecting its two progenitor species.

Mints occasionally employ proof dies in the production of coins intended for circulation. When a recognizable proof die is paired with a standard business die, the resulting coins are known as handsome mules. These specimens typically exhibit noticeably crisper details than ordinary circulation strikes, making them readily distinguishable from standard coins in everyday use.

Roger Federer defeated Mardy Fish in the final to claim the men's singles title at the 2010 Western & Southern Financial Group Masters. The match unfolded over three sets, with Fish taking the opening tiebreak 7–5, Federer leveling the match by winning the second set in a 7–6 (7–1) tiebreak, and Federer securing the championship with a 6–4 third set. As the defending champion, Federer successfully retained the title. The victory marked his fourth Cincinnati Masters crown, his 17th Masters title overall—tying Andre Agassi's record for Masters championships—and his 63rd career title, equaling Björn Borg's career total.

Hillside Farm was a facility of the Multnomah County Poor Farm situated west of Washington Park in Portland. The property spanned 160 acres (65 hectares) and ceased operations in 1922. After the land was sold to the City of Portland, the transaction facilitated the establishment of Hoyt Arboretum in 1930, on the former Hillside Farm site.

Washington Park is a public urban park in Portland, Oregon, United States. The park encompasses a variety of attractions and facilities, including a zoo, a forestry museum, and an arboretum, as well as a rose garden and a Japanese garden. It also houses an amphitheatre, memorials, an archery range, tennis courts, a soccer field, picnic areas, and playgrounds. Beyond its built amenities, the park preserves sizable tracts of wild forest and offers miles of trails, with public art distributed throughout the grounds.

On 1 April 2011, the General Register Office for Scotland merged with the National Archives of Scotland to form the National Records of Scotland, a consolidation that brought together the two bodies. The National Records of Scotland continues all of the functions that were formerly performed by the General Register Office for Scotland within its remit.

New Register House, which houses the registration functions of the former General Register Office for Scotland (GROS), is located near the east end of Princes Street in Edinburgh. It was designed by Robert Matheson, who served as Clerk of Works at the Office of Her Majesty's Works in Scotland. The GROS had previously occupied General Register House, and the New Register House sits on its present site near the Old Register House. The site was acquired in 1856, and the building was opened on 30 March 1861, though it was not completed until 1864. The total cost of construction was £40,000.

Reproducibility in research is commonly supported by a basic workflow consisting of data acquisition, data processing, and data analysis. Data acquisition entails collecting primary information directly from original sources, such as surveys, field observations, and experimental investigations, or drawing on existing datasets. During data processing, researchers clean and review the raw information, undertaking data entry, transformation, and filtering with software tools as needed. Data should be digitized and prepared in a structured form suitable for analysis. In the data analysis stage, software is used to interpret, model, and visualize the data to produce results, including figures, tables, and quantitative summaries. The use of software and automation across these stages helps to enhance the reproducibility of research methods by enabling others to repeat procedures and verify results.

An empirical study published in 2018 in PLOS ONE evaluated reproducibility practices among researchers in the field of public health statistics. The results showed that 14.4% of respondents had made their data or computer code available, or both, underscoring the limited openness of materials necessary to reproduce findings.

Corporate law generally holds that a company is liable for the acts and omissions of its officers and agents acting within the scope of their authority. This form of liability, often described as vicarious or imputational liability, extends to a wide array of torts, making corporations responsible for most civil wrongs arising in the course of business. By contrast, the law governing crimes committed by companies is more complex and shows substantial variation across jurisdictions, reflecting differing approaches to corporate culpability and enforcement.

Corporate governance analyzes how power and control over a corporation are distributed among its top management, the board of directors, the shareholders who elect them (at general meetings) and its employees, and other stakeholders including creditors, customers, the environment, and the surrounding community. A key internal distinction is between one-tier and two-tier governance systems: in one-tier arrangements, a single board holds both supervisory and managerial responsibilities; in two-tier arrangements, these functions are split between a supervisory board and a separate management board. One-tier systems are common in the United Kingdom, the United States, and most Commonwealth countries, whereas Germany employs a two-tier framework in which shareholders and employees elect the supervisory board, which then elects the management board. France allows the option to adopt a two-tier system, and the Societas Europaea, the EU-wide corporate form, likewise permits a two-tier governance structure.

Pterourus bjorkae is notable for its large size, with an average wingspan of about 8.5 cm, making it the largest subspecies within its complex. It is characterized by yellow coloration with dark patterns and orange spots. The caterpillar resembles a small snake, a form of mimicry that deters predators. Adults are commonly found in flower gardens.

Pterourus bjorkae is predominantly found in deciduous forests of eastern North America. Its presence contributes to biodiversity within these ecosystems and adds to the ecological complexity of the region.
Norsk-Tysk Tidsskrift, meaning Norwegian-German Journal, was a Norwegian periodical that appeared during the German occupation of Norway.

Norsk-Tysk Tidsskrift was a monthly journal published from 1942 by the Norwegian-German cultural society Norsk-Tysk Selskap. The periodical appeared regularly during the occupation era until 1945, when publication ended following Norway’s liberation, at which time the Norsk-Tysk Selskap was disbanded.

GOM Player is a media player that includes a suite of built-in video and audio codecs, enabling playback of many formats without the need to install external codecs. The software also provides a codec search feature that helps users locate and obtain any codecs that are missing, aiding in resolving playback problems.

GOM Player is a multimedia software application for Microsoft Windows, developed by GOM & Company. It has garnered over 100 million downloads and is widely regarded as the most popular media player in South Korea. The program includes features such as the ability to play certain broken or damaged media files and an integrated codec finder service that helps users locate and obtain missing codecs.

The 2008 Formula One World Championship saw Sébastien Bourdais enter the series with Scuderia Toro Rosso after securing his fourth consecutive Champ Car title in 2007, and he replaced Vitantonio Liuzzi at Toro Rosso as Liuzzi moved to Force India to assume the role of test driver.

Robert Kubica secured his first Formula One pole position at the Bahrain Grand Prix, while Lewis Hamilton managed to qualify third despite a qualifying crash. Felipe Massa won Bahrain with Kimi Räikkönen finishing second, and Kubica also reached the Bahrain podium as Hamilton finished 13th. Hamilton then scored points in Barcelona, where Räikkönen won for Ferrari and Massa finished second, delivering Ferrari its third consecutive victory of the season and another 1–2 finish.

Open-air museums are located along portions of the former inner German border, where the memory of the division is preserved for visitors. Notable examples are found in Berlin and Mödlareuth. Mödlareuth is a village that has been divided for several hundred years. The memory of the division is kept alive in many places along the border.

Construction of the Berlin Wall began in 1961 with the aim of stemming the exodus of East German workers into West Berlin. West Berlin was an exclave of the Federal Republic of Germany, surrounded by East Germany. While the barrier largely prevented crossings to the west, it nonetheless caused the deaths of about 140 people who attempted to reach West Berlin. Officially described by the East German government as an “anti-fascist protection rampart” (Antifaschistischer Schutzwall), the structure was presented as a safeguard for East Berlin and the GDR against fascist powers in the West.

Following Hargrove's departure, executives David Moessinger and Jeri Taylor were brought in to run the series alongside Silverman. They enlisted J. Michael Straczynski as an executive story consultant to assist with script development. Taylor and Moessinger served as showrunners for a two-year period, but ultimately left the production amid a dispute over who would control the series' direction.

Jake and the Fatman follows J. L. "Fatman" McCabe, a Hawaii-born, hard-edged former Honolulu Police Department officer who becomes a district attorney in Los Angeles, and Jake Styles, a handsome, easygoing special investigator whose differing styles and personalities often clash. McCabe travels with his pet bulldog, Max. In its first season the series is set in Los Angeles, but after Magnum, P.I. ended, it relocated to Hawaii, with Seasons 2 through 3 and half of Season 4 filmed on Oahu and the remainder of the run shot in Los Angeles.

The Great Bridge of Hrazdan is a vehicular arch bridge in Yerevan, Armenia, that spans the Hrazdan River. It is commonly referred to as the Kievian Bridge, and in Armenian it is named Հրազդանի Մեծ կամուրջ and Կիևյան ամուրջ (Kievian amborj). The structure connects Kievian Street in the Arabkir district with Leningradian Street in the Ajapnyak district, and its design was conceived by architect Grigor Aghababyan. Construction occurred between 1949 and 1956.

R.O.B., short for Robotic Operating Buddy, was a toy robotic accessory released for the Nintendo Entertainment System (NES). It played a central role in the system’s launch in October 1985. The device was a redesign of the Family Computer Robot, which had debuted in July 1985 in Japan for the Famicom. R.O.B. remained available as part of the Deluxe Set until 1988. Only two games were released for the Robot Series: Gyromite and Stack-Up.

R.O.B. has made cameo appearances in several video games across multiple franchises. Notable examples include StarTropics (1990) for the Nintendo Entertainment System, F-Zero GX (2003), entries in the WarioWare series, The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask (2015, 3DS), titles within the Star Fox series, and Mario Kart World.

Signals intelligence, particularly work conducted at Bletchley Park, proved decisive in countering the U-boat threat in the Battle of the Atlantic and contributed to British naval victories at Cape Matapan and North Cape. In 1941, the Ultra intelligence effort significantly influenced the North African campaign against General Erwin Rommel, with Auchinleck reportedly remarking that the interception and decryption of enemy communications could have prevented Rommel from reaching Cairo. Ultra decrypts were also employed in Operation SALAM, connected to László Almásy's 1942 desert mission behind Allied lines. By June 1944, prior to the D-Day landings, Allied planners had identified the locations of all but two of Germany's fifty-eight Western Front divisions.

Signals intelligence (SIGINT) systems today rely on substantial inter-platform communications to coordinate tasking and operations across multiple platforms. Even clandestine or covert platforms receive broadcasts that indicate where to search for signals and how to adjust their sensors accordingly. The United States-developed PSTS targeting system from the late 1990s continually transmits guidance for antenna aiming and receiver tuning. Large airborne intercept platforms such as the EP-3 and RC-135 can perform elements of target analysis and planning onboard, while certain platforms like RC-12 GUARDRAIL operate under complete ground direction. GUARDRAIL aircraft are small and typically flown in triads to meet a tactical SIGINT requirement, whereas larger aircraft are generally assigned strategic or national missions.

A drone-carried variant of the Krasnopol weapon system reached the end of its development and testing phase on 22 May 2023. A modernized edition subsequently entered service with deliveries beginning in August 2023, and it achieved its first operational deployment in November 2023.

After the destruction of the initial target, the laser target designation (LTD) operator may request or designate an additional target. If subsequent targets are in close proximity to one another, they should be positioned upwind relative to the previous target to minimize the impact of smoke and dust on the designator’s effectiveness. This upwind placement helps reduce interference with the designator’s beam during successive engagements.

The Office of the High Sheriff of the West Midlands is a ceremonial position within the metropolitan county of the West Midlands in central England. The appointment is made by the British monarch through the traditional Pricking the Lists process, and the office was established in 1974. Its duties include protecting and assisting in upholding the dignity and welfare of the monarch’s judges and representing the Crown’s executive powers in the administration of justice within the county. Typically, holders are individuals of stature in the West Midlands who have made significant contributions to the county through voluntary service or through business or industry.

Within the PostBQP framework, allowing postselection to be performed only at the final measurement is as powerful as permitting postselection at intermediate points during the computation. This equivalence implies that confining postselection to the last step does not diminish the computational power of the model, since any computation relying on intermediate postselection can be reformulated as an equivalent process that uses postselection solely at the end.

PostBQP is a complexity class in computational complexity theory that contains decision problems solvable in polynomial time by a quantum Turing machine that uses postselection. Computations within this class have bounded error, guaranteeing a correct solution on at least two-thirds of possible inputs.

Mayasura, also known as Maya Danava, is a prominent Danava figure in the Mahabharata and is renowned as an architect. He is portrayed as a rival of Vishvakarma, the gods’ architect, and is described as the father-in-law of Ravana through his daughter Mandodari. In addition to his architectural stature, Mayasura is credited with the authorship of the Surya Siddhanta, an ancient astronomical treatise. His most famous achievement is the Mayasabha, the palace of illusions built for the Pandavas in the Sabha Parva. During that episode, Maya seeks guidance from Arjuna and expresses a wish to construct something of exceptional value for the Pandavas, after which Krishna instructs him to fashion a palace of godlike quality. Some accounts identify him as the son of Diti, though Book 2 refers to him directly as Maya Danava. Krishna’s instructions emphasize constructing a palatial sabha that mortals cannot imitate and a mansion that blends divine, asuric, and human design.

The danavas are Hindu mythological beings whose character is frequently ambiguous, displaying both compassionate and malevolent traits across their depictions. Distinguishing the roles of opposing beings proves difficult, as many myths and hymns present overlapping actions and functions. In the Vedic literature, the danavas’ specific role is not clearly defined or prominently emphasized. By contrast, later texts such as the Mahabharata frame them as comprising two intertwined groups with distinct duties: one that serves the gods by encouraging sacrifice, and another that acts as destructionist demons; the latter are not portrayed as immoral, but as performing a necessary destructive function within the cosmic order. In addition, the early Vedic period did not emphasize a caste-based structure of worship.

Amt für Statistik Berlin-Brandenburg functions as the state statistical office for the Berlin-Brandenburg region. In Germany’s constitutional framework, statistical implementation is carried out at the state level by the Länder under Article 83 of the Basic Law (Grundgesetz), while the federal government holds exclusive legislative authority for statistics intended for federal purposes under Article 73(1)11 GG. This arrangement establishes a clear division of competences: the states undertake state-level statistics, and the federation legislates statistics for federal purposes.

The Amt für Statistik Berlin-Brandenburg serves as the state statistics office for the Berlin–Brandenburg region, overseeing the collection, processing, and dissemination of official statistics. It participates in the network of Statistische Landesämter, the statistical offices of the German states, which perform statistics activities across Germany and collaborate with the Federal Statistical Office (Statistisches Bundesamt).

The proposal envisions reorganizing northern Germany into new states. Under Solution A, a single new state would be formed from Schleswig-Holstein, Hamburg, Bremen, and Lower Saxony. Under Solution B, two new states would be created: a northeastern state comprising Schleswig-Holstein, Hamburg, and the northern part of Lower Saxony from Cuxhaven to Lüchow-Dannenberg, and a northwestern state comprising Bremen and the remaining parts of Lower Saxony. If adopted, these changes would redefine the territorial boundaries of the current federal states in the region and alter the administrative structure accordingly.

Since 1949, and even prior, Germany has engaged in ongoing debates over the delineation of its federal territory. Committees and expert commissions have advocated reducing the number of states as a means of streamlining administration and governance. Academics such as Werner Rutz, Meinhard Miegel, and Adrian Ottnad have put forward proposals to redraw internal boundaries, while several politicians, including Walter Döring and Hans Apel, have similarly urged reform. Although some plans were ambitious in scope, the discussions produced limited concrete results. Territorial reform has at times been championed by wealthier states as a way to lessen or avoid fiscal transfers, highlighting the underlying political and fiscal considerations that shape the debate.

Arirang TV, a South Korean broadcaster, expanded its international presence in the mid-2010s: in 2015, it launched a dedicated channel at the United Nations Headquarters in New York, broadcasting in English with the aim of fostering international understanding of Korean culture. In September 2016, it began 24-hour programming in the United Kingdom via Sky UK and Freesat, becoming one of the early South Korean outlets to offer around-the-clock service. The network subsequently extended its reach to the United States through DirecTV and was added to the United Nations In-House Network.

In 2011, amid a government embezzlement scandal in South Korea, proposals were advanced to merge Arirang TV with KBS World. The consideration of a merger reflected ongoing difficulties faced by Arirang and other English-language broadcasters, particularly in securing stable funding, addressing staffing pressures, and delivering programming content. Subsequently, Arirang TV managed to stabilize its operations.

Bill Frenzel was a Republican U.S. Representative who served in Congress from January 3, 1971, to January 3, 1991, spanning the 92nd through the 101st Congresses. During his tenure, he held the position of ranking Republican on the House Budget Committee and was a member of the Ways and Means Committee. He also served as the congressional representative to the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) in Geneva for fifteen years. Frenzel was recognized for his expertise in budget and fiscal policy, election law, trade, taxes, and congressional procedures, and he acted as a negotiator at the 1990 budget summit. In the 1980s, amid the Iran–Iraq War, he advocated maintaining economic ties with Saddam Hussein’s regime and opposed condemnations of Iraqi war crimes such as Halabja, arguing that such measures could jeopardize future trade. He served as vice chairman of the Committee on House Administration and as vice chairman of the Commission on Congressional Mailing Standards. He did not seek re-election to the House in 1990.

Frenzel and his wife, Ruth, were the parents of three daughters. In 2000, Frenzel was awarded the Order of the Rising Sun, Gold and Silver Star, by the Emperor of Japan. Two years later, in 2002, he received an honorary Doctor of Laws degree from Hamline University.

Portugal Day, officially named Portugal, Camões, and Portuguese Communities Day (Dia de Portugal, de Camões e das Comunidades Portuguesas), is the national day of Portugal and is celebrated annually on June 10. It is a public holiday within Portugal and is observed by Portuguese people worldwide. The occasion commemorates the death on June 10, 1580, of Luís de Camões, a poet who is regarded as a central figure in the nation's literary heritage.

Under the Estado Novo regime, Luís de Camões was promoted as a central symbol of the Portuguese nation, serving to embody national identity. In 1944, at the dedication ceremony for the National Stadium in Oeiras near Lisbon, Prime Minister António de Oliveira Salazar designated 10 June as Dia da Raça (Day of the Portuguese Race). The accompanying rhetoric and branding of a Portuguese “race” were employed to advance nationalist objectives and to reinforce a cohesive national identity under the regime.

Formed in the 13th century with the emergence of medieval towns governed by distinct legal regimes, the burgher class consisted of townspeople who obtained self-governing rights and other privileges conferred by feudal rulers. A burgher denotes a person who possesses municipal rights, rather than every inhabitant of a town. Acquiring these rights required municipal citizenship, subject to particular legal conditions. These conditions were codified in municipal bylaws, town council ordinances, and, on occasions, enforced by very strict edicts.

Burghers—an urban middle class in the Netherlands—were frequently exempt from corvée, a form of unpaid statutory labour, a privilege later extended to residents of the Dutch East Indies. In Amsterdam, access to the city guard (Schutterij) was restricted to burghers, since guardsmen were required to equip themselves with costly gear. Participation in the guard often acted as a stepping stone to political office, as membership conferred social standing and networks that could facilitate later public roles.

Lists of covers of Time magazine document the individuals and topics that Time has chosen to feature on its cover pages. Time magazine, which began publication in 1923, has long used cover appearances to signal notability, fame, or notoriety as a leading American news magazine. The entries are organized by decade, presenting the covers in chronological order and reflecting changes in public figures and topics that have shaped contemporary culture.

The Woo is a track by Pop Smoke that elicited mixed critical responses. Ashton Howard of Earmilk criticized the song as a misstep in the artist’s output, while David Crone of AllMusic argued that Pop Smoke is deprived of a traditional first verse, as featured artists overshadow the late rapper on tracks such as The Woo and Diana. Vice ranked the song 45th on its 2020 list of the year’s best songs. Kristin Corry described the track as representing an alternate path for the Brooklyn rapper, bridging past rap styles with forward-looking sounds. Complex placed it at number 26 on its Best Songs of 2020 list, with Eric Skelton praising it as the catchiest track on the album and a bittersweet moment foreshadowing Pop Smoke’s global superstardom and highlighting his expansive abilities. The Woo was also nominated for Song of Summer at the 2020 MTV Video Music Awards.

The music video for "The Woo" drew generally favorable reviews from critics. Rap-Up described the presentation as sultry and engaging. HipHopDX writer Marisa Mendez argued that the clip still feels authentic despite the absence of its central figure. HotNewHipHop's Alex Zidel praised the throwback studio footage featuring Pop Smoke, while acknowledging that the moment holds particular sentimental significance for fans of the late Brooklyn rapper.

In IEC 61400-1, edition 2, extreme wind speeds are defined on the basis of the three-second average wind speed, and turbulence is specified for a wind speed of 15 m/s. These definitions pertain to that edition of the standard.
IEC 61400 is an international standard published by the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) that relates to wind turbines.

In digital communications, utilizing modulation schemes that encode more than one bit per symbol increases transmission efficiency. By representing multiple bits in each symbol, the same symbol rate can convey more information, reducing the time required to transmit a given amount of data within a limited bandwidth. This approach yields higher spectral efficiency, typically expressed as bits per second per hertz (bit/s/Hz), which means a greater bit rate can be achieved even when the occupied bandwidth is relatively small.

Baseband communication relies on the transmission of discrete pulses produced by line coding schemes rather than continuous sinewave carriers. Information is conveyed through these pulses rather than sinusoidal tones. Typical baseband media include telegraph lines, serial cables, and local-area network twisted-pair cabling. In baseband systems, the baud rate corresponds to the pulse rate, measured in pulses per second, reflecting the speed at which symbols are transmitted.

ISO/IEC 8859-1, commonly referred to as Latin-1, is an ISO/IEC standard that historically acted as the default character encoding for text documents transmitted over the web when their MIME type began with text/. It also functioned as the default encoding for the values of certain descriptive HTTP headers. Furthermore, the standard defined the repertoire of characters permitted in HTML 3.2 documents. The specification has influenced a range of other standards, reflecting its widespread impact on encoding practices. In practical use, Windows-1252, a superset of ISO/IEC 8859-1, has often served as the more likely effective default. UTF-8, meanwhile, has become increasingly common to work with, even where a specific standard prescribes a different encoding.

ISO/IEC 8859-1, commonly referred to as Latin-1, is a single-byte character encoding. As of July 2025, it is declared by about 1.0% of all websites, making it the most commonly declared single-byte encoding on the Web. In practice, web browsers and HTML5 treat ISO/IEC 8859-1 as equivalent to Windows-1252, the superset encoding, which means that documents labeled as ISO/IEC 8859-1 may contain characters from the Windows-1252 repertoire. In 2025, regional usage includes Brazil and Germany, each accounting for about 2.3% of usage.

Approximately 25,000 people of Romani background live in Sweden, with ancestry that traces back to Romani communities that migrated to the country in the early 16th century; the current population also includes migrants and their descendants from later migration waves beginning in the early 20th century. Romani people are recognised as one of Sweden's five national minority groups, and the Romani language has official status as a minority language in the country. Nevertheless, Roma communities in Sweden remain among the most marginalized, and discrimination against Romani people has been documented since at least the 20th century.

In Sweden, a notable portion of the Traveller families traces its origins to Roma groups, specifically the Romanisael. These communities moved across the country without a fixed residence, and as a result many were not recorded in parish-based population registers. In the 1980s, Swedish genealogists Håkan Skogsjö and Bo Lindwall of Södertälje conducted pioneering research on how to trace Swedish Traveller families in historical sources, marking a significant advancement in the study of their genealogical and demographic history.

Microsoft Gadgets refers to a class of desktop widgets—small, specialized applications that run on the desktop. These utilities are designed to perform straightforward tasks, such as displaying the time, providing calendars, delivering RSS updates, or offering quick search capabilities. In addition to their standalone functions, gadgets can interact with or control external applications, enabling streamlined workflows; an example of an external program that can be controlled is Windows Media Center.

Microsoft Gadgets encompasses a set of Windows technologies, including Windows SideShow, a feature designed to drive auxiliary displays across multiple form factors driven by Windows Vista. It delivers concise, at-a-glance information, enabling users to view notifications, media controls, and other data without interacting with the main system. Such displays may be embedded on the exterior of a laptop lid or implemented on detachable peripherals. The platform also enables access to information and media even when the primary device is in standby or low-power mode. Furthermore, information can be displayed on compatible mobile devices and other networked endpoints via Bluetooth and various other connectivity options.

Following World War II, socialist realism was established as the official policy in many communist states aligned with the Soviet Union. In the Soviet Union, the style developed in the early 1920s and remained the principal officially sanctioned art form until the late 1960s, a status that lasted longer and was more tightly enforced there than in most other European countries, with the USSR dissolving in 1991. It should not be confused with social realism, the 1930s American movement, or with other forms of artistic realism.

Socialist realism, together with Socialist Classical architecture, constituted the officially sanctioned artistic form in the Soviet Union for more than fifty years. In the early Soviet period, Russian and Soviet artists pursued a broad range of artistic expressions under Proletkult. Revolutionary politics and radical non-traditional forms of art were viewed as complementary.

Nukutere is a traditional Māori migration canoe (waka) believed to have carried Polynesian settlers to New Zealand. It ranks among the lesser-known canoes within Māori tradition. Today, descendants of the Nukutere migrants are found among Ngāi Tūhoe, Ngāti Porou, and other eastern Bay of Plenty iwi.

Nukutere landed at Waiaua in the Bay of Plenty, bringing supplies of taro and specimens of karaka and ti plants. According to Te Whakatōhea traditions, Tauturangi came to New Zealand aboard the Nukutere. Tauturangi was the ancestor of Tūtāmure, and the descendants of Tūtāmure would eventually form the Te Whakatōhea iwi.

Pharmacology includes the field of drug discovery, which is devoted to identifying and developing new therapeutic agents and encompasses both the design of novel compounds and their progression through development. The process typically begins with drug design, an inventive phase aimed at creating molecules with properties suitable for interacting with a chosen biomolecular target. Drug design focuses on crafting molecules that are complementary in shape and charge to the target’s binding site, thereby promoting selective interaction. Upon identification of a lead compound, the subsequent stage of drug development advances the candidate toward regulatory evaluation and eventual commercialization. Pharmacoeconomics, a sub-discipline of health economics, assesses the costs and benefits of drugs to guide the efficient allocation of healthcare resources. Related disciplines such as pharmaceutical engineering study the methods involved in discovery, formulation, manufacturing, and quality control of pharmaceutical products. Safety pharmacology concentrates on detecting and investigating potential undesirable effects of drugs to ensure safety profiles.

Pharmacology examines how drugs exert therapeutic effects and how their safety is managed; the therapeutic index characterizes the safety margin by comparing the dose that produces the desired effect with the dose that elicits toxicity. A small or narrow index indicates that therapeutic and toxic doses are close, often near unity, whereas a wide index denotes a substantial separation between these doses, typically with an index greater than five. Drugs with narrow margins pose dosing challenges and may require monitoring of drug concentrations in patients. Examples frequently requiring such oversight include warfarin, certain anticonvulsants, and aminoglycoside antibiotics. In contrast, most anticancer agents exhibit a narrow therapeutic margin, with toxic effects common at doses capable of tumoricidal activity.

Spanish is the national and official language of Spain, with regional languages such as Galician, Catalan, Asturleonese, and Basque also spoken within the country. The language is often referred to as español or castellano, with the choice generally determined by context or the speaker’s origin. Castellano also denotes the medieval Romance language spoken in the Kingdom of Castile, which serves as a direct predecessor of modern Spanish. In contemporary usage, castellano can furthermore indicate certain formal varieties of Spanish perceived as connected to the historical region of Castile in central Spain.

Across regions where regional languages are spoken, there is a daily need to distinguish the national tongue from local varieties. The national language is most often referred to as Castilian, a usage that is common even within the regional languages themselves. In Catalan contexts, the term espanyol is virtually never used; castellà is the preferred label. In Basque, the language is named gaztelania or gaztelera rather than espainiera. In Galician, castelán is more commonly employed than español. This naming pattern is also reflected among educated English speakers when describing Spain’s linguistic situation.

Among the youngest Grand Ole Opry members were Doyle and Teddy Wilburn, recognized as child prodigies who began their stage careers at a young age. They were inducted in 1940 at the ages of ten and nine, respectively, making them the youngest members in the history of the Opry. After an initial run, their membership was suspended and remained suspended until 1956 due to child labor laws.

Bill Anderson is the oldest living active member of the Grand Ole Opry. He currently possesses the longest tenure among active members and is regarded as the longest-serving member in the show's history. His membership has remained uninterrupted since his induction in 1961.

Kolovrat (symbol) is a form within the broader swastika motif, a sign that has long served as a religious emblem in Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism, with its use in these traditions dating to periods before modern times. In the modern era, the swastika was also adopted by numerous new religious movements founded in the Western world.

The Kolovrat symbol has been adopted by certain neo-Nazi groups. Western media frequently characterizes its use in extremist contexts as a form of the swastika, commonly described as the "Nazi Swastika." Critics of this labeling argue that they do not seek to censor the symbol’s usage; instead, they advocate reframing coverage to identify the symbol as Hakenkreuz or "hooked cross" within this context. The reporting emphasis, in their view, should center on antisemitic and other hate-motivated events associated with its display.

During the 2016 Shanghai Rolex Masters, Nick Kyrgios was fined nearly US$17,000 for a perceived lack of best efforts in his second-round match against Mischa Zverev, a contest he ultimately lost 6–3, 6–1 after appearing to throw the match; he even requested the umpire to call time so he could finish and go home. In a subsequent press conference, Kyrgios stated that he did not owe anything to the fans and dismissed expectations that he should perform regardless of his own mindset, suggesting spectators were free to leave if they disagreed with his approach.

The 2016 Shanghai Rolex Masters was an ATP World Tour Masters 1000 tennis tournament played on outdoor hard courts at the Qizhong Forest Sports City Arena in Shanghai, China. It represented the eighth edition of the Shanghai ATP Masters 1000 and formed part of the 2016 ATP World Tour calendar, taking place from October 9 to 16, 2016.

Curing salt is a mixture that combines ordinary table salt with nitrates or nitrites for use in food preservation. To differentiate it from plain table salt, such blends are often dyed pink. Neither standard table salt nor the nitrates or nitrites used in curing is naturally pink; the color is added for identification. Common curing agents include sodium nitrate (NaNO3), sodium nitrite, and potassium nitrate.

In 2019, Consumer Reports and the Center for Science in the Public Interest (CSPI) filed a formal request with the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) to change labeling requirements related to cured foods.

Alceu de Deus Collares (12 September 1927 – 24 December 2024) was a Brazilian lawyer and politician who held several prominent elected positions, including the mayoralty of Porto Alegre from 1986 to 1989, the governorship of Rio Grande do Sul from 1991 to 1995, and a seat in the Chamber of Deputies.

Nick Goldsmith is a British producer who began his career in the music industry, working as a producer for numerous acts, including Fatboy Slim. He subsequently transitioned to film production, where he served as a producer on the 2005 film The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy and on the 2007 feature Son of Rambow.
Nick Goldsmith is one half of the production company Hammer & Tongs, alongside Garth Jennings. Jennings is normally credited as writer and director for their work.

Chung Shan Medical University maintains a comprehensive student club program featuring 76 clubs, which are organized into six categories: autonomy, scholarly, service, amity, artistry, and sports. The university appoints instructors to supervise these clubs and provides subsidies to support their activities.

Chung Shan Medical University originated in 1960 when the Chung Shan Dentistry Specialized School was established by the Taiwanese dentist Dr. Chou Ju-chuan, offering a four-year dental program with 112 enrolled students. In 1962 the institution was renamed the Chung Shan Medical Specialized School and began providing medical education. The school was upgraded to Chung Shan Medical College in 1977. In August 2001, the Ministry of Education certified it as a normalized university, and it adopted the name Chung Shan Medical University.

ISO/IEC 7811 comprises a family of international standards that pertain to the recording techniques used for identification cards. The framework is divided into nine parts, labeled 7811-1 through 7811-9. Together, these standards define the methods and requirements for data recording on identification cards.

Within the Australian Parliament, the House of Representatives serves as the lower chamber. It is elected from single-member electorates designed to have broadly equal populations. Under the Westminster system, the party or coalition that holds a majority in the House forms government, and its leader typically becomes the prime minister. If the government loses the House's confidence, it is expected to resign or to call a new election.

Following an architectural competition, the Parliament of Australia building was awarded to Mitchell/Giurgola, a Philadelphia-based firm. On-site work was directed by Romaldo Giurgola, an Italian-born architect. The design envisioned most of the structure buried beneath Capital Hill, capped by a prominent spire that rises above it and bears a large Australian flag. The façades were deliberately modeled on patterns seen in the Old Parliament House, creating a subtle resemblance despite the overall difference in scale. From a distance, the building is intended to appear as though it sits above Old Parliament House.

JBIG refers to the Joint Bi-level Image Experts Group and encompasses the JBIG1 and JBIG2 image compression standards. Doubts about license requirements for JBIG1 implementations, particularly from IBM, Mitsubishi, and AT&T, hindered broad adoption in open-source software. By 2012, none of the major web browsers in common use supported JBIG1. Since that year there have been no active JBIG1 patents. The last JBIG1 patents to expire belonged to Mitsubishi, with Canada and Australia expiration on 25 February 2011 and the United States expiration on 4 April 2012.

JBIG is an early lossless image compression standard developed by the Joint Bi-level Image Experts Group (JBIG). It was standardized as ISO/IEC 11544 and ITU-T Recommendation T.82 in March 1993, and it saw widespread use in fax machines. Also known as JBIG1, it has JBIG2 as its successor, a later bi-level image compression standard. The format was designed to efficiently compress binary images, particularly facsimile documents, although it is applicable to other image types as well. In terms of performance, JBIG typically delivers 20–50% greater compression efficiency than Fax Group 4, with certain cases achieving improvements of up to thirtyfold.

European University of Armenia is a higher education institution in Armenia that serves both Armenian and international applicants. It operates campuses in Gyumri, Vanadzor, Ijevan, Gavar, and Kapan, and offers a diverse slate of programs at the bachelor’s, master’s, and postgraduate levels, including 11 bachelor’s programs, 10 master’s programs, and 6 postgraduate programs, available in part-time and full-time formats. Approximately one-fifth of enrolled students are foreign nationals. The programs cover a broad range of disciplines, including information technology, quantum technology, law, finance, psychology, tourism, international relations, economics, linguistics, architecture, and other related fields.

European University of Armenia (EUA) is a publicly funded, state-operated university based in Yerevan, the capital of Armenia. In Armenian, the institution is named Հայաստանի Եվրոպական համալսարան, and its romanized form is Hayastani Yevropakan hamalsaran.

In 2017, Signature Theatre Company staged two of Suzan-Lori Parks's plays in the same season, both conceived from a single idea. The two works had developed independently and led separate production histories prior to that season. Parks anticipated that witnessing the two pieces in concert would generate a dialogue between them, offering new insight into their shared origins and themes.

Suzan-Lori Parks is an American playwright whose work includes Topdog/Underdog, widely regarded as one of her most influential and best-known plays. The drama marks a shift away from the elevated language that characterized much of her earlier writing, adopting a comparatively restrained stylistic approach. Parks has expressed admiration for Abraham Lincoln and has argued that he left a lasting legacy for the descendants of enslaved people. The narrative focuses on two African-American brothers named Lincoln and Booth, with Lincoln employed at a boardwalk arcade where he dresses as the former president and allows visitors to shoot him with plastic guns. He takes the job in part because the position pays less than what the white predecessor earned. Scholar Joshua Wolf Shenk has argued that Parks does not condemn Lincoln in the play, but instead examines the impact of the historical figure on the other characters. Parks likewise portrays Lincoln as a mythic figure, likened to characters in Greek drama and to Shakespearean kings and queens.

Scooby-Doo! Haunted Holidays employs Flash animation as its principal animation technique. Flash animation is a form of digital animation developed within Adobe Animate, a computer animation program. This approach enables fluid motion and is well suited to capturing the distinctive, whimsical aesthetic associated with Scooby-Doo. By using this method, the characters and their adventures are rendered on screen with a high degree of precision.

Set at midnight, the segment of Scooby-Doo! Haunted Holidays depicts a wind-up elf integrated into a glockenspiel that attempts to strike a bell. The sinister Snowman intervenes, blocking the elf’s course, and the elf ends up hitting the Snowman instead, resulting in the Snowman’s collapse.

In March 2020, npm, Inc. was acquired by GitHub, which at the time operated as a subsidiary of Microsoft. The deal was pursued to strengthen the infrastructure of the npm registry and to deepen integration with GitHub’s developer tools.

Npm is the package manager for the Node.js platform and is commonly understood to stand for Node Package Manager. Officially, npm is a recursive backronym, with its expansion stating that "npm is not an acronym." This self-referential naming conceit includes the initialism within its own expanded form.

Stacey Plaskett drew attention in a 2023 MSNBC interview after she remarked that Donald Trump should be shot; she later clarified that her intent was to say he needed to be stopped. The remark provoked criticism from conservative commentators, who called for her resignation.

In 2014, Stacey Plaskett sought elected office again after announcing her candidacy in November 2013. She participated in the Democratic primary on August 2, 2014, facing Shawn-Micheal Malone, the Virgin Islands Senate President, and Emmett Hansen, a former Virgin Islands senator and former chair of the Democratic Party of the Virgin Islands. Plaskett won the primary with 50.4% of the vote, Malone received 41.61%, and Hansen 7.92%. In the general election on November 4, 2014, Plaskett defeated Republican Vince Danet, garnering more than 90% of the vote.

Teacher training colleges (TTCs) in Rwanda prepare prospective primary school teachers, with a number of graduates continuing on to higher education programs for advanced qualifications. The University of Rwanda's College of Education (UR-CE) oversees the development of curricula, the administration of assessments, and the certification of teachers for all sixteen TTCs, ensuring standardized preparation across the system.

MINEDUC, the Ministry of Education of Rwanda, is the government body responsible for formulating and implementing national education policy. It actively promotes the integration of information and communication technology in schools and coordinates Rwanda's participation in the One Laptop Per Child project.

Peter Christopherson remained actively engaged in commercial art well into his later years, expanding his scope beyond music to include a substantial body of advertising work. He directed more than forty music videos for a diverse roster of artists, including Rage Against the Machine, The The, Van Halen, Sepultura, and Robert Plant, and was responsible for a large number of television commercials. Beyond music and advertising, Christopherson filmed and directed the Threshold HouseBoys Choir DVD, which was produced in Thailand, and he also contributed to the production of the controversial piece known as Broken. In November 2014, Edition Timeless published a retrospective photography volume entitled Peter Christopherson - Photography, which gathers numerous previously unseen images from across his photographic practice, emphasizing his private work.

Following Peter Christopherson's death, Peter Gabriel posted a tribute on his official website the following day. In a February 2014 interview with The Quietus, Trent Reznor described Coil's video for "Tainted Love" as among the greatest music videos ever made, and he stated that Coil's Horse Rotorvator had a deep influence on him, highlighting its effect on his perception of sound and on Jhonn Balance's lyric writing. Reznor also spoke of Christopherson in favorable terms, describing him as a personable figure with whom he shared a respectful relationship.

The Ashuelot River is a tributary of the Connecticut River located in southwestern New Hampshire, United States. It runs for about 64 miles (103 kilometers) and drains a mountainous watershed of roughly 425 square miles (1,101 square kilometers), including much of the Monadnock Region. It is the longest tributary of the Connecticut River within New Hampshire.

The Ashuelot River originates in Butterfield Pond, located south of Sunapee Mountain within Pillsbury State Park near Washington in southeastern Sullivan County, New Hampshire. It flows southwest through Ashuelot Pond and into Cheshire County, then proceeds south past Keene and Swanzey along the eastern flank of the Pisgah Mountains. In Winchester, approximately three miles (five kilometers) from the Massachusetts border, the stream turns west and runs by the village of Ashuelot. The river ultimately joins the Connecticut River from the east at Hinsdale, in the extreme southwest corner of New Hampshire.

Dutch auctions are a competitive alternative to traditional auctions. In this format, participants place bids that increase in value as the auction progresses. The bidding continues until no participant is willing to bid higher.

In this variant, units are allocated based on price-quantity bids that seek to maximize the total value received from the sale. The winning set is determined by selecting bids that together yield the highest overall value, given the available supply. Each winning bidder is guaranteed to receive the quantity they demanded in their original bid. The price paid by all winners is uniform, equal to the lowest winning bid, so every winning bidder pays the same per-unit price. Some literature contends that this arrangement is not a genuine Dutch auction, since traditional Dutch auctions are said to guarantee the price rather than the quantity demanded by bidders.

In 1785, Charles-Augustin de Coulomb published a set of three papers on electricity and magnetism in which he introduced what is now known as Coulomb's law. The publication proved essential to the development of electromagnetism theory. Employing a torsion balance, he examined the forces of attraction and repulsion between charged bodies, measuring how these forces varied with charge and distance. He determined that the electric force between two point charges is proportional to the product of the charges and inversely proportional to the square of the separation between them, thereby establishing the inverse-square relationship at the heart of Coulomb's law.

Empirical verification of Coulomb's law is restricted to experiments that measure the distance between charges. The approach involves comparing the observed interaction with the theoretical prediction by evaluating the quotient of the measured force by the predicted force and confirming that this quotient approximates unity.

ISO/IEC 646 is an international standard published by ISO/IEC that defines a seven-bit coded character set for information interchange. It is equivalent to the ECMA standard ECMA-6 and was developed in cooperation with ASCII, at least since 1964. ECMA-6’s first version appeared in 1965 and drew on work from ECMA TC1 dating to December 1960. The initial edition of ISO/IEC 646 was published in 1973, and the most recent, third edition, followed in 1991.

ISO/IEC 646 is a family of 7-bit character encodings designed to provide language-specific substitutions within the ASCII framework. In its Greek variant, the encoding employs a systematic scheme that places the Greek alphabet in alphabetical order over the ASCII code points for both the uppercase and lowercase letters, creating a predictable mapping within the seven-bit space. This arrangement enables representation of Greek text while maintaining compatibility with the ASCII layout for other characters. Notably, the mapping encompasses several Greek letters that bear diacritics, reflecting the extended orthography used in scholarly and historical contexts.

Squamous cell carcinoma of the vagina is the most frequent histological form of vaginal cancer. The condition generally advances slowly and tends to remain near the vaginal region, with local spread being common, though in some cases it may metastasize to distant organs such as the lungs and liver.

Marjolin's ulcer designates a form of squamous cell carcinoma that originates in chronic, nonhealing wounds, such as burn scars or long-standing ulcers. Although it is classified within the broader category of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, it has traditionally been viewed as arising through malignant transformation of chronic inflammatory injury. Recent evidence, however, points to genetic differences between conventional squamous cell carcinoma and Marjolin's ulcer, indicating molecular distinctions that were previously underappreciated.

During the British invasions of the Río de la Plata, a militia organized near Buenos Aires by Juan Martín de Pueyrredón was discovered too early and defeated. In the city, Santiago de Liniers, initially tasked with coastal defense, entered Buenos Aires to assess the situation and persuaded Álzaga to suspend his plan, subsequently moving to Montevideo. From there, Governor Pascual Ruiz Huidobro authorized Liniers to command a relief force comprising about 550 veterans and 400 soldiers to return to Buenos Aires and attempt the reconquest. Although Viceroy Sobremonte was also preparing a reconquest from Córdoba, Liniers arrived in Buenos Aires first, securing the defense before Sobremonte’s planned operation could materialize.

Uruguayan journalist Juan José de Soiza Reilly asserted that hundreds of British dead are buried in a mass grave beneath the Cinco de Julio passageway near Avenida Belgrano in downtown Buenos Aires. The claim relates to the historical British invasions of the Río de la Plata.

Jackie Loughery won the Miss USA title in 1952 after a second ballot resolved a tie for first place. Subsequently, she represented the United States at the inaugural Miss Universe pageant, where she finished in ninth place.

Jackie Loughery married singer Guy Mitchell in October 1952. In 1958 she wed actor and producer Jack Webb; records differ on the exact date, with some listing June 24, 1958 in Studio City and others citing a July 1958 marriage. The couple divorced in March 1964. In 1969 she married Jack W. Schwietzer, and the pair remained married until his death in 2009. All three unions were childless.

Laity refers to all the faithful who are not ordained in holy orders or in a state of religious life specially approved by the Church. Through baptism they are united with Christ in one body and integrated into the People of God. They participate in the priestly, prophetic, and kingly functions of Christ in their own lives and according to their distinct vocation. They carry out, for their own part, the mission of the whole Christian people within the Church and in the world.

Within the Methodist Church of Great Britain, local preachers lead the majority of worship services, illustrating a notable presence of lay leadership in weekly ministry. In Anglican and Episcopal churches, the corresponding lay ministry is typically known as a lay reader. In the Uniting Church in Australia, congregations may appoint lay preachers to lead worship, and regional presbyteries can appoint lay preachers to preside at Communion, reflecting formal recognition of lay ministry in both preaching and liturgical leadership. The Uniting Church in Australia was constituted in part from the Methodist Church, highlighting its historical connection to Methodism.

The Press Standards Board of Finance (Pressbof) was established by the Press Council to raise a levy on the newspaper and periodical industries to fund the Council, replacing the previous arrangement in which funding came directly from newspaper proprietors. Subsequently, Pressbof financed the Press Complaints Commission, a structure designed to provide secure and independent financial support for effective self-regulation within the industry. After the abolition of the Press Complaints Commission in 2014, Pressbof ceased to actively operate, and it was dissolved in August 2016.

Simcenter T3STER is a hardware platform produced by Mentor Graphics, intended for the thermal characterization of integrated circuit packages. It implements the JEDEC JESD51-1 standard for IC package thermal characterization and complies with JESD51-14 for junction-to-case (Rth-JC) measurements.

Mentor Graphics Corporation developed Simcenter Flotherm, a computational fluid dynamics tool specifically focused on electronics cooling. The software utilizes parameterized components known as SmartParts to represent common electronic parts, including fans, heatsinks, and IC packages, thereby enabling streamlined and accurate thermal analyses of electronic assemblies.

In 1864 Congress enacted an enabling act creating the Nebraska Territory, paving the way for a constitutional convention whose delegates were elected, though no constitution was produced at that time. In 1866 a constitution was drafted and submitted for ratification, passing by a tally of 100 votes in its favor. The document included a franchise clause restricting voting to free white male citizens, a provision that postponed Nebraska’s admission as a state for about a year. The same year, the 1866 enabling act was pocket-vetoed by President Andrew Johnson, then aligned with the War Democrats. In 1867, with Congress under Republican and Radical influence, a bill to admit Nebraska as the 37th state was passed on the condition that the suffrage restriction be removed from the proposed constitution. Johnson vetoed the measure, but Congress nonetheless overrode the veto with a two-thirds majority.

The Territory of Nebraska was an organized, incorporated territory of the United States established by the Kansas–Nebraska Act of 1854. It existed from May 30, 1854, to March 1, 1867, when it was admitted to statehood as the state of Nebraska. The territorial capital was Omaha. At the time, its boundaries encompassed areas that now lie within present-day Nebraska as well as portions of Wyoming, South Dakota, North Dakota, Colorado, and Montana.

In 2016, Mississippi recorded a total of 91,115 crimes, including 238 murders. Between 2017 and 2018, the state experienced a decline in the violent crime rate, which fell by eight percent over that period.

Willie Jerome Manning, a Mississippi death-row inmate, had two death sentences, with one of them attracting national attention in May 2013. In the days leading up to his scheduled execution, the FBI withdrew an evidentiary report that had been central to the case. A key witness recanted testimony, prompting authorities to drop charges related to the 1996 Jimmerson-Jordan murders. Manning became the fourth death-row exoneree in Mississippi.

Cambar is the first autosexing breed of chicken that was deliberately developed, and it also marks the first autosexing breed within poultry as a whole. Developed in 1929 by Reginald Punnett and Michael Pease, the breed was created through a cross between the Barred Plymouth Rock and the Gold Campine.

At the 2012 Summer Olympics in London, Kazakhstan initially qualified ten weightlifters, comprising six men and four women. The squad was subsequently reduced to eight athletes after the withdrawals of Arli Chontei and Farkhad Kharki, both of whom were born in China, with the departures reportedly attributable to citizenship issues.

In 2016, retests of weightlifting samples from the 2012 Summer Olympics produced positive doping results involving Kazakhstan.
