As a consequence, four Kazakh weightlifting gold medals from the 2012 Games were disqualified, and the medals and any records associated with those performances were stripped.

Oceans acoustic tomography uses the travel times of acoustic signals to infer temperature fields over long propagation paths. The reported travel times effectively integrate temperature variations along the path, and because ray paths sample different depths, the measurements are inherently averaged over both horizontal distance and vertical extent. Local, single-point observations are often dominated by small-scale turbulence and internal-wave activity, making them noisy. Temperature measurements from conventional instrumentation such as moored thermistors or Argo floats exhibit noise on the order of 1–2 °C and require many instruments to attain reliable accuracy. By contrast, acoustic tomography offers a cost-effective means to estimate the basin-scale mean temperature, since tomographic data average temperature variability over depth as ray paths traverse multiple layers of the water column.

Ocean acoustic tomography is a method for diagnosing temperature and current fields over large regions of the ocean by using estimates of acoustic travel times. In basin-scale studies the technique is frequently called acoustic thermometry. It relies on precise measurements of the travel time of sound between a source and a receiver separated by distances of roughly 100 to 5,000 kilometers. If the positions of the instruments are known with high accuracy, time-of-flight data yield the average speed of sound along each path. Because sound speed in seawater is predominantly controlled by temperature, the resulting travel-time observations serve as proxies for temperature. Quantitatively, a 1°C change in temperature corresponds to about a 4 m/s change in sound speed (13 ft/s). An oceanographic tomography experiment typically uses several source–receiver pairs deployed in a moored array to sample and characterize an ocean region.

The second movement of Sonata in C major for keyboard four-hands, K. 19d, comprises 54 measures in 3/4 time, with a tempo feel reminiscent of Andante. The opening minuet extends to 26 measures, followed by an eight-bar transition that leads into a trio of eight bars, which is then repeated. After the trio, the music returns to the completed minuet and the movement closes. Overall, the movement exemplifies the very typical 18th-century minuet style.

The first movement of the Sonata in C major for keyboard four-hands, K. 19d, spans 107 bars and is written in common time. It follows a conventional sonata-form layout, presenting a principal theme and subsequently developing it. The opening motif is anchored by a pronounced C major triad, establishing the home key from the outset. Around bar 40, the middle section shifts to a darker, more ominous variant of the main theme. After this contrast, the movement returns to the bright C major harmony, with the music shifting back to the tonic after the middle episode.

Hexadecimal is a base-16 numeral system that uses sixteen distinct symbols to represent values. In addition to hex, digit-based counting schemes are used in other bases such as binary. One notable proposal by Arthur C. Clarke envisions mapping each finger to a binary digit, enabling ten fingers to tally from zero up to 1,023 in decimal. A separate example illustrates counting in hexadecimal up to FF, which corresponds to 255 in decimal. Such demonstrations help show how positional numeral systems translate between bases.

During the mid-19th century, scholars explored numeral systems beyond the decimal base, evaluating a variety of alternative bases. Alfred B. Taylor contributed to this discussion by examining senidenary notation as part of his broader study of non-decimal systems. He ultimately dismissed hexadecimal (base 16) on practical grounds, arguing that it would require an unwieldy number of digits to express numbers. This episode reflects the era’s broader interest in the viability and limitations of non-decimal notation.

Within 19-inch rack systems, open-frame designs represent the least costly option. Their open construction leaves air-cooled equipment exposed to dust, lint, and environmental contaminants. By contrast, enclosed sealed cabinets that utilize forced-air cooling include air filtration, which serves to safeguard equipment from dust and related particulates.

In certain 19-inch rack configurations, hardware may employ a folding cable tray mounted behind the installed server. Cables are organized within a compact folded channel inside the rack, and the tray can be unfolded into a long strip when access is required. This design allows the server to remain plugged in and operational while it is fully extended and suspended in front of the rack. Such a arrangement simplifies maintenance tasks, though it incurs a trade-off in the form of restricted airflow to the equipment.

Influenza B virus has a segmented genome comprising eight linear, negative-sense, single-stranded RNA segments, with a total length of 14,548 nucleotides. Each segment is encapsidated within its own nucleocapsid, giving rise to a multipartite genome organization, while all eight nucleocapsids are enclosed by a single lipid envelope forming the virion.

Through hemagglutination inhibition assays using ferret antisera raised after infection, two antigenically distinct influenza B variants were identified during the 1988–1989 season. Each variant shared antigens with one of two reference lineages, either B/Yamagata/16/88 or B/Victoria/2/87. The B/Yamagata/16/88 lineage was first detected in Japan in May 1988, while the B/Victoria/2/87 lineage demonstrated antigenic similarity to all influenza B viruses isolated in the United States during the winter 1988–1989 outbreak.

Peter Newell identifies John Locke as perhaps the most influential figure in shaping the debate over corporal punishment in education. In Some Thoughts Concerning Education, Locke explicitly criticized the central role of corporal punishment in schooling and argued for alternative disciplinary approaches. The work was influential in shaping later educational reform and thought. Some scholars contend that Locke's ideas helped persuade Polish lawmakers to prohibit corporal punishment in schools in 1783, making Poland the first country in the world to ban such practices in educational settings.

Beating the Bounds was an ancient English practice of corporal punishment used to mark parish boundaries. Participants typically paraded boys along the outer limits of a city or parish, administering blows with a switch or cane as a punitive measure. A notable example occurred at the boundary between the parish of St Giles and the area now occupied by Tottenham Court Road in central London, and the corresponding boundary stone for that area lies beneath the Centre Point office tower.

Geastrales is an order of gasterocarpic basidiomycete fungi that is related to the Gomphales. The order comprises four families: Geastraceae, Schenellaceae, Sclerogastraceae, and Sphaerobolaceae. The Geastraceae family includes the earthstars, a group whose members were formerly classified in the Lycoperdales or Phallales.

Earthstars are the fruiting bodies of Geastrum in which the outer exoperidium splits into several ray-like lobes that spread to form a star-shaped envelope around a central endoperidium. The rays protect the spore-bearing body and facilitate spore dispersal. These fungi exhibit hygrometric behavior, drying out in arid conditions and curling around the soft spore sac; in such dry weather the organism may detach and roll across the surface like a tumbleweed. When moisture is present, the rays moisten and straighten, with some bending backward to lift the spore sac, thereby exposing it to rain or animals and enabling spore release when environmental moisture supports germination.

Construction of the Kambarata-1 Dam officially commenced on 8 June 2022, at a ceremony attended by President Sadyr Japarov. In remarks delivered at the event, Japarov stated that the hydroelectric plant would help ensure the country’s energy security and independence, and that the project would make a substantial contribution to national socio-economic development.

The Kambarata-1 Dam provides benefits beyond energy production, notably by improving seasonal water management in Central Asia and increasing irrigation capacity across the region. It is seen as reinforcing regional cooperation among neighboring states. Proponents describe the project as a milestone in Kyrgyzstan’s economic modernization and as a factor that would bolster the country’s independence while strengthening its leadership position within the region.

Lycée Français Anatole France is a French international school located in Yerevan, Armenia, established in 2007. It opened for the 2007–08 academic year with a small cohort of nine students. Ten years after its founding, the school celebrated its tenth anniversary on 3 June 2017, marking a milestone in its development within the Armenian capital.

The Lycée Français Anatole France was renamed on 30 March 2018 in honor of Anatole France, a French poet and novelist who won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1921. The renaming ceremony was attended by Jean-Baptiste Lemoyne, the French Secretary of State for Europe and Foreign Affairs; Levon Mkrtchyan, Armenia’s Minister of Education; and Jonathan Lacôte, the French Ambassador to Armenia. The decision to rename the institution was a tribute to Anatole France for his influence and support of the Armenian cause during challenging times for the Armenian nation.

In universities and other higher education institutions, coursework is typically a required component of degree programs. It serves to broaden students’ knowledge, enhance research skills, and demonstrate their ability to discuss ideas, reason effectively, and translate theoretical concepts into practical outcomes. When conducted in group settings, coursework can also be used to cultivate teamwork and facilitate peer learning.

Coursework was formerly a component of United Kingdom GCSE courses but was subsequently removed and replaced by a framework known as Controlled Assessment (CA). Under CA, tasks had to be completed under examination conditions, with no teacher involvement, and within tightly regulated resources to minimise opportunities for cheating. The CA system has largely been discontinued as well, and GCSE assessment has become predominantly exam-based as part of broader reforms to the GCSE framework.

Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) is employed in the production of bookbinding tools. These instruments are used to fold, score, and separate sheets of paper during the binding process. The devices fashioned from PTFE are typically referred to as Teflon bone folders.

Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), commonly marketed under the Teflon brand, is utilized in air filtration media in two primary forms: porous membrane filters and PTFE-coated filter media. PTFE membrane filters are among the most efficient options for industrial air filtration, delivering high removal performance for fine particulates. PTFE-coated filters are routinely employed in dust collection systems to remove particulate matter from gas streams, especially in environments characterized by elevated temperatures and heavy particulate loads. These media find use across industries such as coal-fired power generation, cement production, and steel foundries, where robust filtration is essential to control emissions and safeguard process equipment.

Candle burning involves the melting and consumption of wax, which reduces the candle’s length as the fuel is used. The tip of the braided wick bends into the flame and is consumed, and incineration of the wick limits the exposed length, helping to maintain a steady flame temperature and a consistent rate of fuel consumption. Historically, wicks required regular trimming of about 0.7 cm (1/4 inch) to promote an even burn and reduce the emission of black smoke. In the 20th century, specialized wick scissors known as snuffers were produced for trimming, often paired with an extinguisher. Modern candles are designed so the wick curves and is consumed as the candle burns, effectively trimming itself.

Candle combustion is self-sustaining: the lit wick heats the adjacent solid wax, which melts, vaporizes, and then reacts with oxygen to maintain the flame. The heat at the flame continues to melt wax at the top, and the liquid wax is drawn up the wick by capillary action to be burned, thereby feeding the flame and sustaining the burn. As fuel is consumed, the candle shortens, and the wick itself shortens as its material is burned away. Before the nineteenth century, wicks typically required regular trimming with scissors or snuffers to promote a steady burn and reduce smoking. By contrast, modern wick designs are intended to curve as they burn, with the end effectively trimmed automatically by incineration as part of the burning process.

Mehmed Kâmil Pasha left the service of Abbas I and joined the Ottoman administration in 1860 after spending a decade in Egypt. Over the following approximately nineteen years, he held a variety of administrative posts across the empire prior to his first entry into the cabinet. He directed or helped direct the administration of several vilayets, including Eastern Rumelia, Hercegovina, Kosovo, and his native Cyprus. He ascended to the office of Grand Vizier, serving from 25 September 1885 to 4 September 1891 under Sultan Abdul Hamid II. During his time in that role, he developed a rivalry with Mehmed Said Pasha.

Mehmed Kâmil Pasha was born in 1833 in Nicosia, Ottoman Cyprus. He was the son of artillery captain Salih Agha, from the village of Pyrogi. His paternal grandfather originated from Karakese village in Anamur, while his mother, Pembe Hanım, was also a native of Cyprus.

During the 1992 campaign, Gore was initially reluctant to join Bill Clinton's ticket as the Democratic vice presidential candidate. He had previously clashed with the George H. W. Bush administration over policy responses to global warming. Nevertheless, he ultimately accepted Clinton's invitation to run alongside him. Clinton later attributed the selection to Gore's foreign policy experience, his environmental work, and his commitment to his family.

From 2006 to 2008, as the 2008 presidential election approached, speculation about Al Gore's potential candidacy resurfaced. Gore repeatedly stated that he had no plans to run but did not close the door to future political involvement, leaving room for continued conjecture. The release and success of An Inconvenient Truth boosted his public profile, with director Davis Guggenheim noting that audiences treated him in a rock-star fashion. Campaign-watchers and party figures, including campaign chair Donna Brazile, speculated that Gore might announce a bid during the Oscars following the film's nomination. At the 79th Academy Awards, Gore and Leonardo DiCaprio discussed greening the ceremony; his speech appeared to hint at a run, but the moment was largely overwhelmed by music and he was escorted offstage, an episode later described as a rehearsed gag. After the film won Best Documentary, interest in a presidential bid intensified. Polls indicated that Gore remained a popular figure even without a run, ranking among the top Democratic potential contenders alongside Hillary Clinton, Barack Obama, and John Edwards. Grassroots draft movements formed hoping to persuade him to run, but Gore remained resolute and declined to pursue the presidency.

US Route 322 enters Chester from the northeast and briefly overlaps with Interstate 95 before crossing the Delaware River on the Commodore Barry Bridge. Prior to the bridge’s 1974 opening, US 322 relied on the Chester-Bridgeport Ferry via Flower Street to cross the river, a arrangement that frequently caused substantial backups due to limited ferry capacity. In response to the Chester Waterfront redevelopment and the expansion of State Route 291, the Delaware River Port Authority and the Pennsylvania Department of Transportation constructed direct-access ramps to PA Route 291 to improve waterfront access without using local streets. The ramps provide a westbound entrance and an eastbound exit to PA Route 291, enabling streamlined movement to and from the waterfront. Construction occurred from 2007 to 2010, and the new ramps opened in 2011.

Chester, Pennsylvania, developed as a major hub of heavy industry, manufacturing, and shipping from the late 19th century through the first half of the 20th century, with a wartime expansion that made it a regional boomtown during World War I and World War II as factories, docks, and shipyards sustained employment. The sustained demand for labor drew entrants from Southern and Eastern Europe and included African-American migrants relocating from southern states, shaping the city’s demographic composition. From the mid-20th century onward, Chester experienced a sharp decline in its manufacturing base and confronted a range of post-industrial challenges, including crime, pollution, and poverty. Financial distress led Pennsylvania to declare Chester a financially distressed municipality in 1995, followed by a formal fiscal emergency designation in 2020, and in 2022 the city became the 31st in the United States to declare bankruptcy.

During the 2000s, drum and bass expanded globally, giving rise to distinct scenes across continental Europe, North America, Australia, and Brazil. In Brazil, the local fusion style sambass combined traditional Brazilian rhythms with drum and bass, illustrating how regional musical practices shaped the genre.

Jump-up, a subgenre within drum and bass, has seen its promotion evolve alongside changes in media dissemination. Before the internet era, the scene relied heavily on pirate radio to reach listeners. In the contemporary landscape, promotion leverages online video platforms, including YouTube and Dailymotion, as well as blogs, radio, and, to a lesser extent, television. Music-focused social networks such as SoundCloud and Mixcloud have emerged as particularly effective tools for artist recognition, offering broad reach and rapid responses to new tracks. The music industry also employs podcasts as a format for record labels to distribute material and showcase releases. Collectively, these developments illustrate a shift from informal, pirate-based broadcasting to structured, globally connected digital promotion.

The Council of Europe promotes cultural cooperation and diversity through its legal instruments, notably the Cultural Convention of 1954, as well as a range of conventions focused on safeguarding cultural heritage. It advances these aims through its Centre for Modern Languages in Graz, Austria, and through the North-South Centre in Lisbon, Portugal.

Established in 1949, the Council of Europe is an international organization dedicated to promoting human rights, democracy, and the rule of law across Europe. Its online archive of speeches provides complete texts in both English and French, irrespective of the language in which they were originally delivered. The archive is searchable by country, by the speaker’s name, and by date, enabling users to locate speeches in a systematic and chronological manner.

North Korea's media landscape is dominated by state-controlled outlets. The main news provider is the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA). In Pyongyang, the capital, there are 12 major newspapers and 20 periodicals published, including Rodong Sinmun, the official organ of the Party Central Committee. The country operates three state-owned television stations; two broadcast only on weekends, while Korean Central Television airs every evening. In 2012, The Associated Press opened the first Western all-format, full-time bureau in Pyongyang.

Within North Korea, science fiction occupies a relatively marginal position in the national literary and media landscape. It is typically regarded as a secondary genre rather than a central tradition. Works in this vein depart from long-standing conventions that emphasize exalted portraits of the leader, instead employing exotic or futuristic settings that provide authors with latitude to depict cyberwarfare, violence, sexual abuse, and crime—themes that are notably scarce in other domestic genres. Science fiction narratives often valorize technological advancement and advance the Juche concept of an anthropocentric existence through motifs such as robotics, space exploration, and the pursuit of immortality.

The 2007 European heatwave was a period of extreme heat that affected most of Southern Europe and the Balkans. It began to affect Italy and Turkey on 17 June, and by 18 June it had expanded to Greece, the rest of the Balkans, Hungary, and Ukraine. The overall economic cost of the heatwave was estimated at approximately €2 billion.

During the 2007 European heatwave, Mainz, Germany recorded an average April daily high of 22.4°C (72.3°F). This value represented a deviation of +6.2°C (11.2°F) from the 1989–2018 April mean, the largest departure from the long-term average for any calendar month in the instrumental record. April 2007 was also the first calendar month with no measurable precipitation in Mainz since February 1959. A daily high of 29.4°C (84.9°F) was reached on 14 April.

Arohana of the Sankarabharanam ragam represents its ascending scale and is expressed as S R2 G3 M1 P D2 N3 S, indicating the use of specific swara variants in Carnatic notation. Sankarabharanam is the 29th Melakarta rāgam within the 72‑parent ragam scheme that underpins Carnatic music, situating it within the foundational framework of the system. The notation employs swaras accompanied by numerical indicators (R2, G3, M1, D2, N3) to designate exact pitch values, and detailed explanations of these conventions can be found under swaras in Carnatic music.

In Multani, the aroha (ascending scale) is rendered as N S g M P N S. In this notation, lowercase letters designate notes in the lower octave while uppercase letters denote notes in the higher octave, and an apostrophe placed before or after a note signals the corresponding octave.

Comparisons of development estimation software indicate that formal estimation models that are not tailored to an organization's context can yield inaccurate results. Consequently, leveraging the organization's own historical data becomes essential when there is doubt that the model's underlying relationships and parameter values are based on project contexts similar to those being estimated.

Forecasting disciplines tend to achieve higher accuracy on average when estimates are synthesized from independent sources, a practice that helps to reduce the impact of individual biases. To maximize predictive performance, it is advisable to employ a variety of estimation methods when generating the input estimates. When these independent estimates are combined, the resulting forecast generally exhibits improved accuracy relative to relying on a single estimate.

Minicomputers were an intermediate class of computing systems whose development was driven by advances in integrated circuit design, notably the 7400-series TTL ICs, which reduced size, simplified manufacturing, and lowered costs. This combination made them smaller, cheaper, and easier to produce than mainframe systems, enabling broader deployment. They found applications in manufacturing process control, telephone switching, and the automated management of laboratory equipment. In the 1970s, minicomputers supplied the hardware foundation for the computer-aided design (CAD) industry and for other sectors that required compact, dedicated computing solutions.

Minicomputers historically occupied the midrange segment of computer systems, with Tandem Computers distinguishing itself by producing fault-tolerant, large-scale machines designed for continuous operation. In 1997, Tandem was acquired by Compaq, and the merged company later formed through the Compaq–Hewlett-Packard merger in 2001. Tandem’s NonStop line was ported from MIPS-based hardware to Itanium-based servers, marketed as HP Integrity NonStop Servers, and, as with the earlier transition from stack machines to MIPS, the software from customer applications was carried forward without requiring changes to source code. The NSK (NonStop Kernel) operating system is now known as NonStop OS and remains the foundational software environment for NonStop servers. NonStop OS has been extended to support Java and to integrate with development tools such as Visual Studio and Eclipse. Following HP’s corporate split, the NonStop and DEC product lines were sold by Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE).

Regional and national music traditions typically do not exert significant commercial influence beyond their places of origin; however, they may gain international visibility when presented as a variant of a broader global genre. Illustrative examples include traditional music and oral traditions, sea shanties, work songs, nursery rhymes, Arabesque, and indigenous music. In North America and Western Europe, non-Western regional or national genres are sometimes categorized under the label “world music” for cataloging and market purposes.

The compilation of music genres and styles is not intended to be exhaustive, as new categories continually emerge with evolving tastes and hybrid forms. Gracenote lists more than two thousand distinct genres, illustrating the breadth and complexity of contemporary musical classification. Some classifications arise from ordinary music lovers who collaboratively tag and organize music, resulting in a folksonomy that complements traditional taxonomies developed by industry professionals. By contrast, many genre labels are crafted by record labels and other industry actors to attract new audiences and facilitate marketing strategies. Overall, genre classification serves practical purposes by helping listeners discover music and by supporting distribution and promotional efforts within the music market.

The Hammer retroazimuthal projection is a form of retroazimuthal map projection that preserves azimuths from a chosen center. In this system, a geographic point is specified by its latitude φ and longitude λ, while the azimuthal accuracy is anchored at a central reference defined by latitude φ1 and longitude λ0, establishing the baseline direction for all angular measurements on the map.

The Hammer retroazimuthal projection is a modified azimuthal map projection devised by Ernst Hammer in 1910. It is retroazimuthal, in that azimuths from any point on the globe to a designated center are represented accurately. Distances from the map’s center are proportional to the globe’s true distances, ensuring that radial scale reflects real geodesic separation. When the projection is used for a full-sphere presentation, the front and back hemispheres overlap, making the map non-injective. To avoid this overlap, the back hemisphere can be rotated 180 degrees relative to the front, though azimuths measured from the back hemisphere must be corrected accordingly.

Victor Navasky purchased The Nation in 1995 and became its publisher in 1996. In 1995, Katrina vanden Heuvel took over the editorship from Navasky, and in 2005 she assumed the publisher’s duties, succeeding him in that role.

Oswald Garrison Villard, the son of Henry Villard, inherited The Nation and the Evening Post in 1900. He sold the Evening Post in 1918 and subsequently remade The Nation into a current affairs publication, giving it an anti-classical liberal editorial orientation.

Tōnacācihuātl is the Central Mexican form of the creator goddess common to Mesoamerican religions. She and her divine counterpart Tōnacātēcuhtli reside in Ōmeyōcān, the thirteenth heaven, from which human souls descend to the earth. Tōnacācihuātl is associated with procreation and appears in pre-Columbian art near depictions of copulating humans. The Florentine Codex records that Aztec midwives told newborns they were created in a realm of duality above the nine heavens by their heavenly parents Ōmetēuctli and Ōmecihuātl. Tōnacātēcuhtli is her divine counterpart.

In Aztec cosmology, the dual rulers Ometecuhtli and Omecihuatl (also known as Tonacatecuhtli and Tonacacihuatl) embody masculine and feminine principles. Omecihuatl gives birth to a multitude of offspring in the Thirteen Heavens, and after these arrivals she bears a flint named tecpatl. The other gods marvel at this event, and their children cast the tecpatl away from the heavens toward the flint. The tecpatl then falls to Earth at Chicomoztoc, which translates as “Seven Caves.” From Chicomoztoc emerge about 1,600 deities known as the Nauhtzonteteo, who subsequently disperse across the earth, the sea, the underworld, and the heavens.

Certified Broadcast Networking Technologist (CBNT) is a credential conferred upon individuals who meet the certification's examination requirements. Regulated by the Society of Broadcast Engineers (SBE), the certification attests to a holder's competence with computer network equipment and their specialized applications within broadcasting. The CBNT designation is protected by copyright law, and unauthorized use of the title without consent from the SBE may result in legal action.

Certified Broadcast Networking Technologist is a certification within the Society of Broadcast Engineers’ certification program. SBE certifications recognize individuals in career fields that are not regulated by state licensing requirements or professional engineering licensure, and the credential was established to acknowledge professionals working in these unregulated fields.

Ingrid Haebler was a pianist whose career included extensive international touring. She is best known for a prolific series of recordings spanning from the 1950s to the 1980s, with particular prominence given to her complete cycle of Mozart's piano sonatas issued on the Denon label. This Denon Mozart sonata set is regarded as among the finest interpretations of Mozart's piano works.

Ingrid Haebler moved with her family to Salzburg at the outbreak of World War II, where she made her debut at the age of eleven and later pursued formal study at the Mozarteum under Professor Heinz Scholz. She graduated in 1949 with distinction for her Mozart playing, and her musical interests broadened to encompass late eighteenth- and early twentieth-century repertoire. In the same year, she was awarded the Lilli Lehmann Medal by the International Mozarteum Foundation.

A weir is a barrier built across a river that impounds water and alters the river's flow regime. These changes can affect the local ecology by modifying habitat conditions and sediment dynamics. Upstream of the structure, river velocity typically decreases, promoting the deposition of fine silt and clay on the riverbed. This siltation can reduce dissolved oxygen levels and smother habitats used by invertebrates and sites vital for fish spawning. After water passes over the weir crest, oxygen levels usually return to normal and may become hyper-oxygenated. Conversely, the increased river velocity downstream can scour the riverbed, leading to erosion and habitat loss.

In many countries, regulatory frameworks require the addition of fish passage facilities, such as ladders or bypass routes, to weirs in order to enable upstream fish to reach their spawning or feeding habitats. Unlike dams, weirs typically do not block downstream migration because the flowing water runs over the crest, allowing fish to pass downstream with the current. However, the altered hydraulic conditions around a weir can subject juvenile fish to injurious flow and turbulence. Recent studies also suggest that navigation locks associated with waterways may increase accessibility for a broader range of aquatic organisms, including species with limited swimming ability.

Two clubs were relegated from the Basketbol Süper Ligi after the 2021–22 season: Semt77 Yalovaspor and HDI Sigorta Afyon Belediye, each finishing in the bottom two positions. Consequently, both teams dropped to the Turkish Basketball First League and competed there ahead of the 2022–23 season.

The 2022–23 Basketbol Süper Ligi season was the 57th edition of the Basketball Super League, the top-tier professional men's club basketball league in Turkey, known in Turkish as Basketbol Süper Ligi.

University Club Tower is a residential condominium tower in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The structure rises to 446 feet, ranking as the fifth tallest building in Wisconsin. The tower is located in Milwaukee's East Town neighborhood, adjacent to the Lake Michigan shoreline.

The University Club Tower in Milwaukee was originally envisioned by architect Santiago Calatrava as a 25-story structure, but the proposal was canceled due to parking concerns and fears that it would obstruct views of the lake. The project was revived in June 2002, with groundbreaking taking place two years later. The tower was designed by Skidmore, Owings and Merrill (SOM) and developed by Mandel Group, a Milwaukee-based real estate developer, with J.H. Findorff & Sons serving as the general contractor.

Following the 2008 conflict, South Ossetia's economy became heavily reliant on Russian financial support, a dependency acknowledged by former president Edurard Kokoity who expressed gratitude a year after the war for reconstruction aid. By 2010, Russian contributions made up nearly the entire budget, and by 2021 their share had fallen to about 83%, indicating a measurable reduction in dependence on Moscow over that period.

In December 2015, former South Ossetian president Leonid Tibilov proposed renaming the state to South Ossetia–Alania to mirror North Ossetia–Alania, and he urged a referendum on joining the Russian Federation to create a unified Ossetia–Alania ahead of 2017. In April 2016, he indicated that the referendum would be held before August 2016. On 30 May 2016, he postponed the referendum until after the presidential election then due in April 2017. The name-change referendum reportedly garnered about eighty percent support in favor of the change. The presidential election resulted in Anatoliy Bibilov defeating the incumbent Tibilov. Moscow backed Tibilov and favored delaying the integration referendum, while Bibilov opposed delaying and supported pursuing the referendum sooner.

The name Việt, known in Chinese sources as Yue, exists in multiple linguistic forms: the Chinese characters 越 with pinyin Yuè, Cantonese Yale Yuht, and Wade–Giles Yüeh4, and the Vietnamese form Việt. In Early Middle Chinese, the logograph 戉, meaning an axe, was used as a homophone to render the name in oracle-bone and bronze inscriptions from the late Shang dynasty (circa 1200 BC). Subsequently, the character 越 came to express the name itself, and at that time it referred to a people or chieftain northwest of the Shang. By the early 8th century BC, a tribe living along the middle Yangtze was identified as the Yangyue, and the term was later extended to encompass peoples farther south. From the 7th to the 4th centuries BC, Yue/Việt came to denote the State of Yue in the lower Yangtze basin and its inhabitants.

The name Việt Nam derives from Nam Việt (Southern Việt), a designation traced to the Triệu dynasty era, also known as the Nanyue Kingdom. Việt originated as a shortened form of Bách Việt, referring to peoples in what is now southern China in ancient times. The modern syllable order Việt Nam first appears in a 16th‑century poem attributed to Nguyễn Bỉnh Khiêm. In English-language sources, the term Vietnam is listed in Josiah Conder’s 1834 Dictionary of Geography, Ancient and Modern as an alternate name for Annam. Annam itself began as a Chinese name in the 7th century and was the common designation during the colonial period. Nationalist writer Phan Bội Châu revived the usage of "Vietnam" in the early 20th century. Following the 1945 division into rival communist and anti‑communist governments, both sides adopted it as the country’s official name. In English usage, the two-syllable form is typically written as Vietnam, while Viet Nam remains the standard name recognized by the United Nations, by ISO, and by the Vietnamese government, which has recently endorsed the form Viet Nam over Vietnam. Previously, the hyphenated Viet-Nam was the standardized spelling recognized by all three Vietnamese governments, but that spelling is now obsolescent.

Never Ending Tour 2011 consisted of a United States leg in July and August, during which Dylan and his backing band performed 28 shows across 22 states. The schedule included a July 15 performance at the Orange County Fair in Costa Mesa, California, and an August 7 show at the Meadow Brook Music Festival in Rochester Hills, Michigan. In the fall of 2011, Dylan returned to Europe for a string of concerts, this time collaborating with Mark Knopfler for a European tour.

The Never Ending Tour is the commonly used designation for Bob Dylan's ongoing concert schedule, which began on June 7, 1988. In 2011, Dylan performed 89 shows as part of the tour. That year's concerts were organized into four legs, with performances taking place across Asia, Oceania, Europe, and the United States.

Psalm 95 serves as the opening portion of the Kabbalat Shabbat liturgy in Ashkenazic, Hasidic, and certain Sephardic communities. It is also recited in some communities on Shabbat Hagadol. In most communities, the first three verses of Psalm 95 are appended to the end of the weekday psalm designated for Shir Shel Yom on Wednesday, which is typically the preceding psalm; this setup makes Wednesday the only day of the week on which the song of the day combines verses from more than one psalm. The addition of these verses appears to be a relatively late development in the tradition. Some communities include them because of their inspirational message.

Psalm 95 has inspired musical settings by several notable composers across the early modern period. William Byrd included the psalm as the Venite in his Great Service, composed circa 1600. Thomas Tallis contributed a setting in the form of one of nine tunes in Archbishop Parker's Psalter (1567), a vernacular metrical psalter prepared for Matthew Parker, the Archbishop of Canterbury. In the German tradition, Heinrich Schütz published a metrical setting in the Becker Psalter, first issued in 1628, entitled "Kommt herzu, laßt uns fröhlich sein" (SWV 193). Later in the 18th century, Jean-Joseph de Mondonville crafted a grand motet on the text, "Venite, exultemus," in 1743.

Trinidad Pardo de Tavera’s father, Félix Pardo de Tavera, died in 1864. His uncle Joaquín, who was childless with Gertrudis Gorricho, offered to become the adoptive father of Trinidad, Félix’s son, and Carmen, known as Chiching. A royal order arrived in Manila to fill Félix’s post on the four‑person Consejo de Administración, and the appointment was offered to Joaquín. Membership on the Consejo de Administración was among the highest honors in the Philippines at the time, providing him with access to the top officials. Joaquín was subsequently conferred knighthood in the Order of Isabella the Catholic.
Trinidad Pardo de Tavera died peacefully in his sleep on March 26, 1925, in Manila. He was cremated, and his ashes were laid to rest beside his mother's grave in Paris.

ISO 22000 is an international standard that provides a framework for managing food safety across the supply chain. It is recognized by both the European Union and the United States Food and Drug Administration as a voluntary tool to help organizations demonstrate compliance with applicable food safety regulations. The standard is aligned with regulatory requirements such as EU Regulation 852/2004 and the FSMA Final Rule for Preventive Controls for Human Food, supporting efforts to satisfy these rules. Adoption of ISO 22000 is voluntary, not mandatory, though certification to the standard is commonly pursued to show conformity with established food safety practices.

ISO 22000 is an international standard that provides a risk-based framework for ensuring food safety across the supply chain, spanning farming, processing, manufacturing, catering, storage, and distribution. It employs the ISO high-level structure (Annex SL) to facilitate alignment and integration with other ISO management system standards, notably ISO 9001. In conformity assessment and auditing contexts, both ISO 9001 and ISO 22000 refer to ISO 17021 and ISO 19011. ISO 17021 sets out the requirements for bodies that audit and certify management systems, while ISO 19011 provides guidance on auditing practices for management systems. The detailed similarities, differences, and combined effects of ISO 9001 and ISO 22000 are discussed in separate sources.

The 2022 Finnish Cup is organized as a traditional knockout tournament without a group stage, marking the first return to this format since 2016. A record 314 teams participate, the highest level of participation seen since 2009.

Lugano is a city and municipality in the Lugano District of the canton of Ticino, Switzerland. It is the most populous urban center in Ticino and in the Italian-speaking region of southern Switzerland. As of December 2020, the municipality had a population of 62,315, with the urban agglomeration numbering over 150,000 residents. It is the ninth largest city in Switzerland. English pronunciations vary, typically loo-GAH-noh, with some UK speakers rendering it luu-GAN-oh; in Italian it is pronounced [luˈɡaːno], and in the Ticinese dialect the name appears as Lugan [lyˈɡãː].

Lugano ranks among the warmest locations in Switzerland, together with Locarno and Grono, and is characterized by a humid subtropical climate (Köppen Cfa). Average temperatures exceed 22°C, supporting subtropical-type vegetation and a deciduous forest component. Winters are relatively mild, while summers tend to be warm and humid. The area records rain or snow on roughly 98.1 days per year, and the mean annual precipitation totals about 1,559 mm (61.4 inches). May is typically the wettest month, receiving around 196 mm (7.7 inches) of precipitation, whereas February is the driest, with about 52 mm (2.0 inches) over roughly 4.6 days.

Amerigo Vespucci served the Spanish Crown from 1505 until his death in 1512, dying in 1512. He continued to work as a chandler, supplying ships bound for the Indies. He was contracted to captain a vessel for a fleet bound for the so-called Spice Islands, though that voyage never proceeded. In March 1508 he was appointed chief pilot for the Casa de Contratación (House of Trade), Spain's central trading house for overseas possessions, receiving an annual salary of 50,000 maravedis plus 25,000 for expenses. In this capacity he was responsible for ensuring that pilots were adequately trained and licensed before sailing to the New World. He was also tasked with compiling the Padrón Real (model map), drawing on information from pilots who were required to share what they learned after each voyage.

Amerigo Vespucci reported that he had returned from regions newly encountered on a voyage financed and led by the King of Portugal. He described the land as a New World, a designation reflecting its novelty to both his contemporaries and earlier generations. On 7 August 1501, the expedition anchored off the shores of the unfamiliar coast. The crew offered thanks to God through prayers and the Mass. Based on their assessments, they concluded that the new land constituted a continent rather than an island.

Transylvania County Schools, the public school district serving Brevard, North Carolina, operates two public high schools, Brevard High School and Rosman High School, as well as an alternative high school, Davidson River School. The district also includes four elementary schools and two middle schools, and it administers one charter school, Brevard Academy. In addition, several smaller private schools operate within the area.

Brevard, North Carolina, located in Transylvania County, hosts Halloweenfest on the final Saturday of October in downtown Brevard. The festival features enthusiastic costume displays and a broad slate of activities conducted all day, including live music, street performances, and arts and crafts, as well as the Flight of the Vampires 5K Run, a pet costume contest, a haunted house, and a ghost tour, among other attractions.

Open Tree of Life is an online, collaborative phylogenetic tree of life funded by the National Science Foundation, with its first draft released in September 2015 that encompassed about 2.3 million species. The project provides an interactive graph that users can zoom to explore taxonomic classifications, the underlying phylogenetic trees, and node information, and selecting a species reveals its source taxonomy and associated references.

Open Tree of Life was launched in June 2012, and its initial funding from the National Science Foundation consisted of a three-year grant awarded to researchers across ten universities. In 2015, the project secured a supplemental two-year NSF award, with the additional funding going to researchers at three institutions.

Kara Ahmed Pasha Mosque is an Ottoman imperial mosque in Istanbul. The courtyard is enclosed on all sides by the cells of a medrese and a dershane, the latter serving as the main classroom. The porch is adorned with apple-green and yellow tiles, while the east wall of the prayer hall features blue-and-white ceramic tiles dating from the mid-16th century. The 12-meter-diameter dome is supported by six red-granite columns. Of the three galleries, the wooden ceiling beneath the western gallery is elaborately painted in red, blue, gold, and black. The mosque stands as the last imperial building in Istanbul decorated with specifically designed cuerda seca tilework, with later structures employing tiles glazed under a clear glaze.

The Kara Ahmed Pasha Mosque, also known as the Gazi Ahmed Pasha Mosque and referred to in Turkish as Kara Ahmet Paşa Camii, is a 16th-century Ottoman mosque located near the city walls of Istanbul, Turkey. It was designed by the imperial architect Mimar Sinan and completed circa 1572.

On September 12, 2025, AT&T announced a partnership with Gigs aimed at enabling more U.S.-based technology companies to launch their own mobile services, with Klarna and Walmart's OnePay cited as beneficiaries.

As of 2019, AT&T Inc. was the world's largest telecommunications company. It was the leading provider of mobile telephone services, and it also held the position as the largest provider of fixed-line telephone services in the United States.
Jesús Enrique Velasco Muñoz (born 16 January 1972 in Madrid, Spain) is a Spanish former professional footballer who played as a right-back.

Sarnath houses a collection of temples and monasteries established by Buddhist-majority countries and regions, including Cambodia, China, Japan, Korea, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Thailand, Tibet, and Vietnam. Each site is constructed in the traditional cultural styles of its country, reflecting a range of architectural and artistic forms. The ensemble is intended to provide visitors with an understanding of Buddhism from multiple cultural perspectives, illustrating how the faith is interpreted and practiced across diverse societies.

Sarnath emerged as a prominent locus for Buddhist activity during the period known as the second urbanisation, roughly between 600 and 200 BCE, a time that saw the expansion of urban centers from the Mahajanapadas through the Nanda and Maurya empires. The development was supported by patronage from kings and wealthy merchants based in Varanasi, which helped sustain Buddhist institutions in the site. By the third century CE, Sarnath had become an important centre for the Sammatiya school of Buddhism, an early Buddhist tradition, and during the same period it gained recognition for its contributions to art and architectural achievement.

Graphs implemented as an adjacency matrix use a two-dimensional array to encode connectivity, with each row corresponding to a source vertex and each column to a destination vertex. In this scheme, the matrix entry at the intersection of a given row and column reflects the presence and cost of the edge from the source vertex to the destination vertex, while the attributes of edges and vertices themselves are stored externally from the matrix. This approach enforces that only a single edge cost can be recorded for any ordered pair of vertices, limiting parallel representations of the same directed connection.

Graphs with trillions of edges appear in fields such as machine learning, social network analysis, and related areas. To manage such scale, compressed graph representations are used to reduce both I/O and memory requirements. A variety of general compression techniques are applicable to graph data, with Huffman coding among those that can be employed. The processing efficiency of a graph can be influenced by the chosen representation, and adjacency lists as well as adjacency matrices can be processed using specialized methods to improve performance, depending on the specific application and access patterns.

Paul Fussell, an American social critic, examined a phenomenon he described as prole drift, arguing that cultural and educational changes gradually alter the markers of social status. This idea is developed in his 1983 work Class: A Guide Through the American Status System, in which Fussell analyzes how class distinctions are signaled through language, credentials, and consumption. He further expanded on these themes in BAD: or, The Dumbing of America (1991), where he contends that intellectual and cultural decline accompanies democratic trends in education and public discourse.

Dumbing down refers to the deliberate oversimplification of intellectual content across education, literature, cinema, news media, video games, and broader culture. The phrase originated in 1933 as film-industry slang used by screenwriters to describe revisions intended to appeal to audiences with limited education or intelligence. The concept denotes a revision of material to make it accessible to those with lower literacy or critical capabilities, though the degree and methods of simplification vary by subject matter. It is typically associated with a reduction in the development of critical thought, often achieved by undermining standard language and established learning benchmarks. As a result, it can trivialize academic standards, culture, and meaningful information, a phenomenon frequently discussed in relation to popular culture.

The 2010 referendum on a law governing Radiotelevizija Slovenija (RTVS) was designed to reverse the 2005 reform proposed by conservative prime minister Janez Janša, a change widely perceived as moving the public broadcaster toward the political right. The earlier 2005 reform had been approved in a referendum by a narrow margin. Pre-referendum polling for the 2010 vote suggested a similarly tight contest and anticipated low turnout. In the 2010 referendum, 55.3% of voters expressed interest in the ballot; among those interested, 28.4% supported the reform and 26.9% opposed it.

The 2010 Slovenian public broadcaster law referendum was decisively rejected by the electorate. Voter turnout was notably low, and analysts attributed this result to public fatigue with the high frequency of referendums held in the country.

Kappa (brand) traces its origins to Maglificio Calzificio Torinese (MCT), a Turin-based producer of socks and underwear established in 1916. In 1956 the company encountered a production problem with its Aquila brand. Once the issue was resolved, all new products bore a K mark, representing German Kontrolle. The marking coincided with a sharp rise in sales. In 1967 the K line was formally named Kappa, adopting the Greek letter kappa as its namesake.

Kappa, an Italian sportswear brand, has a long history of serving as a shirt sponsor for a range of football clubs. Historical partnerships include Juventus, AC Milan, and FC Barcelona, reflecting its prominence in European football. In more recent years, the company has sponsored OGC Nice, ACF Fiorentina, Genoa FC, and Kaizer Chiefs FC, spanning clubs in Italy, Spain, France, and South Africa. This pattern demonstrates Kappa’s broad international footprint in both past and present shirt sponsorships, underscoring its ongoing involvement in football branding.

During the 1980s and 1990s, financial technology experienced notable advances, including the spread of electronic financial services and the emergence of online banking. Michael Bloomberg founded Innovative Market Systems, which later evolved into Bloomberg L.P. and released the Bloomberg Terminal, a system that fundamentally altered how financial professionals obtain and interpret market information. The terminal supplies real-time market data, analytics, and news to financial institutions worldwide, supporting decision-making and analysis across global markets.

The Fedwire Funds Service, established by the Federal Reserve Banks in 1918, marked a milestone in the history of electronic money movement. The system utilized telegraph networks to securely transmit transfer instructions and settlement information among participating member banks. It enabled transfers between these institutions, contributing to more efficient settlement of interbank obligations and representing one of the earliest instances of electronic funds movement.

Google Question Hub is a platform that collects unanswered questions from Google search users across multiple languages, including English, Hindi, and Indonesian. The gathered inquiries are organized within the service under the acronym GQH (Google Question Hub). Publishers can use these questions as a basis for developing new articles.

Google Question Hub (GQH) is a knowledge-market platform developed by Google that aims to reduce the backlog of unanswered web search queries for content creators, including journalists. It gathers these queries through a set of proprietary algorithms whose exact workings are not publicly disclosed. Access to the platform is restricted to users with a registered Google Search Console account linked to a verified web property, a requirement that distinguishes GQH from Google Questions and Answers. By contrast, the general user base contributing queries only needs a Google account and does not require registration with Search Console.

The Times Literary Supplement (TLS) originated in 1902 as a supplement to The Times and became an independent publication in 1914. For many years its reviews appeared anonymously, a practice that continued until 1974. Under the editorship of John Gross, a program of signing reviews was gradually introduced, reflecting Gross’s belief that reviewers should assume responsibility for their opinions.

The Times Literary Supplement (TLS) has published essays, reviews, and poems, and has featured a diverse range of contributors, including D. M. Thomas, John Ashbery, Italo Calvino, Patricia Highsmith, Milan Kundera, Philip Larkin, Mario Vargas Llosa, Joseph Brodsky, Gore Vidal, Orhan Pamuk, Geoffrey Hill, and Seamus Heaney, among others.

Under the Arrhenius framework, acids and bases are defined as substances that form aqueous solutions containing specific ions. An Arrhenius acid such as hydrochloric acid dissociates in water to yield H+ and Cl−, whereas an Arrhenius base such as sodium hydroxide dissociates in water to yield Na+ and OH−.

In aqueous solutions, a common metathesis process is a precipitation reaction, occurring when two solutions containing strong electrolytes are mixed and yield an insoluble solid known as a precipitate. The ability of a substance to dissolve in water depends on its capacity to overcome the strong attractive forces generated by the water molecules, including hydrogen bonding and hydration interactions. When dissolution is unfavorable, the substance remains undissolved, and its molecules form a precipitate rather than remaining in solution.

The Enchanted Desna (Ukrainian: Зачарована Десна; romanized: Zacharovana Desna) is a 1964 Soviet fantasy drama film directed by Yuliya Solntseva. Based on an autobiographical story by Oleksandr Dovzhenko, a prominent Ukrainian writer and cinematographer, the film portrays his whimsical childhood experiences in a Ukrainian village along the Desna River.

Since World War II, the United States Navy has prioritized aircraft carriers as the centerpiece of its fleets. The Ticonderoga-class cruisers, built in the 1980s, were originally conceived and designated as destroyers to provide robust air defense for carrier-centered formations. By 2020, twenty-two of the newest ships in this class remained in active service, and the vessels have continually undergone upgrades that have expanded their capabilities and usefulness. Some units are equipped with ballistic missile defense capabilities through the Aegis BMD system. No new cruisers of this class have been constructed. In the 21st century, design work on larger cruisers provisionally designated as CG(X) emerged, but the program was cancelled in 2010 due to budgetary constraints.

During the early years of World War II, cruisers were involved in several notable actions. In December 1939, three British cruisers engaged the pocket battleship Admiral Graf Spee during the Battle of the River Plate; after raiding merchant ships, Graf Spee sought refuge in the neutral port of Montevideo, Uruguay. British broadcasts subsequently suggested that capital ships were in the area, prompting the Graf Spee’s captain to believe he faced a hopeless fight with dwindling ammunition, leading to the decision to scuttle the vessel. On 8 June 1940, German capital ships Scharnhorst and Gneisenau—classed as battleships but armed with guns more typical of large cruisers—sunk the aircraft carrier HMS Glorious with gunfire. From October 1940 to March 1941, the German heavy cruiser Admiral Scheer conducted a successful commerce-raiding voyage across the Atlantic and Indian Oceans.

Prolog includes special predicates that can steer the procedural flow during goal evaluation, granting programmers the means to influence how the program executes beyond pure logical deduction. The cut serves as a notable instance of such a procedural control mechanism. By contrast, deductive databases do not provide a corresponding mechanism to exert procedural control over evaluation.

In logic programming languages, the use of function symbols permits the construction of complex terms, whereas deductive databases exclude function symbols from their formalism. This restriction creates a clear distinction between deductive databases and broader logic programming, aligning the former with a more constrained, database-oriented approach.
Frederikus Quirinus "Daan" Klinkenberg (born 12 January 1996) is a Dutch footballer who plays as a centre-back for Lisse. He has played professionally in the Netherlands, Finland, Norway, and Sweden.
On 12 January 2019, Klinkenberg's contract with FC Volendam was dissolved by mutual consent. Subsequently, on 17 January 2019, he joined Finnish club FC Inter Turku, signing a one-year contract.

Austria competed at the 2012 Summer Olympics in London, held from 27 July to 12 August 2012. The nation has competed at every Summer Olympic Games except the 1920 Antwerp Games. The Österreichisches Olympisches Comité sent 70 athletes (39 men and 31 women) to participate in 17 sports. Compared with the previous Games, the delegation was of a similar size, with an additional one male and one female athlete and participation in three more sports overall. There was a single Austrian entrant in each of the following sports: eventing, fencing, rhythmic gymnastics, modern pentathlon, and Greco-Roman wrestling.

Austria sent a team of 11 swimmers to the 2012 Summer Olympics in London. The qualification framework allowed up to two swimmers per event who met the Olympic Qualifying Time, with a maximum of one swimmer per event achieving the Olympic Selection Time. Three Austrian swimmers were making their Olympic debuts, including Lisa Zaiser, a medley specialist, who was the youngest Austrian athlete at the Games.

Wuhan Polytechnic University (WHPU) is a comprehensive university with a broad range of disciplines, specializing in food science and engineering. It enrolls about 16,000 full-time students and participates in the development of agricultural products for processing and transformation.

Wuhan Polytechnic University is a provincial public university in Wuhan, Hubei Province, China. Its Chinese name is 武汉轻工大学 (Wǔhàn Qīnggōng Dàxué), which literally translates to "Wuhan Light Industry University." The institution is situated in the Evergreen Garden real estate development (Changqing Huayuan) to the north of Hankou, near Tianhe Airport.

According to the IETF language tag registry, two codes—egy-mdctrans and egy-Latn-mdctrans—are defined for the transliteration of Ancient Egyptian. The transliteration system identified by these tags is encoded in accordance with the Manuel.

Manuel de Codage (MdC) serves as a transliteration framework for ancient Egyptian that offers both a straightforward alphabetic transliteration system and a sophisticated electronic encoding scheme for representing complete texts. The latter encodes details such as the spatial arrangement, orientation, and relative size of individual hieroglyphs within inscriptions. This encoding approach has been adopted—often with modifications—by a range of software tools designed to typeset hieroglyphic texts, enabling digital representation and printing of inscriptions. Notable programs that employ MdC include SignWriter, WinGlyph, MacScribe, InScribe, Glyphotext, WikiHiero, and several others.

A Soldier's Play centers on Captain Richard Davenport, a black Army officer, a rarity within the force, who arrives to investigate a killing. Initially, local Ku Klux Klan members are treated as the primary suspects. As the inquiry proceeds, suspicion shifts to bigoted white soldiers. Davenport eventually reveals that the killer is one of the black soldiers under Waters' command. Waters' men despise him, arguing that he treats Southern black soldiers with disdain and contempt.

Sony Pictures Television announced in September 2021 that it would adapt the play A Soldier's Play into a limited television series, to be titled A Soldier's Story. Grier will reprise his role as Waters in the series and will also serve as an executive producer.

Jim Bankoff held senior leadership as AOL's executive vice president for programming and product development from 2002 until his departure in late 2006. After leaving the company, he transitioned into consulting, and in 2008 he became a consultant for The Huffington Post and SB Nation.

Jim Bankoff began his involvement with SB Nation as an early-stage investor and led its initial financing round. He subsequently became SB Nation's chairman and chief executive in January 2009, guiding an expansion of its editorial network and its pool of contributors. In November 2011, he co-founded Vox Media, the parent company of SB Nation and The Verge. As Vox Media's chairman and chief executive, Bankoff pursued a growth strategy built on acquisitions, overseeing Vox Media's portfolio of media brands.

The bishops of Durham functioned as prince-bishops, exercising extensive secular jurisdiction within the county palatine of Durham while remaining under the ultimate authority of the Crown. In 1075, Walcher, then bishop of Durham, was permitted to acquire the earldom of Northumbria, marking the inception of the bishops’ temporal powers. These powers expanded through the Middle Ages and were gradually restricted from the sixteenth century onward. Aside from a brief suppression during the English Civil War, the bishopric retained some temporal authority until the Durham County Palatine Act 1836, after which those prerogatives were returned to the Crown. The final institution of the palatinate, its court of chancery, was abolished in 1974.

Prince-bishops were ecclesiastical leaders who also held secular princely authority within the Holy Roman Empire. The suffragan sees of Gurk (1070), Chiemsee (1216), Seckau (1218), and Lavant (1225) illustrate such arrangements, with their bishops sometimes bearing the Fürstbischof title. Although these prelates exercised princely rank, none of these sees possessed reichsfrei territory. In 1951, the pope abolished all princely titles associated with bishops.

Guidelines for the Definition of Managed Objects (GDMO) is a specification that provides a framework for defining managed objects within the Telecommunications Management Network (TMN). It is designed for use with the Common Management Information Protocol (CMIP), enabling standardized object definitions and information exchange across TMN systems.

Guidelines for the Definition of Managed Objects (GDMO) provides the specification language used to define objects for a Management Information Base (MIB) intended for use with the Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP) through the Structure of Management Information (SMI). Both GDMO and SMI establish a hierarchical arrangement of managed objects and rely on Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1) as the formal syntax for their definitions.

The article surveys the linguistic conventions surrounding pre-decimal British coinage, focusing on howpence values were named and written. For amounts from two to eleven pence, the usual practice was to form single words such as twopence, tuppence, threepence, and thruppence, whereas other values were typically shown as shillings and pence or as two words, with hyphenation varying by context. When a single coin equaled a round number of pence, it functioned as a singular noun, as in a sixpence, and while phrases like a threepence could refer to the coin of that denomination, the coin was more commonly identified by its colloquial name, the threepenny bit. Distinctions also arose between the value and the coins themselves: three pence denoted the amount in pence, while three pennies referred to three penny coins. In British English, divisions of a penny could be appended to such expressions without a conjunction, producing compounds like sixpence-farthing that were treated as single nouns. When used adjectivally, these coin values took the ending -penny, as in sixpenny.

The Carolingian penny was a silver coin of fineness 0.940 and a weight equal to one two hundred fortieth of a pound. It was adopted by Offa of Mercia and subsequent English rulers, and for several centuries it remained Europe’s principal monetary unit. Through repeated debasements, coins of greater face value were developed as bullion content declined. The British penny stayed silver until 1797, when Napoleonic War expenditures prompted a shift to base metals for coinage. Even after the United States and many British Commonwealth jurisdictions moved to decimal systems, the term penny persists in informal usage.

The harbor is the southernmost harbor in the world, situated in Antarctica's Winter Quarters Bay at a latitude of 77°50′S. Its waters are not consistently ice-bound, and the harbor can be ice-free during the austral summer, depending on the level of pack ice conditions.

Harbors are coastal bodies of water that provide shelter and docking facilities for ships, and they can form naturally or be constructed as artificial facilities. Artificial harbors are typically reinforced with structures such as breakwaters, seawalls, or jetties and may also be created by dredging, a process that requires periodic maintenance to preserve navigable depths. One example of an artificial harbor is Long Beach Harbor in California, which was formed by dredging an area that had consisted of salt marshes and tidal flats too shallow for vessels prior to the early twentieth century. By contrast, natural harbors are typically enclosed on several sides by land, offering inherent protection. Notable natural harbors include Sydney Harbour in Australia, Halifax Harbour in Canada, and Trincomalee Harbour in Sri Lanka.

During World War II, 1944–1945, American servicemen formed groups to minister to members of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints on Saipan, with L. Tom Perry among those involved. After the war, a persistent military presence remained on the island, and these servicemen's groups continued intermittently in the postwar period until 1975. In 1975, full-time missionaries arrived on Saipan, marking the beginning of a regular LDS missionary presence there.

Within the Mariana Islands, The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints established the Yigo Guam Temple, with its groundbreaking ceremony held on September 4, 2019, presided over by Yoon Hwan Choi, who at the time served as president of the church’s Asia North Area. The temple was subsequently dedicated on May 22, 2022, in a ceremony conducted by David A. Bednar.

Bell Labs in the early 1970s was a focal point for programming language development and software tools. In 1972 Dennis Ritchie created the C programming language as a successor to B, enabling a flexible and portable systems language that supported the growing Unix environment. The use of B in a Unix rewrite reflected a pragmatic design ethos that favored functional utility over exhaustive completeness. That same year, Alfred Aho, Peter Weinberger, and Brian Kernighan at Bell Labs designed and implemented AWK, a versatile text-processing language that gained wide adoption for data extraction and reporting. Also in 1972, Marc Rochkind introduced the Source Code Control System (SCCS), one of the earliest tools for managing changes to source code.

Bell Labs, the research arm of the Bell System, played a pivotal role in mid-20th-century information science, most notably through Claude Shannon's 1948 work on the mathematical theory of communication published in the Bell System Technical Journal, which laid the foundations of information theory. The publication drew on earlier Bell researchers Harry Nyquist and Ralph Hartley, though it significantly broadened their ideas. Throughout the 1940s, Bell Labs also introduced a sequence of increasingly sophisticated calculators, illustrating the institution's engagement with computational devices. In 1949 Shannon published a paper on secrecy theory that established the groundwork for modern cryptography.

Within the Tobelos area, Tiana is the dominant language in the two Tobelos villages. The Tobelos communities also have speakers of Tabaru (Tobaru). In the Sarau village, Waioli is spoken in addition to Tiana.

The Tiana language, also known as Tobelo Tiana, is an under-documented language spoken in North Maluku, Indonesia. It is spoken in two coastal villages in Halmahery district, namely Sarau and Tobelos, with the latter located in South Ibu district of West Halmahera Regency. It is reportedly the product of contact between the Galela and Tobelo languages, indicating a mixed linguistic heritage.

During the development of high-performance computing, the ILLIAC IV's partial success was seen by some as signaling the future of the field, while Cray dismissed the notion, quipping that two strong oxen were preferable to a thousand chickens. By the early 1980s, several research groups pursued parallel architectures consisting of thousands of processing units. The Connection Machine, which arose from Massachusetts Institute of Technology research, exemplified this approach; its CM-1 employed as many as 65,536 simplified custom microprocessors linked in a network to facilitate data sharing. Subsequent refinements followed, culminating in the CM-5, a highly parallel system capable of executing billions of arithmetic operations per second.

Energy efficiency in supercomputing is commonly quantified as FLOPS per watt, expressed in MFLOPS/W. The IBM Roadrunner, in 2008, achieved about 376 MFLOPS/W, representing a notable advance in power efficiency for petascale systems. By November 2010, the Blue Gene/Q architecture reached roughly 1,684 MFLOPS/W, illustrating continued rapid gains in efficiency. In June 2011, the Green500 list’s top two entries consisted of Blue Gene machines based in New York, with one of them attaining 2,097 MFLOPS/W, signaling substantial progress at the high end of efficiency. In the same month, the DEGIMA cluster in Nagasaki ranked third on the Green500 with an energy efficiency of 1,375 MFLOPS/W.

Zico is a Brazilian former footballer who played as an attacking midfielder. He netted 48 goals in 71 official appearances for Brazil, placing him fifth on the national team’s all-time scoring list. He represented Brazil at the 1978, 1982, and 1986 FIFA World Cups, although the team did not win the trophy in any of those tournaments. The 1982 Brazil squad is widely regarded as one of the greatest Brazilian national teams in history. He is widely considered the greatest Brazilian never to have won the World Cup.

The 1983–84 Serie A season marked Zico's first campaign in Italy, when he joined Udinese to form a notable partnership with Franco Causio. The duo was expected to lift the club's profile and earned respect from established rivals such as Juventus and Roma. Zico's proficiency with free kicks had a substantial impact, with television programs debating strategies to neutralize his set pieces. Udinese finished ninth with 32 points, despite nearly doubling their goal tally from the previous season, and slipped three places from 1982–83. Zico scored 19 goals, one fewer than the league's top scorer Michel Platini, and did so in four fewer appearances due to injury. He was voted the 1983 Player of the Year by World Soccer Magazine.

Squadron (naval) refers to a substantial formation of warships that is smaller than a fleet and typically forms part of a fleet organization. There is no universal criterion that clearly distinguishes a squadron from a fleet or from a flotilla; the precise size and combat power of a squadron vary across maritime powers and historical periods. Some navies use the term flotilla to denote smaller groupings of minor vessels, or alternatively to describe small assemblies of major warships, reflecting overlapping terminology. The rank of the officer commanding a squadron likewise varies widely depending on the navy’s structure and the unit’s scale.

In modern naval practice, squadrons serve primarily as administrative groupings rather than cohesive tactical formations. They were largely abandoned as a tactical concept during World War II, as the demands of anti-submarine screening by destroyers and the requirement for air cover provided by aircraft carriers drove a reevaluation of how fleets were organized. This shift fostered a greater reliance on carrier battle groups or on ad hoc task forces assembled from available ships to execute specific operations.

The Perse School is a federation of three schools that together serve pupils aged 3 to 18. The Pelican provides nursery and pre-preparatory education for children aged 3–7 and is situated on Glebe Road, close to the main campus. Perse Prep offers preparatory schooling for ages 7–11 and is located near the Upper School, just north of the Long Road–Trumpington Road junction. Beginning in Year 7, most pupils move on to the Upper School, which offers GCSEs and A-Levels.

The Perse School partnered in 2018 with Rob Percival, a Cambridge-based education technology entrepreneur, to support the development of an online artificial intelligence–driven mathematics teaching platform. In 2019, Blutick, in association with The Perse School, exhibited at the BETT Show in London to launch a free beta version of the platform.

Gender studies traces the evolution of thought about gender by incorporating a range of perspectives and theoretical approaches. It analyzes how historical trajectories, cultural norms, and social institutions shape the distribution of gendered roles within different societies. Although it often centers on distinctions between men and women, it also examines variations in sexual differences and how they intersect with gender. In addition, the field critically engages with non-binary and other nontraditional definitions of gender, exploring how categories beyond the binary are constructed and understood.

Gender studies is an interdisciplinary field of scholarship that examines how gender shapes identity and the social representation of gender roles. The discipline traces its roots to women’s studies, which focused on women, feminist theory, gender, and political life, and it has since broadened to encompass a wider range of gendered experiences. It maintains substantial intersections with queer studies and men’s studies, reflecting its expansive scope and diverse methodologies. The field gained prominence in Western universities during the 1990s, as part of broader shifts in academic approaches to power, culture, and identity. This emergence coincided with the rise of deconstructionist thought, which influenced critical analyses of fixed notions of gender.

Urban planning in Taiwan constitutes the framework guiding infrastructure development and land use across the nation. It reflects a balance among swift industrial growth, the preservation of cultural heritage, and sustainable development. There are substantial efforts to coordinate comprehensive planning across administrative levels, encompassing designated districts, redevelopment areas, digital-city initiatives, and urban–rural landscape policies. The overarching aim is to reconcile modernization with community needs and ecological resilience.

Urban planning in Taiwan has produced large-scale mixed-use districts regarded as integrated urban models, most notably the Xinyi Planning District and the Xinban Special District. In Taipei, the Xinyi District was conceived in the 1970s and developed through the 1980s and 1990s; within a 153-hectare area it encompasses landmarks such as Taipei 101, the Taipei City Hall, the Taipei International Convention Center, and numerous department stores, collectively establishing the city’s financial and commercial core. The planning was led by the Japanese architect Kaku Morin, prioritizing coherent street grids, transit integration, and high-density vertical development. Consequently, the district functions as a powerful urban engine for Taipei’s activity and growth. Its branding—characterized by an upscale skyline and architecture oriented around branding—has helped cement Taipei’s identity as a globalized urban center.

In May 2016, Wanda Group expanded its entertainment portfolio by acquiring Propaganda GEM, an agency specializing in entertainment marketing and product placement, and Hoolai Games, a gaming company. Both entities were subsequently integrated into Wanda Group's entertainment arm.

Wanda Plaza is a retail property developed by the Dalian Wanda Group, the conglomerate that has a long history of involvement in Chinese football sponsorship. From 1994 to 2000, Dalian Wanda served as the primary sponsor of Dalian Shide F.C., which during that period was renamed Dalian Wanda F.C. and went on to win four Jia-A League titles, the top tier of Chinese football at the time. In addition to its earlier sponsorship activities, the group has maintained a major sponsorship role in the Chinese Super League since 2011, demonstrating its ongoing engagement with top-tier Chinese football.
