The increment, or step, may be any integer, allowing various spacing between iterations. When the step is negative, the loop advances from a larger value to a smaller one, enabling reverse iteration.

Blue raised pavement markers constitute a subset of raised pavement markers used on motorways to indicate the entrance to police-reserved slip roads. These slip roads are not intended for use by ordinary motorists and do not provide a through route for general traffic, serving instead as locations where police can park and monitor traffic on the motorway.

Blue raised pavement markers are used to indicate the location of fire hydrants. They are typically positioned near the center of the roadway, though offset to one side of the centerline, and may mark hydrants situated on the shoulder or at the curb.

Gulls belong to the order Charadriiformes. They drink both seawater and freshwater. They possess exocrine salt-excreting glands located in the supraorbital grooves of the skull, which release salt through the nostrils. This mechanism supports the kidneys in maintaining electrolyte balance.

Gulls are generalist seabirds that occupy a broad range of habitats and subsist on a varied diet. They are among the least specialized of seabird groups, and their morphology enables them to swim, fly, and walk with comparable effectiveness. They are more adept at walking on land than most other seabirds, a skill especially evident in smaller individuals, which tend to be more maneuverable while on foot. The walking gait includes a slight side-to-side motion, a characteristic that is exaggerated during breeding displays. In flight, gulls can hover and can take off quickly even from confined spaces.

Marsh's Library organized an exhibition in 2020 to commemorate the book's bicentenary, marking two centuries since Melmoth the Wanderer was first published. The exhibition was titled Ragged, Livid & On Fire: The Wanderings of Melmoth at 200 and examined the work's place in literary history and its continuing influence.

Within the narrative, Melmoth relates the Lovers' Tale to a companion, centering on Elinor, a young woman from Yorkshire. Elinor is jilted at the altar, her hopes dashed by the abrupt breakup. While the tale unfolds, she is tempted by Melmoth, who presents offers of aid, yet she ultimately rejects his help.

During the Battle of Rivoli, Quosdanovich realized that forcing passage through the narrow defile was untenable and ordered a retreat beyond the range of French artillery. Lusignan's Austrian column confronted a frontal assault from Guillaume Brune's brigade, while reinforcements began to arrive in the form of Gabriel Rey's division coming up from Castelnuovo and Claude Victor's reserve brigade. The fresh arrivals proved decisive, overwhelming Lusignan's units and forcing a collapse of the Austrian column; Lusignan fled westward with fewer than two thousand men remaining.

On the morning of Saturday 14 January, Austrian General Alvinczi engaged General Joubert's French division. He concentrated three Austrian columns between Caprino on the right and the chapel of San Marco on the left. The Franz Josef de Lusignan brigade advanced to the north of Monte Baldo, while troops under Peter Vitus von Quosdanovich and Josef Philipp Vukassovich pushed along roads on either side of the Adige. Before daybreak, French forces moved along the Rivoli–Incanale road, and Joubert launched an assault, driving the Austrians from the chapel of San Marco.

Ángel Luis Rodríguez made his international debut for Panama in January 1995, appearing in the UNCAF Nations Cup in a match against Nicaragua. He earned 59 caps for the national team and scored three goals. Rodríguez also represented Panama in 18 FIFA World Cup qualification matches. He was a member of the Panama squad at the 2005 CONCACAF Gold Cup, where the team finished as runners-up.

Ángel Luis Rodríguez spent a stint on loan with the Salvadoran club FAS in 1999, but left the team citing urgent family matters. He later denied any involvement in a fatal road accident in El Salvador and subsequently fled Salvadoran authorities. In the summer of 2005, Rodríguez joined Santa Rita, an Ecuadorian second-division club, to play alongside fellow Ecuadorian Juan Carlos Cubillas.

The Peace Preservation Law was enacted earlier than the Universal Manhood Suffrage Law, and the latter expanded democratic participation by extending the franchise to a larger portion of the male population. Nevertheless, even with this broadened electorate, civil liberties such as freedom of the press, freedom of assembly, and freedom of speech were still restricted, illustrating that the increase in democratic rights did not correspond to an overall expansion of individual freedoms.

During the 1924 political realignment in Japan, an alliance between the Kenseikai and the Seiyukai defeated the non-party government led by Kiyoura Keigo, paving the way for Katō Takaaki, the Kenseikai's leader, to become prime minister. As part of the coalition arrangement, the Seiyukai pledged support for the Kenseikai proposal to extend universal male suffrage to all male citizens aged 25 and over. The universal manhood suffrage bill was enacted in 1925 and took effect for the elections held on 20 February 1928.

On 9 April 1991 the Georgian Soviet Socialist Republic proclaimed its independence from the Soviet Union. In Abkhazia, voters approved the New Union Treaty in 1991, a result that Abkhazia cites in arguing that Georgia's de jure independence from the Soviet Union occurred without Abkhazia's involvement. Abkhazia further maintains that it was free to determine its own future.
On 17 March 1991, Abkhazia held a referendum on the New Union Treaty as part of the wider Soviet Union referendum, and the measure was approved by 99.06 percent of voters.

Ornithodoros moubata is a soft tick in the family Argasidae. Like other soft ticks, its mouthparts are located on the ventral surface and are not visible from above. The species lacks a rigid scutum and features a leathery, wrinkled dorsal surface bearing small nodules. It has no eyes and shows no suture line at the junction between the dorsal and ventral surfaces. The mouthparts are elongated and equipped with prominent backward-pointing barbs that facilitate penetration of the host’s skin. Females reach about 10 mm (0.4 in) in length, while males measure around 8 mm (0.3 in).

Ornithodoros moubata is a tick species in the family Argasidae. It is commonly known as the African hut tampan or eyeless tampan. The organism functions as an ectoparasite, feeding on hosts from the outside. It serves as a vector for relapsing fever in humans and for African swine fever in pigs.

Following the Mongol impact, central authority in Anatolia weakened, particularly after the Battle of Köse Dağ in 1243, which precipitated a loss of state cohesion. This erosion of power gave rise to a second group of beyliks, marking a new phase of regional polities in the peninsula. In the ensuing decades, the diminished centralized capacity indirectly facilitated the westward expansion of Turkic rule into western Anatolia, a development that had reached the region by the end of the 13th century.

Anatolian beyliks were Turkish principalities, or small kingdoms, in Anatolia governed by local rulers known as beys. The initial wave of beylik foundations occurred toward the end of the 11th century, signaling the beginnings of localized political authority in the region. A second, more expansive wave emerged in the late 13th century, prompted by the decline of the Seljuq Sultanate of Rûm and the subsequent rise of autonomous Turkish beyliks. In Turkish historical usage these polities are referred to as Anadolu beylikleri, while in Ottoman Turkish they are described as Tavâif-i mülûk; in English, they are generally denoted as beyliks.

In December 2021, the biotechnology company Cellevolve announced the launch of a clinical trial for progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML). The trial investigates BK virus–specific T cells (VSTs) as the therapeutic approach.

Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML) is a rare, often fatal demyelinating disease of the central nervous system caused by reactivation of the JC virus (JCV), a polyomavirus named for John Cunningham, whose tissue yielded the virus in its initial isolation. JCV infection is common in the general population, with serological studies showing antibodies in approximately 39–58% of individuals, indicating current or past exposure, while some surveys report higher rates in the range of 70–90%. The virus typically establishes a persistent, asymptomatic infection in about one-third of adults, as evidenced by renal shedding of the virus in urine. PML occurs principally in the setting of severe immunosuppression, when impaired immune defenses permit JCV reactivation and invasion of the brain.
Komarudin was an ethnic Korean who emerged as a leading figure in the Indonesian independence movement. He was known by his Korean name Yang Chil-seong (양칠성), with the Hanja spelling 楊七性.

The Korean community in Indonesia has existed for several decades. The Jakarta International Korean School, located in East Jakarta, opened on 1 February 1975. By 2007, its enrollment comprised 719 elementary, 357 middle, and 375 high school students. It is the largest Korean day school in Southeast Asia, with enrollment more than double that of the Korean day school in Ho Chi Minh City. A Koreatown began developing in Kebayoran Baru, South Jakarta, as early as 1982. In Kebayoran Baru, Kim Woo-jae opened a shop selling kimchi and doenjang.

Dana Point State Marine Conservation Area (SMCA) is a designated protected area within California’s network of marine protected areas that aims to safeguard critical nearshore habitats, including kelp forests, surf grass beds, and rocky reef communities, along with the species that rely on them. The designation also provides protection for intertidal invertebrates, among them Kellet’s whelks, top shells, limpets, sea cucumbers, and abalone. Extraction is permitted for lobster, sea urchins, and finfish under applicable regulations, reflecting a balance between conservation objectives and regulated, allowable take within the SMCA.

Dana Point State Marine Conservation Area is one of 36 new marine protected areas adopted by the California Fish and Game Commission in December 2010, during the third phase of the Marine Life Protection Act Initiative. The MLPAI is a collaborative public process designed to establish a statewide network of protected areas along California’s coastline. In southern Orange County, the initiative prompted the modification, updating, and reorganization of the region’s marine protected area framework, culminating in the designation of the Dana Point SMCA.

Progressive scan is a method used to scan and store film-based material on DVDs, with examples including 480p24 and 576p25. It was incorporated into the Grand Alliance's HDTV technical standard in the early 1990s, and there was an agreement that all film transmissions by HDTV in the United States would be broadcast in progressive scan. HDTV receivers then deinterlace by converting interlaced signals to progressive frames for display.

Progressive scan refers to a display method in which video frames are drawn in their entirety, generally yielding crisper images and enabling faster processing when scaling to higher display resolutions compared with interlaced video. A common illustration is upconverting 480p content to a 1080p HDTV, where progressive scanning helps preserve image clarity at the higher resolution. Modern HDTVs that are not based on CRT technology cannot natively display interlaced video, so the interlaced signal must be deinterlaced before scaling or display. Deinterlacing can introduce visual artifacts and may add input lag between the video source and the display.

18 Yellow Roses is a 1963 album whose title track achieved notable chart success in the United States during the spring and summer of that year. The single first appeared on the Billboard Hot 100 on May 11, 1963, reaching number ten and remaining on the chart for ten weeks. It also entered the Billboard Easy Listening chart on May 25, 1963, where it peaked at number five over a seven-week period. In addition, the song appeared on the Cashbox singles chart beginning May 11, 1963, climbing to number twelve over an eleven-week run. Furthermore, the track spent one week on the US Hot Rhythm & Blues Singles chart dated July 6, 1963, peaking at number 29. The album's other tracks consist of covers of recent hits, including "On Broadway," "Can't Get Used to Losing You," and "Our Day Will Come."

In an AllMusic review, Richie Unterberger praised the lead single "18 Yellow Roses" and its B-side "Not for Me," while offering a largely negative assessment of the remainder of the album. He described the title track as sounding like a rushed production rather than a deliberate artistic statement.

Ticket prices within the National Basketball Association vary widely by market and by the stage of the season, including preseason, the regular season, and the postseason, with some seats available for as little as about $10 while premium options can reach around $100,000; in 2022 the league's average ticket price was approximately $77.75.

During the 2009 season, the National Basketball Association faced a referees' lockout after the expiration of the officials' collective bargaining agreement on September 1, 2009. Replacement officials from the WNBA and the NBA Development League officiated the first preseason games on October 1, 2009, marking the league's first use of substitutes since the 1995–96 season. After negotiations, a settlement was reached between the NBA and the regular referees on October 23, 2009, restoring the standard officiating staff for subsequent games.

Single instruction, multiple threads (SIMT) is a parallel execution model in which multiple processing units follow a single instruction stream while maintaining individual state. In SIMT, each Processing Unit maintains its own local memory, enabling private data storage for every unit. The approach can allow processing units to have distinct stack pointers, thereby facilitating computations on entirely separate data sets. By comparison, SIMD architectures are characterized by arithmetic logic units that operate without a per-unit memory context and without a per-unit register file.

Within the ILLIAC IV system, the Burroughs B6500 operated primarily as the input/output processor, capable of issuing instructions to the Control Unit, which in turn disseminated those instructions to the array of Processing Elements. As an I/O processor, the B6500 had access to all PEMs, enabling coordinated management of data movement and control signals across the processing elements.

Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) is an international organization dedicated to making biodiversity data accessible on the Internet through web services. Data contributions come from numerous institutions worldwide, forming a broad base of biodiversity information. Its information architecture enables these data to be accessed and searched through a single, centralized portal. The GBIF portal primarily hosts distribution records for plants, animals, fungi, and microorganisms across the globe, and it also provides data on scientific names to support taxonomic reference.

From 2002 to 2014, GBIF administered the Ebbe Nielsen Prize, a prestigious annual award in biodiversity informatics with a prize of €30,000. Beginning in 2018, the GBIF Secretariat established two annual prizes: the GBIF Ebbe Nielsen Challenge and the Young Researchers Award.

Polyphony is a feature of many Sub-Saharan African musical traditions, and it is typically realized in parallel motion rather than through extensive counterpoint. East African groups display comparatively elaborate polyphonic techniques, while the Maasai employ drone-based polyphony to sustain a continuous pitch. The Dorze tradition allows for as many as six independent vocal parts, and the Wagogo are noted for counterpoint in their singing. Among the Aka, ostinato patterns combine with contrapuntal lines and yodeling. In Central Africa, singing generally remains in parallel lines rather than counterpoint. Burundi’s rural women are associated with akazehe, a two-part interlocking vocal rhythm. The San people use melodic repetition along with yodeling and counterpoint. In southern Africa, the Zulu and related Bantu groups typically practice parallel singing, and traditions from Tropical West Africa likewise favor parallel harmonies over counterpoint.

European polyphony developed prior to and during the period of the Western Schism. In this era, Avignon emerged as a vigorous center of secular music-making, with a lively musical life sustained by courts and public performance. The city served as the seat of the papacy, and later of antipopes, reinforcing its cultural prominence during the schismatic years. The thriving secular musical culture of Avignon contributed to the development of sacred polyphony, as interactions between secular and sacred practices helped shape the evolution of church music in this transformative period.

ISO 3166-2:MZ denotes Mozambique's entry in the ISO 3166-2 subset of the ISO 3166 standard. ISO 3166-2 forms part of the broader ISO 3166 framework, published by the International Organization for Standardization (ISO). The standard supplies codes for the names of the principal subdivisions of each country that possesses an ISO 3166-1 code, including administrative divisions such as provinces or states.

ISO 3166-2:MZ defines codes for eleven subnational entities in Mozambique: the city of Maputo and ten provinces. Maputo serves as the capital of the country, and within the ISO 3166-2 framework its status is designated as equivalent to that of the provinces.

OpenChrom is an open‑source software project that has earned notable recognition within its field, receiving the Thomas Krenn Open Source Award in 2010 and the Eclipse Community Award in 2011. Its development team includes founding members of the Eclipse Science Working Group, reflecting its close ties to the Eclipse ecosystem. After the commercialization of contract development and services surrounding OpenChrom, Lablicate reaffirmed its commitment to free and open‑source software. In October 2016, Lablicate released ChemClipse, which serves as the base for all OpenChrom products.

OpenChrom is an open-source software package for chromatography data analysis designed to enhance interoperability in mass spectrometry and chromatographic workflows. Because many vendors store analysis data in proprietary formats, cross-system comparisons and interlaboratory testing are hindered; OpenChrom addresses this by providing native support for a broad range of mass spectrometry data formats. The program enforces data integrity by preventing modification of raw data files, aligning with good laboratory practice. It also supports multiple open formats for importing and exporting analysis results, facilitating data exchange between platforms. In addition, OpenChrom provides its own open-source format, with the file extension .ocb, for saving edited chromatograms, peak lists, and identification results.

OSHA formulates safety and health standards within the Code of Federal Regulations and enforces them through compliance inspections conducted by Compliance Officers. Enforcement resources are directed toward high-hazard industries. Worksites may apply to participate in OSHA’s Voluntary Protection Programs (VPP); a successful application triggers an on-site inspection, and passing that inspection yields VPP status. Once a site attains VPP status, OSHA generally reduces routine annual inspections and typically limits visits to cases of fatal incidents or employee complaints, until the VPP revalidation occurs every three to five years. VPP sites typically report injury and illness rates well below the industry average, often less than half.

Physical hazards constitute a major category of workplace risks, affecting a large portion of workers. In the United States, occupational hearing loss is the most frequently reported work-related injury. An estimated 22 million workers are exposed to hazardous occupational noise, and annual expenditures on workers’ compensation for hearing loss disability are about $242 million. Falls remain a leading cause of workplace injuries and fatalities, with particularly high incidence in construction, mining and extraction, transportation, healthcare, and building cleaning and maintenance. Machinery and equipment introduce additional hazards due to moving parts, sharp edges, hot surfaces, and other dangers that can cause crushing, burning, cutting, shearing, stabbing, or penetrating injuries when used unsafely.

Behind the press gondola at the Bell Centre, seating is designated in sections 318, 319, and 320. These seats have dedicated scoreboards mounted on the back of the gondola, a configuration implemented because the main scoreboard is blocked from this vantage point.

Open since 1996, the Bell Centre is a prominent indoor arena in Montreal with a hockey configuration that accommodates 20,962 spectators. It ranks as the second largest ice hockey venue worldwide, behind SKA Arena in St. Petersburg, Russia. The venue has hosted a wide range of events, including major concerts and occasional mixed martial arts and professional wrestling shows. Since its debut, it has consistently been listed among the globe's busiest arenas and typically records the highest attendance of any Canadian venue. In 2012, it was ranked the fifth busiest arena in the world by ticket sales for non-sporting events.

Māori history is part of the broader narrative of the Polynesian dispersal that traces its roots to Taiwan. A synthesis of genetic, archaeological, linguistic, and physical anthropology evidence supports the view that Polynesian ancestors originated with the indigenous peoples of Taiwan, with language-evolution studies and mtDNA indicating that most Pacific populations descend from Taiwanese-speaking communities dating to roughly 5,200 years ago. From the Austronesian homeland, groups moved south to the Philippines, where some settled for a time, before some Austronesians sailed southeast, skirting Melanesia along the coasts of Papua New Guinea and the Bismarck Islands, leaving Lapita pottery remains and acquiring a modest Melanesian genetic contribution. From the Solomon Islands, some migrated into the western Polynesian islands of Samoa and Tonga, while others island-hopped eastward from Otong Java in the Solomons to the Society Islands of Tahiti and Raʻiātea (Havai'i, or Hawaiki). Through a sequence of migrant waves, eastern Polynesia was progressively settled as far as Hawaiʻi, the Marquesas, and Rapa Nui (Easter Island), culminating in the settlement of New Zealand.

Māori history includes genetic evidence for the origins and movements of the Māori within the broader Polynesian expansion. Analyses of the Māori-Polynesian autosomal genome indicate roughly 21% Melanesian ancestry and about 79% East Asian ancestry, reflecting mixed origins as Polynesians traversed Melanesia relatively quickly and allowed only limited interbreeding with Melanesian populations. Consequently, Polynesian groups show closer genetic relationships to Micronesians, Taiwanese Indigenous peoples, and East Asians than to Melanesians. The colonization process involved a founder effect and subsequent genetic drift, which shaped the genetic landscape of the Polynesian lineage. Additionally, about 40% of Polynesian DNA is shared with populations from southern Philippines, suggesting an ancestral connection during a phase in that region.

The Impossible Trinity, a central idea in international macroeconomics, asserts that advanced economies cannot simultaneously achieve exchange-rate stability, free capital movement, and an independent monetary policy. In the pre-1914 period, then-contemporary systems typically offered stable exchange rates with open capital markets, yet monetary autonomy was limited. Between 1950 and 1971, many economies implemented capital controls, restricting capital movement while maintaining exchange-rate stability and monetary autonomy. Since the 1970s, most advanced economies have operated with floating exchange rates and free capital movement, while preserving monetary autonomy, illustrating the enduring trade-offs highlighted by the trilemma.

Impossible trinity, also known as the trilemma in international economics, holds that policymakers cannot simultaneously achieve a fixed exchange rate, free capital movement, and an independent monetary policy. Empirical research testing this proposition has yielded results consistent with its constraints. Notably, a 2022 study examining the era of the Classical Gold Standard found that advanced economies' responses to international shocks aligned with the trilemma’s limitations. Similarly, a 2018 study focusing on Asian economies provided evidence that supports the trilemma hypothesis.

Following Japan's seizure of Manchuria in September 1931, the League of Nations dispatched the Lytton Commission to investigate the affair in December 1931. The invasion's pretext was the alleged bombing of a railway at Liutiaogou by Chinese soldiers, though it is widely understood that the Japanese army orchestrated the incident. This event, commonly known as the Manchurian Incident, led to the establishment of the puppet state of Manchukuo under Japanese control. Doubts about the truth of the incident persisted, including among members of the Lytton Commission, and later documentation revealed that Japanese military officers had fabricated the attack, a conclusion reinforced by records presented at the Tokyo War Crimes Trials. Manchukuo functioned as a puppet state, and the acts of Japan were regarded as unjustified aggression. When the League endorsed the Lytton Report in February 1933, Japan withdrew from the League of Nations. The case influenced the United States to articulate the Stimson Doctrine, which refused to recognize altered international borders achieved by force.

The Manchukuo Legal Advisory Journal consistently summarized the most recent rulings of the Supreme Court of Japan and the reasoning behind them, serving as a conduit between Japanese jurisprudence and local administration in Manchukuo, where although the legal system was heavily influenced by Japan, it nonetheless retained notable differences. In Japan, corporal punishment had been abolished, a change that ended extraterritorial rights for Europeans, whereas in Korea and Taiwan the practice persisted; Manchukuo, by contrast, maintained flogging as a major penalty, with judges frequently applying it to poor Chinese for minor offenses that would typically merit a fine or short imprisonment in Japan. In 1936, Ono Jitsuo, a Japanese judge working in Manchukuo, expressed regret over the use of flogging but argued it was necessary given the territory’s population—about 30 million people, many illiterate and impoverished who could neither pay fines nor endure imprisonment. While Japanese law held formal supremacy in Taiwan and Korea, judges there were still required to respect local family-law customs. In Manchukuo, the ideology of the five races—Japanese, Chinese, Koreans, Manchus, and Mongols—as political equals led to the existence of multiple family laws reflecting each group’s customs, alongside considerations for Russian and Hui Muslim minorities.

Lath art is a decorative woodworking form closely related to marquetry and intarsia. Like those techniques, it involves assembling pieces of wood to form representational images. However, while marquetry and intarsia rely on the natural grain and figure of the wood as a design element, lath art uses the directional arrangement of lath strips and the coloration achieved with stains to create its imagery.

Lath art is a form of woodworking folk art in which rustic pictures are created from narrow strips salvaged from plaster-and-lath wall structures. Historically derived from reclaimed building materials, the approach emphasizes the textured, weathered character of the wood. In contemporary practice, artists often incorporate lattice fragments, lumber stickers, and discarded weathered lobster traps as elements of the work. The subject matter tends to center on coastal and rural landscapes, with beach scenes and pastoral vistas among the most common themes.

The painting, titled Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II, is a 1992 oil portrait of Elizabeth II by Richard Stone. The work measures 96 by 60 inches (2,400 by 1,500 millimeters) and is hung in Colchester Town Hall, Essex. It was commissioned by Sir Robert Fellowes to commemorate Colchester Borough’s 800th Charter Anniversary. The Queen sat for seven one-hour sessions during sittings held from June 1989 to June 1990, in the Yellow Drawing Room at Buckingham Palace. The portrait was unveiled at the National Portrait Gallery in London and was subsequently presented to Colchester Borough Council in February 1992.

Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II, Realms Portrait is Richard Stone’s second oil painting of the monarch. It was first unveiled in 2015 at a reception held at St James’s Palace, ahead of the Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting that year. The portrait measures 74 inches by 48 1/2 inches (1,880 mm × 1,230 mm) and is part of the Royal Collection. In the work, the Queen is depicted wearing the George IV State Diadem and crimson silk parliamentary robes, attire that mirrors the presentation in Stone’s preceding portrait.

Levites are traditionally identified by patrilineal descent from Levi, with Levitical status transmitted from father to child only when the child is born to a Jewish mother. In situations such as adoption or artificial insemination, Levitical status is determined by the genetic father. Consistently with patrilineal descent, a Levite’s tribal status follows the paternal line, so a child whose biological father is a Levite is itself a Levite. By contrast, Jewish status is matrilineal, and to confer Levitical status under that framework both biological parents must be Israelites and the biological father must be a Levite.

In the account of Israel’s entry into Canaan under Joshua, the Levites are distinguished as unique among the tribes. Unlike most tribes, the Sons of Levi were allotted cities within the territories of other groups, but they were not permitted to possess a conventional land inheritance. Their portion is described as the Lord God of Israel Himself, a designation found in Deuteronomy 18:2. This distinctive status is reflected in Joshua 13:33, which notes the Levites’ lack of a traditional land allotment and emphasizes their special relationship to the divine.

Within Suffolk County, more than 350 properties and districts are listed on the National Register of Historic Places, including 58 National Historic Landmarks. In Boston, the southern portion contains 186 National Register properties and districts and 13 National Historic Landmarks. Two historic districts extend into both northern and southern Boston, comprising the 1767 Milestones. Additionally, the Olmsted Park System traverses much of the city, contributing to its historic landscape.

The National Register of Historic Places listings in southern Boston comprises the properties and districts within the city of Boston that lie south of the Massachusetts Turnpike. Boston as a whole contains a large number of NRHP listings reflecting its long history, architecture, and historic districts. The boundary defined for the southern Boston list mirrors the geographic division created by the Turnpike, with a separate NRHP listings page covering the portion of the city north of the highway. In Suffolk County, the remaining three municipalities—Chelsea, Revere, and Winthrop—are not included on the southern Boston page, and their NRHP listings are compiled on separate listings pages dedicated to those communities.

Addiscombe Military Seminary was established as a sister institution to the East India Company College in Hertfordshire. The East India Company College trained civilian clerks, known as writers, while Addiscombe served as the military counterpart to the Royal Military Academy at Woolwich and to the Royal Military College at Sandhurst, providing parallel military training within the same organizational framework.

Initially bearing the East India Company Military Seminary designation, the institution retained this formal title until 1855, a name that cadets disliked and which prompted its renaming as the East India Company Military College that year. After the government assumed control in 1858, it was subsequently renamed the Royal India Military College. In addition to the official titles, the establishment was commonly referred to by several colloquial names, including Addiscombe Seminary, Addiscombe College, and Addiscombe Military Academy.

Magnetic Ink Character Recognition uses IBM code page 1032 as an extension of code page 1001 by introducing additional encodings for certain characters. The extension provides alternate byte representations for four categories of symbols: transit (0x5C, 0x7A, 0xC1), us (0x4C, 0x61, 0xC3), amount (0x5B, 0x5E, 0xC2), and dash (0x60, 0x7E, 0xC4). In addition, a zero-width space is defined at 0x5A. These alternative encodings were added to improve interoperability with Siemens and Océ printers.

Magnetic ink character recognition (MICR) is a technology that enables automated reading of specially printed characters on cheques, a capability that underpins automated sorting within the national cheque-clearing system. MICR readers serve as the principal instrument for sorting cheques across the distribution network at several stages of processing. Merchants employ MICR-enabled readers to categorize cheques by issuing bank and to forward them to a clearing house for redistribution to the appropriate banks. Upon receipt, banks perform a secondary MICR sort to determine which customer’s account should be debited and to route the cheque to the correct branch as it moves back through the system. In many institutions, physical return of cheques to customers has been supplanted by digital handling, with cheques being scanned and stored electronically. Overall, the sorting aligns with the geographic footprint of banks within a nation.

Within its boundaries the City of London contains no large parks, instead preserving a network of numerous small gardens and open spaces, many of which are maintained by the City of London Corporation. The repertoire includes formal gardens such as Finsbury Circus garden, home to a bowling green and a bandstand. The network also includes churchyards, such as St Olave Hart Street, and features water elements and artworks integrated into courtyards and pedestrianised lanes, contributing to the district's urban landscape.

Several London Underground stations lie in close proximity to the boundary of the City of London. In particular, Aldgate East, Farringdon, Temple, and Tower Hill are all situated within metres of the City's perimeter, illustrating the extent to which the historic financial district is integrated with central London's transport network.

The single "People Loving People" was released on September 3, 2014, marking Brooks' first radio release since 2007's "More Than a Memory." On September 4, 2014, Brooks appeared on Good Morning America to promote the track and his world tour. Later that year, on November 23, 2014, he performed the song live on the American Music Awards via satellite from the Greensboro Coliseum in Greensboro, North Carolina.

In Wyoming, the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints announced its first temple, the Star Valley Wyoming Temple, on October 1, 2011, with the disclosure made by church president Thomas S. Monson. Later, on April 4, 2021, President Russell M. Nelson announced that a second temple would be built in Casper. A few months afterward, on October 3, 2021, Nelson announced a third temple to be constructed in Cody.

Wyoming hosts an established presence of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints across several communities, with two stakes located in Casper, two in Cheyenne, and two in Evanston. In addition to these stakes, the church maintains congregations in Afton, Cody, Green River, Gillette, Kemmerer, Laramie, Lovell, Lyman, Riverton, Rock Springs, Sheridan, Thayne, and Worland, reflecting a statewide organizational footprint.

Within the broad class of chemical substances, a chemical compound is defined as a substance that consists of a particular set of atoms or ions in a fixed proportion. Such compounds are produced when two or more elements undergo a chemical reaction to form a single substance with properties distinct from its constituent elements. Although every compound is a substance, not all substances are compounds.

Chemists designate chemical compounds by their formulas or by their molecular structures. The number of compounds that are synthesized, isolated, and reported in the literature has expanded rapidly, reflecting the vast combinatorial possibilities afforded by the known elements. As of February 2021, roughly 177 million organic and inorganic substances had been described in scientific literature and registered in public databases, including about 68 million defined-sequence biopolymers. The scale of the catalogued substances, together with many nontrivial names that are difficult to recall or cite accurately, poses challenges for tracking and referencing in the literature. International bodies such as IUPAC and CAS have taken steps to streamline these tasks. CAS provides abstracting services of the chemical literature and assigns a numerical identifier, the CAS Registry Number, to each substance reported in the literature; the information is organized in a database popularly known as the Chemical Substances Index. In addition to registry numbers, computer-friendly representations for chemical information, such as SMILES and InChI, are widely used to facilitate data handling and interoperability.

Pacific Blue Cross (PBC), including its subsidiary Work and Wellness, traces its branding to the former BC Life (British Columbia Life & Casualty Company). The organization offers a broad range of insurance products, including health, dental, life, disability, travel, and other health coverages, and serves roughly one in three British Columbians through both group and individual plans. In 2015, BC Business named it the fifteenth most loved brand in the province, and the following year it was recognized as one of British Columbia’s top employers. The company experienced a labour dispute in 2017 with CUPE 1816 over a new collective bargaining agreement, which was resolved in September with a six-year contract. In August 2018, John Crawford was appointed president and chief executive officer after the departure of Jan K. Grude.

Pacific Blue Cross is affiliated with the Canadian Association of Blue Cross Plans and traces its roots to the 1940s. It arose from the union of two predecessor organizations, the Medical Services Association and the Credit Union & Cooperative Health Services Society (CU&C Health Services Society). Both predecessors expanded over time and faced significant challenges, including the introduction of Medicare. In 1997, the two former competitors merged to form Pacific Blue Cross.

Private pensions in Australia are referred to as superannuation. The tax treatment of superannuation can apply at as many as three distinct points, contingent on the individual’s circumstances: at the time contributions are made to the fund, on the investment income earned within the fund, and when benefits are disbursed to recipients.

Australia's capital gains tax system imposes tax on capital gains realized on the disposal of any asset, though certain exemptions apply; the most substantial exemption relates to the family home. In addition, rollover provisions cover a subset of disposals, with a notable example being transfers to beneficiaries upon death. These rollover provisions function to prevent capital gains tax from acting as a de facto death duty.

Union of Chinese Nationalists (Chinese: 中国泛蓝联盟) is a political organization in China that advocates liberal democracy grounded in Sun Yat-sen's Three Principles of the People and aligns with the Pan-Blue Coalition's ideals in Taiwan. The group traces its origins to an online forum discussion held in August 2004. On 25 April 2007, the Taiwan Affairs Office of the State Council designated it an illegal organization.

The Chinese Proletarian Revolutionary Central Committee (Chinese: 中国无产阶级革命中央委员会; abbreviated Chinese: 中革中央) is a minor anti-revisionist communist party that emerged in the 2010s. It was founded by Zhou Qun (周群), and its leadership largely comprised former members of the Cultural Revolution’s rebel faction (造反派). Its core membership consisted of several dozen laid-off workers in Jiangsu province. The organization was suppressed by law enforcement authorities after police identified its online activities as provocative.

Doheny Drive begins at a residential cul-de-sac just south of Cashio Street near the Beverlywood neighborhood of Los Angeles, and then proceeds to run past Pico Boulevard through the Pico-Robertson district. The thoroughfare enters the city of Beverly Hills at Whitworth Drive and continues to cross Olympic Boulevard, after which it intersects a sequence of major east–west arteries, including Wilshire Boulevard, Santa Monica Boulevard, and Sunset Boulevard. The route terminates to the north of Swallow Drive in the Hollywood Hills West area at another residential cul-de-sac. In the segment between Beverly Boulevard and Phyllis Street, Doheny Drive also forms the boundary between the cities of West Hollywood and Beverly Hills.

Doheny Drive is a north-south street notable for its sparsely spaced traffic signals, which facilitates relatively swift travel along the route. Between Santa Monica Boulevard and Sunset Boulevard, the surrounding blocks are predominantly occupied by condominiums and houses. The road forms the western end of the Sunset Strip, whose eastern boundary is defined by Laurel Canyon Boulevard–Crescent Heights Boulevard.

Canada hosts one of the world's most developed networks of angel investors, reflecting a mature ecosystem that supports early-stage ventures. The National Angel Capital Organization (NACO), established in 2002, played a pioneering role in launching the angel-investing movement in the country and in fostering the formation of regional networks. Estimates from NACO and the Business Development Bank of Canada place the number of active angel investors in Canada at roughly 20,000 to 50,000. More than 4,000 of these individuals are members of 45 angel groups that are affiliated with NACO.

Angel investors are high-net-worth individuals who provide early-stage capital in exchange for equity, typically supporting startups at their inception. These investments carry extremely high risk and are often diluted through subsequent rounds of financing as the company raises additional capital. To justify this risk, professional angel investors seek outsized returns, aiming for exits that yield roughly ten times the original investment within about five years through mechanisms such as an initial public offering or a strategic acquisition. Those who manage angel portfolios generally allocate a relatively small portion of their total investments to such opportunities—commonly less than 10 percent. A substantial proportion of angel investments fail completely when the underlying ventures do not succeed. Even for deals that do succeed, the long holding periods and the need to absorb losses mean the typical effective internal rate of return across a successful portfolio is about 20–30 percent. Because early-stage ventures often cannot secure traditional debt financing, angel funding can be comparatively expensive, with bank financing usually not available to most young companies.

The hydraulic telegraph article examines an early hydraulically based signaling device. Aeneas, the author of a work on strategy, writes to find a remedy for a particular difficulty and introduces the hydraulic device as part of his discussion. He advances the topic only modestly, proposing a preliminary apparatus, but the device he describes falls far short of the requirements later telegraph systems would impose. This shortfall is evident from the description of the device itself and its apparent limitations.

Hydraulic telegraph refers to a signaling system comprising identical water-filled containers placed on separate hills that are not connected to each other. Within each container, a vertical rod floats, and the rod bears inscriptions at different heights along its length, encoding predetermined codes.

The 1996 FA Charity Shield saw Manchester United introduce two new signings, Jordi Cruyff and Karel Poborský, who made their Manchester United debuts. Neither Cruyff nor Poborský went on to have a particularly successful career at Old Trafford, and both left the club within four years. The day before the match, Lee Sharpe, one of United’s longest-serving players, was sold.

Dubbed the Littlewoods FA Charity Shield for sponsorship, the 1996 edition was the 74th occurrence of the annual season-opening match in English football. As is customary, the contest paired the previous season's Premier League champions with the FA Cup winners; Manchester United, who had secured the domestic double in 1995–96, faced Newcastle United, the league's runners-up that season. Held on 11 August 1996 at Wembley Stadium, United triumphed 4–0, with Eric Cantona, Nicky Butt, David Beckham and Roy Keane scoring.

Albert Bridge in Glasgow is the fifth crossing at its site. The first structure, known as Hutcheson Bridge, was built in 1794 but was destroyed by flooding in 1795. A second bridge followed in 1803, functioning as a timber footbridge. In 1834, a third bridge replaced the second; this masonry arch design was the work of Robert Stevenson, the grandfather of the writer Robert Louis Stevenson. The current Albert Bridge thus represents the fifth bridge to occupy the same location.

Albert Bridge, Glasgow, occupies the site of the former Stevenson's Bridge, which was removed in 1868. In the interim, a temporary wooden crossing was erected to maintain river access. The interim structure was ultimately replaced by the present Albert Bridge, completed in 1871.

Thirty-five teams took part in the qualifying group stage, including thirty entrants receiving byes and five advancing from the preliminary round. The stage ran from 11 September 2017 to 4 September 2018 within the FIFA Women's International Match Calendar. The teams were drawn into seven groups of five, with each group contesting a home-and-away round-robin. The group winners earned qualification to the 2019 FIFA Women's World Cup, while the four best runners-up, excluding results against the fifth-placed team, advanced to the play-offs.

During the qualification process for the 2019 FIFA Women's World Cup, more than thirty national associations did not enter the competition, opting not to participate in the qualifying rounds. The majority of these non-participants originated from Asia and Africa, reflecting regional disparities in participation. Among the examples are Saudi Arabia, Tunisia, and Egypt. Notably, these nations had men's teams that qualified for the 2018 FIFA World Cup, illustrating a divergence between participation in the women's and men's global events.

Peter Drucker graduated from Döbling Gymnasium in 1927. In the aftermath of World War I, Vienna offered few opportunities, prompting Drucker to relocate to Hamburg, Germany. There, he began an apprenticeship at an established cotton trading firm and also worked as a journalist for Der Österreichische Volkswirt (The Austrian Economist) in Hamburg. He later moved to Frankfurt, where he was employed by the Daily Frankfurter General-Anzeiger. In 1931, Drucker earned a doctorate in international law and public law from Goethe University Frankfurt.

Peter Drucker’s trajectory as a business thinker accelerated in 1942 when his writings on politics and society earned him access to General Motors, then one of the world’s largest companies. His European experiences had left him fascinated by questions of authority, a curiosity he discussed with Donaldson Brown, GM’s head of administrative controls. In 1943 Brown invited him to undertake a “political audit,” described as a two-year social-scientific analysis of GM. Drucker attended every GM board meeting, conducted extensive interviews with employees, and analyzed GM’s production and decision-making processes to assess how authority and governance shaped the firm’s operations.

This article presents a complete listing of the National Register of Historic Places entries in Brown County, Texas. Brown County is home to six NRHP-listed properties. Of these, two are also designated as Recorded Texas Historic Landmarks, and one NRHP-listed property includes two RTHLs.

Xiangfan College originated in 1998 through the merger of Xiangyang Normal Senior Vocational School, Xiangfan Vocational University, and Xiangfan Education College. In 2000, the institution integrated the Hubei Provincial Arts and Crafts School, broadening its academic offerings. Four years later, in 2012, it was renamed Hubei Letters and Science College, signifying a major rebranding within the provincial higher education system.

Hubei University of Arts and Science (Chinese: 湖北文理学院; literally Hubei Letters and Science College) is a provincial public undergraduate college located in Xiangyang, Hubei Province, China. It operates under the auspices of the Hubei provincial government and is sponsored by the Hubei Provincial People's Government. Despite its English name, the institution has not been granted university status by the Ministry of Education of China.

Virgin America Inc. was a low-cost airline headquartered in Burlingame, California, in the San Francisco Bay Area. The carrier pursued a model that combined affordable fares with enhanced service quality, linking West Coast cities to other major metropolitan areas through its routes. It operated both domestic and international flights. The airline’s primary hubs were San Francisco International Airport and Los Angeles International Airport, while it sustained smaller focus-city operations at Dallas Love Field and New York’s John F. Kennedy International Airport.

Subsequent to Alaska Airlines’ integration of Virgin America, the Virgin America Airbus fleet was reconfigured to provide at least three rows designated as Main Cabin Select. Historically, the emergency exit row, and in the A320 fleet the second row, were counted as part of Main Cabin Select. With the completion of the integration, these seats were reclassified as preferred seating with extra legroom rather than Main Cabin Select.

In June 2022, workers at the Buchanan Street Apple Store in Glasgow joined GMB Scotland and filed for unionization, marking the first attempt to organize a UK Apple retail location. Subsequently, in November 2022, Apple voluntarily recognized the Glasgow-based union. On February 8, 2023, Apple and the Glasgow store reached a collective agreement, the first such agreement with an Apple store in the United Kingdom.

On April 20, 2022, an Apple Store at Cumberland Mall in Atlanta, Georgia, with 107 employees, filed a petition with the National Labor Relations Board seeking union recognition. Workers had gathered authorization cards from roughly 70% of the store’s staff, well above the 30% threshold required to move forward with an election. The organizing effort was led by Derrick Bowles and Sydney Rhodes and identifies itself as the Apple Workers Union. A vote was scheduled for June 2, 2022, but was withdrawn following allegations of intimidation against employees. In December of that year, the National Labor Relations Board corroborated that Apple had violated federal labor law in relation to the organizing campaign.

Magtanggol C. Gunigundo is a Filipino government official and politician who served as the sole chair of the Presidential Commission on Good Government (PCGG) during the term of President Fidel V. Ramos. He is the father of Magtanggol T. Gunigundo, a former congressman from Valenzuela. During his PCGG tenure, there was an attempted 1993 compromise with Imelda Marcos regarding partial restitution of the Marcoses' wealth, but the proposal did not materialize.

Lauren Ancel Meyers is an American biologist specializing in integrative biology. She holds the Denton A. Cooley Centennial Professorship in Zoology at the University of Texas at Austin. She is a member of the Santa Fe Institute's External Faculty.

Lauren Meyers earned a Bachelor of Arts magna cum laude in mathematics and philosophy at Harvard University in 1996, and subsequently received a Doctor of Philosophy in biological sciences from Stanford University in 2000. She then undertook a two-year postdoctoral appointment funded by the National Science Foundation.

John Resig earned a bachelor’s degree in computer science from the Rochester Institute of Technology in 2005. He later collaborated with Ankur Teredesai on data mining of instant messaging networks, examining patterns within such communication networks. Resig also partnered with Jon Schull to explore novel approaches for encouraging real-time online collaboration.

John Resig is a software developer notable for his work on the jQuery project. As of 2011, he was employed as an application developer at Khan Academy. Prior to that, he worked as a JavaScript tool developer for the Mozilla Corporation. He was inducted into the Rochester Institute of Technology's Innovation Hall of Fame on April 30, 2010, in recognition of his contributions to jQuery.

Located in Los Angeles, the Skirball Cultural Center grew out of the earlier Skirball Museum, established in 1972 at the Hebrew Union College-Jewish Institute of Religion. Following the completion of the Skirball Cultural Center, the museum relocated there and formed its core presenting program, Visions and Values: Jewish Life from Antiquity to America, which traces the history, experiences, and values of Jewish communities over roughly four millennia. The exhibition draws on rotating displays drawn from the Skirball’s collection and is housed in galleries that feature multimedia installations, rare artifacts, historical documents and photographs, fine art, interactive computer stations, and sound recordings. It guides visitors through the trajectory of the Jewish people, concluding with experiences in the United States.

The Skirball Cultural Center is a family-oriented discovery center that serves approximately 60,000 schoolchildren and teachers each year. Its visitors come from virtually every religious and ethnic background in Southern California. The center features interactive experiences, including a simulated dig site and a field tent, and provides information about the archaeology of ancient Israel and the Near East.

Maxine M. Chesney served as a judge on the San Francisco Municipal Court from 1979 to 1983. In 1983 she was appointed to the Superior Court of California, City and County of San Francisco, and after subsequent elections she continued to serve on the bench until 1995.
Maxine Mackler Chesney (born October 29, 1942) is a senior United States district judge on the United States District Court for the Northern District of California.

Chroma in the cylindrical color spaces CIE LCh(ab) and CIE LCh(uv) is more closely aligned with perceptual linearity, such that changes in chroma track more uniformly with perceived colorfulness. However, chroma in these spaces does not scale linearly with the linear mixing of the underlying color components, so straightforward color component blending yields non‑proportional changes in chroma. Consequently, chroma as defined in the CIE 1976 Lab and LUV color spaces differs considerably from the traditional notion of saturation, reflecting a distinction between perceptual colorfulness and saturation within these models.

Colorfulness refers to the perceived vividness of a color, defined as the colorfulness of an area in relation to its brightness and capturing how far its light departs from white. For objects with fixed spectral reflectance, saturation remains approximately constant across different illumination levels. This approximate constancy generally holds across a wide range of brightness, with deviations occurring only at very high brightness levels where saturation may change.

Armada is a ski equipment company that positions itself as the skiing industry's first rider-owned and rider-operated manufacturer. It works closely with professional skiers who help design products and receive equity in the firm. The brand gained public recognition largely through its association with Tanner Hall, a multiple-time Winter X Games champion and one of its founders. Armada is credited with influencing the mainstream perception of skiing toward a younger, more dynamic direction, aided by its distinctive graphics and marketing approach. The company runs online stores in the United States, Canada, France, and Germany, and in 2011 announced a partnership with Gore, the fabric specialist.

Armada is a United States-based ski equipment manufacturer headquartered in Park City, Utah. The company operates a European office in Innsbruck, Austria. Its product lineup encompasses skis, ski boots, poles, technical outerwear, and other skiing-related soft goods. Armada's products are marketed in more than 40 countries worldwide, with distribution managed through a network that includes wholly owned subsidiaries and external distributors.

Elizabeth Pennisi is a science journalist who began her career in the public relations office of a university, writing for the institution’s science magazine, and briefly worked for United Press International. She joined the journal Science in 1996 and was promoted to editor in 2007, and she also contributes to Science News. Pennisi was the recipient of the 1996 James T. Grady–James H. Stack Award for Interpreting Chemistry.
Elizabeth Pennisi completed a bachelor's degree in biology at Cornell University and earned a master's degree in science writing from Boston University.

An urban settlement is an officially recognized designation that identifies a particular category of urban locality. The designation is applied in some African republics, including those in Southern Africa.

An urban settlement refers to a localized, densely developed community that forms a constituent part of an urban area. It is typified by a high density of built environments and man-made structures, reflecting substantial human settlement within a relatively compact space.

Franz Kafka is widely regarded as a major figure in 20th-century literature. His writings are frequently interpreted as examining alienation, existential anxiety, guilt, and the sense of absurdity that characterizes modern existence. Among his best-known works are The Metamorphosis, a novella published in 1915; The Trial, a novel published in 1924; and The Castle, a novel published in 1926.

German literature denotes the body of literary works written in the German language. It encompasses texts produced in Germany and Austria, the German-speaking areas of Switzerland and Belgium, as well as in Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, and South Tyrol in northern Italy. To a lesser extent, it also includes writings generated by the German diaspora outside these core regions. In the modern period, the predominant form of the language in which such literature is written is Standard German, though various currents incorporate dialectal elements to differing degrees, with Alemannic cited as an example.

The New York Law Journal is a legal daily newspaper published in New York. It is issued Monday through Friday, with publication suspended on February 20 in observance of Presidents' Day. The publication reports a circulation of 11,450 and claims to be the highest-circulation legal daily newspaper in the United States. Its website maintains 3,500 paid subscribers.

The New York Law Journal is a newspaper published Monday through Friday that provides daily coverage of civil and criminal cases from state and federal courts. It covers news relating to court administration, law firms of all sizes, elected officials, government offices, law schools, nonprofit agencies, in-house legal departments, and bar associations, and it also features analysis and insight in columns authored by leading professionals. The publication serves as the official publication for the First and Second Judicial Departments, and it issues special editions, including the NYLJ 100 rankings of New York's 100 largest law firms.

TeleCD-i was developed through a 1992 collaboration between Philips and CDMATICS to connect the CD-i player to data networks, enabling data communication and rich media presentation over PSTN and, later, the Internet. Early adopters included Albert Heijn and Neckermann, which launched award-winning TeleCD-i applications for home shopping and home delivery. CDMATICS also produced the Philips TeleCD-i Assistant and accompanying tools to assist the global multimedia industry in developing and implementing TeleCD-i solutions. At its introduction, TeleCD-i was regarded as the world’s first networked multimedia application. In 1996, Philips acquired the source code rights from CDMATICS.

Philips released CD-i adaptations of popular television game shows, including Jeopardy!, hosted by Alex Trebek; Name That Tune, hosted by Bob Goen; and The Joker's Wild, which appeared in two versions—a adult edition hosted by Wink Martindale and a children’s edition hosted by Marc Summers. In North America, all CD-i game releases featured announcer Charlie O'Donnell, with the exception of Name That Tune. Additionally, the Netherlands released its own version of Lingo in 1994.

Aviation law has historically exhibited fragmentation in international regulation, with significant divergence among states in governing cross-border air transport. This lack of uniformity particularly affected the liability regime applicable to international carriers, generating legal uncertainty for passengers, shippers, and insurers when flights traversed multiple jurisdictions. In response to these inconsistencies, the Warsaw Convention of 1929 established a standardized, internationally applicable framework for carriage by air, introducing uniform rules on liability and damages in international air transport and marking a pivotal development in the regulation of airline liability.

The Air Navigation Act 1920, enacted by the Parliament of the United Kingdom, established the legal framework for governing air navigation and related aviation activities. This legislation laid the groundwork for the regulation of aviation throughout the United Kingdom and its colonies, shaping the early structure of aviation law and governance in British territories.

Name recognition refers to the cognitive ability of citizens to identify a political candidate by name, a factor that can influence voting behavior and the selection of a candidate. Exposure to a candidate’s name can enhance perceived likability even when recognition occurs without conscious awareness. The recognition heuristic describes how voters may rely on name familiarity as a shortcut for deciding whom to support. Recognition may arise deliberately or through subliminal messaging and advertising, making it possible for recognition to operate below the level of conscious awareness. This phenomenon also contributes to the incumbency effect by aiding the reelection prospects of current officeholders. In a study by Cindy D. Kam and Elizabeth J. Zechmeister, three days of subliminal exposure to a candidate’s name increased supporters for that candidate. Taken together, these factors help explain why political campaigns devote substantial resources to building name familiarity, and there is evidence of positive effects when recognition is achieved.

Online advertising is used by political campaigns to raise exposure and garner support by presenting a candidate to a broad audience. It is comparatively low-cost and capable of reaching large numbers quickly, with technology enabling targeting of voters by demographic factors such as age and racial background. By increasing the visibility of a candidate’s name, such efforts can broaden recognition across a wider electorate and potentially contribute to electoral success. Nevertheless, online campaigns do not guarantee a victory, as voters are exposed to numerous ads from multiple contenders. In sum, while digital advertising is an efficient means of promoting name recognition, its overall effect on election outcomes is typically modest.

Non-fiction refers to a broad category of prose that aims to report factual information and real-world detail, as opposed to fictional narratives. It includes a wide range of reference works that provide systematically organized data and authoritative material. Examples of such reference materials include almanacs, encyclopaedias, atlases, bibliographies, chronicles, consumer reports, dictionaries, thesauri, business or telephone directories, handbooks, yearbooks, and collections of quotations.

Non-fiction denotes a broad category of content that presents real information and events rather than fictional narrative. In print and broadcast media, it includes news reporting, editorials, and letters from readers, as well as various opinion writings that advocate a particular viewpoint based on real-world facts. It also encompasses manifestos published by organizations and public notices or announcements intended to inform audiences. In audiovisual media, non-fiction manifests as documentary films and factual television programming that document real subjects and phenomena. Overall, non-fiction aims to convey verifiable information and real-life situations, though it may intersect with interpretation and advocacy depending on the context and form.

ISO/IEC 27000 outlines the purpose, scope, and terminology of information security management systems (ISMS). An ISMS is a management framework designed to systematically identify, assess, and address information security risks through appropriate controls within an organization, a concept that is broadly analogous to other management system standards such as ISO 9000 for quality management and ISO 14000 for environmental management. The core aim of the standard is to bring information security under explicit, visible management oversight, thereby ensuring governance, accountability, and continual improvement of an organization’s information security practices.

ISO/IEC 27000 forms the foundational element of the ISO/IEC 27000 family and is designed to standardize the terminology used in information security. The field features terminology that is complex and continually evolving, and many authors do not supply precise definitions. This lack of precision is problematic in standards contexts, as it can generate confusion and undermine the value of formal assessment and certification. By providing a consistent vocabulary and framing the scope of the series, the base standard seeks to address these issues, in a manner analogous to ISO 9000 for quality management and ISO 14000 for environmental management.

Following the 1996 constitutional reform, Morocco established a bicameral Parliament comprising two chambers. The lower chamber, the Assembly of Representatives of Morocco (Majlis an-Nuwwâb / Assemblée des Répresentants), is composed of 395 members who are elected for five-year terms. Of these seats, 305 are filled through multi-seat constituencies, while the remaining 90 are elected from national lists intended to ensure representation of women and youth.

Morocco is a constitutional monarchy with a Parliament and an independent judiciary. The 2011 constitutional reforms reduced the king’s executive powers while expanding the authority of the prime minister. The monarch nonetheless retains ceremonial prerogatives and acts as both the secular political leader and Amir al-Mu'minin, a title denoting the Commander of the Faithful and his claimed descent from the Prophet Muhammad. He chairs the Council of Ministers and designates the prime minister from the party with the largest representation in Parliament, while, on the prime minister’s advice, he appoints the government’s ministers.

The Rossio railway station features a Neo-Manueline façade that dominates the northwest side of the square, embodying a Romantic reinterpretation of the Manueline style typical of early 16th-century Portugal. Its notable exterior elements include two intertwined horseshoe portals at the entrance, a clock situated in a small turret, and abundant sculptural ornamentation that enriches the façade. Inside, the platforms are connected to the façade level by ramps, while the platform area is covered by a cast-iron structure erected by a Belgian firm. The station is regarded as an important example in Portugal of Romantic façade design and cast-iron architecture.

On 3 May 2016, a 126-year-old statue of King Sebastian of Portugal, which had been placed in a niche between the entrance portals of Rossio railway station, was destroyed after being knocked over by a person who had climbed up to take a photograph; the individual was subsequently arrested.

In 2024, the global effort to eradicate dracunculiasis documented 15 human cases, with nine occurring in Chad and six in South Sudan. The number of animal infections declined by 25% from 2023, totaling 664 cases in 2024, and these infections were predominantly centered in Chad and Cameroon.

In 2017, 30 human cases of dracunculiasis were reported worldwide, with Chad and Ethiopia each accounting for 15 cases. Of these, 13 were fully contained, indicating successful interruption of transmission for those instances. South Sudan reported no human infections for a full calendar year, the last case having occurred on 20 November 2016. Mali also recorded no human cases for the second consecutive year.

Pathein lies along the Bay of Bengal, where the coastline is bordered by the Arakan Mountains. In the surrounding area is Inye Lake, about 1.5 miles long and 1 mile wide (2.4 by 1.6 km), noted for its fishing. Off the coast lies an offshore reef at Diamond Island, which attracts bathers and also serves as a turtle breeding ground, contributing to the region’s coastal biodiversity.

Ayar Stadium, located in Pathein, has a capacity of 6,000 spectators and serves as a key venue for popular local football tournaments. It is the home stadium of Ayeyawady United F.C., a club that competes in the Myanmar National League (MNL).

Under the Palaiologos dynasty, the Byzantine Empire faced a shifting regional dynamic as Bayezid sought to bring Anatolian Turcoman tribes under Ottoman control while preserving European security. Timurid rulers, meanwhile, regarded Anatolia as within their sphere of influence and opposed Bayezid’s moves, prompting a confrontation between the two powers. Timur invaded Anatolia and defeated Bayezid near Ankara in 1402, an outcome that generated widespread alarm among Turk populations in Anatolia. As a consequence, many Turks crossed into Europe, aided by ships from Venice and Genoa, altering the broader northwestern frontier during the late Palaiologan period.

Under the Palaiologos dynasty, late Byzantine efforts to reconcile with Rome culminated in a formal union, driven by Western bargaining power and the assertion of papal primacy. Emperor John VIII Palaiologos, acting as the de facto head of the Byzantine Church, ordered acceptance of papal primacy and framed the Filioque dispute as a semantic clarification rather than a substantive doctrinal divergence. The 1438–1439 Union of Ferrara–Florence was largely unpopular in Byzantium due to its terms and the lack of promised military aid. The union’s most notable effect was to fuel resentment among Byzantium’s populace toward the imperial government.

Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) operates in several modes, including conventional imaging, scanning TEM (STEM), diffraction, spectroscopy, and combinations of these modes. In conventional imaging, a variety of image-contrast mechanisms are employed to visualize specimen structure. These mechanisms include mass-thickness contrast reflecting sample mass and thickness; Z contrast arising from differences in atomic number; crystallographic or diffraction contrast related to crystal structure or orientation; phase contrast resulting from shifts in the electron wave phase; and spectrum imaging based on energy loss, along with additional mechanisms. The particular information that can be extracted depends on the active contrast mechanism as well as the instrument settings, such as lenses, apertures, and detectors. TEM can deliver information from nanometer-scale to atomic-scale resolutions, enabling the potential determination of atom positions, identification of atom types, and insights into chemical bonding. As a versatile tool, TEM is regarded as essential for nanoscience research across biology and materials science.

Photon-Induced Near-field Electron Microscopy (PINEM) is a specialized variant of Ultrafast Transmission Electron Microscopy used within electron microscopes. The technique derives its name from the interaction of fast electrons with optical photons in the near field generated by a surface or nanostructure. This inelastic coupling enables researchers to probe time-varying nanoscale electromagnetic fields inside the electron microscope and offers a means to dynamically tailor the electron beam’s wave properties.

Intentional diversity programs in business aim to address rapid demographic changes in local consumer markets and labor pools by promoting better collaboration and mutual understanding among employees. Implementations commonly proceed through a sequence of steps: conducting a diversity audit to assess current conditions, crafting an action plan aligned with a broader diversity and inclusion strategy, engaging stakeholders to secure support, and establishing accountability through measurable results.

Age diversity in business is addressed through a combination of immediate policy action and long-term cultural change. In the short term, firms may enact and enforce legal prohibitions against age discrimination, exemplified by the federal Age Discrimination in Employment Act. In the longer term, efforts aim to dismantle negative stereotypes about older workers and to emphasize the value added by their experience and knowledge. An optimal workforce mixes different age groups to harness the agility and fresh perspectives of younger employees alongside the expertise and institutional memory of older staff. The change process is typically transformative, with provisional measures intended to create the space needed for more deeply rooted cultural shifts to occur. When pursued coherently, these strategies yield a more inclusive workplace environment.

Guthrie Center, Iowa, had 699 households. Of these, 25.3% contained children under 18, 41.1% were headed by married couples living together, and 6.2% were cohabiting couples. Households headed by a female householder with no spouse or partner present accounted for 32.6%, while those headed by a male householder with no spouse or partner present accounted for 20.2%. Non-family households represented 43.6% of all households, and 37.9% of households were made up of individuals. Additionally, 20.2% of households had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older.

Guthrie Center, Iowa, had 677 households. Among these, 26.3% contained children under 18. Married couples living together accounted for 45.2% of all households, while female householders with no husband present represented 7.8% and male householders with no wife present accounted for 4.1%. Non-family households comprised 42.8% of all households, and 38.0% consisted of individuals living alone. Households with someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older accounted for 21.6%. The average household size was 2.22, and the average family size was 2.96.

Rwanda National Police, established on 16 June 2000 by Law No. 09 of 2000, was formed through the amalgamation of three precursor forces: the Gendarmerie Nationale under the Ministry of Defence, the Communal Police under the Ministry of Internal Affairs, and the Judicial Police under the Ministry of Justice. The current inspector general is Felix Namuhoranye.

Waiting List Service is a registration mechanism that allows a potential registrant to indicate interest in a domain name that is already registered by another party. It does not guarantee eventual registration; the entrant can only obtain the domain if it becomes available for registration, such as when the current holder does not renew or releases it. If the existing holder continues to renew, the waiting list participant will not acquire the domain through this procedure. Consequently, success depends on the domain becoming available and the current holder not renewing.

In 2003, ICANN-accredited registries proposed a waiting-list service to manage domain allocations, but the initiative drew anti-competitive criticism. Today, registrars offer a closely related non-guaranteed service by continually querying the central registry to monitor whether a domain becomes available. When a domain does become available, the registrar rapidly attempts to register it for the intended registrant. In scenarios where several registrars pursue the same domain, the eventual outcome is often determined by timing and other contingent factors rather than by a guaranteed allocation mechanism.

On May 2, 2013, during the funeral service for George Jones, Vince Gill performed "Go Rest High on That Mountain" with Patty Loveless. Gill became momentarily overwhelmed with emotion and was unable to sing certain lines, finishing the performance by focusing on his guitar accompaniment while Loveless provided the harmony and backing vocals. Prior to the rendition, Gill described a perceived special spiritual quality in his duets with Loveless and likened their collaborations to the George Jones–Melba Montgomery duets of the 1960s.

Go Rest High on That Mountain is a song that has earned a number of major industry recognitions and notable chart performance. It won the CMA Song of the Year award in 1996 and received the BMI Most-Performed Song honor in 1997. At the 38th Annual Grammy Awards, the track secured two prizes—Best Male Country Vocal Performance and Best Country Song. In terms of chart performance, the single peaked at No. 14 on the Country Singles chart in 1995. Since it became available for digital download, it has sold 857,000 copies in the United States.

Peter Sloterdijk is a German philosopher and cultural theorist whose work has generated controversy over his treatment of biology and social reproduction. In Germany, the legacies of Nazi-era eugenics have created a taboo against open discussion of genetic manipulation, a context that informs debates on bio-cultural reproduction. Sloterdijk's essay advocates a more forthright public conversation about these issues and calls for regulatory approaches to how biology and culture intersect in reproduction.
