The ensuing controversy involved Jürgen Habermas labeling Sloterdijk a fascist, a charge that Sloterdijk countered by arguing that Habermas employs fascist rhetoric to discredit him. Central to the disagreement are Sloterdijk's ideas and his use of the terms Züchtung (breeding or cultivation) and Selektion (selection).

Peter Sloterdijk has characterized the opening passages of his work Spheres as the kind of book Heidegger should have written, and he has described Spheres as a companion volume to Heidegger’s Being and Time, under the designation Being and Space. These remarks relate to his initial exploration of the notion of Dasein, and they reflect a deliberate distancing from Heidegger’s positions, with Sloterdijk arguing that his own inquiry advances beyond them.

In Scooby-Doo! and the Loch Ness Monster, Shaggy and Scooby are pursued by the creature through the kitchen, during which the playing field is damaged. The next morning, Locksley orders Shannon to repair the damage. Velma then discovers footprints that lead toward a nearby town, not the loch. While the Haggarts work on fixing the field, the Blakes, Velma, and Fred Jones take Pembrooke's boat to search the loch, and Shaggy and Scooby deploy the Mystery Machine to scour the area by land. Both groups are attacked by the monster simultaneously.

Scooby-Doo! and the Loch Ness Monster is a 2004 direct-to-video animated comedy-mystery film in the Scooby-Doo series, serving as the seventh direct-to-video installment derived from the classic Saturday-morning cartoons. It premiered on June 22, 2004, and was produced by Warner Bros. Animation, with Hanna-Barbera credited as the copyright holder despite Warner Bros.’ absorption of the entity, the closing credits featuring the Hanna-Barbera logo. The release marks a departure from the classic format, not employing the original 1969 voice cast while having Mystery Inc. voiced by the regular actors and outfits drawn from What’s New, Scooby-Doo?; notably, it is Mindy Cohn’s first performance as Velma Dinkley. The film also includes the theme song from What’s New, Scooby-Doo? and features Grey DeLisle’s return as Daphne Blake, a role she had last performed in Scooby-Doo and the Cyber Chase.

Operation Black Lion involved Royalist forces establishing an artillery firing base at the road junction where Route 23 from Vietnam intersects Route 13 near Khong Sedone, Laos. In early June the garrison was reinforced by Thai mercenaries returning from a loan to Military Region 2. On 12–13 June, four battalions departed the Plain of Jars, were re-equipped, and stationed at the junction to man the position. A fifth Thai battalion joined later in June. In early July a 4.2-inch mortar was added to the defenses. Despite these reinforcements, the Royalists had secured no foothold on the Bolovens Plateau.

Operation Black Lion unfolded during July and August 1972 as part of the Laotian conflict. In the course of the operation, Groupement Mobile 32 moved against the depleted PAVN 39th Regiment, pursuing it roughly 15 kilometers to the northeast. Along the advance, Royalist forces recovered and destroyed approximately five tons of Communist war materiel. On 12 August, Royalist units captured the village of Moung Wapi. The Royalists were subsequently relieved on 15 August by BI 18 (Bataillon Infanterie 18) of the Forces Armées Neutralistes.

The silimba is a form of xylophone traditionally played by the Nkoya and Lozi of Barotseland in western Zambia. Its tuned wooden keys are mounted over hollow gourds that serve as resonators, amplifying the instrument’s distinctive timbre. Among the Nkoya it is known as shinjimba. The instrument occupies a ceremonial role in Nkoya culture, being featured at the Kazanga, a traditional royal ceremony. In Lozi folk music, the silimba is an essential element and is heard at the Kuomboka, the annual royal procession. In contemporary usage, the instrument is frequently referred to as shilimba and is played across many regions of Zambia.

The western xylophone appeared in early jazz bands and vaudeville performances, and its bright, lively timbre complemented the syncopated dance music of the 1920s and 1930s. Notable players included Red Norvo, George Cary, George Hamilton Green, Teddy Brown, Harry Breuer, and Harry Robbins. Over time, its popularity was surpassed by the metal-key vibraphone, which emerged in the 1920s and gained prominence in ensembles. A xylophone that extends into the marimba range is referred to as a xylorimba.

Nepal began its modern era in 1951, when literacy stood at about five percent and roughly ten thousand students were enrolled across around three hundred schools. By 2017, more than seven million students were enrolled in 35,601 schools. Between 2001 and 2011, the literacy rate for ages five and above increased from 54.1 percent to 65.9 percent. In the same year, 2017, the net primary enrollment rate reached 97 percent. Secondary enrollment remains under sixty percent for grades nine through twelve, while tertiary enrollment is around twelve percent. Although gender disparities persist in literacy, girls have overtaken boys in enrollment at all levels of education. Nepal is home to eleven universities and four independent science academies. On the Global Innovation Index, the country ranked 107th in 2025.

In Nepal, the president is regarded as a symbol of national unity and serves as the ceremonial head of state. Martyrs are widely regarded as symbols of patriotism, reflecting the values and sacrifices celebrated in the national narrative. Among historical figures, Amar Singh Thapa, Bhakti Thapa, and Balbhadra Kunwar are remembered as war heroes for their roles as commanders during the Anglo-Nepalese War. The country has designated sixteen individuals as National Heroes in recognition of exceptional contributions to Nepal's prestige and national development. Prithvi Narayan Shah, founder of modern Nepal, is highly regarded and often described as the Father of the Nation by many.

Gallery Sansawon, a traditional Korean brewery, houses more than 1,000 historical documents and items related to Korean alcohol. Visitors may sample freely ten varieties of traditional alcoholic drinks, and may also try complimentary foods, including alcohol-infused bread, crackers, Yakgwa, and yeot.

Pocheon features a diverse local economy, with approximately 2,166 small and medium-sized manufacturers producing textiles and metal products. Commercial activity is concentrated mainly in Pocheon-dong and Seondan-dong. The Sin-eup 5 day market, held on the 5th and 10th days of each month, draws a substantial number of customers. Local specialties associated with the city and Idong-myeon, including Pocheon makgeolli (unfiltered rice wine) and Idong galbi (marinated short ribs), are widely known nationwide.

The National Trust for Historic Preservation serves as the organizing body behind the Preservation Leadership Forum, an initiative that links professionals involved in historic preservation. The Preservation Leadership Forum functions as a network of preservation professionals, fostering collaboration and knowledge exchange within the field.

The National Trust for Historic Preservation leads campaigns and advocacy efforts to safeguard historic places. It serves as an educational resource through the Preservation Leadership Forum, which provides articles, journals, case studies, conferences, and training. In addition, the organization publishes Preservation magazine on a quarterly basis and also distributes online stories.

In Hamilton, the Low Parks Museum occupies a building dating to the 16th century that formerly operated as an inn and also served as a staging post on the route between Glasgow and Edinburgh. The structure has recently undergone refurbishment, and it stands as the oldest building in Hamilton, located to the north of the Palace Grounds.

Hamilton's economy is dominated by service industries and local government employment. The town centre has undergone regeneration, with the introduction of new indoor shopping facilities such as the Regent Shopping Centre and the New Cross Shopping Centre. Additional retail development has followed, including Hamilton Retail Park and the Palace Grounds Retail Park, expanding the area's shopping provision.

Karl Friedrich von dem Knesebeck was a Prussian military commander of the Napoleonic era who later attained the rank of field marshal. He was first awarded the Pour le Mérite in 1807, and in 1814 he received the oak leaves to the decoration, marking its higher distinction.

The Pour le Mérite ceased to be awarded after Kaiser Wilhelm II abdicated as king of Prussia and German Emperor on 9 November 1918, an act that likewise marked the end of the Prussian monarchy. Consequently, the order was never conferred again after 1918. Nevertheless, the honour continued to be recognized by those who had already received it, with former recipients continuing to wear their insignia in later years.

Software portability describes the extent to which software can run on different computing platforms with minimal modification. By 2011, the majority of desktop and laptop computers used processors compatible with 32- or 64-bit x86 instruction sets, providing a common architectural base for many applications. By contrast, smaller portable devices relied on different, incompatible instruction sets, such as ARM, which constrained cross-platform compatibility. The divergent hardware and display capabilities across devices influence software behavior and design, meaning that an application built for a large screen cannot be directly ported to a small smartphone, even when the underlying functionality is similar.

Software portability describes applications designed to operate on multiple computers that have compatible operating systems and processor architectures, without requiring machine-specific installation. In this context, porting refers to the act of moving a defined set of directories and their contents from one system to another. When packaged on portable mass storage devices such as USB drives, portable software can run on any suitable computer by simply connecting the device, assuming the host supports the necessary environment. A central characteristic is that all configuration data is stored on the removable device, allowing a consistent setup across different machines. By contrast, hardware- and software-specific information is typically kept in standard configuration locations on the host system, such as the Windows registry, illustrating how portability seeks to minimize dependencies on individual computers.

No. 639 Squadron RAF was formed at RAF Cleave on 1 December 1943 from the amalgamation of 1602 Flight, 1603 Flight, 1604 Flight and 1618 Flight. It operated in an anti-aircraft co-operation role, employing Hawker Henley target-tug aircraft with the principal task of towing targets over Cornwall. Hawker Hurricane aircraft were used as radar targets and to simulate low-level attacks on troops. The squadron was disbanded on 30 April 1945.

Density of a crystalline material can be determined from its formula mass, expressed in daltons, together with the volume of its unit cell. A conversion factor exists whereby one dalton per cubic ångström corresponds to a density of 1.66053906892(52) g/cm^3, a value derived from the 2022 CODATA recommended value for the dalton.

Density can be expressed in related metric units that yield the same numerical value: grams per cubic centimeter (g/cm^3), grams per milliliter (g/mL), and kilograms per liter (kg/L). Each of these units corresponds to the density expressed in kilograms per cubic meter (kg/m^3) divided by 1000. Water has a density close to 1 g/cm^3, which is equivalent to about 1000 kg/m^3. In practical terms, the densities of most solids and liquids lie roughly in the range of 0.1 to 20 g/cm^3, contributing to the numerical convenience of these units for everyday measurements.

Big wave surfing features one of its most historic competitions, The Eddie, which stands as the oldest and most prestigious event devoted to large-wave surfing. The contest is named in honor of Eddie Aikau, a Hawaiian lifeguard and surfer from Oahu's North Shore. The event's competition window runs annually from December 1 to the last day of February.

On 4 January 2012, Jaws (Peahi) on Maui’s north shore hosted a landmark day in big-wave surfing, as conditions produced tremendously large breaks that compelled several top riders to attempt the waves without jet-ski assistance, relying on paddling into and riding the faces and surviving the sets. The day drew a lineup that included Greg Long, Ian Walsh, Kohl Christensen, Jeff Rowley, Dave Wassel, Shane Dorian, Mark Healey, Carlos Burle, Nate Fletcher, Garrett McNamara, Kai Barger, along with North Shore locals and other leading big-wave surfers.

Gentrification is often described as a self-reinforcing urban process in which wealthier residents seek the newest housing stock, triggering gradual changes in neighborhood composition. In many cities, new housing is constructed in concentric rings around the urban core, with each decade adding a fresh tier of stock. As central housing ages and becomes comparatively affordable, the affluent migrate into these areas, elevating demand and property values; when the core’s stock reaches the end of its economic life, the outward push continues with the next ring undergoing a similar transition. Scholars identify several interpretations of the phenomenon: some emphasize the rise in asset values for homeowners; others note increases in prices for local goods and services as higher-income consumption becomes more common, including the introduction of higher-priced retail outlets; a third view highlights displacement, as longtime residents may no longer be able to afford to live in the area.

A 2024 study conducted in London, United Kingdom, examined the effects of introducing high-density, mixed-income developments into low-income neighborhoods as part of urban redevelopment. The intervention was associated with improved educational outcomes for children already living in the area. The researchers propose a plausible mechanism: incumbent students were exposed to a greater share of high-ability peers, which may have generated positive peer effects that enhanced academic performance.

Discrete mathematics encompasses several subfields, notably discrete geometry and combinatorial geometry, which examine the combinatorial properties of discrete collections of geometric objects. A prominent topic within discrete geometry is tiling the plane, a long-standing area of inquiry that has engaged researchers for many years.

Discrete mathematics concentrates on discrete objects as its principal objects of study. Although the field centers on discrete structures, it frequently employs analytic methods derived from continuous mathematics to analyze problems and develop theoretical insights.

An overdose refers to the ingestion or application of a drug or substance in quantities greater than those recommended. The term is typically used when such intake poses a potential risk to an individual's health. An overdose may lead to a toxic state and can be fatal.

An overdose of a drug refers to a consumption that surpasses the generally recognized safe dosage, reflecting the notion that a standard therapeutic amount exists for most drugs. The label overdose is predominantly used for medications rather than poisons, although certain toxic agents can be harmless at extremely low exposures. A drug overdose may be employed as a method of suicide, arising from either intentional or unintentional misuse of medications. In deliberate cases, individuals may ingest excessive quantities of both prescribed and non-prescribed drugs in order to achieve a euphoric effect.

In October 1999, the British Defence Procurement Agency awarded Bofors a contract to define the product and develop a weapon prototype within 22 months for the NLAW programme. The performance criteria required the system to hit a moving target at 400 metres and a stationary target at 600 metres, with a maximum weight of 12.5 kilograms. Subsequently, Sweden’s FMV imposed additional requirements, including a smaller backblast footprint, a minimum effective range of 20 metres, and environmental operational suitability for international missions. For the MBT LAW assessment phase, funding was divided equally among Saab Bofors Dynamics, the DPA, and the FMV, with each contributing approximately £6 million of a total £18 million. During the NLAW trials, FMV provided supplementary funding, while the DPA halted further financing until a formal contract was signed.

During the conflict, an undetermined number of NLAW launchers were captured by Russia's armed forces and the Donetsk People's Republic, the pro-Russian separatist authorities in eastern Ukraine. Reports indicate that some of these captured launchers were subsequently transferred to Iran, with the transfer reportedly tied to a deal intended to secure drones.

Historically, estimates of the universe’s age based on models lacking dark energy were younger than the ages determined for the oldest observed astronomical objects, such as ancient stars and globular clusters, producing an age–object-age discrepancy. This mismatch linked the inferred cosmic age to the ages of the oldest objects, a connection that can be leveraged in reverse: the ages of these objects provide a lower bound on the universe’s age and thus constrain the density parameter associated with dark energy. As a result, observations of the oldest objects limit the possible values of dark energy density.

Based on the nine-year data set from the Wilkinson Microwave Anisotropy Probe released by NASA in 2012, the age of the universe is estimated at (13.772 ± 0.059) × 10^9 years, which corresponds to 13.772 billion years with an uncertainty of about ±59 million years. The calculation relies on measurements of the cosmic microwave background radiation.

Jean de Vienne served in the 3rd Cruisers Division alongside La Galissonnière and Marseillaise, with Marseillaise acting as the division’s flagship, and the force attached to the Mediterranean Squadron based at Bizerte. At the outset of World War II, the ship underwent a major refit at Toulon before rejoining the division at Bizerte. The division’s mission was to protect French interests in North Africa in the event of Italian entry into the war. With Italy initially neutral, its activities were limited, though the division’s principal operation during this period involved transporting French gold bullion to Halifax, Nova Scotia, in December 1939. After Italy entered the war on 10 June 1940, a significant French sortie was launched to deter Kriegsmarine attempts to force the Straits of Gibraltar. The only sighting of the enemy during this operation was a failed attack by the Italian cruiser Dandolo.

On 24 November 1943, a USAAF incendiary raid struck the French cruiser Jean de Vienne, setting the vessel ablaze. The damage caused the ship to gradually list and settle against the Toulon quayside. Following the Allied liberation of Toulon in August 1944 as part of Operation Dragoon, a refit was proposed but ultimately abandoned, and Jean de Vienne was scrapped.
The Canadian Radio Music Awards were an annual awards event presented by the Canadian Association of Broadcasters and were part of Canadian Music Week. The awards program began in 1998.

The CONCACAF Champions Cup is a continental club competition organized by CONCACAF for teams from North America, Central America, and the Caribbean. The current format is a knockout-style tournament, with clubs eliminated through successive rounds until a champion is crowned. The competition previously featured a group stage prior to the 2018 edition. In contrast to the UEFA Champions League and the Copa Libertadores, the winner does not automatically qualify for the next edition.

The 1988 Wimbledon Championships was a grass-court tennis tournament held at the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club in Wimbledon, London, United Kingdom. It was the 102nd edition of the Wimbledon Championships and ran from 20 June to 4 July 1988. Rain interruptions on Sunday 3 July caused the men’s final to be completed on 4 July.

Architectural terracotta denotes fired clay elements used in the construction and decoration of buildings. Throughout history, it has been produced by a range of cultures, including the ancient Greeks, Babylonians, Egyptians, and Romans, as well as Chinese artisans, the Indus Valley civilization, and various Native American peoples. In architectural practice, terracotta has served diverse roles, from roofing tiles that provide weatherproofing to decorative discs, sculptural figures, and column capitals, alongside many other small detailing elements that contribute to the visual and functional language of a structure.

Architectural terracotta production employed kilns of varying designs, with adoption shaped by advances in kiln technology and levels of investment. The most common form was the muffle kiln, evidence of which dates to around 1870. These kilns burned gas, coal, or oil to heat an exterior heating chamber that transferred heat to an inner firing chamber containing the greenware. The outer walls served to mollify and insulate the heat, preventing direct exposure of the wares to flames and enabling more controlled firing of architectural ceramic elements.

Histamine binds to H2 receptors on oxyntic (parietal) cells in the stomach, activating an H2-sensitive adenylyl cyclase. This signaling produces a rapid rise in intracellular cyclic adenosine monophosphate, and the elevated cAMP participates in promoting proton secretion and other changes within these cells.

The sound commonly represented by the symbol ⟨ʎ⟩ is typically described as a voiced alveolo-palatal lateral approximant. There is no dedicated IPA symbol for this exact sound, so ⟨ʎ⟩ is ordinarily used to denote it. For greater phonetic specificity, it may alternatively be transcribed as ⟨l̠ʲ⟩, indicating a retracted, palatalized lateral articulation. In addition, a non-IPA character exists, ȴ (Latin small letter l with curl), encoded as U+0234, which combines an ⟨l⟩ with a curling diacritic akin to the curls seen in alveolo-palatal sibilants ⟨ɕ, ʑ⟩ and has been employed especially in Sinological circles.

The voiced palatal lateral approximant is a consonant characterized by voicing and a constriction at the palate, produced with the tongue body raised toward the hard palate while allowing air to flow laterally around the tongue. It employs a pulmonic egressive airstream mechanism, whereby air is propelled from the lungs by the contraction of respiratory muscles, including the intercostal and abdominal muscles, a method common to the majority of speech sounds. In the International Phonetic Alphabet, this sound is typically represented by the symbol [ʎ].

The Type 3C connector may incorporate a logic-controlled latching mechanism designed to deter cable theft. A pin is actuated upward from the underside of the socket, engaging with a corresponding cutout on the plug shroud to secure the connection. The same arrangement also locks the socket cover when the connector is not in use, thereby protecting the enclosure. Together, these features enhance the design’s resistance to vandalism.

Type 3C was developed approximately a decade after Type 3 to enable charging at powers exceeding 3 kW. In March 2010, the EV Plug Alliance was established to promote Type 3C as a high-safety plug and socket solution for Mode 3 AC charging, spanning 3 to 22 kW. The alliance is bi-national, with founding members including Schneider Electric and Legrand of France and Scame of Italy. Schneider Electric regards Type 3C as particularly well suited for the pairing of an EVSE socket outlet with a cord plug, noting that the cord would be supplied by the vehicle manufacturer and be specific to the EV. The concept is drawn analogously to USB, in which the host provides a universal connector (USB-A) while the peripheral supplies its own connector and cable.

Reception of Vermeule's Common Good Constitutionalism, published by Polity in 2022, among natural law scholars has been notably positive, with several commentators welcoming it as a meaningful contribution to legal theory. Richard Helmholz described the work as a serious contribution to pressing legal debates, commending its clarity and skillful composition. Sanford Levinson called it a truly important book that warrants wide readership and vigorous discussion. By contrast, Richard Primus praised the book’s simple and powerful frame for its potential but argued that it does not fully spell out the common good that Vermeule envisions.

Common good constitutionalism, as a jurisprudential framework that centers constitutional commitments on the promotion of communal welfare, may have notable relevance to environmental law. By foregrounding shared interests and intergenerational stewardship, it offers environmental law scholars and practitioners a principled lens to assess regulatory regimes, rights claims, and public duties within its framework. The approach can also function as a catalyst for environmental advocacy, potentially motivating more strategic litigation and policy engagement that align constitutional principles with ecological protection and sustainable governance.

In Canada, a clear distinction exists between colleges and universities. The term “going to university” typically refers to pursuing a bachelor’s degree or equivalent at a university, usually within a three- or four-year program, while “going to college” denotes enrollment in technical or career training at a college that offers non-degree programs. This division reflects the different roles of the institutions: universities are the degree-granting establishments, whereas colleges specialize in technical and career instruction through non-degree offerings.

Students have the option to pursue higher education after a certain point. Higher education comprises undergraduate and graduate programs, including bachelor's degrees and master's degrees. These programs are said to take six years to complete. In addition, students may undertake doctoral studies to earn a PhD.
On 4 July 2008, the Dharmaling Buddhist community and the State of Slovenia signed a formal agreement, the first such accord between the Slovenian state and a Buddhist community.

Buddhism in Slovenia comprises several traditions and schools represented by communities of varying sizes, with Theravada and Vajrayana being the largest among them. A Buddhist temple operates in Ljubljana, the capital, serving as a center for worship and activities. Additionally, a Theravada hermitage is situated in the forested countryside at Goljek near Trebnje, illustrating the presence of monastic practice outside urban areas.

Bellmore is a hamlet and census-designated place (CDP) in Nassau County, New York, United States. According to the 2024 census, its population was 15,937. Located on the south shore of Long Island, Bellmore lies about six miles north of Jones Beach State Park, roughly 27 miles east of Manhattan, and approximately 10 miles east of the Nassau–Queens line that marks the boundary of New York City.

Bellmore, New York originated as a rural farming and fishing locality in the mid-17th century, then referred to by names such as Little Neck and New Bridge. The settlement was largely formed by English settlers who crossed the Long Island Sound from Connecticut during that period. In 1655 Bradley Vogel acquired a 214-acre farm in the area that is now known as North Bellmore. In 1676 Andres Smith deeded 100 acres to his son Jeremiah near the bay. Around 1689, Lee Mattes married Sarah Southard and took up residence along Merrick Road. From these beginnings two communities subsequently emerged: Smithville (later Smithville South), a designation reflecting many Smith family settlers, and New Bridge, a name derived from the bridge that connected the peninsulas south of Merrick Road.

EFI System Partition (ESP) is a partition used to support the firmware boot process. It stores boot loaders, boot managers, and kernel images of installed operating systems, though these components are typically located on other partitions. The ESP also contains device driver files needed by the firmware at boot time to initialize hardware. In addition, it includes system utility programs intended to run before an operating system is loaded. The partition may, furthermore, contain data files such as error logs.
On Apple Macintosh computers equipped with Intel x86-64 processors, the EFI system partition is initially left blank and is not used for booting macOS.

The bulge bracket is a label used in international business discourse to denote the leading providers of professional services. It is applied to global, highly prestigious law firms with deep expertise across a broad range of topics, a group often described within the industry as the Magic Circle and the Silver Circle. The term has also been used to refer to the Big Three management consultancies (the MBB) and the Big Four accounting firms, reflecting their extensive international reach and strong reputations in their respective fields.

There remains ongoing debate regarding which banks qualify as bulge bracket firms. Definitional criteria have been drawn from several ranking frameworks, including Bloomberg 20, Mergermarket M&A league tables, and Thomson Reuters league tables. In addition, other rankings exist that are used to determine bulge bracket membership.

VC-1 is a video compression standard defined by the SMPTE. It is openly available for implementation by anyone, though license payments may be required in some cases. Fees may be paid to Via-LA LLC, the designated licensing body, or directly to individual members who claim essential patent rights covering the format. The licensing framework administered by Via-LA is non-exclusive, allowing multiple patent holders to participate in licensing.

Several video encoding products from Inlet, Digital Rapids, Harmonic, Envivio, Elemental Technologies, Anystream, Telestream, and Rhozet offer support for VC-1 encoding. The VC-1 encoding implementation is based on the Microsoft VC-1 Encoder SDK. This encoding capability is utilized for both IPTV delivery and Web streaming.

Non-line-of-sight propagation is enabled by refraction in the ionosphere, which allows radio signals to reach beyond the geometric line of sight through a mechanism analogous to atmospheric refraction. This bending occurs in the ionospheric layer, at substantially higher altitudes than the lower atmosphere. Ionospheric propagation can be described statistically using Rayleigh fading models, similar to the approaches used for tropospheric propagation, to capture the multipath effects and channel variability inherent in such paths.

Non-line-of-sight propagation in urban environments is significantly influenced by diffraction, particularly at higher cellular frequencies where small obstacles can cause appreciable bending of the radio waves. In such settings, urban cellular signals are dominated by ground-plane effects as they traverse rooftops, effectively traveling along a path that follows the street level. Some portion of the signal diffracts around the edges of roofs, entering street canyons where reception may occur without direct line of sight. Within the street, propagation is governed by multipath components, absorption by building materials, and continued diffraction, producing a complex signal structure and fluctuating received power.

Siemens Smart Infrastructure, as a division of Siemens AG, has historically been involved in a series of prosecutions and settlements related to bribery and improper conduct by its personnel across multiple jurisdictions. Notable events include the 2007 conviction of two former Siemens executives for bribing the Italian energy company Enel, the 2012 €330 million settlement with the Greek government over a Greek bribery scandal, and the 2014 guilty plea by former Siemens executive Andres Truppel for directing nearly $100 million in bribes to Argentine officials. Involving the World Bank, repercussions arose from fraudulent practices by Siemens’ Russian affiliate, which coincided with a two-year ban on bidding for World Bank projects and the establishment of the Siemens Integrity Initiative, a $100 million anti-corruption fund to be deployed over fifteen years. Additional penalties included a 2010 payment of ₦7 billion (about US$46.57 million) to the Nigerian government and a 2014 US$42.7 million penalty in Israel to resolve securities fraud charges.

In March 2024, Siemens announced its intention to acquire ebm-papst's Industrial Drive Technology division (IDT), a transaction connected to its Smart Infrastructure operations. The purchase price for the acquisition was not disclosed.
My Melody & Kuromi premiered on July 24, 2025, on Netflix. The release marks the semicentennial of My Melody at 50 years and the vicennial of Kuromi at 20 years.

In the series My Melody & Kuromi, Baku is depicted as a purple-colored tapir capable of flight and serves as Kuromi's usual companion. Although Kuromi frequently references Baku, the character is largely absent from the program, not appearing in most episodes. Baku makes its return to Mariland in the final episode, marking the character's concluding appearance.

Semaphore programming uses the letters V and P that derive from Dutch terminology. V is typically linked to verhogen, the Dutch verb for "increase" or "raise." The P label has been associated with several Dutch roots, including proberen (to test or to try), passeren (to pass), and pakken (to grab). In Dijkstra's earliest paper on the subject, P is described as passering (passing) and V as vrijgave (release), terms borrowed from railroad signaling. In later writings, Dijkstra indicated that P was intended to denote prolaag, short for proberen te verlagen, meaning to attempt to reduce, or to mirror the "try" notion that accompanies V.

In a producer–consumer synchronization context, several producers may enter the producer critical section concurrently, but the number of simultaneous entrants is limited to N. Access to this region is regulated by a counting semaphore named emptyCount, which constrains entry by representing the number of available entry slots and preventing additional producers from entering once the limit is reached.

The UEFA Champions League anthem, officially titled "Champions League," was arranged by Tony Britten for the competition in 1992, drawing on an adaptation of Handel's 1727 Coronation Anthem "Zadok the Priest." Commissioned by UEFA, the arrangement was performed by the Royal Philharmonic Orchestra of London with the Academy of St. Martin in the Fields supplying the vocal ensemble. UEFA has described the composition as nearly as iconic as the trophy and capable of thrilling top footballers.

Group stage matches were played from September to December, with the knockout rounds commencing in February. Knockout ties were generally conducted over two legs, except for the final, which is decided in a single match. Fixtures were typically scheduled on Tuesday and Wednesday evenings. The 2019–20 season was suspended for five months due to the COVID-19 pandemic, after which the remainder of the tournament was reorganized: the quarter-finals and semi-finals were held as single-match knockouts at neutral venues in Lisbon, Portugal, during the summer. The competition concluded with the final on 23 August 2020.

During the 20th century, Basque nationalism heightened interest in the language as a symbol of ethnic identity. The establishment of autonomous administrations in the Southern Basque Country facilitated a modest revival of Basque. In Spain, Basque-language schooling for children and centers offering Basque instruction to adults expanded into western Enkarterri and the Ribera del Ebro in southern Navarre, areas that had not previously been widely Basque-speaking. In the French Basque Country, Basque-language schools and centers have largely halted the language's decline.

Basque has given rise to several pidgin varieties, either rooted in Basque or exhibiting Basque influence. During the 16th century, Basque mariners used a pidgin blending Basque and Icelandic to communicate with Icelanders. Another contact-induced pidgin, the Algonquian–Basque, developed from interactions between Basque whalers and Algonquian-speaking peoples in the Gulf of Saint Lawrence and the Strait of Belle Isle.

On August 19, 2020, TJX Companies disclosed that the COVID-19 pandemic was taking a toll on its business. Revenues declined by 31 percent over May through July, driven largely by extensive store closures for about one-third of that period. The company also reported a net loss of $214 million for the second quarter.

During 2015, TJX Companies expanded its off-price portfolio by acquiring the Trade Secret and Home Secret brands from Gazal Corporation Limited, an Australian company. The transaction was completed in December 2015. In leadership changes, Ernie Herrman was named chief executive officer in October 2015, succeeding Carol Meyrowitz, and he formally assumed the position in January 2016.

The Kernel-based Virtual Machine Virtual Machine Manager is a management tool for KVM-based virtual machines. It enables users to create and edit KVM-based VMs, as well as to start and stop them. In addition, the VMM supports migrating virtual machines between hosts, offering both live migration for running VMs and cold migration for powered-off VMs, with drag-and-drop operations commonly used to initiate transfers.

Kernel-based Virtual Machine sets up the guest virtual machine's address space within the host environment. The host supplies a firmware image for the guest to use during boot, and when PC hardware is emulated this firmware is typically a custom BIOS. The firmware's primary role is to initialize the virtual hardware and bootstrap the guest into its operating system.

Embedded systems span a wide range of processing capabilities and price points within computer hardware. For example, 8-bit processors may be produced for prices below ten cents per unit. In contrast, high-end processors can deliver billions of operations per second and commonly exceed US$100 in cost. Because cost is a central consideration, designers typically opt for the least expensive component that still satisfies the necessary performance requirements.

Virtual hardware refers to software-based representations that emulate the functionality of physical hardware components. By providing an abstraction layer over the underlying resources, it allows the decoupling of software operations from direct hardware dependencies and enables flexible provisioning and management of compute, storage, and networking resources. This approach is widely used in cloud service models, especially Infrastructure as a Service and Platform as a Service, where multiple virtualized resources can be multiplexed on shared physical infrastructure.

In contemporary South Korea, speakers generally do not clearly pronounce the distinction between long and short vowels in casual speech. Nevertheless, the contrast is maintained in the standard language norms, where it is recognized as part of the conventional vowel system and taught within prescriptive grammar. This retention is attributed to historical tradition and its role in semantic differentiation, helping to distinguish words with otherwise similar forms.

Traditional Korean honorifics were governed by a rigid hierarchy that mirrored the stratified social order of the past. The caste and estate systems produced more complex and layered patterns than those observed today. As a result, the honorific system formed a central, intricate aspect of traditional culture and society. In contemporary Korea, honorifics are still used, but often to reflect social distance or formality, with particular forms reserved for individuals regarded as superior in status, such as older people, teachers, and employers.

1994 is widely regarded as a pivotal and particularly productive year for East Coast hip-hop, marking a critical juncture for the scene. In that year, New York–based rappers released a substantial volume of work characterized by dynamic production and intricate lyricism. Notable acts associated with the period included Digable Planets, Gang Starr, Jeru the Damaja, O.C., and Organized Konfusion, with Pete Rock making a significant impact as a producer. The era's releases were defined by energetic beats and sharp rhymes, signaling a year of substantial artistic achievement for East Coast hip-hop.

East Coast hip-hop in the streaming era saw a number of artists achieve wide recognition, including Cardi B, Lil Uzi Vert, Fetty Wap, A Boogie wit da Hoodie, Rich The Kid, Tekashi 6ix9ine, Sheck Wes, ASAP Ferg, Rico Nasty, Young M.A, Action Bronson, Dave East, Shy Glizzy, YBN Cordae, Brent Faiyaz, GoldLink, PnB Rock, Flipp Dinero, and Jay Critch. A substantial portion of these figures rose to prominence through social media, leveraging online platforms to build followings beyond traditional radio or label-driven routes. Several of them also moved away from classic East Coast sounds by adopting production and stylistic approaches associated with the streaming era, such as trap-oriented beats and Southern hip hop influences. Correspondingly, the period witnessed a waning of sharply delineated regional rap scenes, as intercity rivalries diminished and cross-regional collaborations across genres became more common.

L'Église réformée du Québec maintains a notable association with the Farel Reformed Theological Seminary. The seminary operates as an officially independent institution, distinct from the Reformed Church of Quebec; nevertheless, it preserves strong personal ties to the denomination, which are facilitated by its founder, David Craig.

As of 2018, five congregations remained, located in Montréal, Repentigny, Québec City, Lévis, and Saint-Georges-de-Beauce. The denomination comprises roughly 350 members. It positions itself as a continuation of the French Huguenot tradition, aiming to preserve its historical lineage within French Reformed heritage. Its member churches participate in the North American Presbyterian and Reformed Council (NAPARC) and the World Reformed Fellowship.

The Daily Report Online is a daily legal newspaper based in Atlanta, Georgia. It was established in 1890 and was formerly known as the Fulton County Daily Report. The publication focuses on legal and business news relevant to the state of Georgia. Among its notable special editions are the Daily Report Dozen, which examines Atlanta’s twelve largest law firms; Going Rate, which reports the hourly rates charged by hundreds of Georgia lawyers; and On The Rise, an annual feature that highlights the most promising legal minds under the age of forty.
The Daily Report Online is owned by ALM, the media company formerly known as American Lawyer Media. It has about 4,000 paid subscribers and a readership of approximately 15,000.

Across cultures, the fox figure features prominently in folklore as a shapeshifter and symbol of cunning, with varying moral roles. In Chinese folklore, the huli jing are fox spirits that may possess as many as nine tails. In Korea, the kumiho stands as the Korean counterpart to the huli jing. Japanese mythology presents kitsune as fox spirits whose magical abilities increase with age and wisdom, most notably the power to assume human form, and they can function as tricksters, faithful guardians, friends, lovers, or wives. Arab folklore portrays the fox as cowardly, weak, deceitful, and cunning, and it recounts a feigning-death tactic in which the animal inflates its abdomen to appear bloated, then lies on its side to lure prey. In biblical usage, the term fox is employed metaphorically to describe false prophets in Ezekiel 13:4 and to symbolize the hypocrisy of Herod Antipas in Luke 13:32.

Red fox litters typically consist of four to six offspring, though brood sizes as large as thirteen have been recorded, with larger litters more common in habitats where juvenile mortality is high. Neonates are altricial: born blind, deaf, and toothless, with dark brown fluffy fur; they weigh about 56–110 g and measure roughly 14.5 cm in body length with a 7.5 cm tail, possessing short legs, a relatively large head, and a broad chest at birth. In the early weeks, the dam remains with the litter for about two to three weeks while the sire or barren vixens assist by feeding her. Vixens are highly protective and can repulse intruders such as terriers, and if the mother dies the father may assume caregiving duties. Developmental milestones during the first weeks include eyes opening at roughly 13–15 days, ear canals becoming functional, and the eruption of the first upper teeth, followed by the lower teeth 3–4 days later; eye color shifts from blue at birth to amber by four to five weeks. Coat and facial changes begin around three weeks with a dark eye streak appearing, and by one month red and white facial patches emerge as ears become erect and muzzles lengthen. Weaning and lactation occur as kits leave the den and begin solid food at three to four weeks, with lactation lasting six to seven weeks; the woolly coat develops shiny guard hairs after about eight weeks. Growth proceeds rapidly, with individuals becoming long-legged, narrow-chested, and sinewy between three and four months, and attaining adult proportions by six to seven months. Maturation varies, with some vixens reaching sexual maturity at nine to ten months and giving birth to their first litter around one year of age. In captivity red foxes may live up to about fifteen years, whereas wild individuals typically do not surpass roughly five years.

The term expatriate is occasionally rendered as ex-patriot, a misspelling that Anu Garg identifies as an eggcorn. By characterizing it this way, Garg places the form within the broader eggcorn phenomenon, wherein a phonetically similar substitution yields a plausible but incorrect term.

Quantifying the global expatriate population is difficult due to the absence of a government census that comprehensively counts expatriates; consequently, estimates vary and are not standardized. In 2017, the market research firm Finaccord estimated the expatriate population at 66.2 million.

In the 1771 German novel Geschichte des Fräuleins von Sternheim by Sophie von La Roche, a morally earnest character condemns the newly introduced waltz as it appears among the aristocracy. The narrative depicts a man wrapping an arm around a woman, drawing her close against his chest, and taking part in a brazen, unrestrained whirl of dance. This conduct is presented as a form of familiarity that breaches the boundaries of proper breeding. The narrator's reaction moves from quiet misery to burning anger, underscoring the critique of social propriety embedded in the scene.

The waltz in traditional Irish music originated in the 19th century when itinerant dancing masters taught the dance to those who could afford lessons. By the end of that century, it had spread to middle- and lower-class segments of Irish society. Traditional tunes and songs in triple time were reshaped to accommodate the waltz’s rhythm. In the 20th century, a distinctly Irish waltz playing style emerged among céilí musicians at dances.

ITV3 HD is the high-definition simulcast of the ITV3 channel. It launched on 15 November 2010 on the Sky platform, alongside ITV4 HD, under a non-exclusive arrangement within Sky’s pay subscription service. The service was later introduced to Virgin Media on 14 March 2013. ITV3 HD broadcasts most of ITV3’s recent drama catalogue in high definition, including series such as Lewis, Sherlock Holmes, and Agatha Christie’s Marple, and it also features factual programming like Joanna Lumley’s Nile and Martin Clunes’ Islands of Britain.

ITV3 commemorated Coronation Street's 60th anniversary with a dedicated programming block from 7 to 11 December 2020, airing between 10:00 pm and 11:05 pm. The schedule featured a sequence of re-broadcasts spanning the show's history, including the original series premiere (Episode 1), the 10th anniversary episode from December 1970, two episodes celebrating the 20th anniversary in December 1980, two episodes for the 30th anniversary in December 1990, Coronation Street Live (2000) produced for the 40th anniversary, and Coronation Street Live (2010) produced for the 50th anniversary, which was re-transmitted after a repeat of The Road to Coronation Street.

Oryol Oblast is characterized by a substantial portion of its agricultural land devoted to crop production. Grain cultivation is a primary activity, with winter wheat and rye as the leading crops. Other cultivated crops include buckwheat, oats, barley, and potatoes. Sugar beets are in strong demand. The area planted with feed grains has risen as livestock farming has expanded. The region's livestock sector comprises beef and dairy cattle, pig farming, sheep farming for meat and wool, as well as poultry and horse breeding.

Oryol Oblast is one of the smallest federal subjects by area. It covers a total area of 24,652 square kilometers (9,518 square miles). The oblast extends more than 150 kilometers in the north–south direction and more than 200 kilometers in the west–east direction.

As of 2025, the Schwanberg Spiritual Center is operated by the Communität Casteller Ring. The center comprises a convent, three guest houses, and a café, providing facilities for residents and guests alike. Guests are offered spiritual guidance, and the program includes courses in liturgical singing, psalms, Bible study, meditation, grief counselling, and music therapy.

Communität Casteller Ring is a religious community that follows the Rule of Saint Benedict and embraces Benedictine spirituality in daily life. Its mother house is located at Schwanberg. From 1996 until Easter 2011, the community's sisters staffed St. Augustine's Monastery in Erfurt, the historic house where Martin Luther lived as a monk. The order maintains close ties with Münsterschwarzach Abbey.

Open Archives Initiative develops a set of technical specifications and interoperability standards designed to enable seamless interoperability among repositories and to facilitate automated access to content. Its central objective is to enhance access to electronic preprint archives, thereby broadening the availability of scholarly communications, including journal articles. The initiative is linked to the open access publishing movement, which advocates free and unrestricted access to research outputs. In addition, the technology and standards it promotes are versatile and applicable to domains outside scholarly publishing.

The Open Archives Initiative (OAI) develops interoperable standards to enable the sharing of digital content across repositories. Its Protocol for Metadata Harvesting (OAI-PMH) version 2.0 defines the method by which data providers expose metadata for harvesting by service providers. Repositories typically align their metadata with Dublin Core, the widely used metadata schema employed for this purpose. Together, OAI standards offer a uniform mechanism for delivering content accompanied by metadata described in Dublin Core format. In addition, the OAI-ORE specification establishes standards for describing and exchanging aggregations of web resources.

Irina Blok, a Google graphic designer, designed the Android robot icon on November 5, 2007, at the announcement of Android. She independently developed the emblem and released it as open source, contrary to reports that she had been tasked with creating it. The robot motif was not initially presented to Google; instead, it circulated within the Android development team, where developers produced variations and the design was released under a Creative Commons license. Its popularity among developers led Google to adopt it as the official Android logo and icon when Android was released to consumers in 2008.

During the early history of Android, several tablets were launched rapidly to capitalize on the popularity of the iPad, including Barnes & Noble’s Nook and devices that ran Android alongside competing operating systems such as HP’s TouchPad and BlackBerry’s PlayBook. InfoWorld described the strategy as a makeshift, low-investment effort that repurposed smartphone-optimized Android for tablet use prior to the introduction of Honeycomb, resulting in a user interface that did not fully exploit tablet capabilities. The Dell Streak is frequently cited as an example of this approach, failing to gain market traction and contributing to a damaged perception of Android tablets. Some models, like the Motorola Xoom, were priced at, or above, the iPad’s level, which hindered sales. By contrast, Amazon’s Kindle Fire represented an exception, pursuing aggressive pricing and leveraging access to Amazon’s app and content ecosystem to drive adoption.

Jiaoqu (simplified Chinese: 郊区; traditional Chinese: 郊區; pinyin: Jiāo Qū) is a suburban district of the city of Jiamusi, in Heilongjiang Province, People's Republic of China. The district's Chinese name appears as 郊区 in simplified form and 郊區 in traditional form, pronounced Jiāo Qū, and its literal meaning is "suburbs."

Indigenous Australians refers to the original inhabitants and their descendants of the Australian continent, encompassing two principal groups: Aboriginal Australian peoples and Torres Strait Islander peoples. The Aboriginal peoples comprise a multitude of distinct nations and language groups, reflecting a broad diversity of cultural traditions and social structures. The Torres Strait Islander peoples are organized into sub-groups that correspond to different communities within the Torres Strait region. Collectively, these two groups are commonly identified as Indigenous Australians, although they are also described by alternative terms such as First Nations and First Peoples.

Indonesia maintains that Indigenous peoples do not constitute a recognized category within its borders. In 2012, the government stated support for the promotion and protection of indigenous peoples worldwide, but reiterated that it does not acknowledge the concept domestically. The Papuan population has reportedly endured severe abuses, with conservative estimates suggesting a death toll of around 100,000 in West New Guinea since 1963, a figure associated with the Papua conflict and related violence. International advocacy groups have criticized the situation, and Survival International has condemned Indonesia for treating its Indigenous peoples as among the worst off in the world.

Following the Nuttall Review and associated changes to EOT taxation, interest in employee ownership broadened in the United Kingdom. Several existing employee-owned firms have reorganised to establish an Employee Ownership Trust, and the combined total of newly created EOTs and deemed EOTs—pre-existing trusts that meet the criteria—now accounts for a substantial share of the sector, representing over three-quarters of its companies and more than half of its employees.

An Employee Ownership Trust (EOT) is a form of indirect employee ownership in which a trustee holds the company's shares within a permanent or long-term trust on behalf of all employees. The arrangement can operate in a hybrid model, with the EOT owning shares alongside those held by employees as individuals and/or by other investors. For employee ownership to be effective, the EOT’s shareholding must be paired with an organizational structure that promotes and sustains employee engagement, ensuring that the ownership arrangement translates into meaningful participation and governance within the company.

Edward Stanley was consecrated Bishop of Norwich in 1837 and appointed Clerk of the Closet, positions he held concurrently until his death. At the outset of his episcopate the Norwich diocese was characterized by lax discipline, and he sought to remedy these deficiencies, though his reform program encountered initial opposition. He sought to restore order by regularizing ecclesiastical rites, leading to more regular and frequent ordinations and confirmations, and by ensuring rigorous inspection of schools. He also enforced the Plurality Act, limiting clerics to a single benefice except in specified circumstances, and undertook the removal of clergy considered unsuitable. Through these measures, he aimed to strengthen clerical oversight and discipline within the diocese and the broader Church.

Edward Stanley, a bishop, was born in London and descended from a prominent Cheshire family. He was the second son of Sir John Thomas Stanley and the younger brother of John Stanley, 1st Baron Stanley of Alderley.

Groove metal is a heavy metal subgenre that emerged in the United States in the late 1980s, with White Zombie, formed in 1985, as a foundational influence. Its sound was shaped by a wide array of inspirations, spanning renegade noise and gothic rock—Honeymoon Killers, Swans, Pussy Galore, the Cramps and gothic rock—alongside classic metal and hard rock acts such as Van Halen, Kiss, AC/DC and Black Sabbath. The movement began within New York City’s noise rock milieu, and the band was approached by Cro-Mags and Biohazard to bridge into the New York hardcore scene. Several NYHC groups adopted metal and groove elements, with Sick of It All and Leeway being described as exemplars of a Jackson Heights–based groove metal approach. White Zombie increasingly incorporated groove-oriented heaviness on their second album, Make Them Die Slowly (1989). The band achieved mainstream success in the mid-1990s, exemplified by La Sexorcisto: Devil Music Volume One (1992), which peaked at number two on the Heatseekers Albums chart in 1993 and was certified double platinum by the RIAA in July 1998; its music videos helped boost sales through exposure on Beavis and Butt-Head. Astro Creep: 2000 (1995) reached number six on the Billboard 200, with first-week sales of about 104,000, and was also certified double platinum. The single “More Human than Human” (1995) charted across multiple Billboard lists, peaking at number 53 on Radio Songs, number 7 on Alternative Songs, and number 10 on Mainstream Rock Songs, aided by heavy MTV airplay and its accompanying video, which earned the Best Metal/Hard Rock Video at the 1995 MTV Video Music Awards.

Groove metal experienced a second wave in the 2000s, with notable acts including Damageplan, Lamb of God, Chimaira, and DevilDriver shaping the era. Damageplan was formed in 2003 by the Abbott brothers, Dimebag Darrell and Vinnie Paul, shortly after Pantera disbanded, and the band released New Found Power in 2004 before dissolving in December of that year following the onstage murder of Dimebag Darrell. Five Finger Death Punch, formed in 2005, rose to prominence as one of the genre’s most commercially successful groups, achieving chart placements and gold or platinum certifications in the United States. Vinnie Paul’s post-Damageplan project Hellyeah began in 2006 and likewise enjoyed substantial commercial success. The 2010s saw the emergence of groups such as Killer Be Killed and Bad Wolves. In 2022, Malevolence released its third studio album Malicious Intent, which garnered widespread attention and blended groove metal with sludge metal, beatdown hardcore, and metalcore. Metal Hammer has described Malevolence as a definitive act within the groove metal genre.

The tenor saxophone is best known for its prominent role in jazz, where it has long been celebrated as a principal melodic voice. In the 1930s Coleman Hawkins helped establish the instrument's stature, developing a powerful, resonant tone that elevated the tenor to a leading melodic instrument, a contrast to Lester Young's lighter, more airy approach. Since the 1930s, a diverse array of innovative jazz musicians has explored the instrument, with Hawkins’ robust sound contrasting with Young’s lighter style. In the bebop era, notable tenor lines emerged from the Four Brothers saxophone section of Woody Herman's orchestra, among them Stan Getz, who would go on to achieve wide popularity in the 1960s through his collaborations in the Brazilian bossa nova idiom. Other prominent tenor saxophonists include John Coltrane, Dexter Gordon, and Sonny Rollins. In more recent decades, the tenor has remained popular in smooth jazz, with artists such as Kirk Whalum, Richard Elliot, Steve Cole, and Jessy J. In the jam band scene, saxophonists Ron Holloway and Karl Denson are recognized as major proponents of the tenor. Beyond jazz, the instrument features in popular music contexts as well; for instance, Van Morrison learned music notation and the tenor saxophone from his Hyndford Street neighbor George Cassidy, with whom he formed a lasting friendship.

The tenor saxophone is an approximately conical brass wind instrument with a flared bell at the wider end and a narrow neck that carries a single-reed mouthpiece similar to the clarinet. It contains roughly 20–23 tone holes along the bore, each covered by pads to form airtight seals. Two small vent holes are incorporated; when opened, they alter lower harmonic content and promote overblowing into a higher register. The pads are actuated by keys operated with fingers from both hands, while the left thumb controls an octave key that opens one of the vent holes. In the original design, a separate octave key existed for each vent hole, a arrangement akin to that of the bassoon. The mechanism that selects the appropriate vent hole based on left-hand fingering, notably the left ring finger, was developed shortly after Sax’s patent expired in 1866.

Ljudski vrt is a football stadium in Maribor that is primarily accessed by public transportation, as there are no dedicated parking spaces on-site. Several bus lines run directly past the venue, with lines 3, 7, 8, 12, 18, 19 and 151 stopping within about 150 metres at the Gosposvetska street bus station. The stadium lies about a 15-minute walk from both the Maribor bus station and the Maribor railway station. The latter is situated on the Pan-European Corridor Xa (Zagreb to Graz) and on Corridor V (Barcelona to Kyiv). Maribor Edvard Rusjan Airport is located approximately 15 kilometres to the south.

Ljudski vrt underwent a two-phase expansion beginning with Phase 1 improvements costing around €10 million. The open stands to the north, east and south were demolished and replaced with new covered stands. Construction started in 2006 and was completed in 2008, with the new stands providing a total seating capacity of 8,500. The renovated stands were inaugurated on 10 May 2008 in a league match against Nafta Lendava, a sold-out fixture attended by 12,435 spectators in which Maribor won 3–1. Phase 2 took place from 2009 to 2011 and added facilities beneath the East Stand, including new dressing rooms, two gyms, and a new boiler room.

David Frizzell, born in El Dorado, Arkansas, is an American country music singer who began performing in his brother's show at age twelve and subsequently toured with him throughout the 1950s and 1960s. He served in the United States Air Force during the Vietnam War before signing with Columbia Records in 1970. As a solo artist, Frizzell achieved chart success with the single "I Just Can't Help Believing," which reached the Billboard country top‑40.

David Frizzell is an American country music singer who gained national exposure on Buck Owens' All American TV Show in the 1970s and recorded for Capitol Records. In 1981 he achieved his first chart-topping country hit with the duet "You're the Reason God Made Oklahoma," performed with Shelly West. The song earned the Country Music Association's Song of the Year and Vocal Duo of the Year honors for 1981, and received a nomination for the Grammy Award for Best Country Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocal. It was also featured on the soundtrack of Clint Eastwood's Any Which Way You Can. Frizzell and West were named the ACM Vocal Duo of the Year in 1981 and again in 1982.

Spanning from 29 August 2007 to 16 April 2008, the competition culminated in a final played at Madrid's Vicente Calderón Stadium, where Valencia defeated Getafe 3–1 to secure their seventh Copa del Rey crown. Getafe reached the final for the second consecutive season, having been runners-up the previous year as well. The defending champions, Sevilla, were eliminated in the round of 16, ending their title defense.

Sun News Network expressed disappointment at the denial of mandatory carriage, and its advocacy campaign was described as a catalyst for the CRTC’s decision. The commission’s ruling addresses distribution rules for Category C national news channels and notes potential barriers to premier placement and the exchange of ideas on matters of public concern. In response, the CRTC initiated a rules review and proposed guidelines obliging distributors to carry all national news channels, with considerations for packaging, pricing, lineup proximity, and dispute resolution. A new set of rules was issued on December 19, 2013. By March 19, 2014, providers were required to offer all Category C national news channels to subscribers, though not necessarily on the lowest tier, and by May 18, 2014, channels not on the lowest level had to be included in the best available discretionary package or offered as standalone options. CRTC chair Jean-Pierre Blais stated that the changes were intended to ensure Canadians have access to news services of interest and a range of viewpoints. The ruling does not guarantee Sun News favorable channel placement or a per-subscriber fee, but it was regarded as positive news for the network, with at least one financial analyst describing the changes as incrementally positive for Sun News.

In September 2013, the Canadian Broadcast Standards Council ruled that a broadcast by Ezra Levant on Sun News Network violated the Canadian Association of Broadcasters' Code of Ethics and Equitable Portrayal Code. Levant's remarks about the Roma were abusive and unduly discriminatory toward an ethnic group, and the ruling also found that the segment breached other provisions of the code concerning negative portrayal, stereotyping, stigmatization, and degradation.

The Historic Centre of Guimarães is closely linked to the formation of Portugal's national identity and the development of the Portuguese language in the twelfth century. It is the native city of Afonso Henriques, who would become Portugal's first king, and in 1139 he proclaimed the independence of Portugal.

The Historic Centre of Guimarães is located in the city of Guimarães, Portugal. Its origins lie in the medieval period, and the area encompasses 16 hectares. The ensemble preserves a range of buildings dating from the medieval era through the nineteenth century, reflecting the town’s long urban development. In 2001, the historic centre was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

Trichinella spiralis is a parasitic nematode responsible for trichinellosis in humans and other mammals. In 2005, infection rates were notably higher in parts of Europe, Asia, and Southeast Asia than in the United States. Within the European Union, authorities employ meat surveillance and testing strategies to detect Trichinella spiralis; when testing is consistently negative, the affected meat supply may be designated as Trichinella-free. Despite these measures, sporadic outbreaks continue to occur, including instances linked to the consumption of raw horsemeat in France, Italy, and Poland. At the time, the parasite was considered endemic in Japan and China, and Korea had recently reported its first human cases of trichinosis.

Trichinella spiralis is among the smallest nematode parasites of humans and is of worldwide clinical importance. The life cycle is unusual: adults mature in the small intestine of a definitive host, typically a pig. Adult females produce batches of live larvae (viviparous). The larvae bore through the intestinal wall and enter the bloodstream and lymphatic system, where they are carried to striated muscle. In muscle, they encyst, forming a capsule around the larvae.

In 1988, the Hinckley family acquired Cove Fort and subsequently donated it back to the Church. The Church undertook restoration work and relocated Ira Hinckley's coalville, Utah cabin to the site as part of the fort complex. A visitor center was constructed to support public access, and the fort was then reopened as a historic site. The site offers free guided tours on a daily basis, with tours typically starting around 8:00 a.m. and ending about thirty minutes before sunset.

Brigham Young selected the Cove Fort location because it lay about midway between Fillmore, then the capital of the Utah Territory, and Beaver. The fort functioned as a way station for travelers on the Mormon Road, facilitating rest and resupply along the route. Plans for a town at the site were never realized, as the water supply proved insufficient to sustain a substantial population. Prior to its construction, Willden Fort—a wooden-palisade fort—occupied the site and offered shelter and security for crews during the building of Cove Fort.

The Ob class, designated by the Soviet Navy as Project 320, was a group of hospital ships built for the Soviet fleet and active during the 1980s. The class comprised four vessels—the Ob, Yenisey, Svir, and Irtysh.

Following the 1991 dissolution of the Soviet Union, the Ob-class hospital ships came under the ownership of the Russian government. No reliable sources document any subsequent use or deployment of these vessels by the Russian Navy, leaving their post-Soviet status and activities unclear.

Gale is a wind-strength category with definitions that vary across organizations and contexts, ranging from a lower bound near 28 knots to an upper limit that can extend as high as 90 knots, though the 90-knot maximum is not widely accepted. Historically, the National Hurricane Center defined a gale through 1986 as coastal tropical-force winds within the interval of roughly 33 to 63 knots. In many contemporary references, a more common upper bound is about 55 knots, making 55 knots a frequently cited threshold for gale classification. These differences reflect varying operational criteria and regional usage in maritime meteorology.

A gale is a strong wind, principally used in nautical contexts. The United States National Weather Service defines a gale as a sustained surface wind of 34 to 47 knots, which corresponds to 63.0–87.0 km/h, 17.5–24.2 m/s, or 39.1–54.1 mph. Warnings of this magnitude are issued when such winds are forecast. In the United States, a gale warning functions as a maritime warning, while the land-based equivalent in NWS products is the wind advisory.

Israel is a term historically used to designate both the biblical Land of Israel and the people known as the Children of Israel—the Jewish people. The name is traditionally traced to the patriarch Jacob, who was renamed Israel after wrestling with the Angel of the Lord. In Hebrew the form is Yīsrāʾēl, and in the Septuagint Greek it appears as Israēl, with the meaning often interpreted as “El (God) persists” or “God rules.” The Merneptah Stele, a late 13th–century BCE Egyptian inscription, is the earliest known artifact to mention Israel as a collective.

Israel operates a system of universal military conscription for its citizens, who are required to begin service at age 18. Men typically serve about 32 months (two years and eight months), while women serve for about 24 months. After their initial service, men generally join the reserve forces and are expected to undertake several weeks of reserve duty annually into their forties; most women are exempt from reserve duty. Exemptions from conscription are granted to Arab citizens of Israel (with the Druze being an exception to this exemption) and to individuals devoted to full-time religious studies, although the exemption for yeshiva students has been a matter of public debate. For those exempt from service, Sherut Leumi, or national service, provides an alternative in which individuals perform work in welfare or related sectors. A small minority of Israeli Arabs volunteer for military service. The Israel Defense Forces maintains approximately 176,500 active troops and 465,000 reservists, and Israel has one of the world’s highest shares of citizens with military training.
In 2017, Nobel Prize laureate Robert J. Shiller, the author of the book Irrational Exuberance, identified Bitcoin as the most notable example of a speculative bubble at that time.

During the address that popularized the term irrational exuberance, the Tokyo Stock Exchange was in session as the remarks were delivered; the market fell abruptly in response, closing the day down about three percent. The reaction extended beyond Tokyo, with stock markets across the globe following suit and posting declines in the wake of the speech.

Raymond Berry, a renowned wide receiver for the Baltimore Colts, later joined the New England Patriots' coaching staff under Chuck Fairbanks and eventually became the Patriots' head coach in 1984. One of his early victories came in the form of a 50–17 win over the Colts during New England's first trip to Indianapolis. As head coach, Berry posted a 10–2 record against the Colts, including season sweeps in 1984–86 and again in 1989, contributing a notable chapter to the Colts–Patriots rivalry.

Entering the matchup, the Patriots led the all-time series against the Colts 9–4, and it was the first meeting in the post-Brady era as well as the first since 1997 in which neither Tom Brady, Andrew Luck, nor Peyton Manning started for either team. The Colts opened with Carson Wentz at quarterback while the Patriots started Mac Jones. Indianapolis built a 17–0 halftime cushion behind a stout defensive performance and a blocked punt returned for a touchdown by E. J. Speed. In the second half, the Colts missed a field goal and Wentz threw an interception, allowing New England to close the gap to 20–17. Jonathan Taylor carried 29 times for 170 yards and scored his 17th rushing touchdown, establishing a Colts single-season rushing TD record. The final score was Colts 27, Patriots 17, with Taylor sealing the victory on a 67-yard touchdown run in the final three minutes. Jones finished 26 of 45 for 299 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions, while Wentz went 5 of 12 for 57 yards with one touchdown and one interception. This victory marked the Colts’ first over the Patriots since 2009, after they went 0–8 against New England in the 2010s.
PDF/X-5pg is an extension of PDF/X-4p within the PDF/X family. It enables the use of external graphical content and relies on a reference to an external ICC Profile to define the output intent.

PDF/X is the ISO standard for exchanging PDF files in the graphic arts industry. ISO 15930-7:2008 defines PDF/X-4 as a conformance level that supports color-managed data across CMYK, grayscale, RGB, or spot colors, together with PDF transparency and optional content. A second conformance level, PDF/X-4p, allows the use of externally supplied ICC profiles within the output intent. The specification is based on PDF version 1.6. ISO 15930-7:2010, the second edition, includes minor corrections and improvements that do not change file identifications.

Freight traffic on Vesijärvi station’s siding expanded rapidly, and by 1885 the facility was among the busiest cargo hubs on the Riihimäki–St. Petersburg line, with cargo volumes second only to Saint Petersburg’s Finland Station. The rise in freight activity coincided with the concentration of Lahti’s industry on the station’s northern side, where early industrial enterprises developed, including the Lahden Höyrysaha sawmill, founded in 1870.

Vesijärvi railway station formed part of the Riihimäki–Saint Petersburg line as it reached Lahti in August 1869. To link the main line with the shore of Lake Vesijärvi and thus integrate rail traffic with the Päijänne waterway, a siding was constructed. The Vääksy canal, built between 1868 and 1871, connected the Päijänne and Vesijärvi basins, enabling broader waterborne transport to complement rail services. The Vesijärvi siding began operation on 1 November 1869, coinciding with the opening of the Riihimäki–Lahti section. Passenger service combined local trains to Lahti with transfers to Päijänne vessels for continued travel toward Heinola or Jyväskylä.

Interim Register of Marine and Nonmarine Genera (IRMNG) is a comprehensive taxonomic database that compiles genus‑level names for both marine and nonmarine organisms, providing a reference framework for taxonomic data curation. Its content is used by a range of global biodiversity informatics projects, including the Open Tree of Life, the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF), the Encyclopedia of Life (EOL), the Atlas of Living Australia, and the Global Names Architecture's Global Names Resolver, to support data integration and name concordance. Since 2018, IRMNG data have been employed to populate the taxonomic hierarchy and supply generic names for protists—encompassing the groups Protozoa and Chromista—and for plant algae across divisions such as Charophyta, Chlorophyta, Glaucophyta, and Rhodophyta within the Catalogue of Life.

Interim Register of Marine and Nonmarine Genera (IRMNG) is a taxonomic database developed and launched in 2006 by Tony Rees, an Australian biologist and data manager, and its work earned him the 2014 Ebbe Nielsen Prize from GBIF in recognition of this and related projects. The resource was hosted within CSIRO Marine and Atmospheric Research from its inception until 2014, after which it was relocated to the Flanders Marine Institute (VLIZ) and remained there through 2016. From 2016 onward, all IRMNG releases have been made available online at www.irmng.org, with VLIZ serving as the hosting institution. VLIZ also operates the World Register of Marine Species (WoRMS) on a shared infrastructure, linking the two registries under a common platform.

The ICT Development Index (IDI) is used to rank and compare the level of information and communications technology use and access across countries. In 2014, the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) released the IDI rankings, with Denmark at the top and South Korea following in second place. The top 30 comprises largely high-income economies that generally enjoy a higher-than-average quality of life, including Australia, Bahrain, Canada, Japan, Macao (China), New Zealand, Singapore, and the United States, along with many European nations. Almost all countries surveyed improved their IDI ranking in 2014.

Information and communications technology (ICT) has become a central element in modern education, yet its success depends on its full integration into pedagogy rather than being employed in isolation. When used in literacy and mathematics, ICT is most effective when paired with a writing-to-learn approach, producing better learning outcomes than traditional instruction or ICT alone.

Abtao-class submarines were designed with a diesel-electric propulsion system that uses two General Motors Type 278A diesel engines of the single-acting configuration, paired with two electric motors that drive two propellers. Together, they produce 2,400 brake horsepower (1,800 kW). The class achieves a maximum speed of 16 knots on the surface and 10 knots when submerged.
