By eliminating all variants of the cached content, this method ensures that subsequent responses reflect the most up-to-date information.

Cache invalidation is a technique wherein a request retrieves content from the application rather than serving the cached copy, ensuring that the latest version is used. Once retrieved, the cache entry is updated to store the new version provided by the application, effectively replacing the previously cached item. This method affects only a single variant of the cached content.

The comes sacrarum largitionum, literally meaning “count of the sacred largesses,” was a senior fiscal official of the late Roman Empire. The office was established circa 318 AD under Constantine the Great and is first attested in sources dated to 342–345, succeeding the Principate-era rationalis. It was responsible for supervising financial sectors outside the remit of the praetorian prefects, including the taxation of senators, the chrysargyron tax, customs duties, and the administration of mines, mints, and state-operated mills and textile factories. Initially it controlled the emperor’s private domains, but by the end of the fourth century those assets were transferred to the comes rerum privatarum. Additionally, the office exercised judicial functions relating to taxation within administrative courts, particularly in matters of fiscal debt.

Comes sacrarum largitionum was a senior Byzantine fiscal official responsible for royal revenues and the management of the state’s financial bureaux; its importance gradually declined after the late fifth century, a process accelerated by Emperor Anastasius I (r. 491–518) when he abolished chrysargyron. Nonetheless, during Anastasius’s reign he remained a major fiscal minister, exercising control over the scrinia, or bureaux, and directing a substantial provincial staff. The last known holder is mentioned during the reign of Phocas (r. 602–610); thereafter the role was superseded by the sakellarios and the logothetes tou genikou, who would remain the chief fiscal ministers in the middle Byzantine period (7th–11th centuries).

Under the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS) framework and the International Life-Saving Appliance (LSA) Code, lifeboats and liferafts intended for international voyages are required to carry a prescribed set of emergency equipment. Each individual lifeboat or liferaft must be equipped with the mandated items. In contemporary designs, lifeboats typically include an Emergency Position-Indicating Radio Beacon (EPIRB) to transmit distress signals, and they are outfitted with either a radar reflector or a Search and Rescue Transponder (SART) to aid in detection and location by rescuers.

Under the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS) regulations, merchant ships are required to have liferafts on both the port and starboard sides. These liferafts must be able to serve all persons on board according to their stated capacity, even if the actual occupancy is lower. When liferafts are readily transferable—that is, when an open deck exists between the port and starboard lifeboat decks—the overall number of liferafts may be reduced to correspond to the ship’s capacity. The transferability condition is specifically defined as the presence of an open deck between the two lifeboat decks.

Timber recycling has gained popularity due to its perceived environmental advantages. Many consumers believe that purchasing reclaimed wood lowers demand for freshly milled timber and thus benefits the environment. Greenpeace has described recycled timber as environmentally friendly and has identified it as a preferred timber source on its website. The emergence of recycled timber as a construction material has increased awareness of deforestation within the industry and among consumers. This trend has encouraged timber mills to adopt more environmentally friendly practices.

Timber recycling has a long history as a practice of reusing wood from prior structures. A notable early instance occurred in 1948 when the Golm transmitter tower near Potsdam, Germany, was built from recycled timber. The tower reached a height of 100 metres (about 330 feet) and remained standing for 31 years.

Hibernate (Java) is an object-relational mapping framework for Java that manages the persistence of data objects. In typical mappings, collections of related objects are represented using standard Java collection types, such as Set and List. The framework supports Java generics, introduced with Java 5, enabling type-safe handling of these collections. It can be configured to load associated collections lazily, so related data is retrieved only when accessed. Since Hibernate 3, lazy loading has been the default behavior, contributing to more efficient data access by avoiding unnecessary queries.

The org.hibernate.Session interface represents a Hibernate session and serves as the primary API for manipulating database entities within Hibernate. It manages the persistence state of domain objects across their lifecycle, including transient, persisted (managed), and detached states. Through the session, applications retrieve entities that have been persisted in the database, enabling querying and retrieval operations as needed. It also governs transaction boundaries by providing mechanisms to begin, commit, and roll back transactions, thereby coordinating atomic changes to the persistence context and the underlying database.

The 1981 Avon Championships of Houston was a women's tennis tournament played on indoor carpet courts at The Summit in Houston, Texas, United States. It formed part of the 1981 Avon Championships Circuit and was the 11th edition of the event, held from February 16 through February 22, 1981. The singles title was won by Hana Mandlíková, the second seed, who earned the first-prize money of $22,000. The top seed, Tracy Austin, withdrew from the tournament due to a back injury.

Abuta District, Rumoi District, Sorachi District, and Yufutsu District share a common characteristic in the administrative geography of Japan: each exists as a single district that is assigned to two subprefectures. This configuration demonstrates how certain districts can straddle subprefectural boundaries, illustrating the varying relationships between district and subprefectural divisions within the Japanese system.

Historically, districts served as an administrative subdivision within Japan. From 1878 to 1921, district governments were broadly comparable to counties in the United States. They occupied a hierarchical position below prefectures and above towns or villages, and were considered to share the same level of status as cities. The district government system was abolished entirely by 1926.

The Roman Catholic Diocese of Portalegre-Castelo Branco has been led by a number of bishops across its history. Diego Conra, a nephew of the Venerable Bartholomew of the Martyrs and formerly bishop of Ceuta, became bishop in 1598 and died on 9 October 1614. In the 17th century, the see was held by Ricardo Russell, an Englishman, who took possession of the Portalegre see on 17 September 1671 and was subsequently transferred to the diocese of Vizeu.

The Diocese of Portalegre-Castelo Branco was erected as a see in 1550 by Pope Julius III, taken from parts of the Archdiocese of Évora and the Diocese of Guarda. The first bishop was Julian d'Alva, a Spaniard, who in 1557 was transferred to the Diocese of Miranda. On 17 July 1560, Andiz de Noronha was appointed bishop of Portalegre, a position he would leave in 1581 when promoted to the Diocese of Placencia. Frei Amador Arraes, a Carmelite noted for his celebrated Dialogues, resigned the see in 1582 and retired to the Carmelite college in Coimbra, where he remained until his death. The careers of Lopo Soares de Albergaria and Frei Manoel de Gouveia were marked by the absence of papal bulls confirming their nominations, as both died before such confirmations could be issued.

Floods on the Red River of the North occur when extended periods of heavy precipitation cause water levels to rise above the riverbanks, a process that is often intensified by spring snowmelt and ice jams. Throughout its history, the river has experienced several major floods in 1826, 1897, 1950, 1997, 2009, and 2011, with many additional events in between, and geologists have identified paleofloods preserved in landforms. In the wake of the 1950 flood, Manitoba constructed the Red River Floodway, completed in 1968, to divert floodwaters around Winnipeg toward downstream areas. The 1997 floods caused widespread destruction in Grand Forks, North Dakota, and East Grand Forks, Minnesota, prompting the evacuation of roughly 75% of Grand Forks’s population and the complete evacuation of East Grand Forks, with many residential areas inundated and homes destroyed. Following this event, substantial flood-protection projects were undertaken to safeguard both cities. Research by Atashi and colleagues examined Permanent Water Area and Seasonal Water Area, identifying a vulnerable section near Grafton city (between Grand Forks and Emerson) that is highly susceptible to severe floods.

The Red River of the North flows across the flat bed of glacial Lake Agassiz, an ancient lake formed near the end of the Wisconsin glaciation from meltwaters of the Laurentide Ice Sheet. As the ice sheet retreated and decayed, the lake came into being, and over thousands of years sediments settled on its floor to form lacustrine soils that constitute the parent soils of the modern Red River Valley. The river itself is geologically young, having developed mainly after Lake Agassiz drained, about 9,500 years ago.

Jean Lecanuet was a French politician who held several senior offices in the 1970s and 1980s. He served as Minister of Justice in Jacques Chirac's first cabinet from 1974 to 1976, and thereafter as Minister of State for Territorial Development in Raymond Barre's first cabinet from 1976 to 1977. In 1978 he was elected president of the Union for French Democracy (UDF), a position he retained until 1988. Lecanuet was also a member of the European Parliament from 1979 to 1988. As a Senator for Seine-Maritime, he chaired the Senate's Foreign Affairs and Armed Forces Committee, a post he had previously held from 1971 to 1973.

Jean Lecanuet was a French politician who, in 1972, co-founded the Reforming Movement (Mouvement Réformiste) with Jean-Jacques Servan-Schreiber. In the 1973 legislative elections, he participated in negotiations with Pierre Messmer to withdraw certain candidates in order to consolidate the center-right's majority. He was elected deputy for Seine-Maritime. The following year, 1974, he actively supported Valéry Giscard d'Estaing in the presidential campaign.

Carl Fredrik Adelcrantz’s 1783–84 journey through Italy and France helped steer the King's aesthetic toward radical classicism. Although he adapted to the new fashions, younger architects in step with contemporary tastes gained the monarch’s favor and sidelined him. In 1787, at the age of seventy-two, he petitioned the King to retire on grounds of deteriorating health and financial difficulties, but the request was refused. He was ultimately allowed to retire as öверintendent in 1795, with Carl Fredrik Fredenheim taking over the post on 16 February. He remained an active civil servant until his final days, his last architectural design being an altar for the Stockholms-Näs parish church, created at the age of eighty. Adelcrantz also retired as president of the Academy of Art in June 1795. He died in Stockholm in March 1796 after a period marked by painful cancer and worsening financial problems.

Carl Fredrik Adelcrantz was encouraged by his father, Göran Josua Adelcrantz, to pursue artistic work, receiving drawing lessons and assisting with his father's projects. Among his early design efforts were an altar for Katarina Church during its reconstruction after a fire and a proposed tower for the Finnish Church that was never built. About six months after his father’s death in 1739, he left his post in Kammarrevisionen and departed Stockholm for France and Italy on 11 August 1739, spending two years in Paris and several months in Rome. In December 1741, while still in Rome, he was named to a position on a palace construction project. His talent had to be won over by Count Carl Gustaf Tessin, whom he had sought for a recommendation, and Carl Hårleman secured the appointment on his behalf. Adelcrantz began his return journey to Sweden in late summer 1743 and arrived in Stockholm in November.

The Mount Kumgang Tourist Region, centered on Mount Kumgang in North Korea, developed as a cross-border and international tourist area in the early 2010s. In April 2010 North Korea allowed tours to operate from its side, effectively reducing the likelihood of a revival of South-to-North travel arrangements. On October 1, 2010, a Red Cross agreement facilitated reunions for families separated by the Korean War, with 100 families from each side scheduled to visit the North’s Diamond Mountain resort between October 30 and November 5, a gesture linked to the tensions triggered by the sinking of a South Korean warship. By September 2011 North Korea was offering direct cruises from Rason to Mount Kumgang, enabling visitors to stay in resorts formerly run by South Korea. Throughout these developments, the tours were primarily marketed to Chinese travelers, with Western tour operators also providing options.

In July 2008, Park Wang-ja, a 53-year-old South Korean tourist, was shot twice and killed after entering a military area, according to statements from the North Korean government. South Korea requested a joint inquiry into the death, but the proposal was rejected by North Korea. Forensic evaluations indicated that Park was stationary or moving slowly at the time of the shooting, contrary to North Korea's assertion that she had been running and ignoring warnings. In the immediate aftermath, South Korea suspended tours to the Mount Kumgang resort. In August 2008, North Korea announced the expulsion of a number of South Korean workers from the resort, labeling them as unnecessary.

Protasekretis was a senior Byzantine official in the imperial chancery, supported by subordinates such as the asekretis, an inferior tier of imperial notaries under the protonotarios, and the dekanos who managed the imperial papers, as described in the De Ceremoniis of Constantine VII (reign c. 913–959). The office appears to have been responsible for preparing the emperor’s chrysobulls. After 1106, the holder transferred from chancery duties to the judiciary, heading one of Byzantium’s highest courts. This tribunal was led jointly with other senior officials—eparchos, megas droungarios tes viglas, dikaiodotes, koiaistor, epi ton kriseon—and the katholikos, who chaired the branch dealing with fiscal affairs (demosiaka pragmata). The asekretis class is not attested after the twelfth century, but the office of protasekretis persisted into the Palaiologan period.

At Apple's September 2017 Special Event, Craig Federighi demonstrated Face ID on the iPhone X, but the onstage demo did not operate as intended. Apple later explained that before the event some Apple employees had inadvertently triggered Face ID on the demonstration device, resulting in the phone prompting for a passcode when Federighi attempted to unlock it.

Craig Federighi, Apple's senior vice president of Software Engineering, made a brief cameo during the September 2020 Apple Event. He appeared in a short on-stage segment and did not deliver any spoken remarks.
Sergiu Litvinenco (born 11 July 1981) is a Moldovan politician who served as Minister of Justice from August 2021 to February 2023, in the cabinet of Prime Minister Natalia Gavrilița.

Sovetskaya Latviya (Russian: Советская Латвия) was a prominent Russian-language newspaper published in the Latvian Soviet Socialist Republic. The name literally means “Soviet Latvia” in English. The publication was assigned the ISSN 0233-3643 and served as an important source of news for Russian-speaking readers in the Latvian SSR.

Sovetskaya Latviya was a Russian-language broadsheet newspaper published in Latvia, issued daily with the exception of Mondays. During the Soviet period, it dominated the Russian-language newspaper market in Latvia alongside Sovetskaya Molodëzh' (Soviet Youth). In 1975, its circulation stood at 107,500 copies.

The Charitable Corporation v Sutton addresses the limits of fiduciary power and the accountability that accompanies its exercise. The judgment makes clear that a fiduciary, including a judge or administrator, cannot justify harmful outcomes by claiming that they foresaw them as inevitable after acting; mere anticipation of likely consequences at the time does not excuse the action or absolve the fiduciary of responsibility. When the exercise of power results in harm, those who authorized or carried out the acts may be liable for breach of trust. In this way, the passage underscores the core principles of fiduciary duty and accountability in the use of entrusted authority.

The Charitable Corporation v Sutton deals with the duties of trustees in a charitable body, focusing on members who display gross non-attendance and effectively relinquish governance to others. The court indicated that those absentee trustees may be liable for breaches of trust committed by the individuals who actually manage the charity, given their failure to supervise and participate in the administration of trust affairs. The ruling underscores the responsibility of trustees to oversee the management of trust assets, such that neglecting to engage in governance can implicate them in mismanagement carried out by those entrusted with running the institution.

Super TV was a television service broadcast on two local stations in the United States. It aired on WCQR, channel 50, in Washington, D.C., from 1981 to 1985, and on WNUV, channel 54, in Baltimore, from 1982 to 1986.

Super TV was an American subscription television service that operated in the Washington, D.C., and Baltimore metropolitan areas. It was owned by Subscription Television of Greater Washington, Inc. and represented an early form of subscription television. The service was offered either as a standalone option for households without access to cable-originated premium channels (such as HBO and Showtime) or as an additional viewing option for those who subscribed to such channels.

The Congregation of Our Lady of Charity of the Good Shepherd is a religious community of contemplative sisters dedicated to prayer and spiritual service. To support their life and mission, the order undertakes a variety of income-generating activities, including the manufacture of liturgical vestments and the supply of altar breads to parishes. In addition, members create artistic works and engage in creative computer projects, such as graphic design, Card production, and music composition, which contribute to the congregation's financial self-sufficiency.

The Congregation of Our Lady of Charity of the Good Shepherd is a religious institute of the Catholic Church that originated as a cloistered order and is now predominantly apostolic in character. Its members live according to the Rule of Saint Augustine. Historically, the contemplative and apostolic branches operated as separate communities; these branches eventually united, and today the institute embodies both contemplative and active modes of life within a single structure.

Ed Zschau graduated cum laude from Princeton University in 1961 with an A.B. in philosophy, completing a senior thesis that examined space, time, and geometry from Kant to Einstein. He went on to earn an MBA, a Master of Science in Statistics, and a Ph.D. from Stanford University.

Edwin Van Wyck Zschau (born January 6, 1940) is an American educator and former politician who represented California's 12th congressional district in the United States House of Representatives from 1983 to 1987. In 1986, he pursued the United States Senate as the Republican nominee, prevailing in a crowded primary that included Bruce Herschensohn, Michael D. Antonovich, and Bobbi Fiedler among others. He narrowly lost the general election to incumbent Democrat Alan Cranston.

Fellatio refers to the stimulation of the male genitals through oral contact, typically involving the penis being placed in the mouth and manipulated by the lips and tongue. A more intensive form, commonly termed deep-throating, describes inserting the penis deeper toward the back of the throat. The technique and its name gained prominent public attention following the 1972 adult film Deep Throat, which helped popularize the practice. Some discussions of deep-throating emphasize that achieving greater depth can be constrained by anatomy, with a longer penis able to reach the posterior oropharynx.

In Malaysia, fellatio is illegal under Section 377A of the Penal Code, though the statute is seldom enforced. The act is defined as the insertion of the penis into the mouth or anus of another person, described in legal terms as carnal intercourse against the order of nature. Offenders face penalties of up to 20 years' imprisonment and whipping.

Environmental laws governing ships have grown stricter in recent years, prompting a shift in design philosophy toward sustainability. Ship designers are urged to incorporate design-for-disassembly principles that allow components to be taken apart or disposed of with ease at the vessel’s end of life. Ensuring that end-of-life disassembly is practical is considered essential to reducing material waste and enabling recycling or safe disposal. Taken together, these measures reflect a broader objective to lessen the environmental footprint of ships through careful design and lifecycle considerations.

Steam-powered vessels coexisted with sailing ships from the 19th into the early 20th century, with early viability on shorter routes allowing those who could pay higher fares for passengers and mail to benefit from the new technology. Over time, steam demonstrated improved fuel efficiency and grew more commercially competitive with sail, aided by the relative advantages of screw propulsion over paddle wheels, provided a reliable stern gland could seal the propeller shaft. A notable advance occurred in 1865 when boiler pressures of around 60 psi powering compound engines made long-distance trade feasible, enabling England–China cargo service even before the Suez Canal opened in 1869. Within a few years, steamships displaced many sailing vessels on the England–China route, and further efficiency gains came with triple-expansion engines that offered greater fuel economy but required higher-quality steel for boilers operating at about 125 psi. The 1881 deployment of boilers rated at 125 psi in ships such as the SS Aberdeen marked a milestone in material capability. By that year, steamships could competitively serve virtually all routes, though sail still persisted for certain cargoes where cost considerations outweighed the speed advantage.

ER's fifth season featured the return of original executive producers John Wells and Michael Crichton, along with Lydia Woodward, Carol Flint, and Christopher Chulack in executive producer roles. Flint exited the production team at the end of the season. Walon Green, who had served as co-executive producer, came back for the fifth season but left midway through. Neal Baer and Jack Orman, elevated from their fourth-season posts as producer and co-producer, were promoted to supervising producers for season five. Penny Adams, together with co-producers Wendy Spence Rosato, Richard Thorpe, and Michael Salamunovich, continued in their duties, with Spence Rosato advancing to producer partway through the season. Samantha Howard Corbin, the former executive story editor from season four, was promoted to co-producer for the fifth season but departed mid-season, and Jonathan Kaplan took over Corbin's co-producer duties later in the season.
The fifth season of the American medical drama ER was broadcast on NBC, premiering on September 24, 1998, and concluding on May 20, 1999, comprising 22 episodes.

Steffi Graf, the defending champion, did not participate in the 1995 Australian Open due to injury, and Monica Seles also did not compete as she remained in recovery from the 1993 stabbing incident. Consequently, the tournament marked the first Australian Open since 1987 in which neither Graf nor Seles appeared. Historically, Graf and Seles had dominated the event in the preceding years, together capturing seven consecutive Australian Open titles from 1988 to 1994, with Graf taking the first three editions and Seles the subsequent three.

The 1995 Australian Open – Women's singles event concluded with Mary Pierce defeating Arantxa Sánchez Vicario in the final, 6–3, 6–2, to claim her first major singles title. Pierce did not lose a set during the tournament.

The Yukaghir people comprise two principal groups: the Tundra Yukaghirs, who inhabit the Lower Kolyma region in the Sakha Republic, and the Taiga Yukaghirs, who reside in the Upper Kolyma region of the Sakha Republic as well as in the Srednekansky District of Magadan Oblast. By the 17th century, following Russian expansion, Yukaghir communities occupied territory extending from the Lena River to the mouth of the Anadyr River. The population declined markedly between the 17th and 19th centuries due to epidemics, internecine warfare, and Tsarist colonial policies, which is believed to have included acts of genocide against the sedentary hunter-fisher Anaouls. Over time, some Yukaghirs assimilated with neighboring groups such as the Yakuts, Evens, and Russians.

A genetic study of 11 Yukaghir males found a Y-chromosome haplogroup distribution comprising three individuals in N1c, a subclade distinct from that observed in Yakuts; four in C2 (formerly C3), a subclade largely shared with the Koryaks; and one in O. In terms of broader ancestry, three individuals exhibited Russian genetic influence, including two in R1a and one in I2a. Mitochondrial DNA analysis showed no similarities between Yukaghirs and Chukchis.

Beijing Forestry University (BFU) emphasizes an integration of specialized instruction with the cultivation of well-rounded competencies, pursuing a rigorous yet innovative academic ethos. The institution offers a flexible curriculum that includes optional courses, subsidiary courses, exemptions, and a bachelor-to-master progression track to align with students’ interests. Beyond the classroom, BFU fosters a broad array of extracurricular activities organized by student societies and associations spanning science and technology, the arts, sports, environmental protection, and political engagement. Notable groups include the Society of Scientific Exploration and Wilderness Survival and the Association of Beijing College Volunteers for Environmental Protection; the former has earned the Prize of the Earth, the top prize from the National Bureau of Environmental Protection. BFU students have also achieved notable success in competitions, securing four consecutive prizes at the College Students’ Landscape Gardening Architecture Design Competitions (sponsored by UNESCO and the International Association of Landscape Gardening Architects), including the Golden Prize in the International College Students’ Architecture Design and Garden Design competition. The university likewise records achievements in domestic contests across scientific inventions, mathematics, and the arts.

Beijing Forestry University, founded more than five decades ago, has graduated over 30,000 students, including individuals from China and abroad. Eleven alumni have attained the rank of academician. The institution maintains a large full-time faculty of 956 teachers, among whom five are academicians and 496 are professors. It preserves traditional disciplines while also establishing numerous new fields to address evolving societal needs. The university is organized into 15 schools, including the graduate school, and encompasses programs in biological science and technology; landscape architecture; forestry; environmental science and engineering; soil and water conservation; industry; information science; material science and technology; science; conservation; economic management; humanities and social sciences; foreign languages; and vocational training and continuing education.

Paul Oscher was born in Brooklyn, New York, and took up the harmonica when he was twelve years old. He moved into professional performance at fifteen, playing with Little Jimmy Mae. In shaping his musical approach, Oscher has cited John Lee Williamson as a major influence on his harmonica style.

Paul Allan Oscher (February 26, 1947 – April 18, 2021) was an American blues singer, songwriter, and instrumentalist, primarily known for his harmonica playing. He is noted for becoming the first white musician to secure a permanent position in Muddy Waters' band, contributing as a core member of the ensemble during his tenure.

The Ebbe Nielsen Prize was established in 2001 to honor Ebbe Nielsen, a Danish‑Australian entomologist and advocate of GBIF and biodiversity informatics, and at its inception stood as the sole global award recognizing work in biodiversity. The prize originally carried a cash award of US$35,000, later adjusted to €30,000, and it incorporates both the monetary prize and an invitation for the laureate to deliver a guest lecture at the annual meeting of the GBIF governing body in the host country. A 2003 call for submissions described the award as given annually to a promising researcher typically within about ten years of entering biodiversity informatics, with the aim of fostering novel integrations between biodiversity informatics and biosystematic research. The main criterion for selection is scientific excellence demonstrated through a strong publication record, with particular emphasis on innovative approaches that blend biosystematics and biodiversity informatics. Recipients have originated from Japan, Germany, Sweden, Argentina, the United States (twice), Australia (twice), the United Kingdom, Colombia, Canada, Denmark, and Portugal.

The Ebbe Nielsen Prize was an international annual science prize awarded by the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF). It ran from 2002 to 2014 and honored researchers who had made substantial contributions to biodiversity informatics. The prize was established in memory of Ebbe Nielsen, a prominent entomologist and advocate for biodiversity informatics, who died of a heart attack in the United States while en route to the 2001 GBIF Governing Board meeting.

Adhesions are fibrotic scar tissues that bind two distinct tissues or organs. In the muscular system, these adhesions can attach muscle fibers to surrounding structures such as the fascia, ligaments, or the joints, thereby constraining movement. Fibrosis may also develop within a single organ, producing internal scar tissue. When this fibrotic process involves skeletal muscle, the scar tissue is termed myofibrosis. The presence of myofibrosis reduces the muscle's contractile capability and increases passive stiffness, contributing to the development and maintenance of a muscle contracture.

Muscle contracture is characterized by a persistent shortening of muscle tissue and surrounding connective structures that limits passive range of motion. It commonly arises from an imbalance between opposing muscles, where the agonist and antagonist are differentially affected by neurological disorders, spinal cord injury, myopathies, or chronic lifestyle and postural factors. In some cases, one muscle remains normal while its counterpart becomes atrophic or hypertrophic, or the reverse pattern may occur. Reduced muscle tone can promote ongoing disuse and eventual muscular atrophy, further predisposing the development of a contracture. When the agonist is in a state of sustained contraction with little resistance, the shortened condition can become fixed. Additionally, selective hypertrophy of certain muscles may aggravate contractures and contribute to postural instability.

In early 1782, HMS Agamemnon sailed to the West Indies as part of Admiral Sir George Rodney's squadron, with Rear-Admiral Sir Samuel Hood serving as second in command. On 9 April, the Battle of the Saintes commenced with an indecisive skirmish, during which Hood's vanguard division sustained heavy damage and withdrew to repairs. The ship later took part on 12 April in the second, more decisive phase of the engagement. Casualties from the action included two lieutenants killed, 14 crewmen killed, and 22 others wounded.

HMS Agamemnon (1781) was a Royal Navy ship that, though highly valued by Admiral Lord Nelson, repeatedly required repairs and refits throughout its career, and would likely have been hulked or broken up in 1802 had the war with France not recommenced. The vessel fought at the Battle of Trafalgar on 21 October 1805, serving within Nelson's weather division and contributing to the forced surrender of the Spanish four-decker Santísima Trinidad. In its later years, Agamemnon operated in South American waters, including off the coast of Brazil.

1961 in film was marked by the death of Gary Cooper, who died in Los Angeles on May 13 at the age of 60 from colon and prostate cancer. He was one of the era's leading figures in Hollywood's Golden Age and was celebrated for his performances in Wings, Mr. Deeds Goes to Town, Sergeant York, The Pride of the Yankees, and High Noon. Over the course of his career, Cooper won two Academy Awards for Best Actor.

On June 28, 1961, producers Cubby Broccoli and Harry Saltzman signed a multi-film agreement with United Artists to develop a series of adaptations based on Ian Fleming's novels. The plan envisaged launching the franchise with either Dr. No or Diamonds Are Forever as its initial installment. The Bond film series would later become the highest-grossing film franchise of all time.

OBS! magazine was established in 1944 by Swedish journalists, including Arvid Fredborg, Th Åke Leissner, and Gunnar Unger, and was financially backed by the Vienna-based International Freedom Academy. The inaugural issue appeared in April 1944, and the publication followed a biweekly schedule. The stated objective of the magazine was to promote a sound economy and free enterprise. Fredborg served as the founding editor, while Unger wrote the first editorial and later became editor in 1949. Leissner, one of the founders, contributed articles under a pseudonym, and illustrators such as Ove Dahlstrand contributed to the magazine’s visual content.

OBS! was a magazine that, in its inaugural year, sold an estimated 20,000 to 25,000 copies. Financial support from the International Freedom Academy continued through 1953; after that year, the publication was financed by businessmen. The magazine ceased publication in 1955.

Originating as Harry Coonce's effort to learn the name of his advisor's advisor, the Mathematics Genealogy Project was established and placed online at Minnesota State University, Mankato, where Coonce taught mathematics, in autumn 1997. After Coonce retired from Mankato in 1999, the project moved in autumn 2002 when Mankato ceased supporting it, transferring to North Dakota State University. From 2003 onward, it has operated under the auspices of the American Mathematical Society. In 2005 the project was awarded a grant by the Clay Mathematics Institute. Coonce is aided by Mitchel T. Keller, an assistant professor at Morningside College, who serves as the project's managing director.

Within the Mathematics Genealogy Project, the earliest entries by date are Abu Sahl 'Isa ibn Yahya al-Masihi (died circa 1010) and his pupil Ibn Sina, known in the West as Avicenna. By May 2024, each of these two figures is credited with more than 220,000 descendants in the project’s genealogical records, reflecting the extensive network of mathematical lineages documented by the initiative.

Nicola Danti is a Member of the European Parliament who holds assignments on several parliamentary committees. He participates in the European Parliament's Intergroup on Fighting Against Poverty and in the Intergroup on Integrity (Transparency, Anti-Corruption and Organized Crime). Danti has advocated for the protection of Made in production labels to safeguard regional and national manufacturing. He also supported the resolution endorsing the Transatlantic Trade and Investment Partnership (TTIP).

Nicola Danti is an Italian politician affiliated with the Democratic Party (Pd). During the center-left coalition primary election in Tuscany in November–December 2012, he coordinated Matteo Renzi's committees in the region. He has since served as a member of the Pd National Directorate and as the spokesman for the party's regional secretariat, representing the regional leadership in public communications.

The 1936 United States Senate election in Iowa was held on November 3, 1936, in the state of Iowa. The sitting Republican senator, Lester J. Dickinson, sought re-election to a second term but was defeated by Democrat Clyde Herring. Herring’s victory gave the Democrats both of Iowa’s U.S. Senate seats, a situation not seen in the state since 1855.

During the interwar period, the Soviet Union pursued heavily armed twin‑engine aircraft to fulfill the heavy‑fighter role, functioning as both interceptors and bomber destroyers. Recoilless rifles were experimented with as the primary armament, but they were abandoned as impractical by the late 1930s. Twin‑engine proposals such as the Tupolev ANT-29 and the Petlyakov VI‑100 never progressed beyond the prototype stage. Consequently, the USSR entered World War II without a viable heavy fighter capability.

The Pe-3bis, designated as the Pe-3 "Improved," was developed to address defects identified during flight trials and field testing of the preceding Pe-3. Production of the Pe-3bis began in April 1942, after which 207 standard Pe-3 aircraft had already been built. Following its introduction, additional problems were found with the Pe-3bis. In May 1942, production shifted to a Pe-3bis incorporating further minor modifications, while the designation remained unchanged.

Matthew Quay, in his later years, pursued statehood for Oklahoma, New Mexico, and Arizona. A statehood bill secured bipartisan support when it passed the House in 1902. Quay hoped its passage would enable William "Bull" Andrews, his longtime lieutenant with financial interests in the New Mexico Territory, to move onto the Senate. As a member of the Senate Committee on Territories, Quay built support in the chamber for the measure. Yet committee chair Albert Beveridge of Indiana believed the three territories were not yet ready and employed Senate procedures to avert a vote for the remainder of the session. Quay remained in Washington through the winter of 1903 to press the bill, foregoing his usual Florida sojourn in order to protect his health. Ultimately, the territories did not achieve statehood during Quay's lifetime.

At the August 1900 Republican State Convention, Matthew Quay was endorsed and the convention condemned the Senate’s action, urging the legislature elected the following year to restore him to the Senate. In the fall campaign, Wanamaker spoke on the stump, and Quay also campaigned across the state. Though he had already served two terms in the Senate, Quay rarely gave public addresses; nevertheless, he delivered 19 speeches throughout Pennsylvania in October and November 1900. The McKinley–Roosevelt ticket carried Pennsylvania in the election. Despite the campaign activity, it remained uncertain whether Quay could command enough support in the legislature to secure his election.

Omar Al Midani (Arabic: عُمَر مَيْدَانِيّ; born 26 January 1994) is a Syrian professional footballer who plays as a centre back or right back for Al-Salmiya, a club that competes in the Kuwait Premier League, the top division of Kuwaiti football. Born in Syria, he has established himself as a defender at the club level within the Kuwaiti league system.

In Lake Norman of Catawba, North Carolina, there were 1,988 households. Among them, 25.7% contained children under 18, and 64.7% were households of married couples living together. Female-headed households with no husband present accounted for 5.7%. Non-family arrangements comprised 26.8% of all households, while 21.3% consisted of individuals living alone. Households with someone 65 years of age or older living alone represented 6.2%. The average household size was 2.39 persons, and the average family size was 2.77.

Lake Norman of Catawba, North Carolina exhibits a set of economic indicators including a median household income of $50,367 and a median family income of $55,192. Median earnings for males were $40,250, while females earned a median of $28,650, and the per capita income stood at $27,278. Poverty affected 5.6% of families and 7.1% of the population, with 12.0% of those under 18 and 5.5% of those 65 and older living below the poverty line.

Les Démocrates was a provincial political party in Quebec, Canada, founded on November 18, 1978, by Camil Samson and Pierre Sévigny. Samson had previously led the Ralliement créditiste du Québec, while Sévigny was a former federal cabinet minister with the Progressive Conservative Party. The group was renamed Parti démocrate créditiste on January 1, 1980, a change that reflected the social credit theory of monetary economics. On September 2, 1980, Samson joined the Liberal Party of Quebec. Sévigny remained the party’s leader and campaigned ahead of the 1981 Quebec election, though he did not stand as a candidate. The party was unable to nominate candidates in ten electoral districts and dissolved prior to the 1981 election.

Within Les Démocrates, several social credit supporters who did not accompany Samson to the Liberal Party joined the Parti credit social uni. The Parti credit social uni was established in 1979 as the province's branch of the Social Credit Party of Canada, created to organize and represent social credit adherents at the provincial level.

From 1997 to 2000 the station was known as W1 (Wien 1), a designation that referenced Vienna. Initially, it offered only regional programming to viewers on the Vienna cable network. On 17 January 2000 it began broadcasting nationwide, extending its distribution to all other Austrian cable networks. Subsequently, the station was renamed ATV.

Following its acquisition by a new owner, ATV stated that ATV2 would continue to operate under the new management. The custodian announced plans to develop a refreshed concept by the end of 2017, with a soft re-launch of the channel scheduled for early 2018.

Electric displacement gained its present significance largely through Oliver Heaviside’s reformulation of Maxwell’s equations into their modern form. In 1884, Heaviside, together with Willard Gibbs and Heinrich Hertz, organized the equations into a distinct quartet. This four-equation set is known as the Hertz–Heaviside equations, also referred to as Maxwell–Hertz or Maxwell–Heaviside. Heaviside is credited with lending the electric displacement D its current prominence within this formulation.

The designation electric displacement first appeared in 1864 and was used by James Clerk Maxwell in his paper A Dynamical Theory of the Electromagnetic Field. In that work, Maxwell introduced the symbol D to represent the specific capacity of electric induction, a quantity that corresponds to what is now referred to as the electric displacement field. The original form of the symbol D as employed by Maxwell differed from the notation used in contemporary formulations.

In Spain, the term juez de instrucción denotes an examining magistrate, and the corresponding office is known as the juzgado de instrucción. An investigating judge is responsible for directing the inquiry into criminal cases within their district, handling a broad range of offenses. The framework provides exceptions for matters allocated to the National Court (Audiencia Nacional) or to other courts that have jurisdiction ratione personae. In addition to supervising investigations, examining judges are competent to adjudicate petty offenses as well as crimes, thereby performing both investigative and judicial functions within their remit.

Dating from 1926, the examining magistrate is a formal office whose powers were significantly strengthened in 1999. Public prosecutors oversee investigations to ensure their legality, fairness, and integrity across the investigative and pretrial stages. The examining magistrate determines the lawfulness of arrests and of pretrial detention. The examining magistrate also reviews prosecutors' requests to use invasive special investigative techniques. For the most intrusive methods, such as wiretapping and other telecommunications intercepts, prosecutors must obtain the examining magistrate's approval.

Primghar, Iowa, has a median household income of $31,304 and a median family income of $40,982. The median income for males is $30,134, while for females it is $20,694, and the per capita income is $17,791. About 5.2% of families and 9.6% of the overall population live below the poverty line, including 9.8% of those under 18 and 6.7% of residents aged 65 and over.

Primghar lies in the gently rolling terrain of Northwest Iowa, at an elevation of 1,520 feet. The area is characterized by minimal boggy spots, with much of the land terraced to reduce erosion. To the south of the courthouse square, a boggy, muddy slough existed before fill was hauled in. At the time of settlement, trees were scarce, and prairie grasses reached heights of about six feet.

Creative Commons Korea serves as the national affiliate network of Creative Commons in South Korea. It was initiated in March 2005 by Jongsoo Yoon (윤종수), who at the time acted as the presiding judge of the Incheon District Court. The initiative began as a project of the Korea Association for Infomedia Law (KAFIL). Subsequently, major Korean portal sites, including Daum and Naver, began to adopt and promote Creative Commons licenses within their platforms. In January 2009, the Creative Commons Korea Association was founded as a non-profit incorporated association. Since its establishment, CC Korea has actively fostered a liberal, open culture of creation and has played a leading role in spreading Creative Commons throughout the country.

Creative Commons is a nonprofit organization that provides free licenses intended to facilitate the sharing and reuse of creative works. All current CC licenses require attribution to the authors of the original works, with CC0 exempting the attribution requirement. The attribution obligation can be cumbersome for works that incorporate multiple sources, complicating the task of properly crediting all contributors. Critics have argued that the CC framework could gradually erode the traditional copyright system by expanding the range of permissible uses without compensation. They have also warned that it might cast individual creativity into a broad commons, making it vulnerable to exploitation by anyone with time to repurpose or appropriate the material.

Self Entitled has drawn mixed critical responses. AllMusic's Fred Thomas offered a middling assessment, noting that nothing on the album stands out while suggesting it should satisfy longtime fans and serve as a solid entry point for new listeners; he described the record as balancing inventive moments with mediocrity in a way that echoes other phases of the band's discography. By contrast, Jason Gardner of AbsolutePunk delivered a highly positive evaluation, arguing that NOFX addresses internal and external matters and achieves a cohesive expression of both sides, complemented by several memorable jams.

Self Entitled, NOFX's album, took more than a year to materialize. In January 2011, Fat Mike indicated that a follow-up to Coaster was in production, noting that although Coaster contained strong material, he had written roughly 300 songs in total. He also mentioned that some tracks on Coaster referenced Iron Maiden and Tegan and Sara. He described his writing method as exploratory, moving in various directions and sometimes retaining fragments simply to have them. By December 2011, he stated that work had begun on a new NOFX album in addition to a Rubber Bordello soundtrack for a fetish film.

During the Soviet era, each republic, including the Russian SFSR, established its own laws for classifying inhabited localities. After the dissolution of the Soviet Union, Russia delegated the responsibility for classification to its federal subjects. In the present day, the framework remains largely rooted in the RSFSR model, though subject-level peculiarities appear in practice. All federal subjects classify inhabited localities into two primary groups: urban and rural. Within these broad categories, the specific subdivisions and criteria differ by subject, yet they generally follow common overarching patterns.

Thiruppugazh refers to a collection of devotional hymns attributed to Arunagirinathar, though there are no contemporary historical records confirming his life or the authorship, with most knowledge about the poet and the work surviving through oral tradition and later commentaries. According to tradition, Arunagirinathar led a hedonistic youth and once attempted suicide by leaping from the temple tower at Tiruvannamalai, an act he survived through the grace of Murugan. After this transformation, he undertook a long pilgrimage to the Six Abodes of Murugan (Arupadai Veedu) and to more than two hundred other shrines across India and Sri Lanka, composing songs in praise of Murugan at each shrine; these hymns are collected as Thiruppugazh. The majority of the songs address Murugan, though some recount the deeds of Shiva or the avatars of Vishnu and celebrate Parvati’s power as well. Almost all the compositions end by invoking Murugan with the epithet Perumal, a term traditionally linked to Tamil Vaishnavism. In Tamil, Perumal literally means “Great God” or “Great Man.”

Thiruppugal, a Tamil devotional text, was carried forward after the death of Vadakkupattu Subramaniya Pillai by his son, V. S. Chengalvaraya Pillai. He undertook a comprehensive commentary on the Tiruppugal, incorporating extensive research notes to illuminate the text. The project spanned seven years, from 1950 to 1958, and culminated in the publication of a set of books that presented the detailed analysis and accompanying scholarly apparatus.

Hans Krebs, a renowned biochemist, received the Gold Medal of the Netherlands Society for Physics, Medical Science and Surgery in 1958 and was knighted in the same year. In 1979 he was named an Honorary Fellow of Girton College, Cambridge University. He was an original member of the Society for General Microbiology, and was subsequently granted honorary membership in 1980. He was elected to the American Philosophical Society and to the United States National Academy of Sciences. Throughout his career he received honorary doctorates from twenty-one universities.

In 1990, the Federation of European Biochemical Societies established the Sir Hans Krebs Lecture and Medal, endowed by the Lord Rank Centre for Research, to honor exceptional contributions to biochemistry and molecular biology. The prize is awarded for outstanding achievements in these disciplines.

During the War of 1812 the residents of the Indiana Territory enlisted in the United States Army and in local militias, including the Indiana Rangers, and served in multiple theaters of the conflict. In September 1812, British-allied Native American forces besieged Fort Harrison and Fort Wayne in Indiana; both sieges proved unsuccessful due to a lack of reinforcements. In November 1812, U.S. forces were defeated at the Battle of Wild Cat Creek in Indiana by Native American fighters. In December 1812, U.S. forces achieved victory at the Battle of the Mississinewa.

As hostilities approached during the War of 1812, William Henry Harrison sought military assistance from Kentucky to defend the Indiana Territory’s government at Vincennes. He was appointed brigadier general of the Kentucky militia on August 22 and organized efforts to raise forces for the protection of Vincennes and its administration. Although he had resigned his 1811 commission, Governor Charles Scott of Kentucky assisted in recruiting Kentucky volunteers for Indiana’s defense. In contrast, residents of Ohio and Indiana generally declined to participate, citing concerns about the provisioning and hardships of camp life. Some observers suggest Harrison pursued command in part because his popularity within the territory was flagging, particularly over his stance on slavery there. In September, the Territorial Legislature convened and Dennis Pennington introduced a bill to transfer the capitol away from Vincennes, citing its strategic distance from frontier tensions and its proximity to hostile groups; the measure passed with plans to select a new capitol and evacuate territorial records. The accompanying resolution stated that the capitol should be moved because of the threat posed by Indians and the risk to valuable records.

Beastie Boys is the title of the article, and within it an anecdote is noted about a bus driver from years past who drove Elvis’s backup singers; the driver’s name was Tadlock. Elvis reportedly gave him a pair of glasses, and Tadlock was very proud of them. The phrase “Tadlock’s Glasses” has circulated as a potential or remembered alternative title for the article.

The Beastie Boys' initial foray into hip hop occurred in 1983 with Cooky Puss, a track conceived from a prank telephone call to a Carvel Ice Cream franchise and performed by the group during its early period. The song was included on the lineup’s first EP, also titled Cooky Puss, which signaled their early use of sampling and their engagement with underground rap aesthetics. Cooky Puss quickly established itself as a hit within New York's underground dance clubs and nightspots. Later, the track Beastie Revolution was sampled in a British Airways commercial, prompting the group to threaten legal action; the airline ultimately compensated them with $40,000 in royalties.

Transport Layer Security has undergone a formal deprecation process for its older protocol versions. The PCI Security Standards Council urged organizations to migrate away from TLS 1.0 toward at least TLS 1.1 or higher by 30 June 2018, in order to enhance the security of payment card data. In October 2018, Apple, Google, Microsoft, and Mozilla announced plans to retire TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1, with a target implementation date of March 2020. The deprecation of TLS 1.0 and 1.1 was subsequently formalized in RFC 8996 in March 2021.

Transport Layer Security (TLS) and its predecessor SSL do not map neatly to any single layer within the OSI or TCP/IP models. Implemented on top of a reliable transport protocol such as TCP, TLS sits above the transport layer and provides encryption services for higher-layer protocols. This arrangement effectively delivers confidentiality and data integrity to application data, a function traditionally associated with the presentation layer. In practical use, software applications interact with TLS as though it were a transport-layer mechanism. Deployment requires applications to actively initiate a TLS handshake to establish a secure session, and applications must manage the exchange and validation of authentication certificates.

The aperture of molluscan snail shells can assume several forms, including semicircular, trilobate, and auriculate configurations. In some gastropods, the opening is narrowed by protruding folds, or plaits, that constrict the aperture. These plaits contribute to the defense of the animal by reducing the vulnerability of the soft parts to predators.
In molluscan anatomy, the term aperture is not applied to describe the shells of bivalves. The natural opening between the two shell valves in their closed position is termed the gape.

The Padrón Real, the royal chart, served as the definitive cartographic resource of the Spanish crown for navigation and territorial delineation. Diego Ribeiro entered service with Spain in 1518 and directed the production of several versions of the chart from 1525 to 1532. Revisions followed in the wake of Juan Sebastián Elcano’s circumnavigation and of Spanish explorations in North America. Alonso de Chaves oversaw updates in 1536, and Alonso de Santa Cruz directed further revisions in 1542.

The Padrón Real was a large-scale, ambitious undertaking initiated to compile and manage a comprehensive register of discoveries and maritime routes. The availability of reliable navigational aids was essential, for without them Spain’s capacity to exploit and profit from its discoveries would have been more limited. The Casa de Contratación governed the effort, employing a wide range of specialists—cartographers, navigators (pilots), archivists, record keepers, administrators, and others—to produce and oversee the Padrón Real.

Under the system of national accounts, disposable income is defined for every institutional sector of the economy. Within this framework, a corporation's disposable income is represented by its retained profit, while the government's disposable income consists of tax revenues plus income obtained from public corporations. When aggregated across all sectors, these amounts constitute national disposable income.

The marginal propensity to consume (MPC) denotes the portion of a change in disposable income that is used for consumption. For example, if disposable income rises by $100 and households spend $65 of that amount, the MPC equals 0.65. The marginal propensity to save (MPS) represents the remaining portion of the change in disposable income that is saved; in the example, saving amounts to $35, giving an MPS of 0.35. Together, MPC and MPS exhaust the change in disposable income, since MPC plus MPS equals 1.

Bromomethyl ethyl ketone is a brominated ketone that possesses lachrymatory properties, causing tearing when exposure occurs. It was employed as a chemical warfare agent during World War I. The compound was developed as an alternative to bromoacetone because acetone, the precursor to bromoacetone, was required for explosives production.

The 1993 Davis Cup World Group qualifying round took place from September 22 to 27, 1993. Functioning as the primary promotional and relegation series for that year’s Davis Cup, the ties determined which nations would compete in the 1994 World Group. The victors earned a place in the 1994 World Group, while the defeated teams were relegated to their respective Zonal Regions I for the following season.

The World Group qualifying round of the 1993 Davis Cup brought together sixteen national teams, comprised of the eight sides defeated in the World Group first round and eight teams that had prevailed in the final round of Zonal Group I. These sixteen competitors then contended in the World Group qualifying round with the aim of securing a place in the 1994 Davis Cup World Group.

Following Stalin's death, a brief thaw in the Cold War emerged, even as by that time 18 UN membership applications had been blocked. The superpowers stated they would not oppose a simultaneous vote on admissions. Mongolia's bid was vetoed by the Republic of China, delaying proceedings by a day; the Soviet Union then proposed that Mongolia could be excluded if Japan were also excluded, a suggestion to which the United States abstained. Ultimately, 16 remaining applicants were admitted to the United Nations on 14 December 1955 under UNSC Resolution 109, described as a package deal. The admitted states were Albania, Jordan, Ireland, Portugal, Italy, Austria, Finland, Ceylon, Nepal, Libya, Cambodia, Laos, Hungary, Romania, Bulgaria, and Spain.

In the context of member state status within the United Nations, fourteen attempts to advance the issue proved unsuccessful. The General Assembly's General Committee declined to place the matter on the agenda for debate, effectively preventing formal discussion. The decision occurred amid strong opposition from the People's Republic of China.

During the High Middle Ages, European knights were armored mounted warriors who formed the martial core of feudal society. The subinfeudation characteristic of feudalism allowed knights’ commanders to confer knighthood on their most capable soldiers, who themselves could confer the order on others once they reached command, producing a gradual diffusion of knighthood through the ranks. This practice persisted into the Renaissance. Scholar Lawrence Stone estimated that as many as a quarter of about 550 English knights at the end of Elizabeth I’s reign in 1603 had been created by a single nobleman, the Earl of Essex, illustrating that the fount of honour could lie in private hands. For much of the Middle Ages, private individuals could establish orders of chivalry, and the oldest surviving order, the Order of Saint John of the Sovereign Military Order of Malta, began as a private organization before later receiving formal sanction from church and state.

Fount of honour denotes the lawful source of authority to confer honours, providing a test for the legitimacy of orders by distinguishing those granted by a recognized sovereign from self-styled or private decorations. A legitimate fount of honour is a sovereign (a person or entity) who holds sovereignty at the moment the order is awarded. Accordingly, state authority—typically exercised by a monarch or president—marks the boundary between official orders of chivalry and those belonging to private organizations lacking state sanction. In Canada, the conferment of titles of nobility, knighthoods, or orders is reserved to the Crown, with non-sovereign individuals (including commoners, knights, or nobles) no longer having the right to grant such honours to others.

Laphroaig is a single malt Scotch whisky distillery located on the island of Islay in Scotland, positioned on the southern coast near the town of Port Ellen and at the head of a small bay called Loch Laphroaig. The name is pronounced lə-FROYG. In its vicinity are other well-known Islay distilleries, including Lagavulin and Ardbeg.

Laphroaig distillery was established in 1815 by Donald Johnston and Alexander Johnston. The Johnston family traced its origins to Clan Donald, most likely the MacIain of Ardnamurchan branch, with the surname subsequently anglicised to Johnston. The last family member to run the distillery was Ian Hunter, who was the nephew of Sandy Johnston; Hunter died childless in 1954 and left the distillery to one of his managers, Bessie Williamson.

The 2002 Brownlow Medal marked the 75th presentation of the award, which is given to the fairest and best player during the Australian Football League's home-and-away season. Brisbane Lions player Simon Black won the medal, polling 25 votes during the 2002 AFL season.

During the 1970s, the Soviet Union explored designs for a space shuttle program intended to complement its orbital capabilities. Persistent shortcomings, notably overheating in electronics, delayed the program into the late 1980s. The first shuttle, Buran, flew in 1988, but it was unmanned. A second initiative, Ptichka, was proposed as well but required lengthy construction and was canceled in 1991. The Energia rocket, developed for the Buran program, remains unused in regular service and stands as one of the most powerful rockets ever built.

Education in the Soviet Union was highly centralized and universally accessible to all citizens. The state also implemented affirmative action for applicants from nations designated as culturally underdeveloped. An unofficial quota affected Jewish applicants seeking admission to leading higher-education institutions, with Jewish entrants often facing more stringent entrance examinations. In the Brezhnev era, prospective university students were required to present a reference from the local Komsomol secretary. By 1986, higher-education enrollment stood at 181 students per 10,000 people in the USSR, compared with 517 per 10,000 in the United States, indicating lower participation in tertiary education relative to the United States.

Pavillon Le Corbusier originated in 1960 when Heidi Weber commissioned Le Corbusier to design a public exhibition pavilion. In 1961 the first drawings outlined a concrete-building concept, which by 1962 was redesigned as a steel-frame construction. A construction permit was issued on 13 May 1964 at no cost to the claimant, with the condition that ownership would revert to the municipality after fifty years. Construction began in 1964, two years after the initial concept change, and Le Corbusier died in 1965. The Centre Le Corbusier was officially inaugurated on 15 July 1967. On 13 May 2014, the building became the property of the City of Zürich, represented by the Heidi Weber Foundation – Centre Le Corbusier, under the agreed fifty-year term. Governance is provided by a board of trustees comprising representatives from the city and Heidi Weber. Weber welcomed the arrangement, which facilitated transitioning the management to new hands.

Pavillon Le Corbusier, associated with Centre Le Corbusier, is regarded as a Gesamtkunstwerk that unites Le Corbusier’s architecture with his sculptures, paintings, furniture, and writings into a single, cohesive work. It is considered unique and possibly the only structure of its kind in the world. In 1968–69, photographer Jürg Gasser carried out a comprehensive photographic survey related to Chandigarh, visiting the capital of Punjab on behalf of Heidi Weber. In mid-May 2016, Heidi Weber removed Le Corbusier's sculptures, designs, and mementos for personal reasons, and the city of Zürich, as the new owner, subsequently replaced these items with pieces sourced from other collections.

Milman Parry and Albert Lord advanced the oral-formulaic theory, arguing that the Homeric epics were composed and transmitted primarily through oral performance rather than being fixed, fully written works from the outset. These poems are regarded as foundational to the Western epic tradition, shaping its conventions, themes, and narrative techniques. Consequently, a large portion of Western epic poetry, including Virgil's Aeneid and Dante's Divine Comedy, presents itself as a deliberate continuation of the tradition established by these early poems.

Balto-Finnic folk poetry is written in a trochaic tetrameter known as the Kalevala meter. The Finnish epic Kalevala and the Estonian epic Kalevipoeg are composed in this meter, which is characteristic of the Balto-Finnic tradition. Scholars attribute the Kalevala meter to the Proto-Finnic period, indicating its deep historical roots. Estonian, Finnish, and Karelian are among the Balto-Finnic languages that employ this poetic form.

Mikael Ishak is a Swedish professional footballer who has represented Sweden at full international level. He made his first appearance for the Sweden national team on 15 January 2015, coming on as a 82nd-minute substitute for Isaac Kiese Thelin in a 2–0 friendly victory over Ivory Coast. Ishak scored his first international goal on 6 January 2016, in a 1–1 draw with Estonia. His competitive international debut followed on 24 September 2022 in the 2022–23 UEFA Nations League B match against Serbia, where he entered as a substitute for Dejan Kulusevski in the 85th minute of a 1–4 defeat.

Mikael Ishak joined 1. FC Nürnberg from Randers FC in January 2017, arriving six months before Randers’ contract with him was due to expire. During his time with Nürnberg, he scored the club’s 1000th goal in the 2. Bundesliga on 25 November 2017 in a match against Eintracht Braunschweig. The club subsequently earned promotion to the Bundesliga at the end of the 2017–18 season. Ishak went on to score his first Bundesliga goal on 1 September 2018, converting the equaliser in a 1–1 away draw with Mainz 05.

Talking Back to the Night is the third solo studio album by English musician Steve Winwood, released in 1982 less than two years after Arc of a Diver. The record did not match the commercial impact of its predecessor, peaking at number 28 on the Billboard 200. The album features “Valerie,” which became a modest hit in 1982. In 1987, for the Chronicles collection, “Valerie” was remixed and re-released, subsequently reaching the top ten on the charts. A separate remix of the title track also appeared on the Billboard Hot 100, though it failed to break into the Top 40. Additionally, “Help Me Angel” was remixed for Chronicles and issued as a single for the first time.

Talking Back to the Night, released in 1982, drew critical attention for its departure from some of Winwood's earlier, more acclaimed work. Parke Puterbaugh of Rolling Stone described the album as largely bland and oriented toward an easy-listening electropop sound. Fellow critic Mark Cooper argued that the music lacked the eccentricity or excitement that had characterized Traffic's best periods, and he added that the prominent use of synthesizers emphasized what he viewed as the blandness of Winwood's current style.

On the palms and soles, the epidermis includes a narrow, extra layer that is not found elsewhere; this region is termed thick skin. As a result of the additional layer, thick skin comprises five epidermal strata rather than the typical four.

Keratinocytes cultured in vitro can organize into a three-dimensional tissue that functions as artificial skin. This engineered construct recapitulates most of the properties of the native epidermis, providing a representative model of epidermal structure and function. Consequently, such 3D skin models are routinely used as tools in drug development and testing, offering a platform for screening and preclinical evaluation of candidate compounds.

The pelagic zone supports a diverse assemblage of invertebrate life, with pelagic invertebrates occupying various ecological roles in the open-water column. Notable members of this community include the crustacean taxa krill and copepods, as well as decapod larvae, and the gelatinous animals such as jellyfish. The group also comprises hyperiid amphipods and microscopic plankton such as rotifers and cladocerans, collectively contributing to the structure of pelagic ecosystems.

The pelagic zone is said to derive its name from Hades, the Greek underworld, and is described as the ocean’s deepest region, exceeding 6,000 meters (20,000 feet) in depth. Such extremes are typically found within trenches, and the zone is described as containing 13 short, narrow troughs and 33 trenches. The deepest trenches reach about 10,924 meters, while average trench depths commonly range from 5 to 10 kilometers. Atmospheric pressure in this zone can attain up to 1,100 atmospheres, and temperatures are noted to increase with depth owing to adiabatic heating. Very few organisms are known to inhabit this zone, with recorded taxa including coelenterates, polychaetes, amphipods, echinoderms, and mollusks.

The Kosovar Cup, known in Albanian as Kupa e Kosovës, is the premier national football cup competition in Kosovo. Established in 1991, it is organized by the Football Federation of Kosovo. The current champions are Prishtina, who secured their second Kosovar Cup title in the 2022–23 final after defeating Gjilani at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

During the 1901 Australian federal election, the Hare–Clark electoral system was employed in the Division of Tasmania to elect five members to the Australian House of Representatives. The rules governing federal voting in that election were determined by the state government rather than by a centralized federal authority, reflecting the state's responsibility for administering the electoral process at the time.

Under the Hare–Clark system, which employs the single transferable vote to elect multiple representatives, ballots are redistributed through transfers as candidates reach a specified quota. A candidate who exceeds the quota as a result of transfers is declared elected. The surplus votes of the elected candidate are also transferred to remaining candidates according to voters’ preferences. The transfer value applied to these surplus votes is determined solely by the particular transfer that first achieved the quota, and is not recalculated from subsequent transfers. For example, if a candidate has a surplus of 199 votes and the final transfer that brought them to quota consisted of 300 ballots, the transfer value would be 199/300.

Palm-wine music originated from the blending of local and foreign sailors, dock workers, and other urban working-class communities who gathered in palm-wine bars to drink and listen to music. The fusion integrated portable, easily transported instruments with indigenous string and percussion traditions to form the distinctive style. From this milieu, a traditional two-finger guitar picking technique developed, performed in a way analogous to the plucking of the region’s lute or harp. The genre is typically delivered in a syncopated 4/4 rhythm.

Palm-wine music derives its name from palm wine, a beverage produced from the naturally fermenting sap of the oil palm. This drink was traditionally consumed at social gatherings where early African guitarists performed, a context that contributed to the emergence of the genre.

Universidade Salvador (UNIFACS) began offering postgraduate programs in 1993, and soon emerged as a leading institution for postgraduate education in the North-Northeast region of Brazil. Since 1997, VOCÊ S.A. has maintained annual awards recognizing the best postgraduate programs in the country. UNIFACS has been the sole Bahia-based institution to appear in VOCÊ S.A. rankings and has taken part in every edition. In the prize’s final year, 2010, UNIFACS earned multiple top positions, including second and third places, two fourth-place finishes, as well as a fifth, a seventh, and a tenth. Today, UNIFACS offers 42 postgraduate programs, comprising MBAs, specializations, master’s degrees, and doctoral programs.

Universidade Salvador participates in the Laureate International Universities network, which facilitates international study opportunities by providing access and discounted rates for exchange programs, summer courses, and other academic activities. For architecture students, the network enables one to two semesters of study at Laureate-affiliated campuses abroad in countries such as Spain, the United States, Turkey, or Chile, provided these campuses offer architecture programs. During the exchange term, the student pays tuition at the same rate as at the Brazilian institution. Upon completing the exchange, the student may return to Brazil to continue studies or pursue an additional one to two semesters at another Laureate university.

Praporshchik is a designation for a non-commissioned officer rank in the Russian Armed Forces. On 1 July the Ministry of Defense introduced a revised staffing table, marking the first time in five years that dedicated posts for praporshchiks and michmans appeared; about 100 such positions were allocated, all in combat roles, with Defense Minister Shoigu stressing that duties should exclude warehouses or bases. The posts are divided into two main categories: command positions, such as service platoon commander, commander of a combat group, commander of a combat vehicle, and head of a combat post; and technical posts, including company technician, head of a radio station, electrician, medic, head of a repair shop, and head of a technical unit. Since 1 December 2008 these roles have been regarded as non-commissioned officer positions. State Secretary Nikolai Pankov indicated that these posts demand specialized training, but do not require the same level of education as commissioned officers.

In 2010, there were no new appointments to the ranks of praporshchik or senior praporshchik. Existing holders of these ranks were allowed to serve out the remainder of their contracts, and they retained their ranks and rank insignia during continued service. The measure was described as an assumption or policy directive.

The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon is an American late-night talk show on NBC hosted by Jimmy Fallon, which premiered on February 17, 2014. It is produced by Broadway Video and Universal Television and marks the seventh iteration of NBC's Tonight Show franchise, with Fallon serving as the sixth host. The program features Steve Higgins as the sidekick and announcer and features The Roots as its house band. Production is led by producer Katie Hockmeyer, with Lorne Michaels serving as executive producer. New episodes are streamed the following day on Peacock. The show is filmed in Studio 6B at Rockefeller Center in New York City, the same venue previously used for Tonight Starring Jack Paar and Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson (1957–1992).

The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon is carried in Belgium by Vier with a delay of several days. Weekday episodes are aired from Monday to Friday at midnight CET, while a Sunday edition is broadcast at 11:05 pm CET. The Belgian broadcast first aired on October 12, 2015.

Octroi is a term of French origin used to denote a local tax on goods entering a jurisdiction. In Roman times, a comparable set of charges called vectigalia encompassed three principal forms: portorium, a duty on entry to or departure from provinces with the resulting revenue shared with the public treasury; ansarium or foricarium, a toll collected at the gates of towns; and edulia, a sales impost levied in markets. Vectigalia were applied to wine and certain foods, and urban authorities seldom retained the entire proceeds. Some scholars, including Charles Ellicott, have proposed that the tax collector mentioned in Matthew 9:9 operated as an octroi official, collecting duties on fish, fruit, and other produce that made up Capernaum’s exports and imports along the Sea of Galilee.

Octroi is a local tax levied on various articles brought into a district for consumption. The pronunciation in French is [ɔktʁwa]. Etymologically, the term derives from the Old French octroyer, meaning to grant or authorize, itself ultimately derived from the Latin auctor.

The 1967 Wimbledon Championships, the 81st edition of the prestigious tennis tournament, took place at the All England Lawn Tennis and Croquet Club in Wimbledon, London, United Kingdom. Played on outdoor grass courts, the championships ran from 26 June to 8 July 1967 and formed the third Grand Slam event of the year. In the men's singles, John Newcombe emerged as champion, while Billie Jean King won the women's singles title.

On 1 July 1967, during the Wimbledon Championships' opening Saturday, the event became the site of the first colour television broadcasts in the United Kingdom and Europe, transmitted on BBC2. The coverage began at 2 pm and ran for four hours of live programming, with presentation by David Vine and commentary by Keith Fordyce. The first colour match shown was Cliff Drysdale versus Roger Taylor on Centre Court. Colour transmissions continued with additional afternoon broadcasts in the following week, and nightly 30-minute highlight programmes were aired each evening.

ERDE experienced a rightward realignment in 1918, after which Päts departed to join the Rural League and Ado Birk emerged as the party’s leading figure. In the 1918 elections, the party participated as part of a bloc, which together secured about 23 percent of the vote.
