Ahead of the 1919 elections, ERDE merged with the Democratic Party to form the Estonian People's Party, marking a consolidation of liberal-democratic forces in the newly independent state's political landscape.

The Estonian Radical Democratic Party traces its origins to the Tallinn Radicals, a movement active in the early 20th century around the leadership of Konstantin Päts and the Teataja newspaper. By 1917 the Tallinn Radicals had merged to form the Radical Democratic Party. In that year the party secured four seats in the Estonian Provincial Assembly. During its tenure in the Provincial Assembly, it participated as part of the Democratic Bloc, a coalition that also included the Estonian Democratic Party and the Rural League.

International registered mail employs a label that carries a unique 13-digit reference number and an accompanying barcode in accordance with the UPU S10 standard. The label typically begins with a two-letter registration prefix, most commonly "RR," though examples exist with "RB." The middle portion contains the numeric 13-digit reference, and the label concludes with a two-letter country code indicating the country where the item was posted, such as SG for Singapore, CN for China, or KR for South Korea. Representative labels include RR913282511SG for Singapore, RB5584847749CN for China, and RR123456785KR for South Korea.

Registration of letters in Great Britain was introduced in 1841. The service initially required the registered item to be enclosed in a large green sheet of paper addressed to the recipient's Post Office, a document that functioned as a receipt returned to the sender once the letter was delivered. On 1 July 1858, the green sheet was replaced by a green silk ribbon. Shortly thereafter, the ribbon was replaced by green linen tape, and in 1870 the green tape gave way to green string. With the advent of postal stationery registration envelopes in 1878, the string was replaced by printed blue crossed lines, a marking that has remained on registered letters up to the present day.
More than three years after its launch, Sky+ HD had substantially increased the range of HD channels available. By that time, it had become the most extensive HD channel lineup outside North America.

Sky+ HD is a high-definition television service that delivers all of its HD channels in 1080i, with the accompanying set-top box capable of scaling output to 720p if the user prefers. The video streams are encoded using the H.264/MPEG-4 AVC compression scheme. Broadcasts are transmitted via a group of satellites, including Astra 2A, Astra 2E and Astra 2F, along with Eutelsat 28A, which are located at approximately 28.2°E and 28.5°E. The transmission standard employed is DVB-S2, the newer DVB specification. BBC HD, one of the early HD channels on the platform, initially used DVB-S but transitioned to DVB-S2 on 6 June 2011.

During 1944, assassinations of high-ranking German and collaborationist figures increased within the Belgian Resistance. In July of that year, the Légion Belge killed the brother of Léon Degrelle, a leading Belgian fascist who headed the collaborationist Rexist Party. Alongside these prominent executions, informants and suspected double agents were also targeted as part of the broader resistance effort. The armed Communist Partisans Armés claimed to have killed more than 1,000 traitors between June and September 1944.

After liberation, a substantial number of former Belgian Resistance members enlisted in the regular army, contributing a large share of its manpower. They formed roughly 80 percent of the strength of the Belgian Fusilier Battalions, units that served on the Western Front until VE Day.

ISO 3166-2:CH is the entry for Switzerland in the ISO 3166-2 standard, which forms part of the broader ISO 3166 framework. ISO stands for the International Organization for Standardization. The 3166-2 subset defines codes for the names of the principal subdivisions of all countries that possess an ISO 3166-1 code, encompassing divisions such as cantons, states, or provinces in different jurisdictions.

ISO 3166-2:CH is the entry within the ISO 3166-2 standard that covers Switzerland’s principal administrative subdivisions. Each code follows the format CH-XX, where CH is the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code for Switzerland, and XX is a two-letter sequence that identifies a canton. The two-letter suffixes correspond to cantonal abbreviations and are the codes currently used on Swiss vehicle registration plates to indicate the origin of a vehicle.

Narendra Deva, also known as Narendradeva, was a Licchavi king who ruled from 643 to 679 CE and was the son of Uday Deva. During his reign he established diplomatic relations with the Chinese emperor, and under his leadership Nepal developed as a commercial gateway linking India and Tibet. His period of rule coincided with renewed prosperity and power for the kingdom, as improved relations with both China and Tibet enhanced Nepal’s role as a conduit for travelers and merchants moving between India and China. The era also saw the introduction of papermaking from China to Nepal, contributing to cultural and economic exchanges. Nepal exported a variety of goods to India, including high-quality handmade paper, musk, orpiment, and blankets.

Narendradeva was a ruler who adopted the same royal title as Amshuverma, namely paramabhattaraka maharajadhiraj. He is described as a devotee of Lord Shiva. According to legend, in his old age he retired to a monastery. He was succeeded on the throne by his son Shivadeva II.

Alessandro Pirzio Biroli was an Italian military officer who held a series of high-profile commands and governance roles across two world wars and the Italian colonial empire. He fought on the Macedonian Front in World War I as the commander of a battalion and was decorated by the Kingdom of Serbia with the Order of the White Eagle with swords. In 1918 he became the commanding officer of the 8th Bersaglieri Regiment. From 1921 to 1927 he headed a military mission to Ecuador. He served as commanding general of the Monte Nero Division from 1932 to 1933, and then as commanding general of the Italian V Trieste Corps from 1933 to 1935. Pirzio Biroli commanded the Eritrean Corps during the Second Italo-Ethiopian War and served as Governor of Amhara province in Italian East Africa from 1936 to 1937. Although not a fascist, he participated in actions described as fascist wartime crimes. In 1941 he held the rank of general of the Italian 9th Army and was Governor of Montenegro from 1941 to 1943.

According to Pajović, Pirzio Biroli bore personal responsibility for numerous executions and acts of mass terror in Montenegro. He was listed among the higher-ranking individuals on the United Nations War Crimes Commission's list of war criminals, though he was never tried. In his later years, he resided in Rome.

Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications (BUPT; 北京邮电大学) is a public university situated in Beijing, China. It operates under the oversight of the Ministry of Education and receives joint funding from the Ministry of Education and the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. The institution is a participant in Project 211 and is included in the Double First-Class Initiative, highlighting its status as a nationally prioritized higher education establishment.
Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, established in 1955, is a university that was previously named the Beijing Institute of Posts and Telecommunications.

John C. Malone lives in Elizabeth, Colorado, with his wife, Leslie. They have two children, including their son Evan D. Malone, who joined the Liberty Media board in 2008. Leslie Malone is active in dressage and horse breeding and founded Harmony Sporthorses in Kiowa, Colorado. Malone shuns the limelight and glamorous lifestyle, taking family vacations with his long-time friend Gary Biskup in a recreational vehicle. In 2016, Colorado named him a Citizen of the West.

John C. Malone (born March 7, 1941) is an American billionaire businessman, landowner, and philanthropist. He led Tele-Communications Inc. (TCI), a major cable and media conglomerate, as chief executive officer from 1973 to 1996, guiding the company through its growth during the cable industry’s expansion. By 2016, Malone served as chairman and the largest voting shareholder of several major media and telecommunications groups, including Liberty Media, Liberty Global, Warner Bros. Discovery, and Qurate Retail Group, the latter formerly known as Liberty Interactive. Earlier in his career, he held about 7 percent ownership stakes in Lionsgate and Starz Inc.

In 186 BCE, Roman forces were defeated by the Ligurians in the Magra valley, with the engagement taking place in a narrow, precipitous setting. The Romans endured heavy losses, amounting to about 4,000 soldiers, and the defeat saw the loss of three eagle standards of the Second Legion along with eleven banners of the Latin allies, while the consul Quintus Martius was killed. The battle site is thought to have influenced local toponyms, such as Marciaso or the Canal of March on Mount Caprione in Lerici, near the ruins of Luni. The Caprione mountain was subsequently founded by the Romans and came to play a strategic role in controlling the Magra valley and access to the sea.

In 197 BC Rome reasserted authority over the Placentia region, under the leadership of Minucius Rufus. The campaign brought several local communities under Roman influence, including the Celeates, Cerdicates, Ilvati, and the Boii Gauls. The operations culminated in the occupation of the oppidum at Clastidium, reinforcing Roman control in the area.

Within the Torah, disability is described as a consequence decreed by Yahweh for transgressions. The text also instructs Israelites not to insult the deaf and not to place a stumbling block before the blind, reflecting a prohibition on mistreatment or hindrance of people with sensory impairments. In Halakha, Jewish law, there is an obligation to aid those who are sick, underscoring the duty of community members to provide support and care for the ill.

Within Buddhist thought, some adherents attribute disability to negative karma arising from immoral actions, while others emphasize compassion toward the less fortunate, including disabled individuals, an approach often associated with the concept of songsarn. This compassion is believed to benefit donors by generating good karma, yet it yields mixed consequences for disabled people in predominantly Buddhist societies. Disabled Buddhists report condescending attitudes from others, illustrating the ambivalence of religiously influenced communities. Moreover, the emphasis on compassion has been linked to reluctance to promote independence and social participation among people with disabilities, as charitable responses may substitute for broader inclusion. In Thailand, the World Bank notes that such compassion leads people to donate to beggars with disabilities or to charities aiding disabled populations; while this generosity may be commendable, the Bank argues that it does not automatically advance equality for people with disabilities.

Lloyd Richards was an acting educator who contributed to the dissemination of the Moscow Art Theatre's acting method. Working under Paul Mann, he taught at the Actor's Workshop in New York, where he collaborated with Morris Carnovsky.

Lloyd Richards was born in Toronto, Ontario, and raised in Detroit, Michigan. His father, a Jamaican carpenter who later worked in the auto industry, died from an infection when Richards was nine, around 1928, and four years later, in 1932, his mother became blind. He and his brother Allan helped keep the family together during these years. Richards initially studied law at Wayne State University but ultimately pursued the theatre arts. During World War II, he served in the United States Army Air Corps, taking a brief break from his studies and formal pursuits.

North Korea publishes a portfolio of roughly 70 to 80 periodicals, of which around 20 are considered major publications. The overwhelming majority are official magazines issued by specialized state institutions. In practice, each field is typically covered by a single magazine, and launching additional titles within the same field is regarded as an unnecessary expenditure of resources.

Following the British blockade of the French coasts on 16 May 1806, Napoleon issued the Berlin Decree on 21 November 1806, initiating the Continental System intended to undermine Britain by restricting British trade within territories under French influence. The policy aimed to neutralize Britain's ability to wage war by cutting off its commerce in continental Europe. Britain maintained a standing army of about 220,000 at the height of the Napoleonic Wars, with fewer than half available for campaigning; the remainder was deployed to garrison Ireland and overseas colonies and for national security. France’s armed forces reached a peak strength of roughly 2.5 million soldiers when counting both full-time and part-time units, including several hundred thousand National Guardsmen who could be drafted if necessary. In both countries, large numbers of sedentary militia were raised, largely unsuited for campaigning, in order to free regular troops for active duty.

Following 1807, Napoleon reorganized the French artillery, creating a highly mobile and well-armed corps. The change elevated artillery’s tactical prominence on the battlefield. Napoleon frequently employed concentrated batteries as the offensive spearhead to rupture enemy lines, rather than relying on infantry to wear down defenses. After a breach was opened, he moved in infantry and cavalry to exploit the gap and pursue retreating forces.

The miniseries opens with Richland visiting a government facility on a remote Caribbean island, where Peniston escorts him inside. Inside, Dr. Bishop, the chief scientist, outlines several experiments, including a project involving a shark and a human hybrid referred to as the Creature. The Creature is described as capable of adapting to any environment. It then breaks free from its tank and kills Dr. Bishop. Acting on Richland's orders to eliminate the Creature, Peniston traps it in a containment unit and dumps it into the sea.

The film follows a team of researchers on an isolated island as Dr. Chase, who argues that a Great White shark is not responsible, finds claw marks on his boat that lend support to his theory. A concealed passage is revealed by Peniston, providing access to the real research facility, prompting Richland and a squad of SEALs to reach the island by helicopter. Dr. Chase and Dr. Macy descend the tunnel and discover that it is partially flooded and connected to the ocean, where they uncover equipment and notes and encounter traps planted by Puckett. They realize who placed the traps only too late, as the creature ambushes them and pursues them; at first its terrestrial limbs hinder its speed, but it halts, then evolves its arms and legs toward a more human-like form and resumes the chase. The doctors and their companions manage to escape and reseal the tunnel to block the creature, then depart the facility by boat, only to be confronted by an attack at the dock; the creature nearly kills Max but ultimately spares him.

Supply chain management encompasses the coordination of activities across organizations involved in the production and delivery of goods and services. It supports organizational learning by enabling systematic information exchange, feedback mechanisms, and collaborative problem-solving throughout the supply network. Moreover, literature and practice suggest that supply chains with broad geographic reach and connections among diverse trading communities are associated with greater innovation and productivity, reflecting the benefits of expansive and heterogeneous networks for knowledge transfer and capability development. Consequently, SCM plays a key role in both fostering learning within organizations and driving performance advantages through interconnected, widespread networks.

Within the field of supply chain management, warehousing management is concerned with optimizing storage and related activities to minimize costs and expenditures. It encompasses the management of storage facilities, aiming to improve the handling and retention of goods across the warehouse network while reducing personnel-related expenses. The function also provides dispatch authority to coordinate timely deliveries and maintain on-schedule fulfillment. In addition, warehousing management ensures the availability of appropriate loading and unloading facilities with sufficient space and infrastructure to handle goods efficiently. It incorporates inventory management systems to track stock levels, movements, and replenishment needs, supporting overall efficiency and accuracy in the supply chain.

Within the Milky Way, a broad ultraviolet extinction bump centered at approximately 2175 Å is observed along many sightlines, forming a distinctive feature of interstellar extinction. The feature was first identified in the 1960s, and despite extensive study its precise origin remains not well understood. Among the proposed explanations are models in which the bump arises from electronic transitions in graphitic carbonaceous grains, potentially with a mixture of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon molecules. Analyses of interstellar grains recovered from interplanetary dust particles (IDPs) show the persistence of this feature, with the carrier identified as organic carbon and amorphous silicates within the grains.

Atmospheric extinction is the diminution of light by the Earth's atmosphere and results from three principal mechanisms: Rayleigh scattering by atmospheric molecules, scattering by aerosols or particulates, and absorption by atmospheric gases. The absorption component is commonly described as telluric absorption, since it originates within the Earth’s atmosphere. Among the telluric absorbers, molecular oxygen (O2) and ozone (O3) are especially significant, as they substantially absorb radiation in the near-ultraviolet part of the spectrum. In contrast, water vapor (H2O) is a major infrared absorber, leading to pronounced attenuation at infrared wavelengths.

Elmhurst Park is a six-acre (2.4-hectare) urban park established on the site of former gas tanks. Initiated in 2007 and led by former New York City Mayor Michael Bloomberg, the project had a construction cost of around $20 million. The park opened on May 24, 2011, and includes amenities such as benches, lighting, lawns, jogging paths, a playground, and more than 620 trees. Restroom facilities, initially delayed, opened in September 2012. The restrooms were described as stylish and spacious but provoked considerable controversy due to their $2.3 million price tag.

Elmhurst Park was developed between 1910 and 1921 to serve as a gas storage facility. The tanks were maintained by an inspector who accessed the site by rowboat until the 1960s. In 1996, Brooklyn Union Gas began dismantling the gas tanks as the prevalence of compact gas cylinders increased.

Since the release of Mr. Tambourine Man, the Byrds' folk-rock approach has been cited as influential on a number of contemporary Los Angeles–based acts, including the Turtles, the Leaves, Barry McGuire, and Sonny & Cher. Music historian Richie Unterberger notes that the Byrds’ influence extended to later folk-rock acts such as the Lovin’ Spoonful, the Mamas & the Papas, Simon & Garfunkel, and the band Love. Author John Einarson contends that The Grass Roots and We Five achieved commercial success by emulating the Byrds’ folk-rock sound. Unterberger further argues that the Beatles assimilated the Byrds’ sound into Rubber Soul by late 1965, with noticeable impact on tracks such as Nowhere Man and If I Needed Someone. Additionally, Unterberger and Peter Lavezzoli contend that Bob Dylan’s decision to go electric on Bringing It All Back Home in 1965 was partly prompted by the Byrds’ electric adaptation of Mr. Tambourine Man.

At the Roy Orbison tribute concert on February 24, 1990, a temporarily re-formed Byrds lineup—comprising Roger McGuinn, Chris Hillman, and David Crosby—performed Mr. Tambourine Man with Bob Dylan. The live rendition was later released on the 1990 box set The Byrds. In October 1992, during Bob Dylan's 30th anniversary tribute concert at Madison Square Garden, McGuinn performed the song again, backed by Tom Petty, Mike Campbell, and Benmont Tench, among others.

The United States Congress is the bicameral federal legislature of the United States, whose members are chosen through direct elections. When vacancies arise in the Senate, they may be filled by appointment by the governor of the affected state under applicable law. The Congress comprises 535 voting members: 100 senators and 435 representatives, in addition to six non-voting members who represent the District of Columbia and several U.S. territories. The Vice President serves as President of the Senate and casts a vote only to break ties.

The United States Congress refers to the federal legislature of the United States and can denote either a specific meeting of the body or, more commonly, the two-year term that encompasses its sessions. Each Congress lasts two years. The present Congress is the 119th, running from January 3, 2025, to January 3, 2027. In accordance with the Twentieth Amendment, Congress begins and ends at noon on January 3 of every odd-numbered year. Members of the Senate are known as senators, while members of the House of Representatives are referred to as representatives, congressmen, or congresswomen.

The Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index is the principal measure of household consumption within gross domestic product (GDP), compiled by the U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). It incorporates both observed and imputed expenditures by households and covers durable and nondurable goods as well as services consumed by individuals. A related series, the core PCE price index (CPCE), is designed to be less volatile by excluding the volatile prices of food and energy, such as oil, natural gas, and electricity, thereby providing a more stable gauge of inflation in consumer spending.

The consumer price index (CPI) and the personal consumption expenditures price index (PCE) are both measures of inflation for household goods and services, but they differ in data sources and construction. The CPI relies on price data and expenditure weights derived from household surveys, whereas the PCE price index draws on data from business surveys and uses weights aligned with the national accounts framework. The difference in their underlying formulas partly stems from the fact that not all information required for the Fisher‑Ideal index is available on a monthly basis, although that approach is regarded as theoretically superior. The CPI is typically viewed as providing a practical, timely read on price changes from the preceding month, while the PCE price index is revised three times in the months following the end of each quarter to incorporate new information. In addition, the related NIPA tables underpinning the PCE are rebased annually and again every five years. Despite these methodological differences, the two indexes tend to track fairly closely when averaged over multi-year periods.

Blue Labour was founded in 2009 as a counterweight to New Labour and subsequently rose to prominence after Labour’s defeat in the 2010 general election. In that year’s contest, Labour secured fewer votes from working-class voters than from middle-class voters for the first time. The movement influenced a small cohort of Labour MPs and frontbenchers. Its founder, Maurice Glasman, was a close ally of Ed Miliband during the latter’s early years as Leader of the Opposition, and Glasman later received a life peerage in the House of Lords. Interest in Blue Labour revived after Labour’s 2019 general election loss of red-wall seats.

Blue Labour: Forging a New Politics is a 2015 collection of essays edited by Ian Geary and Adrian Pabst. The volume explores questions of political philosophy while offering analysis of European models of capitalism and addressing immigration in Britain. Its theoretical orientation is indebted to Catholic social teaching, shaping the arguments and proposals presented. Notable contributors to the work include David Lammy, John Milbank, and David Goodhart.

Public transit in Košice is operated by Dopravný podnik mesta Košice, the Public Transport Company of the City of Košice. It is the oldest municipal mass transit system in the territory of present-day Slovakia. Its origins lie in a horse-drawn streetcar line that began service in 1891 and was electrified in 1914. The current network comprises buses (in use since the 1950s) and trams, while trolleybuses operated from 1993 to 2014.

Košice was ceded to Hungary after the First and Second Vienna Awards. Beginning on 15 May 1944, during the German occupation of Hungary, roughly 10,000 Jews from the city were deported with the assistance of the Hungarian Interior Ministry and the gendarmerie (csendőrség); the final transport to Auschwitz departed Košice on 2 June 1944, about three months before the Arrow Cross Party gained control in Hungary. In the ensuing period, the town’s ethnic makeup was profoundly altered by the persecution of Hungarians, population exchanges with Slovakia, Slovakization, and mass Slovak migration into newly built paneláks of the communist era. These demographic shifts quadrupled Košice’s population by 1989, making it the fastest-growing city in Czechoslovakia.

Soccerway is an online platform and database dedicated to association football, offering comprehensive information on matches, leagues, clubs, and players. It is followed by more than one million users and provides coverage of over 700 leagues worldwide, delivering statistics, fixtures, results, and standings across international and domestic competitions.

Chancery hand is a later cursive script developed in the Vatican, drawing on humanist minuscule, which itself derives from Carolingian minuscule. Introduced in the 1420s by Niccolò Niccoli, it became the manuscript model for the early italic typefaces.

Chancery hand is a historical handwriting style developed for chancery offices, noted for its rapid execution achieved by holding the pen at a slanted angle of about 45 degrees, a position that also enables the production of elegant calligraphic forms. In fifteenth-century Italy, it was employed for correspondence, routine commercial and clerical tasks, and documents of limited ceremonial significance.

Lithuanian is one of two living Baltic languages, together with Latvian, and they constitute the eastern branch of the Baltic language family, while the Western Baltic languages—including Old Prussian, Curonian, and Sudovian—have become extinct, with Old Prussian dying out by the eighteenth century and the others earlier. In the scholarly debate over the relationship of Baltic to the broader Indo-European family, Jānis Endzelīns argued that Baltic forms its own distinct branch within Indo-European and that similarities with Slavic arise from language contact rather than a shared descent. By contrast, other linguists have posited a Balto-Slavic sub-family within Indo-European that unites Baltic and Slavic, a view associated with early proponents such as August Schleicher. Some researchers have even questioned the existence of Proto-Baltic, proposing instead a division into East Baltic, West Baltic, and Proto-Slavic. Notable advocates of this sceptical position include Antoine Meillet and Jan Baudouin de Courtenay, who maintained that Slavic–Baltic similarities reflect parallel development rather than a common proto-stage.

Within the Lithuanian language, the indirect mood is used exclusively in written narrative speech. It is a nominal form that cannot be conjugated; its tense is aligned with the tense of the corresponding active participle, which is in the nominative case. For example, the past tense of the indirect mood is nešęs, and the past iterative inchoative form would be būdavęs benešąs. Because of its nominal nature, it must agree with the subject in both number and gender.

Mississippi House Bill 1523, a religious liberty statute enacted in April 2016, permitted individuals and businesses to refuse service to same-sex couples on the basis of religious beliefs beginning in July 2016. The measure sparked significant controversy and legal challenges, culminating in a federal district court issuing an injunction blocking its enforcement in July 2016. In October 2017, the United States Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit ruled in favor of the law, upholding its provisions.

Momentum Mississippi is a statewide public–private partnership dedicated to the development of economic and employment opportunities in Mississippi. The initiative was adopted in 2005 as part of the state's broader strategy to promote economic growth and job creation.

China University of Geosciences (Wuhan) has its main campus known as the Nanwangshan Mountain Campus, situated at the foot of Nanwangshan Mountain. A tunnel through the mountain connects the West Campus and the North Campus, facilitating movement between the campuses. The university maintains a large annual enrollment and offers a broad range of programs beyond geosciences. On the campus, the Yifu Museum, donated by Sir Run Run Shaw, houses among the nation’s most prominent displays of dinosaur fossils, minerals, and rock specimens.

China University of Geosciences (Wuhan) and China University of Geosciences (Beijing) are separate institutions. They shared a common history until 2005, after which they became independent entities with distinct constitutions, presidents, and governing boards. Each university operates under its own legal entity registration, admission procedures, financial systems, Internet domains, and logos.

Island Records' early UK period, described by sales manager Tom Hayes (1965–1967) as organized chaos, nonetheless yielded the label's first major success in 1964 with My Boy Lollipop, a hit by Jamaican artist Millie Small (1947–2020). The song helped establish Island's presence in Britain and led to a worldwide tour that included Chris Blackwell. In a 50th anniversary documentary, Blackwell stated that his focus at the time was on building enduring careers rather than pursuing short-term projects. Suzette Newman, a close colleague of Blackwell since Island's early days, later ran the Mango world music label. Newman and journalist Chris Salewicz were editors of The Story of Island Records: Keep On Running.

Originally consisting of Toots, Raleigh, and Jerry, the group was signed to Island Records by Chris Blackwell and became the label’s recording act. Blackwell had already brought Bob Marley into Island's fold, and the roster containing both Marley and Toots and the Maytals signaled reggae’s growing international profile. He then stipulated that the Maytals would serve as the backing band for all Island recordings, leading to the project being billed as Toots and the Maytals, though the act was also known simply as the Maytals. In 1975, during a tour, they opened for the Eagles, Linda Ronstadt, and Jackson Browne, and they also opened for The Who for about two weeks.

The Net Promoter Score (NPS) was introduced in 2003 by Fred Reichheld and is employed as a word-of-mouth marketing metric that assesses the share of customers who would promote a brand to others. This approach centers on positive customer experiences as the key engine of organic word-of-mouth marketing, linking favorable interactions with spontaneous recommendations.

Word-of-mouth marketing encompasses the Organic Inter-consumer Influence Model, which stands as the original form of the practice. Under this model, organizations exert no direct control over consumer discourse about their products. It generally involves one consumer sharing product reviews or customer-service experiences with another. The driving motive is to inform and caution potential buyers out of sincere concern, rather than for personal gain. The process is described as organic, since it arises naturally when consumers choose to share their experiences with a brand or product.

The Book of Proverbs, a part of the Hebrew Bible’s wisdom literature, presents a layered structure beginning with chapters 1–9, which exhort young men to pursue wisdom and include ten admonitions alongside five poems that personify Lady Wisdom, with 1:1–7 serving as the prologue to this section. The central collection extends from 10:1 to 22:16 and comprises 375 proverbs, divided into two main subsections: chapters 10–14 contrast the wise and the fool, while chapters 15–22:16 focus on the dynamics of speech and the distinction between wise and foolish talk. Beginning at 22:17, the text introduces a passage known as the sayings of the wise, which leads into 24:22 with concise moral discourses on a range of topics, and an additional cluster in 24:23–34 that is also attributed to the wise tradition. Chapters 25–29 are traditionally ascribed to the editorial activity of the men of Hezekiah, presenting further contrasts between the just and the wicked and addressing issues of wealth and poverty. Chapter 30 comprises the sayings of Agur, opening with reflections on creation, divine power, and human ignorance. The book then closes with Chapter 31, which contains the sayings of King Lemuel, taught by his mother, and culminates in a portrayal of a virtuous woman, a wife of noble character.

The Book of Proverbs sits within the broader wisdom-literature of the ancient Near East, sharing thematic concerns and didactic aims with contemporaneous Egyptian and Mesopotamian traditions, and illustrating common ground across cultural boundaries. Israelite wisdom writings are thought to have developed in a variety of social settings, including family households, the royal court, and institutions devoted to teaching and study. Nevertheless, the prevailing view is that Proverbs primarily functioned as household instruction, conveying practical guidance and ethical norms within small village communities rather than serving only elite audiences.
Within the vicinity of the Shabla lighthouse lies Bulgaria's sole oil field. At present, several drilling operations in the area are yielding hot mineral water with high sulfur content.

On the coastal route south from Shabla, the next village encountered is Tyulenovo. Tyulenovo marks the start of the rocky coast and high cliffs, a rugged shoreline that extends from Tyulenovo through Kamen Bryag to Kavarna, where Kavarna is described as a small bay.

Farce constitutes a subgenre of comedy in theatre that leans on absurd situations and broad physical humor to entertain audiences. Such works typically generate laughter through exaggerated scenarios and slapstick, often with rapid pacing and a focus on mistaken identities, deceptions, and comic mishaps. Notable examples include William Shakespeare's The Comedy of Errors and Mark Twain's Is He Dead?, both cited for their deployment of farcical devices to produce humorous effects.

The Theatre of the Absurd is distinguished by metaphysical representations of existential questions and dilemmas. It rejects conventional rational explanations and emphasizes the necessity of probing the depths of the human condition. These concerns are conveyed not through direct discussion but through embodiment, action, and often illogical or non-linear narrative devices that foreground ambiguity. Consequently, the form invites spectators to participate in personal reflection and discussion about the play's content, encouraging contemplation of meaning within an open-ended dramatic experience.

Fernando Lopez (born April 13, 1904, in Jaro, Iloilo City) was a member of the prominent Lopez family of Iloilo, widely regarded as the wealthiest and most influential in the province. He was the younger brother and the only sibling of Eugenio Lopez Sr., and was the son of Benito Villanueva Lopez and Presentacion Javelona Hofileña.

Fernando "Nanding" Hofileña Lopez Sr. (April 13, 1904 – May 26, 1993) was a Filipino statesman and a member of Iloilo's prominent López lineage. He held the office of vice president of the Philippines in two nonconsecutive terms: first from 1949 to 1953 under President Elpidio Quirino as a Liberal Party member, and later from 1965 to 1972 under President Ferdinand Marcos as a Nacionalista Party affiliate. In addition to his public service, Lopez served as chairman of ABS-CBN Corporation from 1986 until his death in 1993.

Rising energy prices in 2013 provided additional state funds, enabling a renaissance of the Russian Navy and expanding its modernization potential. In August 2014, Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu announced plans to bolster naval capabilities with new weapons and equipment within six years, citing NATO’s enlargement and the ongoing Russo-Ukrainian War as justification. Following Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the Russian Navy experienced significant losses, including the cruiser Moskva, the Black Sea Fleet’s flagship. These developments illustrate how shifts in economic conditions and strategic priorities have influenced the fleet’s modernization and operational history.

The Russian Navy, founded as the Imperial Russian Navy, traces its origins to Tsar Peter the Great, who established the service in October 1696. The St. Andrew's ensign was adopted as its emblem, a flag that has come to symbolize the naval force. Many of the Navy's traditions were laid down by Peter I himself, shaping its ceremonial practices and institutional culture from the outset.
Lalthanmawia Renthlei (born 9 May 2002), nicknamed Amawia, is an Indian professional footballer who plays as a left winger for Kerala Blasters in the Indian Super League.

Lalthanmawia Renthlei joined the Aizawl FC under-14 academy in 2015 and spent six years within the youth setup before being promoted to the senior squad in 2021. During his time with the first team, he accumulated 42 appearances, scoring five goals and providing eight assists. In May 2024, Renthlei announced his departure from Aizawl FC via Instagram, marking the end of a nine-year association with the club.

The Boeing C-135 Stratolifter was developed as a temporary measure pending the introduction of more specialized jet-powered transports, notably the Lockheed C-141 Starlifter. It embodied several compromises in strategic airlift capability. Its design placed the load floor approximately ten feet above ground level, which required ground-handling equipment for loading and unloading. Access to cargo was limited by a single side-loading door, constraining what could be moved. With a practical range around 6,000 miles (9,700 kilometers), it could not reach many Asia-Pacific operating locations. The airframe lacked aerial-refueling receptacles, preventing mid-air augmentation of range. Additionally, operations demanded long runways at major bases or commercial airports, rather than proximity to potential combat zones.

Entering service in the early 1960s, the Boeing C-135 Stratolifter was developed to modernize the Military Air Transport Service fleet, which at that time relied heavily on piston-powered C-124 Globemaster II transports and turboprop C-133 Cargomaster aircraft. Although capable of carrying large payloads, these propeller-driven models were becoming obsolescent and lacked the global reach required by the Air Force’s expanding mission set. In May 1960, Congress approved an order for 50 C-135s. The selection favored the aircraft because of its low development cost and its straightforward derivative relationship to the KC-135 tanker already in production, allowing efficiencies in manufacturing and support. Production yielded 15 C-135As, with three additional airframes converted from KC-135s while on the assembly line, while a further 30 aircraft were delivered as the C-135B, equipped with the improved Pratt & Whitney TF33 turbofan engine.

Tacitus in Germania describes the Harii as bearing black shields and darkened bodies, conducting nocturnal raids as a shadowy force intended to terrify their opponents. Scholarly theories have proposed connections between the Harii and later Norse mythic figures, such as the einherjar—the dead warriors said to serve Odin—though these links remain speculative. Other proposals associate the Harii with the Wild Hunt, a legendary procession of the dead across the winter night sky sometimes led by Odin.

According to Rudolf Simek, the linkage between the Harii and living dead hosts has become widespread in contemporary scholarship. These animated hosts of the dead are typically regarded as religiously inspired bands of warriors. This interpretation helped shape the later concept of the einherjar in Norse mythology and also contributed to the development of the Wild Hunt motif.

The Metropolitan Borough of Lambeth, in line with a common practice among English local authorities, bears the motto Spectemur Agendo. While the standard English rendering is typically expressed as “Judge us by our deeds,” Lambeth’s official translation is given as “Let us be regarded according to our conduct,” a rendering that is traditionally considered more ponderous.

On 22 February 1966, the arms of the Metropolitan Borough of Lambeth were transferred by royal licence to the London Borough of Lambeth. The transfer was registered with the College of Arms. Two gold stars were added in the second and third quarters, symbolizing the addition of Clapham and Streatham to Lambeth.

Minervino Pietra, born in Lisbon, began his professional career with C.F. Os Belenenses, the local club. Over a five-season spell in the Primeira Liga, he made around 150 official first-team appearances for Belenenses and scored nine goals. In 1976, at the age of 22, he transferred to S.L. Benfica, where he remained for the remainder of his playing career until his retirement.

Minervino Pietra was a Portuguese footballer who spent the bulk of his career with Benfica, where he established himself as a regular in the club's defensive line. In 11 seasons with the Portuguese side, he appeared in 320 competitive matches and scored 25 goals. Pietra helped Benfica win four Primeira Liga titles (in 1977, 1981, 1983 and 1984) and secure five Taça de Portugal trophies. He also featured in the 1982–83 UEFA Cup Final, as Benfica were defeated by Anderlecht, losing 1–0 away and 1–1 at home.

Sometime after 216 CE, Lu Xun was commissioned as Dingwei Xiaowei (Colonel Who Establishes Might). Subsequently, Sun Quan arranged a marriage for Lu Xun with Sun Ce's eldest daughter, Sun Ce being Sun Quan's elder brother and predecessor.

In 237 CE, Zhou Zhi attempted to recruit troops from Poyang Commandery, but Lu Xun warned that Poyang was volatile and could revolt if conscription proceeded. Zhou Zhi ignored the warning, and Poyang rose in rebellion under Wu Ju, who killed Zhou Zhi and seized many counties. The neighboring commanderies of Yuzhang and Luling, both with histories of uprisings, joined Wu Ju’s revolt. Lu Xun then led a campaign to suppress the rebellion, forcing Wu Ju and the insurgents to surrender. He raised a force of more than eight thousand men and pacified the three commanderies of Poyang, Yuzhang, and Luling.

During the early years of the AIDS epidemic, there was widespread denial that Seattle would be affected by HIV/AIDS. In response, the Seattle LGBTQ community organized swiftly to confront the crisis, coordinating outreach, education, and mutual-aid efforts. Activists have since described Seattle's gay community as possessing one of the strongest HIV/AIDS networks, reflecting the lasting impact of that early mobilization.

From June 24 to 30, 1974, Seattle held its first Gay Pride Week, a milestone as the first regional event in which the local gay community publicly asserted its identity and visibility. The Gay Community Center opened on June 28 at 1726 16th Avenue East. On June 29, a picnic at Occidental Park drew roughly 200 attendees and featured entertainment that included a guerrilla-theatre style performance, with banners expressing pride in lesbian and gay identities. Afternoon activities included roller-skating and a sing-along atop the Volunteer Park Water Tower, while the evening program featured a street dance in Occidental Park with performances by Blue Moon and Sue Isaacs. The week concluded on June 30 with a Gay-In at Seattle Center, noted for its playful dress, general merriment, socializing, and a circle dance around the International Fountain.

JPEG XT Part 2 HDR coding is built on the Dolby JPEG-HDR framework, a 2005 specification designed to embed high-dynamic-range imagery within a standard JPEG file. The Dolby JPEG-HDR format originated from the work of Greg Ward of BrightSide Technologies and Maryann Simmons of Walt Disney Feature Animation. BrightSide Technologies was acquired by Dolby Laboratories in 2007, a corporate development that subsequently influenced HDR-oriented JPEG extensions.

JPEG XT Part 9 provides an alpha channel extension that enables both lossy and lossless encoding of images with transparency and arbitrary shapes. A dedicated opacity layer carries the alpha information, allowing for efficient representation of transparency. This layer can be encoded with either integer precision or floating-point precision, depending on the desired accuracy and compression characteristics. Metadata accompanying the content specifies whether the image data were premultiplied by the alpha channel, or premultiplied and subsequently blended with a background color.

Portions of the concert footage filmed for Eat the Document were later incorporated into Martin Scorsese's Dylan documentary No Direction Home. Among these is the sequence depicting the infamous "Judas" incident at Manchester's Free Trade Hall. No Direction Home also includes footage of Johnny Cash performing with Dylan on Hank Williams's "I'm So Lonesome I Could Cry."

Eat the Document is a documentary film that compiles footage from Bob Dylan's European tour with his backing group the Hawks, who would later become The Band. The material was recorded at a range of venues in Dublin, Belfast, Cardiff, Liverpool, Glasgow, Edinburgh, Newcastle, and Paris. The film presents performances drawn from several shows and includes songs such as "Tell Me, Momma"; "I Don't Believe You (She Acts Like We Never Have Met)"; "Ballad of a Thin Man"; and "One Too Many Mornings."

On 11 September 2000, astronauts Ed Lu and Yuri Malenchenko conducted an extravehicular activity to complete the final wiring between the Zvezda service module and the Zarya Functional Cargo Block. The spacewalk lasted six hours and fourteen minutes, during which nine cables were installed to connect the two modules, comprising four power cables, four video and data cables, and one fiber-optic telemetry cable. The successful installation completed the final connections between Zvezda and Zarya. The following day, the STS-106 crew entered Zvezda for the first time, with the initial entry recorded at 05:20 UTC on 12 September 2000.

Zvezda (ISS module) is a component of the International Space Station that serves as the Russian service module. It comprises three pressurized compartments and one unpressurized compartment. The pressurized sections, listed from forward to aft, consist of a spherical transfer compartment, a long cylindrical main working compartment, and a short cylindrical transfer tunnel. The unpressurized assembly compartment surrounds the exterior of the transfer tunnel. The module has a mass of about 19,050 kilograms (42,000 pounds) and a length of 13.1 meters (43 feet), with its solar arrays extending 29.7 meters (97 feet).

Dirac measure δ_x on a topological space (X, T) is the probability measure that places all mass at the point x. If the singleton {x} is closed in T, the support of δ_x is exactly {x}; when {x} is not closed, the support becomes the closure of {x} in (X, T). Moreover, δ_x is the unique probability measure whose support is {x}.

Let X = R^n be endowed with its standard σ-algebra and Lebesgue measure λ_n. The Dirac measure δ_x, concentrated at a point x ∈ R^n, assigns mass 1 to the singleton {x} and 0 to every measurable set not containing x. Since the Lebesgue measure of a single point is zero, one can partition R^n into A = R^n \ {x} and B = {x}, with A ∪ B = R^n and A ∩ B = ∅; consequently δ_x(A) = 0 and λ_n(B) = 0. This shows that δ_x is concentrated on the Lebesgue-null set B, illustrating the singularity of the Dirac measure with respect to λ_n.

According to Trans Murder Monitoring, the period from October 1, 2022 to September 30, 2023 recorded a total of 321 fatalities among trans and gender-diverse individuals. Of these deaths, approximately 94 percent occurred among trans women or trans-feminine individuals.

A 2009 report by the National Coalition of Anti-Violence Programs (NCAVP) found that transgender women comprised 11% of all hate crimes directed at LGBTQ individuals, a statistic that was quoted by the Office for Victims of Crime (OVC).

CNIL was established in part in response to public outrage over the SAFARI program, which aimed to create a centralized database that would allow government services to identify French citizens on an individual basis. A Le Monde article published on 21 March 1974 drew attention to the project and heightened public scrutiny of state data practices. Interior Minister Jacques Chirac, who had just taken office following the May 1968 upheavals, faced the controversy, succeeding Raymond Marcellin, who resigned in February 1974 after an attempt to place wiretaps in the offices of Le Canard enchaîné. The broad rejection by the public of the government's activities in this area helped prompt the creation of the CNIL.

The Commission Nationale de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CNIL) is an autonomous administrative authority in France charged with safeguarding personal information and individual liberties in the context of information technology. It enjoys full independence in deciding its course of action and enforcing its mandates. The scope of its authority is limited and defined by statute, which delineates its powers, procedures, and remedies. The CNIL is funded through the national budget of the French Republic, reflecting its status as a public institutional body.

The NAMM Oral History Program is an ongoing archival initiative of the National Association of Music Merchants that collects oral history interviews with musicians from a broad range of eras and genres. Notable interviewees include Les Paul, B.B. King, Emmylou Harris, Roy Clark, Lita Ford, Ike Turner, Steve Miller, John Waite, and Jason Mraz. The collection extends across jazz, rock, and beyond, featuring artists such as Herbie Hancock, Keith Emerson, Rick Wakeman, and Chick Corea, the latter a 27-time Grammy winner. Jazz and big-band connections are represented by figures like Ray Anthony and Joe Morello. In rock and related spheres, the program covers figures such as Scotty Moore, Hal Blaine, J. M. Van Eaton, W. S. Holland, Brian Setzer, Sheila E., and A. R. Rahman. The archive also encompasses pioneering contributions to hip-hop and DJ culture, including Afrika Bambaataa, Grand Wizzard Theodore, DJ Jazzy Joyce, Grandmaster Caz, and Jazzy Jay.

Established in 1996 to preserve the history of the music products industry, the NAMM Resource Center preceded NAMM’s creation of the Oral History Program in 2000. The program is led by Dan Del Fiorentino, NAMM’s Music Historian and former curator of the NAMM Foundation’s Museum of Making Music. The first NAMM Oral History interview featured professional harmonica player Bill Walden and was conducted on March 5, 2000, the opening day of the Museum of Making Music.

Daniel Davis Jr. patented an electroplating method for coloring daguerreotypes in 1842. The following year, Warren Thompson refined Davis's approach, advancing the technique and its application to photographic colorization.

Construction of the Euston tube station proceeded in two linked stages. Tunnelling for the Charing Cross, Euston and Hampstead Railway (CCE&HR) occurred between September 1903 and December 1905, after which the station buildings and tunnel fitting-out followed. At the same time, the Euston extension of the City and South London Railway (C&SLR) was built from Angel station and opened to the public on 12 May 1907. The extension's station building was designed by Sidney Smith and stood on the east side of Eversholt Street. The CCE&HR itself opened on 22 June 1907, with its station building designed by Leslie Green at the corner of Drummond Street and Melton Street.

Euston tube station underwent major reconstruction of the main-line station above, which included a new ticket hall excavated beneath the concourse. Two additional escalators replaced lifts, providing access to an intermediate passenger circulation level. That intermediate level affords access to the Northern line Charing Cross branch platforms and to two further escalators. A subsequent pair of escalators, one for northbound and one for southbound traffic, serves the Victoria line as well as the Northern line Bank branch platforms. Interchanges between the northbound and southbound Victoria and Northern Bank Line platforms are arranged via a lower-level passageway to avoid the use of escalators. An emergency stair to the intermediate interchange level is located midway along this passage. The Victoria line platforms opened on 1 December 1968 when the second section of the line opened between Highbury & Islington and Warren Street. Disused passages remain, retaining 1960s tiling and posters.

Ranger's House, located near Greenwich Park in London, was first used as the official residence of the Ranger of Greenwich Park in 1816. Caroline of Brunswick, appointed Ranger in 1806, had previously lived in the neighboring Montagu House, which was demolished in 1815.

Ranger's House is a medium-sized red-brick Georgian mansion constructed in the Palladian style, located in Blackheath in southeast London. It sits adjacent to and backs onto Greenwich Park, with a rose garden positioned behind the house. Formerly known as Chesterfield House, the building takes its name from its historical role as the official residence of the Ranger of Greenwich Park for much of the nineteenth century. It is a Grade I listed structure, reflecting its significance, and since 2002 it has housed the Wernher Collection of art.

The Delphic Fraternity derives its name from Delphi, the ancient city in Greece. Its motto underscores values of friendship, fellowship, and fidelity, while its guiding maxim advocates unity among all members.

Delphic Fraternity established its Theta chapter at Binghamton University in 2003, marking the first Delphic chapter of the 21st century. In 2009, the fraternity expanded beyond the Northeast with the chartering of its first chapter outside that region at the University of Virginia. The UVA chapter, designated the Kappa chapter, is the first multicultural fraternity at the University of Virginia.

Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono is an Indonesian politician who served as the president of Indonesia from 2004 to 2014. He makes a brief on-screen appearance in the science-fiction film The Tomorrow War, appearing in a short clip of footage from his 31 March 2009 visit with former British Prime Minister Gordon Brown during a G20 forum held in London. In July 2021, Herzaky Mahendra Putra, a Democratic Party official, described Yudhoyono as a leading figure and a decisive actor within the political sphere.

Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono continued his military education at the Indonesian Army's Staff and Command College (Seskoad). He subsequently studied at the United States Army Command and General Staff College at Fort Leavenworth, Kansas. During his time in the United States, he earned a Master of Arts degree in business management from Webster University in 1991.

Veterinary care and animal health management are led by veterinary physicians, commonly known as veterinarians or veterinary surgeons (often referred to simply as vets). These professionals hold the Doctor of Veterinary Medicine (DVM) degree, and their role is regarded as equivalent to that of a physician or surgeon in human medicine. The path into the profession involves extensive postgraduate study and formal qualification prior to practicing.

Most veterinarians work in clinical settings where they treat animals directly. In general practice, they may provide broad, species-spanning care, treating animals of diverse types. They may specialize by animal group, focusing on companion animals, livestock, laboratory animals, zoo animals, or horses. They may also pursue specialization in narrow medical disciplines, such as surgery, dermatology, cardiology, neurology, laboratory animal medicine, internal medicine, and related fields.

The usefulness of incorporating fluoride-specific complexity in chemical modeling depends on the fluoride concentration present in the medium; when fluoride levels are relatively low, adding fluoride-related terms yields limited incremental accuracy. In seawater, sulfate ions greatly outnumber fluoride, by more than four hundred to one. As a result, for most practical purposes, the distinction between total-scale treatments and seawater-scale treatments is negligible.

Sørensen's 1909 definition of pH was superseded by the modern pH definition in 1924. In contemporary chemistry, the hydrogen ion concentration is denoted as [H+], rather than the older [H]. For dilute solutions, the thermodynamic activity of H+ (aH+) is replaced by the dimensionless ratio [H+]/c0, where the standard state concentration c0 is 1 mol/L. This ratio constitutes a pure number whose logarithm can be defined.

Oakley, Inc. engaged in two notable corporate actions in 2013: in August, the company divested its REVO brand by selling it to Sequential Brands for $20 million, and in November, it entered into a multi-year agreement with Scuderia Ferrari to expand its involvement in motorsport sponsorship.

During the October 2010 rescue of 33 miners who had been trapped for ten weeks in a Chilean mine, Oakley, Inc. provided eye protection by donating sunglasses after a journalist requested assistance for the operation. The company contributed 35 pairs of Radar sports glasses, with lenses selected to suit the rescue conditions.

Canadian Thanksgiving is celebrated with community events that take place during the week before the holiday and on Thanksgiving Day. The Markham Fair is a yearly agricultural and harvest festival staged in the weekend preceding Thanksgiving. The Kitchener-Waterloo Oktoberfest features an annual parade that includes floats, regional civic figures, local performance troupes, and marching bands. Fort Langley hosts a widely attended neighbourhood festival celebrating the cranberry harvest, highlighting local crafts, produce, and artisan goods.

On January 31, 1957, Governor General Vincent Massey issued a proclamation establishing a national Day of General Thanksgiving to Almighty God in gratitude for the bountiful harvest blessed upon Canada. The proclamation designated that the observance should occur on the second Monday in October each year, thereby formalizing the annual celebration within the Canadian calendar.

Lubbock Christian University maintains an a cappella group known as Best Friends. The ensemble tours nationwide and records studio albums, contributing to the university’s musical outreach. Several alumni have pursued roles with The Acappella Company, a well-established entity within the a cappella community.

Within the Talkington Center for Nursing Excellence lie the LCU Department of Nursing and the Covenant School of Nursing. The Collier Auditorium is located at the western end of the building and has a seating capacity of about 500.

Quincy, California had a population of 1,728 residents, with an age distribution comprising 341 people (19.7%) under 18, 163 (9.4%) aged 18–24, 350 (20.3%) aged 25–44, 556 (32.2%) aged 45–64, and 318 (18.4%) aged 65 or older. The median age was 45.5 years. The overall sex ratio equates to 84.2 males per 100 females, and among residents aged 18 and over the ratio was 81.1 males per 100 females.

Quincy, California, had 872 housing units at an average density of 205.7 per square mile. Of the occupied units, 388 (48.6%) were owner-occupied and 410 (51.4%) were rented. The homeowner vacancy rate stood at 2.7%, while the rental vacancy rate was 5.5%. The population living in owner-occupied housing units amounted to 872 people (50.5%), and 801 residents (46.4%) lived in rental housing units.

The Press Complaints Commission (PCC) was a voluntary regulatory body for British printed newspapers and magazines. It consisted of representatives from the major publishers and operated from its inception in 1991 until its dissolution in September 2014. The shutdown followed the News International phone-hacking scandal in 2011.

The Press Complaints Commission (PCC) faced intense scrutiny in the wake of the News International phone-hacking scandal, with British Members of Parliament and then-Prime Minister David Cameron criticizing its effectiveness in regulating the press. In July 2011, Cameron publicly urged that the PCC be replaced by a new regulatory arrangement, signaling a shift toward reform of the press self-regulation framework.

A junior officer is a term used to describe commissioned officers at the lower end of the hierarchical scale in many armed forces. The labels "company officer" or "company-grade officer" are more common in the Army, Air Force, and Marine Corps and derive from the historical responsibility of commanding a company-sized unit (including cavalry troops or artillery batteries). The designation typically applies to officers whose ranks are considered equivalent to a naval lieutenant, an army captain, or a flight lieutenant, or ranks below them. In the United States, the term is used by the Navy, Coast Guard, Public Health Service, and NOAA Corps to refer to certain ranks, including chief warrant officers (W-2 to W-4), ensign (O-1), lieutenant (junior grade) (O-2), and lieutenant (O-3).

Junior officer, sometimes termed a company officer or company grade officer, refers to the lowest operational tier within the commissioned officer ranks in a military or paramilitary organization. This category ranks above non-commissioned officers and below senior officers.

During the summer and autumn of 1919, Denikin petitioned Józef Piłsudski for military assistance, warning that a defeat of the White forces in southern Russia would empower groups that threatened Poland’s cultural and political foundations. Piłsudski countered that the lesser evil for Poland was to allow the Red Army to defeat White Russia, arguing that Poland could pursue its interests with any Russian state while avoiding involvement in anti-Russian revolutionary movements. He also asserted that Poland’s enduring interests lay in facilitating the revolutionary army’s pressure on the counter-revolutionaries. Later, on 12 December, the Red Army drove Denikin out of Kyiv.

Poland's eastern borders were discussed at the Tehran Conference in 1943, where Winston Churchill urged that the 1920 Curzon Line serve as the basis for Poland's eastern frontier rather than the borders established by the Peace of Riga. This position was carried forward to the Yalta Conference in 1945, where the Allied leaders reached an understanding effectively endorsing that alignment. Despite Poland's wartime contributions and existing treaties, the Western Allies allowed the country to remain within the Soviet sphere of influence, shaping its postwar political trajectory. As compensation for losing the eastern territories, Poland acquired the bulk of the lands formerly part of Germany east of the Oder-Neisse line, thereby extending its western and northern borders. The resulting settlement is often described in Polish discourse as the Western betrayal.

Alessandro Peretti di Montalto, born in Montalto delle Marche, was the son of Fabio Damasceni and Maria Felice Mignucci Peretti, who on her mother's side was a niece of a pope. He is commonly known as Cardinal di Montalto, a designation shared with his great-uncle. As a major patron, he supported Villa Lante at Bagnaia, adding a garden casino modeled on an earlier one. He also sponsored the church of Sant’Andrea della Valle in Rome, a project begun in 1591, though its façade was not his. At the cardinal’s expense, Carlo Maderno designed and oversaw the construction of the second-largest dome in Rome for Sant’Andrea della Valle, built between 1608 and 1621.

Alessandro Peretti di Montalto, a cardinal, was known for an extravagant lifestyle and a keen interest in music and lavish theatrical productions. He staged these performances at his residence, the Cancelleria Palace, and employed a number of musicians to sustain his court. In addition to patronage, he actively encouraged the monodic tradition, promoting solo song as a distinctive musical expression of his era.

In 2020, Six Flags St. Louis replaced Fright Fest with HALLOWFEST as part of the response to the COVID-19 pandemic. To minimize health risks, park capacity was limited to 25 percent of its normal level, and all haunted houses, scare zones, and shows were substituted with outdoor, socially distanced alternatives.

Six Flags St. Louis was conceived in the 1960s by Angus G. Wynne, the founder of Six Flags, and was the last of the company's original three parks. It marked the first instance of a park designed by the Six Flags company itself, as Randall Duell, who had designed the first two parks, was occupied with AstroWorld at the time. The park subsequently opened on June 5, 1971.

P3 Gull, commonly referred to as P3 Gold, is a Norwegian music show and award ceremony organized by NRK P3, the music-focused radio channel of the Norwegian public broadcaster. The event was first held on 29 November 2013 at Sentrum Scene in Oslo. It awards four categories: Newcomer of the Year (Årets nykommer), Live Artist of the Year (Årets liveartist), Song of the Year (Årets låt), and the P3-Prize (P3-prisen). The accompanying live performances bring together the listening audience and the music featured on P3, underscoring the program's role in promoting contemporary Norwegian music.

P3 Gull has accumulated six Gullruten Professional Awards in total. The Best Directing Multi-Camera prize was awarded to Nicolai Sørensen for the program in three consecutive years: 2014, 2015, and 2016. In the Best Cinematography category, the work earned recognition in 2014 and again in 2016, with credits to Henning Våge and Mats Lian. The 2016 ceremony also yielded three further accolades: Best Sound Design, Best Art Direction, and Best Production Design, awarded to Audun Stjernstad and Joakim Faxvaag.

The Kantonsschule Stadelhofen occupies Villa Hohenbühl, a villa constructed from 1887 to 1889 by the Swiss architect Alfred Friedrich Bluntschli for Friedrich Wegmann-Schoch. Bluntschli, who also designed the Enge Church on the opposite shore of Lake Zürich, imparted architectural features to Villa Hohenbühl that bear notable similarities to his church, reflecting a coherent stylistic approach. The property is set in a landscaped park, contributing to its historic ambience. Today, the villa serves as the premises of the adjacent Stadelhofen college, integrating the cantonal school with the historic building.

Kantonsschule Stadelhofen (KST) is a public secondary school that offers four maturity profiles: altsprachlich (classical languages), neusprachlich (modern languages), musisch (fine arts), and mathematisch-naturwissenschaftlich (mathematical and natural sciences). In its present form, the school was established in 1975, while its predecessor can be traced back to the Töchterschule der Stadt Zürich, founded in 1874.

In April 1982, portions of East District were transferred to neighboring districts, with Chuannan, Fahua, Junwang, Kaishan and Xiaonan incorporated into Central District, and Daen, Dalin, Dazhong and Xinsheng reassigned to South District. Subsequently, in August 1982, the remaining area underwent subdivision into smaller villages: Degao was divided into Chongshan, Chongxue and Degao; Dongguang was divided into Dongguang, Yunong and Zhuangjing; Fuqiang was partitioned into Fuqiang and Fuyu; Zhongxiao was split into Chongming and Zhongxiao; and Renhe was separated into Heping and Renhe. These alterations brought the district's total to 40 villages.

In February 1972, Daxing and Daxue were added to the East District of Tainan. Following this expansion, the Ludong and Xiaodong areas were subdivided into four villages, resulting in the district administering a total of 32 villages.

Sunset Pass is a 1933 American pre-Code Western film directed by Henry Hathaway. The film stars Randolph Scott, Tom Keene, Harry Carey, and Noah Beery, and it is adapted from a novel by Zane Grey. In the same year, Hathaway directed several additional Zane Grey adaptations featuring a similar ensemble, including Scott, Carey, and Beery.

Hazaragi employs a set of verbal prefixes to mark aspect, mood, and negation on finite verbs. For imperfective aspect, the marker mi- may surface as assimilated forms m-, mu-, or mê-, as illustrated by mi-zan-um, which expresses “I hit” or “I am hitting.” The subjunctive and imperative moods are indicated with the bi- prefix, which shows similar assimilation patterns. Negation is carried by the na- prefix, for instance na-mi-zad-um, meaning “I was not hitting.” Across these markers, stress is typically placed on the verb.

Hazaragi comprises a group of Afghan Persian dialects, a form of Afghan Persian that is regarded as the more formal or classical variety of Persian. The dialect preserves certain phonological features, including the voiced velar fricative [ɣ] and the bilabial approximant [w]. It has incorporated rare retroflex consonants [ʈ] and [ɖ], a distinction illustrated by pairs such as buṭ (boot) versus but (idol), which reflect a retroflex versus non-retroflex contrast. The glottal fricative [h] is often dropped in Hazaragi speech. Unlike Western Persian, where the phonemes associated with the letters ق and غ may converge, Hazaragi dialects maintain a separation between the voiced uvular stop [ɢ] and the voiced velar fricative [ɣ].

During World War II, the Imperial Japanese Navy submarine I-25, commanded by Akiji Tagami, entered United States coastal waters on 21 June 1942 with the aim of sinking enemy shipping and striking land targets with its 14 cm deck gun. The vessel also carried a Yokosuka E14Y seaplane and operated with a crew of 97. To minimize exposure to coastal minefields, I-25 trailed fishing boats as it approached the American coast, culminating in the bombardment of Fort Stevens.

Late that night, Commander Tagami ordered his crew to surface the submarine at the mouth of the Columbia River, with Fort Stevens as the intended target. The fort itself dates to the American Civil War and, by the time of the bombardment, was equipped with artillery regarded as obsolete and characteristic of the Endicott era. Its armament included 12-inch (305 mm) mortars and several disappearing guns in 10-inch (254 mm) and 6-inch (152 mm) calibers.

Under Swedish rule, Estonia experienced extensive supervision of religious and intellectual life by the state, with authorities enforcing conformity through a system of regular visitations and inspections from the late sixteenth through the seventeenth century. Higher clergy, such as bishops or regional superintendents, visited congregations to assess beliefs and to eradicate lingering practices associated with paganism or Catholicism. The first large-scale visitation was led by Johannes Rudbeckius, marking a notable start to these oversight efforts. Later, Gustavus Adolphus, in collaboration with governor Johan Skytte, established the Court of Appeal in Tartu and founded the University of Tartu, moves that reinforced institutional control over law, education, and religious life in the province.

Toward the close of the 16th century, most Estonian lands were privately owned, with ownership concentrated among Baltic German elites. The Baltic German nobility wielded substantial influence over economic life and political affairs. The crown's attempts to curb this dominance faced significant resistance. As a result, central authority remained largely compliant for an extended period, since ongoing wars made the loyalty of the local aristocracy an important consideration for Swedish rule in the region.

Under President Young, Pepperdine pursued expansion by identifying suburban locations. In 1966 a committee was convened to evaluate potential sites, including Westlake Village and Calabasas. The university initially favored Westlake Village, but the Adamson-Rindge family offered to donate 138 acres and to sell an additional 58.7 acres near Malibu. Despite concerns about the higher construction costs associated with the mountainous Malibu site, the school proceeded due to its advantageous location and fundraising potential, accepting the Malibu land in 1968.

Pepperdine University was included in 2019 in the American Council of Trustees and Alumni's What Will They Learn? assessment, which surveys roughly 1,120 colleges and universities and assigns a letter grade based on adherence to a defined set of core curriculum requirements. The assessment identifies seven core subjects: composition, literature, foreign language, American history, economics, mathematics, and science. Pepperdine earned an A grade, indicating that its core curriculum requires at least six of the seven subjects. In that year, 23 institutions achieved an A.

The Free Zone is a territorial area in Western Sahara that has been controlled by the Polisario Front since the 1991 cease-fire between the Polisario Front and Morocco, established under the Settlement Plan. Morocco occupies the territories to the west of the Berm, including the majority of the Free Zone’s population. The cease-fire is supervised by the United Nations peacekeeping mission MINURSO, whose mandate includes maintaining the cease-fire and organizing a referendum on independence.

Annual demonstrations against the Moroccan Wall are staged in the Free Zone region, attracting participants that include Sahrawis as well as international activists from Spain, Italy, and other predominantly European countries. The United Nations maintains close oversight of these demonstrations and the related activities in the area.

During the Third Battle of Kharkov, German forces were estimated at around 160,000 troops in opposition to approximately 210,000 Red Army soldiers. The Wehrmacht remained understrength after a long period of operations spanning June 1942 to February 1943, prompting the leadership to seek a substantial expansion of manpower. Adolf Hitler established a committee—involving Wilhelm Keitel, Martin Bormann, and Hans Lammers—to recruit as many as 800,000 additional able-bodied men, with about half drawn from nonessential industries; however, the effects of this mobilization would not be apparent until roughly May 1943. By that time, German armed forces had reached about 9.5 million personnel, the highest strength recorded since the war began.

In March 1943, German forces reversed a Soviet advance south of Kharkov as Manstein renewed the offensive against Kharkov proper on 7 March after encirclements of Red Army armored spearheads, with the Wehrmacht achieving flanking and encirclement success. The SS Panzer Corps, disregarding orders to seal off Kharkov from the north, directly engaged on 11 March, and four days of house-to-house fighting followed, culminating in the recapture of Kharkov by the SS Division Leibstandarte on 15 March. Two days later, German units also regained Belgorod, creating a Kharkov–Belgorod salient that would set the stage for the Battle of Kursk in July 1943. The operation inflicted approximately 90,000 Soviet casualties, while the house-to-house fighting proved particularly costly for the SS Panzer Corps, which sustained around 4,300 killed and wounded by mid-March.

Profit margin is a financial metric that expresses net income as a proportion of revenue, indicating how much profit is earned for each dollar of sales. A margin of 35 percent implies a net profit of 35 cents for every dollar of sales. The example described here relies on figures from the most recent quarter.

Profit margins are a measure of how much profit a company earns from its revenue and are useful for comparing profitability across firms within the same industry. Investors often examine the margins of similar companies to identify those that are more profitable and may represent more attractive investment opportunities. A low profit margin can indicate that a company is in distress or is pricing its goods too cheaply relative to costs. Regardless of the underlying cause, persistently low margins may signal trouble for the firm's prospects over the long term.

Portuguese phonology features two rhotic phonemes, /ʁ/ and /ɾ/, which correspond to distinct phonological categories within the language. The distribution of these rhotics is largely conditioned by the surrounding context, with specific environments favoring one phoneme over the other. In addition, there is dialectal variation in their phonetic realization, as different Portuguese varieties pronounce the rhotics in diverse ways while preserving the underlying contrast between them.

In Portuguese phonology, a word-final sibilant before a following word that begins with a vowel is realized as an intervocalic z, producing cross-word liaison across the word boundary. This phenomenon is illustrated by the phrase bons amigos, which is heard as [bõz ɐˈmiɣuʃ] or [bõz aˈmiɡus], reflecting dialectal variation in the realization of the following segment.

Screw piles, also called helical piles, constitute an environmentally friendly option for ready-to-build foundations. Their use has broadened from commercial settings to residential applications, with many homeowners preferring screw pile foundations for suitable projects. Common applications include wooden decks, fences, garden houses, pergolas, and carports.

Foundation (engineering) is a form of deep foundation that employs a single, large-diameter structural element which is embedded into the ground. This element transfers the loads from a substantial above-surface structure to deeper soil layers or bedrock, thereby supporting all imposed loads—such as the structure’s weight and wind forces.

In the context of funk rock, Britpop bands incorporated funk influences, with experimentation concentrated largely on bass lines. An illustrative example is Blur's "Girls & Boys," from the 1994 album Parklife.

Funk rock emerged in the 1970s with several American artists identified as early pioneers, including Rick Derringer, Redbone, the Bar-Kays, and Mother's Finest. The latter's lead singer, Glenn "Doc" Murdock, has stated that the band identified itself as funk rock and may have helped invent the style, noting that they even lived in a house named Funk Rock, Georgia and felt they were at the forefront of the genre. Mother's Finest and their peers occasionally shared stages with acts such as Lynyrd Skynyrd and AC/DC, groups whose music contained considerable funk influence.
