In some black clubs, however, the band faced backlash for being too loud, reflecting tensions over loudness and genre boundaries within certain audiences.

Xiancun station on Line 18 reached key construction milestones in late 2020, with the station’s main structure topped out on 28 November 2020, and by 31 December 2020 the concrete pouring for the inverted roof of the open-cut section had been completed.

Xiancun Station (Chinese: 冼村站; pinyin: Xiǎncūn Zhàn; Jyutping: sin2cyun4 zaam6) is an underground station on Line 18 of the Guangzhou Metro, located at the junction of Huangpu Avenue West, Tiyu East Road, and Xiancun Road in the Tianhe District of Guangzhou. The station opened on 28 September 2021 and presently serves as the northern terminus of Line 18.

The Ecologist Party of Romania opposed the policies of the Front of the National Salvation (FSN) from the outset. In April 1990, it formed an alliance with Radu Câmpeanu's National Liberal Party (PNL). It also supported the Timișoara Proclamation (Proclamația de la Timișoara), which urged former Communist Party structures and their members to refrain from taking part in post-revolutionary politics.

In the summer of 2023, the Ecologist Party of Romania announced a relaunch under new leadership. The party subsequently reoriented its policy platform toward contemporary priorities, notably food safety and the protection of the environment. This recalibration occurred amid an increasingly complex context for agriculture and environmental policy, reflecting broader challenges facing the sector.

Armenia's National Security Service (NSS) has played a central role in several notable internal security operations and political developments. It participated in the 2016 Yerevan hostage crisis and supported the 2018 anti-corruption crackdown. In the 2020 Nagorno-Karabakh war, NSS border troops sustained casualties, with 46 servicemen killed, 191 wounded, and two missing. Following the 2020 ceasefire protests over Karabakh, the NSS foiled an assassination attempt against Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan. The agency also uncovered illegal procurement and storage of weapons and explosives by a group led by Artur Vanetsyan, a former NSS operative and director.

Within Armenia's National Security Service, recruits for the Armenian Border Guard undertake training in Russia through five-year residential programs. The training is conducted at several Russian institutions, including the Oryol campus of the Moscow Border Institute of the Federal Security Service, as well as the Kurgan Border Guard Institute and the Kaliningrad Border Guard Institute. Upon graduation, they earn a degree in engineering and are commissioned as lieutenants in the Armenian Border Guard.

Jean Émile Laboureur was a French illustrator and engraver renowned for producing artwork for 66 titles and for pairing illustrations with works by prominent authors such as Jean Giraudoux, Jacques Cazotte, Rémy de Gourmont, Auguste de Villiers de L’Isle-Adam, André Maurois, Colette, Tristan Derème, Anna de Noailles, Paul-Jean Toulet, and Marcel Proust. He contributed to notable periodicals, including the Gazette du Bon Ton and La Revue musicale, and taught engraving in his workshop, shaping the skills of artists such as Marie Laurencin and André Dunoyer de Segonzac. In the early 1930s, Laboureur received commissions to illustrate for the Catalogue Manufrance, with his engravings remaining in use for several decades.

Following a period of museum visits in Germany, Laboureur traveled to the United States in 1904, where he began using the name Jean Émile. He subsequently made several returns to the United States and to Canada between 1905 and 1909 to participate in exhibitions. After 1911, his travels extended to England, Italy, Greece, and Turkey.

Aptoide is an alternative app store for the Android platform. The Android client used to access its stores is open source, and the project has spawned several forks, including F-Droid. Client–server communications are conducted via an open XML-based protocol, enabling standardized data exchange between devices and servers.

Aptoide Uploader is an Android application released in June 2011 as a companion tool to the Aptoide platform, developed by the same team behind Aptoide. The software enables users to upload apps to an existing Aptoide store, thereby contributing content to the platform's community catalogs.

Under delegation from the secretary, the deputy secretary of defense possesses full power and authority to act on the secretary’s behalf. The deputy secretary may exercise the secretary’s powers in all matters for which the secretary is authorized to act under statute or executive order. Additionally, the deputy secretary is first in the line of succession to the secretary of defense.

The Deputy Secretary of Defense (DepSecDef) is a statutory office that ranks as the second-highest official within the Department of Defense. The position is informally known as the Deputy Secretary of War (DepSecWar). The office was created by law under 10 U.S.C. § 132.

DokuWiki employs a built-in user management system to define users and groups, which underpins its access control framework. Administrators use access control lists to assign permissions at both the page and namespace levels, enabling more granular control than is typically available in other wiki platforms such as MediaWiki. In addition to the included user management features, DokuWiki supports authentication against various backends, including databases, LDAP directories, and Microsoft Active Directory, with additional authentication methods achievable through a range of plugins.

DokuWiki is a wiki software that implements Unicode using UTF-8, enabling support for languages with right-to-left scripts and the display of languages such as Chinese, Thai, and Hebrew. The interface is available in roughly seventy languages, and multilingual wikis can be created or managed through dedicated plugins. In addition, users can contribute translations of the DokuWiki core and its plugins via a web-based interface.

The Peace of Szeged was concluded in a context in which Vladislaus issued a declaration shortly after, and roughly concurrent with, the drafting of a letter to Hunyadi. Ciriaco conveyed the developing news to the Pope, who then informed Cardinal Cesarini. Cesarini had anchored his political career on the crusade, a venture arising from his support of the papal position against the Council of Basel; he abandoned Basel in the late 1430s. Consequently, he was compelled to fashion a settlement acceptable to both sides, a dynamic that shaped the terms of the Szeged agreement.

The Peace of Szeged, concluded in 1444 and, together with the Treaty of Edirne, formed a peace arrangement between Sultan Murad II of the Ottoman Empire and King Vladislaus of Hungary, with Despot Đurađ Branković of the Serbian Despotate taking part in the proceedings. The agreement marked the cessation of the Christian crusade against the Ottomans and yielded notable gains for the Christian side. Nevertheless, within a month Vladislaus repudiated his oath under papal urging, and the crusade continued. On 10 November 1444, the crusaders were defeated at the Battle of Varna, and Vladislaus was killed.

The Strategy and External Affairs Directorates form part of the Scottish Government's civil service, administered under the office of the Permanent Secretary to the Scottish Government, the most senior civil servant in Scotland. The current holder of the post is Joe Griffin, who was appointed on 7 April 2025.

In the Scottish Government, work is organized into directorates, each headed by a Director, with directorates grouped into directorate-general families led by a Director-General. Directorates constitute the fundamental components of the administration and are subdivided into divisions, which are further divided into units (often called branches) and, ultimately, teams. Divisions typically comprise around 25–50 staff. There is no direct one-to-one correspondence between Ministers’ political responsibilities and specific directorates, although some overlap can occur. Directorates are responsible for government agencies and non-departmental public bodies, while some government functions are carried out by Executive Agencies, such as Transport Scotland, that sit outside the directorates but are staffed by civil servants.

Syd began making music while living with her parents. Her stage name was given by her older brother Ty during childhood, a name she later reclaimed after joining Odd Future. Much of Odd Future's early material was recorded at Syd's house, known to associates as "The Trap." Within the collective, she served as a DJ and producer. She was the only female member during the group's active years and publicly identified as gay, a stance that contrasted with the group's often homophobic and misogynistic lyrics. In 2011, she co-founded The Internet, and the group's debut album Purple Naked Ladies was released that year. In 2014, Syd opened for Eminem at Wembley Stadium as part of the Odd Future collective.

Syd is credited on Beyoncé's "Plastic Off the Sofa," the eighth track on her seventh studio album Renaissance. She also appears on Duckwrth's single "Ce Soir," a track that later appeared on Chrome Bull, Duckwrth's third EP.

Xeer is a customary Somali legal system in which crimes are regarded as transgressions against property rights, and justice is expressed through material compensation to the victim. If the accused is found guilty, restitution of a material nature must be paid; when such restitution cannot be provided, mag retribution is due, measured in livestock—typically healthy female camels—and paid to the victim or their family. There is no concept of imprisonment within xeer. Elders may advise that neither side seeks restitution or retribution. Enforcement of a verdict is carried out by the victim's family or by all able-bodied clansmen in the area where the decision is to be executed.

Xeer is a traditional system of dispute resolution whose aim is to secure consensus between the disputing parties. Historically, arbitration took place beneath a large tree, with mediators guiding the parties toward voluntary submission to the judge’s ruling; in contemporary practice, proceedings are typically held in meeting halls rather than under the tree. Each party may appoint a representative to present its case, while a recorder captures the essential points. When a fact is contested, its truth must be established by the testimony of three witnesses; if this is not possible, an oath may be sworn. If proceedings become heated, the presiding judge may order a recess to permit informal discussion in small groups by the parties. After mediation is concluded, an appeal may be requested, but unanimous consent of all parties is required.

Open o, sometimes described as the turned C, is a letter of the extended Latin alphabet with the forms Ɔ (uppercase) and ɔ (lowercase). It is employed in the orthographies of many African languages that use the African Reference Alphabet. In the International Phonetic Alphabet, the symbol denotes the open-mid back rounded vowel, typically realized as [ɔ].

During the colonial-period orthography of Yucatec Maya, the glyph Ɔ was employed to denote the alveolar ejective affricate [t͡sʼ], a phoneme that corresponds to that specific ejective sound. In contemporary transcription practices, scholars typically render this sound as dz or tsʼ, reflecting a shift in how the phoneme is represented in modern phonological notation.

Self-capacitive touch screen layers are employed in mobile phones to detect input from finger contact. These layers operate by sensing changes in the electrical capacitance at a transparent conductor, enabling precise and responsive touch interaction. Notable examples of devices using this technology include Sony's Xperia Sola and several Samsung smartphones such as the Galaxy S4, Galaxy Note 3, Galaxy S5, and Galaxy Alpha.

Touchscreen technology has become increasingly integrated into customer service across the 21st century, with widespread adoption in many areas. In the restaurant industry, touchscreens have emerged as a significant feature, with several chain brands such as Taco Bell, Panera Bread, and McDonald’s offering self-service ordering options alongside traditional cashiers. While customers retain the option to place orders with a human cashier, self-ordering interfaces are commonplace. A Bangalore restaurant pursued a fully automated ordering model, equipping tables with integrated touchscreens to access an extensive menu. Upon selection, orders are transmitted electronically to the kitchen, illustrating how these devices operate within modern point-of-sale systems.

The Burns Times-Herald arose from a long process of consolidation that brought together roughly six local newspapers over several decades. The earliest newspaper published in Burns, Oregon was the Harney Valley Item, launched by Horace A. Dillard in July 1885. It was a four-page, six-column paper printed on a Washington hand press and described at the time as a patent-out publication. After two years Dillard sold the Item to J. M. Vaughn. Ultimately, the Harney Valley Item was absorbed into the chain of titles that would evolve into the Times-Herald.

The East Oregon Herald, the second Burns newspaper, was founded in November 1887 by David Louis Grace and Nellie R. Grace. Approximately a century later, it had outlived or consolidated with 34 papers to become Harney County’s sole remaining title. Julian Byrd joined the Graces as an apprentice at age 15, while his brother Charles A. Byrd, then 21, worked as a compositor for the Graces; Julian Byrd became the printer's devil in December 1889. W. C. Byrd, Julian’s father, purchased the Herald circa 1890. In 1890, Charles Byrd bought the Item and published it for three years. Julian Byrd then bought Harney Times and merged it with the Herald to form Burns Times-Herald, a title he subsequently expanded by purchasing and absorbing the Burns Tribune into his paper.

Bid for Love is a 2022 American romantic drama film directed by Arthur Muhammad and written by Erick S. Gray and N'Tyse. It is loosely based on the play My Mistakes Do Not Define Me by Lawainna Patterson and Shelly Garrett. The cast includes Dawn Halfkenny as Sasha, Adrian Lockett as Malik, Blue Kimble as Memphis, and Tami Roman portraying a therapist. The narrative centers on Sasha, who has just been released from prison, as she enters a relationship with the manipulative Malik. A therapist helps Sasha recognize and avoid the patterns that previously led to her incarceration in an earlier relationship with Memphis.

Bid for Love 2, the sequel to Bid for Love, was filmed in Dallas in May 2023 and is slated for a 2024 release. Its ensemble features Clifton Powell, Eva Marcille, Cynthia Bailey, Darrin Dewitt Henson, Erica Peeples, Angela White, David Banner, DreamDoll, and Stephen Cofield Jr., alongside the original cast.

Julien Lavallée, a Montreal-born individual who was 30 years old in 2017, was identified as one of StubHub's leading sellers in the ticket resale market. A Toronto Star report published on November 9, 2017 described his growth as relying on aggressive tactics that manipulated the ticket marketplace and restricted access for fans. Leaked documents reportedly indicate that Lavallée used StubHub, alongside Vivid Seats and Ticketmaster, as primary channels to scalp tickets. Prior to October 2017, he operated I Want Ticket Inc, a company registered in the Isle of Man, which posted listings on StubHub's United Kingdom marketplace.

StubHub offers mobile applications across Apple's iPhone and iPad platforms as well as devices running Android. The apps provide interactive venue maps for seat selection and allow users to specify the number of seats, facilitating precise ticket planning. In addition, they include features to help users plan an outing by locating nearby restaurants, bars, and parking facilities.

Following the Soviet–Afghan War, Afghanistan faced a substantial external debt burden that reflected the long-term economic fallout of the conflict. The CIA World Fact Book reported that by 2004 the country owed about $8 billion in bilateral debt, with the majority of this obligation held by Russia. In 2007, Russia agreed to cancel most of the outstanding debt, marking a significant move in the postwar financial relationship between the two states.

The Sarandoy were a centrally controlled paramilitary force under the Ministry of Interior, later incorporated into the unified Ministry of State Security (WAD) in 1986. The designation covered a range of units, including traffic police, provincial officers, and corrections and labor facility staff. Their effectiveness was mixed; while the force was well funded and armed, its performance varied, and it faced stiff resistance from insurgents, including Osama bin Laden and his Arab mujahideen opponents, who confronted the Sarandoy’s 7th Operative Regiment and inflicted heavy casualties. A substantial portion of recruits joined not out of ideological loyalty but in pursuit of material advantages, with many Mujahideen entering the ranks to procure arms, ammunition, and money and to glean intelligence about forthcoming operations. By late 1981, Bulgarian Armed Forces were deployed to Mazar-i-Sharif, while the Warsaw Pact and the Cuban Revolutionary Armed Forces were active across Afghanistan. Mujahideen testimonies described Cuban troops as physically imposing and loud in combat, and, unlike the Soviet troops, willing to attack openly.

From 4 September 1770 to 7 October 1771, Denmark–Norway experienced a period in which freedom of the press was among the most unrestricted in Europe, under the rule of Johann Friedrich Struensee. His second reform act abolished the existing censorship laws, removing prior controls on printing and publication. This liberalization coincided with a substantial circulation of anonymous pamphlets that were critical of, and at times defamatory toward, Struensee's regime. On 7 October 1771, Struensee reimposed certain press restrictions, signaling a renewed regulation of printed material.

According to Reporters Without Borders (RSF), its 2018 annual report documents deadly violence and abuses against journalists. That year saw 80 reporters killed, 348 detained, and 60 taken hostage, indicating an unprecedented level of hostility toward media personnel. Iran was named as one of five states labeled a “prison of reporters,” alongside China, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and Turkey. In RSF's rankings, Iran stood 144th and was described as one of the world's worst prisons for journalists.

Georgia is a country in the Caucasus region of Eurasia, situated at the crossroads of Western Asia and Eastern Europe. Following the Russian Revolution of 1917, it experienced a short-lived period of independence. In 1921, Soviet forces occupied the country, and it became the Georgian Soviet Socialist Republic within the Soviet Union. Georgia regained independence in 1991 with the dissolution of the Soviet Union. The post-communist era in the 1990s was marked by civil unrest and economic difficulties. The Rose Revolution of 2003 brought about a new government and initiated democratic and economic reforms.

In 1882, Lt. Col. Eduard Rubin developed a copper-jacketed bullet featuring a lead core encased in a copper jacket. The design was a small-caliber configuration in 7.5 mm and 8 mm variants. It served as the forerunner of the 8 mm Lebel bullet used in the Lebel Model 1886 smokeless-powder rifle ammunition. At high velocities, lead-core projectiles can melt due to heat from propellant gases and bore friction; copper jackets, however, possess a higher melting point, greater specific heat capacity, and increased hardness, enabling higher muzzle velocities by better withstanding heat and wear.

Bullets encompass a wide variety of shapes and profiles to accommodate different firearms and uses. Where legal, individuals may produce bullets at home by melting and casting lead in reloading molds. Hand-casting, while feasible, is typically only economical and practical for producing solid lead projectiles due to time and material considerations. For most handloaders, cast and jacketed bullets are commercially manufactured and readily available from numerous producers. In general, commercially manufactured bullets provide greater convenience than attempting to cast bullets from bulk or scrap lead, owing to standardization and supply reliability.

Transfer zones are structural features found in continental rift systems where principal fault boundaries progressively enlarge as sustained extensional forces drive ongoing fault propagation. They are identified by examining the evolution and interaction of faults during propagation, linkage, and deformation, which reflects their deformational history. A widely used classification distinguishes four types: approaching, overlapping, collateral, and collinear transfer zones. This typology aids visualization and interpretation of the deformational history and overall evolution of the transfer zone within the rift system.

Transfer zones, particularly synthetic ones formed by major normal faults dipping in the same direction, often incorporate relay ramps that connect offset basins. Such features have been studied in the East African Rift, including Lake Malawi, and in the Gulf of Suez rift, where relay ramps are recognized as important structural elements. Drainage basins within a transfer zone comprise sediments that are transported through the transfer zone and into the adjacent half graben, thereby influencing where and how deposition occurs. The Gulf of Evvia serves as a prominent example, in which a relay ramp plays a major role in drainage, with footwall drainage being limited while transfer zone drainage is more pronounced. Drainage basin size emerges as a key control on sediment flux, and both interbasin and intrabasin synthetic relay ramp transfer zones are expected to exert strong influence on overall sedimentation, while intrabasinal transfer zones, though smaller, still function as conduits for sediment transport.

Koshi Province, known in Japanese as Koshi no Kuni (越国), was an ancient province of Japan. Its territory generally corresponded to parts of the region that today constitutes the Hokuriku region. The area was sometimes referred to as Esshū (越州).

At the close of the 7th century, the ancient Koshi was subdivided into Echizen, Etchū, and Echigo under the Taihō Code, marking a formal reorganization within the Ritsuryō state framework. The names reflect their relative positions to the capital region, the Kinki area, with Echizen designated as Inner-Koshi, Etchū as Middle-Koshi, and Echigo as Outer-Koshi. This division arose as part of the enactment of the Ritsuryō system, aligning provincial administration with geographical proximity to the center. Subsequently, portions of Echizen were carved out to form the separate provinces of Noto and Kaga.

La plus belle pour aller danser is a song that has been covered by several artists from different countries. Notable renditions include Pompilia Stoian of Romania, Thanh Lan of Vietnam, Michèle Richard of Canada, and Huoy Meas of Cambodia, as well as contemporary performers Chris Garneau and Sarah Dagenais-Hakim. Additionally, Canadian singer Emilie-Claire Barlow recorded a version on her Juno Award-winning album Seule ce soir.

Cynogale, commonly referred to as the otter civet, is a semiaquatic carnivoran noted for its webbed feet, an adaptation that facilitates life in aquatic habitats. It also bears long, stiff whiskers that may assist in foraging, helping the animal detect prey and navigate its environment.

Cynogale, commonly known as otter civets, are distributed across Sumatra, Borneo, and the Thai peninsula. The species favors lowland primary forests, which constitute its preferred habitat, though individuals have also been observed in secondary forest. Their presence in northern Vietnam remains uncertain.

Rock music spawned several distinct subgenres, among them rockabilly, which fuses rock and roll with hillbilly country music. In rockabilly, mid-1950s white vocalists such as Carl Perkins, Jerry Lee Lewis, Roy Orbison, Buddy Holly, and Elvis Presley achieved substantial commercial success. Hispanic and Latino American movements in rock and roll contributed to the emergence of Latin rock and Chicano rock in the United States, beginning in the Southwest, while artists like Ritchie Valens and Al Hurricane with his brothers Tiny Morrie and Baby Gaby blended rock and roll with country-western within traditional New Mexico music. The 1950s also witnessed growing popularity of the electric guitar and the development of a distinctive rock and roll playing style by Chuck Berry, Link Wray, and Scotty Moore. Distortion effects were pioneered by Western swing guitarists Junior Barnard and Eldon Shamlin, later popularized by Berry in the mid-1950s. The concept of power chords is traced to the 19th century with Francisco Tárrega and Heitor Villa-Lobos, subsequently adopted by Willie Johnson and Pat Hare in the early 1950s and brought to wider prominence by Link Wray in the late 1950s.

Rock music’s British blues-rock lineage was shaped by a series of interlinked groups and musicians. John Mayall's Bluesbreakers operated as a foundational blues outfits, featuring Eric Clapton after his departure from the Yardbirds and later Peter Green; their 1966 album Blues Breakers with Eric Clapton, commonly known as Beano, is regarded as a landmark British blues recording whose influence spread across Britain and the United States. Clapton went on to form Cream, and later participated in Blind Faith and Derek and the Dominos, pursuing a lengthy solo career that helped bring blues rock into the mainstream. Peter Green, joined by Bluesbreakers’ rhythm section Mick Fleetwood and John McVie, formed Peter Green's Fleetwood Mac, achieving major commercial success within the genre. In the late 1960s, Jeff Beck, another Yardbirds alumnus, steered blues rock toward heavier terrain with the Jeff Beck Group. Jimmy Page, the final guitarist to leave the Yardbirds, formed The New Yardbirds, which soon evolved into Led Zeppelin. Led Zeppelin’s first three albums, along with much of their subsequent work, undertook expansions of traditional blues songs, shaping the direction of rock through their blues-inflected approach.

David Mamet's filmmaking method is grounded in Eisensteinian montage, presenting narrative through the juxtaposition of images that carry little overt interpretation. The technique relies heavily on cuts between scenes, with directors urged to minimize narrated exposition. The aim is to communicate the essential point of a scene rather than track a single protagonist or pursue purely aesthetically pleasing imagery. Mamet's approach envisions cinema as a means to impose order on disorder in pursuit of a clear objective, guiding the audience toward intended meaning through disciplined editing rather than elaborate visual flourish.

Deadline reported in June 2024 that the project The Prince would be directed by Cameron Van Hoy. The narrative centers on Hunter Biden, the second son of U.S. President Joe Biden, with Scott Haze portraying the lead character Parker. The ensemble cast includes Nicolas Cage, J. K. Simmons, Giancarlo Esposito, and Andy Garcia. David Mamet described the film as not a travelogue, noting that it would draw on aspects of Hunter Biden's life rather than presenting a straightforward biographical portrait.

Army Group Liguria was a World War II formation created when the remaining divisions of the Italian Social Republic completed their training and were combined with German units in the Liguria region. The new formation was commanded by Rodolfo Graziani, who served as the RSI Minister of Defense and presided over all RSI Army forces.

Army Group Liguria, also known as Armeegruppe Ligurien in German, was a temporary German Army Group formed in the Italian theater during World War II. It came into existence in November 1944, created to place the 14th Army under its command and to unify control of operations in the Ligurian region under a single headquarters. The formation existed from November 1944 to February 1945.

The music video for Young, Wild & Free was shot in Montclair, California in October 2011 under the direction of Dylan Brown and features Snoop Dogg and Wiz Khalifa driving go-karts, skateboarding, and partying with women, while also incorporating footage from the film Mac & Devin Go to High School. Live performances of the track took place during the 2012 VMA Tour and at Coachella in 2012. It later formed part of the 2015 Boys of Zummer tour, the American leg of Khalifa's joint trek with Fall Out Boy, and was included in Snoop Dogg's 2016 Puff Puff Pass Tour Part 2. The song has also appeared on two collaborative Snoop Dogg–Wiz Khalifa tours, namely the 2011 High School Tour and the 2016 High Road Summer Tour. In 2013, it was nominated for Best Rap Song at the 55th Annual Grammy Awards.

Young, Wild & Free has elicited mixed critical reception for its accessible production and pop sensibility; AllMusic's David Jeffries described the track as having a more contemporary, friendly sound relative to the rest of the album, characterizing it as polished, bright, and sunshine-like. Consequence of Sound's Michael Madden argued that it stands out as one of the few songs fit for a soundtrack, thanks to Bruno Mars's smooth pop vocals and the glitzy, Hollywood-style production. The A.V. Club's Chris Martins praised its sharp keyboard work and a lite Jackson 5 bounce, placing it in relief against other G-Funk tracks on the soundtrack. The track earned nominations and awards, including a nomination for Best Rap Song at the 2013 Grammys and the 2013 ASCAP Pop Music Awards' Most Performed Songs award. Billboard gave it a 7 out of 10, noting its playful tone and broad appeal to listeners, from devoted stoners to a wider audience. Highsnobiety's David Opie also listed it among the ten most essential rap songs about weed.

Shangri-La at the Fort, Manila, marked its groundbreaking on July 3, 2008, in a ceremony led by President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo. Construction of the hotel began in 2011, and it proceeded toward a soft opening on March 1, 2016.

Shangri-La at The Fort, Manila, also known as Shangri-La The Fort, Manila, is a mixed-use development located in Bonifacio Global City, Fort Bonifacio, Taguig. The complex houses a five-star luxury hotel, event venues, retail space, and upscale residential units. The residential components comprise Shangri-La Residences The Fort, Manila and Horizon Homes, operated by Shang Properties. The property opened on March 1, 2016, and it is one of three hotels managed by Shangri-La Hotels and Resorts in Metro Manila.

In 1997, the company then known as Karhu-Titan changed its name to Karhu Sporting Goods. In 2008, Karhu Sporting Goods sold the Karhu brand to Karhu Holding B.V., a Dutch holding company led by Huub Valkenburg and Jay Duke.

Karhu is a Finnish sports equipment company focused on running, tracing its origins to the brand established as Oy Urheilutarpeita in 1916 and renamed Karhu (Finnish for bear) in 1920. The Finnish origin is reflected in the name, which means bear in Finnish. Its product range includes sneakers, T-shirts, and jackets, and skis were manufactured in earlier periods. In 2008 the company was sold to investors through Karhu Holding B.V., a Netherlands-based entity led by Emanuele Arese. The investors responsible for operations are Huub Valkenburg, a Dutch-American, and the Arese family of Italy.

The Canberra, introduced as a foreign design, encountered political opposition in the United States despite its performance advantages over rival domestic designs, with doubts about production capacity, spare parts supply, and the ability to meet United States Air Force demands. By March 1951, production lines were operating at full capacity to fulfill Royal Air Force orders and other export commitments, addressing many of these questions. English Electric subsequently opened discussions with the Glenn L. Martin Company to license-build the Canberra in the United States, with a plan under which Martin would receive a license to produce the aircraft domestically. Gunston and Gilchrist contend that the Americanization of the Canberra program helped to dismiss much of the political opposition.

The RB-57 Canberra was the dual-control, combat-capable production variant derived from the B-57B. Its first flight occurred on 30 December 1954. A total of 38 aircraft were ordered, with 36 ultimately built. Two examples rolled off the production line were completed as target-towing B-57Es and redesignated accordingly.

During the Last Glacial Maximum, the Patagonian Ice Sheet extended across the southern third of Chile and into adjacent areas of Argentina. On the western side of the Andes, the ice reached sea level as far north as the Chacao Channel at about 41°S. The western Patagonian coast was largely glaciated, though some authors have proposed the existence of ice-free refugia for certain plant species. On the eastern side of the Andes, glacier lobes occupied depressions in Seno Skyring, Seno Otway, Inútil Bay, and Beagle Channel. In the Straits of Magellan, ice extended as far as Segunda Angostura.

During the Last Glacial Maximum, the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation operated at reduced strength and with a shallower vertical extent. This slowdown coincided with cooler conditions in the western subtropical North Atlantic, where sea surface temperatures were about five degrees Celsius lower than in the present. In the intermediate depths of the North Atlantic, water masses were better ventilated during the LGM, primarily due to the Glacial North Atlantic Intermediate Water, in contrast to ventilation by the modern upper North Atlantic Deep Water. The Glacial North Atlantic Intermediate Water possessed relatively low nutrient content compared with the modern upper NADW. Below this intermediate layer, southern-source bottom water—characterized by high nutrient concentrations—dominated the deepest levels of the North Atlantic.

Irreligion in Australia includes scholarly attention such as the 2010 publication The Australian Book of Atheism, described as the first collection to examine atheism from an Australian perspective. The work emerged in response to a perceived gap between the rise of secular outlooks and the increasing political and educational influence and funding of religion within Australia. It brings together contributions from 33 authors, including notable figures such as Leslie Cannold, Robyn Williams, Tim Minchin, Graham Oppy, Philip Nitschke, Ian Hunter, Lyn Allison, Russell Blackford, and Ian Robinson. The essays explore atheism-related topics across historical development, legal contexts, educational issues, philosophy, and neurobiology.

Studies and surveys in Australia have repeatedly shown a sustained decline in regular church attendance, contributing to broader patterns of irreligion. The National Church Life Survey recorded a drop in monthly attendance from about 44% of the population in 1950 to 17% in 2007. A 2009 Christian Research Association survey of 1,718 Australians found that 16% attended a religious service at least once a month, down from 23% in 1993. Some observers suggested the overall rate of decline had moderated in subsequent years; in 2016 reports indicated monthly attendance remained around 16%. A 2013 McCrindle Research survey of Christians found only 8% attended church at least monthly. The same study also identified several reasons given for not attending: 47% said church is irrelevant to their life, 26% did not accept how its teachings are presented, and 19% did not believe the Bible.
Ardagh Group conducted an initial public offering in March 2017, listing its shares on the New York Stock Exchange. The offering raised just over $300 million in proceeds.
As of 2012, Ardagh Group operated 89 facilities in 22 countries, employed roughly 23,500 people, and reported revenues of about €7.7 billion.

Ring laser gyroscopes (RLGs) are employed in inertial guidance systems by circulating two laser beams in opposite directions around a closed optical loop. The loop follows the perimeter of a triangular block of temperature-stable Cervit glass with mirrors mounted at each corner to reflect the beams. When the apparatus rotates, the counter-propagating beams experience different optical path lengths; the beam traveling in the same sense as the rotation effectively traverses a longer path, while the one moving opposite to the rotation takes a shorter path. The consequent phase difference between the two beams arises from this path length disparity, and an interferometer is used to measure the resulting phase shift. This phase change is proportional to the rotation rate, a direct consequence of the Sagnac effect, providing angular-rate information essential for inertial navigation.

An inertial guidance system may employ a hemispherical resonator gyroscope, wherein a standing wave is established inside a hemispherical resonant structure. When the device undergoes rotation, the Coriolis force causes the standing wave to rotate at an angle different from that of the resonator itself. The relative motion between the outer case and the standing wave pattern is proportional to the total rotation angle and can be detected by electronic sensing circuitry. The resonator is typically machined from fused quartz to exploit its favorable mechanical properties, and electrostatic electrodes used to drive and sense the standing waves are deposited directly onto separate quartz structures surrounding the resonator. The gyro can operate in two modes: a whole-angle mode that affords high rate capability, and a force-rebalance mode that enhances accuracy by locking the standing wave orientation to the gyro housing.

The High German consonant shift is a historical phonological development that affected the voiceless stop consonants p, t, and k in German. In Modern Standard German, the original p, t, and k remain unshifted only in limited contexts, specifically after a fricative or within the /tr/ cluster. For example, Stein preserves the unshifted stop after a fricative, and treu retains it in the /tr/ sequence. When describing this pattern, loanwords from Low German and other foreign borrowings are typically excluded, as they do not consistently reflect the standard shift. Nevertheless, borrowings can show unshifted pronunciations, such as Park, borrowed from the French parc, and Pferch, a German doublet derived from Latin parricus, illustrating how non-native terms may diverge from the core pattern.

The High German consonant shift, also referred to as the second Germanic consonant shift, is a historical phonological development observed in the southern West Germanic dialects. It serves to distinguish High German from other continental West Germanic languages, notably Low Franconian (Dutch) and Low German, which did not undergo the shift. The shift primarily involves the affrication or spirantization of the voiceless stops /t/, /p/, and /k/, with the realized sound depending on the consonant’s position within a word. A related phenomenon is the de-voicing of the voiced stops /d/, /b/, and /g/, though this de-voicing is less widespread, with /d/ being de-voiced in most dialects.

Freei’s remaining workforce was laid off on October 16, 2000, after which its corporate headquarters in Federal Way, Washington, was permanently closed. In early November 2000, the company’s remaining assets were sold at auction.

Freei Networks, Inc. operated as a free Internet service provider from 1998 to 2000, commonly known as Freei.net and FreeInternet.com. In 2000, FreeInternet.com was acquired by United Online, Inc., a company also responsible for NetZero, Juno, Classmates.com, and other online services. Eight years later, in 2008, United Online relaunched FreeInternet.com as a site dedicated to free and discounted retail offers.

The 2020 Group is a United Kingdom–based think tank whose stated aim links the pursuit of enterprise and innovation with addressing deep-seated welfare dependence and social inequality. It promotes an Enterprise Economy paired with greater social mobility, arguing that advances in technology and entrepreneurship can create new opportunities to tackle these challenges. The organization also rejects the orthodoxies of both the traditional left and the traditional right in seeking solutions for the current generation.

The 2020 Group was described by journalist Michael Crick as a Cameron-aligned supporters group during David Cameron's prime ministership. It was reported that the group planned to establish a website to challenge Conservative Home.

Concept programming is a paradigm in which the programmer can tailor a language’s syntax and semantics to suit specific tasks. In this approach, the XL system exemplifies programmer-reconfigurable syntax and semantics, with compiler plug-ins capable of introducing new features into the language without altering the core implementation. A foundational set of plug-ins provides a relatively standard imperative language, giving users a ready-made baseline while still allowing extension. Developers can also create plug-ins that express domain-specific notations, such as symbolic differentiation, enabling specialized representations and operations within the same framework. Because these plug-ins integrate with the language as readily as built-in constructs, they can be used interchangeably with native features to customize both the syntax and the semantics used in programs.

Concept programming is a methodology associated with the XL programming language. Designed by Dinechin, XL underpins this approach by leveraging the language’s features to model concepts and their interactions in a flexible, extensible manner. The acronym XL stands for eXtensible Language, highlighting the emphasis on adaptable and reusable programming constructs.

ISO 2921 describes a method for determining the temperature at which a rubber specimen, held under tension, retracts as it is warmed after being cooled under load. In the procedure, a tension is applied to the sample and it is cooled until it ceases to retract. It is then gradually heated, and the temperature at which the specimen shrinks back to the specified dimensions is recorded. The test is conducted with the sample placed in a fluid bath to control the environment, although gases may be used if they do not affect the result.

ISO 2921 is an international standard that prescribes a method for determining the temperature-retraction characteristics of stretched vulcanized rubber. The procedure evaluates how a rubber specimen, held under initial elongation, retracts as temperature changes, providing a measure of its performance under thermal conditions. The scope does not extend to many thermoplastic elastomers, which often exhibit a yield point at relatively low elongations—approximately 5% to 20%—placing them outside the test conditions defined by the standard.

Circumesophageal nerve ring, also termed circumpharyngeal nerve ring, denotes an arrangement of nerve ganglia arranged around the esophagus or pharynx. It is common in nematodes, molluscs, and numerous other invertebrate groups, while it is absent in all vertebrate animals. The formation is not structurally possible in simpler organisms such as tardigrades (water bears).

The circumesophageal nerve ring consists of a dorsal cerebral ganglion positioned above the esophagus and a ventral subesophageal ganglion situated below it; these two ganglia are linked by commissures, forming a continuous ring that encircles the esophagus.

During the early modern period, Barcelona ceded political primacy yet sustained a balanced economy that combined local production with imports. Catalonia’s broader post-crisis recovery in the latter half of the 17th century coincided with a surge in the city’s maritime activity, with port traffic more than doubling by 1675 compared with the beginning of the century. In the late 17th and early 18th centuries, the city endured a series of wars, including a bombing in 1691 and sieges in 1697, 1704–1706, the 1713 blockade, and the 1714 siege and assault. The 18th century saw rapid population growth, rising from about 30,000 to around 100,000 inhabitants, and Barcelona emerged as a leading Western Mediterranean mercantile center, extending its inland influence to Zaragoza and its southern reach to Alicante. A fortress was constructed on Montjuïc to overlook the harbor. Although the Napoleonic wars adversely affected much of Barcelona, the beginning of industrialization gradually improved the fortunes of the province.

Barcelona's local public transport network comprises the metro, bus system, regional rail, tram lines, and funiculars, along with rack railways, gondola lifts, and aerial cable cars. The various networks are operated by multiple operators. All components are integrated under a coordinated fare system administered by the Autoritat del Transport Metropolità (ATM). The fare structure is divided into six zones, numbered from 1 to 6. A range of Integrated Travel Cards is available for use across the network.

Parts of the 2018 biographical drama Red Joan were filmed at the University of Cambridge. In the film, the fictional Joan Smith, played by Judi Dench, is depicted as studying physics at Cambridge. The character of Joan Smith is loosely inspired by Melita Norwood.

Opened in August 2013, the University of Cambridge Sports Centre was constructed in a series of phases. The initial phase provisioned a sports hall, a fitness suite, a strength and conditioning room, a multi-purpose room, and courts for Eton and Rugby fives. In the subsequent phase, five squash courts with glass backs and a team training room were introduced. Plans for future phases envisage the addition of indoor and outdoor tennis facilities as well as a swimming pool.

In 2001, Roger Linn established the company Roger Linn Design. The venture’s inaugural product was the AdrenaLinn, and subsequent development led to the LinnStrument, a music performance controller, being introduced later.

Roger Linn, with Alex Moffett, founded Linn Moffett Electronics in 1979, a venture later renamed Linn Electronics, to pursue Linn’sConcept for a sampling-based drum machine. The resulting instrument was the LM-1, an acronym derived from Linn, Moffett, and the unit number. Moffett departed the company in 1982. Beyond development, Linn used the LM-1 in performances, including a collaboration with Leon Russell on the 1979 album Life and Love.

ArXiv derives its name from a naming session conducted by its founder, Paul Ginsparg, together with his wife. When the straightforward domain for “archive” was already claimed, he reworked the term by substituting the Greek letter chi with the letter X and dropping the final e to achieve symmetry around the X, yielding the final form ArXiv.

ArXiv is a free online repository for scholarly preprints across a range of disciplines, notably physics, mathematics, and computer science. In some cases, the works are copyrighted by publishers, but authors retain the right to distribute their manuscripts, and they grant arXiv a non-exclusive irrevocable license to disseminate the material through the arXiv platform.

The 1941 film The Shepherd of the Hills centers on Daniel Howitt, who assists his new neighbors and, in recognition of his benevolent acts, earns a nickname associated with his protective presence on the hills. Through these deeds, Howitt also forms a friendship with Young Matt, underscoring themes of community and mutual support in the story.

The Shepherd of the Hills (1941 film) tells the story of Daniel Howitt, an elderly, educated stranger who arrives from the city and purchases a tract of land known as Moanin' Meadow. The land had previously belonged to Young Matt's mother and is the site where she is buried, a fact that intensifies the emotional stakes of the sale. Young Matt objects to the purchase because of the land's association with his mother and her grave. Complicating matters, locals regard Moanin' Meadow as cursed and haunted, a belief that colors the community's response to the land and its new owner.

An expansion tank is a standard component in many domestic hydronic heating and cooling systems. It functions to buffer pressure changes that arise from the expansion and contraction of the water used for heat transfer, thereby accommodating the associated volume changes within the system.

An expansion tank is a plumbing component installed in closed domestic water heating and supply systems to absorb the effects of thermal expansion. Historically, domestic plumbing systems contained more trapped air, which served as a crude buffer against pressure changes arising from heating and expansion. In modern or upgraded installations, expansion tanks are designed into systems and installed more frequently than in the past, reflecting a shift toward formalized expansion management.
Seattle Eagle is the oldest leather bar in Seattle. It draws a young and relatively diverse clientele, and by 2003 the venue offered theme nights such as Underbear, Vibrator, and Western.

Matt Baume of The Stranger described the experience of being at the Seattle Eagle during daylight as producing an unusual atmosphere, as if the venue were meant to be shrouded in perpetual darkness. He compared the scene to Gotham City, invoking imagery of Batman in a shadowy corner with a suggestive nod to Burt Ward, and concluded that the moment produces an audible squeak.

Rooted in the teachings of Caspar Schwenckfeld, the Schwenkfeldian tradition has preserved his emphasis on inner spirituality over outward form dating from the sixteenth century. In the twentieth century, these beliefs culminated in the formal establishment of the Schwenkfelder Church. The church's formation reflected Schwenckfeld's advocacy for a fellowship of all believers and for a single church.

The Society of the Descendants of the Schwenkfeldian Exiles is a lineage organization for the descendants of 209 members of the Schwenkfelder Church who arrived near Penn's Landing between 1731 and 1737 and subsequently settled in the colonial Province of Pennsylvania. The society was founded in 1921 by William Wagener Porter, with an initial membership of 125 individuals. Its publications have included Exile Herald (1924–1954) and Der Bericht.

Jean-François Thiriart was a member of the small pan-European European Liberation Front who spent extensive periods in Russia, where he developed his views on the prospects of European nationalism. He saw potential for a rapid surge in European nationalist sentiment and promoted a pan-European political project aimed at uniting disparate nationalist currents. In addition to his organizational activity, Thiriart was an author, producing several books that articulated his theoretical and strategic perspectives on Europe.

Jean-François Thiriart shifted his ideological orientation toward National Bolshevism, integrating nationalist and socialist-influenced ideas. In his later years, he maintained close collaboration with prominent exponents of National Bolshevism, among them Aleksandr Dugin, reflecting enduring ties within that ideological current.

The Commercial Appeal won the 1923 Pulitzer Prize for Public Service for its opposition to the Ku Klux Klan's operations in the region. In 1994, the newspaper earned a Pulitzer Prize for Editorial Cartooning for work by Michael Ramirez.

In the fall of 2007, The Commercial Appeal explored native advertising by attempting to pair select stories with paying advertisers in the form of advertorials. The initiative drew sharp criticism from media analysts. The concept was laid out in a memo on monetization authored by the newspaper’s editor and its sales manager. The authors subsequently withdrew the proposal quietly.

Britain operated Armed Merchant Cruisers (AMCs) during World War I and World War II. Typically created by converting passenger liners, AMCs were larger than their German merchant-raider counterparts. They served prominently in convoy escort roles, and generally did not disguise their own identities. A notable engagement involving an AMC occurred when the Carmania sank the German raider SMS Cap Trafalgar, a vessel that had been altered to resemble Carmania.

During World War I, the British Royal Navy employed Q-ships as a response to the German U-boat threat. These vessels operated covertly as ordinary merchant ships while concealing armament, with the aim of drawing submarines into attacking them and then surfacing to unleash their hidden weapons. This tactic marked a strategic shift from traditional raiding, which aimed to disrupt enemy trade, because Q-ships sought to destroy enemy warships rather than merely target commercial shipping.

Microsoft relocated its headquarters from Bellevue to Redmond in January 1985, selecting a 29-acre site to be developed by Wright Runstad & Company. Construction on the new campus commenced on August 9, 1985, and the company moved into the $25 million facility on February 26, 1986. The relocation occurred just weeks before the company’s initial public offering and drew attention to traffic concerns on the unfinished State Route 520 corridor between Bellevue and Redmond. To better serve the campus, a new freeway interchange at Northeast 40th Street was built in 2000, a project that followed lobbying and partial funding by Microsoft.

In February 2015, the City of Redmond approved a zoning rezone that raised the campus building height limit from six to ten stories, enabling taller structures as part of the redevelopment tied to an agreement with the city. Later that year, The Seattle Times reported in September 2015 that Microsoft had engaged Skidmore, Owings & Merrill to commence a multibillion-dollar redesign of its Redmond campus. The planned redesign would add about 1.4 million square feet (roughly 130,000 square meters) of new development, permitted by the city agreement accompanying the height increase.

Resynthesizer is a plug-in for the GNU Image Manipulation Program (GIMP) that provides content-aware fill capabilities. It originated in Paul Harrison's doctoral research and is now maintained by Lloyd Konneker.

GIMP version 2.8 offered only eight-bit color per channel, a limitation that left its color depth substantially lower than the 12-bit or higher precision commonly used by most digital cameras. The following release, GIMP 2.10, added full support for high bit-depth color, enhancing accuracy for professional workflows. In addition, OpenCL-enabled hardware acceleration was introduced for a subset of tasks, leveraging compatible devices to improve performance.

Alar Karis (born 26 March 1958) is an Estonian politician and scientist who serves as the sixth president of Estonia, having taken office on 11 October 2021. His background encompasses work as a molecular geneticist and a developmental biologist, and he has held several positions within the Estonian civil service.

Alar Karis graduated from the Estonian Agricultural Academy in Tartu in 1981, an institution that is today the Estonian University of Life Sciences. In 1999, he was appointed as a professor at the University of Tartu.

During the Soviet period, the Ukrainian Insurgent Army was officially banned and its activities were denounced as terrorist in character. After Ukraine gained independence in 1991, debates emerged about whether former UPA members should be recognized as legitimate military veterans and eligible for war pensions and related benefits. UPA veterans have pursued public commemorations and annual parades, with the strongest participation reported in western Ukraine. These efforts have provoked opposition from veterans of the Soviet Army and from some Ukrainian politicians, particularly in the southern and eastern regions.

The Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA) was a decentralized resistance movement that operated widely across Ukrainian territory. It was organized into three operational regions, each pursuing a somewhat different agenda in response to local conditions. The regional differences reflected the evolving front lines and the dual threats posed by Soviet and Nazi forces during World War II. Additionally, not all UPA fighters were members of the Organization of Ukrainian Nationalists (OUN) or shared the OUN’s political ideology.

Loncong is a Malayic language within the Austronesian language family. It is one of the native languages spoken by the Orang Laut, the Sea People, who inhabit the Bangka and Belitung Islands in Indonesia. Some linguists have proposed that Loncong may consist of two distinct language varieties rather than a single language.

According to Anderbeck, the Orang Laut constitutes a genetically related group of languages. Within this grouping, three subgroups are recognized: Kedah, Riau, and Sekak. By contrast, the Malayic language Duano is divergent and not included in the Orang Laut grouping.

Louis-Charles de Flers, a French general of division, assumed command of the Army of the Eastern Pyrenees on 14 May as the War of the Pyrenees began unfavorably for France. The conflict opened badly when the Spanish Army of Catalonia, commanded by Captain General Antonio Ricardos, crossed into French territory on 17 April with approximately 4,500 troops, rapidly routing the 400-strong garrison at Saint-Laurent-de-Cerdans. Three days later, Ricardos’s forces defeated about 1,800 French defenders at Céret. French losses at Céret were reported as between 100 and 200 killed, wounded, or missing, with 200 soldiers drowned in the Tech River, while Ricardos claimed Spanish losses of only 17 wounded.

Louis-Charles de Flers was a French general who commanded during the defense of Bellegarde, a fortress guarding the Le Perthus pass at about 300 metres above sea level on the main road between Barcelona and Perpignan. He attempted to relieve the garrison but was unsuccessful. An additional effort involved about 3,350 men attempting to escort a supply convoy through the siege lines on 29 May, which also failed. While the Spanish army remained focused on the siege, de Flers conducted operations that drove an enemy force away from the port of Collioure. The Siege of Bellegarde ended with a French surrender on 24 June.

Observations of stellar proper motions in the Galactic center have revealed the presence of a supermassive black hole at the core of the Milky Way. The reality of this black hole has since been confirmed. It is designated Sgr A* and has an estimated mass of about 4.3 × 10^6 solar masses (M☉).

Proper motion, in its secondary lexical sense, arises from an older meaning of the adjective proper as belonging to or owned, a usage still seen in phrases such as the city itself. The term improper motion, by contrast, denotes perceived movement that does not stem from the object's own intrinsic trajectory. Such apparent motion can result from external factors, including the Earth's axial precession and small irregularities known as nutations, which are minor deviations within the approximately 26,000-year precession cycle.

Granules in cell biology are distinguished by whether they are enclosed within a membrane, resulting in two principal categories: membrane-bound granules and non-membrane-bound granules. The membrane-bound category contains eosinophilic granules, basophilic granules, and secretory granules. Conversely, the non-membrane-bound category comprises P-granules and stress granules.

Platelets contain small organelles including lysosomes and peroxisomes, with roughly one to three lysosomes and peroxisomes per platelet; the precise platelet-specific functions of these organelles remain unclear. Lysosomal exocytosis in platelets is typically evaluated by estimating released lysosomal enzymes, such as beta-hexosaminidase. A proposed electron-dense granule, defined by the presence of Toll-like receptor 9 (TLR9) and protein disulfide isomerase (PDI) and referred to as the T granule, has been described, though its existence is controversial. Furthermore, protein disulfide isomerase and other platelet-borne thiol isomerases are packaged within a non-granular compartment derived from the megakaryocyte endoplasmic reticulum, which may be associated with the dense tubular system.

During the Revolution of the King and the People, Mohammed V, speaking from Paris, pledged reforms aimed at steering Morocco toward a democratic state founded on a constitutional monarchy. The following Friday, Muslims gathered in mosques to hear Mohammed V deliver his sermon. In Rabat, the national council of Moroccan rabbis met and issued a declaration of joy in response to these developments.

The Revolution of the King and the People refers to a phase of Moroccan nationalist mobilization triggered by the assassination of Farhat Hached by La Main Rouge, the clandestine wing of France’s external intelligence service. The incident sparked protests worldwide and culminated in the Casablanca riots on 7–8 December 1952, with significant demonstrations in the bidonville Carrières Centrales in Hay Mohammadi; the violence left approximately one hundred people dead. These events were aided by a transnational support network established by Moroccan nationalists, which included diplomats and intelligence operatives providing information and strategic backing. The activities of this network helped shape both local and international perceptions of the Moroccan independence movement.

Boholano refers to the people of Bohol, a province in the Philippines. The name Bohol is derived from the native word Bo-ol. Historically, Bohol was the site of what is regarded as the earliest international accord of peace and unity between the local ruler Datu Sikatuna and the Spanish conquistador Miguel López de Legazpi, concluded on March 16, 1565. The agreement is popularly known as the Sandugo, a blood-compact alliance.

The Boholano people are an indigenous community from the island province of Bohol in the Philippines, believed to be descendants of the last group of inhabitants in the archipelago, historically known as pintados or the “tattooed ones.” Their culture is considered established, with archaeological finds illustrating their heritage through artifacts unearthed at Mansasa in Tagbilaran City and at sites in Dauis and Panglao.

Night diver is a recreational scuba certification level that encompasses the skills necessary for diving in natural darkness between sunset and sunrise. Night diving requires the use of artificial light.

The concept of a dive leader establishes the minimum training and certification requirements for recreational scuba divers in accordance with international standards such as ISO 24801-3 and EN 14153-3. Recreational dive leaders are deemed competent to plan, organize, and conduct dives and to supervise other recreational divers on open-water excursions, including specialized activities for which they have received training. They are also capable of performing emergency procedures relevant to these activities and the surrounding diving environment, though they may require orientation when faced with unfamiliar local conditions. Further advancement to lead more demanding dives necessitates additional specialized training and experience. The designation is used by BSAC to denote a specific certification, and many organizations offer training that conforms to the dive leader standard under various titles, including Dive Leader, Divemaster, and Dive Supervisor, with the latter identifying a role distinct from that of a professional diving supervisor. CMAS-affiliated certifications that meet CMAS three-star diver requirements are generally expected to satisfy the standard by default.

The play clock is the regulatory interval within which the offense must snap the ball. In college football before 2008, a 25-second clock ran after the ball was set, and the clock was not stopped to facilitate ball placement unless the preceding play ended with a stoppage. From 2008 onward, college football adopted an NFL-like play-clock system, with only minor differences in the final two minutes of each half. Beginning in 2019, high school football aligned with the NCAA and NFL standards by adopting a 40-second play clock, subject to small regional exceptions. Professional leagues have varied, with the original XFL and the Alliance of American Football using a 35-second clock to speed up play, while the revived XFL implemented a 25-second clock measured from the spot of the ball, and arena football has utilized a 35-second play clock.

In gridiron football, the play clock is a timer that governs the interval between successive plays, and teams frequently employ clock management to slow the game by maximizing the time between snaps. A common tactic is to snap the ball with only one second remaining on the play clock, effectively delaying the offense’s cadence and leaving little margin for error. Another frequent method is to call a timeout to stop the clock, a strategy especially common in the closing minute of the second and fourth quarters before a field goal attempt. Officials, with the referee typically standing near the offense’s sideline, the quarterback, or the coaching staff, verify the maximum time that may elapse before a delay of game is assessed. When a timeout is signaled, the play clock is immediately whistled dead.

Rocket Lab is developing Neutron, a larger reusable launch vehicle built around an integrated, single-structure design, as of 2024. The Neutron program includes multiple spacecraft bus architectures, reflecting a modular approach to payload platforms. A family of engines is under development for Neutron, including Rutherford, Curie, HyperCurie, and Archimedes. In mid-2024, Neutron progressed into the engine-testing phase of its development.

Rocket Lab expanded its manufacturing and space-systems capabilities through a series of acquisitions that established new facilities across North America and Australasia. The acquisition of SolAero yielded facilities in Albuquerque, New Mexico; the purchase of ASI added operations in Littleton, Colorado; the acquisition of Planetary Systems Corporation established a presence in Maryland; and the acquisition of Sinclair Interplanetary created a facility in Toronto, Canada. In September 2021, Rocket Lab opened a new production line in Auckland to augment reaction wheel production, with capacity up to 2,000 units per year for an undisclosed mega-constellation customer.

The 10th Mountain Division’s operations in Somalia contributed to ending the food emergency and diminishing factional fighting in the region. It supplied infantry for the United Nations quick-reaction force during the Battle of Mogadishu to assist in rescuing Task Force Ranger and the SAR team. Two division soldiers were killed during the engagement, which represented the longest sustained firefight by regular U.S. Army forces since the Vietnam War. Beginning in February 1994, the division initiated a gradual drawdown of its forces in Somalia, with the last soldiers of the 2nd Battalion, 22nd Infantry returning in March 1994.

In 2002, David Hackworth, a columnist and decorated veteran, criticized the 10th Mountain Division as ill-prepared for combat. He cited several contributing factors, including insufficient training, poor physical conditioning, leadership that was not adequately prepared, and low morale. Hackworth concluded that the division no longer possessed the capacity to conduct mountain warfare.

During the first session of Saddam Hussein's trial, the hearing lasted about three hours before the court adjourned the case to 28 November 2005. The adjournment was attributed to witnesses being too frightened to attend and to the defense needing additional time to study the evidence. Following the opening, Saddam's eldest daughter, Raghad Hussein, gave an interview to Al Arabiya in which she criticized the court as a farce and described her father's demeanor as exhibiting strong, lion-like poise during proceedings, stating that he would remain formidable even in confinement and that those who know him recognize his firmness and power.

On 30 December 2006, Saddam Hussein was executed by hanging after being convicted of crimes against humanity for the 1982 killings of 148 Shi'ites in Dujail. The execution occurred on Eid al-Adha, the first day of the Islamic holiday, at approximately 06:05 local time (03:05 UTC) at Camp Justice, an Iraqi Army base in Kazimain, northeast Baghdad.

Apache Camel is complemented by an Eclipse-based graphical tooling suite freely available from Red Hat, which offers graphical editing capabilities, integrated debugging support, and advanced validation to help users design, test, and verify Camel routes and configurations.

Apache Camel is an open-source integration framework for message-oriented middleware. It employs a rule-based routing and mediation engine to implement the Enterprise Integration Patterns (EIPs), with these patterns realized through Java objects. The framework provides an API that includes a declarative Java domain-specific language for configuring routing and mediation rules.

John L. Heilbron was born in San Francisco on March 17, 1934. He attended Lowell High School, where he participated in the Lowell Forensic Society. Heilbron earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in physics in 1955 and a Master of Arts in physics in 1958, followed by a Ph.D. in history in 1964, all from the University of California, Berkeley. In the 1960s, he studied under Thomas Kuhn as a graduate student while Kuhn was composing The Structure of Scientific Revolutions.

John Lewis Heilbron (March 17, 1934 – November 5, 2023) was an American historian of science whose scholarship focused on the history of physics and astronomy. He served as a professor of history at the University of California, Berkeley, and held the position of vice-chancellor from 1990 to 1994, later attaining emeritus status as vice-chancellor. Heilbron was a senior research fellow at Worcester College, Oxford, and his career included visiting professorships at Yale University and the California Institute of Technology. In addition to his teaching and research, he edited the journal Historical Studies in the Physical and Biological Sciences for twenty-five years.

Albert Abramson credits A. A. Polumordvinov with inventing the first field-sequential color system, a claim supported by Polumordvinov’s 1899 Russian patent application (No. 10738). Polumordvinov’s approach employed two rotating cylinders to scan images in sequential color fields. Later, A. Frankenstein and Werner von Jaworski described another field-sequential configuration in a German patent, culminating in the Frankenstein–Jaworski patent filed in 1904 as German patent No. 172376, which, like the CBS System, incorporated a color wheel.

Field-sequential color systems, as implemented in DLP projectors, rely on a color wheel to generate color images by sequentially displaying different colors. The wheels typically run at a speed that is a multiple of the video frame rate, reflecting synchronization between wheel rotation and frame timing.

The Coase theorem posits that, when property rights over pollution are clearly defined and transaction costs are negligible, the distribution of those rights shapes parties’ incentives to reveal or distort information about the costs and benefits of pollution. If the rights to pollute are owned by the polluter, the holder may overstate the benefits of emitting; if the rights are owned by the victims, the affected party may misrepresent the damages suffered. In practice, however, negotiations over externalities occur under incomplete information, and under such conditions Coasean bargaining is unlikely to achieve the efficient outcome predicted by the theorem, leading to an inefficient allocation.

The Coase theorem addresses how externalities can be resolved through private bargaining, but its practical relevance hinges on transaction costs and the initial allocation of property rights. Coase argued that when bargaining costs are negligible, efficient outcomes can emerge regardless of initial rights, yet in the real world transaction costs are significant, making the initial allocation often important; this distinction was clarified in The Problem of Social Cost (1960) and has been cited in discussions surrounding his Nobel Prize in 1991. A normative implication derived from the analysis is that liability should initially be assigned to the party for whom avoiding the externality costs is least costly. Nevertheless, real-world challenges temper this claim: nobody can know ex ante which use of a resource will be valued most highly, and government reallocations entail their own costs. A refined normative conclusion thus contends that government should establish institutions that minimize transaction costs, enabling misallocations to be corrected at relatively low expense.

Alex O'Brien is a former professional tennis player who specialized in doubles, winning 13 doubles titles. Alongside Sébastien Lareau, he captured the 1999 US Open doubles title, a Grand Slam championship, and the 1999 ATP Doubles Championships, the season-ending event. O'Brien and Lareau also reached the doubles final at the Australian Open in 1996 and 1997.

Alex O'Brien is an American former professional tennis player who represented the United States on the Davis Cup team. He competed at the 2000 Summer Olympics in Sydney. While at Stanford University, O'Brien was a four-time All-American and in 1992 captured NCAA championships in both singles and doubles, as well as contributing to Stanford's team title that year. He earned a Bachelor of Arts degree in American Studies from Stanford in 1992.

In January 2008, Netscape announced the transfer of stewardship for the RSS 0.9 and RSS 0.91 specifications, along with their DTDs and related documentation, to the RSS Advisory Board. The materials had been published since their inception in 1999. The move entailed shifting custodianship from Netscape to the RSS Advisory Board, establishing the board as the responsible stewards of these early RSS specifications.

In January 2006, Rogers Cadenhead announced that eight new members had joined the RSS Advisory Board to continue RSS development and resolve ambiguities in the RSS 2.0 specification. In March 2007, Netscape developer Christopher Finke joined the board, marking Netscape's first involvement in RSS since the publication of RSS 0.91.

In computing, a handle is an abstract reference used to access a resource. It can be represented in various forms, acting as an opaque identifier rather than the resource itself. A common illustration is a file handle, such as the FILE data structure used in the C standard I/O library. File handles provide an abstraction of the file's contents, decoupling the program from the details of storage. Typically, a handle denotes both the resource to which it refers and a current position within that resource—for example, when performing locking operations or reading data from a particular offset.

Pointers represent the most fundamental type of reference in computing. Their power and efficiency stem from their close ties to hardware, but this advantage requires programmers to have a solid grasp of memory architecture. Pointers store memory addresses rather than the actual data values. Misuse of pointers can lead to undefined behavior, including the creation of dangling or wild pointers. Smart pointers are opaque data structures that behave like pointers while being accessed exclusively through designated methods.

ISO/IEC 17024, in its framework for personnel certification bodies, includes a dedicated section on records and information management. This portion sets out the retention, access, and handling requirements for records related to applicants, candidates, and certified individuals, clarifying which information must be publicly disclosed and which must remain confidential. It also specifies criteria for information security practices governing certification materials, such as examination papers, to safeguard against unauthorized access and uphold the integrity of the certification process. Taken together, these provisions aim to ensure appropriate transparency while protecting sensitive data and maintaining the security of information within personnel certification programs.

ISO/IEC 17024 has undergone terminology updates, notably renaming the term “personnel certification body” to “certification body for persons.” The revision also introduces new definitions for several terms, including validity and reliability, to clarify key concepts used in the standard. In addition, a new Principals section was added to articulate the foundational principles that guide the standard’s framework and interpretation.

The Dwarves are an American punk rock group noted for provocative onstage conduct, including self-mutilation, sexual acts performed during performances, and hard drug use. Their live shows typically lasted about 15 minutes and were occasionally cut short due to injuries sustained by audience members. Musically, the band evolved from early garage-leaning roots, with their second LP, Toolin' for a Warm Teabag (nine minutes), drifting toward a truculent punk rock sound influenced by GG Allin. In 1999 Recess Records released Free Cocaine 86–88, a 39-track compilation illustrating the group’s transition to a nihilistic style that preceded the Sub Pop era. Blood Guts & Pussy, issued on Sub Pop in 1990, signaled a move away from psychedelic sensibilities toward hardcore punk. Subsequently, in 1991 the band released Lucifer's Crank (EP) on No.6 Records and the Sub Pop LP Thank Heaven For Little Girls, described as metal-punk.

The Dwarves' frontman Blag Dahlia has given occasional solo acoustic performances, describing the format as embodying a camp counselor persona. In 1995, he issued a bluegrass-oriented album titled Blackgrass, released under the alias Earl Lee Grace.

Louis Even (March 23, 1885 – September 27, 1974) was a lay Christian leader and publisher who founded the social credit movement in Quebec. He co-founded and led the Pilgrims of Saint Michael, a Catholic lay movement known for its white berets, alongside Gilberte Côté-Mercier. He also established the Union of Electors, which later served as a predecessor to Réal Caouette's Ralliement créditiste.
In the 1940 federal election, Louis Even contested the Lake St-John—Roberval riding as a candidate for the New Democracy party, finishing in third place and earning over 3,000 votes.

Death Canyon is a valley located within Grand Teton National Park in Wyoming, United States. It was formed by glacial action, with the ice retreating about 15,000 years ago after the last glacial maximum, leaving a characteristic U-shaped valley. The trailhead is positioned on a side road off Moose-Wilson Road, approximately 5 miles (8.0 km) from park headquarters in Moose, Wyoming. Phelps Lake lies at the base of the canyon, a basin created by glacial activity. The Death Canyon Trail climbs toward Fox Creek Pass, and beyond the pass hikers may traverse the Death Canyon Shelf, a relatively narrow and level plateau. The canyon supports stands of Whitebark Pine, especially near the tree line.
