A historic feature in the area is the Death Canyon Barn, located at the junction with the Alaska Basin trails; it was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1998.

The Recording Industry of South Africa (RISA) announced on 2 September 2021 the launch of The Official South African Charts (TOSAC). The charting framework comprises two top-100 streaming charts: a South African artist–focused ranking that includes tracks by South African artists or those featuring at least one South African artist, and a combined top-100 chart that covers both international and local songs. TOSAC’s streaming data are collected from major platforms, including Spotify, Apple Music, and Deezer, to determine the rankings.

The Recording Industry of South Africa (RiSA) administers certification thresholds for several product formats, applying standardized sales milestones to recognize achievement. For multi-box audio sets (three or more units per box), Gold certification is awarded at 12,500 units and Platinum at 25,000 units. For music videos, RiSA assigns Gold at 5,000 units and Platinum at 10,000 units. For DVD releases, Gold certification is granted at 10,000 units and Platinum at 20,000 units, reflecting distinct thresholds across formats.

The National Science and Media Museum houses Pictureville Cinema, which opened in 1992 and has been described by film producer David Puttnam as among the world’s premier cinemas. The venue screens a broad range of formats and genres, from 70 mm films to contemporary video, and covers productions from Hollywood to Bollywood, as well as silent cinema to digital sound, holding THX and Dolby EX presentation certifications. In 2008, Pictureville hosted the only publicly recorded screening of Danny Boyle’s 2002 film Alien Love Triangle.

Wonderlab is a gallery within the National Science and Media Museum that explores light and sound through hands-on exhibits and live experiments. The facility opened in 2016, replacing the former Experience TV gallery.

Calendar, Apple's personal calendar application, was formerly known as iCal before the introduction of OS X Mountain Lion. It began as a free download for Mac OS X v10.2 on September 10, 2002, and later was bundled with OS X as iCal 1.5 with Mac OS X v10.3. The program enables users to track their events and appointments and displays holidays based on the device’s location, as well as birthdays drawn from the user’s Contacts. It also supports subscribing to calendars shared by friends or third parties, allowing calendar data to be kept in sync with external sources.

The Home app is a smart-home management application released by Apple as part of macOS 10.14 Mojave. It functions as the front-end for Apple's HomeKit framework, offering a single interface to configure, communicate with, and control HomeKit-enabled devices. Devices can be organized into separate rooms to improve organization and navigation. The app also supports sharing access to home controls with other users, enabling collaborative management of the smart-home setup.

Batuque sessions are typically organized around a group of performers who gather in a circle, with the participants predominantly women. This circular formation is known as terreru, pronounced teˈʀeɾu. The terreru is not tied to a precise location and may be held in places as varied as a backyard or a public square.

During the second movement, the ensemble sustains the rhythmic pattern while singing in unison, even as the dancer transitions to a different form of dance. This newly adopted style is known as da ku tornu (phonetic: dɐ ku ˈtoɾnu). Da ku tornu is defined by a pronounced hip swing, produced through rapid knee flexion, a movement that accompanies the rhythm throughout the section.

Asian Theatre Journal is published biannually, with issues issued in March and September. The first electronic edition appeared in 2000 on Project MUSE. JSTOR provides access to back volumes through its electronic archive, with volumes up to three years behind the current issue available.

Asian Theatre Journal, founded in 1984 by James R. Brandon of the University of Hawaii, functions as the official publication of the Association for Asian Performance, an organization affiliated with the Association for Theatre in Higher Education. The journal is published by University of Hawaii Press. In 1992 editorial leadership passed to Samuel L. Leiter of Brooklyn College, who introduced the practice of featuring a translated play in every issue. From 2005 to 2018, Kathy Foley of the University of California, Santa Cruz, served as editor, followed by Siyuan Liu of the University of British Columbia, who remained at the helm until September 2025. The current editor is Dr. Man He.

In the American animated series Big Mouth, Lola Ugfuglio Skumpy is depicted as a hot-tempered yet popular girl who is anxious about preserving her social standing and winning the approval of her best friend Devin. In season four she enters into a relationship with Jay, a romance that ends badly. In the following season, the relationship remains unstable, alternating between moments of reconciliation and distance as the pair stays intermittently involved.

Season three of Big Mouth received strong reviews on Rotten Tomatoes, with an approval rating of 97% from 33 reviews and an average score of 8.0/10. The Rotten Tomatoes critics consensus states that, much like its central characters, the season broadens its scope by addressing intricate new themes with a blend of crude humor and genuine empathy that has defined the series from the start. On Metacritic, season three earned a score of 84 out of 100, based on five critics.

Ashley Seaver is a fictional FBI agent who joins the Behavioral Analysis Unit (BAU) as a replacement for Jennifer Jareau after Jareau accepts a promotion at the Pentagon. Seaver is selected for her distinctive background, notably being the daughter of Charles Beauchamp, the serial killer known as the Redmond Ripper who murdered dozens of women before his capture by the BAU. Unit Chief Aaron Hotchner initially envisions her as a special one-time consultant to the BAU. SSA David Rossi intervenes and allows her to complete remedial training with the team under SSA Emily Prentiss. In the season six episode "...With Friends Like These," she graduates from the academy and becomes a probationary agent on the team. In the season seven premiere "It Takes a Village," Jennifer Jareau reveals to Emily that Ashley has transferred to the domestic trafficking task force led by Andi Swann.

Criminal Minds centers on the FBI's Behavioral Analysis Unit as its analysts and investigators pursue violent offenders by developing psychological profiles. Unit Chief supervision is initially provided by Aaron Hotchner, with Emily Prentiss later succeeding him. Jason Gideon is presented as the founder of the BAU and a renowned profiler. The team comprises Derek Morgan, a former Chicago Police officer specializing in obsessional crimes; Spencer Reid, an expert in geographic profiling; Jennifer Jareau, often referred to as JJ, who begins as the unit's communications liaison and later becomes a profiler; Elle Greenaway, an expert on sex crimes; David Rossi, one of the original BAU agents and an authority on criminal profiling; Ashley Seaver, a rookie FBI agent; Alex Blake, a linguistics specialist who assists with language-related communication; Kate Callahan, a seasoned undercover agent; Tara Lewis, a forensic psychologist; Luke Alvez, a top fugitive tracker who eventually joins the ranks as a profiler; Stephen Walker, an expert in counterintelligence; and Matt Simmons, a profiler who joins from the FBI's International Response Team.

Sue Desmond-Hellmann (born 1958) is an American oncologist and biotechnology leader. She served as chief executive officer of the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation from 2014 to 2020, overseeing the organization's global health and development initiatives. In March 2024 she was elected to the OpenAI board of directors. Earlier in her career, Desmond-Hellmann was the chancellor of the University of California, San Francisco, becoming its first female chancellor. She holds the Arthur and Toni Rembe Rock Distinguished Professor title and previously served as President of Product Development at Genentech, where she helped advance early gene-targeted cancer therapies, including Avastin and Herceptin.

In 2011, Sue Desmond-Hellmann co-chaired a National Academy of Sciences committee focused on advancing precision medicine. The committee proposed the creation of a knowledge network, envisioned as a Google Maps–like data platform for biomedical information, to integrate molecular disease data, environmental factors, and patients’ electronic medical records. This network would enable faster sharing of emerging research findings to accelerate the development of tailored diagnostics and treatments. It was argued that such a system would assist clinicians in making more informed treatment decisions, reduce health care costs, and improve patient care. The NAS report detailing these recommendations is titled Toward Precision Medicine: Building a Knowledge Network for Biomedical Research and a New Taxonomy of Disease. Keith Yamamoto described the report as the most important NAS Framework Analysis since the U.S. Human Genome Project recommendation.

Records indicate that the Fraser River reached its highest historical discharge during the June 1894 flood, with the Hope site estimated at about 17,000 m3/s (roughly 600,000 ft3/s). This figure derives from high-water marks near Hope’s hydrometric station and is supported by several statistical methods. In 1948, the Fraser River Board adopted the 1894 flood discharge as the official maximum for regulatory and flood-control purposes, and that value remains the standard reference used by agencies responsible for flood-control works on the river. Later studies and hydraulic modeling have produced a similar range for the Hope maximum, approximately between 16,000 and 18,000 m3/s (about 570,000–640,000 ft3/s). All measurements and estimates are specifically tied to the Hope site.

Fraser River is the longest river in the Canadian province of British Columbia. It originates at Fraser Pass near Blackrock Mountain in the Canadian Rockies and proceeds for about 1,375 kilometres (approximately 854 miles) before draining into the Strait of Georgia just south of Vancouver. At its mouth, the river's annual discharge is roughly 112 cubic kilometres, equal to about 3,550 cubic metres per second. Each year, the Fraser transports approximately 20 million tonnes of sediment to the ocean.

Following the adoption of a unified DVD standard, several game console makers, including Sega and The 3DO Company, planned to design systems that used DVDs as the primary game medium. Sony, at that time, stated there were no intentions to incorporate DVD into its gaming hardware, despite contributing to the format’s development and later releasing a console that relied on DVD discs. Ultimately, the PlayStation 2, Xbox, and Xbox 360 systems used DVD media for games and related software. In the software distribution market, Windows titles were commonly distributed on DVD as well. Early DVD mastering was accomplished on digital linear tapes, with DVD-R Dual Layer and DVD+R Dual Layer recordable formats becoming widespread later. In consumer electronics, TV/DVD combinations (including CRT or high-definition sets with integrated DVD players) and VCR/DVD combinations were available on the market.

Within the DVD article, the discussion of disc types is anchored to 12-centimeter discs. When referring to 8-centimeter media, ISO standards continue to classify them under Types A through D. By contrast, the DVD Book specifies 8 cm media as belonging to distinct categories separate from the A–D designation. Moreover, DVD-14 does not include an equivalent 8 cm type. Comparative data for 8 cm discs is provided in a later section of the article.

In the wake of turmoil during the 2004 season, Hawthorn appointed Alastair Clarkson as head coach for 2005, selecting the Port Adelaide assistant over contenders Terry Wallace and Gary Ayres. Clarkson initiated a rebuilding program centered on youth, overseeing the delisting of several veteran players, with departures including Rayden Tallis, Mark Graham, Kris Barlow, Luke McCabe, and Lance Picioane, while Nathan Thompson was traded to North Melbourne. In the 2004 national draft Hawthorn acquired key young talents, notably Jarryd Roughead at pick 2, Lance Franklin at 5, and Jordan Lewis at 7. The 2005 season under Clarkson was characterized by a disciplined culture and steady progress, culminating in five wins and a 14th-place finish. Young players Franklin, Roughead, and Lewis earned Rising Star nominations that year, and veteran Shane Crawford returned to form after a broken arm in 2004, finishing third in Hawthorn's Peter Crimmins Medal.

Hawthorn Football Club launched the HANZ-UP! AFL Program in New Zealand in 2009 as part of its international development efforts. The club entered the New Zealand market on an initial three-year contract, with an option to extend the agreement to the end of 2018. In collaboration with AFLNZ, Hawthorn promotes HANZ-UP! through a trio of initiatives named KiwiKick, the Hawks Cup, and the Trent Croad Scholarship Scheme. KiwiKick serves as the New Zealand counterpart to Auskick, the Hawks Cup provides a Year 9–10 schools competition, and the Trent Croad Scholarship Scheme offers AFL international scholarship opportunities. Annually, Hawthorn plans to conduct skills clinics across New Zealand featuring its players. Participants in KiwiKick receive kits branded with Hawthorn and HANZ-UP! logos, while Hawks Cup competitors are issued exclusive Hawthorn merchandise.

Pendant lights are widely used to illuminate kitchen work areas, especially above countertops. When arranged in groups, the fixtures are typically spaced about 75–80 cm apart to achieve even lighting and a cohesive look. For installations over an island bench, the usual height places the lights approximately 75–80 cm above the surface, balancing illumination with clearance. The guideline is frequently employed when a symmetrical arrangement is desired.

A billiard pendant, also called a linear pendant, represents a longer variant of pendant lighting. It normally employs fluorescent tubes, or multiple incandescent lamps, or LED light sources. Its typical installations are above kitchen islands, dining tables, or billiard tables, where it provides focused overhead illumination. Some classifications regard it as a form of chandelier, reflecting its horizontal profile and scale within the broader chandelier family.

During the late 20th and early 21st centuries, Richmond, Virginia experienced a notable rise in crime, with the murder rate increasing markedly. This uptick occurred throughout the 1980s, 1990s, and into the early 2000s, and during that period the city was consistently listed among the most dangerous large cities in the United States.

Richmond, Virginia, has long been anchored by its legal and financial sectors, which form core pillars of the city's economy. The city is the location of the Virginia Supreme Court and houses one of the four courts of the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia, as well as one of the four divisions of the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for that district. It also hosts the United States Court of Appeals for the Fourth Circuit, one of the nation’s thirteen appellate circuits. Richmond serves as a headquarters site for several leading law firms, including Hunton Andrews Kurth, McGuireWoods, and Williams Mullen, while Troutman Sanders merged with Mays & Valentine LLP in 2001 and maintains a substantial presence in the city.

Following nightfall on October 6, American and French forces began constructing the first parallel around Yorktown amid stormy weather. An overcast sky hid the waning moon, aiding concealment from British sentries. General George Washington himself struck the initial blows with a pickaxe to commence the trench, which was planned to run about 2,000 yards (roughly 1,800 meters) from the head of Yorktown to the York River. The work was to be divided, with roughly half of the trench under French command and the other half under American oversight. At the northern end of the French line, a support trench was dug to enable bombardment of British ships in the river. The French were instructed to distract the British with a feint attack; however, a French deserter informed the British of the ruse, who then fired on the French from the Fusiliers’ Redoubt.

During the Yorktown siege, by October 5 General George Washington was nearly ready to open the first parallel. That night, sappers and miners carried out work on the earthworks. They laid strips of pine on the damp sand to delineate the routes of the planned trenches. The opening phase of the operation involved movements primarily on foot and on horseback, with infantry advancing on foot and mounted cavalry taking part in the initial maneuvers.

Within the IANA time zone database, timekeeping information for Germany is maintained from the Unix epoch onward. Germany’s history includes a division into East and West during and after that period, yet the tz database treats the country as a single entity for the purposes of time zones. The database aims to provide at least one time zone for each two-letter ISO country code defined by ISO 3166-1, and its first comprehensive list was published in 1997. That 1997 publication followed the reunification of Germany in 1990, resulting in Germany being represented as a unified state rather than the earlier split.

Time in Germany is governed by Mitteleuropäische Zeit (MEZ; Central European Time) as standard time and by Mitteleuropäische Sommerzeit (MESZ; Central European Summer Time) during daylight saving, corresponding to UTC+1 and UTC+2, respectively. Daylight saving begins on the last Sunday in March at 02:00 CET, when clocks are advanced to 03:00 CEST, and ends on the last Sunday in October at 03:00 CEST, when clocks are returned to 02:00 CET. The autumn transition produces a repeated hour from 02:00 to 03:00, which is typically distinguished as 2A (02:00–03:00 CEST) and 2B (02:00–03:00 CET).

MPEG-4 includes a standardized mechanism for signaling digital rights management within its specification. In MPEG terminology, this signaling is designated as IPMP, an acronym for Intellectual Property Management and Protection.

MPEG-4 is an ISO/IEC standard for multimedia compression and delivery that provides data transparency for data network providers by defining a flexible representation of audiovisual content and related data. The standard outlines procedures for reliably interpreting MPEG-4 data, facilitating consistent decoding and processing across diverse systems. In addition, MPEG-4 supports converting its data into alternative signal formats, enabling adaptation to different transmission and display contexts. These transformed signal types are designed to be interoperable with any available network, supporting broad compatibility and deployment flexibility in multimedia services.

Prentiss County, Mississippi, has been reliably Republican in presidential elections. The last time the county supported a Democratic presidential nominee was in 1976. Since 1996, the Republican share of the presidential vote in the county has increased in every election. In the 2024 election, Prentiss was one of twelve Mississippi counties where the Republican candidate garnered more than 80 percent of the vote.

Prentiss County, Mississippi has a relatively young overall population, with 25.0% of residents under 18, 11.6% aged 18–24, 27.1% aged 25–44, 22.4% aged 45–64, and 13.9% aged 65 and over, and a median age of 35 years. The sex composition shows 100 females for every 94.1 males across all ages, while among those aged 18 and older the ratio is 100 females to 89.4 males.

The Workers' Party of Korea (WPK) is the ruling party of North Korea and its principal political organization. Central to its ideology is Juche, a doctrine that contends human consciousness grants individuals ultimate control over their own fate and the capacity to alter the course of society, emphasizing self-reliance and ideological autonomy. Juche stands in contrast to classical Marxism, which stresses that social change is determined by the relations of production rather than by individual agency. Within Juche, political transformation is envisaged as being led by a Great Leader rather than by a group of formally educated revolutionaries, marking a departure from Lenin's notion of a vanguard party.

Within the Workers' Party of Korea, membership has been categorized into three principal social strata: industrial workers, peasants, and the samuwon, a group encompassing the intelligentsia and the petite bourgeoisie. Since 1948, industrial workers have represented the largest share of party members, followed by peasants and then the samuwon. During the 1970s, as urbanization rose and cities comprised roughly half of the population, the composition of the membership shifted toward a greater representation from state-owned enterprises, while participation from agricultural cooperatives diminished.

In Madhya Pradesh, the Satpura Range, including the Gawilgarh and Mahadeo Hills, forms a south-facing watershed that influences the state's drainage patterns. Rivers such as the Wainganga, Wardha, Pench, and Kanhan carry substantial volumes of water into the Godavari river system, underscoring the region’s role in this extensive basin. The Godavari basin hosts subtropical, semi-moist forests, with the forested character most notable in the Indravati valley. Additionally, numerous multi-state irrigation projects are being developed within the Godavari basin, among them the Godavari River Basin Irrigation Projects.

In 1950, Madhya Pradesh was formed from the Central Provinces and Berar together with the princely states of Makrai and Chhattisgarh, with Nagpur initially designated as the capital. Within the same period, the Central India Agency saw the creation of three states: Madhya Bharat, Vindhya Pradesh, and Bhopal. In 1956, these three were merged into Madhya Pradesh, while Vidarbha—the Marathi-speaking southern region that includes Nagpur—was ceded to Bombay state. Although Jabalpur was initially chosen as the capital, political interference led to Bhopal being retained as the administrative center. Finally, in November 2000, the Madhya Pradesh Reorganization Act carved out a new state, Chhattisgarh, from the southeastern portion of Madhya Pradesh.

Between 1912 and 1949, the country experienced a period marked by warlordism, Japanese invasion, and civil conflict, during which several governments laid competing claims to legitimacy over territory and sovereignty. The Beiyang government governed from 1912 to 1928, emerging after the collapse of the Qing dynasty, while the Chinese Soviet Republic was proclaimed by the Communist Party and existed from 1931 to 1937. In Manchuria, Manchukuo operated as a Japanese-sponsored puppet state from 1932 to 1945, with Mengjiang similarly functioning as a puppet regime in Inner Mongolia from 1939 to 1945. The Fujian People's Government held a brief existence in 1933–1934, and Wang Jingwei’s collaborationist government served as a Japanese-backed administration from 1940 to 1945. In the border regions, Tibet was governed by the Ganden Phodrang administration from 1912 to 1951. The region of Xinjiang saw the short-lived Turkic Islamic Republic of East Turkestan (1933–1934) and the East Turkestan Republic, which lasted from 1944 to 1949. The Tuvan People's Republic persisted from 1921 to 1944. In Outer Mongolia, Bogd Khan's Mongolian State existed from 1911 to 1924, followed by the Mongolian People's Republic, which endured from 1924 to 1992 and was formally recognized by the People's Republic of China in 1946.

Two Chinas refers to the existence of two distinct political entities that govern China, each possessing its own political system and ideological orientation. The People's Republic of China is a one-party communist state, while the Republic of China has evolved into a multi-party democracy after transitioning from a one-party military rule. Consequently, the two governments maintain separate diplomatic relations.

The Small Form Factor Committee (SFF) operated as an ad hoc electronics industry group established to rapidly develop interoperability specifications as a complement to the traditional standards process. It produced the Small Form-factor Pluggable network interface module format. In 2016, the committee was absorbed by the Storage Networking Industry Association (SNIA).

The Small Form Factor Committee (SFF Committee) was established in 1990 to define the form factor for disk drives used in portable computers, with the aim of facilitating interoperability and efficient manufacturing. In November 1992, its mandate was broadened to supplement the formal standards process by addressing storage-industry areas that required timely attention. Accordingly, SFF undertakes projects in domains not covered by standards committees, typically because of timing, charter limitations, or other considerations.

Norway competed in tennis at the 1920 Summer Olympics with three players—two men and one woman—marking the nation's second appearance in Olympic tennis. In the singles events, all three Norwegians were eliminated in the opening round. The two male players did compete in the doubles competition, recording one victory to advance to the quarterfinals before their run ended with a defeat.

Seven Norwegian wrestlers competed at the 1920 Summer Olympics, marking Norway's third appearance in Olympic wrestling. Andersen was the team's sole medalist, earning bronze in the Greco-Roman lightweight division. Johnsen finished in fourth place in the middleweight category after losing the bronze medal match.

The United States Army is the land service branch of the U.S. Armed Forces and, in constitutional terms, designated as the Army of the United States. It operates under the authority, direction, and control of the Secretary of Defense and forms part of the Department of Defense, one of six armed forces and one of eight uniformed services. It is the senior branch in order of precedence among the armed services. The Army's lineage extends to the Continental Army, established on June 14, 1775, during the American Revolutionary War; after the war, the Congress of the Confederation created the United States Army on June 3, 1784 to replace the disbanded Continental Army.

On 11 November 2018, the United States Army announced a revised version of the Army Greens, drawing design cues from World War II–era uniforms. The new Army Greens were planned to become the standard garrison service uniform, while the blue Army Service Uniform would remain in use as the dress uniform. The Army Greens were projected to enter initial fielding in the summer of 2020.

Churchmanship originally referred to an ecclesiastic or clergyman, and before 1677 the term was broadened to denote strong supporters of the Church of England. By the nineteenth century it had come to distinguish Anglicans from Dissenters, and the noun “churchmanship” was first attested in 1680 to describe the attitudes of these supporters, later acquiring its modern sense as a label for the different liturgical and doctrinal tendencies within Anglicanism. In contemporary usage, many Anglicans are comfortable identifying themselves by their particular churchmanship, but not all prefer to be described beyond the umbrella term “Anglican”; in official contexts today, the related notion of “tradition” is sometimes favored.

Churchmanship denotes the range of tendencies, factions, or schools of thought active within the Church of England and its sister churches in the Anglican Communion. In many official contexts, it is referred to as churchpersonship, or more commonly as tradition. The term is used to describe and classify the internal diversity, distinctive practices, and ecclesial loyalties that characterize Anglican communities. A comparable usage exists in Lutheranism, where similar divisions are described under analogous terms.

Angular momentum is conserved in an inertial reference frame, a principle that underpins inertial navigation systems by providing a stable frame of reference in space. This approach enables submarines to navigate beneath polar ice caps, where external navigation signals are blocked by the overlying ice. More broadly, inertial navigation is a foundational technology for modern navigation, essential to a wide range of applications across aviation, maritime, and space domains.

Angular momentum, as defined by Rankine in 1858, is described as a vector quantity whose magnitude is proportional to the rotational effect about a fixed point and whose direction is perpendicular to the plane of motion, with the sense determined by the right-hand rule when viewed along the axis from its positive end. In 1872 Rankine claimed that the term was introduced by Mr. Hayward, likely referring to R. B. Hayward’s 1856 article, published in 1864, which proposed a direct method for estimating velocities, accelerations, and related quantities with respect to axes movable in space. However, Rankine’s attribution is considered incorrect, since the term angular momentum had already appeared in literature dating from the late eighteenth to early nineteenth centuries. Hayward’s work is widely recognized as the first to use the term and to popularize the concept in the English-speaking world. Before Hayward, the concept was typically described in English as the “momentum of rotation.”

Spanish naming conventions ordinarily include two surnames: the first from the paternal line and the second from the maternal line. When the paternal surname is very common or potentially ambiguous, individuals may be referred to in formal contexts by both surnames or informally by the second surname alone. For example, José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero is frequently addressed simply as Zapatero, since Rodríguez is a widespread surname and could be unclear; Zapatero is his maternal surname. A similar pattern is observed with Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba, Federico García Lorca, and Pablo Ruiz Picasso, who are commonly known by their maternal surnames Rubalcaba, Lorca, and Picasso. Nevertheless, indexing by the second surname alone can be inappropriate in some cases, such as Rodríguez Zapatero under Z or García Lorca under L. Picasso, who spent much of his adult life in France, is normally indexed under P in many catalogs.

According to the Chicago Manual of Style, Spanish and Hispanophone names are indexed by the family name in cataloging and reference work. When an individual bears two family surnames, entry is typically made under the paternal surname, and if the paternal and maternal or husband’s surnames are joined by the conjunction “y,” the first element of that compound is treated as the surname for indexing. The particle de may be regarded as part of a surname or detached from it, depending on the naming tradition of the person. In Lusophone (Portuguese) naming conventions, the final element is indexed because the father’s surname follows the mother’s. Consequently, the father’s surname serves as the indexed element for both Spanish and Portuguese names.

In 1903, police raided Madam Ida Bailey's Canary Cottage, a house of prostitution in the Stingaree District, without the usual advance warnings. Reputed customers, including Frank P. Frary, the mayor at the time, and the chief of police, are reported to have been inconvenienced by the operation.

Frank Phineas Frary (December 7, 1856 – August 16, 1911) was an American Republican politician from California. Born in Fremont, Ohio, he moved to San Diego in 1875 and began his career as an agent and driver on a stage line linking San Diego with San Luis Rey. By obtaining a government contract to carry mail between San Diego and Julian and on to Cuyamaca, he helped establish a general hauling business that grew substantially. Frary led the hauling company until his retirement in 1910 due to ill health. Additionally, he owned a bee ranch at Capitan Grande, near El Cajon.

Fuzhou railway station, situated on the Taiwan Railways Administration's West Coast line, serves Banqiao District in New Taipei City, Taiwan. The station is identified in Chinese as 浮洲車站, with the pinyin transliteration Fúzhōu Chēzhàn.

Fuzhou railway station, located on the outskirts of Banqiao in New Taipei City, Taiwan, primarily serves commuter traffic. It first opened in 1932 as a temporary stop, but was closed in 1942. The station reopened in 1953, but it soon ceased operation again. A new station facility began operating on 2 September 2011 under the Taiwan Railways Administration’s policy to convert certain rail lines into MRT‑style services. Currently, the only train that stops at Fuzhou station is the local train.

In 2009, Jewish Life Television reached an agreement with Channel 33, the second outlet of the Israeli Broadcasting Authority, to distribute JLTV’s programming on Israeli over-the-air and cable networks, and to beam the content by satellite to Europe and the Middle East. The implementation, however, proceeded slowly, stymied by bureaucratic hurdles at the broadcaster. A subsequent period of resignations within Channel 33 further impeded progress and contributed to the delays.

As of 2025, Jewish Life Television expanded its online offerings into a free, ad-supported streaming television suite. The suite aggregates the network’s main JLTV service with several specialty channels, including a fitness channel and a comedy channel, as well as an Israel-focused programming channel. It also includes a "classic" channel featuring public-domain television titles and maintains a full-time channel dedicated to Soupy Sales.

Triumph Group, by 1996, had a workforce of about 1,500 employees and reported annual earnings of roughly $300 million. The company's organizational structure comprised six aviation divisions and seven divisions dedicated to specialty materials. In 1996 the firm conducted an initial public offering, raising more than $50 million in capital.

During the early 1990s, Alco reorganized its business, selling its food division in 1991. In 1992, it announced plans to divest Alco Diversified Services and to purchase 49.9 percent of IMM Office Systems Holding. In 1993, Triumph Group acquired Alco Diversified Services in a leveraged buyout. Triumph conducted aviation repair and overhaul, industrial machining, paper converting and steel converting. The companies employed 1,450 people at 22 U.S. locations, with aviation accounting for just over 25% of total sales.

Frederick Grey, the son of Charles Grey, 2nd Earl Grey, who would serve as British prime minister in the 1830s, and Mary Elizabeth Ponsonby, daughter of William Ponsonby, 1st Baron Ponsonby, joined the Royal Navy in January 1819. Serving as a midshipman aboard HMS Naiad, a fifth-rate ship of the Mediterranean Fleet, he took part in anti-piracy operations off Cap Bon, Tunisia, in 1824. He was promoted to lieutenant on 7 April 1825 and, in the same month, transferred to HMS Sybille, another fifth-rate vessel in the Mediterranean Fleet. In September 1825 he moved to HMS Volage, a sixth-rate ship, serving on the South America Station. Grey was promoted to commander on 17 April 1827 and was posted to HMS Heron, a sloop on the South America Station, in April 1827.

In March 1854 Grey assumed command of HMS Hannibal, a second-rate ship of the line. He carried 10,000 French troops to the Åland Islands off the coast of Finland before proceeding to the Bosporus. During the Crimean War he served as the chief transport officer for Allied operations, coordinating troop and supply movements as the principal agent of transports.

Die Welt has faced repeated criticism for publishing climate-sceptic articles. A 2017 study analyzing a year of newspaper publications from June 2012 to May 2013 found that 43% of Die Welt’s articles were climate-sceptical, the highest share reported among German newspapers in the sample.
Die Welt is a German national daily newspaper published in broadsheet format by Axel Springer SE. The name is pronounced [diː ˈvɛlt] and literally means "The World."

The Open Notebook Science Network is a WordPress-based network of blogs designed to facilitate the creation and upkeep of individual and laboratory notebooks. By January 2018, the network counted 126 active members.

Open-notebook science refers to the practice of documenting and sharing research processes publicly as they unfold. In this vein, Daniel Himmelstein led Project Rephetio, a drug repurposing study that sought new therapeutic uses for existing medications. The project leveraged platforms such as GitHub and Thinklab to publish code, data, and discussions in real time, thereby enabling open, notebook-style science and fostering collaboration among researchers and the broader community.

Vartan recorded an Italian-language version of the song, releasing it under the title La Maritza. A German-language rendition followed, issued as Lied ohne Wiederkehr, a designation that translates to Song of No Return.
In Wallonia, the French-speaking region of Belgium, La Maritza was issued as a double A-side with Un p'tit peu beaucoup. The release spent 19 weeks on the Belgian singles chart, peaking at number 4.

As of 1 January 2025, Bonaire's permanent resident population stood at 26,552, reflecting a growth of 10,011 since 2012. The island encompasses a total land area of 288 square kilometres (111 square miles) and measures 38.6 kilometres from north to south, with a width of 5 to 8 kilometres (3–5 miles) from east to west. Off its coast lies Klein Bonaire, an uninhabited islet located about 800 metres to the west of Bonaire, with a land area of 6 square kilometres (2.3 square miles). Klein Bonaire is characterized by low-growing vegetation such as cactus, sparse palms near the shoreline, white sandy beaches, and a fringing reef. Reefs, beaches, and on-island reserves on both Bonaire and Klein Bonaire are protected within the Bonaire National Marine Park, which is administered by STINAPA Bonaire.

During the late 20th century, Bonaire's growing diving tourism prompted plans to develop hotel infrastructure on Klein Bonaire. In 1999, Klein Bonaire was purchased and safeguarded by the Island Territory of Bonaire with backing from the Netherlands, WWF, and other conservationists. In 2001, Klein Bonaire was established as a legally protected nature reserve and incorporated into the Bonaire National Marine Park. The site is also designated as a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance under the Ramsar Convention, reflecting its international ecological significance.

Ibadan is naturally drained by five main rivers and numerous tributaries, namely the Ona River to the north and west, the Ogbere River to the east, the Ogunpa River passing through the city, the Kudeti River in the central area, and the Odo-Ogun system forming the boundary with Oke-Ogun communities. The Ogunpa is a third-order stream, with a channel length of 12.76 kilometers and a catchment area of about 54.92 square kilometers. Lake Eleyele lies in the northwestern part of Ibadan, while the Osun River and Asejire Lake bound the city to the east. The Odo-Ogun rivers delineate Ibadan's borders with other Oke-Ogun towns across Lagos, Ogun, and Osun states, including boundary areas near Iseyin Town and Eruwa Town.

Ibadan derives its name from the Yoruba term Eba-Odan, which denotes a location at the edge of a meadow. The town is traditionally dated to 1829, a time of upheaval in Yorubaland when several ancient Yoruba polities, including Old Oyo, Ijaye, and Owu, declined, and new settlements such as Abeokuta, New Oyo, and Ibadan arose. Lagelu is widely regarded as the city's founder. It was initially planned as a war camp for contingents from Oyo, Ife, and Ijebu. The site sits in a forested area with hills rising from about 160 to 275 meters above sea level. Its position on the forest fringe helped give rise to its name and facilitated its development as a trading center for forest and grassland traders.

Brookfield Place (Toronto) features the Allen Lambert Galleria, a six-storey atrium nicknamed the "crystal cathedral of commerce" for its striking design. Designed by Spanish architect Santiago Calatrava, the galleria connects Bay Street to Sam Pollock Square. The structural design was carried out by Yolles Partnership Inc., with PCL Construction serving as the general contractor and Canron Construction Corporation handling the structural steel fabrication. The pedestrian thoroughfare is supported by eight freestanding columns on each side, whose branches form parabolic shapes that evoke a forest canopy, a visual effect enhanced by the surrounding facades of adjacent buildings.

Within Brookfield Place in Toronto, The Galleria originated from an international design competition and was subsequently integrated into the development to satisfy the City of Toronto's public art requirements. The space has become a frequently photographed feature and is widely used as a backdrop for news reports as well as television and film productions.

Khmer script utilizes vowel signs that can be pronounced in two ways, depending on the inherent vowel of the consonant to which they attach. The exact pronunciation of these vowel signs may change in weak syllables and when the sign is shortened by a diacritic. When a dependent vowel sign or diacritic is not present, the syllable-initial consonant is typically followed by the sound of its inherent vowel, yielding the default pronunciation.

In Khmer orthography, the reăhmŭkh diacritic occurs in relatively uncommon configurations, producing distinct spellings and pronunciations. For example, the forms អើះ and, in some cases, អឹះ, are pronounced [əh]. A further instance is អែះ, pronounced [eh]. The word ចា៎ះ, meaning "yes" and typically used by women, is pronounced [caː], with occasional realization as [caːh].

The Strad is a monthly classical music magazine based in the United Kingdom that concentrates on string instruments—violin, viola, cello, and double bass—for both amateur and professional musicians. Established in 1889, it provides information, photographs, and reviews of instruments, along with feature articles and news, and notices about concerts. The publication also offers practical guidance on technique, profiles of leading performers, and coverage of master classes and instrument makers (luthiers). Additionally, it includes articles about orchestras and music schools.

The Strad derives its name from the common abbreviation of the Stradivarius family of luthiers and their instruments. The magazine’s inaugural issue appeared in June 1890. The current editor is Emma Baker. The Strad is owned by Newsquest Specialist Media Limited, a Gannett company.

East Frisian Low Saxon remains part of daily life for a subset of the coastal population in East Frisia. Its use tends to be more prevalent among older generations and in rural communities. Around half of the regional population retains some degree of active engagement with the language. Both fluent speakers and individuals who understand it passively are diminishing in number. The decline is attributed to sociolinguistic shifts and the increasing dominance of Standard German.

East Frisian Low Saxon is a Northern Low Saxon dialect spoken on the East Frisian peninsula, a geographically defined region in northwestern Lower Saxony, Germany. The variety is also known as East Frisian Low German, or simply East Frisian in cases where the naming is ambiguous.

Turtle, defined by Dave Beckett, is a compact syntax that forms a subset of Notation3 (N3) while simultaneously acting as a superset of the minimal N-Triples format. Its expressive scope is limited to serializing valid RDF graphs, with the full N3 language offering features beyond RDF. Turtle serves as an alternative syntax to RDF/XML, the original RDF standard. Unlike RDF/XML, Turtle does not rely on XML and is generally more readable and easier to edit manually.

Turtle, which stands for Terse RDF Triple Language, is a syntax and file format used to express data in the RDF data model. Its syntax bears similarities to SPARQL, contributing to its readability and ease of use for those acquainted with that query language. As a common RDF serialization, Turtle is widely employed for storing RDF data, alongside other formats such as N-Triples, JSON-LD, and RDF/XML.

Anton Chekhov, a Russian physician and writer, balanced a medical career with his literary output and devoted substantial resources to his practice, with the largest cost being time spent traveling to visit patients, which in turn reduced the time available for writing. His work as a doctor enriched his storytelling by placing him in intimate contact with all strata of Russian society, from peasants to the upper classes, and this exposure informed his literary realism. He witnessed the cramped and unhealthy living conditions of peasants, a theme later recalled in the short story Peasants. He also engaged with the upper echelons; his notebook records that aristocrats possess the same bodily uncleanliness, the same toothless old age, and the same unseemly death as market-women. In 1893–1894 he served as a Zemstvo doctor in Zvenigorod, an area noted for numerous sanatoriums and rest homes. A local hospital in Zvenigorod is named after him.

Several of Chekhov's short stories were adapted into episodes of Katha Sagar, a 1986 Indian anthology television series. In the 1990s, a second Indian television series, Chekhov Ki Duniya, aired on DD National, and it presented adaptations drawn from different Chekhov works than those featured in Katha Sagar.

During the 1995–96 NBA season, the Philadelphia 76ers concluded their tenure at The Spectrum, which at the time carried the CoreStates Spectrum sponsorship. The CoreStates branding would later be incorporated into the naming of the team’s forthcoming home arena under construction. Subsequently, the franchise returned to the venue, by then renamed Wachovia Spectrum, for a farewell game in the 2008–09 season before the arena was demolished.

During the 1995–96 NBA season, the New York Knicks updated their branding by incorporating a “New York” script into the team logo. They also unveiled blue alternate uniforms featuring black side panels on the jersey, representing a notable change in their uniforms for that season.

The term classicide was first introduced by Schwarz in 1972 in The Three Faces of Revolution. It was subsequently refined and popularized as a distinct concept by Mann. Since then, sociologists such as Mann and Martin Shaw have employed classicide to describe genocide-like processes that target a social class. These processes entail the elimination of a social class through murder or displacement, and the destruction of the bourgeoisie to forge an egalitarian proletariat. Mann does not apply the label genocide to examples occurring under Communist states.

Harry Wu has described the killings during Mao Zedong's Chinese Land Reform as "classicide," arguing that a nationwide ideological campaign was used to consolidate power by sorting people into five class categories defined by land, capital, property, and income. The categories included landlords, the rich peasantry, the middle peasantry, and the poor workers and peasants. Supporters of the regime lauded the lower classes for their perceived humility and diligence, while landlords and the wealthy were demonized and targeted. Property was expropriated, and those labeled as targets were sent to arduous labor in the countryside; many were killed. Wu cites figures indicating that, in 1949, roughly 10 to 15 million individuals belonged to the landlord and rich peasant classes nationwide, and by the end of the 1970s, after the Cultural Revolution, only about 10–15 percent of that group remained alive.

Sinclair BASIC employs a tokenized memory model in which every keyword that would ordinarily span multiple characters is stored as a single byte, and the token set even encompasses multicharacter symbols such as <>. This approach reduces memory usage on early hardware that had roughly one kilobyte of RAM available for programs. It also simplifies the interpreter’s runtime, since the processor can immediately determine whether a given character begins a keyword or is ordinary text. As a result, keywords are not stored or entered as literal text; they are represented by tokens during input, storage, and execution. The design further allows identifiers that resemble keywords (for example, a variable named PRINT) because the distinction between keywords and identifiers is made by context within the program.

Sinclair BASIC's editor lacks support for freeform on-screen editing; when the EDIT command is invoked, the line currently being edited is duplicated at the bottom of the screen, producing a copy that the user can modify by moving horizontally with the cursor keys. Changes are committed by pressing NEW LINE again. By contrast, editors on the Commodore 64 and the Atari 8-bit systems allow navigation between lines using the up and down arrow keys and support editing directly within a line in place, without requiring a duplicate line to be created.

In Socialist Republic Romania, George Călinescu offered an officially sanctioned critique of Junimea in his late, Communist-inspired Compendium of Istoria literaturii române. He argued that Junimea functioned as a bridge linking peasants with the boyar elite, thereby connecting disparate social strata. Călinescu criticized Maiorescu's strict art-for-art's-sake stance as indicative of rigidity, and he extended the critique to Arthur Schopenhauer's ideas as signs of inflexibility within the movement. He downplayed Junimea's literary achievements, contending that many of its members did not fulfill their stated objectives. He rejected Petre Carp's criticism of Bogdan Petriceicu Hasdeu as "little and unprofessional." Nevertheless, Călinescu favored the principal figures associated with Junimea—Mihai Eminescu, Ion Luca Caragiale, and Ion Creangă—and he also praised certain secondary Junimists, such as the materialist philosopher Vasile Conta.

Junimea's founders included four individuals from the Romanian boyar class, reflecting the group’s roots in the traditional elite. Theodor Rosetti was the brother-in-law of Domnitor Alexandru Ioan Cuza, establishing a marital link to the ruling dynasty, while Petre Carp and Ioan Pogor were both sons of local boyars, underscoring their aristocratic lineage. Iacob Negruzzi was the son of Costache Negruzzi, tying the circle to another prominent family. By contrast, Titu Maiorescu was the sole founder born into the urban elite; his father, Ioan Maiorescu, served as a professor at Craiova’s National College and acted as a representative of the Wallachian government to the Frankfurt Parliament during the 1848 Wallachian Revolution.

Tolerance intervals are statistical constructs that bound the range of observations expected to contain a specified fraction of the population. By contrast, confidence intervals bound a single population parameter, such as the mean or variance, with a stated level of confidence. The width of a confidence interval arises solely from sampling error and narrows toward zero as the sample size increases. In comparison, the width of a tolerance interval reflects both sampling error and the intrinsic variability of the population, and with larger samples it converges toward the population’s p-proportion interval. In essence, confidence intervals express uncertainty about estimating a parameter, whereas tolerance intervals express the variability of the population data that would cover a given proportion.

Tolerance intervals are statistical tools used to estimate the range within which a specified proportion of a population will fall with a given level of confidence. Among these, one-sided normal tolerance intervals admit an exact solution under the normal model. Their construction yields endpoints that are expressed in terms of the sample mean and the sample variance, with the critical value derived from the noncentral t-distribution. Consequently, the resulting interval provides a precise upper (or lower) bound that contains the target proportion of the population with the prescribed confidence.

Broad sheet glass production is recorded as occurring earlier than the figures most often cited in later sources. Historical evidence indicates that French glassmakers, among others, were producing broad sheets prior to the subsequent practitioners named in accounts. Among the notable makers associated with broad sheet glass are William Le Verrier, the Schurterrers, and John Alemayne. In the period between 1350 and 1356, Alemayne secured commissions for glass intended for use in St Stephen's Chapel, Westminster, and St George's Chapel, Windsor.

Broad sheet glass was first produced in the United Kingdom at Chiddingfold, Surrey, near the border with Sussex, circa 1226. In 1240, Westminster Abbey placed an order for this glass, indicating its use in major ecclesiastical architecture. The glass produced at this site was of poor quality and relatively opaque, and its manufacture declined, ceasing by the early 16th century. The location is thought to have been chosen due to access to suitable sand, the availability of bracken used to produce potash for soda glass, and beech forests that supplied charcoal for the kiln. Surviving examples of glass from this area can be found in Guildford Museum.

The Turk Shahis were a polity based in the Kabul region who, from around 658 CE, were nominally part of the Tang dynasty’s protectorate system. Their territory was formally partitioned into Chinese commanderies under the Anxi Protectorate, including Xiuxian Commandery (Xiūxiān Dūdùfû), seated at Yege (modern Mihtarlam) to the east of Kabul for the Jibin country; Yuepan Commandery (Yuèpān Dūdùfû), with its seat at Yan at the Gandhara frontier; and Tiaozhi Commandery (Tiáozhī Dūdùfû), seated at Ghazni.

From 711 CE, the Turk Shahis faced a rising Muslim threat from the southeast, sparked by the campaigns of Muhammad ibn Qasim. These campaigns established the Caliphal province of Sind, extending as far as Multan at the gates of the Punjab. The province remained under Caliphal influence for several decades, initially under Umayyad suzerainty and later under Abbasid dependency, until 854 CE. This frontier presence of the Caliphate thus constituted a significant external pressure on the Turk Shahis during the period.

Danei District was formerly home to the Tevorangh, a branch of the Taiwanese Plains Aborigines within the Siraya people, identified with the Baccloangh subtribe. In 1920, the area was designated as Ōuchi Village (大内庄) in Sobun District (曽文郡) of Tainan Prefecture.

Danei District is a rural district located in Tainan, Taiwan, with a population of approximately 8,948 residents. The district's name is written in Chinese characters as 大內區; in Mandarin pinyin it is Dà nèi Qū, in Wade–Giles as Ta4-nei4 Ch'ü1, and in Pe̍h-ōe-jī as Toā-lā-khu.

Olivia Dean is an English singer-songwriter from London whose discography comprises two studio albums, five EPs, and twenty-eight singles. Her debut single, "Reason to Stay," was self-released in October 2018, and after signing with AFM Records she issued her debut EP OK Love You Bye in November 2019, followed by the second EP What Am I Gonna Do on Sundays? in December 2020. Dean released her debut studio album Messy in June 2023, which peaked at number four on the UK Albums Chart. Her second studio album, The Art of Loving, appeared in September 2025; its singles include "Nice to Each Other," "Lady Lady," "Man I Need," and the concurrent release of "So Easy (To Fall in Love)." The Art of Loving subsequently reached number one on the UK Albums Chart.

OCLC operates the Virtual International Authority File (VIAF), an international name authority resource designed to consolidate authority records for names across participating libraries. The governance of VIAF is provided by the VIAF Council, whose members are representatives from institutions that contribute data to VIAF. VIAF assigns identifiers known as VIAF numbers, which are widely used as standard identifiers, including by Wikipedia.

In January 2015, OCLC acquired Sustainable Collection Services (SCS), which offered consulting services grounded in analysis of library print collection data to help libraries optimize the management and sharing of materials. In 2017, OCLC expanded its interlibrary loan offerings by acquiring Relais International, an Ottawa, Canada–based provider of interlibrary loan services.

Parafoil is a form of parachute whose wing expands into an airfoil-shaped canopy as it deploys, driven by multiple suspension lines. Early deployment shocks prevented its acceptance as a standard parachute, but adding a drag-inducing canopy on the riser lines, or slider, slowed the canopy’s expansion and made it suitable for parachute use. Compared with simple round canopies, parafoil parachutes offer greater maneuverability, enabling better steering, longer glide distances, and increased control over descent rate. Mechanically, the parafoil operates as a glider of the free-flight kite type. These features contributed to the later development of paragliders.

Parafoil, developed in 1964 by Domina Jalbert (1904–1991), followed his career as a kite designer and his work on hybrid balloon-kite aerial platforms for scientific instruments. Jalbert conceived the device as capable of suspending an aerial platform or facilitating the recovery of space equipment. A patent for the parafoil was granted in 1966.

Örgryte IS maintains an organized network of supporters led by the official club, ÖIS Supporterklubb Balders Hage. In addition to this sanctioned group, the club's fanbase includes several independent supporter organizations. The second-largest among these is Inferno Örgryte, a group characterized by an ultras-inspired culture.

Örgryte IS is a Swedish football club based in Gothenburg that has won twelve national championship titles and one national cup. In February 2011, the club’s operating company, Örgryte Fotboll AB, went bankrupt due to financial difficulties, and the resulting insolvency led to Örgryte's relegation to Division 1 Södra, the third tier of Swedish football. The team plays its home matches at Gamla Ullevi, and the club is affiliated with Göteborgs Fotbollförbund.

The history of Simplified Chinese characters includes a progression of cataloging efforts beginning with the 1988 publication Chart of Generally Utilized Characters of Modern Chinese, which listed 7,000 characters in both their simplified and traditional forms. Of these, roughly one-half were later incorporated into the revised List of Commonly Used Characters in Modern Chinese, comprising 2,500 characters deemed common and 1,000 considered less common. A major revision in 2009 expanded the list to 8,300 characters, though no new simplifications were introduced. Proposals to make slight orthographic adjustments to 44 characters in order to align with traditional calligraphic conventions were not implemented after public opposition. In more recent practice, the unrestricted simplification of rare or archaic characters by analogy using simplified radicals or components has been discouraged. A State Language Commission official cited oversimplification as the reason for restoring some characters, and an open public comment period was announced to run until 31 August 2009 to solicit feedback.

In Singapore, Mandarin Chinese is one of the official languages, and Simplified Chinese characters constitute the official standard for Chinese writing in the country, appearing in most official publications and government-controlled media. Simplified characters are taught exclusively in schools, while the government does not discourage traditional characters; parents may choose whether their child’s Chinese name is registered in simplified or traditional form. Traditional characters, however, remain widely used by older Singaporeans and are common in many everyday contexts, including billboards, stall menus, decorations, newspapers, and television, with no restrictions on their use in mass media. Imported media from Hong Kong and Taiwan, such as television programs, books, magazines, and music, are widely available and typically employ traditional characters. Moreover, many shop signs and menus in hawker centres and coffee shops continue to be written in traditional characters.

Initial planning for the 2030 United States Census began in October 2018. A design selection phase is currently underway. Public input was collected from August through November 2022, and this input informed the Census Bureau’s decisions regarding the operational design of the 2030 census, including which languages should be used to collect census data.

The 2030 United States census, commonly known as Census 2030, is the planned twenty-fifth decennial census of the United States. National Census Day serves as the reference date for the enumeration and will be observed on April 1, 2030.

In the context of the Heisenberg group, the underlying Lie algebra is nilpotent, and for such algebras the exponential map exp: 𝔤 → G is a diffeomorphism onto the associated connected, simply-connected Lie group. This diffeomorphism provides a smooth identification between the Lie algebra and its corresponding Lie group, and the resulting group is the unique connected, simply-connected Lie group whose Lie algebra is the given nilpotent algebra (unique up to isomorphism).

Analogues of Heisenberg groups over finite fields of odd prime order p are referred to as extra special groups, specifically the exponent-p variety. More generally, when a group's derived subgroup [G,G] is contained in its center Z(G), the commutator operation induces a map from (G/Z(G)) × (G/Z(G)) to Z(G). This induced commutator map is bilinear on the abelian group G/Z(G) and is skew-symmetric (alternating) in nature.

The Hawaii–Aleutian Standard Time (HST) was established as the standard time for the region, applying across the Hawaiian Islands and the Aleutian Islands. It was adopted to ensure consistent scheduling for both commercial and governmental activities.

The Hawaii–Aleutian Time Zone corresponds to Hawaii–Aleutian Standard Time (HST). The standard time offset is UTC−10:00, placing local time ten hours behind Coordinated Universal Time. The zone’s clock time is based on the mean solar time of the 150th meridian west of the Greenwich Observatory.

Culture of poverty refers to a set of characteristics attributed to some impoverished communities. Individuals described as belonging to this culture are said to have very little sense of history and to constitute a marginal group that knows only their own troubles, local conditions, neighborhood, and day-to-day way of life. They are described as lacking knowledge, vision, or ideology that would enable them to perceive similarities between their problems and those of others like themselves elsewhere in the world. According to the concept, they are not class conscious and are highly sensitive to status distinctions within their social environment.

Lewis (1998) studied poverty in the developing world, and his culture of poverty concept proved attractive to policymakers and politicians in the United States. The notion subsequently exerted considerable influence on policy debates, most notably informing the Moynihan Report (1965) and shaping the War on Poverty.

At the 2023 Australian Open, Sam Schröder and Niels Vink captured the quad doubles wheelchair tennis title after defeating Donald Ramphadi and Ymanitu Silva in the final, 6–1, 6–3. Their triumph completed for Schröder and Vink both a non-calendar-year Grand Slam and the career Super Slam in wheelchair quad doubles.

Comedy Central Extra was a television channel whose weekend schedules historically spotlighted classic British comedies. The repertoire included notables such as The Upper Hand, Bless This House, George and Mildred, Brush Strokes, Monty Python's Flying Circus, Don't Wait Up, and Mr. Bean.

Comedy Central Extra, originally launched in the United Kingdom and Ireland as Paramount Comedy 2, began broadcasting on Sky on 1 September 2003, with subsequent launches on Telewest on 22 September 2003 and on NTL on 15 October 2003. The channel initially operated as a timeshift service that repeated Paramount Comedy programming at different times, but it later began airing a distinct slate of programming sourced from Paramount and, increasingly, programming of British origin.

District 11 of Zurich comprises the three quarters Affoltern, Oerlikon, and Seebach. Each of these areas previously functioned as an independent municipality, before being incorporated into the city of Zurich in 1934.

In Poland, the higher doctorate is the habilitation, officially known as doktor habilitowany (dr hab.), and it is a degree that ranks above the PhD. It is awarded in recognition of substantial accomplishments in teaching, research, and service attained after earning the doctoral degree. Typical requirements include up to eight years of original research, a record of multiple peer‑reviewed publications, the production of a monograph, and the submission and defense of a habilitation dissertation following the PhD. The Polish habilitation is comparable to habilitation degrees in Germany and Austria and is regarded as being equivalent, in terms of qualifications, to attaining the status of associate professor with tenure.

In Ukraine, the Doctor of Sciences (DSc; Ukrainian: Доктор наук) is the second and highest science degree, awarded to researchers who have made substantial contributions to scientific knowledge and who have originated new directions and visions in their field. Since 2016, the PhD (Doctor of Philosophy; Ukrainian: Доктор філософії) has been the highest level of formal education and the first science degree in the Ukrainian system. In addition, since 2016, holding a PhD has been one of the prerequisites for heading a university department in Ukraine.

Following the May 2019 update to Windows 10 (version 1903), Microsoft announced that Windows To Go would no longer be developed. The discontinuation statement noted that Windows To Go does not support feature updates and therefore cannot stay current. The configuration required a specific type of USB drive, a requirement that many OEMs no longer supported. Windows To Go was subsequently removed from Windows 10 starting with the May 2020 update (version 2004).

Simon Bisson of ZDNet described Windows To Go as among the more notable features introduced with Windows 8. He observed that performance remained solid even when using a USB 2.0 connection, with no perceptible lag. He characterized Windows To Go as a highly useful means of running Windows 8.

In Israel, bed-and-breakfast establishments are commonly known as zimmers, a term borrowed from the German word for "room." The practice is widespread across the country, with a notable concentration in the northern regions such as the Galilee, the Upper Galilee, and the Golan Heights. Over time, the zimmer sector has grown into a sizeable industry. Its development began in the 1990s, when traditional agriculture faced declining profitability. Consequently, farming families from moshavim and kibbutzim, as well as urban residents, established hospitality ventures. In the past decade, B&Bs have also emerged in the southern Negev region.

Bed and breakfast denotes the level of catering included in the price of a hotel room, indicating what meals are provided as part of the stay. It stands in contrast to other lodging meal options, including room-only, half-board, and full-board arrangements.

During the Rhine crossing, Polish forces constructed improvised boats and advanced under German fire to cross at Westerbouwing on the north bank of the river. The initial crossing was undertaken by the 8th Parachute Company, with later participation from elements of the Polish 3rd Battalion. The operation unfolded in two attempts, and roughly 200 Polish paratroopers completed the crossing over two days, in part to facilitate the withdrawal of the remaining forces of the British 1st Airborne Division.

Paratroopers are present in many countries, with most nations maintaining one or more dedicated paratrooper units. These formations are typically affiliated with the national army or air force, reflecting their primary role in airborne operations. In a number of cases, paratrooper units are instead associated with naval forces.

Kappa Delta Chi began at Texas Tech University when four founders initiated efforts to secure formal recognition for the organization on campus. They enlisted Marlene Hernandez, the university’s associate director of new student relations, to serve as adviser. The founders then recruited ten women to promote the sorority’s ideals and philosophy among Hispanic women at Texas Tech, who became the sorority’s charter members: Rocio Briseno, Dahlia Cavazos, Melissa Chavez, Suzanna Cisneros, Mary Garza, Doris Mendiola, Maria Pando, Theresa Reyes, Christella Rivera, and Carline Soto.

Kappa Delta Chi (KDChi) adopted its official motto in 2008, a phrasing that emphasizes advancing with integrity while uniting members through service. Its guiding framework centers on four core pillars—unity, honesty, integrity, and leadership.

In the United States, the middle school model has largely supplanted the traditional junior high format, with roughly ten middle schools for every junior high school. Nevertheless, some districts continue to operate both systems or employ a hybrid arrangement that incorporates elements of both.

In Somalia, middle school, also known as intermediate school, comprises a four-year span between primary and secondary education. The program runs from form (year) 5 through year 8, with students typically beginning at age 11 and completing their studies around ages 14 to 15. The standard curriculum generally includes Somali, Arabic, and English language instruction, religious studies, science, geography, history, and mathematics, along with practical subjects such as textiles, art and design, and physical education, where football is often emphasized; music is sometimes offered. In a number of middle schools, Italian is a compulsory subject.

Luxembourg's industrial base was steel-dominated through the mid-20th century, after which it diversified into chemicals, rubber, and other products. In recent decades, growth in the financial sector has more than offset the decline in steel production, and services—especially banking and finance—now account for the majority of economic output. The country hosts the world's second-largest investment fund center, behind the United States, and is the eurozone's most important private banking hub as well as Europe’s leading center for reinsurance companies. The government has sought to attract Internet startups, with companies such as Skype and Amazon relocating their regional headquarters to Luxembourg. Other high-tech firms operate in Luxembourg, including Artec 3D, a developer and manufacturer of 3D scanners.

Luxembourg is divided into twelve cantons, which are further subdivided into a total of one hundred communes. Among these municipalities, twelve have been granted city status, and the city of Luxembourg is the largest commune in the country.

The Green Party of British Columbia conducted a leadership election from September 13 to 23, 2025, to select a successor to Sonia Furstenau, who resigned as party leader on January 28, 2025. Following Furstenau's departure, Jeremy Valeriote served as interim leader. The contest concluded on September 24, 2025, with Emily Lowan winning the leadership on the first ballot.

The 2025 leadership election of the Green Party of British Columbia followed the party’s performance in the 2024 provincial general election, which took place on October 19 and saw the Greens win two seats in the Legislative Assembly. Although Sonia Furstenau was defeated in the Victoria–Beacon Hill riding, she continued to serve as the party’s leader, providing continuity as the leadership contest proceeded.

Sastamala is a municipality in the Pirkanmaa region of Finland. It encompasses a total area of 1,531.75 square kilometers (591.41 square miles), of which 96.14 square kilometers (37.12 square miles) are covered by water, making it the largest municipality in Pirkanmaa by total area. The population density is 16.4 inhabitants per square kilometer (42 per square mile). The municipality is unilingual, with Finnish as the sole official language.

In 2015, Sastamala recorded 8,426 jobs, with employment shares distributed as 8.5 percent in primary production, 63 percent in services, and 27 percent in processing. The unemployment rate within the labor force stood at 12.3 percent. Among the municipality’s largest corporate taxpayers were Partnos, a building-design company; Teknikum, a producer of rubber and plastic products; and a manufacturer of reed valves used in district heating systems.

Omegathon is a festival-long tournament held at PAX, in which randomly selected attendees compete in a game bracket. The event unfolds during the convention, with the final round integrated into PAX closing ceremonies. Prizes for the grand winner have varied, including a large game bundle, a trip to Japan, or a trip to any PAX location around the world. Past final-round games have included Tetris, Pong, Halo 3, and skee-ball.

PAX Dev was an annual conference organized by Penny Arcade that ran from 2011 to 2020. The event aimed to provide game developers with a forum to discuss their work candidly and to focus exclusively on their craft, free from external media attention. Unlike many other industry gatherings such as the Game Developers Conference (GDC), press access was not permitted at PAX Dev. The first edition attracted about 750 attendees in 2011.

Beginning in 1992, Vietnamese migrant workers began arriving in Cambodia as UNTAC created employment opportunities in the transitional period following the peace process. UNTAC’s mandate allowed political offices and parties, including FUNCINPEC and the BLDP, and their campaigns helped propagate anti-Vietnamese sentiment to attract support in the 1993 elections. In November 1992, the Khmer Rouge, then in control of northwestern Cambodia, adopted a resolution targeting the systematic killing of Vietnamese soldiers and civilians. The following month, December 1992, saw the first guerrilla-style assaults by Khmer Rouge against Vietnamese civilians, with killings justified by claims that some victims were Vietnamese soldiers in disguise. By March 1993, approximately 21,000 ethnic Vietnamese had fled to Vietnam due to the killings.

Vietnamese Cambodians are an ethnic minority in Cambodia who have faced longstanding legal and social challenges. Following Cambodia's 1954 independence, the citizenship framework tied eligibility to proficiency in the Khmer language and to national origin, effectively excluding most Vietnamese Cambodians as well as Chinese Cambodians from obtaining citizenship. At the grassroots level, members of the Vietnamese community experienced periodic violent intimidation by some Cambodian compatriots. In 1962, during the Sangkum era, the congress discussed citizenship defined by ethnicity, and it ultimately approved a resolution denying naturalization to Vietnamese residents.

Although time has historically been regarded by logicians as an extralogical matter, the speaker does not share this conventional assessment. The speaker contends that logic has not yet developed sufficiently to introduce temporal modifications without inviting considerable confusion. Nevertheless, the speaker continues to largely adhere to the traditional view that time remains outside the scope of logic.

Temporal logic defines the admissible formulas through explicit formation rules that govern their construction. A unary operator produces a well-formed expression when its application to a formula, denoted B(φ), is itself well-formed. Similarly, a binary operator yields a well-formed formula only if both affected subformulas, B(φ) and C(φ), are well-formed. These guidelines together establish the recursive syntax used to express temporal properties.

Telecommunications in Switzerland are marked by high levels of internet usage. In 2021, 96% of the population aged 15–88 used the internet, indicating broad access and adoption across a wide segment of society. Among those aged 75 and over, more than half were daily internet users, reflecting substantial daily online engagement among seniors.

Over the past decade, the share of contract customers in Switzerland’s telecommunications market rose from 60% in 2012 to 83% in 2022. By 2022, contract subscribers accounted for 84.1% of Sunrise’s customer base, 83.4% of Swisscom’s, and 78.8% of Salt’s, illustrating differing levels of dependency on postpaid plans among the leading operators. In that year, the three major providers together gained more than 440,000 additional postpaid contract customers, highlighting a shift toward longer-term service commitments and a more stable revenue base in the Swiss telecom sector.

Master sergeant (MSG) is the eighth enlisted rank (pay grade E-8) in the United States Army. It sits above sergeant first class and below the positions of sergeant major, command sergeant major, and the Sergeant Major of the Army. Although it shares the same grade as a first sergeant, the two roles confer different authorities. The abbreviation MSG is used to designate the rank, and its insignia features three chevrons above three inverted arcs, often referred to as rockers.

Master sergeant insignia underwent a notable redesign in 1991 when the Air Force restricted noncommissioned officer insignia to five stripes or rockers at the bottom of the chevrons. The change removed the bottom sixth rocker and moved it above the five lower stripes as a single upper chevron, creating a two-tier arrangement that marks senior NCO status. The upper chevron indicates the senior NCO tier, with one above for E-7, two above for E-8, and three above for E-9. In 2015, the Air Force announced a reform of its promotion process and established new selection boards for master sergeant.

Chander Singh Rahi, often described as the Bhishma Pitamaha of Uttarakhand folk music, devoted his career to the preservation and promotion of the region’s traditional repertoire. He compiled and curated more than 2,500 Uttarakhand folk songs, creating a substantial archival resource for the genre. As a performer, he rendered over 500 songs in the principal regional languages, Garhwali and Kumaoni. He is credited with introducing the ghazal form to Garhwali singing, most notably with the piece Teri Mukhiri, marking a milestone in the cross-cultural development of Uttarakhand’s musical landscape.

Narendra Singh Negi (born 1949) is a prominent figure in Uttarakhand’s music scene, noted for performing and recording the region’s folk traditions, including Jagar, Chaumasa, and Thadya, as well as for his work in playback singing.
