His extensive repertoire exceeds one thousand songs composed in local languages such as Garhwali, Jaunsari, and Rawalti, illustrating the linguistic diversity of Uttarakhand’s musical landscape. Negi’s contributions have been recognized with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, one of India’s premier honors for the performing arts.

In the Blood was staged at the Schaeberle Studio Theatre on Pace University’s campus during fall 2004. The limited engagement lasted one week and sold out in its entirety, with the production described as well received by audiences.

In the Blood explores the oppression of the poor and the way individuals exploit one another within society. The central figure, Hester, is repeatedly taken advantage of by many people she confides in, underscoring her vulnerable position. Figures such as the Doctor, the Reverend, and Welfare are depicted as having stable homes and families, yet they contribute little to helping Hester and her children escape poverty, highlighting a pattern of social neglect. The title’s meaning is conveyed through Hester’s belief that adultery, poverty, and recklessness are in her blood, suggesting that these factors are perceived as inherent or inescapable parts of her identity rather than solely the product of circumstance.

Stefanie de Roux began her involvement in show business at age fifteen after participating in a charity fashion show to support cancer research, an early appearance that led to interest from an agency and launched her modeling career. She subsequently earned a degree in Corporate Communications from Southern Methodist University (SMU) in Dallas, Texas. She is the current director of a model school.
Stefanie de Roux is a pageant contestant who was a finalist in the 2006 Miss Earth competition. She has been included on Southern Methodist University's distinguished alumni list.

ATN SVBC is a Canadian exempt Category B Telugu-language specialty channel owned by Asian Television Network (ATN). It marked the introduction of Telugu-language broadcasting in Canada as the first channel of its kind, serving the Telugu-speaking audience nationwide. The channel is distributed via major providers, including Bell Fibe TV and Rogers Cable, facilitating access for subscribers across the country.

ATN SVBC is a devotional Bhakti channel that broadcasts Hindu devotional programming and provides live telecasts of poojas conducted by the Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams. These poojas are performed in Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh, India.

The Kahramanmaraş Grand Mosque was constructed under the patronage of Suleiman of the Dulkadirid dynasty, which ruled the Dulkadirid realm from 1442 to 1454. In 1501–1502, the mosque was renewed in a renovation carried out by Suleiman's son, Bozkurt of the Dulkadir.

The Kahramanmaraş Grand Mosque features a wooden roof. Unlike most mosques, its minaret is not constructed as part of the main building and is located in the surrounding yard. The minaret is adorned with ceramic plates.

Throughout 1976, cooperation between the Italian Communist Party (PCI) and Christian Democracy (DC) evolved into an ambivalent political alliance widely associated with the Historic Compromise. In a notable development, Prime Minister Moro invited Enrico Berlinguer to participate in an emergency meeting with the leaders of Italy’s major parties on March 17, 1976, to discuss measures aimed at averting an economic collapse. This emergent accord supplanted the Organic Centre-left governing bloc formed by the DC and other center-left factions. Within the PCI, Berlinguer’s leadership sought to distance the party from the Soviet Union. The period also saw the launch of Eurocommunism by the PCI, in collaboration with the Communist Party of Spain and the French Communist Party.

Known as the Historic Compromise, the accord sought to bring the Italian Communist Party more directly into national governance by accommodating it within a Christian Democratic-led framework, but it faced opposition from center-left groups such as the PRI and PSI, led by Ugo La Malfa and Bettino Craxi. Right-leaning Christian Democrat Giulio Andreotti expressed doubts about the arrangement. Among PCI sympathizers, estrangement arose because the party refused to rule out excluding the DC from power, fueling perceptions that the PCI was moving toward full collaboration with the DC. Within the PCI leadership, uncertainty persisted due to the vagueness of the arrangement and the lack of a clear programme. Former party secretary Luigi Longo criticized it as enigmatic and impracticable, warning that its ambiguity could foster passivity, while some argued that such vagueness might aid electoral appeal. Lucio Magri notes that Enrico Berlinguer enjoyed broad trust within the party and was not rebuked for a centrist shift on sensitive issues such as NATO membership.

Interdigital transducers (IDTs) convert electrical signals into surface acoustic waves (SAWs) by generating a periodically distributed pattern of mechanical forces in a piezoelectric substrate. This conversion relies on the piezoelectric effect, which couples electrical energy to acoustic wave propagation. Thus, IDTs function as input transducers that initiate SAW generation.

An interdigital transducer (IDT) is a device comprising two interlocking, comb-shaped arrays of metallic electrodes deposited on the surface of a piezoelectric substrate, giving it the appearance of a zipper. The electrode fingers are arranged on the substrate to form a periodic interdigitated structure. Common piezoelectric substrates used for IDTs include quartz and lithium niobate.

An institutional repository is a digital platform that enables researchers to submit and store digital copies of their scholarly outputs. By centralizing an institution’s research materials, such repositories can enhance the visibility of its work, promote greater usage by scholars and practitioners, and increase overall research impact. Beyond dissemination, they perform additional roles in knowledge management, facilitate assessments of research activity, and provide open access to scholarly research.

An institutional repository (IR) is a digital archive designed to collect, preserve, and disseminate the intellectual output of an institution, with particular emphasis on research organizations. It enables academics to deposit their published works to enhance visibility and facilitate collaboration with peers. Nevertheless, a substantial share of university-produced outputs remains difficult to access or share effectively with researchers and other stakeholders. Involving faculty and researchers in the design, implementation, and ongoing development of an IR can help them recognize the purpose and benefits of such a repository, supporting broader participation and long-term sustainability.

GfK Chart-Track is a United Kingdom–based market research organization that tracks sales of music, videos, and software. The company was established in 1996, and in July 2008, GfK acquired a majority stake in it, bringing Chart-Track under GfK's ownership.

GfK Chart-Track is a United Kingdom–based company that compiles the country's official software charts for the entertainment software industry, doing so on behalf of UKIE. Its key reporting services include the UK Leisure Software chart and the UK Hardware and Peripherals chart.

Within contemporary psychiatry, two principal classification schemes for mental disorders provide structured categories and standardized diagnostic criteria: the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM) and the International Classification of Diseases (ICD). In recent revisions, the codes used by these manuals have been increasingly harmonized, enabling greater cross-system comparability, although notable divergences remain. Outside Western contexts, other classification schemes are used, such as the Chinese Classification of Mental Disorders, reflecting regional and cultural variations in diagnostic practice. Additionally, some practitioners follow manuals developed to accommodate alternative theoretical perspectives, for example the Psychodynamic Diagnostic Manual. In clinical practice, mental disorders are typically categorized separately from neurological disorders, learning disabilities, or intellectual disability, reflecting distinct classificatory domains rather than a single global system.

In clinical practice, time and budget constraints often prevent thorough diagnostic evaluations by practicing psychiatrists, leading many clinicians to rely on unstructured, open-ended assessment approaches. This situation is exacerbated by limited training in evidence-based assessment methods, which can contribute to the prevalence of inaccurate diagnoses in routine care. Comorbidity is very common, with numerous individuals meeting criteria for more than one disorder; some people present multiple difficulties but only a portion meet formal diagnostic criteria. Additionally, there may be specific challenges to accurate diagnosis in developing countries, where resource limitations and systemic factors can further impede precise identification of psychiatric conditions.

Newton Advanced Fellowships are awards for established international researchers, designed to strengthen the research strengths and capabilities of the recipient's research group through collaboration and capacity-building activities. The program is funded by the Newton Fund as part of the United Kingdom's official development assistance.

Fellowship of the Royal Society (FRS), Foreign Member (ForMemRS), and Honorary Fellow (HonFRS) constitute the principal honors awarded by the Fellows of the Royal Society of London. The award recognizes individuals who have made substantial contributions to the improvement of natural knowledge, across a range of disciplines that includes mathematics, engineering science, and medical science. The abbreviations indicate the distinct categories within the fellowship: FRS for a standard Fellow, ForMemRS for a foreign member, and HonFRS for an honorary fellow.

Richard A. Jones (born 1950) was born in Seattle, Washington. He is the son of Quincy Delight Jones Sr. and his second wife. His father worked as a semi-professional baseball player and a carpenter. He has a half-brother named Quincy Jones, a renowned musician and producer, who is seventeen years his senior.

Richard A. Jones attended Seattle public schools. He earned a Bachelor of Public Administration from Seattle University in 1972 and a Juris Doctor from the University of Washington School of Law in 1975. He was admitted to the Washington State Bar Association in 1977.

During the Nickelodeon broadcast of an NFL game, Sean Payton volunteered to be slimed and was subsequently subjected to the slime following the Saints’ 21–9 victory. A communication disconnect prevented Cameron Jordan from joining Payton in the slime segment. Sideline reporter Lex Lumpkin also attempted to participate in the sliming but did not end up taking part.

Nickelodeon's presentation of the NFL for Super Bowl LVIII was billed as Super Bowl LVIII: Live from Bikini Bottom, featuring SpongeBob-themed augmented reality effects throughout the telecast. Burleson and Eagle returned to call the game, while Gilmer and Schefter served as sideline reporters. In a distinctive integration, the SpongeBob characters provided live commentary during the game, with SpongeBob SquarePants voiced by Tom Kenny, Sandy Cheeks by Carolyn Lawrence, Larry the Lobster by Mr. Lawrence, and Patrick by Fagerbakke. The broadcast opened with a three-dimensional animated rendition of the "Sweet Victory" sequence from the SpongeBob episode Band Geeks. Additionally, as cross-promotion, CBS aired an episode of NFL Slimetime as part of its pre-game programming for the game.

Phil Collins and producer Hugh Padgham sought to reproduce the distinctive Sixties drum sound of the original You Can't Hurry Love, aiming for a faithful remake rather than a new interpretation. The effort faced the reality that modern recording facilities, while technologically advanced, can complicate attempts to recreate the raw, punchy drum texture characteristic of the era. The principal challenge lay in capturing the gritty drum character of the 1960s within a contemporary studio environment.

"You Can't Hurry Love" is built around a mother's admonition that romantic love cannot be hurried and must be allowed to develop in its own time, presenting patience as essential to finding lasting affection. The track is inspired by, and in part based on, a 1950s gospel song titled "(You Can't Hurry God) He's Right on Time," whose central message emphasizes not rushing divine timing and the importance of trusting the process. That gospel piece was written by Dorothy Love Coates of the Original Gospel Harmonettes.

In 2018, Viacom acquired AwesomenessTV for an estimated $50 million. The transaction followed NBCUniversal's purchase of DreamWorks Animation and the shutdown of go90, amid tensions arising from DreamWorks’ ownership by Comcast, a company that competes with Verizon. The deal represented only a fraction of AwesomenessTV's valuation in 2016. Since the acquisition, the studio has shifted toward developing long-form television series and feature films, with its more recent productions mainly for Paramount+ and Nickelodeon.

In October 2025, Paramount Global merged with Skydance Media to form Paramount Skydance. As part of the consolidation, Awesomeness and Nickelodeon’s live-action production arm and its slate, including XO, Kitty and School Spirits, were absorbed into Paramount Skydance’s Paramount Television Studios during the production of the Victorious spin-off Hollywood Arts. Hollywood Arts had been ordered at the former Awesomeness/Nickelodeon live-action production facility. Paramount Television Studios assumed production of Awesomeness and Nickelodeon’s live-action unit and slate beginning with Hollywood Arts. A week later, it was announced that Awesomeness would be merged into Paramount Television Studios following Paramount’s absorption of its production assets.

Slow Jamz is a song associated with Kanye West that originated after a party hosted by Jamie Foxx, attended by prominent figures including Sean Combs, Missy Elliott, the Neptunes, and Jay-Z; it was there that Foxx met a then-injured West, who had recently recovered from a car crash in which his jaw was shattered. West performed a freestyle at the gathering that impressed Foxx and led to an invitation for Foxx to visit West’s recording studio to record the track. Foxx had originally sung the song’s hook, which referenced classic soul artists Marvin Gaye and Luther Vandross, but West ridiculed Foxx’s singing, insisting that the piece belonged to hip hop rather than R&B, leaving Foxx doubtful about his prospects in music. In a 2017 Power 106 interview, Foxx explained that his eagerness to crossover into a broader audience motivated him to host parties with leading musicians in the hope of future collaborations.

Slow Jamz is a track by Kanye West featuring Jamie Foxx and Twista. Foxx delivers the chorus in a smooth croon over a brisk, drum-driven groove. After West’s opening verse, Aisha Tyler urges a faster tempo, prompting West to concede that Twista can accelerate. Twista responds with a rapid six-beat verse delivered in a staccato cadence atop a relaxed, groove-based instrumental, name-dropping several artists. The verse blends streetwise bravado with R&B sensibilities and contains references to Luther Vandross. Lyrically, the song alludes to earlier slow-jam icons such as Marvin Gaye, Vandross, and Anita Baker, as well as to 1980s R&B groups, through puns and allusions. Music critic Jon Caramanica of The Village Voice observed that West's measured rap allows Twista's brisk verse to complete the song’s narrative arc.

The Mainland Travel Permit for Taiwan Resident functioned as a de facto identification document for Taiwan residents in mainland China. The policy was influenced by increasing long-term stays and settlement of Taiwanese people in the mainland. By 24 September 2008, the serial number assigned to the permit was fixed for the holder’s lifetime. In September 2018, the Residence Permit for Taiwan Residents was issued, superseding the Mainland Travel Permit for Taiwan Residents in its identification role.

The Mainland Travel Permit for Taiwan Residents, issued by the Exit and Entry Administration of the People's Republic of China, is a card-size biometric travel document presented to Taiwan residents for travel to the Chinese mainland. It is also known as the Taiwan Compatriot Permit or Taiwan Compatriot Pass. Since 2017, holders have been able to stay in mainland China indefinitely for any purpose, including employment and study, with no restrictions.

Beach nourishment is a coastal management technique that replenishes eroding shorelines with sand to widen beaches and restore dune systems, thereby reducing erosion and protecting upland areas. The freshly deposited sand can harden over time, potentially hindering sea turtle nest digging and influencing nesting success. At the same time, nourishment can enhance habitat quality and availability for sea turtles, seabirds, and beach vegetation by increasing habitat complexity and vegetation cover. In Florida, to address the risk of turtles being drawn into dredge pumps during nourishment operations, authorities installed a specialized grill on the dredge pipes to prevent entrainment.

Beach nourishment involves adding sand along a shoreline to widen the dry beach area and raise the beach profile, thereby improving resilience to storms. The success of such projects is assessed by tracking changes in the dry beach width and elevation, as well as the total volume of sand in the nourished zone, including the portion that remains submerged in the nearshore (aqueous sand volume). After storm events, analysts evaluate the remaining sand volume to understand sediment loss and redistribution. They also conduct assessments of damages avoided by the widened beach to determine the extent to which the nourishment mitigates impacts to infrastructure and coastal ecosystems, informing maintenance planning and future management decisions.

The Sao civilization developed to the south of Lake Chad along the Chari River, with origins traced to the 6th century BCE and enduring for more than a millennium in areas that now lie within modern Cameroon and Chad. Their material culture reveals sophisticated bronze, copper, and iron workmanship, including bronze sculptures, terracotta figurines of both humans and animals, coins, funerary urns, domestic utensils, jewelry, decorated pottery, and spears. In the southwest of Cameroon, the Ekoi civilization arose around Lake Ejagham, with origins dating to roughly the 2nd century CE. The Ekoi are particularly noted for the Ikom monoliths and for the development of the Nsibidi writing system.

Homo sapiens originated in Africa between about 350,000 and 260,000 years before present, after which the continent was largely populated by hunter-gatherer communities. Around 50,000 years ago, a later migratory wave—often described as Out of Africa II—led to the spread of modern humans to the rest of the globe. Exits from Africa occurred via three principal routes: Bab-el-Mandeb at the southern end of the Red Sea, the Strait of Gibraltar between Africa and Europe, and the Isthmus of Suez in northeastern Egypt.

In Ireland, there are more than 4,500 commonages, with grazing rights held by roughly 11,000 to 14,000 farmers. About 4,260 square kilometres (1,640 square miles; 1,050,000 acres) of commonage are currently grazed. Grazing activity is heavily concentrated in the counties of Mayo, Galway, Sligo, Donegal, Kerry, and Wicklow. The land is predominantly used for sheep grazing in upland areas. In the 1980s and 1990s, overgrazing damaged hill ecosystems and river banks, leading to tighter controls on grazing; today the numbers of grazing animals are limited.

Among the historical notions surrounding common land was a widespread but erroneous belief that a squatter could secure undisturbed possession by erecting a house on such land within a single day, from dawn to dusk, a practice popularly known as “keyhole tenure.” Although this belief persisted into the early twentieth century, it is regarded as a fallacy. To deter landless peasants from unlawfully squatting on commons, the Erection of Cottages Act 1588 (31 Eliz. 1. c. 7) was enacted.

In Christian belief, the crucifixion and the subsequent resurrection of Jesus are central events that shape the understanding of his identity and mission. These occurrences provide a substantial foundation for Christological analysis, inviting examination of how Jesus is portrayed and interpreted as the Messiah, the Son of God, and the savior of humanity. The inquiry spans a range of sources, extending from the canonical gospels to the Pauline epistles, reflecting how early Christian communities articulated Jesus’ work and significance. Through these texts, scholars and theologians explore questions about Jesus’ nature, his role in salvation, and the meaning of his death and resurrection within the broader Christian narrative. Together, the gospel accounts and Paul’s letters offer a comprehensive framework for understanding Jesus within the Christian tradition.

In Christology, the concept of the Logos underpins the divinity of Jesus and his status as God the Son within the Trinity. This understanding is linked with the Chalcedonian Creed, which articulates the doctrinal framework for Christ’s two natures in one person. The idea originates with the opening of the Gospel of John, which presents the Word as existing from the beginning with God and as God. The Greek term λόγος means “Word,” and in theological discourse it is commonly retained in its transliterated form as Logos.

Cornelis Corneliszoon, also known as Krelis Lootjes, was a Dutch windmill owner from Uitgeest. In 1593 he invented the earliest wind-powered sawmill, a breakthrough that dramatically increased timber production by enabling logs to be converted into planks at roughly thirty times the speed of earlier manually operated sawmills.

Rough-sawn lumber refers to timber that has not yet been milled to standardized dimensions and, as a result, should not be confused with milled dimension lumber, which is sized by its actual thickness after processing. Milled dimension lumber is measured after machining to reflect its true, finished dimensions, enabling consistent specifications across projects. Rough-sawn sizes illustrate pre-finish designations, with examples such as 3/4-inch, 19 mm, or 1x. In contemporary practice, architects, designers, and builders have increasingly adopted the quarter system in specifications for finished lumber; however, because this system is used alongside other sizing conventions, it can blur distinctions between different measurement schemes and lead to confusion.

Plans to redevelop Lansdowne Park in Ottawa to accommodate a Canadian Football League franchise prompted a public two-day debate on November 12–13, featuring guest speakers that included CFL Commissioner Mark Cohon and former Rough Riders Jock Climie and Mark Kosmos, who argued that the Lansdowne Live proposal would be a significant boon for the city. On November 16, the city council voted 15–9 in favor of the redevelopment plan to house a CFL team. The ownership group was given until June 2010 to finalize redevelopment details, with construction slated to begin in spring 2011.

During December 2012, the Canadian Football League conducted an online public voting process to determine a name for the Ottawa franchise, hosting six days of voting on the Name Our Teams website. Although speculation suggested the name might be "Rush," this possibility was later debunked. In January 2013, a focus group organized by the team's owners reviewed a shortlist of five potential names, which included Rush alongside Nationals, Voyageurs, Redblacks, and Raftsmen.

Within endorheic basins, relatively humid regions can occur at high elevations. These zones tend to be marshy and prone to substantial flooding in wet years. The region surrounding Mexico City exemplifies such a high-altitude humid area within an endorheic basin. It receives about 850 mm (33 inches) of annual precipitation and features waterlogged soils that require drainage.

An endorheic basin is a closed drainage system with no outlet to the sea. Buena Vista Lake lies at the southern end of the San Joaquin Valley in Southern California and historically received water from the Kern River. In exceptionally wet years, its surface could contribute to Tulare Lake and ultimately the San Joaquin River system. Due to extensive agricultural development and irrigation diversions in the region, inflows declined and the lake has since dried up, leaving the basin without standing surface water.

Chongnyon Jonwi was one of three North Korean newspapers that jointly published New Year editorials during Kim Jong Il's rule, alongside Rodong Sinmun and Joson Inmingun. After Kim Jong Il ceased delivering New Year addresses to live audiences, the editorials were issued collectively by the three papers. The first joint New Year editorial appeared in 1995, with the last published in 2012. Rodong Sinmun serves as the official organ of the Workers' Party of Korea, while Joson Inmingun is the military newspaper of the Korean People's Army; together with Chongnyon Jonwi, these publications are linked to North Korea's three principal organizations—the party, the army, and the youth league—and are considered among the most influential outlets in the country. However, Fyodor Tertitskiy of NK News has argued that Chongnyon Jonwi does not carry the same level of significance as its two counterparts.

In November 2022, ICG plc announced the acquisition of Dos Grados, a Madrid-headquartered renewable energy platform. The deal was conducted on behalf of ICG’s inaugural Infrastructure Fund, ICG Infra, which has a fund size of €1.5 billion (US$1.56 billion).

ICG plc is a private equity investment firm that concentrates on providing capital to support the growth of companies through both private and public markets. The firm offers a range of investment strategies and funds designed for institutional investors. Based in London, England, it maintains a global presence with offices in 17 other countries. ICG plc is a constituent of the FTSE 100 Index.

Wild Horse Mesa (1932 film) is a 1932 American Pre-Code Western directed by Henry Hathaway, starring Randolph Scott and Sally Blane. The production is based on the novel Wild Horse Mesa by Zane Grey and serves as a remake of Paramount's 1925 silent film of the same name.

In 1562, Diego Gutiérrez published a map titled Americae Sive Quartae Orbis Partis Nova Et Exactissima Descriptio. The work appeared in Antwerp, then part of the Spanish Netherlands, and was produced in collaboration with the printer Hieronymus Cock. Antwerp was chosen because Spanish engravers lacked the necessary skill to print such a technically demanding plate.

Diego Gutiérrez was a Spanish cosmographer and cartographer affiliated with the Casa de la Contratación. He was appointed to his post by royal appointment on 22 October 1554, following the death of his father, Diego Gutiérrez, in January 1554. In this capacity, he worked on the Padrón Real, the master map used on all royal sailing ships in the Spanish fleet.

Wembley Arena's on-site parking is shared with Wembley Stadium and consists of two facilities: an open-air surface car park around the eastern flank of the stadium known as the Green Car Park, and a multi-storey car park known as the Red Car Park. Disabled parking is provided at Green Car Park, offered at a reduced rate and on a first-come, first-served basis.

Wembley Arena was designed by engineer Sir Owen Williams with no architect engaged in the project. The design employs cantilevers that meet at the center to eliminate the need for internal supporting columns, allowing a clear interior space. It was constructed with high-quality concrete and rests on a reinforced concrete frame of three-hinged arches spanning 240 feet (73 meters), a span that was the largest of its kind in the world at that time. The choice of materials and the structural form contributed to notable durability, with the building aging better than many contemporary structures from the same era.

Boosey & Hawkes is a British music publisher, often described as the world's largest specialist publisher of classical music. Until 2003, the company also operated as a major manufacturer of brass, string, and woodwind instruments.

Boosey & Hawkes traces its origins to the Franco-Flemish Boosey family. The enterprise that would become Boosey & Company was founded by John Boosey, a London bookseller active in the 1760s and 1770s. His son Thomas continued the business at 4 Old Bond Street. By 1819 the bookseller had adopted the name Boosey & Sons, sometimes rendered as T. & T. Boosey.

On 4 July 2021, Khogen Singh was appointed head coach for NEROCA FC ahead of the 2021–22 I-League season, and the side opened its league campaign with a 3–2 victory over Sreenidi Deccan on 27 December 2021. In the 2021–22 I-League, the club finished seventh, and it participated in the 2022 Durand Cup. The following season, the 2022–23 I-League, saw NEROCA finish in tenth place, and the team did not qualify for the 2023 Indian Super Cup. In October 2023, Jacob Joseph was named head coach for the 2023–24 season. In April 2024, NEROCA and TRAU declined to travel to Mizoram to play Aizawl, leading the AIFF to cancel the matches and relegate both clubs to I-League 2. For the 2024–25 I-League 2 season, NEROCA participated and contended in the relegation battle alongside TRAU.

NEROCA FC is a professional football club that has included players who have earned international caps for their countries at senior or youth levels. These internationals represented their national teams either before they joined NEROCA FC or after their tenure with the club.

Hawaiian Vacation portrays Ken and Barbie sharing their first kiss outside Bonnie’s house at sunset, echoing a scene from a brochure. They step off the porch edge and are buried in the snow, from which they are later dug out by Bonnie’s toys. The toys then release them from a block of ice with the aid of a hair dryer and a screwdriver.

Hawaiian Vacation is a 2011 American computer-animated short film produced by Pixar Animation Studios. Directed by Gary Rydstrom, it is the first entry in the Toy Story Toons series. The film features Toy Story characters and is set after the events of Toy Story 3. It premiered in theaters alongside Cars 2 and was later included on the Cars 2 home video release.

Halim El-Dabh, an Egyptian composer, is regarded as a leading figure among the early pioneers of electronic music. He operated in the same era as, and perhaps even earlier than, the French Studio d’Essai electronic collaborators who helped inaugurate electronic experimentation. He is commonly described as one of the first composers to create music entirely through electronic means. In 1944, while a student in Cairo, he produced The Expression of Zar, an early example of tape music within the musique concrète tradition and among the earliest such works. The piece was composed in Egypt by recording street sounds on a wire recorder, which were subsequently manipulated to form the final work.

In Egypt, music is deeply tied to religious life, with traditional mulids playing a central role in both Sufi Muslim and Coptic Christian celebrations. These festivals honor the saint associated with a particular church or, in the Muslim context, an esteemed local figure, and they are often connected to the Sufi zikr ritual, a devotional practice of remembrance. The ney, a iconic Egyptian flute, is commonly featured at mulids, contributing to the distinctive sound of these gatherings. In addition to festival music, the liturgical music of the Alexandrian Rite constitutes an important element of Egyptian musical culture and is regarded as preserving many features of ancient Egyptian musical practice.

Newsquest was founded in 1995 through a management buy-out financed by the U.S. private equity firm Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR). The £210 million transaction allowed the management team to acquire the Reed Regional Newspapers group, a portfolio of British regional titles, from Reed Elsevier.

Newsquest Media Group Limited is the second-largest publisher of regional and local newspapers in the United Kingdom, operating a substantial portfolio of titles across multiple regions. It is owned by Gannett Co., Inc., an American mass media holding company.

End-to-end encryption protocols ensure that only the intended endpoints can access plaintext messages, with endpoint authentication a key mechanism for preventing man-in-the-middle incursions. Common authentication methods include the use of certificates issued by trusted authorities (CAs) or the establishment of a web of trust. An alternative approach is to generate cryptographic fingerprints, or hashes, of the communicating parties’ public keys or of their shared secret keys. These fingerprints are then compared via an out-of-band channel that guarantees integrity and authenticity, though it does not necessarily assure secrecy. The verification takes place before any conversational data is exchanged. When the fingerprints align, a man-in-the-middle attack is, in principle, ruled out.

During the 2025 Minneapolis City Council election, Millard's campaign received backing from the We Love Minneapolis PAC. The PAC, which dissolved after its activities, reported a $30,000 contribution from Hornig Properties, a corporate landlord based in Ward 10, in its first quarter of operation. Claims have been made that Millard's team benefited from door-knocking assistance arranged through Hornig Properties. Jim Rubin, owner of Mint Properties, a prominent Ward 10 landlord, has been identified as a leader of the PAC.

The 2025 Minneapolis City Council election follows the 2023 results, which produced a progressive-leaning, democratic socialist majority that displaced a previously more moderate bloc. The core progressive faction comprises Payne, Chavez, Wonsley, Chughtai, Chowdhury, Ellison, and Cashman, while the moderates are represented by Jenkins, Rainville, Vetaw, and Palmisano, with Koski having formerly served on the council. In 2023, Wonsley, Chughtai, Chowdhury, and Chavez received endorsements from the Twin Cities chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America, whereas Chowdhury was not endorsed for the 2025 race. The two largest campaign committees in both 2023 and 2025 are All of Mpls, which generally backs moderates, and Mpls for the Many, which endorses progressives. Councilmember Jamal Osman did not receive endorsements from either PAC in 2023, but in practice has voted more often with the progressives. Emily Koski has been identified as the council’s most reliable swing vote, supporting moderates and progressives in roughly equal measure; she is retiring from the council and had launched a mayoral bid, which was withdrawn in April.
Song Cry was included in the setlists of two all-stadium tours, the On the Run Tour (2014) and OTR II (2018). Both tours were co-headlined by Beyoncé, who is Jay-Z's wife.

"Song Cry" is a slow, subdued melodic rap ballad by Jay-Z that centers on a breakup caused by the narrator's neglect and infidelity. The lyrics portray the artist acknowledging that pride prevents him from publicly displaying emotions, with the track functioning as a controlled outlet for mourning that allows tears to be expressed within the song without compromising his masculine image as a street hustler. In its exploration of vulnerability, the piece engages with the notion that emotional openness is often viewed as a weakness, a stance that resonates with broader discussions within the Black community about men suppressing vulnerability in order to survive.

Jit is a brisk, highly danceable Zimbabwean beat that invites listeners to move. A number of dances are associated with Jit, including hwishu, tuwisti, kongonya, borodhero, honda, chipisi, and others, reflecting the genre’s wide repertoire. The most prominent Jit dance is Bhorodhero, whose popularity is largely attributed to its incorporation into the repertoires of Alick Macheso and System Tazvida’s Chazezesa Challengers. The name Bhorodhero derives from Borrowdale Race Course in Harare. The dance is typified by movements that resemble a galloping horse.

Jit is a musical tradition that developed from communal singing in a circle, typically accompanied by one or two Mutumba drums. The percussionists play the Mutumba in coordinated rhythms that align with the vocal lines, creating a tight interlocking accompaniment. A lead vocalist initiates the song, while other participants respond in a call-and-response pattern. At times the group performs together in harmony, enriching the overall texture. The lead may incorporate chanting, with responders providing space for ad-libbing before delivering the ensuing answer.

During the 2004 Democratic National Convention in Boston, peace advocates staged a rally a few hundred feet from the FleetCenter. Local Boston politicians joined Dennis Kucinich and Tom Hayden at the event. The gathering urged an end to the Iraq occupation, calling for the withdrawal of U.S. troops and the deployment of an international peacekeeping force. Hayden and Kucinich also urged antiwar Democrats to support John Kerry in the general election against President George W. Bush.

Boston's designation as the host city for the 2004 Democratic National Convention strained lodging capacity in the Boston metropolitan area. The ensuing hotel shortage influenced related events, leading the Reebok Pro Summer League to fold its operations into the Las Vegas Summer League, which was a relatively new venture at that time. As a result, the two leagues were consolidated under the Las Vegas Summer League umbrella, effectively merging their programs and schedules.
Michael Joseph Oakeshott (11 December 1901 – 19 December 1990) was an English philosopher noted for his contributions to the philosophy of history, religion, aesthetics, education, and law.

Michael Oakeshott, an English philosopher and political theorist, lived to witness growing recognition of his work, and since his death he has been the subject of substantially more extensive scholarship and discussion. He declined an offer to be made a Companion of Honour, an invitation that had been proposed by Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher.

Negotiations over a new Sino-Soviet Treaty of Friendship, Alliance and Mutual Assistance centered on Mao Zedong's demand for military aid to back an operation against Taiwan. Stalin declined to provide such assistance, arguing that it would give the United States a pretext to intervene. After Stalin’s 70th birthday, Mao pressed for the treaty but Moscow remained unwilling to commit to military support and suggested Mao consult Stalin’s associates instead. Mao chose to wait, while rumors spread that he was being held by Stalin; in response, both sides sought clarification and arranged an interview with Mao for the Soviet news agency TASS, an exchange that is regarded as marking a turning point in the treaty discussions.

Following the Communist victory in China, Mao Zedong announced the “leaning to one side” policy on July 1, 1949, signaling an alignment with the Soviet-led socialist bloc and a rejection of any third way in foreign affairs. In a world increasingly divided between socialist and imperialist camps, Beijing sought to consolidate the Communist regime amid both internal and external threats. China thus firmly aligned with the Soviet Union and joined the socialist camp, presenting such cooperation as evidence of goodwill and a means to secure development assistance, in part contrasted with Western initiatives like the Marshall Plan, which Beijing viewed as exploitative U.S. influence. Central to this approach was China's aim of rapid industrialization, pursued with the aid of Soviet economic and technological support, which in turn helped drive the 1950 Sino-Soviet Treaty of Friendship, Alliance and Mutual Assistance and deepen bilateral security and economic cooperation within the socialist bloc.

Following the October Revolution, Butyrka served as a detention site for political prisoners. During the Great Purge, the facility at times housed as many as twenty thousand inmates concurrently. A substantial number of these detainees were executed after investigations. Notable political prisoners held there during Stalin's rule included writers Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn and Yevgenia Ginzburg.

Butyrka prison, a historic facility in Moscow, has its current structure dating from 1879 and stands near the Butyrsk gate on the site of a fortress-like prison. That earlier fortress-like complex on the same site was designed by architect Matvei Kazakov during the reign of Catherine the Great. The older towers housed hundreds of participants of the 1863 January Uprising in Poland. In the late 19th century, the prison also held members of Narodnaya Volya who were imprisoned there in 1883, as well as participants in the Morozov Strike of 1885. Butyrka became infamous for its harsh regime, with the administration frequently resorting to violence in response to inmate protests.

Since 1999, the deputy first minister has been empowered to perform the duties of the first minister and to assume the office's powers during the absence or incapacity of the incumbent. Jim Wallace, who held the post of deputy first minister, served as acting first minister on two occasions. He first did so from 11 October 2000 to 26 October 2000 after the death of Donald Dewar, with his tenure ending when Labour appointed a new leader and thus a new first minister. Wallace again acted as first minister from 8 November 2001 to 22 November 2001 following Henry McLeish’s resignation.

Donald Dewar's tenure as First Minister of Scotland included five international visits to Belgium, the Republic of Ireland, the Netherlands, Japan, and a second visit to Ireland; he died in October 2000. His successor, Henry McLeish, conducted six international visits—Italy; three visits to Belgium; the United States; Finland; and a joint visit to Japan and Taiwan. McLeish also led the Scottish Executive's response to the September 11 attacks in the United States. Earlier in his tenure he expressed concerns about Scotland's defence strategy, warning that Glasgow, Edinburgh and Aberdeen could be targeted due to their economic significance to Scottish, UK and European economies.

The music video for "Grace" premiered on YouTube on 21 September 2018 and runs three minutes and thirty-two seconds. In the clip, Lewis Capaldi steps in for a friend at a local gentlemen's club, presenting the performance as part of a lighthearted narrative. The concept draws inspiration from Napoleon Dynamite's choreographed dance scenes and the British television comedy series I'm Alan Partridge.
In November 2018, during a live show in London, Lewis Capaldi performed Grace with an onstage recreation of its choreography, featuring male dancers as part of the routine.

In 1938, the Behistun Inscription attracted the attention of the Ahnenerbe, the Nazi German research organization associated with the regime. Plans to conduct scholarly investigations into the inscription were subsequently abandoned with the outbreak of World War II, halting further Nazi-era research on the site.

The Behistun Inscription, also known by its variants Bisotun or Bisutun and bearing the Old Persian toponym Bagastana meaning “the place of god,” is a monumental Achaemenid royal inscription accompanied by a large rock relief carved on a cliff at Mount Behistun in western Iran. It is located in Kermanshah Province near the city of Kermanshah. Commissioned by Darius the Great, who ruled from 522 to 486 BCE, the monument serves as a key royal record of his reign. The inscription is especially notable for its crucial role in the decipherment of cuneiform, as it is the longest known trilingual cuneiform text, containing Old Persian, Elamite, and Babylonian (Akkadian) versions.

Shima was an autonomous district within the historical Ise Province and developed as a prosperous coastal fishing region. In the Nara period, its governors sent annual gifts of fish and abalone to the Emperor, reflecting its economic connections to the central court. The district separated from Ise Province in the late seventh or early eighth century, establishing a distinct administrative entity. Throughout the Asuka and early Nara periods, Shima came under the influence and control of the Takahashi clan. Owing to its scant arable land, portions of the rice lands in Ise, Mikawa, and Owari were counted as Shima’s taxable revenues to support its capital and the associated shrines and temples.

Shima Province (志摩国, Shima no Kuni) was a historic province of Japan, consisting of a peninsula in the southeastern part of what is now Mie Prefecture. Its abbreviated name was Shishū (志州). The province bordered Ise Province to the west and was surrounded by Ise Bay on the north, east, and south. Geographically, it roughly corresponds to the modern municipalities of Shima and Toba. In Japanese, the name is pronounced [ɕiꜜ.ma (no kɯ.ɲi)].

Aubrey de Sélincourt withdrew from active work in 1947 and settled in Niton on the Isle of Wight, where he devoted himself to writing. He died in December 1962 at Niton, his death following the publication of The World of Herodotus, one of his most successful books.

Aubrey de Sélincourt served as editor of The Oxford Magazine from 1927 to 1929. He contributed to the Manchester Guardian, the English Review, and The Times Literary Supplement, among other periodicals. A keen yachtsman, he wrote several books on sailing.

Reed Tech offers a suite of intellectual property products and services that span data capture and conversion, digital preservation, analysis, e-submission, and publication for corporate, legal, and government clients. In 2013, the company partnered with PatentCore to launch PatentAdvisor, a tool that provides searchable and filterable access to historical behavior data for nearly all U.S. patent examiners and art units, targeted at patent attorneys and IP‑driven firms to assist in prosecution and portfolio management. Its IP Services division, formerly ReedFax, delivers document retrieval, translations, and research and analysis of both U.S. and international patent documents.

Reed Tech specializes in electronic data conversion and regulatory submissions for the life sciences sector. The company supports the U.S. FDA's Structured Product Labeling (SPL) standard and the European Medicines Agency's XEVMPD format, and has collaborated with both the pharmaceutical industry and the U.S. Food and Drug Administration since SPL was introduced in 2005. It participates as a member of the HL7 working group. Additionally, Reed Tech provides label printing and publishing solutions based on SPL XML, enabling the reuse of FDA-approved drug labels for printed marketing and manufacturing materials.

The article presents the list of seeded players for the women's singles at the 2025 Australian Open. Seedings are determined by the WTA rankings as of 6 January 2025, while the rankings and points used for pre-tournament comparison are those published on 13 January 2025.

At the 2025 Australian Open women's singles, Madison Keys defeated two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka in the final, 6–3, 2–6, 7–5, to capture her first major title. Keys had previously saved a match point in the semifinals against Iga Świątek. The triumph set an Open Era record for the longest gap between two major final appearances by a woman, surpassing the seven-year interval previously held by Amélie Mauresmo (1999–2006 Australian Open) and Victoria Azarenka (2013–2020 US Open). Additionally, Keys became the fourth Open Era woman to defeat four top-10 seeds on her path to a major title, following Evonne Goolagong Cawley (1980 Wimbledon), Mary Pierce (1995 Australian Open), and Li Na (2011 French Open).

The list comprises political parties and related organizations around the world that identify with democratic socialism or host a substantial democratic socialist current within their ranks. Many entries do not explicitly include the label “Democratic Socialist” in their official names, despite aligning with the ideology. Several members also participate in international groupings such as Socialist International, the Progressive International, the São Paulo Forum, the Party of European Left, and the Progressive Alliance.

The Executive Council, established in 1949 and chaired by the Lieutenant Governor with participation from Tynwald members, gradually came to function as the Isle of Man’s effective government. In 1980 the Lieutenant Governor ceased to chair the body, with the chairmanship taken by a member elected by Tynwald. A further reconstitution in 1985 broadened the council to include the chairmen of the eight principal boards of Tynwald. In 1986 those chairmen were given the title Minister, while the chair was designated Chief Minister. The council was renamed the Council of Ministers in 1990.

The Council of Ministers functions as the principal executive organ of the Isle of Man Government. In Manx Gaelic, it is known as Coonseil ny Shirveishee, and it is informally abbreviated as CoMin. Its role is similar to, though not identical with, the Cabinet of the United Kingdom. The body was known as the Executive Council until 1990.

Novell published online videos that parodied Apple's Get a Mac advertising campaign as a strategy to promote Linux. In one installment, the Linux figure is depicted as a stylish, young woman, while a separate set presents Linux as a stereotypical male computer nerd.

Get a Mac is a marketing campaign by Apple that personifies a Mac and a PC in a series of television advertisements. In the spots, the PC is depicted warning the Mac about a new computer virus, portrayed as a cold, and advising the Mac to stay away. The PC character cites about 114,000 known viruses targeting PCs to emphasize the perceived threat. The Mac character counters by claiming that viruses directed at PCs do not affect it. In a later exchange, the PC states that he will crash and faint, signaling an imminent collapse of the PC.

Roche moutonnée is a landform produced by glacial abrasion, characterized by a smooth up-glacier surface and a steeper, lee-facing side shaped by glacial processes. In Sweden, the larger instances of this feature are known as flyggbergs; Swedish researchers including Sten Rudberg have interpreted these flyggbergs as reshaped inselbergs. Additionally, ice-smoothed bedrock bumps that lack a pronounced steep, plucked lee-side face are referred to as whalebacks or rock drumlins.

Roche moutonnée are glacially sculpted bedrock features formed as a glacier moves over the rock, typically presenting a smoother up-glacier face and a rough, craggy down-ice (lee) side. The rugged lee face results from plucking, a quarrying-like process driven by the pressure of the passing ice. Erosion begins when ice melts under pressure and seeps into fractures in the rock; the infiltrating water refreezes, temporarily causing the rock to adhere to the glacier. As the glacier advances, frost shattering then rips chunks away from the rock, reinforcing the irregular lee surface. Studies indicate that lee-side plucking is a much more significant erosional mechanism than stoss-side abrasion.

M. N. Roy was influenced by C. R. Das, whose ideas aligned him with the Jugantar movement in spirit and action. While based in Moscow, he issued India in Transition, a work that was translated into multiple languages. In 1922 he launched his own journal, Vanguard, and later published The Future of Indian Politics in 1926. His 1930 work, Revolution and Counter-revolution in China, followed as he continued to move between Germany and France during this period.

Manabendra Nath Roy, an Indian revolutionary and later a prominent political thinker, operated in a period shaped by the onset of World War I in August 1914, a conflict that altered the dynamics between Britain and Germany. In Berlin, expatriate Indian nationalists formed the Indian Revolutionary Committee and privately urged the German government to back a revolution against British rule in India. By the close of 1914, Germany had agreed to provide funding and material support to foster such an uprising, a development that convinced many observers that a revolution against colonial rule was imminent. These episodes form part of the historical backdrop of Roy’s early anti-colonial milieu.

Barney Stinson introduces a book titled The Playbook, a collection of elaborate pickup schemes, in the fifth-season episode The Playbook. The volume soon becomes a recurring element throughout How I Met Your Mother, with Barney frequently drawing on the strategies it contains. It also plays a major role in the eighth-season finale arc, The Final Page – Part 2, in which Barney burns the book as part of a final ploy to propose to Robin.

During this arc, Lily's tendency to undermine Ted's relationships with dating partners she disapproves of appears to influence his breakup with Robin, though it prompts a later discussion between Robin and Ted, after which their friendship moves toward a more positive footing. Concurrently, Barney achieves several personal milestones: he sleeps with his two-hundredth partner, taunts a childhood bully, and thereafter questions the purpose of life while his emotional interest in Robin grows more definite. In addition, Barney assists Ted by helping him secure a role designing the headquarters for the Goliath National Bank. When the GN Bank project is put on hold, Marshall and Barney attempt to shield Ted from the news. Following a layoff, Ted launches Mosbius Designs, yet his fear of failure keeps him from contacting potential clients.

Lower Risk was a former classification on the IUCN Red List, later replaced by the Least Concern category as part of an overhaul of the system. The IUCN Red List categories comprise nine designations: Extinct; Extinct in the Wild; Critically Endangered; Endangered; Vulnerable; Near Threatened; Least Concern; Data Deficient; and Not Evaluated.

A Lower Risk designation denotes that a species’ population is large enough to support its long-term persistence and that it is not currently classified as threatened or extinct. The status therefore indicates that the species is not presently at risk of extinction. However, this designation is not permanent, and populations may later be reassessed and moved to a higher-risk category—or to extinct—if factors such as natural disasters or certain human activities compromise their viability.

Rat Cage Records served as the Beastie Boys' initial record label, through which they released their debut EP Polly Wog Stew. The group remained with Rat Cage until 1984, when they signed with Def Jam Recordings, marking a turning point in their career.
Rat Cage Records was an independent record label headquartered in New York City. It was established by Donna Lee Parsons and operated from a record shop of the same name.

Incubation periods for echinococcosis caused by Echinococcus species are highly variable, ranging from several months to many years, and in some cases extending over decades. The duration before clinical presentation may depend on where the cyst develops in the body and on how rapidly the cyst grows.

Echinococcosis is a parasitic disease caused by tapeworms of the genus Echinococcus. Diagnostic imaging, including ultrasound and computed tomography, can reveal multichambered cystic lesions characteristic of the infection, but imaging alone is not regarded as the preferred diagnostic method. The gold-standard diagnosis is the isolation of protoscoleces from surgical specimens or postmortem material, which provides definitive confirmation of the infection. In particular, definitive identification of infections caused by Echinococcus oligarthrus or E. vogeli can be achieved through examination of isolated protoscoleces that display species-specific features. Molecular methods, such as PCR, may identify E. oligarthrus and E. vogeli in tissue samples; however, their utility is limited by the relatively small number of species-specific genetic sequences available for these two species.

Chalcedon is an ancient city situated on a small peninsula along the northern coast of the Sea of Marmara, near the mouth of the Bosporus, opposite Byzantium. The stream known in antiquity as Chalcis (Chalcedon) is today called Kurbağalıdere and flows into Fenerbahçe Bay. The city was founded by Greek colonists from Megara in Attica in 685 BC, and it was established about seventeen years before Byzantium.

Chalcedon’s Greek Orthodox Metropolitan holds the third position in the patriarchal synod of the Ecumenical Patriarchate of Constantinople. The current officeholder is Metropolitan Athanasios Papas. The see's cathedral is the Church of Saint Euphemia located in Chalcedon.

"Lady Lady" has been described by Louella Venus of The Indiependent as possessing a sun-kissed, orange-toned sonic character. The song’s theme centers on growth that emerges from moving away from old habits, suggesting that such evolution can contribute to the greater good, a notion its lyrics convey through a sense of ongoing development and forward motion. The chorus features stacked vocal harmonies that ground the track’s texture, while the production and vocal approach are said to reinforce the artist’s broader message of alignment and intentionality.

Critical reception for Lady Lady has highlighted its emotional depth and thematic scope. Aswan Magumbe of New Wave Magazine described the track as emotionally stirring, characterizing it as delicate yet empowering and as a tranquil meditation on womanhood, surrender, and personal evolution. Chancey Stefanos of Ones to Watch commended Dean's ongoing emotional clarity, the striking quality of her vocals, and the palpable warmth, noting that the artist's unrestrained confidence and clear self-perception flow throughout the composition.

Joe Paopao (born June 30, 1955) is a former professional Canadian football quarterback and CFL coach. He played 11 seasons in the Canadian Football League for the BC Lions, Saskatchewan Roughriders, and Ottawa Rough Riders. Paopao began his coaching career with the BC Lions and has since coached for five different CFL organizations. He served as head coach of the BC Lions in 1996 and later led the Ottawa Renegades from 2002 to 2005. Most recently, he worked as the quarterbacks coach for the Ottawa Redblacks.

Joe Paopao is a longtime resident of Oceanside, California. He was inducted into the BC Lions Wall of Fame in 2007. He is the uncle of Jordan Paopao, who serves as the Washington Huskies' special teams coordinator and tight ends coach.

Liquid nitrogen rapidly boils away at its boiling point to form nitrogen gas, so the safety measures used for gaseous nitrogen are also applicable to liquid nitrogen. Accordingly, ventilation, monitoring, and other precautions designed for nitrogen gas are relevant when handling liquid nitrogen as well. To enhance safety, oxygen sensors are sometimes installed in environments where liquid nitrogen is used, as they monitor ambient oxygen levels and alert workers if nitrogen gas accumulates and displaces oxygen in confined spaces.

Nitrogen-15, a stable isotope of nitrogen, was identified by S. M. Naudé in 1929, with the heavier isotopes of oxygen and carbon discovered shortly thereafter. It possesses a notably low thermal neutron capture cross-section among isotopes. The isotope is widely used in NMR spectroscopy to determine the structures of nitrogen-containing molecules because its nuclear spin of 1/2 allows relatively narrow resonance lines; by contrast, the predominant 14N has spin 1 and a quadrupole moment that broadens spectra. Consequently, 15N NMR presents certain complications not encountered in 1H or 13C NMR. The natural abundance of 15N is about 0.36%, which results in low sensitivity, and its gyromagnetic ratio is only 10.14% that of 1H, leading to a signal-to-noise advantage for 1H that is roughly 300 times higher at the same magnetic field. Sensitivity can be improved through isotopic enrichment of 15N, achieved by methods such as chemical exchange or fractional distillation. Unlike labeled hydrogen, carbon, and oxygen compounds, 15N-enriched materials generally do not exchange with atmospheric N2 under standard conditions. The 15N to 14N ratio, referred to as δ15N, is used in stable isotope analyses across geochemistry, hydrology, paleoclimatology, and paleoceanography.

Following the dissolution of Gran Colombia in 1826, precipitated by the Morrocoyes Revolution (La Cosiata), New Granada retained its 17 provinces. In the ensuing years, the provincial framework was expanded with the creation of Vélez and Barbacoas in 1832, followed by Buenaventura and Pasto in 1835, and then Cauca, Mompós, and Túquerres in 1843. Concurrently, cantons and parish districts were established during this period, laying the groundwork for present-day municipalities.

Within Colombia’s territorial structure, departments organize municipalities into larger regional units known as provinces or subregions. These regions act as an intermediate tier between the departmental and municipal levels, providing a framework for regional administration and coordination. Provinces or subregions are not part of the 1991 Colombian Constitution, and their existence is not established by constitutional law. Instead, their definitions and boundaries are determined by the respective departmental governments and assemblies.

Contemporary spoken Arabic is not best described as a set of discrete dialects, but rather as a continuum of related varieties with gradual transitions linking regional speech. Modern Standard Arabic functions as the standard form shared by educated speakers across Arabic-speaking regions. It is used in writing for formal print media and is also employed orally in public contexts such as newscasts, speeches, and other formal declarations.

Among the modern varieties of Arabic, Hassaniya Arabic, Maltese, and Cypriot Arabic are the only ones with official recognition. Hassaniya is officially recognized in Mali, is acknowledged as a minority language in Morocco, and Senegal has adopted the Latin script for its writing. Maltese holds official status in Malta and is written with the Latin alphabet; linguists typically classify Maltese as a variety of Arabic descended from Siculo-Arabic, with substantial influence from Italo-Romance and English, though many Maltese people regard it as Semitic rather than Arabic. Cypriot Arabic is recognized as a minority language in Cyprus.

Tuwali Ifugao, also known by several alternative names such as Gilipanes, Ifugaw, Kiangan Ifugao, Quiangan, and Tuwali, is spoken in the southern portion of Ifugao Province. As of 2000, the language was estimated to have about 30,000 speakers. It encompasses multiple dialects, including Hapao Ifugao, Hungduan Ifugao, and Lagawe Ifugao.

The Ifugao language, also known as Batad, is a Malayo-Polynesian language spoken in the northern valleys of Ifugao province in the Philippines. It is part of the Northern Luzon subfamily and has close linguistic affinities with the Bontoc and Kankanaey languages. The language exists as a dialect continuum, consisting of four principal varieties, including Tuwali, which is sometimes treated as a separate language.

Among the Four Masters of the Ming dynasty, relationships among the painters varied, with some forming friendships in life and sharing familiarity with one another’s works. The artists also exhibited diverse family backgrounds, ranging from modest to more prosperous circumstances. Tang Yin was born into a poor merchant family, while Wen Zhengming benefited from a well-connected lineage, with his father acting as Tang Yin’s patron, a situation that points to a relatively better means. In addition to their painting, Tang Yin and Wen Zhengming were also accomplished in poetry and calligraphy, reflecting their broader scholarly talents.

Shen is regarded as the most accomplished figure in shan shui painting, employing a firm and well-structured technique and likely drawing on the methods of Wang Ming. Tang is noted for his landscape paintings and his work in the semi-cursive script. Wen, who studied under Shen, would have adopted and borrowed Shen’s painting techniques through their mentor–pupil relationship.

Gola, a British sportswear manufacturer, sponsored the Alliance Premier League from 1984 to 1986. During this period the Alliance Premier League stood as the top tier of English non-League football, and the sponsorship led to the league being referred to as the Gola League.

Gola, a former footwear and sportswear manufacturer, was acquired in 1996 by the Jacobson Group. Following the acquisition, the company broadened its product range, expanding its offerings. In the early 2000s, Gola was relaunched in the United Kingdom as a retro sports fashion brand, targeting adults who recalled the brand from their childhood. The relaunch adopted premium pricing.

Baie-Comeau hosts several French-language public elementary schools and operates two French-language public high schools. In addition, the city contains one English-language public school that serves both elementary and high school levels.

Baie-Comeau's city council consists of the mayor and eight elected councillors, with four councillors coming from each of the town's two sectors. Former mayor Yves Montigny left the position after being elected to the National Assembly of Quebec in the 2022 provincial election. Michel Desbiens became mayor in 2023, succeeding Montigny.

HDCAM is a high-definition digital videocassette format developed as a high-definition recording variant of Digital Betacam, introduced in 1997. It uses an 8-bit DCT encoding with 3:1:1 chroma subsampling for recording. The format records 1440×1080 content, which is down-sampled to be compatible with 1080i systems; later generations added support for 24p and 23.976 PsF. The codec employs rectangular pixels, and playback upscales 1440×1080 material to 1920×1080. The video bitrate is approximately 144 Mbps. Audio is carried as four AES3 digital channels at 20-bit depth and 48 kHz. Tapes are available in small and large cassette sizes, with the small cartridge sharing the same form factor as the original Betamax. The principal competitor is Panasonic's DVCPRO HD, which uses a similar compression and offers a bitrate ranging roughly from 40 to 100 Mbps depending on frame rate.

Sony introduced SR Lite, a higher-compression variant of the HDCAM format. It employs the MPEG-4 Part 2 Simple Studio Profile, the same encoding profile as used in the 440 and 880 modes. The bit rate is reduced to 220 Mbit/s for 60i recording and 183 Mbit/s for 50i, while color sampling remains locked at 4:2:2 and the pixel depth at 10-bit. In addition, SR Lite supports progressive formats at 50p and 60p, with the data rate for 60p increased to 440 Mbit/s.

The Mili language is a Loloish language spoken in Jingdong County, specifically in the Anding and Wenlong townships, as well as in Yun, Zhenyuan, and Xinping counties in Yunnan Province, China. It is considered a variety of Lolopo within the Loloish subgroup.

Emerging technologies are novel technologies whose development or practical applications remain largely unrealized, reflecting their tentative and evolving status. They encompass several fields, including nanotechnology, biotechnology, robotics, 3D printing, and blockchain technologies.

During the Paleolithic, humans developed basic technologies such as clothing and shelter. Scholarly consensus on the exact timing of when clothing and shelter were first adopted remains unsettled; nonetheless, material evidence indicates that clothing dates to roughly 90,000 to 120,000 years ago, while shelter dates to around 450,000 years ago. Over time, dwellings grew more sophisticated, with indications of temporary wooden huts appearing as early as about 380,000 years ago. Clothing crafted from fur and hides of hunted animals facilitated expansion into colder regions. Additionally, Homo sapiens began migrating out of Africa around 200,000 years ago, with initial movements into Eurasia.

During the Turkish War of Independence, the United Kingdom provided substantial support to Greece in the form of equipment, finance, and strategic backing. The British government supplied the Greek forces with aircraft such as Airco DH.9s, Sopwith Camel F.1s, and Gotha WD.13 seaplanes, while many Greek operations proceeded with British permission or assistance, including the Greek Summer Offensive and the Second Battle of İnönü. On 17 February 1920, Lord Curzon informed Admiral John de Robeck that he had issued the necessary order for the Greek army to attack the Turks. Some historians, including Toynbee, note that the Greeks were equipped with weapons that had not been used in combat, provided by British and French sources. British aid to Greece from 1914 to 1920 exceeded £16 million, and Greece, lacking its own cannon or rifle factories, relied largely on weapons and ammunition supplied by English arms firms. In the run-up to the Battle of Sakarya, the Bank of England extended short-term credit to Greece, and in the Second Battle of İnönü the Greek army received 6-inch howitzers from British sources. The British Empire also contributed winter equipment to Greece as part of the broader assistance.

During the Turkish War of Independence, Özdemir Bey organized and led an insurgent effort in the Mosul region. Departing Ankara with only a small staff for Revandiz, he sought to recruit Turkmen and other loyal tribes, as well as soldiers from Tunisia and Algeria who had deserted the French garrison at Nizip. He arrived in Diyarbakır on 22 April and met Cevat Pasha, the commander of the Al Jazira Front. After clearing outstanding financial difficulties, he received operational directives from the Ankara government and mobilized in its name to restore order in areas where central authority had lapsed. The detachment reached Revandiz on 22 June 1922 after a difficult journey. He entered Revandiz to an enthusiastic welcome, with ceremonies and tribal leaders greeting him. In the region, he established an organizational framework and acted in accordance with the broad wishes of the local population. The Revandizians, long without a functioning government, welcomed him as the representative of Mustafa Kemal Pasha and affectionately called him Özdemir Pasha.

During the production of Office Space, improvisation helped address several script problems. An early version contained a line directed at the character who shares a name with a famous singer, using a crude insult that implied the singer did not perform his own songs. To avoid suggesting that the real artist did not sing his material, the line was replaced by Herman with a different blunt epithet.

Following the release of Office Space, Mike Judge began developing Extract as a companion project, even though its initial box-office performance was disappointing. The studio urged him to set Extract aside to concentrate on Idiocracy, anticipating greater commercial appeal. Idiocracy likewise underperformed at the box office upon release, though it later developed a cult following. Judge eventually returned to Extract, which was released in 2009. Like Office Space, Extract satirizes workplace dysfunction, but it does so from the perspective of a manager rather than an employee.

Drut (द्रुत), also called drut laya, designates the final portion of a vocal raga performance in Hindustani classical music. It is rendered at a rapid tempo, characteristic of a fast laya, with a tempo range typically between 160 and 320 beats per minute.

The Internet Hall of Fame did not announce any inductees in 2015 or 2016. To guide the program’s direction, the Internet Society (ISOC) began establishing an Advisory Board to provide leadership and oversight. The Advisory Board would be responsible for selecting inductees going forward.

The Global Connectors category of the Internet Hall of Fame honors individuals from diverse regions worldwide who have played a significant role in fostering the growth and global adoption of the Internet. Nominees in this category are celebrated for contributions that extend Internet access and use across borders, helping to connect people, institutions, and economies. Their work spans initiatives in infrastructure, policy, education, and technology development that have facilitated widespread connectivity and expanded Internet-enabled opportunities on a global scale.

Yom Kippur is described in Jewish tradition as a day of atonement marked by the sounding of a great shofar and the hearing of a quiet, inner voice, with angels trembling as they proclaim the day of judgment. Liturgy expresses that on Rosh Hashanah the fate of individuals is written, and on the fast of Yom Kippur the decree is sealed, determining who will pass away and be created, who will live and die, and within what time frame. Repentance (teshuva), prayer (tefillah), and charity (tzedakah) are believed to remove or modify the evil decree. God is depicted as preferring that a person repent and live rather than die. It is held that God awaits a person’s response until the day of death, and if repentance occurs, divine acceptance is considered immediate.

Yom Kippur is a legal holiday in Israel. During the observance, radio and television broadcasts cease, airports are closed, public transportation ceases, and all shops and businesses close for the day.

Under the ATP ranking system, certain entries contribute to a player’s points even if they do not compete. Specifically, being granted entry into the main draw of a Grand Slam or an ATP Masters 1000 event yields ranking points regardless of whether the player participates. If a player withdraws from an ATP 500 event, the event yields zero points, and this zero is counted as one of the best four results determining the ranking, irrespective of when the withdrawal occurs. Furthermore, additional non-consecutive withdrawals replace the next-best positive result with a zero point, reducing the impact of those events on the overall ranking.

Entitled ATP rankings, this article documents players who have achieved a world No. 6 through No. 10 ranking in the ATP system since its introduction in 1973. It focuses on the men’s tour and includes both former and active competitors; names of players who are still active on the circuit are shown in bold to distinguish them from retired players.

"Praise God" is a gospel music release that maintains traditional gospel content even when expressed through a raw, gritty musical style. It aims to modernize gospel by making it cooler and more appealing, explicitly targeting listeners who do not routinely listen to gospel. The project prioritizes delivering its message to this audience, employing hip-hop-influenced production to bridge the gap and effectively communicate the gospel.

Praise God originated as a beat produced by 30 Roc and Zentachi in early 2020, initially built around a sample from a Japanese song and incorporating Spinz’s distinctive 808 drum pattern. During the first listening event held in Atlanta, the original sample was swapped for a choir-based arrangement. By the second listening party, the drums and 808s added by Zentachi and 30 Roc were removed entirely, leaving a substantially altered instrumental. Despite these major changes, the producers retained credit for the original track that inspired the song, while Japanese writers Machiko Ryu and Kazuhiko Katō were credited for the original sampled composition.

Digital Rapids Corporation is a privately held technology company headquartered in Markham, Ontario, Canada, founded in 2001. It develops and supplies hardware and software for the digital media industry. The company designs systems and software for media ingest, multi-screen video encoding, transcoding, streaming, and workflow automation. Its customer base includes notable organizations such as Deluxe, Foxtel, NBC Universal, Starz, Turner Broadcasting, and the Miami Heat NBA team. In addition to serving the media sector, Digital Rapids also provides solutions to education, government, corporate, and worship markets.

Digital Rapids Corporation developed Broadcast Manager, an enterprise-grade software solution that provides centralized control and automation for the numerous output streams produced by Digital Rapids encoders, enabling streamlined management of professional broadcast workflows.

On a cathode-ray tube display, the vertical refresh rate denotes how many times per second the electron beam returns to the top-left corner to begin drawing a new frame. This timing is governed by the vertical blanking signal generated by the video controller, which coordinates the end of one frame with the start of the next. In practice, the vertical refresh rate is partly constrained by the monitor’s maximum horizontal scan rate, since the vertical retrace must occur within the available horizontal sweep.

Refresh rate denotes how often a display refreshes its image per second. In the era of cathode-ray tube displays, this parameter became a central concern in video game programming. Early systems leveraged the vertical blanking interval, the portion of the scan when the beam returns to the top and no image is drawn, as a convenient window for computation. To minimize flicker and prevent screen tearing, updates to the video buffer were performed only during vertical retrace, thereby synchronizing rendering with the display’s retrace period. This approach, which ties graphical updates to the display’s timing, has persisted in modern game development as a means of reducing visual artifacts.
The Daily Grind is an EP by the punk rock band No Use for a Name, released in 1993. It marked the group's first release on the Fat Wreck Chords label.

CNN/US HD began broadcasting to American viewers in late 2010. In Japan, the high-definition feed is distributed by Japan Cable Television (JCTV) and is made available through several providers, including J:COM, SKY PerfecTV!, iTSCOM, and the JCTVWiFi service.

On July 27, 2012, CNN announced that Jim Walton, who had led the network for three decades, would resign from the presidency. Walton remained in the role through the end of 2012, overseeing a transition period. In January 2013, Jeff Zucker, the former president of NBCUniversal, was appointed to succeed Walton as CNN's president, marking a new phase in the network's leadership.

In July 1971, Ditcham departed from Henry Cow, and by September of the same year Chris Cutler had joined as the band's drummer after answering a Melody Maker advert and attending a rehearsal. Following Cutler’s arrival, the group established a permanent core lineup comprising Fred Frith, Tim Hodgkinson, Chris Cutler, and John Greaves. The band subsequently relocated to London and instituted an intensive rehearsal schedule to consolidate its direction and repertoire.
