Henry Cow was an English experimental rock group formed at the University of Cambridge in 1968 by Fred Frith and Tim Hodgkinson, both multi-instrumentalists. The ensemble's membership fluctuated over roughly ten years, with a rotating lineup that reflected its exploratory approach. Among the more enduring members were Frith and Hodgkinson, together with drummer Chris Cutler, bassist John Greaves, and Lindsay Cooper, who contributed on bassoon and oboe.

Sultan Ali bin Abdulla, who ruled the Mahra Sultanate, had three sons, all of whom predeceased him, and he died in 1907, after which his successor was Sultan Abdulla bin Isa. The annual stipend previously paid to his predecessor was continued for Abdulla bin Isa. Additionally, the Sultan of Socotra and Qishn was accorded a nine-gun salute, a prerogative made permanent in 1902.

During the 1940s, Al-Mahra and neighboring Gulf territories were pressured into signing Advisory Treaties with Britain. The agreements curtailed local leadership by transferring control over internal affairs to the British authorities and by placing the issue of succession under British oversight. Those who refused to sign faced punitive airstrikes conducted by the Royal Air Force. The treaties fostered substantial resentment toward colonial rule and contributed to the emergence and spread of Arab nationalist sentiments in Al-Mahra and the wider Arabian Peninsula.

Self-cleaning glass generally uses a titanium dioxide coating that enables photocatalytic degradation of organic dirt and increases surface hydrophilicity to facilitate rain-based cleansing. While effective for light soiling, this technology cannot address thick, non-transparent accumulations. In particular, it does not readily remove substances such as paint coatings, silicone residues, weathering-induced water staining or bleed, or construction-related stucco dust.

Titanium dioxide (TiO2) is widely used in self-cleaning glazing and hydrophilic surfaces because of its advantageous properties. Under sunlight it functions as a photocatalyst, degrading organic dirt on the surface, and it can develop a superhydrophilic state that improves water spreading and cleaning action. In the absence of light it is chemically inert and non-toxic. It is inexpensive and relatively easy to handle, and can be deposited as thin films by a range of techniques. Additionally, TiO2 is a well-established household chemical, commonly employed as a pigment in cosmetics and paint and as a food additive.

Several long-standing Canadian general stores are noted for their enduring operation and regional significance. Trousdale's in Sydenham, Ontario, operated by the Trousdale family since 1836, is regarded as the oldest continually operated general store in Canada and is noted for a sociable atmosphere in which locals chat while shopping. Gray Creek Store in Gray Creek near Kootenay Bay is described as the largest and oldest general dealer in the Kootenay Lake region. Enniskillen General Store in Clarington, Ontario, has been in operation since 1840 and remains active today. Robinson's General Store in Dorset, Ontario, has been owned and operated by the same family since 1921 and has been recognized as Canada's Best Country Store.

General stores in rural villages frequently serve as community hubs, often being owned and operated by residents as co-operatives. The Village Retail Services Association promotes the role and function of village shops in the United Kingdom. In contemporary practice, such stores expand their offerings to attract customers from neighboring areas, stocking locally sourced, organic, and specialty products, including regional meats, cheeses, and wines.

Common Sense, the pamphlet authored by Thomas Paine, benefited from the involvement of Benjamin Rush, who recommended the Philadelphia printer Robert Bell to Paine and asserted that Bell would publish the tract without hesitation or delay. The pamphlet was first published on January 10, 1776, and Bell actively promoted it in Philadelphia's newspapers, helping to drive demand that soon warranted a second printing. Paine was overjoyed by the reception and sought to collect his share of the profits. He also planned to donate the proceeds to purchase mittens for General Montgomery's troops in Quebec.

Common Sense presents a line of argument that ties Enlightenment notions of the state of nature to a defense of republican government, drawing a clear distinction between society and government. It argues that society arises when isolated individuals choose to live together, thereby forming a community. As social life expands and becomes more complex, government is seen as a necessary instrument to restrain the natural faults of humanity. Paine describes the government's purpose as curbing inherent imperfections that cannot be contained by society alone, establishing a framework in which political authority exists to manage these tensions.

Under Mexican rule as part of California, the area that would become Los Angeles remained until the Mexican–American War brought American forces into the region, where they defeated Californios in a sequence of battles that culminated in the transfer of control. The change in sovereignty was formally realized with the signing of the Treaty of Cahuenga on January 13, 1847, effectively ending hostilities in Alta California. The broader settlement of the conflict followed in 1848 with the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, through which Mexico ceded Alta California, including Los Angeles, to the United States.

The A Line began operation in 1990 as the Metro Rail system's first line, marking the origin of Los Angeles' modern rail network. Since then, the system has been substantially extended, with additional extensions currently under way. The Metro Rail spans 107.4 miles (172.8 kilometers) of track across Los Angeles County and serves a broad range of communities including Long Beach, Pasadena, Santa Monica, Norwalk, El Segundo, North Hollywood, Inglewood, and downtown Los Angeles. As of 2023, the network comprises 101 stations.
In 2013, Arrington was accused of physical abuse by an ex-girlfriend. He subsequently filed a defamation lawsuit against her, and she later agreed to retract the accusations and issue an apology.

Arrington left the practice of law to join RealNames, a move that preceded the company’s failure after it raised around $100 million in funding. He was a co-founder of Achex, an Internet payments company, which was sold to First Data Corp for $32 million, and whose platform later served as the backend for Western Union Online. In 2007, Arrington remarked that his funds at the time were sufficient to buy a Porsche, with little beyond that.

On 3 November 2021, the prime-time adult block of M2, known as M2 Petőfi, underwent a rebranding. This represented the first overhaul of that block since 2015. The refresh aimed to unify its visual identity with that of M2, the network’s main children's channel. The broader M2 branding had already introduced its contemporary look earlier, with the new on-air identity debuting on 1 October 2020.

M2 operates with a daytime schedule devoted to children's programming, while its nighttime block, known as M2 Petőfi, targets youth audiences. The evening and late-night content features a mix of local and international music videos, music concerts, and programming related to younger viewers. M2 Petőfi also showcases exclusive material drawn from its radio counterpart, Petőfi Rádió. The channel’s dual-format model is comparable to similar youth-oriented services in other countries, such as TVP ABC in Poland, CBeebies, CBBC and BBC Three in the United Kingdom, and ČT :D in the Czech Republic.

During the opening phase of the 1939 invasion of Poland, a portion of the German 3rd Army advanced toward the Polish Corridor and linked up with General Günther von Kluge's 4th Army as operations commenced. The 3rd Army, together with the 4th, executed its plans effectively, contributing to a German victory in the Polish Campaign. To the east, the Soviet Red Army launched a substantial assault on Poland, estimated at about one million troops, pushing westward to meet German forces despite higher-than-expected casualties. A joint German–Soviet victory parade was subsequently held in Brest-Litovsk.

On 5 November 1939, roughly five weeks after the conclusion of the Polish Campaign, the Third Army was disbanded, making it one of the first German field armies to be dissolved in World War II, with its staff relocated to Bad Bertrich to form the nucleus of the 16th Army for operations in the West. Its former commander, Küchler, was appointed to command the newly formed 18th Army and led it during the Western Campaign of 1940. He remained in command of the 18th Army until 1942, when he was named commander of Army Group North to oversee the Siege of Leningrad; in the same year he was promoted to Generalfeldmarschall. He was replaced in 1944 following the Soviet breakthrough against Army Group North.

Channel I/O relies on specialized I/O instructions designed for handling input and output tasks. These instructions specifically address the channel, and, in some configurations, the connected device. The channel autonomously accesses all remaining addressing and control information in an asynchronous manner. Channel I/O is similar to DMA in concept, but offers greater flexibility in its addressing and control capabilities.

In some functional programming languages, the I/O monad is presented as an alternative to embedding I/O through primitive language operations. It permits programs to describe input and output actions as composable computations, while the actual effects are performed outside the pure program by the runtime system. This separation preserves the language’s referential transparency by ensuring that I/O actions do not introduce side effects into the functional core. As a result, purely functional programming becomes practical for handling I/O-related tasks without sacrificing the benefits of functional reasoning.

Traffic density in Metro Manila is largely attributed to the state of the capital region’s transportation infrastructure, whose limited capacity and uneven quality impede mobility. The deficiency of high-quality infrastructure reduces available mobility options, contributing to persistent congestion and delays for commuters and goods. In response, the Duterte administration has framed a forthcoming era of extensive infrastructure development, presenting it as a transformative phase for the country’s built environment. As part of this program, officials have outlined roughly $168 billion in spending to support about 5,000 projects nationwide, including transportation initiatives intended to ease congestion and expand mobility across regions.

The U-turn Scheme, introduced by the Metropolitan Manila Development Authority in 2002, was designed to account for roundabout operations on the region’s roads by establishing median openings along busy arterial corridors. The initiative originally comprised two distinct components, the Big Rotunda Scheme and the Clearway Scheme, which together formed the framework of the program.

The article presents a list of national capitals arranged by total land area. Capitals of dependent territories and of disputed territories are indicated in italics. In most cases, the area shown corresponds to the city proper, excluding wider urban, metropolitan, or other city-specific administrative divisions. An exception is Ankara, which, as a metropolitan municipality, is treated under Turkish administrative practice as incorporating its entire metropolitan area within the capital of Turkey.

Al Manara is a locality in western Dubai, United Arab Emirates. The area’s Arabic name is المنارة, and its meaning is "The Beacon." It is bordered to the north by Umm Suqeim, to the east and south by Al Quoz, and to the west by Umm Al Sheif. The southeastern boundary runs along the E11 Sheikh Zayed Road, with Interchange No. 3, known as the Al Manara Interchange, marking the area’s southeastern edge. Al Manara is a developing residential community characterized by upscale villas and townhouses, and it is separated from Umm Al Sheif by Al Thaniya Road.

Members of the Australian Senate, 1926–1929, lists those who served in the Senate during that period. The membership was divided into two cohorts: one elected on 16 December 1922, with terms running from 1 July 1923 to 30 June 1929, and the other elected on 14 November 1925, with terms spanning 1 July 1926 to 30 June 1932. Senators were elected to six-year terms, and when casual vacancies occurred, appointees filled them until the earlier of the next election for the House of Representatives or the Senate, a process that was notably complex in its application. The article thus records the Senators who sat during 1926–1929, reflecting the staggered terms and the vacancy rules that governed the chamber at the time.

Květa Peschke began the season at Hobart, a Tier-V event, where she reached the quarterfinals in the opening tournament. At Wimbledon, she advanced to the fourth round, defeating Vera Zvonareva and former Wimbledon champion Conchita Martínez. In Linz, a Tier-II event, she achieved her first semifinal of the year after defeating Elena Dementieva, Vera Zvonareva, and Ai Sugiyama. At Philadelphia, another Tier-II event, she reached the quarterfinals but was defeated by Elena Dementieva in three sets.

Květa Peschke, a Czech professional tennis player, teamed with Pakistan's Aisam-ul-Haq Qureshi in the US Open mixed doubles competition. The pair progressed to the championship match, where they were defeated by Bob Bryan and Liezel Huber in straight sets.

ITV Weather provides the national and regional weather forecasts for the United Kingdom on ITV's terrestrial network. Forecasts are supplied by the Met Office, with the exception of the Channel Islands forecast, which is produced by the Jersey Meteorological Department. Bulletins are typically broadcast after each ITV News program as well as after regional bulletins. Since March 2022, ITV Weather has operated as a segment of the ITV Evening News, broadcast live from the news studio on weekdays. Emma Jesson is the longest-serving forecaster for ITV Weather, having accumulated 30 years with the program.

The national ITV weather bulletin was introduced on 13 February 1989 and was carried after ITN's bulletins, providing a centralized forecast service that complemented the existing regional framework. Previously, weather forecasts on ITV were produced by separate regional licence holders and were limited to their respective franchise areas.

The Prime Minister of Iraq exercises direct oversight over several key security and intelligence bodies, including the Counter Terrorism Bureau, the National Intelligence Service, the National Security Service, the Falcons Intelligence Cell, and the Popular Mobilization Commission. The Iraqi Counter Terrorism Bureau administers the Iraqi Counter Terrorism Command, a unified formation that comprises all Iraqi Special Operations Forces. As of June 2009, there were ongoing efforts to elevate the CTB to the status of a separate ministry within the government.

Under the Iraqi constitutional framework, following parliamentary elections the Council of Representatives elects the Presidency Council, which includes the president of the Council of Ministers. The Presidency Council is required to unanimously designate a prime minister within fourteen days. If the Presidency Council fails to do so, the responsibility to appoint passes back to the Council of Representatives, which must confirm the nomination by an absolute majority. Should the prime minister-designate be unable to nominate a full cabinet within one month, the Presidency Council is obliged to name another prime minister.

With the allocation of an amateur radio band spanning roughly 150 to 200 meters in 1923, interference at the long edge of this band spurred amateurs to explore shorter wavelengths. Regulatory rules at the time restricted amateurs to wavelengths longer than 150 meters (about 2 MHz). A small number of operators nevertheless obtained special permissions to experiment at wavelengths below that threshold. These trials yielded hundreds of long-distance two-way contacts on 100 meters (3 MHz) during 1923, including the first transatlantic two-way exchanges.

Shortwave radio provides a fallback means of receiving information and entertainment when other communication and media options are inaccessible or cost-prohibitive. Such alternatives include traditional television services delivered by broadcast, cable, or satellite, landline telephone service, mobile phone networks, satellite communications and satellite telephones, and Internet access. The absence of these services can be temporary, prolonged, or permanent, depending on the circumstances.

On 27 April 2022, Disney China announced the launch of the Disney's Home of Film and Television Club (迪家影视俱乐部) on Tencent Video. The club was described as providing Disney’s feature films, children's animation series, and documentaries, and would include a selection of Disney+ original films.

Tencent Video is a Chinese video streaming service operated by Tencent. The platform's relationship with the Chinese government has been a subject of controversy, with implications for governance and content decisions. Content available on Tencent Video is subject to censorship in line with regulatory controls over online media in China. The platform has also been associated with high levels of surveillance, raising concerns about user privacy and data monitoring.

The article surveys recessions and depressions affecting the United Kingdom and its predecessor states. In the United Kingdom, a recession is generally defined as two consecutive quarters of negative economic growth, with growth measured using seasonally adjusted quarter-on-quarter real GDP figures.
The term HIPS denotes a host-based intrusion prevention system, an installed software package that monitors a single computer for suspicious activity by analyzing events occurring within that host.

An intrusion-prevention system (IPS) is a network security appliance that can be deployed within an organization's internal network. It monitors traffic from inside the network to identify attacks or suspicious activity as they occur, thereby exposing internal threats. Neglecting internal network security creates risks because attackers already inside the network can roam laterally and compromise further resources. On the other hand, strong intranet security makes it difficult for adversaries within the network to maneuver and escalate their privileges.

Tim Westwood is the son of Bill Westwood, who later became the Anglican Bishop of Peterborough. He spent his early years in Lowestoft, where his father served as a parish priest, before moving to Norwich at the age of eight when his father became the vicar of St Peter Mancroft. Westwood attended Norwich School, an independent institution, and Hewett School, a state comprehensive, both in Norwich. He was diagnosed with dyslexia, and he has said that during his schooling he was at the bottom of his class, clueless about work, and poor at sports.

Tim Westwood faced a series of allegations of sexual offences that emerged in 2022. In July 2022, The Sunday Times reported that seventeen women had made allegations against him. One of the claims involved sexual activity with a woman who was fourteen at the time, an age at which such acts are illegal under UK law. In August 2022, the Metropolitan Police confirmed they were investigating the allegations of sexual offences against Westwood. By November 2024, the police had submitted the collected evidence to the Crown Prosecution Service to determine whether charges should be brought.

During its service in the Wehrmacht, the Indian Legion wore the standard German Army uniforms, feldgrau in winter and khaki in summer. Its arm badge was shield-shaped, showing three horizontal stripes in saffron, white, and green, with a leaping tiger emblazoned on the white central stripe, and the inscription Freies Indien in black on a white background positioned above the tricolor. The helmet decal consisted of a saffron–white–green transfer on the left side of the helmets, analogous to the German black–white–red decal. Sikhs serving in the unit were permitted to wear turbans in lieu of the peaked field cap, with the turbans dyed to match the uniform color scheme.

The Indian Legion introduced its standard in late 1942 or early 1943, reflecting the design of the unit’s earlier arm badge. It is composed of three horizontal bands: saffron on the top, white in the middle, and green on the bottom, with the white central band featuring a leaping tiger; the saffron band bears the white inscription "Azad" and the green band bears the white inscription "Hind." The overall motif is essentially the same as the flag later adopted by the Azad Hind Government. Photographic evidence indicates that during the Burma Campaign the Indian National Army used the Swaraj flag of the Indian National Congress.

During spring 1942, Britain and the United States reached an understanding on a worldwide division of strategic responsibility that would structure Allied command arrangements. On 24 March 1942, the U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff were designated as primarily responsible for the Pacific, the British Chiefs of Staff took charge of the Middle East and Indian Ocean theaters, and the European-Mediterranean-Atlantic area was assigned a jointly held remit. China was designated as a separate theater under Chiang Kai-shek, yet it remained within the United States’ sphere of responsibility. A further reallocation occurred on 30 March 1942, when the JCS subdivided the Pacific into three areas: the Pacific Ocean Areas (POA), the South West Pacific Area (SWPA), and the Southeast Pacific Area. The Pacific Ocean Area command became operational on 8 May 1942.

Under George C. Marshall's plan, President Franklin D. Roosevelt established a Joint Chiefs of Staff on the American side to coordinate broader Allied military efforts. The resulting Combined Chiefs of Staff (CCS) was permanently stationed in the United States Public Health Service Building in Washington, D.C. Field Marshal John Dill represented the British half, while the CCS was constituted from the British Chiefs of Staff Committee and the American Joint Chiefs of Staff. The American unit was created in part to present a common front to the British Chiefs of Staff. The CCS held its first formal meeting on 9 February 1942 to coordinate U.S. military operations between the War and Navy Departments.

Chirality is a property of certain three-dimensional objects that can be assigned a handedness, described as either right-handed or left-handed. A helix serves as a classic example of such an object. The determination of handedness is made in accordance with the right-hand rule, whereby the sense of twisting corresponds to the orientation of the corresponding axial direction.

Chirality is a fundamental property of living systems, evident in chemical structures as well as in macroscopic anatomy, development, and behavior. Within related groups of organisms, individuals typically share a single dominant enantiomorph for many compounds, organs, and behaviors, reflecting a conserved handedness. Deviations to the opposite enantiomorphic form can occur for certain features or compounds, but such variation is determined by genetic factors. Biochemical systems exhibit pronounced stereospecificity in synthesis, uptake, sensing, and metabolic processing. Consequently, living systems tend to treat the two enantiomers of a given compound in substantially different ways.

EMBOSS is a free, open-source software package for molecular biology and bioinformatics analysis. It handles data in multiple formats and provides transparent retrieval of sequence data from the web. The suite offers extensive libraries that enable researchers to develop and release software within an open-source framework. Additionally, it integrates a wide range of existing sequence analysis tools and packages into a cohesive, seamless platform.

EMBOSS is a software package in bioinformatics that comprises a diverse set of applications for molecular sequence analysis. Among its standard tools are programs for sequence alignment, enabling users to compare nucleotide or amino acid sequences. The suite also includes utilities for rapid searching of sequence databases through pattern-based queries, facilitating efficient motif discovery. In addition, EMBOSS supports protein motif identification and domain analysis, aiding the characterization of protein families and their functional regions. Beyond these core capabilities, the package offers a broad array of supplementary features that extend its utility for researchers working with biological sequence data.

MOD and TOD are standard-definition video formats capable of recording in either 4:3 or 16:9 aspect ratios. In some cases, certain video decoders misread the aspect ratio from the file header, which can cause 16:9 material to appear squeezed or distorted. Camcorder-supplied software generally handles aspect ratio information correctly, aided by MOI metadata to ensure proper presentation. Third-party tools exist that adjust the header’s widescreen aspect ratio metadata, improving decoders' interpretation of MOD files. Applications such as MediaInfo can report the aspect ratio of widescreen MOD content, but the correct display still depends on the specific video decoder being used.
Canon introduced a line of tapeless standard-definition consumer camcorders in January 2008, comprising the FS100, FS10, and FS11 models. All three devices record video in the MOD format.

When You Hear Lou, You've Heard It All is a 1977 studio album by American R&B singer Lou Rawls, released on Philadelphia International Records. Four tracks on the set were produced by Gamble & Huff, while the remaining songs were handled by other producers. The lead single, "Lady Love," achieved moderate success on the R&B charts and crossed over to the pop market, reaching the top 30 on the Billboard Hot 100, marking Rawls's last top-30 hit on that chart. The album itself peaked at number 13 on the R&B albums chart and number 41 on the Billboard pop chart.

When You Hear Lou, You've Heard It All is a live album by soul singer Lou Rawls, with a title that nods to Budweiser's slogan in use at the time, which claimed that merely mentioning the brand conveyed everything. Budweiser sponsored Rawls' live performances in 1976 and 1977, and Rawls also performed in Budweiser television commercials during that period. The 1978 live album Lou Rawls Live includes a brief rendition of the original Budweiser jingle, thereby underscoring the promotional connection between Rawls and the sponsor.

International broadcasting has evolved from a period when shortwave transmissions served as the principal, and in some cases the sole, means of addressing an international audience. High-powered mediumwave broadcasts were occasionally used to reach international listeners as well. In more recent times, technological developments—including satellite transmission, Internet distribution, and rebroadcasts on AM/FM within target nations—have diversified the methods available for delivering international programming. Consequently, shortwave and mediumwave are no longer the exclusive or primary vehicles for reaching international audiences.

During the Spanish Civil War, Nationalist forces received a powerful Telefunken broadcasting transmitter as a gift from Nazi Germany to bolster propaganda efforts. Until 1943, Radio Nacional de España operated in close alignment with the Axis powers, and it routinely retransmitted Spanish-language news produced by the official radio networks of Germany and Italy.

Javanese script, or aksara Jawa, also known as hanacaraka, carakan, and dentawyanjana, developed on the Indonesian island of Java and represents one of the country’s traditional writing systems. It is primarily used to write the Javanese language, but it has also been employed for Sundanese, Madurese, and Malay, as well as for historical languages such as Kawi and Sanskrit. The script exerted a strong influence on the Balinese script, and the Sasak writing system descended from it. Its widespread use persisted from roughly the mid-16th century to the mid-20th century before being gradually supplanted by the Latin alphabet. Today, it is taught in the Yogyakarta Special Region and in Central Java and East Java as part of local curricula, but its everyday use remains very limited.

Javanese script remains part of the local curriculum in Yogyakarta, Central Java, and East Java Province, where it is taught alongside traditional Javanese language instruction. Beyond education, the script appears in the columns of some local newspapers and magazines and is visible on public signage in certain areas. Revival efforts have been largely symbolic rather than practically oriented, and no periodical akin to Kajawèn regularly publishes substantial content in Javanese script. While most Javanese people are aware of the script and can recognize several of its letters, only a minority can read and write it in a meaningful way. By 2019, public signage in Javanese script often contained misspellings and basic mistakes. Hurdles to revitalization include IT equipment that does not render the script correctly, a lack of competent governing bodies to advise on usage, and insufficient typographic experimentation to engage contemporary viewers. Nevertheless, revival initiatives continue through communities and public figures to promote Javanese script in public life, particularly with digital devices.

Islip Hamlet features a quaint shopping district along Main Street, a stretch designated as New York State Route 27A. The district includes gift shops, hairdressers, boutiques, restaurants, pubs, natural food stores, and a variety of other local establishments.

In Islip (hamlet), New York, there were 6,868 households. Of these, 38.4% had children under 18, 61.4% were married couples living together, and 12.0% were led by a female householder with no husband present. Non-family households accounted for 22.8%, and 18.4% consisted of individuals living alone. Among households, 7.7% had someone living alone who was 65 years of age or older. The average household size was 2.97, while the average family size was 3.38.

A GTK+2 based fork of the XMMS media player, named XMMS2, was created by Mohammed Sameer. This XMMS2 fork is unrelated to the contemporary XMMS2 project. The current XMMS2 project, by contrast, uses a new codebase and implements a client-server architecture that is not derived from XMMS.
XMMS2 was launched in 2002 by Peter Alm with the aim of creating a successor to XMMS. The project employs an entirely new code base and is devoted exclusively to audio playback.

ISO 3166-2:GH is the Ghana entry in ISO 3166-2, the segment of the ISO 3166 standard that provides codes for the names of the principal subdivisions of countries coded in ISO 3166-1. ISO 3166-2 is part of the broader ISO 3166 standard, developed by the International Organization for Standardization. The standard assigns codes to the main subnational entities, such as provinces or states, within each country covered by ISO 3166-1. Specifically for Ghana, ISO 3166-2 defines the codes used for its administrative subdivisions.

ISO 3166-2:GH designates Ghana within the ISO 3166-2 standard, which provides codes for the country’s principal subdivisions. Each code comprises two parts separated by a hyphen; the initial element, GH, is the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code assigned to Ghana, while the trailing element consists of two alphabetical characters.

Apache NiFi employs a FlowFile repository as a core component of its dataflow architecture. The repository is responsible for maintaining the state and status of the currently active FlowFile, enabling accurate tracking as flows are processed. It also stores information about FlowFiles as they are transferred between systems, supporting reliable visibility and management of data movement across NiFi workflows.

Apache NiFi's Flow Controller is the central component responsible for governing the system's behavior. It manages the operation of NiFi extensions, controlling their execution within flows. In addition, it handles the allocation and scheduling of resources necessary to enable these components to function effectively.
Stephen Neal is a lawyer who has served as chair of the board of trustees governing Meta's Oversight Board since 2021. Meta's Oversight Board supervises the activities of Facebook and Instagram.

Stephen Neal is an American lawyer. In 2006, The National Law Journal named him among the 100 most influential lawyers in the United States. In September 2009, The Los Angeles Daily Journal ranked him among California's top 100 lawyers.

The Rano massacre was a violent incident attributed to the New People's Army that damaged the group's reputation and challenged its portrayal as defenders of the people's most cherished aspirations. Weeks earlier, media reports alleged that the NPA had tortured and killed hundreds of its own members suspected of being deep-penetration agents or spies for the Philippine government. The massacre followed the April assassination of U.S. Colonel James N. Rowe, an act condemned by several national newspapers.

According to the United Church of Christ in the Philippines (UCCP), a probe conducted by the church condemned the New People’s Army (NPA) for its role in the Rano massacre. The incident prompted serious questions about the NPA’s commitment to a social transformation grounded in justice. The UCCP also charged the NPA with violations of the Geneva Convention and, in its statements, condemned the Philippine government. Additionally, reports indicated that elements of the army used UCCP chapels as bases of operation and organized congregations into anti-communist vigilante groups.

At the Party of European Socialists (PES) Congress held in Brussels on 28–29 September 2012, Sergey Stanishev was elected as the organization’s full president after previously serving in an interim capacity. The meeting also selected four deputy presidents: Jean-Christophe Cambadélis of the French Socialist Party as First Vice-President, Elena Valenciano of the Spanish Socialist Workers’ Party, Jan Royall of the Labour Party, and Katarína Neveďalová of Smer-SD. Achim Post of the Social Democratic Party of Germany was elected Secretary General. The congress furthermore endorsed a democratic and transparent procedure for choosing the PES candidate for the 2014 European Commission presidency.

At its Congress held in Lisbon from 7 to 8 December 2018, the Party of European Socialists elected its leadership, with Sergey Stanishev confirmed as PES President and Achim Post of the SPD appointed secretary-general. The leadership team also included Iratxe García of the Spanish Socialist Workers' Party as 1st Vice-President, Francisco André of the Socialist Party of Portugal as a Vice-President, Katarína Neveďalová of Smer-SD as a Vice-President, and Marita Ulvskog of the Swedish Social Democratic Party as a Vice-President. In October 2019, Heléne Fritzon, also from the Swedish Social Democratic Party, became PES Vice-President, replacing Ulvskog.

William Hogarth, an English satirist and editorial cartoonist who rose to prominence in the eighteenth century, established a tradition of visual commentary that critiqued contemporary politics and social mores; works in his vein are often described as Hogarthian in style. Following Hogarth, England saw the growth of editorial and political cartoons in the latter part of the century, with London-based artists James Gillray and Thomas Rowlandson emerging as leading figures. Gillray in particular refined the art of lampoon and caricature, directing his satire at figures such as King George III, successive prime ministers, and military leaders. He is widely regarded as the father of the political cartoon, a designation reflecting his influential role in shaping the genre.

The work of a cartoonist combines narrative authorship with the drafting of images, encompassing both storytelling and drawing skills. The terms comics illustrator, comics artist, and comic book artist denote the visual-making component of cartooning. While every cartoonist can be regarded as a comics illustrator, artist, or comic book artist, not every person identified as a comics illustrator, artist, or book artist is a cartoonist.

Recent research indicates that psychological safety can negatively affect work motivation among group members and also reduce their willingness to take risks. In several studies, higher psychological safety has been associated with lower motivation, suggesting an inverse relationship in certain contexts. The mechanism appears to be motivational: diminished motivation leads to a decreased likelihood of speaking up with new ideas or concerns. Consequently, lower motivation can hinder learning and process improvement within teams.

Psychological safety denotes an organizational climate in which individuals feel able to raise concerns and voice issues without fear of negative consequences, a concept that echoes Deming's eighth point in his 1982 framework, which argues that fear must be eliminated so that all members can work effectively. Proponents stress the importance of cultivating environments where people feel interpersonal safety when speaking up. The notion marks a departure from traditional Taylorist management practices toward more open and safer channels of communication. The presence of interpersonal safety in raising concerns is considered essential for achieving high-quality business outcomes.

Galileo Galilei's The Assayer is widely regarded as his scientific manifesto for its extensive articulation of how science should be conducted and its emphasis on empirical and mathematical inquiry. In the same period, in early 1619, Father Grassi anonymously published An Astronomical Disputation on the Three Comets of the Year 1618, a pamphlet addressing a comet observed toward the end of November 1618. Grassi argued that the comet was a fiery body moving along a segment of a great circle at a constant distance from the Earth, and he concluded that the object must lie farther away than the Moon because it appeared to move more slowly than the Moon.

During the 17th century, suction pumps were capable of generating measurable vacuums, though the underlying physics remained poorly understood. These pumps could not lift water higher than about 34 feet (approximately 10 meters), a constraint that hindered irrigation schemes, mine drainage, and the fountains envisioned by the Duke of Tuscany. In response, the duke commissioned Galileo Galilei to investigate the problem. In his 1638 work Two New Sciences, Galileo incorrectly argued that a water column would break from its own weight once its height exceeded 34 feet.

Set functions may be defined on domains with diverse properties, reflecting the range of possible structures. The article identifies a number of commonly observed properties and classifications for families of sets, and a subsequent table catalogs these properties and categories in a systematic format.

In possibility theory, a set function is a mapping from the power set of a given set S to the unit interval [0,1], assigning to every subset a degree of possibility. This means that each event, represented by a subset of S, is given a plausibility value within [0,1], reflecting its relative likelihood in a non-probabilistic framework. When such a function is induced by a possibility distribution defined on the elements of S, the value assigned to a subset A is obtained by taking the maximum of the distribution over all elements of A, yielding the corresponding subset-level measure of possibility.

Argyria was an ancient town in the Troad region of northwestern Asia Minor. It lay on the right bank of the Aesepus River, identified with the modern Gönen Çay, and was situated near Scepsis. The settlement was notable for its silver mines, and its name derives from the Greek argyros, meaning "silver." Geographer Strabo places Argyria at the foot of Mount Ida near the source of the Aesepus.

Impur II is an album by English guitarist, composer and improvisor Fred Frith. Composed in 1996 by Frith, the work was realized through a live performance held in December 1997 at RamDam in Lyon, France. The performers were drawn from the students and teachers of L’Ecole Nationale de Musique, Villeurbanne, with Frith conducting and performing alongside the ensemble.

The 2013–14 Nemzeti Bajnokság II was organized as a single, nationwide league consisting of 16 teams, a departure from the previous seasons in which the competition was split into two regional groups of 16. Relegated from the previous season's NB I were BFC Siofok and Egri FC, though Egri FC failed to obtain the license required to participate in the national championship. Eight clubs qualified directly from the 2012–13 NB II by finishing 2nd–5th in each of the East and West divisions. The remaining eight places were filled through promotion play-offs in which the teams that finished 6th–8th in each NB II group faced the group winners of NB III to determine the final lineup. The season thus featured a 16-team table formed by direct qualifiers and playoff entrants.

The 2013–14 Nemzeti Bajnokság II article covers Hungary's second-tier football competition for the 2013–14 season and lists the clubs that competed in the campaign. For each club, the entry provides the manager, the team captain, the kit manufacturer, and the shirt sponsor, offering a standardized snapshot of both leadership and commercial partners associated with the clubs during that season.

Oricon's chart lineage traces back to the Tokushin Music Report, which began in 1962 and whose chart listings preceded the establishment of Oricon. Original Confidence served as an exclusive information magazine for professionals in the music industry. In the 1970s, Koike actively promoted his company's charts to raise public awareness, employing intensive promotional efforts across multiple media, including television programs. By the late 1970s, the hit parade had come to be known by the abbreviation Oricon.

Oricon is a Japanese entertainment statistics organization that compiles weekly sales charts from data gathered from approximately 39,700 retail outlets as of April 2011. These charts provide rankings of sales for music CDs, DVDs, electronic games, and other entertainment products based on weekly tabulations. The results are announced every Tuesday and published in Oricon Style by its subsidiary, Oricon Entertainment Inc. In addition, the group maintains panel survey–based popularity ratings for television commercials on its official website.

From the late 1930s, William L. Wilkerson used The Hollywood Reporter to depict the film industry as influenced by communism, presenting a view that drew increasingly on anti-Communist rhetoric. He was a vocal opponent of the Screen Writers Guild, denouncing it as a “Red Beachhead.” In 1946 the Guild discussed the possibility of creating an American Authors’ Authority to hold writers’ copyrights rather than allowing studios to own them. Wilkerson devoted his Tradeviews column to this issue on July 29, 1946, under the headline “A Vote for Joe Stalin.” Reports indicate that he went to confession before publishing the piece, aware of the potential damage, but was apparently encouraged by the priest to proceed.

Jack Moffitt was an American screenwriter and a vocal anti-Communist figure who crafted scripts for dozens of films during Hollywood's Golden Age. He is also recognized as the father of Peggy Moffitt, a well-known model and actress. In 1955, Moffitt was hired by Wilkerson and subsequently contributed a substantial number of reviews to The Hollywood Reporter (THR).

In the United States, the job outlook for programmers has been shaped by economic downturns and shifting labor demand. Following the dot-com crash and the Great Recession, many programmers experienced unemployment or depressed wages, and broader STEM attrition—especially among women—has been linked to limited interest in science and mathematics and to fears that programming could face pressures similar to those seen in manufacturing or agriculture. Long-term projections from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics indicate a continuing decline in programmer employment, with anticipated declines of about 7% for 2016–2026, 9% for 2019–2029, 10% for 2021–2031, 11% for 2022–2032, and a current forecast around −6% for 2024–2034; by contrast, the category of software developers is expected to grow, albeit more slowly than earlier forecasts, at roughly 17% over the same broad period (down from about 22% projected for 2019–2029), with employment rising from approximately 1.47 million to 1.785 million and a median annual salary near $110,000. Earlier periods such as 2010–2020 had projected about a 30% increase for software developers. The outsourcing of programming work to countries with lower wages, enabled by remote work, has limited domestic demand to mainly replacement hires rather than net new openings. Software developers are typically higher-skilled and undertake a wider range of development tasks, making offshoring less risky for them than for general programmers. A contributing factor to the overall programmer decline is the merging of programming skills into related roles, such as full-stack development, as job requirements expand. Additionally, advances in artificial intelligence are expected to have a substantial impact on the demand for future software professions.

Programmers tailor their approach to the industry and organization they serve, as requirements and constraints vary by domain—for instance, financial record-keeping versus conditions used in flight-simulation training. Simple applications may be produced within a few hours, whereas more sophisticated systems can require more than a year to develop. Some programs are treated as ongoing projects, never considered finished while in use and continually improved. The majority of initiatives involve teamwork, with several programmers collaborating under the supervision of a senior programmer or lead developer.

Following the death of his wife shortly after 1134, Emperor John II Komnenos oversaw the construction of a second church situated to the north of the original sanctuary. The initial church was dedicated to Theotokos Eleousa (the Merciful Mother of God) and was served by a lay clergy. By 1136 at the latest, a southern courtyard and an exonarthex were added to the complex, and the two shrines were connected by a chapel dedicated to Saint Michael, which subsequently became the imperial mausoleum (heroon) of the Komnenos and Palaiologos dynasties. Burials at the site include Emperor John II, his wife Irene, and Bertha of Sulzbach (also known as Irene), wife of Manuel I Komnenos.

Within the Zeyrek Mosque complex, the northern church is notable for its single-dome design. Its exterior features a frieze adorned with dog-tooth and triangular motifs, a decorative band that runs along the eaves.

Barbie Super Sports is a PC game that includes two sports, roller-blading and snowboarding. Players begin by selecting a name and choosing a character from Barbie, Teresa, Christie, or Kira. The chosen character appears in a shop where outfits for skating or snowboarding can be purchased. Exiting the shop, the player enters a lobby that serves as the hub for progression, with four stages available to enter. Each group of four stages concludes at a finish line gated by specific criteria, such as achieving a certain number of points. Throughout the stages, players can earn tickets, which can later be redeemed in the shop for additional gear.

Barbie: Super Sports received a largely negative reception on GameFAQs, which rated it 2.38 out of 5 overall. The sound design was criticized for failing to meet expectations in both quantity and quality. By contrast, the graphics were praised, with character models and backdrops identified as the standout elements of the package. Animation was described as blocky, with certain movements appearing as if performed underwater. Additionally, reviewers argued that the on-screen characters were too small, diminishing on-screen presence.

Beginning in 645 CE, Armenia entered a period of Arab rule that endured for about two centuries, under the Umayyad and later Abbasid caliphates. During this era, Armenian Christians possessed political autonomy and enjoyed relative religious toleration while remaining dhimmis, or second-class subjects. Early attempts to compel conversion to Islam prompted some Armenians to flee to Byzantine-controlled Armenia, though Byzantine Armenia was largely left unsettled by Muslim forces due to its rugged, mountainous terrain. The policy sparked uprisings, yet the Armenian Church gained greater formal recognition than under Byzantine or Sassanid rule. The Caliph appointed ostikans as provincial governors, including several of Armenian origin, the first being Theodorus Rshtuni. An Armenian-origin commander led the 15,000-strong army, with leadership repeatedly drawn from the principal noble houses, notably the Mamikonian, Bagratuni, or Artsruni families; the Rshtuni line supplied the largest contingent, about 10,000 troops. Armenians defended the realm from external threats and also assisted the Caliphate in military campaigns, such as their help against Khazar incursions.

Various Armenian chronicles present differing dates and details, but they align with Muslim accounts in outlining the broad arc of the early Arab activity in Armenia. Arab forces arrived in 642, penetrated the central Ayrarat region, and sacked the city of Dvin, taking roughly 35,000 captives. In 643, a further Arab incursion came from the Azerbaijan region, devastating Ayrarat and extending toward the Anatolian peninsula. Theodore Rshtuni opposed the invaders, defeating them in battle and forcing their retreat. In the aftermath, Rshtuni was recognized as the ruler of Armenia by Byzantine emperor Constans II, and soon thereafter the Armenian population recognized Byzantine suzerainty.

Digital distribution refers to the dissemination of media, software, and other content through digital networks rather than physical media. Although the World Wide Web had been established many years prior, organizations continued to adjust their strategies for delivering content in digital form. By 2019, businesses across various sectors were still refining these approaches, a process that included redefining and clarifying the basic terminology used to describe distribution channels, formats, rights, and delivery methods.

Digital distribution encompasses the delivery of digital media and software through electronic channels. It faces fragmentation due to a wide variety of incompatible data formats, which can limit the range of compatible devices or require users to convert content for use. Streaming services, a dominant form of digital distribution, depend on continuous Internet connectivity to access content and catalogs. This model often restricts local storage of material and prevents transferring files to physical media. Additionally, the control mechanisms surrounding streaming can enable greater censorship by content owners, infrastructure operators, and owners of consumer devices, shaping what can be accessed and how it can be distributed.

According to a 2017 meta-analysis of 44 studies, daylight saving time is associated with a modest reduction in electricity consumption, estimated at roughly 0.3 percent on days when the practice is in effect. By contrast, several studies have suggested that DST may lead to higher motor fuel usage. A 2008 report from the United States Department of Energy found no significant increase in motor gasoline consumption resulting from the 2007 extension of DST. Early objectives of daylight saving time included decreasing the amount of incandescent lighting used in the evenings.

Industrialized societies organize daily life around fixed clock-based schedules throughout the year, governing work and school hours as well as mass transit. By contrast, agrarian communities tend to time activities according to daylight length and solar time, which vary seasonally as a result of the Earth's axial tilt. In regions located north and south of the Tropics, daylight is longer in summer and shorter in winter, with the extent of seasonal variation increasing with distance from the equator. Consequently, near the equator the annual change in daylight is minimal, making daylight saving time largely unnecessary or of limited usefulness.

Within Roman Catholicism, the Eucharist, also known as Holy Communion, is the sacrament that completes a Catholic's initiation into the Christian life. It is frequently described as the wellspring and culmination of the Christian life, reflecting its central role in Catholic worship and discipleship. The ceremony in which a Catholic first receives the Eucharist is celebrated as First Communion, marking the transition from catechetical formation to active participation in the Eucharistic liturgy.

During the first millennium, Christianity developed in diverse forms across Western and Eastern Europe, Asia, and Africa. Most Eastern Christian churches are no longer in communion with the Catholic Church after the Great Schism of 1054, as well as due to earlier Nestorian and Chalcedonian separations. The Catholic Church comprises 23 autonomous Eastern Catholic Churches, collectively known as churches sui iuris, that remain in full communion with Rome. The Latin Church, the largest and sole Western tradition, has more than a billion members worldwide, whereas the 23 Eastern Catholic Churches together accounted for about 17.3 million members in 2010, far smaller than the Latin Church.

External evidence concerning the origin of Heliand is found in a Latin document printed by Flacius Illyricus in 1562, which comprises two parts: a prose Praefatio and a verse section titled Versus de poeta et Interpreta hujus codicis. The Praefatio asserts that Emperor Louis the Pious commissioned a Saxon poet to translate the Bible (Old and New Testaments) into German verse for his subjects, and that the poet, esteemed among his compatriots, obeyed this command due to a prior divine injunction and rendered the principal parts of the Bible into verse, arranged as vitteas, or lessons in sententiae. It is further claimed that the poet, previously ignorant of poetry, was instructed in a dream to convert the divine precepts into verse, and that he accomplished the task with such skill that his work is said to surpass all other German poetry in beauty. By contrast, the Versus largely reproduces Bede’s Caedmon dream narrative but does not mention the dream, instead portraying the poet as a herdsman. The Versus states that the poems begin with the creation and recount the history of the five ages of the world up to the coming of Christ.

Scholarly engagement with Heliand includes several key studies and collections. G. Ronald Murphy's The Saxon Saviour: The Germanic Transformation of the Gospel in the Ninth-Century Heliand (1989) analyzes how the Gospel was transformed within the ninth-century Old Saxon epic and was published by Oxford University Press. A 2010 collection edited by Valentine A. Pakis, Perspectives on the Old Saxon Heliand, gathers critical essays and commentaries offering diverse interpretations. In 2011 Timothy Blaine Price published Luther's Heliand: Resurrection of the Old Saxon Epic in Leipzig, a self-published volume that outlines the author's personal research and travels related to the work.
Mitch Richmond was elected to the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame in 2014 and later inducted into the Bay Area Sports Hall of Fame in 2016.

Mitch Richmond joined the Los Angeles Lakers as a free agent, marking the final season of his NBA career. He came off the bench and averaged four points per game. He earned an NBA championship ring with the Lakers in 2002, although his postseason playing time was limited to a total of four minutes. In Game 4 of the 2002 Finals, seconds after scoring the last basket of his career, he dribbled out the clock to seal the Lakers’ title.

Jean Ousset (28 July 1914 – 20 April 1994) was a French advocate and theorist of National Catholicism. Born in Porto, Portugal, he became active in the Action Française monarchist movement during the 1930s and served as personal secretary to its leader, Charles Maurras. In the Second World War, while operating under the Vichy regime, he headed the research bureau of Jeune Légion, an entity aligned with the Légion française des combattants, a veterans' association founded in 1940 and headed by Xavier Vallat.

Jean Ousset, a French writer, published in 1949 a book titled Pour qu'il règne (That He May Reign). The title was later adopted by the Belgian section of the Society of St. Pius X as the name of its newspaper. The book's preface was signed by Marcel Lefebvre.

Frank W. Hackett was born on April 11, 1841, in Portsmouth, New Hampshire. He studied at Harvard University, where he completed a bachelor’s degree in 1861 and later obtained a Master of Arts degree in 1864.
Frank Warren Hackett (April 11, 1841 – August 10, 1926) was an American civilian administrator and lawyer. He served as Assistant Secretary of the Navy under President William McKinley.

From the fall of 1955 onward, The George Burns and Gracie Allen Show frequently resumed after the main episode with Burns and Allen reappearing before a curtain decorated with the theater names and locations drawn from their vaudeville days. In these closing moments they performed one of their signature double routines. Their exchanges often touched on Gracie's fictional relatives—Death Valley Allen, a prospector; Florence Allen, a nurse; and Casey Allen, a railroad man. Burns typically concluded the program by inviting Gracie to bid goodnight, to which Gracie would reply with a simple goodnight. Contrary to popular legend, Gracie never spoke the line that would explicitly name her as "Goodnight, Gracie." When asked whether she should say it, Burns reportedly judged it to be a funny line, and when asked why he had not used it, he replied that, incredibly enough, no one had ever thought of it.

The George Burns and Gracie Allen Show is notable for a running gag in which visitors secretly leave their hats in a closet to slip away from Gracie’s antics. Another key aspect of the program is George Burns’s role as a spectator of the action: in the earliest live episodes he appears outside the proscenium, later watching events on television from his study, and he frequently breaks the fourth wall by addressing the audience directly. A further recurring bit centers on George repeatedly “firing” his announcer, Harry Von Zell, whenever the announcer assists or fails to halt Gracie’s illogical mayhem.

Approximately half of The Hague's residents identify with a religious group, with Christianity accounting for about 29% and Islam roughly 14.1% of the population. Religiosity is higher among people with a recent migration background from Indonesia, Turkey, Morocco, and Suriname, and Islam is the most common religion among those with Turkish or Moroccan origins. Among residents of Surinamese heritage, Hinduism is the leading faith, accompanied by greater religious diversity overall. Among the native Dutch population, Christianity is the most common affiliation among those who identify as religious. Just under 40% of the population regularly attends a house of worship.

The Hague, located in the western Netherlands, emerged as a central political center during the late 16th century. At the outset of the Eighty Years' War, its absence of defensive walls left the town vulnerable to Spanish occupation. In 1575 the States of Holland, temporarily based in Delft, discussed tearing down the city, but the proposal was dropped after mediation by William the Silent. By 1588 The Hague had become the permanent seat of both the States of Holland and the States General of the Dutch Republic. Although it never obtained formal city status, the town possessed numerous privileges typically granted to cities, enabling the administration to govern municipal matters without official recognition. In modern administrative law, the concept of formal city rights has disappeared.

Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour is a concert series headlined by Billie Eilish that critics have characterized as emblematic of Generation Z. Thomas Turner of The Line of Best Fit described Eilish as a forerunner of Gen Z, and over roughly eight years she has acted as a vocal patron and insightful commentator on Gen-Z, maintaining a symbiotic relationship with the zeitgeist while pushing the boundaries of pop culture. The tour has been marked by deliberate attention to the live show design, with extensive care given to the layout and staging. Critics have described Eilish as a commanding onstage presence, moving between vantage points to provide audience members with near-front-row sightlines.

Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour drew widespread critical acclaim, with reviewers highlighting Billie Eilish’s ability to translate the intimacy of her studio material to a large-venue setting. The New York Times’ Lindsay Zoladz praised her for preserving the personal feel of the songs on arena stages, noting that she reimagines acoustic numbers as arena-rocking power ballads and engages the crowd with the precision of a well-tuned instrument. USA Today’s Melissa Ruggieri emphasized her authenticity in live interaction, pointing to a lack of artifice and describing a sincere devotion to fans, communicated through heartfelt assurances of lasting support.

The Sharp Project is a media and creative facilities complex in Manchester, developed on the site of the former Sharp Corporation warehouse. In 2006, Manchester City Council purchased the warehouse for £6.1 million. The council chose to retain the Sharp name for the development, preserving its corporate heritage. Development of the facility was led by Sue Woodward, who had previously served as managing director of the Granada Television franchise.

The Sharp Project is a £16.5 million profit-for-purpose development in Manchester, owned by Manchester City Council. It was completed in June 2011 and funded by Manchester City Council, the Northwest Development Agency (NWDA), and the European Regional Development Fund (ERDF). The project sits within Manchester’s significant concentration of creative and media industries, which is the second-largest cluster of its kind in Europe.

On September 15, 2021, Time unveiled its annual Time 100 list. The selection is organized into six categories: Icons, Pioneers, Titans, Artists, Leaders, and Innovators. The category covers feature notable individuals, including Prince Harry and Meghan Markle on the Icons cover; Billie Eilish on the Pioneer cover; Simone Biles on the Titan cover; Kate Winslet on the Artist cover; Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala on the Leader cover; and Jensen Huang on the Innovator cover. Before the reveal, Time conducted a reader poll to assess potential inclusions, which attracted nearly 1.8 million votes. Britney Spears led the poll and was subsequently included as an Icon in the 2021 Time 100.

Time 100 is Time magazine's annual list recognizing the world's most influential figures and the diverse ways in which they shape events. Some recipients attain prominence through openly exercised political power, with former U.S. president George W. Bush frequently cited as a principal exemplar. Others exert influence without public visibility, as in the case of Ayatollah Ali al-Sistani, whose position effectively gives him a veto over plans to transfer power in Iraq. A third mode of influence is moral example, exemplified by Nelson Mandela’s willingness to forgive his captors and to serve only one term, which has been cited as an enduring form of ethical leadership.

Stay with Me, originally performed by Sam Smith, has been covered by other artists, including The Temptations, an American R&B group, who included a rendition on their 2018 album All the Time. English folk duo Bear's Den also offered a cover for the Sunday Sessions, illustrating the song’s cross-genre appeal.

Stay with Me (Sam Smith song) is a track by Sam Smith. According to Musicnotes.com, the composition is in the key of C major with no accidentals, set in common time (4/4), and performed at a tempo of 84 beats per minute.

Under Michigan's 1963 constitution, the governor's term was extended to four years, taking effect with the 1967 election. Since then, gubernatorial elections have been scheduled two years after U.S. presidential elections; for example, presidential elections in 2008 and 2012 were followed by gubernatorial elections in 2010 and 2014. These elections are held concurrently with state Senate elections. The winner takes office at noon on January 1 of the year following the election.

Forty-seven individuals have served as Governor of Michigan across forty-nine distinct terms, with John S. Barry and Frank Fitzgerald each returning to the office after gaps. Before statehood, five governors led the Michigan Territory. Stevens T. Mason is recognized as the first governor of the state, having previously filled the territory's top office as well. Mason won the governorship in 1835 at the age of 23, as a Democrat, and served until 1840. He remains the youngest person to hold a state governorship in U.S. history.

Runaway Love is a song by Ludacris that dramatizes the difficult circumstances faced by young girls who attempt to escape abusive environments. The narrative centers on Nicole, a ten-year-old who believes she is not beautiful and fears that no one cares for her. She endures physical abuse from her alcoholic stepfather and lies to teachers about the bruises he causes. Nicole’s best friend is Stacy, and the two vow to stay close forever. Stacy is later killed in an accidental drive-by shooting, leaving Nicole feeling isolated once again. Overcome by loneliness, Nicole resolves to run away.

Runaway Love is a Ludacris track that comprises three verses, each presenting a fictional account of a runaway preadolescent girl. The first verse follows Lisa, who is nine years old; the second centers on Nicole, aged ten; and the third focuses on Erika, aged eleven. In each narrative, the girl leaves home to escape the difficulties she faces.

Intergovernmental organizations are international bodies established by a formal treaty that acts as their constitutional charter. This treaty is negotiated among states and becomes binding through ratification by governments representing multiple states. Upon ratification, the instrument typically endows the organization with international legal personality, enabling it to enter into agreements, perform duties, and, in some cases, bring or defend claims under international law. Consequently, IGOs constitute a significant component of public international law, facilitating cooperation and governance across diverse policy areas.

Intergovernmental organizations are endowed with a framework of privileges and immunities designed to safeguard their independence and ensure their independent and effective functioning. These privileges are established by the treaties that create the organization, as illustrated by instruments such as the Convention on the Privileges and Immunities of the United Nations and the Agreement on the Privileges and Immunities of the International Criminal Court. In practice, these arrangements are typically supplemented by additional multilateral agreements and national regulations, for example the International Organizations Immunities Act in the United States. As a result, intergovernmental organizations enjoy immunity from the jurisdiction of national courts. The Vienna Convention on the Representation of States in their Relations with International Organizations of a Universal Character (1975) also sets out certain privileges and immunities, but as of 2022 it had not yet entered into force, having not been signed by 35 states.

Gardelegen traces its origins to the 10th century, with the first recorded name appearing in 1196. The castle of Isenschnibbe was held by the House of Alvensleben from 1378 to 1857. In 1343, on the neighboring heath, Margrave Louis I of Brandenburg defeated Otto the Mild of Brunswick. The town joined the Hanseatic League in 1358. It endured substantial damage during the Thirty Years' War and narrowly avoided destruction by French forces in 1757. In World War I, Germany operated a special prisoner-of-war camp for ethnic Poles taken from the Russian Army, intended to promote and recruit for a German-controlled Polish army against Russia. In the final stages of World War II, an air raid on 15 March 1945 killed 52 people. On 13 April 1945, the Isenschnibbe Barn site witnessed a massacre in which more than 1,000 concentration camp inmates were murdered by SS, Wehrmacht, Volkssturm and other Nazi groups alongside local civilians; many victims were Polish, Soviet, French or from other nations, and the majority remain unidentified. Today the site serves as a memorial, with a cemetery inscription noting that 1,016 Allied prisoners of war were murdered by their captors and that the graves are to be kept in perpetuity to honor their memory.

Gardelegen's historic core contains several notable religious and civic monuments. St. Nicolai Church traces to the 14th century and suffered extensive bomb damage on 15 March 1945, leaving the nave ruined while the tower was subsequently renovated; there have been proposals to convert the nave into a concert hall. St. Spiritus is a Renaissance building completed in 1591, historically linked to a monastery first mentioned in 1319, and it formerly functioned as a hospital for the sick and elderly. St. Mary's Church dates from around 1200 and is described as being in a Romantic style; the structure includes five naves and was enlarged during the 14th century. The town hall is a Baroque structure, with construction dates given in the source as 1526–1522.

The military ranks of Saudi Arabia refer to the insignia used by the Saudi Arabian Military Forces. The system bears the imprint of the British model, which provided the early basis for the rank structure and insignia design. As the Saudi armed forces developed, close bilateral relations with the United Kingdom laid the groundwork for that initial framework, and subsequent cooperation with the United States introduced additional conventions to the rank scheme during modernization efforts. This combination produced a hybrid hierarchy that reflects both historical British traditions and later American adaptations, aligned with the kingdom’s ongoing defense partnerships.

Polyandrous marriage has existed in Tibet but remains relatively uncommon. In households with only female offspring, a form of sisterly polyandry—where a single husband is shared among sisters—becomes the most frequently observed pattern. Traditional inheritance typically grants land rights to male heirs; however, in the absence of sons, daughters may acquire rights to the family’s land, or the family estate. To preserve the estate, the sisters share one husband. The husband relocates to the wife’s lineage, joining and becoming a member of the wife’s family through a matrilocal arrangement. This matrilocal pattern stands in contrast to patrilocal norms, where brides move to live within the husband’s family.

Within Tibetan polyandrous society, mono-marital stem households are led by a dominant male head called the trong bey abo, or simply the abo. The abo is responsible for managing the family’s property and resources and is always male. He is typically the oldest male of the elder generation who holds centralized authority. In some cases, the role may be assumed by a younger brother when the eldest male retires.

Don Nelson began his NBA career with the Chicago Zephyrs during his rookie season, appearing in roughly 17 minutes per game. The club featured prolific scorers such as Walt Bellamy, who averaged 27.9 points per game, and Terry Dischinger at 25.5 points per game, along with Si Green and Charlie Hardnett. Midseason, the Zephyrs underwent a coaching change, with Jack McMahon being replaced by Slick Leonard. The team finished the year with a 25–55 record, and after the season the franchise relocated to Baltimore, becoming the Baltimore Bullets, a predecessor of today’s Washington Wizards. Nelson posted averages of 6.8 points, 4.5 rebounds, and 1.2 assists per game in his 17 minutes per contest. In 1963, Nelson was acquired by the Los Angeles Lakers.

Don Nelson popularized the Hack-a-Shaq strategy in the NBA during his tenure with the Dallas Mavericks, developing it in response to the team's limited interior presence against dominant low-post players such as Shaquille O'Neal. In the 2004 off-season, the Phoenix Suns offered Steve Nash a maximum contract; Nelson urged Mavericks owner Mark Cuban to match the offer, but Cuban declined. Nash ultimately signed with Phoenix, where he went on to win back-to-back Most Valuable Player awards in the following two seasons.

West Jersey’s early European presence remained limited until the territory came under English control in 1664, following the Dutch defeat of New Sweden in 1655. From the late 1670s onward, a substantial influx of Quakers established settlements in the region, initially in what is now Salem County and subsequently in Burlington, which later served as the capital of West Jersey.

Long before European contact, the Delaware Valley was inhabited by the Lenape, also known as the Delaware people. Beginning around 1609, European exploration and settlement in the region involved Dutch, Swedish, and English interests. The Dutch West India Company established one or two settlements along the Delaware River, but by the late 1620s most of the initial inhabitants had relocated to Manhattan, which had become the core of New Netherland. In the colonial era, the western portion of New Jersey was later organized as West Jersey, one of two sections of the province alongside East Jersey.

The Dirty Girls Social Club is a novel whose storytelling is presented from a first-person perspective that alternates among six friends: Lauren, Usnavys, Rebecca, Sara, Elisabeth, and Amber. The group formed while they were in college and each member comes from diverse racial and ethnic backgrounds, all sharing a Latina heritage. They refer to themselves as the "sucias"—a Spanish term meaning "dirty girls"—as a humorous, self-deprecating nickname. Through these interwoven voices, the narrative traces their personal ambitions, relationships, and evolving identities as they navigate adulthood together.

Elisabeth is revealed by a tabloid journalist after being photographed kissing a woman, prompting the other members of the sucias to rally around her in support. Sara's husband, Roberto, driven by jealousy and possessiveness, pressures her to end the friendship. Elisabeth later goes to Sara's house to seek help as paparazzi swarm the residence, and the two friends briefly reunite. When Roberto discovers Elisabeth has visited their home, he assaults Sara, and she suffers a miscarriage as a result.

ATN Food Food is a Canadian television channel that launched with programming focused on South Asian cuisine. The Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission granted a license on September 7, 2012, under the license name ATN South Asian Cooking Channel 1. The channel subsequently began broadcasting on November 29, 2012, under the launch name ATN Food Food.

On September 28, 2018, the Canadian Radio-television and Telecommunications Commission approved an application from Asian Television Network for its service ATN Food Food. The decision reclassified the service from a licensed Category B specialty service to an exempted Category B third-language service, effecting a transition from licensed to exempted status within the third-language service category.

Situated in Jiaolin Alley within Dongcheng District, Beijing, the route proceeds southward through surrounding residential areas and winds to a point just east of Minwang Hutong. It runs along a river that parallels the northern side of the Second Ring Road, then turns east briefly to follow the waterway before passing beneath the Airport Expressway via Xiangheyuan Middle Street. A short northerly detour offers views of the buildings on the north side of Xiangheyuan Road, and after the detour the route returns to Xiangheyuan North Street.

In Beijing’s Dongcheng District, the boundary turns east at Huangsi Street and then follows the rear property lines of buildings along the northern side. It crosses a street again about one block east of Gulou Outer Street, after which it traces the northern edge of Liuyin Park. From the park’s northeastern corner, the boundary advances due east to Andingmen Outer Street, where it then turns north.

The music video for After All This Time was directed by Bill Pope. In the clip, Crowell is shown singing into a microphone against a black backdrop, dressed in an all-black ensemble. Interspersed scenes depict him in a cafe, where he notices a waitress’s name tag and finds comfort in her presence, a moment that triggers memories of his departed lover. Additional footage features him seated on a couch, tuning his guitar. The video received a nomination for the Country Music Association Award for Video of the Year.

Dinah is a song linked to Wynton Marsalis and was released in 2019 as part of the Bolden soundtrack. Bolden is a biopic about jazz pioneer Buddy Bolden. The song Dinah is performed by Reno Wilson, who portrayed Louis Armstrong in the Bolden film.

Louis Armstrong recorded the song "Dinah" in New York City on May 4, 1930. The recording was released by Okeh Records. Subsequently, "Dinah" became a regular feature in Armstrong's live performances and radio broadcasts.

Gaël Monfils’s season included a result at the Indian Wells Masters where he was the 12th seed, had a bye in the first round, and was defeated by Simon Greul in three sets. He then withdrew from three consecutive Masters 1000 events—the Sony Ericsson Open, the Monte Carlo Masters, and the Rome Masters. He was set to return at the Estoril Open with a wildcard but withdrew due to a stomach injury. Returning at the Madrid Masters, he advanced to the quarterfinals without dropping a set, ultimately losing to the third seed Rafael Nadal. In the Open de Nice Côte d’Azur he reached the quarterfinals before losing to Potito Starace. At the French Open, having reached the quarterfinals the previous year, he led two sets to love and secured a break, but was upset by Fabio Fognini in a five-set contest that stretched over two days.
Gaël Monfils began the 2004 season with a ranking of No. 925 and achieved a considerable rise over the year, culminating in a year-end ranking of No. 239 in the ATP world rankings.

Jeff Rulifson began his career at Xerox PARC, contributing to the development of distributed office systems. In 1980 he served as engineering manager at ROLM, and in 1985 he joined Syntelligence in Sunnyvale, California, an AI applications vendor.
