He began working for Sun Microsystems Laboratories in 1987, where he held leadership roles including director of engineering, head of technology development, and leadership of various research groups. From 2003 he managed Ivan Sutherland's laboratory until his retirement. He is an emeritus board member of the Doug Engelbart Institute and has served as chairman of The Open Group.

Jeff Rulifson is a computer scientist whose work contributed to the early development of hypertext, outline processing systems, and video conferencing. In 1990, he received the ACM Software System Award in recognition of implementing these transformative technologies. Four years later, he was elected as an ACM Fellow for his pioneering efforts to augment human intellect through hypertext, outline processors, and video conferencing. In 2006, he was inducted into the SRI International Hall of Fame, acknowledging his lasting impact at the organization.

The Microsoft Cognitive Toolkit, formerly known as CNTK, is a deprecated deep learning framework developed by Microsoft Research. It is sometimes styled as "The Microsoft Cognitive Toolkit." The toolkit describes neural networks as a series of computational steps organized within a directed graph.

Three provincial by-elections were held in Alberta on June 23, 2025, to fill vacancies in the Legislative Assembly of Alberta. These contests were conducted across the province to elect replacements for members who had vacated their seats.

In May 2025, the Independence Party of Alberta and the Republican Party of Alberta signed a memorandum of understanding to advance and unify the independence movement in Alberta. The agreement facilitated collaboration between the two parties and led to candidates who ran under the Republican banner in the 2025 Alberta provincial by-elections.

Following the Russo-Persian War of 1826–1828, Abbas Mirza on 2 February 1828 signed the Treaty of Turkmenchay. Under its terms, Iran ceded Erivan (Yerevan) and Nakhichevan to Russia and agreed to substantial war reparations along with other concessions. The financial burden of these payments was borne largely by the Azerbaijan province and Abbas Mirza’s personal fortune, with a minor contribution from the British and none from the shah. The obligation to pay provided Russia with leverage over Iran in the ensuing period. In addition, the treaty broadened Russian influence in Iranian politics, as the shah sought Russia’s recognition of his designated heir apparent.

During the lead-up to the Russo-Persian War of 1826–1828, Russian forces under Aleksey Yermolov advanced into disputed border areas, seizing the northern bank of Lake Gokcha in early 1825, a region Iran regarded as Iranian territory. The Russians continued their advance and captured Balagh-lu. Iranians viewed these locations as potentially serving as staging grounds for an attack on Erivan, signaling broader strategic significance beyond the sites themselves. Yermolov acknowledged the territory but defended the seizures by arguing that Iran clung to a large portion of Karabakh. The Russians also erected a small fort on the frontier near Erivan, which drew protests from Qajar crown prince Abbas Mirza.

The Bay City Times originally published seven days a week. On June 1, 2009, it shortened its print schedule to three days weekly, specifically Thursdays, Fridays, and Sundays. The Saginaw News and The Flint Journal, its sister publications, adopted the same three-day print arrangement. In response to the reduced print run, all three papers expanded their online presence. The Times, The Saginaw News, and The Flint Journal are produced at the Valley Publishing Co. printing plant in Monitor Township, near Bay City, and Valley Publishing Co. is Booth-owned.

The Bay City Times is a newspaper based in Bay City, Michigan, United States. It publishes editions on Thursdays, Fridays, and Sundays, with a Tuesday edition issued jointly with The Saginaw News. The paper is produced by Booth Newspapers, a subsidiary of Advance Publications. It is the most widely circulated newspaper in northeastern Michigan. Established in 1873, it ranks among the oldest continuously operating newspapers in the region.

In July 2012, the United Kingdom's Serious Fraud Office determined that Oxford University Press (OUP) branches in Kenya and Tanzania engaged in bribery to obtain World Bank-sponsored school bookselling contracts. The SFO imposed a fine of £1.9 million for sums derived from unlawful conduct, and OUP was barred from bidding on World Bank-financed projects for a period of three years.

OUP is the publishing arm of the University of Oxford and the largest university press in the world. Its first printed book appeared in Oxford in 1478, and it was legally authorized to print by decree in 1586. As a result, it stands as the second-oldest university press, behind Cambridge University Press, which was founded in 1534.

Personal identifiers (PID) are a subset of the broader category known as personally identifiable information (PII). PII comprises data elements that can identify an individual, either directly or when combined with other information. Direct identifiers include elements such as a person’s name or a social security number, which alone can reveal identity, while indirect identifiers—such as race, ethnicity, or age—may disclose who a person is when analyzed together with additional data. In this framework, PID denotes those components within PII that identify individuals, reflecting the overall distinction between explicit identifiers and contextual attributes that can lead to identification.

In the early medieval period, the South West of England experienced persistent conflicts involving local and foreign forces. In 838, an English army defeated a combined Cornish and Danish force at Hingston Down near Gunnislake. Edward the Elder later established similar fortifications at Barnstaple and Totnes to strengthen regional defenses. Viking incursions continued intermittently until the Norman Conquest, with notable defeats such as the Devonians at Pinhoe. In 876, Alfred the Great encircled a Danish fleet at Arne and drove it off, leaving around 120 ships wrecked at Studland. Although Alfred possessed lands in Cornwall, the region retained a native kingship, and Cornwall is generally regarded as having come under the English Crown during Athelstan’s reign (924–939). Owing to limited contemporary documentation, proponents of Cornwall’s English status locate its incorporation in that period. A 944 charter issued by Edmund presents him as king of the English and ruler of the Britons’ province, signaling that the so‑called province constituted a territorial possession with a long‑standing, special relationship to the English Crown.

In Bournemouth, a coastal town within South West England, several notable financial and professional firms maintain a presence, reflecting the area’s diversified economy. Tata Consultancy Services, which operated as Unisys Insurance Services prior to 2010, is based in Bournemouth. Imagine Publishing, a magazine publisher, together with The Mortgage Works (owned by Nationwide Building Society), occupies premises at the A35/A347 Richmond Hill Roundabout. Organix is located in the town centre, while retirement housing provider McCarthy & Stone has facilities on the B3066. LV=, the insurance company, is housed at Frizzell House in Westbourne, adjacent to the County Gates Gyratory where the A35 and A338 meet. JPMorgan Chase maintains a large Chaseside site at the junction of the A3060 and A338, opposite the Royal Bournemouth Hospital. Additionally, RIAS (insurance) and Teachers Assurance are situated toward Holdenhurst.

Common Lisp defines four floating-point types: SHORT-FLOAT, SINGLE-FLOAT, DOUBLE-FLOAT, and LONG-FLOAT. In most implementations, only SINGLE-FLOAT and DOUBLE-FLOAT are realized as distinct types, with SHORT-FLOAT and LONG-FLOAT commonly treated as synonyms of the corresponding precision levels; some systems may provide all four as separate types. Consistent with IEEE 754, implementations deliver handling for exceptional conditions such as underflow, overflow, and inexact results. The ANSI standard for Common Lisp does not specify infinities or NaNs, and their representation is not mandated; however, several implementations extend the language by supplying infinities and NaN values.

Double-precision floating-point format uses an 11-bit exponent to encode the scale of the value. Its normal range covers roughly 1×10^-308 to 1×10^308, and the representation offers about 15 to 17 significant decimal digits of precision. In addition, subnormal (denormal) numbers extend the range toward zero to approximately 5×10^-324, albeit with reduced precision compared with normal numbers.

Bastards is the third remix album by Icelandic musician Björk, released on 19 November 2012. The collection features remixes derived from tracks on Biophilia (2011), her seventh studio album. Several of the remixes had previously appeared in The Crystalline Series or the Biophilia Remix Series before being issued on Bastards. The remixes were remastered by Mandy Parnell for this release.

Bastards is a Björk compilation album consisting of remixes that had already been released prior to the collection. The project aimed to distill the essence of the remixes into a single package, with Björk selecting roughly a quarter of the available remixes for inclusion on one CD. The release was intended for listeners who are not proficient at online downloading or who lack the time to search for individual remixes. The cover art features Björk’s 'strata' persona drawn from the Mutual Core music video, which was directed by Andrew Thomas Huang.

On May 10, 1982, the Federal Communications Commission granted approval to KASA-TV's application, which by that time had been amended to relocate the transmitter site to No Name Peak in the Jemez Mountains.

KASA-TV, an independent television station identified as KSAF-TV, began broadcasting on October 31, 1983, one day later than had been announced. The station issued an apology on local radio, noting the delay but assuring that no programming would be omitted. Based in a newly constructed studio at the corner of St. Francis and St. Michael's Drive in Santa Fe, it pledged a strong signal for both Santa Fe and Albuquerque and promised the first live newscast for Santa Fe, the capital of New Mexico. The 9 p.m. newscast, however, was scrapped after three months, with the general manager describing the move as a drain on the startup operation’s resources.

Alps Electric's Automotive Division concentrates on the development of bespoke products and modular systems for automotive applications. Its product lineup includes control panels and steering modules, which are supplied for particular vehicle models. In addition to model-specific solutions, the division also offers components engineered for universal applicability, enabling use across a wide range of vehicles.

Alps Alpine Co., Ltd., a Japanese multinational corporation headquartered in Tokyo, designs and manufactures a broad range of electronic components and devices, including switches, potentiometers, sensors, encoders, and touchpads. In Japanese, the firm is named アルプスアルパイン株式会社 (Arupusu Arupain kabushiki-gaisha), and it was formerly known as Alps Electric Co., Ltd (アルプス電気株式会社, Arupusu Denki Kabushiki-gaisha).

An economic entity is an assumption employed in generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP). It posits that the activities of a given organization or unit can be treated as distinct for accounting and reporting purposes, and it recognizes that nearly any type of organization or unit in society may be regarded as an economic entity.

An ontic inquiry examines the properties, physical relations, and structural aspects of a specific entity, with the pen presented as the exemplar under consideration. The observed property of the pen is that it is black in color. Its internal state is described as being filled with blue ink. In terms of spatial relations, the pen is resting on the desk.

In mid-2010, Covad announced Ethernet-over-Copper services in the Los Angeles market, delivering a product that ran on a Fujitsu Flashwave-based Ethernet core and offering symmetric speeds of up to 20 Mbps. Soon after, Ethernet over DS1 service was added to the portfolio. In early 2011, Covad, then operating as Megapath, announced plans to expand the service nationally by the end of 2012.

Covad's name is derived from a sequence of acronyms that evolved over time to describe the company's concept. The earliest interpretation signified copper with added value, a meaning that later shifted to refer to copper used for voice and data transmission, and eventually to a combined voice-and-data offering. The progression of these acronyms reflects the historical emphasis on copper-based communications within the company's branding.

Albert Rösti served as president of the Agricultural Information Service (LID) from 2007 to 2014. In May 2014, he was elected president of Action for a Sensible Energy Policy Switzerland (AVES). A year later, in May 2015, he succeeded Caspar Baader as president of Swiss Oil, the Swiss association of fuel traders.

Albert Rösti is a Swiss politician affiliated with the Swiss People's Party (SVP). He ran unsuccessfully in the 2010 Bernese Government elections, and in the 2011 federal elections he was elected to the National Council. In 2015, Rösti served as the SVP's campaign manager in the federal election and sought a seat in the Council of States for Bern, though he was not elected. He served in the National Council until December 31, 2022.

GNU TeXmacs is a document preparation system that, similar to LyX, provides visual editing of structured documents within the editing and document‑preparation domain. It emphasizes the organizational structure of a document rather than immediate formatting, and it does not aim to deliver traditional WYSIWYG editing. Instead, the system seeks to render the document’s underlying structure visually, consistent with the WYSIWYM approach, in which What You See Is What You Mean is the guiding principle.

GNU TeXmacs is a structured WYSIWYG editor and document preparation system. It belongs to the lineage of early structured document editors and is comparable to predecessors such as Interleaf (first released in 1985), Framemaker (1986), SoftQuad Author/Editor (1988), Lilac, Grif (1991), and Thot. Academic research has explored interactive editing of complex typographical constructs that are represented in a logical structure.

Lachoudisch is a linguistic variety associated with a Jewish community, notable for its incorporation of Hebrew and Yiddish loanwords. These loanwords reflect the community's hostility to Christianity and to governmental authority, signaling a critical stance toward both religious and political power. The distinctive vocabulary thus serves as a marker of group identity and social sentiment within the broader linguistic landscape.

Lachoudisch was a German dialect native to Schopfloch, a town in Bavaria, notable for its substantial incorporation of Hebrew and Yiddish vocabulary. The dialect originated in the 16th century and endured for several centuries before undergoing a drastic decline; after the Holocaust, only a few speakers remained, and it eventually became extinct sometime in the postwar period.

Alberta Beach is a community whose economy centers on tourism and recreation. It hosts the Lac Ste. Anne Pilgrimage, a significant event for Indigenous peoples, including Cree, Dene, Blackfoot and Métis Roman Catholics. The locality is also widely regarded as a principal cottage weekend retreat for residents of Edmonton, contributing to its role as a popular getaway destination.

The popularity of the Alberta Beach atmosphere spurred the creation of the Moonlight Express, a weekend railway service linking Edmonton with Alberta Beach. The service collected passengers in Edmonton on Saturday mornings and transported them to Alberta Beach, with return trips from Alberta Beach to Edmonton on Sunday nights.

On 14 June 1940 the first mass transport arrived at Auschwitz, comprising 728 Polish male political prisoners from Tarnów, including Catholic priests and Jews. The detainees were registered with serial numbers 31 through 758. On 12 July 1940 Höss wrote to Glücks that the local population was fanatically Polish and ready to undertake any operation against the hated SS men. By the end of 1940 the SS confiscated land surrounding the camp to establish a 40-square-kilometer zone of interest (Interessengebiet) patrolled by the SS, Gestapo, and local police. By March 1941, the camp housed about 10,900 prisoners, most of them Polish.

Within Auschwitz, certain prisoners were designated as Funktionshäftlinge (functionaries), a status initially assigned to non-Jewish Germans and later extended to Jews and non-Jewish Poles. Those labeled as functionaries were afforded relatively better housing and food compared with the general inmate population. The camp elite, known as Lagerprominenz, encompassed roles such as Blockschreiber (barracks clerk), Kapo (overseer), Stubendienst (barracks orderly), and Kommandierte (trusties), who exercised substantial authority over fellow prisoners and gained a reputation for cruelty. This concentration of power among a small group contributed to a climate in which abuses could be perpetrated with relative impunity. After the war, only a small number of these individuals were prosecuted, in part because it was difficult to determine which atrocities were carried out under direct SS orders.

Jingxing County is a county in Hebei Province, located in northern China. It falls under the administration of the prefecture-level city of Shijiazhuang, which also serves as the provincial capital. In Chinese, the county’s name is written as 井陉县 in simplified form and 井陘縣 in traditional form, with the pinyin rendering Jǐngxíng Xiàn, and it literally means "Well Border."

According to traditional accounts, King Mu of Zhou hunted in the area and described the land as being higher around its outer perimeter with a deep central hollow, a configuration likened to a well. This resemblance to the border of a stove is said to have inspired the name of the locality, which subsequently became Jingxing County.

The Red Sea is recognized for its rich and diverse marine ecosystem. Its waters have yielded records of more than 1,200 fish species, reflecting substantial biodiversity. Approximately one-tenth of these species are endemic to the Red Sea, occurring nowhere else. This combination of high species richness and endemism highlights the region's distinctive evolutionary history and its significance for conservation and scientific study.

During the 6th century BCE, Darius the Great, ruler of the Achaemenid Empire in Persia, undertook initiatives to develop and extend maritime navigation in the Red Sea. He dispatched reconnaissance missions to survey the Red Sea and identify navigational hazards, such as rocks and currents. These efforts contributed to safer and more efficient routes for navigation in the region.

Phanaʼ is a language that was first documented by the linguist Lefèvre-Pontalis in 1892, who reported its use in the locality of Poufang, Lai Châu Province, Vietnam. In his documentation, he also provides a word list for Phanaʼ, offering an early lexical record of the language.

Phanaʼ is a Loloish language spoken in Laos and China, whose self-designation is pa55 na33 and which is also referred to as Bana or Pana. In Laos it is spoken by about 500 people, while in China it occurs in Mengla County, Yunnan Province. The language is closely related to Sila, which is spoken by roughly 2,000 people in Laos and Vietnam. Research by Badenoch indicates that Phanaʼ is similar to Ban Ban Sida, described with the phonetic form vɛ33 ɲɯ33.

ALGOL 68 employs a distinctive set of special symbols beyond the ASCII repertoire, featuring characters such as ⊂, ≡, ␣, ×, ÷, ≤, ≥, ≠, ¬, ⊃, ∨, ∧, →, ↓, ↑, ⌊, ⌈, ⎩, ⎧, ⊥, ⏨, ¢, ○ and □. These glyphs were accessible on the IBM 2741 teletype when it was fitted with an APL 'golf-ball' print head, a hardware configuration used in the language's drafting in the mid-1960s. In contemporary standards, the symbols have been incorporated into Unicode, and the majority are available in several widely used fonts.

In ALGOL 68, declaring a variable as REAL x does not create a plain value but rather introduces a reference to a REAL object, initialized to a newly created local REAL storage. Put simply, this declaration functions as a shorthand for establishing a reference to a locally scoped REAL and binding x to that reference; consequently, x serves as a constant identifier that points to the newly generated local REAL variable.

A convex measure is a probability measure characterized by the property that for any pair of measurable sets A and B and any measurable intermediate set C with A ⊆ C ⊆ B, the measure of C does not exceed the larger of the measures of A and B. Different schemes for comparing the probabilities of A, B, and their intermediate sets give rise to several definitions of convexity, including concepts such as log-concavity and harmonic convexity. Christer Borell is recognized as a pioneer in the detailed study of convex measures on locally convex spaces, beginning in the 1970s.

Convex measures are arranged in a hierarchical order according to a convexity parameter that ranges from −∞ to 0. The −∞-convex measures form the largest class within this hierarchy, whereas the 0-convex measures constitute the smallest one. The 0-convex class corresponds precisely to the log-concave measures (also known as logarithmically concave measures).

Riding and archery were central to Manchu culture, and Huangtaiji regarded these activities as the most important martial arts. The Manchus were well-trained horsemen, and the Qing dynasty treasured riding and archery as core military skills. To maintain proficiency across society, riding and archery tests were held each spring and fall for all Manchus, spanning the social spectrum from commoners to aristocrats, with the outcomes affecting noble rank. In the early Qing period, Manchus were noted for excellent shooting skills, and arrows were reputed to penetrate two bodies.

The Manchu people show a range of paternal lineages, including a royal lineage linked to Y-DNA haplogroup C2b1a3a2-F8951, a subclade of C2a-L1373 within the northern branch of C2-M217, indicating a close paternal connection to the Ao clan of the Daghur group. Data from the 23Mofang project for the Gūwalgiya clan indicate that roughly one third belong to haplogroup C-F11330, descending from the northern C2a-L1373 lineage. In the Yehe Nara clan, 23Mofang data record about 40% of individuals carrying haplogroup C, with approximately 20% assigned to C-MF46267, a lineage that descends from C-M407, the same branch as Dayan Khan. The C-M407 lineage is predominant among Buryats and Oirats, suggesting shared paternal origins with Yehe Nara.

The endometrium is the innermost mucosal lining of the uterus. It serves to prevent adhesions between opposing walls of the myometrium, thereby maintaining the patency of the uterine cavity. Over the course of the menstrual cycle, it thickens into a vascular, glandular tissue layer that provides an optimal environment for blastocyst implantation. Radiographically, the endometrium is centrally located within the uterine cavity and is typically visible as echogenic tissue on ultrasound. Its average thickness is about 6.7 millimeters.

Following fertilization, an embryo may implant into the uterine wall, a process that is accompanied by the production of human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG) which serves as a feedback signal. The hCG stimulus maintains the corpus luteum, enabling it to continue secreting progesterone and estrogen to support the early pregnancy and sustain the endometrial environment. If implantation occurs, the endometrial lining undergoes decidualization, forming the decidua. The decidua contributes to the maternal portion of the placenta and provides essential support and protection for gestation, helping to stabilize and nourish the developing fetus throughout pregnancy.
The ribbon seal is the only living species in the genus Histriophoca. A putative fossil species, Histriophoca alekseevi, has been described, with the fossil dating to the Miocene of Moldova.

In March 2008, the United States government initiated a review of the ribbon seal population in Alaska and considered placing the species on the Endangered Species List. By December 2008, officials determined that the sea ice critical to the ribbon seal's survival would not be endangered by global warming and thus declined to list the species under the Endangered Species Act. Consequently, the ribbon seal was designated a National Marine Fisheries Service (NMFS) Species of Concern rather than being listed under the Endangered Species Act. NMFS, a component of NOAA, has noted concerns about the status and threats facing some species because information is insufficient to support listing them under the ESA.

Matthäus Merian was renowned for the finesse of his alchemical illustrations, and his engraving work extended to several significant hermetic and natural history texts of the early modern period. He produced engravings for the Musaeum Hermeticum (1678) and for Atalanta Fugiens (1618), as well as plates for De Serpentibus, compiled by John Jonston as an encyclopedic work on insect natural history. The stylistic tradition he helped establish in this realm would be carried forward by his daughter.

Matthäus Merian was a Swiss-born engraver who trained in copperplate engraving in Zürich and subsequently studied and worked in Strasbourg, Nancy, and Paris. He returned to Basel in 1615 and moved to Oppenheim in 1616, where he produced work for the publisher Johann Theodor de Bry, who was the son of the renowned engraver and traveler Theodor de Bry.

Spain's national under-17 football team is regarded as one of the strongest national sides at the under-17 level. It has participated in nine of the fourteen FIFA U-17 World Cup tournaments, illustrating its long-standing presence in youth international competition. The team holds the record for reaching the final the most times without ever winning the tournament, having finished as runners-up on four occasions.

Representing Spain at the under-17 level, the national team is governed by the Royal Spanish Football Federation and competes in major youth international tournaments. In published summaries of its tournament results, a color-coding scheme is used to denote podium finishes, with gold backgrounds marking first place, silver backgrounds marking second place, and bronze backgrounds marking third place.

The Military Forces of Colombia, the nation’s armed forces, have played a central role in both external and internal security matters. During World War II, Colombia contributed to Allied operations, and it was the only Latin American country to dispatch troops to the Korean War, where Colombian units served under United Nations command. Within the country, since the beginning of the long-running internal conflict, the armed forces have carried out combat, pacification, counter-insurgency, and drug interdiction across the national territory. In more recent years, elements of the force have participated in international counter-piracy efforts in the Horn of Africa, operating under Operation Ocean Shield and Operation Atalanta.

Defense spending in 2000 accounted for about 3.9 percent of gross domestic product, and by 2008 it had risen to roughly 4.8 percent, ranking Colombia fourteenth worldwide in military expenditure. The armed forces numbered around 250,000 uniformed personnel, including about 145,000 military and 105,000 police, with figures excluding support and ancillary staff such as cooks, medics, and mechanics. This composition underpins Colombia’s status as one of the largest and most capable, and among the best equipped, military forces in Latin America. A notable portion of personnel have received training assistance within Colombia and the United States, while the U.S. contributed equipment and financing through programs such as the Military Assistance Program, Foreign Military Sales, and the International Narcotics Control Program, all conducted under Plan Colombia.

Invisible disability refers to disabilities that are not readily visible, with mental disorders forming a major category, though they are not the sole type. The National Institute of Mental Health estimates that roughly twenty percent of United States residents receive a formal diagnosis of a mental disorder, a figure that suggests many individuals remain undiagnosed because they do not seek help or encounter barriers to care. About 57 million American adults are diagnosed with mental disorders. In addition, approximately four percent of Americans have a serious mental condition that substantially interferes with daily functioning, including work and relationships.

Invisible disabilities encompass mobility-related conditions that may not be readily observable, including sitting disabilities arising from chronic back pain, joint problems, or chronic pain. The severity of impairment and the ability to move can vary from day to day, leading to inconsistent use of mobility aids and accommodations. People with repetitive strain injury often move in a typical, unobtrusive manner, which can conceal the underlying impairment. In medical practice, there is a tendency to encourage RSI patients to remain active, including participation in sports. Nevertheless, despite outward appearances, RSI can impose substantial limitations on activities such as typing, writing, or gripping objects like a phone. The inconspicuous nature of these disabilities frequently leads to underestimation of their impact and challenges.

Maha Sura Singhanat (Surasi) participated from 1771 to 1781 in campaigns with his brother to subdue the Laotian kingdoms of Vientiane, Luang Prabang, and Champasak, as well as Cambodia. In 1781, as Taksin’s rule faced a rebellion aimed at deposing him, Surasi’s brother Somdet Chao Phraya Maha Kasatsuek returned to Bangkok to quell the uprising. Maha Kasatsuek then proclaimed himself Ramathibodi (Rama I) and relocated the capital to the left bank of the Chao Phraya River (the site of present-day Bangkok). As Ramathibodi’s close aide, Surasi was appointed the Front Palace, the office designated for the throne’s heir.

Maha Sura Singhanat, born Bunma in 1744 to Thongdee and Daoreung, belonged to a prominent Northern Siamese lineage. His father served as the Royal Secretary of Northern Siam and Keeper of the Royal Seal, situating Bunma within the high aristocracy from birth. He began his aristocratic career within the palace as a royal page, marking the initial phase of his life at court. Thongdee was a descendant of Kosa Pan, who led Siam’s 17th-century mission to France, connecting Bunma to a notable diplomatic lineage. Bunma had four full siblings and two half-siblings, making him the youngest child of Daoreung.

Master of Arts at Oxford, Cambridge, and Dublin is a traditional degree conferred upon holders of the undergraduate BA after a substantial interval following matriculation, typically around seven years. This occurs notwithstanding the general shortening of undergraduate programmes across subjects to three or four years, and it reflects historic patterns in liberal arts education that align with earlier schooling and higher entry ages for university, typically 17 to 19. In a contrasting national framework, France awards the baccalauréat as its principal school-leaving certificate.

Up to 1865, King's College, Cambridge admitted exclusively pupils from Eton College, and those Eton-educated graduates could obtain the BA and subsequently the MA without performing university examinations. At New College, Oxford, the intake likewise came solely from Winchester College, and these students enjoyed the same BA and MA exam exemptions until 1834. In both cases, the exemptions were tied to the feeder schools and were discontinued after the specified dates.

Embankment is a London Underground station on the Circle and District lines that has experienced a series of historical service realignments. On 30 June 1900, the Middle Circle service was shortened to terminate at Earl’s Court, altering through-routing through the station. Later, on 31 December 1908, the Outer Circle service was withdrawn from District Railway tracks, changing the pattern of trains serving Embankment. In 1949, the Metropolitan line-operated Inner Circle route was given its own identity on the tube map as the Circle line, clarifying the branding and passenger guidance for the route that serves the station.

In 1897, the District Railway obtained parliamentary permission to construct a deep-level tube railway beneath the sub-surface line, running between Gloucester Road and Mansion House as an express electric-train route designed to relieve congestion on the sub-surface tracks. An intermediate station was planned at Charing Cross, situated about 63 feet (19 metres) below the sub-surface platforms. No immediate construction occurred. After the District Railway was taken over by the Underground Electric Railways Company of London and resignalling and electrification of DR routes were completed in 1903–1905, the anticipated congestion relief was achieved without building the deep-level line, and the plan was dropped in 1908.

In labor economics, seniority refers to wage progression tied to length of service within a firm and can operate as an incentive mechanism under imperfect supervision. Firms may employ delayed compensation schemes in which initial pay falls short of the discounted value of early output, while later earnings exceed it, thereby encouraging sustained effort. As tenure increases, wages rise progressively, producing a continuous upward trajectory with time on the job. The prospect of dismissal and the loss of higher, tenure‑linked future wages heightens the cost of shirking, reinforcing effort and aligning employees’ incentives with long‑run employment.

In the late 20th century, the United States federal government reoriented its compensation policy for white-collar employees, reducing dependence on seniority as the primary basis for pay raises. Under the Reagan administration, the longstanding seniority-based pay increase system was replaced with a merit-based framework that linked raises to performance evaluations, thereby introducing an appraisal-driven component to federal pay.

In Eswatini, the principal Swazi social unit is the homestead, a traditional beehive-shaped dwelling thatched with dry grass. In polygynous households, each wife maintains her own hut and a surrounding yard enclosed by reed fences. A typical homestead comprises separate structures designated for sleeping, cooking, and storage, with the latter often used for beer brewing; larger homesteads may include quarters for unmarried men and space for guests. At the center of the homestead lies the cattle byre, a circular enclosure formed by large logs and interwoven branches, which functions as both a store of wealth and a symbol of prestige, and it houses sealed grain pits. Opposite the cattle byre is the great hut, occupied by the mother of the headman. The headman is central to all homestead affairs and is often polygynous; he leads by example and provides counsel to his wives on social matters and the family’s welfare. Additionally, he spends time with younger males—typically his sons or other close relatives—offering guidance on growing up and manhood.

Eswatini contends with substantial public health challenges, especially a heavy burden of HIV/AIDS and tuberculosis, with HIV infection more widespread than tuberculosis. Approximately 28 percent of adults are HIV-positive. As of 2018, life expectancy at birth was around 58 years, placing the country among those with the lowest life expectancies globally (the twelfth-lowest). Additionally, the population is notably young: about 35 percent were aged 14 years or younger in 2018, and the median age stood at roughly 22 years.
In 2008, Google released the Chrome browser, which introduced the V8 JavaScript engine. V8 was significantly faster than competing JavaScript engines at the time.

V8’s influence extended beyond traditional web browsers with the introduction of Node.js in 2009 and the accompanying npm package manager in 2010. Together, Node.js and npm enabled V8 to power substantial amounts of server-side JavaScript code, broadening the engine’s reach beyond client-side execution. In 2013, Electron emerged, enabling desktop applications to be built with web technologies by integrating Chromium, V8, and Node.js.

Chugai Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. is a Japanese drug manufacturer headquartered in Tokyo. It operates as a subsidiary under the control of Hoffmann-La Roche, which owned 62% of Chugai as of 30 June 2014. Osamu Nagayama serves as representative director and chairman, while Tatsuro Kosaka holds the roles of representative director, president and chief executive officer.

The medical imaging industry encompasses a diverse set of organizations, including producers of imaging devices, independent radiology centers, and hospitals. Together, these entities provide diagnostic imaging services and related equipment across various healthcare settings.

Medical imaging, while primarily a medical technology for visualizing internal structures, has been described in some contexts as forming part of the broader practice of photography. A U.S. government statement has explicitly characterized magnetic resonance imaging and computed tomography scans, along with related imaging modalities, as being analogous to photography. The central idea in this framing is to treat the outputs produced by medical imaging technologies as comparable to conventional photographs, highlighting similarities in image production, representation, and interpretation despite differences in purpose and content.

Following the death of Liu Yuan, his son Liu Cong killed his elder brother Liu He and seized the throne. He then overran the Jin heartland, capturing Luoyang and Emperor Huai in 311. In 316, Liu Cong’s cousin Liu Yao seized Chang’an and Emperor Min, bringing an end to the Western Jin dynasty. A Jin prince who had moved south maintained Jin authority as the Eastern Jin, established at Jiankang (present-day Nanjing). The collapse of Jin power in the northern regions prompted numerous other leaders to declare independence, contributing to the fragmentation characteristic of the period. In 315, Tuoba Yilu, a Xianbei chieftain, founded the Dai in what is now Inner Mongolia, and in 318 Zhang Shi, an ethnic Chinese governor of Liangzhou, established the Former Liang in the area of modern-day Gansu.

The Sixteen Kingdoms denotes a chaotic interval in northern China from AD 304 to 439, during which a multitude of short-lived dynastic states emerged and dissolved. Most of these regimes were founded by non-Han groups, including the Xiongnu, Xianbei, Di, Jie, and Qiang, though several were established by Han Chinese. Regardless of origins, all of the states adopted Han dynasty–style constitutional and administrative forms and claimed legitimate monarchy. The period was marked by frequent warfare, both among the rival kingdoms and against the Eastern Jin following the collapse of the Western Jin in 317. The era ended in 439 when the Northern Wei, founded by the Tuoba Xianbei, succeeded in reunifying the north. In the south, the Eastern Jin collapsed in 420, giving way to Liu Song, the first of the Southern Dynasties. The reunification of the north thus ushered in the broader Northern and Southern Dynasties era.

At the CFMEU Construction National Conference held in Cairns on 16 October 2013, David Hanna, secretary of the Builders Labourers Federation, and Michael Ravbar, secretary of CFMEU Queensland Construction Division, announced that the two unions would merge. The merger was finalised in 2014.

Although the Builders Labourers Federation is generally associated with left-leaning politics, the Queensland branch aligned with the Australian Labor Party’s right-wing faction. In Queensland, the BLF was part of the Labor Unity faction, a group also known as the Old Guard. At state Labor conferences, the Labor Unity faction frequently cast votes in concert with the right-leaning AWU/Forum faction, reflecting its cross-faction alignment within the ALP structure.

one news is a 24/7 philippine pay television and news channel owned by mediaquest holdings through its subsidiary cignal tv. launched in may 2018 exclusively on the satellite platform cignal, it was the first mediaquest channel to adopt the one branding, which is now known as the one network media group. it is part of the one-branded lineup alongside one sports (free tv), one sports+ (cable), one ph (filipino-language news), one life (lifestyle portal), and the now-defunct one screen (premium entertainment).

One News is an English-language television news channel launched by Cignal TV on May 28, 2018. It provides news and related programming in English and features content from MediaQuest Group’s news divisions, including News5, The Philippine Star, and BusinessWorld. The channel also incorporates material from Bloomberg TV Philippines and Probe Productions, expanding its coverage with international and investigative offerings. Most programs from its predecessor were retained on the new channel, ensuring continuity with its earlier lineup.

Zhuifen railway station is a railway facility situated on the route from Zhuifen to Chenggong, served by the Chengzhui line. Tickets issued there are regarded as auspicious among students, reflecting a linguistic double meaning: the wording resembles an expression associated with achieving a good grade, implying academic success, and a slight variation in pronunciation can also be interpreted as a wish for marriage.

Zhuifen railway station (Chinese: 追分車站; Hanyu Pinyin: Zhuīfēn chēzhàn; Tongyong Pinyin: Jhueifen Chejhàn) is a railway station on the Taiwan Railways Administration Western Trunk line, located in Dadu District, Taichung, Taiwan.

Google Pay Send is a component of Google Pay that permits users to transfer funds to one another. To initiate a payment, the sender supplies the recipient's email address or mobile phone number. The recipient must associate that email address or phone number with a bank account to access the funds. If the recipient already holds a Google Pay account, the funds are deposited directly into that account.

Google Checkout, introduced as Google's competitor to PayPal, operated from 2006 until its discontinuation in 2013. In 2011, Google Wallet assumed the services previously provided by Checkout, effectively replacing its core functionality. The development and support for Google Checkout were subsequently halted in 2013 as Google redirected its emphasis to Wallet and related payment initiatives.

Within the Yogācāra tradition, the logico-epistemological wing avoided direct critique by adopting the designation citta-santāna, commonly rendered as "mind-stream," in place of ālaya-vijñāna. The term citta-santāna denotes a concept broadly equivalent to storehouse-consciousness, capturing the idea of a repository of latent imprints shaping experience. By framing the continuum as a dynamic mind-stream rather than a fixed substratum, proponents argued that it does not constitute a reified self, presenting the stream as an ongoing process rather than an enduring ego.

In Sanskrit, citta-saṃtāna is rendered as the "stream of mind" and refers to the continuum of mind or awareness—the succession of mental moments in which each moment arises as the previous one ceases. The mindstream denotes the ongoing flow of conscious experience and provides continuity of mentation without a permanently abiding self (ātman), a concept Buddhist doctrine denies. This continuity is conceived as persisting from one life to another, often illustrated by the analogy of a candle flame passed from one candle to another. Indian Buddhist thought views the evolution of mind as the persistence of individual mind-streams across lifetimes, with karma functioning as the primary causal mechanism that transmits transformations from one life to the next.

HTMS Krabi was the first modified River-class offshore patrol vessel built for the Royal Thai Navy, constructed in Thailand with design, technology transfer, and ongoing support provided by BAE Systems. In January 2016, a contract was signed to supply a second River-class OPV to the Royal Thai Navy, to be built under licence at Bangkok Dock Company. The second Thai-built ship is HTMS Prachuap Khiri Khan, which was launched in August 2019 and is fitted with four RGM-84 Harpoon anti-ship missiles, a capability not present on Krabi. Prachuap Khiri Khan was commissioned less than two months after its launch.

The River-class offshore patrol vessel project began with an Agreement in Principle announced on 6 November 2013 for the construction of three patrol vessels for the Royal Navy at a fixed price of £348 million, including spares and support. In August 2014, BAE Systems signed the contract to build the ships at its Glasgow-based yards along the River Clyde. The subsequent Batch 2 units are configured to undertake constabulary duties, including counter-terrorism, counter-piracy, and anti-smuggling operations. Designed for global deployment, the class performs anti-piracy, counter-terrorism, and anti-smuggling tasks that are typically associated with larger frigates and destroyers. Steel cutting for the program occurred on 10 October 2014. The River-class began entering service in 2017, with the final vessel delivered in August 2020. Construction takes place at BAE Systems' Govan shipyard before ships are transferred to Scotstoun for fitting out.

Numerical optimization is organized into subfields according to the form of the objective function and the constraint set. Linear programming constitutes the subfield in which the objective function and all constraints are linear. Within linear programming, the simplex method stands as a classical and widely employed algorithm for determining an optimal solution by moving along a sequence of basic feasible solutions.

In this context, the exact solution is known to lie between 1.875 and 2.0625. The algorithm may produce any approximation within that interval, rather than a unique value. Accordingly, the absolute error of such outputs is guaranteed to be less than 0.2.

Following the 1989 military coup in Sudan, which imposed sharia law, music halls and outdoor performances were closed and restrictions were placed on musicians and audiences. The crackdown sidelined many prominent musicians and writers, with some being barred from public life and a number imprisoned, while others went into exile, including Mohammed al Amin and Mohammed Wardi who sought refuge in Cairo. Traditional music suffered as East African zār ceremonies were interrupted and labeled pagan. Singers such as Setona, born in Kordofan and raised in Khartoum who emigrated to Cairo in 1989, published two albums, Tariq Sudan and Queen of Hena, both linked to henna ceremonies. Nada Al-Qalaa emerged in the 1990s with conservative views on social life and gender roles, drawing criticism for perceived closeness to the military government due to wealthy patronage, yet she built a wide following over more than twenty years. Abu Araki al-Bakheit was barred from performing political songs but continued to perform, making a notable comeback in 2019 during the Sudanese revolution. Yousif Fataki, a southern Sudanese singer, had all of his tapes erased by Radio Omdurman. Other popular performers during this period included Abdel Karim al Kabli, Mahmoud Abdulaziz, Mohammed al Amin, and Mohammed Wardi. Awad Ahmoudi, a blind oud player, was known for a distinctive oud style and pentatonic scales, often accompanying Wardi and poetry recitals.

The Bells of Dublin, released in 1991, is a Christmas album by the Irish ensemble The Chieftains. The collection features Christmas songs and traditional carols and includes guest performances from Elvis Costello, Jackson Browne, Kate and Anna McGarrigle, Marianne Faithfull, Nanci Griffith, Rickie Lee Jones, and Burgess Meredith.

In the liner notes for The Bells of Dublin, Paddy Moloney states that the recording sessions hold special memories for The Chieftains and for himself, and he describes the sessions as bringing together the full spectrum of the festive season.

Within Ukrainian literature, the Union of Ukrainian Writers, an artists’ organization that had operated since the Soviet era, stood as a longstanding but controversial institution, garnering a negative reputation among many younger writers. The organization was re-established in 1997, reflecting a post-Soviet recalibration of its role in the literary field. In the following year, 1998, PEN Ukraine was founded to promote literary freedom and international engagement for Ukrainian writers.

Ukrainian literature traces its origins to the age of Kievan Rus', with early Rus' chronicles and epic poetry composed in Old Church Slavonic, while oral folktales circulated within the culture. Although Old Church Slavonic served as a literary vehicle, the everyday language of the region was Old East Slavic, which later diverged into Ukrainian, Russian, and Belarusian. Ukrainian culture flourished under the Cossack state, a polity that was subsequently partitioned by neighboring powers into eastern and western parts. Beginning in the 19th century, literature in Ukrainian increasingly adopted a vernacular form, as poetry, novels, plays, and other genres appeared and aided the growth of nationalist and independence movements. Throughout the period, the Russian Empire and later the Soviet Union frequently restricted or suppressed the Ukrainian language, its modes of expression, and its chosen subjects.

The Moto X is an Android smartphone released in August 2013 and is one of Lenovo's first new products after its acquisition by Google in 2012. It was initially developed under the codename “X Phone” and targeted at mainstream consumers. The device featured voice recognition and contextual awareness, and offered customizable color options. Final assembly of the Moto X was completed in the United States.

ZUK Mobile is a Lenovo subsidiary that markets exclusively under its own brand rather than the Lenovo label. The brand name ZUK is pronounced by spelling each letter individually (Z-U-K). Originally, the entity was known as Shenqi before adopting the ZUK name. As part of Lenovo's strategy, ZUK seeks to offer higher-quality, higher-margin devices and to cultivate a youthful, refreshed brand image. Xiaomi is considered ZUK's primary competitor in the market. The company plans to market its products on a global scale, targeting customers worldwide.

Percussion instruments are classified according to several criteria. These include the instrument’s construction, its ethnic origin, its function within musical theory and orchestration, and the extent to which it is familiar in common knowledge.

Percussion instruments are central to many musical ensembles, providing rhythmic foundation and contributing to tempo and texture alongside bass instruments. In jazz and other popular genres, the rhythm section typically includes a pianist, a bassist, and a drummer, with a guitarist often joining as well to shape harmony and drive. In classical orchestral writing dating back to Haydn and Mozart, emphasis tends to be on strings, woodwinds, and brass, with percussion playing a supporting yet vital role. The standard orchestral percussion section usually includes timpani, at least in pairs, though these drums are not played continuously; instead they deliver accents and tonal color as required. During the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries, other percussion instruments such as the triangle and cymbals were employed only sparingly. By the twentieth century, composers expanded percussion usage and integrated a broader range of percussion instruments more prominently within classical works.

Happier Than Ever, the second studio album by Billie Eilish, was supported by seven singles, six of which reached the top 40 on the US Billboard Hot 100. The lead single, My Future, was released on July 30, 2020—roughly a year before the album’s anticipated release—with an accompanying animated video directed by Australian animator Andrew Onorato released on the same day. My Future was widely praised by critics and appeared on year-end lists as one of the year's best songs; it debuted at number six on the Hot 100, marking Eilish’s third top-ten entry, though it did not receive radio airplay in the United States and remains the only album single issued on physical discs. The second single, Therefore I Am, followed on November 12, 2020, with a music video directed by Eilish herself; it received positive critical reception and emerged as the album’s most commercially successful track. Therefore I Am debuted at number 94 on the Hot 100 and climbed to number two the next week, a 92-position jump that stands among the fourth-largest advances in Hot 100 history, aided by promotion including a live performance at the 2020 American Music Awards.

Promotional appearances for Happier Than Ever spanned late 2021 and mid-2022, featuring live and televised performances of its tracks. On July 29, 2021, Billie Eilish performed 'NDA' and 'Billie Bossa Nova' on the German television program Undersing. A week later, on August 5, 2021, she delivered a four-song set on BBC Radio 1's Live Lounge, including 'Getting Older,' 'I Didn't Change My Number,' 'NDA,' and a cover of 'I'm in the Mood for Love.' In September 2021, Eilish showcased material from the album at the iHeartRadio Music Festival and the Life Is Beautiful Music & Art Festival, and she also performed 'Getting Older' and 'Billie Bossa Nova' for ABC. In November 2021, she appeared on Sesame Street, offering an alternate rendition of the title track with Count von Count. December 2021 saw her on Saturday Night Live as both host and musical guest, performing the title track and 'Male Fantasy' in a set that echoed the visuals of the music videos. In July 2022, to mark the one-year anniversary, Amoeba Music in Hollywood hosted performances by Eilish and Finneas, with a set list that included 'Getting Older,' 'Billie Bossa Nova,' the title track 'Happier Than Ever,' and 'TV' from Guitar Songs.

Science of team science (SciTS) is an interdisciplinary field that investigates how research teams collaborate to advance scientific knowledge. The definition of a successful team, however, varies across stakeholders and is not universal. To analyze team science, SciTS employs a mix of qualitative and quantitative methods to assess antecedent conditions, the dynamics of collaboration, and the resulting outcomes. In addition, it takes into account the organizational, social, and political contexts that shape and influence team science.

Science of Team Science (SciTS) is a methodological field that studies cross-disciplinary collaboration in research. It aims to understand how researchers from different disciplines collaborate and to enhance the effectiveness of such teamwork. The discipline develops conceptual frameworks and methodological tools for organizing research teams and processes to achieve greater efficiency and impact. SciTS initiatives examine and address factors that influence collaborative science, including organizational, institutional, and cultural determinants, with the goal of enabling more productive cooperation. Additionally, it emphasizes the assessment of collaborative science outcomes, evaluating impacts and results to inform practice and policy decisions.

As of May 2016, the total number of federally recognized tribes reached 567 following the federal recognition of the Pamunkey Indian Tribe of Virginia in July 2015. The Thomasina E. Jordan Indian Tribes of Virginia Federal Recognition Act subsequently added six Virginia tribes, with the bill signed into law in January 2018 after an initial passage in 2017. In July 2018, the Federal Register listed 573 Indian Entities Recognized and Eligible To Receive Services From the Bureau of Indian Affairs. On December 20, 2019, the Little Shell Tribe of Chippewa Indians of Montana was recognized as the 574th federally recognized tribe. The United States government maintains an updated roster of tribal governments through USA.gov, and ancillary information from earlier versions that is no longer current is sometimes presented in italics in archival material.

The federal acknowledgment process for Indian tribes can extend for many years or even decades, with documented delays of roughly 12 to 14 years in some instances. A notable example is the Shinnecock Indian Nation, which petitioned for recognition in 1978 and was acknowledged in 2010, a 32-year span from petition to recognition. In a Senate Committee on Indian Affairs hearing, witnesses described the process as broken and characterized it as lengthy, expensive, burdensome, intrusive, and unfair, further noting that it is arbitrary and capricious, less than transparent, unpredictable, and susceptible to undue political influence and manipulation.

Under a royal order dated August 14, 1569, Miguel López de Legazpi was confirmed as Governor and Captain-General of the Philippines, empowered to administer civil and criminal justice throughout the islands and to exercise both original and appellate jurisdiction in all suits, thereby centralizing judicial authority and effectively functioning as a department of justice. Subsequent cédulas and royal directives charged all officials with enforcing laws and ordinances for the benefit of the local population, though enforcement frequently did not occur in practice. This centralized, enforcement-dependent system drew scrutiny, notably in 1583 when Bishop Domingo de Salazar wrote to King Philip II detailing oppression and injustices against native Filipinos and asserting that decrees meant to protect natives were generally disregarded by the Governor-General and his subordinates.

Supreme Court justices in the Philippines are subject to a mandatory retirement age of 70. Some nonetheless retire before reaching that age. Florentino Feliciano retired at 67 to accept an appointment to the World Trade Organization Appellate Body, while Alicia Austria-Martinez retired at 68 for health reasons.

What Goes Around... Comes Around emerged from early sessions for Justin Timberlake's FutureSex/LoveSounds at Timbaland's Virginia Beach studio, where the project initially lacked a formal plan or title and the overall direction of the work was uncertain. Timberlake instructed collaborators to create a reinterpretation of his previous single Cry Me a River as a point of reference rather than an exact reproduction. Producer Danja later stated that there was essentially no set direction beyond attempting to convey the grandeur of Cry Me a River, with no predetermined sonic blueprint for either the track or the album. This absence of a fixed artistic path during the early stages reflects the exploratory nature of the album's creation.

In the video’s narrative sequence, Timberlake is shown introducing Johansson’s character to a drunk Shawn Hatosy at a club, with Timberlake implying that Hatosy should watch over her. He grows suspicious that she may have another man on the side after the introduction. Upon returning, he finds Johansson kissing Hatosy in a stairwell and responds by punching Hatosy. Johansson then speeds away in a 1967 Corvette Sting Ray, chased by Timberlake in a Porsche Carrera GT. The pursuit culminates in a fiery multi-vehicle crash, with Johansson ejected from the car as it tumbles and comes to rest several feet away, twice. Timberlake discovers her motionless on the ground and kneels beside her as the camera moves toward the sky. The ending references BUtterfield 8 (1960) with Elizabeth Taylor, depicting Gloria dying in a similar manner and employing many comparable shots.

Gh hiphop is a Ghanaian musical movement that blends hip hop with local Ghanaian languages, notably Twi, Ga, Ewe, and Hausa, and with Ghanaian Pidgin English, giving it a distinct linguistic profile compared with Western hip hop. In the genre’s early phase, prominent figures included Reggie Rockstone, Kae Sun, Sway DeSafo, Samini, Okyeame Kwame, Bradez, Buk Bak, D-Black, Sarkodie, Tic Tac, Obrafour, 4x4, Kwaw Kese, and Ayigbe Edem. The scene has continued to grow with a newer generation of artists such as Lil Shaker, Bra Kevin, Rayoe, Yaa Pono, Loone, Asem, and EL. Notable songs from this period include Asabone, Eye Mo De Anaa, and You No Get Money.

Ghanaian hip hop has seen the ascendancy of a new-school generation that dominates the contemporary scene. Notable figures of this movement include Patapaa, Pappy Kojo, Joey B, La Meme Gang, Big Ghun, Amerado, B4bonah, Teephlow, Kojo Cue, Lil Shaker, R2Bees, and Kwesi Arthur.

Angela's Christmas presents a family narrative in which Pat repeatedly tries to persuade the others to accept a certain belief. The scene shifts upstairs, where Angela is found with Baby Jesus, and they bring both downstairs. Pat debates with Angela about how the event occurred, prompting the mother to intervene and recount a story from New Year’s Eve. Shortly after Angela’s birth, the father is arrested for taking coal from the back of a fuel cart, an arrest described as resulting from a bid to keep the house warm for the baby. The mother expresses sadness over the situation, reflecting on the circumstances surrounding these events.

Set in Limerick, Ireland, in 1914, the story centers on Angela and her family—her two older brothers, Pat and Tom, her younger sister Aggie, and their mother—as they attend Mass at a local church. While there, Angela notices the infant Jesus in the crib and believes the child is cold, prompting her to feel sympathy for him. After Mass, she convinces her mother to permit a return to light a candle for the figure. However, Angela instead quietly removes the infant Jesus from the crib and conceals him during the journey home.

Following the dissolution of Dire Straits, Mark Knopfler has shown no interest in reviving the band. In his solo career, keyboardist Guy Fletcher has been involved with nearly every recording, reflecting a sustained collaborative relationship. Danny Cummings has been a frequent contributor to Knopfler's solo material, notably on four recent albums: All the Roadrunning (with Emmylou Harris), Kill to Get Crimson, Get Lucky, and One Deep River.

Mark Knopfler began his career in journalism after a year of study at Harlow College, taking up a post as a junior reporter with the Yorkshire Evening Post in Leeds in 1968. During this period he befriended Steve Phillips, a furniture restorer and part-time performer with a strong interest in country blues, who was a year his senior. Through Phillips's record collection and guitar style, Knopfler absorbed knowledge of early blues artists and their approaches. The pair formed the duo The Duolian String Pickers and performed in local folk and acoustic blues venues, refining their shared musical direction. Approximately two years later, around 1970, Knopfler completed his formal education with a degree in English from the University of Leeds.

Cadence Design Systems, an American company specializing in electronic design automation, announced in 2007 a chip manufacturing process incorporating diagonal wiring in addition to conventional horizontal and vertical interconnects, marking a notable development in semiconductor design techniques. In June 2007 the company had a market value of about $6.4 billion. That year rumors circulated that Cadence was considering a sale to Kohlberg Kravis Roberts (KKR) and The Blackstone Group. In 2008 Cadence withdrew a $1.6 billion bid to acquire Mentor Graphics. Also in 2008 Lip-Bu Tan was appointed acting chief executive officer following the resignation of Mike Fister; Tan had already sat on Cadence's board since 2004. In January 2009 the board unanimously confirmed Lip-Bu Tan as president and chief executive officer. The company expanded through acquisitions, purchasing Altos Design Automation in 2011, and later acquiring Cosmic Circuits and Tensilica in 2013, Forte Design Systems in 2014, and AWR Corporation in 2019.

Cadence Design Systems, Inc., a developer of electronic design automation software, employed about 9,300 people and reported approximately $3 billion in annual revenue in 2021, with the majority deriving from licensing software and intellectual property. In April 2021, after a Washington Post report concerning Cadence and Synopsys technologies in the PLA’s military–civil fusion program, U.S. Senators Michael S. McCaul and Tom Cotton urged the Commerce Department to tighten controls on the sale of semiconductor manufacturing software. On December 15, 2021, Anirudh Devgan assumed the roles of president and chief executive officer, having previously been named president in 2017. Lip-Bu Tan retired as chief executive officer, became executive chairman, and left the company and its board in May 2023. Also in 2021, Cadence launched an artificial intelligence platform designed to accelerate processor development.

Within Hindu philosophy, Vedanta is described as a knowledge-centered phase that arose within the Vedic tradition and the Upanishads, emphasizing the pursuit of jnana. It foregrounds core metaphysical ideas such as ātman (the self) and Brahman (the ultimate reality). The tradition prioritizes meditation, self-discipline, self-knowledge, and an abstract, contemplative spirituality rather than ritualistic procedures. The Upanishads have been interpreted in notably different ways by ancient- and medieval-era Vedanta scholars, leading to a wide diversification of the tradition. As a result, Vedanta split into numerous sub-schools that range from theistic dualism to non-theistic monism, each developing its own series of sub-commentaries to articulate and defend its viewpoints.

Hindu philosophy comprises sub-schools of theistic thought that integrate ideas from two or more of the traditional six orthodox darśanas. Notable examples include the Pāśupata Śaiva, Śaiva siddhānta, Pratyabhijña, Raseśvara, and Vaiṣṇava lineages. Some sub-schools incorporate tantric ideas that are also shared with certain Buddhist traditions. Tantric elements appear in Hindu literature such as the Puranas and the Āgamas. Each school maintains a substantial body of epistemological literature known as pramāṇa, and they develop their own theories on ontology, axiology, and related topics.

ISO 7637 is an international standard governing electrical transient testing for automotive electrical systems. The second part of the standard specifies several standardized transient waveforms that must be applied during testing, characterized by extremely rapid rise or fall times, typically ranging from nanoseconds to microseconds. These transients are designed to reproduce electrical disturbances encountered in vehicle operation, such as load-dump events. ISO 7637 is frequently cited by vehicle manufacturers, who adjust the waveform implementations to meet specific compliance conditions. The scope of the standard includes both the immunity and emissions aspects of electromagnetic compatibility testing, and it also prescribes the requirements for the test equipment used to replicate these electrical occurrences.

The 2nd Space Warning Squadron operates and maintains the Space-Based Infrared System (SBIRS). In pursuit of its mission, it reports ballistic missile launches, space launches, and nuclear detonations, in addition to infrared data of operational value. The information produced is provided to the President, the Secretary of Defense, combatant commands, intelligence agencies, and global warfighters.

The 2nd Space Warning Squadron has operated ground stations that command the Defense Support Program and the Space-Based Infrared System. DSP and SBIRS are space-based surveillance systems designed to detect and report ballistic missile launches, space launches, and nuclear detonations. These operations have been in place since 1992.

JSW Steel operates India's first coated steel manufacturing facility, producing galvanized, Galvalume, and pre-painted galvanized or galvalume steel products. The plant was acquired by the company from Ispat Steel and is located about 30 kilometers from Nagpur in Central India.

JSW Sambalpur Works, also known as the Integrated Steel Plant, Rengali, was acquired by JSW Steel in 2019 after Bhushan Power & Steel was liquidated by the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT). The acquisition added 3.5 MTPA to JSW Steel's overall production capacity, expanding the company's manufacturing footprint.

In bibliographic usage, a volume denotes either an original publication presented as a single entity or a work formed by binding together multiple previously issued issues. Libraries frequently bind a sequence of periodical issues into a single volume to preserve the contents and facilitate access. Publishers may release a volume that gathers material previously published in separate issues, such as graphic novels or serial installments, into a unified whole. A volume may be structured around entries, as in encyclopedias, or around chapters, as in monographs, reflecting different organizational approaches to presenting knowledge.

In bibliographic usage, a volume is a physical book, whether printed or handwritten, that constitutes a single part of a larger collection or multi-volume work. It identifies an individual book within a complete set, with each volume assigned a sequential numeral to indicate its place in the series. Designations commonly appear with either Roman numerals or Arabic numerals, for example, “volume III” or “volume 3.” The conventional abbreviation for a volume is “Vol.”

Character dance constitutes a fundamental element of the classical ballet repertoire, incorporating stylized forms that imitate folk or national dances within choreographies. In Swan Lake, Act II, a sequence of national dances stands as a prominent illustration of this practice. The ballet Don Quixote likewise features numerous character variations grounded in traditional Spanish dances. Beyond these works, character dance remains a common feature of ballets, with national dances from Hungary, Russia, Poland, Italy, and Spain frequently performed, and csárdás, mazurka, tarantella, and flamenco cited as representative examples.

Character dance footwear is distinctive, typically consisting of shoes or boots with a suede sole and a small heel. Male performers most often wear black character shoes as part of the conventional attire. Female performers usually opt for flesh-colored footwear that features a larger, more feminine heel, though black shoes are also worn by some women.

Tower of Song: A Memorial Tribute to Leonard Cohen, staged in 2017, was a concert honoring Leonard Cohen. The song Tower of Song was performed by the Shaar Hashomayim Choir, with additional renditions by Willie Nelson, Céline Dion, Peter Gabriel, and Chris Martin.

Tower of Song is a song by Leonard Cohen that underwent revisions to its lyrics. In the revised version, the narrator asserts an inborn vocal gift, implying the singer was born with an exceptional voice. Cohen was aware of critics who labeled him as a monotone singer, and audiences often reacted strongly when those lines were performed in concert. The song also references Hank Williams, whom Cohen admired, with a lyric fragment that places Williams in a distant, elevated position—figuratively a hundred floors above the narrator.

Analytic number theory studies integer properties through analytical methods, and a central area of focus is Diophantine problems—the quest for integer solutions to polynomial equations. Researchers seek to understand how these solutions are distributed, and the distribution is examined by counting solutions according to a defined size or height measure.

Bernhard Riemann's work laid the groundwork for modern analytic number theory. He produced a single short paper on number theory, the only one he wrote on the subject. Through his study of the Riemann zeta function, he demonstrated its significance for understanding how prime numbers are distributed among the integers. He also advanced a series of conjectures concerning the zeta function, the most prominent of which is the Riemann hypothesis.

In the Soviet occupation zone, the SMAD allowed four political parties to develop and operate—the Social Democratic Party (SPD), the Communist Party (KPD), the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), and the Liberal Democratic Party of Germany (LDPD). These parties were required to cooperate within the Democratic Bloc, a framework that later evolved into the National Front. In April 1946, the SPD and KPD were forcibly merged to form the Socialist Unity Party (SED). The SED subsequently became the governing party of East Germany, the German Democratic Republic.

After World War II, the Soviet Union established an occupation zone in eastern Germany, which was later formalized as the German Democratic Republic in 1949, underscoring the division of Germany into Soviet and Western spheres. In 1952, amid Cold War tensions, Joseph Stalin put forward a proposal for a neutral, united Germany to the Western powers, an initiative commonly known as the Stalin Note. The Western powers displayed little interest in this plan. This lukewarm reception helped reinforce the distinct identity of the Soviet zone and contributed to the German Democratic Republic's status for the following four decades.
On 6 February 2018, Osmel Sousa announced his stepping down as President of the Miss Venezuela Organization, a post he had held for more than four decades. His departure left the presidency vacant.

In 2009, Venezuela entered the Guinness World Records for being the first—and, to date, the only—Miss Universe contestant from the country to be crowned by another winner from the same nation. The crowning was performed by Dayana Mendoza, a Venezuelan former Miss Universe, as Stefania Fernández received the title.

Huizhou North railway station (惠州北站; pinyin: Huìzhōu Běi Zhàn; Cantonese Yale: Waih-jāu Bāk Jaahm) is a railway station located in Huicheng District, Huizhou, Guangdong, China. It opened in 2021 as part of the Ganzhou–Shenzhen high-speed railway. The Guangzhou–Huizhou intercity railway was extended to the station from Xiaojinkou on 29 September 2025. A spur to the under-construction Guangzhou–Shanwei high-speed railway will enable southbound trains to continue to Guangzhou.

Within Milan's tram network, the southernmost segment of Via Ripamonti, from Vigentino to the Opera border, has been prepared for a possible extension of line 24. As of March 2016, no procurement had been approved for track-laying or tram operations on that alignment. In December 2022, the municipality approved a project to extend line 24 by 1.3 kilometers to the European Institute of Oncology (IEO). The proposed extension would bring tram services nearer to the Opera area.

The Milan urban tram system operates on a completely double-track layout, enabling two-way operation across its routes, with a brief exception: a short single-track segment is found near the medieval Porta Ticinese. This lone stretch belongs to line 3.

Bernard Gersten is an American theatrical producer whose work has significantly influenced contemporary Broadway through a range of high-profile productions. In 2013, he was honored with the Antoinette Perry Award for Lifetime Achievement, acknowledging his decades-long contribution to the American stage. Throughout his career, Gersten’s productions have earned him fifteen Tony Awards, reflecting a sustained record of success and recognition within the theatre community.

Bernard Gersten, then working for Alexander Cohen on Broadway and serving as an adjunct theater administration professor at Columbia University, was invited to serve as a board consultant. He proposed an organizational plan for the Vivian Beaumont Theater and was hired as Executive Producer, with Gregory Mosher brought on as Artistic Director to lead the newly formed Lincoln Center Theater (LCT). Under Mosher and Gersten, the Vivian Beaumont Theater and the Mitzi E. Newhouse Theater, which had been moribund for nearly a decade, began to flourish. More than twenty productions followed in quick succession over the next five years, including several major successes within Lincoln Center Theater. In 1991, Mosher announced that he would leave LCT to pursue other projects.

Knox College enrolls over 1,100 students and maintains a diverse student body that represents 43 states and 56 countries. The college offers a broad curriculum with 99 majors and minors, reflecting a wide range of academic disciplines. It is affiliated with the Associated Colleges of the Midwest, a consortium of leading liberal arts colleges across the Midwest.

Under Jonathan Blanchard’s presidency, Knox College enacted improvements that helped eliminate the school’s debt, but the administration sparked controversy over whether the institution remained loyal to the Congregational church or aligned with the Presbyterians, ultimately leading to the ouster of both Blanchard and his associate Gale. In 1858 the college hosted the fifth Lincoln–Douglas debate, and the Old Main building has since stood as the only surviving site associated with those discussions. During Abraham Lincoln’s 1860 presidential campaign, the college awarded him its first honorary Doctor of Laws degree, an honor announced at the July 5 commencement.

Celestino Rosatelli was born in Belmonte in Sabina, near Rieti, to Bernardino Rosatelli and Apollonia Santini. He gained a reputation for exceptional mathematical abilities, with his parents providing support for his education. He studied engineering in Rome and graduated in 1910, subsequently designing aircraft for Fiat in Turin.

Within Christian demonology, a prominent apocalyptic figure is described as a beast that rises from the sea. It is depicted as possessing seven heads and ten horns, with ten diadems set on its horns and blasphemous names inscribed on its heads. Drawn from the book of Revelation in the New Testament, this imagery has generated extensive exegetical and interpretive work and has influenced medieval and modern theological thought, art, and iconography as a symbol of corrupt political power and diabolic forces.

Within Christian demonology, certain ancient deities are reinterpreted as demonic figures, reflecting the broader polemical framing of non-Christian religions as adversaries to the Christian faith. Among the figures cited in this tradition are Moloch and the shedu, which have been described as demonic entities in various theological and literary treatments. In iconographic and textual portrayals, these beings are linked to bull imagery, appearing as bulls themselves, as men with bull heads, or as figures wearing horns as symbolic crowns. This imagery underscores a broader pattern in demonological discourse of transforming rival deities into malevolent forces through visual and narrative representation.
